nodes.summary: Implements USE <namespace>: for the session catalog with a one-part namespace it updates the V1 current database with a namespace-exists check, otherwise it asserts the namespace exists in the current catalog; the manager lock is intentionally not held across V1 callbacks (SPARK-56939).

nodes.name: sessionPathEntries
nodes.summary: Effective SQL PATH entries: the stored SET PATH value, else the parsed DEFAULT_PATH conf; None when PATH is disabled.

nodes.name: confDefaultPathEntries
nodes.summary: Parses and expands the DEFAULT_PATH conf with CatalystSqlParser.parsePathElements and PathElement.expand, caching the result in an AtomicReference keyed by the trimmed string and the function resolution order.

nodes.name: sqlResolutionPathEntries
nodes.summary: Ordered catalog and schema path entries for resolving unqualified names: resolved session path when PATH is in effect, otherwise conf.defaultPathOrder (legacy). A two-argument overload at lines 356-361 delegates here.

nodes.name: resolutionPathEntriesForAnalysis
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for analysis-time path entries (relations, routines, procedures): returns pinned path from a view or SQL function when PATH is enabled, otherwise sqlResolutionPathEntries using the view home schema as path default.

nodes.name: currentCatalog
nodes.summary: Returns catalog(name) where name is the explicitly set current catalog or SQLConf.DEFAULT_CATALOG.

nodes.name: setCurrentCatalog
nodes.summary: Implements USE CATALOG: no-op if unchanged; otherwise force-loads the catalog (failing early if unknown), resets the V1 current database to the default database, then publishes the new catalog name and clears the current namespace.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Test-only: clears loaded catalogs, current catalog and namespace, session path and path cache, and resets the V1 current database.

nodes.name: CatalogManager$
nodes.summary: Companion object: SESSION_CATALOG_NAME = "spark_catalog", SYSTEM_CATALOG_NAME = "system", SESSION_NAMESPACE = "session", BUILTIN_NAMESPACE = "builtin"; the SessionPathEntry types (CurrentSchemaEntry, LiteralPathEntry); and helpers to recognise system.session and system.builtin paths and to serialize or parse frozen PATH metadata stored with views and SQL functions.

nodes.name: databaseForSessionQualifiedViewIdentifier
nodes.summary: Maps a view identifier namespace to the V1 database name: system.session or session becomes "session", other non-empty namespaces use the head, empty gives None.

nodes.name: pathEntriesForPersistence
nodes.summary: Computes resolved path entries to persist in view or SQL function metadata, optionally stripping system.session since persisted objects cannot reference temporary objects.

nodes.name: deserializePathEntriesOrFail
nodes.summary: Parses the stored frozen path JSON for a view or function and raises an AnalysisException if the payload is malformed.

nodes.name: V1Table.scala
nodes.summary: Wraps a V1 CatalogTable as a V2 Table (V1Table) so V1 session-catalog tables can flow through V2 code paths, with converters between V1 CatalogTable and V2 table or view metadata (toCatalogTable) and the V2TableWithV1Fallback marker trait.

nodes.name: V1Table
nodes.summary: Case class V1Table(v1Table: CatalogTable) extends the V2 Table: name is the quoted identifier, schema from the V1 schema, partitioning built from partition columns, bucket spec and cluster-by spec, properties from addV2TableProperties, and capabilities is an empty EnumSet (it can describe a table but not be read or written through V2 by itself).

nodes.name: properties
nodes.summary: Lazily exposes V1 table metadata as V2 properties via V1Table.addV2TableProperties.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Builds V2 Transforms: identity transform per partition column, then the bucket spec and cluster-by spec as transforms.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Returns an empty EnumSet of TableCapability, so Spark treats a bare V1Table as having no V2 read or write capability.

nodes.name: V1Table$
nodes.summary: Companion object with addV2TableProperties (V1 to V2 property mapping), getV2TableType, and three toCatalogTable converters (from DelegatingTable, from TableInfo, from View) that turn V2 metadata back into V1 CatalogTable.

nodes.name: addV2TableProperties
nodes.summary: Merges V1 properties, storage properties prefixed with "option.", provider, comment, collation, location, is_managed_location, external, table_type and owner into the V2 property map using TableCatalog.PROP_* keys.

nodes.name: toCatalogTable
nodes.summary: Converts a V2 TableInfo into a V1 CatalogTable: table_type MANAGED stays managed else EXTERNAL, reserved keys are promoted to first-class fields, option.* become storage properties, partition transforms become partition columns, bucket spec or cluster-by. Overloads at lines 113-117 (from DelegatingTable) and 167-217 (from View) share the name.

nodes.name: V2TableWithV1Fallback
nodes.summary: Trait for a V2 Table that also exposes its V1 CatalogTable so Spark can fall back to the V1 path when the V2 table lacks a capability that V1 provides.

nodes.name: FileDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: DataSource V2 base trait for the built-in file sources (parquet, orc, csv, json, text): a TableProvider and DataSourceRegister that declares fallbackFileFormat (the V1 FileFormat), parses path and paths options, and builds a FileTable through getTable. The companion object attaches file paths to read errors.

nodes.name: FileDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: What a file format implements to be a V2 source: fallbackFileFormat names the V1 FileFormat class used when V2 regresses or when catalog support is needed (see FallBackFileSourceV2 and DataSource.lookupDataSourceV2); getTable(options[, schema]) returns the FileTable; inferSchema caches the first table so getTable reuses it.

nodes.name: fallbackFileFormat
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the V1 FileFormat class for the same data source, used for fallback when the V2 implementation causes regressions (disable via SQL config) or when catalog support is needed.

nodes.name: getTableName
nodes.summary: Builds the table display name as shortName plus the qualified Hadoop paths, with sensitive parts redacted by the configured pattern.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: TableProvider hook: creates and caches the table with getTable(options) and returns its columns as a StructType; partition inference happens inside getTable.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: TableProvider.getTable: returns the table cached during schema inference, or builds one with the user-specified schema; two protected abstract/stub overloads (options only, options plus schema) are implemented by each format.

nodes.name: FileDataSourceV2$
nodes.summary: Companion with readPathsToSeq (JSON array of paths) and attachFilePath, which rewrites read failures into FAILED_READ_FILE style errors that name the file.

nodes.name: attachFilePath
nodes.summary: Maps exceptions to file-aware errors: upgrade errors and existing FAILED_READ_FILE pass through, schema column mismatch becomes a Parquet type mismatch error, FileNotFoundException a file-not-exist error, other non-fatal errors a cannot-read-files error.

nodes.name: FileScan.scala
nodes.summary: FileScan trait: the shared V2 Scan and Batch for file sources. It prunes files via the PartitioningAwareFileIndex using partition and data filters, splits files into FilePartitions with PartitionedFileUtil, reports size statistics and describes itself for explain output; format-specific scans only supply the reader factory.

nodes.name: FileScan
nodes.summary: Trait mixing Scan, Batch, SupportsReportStatistics, SupportsMetadata, SQLConfHelper and Logging. Abstract members: fileIndex, dataSchema, readDataSchema, readPartitionSchema, partitionFilters, dataFilters, sparkSession. Overrides toBatch (returns this), planInputPartitions, estimateStatistics, readSchema, description and getMetaData; createReaderFactory from Batch is not defined here and is left to concrete scans such as ParquetScan or OrcScan.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Whether a file path may be split across partitions; false by default, formats override.

nodes.name: readPartitionSchema
nodes.summary: Abstract: the partition columns that the query actually requires.

nodes.name: partitionFilters
nodes.summary: Abstract: filters used for partition pruning when listing files.

nodes.name: dataFilters
nodes.summary: Abstract: data filters usable for file listing.

nodes.name: partitions
nodes.summary: Core planning: lists files through fileIndex.listFiles(partitionFilters, dataFilters), computes maxSplitBytes, prunes partition values to the required partition columns, splits each file with PartitionedFileUtil.splitFiles (largest first), warns for one large unsplittable file, then packs into FilePartitions with FilePartition.getFilePartitions.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Batch implementation returning the FilePartitions as an array of InputPartition.

nodes.name: estimateStatistics
nodes.summary: SupportsReportStatistics: scales fileIndex.sizeInBytes by the compression factor and the ratio of read schema to full schema default sizes; row count is unknown.

nodes.name: readSchema
nodes.summary: Scan output schema: required data fields followed by required partition fields.

nodes.name: FileTable.scala
nodes.summary: FileTable abstract class: the V2 Table for file sources, supporting read and write with BATCH_READ and BATCH_WRITE capabilities. It lazily builds a PartitioningAwareFileIndex (metadata-log index for streaming sink output, else InMemoryFileIndex over globbed paths), resolves data and table schemas, and merges table options into per-operation options.

nodes.name: FileTable
nodes.summary: Base for ParquetTable, OrcTable, CSVTable, JsonTable and TextTable. Implements Table with SupportsRead with SupportsWrite but leaves newScanBuilder and newWriteBuilder to the format; subclasses supply inferSchema, formatName and fallbackFileFormat (the V1 FileFormat class).

nodes.name: fileIndex
nodes.summary: Builds the file index: MetadataLogFileIndex when the path holds streaming sink metadata, otherwise globs/validates paths via DataSource.checkAndGlobPathIfNecessary and creates an InMemoryFileIndex with a shared FileStatusCache.

nodes.name: dataSchema
nodes.summary: Uses the user-specified schema minus partition columns, else inferSchema over fileIndex.allFiles(), else fails; result is made nullable except for metadata-log indexes.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Table schema = dataSchema without overlapping columns plus partitionSchema; checks duplicate column names and that every data type is supported by the format.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Exposes the file index partition column names as V2 identity transforms.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Returns FileTable.CAPABILITIES, the EnumSet of BATCH_READ and BATCH_WRITE.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Abstract: infer the schema of the given files, or None when unsupported so the user must specify a schema.

nodes.name: fallbackFileFormat
nodes.summary: Abstract: V1 FileFormat class for the same source; FallBackFileSourceV2 uses it to turn an insert into a FileTable into a V1 HadoopFsRelation write.

nodes.name: FileTable$
nodes.summary: Companion holding the private CAPABILITIES EnumSet (BATCH_READ, BATCH_WRITE).

nodes.name: DataSourceV2Strategy.scala
nodes.summary: Physical planning strategy for DataSource V2. It turns V2 scan relations into BatchScanExec, MicroBatchScanExec, ContinuousScanExec or LocalTableScanExec (filters and projections were already pushed by V2ScanRelationPushDown in the optimizer), and maps V2 write, DDL, view, namespace, partition, cache and row-level-operation logical plans to their *Exec nodes. Its companion object also translates Catalyst expressions into V2 Predicates.

nodes.name: DataSourceV2Strategy
nodes.summary: SparkStrategy used by SparkPlanner that plans DataSource V2 logical operators into physical plans. For reads it wraps the already optimized DataSourceV2ScanRelation (with pushed filters, columns, aggregates and limits) into BatchScanExec, and for everything else (CREATE/REPLACE TABLE, INSERT, DELETE, MERGE, SHOW, ALTER, ...) it builds the matching V2 exec node that calls the catalog or table API. It also owns cache refresh helpers used after writes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Giant pattern match from LogicalPlan to Seq[SparkPlan], tried in order. First the read cases (V1 fallback scan, LocalScan, DataSourceV2ScanRelation to BatchScanExec, streaming micro-batch/continuous/real-time scans), then writes (WriteToDataSourceV2, AppendData, OverwriteByExpression, OverwritePartitionsDynamic, ReplaceData, WriteDelta, MergeRows), table/view/namespace DDL, partition management, cache, index and function commands. Unmatched plans return Nil so that the next strategy in SparkPlanner can try.

nodes.name: refreshCache
nodes.summary: Returns the callback that re-caches cached queries after a V2 write: recacheTableOrView by qualified name (without time travel) for catalog tables, or recacheByPlan for tables loaded through TableProvider.

nodes.name: recacheTable
nodes.summary: Builds the callback that recaches a ResolvedTable (optionally including time-travel entries) after DDL.

nodes.name: invalidateTableCache
nodes.summary: Invalidates the cache entry of a ResolvedTable and returns its StorageLevel if it was cached, so RENAME TABLE can re-cache it under the new name.

nodes.name: invalidateCache
nodes.summary: Uncaches a table or view (cascade) given its catalog and Identifier; used by REPLACE TABLE variants.

nodes.name: makeQualifiedDBObjectPath
nodes.summary: Qualifies a namespace location against the warehouse path and Hadoop conf (CatalogUtils.makeQualifiedDBObjectPath).

nodes.name: qualifyLocInTableSpec
nodes.summary: Qualifies a relative table location in a TableSpec using the Hadoop conf, but leaves relative paths to the catalog implementation to resolve.

nodes.name: case: V1 fallback scan
nodes.summary: When the DataSourceV2ScanRelation's scan is a V1ScanWrapper (the source implements V1Scan), builds the V1 TableScan relation, checks its schema equals scan.readSchema(), converts the RDD to InternalRow and plans a RowDataSourceScanExec carrying the pushed V1 filters and PushedDownOperators. Filters and projection are re-applied with withProjectAndFilter.

nodes.name: case: LocalScan
nodes.summary: When the scan is a LocalScan, reads scan.rows() on the driver and plans a LocalTableScanExec (no RDD), wrapped by withProjectAndFilter.

nodes.name: case: DataSourceV2ScanRelation to BatchScanExec
nodes.summary: Main batch read path. Projection and filters were already pushed down by V2ScanRelationPushDown, so the remaining filters are split into DynamicPruning filters and post-scan filters. Scalar-subquery filters on runtime-filterable columns are also routed as runtime filters (they stay in FilterExec for correctness) and BatchScanExec can use them via SupportsRuntimeV2Filtering. Builds BatchScanExec and adds a Project when the scan is not columnar so rows become UnsafeRow.

nodes.name: case: streaming micro-batch scan
nodes.summary: StreamingDataSourceV2ScanRelation with both start and end offsets is planned as MicroBatchScanExec over the MicroBatchStream, wrapped by withProjectAndFilter.

nodes.name: case: streaming continuous or real-time scan
nodes.summary: StreamingDataSourceV2ScanRelation with a start offset but no end offset: if realTimeModeDuration is set the stream must implement SupportsRealTimeMode and RealTimeStreamScanExec is created, otherwise ContinuousScanExec over the ContinuousStream (its inputPartitions are initialized eagerly).

nodes.name: case: WriteToDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Plans WriteToDataSourceV2Exec for a streaming/micro-batch write, with a callback that uncaches the target relation's cached queries.

nodes.name: case: CreateTable
nodes.summary: Validates default values, table constraints, generated and identity columns against the TableCatalog, then plans CreateTableExec with V2 columns and a table spec whose location is qualified.

nodes.name: case: CreateTableAsSelect
nodes.summary: CTAS planning: an atomic AtomicCreateTableAsSelectExec if the catalog is a StagingTableCatalog, otherwise CreateTableAsSelectExec.

nodes.name: case: CreateTableLike
nodes.summary: CREATE TABLE ... LIKE for a v2 catalog target; the source Table, persistent view or temp view is normalized to a table (views via V1Table) and CreateTableLikeExec is planned with a qualified location.

nodes.name: case: ReplaceTable
nodes.summary: Validates default values, constraints and generated/identity columns, then plans AtomicReplaceTableExec (StagingTableCatalog) or ReplaceTableExec, with an invalidateCache callback.

nodes.name: case group: v2 view DDL and inspection
nodes.summary: Routes view DDL and inspection on a non-session ViewCatalog to dedicated v2 execs: CreateV2ViewExec, AlterV2ViewExec, set/unset properties, schema binding, rename, SHOW CREATE TABLE, SHOW TBLPROPERTIES, SHOW COLUMNS, DESCRIBE, and DropViewExec. REFRESH TABLE and ANALYZE TABLE on such views are rejected with a clear UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE error instead of a generic no-plan failure.

nodes.name: case: CreateMetricView on v2 catalog
nodes.summary: CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS on a non-session v2 catalog: analyzes the metric view YAML during planning, collects table dependencies into a DependencyList and plans CreateV2MetricViewExec.

nodes.name: case: ReplaceTableAsSelect
nodes.summary: RTAS planning: AtomicReplaceTableAsSelectExec for a StagingTableCatalog, otherwise ReplaceTableAsSelectExec.

nodes.name: case: V1 batch write fallback append
nodes.summary: AppendData/InsertOnlyMerge on a SupportsWrite table with TableCapability.V1_BATCH_WRITE is planned as AppendDataExecV1 when the Write is a V1Write; any other Write type raises a batchWriteCapabilityError.

nodes.name: case: AppendData
nodes.summary: df.writeTo(...).append / INSERT INTO on a V2 table: AppendDataExec wrapping the planned query, with a cache refresh callback.

nodes.name: case: InsertOnlyMerge
nodes.summary: Insert-only MERGE planned as InsertOnlyMergeExec, same shape as AppendDataExec.

nodes.name: case: OverwriteByExpression
nodes.summary: INSERT OVERWRITE / overwrite by condition: OverwriteByExpressionExecV1 for V1_BATCH_WRITE tables, otherwise OverwriteByExpressionExec.

nodes.name: case: OverwritePartitionsDynamic
nodes.summary: Dynamic partition overwrite planned as OverwritePartitionsDynamicExec.

nodes.name: case: DELETE FROM
nodes.summary: DeleteFromTableWithFilters goes straight to DeleteFromTableExec. A general DeleteFromTable must have no subquery, every conjunct must be translated by translateFilterV2 (otherwise an error, since correctness depends on removing all matching rows), and the table must be SupportsDeleteV2.canDeleteWhere or a TruncatableTable with a TRUE condition (TruncateTableExec).

nodes.name: case group: ReplaceData, WriteDelta, MergeRows
nodes.summary: Row-level operations (DELETE/UPDATE/MERGE): ReplaceDataExec for group-based, WriteDeltaExec for delta-based sources, both refreshing the original relation's cache, and MergeRowsExec for the MergeRows operator.

nodes.name: case: WriteToContinuousDataSource
nodes.summary: Plans WriteToContinuousDataSourceExec for continuous-processing streaming writes.

nodes.name: case group: namespace, describe, show, drop/rename table
nodes.summary: Namespace and table-inspection commands: DescribeNamespaceExec, DescribeTableExec/DescribeColumnExec, DropTableExec, RenameTableExec, AlterNamespaceSetPropertiesExec, CreateNamespaceExec, DropNamespaceExec, ShowTablesExec/ShowViewsExec, ShowTablePartitionExec, SetCatalogAndNamespaceExec, ShowTablePropertiesExec. ANALYZE TABLE on a v2 table is rejected.

nodes.name: case group: partition management and unsupported v1-only commands
nodes.summary: AddPartitionExec, DropPartitionExec, RenamePartitionExec, TruncateTableExec, TruncatePartitionExec, ShowColumnsExec, ShowPartitionsExec and ShowCreateTableExec for tables implementing SupportsPartitionManagement; RECOVER PARTITIONS, SET SERDE, LOAD DATA, REPAIR TABLE and SHOW CREATE TABLE AS SERDE are rejected for v2 tables.

nodes.name: case group: CACHE / UNCACHE TABLE
nodes.summary: CacheTable, CacheTableAsSelect and UncacheTable are planned as CacheTableExec, CacheTableAsSelectExec and UncacheTableExec.

nodes.name: case: AddCheckConstraint
nodes.summary: Adds a CHECK constraint through a TableChange.addConstraint after validating catalog support, planned as AddCheckConstraintExec over the planned child (the existing data is validated).

nodes.name: case: AlterTableCommand
nodes.summary: ALTER TABLE changes on a resolved v2 table: validates the catalog supports the TableChanges and plans AlterTableExec with a recache callback.

nodes.name: case group: CREATE/DROP INDEX
nodes.summary: CreateIndexExec and DropIndexExec when the table implements SupportsIndex; otherwise a tableIndexNotSupportedError.

nodes.name: case group: SHOW FUNCTIONS and CALL
nodes.summary: ShowFunctionsExec for a FunctionCatalog namespace, and ExplainOnlySparkPlan for CALL procedure commands (the procedure is executed at analysis time, the plan only shows in EXPLAIN).

nodes.name: AppendWrite
nodes.summary: Private extractor object matching AppendData or InsertOnlyMerge and exposing (table, write, analyzedQuery); used by the V1 batch-write fallback case.

nodes.name: translateLeafNodeFilterV2
nodes.summary: Translates a leaf Catalyst predicate into a V2 Predicate using the PushablePredicate extractor.

nodes.name: translateFilterV2
nodes.summary: Public entry for translating a Catalyst Expression into a V2 Predicate (Option); delegates to translateFilterV2WithMapping with no mapping. Used by pushdown rules, DELETE planning and V2Writes.

nodes.name: translateFilterV2WithMapping
nodes.summary: Recursively converts And/Or/Not trees into V2 And/Or/Not Predicates and translates leaves via PushablePredicate. Both sides of And/Or must be translatable (see SPARK-12218), so a partly understood conjunct is not converted. An optional map records which Catalyst leaf produced each V2 leaf so PushDownUtils can rebuild expressions.

nodes.name: rebuildExpressionFromFilter
nodes.summary: Inverse of translateFilterV2WithMapping: rebuilds a Catalyst Expression from a V2 Predicate using the recorded mapping of leaf predicates; throws an internal error if a leaf is missing.

nodes.name: translateRuntimeFilterV2
nodes.summary: Translates a runtime filter InSubqueryExec on a pushable (nested) column into a V2 IN Predicate once the subquery has produced values; throws if the subquery has not finished, and logs a warning and returns None for other expressions.

nodes.name: translateScalarSubqueryFilterV2
nodes.summary: Replaces evaluated scalar subqueries by literals and translates the result to a V2 Predicate; used at runtime in BatchScanExec for scalar-subquery runtime filters.

nodes.name: withProjectAndFilter
nodes.summary: Builds the plan above a scan leaf: ANDs the filters into a FilterExec, and adds a ProjectExec when the output differs from the required projection or when an unsafe-row conversion is needed.

nodes.name: PushablePredicate
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply asks V2ExpressionBuilder (predicate mode) to turn a Catalyst Expression into a data source V2 Predicate when it is pushable.

nodes.name: V2ScanRelationPushDown.scala
nodes.summary: Optimizer rule (non-excludable, in SparkOptimizer.earlyScanPushDownRules) that pushes operators of a query into DataSource V2 scans in a fixed order: sample, filters, join, aggregates, variant extractions, limit/offset/top-N, then builds the Scan and prunes columns. What the source accepts shows up in the EXPLAIN scan node as PushedFilters, PushedAggregates, PushedLimit, PushedTopN, PushedSample and so on; whatever it rejects stays in Spark as Filter/Aggregate/Limit/Sort.

nodes.name: V2ScanRelationPushDown
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] object that drives operator pushdown into V2 data sources. It first replaces every DataSourceV2Relation with a ScanBuilderHolder (a mutable leaf holding the ScanBuilder and the pushed state), lets each pushdown step offer its operator to the builder through the SupportsPushDown* interfaces, and finally calls build() and prunes columns to produce DataSourceV2ScanRelation. Data sources only see operators that Spark could translate; anything not accepted remains in the plan.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object extending Rule[LogicalPlan] with PredicateHelper; all steps are LogicalPlan => LogicalPlan functions folded in a fixed sequence.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Runs eleven steps as a foldLeft in this exact order: createScanBuilder, pushDownSample, pushDownFilters, pushDownJoin, pushDownAggregates, pushDownVariants, pushDownLimitAndOffset, buildScanWithPushedAggregate, buildScanWithPushedJoin, buildScanWithPushedVariants, pruneColumns. The first seven only record decisions on the ScanBuilderHolder; the build* steps call builder.build() to create the Scan, and pruneColumns last.

nodes.name: createScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Step 1. Replaces each DataSourceV2Relation with ScanBuilderHolder(output, relation, table.asReadable.newScanBuilder(options)), so later steps can push operators into the source's ScanBuilder.

nodes.name: pushDownSample
nodes.summary: Step 2. Pushes TABLESAMPLE (Sample over a scan, with no filters between) into the builder via PushDownUtils.pushTableSample (SupportsPushDownTableSample) and removes the Sample node when accepted. If the source rejects a SYSTEM sample, or there is no scan under it, the query fails with an AnalysisException; other samples stay in Spark.

nodes.name: pushDownFilters
nodes.summary: Step 3. For Filter over a ScanBuilderHolder: splits conjuncts, normalizes them to the relation output, keeps subquery predicates in Spark, and asks PushDownUtils.pushFilters to offer the rest to the builder (V1 Filter, V2 Predicate, or Catalyst filter interfaces). Returns the filters the source did not fully handle as post-scan filters (they may overlap with pushed ones, e.g. Parquet row-group filtering), records pushedPredicates and pushedFilterExpressions on the holder, and logs Pushed Filters / Post-Scan Filters. This is what EXPLAIN shows as PushedFilters.

nodes.name: pushDownJoin
nodes.summary: Step 4. Bottom-up, tries to push a Join whose two sides are ScanBuilderHolders with SupportsPushDownJoin builders that are compatible. Requires the join-pushdown config, only AttributeReference projections between join and holder, a join condition (no cross joins), no pushed samples (unless a no-op), and isOtherSideCompatibleForJoin. Generates aliases for duplicate column names, translates the condition and join type, calls lBuilder.pushDownJoin, and on success merges both holders into one; otherwise the Join stays in Spark.

nodes.name: generateColumnAliasesForDuplicatedName
nodes.summary: Computes SupportsPushDownJoin.ColumnWithAlias arrays for both join sides so output column names are unique case-insensitively (suffix _1, _2, ... for duplicates; unique names get no alias).

nodes.name: getRequiredColumnNames
nodes.summary: Returns the up-to-date column names of join projections, mapped through pushedJoinOutputMap when joins were pushed before.

nodes.name: pushDownAggregates
nodes.summary: Step 5. Applies rewriteAggregate to every Aggregate node to push aggregate functions and GROUP BY into sources implementing SupportsPushDownAggregates.

nodes.name: pushDownVariants
nodes.summary: Step 6. For scans whose builder implements SupportsPushDownVariantExtractions (when PUSH_VARIANT_INTO_SCAN is enabled), pushes variant field extractions found in the projection and filters via pushVariantExtractions.

nodes.name: getColumnName
nodes.summary: Converts an ordinal path into nested struct field names (throws an internal error if a non-struct is reached).

nodes.name: pushVariantExtractions
nodes.summary: Collects variant field accesses with VariantInRelation, builds VariantExtraction requests, calls builder.pushVariantExtractions and keeps the accepted ones. The holder's output attributes are rewritten to the struct types the source will return and the transformation info is stored on the holder; the plan itself is returned unchanged, because the rewrite happens in buildScanWithPushedVariants.

nodes.name: rewriteAggregate
nodes.summary: Core of aggregate pushdown. Collapses projections under the Aggregate, translates aggregate functions and grouping expressions to a V2 Aggregation (DataSourceStrategy.translateAggregation), and asks the builder supportCompletePushDown then pushAggregation. AVG is rewritten to SUM/COUNT when complete pushdown is not supported; partial pushdown is allowed only for min/max/sum/count without DISTINCT. On success the holder output becomes group_col_i / agg_func_i columns. With complete pushdown the Aggregate is replaced by a Project over the holder; with partial pushdown a final Aggregate stays in Spark (count becomes sum, etc.).

nodes.name: collectAggregates
nodes.summary: Collects distinct AggregateExpressions (by canonical form) and records their output ordinal, so duplicates such as max(a)+1 and max(a)+2 push down once.

nodes.name: supportPartialAggPushDown
nodes.summary: Returns true if the V2 Aggregation contains only SUM/COUNT without DISTINCT, MIN, MAX or COUNT(*), which are the only functions allowed for partial pushdown.

nodes.name: addCastIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Wraps an expression in a Cast (with session time zone if needed) when its data type differs from the expected one.

nodes.name: buildScanWithPushedAggregate
nodes.summary: Step 8. For a holder with a pushed aggregate, calls builder.build(), turns scan.readSchema() into the real output, wraps V1 scans, creates DataSourceV2ScanRelation and adds a Project that casts each source column to the expected data type.

nodes.name: buildScanWithPushedJoin
nodes.summary: Step 9. For a holder with more than one joined relation, builds the scan and projects the real columns back to the original names via aliases.

nodes.name: buildScanWithPushedVariants
nodes.summary: Step 10. For a holder with pushed variants, builds the scan and rewrites filters and project list expressions with the variant transformation so they use the extracted struct fields.

nodes.name: pruneColumns
nodes.summary: Step 11. For each remaining ScanBuilderHolder under a ScanOperation, prunes columns with PushDownUtils.pruneColumns (SupportsPushDownRequiredColumns, including nested schema pruning), builds the Scan and creates the DataSourceV2ScanRelation with the pruned output and the remapped pushed filters. Filters that stay in Spark are re-applied above the scan and a Project restores the original output names. The scan's readSchema is what appears as ReadSchema in EXPLAIN.

nodes.name: pushDownLimit
nodes.summary: Pushes a LIMIT into the builder (SupportsPushDownLimit) and, through a Sort over the scan, a top-N (ORDER BY ... LIMIT) via PushDownUtils.pushTopN (SupportsPushDownTopN) after translating the sort orders. Returns the new plan and whether the Limit can be dropped (not when the push was only partial). Sees through Projects; records pushedLimit and sortOrders on the holder.

nodes.name: pushDownOffset
nodes.summary: Pushes OFFSET into the builder via PushDownUtils.pushOffset (SupportsPushDownOffset), through deterministic Projects; records pushedOffset on the holder.

nodes.name: pushDownLimitAndOffset
nodes.summary: Step 7. Handles LimitAndOffset, OffsetAndLimit (offset(n).limit(m) pushes limit m+n), plain Limit and plain Offset. A limit is pushed first; OFFSET is pushed only when the limit was pushed and can be removed. Anything the source does not accept (or accepts only partially) keeps the Limit/Offset operators in Spark.

nodes.name: normalizeExpressions
nodes.summary: Normalizes expressions against relation output, or against up-to-date names via pushedJoinOutputMap when a join has been pushed.

nodes.name: getWrappedScan
nodes.summary: For V1Scan sources, wraps the scan in V1ScanWrapper together with the pushed V1 filters (SupportsPushDownFilters) and PushedDownOperators; other scans are returned unchanged.

nodes.name: getPushedDownOperators
nodes.summary: Snapshots the holder's pushed aggregate, sample, limit, offset, sort orders, predicates and joined-relation operators into PushedDownOperators (what EXPLAIN reports).

nodes.name: ScanBuilderHolder
nodes.summary: Leaf logical node used between createScanBuilder and build: it holds the ScanBuilder, the relation, a mutable output and all pushdown state (pushedPredicates, pushedAggregate, pushedLimit, pushedOffset, sortOrders, pushedSample, join and variant info, pushedFilterExpressions). It is replaced by DataSourceV2ScanRelation by the end of the rule.

nodes.name: V1ScanWrapper
nodes.summary: Scan wrapper for V1Scan sources carrying handled V1 filters and PushedDownOperators so DataSourceV2Strategy can plan a RowDataSourceScanExec.

nodes.name: V2Writes.scala
nodes.summary: Optimizer rule that turns V2 write logical plans into ones carrying a built Write. For df.writeTo(...).append() or saveAsTable on a V2 table it asks the table for a WriteBuilder, builds the Write, and rewrites the query to satisfy the Write's required distribution and ordering.

nodes.name: V2Writes
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] object that fills the write field of AppendData, InsertOnlyMerge, OverwriteByExpression, OverwritePartitionsDynamic, ReplaceData and WriteDelta, and converts WriteToMicroBatchDataSource into WriteToDataSourceV2. Every case obtains a WriteBuilder from the table, builds the Write, then calls DistributionAndOrderingUtils.prepareQuery so the query is repartitioned and sorted as the Write requires. It is listed in SparkOptimizer (early scan push down rules).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object extending Rule[LogicalPlan]; apply is a transformDown with one pattern-match case per V2 write command.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rewrites the plan with transformDown. AppendData, InsertOnlyMerge, ReplaceData and WriteDelta build the Write directly; OverwriteByExpression translates the delete predicates to V2 filters (failing if any cannot be translated) and requires SupportsTruncate or SupportsOverwriteV2; OverwritePartitionsDynamic requires SupportsDynamicOverwrite; WriteToMicroBatchDataSource becomes WriteToDataSourceV2 wrapping a MicroBatchWrite. Each case then prepares the query for the Write's distribution and ordering.

nodes.name: mergeOptions
nodes.summary: Merges command options with the DataSourceV2Relation options, asserting they agree or that one side is empty (DataFrame API carries both, DataFrameV2 only the command, SQL only the relation).

nodes.name: buildWriteForMicroBatch
nodes.summary: Builds a Write for a streaming micro-batch by output mode: Append uses build(), Complete requires SupportsTruncate and truncates first, Update requires SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend.

nodes.name: isTruncate
nodes.summary: Returns true when the delete predicates are exactly one ALWAYS_TRUE predicate, which is how an overwrite of everything (truncate) is recognised.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates a LogicalWriteInfoImpl (query id, row schema, options, optional metadata schema) and calls newWriteBuilder on the writable table. This is where a V2 table is asked how it wants to write.

nodes.name: newDeltaWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a LogicalWriteInfoImpl from WriteDeltaProjections (row, row id and metadata schemas) and returns the table's WriteBuilder, asserted to be a DeltaWriteBuilder, for delta-based row-level operations.

nodes.name: WriteToDataSourceV2Exec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical write path for DataSource V2: exec nodes for append, overwrite, dynamic overwrite, row-level replace and delta, CTAS/RTAS and streaming micro-batch writes, plus the shared V2TableWriteExec that runs one DataWriter per task, collects commit messages on the driver, and commits or aborts the BatchWrite.

nodes.name: WriteToDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Deprecated logical plan carrying a BatchWrite, query and custom metrics; V2Writes produces it for streaming micro-batch writes. It outputs nothing and wraps the query as its only child.

nodes.name: V2CreateTableAsSelectBaseExec
nodes.summary: Shared base for CTAS/RTAS execs. It converts the query schema to V2 columns and implements writeToTable, which runs an AppendData or OverwriteByExpression command on the new table via QueryExecution.runCommand, commits staged changes, and on failure aborts staged changes or drops the table.

nodes.name: getV2Columns
nodes.summary: Converts a Catalyst StructType into V2 Column definitions, restoring raw char/varchar types and forcing nullable when the catalog requires it.

nodes.name: writeToTable
nodes.summary: Builds a DataSourceV2Relation for the new table, wraps the query in AppendData.byPosition (or OverwriteByExpression with a true literal for RTAS), runs it as a nested command, then calls commitStagedChanges. If it fails, a StagedTable aborts its staged changes; otherwise the table is dropped.

nodes.name: CreateTableAsSelectExec
nodes.summary: Non-atomic CTAS exec for catalogs without staging: creates the table from the query schema and appends the query result through writeToTable. The table is dropped if creation or append fails.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Fails or returns empty if the table exists, creates the table with a TableInfo, calls writeToTable with overwrite=false, then commits the transaction if present.

nodes.name: AtomicCreateTableAsSelectExec
nodes.summary: Atomic CTAS exec for StagingTableCatalog: the table creation is staged and the write commit bundles metadata and data, with rollback of staged changes on failure.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Stages the table creation via stageCreate (or loads the table when none is returned) and writes the query result into it with writeToTable.

nodes.name: ReplaceTableAsSelectExec
nodes.summary: Non-atomic RTAS exec: drops the existing table, recreates it from the query schema and writes with overwrite=true. Documented as potentially unsafe because the old table is lost if later steps fail.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Refreshes the query with versioned relations pinned, invalidates the cache and drops the table (or fails if it is missing and not orCreate), creates the new table, writes with writeToTable(overwrite=true), then commits the transaction if present.

nodes.name: AtomicReplaceTableAsSelectExec
nodes.summary: Atomic RTAS exec for StagingTableCatalog: stageCreateOrReplace or stageReplace, then writes the query with overwrite=true. On failure staged changes are rolled back and the previous table is untouched.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Chooses stageCreateOrReplace (orCreate) or stageReplace (table exists, else error), then writes the query into the staged table with writeToTable(overwrite=true).

nodes.name: TransactionalExec
nodes.summary: Trait for physical write nodes that run inside a catalog transaction; the Transaction option is injected after planning by QueryExecution via withTransaction.

nodes.name: V2TableWriteExec
nodes.summary: Base physical plan for writing into DataSource V2. It runs the query child as an RDD, creates the DataWriterFactory from the BatchWrite, runs one write task per partition, gathers WriterCommitMessages on the driver, and commits the BatchWrite or aborts it on failure.

nodes.name: writeWithV2
nodes.summary: Core V2 job. Executes the query (substituting a one-partition empty RDD when there are zero partitions so metadata is still written), creates the DataWriterFactory from BatchWrite.createBatchWriterFactory, and runs a Spark job where each partition runs WritingSparkTask.run. As each task finishes the driver stores its WriterCommitMessage, adds to the output-row metric, and calls onDataWriterCommit. After all tasks succeed it calls BatchWrite.commit (with a WriteSummary when available), the atomic job commit; on any failure it calls BatchWrite.abort with the messages collected so far.

nodes.name: WritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Serializable per-task writing logic. Subclasses supply write(writer, iter); the shared run method creates the DataWriter, drives it over the partition iterator while updating metrics, commits (optionally gated by the output commit coordinator), and aborts and closes the writer on failure.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs on an executor for one partition: calls writerFactory.createWriter(partitionId, taskAttemptId), writes all rows with metric updates, then dataWriter.commit() returns the per-task WriterCommitMessage. With useCommitCoordinator it first asks the OutputCommitCoordinator and throws a commit-denied error if not authorized. On error it calls dataWriter.abort(); in all cases dataWriter.close(). Returns a DataWritingSparkTaskResult with the row count and commit message.

nodes.name: IteratorWithMetrics
nodes.summary: Private java.util.Iterator wrapper around the row iterator that counts rows and refreshes the DataWriter's custom metrics every NUM_ROWS_PER_UPDATE rows.

nodes.name: DataWritingSparkTaskResult
nodes.summary: Per-task result sent back to the driver: the number of rows written and the WriterCommitMessage returned by DataWriter.commit().

nodes.name: StreamWriterCommitProgress
nodes.summary: Sink progress information (number of output rows) recorded in V2TableWriteExec.commitProgress after a successful commit, for streaming progress reporting.

nodes.name: DataWritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Default WritingSparkTask used by V2TableWriteExec: writes the row iterator with DataWriter.writeAll. The commit and abort logic lives in the inherited WritingSparkTask.run.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the whole row iterator through DataWriter.writeAll.

nodes.name: DataAndMetadataWritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Row-level write task for ReplaceData with a metadata projection: routes UPDATE and COPY rows to writer.write(metadata, data) and INSERT rows to writer.write(data), counting updated and copied rows into SQL metrics.

nodes.name: DataWithProjectionWritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Row-level write task for ReplaceData without metadata: projects each row by operation (UPDATE, COPY, INSERT), writes it, and counts updated and copied rows.

nodes.name: DeltaWritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Delta write task: dispatches DELETE, UPDATE, REINSERT and INSERT rows to the DeltaWriter delete/update/reinsert/insert methods using row and row-id projections, counting updated and deleted rows.

nodes.name: DeltaWithMetadataWritingSparkTask
nodes.summary: Same as DeltaWritingSparkTask but also projects metadata columns and passes them to the DeltaWriter delete, update and reinsert calls.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Loops over rows and switches on the operation code in column 0, projecting data and metadata before writer.write; throws on unknown operations and adds counters to the SQL metrics.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Loops over rows, switches on the operation code, projects each row and calls writer.write; adds updated and copied counters to the SQL metrics.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Loops over rows and calls writer.delete, update, reinsert or insert depending on the operation code, counting updated and deleted rows.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Like DeltaWritingSparkTask.write but also projects metadata and passes it to delete, update and reinsert.

nodes.name: V2ExistingTableWriteExec
nodes.summary: Trait for write execs targeting an existing table (append, overwrite, row-level). Its custom metrics come from the Write, and run writes through write.toBatch, posts driver metrics, commits the transaction if any, and refreshes the cache.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls writeWithV2(write.toBatch) in try/finally so driver metrics from write.reportDriverMetrics() are always posted, then commits the transaction (if any) and refreshes the table cache. The BatchWrite commit or abort happens inside writeWithV2.

nodes.name: AppendDataExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for appending to a V2 table. This is what df.writeTo(t).append() and INSERT INTO run on a V2 table: it writes the query rows through the Write and reports an InsertSummary with the number of inserted rows.

nodes.name: InsertOnlyMergeExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for an insert-only MERGE rewrite. It behaves like AppendDataExec but reports a MergeSummary with all output rows counted as inserted.

nodes.name: OverwriteByExpressionExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for overwrite by filter in a V2 table. Rows matching the delete filters are removed and the query rows appended; SaveMode.Overwrite uses an always-true filter, which truncates the table.

nodes.name: OverwritePartitionsDynamicExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for dynamic partition overwrite: each partition present in the output replaces the existing partition, others are left untouched (Hive INSERT OVERWRITE semantics with partitionOverwriteMode=dynamic).

nodes.name: RowLevelWriteExec
nodes.summary: Trait for row-level operations (UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE) on V2 tables. It adds update, delete and copy row count metrics based on the command and builds the matching UpdateSummary, DeleteSummary or MergeSummary passed to BatchWrite.commit.

nodes.name: getMetricValue
nodes.summary: Reads a metric value by name, preferring the last-attempt value for SQLLastAttemptMetric so the number is stable across stage retries, and returns -1 if not found.

nodes.name: getWriteSummary
nodes.summary: Selects the merge, update or delete summary based on the row-level command.

nodes.name: getMergeSummary
nodes.summary: Finds the MergeRowsExec in the query and builds a MergeSummaryImpl from its target-row metrics.

nodes.name: getUpdateSummary
nodes.summary: Builds an UpdateSummaryImpl from the numUpdatedRows and numCopiedRows metrics.

nodes.name: getDeleteSummary
nodes.summary: Builds a DeleteSummaryImpl from the numDeletedRows and numCopiedRows metrics.

nodes.name: ReplaceDataExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for group-based row-level operations that rewrite whole groups of data in an existing table (DELETE, UPDATE, MERGE on tables using ReplaceData). It picks the writing task depending on whether a metadata projection exists.

nodes.name: writingTask
nodes.summary: Returns DataAndMetadataWritingSparkTask when a metadata projection exists, otherwise DataWithProjectionWritingSparkTask.

nodes.name: getDeleteSummary
nodes.summary: For DELETE, deleted rows are computed as scanned rows (from the BatchScanExec on a RowLevelOperationTable) minus copied rows, because deleted rows are filtered out before this node.

nodes.name: WriteDeltaExec
nodes.summary: Physical node that writes a delta of rows (delete, update, reinsert, insert operations) to an existing table through a DeltaWrite and DeltaWriter.

nodes.name: writingTask
nodes.summary: Lazily chooses DeltaWithMetadataWritingSparkTask or DeltaWritingSparkTask depending on whether a metadata projection is defined.

nodes.name: WriteToDataSourceV2Exec
nodes.summary: Physical node for WriteToDataSourceV2, used by streaming micro-batch sinks. It holds a ready BatchWrite and custom metrics, runs writeWithV2(batchWrite), then commits the transaction and refreshes the cache.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls writeWithV2(batchWrite), commits the transaction if present, refreshes the cache and returns the written rows (Nil).

nodes.name: CatalogPlugin.java
nodes.summary: Marker interface for a pluggable Spark catalog: initialize(name, options), name() and an optional defaultNamespace(). A catalog is registered with spark.sql.catalog.<name>=<class>, instantiated through its no-arg constructor by Catalogs.load and then configured by initialize. This is the entry point third-party connectors implement to plug their own tables into Spark.

nodes.name: CatalogPlugin
nodes.summary: Java interface (since 3.0.0) that every V2 catalog implements. Options passed to initialize come from all spark.sql.catalog.<name>.(key)=(value) settings with the prefix removed. Extra capabilities (tables, views, functions, namespaces) are added by implementing further interfaces such as TableCatalog.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Called exactly once right after the catalog class is instantiated, receiving the catalog name and a case-insensitive map of the spark.sql.catalog.<name>.* options.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Returns the catalog name that was passed to initialize; only valid after initialize has been called.

nodes.name: defaultNamespace
nodes.summary: Default method returning an empty namespace; when this catalog becomes the current catalog the returned multi-part namespace becomes the current namespace (it need not exist).

nodes.name: Table.java
nodes.summary: Defines the V2 Table interface: a logical structured data set (a file directory, a Kafka topic, a catalog table) described by name, columns, partitioning, properties, constraints, version and a set of TableCapability values. Readability and writability are added by mixing in SupportsRead and SupportsWrite.

nodes.name: Table
nodes.summary: Core V2 table abstraction (extends Relation; the other kind of Relation is View). Only name() and capabilities() are abstract; schema/columns, partitioning, properties, constraints, id and version have defaults. This is what makes a source "V2": Spark asks the table what it can do through capabilities() and then calls the mix-in interfaces.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Abstract: a meaningful identifier for the table, such as catalog database and table name or the file location.

nodes.name: id
nodes.summary: Optional table ID used to tell whether two Table objects refer to the same metastore entity (a dropped and recreated table must get a new ID); null when the connector has no such notion.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.4.0 default that throws a "must override one method" error; implementors should override columns() instead. columns() default derives from schema().

nodes.name: columns
nodes.summary: Returns the table columns; the default converts schema() via CatalogV2Util.structTypeToV2Columns keeping IDs.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Physical partitioning as an array of V2 Transform expressions; defaults to no partitioning.

nodes.name: properties
nodes.summary: String map of table properties; defaults to an empty map.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Abstract: the set of TableCapability values (BATCH_READ, BATCH_WRITE, TRUNCATE, ...) that Spark checks before planning reads and writes against this table.

nodes.name: TableCapability.java
nodes.summary: Java enum TableCapability listing the features a Table can advertise: BATCH_READ, MICRO_BATCH_READ, CONTINUOUS_READ, BATCH_WRITE, STREAMING_WRITE, TRUNCATE, OVERWRITE_BY_FILTER, OVERWRITE_DYNAMIC, ACCEPT_ANY_SCHEMA, AUTOMATIC_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION and V1_BATCH_WRITE.

nodes.name: TableCapability
nodes.summary: Enum of table capabilities returned from Table.capabilities(). Read: BATCH_READ, MICRO_BATCH_READ, CONTINUOUS_READ. Write: BATCH_WRITE and STREAMING_WRITE (append, with optional TRUNCATE, OVERWRITE_BY_FILTER, OVERWRITE_DYNAMIC), V1_BATCH_WRITE (append through the V1 InsertableRelation, no OVERWRITE_DYNAMIC). Others: ACCEPT_ANY_SCHEMA (any input schema on write) and AUTOMATIC_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION (Spark may alter the schema as part of an operation).

nodes.name: SupportsRead.java
nodes.summary: Mix-in interface that marks a Table as readable and adds newScanBuilder(options), the entry point from which Spark builds a Scan for batch, micro-batch or continuous reads.

nodes.name: SupportsRead
nodes.summary: Mix-in of Table for the read path. A table that implements it (and returns a read capability) lets the planner obtain a ScanBuilder, then a Scan, per data source scan.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder for the given immutable case-insensitive read options; Spark calls it to configure each data source scan.

nodes.name: SupportsWrite.java
nodes.summary: Mix-in interface that marks a Table as writable and adds newWriteBuilder(LogicalWriteInfo), used to create writes for batch or streaming.

nodes.name: SupportsWrite
nodes.summary: Mix-in of Table for the write path; Spark calls newWriteBuilder to configure each data source write that eventually yields a BatchWrite.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a WriteBuilder, from which a BatchWrite can be created, for the given logical write info (query id, schema, options).

nodes.name: SupportsRowLevelOperations.java
nodes.summary: Experimental mix-in interface letting a Table support row-level DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE by rewriting data, through newRowLevelOperationBuilder.

nodes.name: SupportsRowLevelOperations
nodes.summary: Experimental (since 3.3.0) Table mix-in signalling that the source can rewrite data to carry out DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE; this is the hook table formats use for row-level changes.

nodes.name: newRowLevelOperationBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a RowLevelOperationBuilder for the command info (such as DELETE and its options); Spark calls it while planning DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE that need data rewrites.

nodes.name: TableCatalog.java
nodes.summary: Catalog API for connectors that expose tables: listTables, loadTable (plus version, timestamp, write-privilege and CDC changelog variants), createTable, createTableLike, alterTable, dropTable, purgeTable, renameTable, and the reserved table property keys (location, provider, owner, comment ...). Extends CatalogPlugin.

nodes.name: TableCatalog
nodes.summary: The catalog interface that third-party connectors implement to expose tables to Spark SQL, extending CatalogPlugin. Abstract: listTables, loadTable, alterTable, dropTable, renameTable; everything else has a default. Also defines reserved property keys PROP_LOCATION, PROP_IS_MANAGED_LOCATION, PROP_EXTERNAL, PROP_TABLE_TYPE, PROP_COMMENT, PROP_COLLATION, PROP_PROVIDER, PROP_OWNER and OPTION_PREFIX ("option."). Views are handled by ViewCatalog, and RelationCatalog combines both.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Catalog-level capabilities (TableCatalogCapability), distinct from Table.capabilities; defaults to an empty set.

nodes.name: listTables
nodes.summary: Abstract: lists table identifiers in a multi-part namespace; may throw NoSuchNamespaceException.

nodes.name: listTableSummaries
nodes.summary: Default implementation enumerates listTables then loadTable for each entry and reads the table_type property (FOREIGN when absent); catalogs that can answer in one round trip should override.

nodes.name: loadTable
nodes.summary: Abstract: loads table metadata (a Table) by identifier, throwing NoSuchTableException if missing. Default overloads add loadTable(ident, writePrivileges) for tables about to be written (delegates to the plain form), loadTable(ident, String version) and loadTable(ident, long timestamp) for time travel (default: no such table error).

nodes.name: loadChangelog
nodes.summary: Since 4.2.0: returns a Changelog describing row-level changes in a range for Change Data Capture queries; default throws UnsupportedOperationException, catalogs supporting CDC override it.

nodes.name: invalidateTable
nodes.summary: Drops any cached metadata for an identifier; no-op by default and must not query remote services.

nodes.name: tableExists
nodes.summary: Default existence check implemented as loadTable(ident) != null, mapping NoSuchTableException to false.

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: Preferred since 4.1.0 form: creates a table from a TableInfo (columns, partitions, properties); the default forwards to the deprecated Column[] overload which in turn forwards to the deprecated StructType overload that throws "must override". May return null when metadata is expensive; Spark then calls loadTable (for example for CTAS).

nodes.name: createTableLike
nodes.summary: Since 4.2.0: hook for CREATE TABLE ... LIKE, receiving the new TableInfo (with owner set, source properties excluded) and the resolved source Table; default throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: useNullableQuerySchema
nodes.summary: If true (default), all query-schema fields are marked nullable when creating a table in CREATE or REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT.

nodes.name: alterTable
nodes.summary: Abstract: applies an ordered set of TableChange objects atomically (none applied if any is rejected); Spark discards the returned table.

nodes.name: dropTable
nodes.summary: Abstract: drops a table, returning whether one existed.

nodes.name: purgeTable
nodes.summary: Since 3.1.0: drop that skips any trash; default throws an unsupported purge error, catalogs able to purge must override.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Abstract: renames a table; may throw UnsupportedOperationException when old and new namespaces differ and the catalog cannot move tables.

nodes.name: StagingTableCatalog.java
nodes.summary: Optional TableCatalog mix-in for atomic CREATE TABLE AS SELECT and REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT: stageCreate, stageReplace and stageCreateOrReplace return a StagedTable whose commitStagedChanges is called after the BatchWrite commit.

nodes.name: StagingTableCatalog
nodes.summary: Without it, REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT is drop, create, then write via SupportsWrite.newWriteBuilder, so a failed write leaves the table dropped. With it, the planner stages the table, writes, and then StagedTable.commitStagedChanges swaps metadata and data atomically. Each stage method has deprecated StructType and Column[] overloads and a TableInfo form to override.

nodes.name: stageCreate
nodes.summary: Stages creation of a table (fails if it exists, concurrent creation fails at commit); default TableInfo form forwards to deprecated Column[] and StructType overloads.

nodes.name: stageReplace
nodes.summary: Stages replacement of an existing table; committing fails with NoSuchTableException if the table no longer exists.

nodes.name: stageCreateOrReplace
nodes.summary: Stages create-or-replace; unlike stageReplace the table is created at commit time if it does not exist.

nodes.name: supportedCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Declares commit metrics the catalog reports (analogous to Write.supportedCustomMetrics); values are read via StagedTable.reportDriverMetrics. Default none.

nodes.name: Scan.java
nodes.summary: Defines the Scan interface of the DataSource V2 read API: the logical description of a read that exposes the read schema and converts itself into a batch, micro-batch or continuous physical scan.

nodes.name: Scan
nodes.summary: Logical representation of a data source scan shared by batch, micro-batch and continuous reads. Spark asks it for readSchema() and then for the physical form (toBatch, toMicroBatchStream, toContinuousStream) that matches the capabilities the Table declared; it also reports custom metrics and whether partitions return columnar data.

nodes.name: readSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the actual schema this scan will produce, which can differ from the physical storage schema because of column pruning or other pushed-down optimizations.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Returns a human-readable description of the scan (filters, options such as path). Defaults to the implementation class name; implementations should override it. It does not need to repeat the read schema.

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Returns the physical Batch for a batch query. Throws by default, so a source must override it when its Table advertises BATCH_READ. May be called more than once if the scan supports runtime filtering, so implementations can cache planning state.

nodes.name: toMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: Returns the physical MicroBatchStream for micro-batch streaming reads. Throws by default; must be overridden when the Table advertises MICRO_BATCH_READ. The checkpoint location is a Hadoop FS scratch path usable for failure recovery.

nodes.name: toContinuousStream
nodes.summary: Returns the physical ContinuousStream for continuous streaming reads. Throws by default; must be overridden when the Table advertises CONTINUOUS_READ.

nodes.name: supportedCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the custom metrics (name and description) this scan supports; empty by default.

nodes.name: reportDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns custom metrics whose values are collected only on the driver side; they must be among the metrics returned by supportedCustomMetrics. Empty by default. Since 3.4.0.

nodes.name: columnarSupportMode
nodes.summary: Tells Spark whether columnar reads are decided per partition (PARTITION_DEFINED, the default) or fixed for the whole scan (SUPPORTED or UNSUPPORTED), using the nested ColumnarSupportMode enum. Since 3.5.0.

nodes.name: ScanBuilder.java
nodes.summary: Defines ScanBuilder, the builder interface that produces a Scan and the base for the SupportsPushDown mix-ins.

nodes.name: ScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for a Scan. Implementations mix in SupportsPushDownXYZ interfaces so Spark can push operators down, and keep the pushdown result in the Scan returned by build(). The documented pushdown order is sample, filter, aggregate, limit/top-n, offset, then column pruning.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the Scan reflecting every operator pushed into this builder so far.

nodes.name: SupportsRuntimeV2Filtering.java
nodes.summary: Mix-in for Scan that lets a data source prune already planned input partitions using V2 predicates that Spark derives at runtime, with optional iterative pushdown.

nodes.name: SupportsRuntimeV2Filtering
nodes.summary: Scan mix-in for runtime filtering with data source V2 Predicates (preferred over the V1 SupportsRuntimeFiltering; implement only one). Spark calls filter() when it can derive a predicate for one of filterAttributes(), then calls toBatch() again. With iterative pushdown, filter() may be called several times and state must accumulate.

nodes.name: filterAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the attributes this scan can be filtered by at runtime; Spark calls filter() when it can derive a runtime predicate for any of them.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Applies runtime predicates (ANDed together) to prune initially planned InputPartitions, which are replaced by empty ones or dropped from the reported partitioning. Must preserve any reported partitioning and may be called multiple times when iterative pushdown is enabled.

nodes.name: pushedPredicates
nodes.summary: Returns the predicates pushed via filter(), accumulated across all calls; empty if filter() was never called. Since 4.2.0.

nodes.name: supportsIterativePushdown
nodes.summary: Returns true if filter() may be called repeatedly, so Spark also pushes PartitionPredicates derived from runtime filters. False by default. Since 4.2.0.

nodes.name: BatchWrite.java
nodes.summary: Defines BatchWrite, the driver-side object that controls a batch write job: it creates the writer factory, receives per-task commit messages, and performs the atomic job commit or abort.

nodes.name: BatchWrite
nodes.summary: Defines how data is written to a source for batch processing. Lifecycle: createBatchWriterFactory is serialized to executors; each partition writer ends with DataWriter.commit() or abort(); if all succeed the driver calls commit(messages), otherwise abort(messages). onDataWriterCommit sees each message as it arrives. Spark retries failed tasks but not failed jobs.

nodes.name: createBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Creates the DataWriterFactory that is serialized and sent to executors, given physical info about the input data. If it throws, the action fails and no Spark job is submitted.

nodes.name: useCommitCoordinator
nodes.summary: Returns whether Spark uses the commit coordinator so at most one task per partition commits (true by default). If disabled, speculative tasks may all commit and one message per task reaches commit().

nodes.name: onDataWriterCommit
nodes.summary: Hook invoked on the driver with the commit message of each successful data writer; a no-op by default. If it throws, the job is treated as failed and abort() is called.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Atomic job commit: called with the commit messages of all successful data writers once all data is written. If it throws, the job failed and abort() is called with the destination state undefined. Inside a Transaction the data should be staged durably but not made visible until the transaction commits.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Overload of commit that also receives a best-effort WriteSummary of the operation; the default implementation ignores the summary and delegates to commit(messages).

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Best-effort cleanup when writers keep failing, the job fails, or onDataWriterCommit or commit throws. The messages array may contain null slots unless abort follows a commit failure; if it throws, manual cleanup of the source may be needed.

nodes.name: LogicalWriteInfo.java
nodes.summary: Defines LogicalWriteInfo, the logical information (options, query id, schemas) handed to a data source when it builds a WriteBuilder.

nodes.name: LogicalWriteInfo
nodes.summary: Logical write information available when creating a WriteBuilder: user write options, a unique query id (usable by a BatchWrite to identify the query across restarts), the input data schema, and optional row-id and metadata schemas used by row-level operations.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Returns the case-insensitive options the user specified when writing the dataset.

nodes.name: queryId
nodes.summary: Returns the unique id of the query; a restarted or resumed query keeps its id, so a BatchWrite can use it to identify the query.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns the schema of the input data Spark sends to the data source.

nodes.name: rowIdSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the schema of the row ID columns Spark sends to the source; throws a not-implemented error by default.

nodes.name: metadataSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the schema of the metadata columns Spark sends to the source; throws a not-implemented error by default.

nodes.name: RowLevelOperation.java
nodes.summary: Defines RowLevelOperation, the contract for DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE commands that a data source executes by rewriting data, pairing a scan builder with a write builder.

nodes.name: RowLevelOperation
nodes.summary: Logical representation of a data source DELETE, UPDATE or MERGE that requires rewriting data. It supplies a ScanBuilder and a WriteBuilder (Spark configures the scan first so the write can use scan information) and distinguishes delta-based sources, which take only changed rows, from group-based sources, which must get all rows of a group back and may filter groups at runtime.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Returns a description of this row-level operation; defaults to the implementation class name.

nodes.name: command
nodes.summary: Returns which SQL command is being performed, using the nested Command enum (DELETE, UPDATE or MERGE).

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder for reading the rows to change. Delta-based sources have no requirements on the scan; group-based sources must return every row of a group if any is returned, and may use runtime filtering through SupportsRuntimeV2Filtering to narrow down the groups to rewrite.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a WriteBuilder for writing the result back. Spark builds the scan before the write, so implementations may capture scan information (such as the read condition) for use under certain isolation levels.

nodes.name: requiredMetadataAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns metadata attributes needed to perform the operation (for example metadata columns used to group data when writing back); empty by default.

nodes.name: Write.java
nodes.summary: Defines the Write interface of the DataSource V2 write API: the logical write that converts into a BatchWrite or StreamingWrite and reports custom metrics.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: Logical representation of a data source write shared by batch and streaming. Spark obtains the physical form through toBatch() or toStreaming(); the one a source must implement depends on the BATCH_WRITE or STREAMING_WRITE capability its Table declares. Also reports custom metrics.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Returns a description of this write; defaults to the implementation class name.

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Returns the BatchWrite for batch writes. Throws by default, so a source must override it when its Table advertises BATCH_WRITE.

nodes.name: toStreaming
nodes.summary: Returns the StreamingWrite for streaming writes. Throws by default, so a source must override it when its Table advertises STREAMING_WRITE.

nodes.name: supportedCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the custom metrics (name and description) this write supports; empty by default.

nodes.name: reportDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns custom metrics collected only on the driver side; they must be among supportedCustomMetrics. Empty by default.

nodes.name: WriteBuilder.java
nodes.summary: Defines WriteBuilder, the builder that produces a Write and the base of the SupportsTruncate and SupportsOverwrite style mix-ins.

nodes.name: WriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for a Write. Without a mix-in the resulting Write appends data without touching existing data; mix-ins add other modes. The default build() returns a Write that delegates to the deprecated buildForBatch and buildForStreaming methods.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Returns the logical Write shared by batch and streaming. The default implementation wraps buildForBatch() and buildForStreaming() in an anonymous Write. Since 3.2.0.

nodes.name: buildForBatch
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.2.0 in favor of build(); returns a BatchWrite and throws by default.

nodes.name: buildForStreaming
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.2.0 in favor of build(); returns a StreamingWrite and throws by default.

nodes.name: WriterCommitMessage.java
nodes.summary: Defines WriterCommitMessage, the empty serializable marker interface for the message each data writer sends back to the driver.

nodes.name: WriterCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Commit message returned by DataWriter.commit() on the executor and delivered to the driver as input to BatchWrite.commit or StreamingWrite.commit. It is an empty Serializable interface: each data source defines its own message class carrying whatever the driver needs to finish the job commit.

nodes.name: TableProvider.java
nodes.summary: Declares the TableProvider interface, the base contract for v2 data sources that have no real catalog. It is what a data source named in format("x").load() or format("x").save() implements so Spark can obtain a Table.

nodes.name: TableProvider
nodes.summary: Base interface for v2 data sources without a catalog; implementations need a public 0-arg constructor. Spark calls inferSchema and inferPartitioning from the reader options, then getTable to get the Table used for read/write. It only supports data operations on existing tables, not create or drop.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the table schema from case-insensitive options that identify a table (for example a file path or topic name). Abstract: every provider must implement it.

nodes.name: inferPartitioning
nodes.summary: Infers table partitioning from the options. Default returns an empty Transform array; override if the source supports partitioning.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Returns a Table for the given schema, partitioning and properties, used for read and write. The table should report the same schema and partitioning as passed in, or Spark may fail the operation.

nodes.name: supportsExternalMetadata
nodes.summary: Returns true if the source accepts external table metadata (user-specified schema from the reader or writer, or schema/partitioning stored in the Spark catalog) when getting tables. Default false, meaning schema and partitioning come from the infer methods.

nodes.name: Batch.java
nodes.summary: Declares the Batch interface, the physical representation of a batch scan that plans input partitions and supplies the reader factory.

nodes.name: Batch
nodes.summary: Physical representation of a data source scan for batch queries. It tells Spark how many partitions the scanned data has (planInputPartitions) and how to read records from them (createReaderFactory).

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the InputPartition array, one per Spark task; its length equals the number of RDD partitions the scan outputs. Called once per scan to launch a single Spark job, and reflects any pushed filters.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Returns the PartitionReaderFactory used to create a PartitionReader for each InputPartition on executors.

nodes.name: InputPartition.java
nodes.summary: Declares InputPartition, the serializable description of one data split that is shipped to executors.

nodes.name: InputPartition
nodes.summary: Serializable representation of one input partition returned by Batch.planInputPartitions (and streaming equivalents). It is sent to executors, where a PartitionReader is created from it; the partition must be serializable but the reader need not be.

nodes.name: preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns host names where reading this partition is likely faster; Spark does not guarantee placement and unrecognized hosts are ignored. Default is an empty array, meaning no locality preference.

nodes.name: PartitionReader.java
nodes.summary: Declares PartitionReader, the executor-side iterator that outputs the records of one RDD partition.

nodes.name: PartitionReader
nodes.summary: Closeable reader returned by PartitionReaderFactory.createReader or createColumnarReader that outputs data for one RDD partition. Spark loops next() then get(); T is InternalRow for row sources or ColumnarBatch for columnar sources.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances to the next record and returns false when there are no more. May throw IOException on disk or network failure.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the current record; must return the same value until next() is called again.

nodes.name: currentMetricsValues
nodes.summary: Returns custom task metrics for this reader. Default is an empty array; should not do heavy work since it can affect read performance.

nodes.name: initMetricsValues
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 4.2.0 hook to seed metrics from the previous reader when readers are grouped into one partition. Default does nothing; replaced by CustomTaskMetric.mergeWith.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderFactory.java
nodes.summary: Declares PartitionReaderFactory, the serializable factory that builds row or columnar PartitionReaders on executors.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable factory of PartitionReader instances, returned by Batch.createReaderFactory. Spark calls createReader for rows or createColumnarReader when supportColumnarReads is true; failures in any of its methods fail and retry the Spark task.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Returns a row-based PartitionReader of InternalRow for the given InputPartition. Implementations usually cast the partition to their own concrete class.

nodes.name: createColumnarReader
nodes.summary: Returns a columnar PartitionReader of ColumnarBatch for the given InputPartition. Default throws a SparkUnsupportedOperationException (DATA_SOURCE_COLUMNAR_READER_NOT_SUPPORTED).

nodes.name: supportColumnarReads
nodes.summary: Returns true if the partition should be read in columnar mode, in which case createColumnarReader must be implemented. Default false; Spark reads all partitions columnar or none.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownAggregates.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ScanBuilder mix-in that lets a source accept aggregate push-down (such as min or max with GROUP BY).

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownAggregates
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder to push down aggregates. If the source cannot finish grouping, supportCompletePushDown returns false and Spark groups the output again. Filters are pushed first; aggregates cannot be pushed if pushed filters still need post-scan evaluation.

nodes.name: supportCompletePushDown
nodes.summary: Whether the source can do the aggregation completely. Default false, so Spark applies the grouping again over the source output.

nodes.name: pushAggregation
nodes.summary: Pushes the Aggregation to the source and returns true if accepted. Output columns must be the grouping columns followed by the aggregate columns in the order of the aggregate functions.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownFilters.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ScanBuilder mix-in for pushing V1 sources.Filter predicates into the source to shrink the data read.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownFilters
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder that accepts pushed V1 Filters. pushFilters returns the filters Spark still has to evaluate after the scan, and pushedFilters reports what was pushed. Filters are ANDed together. SupportsPushDownV2Filters is preferred.

nodes.name: pushFilters
nodes.summary: Receives the filters Spark would like to push and returns those that must still be evaluated after scanning (the residual). Rows returned must match all filters, which are ANDed.

nodes.name: pushedFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the filters pushed via pushFilters, including pushable ones that still need post-scan evaluation (for example a row group filter); returns an empty array if pushFilters was never called.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownLimit.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ScanBuilder mix-in for pushing a LIMIT into the source.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownLimit
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder to push down LIMIT, combinable with other operators in the order defined in the ScanBuilder class doc. pushLimit reports acceptance and isPartiallyPushed says whether Spark must still apply the limit.

nodes.name: pushLimit
nodes.summary: Pushes LIMIT n to the source and returns true if it was accepted.

nodes.name: isPartiallyPushed
nodes.summary: Whether the limit is only partially pushed. Default true, so Spark applies LIMIT again; only called when pushLimit returned true.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownRequiredColumns.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ScanBuilder mix-in for column pruning.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownRequiredColumns
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder so Spark can tell the source which columns are needed and the source reads only those. Pruning of nested fields may be partial; Scan.readSchema must reflect the pruning applied.

nodes.name: pruneColumns
nodes.summary: Applies column pruning for the given requiredSchema. Best effort: a source may prune only top-level columns and not nested fields.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownTopN.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ScanBuilder mix-in for pushing ORDER BY ... LIMIT n (top-N) into the source.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownTopN
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder to push down top N (ORDER BY with LIMIT), combinable with other operators per the ScanBuilder class doc order. pushTopN reports acceptance and isPartiallyPushed says whether Spark must redo the top N.

nodes.name: pushTopN
nodes.summary: Pushes the sort orders and limit to the source and returns true if accepted.

nodes.name: isPartiallyPushed
nodes.summary: Whether the top N is only partially pushed. Default true, so Spark applies top N again; only called when pushTopN returned true.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownV2Filters.java
