nodes.summary: Declares the preferred ScanBuilder mix-in for pushing V2 Predicate expressions, including iterative push-down.

nodes.name: SupportsPushDownV2Filters
nodes.summary: Mix-in for ScanBuilder that accepts V2 Predicates, preferred over SupportsPushDownFilters because it avoids internal to external data conversion. pushPredicates returns the residual predicates; with supportsIterativePushdown it may be called several times (for example with PartitionPredicate) and must accumulate state.

nodes.name: pushPredicates
nodes.summary: Pushes predicates and returns those that must be evaluated after the scan; unpushable ones must be returned unchanged. Predicates are ANDed, and state must accumulate across calls.

nodes.name: pushedPredicates
nodes.summary: Returns all predicates pushed via pushPredicates across every call, including those still needing post-scan evaluation; empty if none were pushed.

nodes.name: supportsIterativePushdown
nodes.summary: Returns true if pushPredicates may be called multiple times with additional predicates. Default false. Added in 4.2.0.

nodes.name: SupportsReportPartitioning.java
nodes.summary: Declares the Scan mix-in that lets a source report its output partitioning so Spark can avoid a shuffle.

nodes.name: SupportsReportPartitioning
nodes.summary: Mix-in for Scan to report data partitioning and avoid a shuffle on the Spark side. A scan that creates exactly one InputPartition may avoid a shuffle even without this interface.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Returns the output data Partitioning that this reader guarantees.

nodes.name: SupportsReportStatistics.java
nodes.summary: Declares the Scan mix-in that lets a source report statistics to the optimizer.

nodes.name: SupportsReportStatistics
nodes.summary: Mix-in for Scan to report statistics. Statistics are requested after operators are pushed to the source, so implementations can return more accurate numbers that help the optimizer.

nodes.name: estimateStatistics
nodes.summary: Returns the estimated Statistics of this scan, taking pushed operators into account.

nodes.name: DataWriter.java
nodes.summary: Declares DataWriter, the executor-side writer with the write, commit, abort and close lifecycle.

nodes.name: DataWriter
nodes.summary: Per-task writer (one exclusive writer per Spark task, so no thread safety needed) created by DataWriterFactory.createWriter. Lifecycle: write is called per record; if all succeed commit() returns a WriterCommitMessage for BatchWrite.commit, on any failure abort() is called, and close() follows commit or abort. Speculative tasks may run concurrently, so sources must handle conflicts. T is InternalRow.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Overload write(metadata, record) for group-based row-level operations that pass back metadata for updated or copied records. Default ignores the metadata and calls write(record). Since 4.0.0.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one record; if it throws, abort() is called and the writer is considered failed.

nodes.name: writeAll
nodes.summary: Writes all records from an iterator. Default calls write for each record. Since 4.0.0.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits after all records are written and returns a WriterCommitMessage sent to the driver and passed to BatchWrite.commit. Data should stay hidden from readers until that driver commit succeeds.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts a failed writer and cleans up already written records. Only called when a record failed to write or commit() failed.

nodes.name: currentMetricsValues
nodes.summary: Returns custom task metrics for this writer. Default is an empty array; avoid heavy logic as it can affect writing performance.

nodes.name: DataWriterFactory.java
nodes.summary: Declares DataWriterFactory, the serializable factory that creates one DataWriter per task on executors.

nodes.name: DataWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable factory of DataWriter returned by BatchWrite.createBatchWriterFactory. It is sent to executors, which call createWriter to create the writer; the DataWriter itself need not be serializable.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the DataWriter of InternalRow for a partition id and task attempt id (TaskContext.taskAttemptId). Spark reuses the row object, so writers must copy data before buffering. Failures fail and retry the task.

nodes.name: RequiresDistributionAndOrdering.java
nodes.summary: Declares the Write extension through which a sink requests how Spark distributes and orders data before writing.

nodes.name: RequiresDistributionAndOrdering
nodes.summary: Extends Write so a data source can require a data distribution, number of partitions or advisory partition size, and an ordering on write. Supported for batch and micro-batch writes (per micro batch); continuous mode does not support these requirements.

nodes.name: requiredDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns the Distribution Spark must satisfy by repartitioning before writing; may return UnspecifiedDistribution for no requirement.

nodes.name: distributionStrictlyRequired
nodes.summary: Whether the distribution is strictly required (default true) or best effort, in which case Spark may skip it for speed.

nodes.name: requiredNumPartitions
nodes.summary: Number of partitions required for the write. Default 0; any value below 1 means no requirement. Not allowed together with an unspecified distribution or an advisory partition size.

nodes.name: advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes
nodes.summary: Advisory shuffle partition size in bytes for the write. Default 0 means no preference; guidance only, ignored if adaptive execution is disabled.

nodes.name: requiredOrdering
nodes.summary: Returns the SortOrder array Spark must satisfy within partitions before writing; an empty array means no ordering.

nodes.name: SupportsDynamicOverwrite.java
nodes.summary: Declares the WriteBuilder mix-in for dynamic partition overwrite.

nodes.name: SupportsDynamicOverwrite
nodes.summary: WriteBuilder mix-in for dynamic partition overwrite: each logical partition that receives new data is fully replaced while other partitions are unchanged. Provided for Hive-compatible SQL but not recommended over overwrite by filter.

nodes.name: overwriteDynamicPartitions
nodes.summary: Configures the write to dynamically replace partitions with the data committed by the write; returns this builder for chaining.

nodes.name: SupportsOverwrite.java
nodes.summary: Declares the WriteBuilder mix-in for overwrite by V1 Filter, bridging the V2 Predicate overloads to it.

nodes.name: SupportsOverwrite
nodes.summary: WriteBuilder mix-in (extends SupportsOverwriteV2) for overwrite by filter: rows matching all ANDed filters are deleted and replaced by the committed data. Its default Predicate-based overloads convert to V1 filters, and truncate() overwrites with AlwaysTrue.

nodes.name: canOverwrite
nodes.summary: Checks whether data matching the V1 filters (ANDed) can be overwritten. Default returns true. Since 3.4.0.

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Configures the write to replace data matching the V1 filters (ANDed) with committed data; returns this builder.

nodes.name: canOverwrite
nodes.summary: Overload taking V2 Predicates: converts them to V1 filters and returns false if any cannot be converted, otherwise delegates to canOverwrite(Filter[]).

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Overload taking V2 Predicates: converts them to V1 filters and delegates to overwrite(Filter[]).

nodes.name: truncate
nodes.summary: Overrides truncate() to overwrite with the always-true filter, which replaces all data.

nodes.name: SupportsOverwriteV2.java
nodes.summary: Defines SupportsOverwriteV2, a WriteBuilder mix-in for overwrite-by-filter using V2 predicates, with truncate expressed as overwrite with an always-true predicate.

nodes.name: SupportsOverwriteV2
nodes.summary: WriteBuilder mix-in for tables that support overwrite by filter: rows matching all (ANDed) V2 Predicates are deleted and replaced by the data committed in the write. It also extends SupportsTruncate, implementing truncate() as overwrite with AlwaysTrue.

nodes.name: canOverwrite
nodes.summary: Checks whether rows matching the given V2 predicates can be overwritten; returns true by default. Since 3.4.0.

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Configures the write to replace data matching all of the ANDed predicates with the data committed in the write, and returns the builder for chaining.

nodes.name: truncate
nodes.summary: Overrides SupportsTruncate.truncate to overwrite with a single AlwaysTrue predicate, replacing all existing data.

nodes.name: SupportsTruncate.java
nodes.summary: Defines SupportsTruncate, a WriteBuilder mix-in for tables that can replace all of their data in one write.

nodes.name: SupportsTruncate
nodes.summary: WriteBuilder mix-in for tables that support truncation: all existing data is removed and replaced by the data committed in the write.

nodes.name: truncate
nodes.summary: Configures the write to replace all existing data with the data committed in the write, and returns the builder for chaining.

nodes.name: StorageLevel.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StorageLevel, the flag set (useDisk, useMemory, useOffHeap, deserialized, replication) that tells Spark how a cached RDD partition or block is stored, together with its companion object of named constants (MEMORY_ONLY, MEMORY_AND_DISK, DISK_ONLY, OFF_HEAP and their _2/_SER variants) and cached factory methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a private constructor plus a companion object; instances are interned through a ConcurrentHashMap cache so equal levels share one object.

nodes.name: StorageLevel
nodes.summary: A StorageLevel (class at lines 39-141 plus its companion object at 148-231, one node for both) records five settings. useDisk: keep/spill blocks on disk. useMemory: keep blocks in memory. useOffHeap: use off-heap memory (memoryMode returns OFF_HEAP instead of ON_HEAP). deserialized: keep memory data as deserialized objects (false means serialized bytes). replication: number of copies on different nodes (asserted to be less than 40). Companion constants: NONE (nothing), DISK_ONLY and _2/_3 (disk only, serialized); MEMORY_ONLY and _2 (memory, deserialized); MEMORY_ONLY_SER and _2 (memory, serialized); MEMORY_AND_DISK and _2 (disk + memory, deserialized); MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER and _2 (disk + memory, serialized); OFF_HEAP (disk + memory + off-heap, serialized, 1 replica). The suffix _2/_3 means that many replicas. It is Externalizable and serializes as two bytes (flag bits and replication).

nodes.name: useDisk
nodes.summary: Flag accessor: true if blocks may be stored on disk.

nodes.name: useMemory
nodes.summary: Flag accessor: true if blocks are kept in memory.

nodes.name: useOffHeap
nodes.summary: Flag accessor: true if memory storage uses off-heap rather than on-heap memory.

nodes.name: deserialized
nodes.summary: Flag accessor: true if in-memory data is kept as deserialized objects; false means serialized form.

nodes.name: replication
nodes.summary: Accessor for the number of replicas (copies on different nodes) of each block.

nodes.name: memoryMode
nodes.summary: Maps the useOffHeap flag to MemoryMode.OFF_HEAP or MemoryMode.ON_HEAP.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Returns a new StorageLevel with the same five settings.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two levels are equal when useDisk, useMemory, useOffHeap, deserialized and replication all match.

nodes.name: isValid
nodes.summary: A level is valid when it uses memory or disk and has more than zero replicas.

nodes.name: toInt
nodes.summary: Packs the flags into an integer: disk = 8, memory = 4, off-heap = 2, deserialized = 1 (replication is stored separately).

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable write: emits the flag integer from toInt and the replication count as two bytes.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable read: decodes the flag byte (8 disk, 4 memory, 2 off-heap, 1 deserialized) and the replication byte back into the fields.

nodes.name: readResolve
nodes.summary: Java deserialization hook that returns the interned copy of the level from the companion cache.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Builds text such as StorageLevel(disk, memory, deserialized, 1 replicas) listing only the enabled flags.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hash code computed as toInt * 41 + replication (hence the replication < 40 assertion).

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Human-readable description, for example 'Disk Memory Deserialized 1x Replicated'.

nodes.name: fromString
nodes.summary: Looks up a StorageLevel by its constant name (for example MEMORY_AND_DISK) via StorageLevelMapper and rewraps an unknown name as IllegalArgumentException 'Invalid StorageLevel'.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Four overloaded factories (lines 182-223): from all five flags, from flags without useOffHeap (replication defaults to 1), from the integer flag encoding plus replication, and from an ObjectInput stream. All return the interned instance from getCachedStorageLevel.

nodes.name: getCachedStorageLevel
nodes.summary: Interns a level in a ConcurrentHashMap (putIfAbsent then get) so equal StorageLevels are the same object.

nodes.name: Partition.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the Partition trait, the identifier of one partition of an RDD, which exposes its index within the parent RDD and uses that index as its hash code.

nodes.name: Partition
nodes.summary: Serializable trait identifying a single partition of an RDD. Concrete RDDs subclass it to carry per-partition info; the only abstract member is index, the position in the parent RDD, and hashCode is defined as that index.

nodes.name: index
nodes.summary: Abstract: the partition's index within its parent RDD.

nodes.name: Partitioner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Partitioner contract (key to partition id) and its implementations: HashPartitioner, RangePartitioner (sampling-based), plus internal PartitionIdPassthrough, KeyGroupedPartitioner and ConstantPartitioner, and the defaultPartitioner choice logic for cogroup-like operations.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file where Partitioner and RangePartitioner each have a companion object; RangePartitioner uses context bounds (Ordering, ClassTag) and custom Java serialization hooks.

nodes.name: Partitioner
nodes.summary: Abstract base class (lines 42-45) that maps a key of a key-value RDD to a partition id from 0 to numPartitions - 1; it must be deterministic. The companion object (47-104) holds defaultPartitioner for cogroup-like operations.

nodes.name: numPartitions
nodes.summary: Abstract: total number of partitions this partitioner produces.

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the partition id (0 to numPartitions - 1) for a key.

nodes.name: defaultPartitioner
nodes.summary: Chooses the partitioner for a cogroup-like op over several RDDs. If spark.default.parallelism is set it uses SparkContext defaultParallelism as the default partition count, otherwise the largest upstream partition count. It reuses the partitioner of the RDD with the most partitions if that is eligible (within one order of magnitude of the maximum) or has at least the default count; otherwise it builds a new HashPartitioner with the default count.

nodes.name: isEligiblePartitioner
nodes.summary: True when the RDD's partition count is at least the max upstream count or less than a factor of 10 below it (log10 difference under 1).

nodes.name: HashPartitioner
nodes.summary: Partitions by key.hashCode modulo the number of partitions (non-negative mod); a null key goes to partition 0. Two HashPartitioners are equal when their numPartitions match. Not suitable for array keys because Java array hash codes are identity-based.

nodes.name: numPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the partition count given at construction (must be non-negative).

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Returns 0 for a null key, otherwise Utils.nonNegativeMod(key.hashCode, numPartitions).

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Equality based only on numPartitions, so Spark can detect an already-matching partitioner and avoid a shuffle.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hash code equal to numPartitions.

nodes.name: PartitionIdPassthrough
nodes.summary: Internal dummy partitioner for records whose key is already a partition id; getPartition just casts the key to Int.

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Returns the key cast to Int as the partition id.

nodes.name: KeyGroupedPartitioner
nodes.summary: Internal partitioner that uses a (partition value -> partition id) map built from KeyedPartitioning so the other side of a join lands records with equal partition values in the same partition; unseen values fall back to a hash of the key sequence.

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Looks up the key sequence in valueMap, inserting a non-negative mod of its hash code when absent.

nodes.name: ConstantPartitioner
nodes.summary: Internal partitioner that puts every record into a single partition (numPartitions = 1, getPartition always 0).

nodes.name: RangePartitioner
nodes.summary: Partitions sortable keys into roughly equal contiguous ranges (class at lines 176-324 plus companion object at 326-388). On construction it samples the RDD's keys: sample size is samplePointsPerPartitionHint (default 20) times partitions, capped at 1,000,000, and each input partition is sketched by reservoir sampling with a 3x oversample. Partitions much larger than average are re-sampled with a PartitionPruningRDD; candidates carry weights (1 over sampling probability) and determineBounds walks the sorted candidates to pick partitions - 1 upper bounds, skipping duplicates. The actual partition count can be lower than requested when there are few distinct sampled keys. getPartition scans linearly for up to 128 bounds, else uses binary search, and flips the order when ascending is false.

nodes.name: numPartitions
nodes.summary: Number of partitions is rangeBounds.length + 1.

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Finds the key's range: linear search while there are at most 128 bounds, otherwise binary search (negative result converted from the insertion point); for descending order it returns rangeBounds.length minus the index.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Equal when the range bounds arrays have the same elements and ascending matches.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hash code combining each range bound and the ascending flag with prime 31.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Custom Java serialization: with JavaSerializer it uses default serialization, otherwise it writes ascending, ordering, the binary search function and the range bounds through the configured serializer in a nested stream.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Custom Java deserialization mirroring writeObject: restores ascending, ordering, the binary search function and the range bounds via a nested stream unless JavaSerializer is in use.

nodes.name: sketch
nodes.summary: Companion helper that reservoir-samples each partition of the key RDD (seeded per partition) with mapPartitionsWithIndex and collects (partitionId, item count, sample) tuples; returns the total item count and the sketches.

nodes.name: determineBounds
nodes.summary: Sorts weighted candidate keys and walks them accumulating weight; each time the cumulative weight reaches the next multiple of totalWeight / partitions it emits that key as an upper bound, skipping duplicates, until partitions - 1 bounds are chosen.

nodes.name: Broadcast.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Broadcast[T] class, a read-only variable cached on each machine and created via SparkContext.broadcast, with the value/unpersist/destroy lifecycle and a validity check once destroyed.

nodes.name: Broadcast
nodes.summary: Abstract base of broadcast variables: a read-only value kept cached on each machine instead of being shipped with every task. value returns the data, unpersist drops cached executor copies (it can be re-sent if used again), and destroy removes all data and metadata so the variable can never be used again; using it afterwards raises an internal error. Subclasses implement getValue, doUnpersist and doDestroy. Created by SparkContext.broadcast; the object must not be modified after broadcasting.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Returns the broadcast data after asserting the variable is still valid.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Deletes cached copies on executors (asynchronously by default, blocking if requested); the variable is re-sent if used again.

nodes.name: destroy
nodes.summary: Marks the variable invalid, records the destroy call site, logs it, then calls doDestroy; the variable cannot be used afterwards.

nodes.name: isValid
nodes.summary: True while the broadcast has not been destroyed.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Abstract: how a concrete implementation fetches the value.

nodes.name: doUnpersist
nodes.summary: Abstract: how a concrete implementation removes executor-side copies.

nodes.name: doDestroy
nodes.summary: Abstract: how a concrete implementation destroys its data and metadata.

nodes.name: assertValid
nodes.summary: Throws SparkException.internalError (category BROADCAST) naming the destroy site if the broadcast was already destroyed.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats as Broadcast(<id>).

nodes.name: SparkConf.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkConf, the key/value configuration holder for a Spark application, with typed getters (time, size, int, boolean), the ReadOnlySparkConf trait, chaining setters such as setMaster and setAppName, validation of settings, and the companion tables of deprecated and renamed spark.* keys.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file: a trait with abstract getters, a class with chaining setters, and a private[spark] companion object holding the deprecation maps as private case classes.

nodes.name: ReadOnlySparkConf
nodes.summary: Trait holding the read-only side of configuration: string get/getOption/getAll/contains, typed getters (getInt, getLong, getDouble, getBoolean), time getters (getTimeAsSeconds, getTimeAsMs) and size getters (getSizeAsBytes, Kb, Mb, Gb) that parse suffixes like '5s' or '64k'. A missing value without a default throws NoSuchElementException; a malformed value is re-raised with the offending key in the message.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: String overloads: get(key) throws NoSuchElementException if unset, get(key, default) falls back to the default; both read through getOption.

nodes.name: getTimeAsSeconds
nodes.summary: Reads a time setting in seconds (default unit seconds, suffixes accepted), with or without a default value.

nodes.name: getTimeAsMs
nodes.summary: Reads a time setting in milliseconds (default unit ms, suffixes accepted), with or without a default value.

nodes.name: getSizeAsBytes
nodes.summary: Reads a size setting as bytes (no suffix means bytes); overloads take no default, a string default, or a Long default.

nodes.name: getSizeAsKb
nodes.summary: Reads a size setting as Kibibytes (no suffix means KiB), with or without a default.

nodes.name: getSizeAsMb
nodes.summary: Reads a size setting as Mebibytes (no suffix means MiB), with or without a default.

nodes.name: getSizeAsGb
nodes.summary: Reads a size setting as Gibibytes (no suffix means GiB), with or without a default.

nodes.name: getOption
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the value of a key as Option[String].

nodes.name: getAll
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns all settings as an array of (key, value) pairs.

nodes.name: getAllAsJavaMap
nodes.summary: Returns all settings as a java.util.Map for Java callers.

nodes.name: getInt
nodes.summary: Reads a setting as Int, returning the default when unset; a bad number raises NumberFormatException naming the key.

nodes.name: getLong
nodes.summary: Reads a setting as Long, returning the default when unset.

nodes.name: getDouble
nodes.summary: Reads a setting as Double, returning the default when unset.

nodes.name: getBoolean
nodes.summary: Reads a setting as Boolean, returning the default when unset; a bad value raises IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Tells whether a key (or a typed ConfigEntry's key) is present in the configuration.

nodes.name: catchIllegalValue
nodes.summary: Wrapper used by the typed getters: catches NumberFormatException or IllegalArgumentException and rethrows it with 'Illegal value for config key <key>' in the message.

nodes.name: getenv
nodes.summary: Wraps System.getenv so tests can mock environment variables.

nodes.name: SparkConf
nodes.summary: Configuration of a Spark application as spark.* key/value strings (class at lines 287-657 plus companion object at 659-902, one node for both). new SparkConf() also loads every spark.* Java system property, and values set directly on the object override those; new SparkConf(false) skips them (used in tests). Settings live in a ConcurrentHashMap and all setters chain. Once handed to Spark the conf is cloned and no longer modifiable by the user. The companion keeps deprecatedConfigs (key, version, message, logged as a warning when used) and configsWithAlternatives (current key to older keys such as spark.reducer.maxMbInFlight, optionally translating the old value), which getOption consults as a fallback. It also provides isExecutorStartupConf and isSparkPortConf helpers.

nodes.name: loadFromSystemProperties
nodes.summary: Copies every Java system property whose name starts with 'spark.' into the conf (optionally without deprecation warnings).

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets a key to a value (null key or value throws NullPointerException) and logs a deprecation warning unless silent; returns this for chaining. Overloads also accept a ConfigEntry or OptionalConfigEntry and convert the value to a string.

nodes.name: setMaster
nodes.summary: Sets spark.master, e.g. 'local', 'local[4]' or 'spark://master:7077'.

nodes.name: setAppName
nodes.summary: Sets spark.app.name, the application name shown in the web UI.

nodes.name: setJars
nodes.summary: Sets the JAR files to distribute to the cluster (Seq and Java Array overloads), dropping and warning about null entries.

nodes.name: setExecutorEnv
nodes.summary: Sets environment variables for executors, stored as spark.executorEnv.<NAME>; overloads take one pair, a Seq of pairs, or an Array of pairs.

nodes.name: setSparkHome
nodes.summary: Sets spark.home, the Spark installation location on worker nodes.

nodes.name: setAll
nodes.summary: Sets many key/value pairs at once by calling set for each.

nodes.name: setIfMissing
nodes.summary: Sets a key only if it is not already configured (putIfAbsent), warning about deprecation when it is added; also has ConfigEntry overloads.

nodes.name: registerKryoClasses
nodes.summary: Switches spark.serializer to KryoSerializer and appends the given classes to the Kryo registration list (repeat calls accumulate).

nodes.name: registerAvroSchemas
nodes.summary: Registers Avro schemas under avro.schema.<fingerprint> keys so the generic record serializer can reduce network IO.

nodes.name: getAvroSchema
nodes.summary: Collects the avro.schema.* entries into a map from schema fingerprint to schema string.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a key from the configuration (also accepts a ConfigEntry).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Internal typed read: resolves a ConfigEntry through the ConfigReader, which applies defaults and variable substitution.

nodes.name: getOption
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the settings map and, if absent, falls back to values stored under deprecated alternate keys.

nodes.name: getWithSubstitution
nodes.summary: Gets an optional value and applies ${...} variable substitution through the ConfigReader.

nodes.name: getAll
nodes.summary: Returns all settings as an array of (key, value) pairs.

nodes.name: getAllWithPrefix
nodes.summary: Returns settings whose key starts with a prefix (prefix stripped), or with a key-mapping function in the second overload.

nodes.name: getExecutorEnv
nodes.summary: Returns the executor environment variables stored under spark.executorEnv.

nodes.name: getAppId
nodes.summary: Returns spark.app.id, valid in the driver after TaskScheduler registration and from the start in the executor.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: True if the key is set or any of its deprecated alternate keys is set.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Copies the conf into a new SparkConf(false), setting each entry silently (no deprecation warnings).

nodes.name: validateSettings
nodes.summary: Checks for illegal or deprecated settings and may throw. It warns about spark.local.dir and the deprecated spark.driver.libraryPath; rejects -Dspark or -Xmx inside executor Java options; requires memory fractions within 0 and 1; limits deploy mode to cluster or client; warns when max cores is not divisible by executor cores; requires network auth when encryption is on; and requires the network timeout to exceed the executor heartbeat interval.

nodes.name: toDebugString
nodes.summary: Returns all keys and values, sorted, one 'key=value' per line, with sensitive values redacted; for debugging.

nodes.name: isExecutorStartupConf
nodes.summary: True for configs the executor needs at startup to connect to the scheduler: spark.auth* (except the secret), spark.rpc*, spark.network*, spark.ssl* (except passwords) and port settings.

nodes.name: isSparkPortConf
nodes.summary: True if the key matches spark.*.port or spark.port.*.

nodes.name: getDeprecatedConfig
nodes.summary: Finds the first deprecated alternate key present in a settings map for a current key, applying its optional value translation.

nodes.name: logDeprecationWarning
nodes.summary: Logs a warning if a key is in deprecatedConfigs (no replacement, with message) or is an old alternate name (points to the new key).

nodes.name: DeprecatedConfig
nodes.summary: Private case class (key, version, deprecationMessage) describing a deprecated key that has no replacement.

nodes.name: AlternateConfig
nodes.summary: Private case class (key, version, optional translation function) describing an older name of a config and how to convert its value to the current format.

nodes.name: BroadcastManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BroadcastManager, the driver/executor-side manager that creates broadcast variables with increasing ids through a BroadcastFactory (TorrentBroadcastFactory) and removes them again.

nodes.name: BroadcastManager
nodes.summary: Per-process manager of broadcast variables. On construction it initializes a TorrentBroadcastFactory (called by SparkContext on the driver or by Executor), keeps an AtomicLong for the next broadcast id and a synchronized weak-valued cachedValues map. newBroadcast assigns an id, tags a PythonBroadcast with that id, and delegates creation to the factory; unbroadcast removes a variable; stop stops the factory.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Synchronized one-time setup: creates a TorrentBroadcastFactory and initializes it with the driver flag and the SparkConf.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the underlying BroadcastFactory.

nodes.name: newBroadcast
nodes.summary: Allocates the next broadcast id, attaches it to a PythonBroadcast value (SPARK-28486) so its data file maps to the BroadcastBlockId, and asks the factory to create the Broadcast.

nodes.name: unbroadcast
nodes.summary: Removes a broadcast by id via the factory, optionally also from the driver and optionally blocking.

nodes.name: TorrentBroadcast.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TorrentBroadcast, the BitTorrent-like Broadcast implementation behind sc.broadcast(...) values. The driver serializes the value, splits it into chunks stored in its BlockManager, and each executor fetches missing chunks from the driver and/or other executors, re-publishing them so the driver is not the bottleneck.

nodes.name: TorrentBroadcast
nodes.summary: Broadcast subclass that serializes (and optionally compresses) the object, splits it into blocks of the configured block size and stores them as BroadcastBlockId pieces ("piece0", "piece1", ...) in the driver BlockManager. On first use of the value, an executor looks in its local BlockManager, then fetches the pieces in random order from remote BlockManagers, optionally verifies Adler32 checksums, puts them in its own BlockManager, and reassembles the object. The value is memoized behind a SoftReference (WeakReference when serializedOnly). Its companion object (lines 351-401) holds blockifyObject, unBlockifyObject, unpersist and the per-broadcast KeyLock.

nodes.name: setConf
nodes.summary: Reads compression codec, block size, checksum flag and local-master flag from a SparkConf; called at construction and again on executors before reading.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Returns the broadcast value from a Soft/WeakReference if still present, otherwise rebuilds it via readBroadcastBlock and memoizes it (WeakReference when serializedOnly, else SoftReference).

nodes.name: calcChecksum
nodes.summary: Computes an Adler32 checksum of a ByteBuffer block, handling both array-backed and direct buffers.

nodes.name: writeBlocks
nodes.summary: Driver-side write path: optionally stores the whole value in the driver BlockManager (skipped for serializedOnly outside local mode), blockifies the object, records optional checksums and stores each chunk as a 'piece' block with MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER; on failure removes all pieces of the broadcast.

nodes.name: readBlocks
nodes.summary: Fetches all pieces in random order: tries the local BlockManager first, then remote executors/driver, validates checksums when enabled, and stores fetched pieces locally so other executors can pull them from here.

nodes.name: doUnpersist
nodes.summary: Removes the broadcast's persisted blocks on executors only, delegating to TorrentBroadcast.unpersist with removeFromDriver = false.

nodes.name: doDestroy
nodes.summary: Removes the broadcast's persisted blocks on executors and the driver, delegating to TorrentBroadcast.unpersist with removeFromDriver = true.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook: asserts the broadcast is still valid, then default-serializes only the non-transient fields (the value itself is transient and not shipped with the task).

nodes.name: readBroadcastBlock
nodes.summary: Executor-side read path under a per-broadcast KeyLock: checks the BroadcastManager cache and local BlockManager, otherwise reads the pieces, unblockifies them into the object, optionally stores the merged copy in the BlockManager and caches it, and disposes the piece buffers.

nodes.name: releaseBlockManagerLock
nodes.summary: Releases a BlockManager read lock: deferred to task completion when running inside a task, immediately otherwise (driver-side access outside tasks).

nodes.name: hasCachedValue
nodes.summary: Test-only helper reporting whether the unserialized value is cached in the local BlockManager.

nodes.name: blockifyObject
nodes.summary: Serializes the object (through the given Serializer and optional CompressionCodec) into a chunked buffer of at most blockSize bytes and returns the chunks as ByteBuffers.

nodes.name: unBlockifyObject
nodes.summary: Reverse of blockifyObject: concatenates the block input streams, optionally decompresses, and deserializes the original object.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Asks the block manager master to remove all blocks of the broadcast id, optionally also from the driver.

nodes.name: CartesianRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CartesianRDD, the RDD of all (x, y) pairs from two parent RDDs, and CartesianPartition, which pairs one partition of each parent. The result has numPartitions(rdd1) * numPartitions(rdd2) partitions and depends narrowly on both parents.

nodes.name: CartesianPartition
nodes.summary: Partition of CartesianRDD identified by an index plus the indices of one partition from each parent. It re-reads the parent partitions at task serialization time (writeObject) so the transient parent RDD references are not shipped.

nodes.name: CartesianRDD
nodes.summary: RDD of pairs (T, U) built from two RDDs. Partition index = s1.index * numPartitionsInRdd2 + s2.index, so each output partition is one pair of parent partitions; compute iterates the nested product of the two parent iterators. It declares two NarrowDependencies whose getParents map a child partition back to id / numPartitionsInRdd2 in rdd1 and id % numPartitionsInRdd2 in rdd2. Fails if the product exceeds Int.MaxValue partitions.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook that refreshes s1 and s2 from the parent RDDs just before the task is serialized.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Builds the cross product of parent partitions: one CartesianPartition per (s1, s2) pair, throwing a too-many-elements error if the count exceeds Int.MaxValue.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the distinct union of the preferred locations of the two parent partitions of a CartesianPartition.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Yields (x, y) for every x in the first parent partition iterator and every y in the second parent partition iterator.

nodes.name: getDependencies
nodes.summary: Declares two anonymous NarrowDependency instances, one per parent, mapping a child partition id to the single parent partition it reads (id / numPartitionsInRdd2 and id % numPartitionsInRdd2).

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Calls the parent implementation and nulls the rdd1 and rdd2 references so they can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: CoGroupedRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CoGroupedRDD, the DeveloperApi RDD that cogroups several parent key-value RDDs into (key, Array of value Iterables) per key, plus its partition and split-dependency helpers. For each parent it picks a narrow OneToOneDependency when the parent already has the target partitioner, otherwise a ShuffleDependency; the source comment points users to RDD.cogroup(...) instead of instantiating it directly.

nodes.name: NarrowCoGroupSplitDep
nodes.summary: Case class holding, for a narrow-dependency parent, the parent partition used by one CoGroupPartition. rdd and splitIndex are transient (stored once in the CoGroupedRDD) and the split is refreshed at serialization time.

nodes.name: CoGroupPartition
nodes.summary: Partition of CoGroupedRDD with one optional NarrowCoGroupSplitDep per parent RDD: Some for parents read through a narrow dependency and None for parents read through a shuffle.

nodes.name: CoGroupedRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that cogroups its parents: for each key k it produces (k, Array of Iterables, one per parent RDD). getDependencies decides per parent: if parent.partitioner == Some(part) a OneToOneDependency (no shuffle), else a ShuffleDependency with the given Partitioner; getPartitions creates part.numPartitions CoGroupPartitions; compute reads narrow parents directly and shuffle parents through ShuffleManager readers, then merges all values into an ExternalAppendOnlyMap (spillable) keyed by the cogroup key. It reports part as its own partitioner.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook that refreshes the parent partition from the parent RDD just before the task is serialized.

nodes.name: setSerializer
nodes.summary: Sets the Serializer used for this RDD's shuffle (null means the default spark.serializer) and returns this RDD.

nodes.name: getDependencies
nodes.summary: Maps each parent to a OneToOneDependency when its partitioner equals the target partitioner, otherwise to a ShuffleDependency using the target partitioner and serializer. This is where narrow vs shuffle is decided.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Creates one CoGroupPartition per output partition, recording a NarrowCoGroupSplitDep for narrow parents and None for shuffled parents.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Collects iterators for each dependency (narrow parent partition iterator or ShuffleManager reader output), inserts all values tagged with their dependency number into an external map, updates spill and peak-memory task metrics, and returns the grouped iterator.

nodes.name: createExternalMap
nodes.summary: Builds the ExternalAppendOnlyMap with createCombiner, mergeValue and mergeCombiners functions that append each value to the CompactBuffer of its dependency number.

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Calls the parent implementation and nulls the rdds reference so parents can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: CoalescedRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CoalescedRDD, which groups the partitions of a parent RDD into fewer partitions through a NarrowDependency, together with its partition class and DefaultPartitionCoalescer, the locality-aware, load-balancing grouping algorithm used when no custom PartitionCoalescer is passed. Each coalesced partition computes one or more whole parent partitions.

nodes.name: CoalescedRDDPartition
nodes.summary: Partition of a CoalescedRDD: its index, the indices of the parent partitions merged into it, and an optional preferred host. It re-reads the parent partitions at serialization time, and localFraction reports the fraction of parents whose preferred hosts include the preferred location.

nodes.name: CoalescedRDD
nodes.summary: RDD with at most maxPartitions partitions, each built by concatenating the iterators of several parent partitions (compute flatMaps over the parent partitions). The grouping comes from a PartitionCoalescer (the supplied one, which must be Serializable, or DefaultPartitionCoalescer); the dependency is a single NarrowDependency whose getParents returns the grouped parent indices, not a ShuffleDependency. The preferred location of a partition is the host chosen by the coalescer.

nodes.name: DefaultPartitionCoalescer
nodes.summary: Default PartitionCoalescer. Without locality information it chunks parent partitions into contiguous ranges; with locality it creates up to maxPartitions groups, assigns each a preferred host (using a coupon-collector estimate to rotate through hosts), and throws each parent partition into a group using power-of-two random choices, trading load balance against locality via balanceSlack (default 0.10). Uses a fixed Random seed to stay deterministic and drops empty groups from the result.

nodes.name: PartitionLocations
nodes.summary: Private helper inside DefaultPartitionCoalescer that splits the parent partitions into those with and without preferred locations, listing up to three preferred hosts per partition for the ones that have them.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook that refreshes the parent partitions from the parent RDD just before the task is serialized.

nodes.name: localFraction
nodes.summary: Computes the fraction (0 to 1) of parent partitions whose current preferred hosts (from the scheduler) contain this partition's preferred location.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Runs the partition coalescer on the parent and turns each returned PartitionGroup into a CoalescedRDDPartition with the group's parent indices and preferred location.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Iterates over the parent partitions of the coalesced partition and concatenates the parent RDD's iterators for each.

nodes.name: getDependencies
nodes.summary: Declares one NarrowDependency on the parent RDD whose getParents returns the parent partition indices assigned to the child partition.

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Calls the parent implementation and nulls prev so the parent RDD can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the single preferred host chosen for the coalesced partition, if any.

nodes.name: currPrefLocs
nodes.summary: Gets the current preferred hosts of a parent partition from the SparkContext (DAGScheduler) rather than the static ones.

nodes.name: getLeastGroupHash
nodes.summary: Returns the least loaded partition group among those assigned to the given preferred machine key.

nodes.name: addPartToPGroup
nodes.summary: Adds a partition to a group unless it was already assigned, tracking assigned partitions so none lands in two groups.

nodes.name: setupGroups
nodes.summary: Creates targetLen partition groups, giving each a preferred host when locality exists (rotating through hosts using a coupon-collector estimate, then duplicating hosts picked at random if needed).

nodes.name: pickBin
nodes.summary: Chooses the group for a parent partition: the less loaded of two random groups versus the least loaded group on a preferred host, preferring locality unless imbalance exceeds the balanceSlack allowance.

nodes.name: throwBalls
nodes.summary: Assigns every parent partition to a group: contiguous ranges when there is no locality, otherwise first filling empty groups (with-locality partitions first, then without) and then calling pickBin for the rest.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the non-empty partition groups as an array.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Entry point of the packing algorithm: collects parent preferred locations, sets up the groups, throws the parent partitions into them and returns the resulting PartitionGroups.

nodes.name: getAllPrefLocs
nodes.summary: Queries each parent partition's preferred locations once, separating partitions without locations and building (host, partition) pairs for up to the first three preferred hosts.

nodes.name: HadoopRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HadoopRDD, the DeveloperApi RDD that reads data through the old Hadoop MapReduce API (org.apache.hadoop.mapred), with one Spark partition per Hadoop InputSplit, plus HadoopPartition and the HadoopRDD companion helpers. The Hadoop Configuration arrives as a broadcast SerializableConfiguration, a JobConf is built or reused per executor, and the file being read is exposed to InputFileBlockHolder.

nodes.name: HadoopPartition
nodes.summary: Spark Partition wrapping a Hadoop InputSplit in a SerializableWritable, with hashCode based on RDD id and index. getPipeEnvVars exposes map_input_file for FileSplits (used when piping).

nodes.name: HadoopRDD
nodes.summary: RDD of (K, V) pairs read via a Hadoop InputFormat. getPartitions asks the InputFormat for splits (at least minPartitions, optionally dropping empty splits, warning about one large file) and makes one HadoopPartition per split; compute opens a RecordReader for the split, sets InputFileBlockHolder for FileSplits, tracks input metrics and handles ignoreCorruptFiles/ignoreMissingFiles. The Hadoop conf is a Broadcast[SerializableConfiguration]; getJobConf reuses a broadcast JobConf, or builds and caches one per RDD in the local process (or clones it when spark.hadoop.cloneConf is true). Checkpointing is a no-op and persisting deserialized records triggers a warning because RecordReaders reuse Writable objects. Companion object (lines 430-501) holds the conf lock, metadata cache helpers and the nested mapPartitionsWithInputSplit RDD.

nodes.name: HadoopMapPartitionsWithSplitRDD
nodes.summary: Nested RDD in the HadoopRDD companion, analogous to MapPartitionsRDD, that passes the Hadoop InputSplit (instead of the partition index) to the user function; used by HadoopRDD.mapPartitionsWithInputSplit.

nodes.name: getPipeEnvVars
nodes.summary: Returns map_input_file and mapreduce_map_input_file environment variables holding the file path for FileSplit partitions, otherwise an empty map.

nodes.name: getJobConf
nodes.summary: Returns the JobConf for executors: a clone when spark.hadoop.cloneConf is set, the broadcast value itself if it is already a JobConf, otherwise a JobConf created from the broadcast Configuration, initialized by the optional function and cached in the local process under a per-RDD key.

nodes.name: getInputFormat
nodes.summary: Instantiates the configured InputFormat class via Hadoop ReflectionUtils, wrapping instantiation failures in a RuntimeException.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Adds credentials, obtains InputSplits from the InputFormat, optionally filters empty splits, warns when a single large file yields one partition, and creates one HadoopPartition per split; returns no partitions for a missing input path when ignoreMissingFiles is set.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Builds a NextIterator that opens the split's RecordReader, publishes the file path, start and length through InputFileBlockHolder for FileSplits, updates input metrics (bytes and records read), skips missing or corrupt files according to the ignore flags, and closes the reader on task completion.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithInputSplit
nodes.summary: Developer API that maps over each partition while also providing the underlying Hadoop InputSplit, via HadoopMapPartitionsWithSplitRDD.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns host locations from the InputSplit (using location info with in-memory/HDFS cache details when available), filtering out localhost.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: No-op override: a HadoopRDD is not checkpointed.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Warns that caching HadoopRDDs as deserialized objects is usually undesirable because RecordReader reuses Writable objects, then delegates to the parent persist.

nodes.name: getConf
nodes.summary: Returns the Hadoop Configuration (the JobConf from getJobConf) used by this RDD.

nodes.name: getCachedMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads a cached object (such as a JobConf) from the process-local hadoopJobMetadata map of SparkEnv.

nodes.name: putCachedMetadata
nodes.summary: Stores an object in the process-local hadoopJobMetadata map of SparkEnv.

nodes.name: addLocalConfiguration
nodes.summary: Sets per-partition, per-attempt Hadoop properties (mapreduce.task.id, task attempt id, ismap, partition, job id) on the JobConf.

nodes.name: convertSplitLocationInfo
nodes.summary: Converts Hadoop SplitLocationInfo entries into host task-location strings, tagging in-memory (HDFS cached) locations and skipping localhost.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Reuses the partitions of the first parent RDD.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Extracts the InputSplit from the HadoopPartition and calls the user function with the split and the parent partition iterator.

nodes.name: OrderedRDDFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrderedRDDFunctions, adding sort-related operations (sortByKey, repartitionAndSortWithinPartitions, filterByRange) to key-value RDDs whose key has an implicit Ordering. sortByKey range-partitions with a RangePartitioner and sorts through the shuffle, This is how sort-by-key ordering is produced across partitions.

nodes.name: OrderedRDDFunctions
nodes.summary: Implicit wrapper for RDDs of Product2[K, V] with an Ordering[K]. It pushes sorting into the shuffle (ShuffledRDD with a key ordering) instead of sorting after repartitioning.
nodes.languageNotes: Context bounds [K: Ordering: ClassTag] bring the Ordering and ClassTag in as implicit parameters; a TODO in the source notes sortByKey only works on Tuple2.

nodes.name: sortByKey
nodes.summary: Sorts by key globally: creates a RangePartitioner (numPartitions defaults to the current partition count) and a ShuffledRDD with the key ordering, reversed for descending order. Each output partition holds a sorted contiguous range, so collect or save yields keys in order.

nodes.name: repartitionAndSortWithinPartitions
nodes.summary: Repartitions by the given Partitioner and sorts by key inside each partition in the shuffle machinery, which is more efficient than repartition followed by a separate sort. If the RDD already has an equal partitioner, it sorts each partition locally with an ExternalSorter instead.

nodes.name: filterByRange
nodes.summary: Keeps pairs whose key lies in the inclusive range [lower, upper]. If the RDD is range-partitioned it prunes to the partitions between the two boundary partitions with PartitionPruningRDD.create; otherwise it filters every partition.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapPartitionsRDD, the narrow-dependency RDD that applies a function to each parent partition's iterator (the pair-RDD mapValues and flatMapValues in this batch build one). It carries flags for partitioner preservation, barrier stages, order sensitivity and partition-size preservation.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that applies f(TaskContext, partitionIndex, iterator) to every partition of its parent. preservesPartitioning keeps the parent's partitioner (otherwise partitioner is None), isFromBarrier marks it as coming from an RDDBarrier so its stage becomes a barrier stage, isOrderSensitive can raise the output determinism level to INDETERMINATE, and preservesPartitionSizes records that row counts per partition are unchanged (used to optimize zipWithIndex).
nodes.languageNotes: Declared private[spark]; the partitioner is an override val computed once from preservesPartitioning.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Reuses the first parent's partitions unchanged, since this is a one-to-one narrow transformation.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Computes a partition by calling the user function with the TaskContext, the partition index and the parent's iterator for the same partition.

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Clears dependencies after checkpointing by calling super and nulling the prev reference so the parent RDD can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: isBarrier_
nodes.summary: Lazy flag that is true if this RDD was created from an RDDBarrier or any dependency's RDD is a barrier RDD, which makes the enclosing stage a barrier stage.

nodes.name: getOutputDeterministicLevel
nodes.summary: Returns INDETERMINATE when the function is order-sensitive and the parent output is UNORDERED; otherwise defers to the superclass level.

nodes.name: LocalRDDCheckpointData.scala
nodes.summary: Implements local checkpointing on top of Spark's caching layer: the RDD's data stays in executors' local block storage instead of reliable storage, trading fault tolerance for speed. Its companion object supplies the default MEMORY_AND_DISK storage level and a helper that forces a level to use disk.

nodes.name: LocalRDDCheckpointData
nodes.summary: RDDCheckpointData subclass for local checkpoints. doCheckpoint requires a storage level that uses disk, computes any partitions not yet in the block manager by running a job, and returns a LocalCheckpointRDD. The companion object (lines 63-79) holds DEFAULT_STORAGE_LEVEL and transformStorageLevel.
nodes.languageNotes: Declared private[spark]; the class and its companion object share one node id.

nodes.name: doCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Asserts the RDD's storage level uses disk, finds partitions whose blocks are missing from the block manager master, runs a job over them to cache them (a TODO notes the extra job), and returns a new LocalCheckpointRDD.

nodes.name: transformStorageLevel
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the given StorageLevel with useDisk forced to true, so a locally checkpointed RDD can be recomputed from disk if memory blocks are evicted. Idempotent.

nodes.name: NewHadoopRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines NewHadoopRDD, the RDD that reads data via the new Hadoop MapReduce InputFormat API (the class SparkContext.newAPIHadoopRDD is documented to construct), plus NewHadoopPartition and a split-aware map-partitions RDD in its companion object. Handles split listing, per-task record reading, input metrics and ignore-corrupt/missing-file behavior.

nodes.name: NewHadoopPartition
nodes.summary: Partition wrapping one Hadoop InputSplit (as a SerializableWritable) with its index; hashCode is derived from the RDD id and index.
nodes.languageNotes: Declared private[spark].

nodes.name: NewHadoopRDD
nodes.summary: RDD of (K, V) pairs read through a new-API InputFormat. It lists splits to make partitions, broadcasts the Hadoop Configuration, builds a RecordReader per partition in compute, tracks bytes and records read, and can skip missing or corrupt files. Warns when persisted as deserialized objects because Hadoop reuses Writable objects. The companion object (lines 381-408) holds a configuration lock and NewHadoopMapPartitionsWithSplitRDD.
nodes.languageNotes: Annotated @DeveloperApi; the source recommends SparkContext.newAPIHadoopRDD over direct construction. The class and its companion object share one node id.

nodes.name: getConf
nodes.summary: Returns the Hadoop Configuration from the broadcast variable, cloning it under a global lock when spark.hadoop.cloneConf is set (off by default because the clone is expensive) to avoid thread-safety problems with shared Configuration objects.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Instantiates the InputFormat, calls getSplits, optionally drops empty splits, warns about a single large file in one partition, and wraps each split in a NewHadoopPartition. A missing input directory returns no partitions when ignoreMissingFiles is on.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Returns an InterruptibleIterator over a new-API RecordReader for the partition's split. It records input metrics and file info, builds the TaskAttemptContext and reader, honors ignoreMissingFiles and ignoreCorruptFiles, and registers a task-completion listener to update bytes read and close the reader.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithInputSplit
nodes.summary: Developer API that maps each partition while also passing the Hadoop InputSplit it came from, using NewHadoopMapPartitionsWithSplitRDD.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns preferred hosts for a partition from the split's location info (via HadoopRDD.convertSplitLocationInfo), falling back to split locations other than localhost.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Warns when the RDD is persisted as deserialized objects (Hadoop's RecordReader reuses the same Writable instance for all records, so users should map to copies), then calls super.persist.

nodes.name: NewHadoopMapPartitionsWithSplitRDD
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper RDD, analogous to MapPartitionsRDD, whose function receives the Hadoop InputSplit instead of the partition index. Optionally preserves the parent's partitioner.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested private[spark] class inside the NewHadoopRDD companion object.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Casts the partition to NewHadoopPartition, extracts its InputSplit, and calls the user function with the split and the parent's iterator.

nodes.name: PairRDDFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PairRDDFunctions, the class that adds key-value operations (combineByKey, reduceByKey, groupByKey, joins, cogroup, partitionBy, saveAsHadoopFile and more) to RDD[(K, V)] through an implicit conversion. It is the home of the Scala pair-RDD operations (reduceByKey, groupByKey, combineByKey, join, partitionBy and others).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala implicit class pattern with many overloaded methods: most variants delegate to one general overload taking an explicit Partitioner, and ClassTag implicits are threaded through for shuffle serialization. Overloaded methods share one function node id; the line range given is the most general overload.

nodes.name: PairRDDFunctions
nodes.summary: Wrapper class that gives an RDD[(K, V)] the by-key operations. Nearly everything funnels into combineByKeyWithClassTag (aggregations) or cogroup (joins), and partitioner choice defaults to Partitioner.defaultPartitioner when the caller does not supply a Partitioner or partition count.
nodes.languageNotes: Constructor takes implicit ClassTag[K], ClassTag[V] and an optional Ordering[K] (default null); array keys are rejected for hash partitioning and map-side combine.

nodes.name: combineByKeyWithClassTag
nodes.summary: The core by-key aggregation primitive: builds an Aggregator from createCombiner, mergeValue and mergeCombiners, then either combines in place (when the RDD already has the target partitioner) or creates a ShuffledRDD with the aggregator and the mapSideCombine flag. Map-side combine (default true) pre-merges values per key inside each mapper so less data is shuffled; array keys are rejected when map-side combine or a HashPartitioner is used. Overloads at lines 141 and 620 default to a HashPartitioner or Partitioner.defaultPartitioner.

nodes.name: combineByKey
nodes.summary: Backward-compatible entry point for combineByKey: same semantics as combineByKeyWithClassTag but without passing the combiner ClassTag to the shuffle (it passes null). Overloads at lines 130 and 609 take a partition count or no partitioner at all.

nodes.name: aggregateByKey
nodes.summary: Aggregates values per key with a zero value, a seqOp (merge a V into a U within a partition) and a combOp (merge two U's across partitions). The zero value is serialized once and deserialized to give each key a fresh copy, then the work is delegated to combineByKeyWithClassTag. Overloads at lines 184 and 198 take a partition count or fall back to Partitioner.defaultPartitioner.

nodes.name: foldByKey
nodes.summary: Merges values per key with one associative function and a neutral zero value, cloning the zero value per key through the serializer. The function serves as createCombiner, mergeValue and mergeCombiners in a call to combineByKeyWithClassTag. Overloads at lines 230 and 239 take a partition count or the default partitioner.

nodes.name: sampleByKey
nodes.summary: Stratified sampling by key in one pass: each key gets its own sampling rate from the fractions map, using a Poisson sampler with replacement or a Bernoulli sampler without. Applied with mapPartitionsWithIndex while preserving partitioning.

nodes.name: sampleByKeyExact
nodes.summary: Like sampleByKey but makes extra passes over the RDD so the sample size per key is exactly ceil(numItems * rate) with 99.99% confidence (one extra pass without replacement, two with).

nodes.name: reduceByKey
nodes.summary: Merges values for each key with an associative and commutative function, doing a combiner-style merge on each mapper before the shuffle. It is combineByKeyWithClassTag with an identity createCombiner and the same function for merging values and combiners. Overloads at lines 314 and 324 take a partition count or use Partitioner.defaultPartitioner.

nodes.name: reduceByKeyLocally
nodes.summary: Reduces values per key into a per-partition Java HashMap, then merges the maps on the driver with reduce and returns a local Map. Not supported for array keys.

nodes.name: countByKey
nodes.summary: Counts elements per key and returns them as a local Map on the driver by mapping values to 1L, calling reduceByKey and collecting. The source warns it should only be used when the result is small; mapValues(_ => 1L).reduceByKey(_ + _) keeps the result distributed.

nodes.name: countByKeyApprox
nodes.summary: Approximate countByKey that can return a partial result (PartialResult with BoundedDouble bounds) if the job does not finish within the timeout, by taking the keys and calling countByValueApprox.

nodes.name: countApproxDistinctByKey
nodes.summary: Estimates the number of distinct values per key with HyperLogLogPlus sketches (precision p and sparse precision sp) merged through combineByKeyWithClassTag. Overloads at lines 444, 464 and 480 derive p from a relative standard deviation and pick a Partitioner, a partition count or the default partitioner.

nodes.name: groupByKey
nodes.summary: Groups all values of each key into one Iterable via combineByKeyWithClassTag with a CompactBuffer combiner and mapSideCombine = false. The source explains why: map-side combine would not shrink the data shuffled and would force all map-side data into a hash table, creating more objects in the old generation. All values of a key must fit in memory, and reduceByKey or aggregateByKey are recommended when aggregating. Overloads at lines 521 and 637 take a partition count or use Partitioner.defaultPartitioner.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Returns the RDD repartitioned with the given Partitioner by building a plain ShuffledRDD (no aggregator), or returns the RDD itself if it already has an equal partitioner. HashPartitioner is rejected for array keys.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Inner join: cogroups the two RDDs with the given Partitioner and flatMapValues each (values1, values2) pair into the cross product (v, w). Overloads at lines 646 and 655 choose Partitioner.defaultPartitioner(self, other) or a HashPartitioner of numPartitions.

nodes.name: leftOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Left outer join built on cogroup: emits (v, None) for keys missing in the other RDD and (v, Some(w)) pairs otherwise, via flatMapValues. Overloads at lines 665 and 675 supply the default partitioner or a partition count.

nodes.name: rightOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Right outer join built on cogroup: emits (None, w) for keys missing in this RDD and (Some(v), w) pairs otherwise. Overloads at lines 687 and 697 supply the default partitioner or a partition count.

nodes.name: fullOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Full outer join built on cogroup, pattern-matching empty value sequences on either side to produce (Some(v), None), (None, Some(w)) or the Some/Some cross product. Overloads at lines 712 and 724 supply the default partitioner or a partition count.

nodes.name: collectAsMap
nodes.summary: Collects the pairs to the driver as a Map. If a key has several values only one is kept, and all data lands in driver memory, so it is only safe for small RDDs.

nodes.name: mapValues
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each value while leaving keys untouched, implemented as a MapPartitionsRDD created with preservesPartitioning = true so the parent's partitioner survives and later by-key operations avoid a shuffle.

nodes.name: flatMapValues
nodes.summary: Flat-maps each value to zero or more values while keeping the key, again as a MapPartitionsRDD with preservesPartitioning = true; used by the join family to expand cogrouped value lists.

nodes.name: cogroup
nodes.summary: Groups the values of this RDD and another by key into (Iterable[V], Iterable[W]) using a CoGroupedRDD with the given Partitioner and mapValues to unpack the arrays. Overloads cover up to three other RDDs, plus partition-count and default-partitioner variants; HashPartitioner is rejected for array keys. This is the shuffle underlying every join variant here.

nodes.name: groupWith
nodes.summary: Alias for cogroup with the default partitioner; overloads at lines 890 and 896 handle two and three other RDDs.

nodes.name: subtractByKey
nodes.summary: Returns the pairs of this RDD whose keys do not appear in the other RDD by building a SubtractedRDD with the given partitioner. Overloads at lines 907 and 914 default to this RDD's partitioner (or a HashPartitioner of its partition count) or a given partition count.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Returns all values for a key. If the RDD has a partitioner it runs a job on only the partition the key maps to; otherwise it filters all partitions and collects.

nodes.name: saveAsHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Writes the RDD using an old-API (mapred) OutputFormat: sets output key, value and format classes, applies compression settings when a codec is given, installs FileOutputCommitter if none is configured, warns when speculation is enabled together with a 'Direct' output committer (data-loss risk per SPARK-10063), sets the output path, then calls saveAsHadoopDataset. Overloads at lines 953, 963 and 1004 take a ClassTag format, an optional codec, or explicit key and value classes.

nodes.name: saveAsNewAPIHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Writes the RDD using a new-API (mapreduce) OutputFormat by configuring a Hadoop Job with key, value and format classes plus the output directory, then calling saveAsNewAPIHadoopDataset. A ClassTag-based overload at line 974 infers the format class.

nodes.name: saveAsNewAPIHadoopDataset
nodes.summary: Writes the RDD to any Hadoop-supported storage using a new-API Configuration that already names the OutputFormat and output settings. It wraps the configuration in a HadoopMapReduceWriteConfigUtil and hands off to SparkHadoopWriter.write, which owns the task and job commit protocol (not shown in this file).

nodes.name: saveAsHadoopDataset
nodes.summary: Writes the RDD using an old-API JobConf that already names the OutputFormat and paths. It wraps the JobConf in a HadoopMapRedWriteConfigUtil and delegates to SparkHadoopWriter.write, which owns the commit protocol (not shown in this file).

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD of just the keys by mapping each pair to its first element.

nodes.name: values
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD of just the values by mapping each pair to its second element.

nodes.name: keyClass
nodes.summary: Returns the runtime class of the key type from the ClassTag; used to detect array keys that cannot use hash partitioning or map-side combine.

nodes.name: ParallelCollectionRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParallelCollectionRDD, the RDD that backs local collections turned into RDDs, plus its ParallelCollectionPartition and a companion slice helper that cuts a local Seq into numSlices pieces. Ranges are sliced into smaller Ranges to save memory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source with a private companion object and custom Java serialization hooks (writeObject/readObject) on the partition class.

nodes.name: ParallelCollectionPartition
nodes.summary: Partition of a ParallelCollectionRDD holding its rddId, slice index and the actual values of that slice. It carries its data inside the partition object and has custom writeObject/readObject that use the Java default for JavaSerializer or the configured Spark serializer otherwise.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the values stored in this slice.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two partitions are equal when they have the same rddId and slice index.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Custom serialization: with JavaSerializer it uses the default write, otherwise it writes rddId and slice and serializes the values through the configured Spark serializer in a nested stream.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Mirror of writeObject: restores rddId, slice and values using the default Java read or the Spark serializer from SparkEnv.

nodes.name: ParallelCollectionRDD
nodes.summary: RDD built from an in-memory local collection; the collection is split into numSlices partitions, each partition shipping its own slice of data to the tasks. The companion object provides slice(), and optional per-partition location preferences are supported.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and private companion object share one node id; lineRange covers both (class 85-108, object 110-157).

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Slices the data with the companion slice() and wraps each slice in a ParallelCollectionPartition using the RDD id and the slice index.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Returns the slice values of the partition wrapped in an InterruptibleIterator tied to the task context.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Looks up the optional location preference map by partition index, defaulting to no preference.

nodes.name: slice
nodes.summary: Splits a Seq into numSlices sub-collections at consistent index positions so operations like zip behave as expected. Ranges become Ranges (inclusive last slice kept inclusive), NumericRanges are taken/dropped, and other sequences are copied to an array and sliced; numSlices below 1 is rejected.

nodes.name: RDDBarrier.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RDDBarrier, the Experimental wrapper returned by RDD.barrier that forces all tasks of the stage to be launched together (barrier execution mode). It exposes mapPartitions, mapPartitionsWithIndex and mapPartitionsWithEvaluator; the first two build a MapPartitionsRDD flagged isFromBarrier.

nodes.name: RDDBarrier
nodes.summary: Wraps an RDD in a barrier stage so Spark launches all tasks of the stage together; tasks can use BarrierTaskContext. Instances are created by RDD.barrier and the class mirrors the mapPartitions family of the wrapped RDD.

nodes.name: mapPartitions
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each partition like RDD.mapPartitions but builds a MapPartitionsRDD with isFromBarrier = true, so the stage runs as a barrier stage.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithIndex
nodes.summary: Barrier version of mapPartitionsWithIndex: the function receives the partition index and iterator, and the new MapPartitionsRDD is flagged isFromBarrier = true.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithEvaluator
nodes.summary: Wraps the RDD in a MapPartitionsWithEvaluatorRDD built from a PartitionEvaluatorFactory (DeveloperApi); the factory is serialized to executors where each task creates its own evaluator.

nodes.name: RDDCheckpointData.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the checkpoint state machine for one RDD: CheckpointState (Initialized, CheckpointingInProgress, Checkpointed) and the abstract RDDCheckpointData that atomically moves between those states, calls the subclass doCheckpoint, and then truncates the lineage with markCheckpointed.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala Enumeration plus an abstract class and an empty companion object used only as a global lock for synchronized blocks.

nodes.name: CheckpointState
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the checkpoint life cycle of an RDD: Initialized, then CheckpointingInProgress, then Checkpointed.

nodes.name: RDDCheckpointData
nodes.summary: Base class for all checkpoint data of an RDD (one instance per RDD). It tracks cpState and the resulting checkpoint RDD, runs checkpoint() once, and exposes the checkpointed RDD and its partitions. The companion object is just a global lock for the synchronized state changes.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and the empty companion lock object share one node id; lineRange covers both (class 40-107, object 112).

nodes.name: isCheckpointed
nodes.summary: Returns true when the state is Checkpointed, read under the global lock.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Final method that flips Initialized to CheckpointingInProgress under a lock (returning early if another call already did), calls doCheckpoint, then stores the new checkpoint RDD, sets state Checkpointed and calls rdd.markCheckpointed to truncate lineage.

nodes.name: doCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that subclasses implement to materialize and persist the RDD and return the resulting CheckpointRDD.

nodes.name: checkpointRDD
nodes.summary: Returns the RDD holding the checkpointed data; only defined once the state is Checkpointed.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the partitions of the checkpoint RDD (empty if none); documented as for tests only.

nodes.name: ReliableCheckpointRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Reads and writes RDD checkpoints on reliable storage (for example HDFS): the ReliableCheckpointRDD class reads back part-NNNNN files, and its companion writes one file per partition via a job, plus an optional _partitioner file, then returns a ReliableCheckpointRDD for the written directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a private[spark] companion object holding the write and read helpers; both share one class node id.

nodes.name: ReliableCheckpointRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that reads previously written checkpoint files from a reliable checkpoint directory; each part-NNNNN file becomes one partition, and the partitioner is taken from the constructor or from the saved _partitioner file. Its companion object writes partition files (via a job on the original RDD), writes the partitioner on a best-effort basis, and reads files back.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id; lineRange covers both (class 41-130, object 132-336).

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Lists part-* files in the checkpoint directory, sorts them by number, verifies each name matches the expected part-%05d file name, and creates one CheckpointRDDPartition per file.

nodes.name: getPartitionBlockLocations
nodes.summary: Asks the file system for the block locations of the partition file and returns the host names, filtering out localhost.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the hosts holding the checkpoint file of a partition, using a Guava cache when the expire-time config is positive and querying the file system directly otherwise.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Reads one partition by opening the checkpoint file for that partition index through the companion readCheckpointFile.

nodes.name: checkpointFileName
nodes.summary: Returns the file name part-%05d for a partition index.

nodes.name: checkpointPartitionerFileName
nodes.summary: Returns the constant name _partitioner for the partitioner file inside the checkpoint directory.

nodes.name: writeRDDToCheckpointDirectory
nodes.summary: Creates the checkpoint directory, runs a Spark job that writes each partition to its own file, writes the partitioner file if the original RDD has one, builds a ReliableCheckpointRDD and fails if its partition count differs from the original RDD.

nodes.name: writePartitionToCheckpointFile
nodes.summary: Task-side writer: serializes the partition iterator to a temp file named with the task attempt id (optionally compressed), then renames it to part-NNNNN, tolerating another attempt having already produced the final file.

nodes.name: writePartitionerToCheckpointDir
nodes.summary: Best-effort write of the partitioner object to the _partitioner file; any non-fatal exception is logged and ignored.

nodes.name: readCheckpointedPartitionerFile
nodes.summary: Best-effort read of the saved partitioner; returns None if the file is missing or on error (the error case logs a warning about possible performance loss).

nodes.name: readCheckpointFile
nodes.summary: Opens a checkpoint file (decompressing if configured), registers a task completion listener to close the stream, and returns a deserializing iterator over its elements.

nodes.name: ReliableRDDCheckpointData.scala
nodes.summary: Implements RDDCheckpointData for reliable storage: doCheckpoint writes the RDD to an rdd-<id> directory under the SparkContext checkpoint dir through ReliableCheckpointRDD, optionally registers the result with the ContextCleaner, and the companion offers path and cleanup helpers.

nodes.name: ReliableRDDCheckpointData
nodes.summary: Checkpoint data for RDD.checkpoint() that writes to a non-local reliable directory so a restarted driver can reuse the computed state. It fails with an error if no checkpoint directory was set, and its companion computes the rdd-<id> path and deletes it on cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id; lineRange covers both (class 34-75, object 77-90).

nodes.name: getCheckpointDir
nodes.summary: Returns the checkpoint directory if the RDD is already checkpointed, otherwise None.

nodes.name: doCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Writes the RDD to the checkpoint directory with ReliableCheckpointRDD.writeRDDToCheckpointDirectory, registers the new RDD with the cleaner when reference-tracking clean-up of checkpoints is enabled, logs, and returns the new checkpoint RDD.

nodes.name: checkpointPath
nodes.summary: Builds the path rdd-<rddId> under the SparkContext checkpoint directory, or None if no directory is set.

nodes.name: cleanCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Recursively deletes the checkpoint directory of the given RDD id on its file system.

nodes.name: UnionRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UnionRDD, which concatenates the partitions of several parent RDDs into one RDD with range dependencies on each parent, and UnionPartition that points a union partition to its parent RDD and parent partition. Partition listing can run in parallel when the number of RDDs exceeds a threshold.

nodes.name: UnionPartition
