nodes.summary: Encoder for Scala product types (tuples, case classes) using ScalaReflection.encoderFor and a TypeTag.

nodes.name: scalaInt
nodes.summary: Encoder for Scala primitive Int (PrimitiveIntEncoder), as opposed to the nullable boxed INT.

nodes.name: udt
nodes.summary: Encoder for a UserDefinedType (UDTEncoder), since 4.1.0.

nodes.name: Row.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Row, the generic one-record result type of the DataFrame API, and its companion object. A Row gives access by ordinal (get, apply), by primitive getters (getInt, getString ...), by field name (getAs, fieldIndex, getValuesMap) and as JSON; the companion creates rows (Row(...), fromSeq, fromTuple) and supports pattern matching via unapplySeq.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: Trait for one row of output from a relational operator. Generic access by ordinal boxes primitives, while native getters such as getInt require checking isNullAt first (a null raises an error through getAnyValAs). Name-based access (getAs, fieldIndex, getValuesMap) needs a schema, otherwise the default fieldIndex throws. The companion object (lines 48-86) creates GenericRow instances; the trait starts at line 145.

nodes.name: unapplySeq
nodes.summary: Lets a Row be used in a pattern match, for example case Row(key: Int, value: String); it returns the row as a Seq.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: Row(values: Any*) creates a GenericRow from the given values.

nodes.name: fromSeq
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a GenericRow from a Seq of values.

nodes.name: fromTuple
nodes.summary: Companion factory that turns a tuple (Product) into a Row via fromSeq(tuple.productIterator.toSeq).

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.0.0: concatenates the values of several rows into a new GenericRow (a TODO in the source notes the performance could be improved).

nodes.name: length
nodes.summary: Abstract number of elements in the Row; size is defined as length.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Schema (StructType) of the row; defaults to null, so rows without a schema cannot use name-based access or json.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Abstract generic access to the value at position i (null stays null). The doc lists the Scala/Java type returned for each Spark SQL type, e.g. StringType to String, StructType to Row; apply(i) is an alias.

nodes.name: isNullAt
nodes.summary: Checks whether the value at position i is null; must be used before native primitive getters.

nodes.name: getBoolean
nodes.summary: Primitive Boolean at position i through getAnyValAs. The other primitive getters (getByte, getShort, getInt, getLong, getFloat, getDouble) follow the same pattern.

nodes.name: getInt
nodes.summary: Primitive Int at position i through getAnyValAs; throws ClassCastException on a type mismatch and a SparkRuntimeException when the value is null.

nodes.name: getString
nodes.summary: String at position i via getAs[String].

nodes.name: getSeq
nodes.summary: Array value at position i as a Scala Seq; a mutable.ArraySeq is rewrapped as an immutable ArraySeq to avoid a copy (SPARK-49178 in the source comment). getList and getJavaMap are the java.util variants.

nodes.name: getMap
nodes.summary: Map value at position i as a Scala Map.

nodes.name: getStruct
nodes.summary: Struct value at position i as a nested Row.

nodes.name: getAs
nodes.summary: Generic typed access: getAs[T](i) casts get(i) to T (primitive nulls yield the zero value), and getAs[T](fieldName) looks the index up with fieldIndex first. Overloads at lines 415 and 428.

nodes.name: fieldIndex
nodes.summary: Returns the index of a field name. The default implementation in the trait throws DataTypeErrors.fieldIndexOnRowWithoutSchemaError, so rows that have a schema must override it.

nodes.name: getValuesMap
nodes.summary: Returns a Map from the requested field names to their values, using getAs for each name.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Abstract method to make a copy of the Row.

nodes.name: anyNull
nodes.summary: True if any element of the row is null, checked with a while loop over isNullAt.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Element-wise equality: same length and nullness, byte arrays compared with Arrays.equals, NaN equal to NaN for Float and Double, BigDecimal compared with compareTo.

nodes.name: toSeq
nodes.summary: Copies the row into an Array and returns it as an immutable Seq.

nodes.name: mkString
nodes.summary: Joins all elements into a string, with optional separator or start/sep/end strings (three overloads); toString uses mkString("[", ",", "]").

nodes.name: getAnyValAs
nodes.summary: Private helper for primitive getters: throws DataTypeErrors.valueIsNullError if the value is null, otherwise getAs[T].

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Compact JSON representation of the row (marked @Unstable); compact(jsonValue).

nodes.name: prettyJson
nodes.summary: Indented JSON representation of the row (marked @Unstable).

nodes.name: jsonValue
nodes.summary: Converts the row to a json4s JValue using its schema (requires a non-null schema). Local helpers handle booleans, numbers, decimals, strings, binary as Base64, date/time values, intervals, arrays, maps, nested rows and UDTs; other values raise SparkIllegalArgumentException with error class FAILED_ROW_TO_JSON.

nodes.name: Dataset.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Dataset[T] class of the Spark SQL API module: the typed, lazily evaluated collection that DataFrame (Dataset[Row]) is built on. Most operations are abstract here and implemented by the classic (sql/core) and Connect Datasets; the file implements only convenience overloads that delegate to the abstract ones.

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.summary: Abstract Dataset[T] shared by classic Spark and Spark Connect. Transformations (select, filter, join, groupBy, union, withColumn, ...) return a new Dataset or DataFrame and are lazy: a Dataset represents a logical plan, and only actions such as count, collect, show or write trigger execution. Overloads that merely forward (where, orderBy, distinct, unionAll, drop(String), withColumn) are implemented here in terms of abstract primitives like filter, sortInternal, dropDuplicates and withColumns.

nodes.name: queryExecution
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the QueryExecution that holds the analyzed, optimized and physical plans. Marked @ClassicOnly, @DeveloperApi and @Unstable, so it is not available through Spark Connect.

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: Converts the strongly typed Dataset to a DataFrame (Dataset of Row), optionally renaming the columns. The no-arg and varargs forms are abstract and implemented by subclasses.

nodes.name: as
nodes.summary: Abstract typed view change: returns a new Dataset[U] using an implicit Encoder, mapping columns by name for classes, by ordinal for tuples, or the first column for primitives. Only changes the view for typed operations and does not project away columns.

nodes.name: alias
nodes.summary: Overloads as(alias: String), as(alias: Symbol), alias(String) and alias(Symbol): gives the Dataset an alias, which is useful for disambiguating columns in self-joins. The Symbol and alias variants delegate to the abstract as(String).

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the StructType schema of the Dataset. printSchema, dtypes and columns are implemented here on top of it.

nodes.name: explain
nodes.summary: Prints the logical and physical plans. The explain(mode: String) overload is abstract (modes: simple, extended, codegen, cost, formatted); explain(extended: Boolean) and explain() delegate to it.

nodes.name: columns
nodes.summary: Returns all column names as an array, computed from schema.fields in this API class.

nodes.name: isStreaming
nodes.summary: Abstract flag telling whether the Dataset reads from a streaming source. Streaming Datasets must be started with DataStreamWriter.start, and single-answer actions like count or collect throw AnalysisException for them.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Checkpoint family: checkpoint(), checkpoint(eager), localCheckpoint(...) all delegate to the protected abstract checkpoint(eager, reliableCheckpoint, storageLevel). Used to truncate a growing logical plan in iterative algorithms; eager=true materializes immediately.

nodes.name: withWatermark
nodes.summary: Abstract: defines an event-time watermark on the Dataset (column name plus delay threshold), used to finalize window aggregations and bound state of streaming operators. Returns a new Dataset.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Overloads that print the first rows in tabular form (default 20 rows, 20 char truncation). Only show(numRows, truncate: Boolean) and show(numRows, truncate: Int, vertical) are abstract; the others delegate. An action: it triggers execution.

nodes.name: na
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning DataFrameNaFunctions for handling missing data (for example ds.na.drop()).

nodes.name: stat
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning DataFrameStatFunctions for statistics helpers such as freqItems.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: All untyped join overloads plus crossJoin. The using-column variants (String, Array, Seq) delegate to join(right, usingColumns: Seq[String], joinType), and join(right, joinExprs) delegates to the joinExprs/joinType form with inner; the two joinType variants, join(right) and crossJoin are abstract. Each call returns a new DataFrame lazily; a using-column join emits the key column once.

nodes.name: joinWith
nodes.summary: Typed join that returns Dataset[(T, U)], keeping both sides as objects. The condition-only overload delegates to the abstract form with an inner join.

nodes.name: sortWithinPartitions
nodes.summary: Sorts rows inside each partition only. Both overloads end in sortInternal(global = false, ...), which subclasses implement.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Global sort. The String overload maps names to Column and both end in sortInternal(global = true, ...), the abstract primitive implemented by subclasses.

nodes.name: orderBy
nodes.summary: Alias of sort for both String and Column forms.

nodes.name: col
nodes.summary: Abstract: resolves a column name to a Column against this Dataset. apply(colName) in this class delegates to it, which is how ds("age") works in Scala.

nodes.name: select
nodes.summary: Projection overloads. select(cols: Column*) and select(TypedColumn) are abstract; select(String, String*) wraps names into Columns; typed overloads with 2 to 5 TypedColumns call the protected selectUntyped and cast to a tuple Dataset. Returns a new DataFrame or Dataset lazily.

nodes.name: selectExpr
nodes.summary: Selects SQL expression strings by mapping each through functions.expr and calling select.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Row filtering overloads: Column and function variants (Scala func, Java FilterFunction) are abstract; the SQL-string overload parses via functions.expr and delegates to filter(Column). Returns a new Dataset.

nodes.name: where
nodes.summary: Alias for filter, both for Column conditions and SQL expression strings.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Groups rows by columns and returns a RelationalGroupedDataset on which aggregations are called. The Column form is abstract; the String form maps names via col and delegates.

nodes.name: rollup
nodes.summary: rollup and cube (Column and String overloads): produce multi-level grouped RelationalGroupedDatasets; the Column forms are abstract and the String forms map names through col.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Aggregates the whole Dataset without grouping. All overloads (tuples, Map, java Map, Columns) are implemented here as groupBy().agg(...).

nodes.name: reduce
nodes.summary: Action reducing elements with a commutative and associative binary function. The Scala form is abstract; the Java ReduceFunction form adapts through ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: groupByKey
nodes.summary: Typed grouping by a key function returning a KeyValueGroupedDataset[K, T]. The Scala form is abstract; the Java MapFunction form adapts with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: unpivot
nodes.summary: Abstract wide-to-long reshape (unpivot, with melt as an alias in this class) into variable and value columns.

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Abstract: attaches named metrics (aggregate columns) to the Dataset without changing its result. Metrics are reported at the end of a batch query or streaming epoch, either by name or through an Observation object.

nodes.name: limit
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns a new Dataset with the first n rows. Unlike head it is a transformation, not an action.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: UNION ALL semantics by column position; unionAll is an alias. Use distinct afterwards for SQL set union.

nodes.name: unionByName
nodes.summary: Union that resolves columns by name; the one-argument form delegates with allowMissingColumns = false to the abstract two-argument form.

nodes.name: intersect
nodes.summary: Set operations intersect, intersectAll, except and exceptAll, all abstract here. Equality uses the encoded representation, not a custom equals on T.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Random sampling overloads. Only sample(withReplacement, fraction, seed) is abstract; the others fill in defaults (random seed from SparkClassUtils.random, withReplacement = false).

nodes.name: withColumn
nodes.summary: Adds or replaces columns. withColumn and the Map overloads delegate to the private[spark] abstract withColumns(names, cols); a metadata variant wraps columns with col.as(name, metadata) before delegating. Returns a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: withColumnRenamed
nodes.summary: Renames columns. Single and Map forms both end in the protected abstract withColumnsRenamed(colNames, newColNames).

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: Drops top-level columns by name or Column; no-op if absent. The single-argument forms delegate to the abstract varargs variants.

nodes.name: dropDuplicates
nodes.summary: Removes duplicate rows, optionally by a subset of columns; the no-arg and Seq forms are abstract, the Array and varargs forms delegate. In streaming it keeps state across triggers, bounded by a watermark if set.

nodes.name: dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark
nodes.summary: Streaming deduplication that only remembers keys within the watermark delay; the no-arg and Seq forms are abstract and the Array and varargs forms delegate.

nodes.name: head
nodes.summary: Action returning the first n rows to the driver as an array. head() and first() are defined in terms of head(n). Only for small results, since data is loaded into driver memory.

nodes.name: transform
nodes.summary: Concise chaining of custom transformations: applies the function t to this Dataset and returns its result.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Typed element-wise transformation producing a Dataset[U]; Scala (with Encoder) and Java (MapFunction plus Encoder) forms are abstract.

nodes.name: mapPartitions
nodes.summary: Typed per-partition transformation. The Scala form is abstract; the Java MapPartitionsFunction form adapts via ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: flatMap
nodes.summary: Typed flatMap implemented here by adapting the function with UDFAdaptors.flatMapToMapPartitions and calling mapPartitions.

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Action that runs a function on each element; foreach is adapted by UDFAdaptors into the abstract foreachPartition.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Abstract action returning all rows as an array in the driver, which can cause OutOfMemoryError on large Datasets. collectAsList is the Java variant.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Abstract action returning the number of rows; triggers execution.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Repartition by number and/or expressions. The numeric form is abstract; expression forms call protected repartitionByExpression (Some(n) or None).

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Abstract: reduces the number of partitions via a narrow dependency without a shuffle; stays unchanged if more partitions are requested.

nodes.name: distinct
nodes.summary: Returns unique rows; implemented as dropDuplicates().

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Caching: persist(), cache() and persist(StorageLevel) are abstract (default level MEMORY_AND_DISK). The doc notes cached data is shared across all Spark sessions on the cluster.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Abstract: marks the Dataset non-persistent and removes its blocks; the doc notes this affects all sessions.

nodes.name: createTempView
nodes.summary: Temp view registration: createTempView, createOrReplaceTempView, createGlobalTempView, createOrReplaceGlobalTempView (and deprecated registerTempTable) all delegate to the protected abstract createTempView(viewName, replace, global). Local views live as long as the session.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning a DataFrameWriter for saving a non-streaming Dataset to external storage. Writing is an action.

nodes.name: writeStream
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning a DataStreamWriter for writing a streaming Dataset.

nodes.name: SparkSession.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract SparkSession API (the entry point of the Dataset and DataFrame API), its companion object with a nested Builder, and the shared SparkSessionCompanion and SparkSessionBuilder base types that track the active and default sessions. Concrete sessions live in the classic and Connect implementations, which the companion locates by reflection.

nodes.name: SparkSession
nodes.summary: Abstract SparkSession shared by classic Spark and Spark Connect. Declares the session surface (sql, read, readStream, table, range, createDataFrame, createDataset, udf, conf, catalog, streams, newSession) as mostly abstract members; some are annotated @ClassicOnly (sparkContext, sharedState, sessionState, RDD based createDataFrame) and are not available in Connect. The companion object (lines 817 to 958) is the user-facing SparkSession.builder() entry point.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Nested SparkSession.Builder that collects options and picks the classic or Connect companion (default: classic if found on the classpath, else Connect, otherwise IllegalStateException). Its getOrCreate and create build an implementation specific builder, copy the SparkContext, options and extensions into it, and delegate.

nodes.name: SparkSessionCompanion
nodes.summary: Private[sql] base class for the session companion objects, with its own companion object holding an InheritableThreadLocal active session and an AtomicReference default session. Provides set/get/clear of the active (thread-local) and default (global) sessions and leaves builder() and tryCastToImplementation to implementations.

nodes.name: SparkSessionBuilder
nodes.summary: Private[sql] @Stable abstract builder base class that stores options in a mutable HashMap and defines the config overloads, appName, master, enableHiveSupport and remote in terms of config keys (spark.app.name, spark.master, spark.sql.catalogImplementation, spark.connect.remote). getOrCreate, create and withExtensions are left to implementations; its companion holds the key constants and the spark.api.mode values.

nodes.name: sparkContext
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the SparkContext of the session; annotated @ClassicOnly, so it is only supported in classic Spark.

nodes.name: conf
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the RuntimeConfig used to get and set Spark SQL configurations at runtime.

nodes.name: udf
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the UDFRegistration used to register user defined functions (UDFs must be deterministic according to the doc).

nodes.name: streams
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the StreamingQueryManager that manages all active StreamingQuery instances of the session.

nodes.name: newSession
nodes.summary: Abstract: starts a new session with isolated SQL configurations, temporary views and registered functions, while sharing the underlying SparkContext and cached data.

nodes.name: emptyDataFrame
nodes.summary: emptyDataFrame (abstract, no rows or columns) and emptyDataFrame(schema), which is implemented here as emptyDataset(Encoders.row(schema)).

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Group of createDataFrame overloads, all abstract: from a Seq of Product, Java lists with a schema or bean class, and (annotated @ClassicOnly) from RDD, JavaRDD with a schema or bean class. Returns a DataFrame; rows must match the given schema or a runtime exception is thrown.

nodes.name: emptyDataset
nodes.summary: Abstract: creates a Dataset[T] with zero elements, using an implicit Encoder.

nodes.name: createDataset
nodes.summary: Abstract overloads that build a Dataset[T] from a local Seq, a java.util.List or (ClassicOnly) an RDD; they need an Encoder, normally supplied by implicits from the session or by Encoders.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Abstract overloads creating a Dataset[java.lang.Long] with a single LongType column named id, over [start, end) with optional step and number of partitions.

nodes.name: catalog
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the Catalog interface used to create, drop, alter or query databases, tables and functions.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the named table or view as a DataFrame. A table must support batch reading; a view returns its query plan, which can be batch or streaming. Names resolve temp views first, then the current database.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL statement and returns a DataFrame. The positional (Array) and named (Map) parameter variants are abstract; the java.util.Map variant converts to a Scala Map and sql(sqlText) calls sql(sqlText, Map.empty). The doc states DDL/DML commands run eagerly while SELECT queries are lazy.

nodes.name: executeCommand
nodes.summary: Abstract @Unstable: eagerly executes an arbitrary string command in an external engine through a named ExternalCommandRunner and returns its output as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: addArtifact
nodes.summary: Experimental abstract overloads (addArtifact and addArtifacts) for adding .jar and .class artifacts to the session from a path, URI, in-memory bytes or a source/target pair.

nodes.name: addTag
nodes.summary: Abstract: adds a tag to all operations started by this thread in this session so they can be cancelled together; companions are removeTag, getTags and clearTags.

nodes.name: interruptTag
nodes.summary: Abstract: requests interruption of all running operations of the session with the given tag; interruptAll and interruptOperation are siblings. Waits up to 60 seconds for the request to be issued, per the doc.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning a DataFrameReader for loading non-streaming data into a DataFrame.

nodes.name: readStream
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning a DataStreamReader for loading streaming data into a DataFrame.

nodes.name: tvf
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor returning a TableValuedFunction for calling table-valued functions.

nodes.name: time
nodes.summary: Runs a code block and prints the elapsed milliseconds to stdout; meant for interactive testing and debugging in Scala.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Synonym for close() (the class extends Closeable).

nodes.name: isUsable
nodes.summary: Private[sql] abstract check whether the session is still usable: in classic the SparkContext is still active, in Connect the connection to the server is usable.

nodes.name: withActive
nodes.summary: Runs a block with this session set as the thread's active session and restores the previous one in a finally clause; reads the active-session thread local directly so the default session is not promoted.

nodes.name: DEFAULT_COMPANION
nodes.summary: Private default API-mode selection: tries the classic companion first, then the Connect companion, otherwise throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: lookupCompanion
nodes.summary: Private helper that loads a companion class by name (classic.SparkSession or connect.SparkSession) with SparkClassUtils.classForName and Scala runtime reflection, returning it as a SparkSessionCompanion.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: SparkSession.builder(): returns a new SparkSession.Builder, the usual way to get or create a session.

nodes.name: appName
nodes.summary: ClassicOnly override of appName that delegates to the base builder.

nodes.name: master
nodes.summary: ClassicOnly override of master that delegates to the base builder.

nodes.name: enableHiveSupport
nodes.summary: ClassicOnly override of enableHiveSupport that delegates to the base builder.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Overrides of the config overloads (String, Long, Double, Boolean, Map, java Map, SparkConf), each delegating to the base builder.

nodes.name: remote
nodes.summary: Override of remote(connectionString) that delegates to the base builder, which sets spark.connect.remote.

nodes.name: withExtensions
nodes.summary: ClassicOnly: records the extension functions in a buffer so they can be applied to the implementation specific builder later.

nodes.name: classic
nodes.summary: Selects the classic API mode via mode(...). Note: the source passes CONNECT_COMPANION here (same as connect()), which looks like a copy and paste slip.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Selects the Connect API mode via mode(CONNECT_COMPANION).

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Builds the implementation specific builder and calls its getOrCreate().

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builds the implementation specific builder and calls its create(), which always returns a new session.

nodes.name: handleBuilderConfig
nodes.summary: Intercepts the spark.api.mode option and switches the companion to the classic or Connect one (throws IllegalArgumentException on an unknown mode); other keys are stored as normal options.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Private: creates the implementation builder from the chosen companion and copies the SparkContext, the collected options and the extension functions into it.

nodes.name: setActiveSession
nodes.summary: Sets the thread-local (inheritable) active session returned by getOrCreate in this thread and its children.

nodes.name: clearActiveSession
nodes.summary: Removes the thread-local active session so later getOrCreate calls return the first created session.

nodes.name: setDefaultSession
nodes.summary: Sets the global default session in an AtomicReference.

nodes.name: clearDefaultSession
nodes.summary: Clears the global default session.

nodes.name: getActiveSession
nodes.summary: Returns the usable active session of the current thread as Option; None on executors.

nodes.name: getDefaultSession
nodes.summary: Returns the usable default session as Option; None on executors.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Returns the active session, else the default one, else throws an internal error because no session exists.

nodes.name: usableSession
nodes.summary: Private filter returning Some(session) only when it is non null and isUsable, after casting to the implementation type.

nodes.name: setDefaultAndActiveSession
nodes.summary: Sets the default (compare-and-set) and active sessions only when they are unset or not usable.

nodes.name: onSessionClose
nodes.summary: On session close, removes the session from the default reference and from the active slot if it is the active one.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Abstract factory that implementations override to return their SparkSessionBuilder.

nodes.name: putConfig
nodes.summary: Private: lets handleBuilderConfig consume a builder-only key, otherwise stores the key/value in the options map.

nodes.name: handleBuilderConfig
nodes.summary: Protected abstract hook for config changes that are relevant only to the builder; returns true when handled.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Base implementations of all config overloads; each converts the value to a string and stores it in the options (synchronized), so the options are applied when the session is built.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the valid thread-local session, else the valid default session, else creates and registers a new one, applying non-static options to an existing session.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Abstract: always creates a new session, updating default and active sessions when they are unset.

nodes.name: DataFrameReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract, engine-independent DataFrameReader used by SparkSession.read in both classic and Connect. It holds the builder state (source, user schema, case-insensitive options) and implements the format-specific shortcuts (json, csv, parquet, ...) by setting the format and delegating to the abstract load.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with this.type builder methods, overloaded varargs methods and protected hook methods that subclasses override.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract, engine-independent DataFrameWriter[T] reached through Dataset.write. It stores the builder state (save mode, format, options, partitioning, bucketing, sorting, clustering, schema evolution flag), validates partitioning combinations, and leaves save, insertInto and saveAsTable to concrete subclasses.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with this.type builder methods and protected state variables shared with the classic and Connect implementations.

nodes.name: DataFrameReader
nodes.summary: Abstract builder for loading a Dataset from external storage. format, schema, option and options only record state in protected vars (source, userSpecifiedSchema, extraOptions); load, jdbc with predicates, Dataset[String] variants, table and changes are abstract. Subclasses decide what load() actually builds.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Stores the input data source name in the protected source var and returns this for chaining.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Sets the user-specified schema, either from a StructType (rejecting CHAR/VARCHAR via SparkCharVarcharUtils, then calling validateSingleVariantColumn) or from a DDL string parsed with StructType.fromDDL.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one input option (String, Boolean, Long or Double overloads) to the case-insensitive extraOptions map, overriding an existing key, and re-runs validateSingleVariantColumn for the String form.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Merges a Scala map (or a java.util.Map converted with asScala) into extraOptions and re-runs validateSingleVariantColumn.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Abstract entry points that turn the accumulated source, schema and options into a DataFrame: load() for path-less sources, load(path) and load(paths*) for path-based sources. All format-specific shortcuts end up here.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Three JDBC overloads. The url/table/properties form merges the properties and url/dbtable into extraOptions after assertNoSpecifiedSchema and calls format("jdbc").load(). The partition-column form adds partitionColumn, lowerBound, upperBound and numPartitions options and delegates to it. The predicates form is abstract.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: JSON loading overloads. The path forms call validateJsonSchema, then format("json").load(paths); the Dataset[String], JavaRDD[String] and RDD[String] forms are abstract (the RDD forms are deprecated and not supported in Spark Connect).

nodes.name: csv
nodes.summary: CSV loading overloads. The path forms call format("csv").load(paths); the Dataset[String] form is abstract.

nodes.name: xml
nodes.summary: XML loading overloads. The path forms call validateXmlSchema, then format("xml").load(paths); the Dataset[String] form is abstract.

nodes.name: parquet
nodes.summary: Loads Parquet files by setting format("parquet") and calling load(paths).

nodes.name: orc
nodes.summary: Loads ORC files by setting format("orc") and calling load(paths).

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns a table or view as a DataFrame; for a table it must support batch reading.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Abstract method (since 4.2.0) returning row-level changes (Change Data Capture) of a Data Source V2 table whose catalog implements TableCatalog.loadChangelog().

nodes.name: text
nodes.summary: Loads text files by setting format("text") and calling load(paths); the resulting schema starts with a string column named value.

nodes.name: textFile
nodes.summary: Loads text files as Dataset[String]: asserts no user schema was set, calls text(paths), selects the value column and applies StringEncoder.

nodes.name: assertNoSpecifiedSchema
nodes.summary: Throws DataTypeErrors.userSpecifiedSchemaUnsupportedError(operation) when a user schema was set; used by jdbc, textFile and the classic table and changes.

nodes.name: validateSingleVariantColumn
nodes.summary: Protected no-op hook meant to reject the singleVariantColumn option together with a user schema; the classic reader overrides it.

nodes.name: validateJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Protected no-op hook called before JSON path loading; subclasses override it to check the user schema.

nodes.name: validateXmlSchema
nodes.summary: Protected no-op hook called before XML path loading; subclasses override it to check the user schema.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract builder for writing a Dataset. mode, format, option(s), partitionBy, bucketBy, sortBy, clusterBy and withSchemaEvolution only record state in protected vars (curmode defaults to SaveMode.ErrorIfExists); save(), save(path), insertInto and saveAsTable are abstract. The json/parquet/orc/text/csv/xml shortcuts set the format and call save(path).

nodes.name: mode
nodes.summary: Sets the SaveMode (Overwrite, Append, Ignore, ErrorIfExists). The String overload lower-cases the text and maps overwrite, append, ignore and error/errorifexists/default, otherwise throws CompilationErrors.invalidSaveModeError.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Stores the output data source name in the protected source var and returns this.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one output option (String, Boolean, Long or Double overloads) to the case-insensitive extraOptions map.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Merges a Scala map or a java.util.Map of options into extraOptions.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Records the partitioning column names (Hive-style directory layout) and calls validatePartitioning so clusterBy cannot be combined with it.

nodes.name: bucketBy
nodes.summary: Records the bucket count and bucket column names, then calls validatePartitioning.

nodes.name: sortBy
nodes.summary: Records the sort columns used inside each bucket; the requirement that bucketBy was called is checked later in isBucketed.

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Records the clustering columns (since 4.0) and calls validatePartitioning.

nodes.name: withSchemaEvolution
nodes.summary: Experimental (since 4.2.0) switch that sets the _withSchemaEvolution flag; the target table must declare the AUTOMATIC_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION capability.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Abstract save(path) and save() methods that write the Dataset to the configured data source.

nodes.name: insertInto
nodes.summary: Abstract method that inserts into an existing table by column position; format and options are ignored and ErrorIfExists and Ignore behave like Append.

nodes.name: saveAsTable
nodes.summary: Abstract method that saves the Dataset as a table, resolving columns by name; behavior on an existing table depends on the save mode.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Asserts the write is not partitioned, bucketed or clustered, merges connection properties and url/dbtable into extraOptions, then calls format("jdbc").save().

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("json").save(path).

nodes.name: parquet
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("parquet").save(path).

nodes.name: orc
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("orc").save(path).

nodes.name: text
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("text").save(path).

nodes.name: csv
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("csv").save(path).

nodes.name: xml
nodes.summary: Shortcut for format("xml").save(path).

nodes.name: isBucketed
nodes.summary: Throws sortByWithoutBucketingError when sortBy was used without bucketBy, otherwise returns whether a bucket count is set.

nodes.name: assertNotBucketed
nodes.summary: Throws a CompilationErrors error (bucketBy, or bucketBy plus sortBy) when the writer is bucketed and the named operation does not support it.

nodes.name: assertNotPartitioned
nodes.summary: Throws operationNotSupportPartitioningError when partitionBy columns are set and the operation does not support partitioning.

nodes.name: assertNotClustered
nodes.summary: Throws operationNotSupportClusteringError when clusterBy columns are set and the operation does not support clustering.

nodes.name: validatePartitioning
nodes.summary: Throws when clusterBy is combined with partitionBy or with bucketing.

nodes.name: DataFrameReader.scala
nodes.summary: Classic (in-process) implementation of DataFrameReader. load builds an UnresolvedDataSource logical plan that is wrapped by Dataset.ofRows, table and changes build UnresolvedRelation based plans, and the Dataset[String] json/csv/xml readers parse the text RDD directly into a DataFrame; the explicit-predicates jdbc builds a JDBCRelation.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of DataFrameWriter. save, insertInto and saveAsTable each build a logical plan (V1 DataSource planForWriting, V2 AppendData/OverwriteByExpression/CreateTableAsSelect/ReplaceTableAsSelect, InsertIntoStatement or SaveAsV1TableCommand) according to SaveMode and the resolved provider, and runCommand executes it through a QueryExecution.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriterV2.scala
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of the DataFrameWriterV2 API (Dataset.writeTo). Each action (create, replace, createOrReplace, append, overwrite, overwritePartitions) builds a V2 logical plan (CreateTableAsSelect, ReplaceTableAsSelect, AppendData, OverwriteByExpression, OverwritePartitionsDynamic) and runs it through a QueryExecution; also holds the PartitionTransform extractor for partitionedBy.

nodes.name: DataFrameReader
nodes.summary: Classic subclass of the api DataFrameReader created with a SparkSession; its constructor sets the format to the session's defaultDataSourceName. Most option and format-shortcut methods only forward to super, while load, jdbc (predicates), table, changes and the Dataset[String] json/csv/xml methods are implemented here.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: load() calls load(Nil); load(path) either sets the path option (legacyPathOptionBehavior) or forwards the path. load(paths*) is the real work: it wraps UnresolvedDataSource(source, userSpecifiedSchema, extraOptions, isStreaming = false, paths) with Dataset.ofRows, so the V1 vs V2 resolution of the source is not done here but when that plan is analyzed.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: The simple and partitioned overloads forward to the api implementation. The predicates overload asserts no user schema, merges connection properties into the options, builds JDBCOptions and one JDBCPartition per predicate, creates a JDBCRelation and converts it with baseRelationToDataFrame.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: json(JavaRDD) and json(RDD) convert the RDD to a Dataset[String]; json(Dataset[String]) parses JSONOptions, infers the schema with TextInputJsonDataSource.inferFromDataset unless a user schema is given, parses each partition with JacksonParser wrapped in FailureSafeParser, and builds the DataFrame via internalCreateDataFrame.

nodes.name: csv
nodes.summary: csv(path) and csv(paths*) forward to super. csv(Dataset[String]) parses CSVOptions, filters comment and empty lines with CSVUtils, optionally reads the first line, infers or applies the schema, checks the header with CSVHeaderChecker, parses rows with UnivocityParser inside FailureSafeParser and builds the DataFrame via internalCreateDataFrame.

nodes.name: xml
nodes.summary: xml(path) and xml(paths*) forward to super. xml(Dataset[String]) parses XmlOptions, checks or infers the schema with TextInputXmlDataSource, parses each partition with StaxXmlParser inside FailureSafeParser and builds the DataFrame via internalCreateDataFrame.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Asserts no user schema, parses the table name with the session SQL parser and returns Dataset.ofRows over an UnresolvedRelation carrying the reader options as CaseInsensitiveStringMap.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Validates the table name, asserts no user schema, builds a changelog context from the options and the session time zone, and returns Dataset.ofRows over RelationChanges(UnresolvedRelation, changelogContext).

nodes.name: validateSingleVariantColumn
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook to call DataSourceOptions.validateSingleVariantColumn(extraOptions, userSpecifiedSchema).

nodes.name: validateJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook to run checkJsonSchema on the user-specified schema, if any.

nodes.name: validateXmlSchema
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook to run checkXmlSchema on the user-specified schema, if any.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriter
nodes.summary: Final classic subclass of the api DataFrameWriter, created from a Dataset (its constructor sets the format to defaultDataSourceName and keeps df = ds.toDF()). The mode, format, option(s), partitionBy, bucketBy, sortBy and clusterBy methods just forward to super; the class implements save, insertInto and saveAsTable by building logical plans that depend on the save mode and the resolved V1/V2 provider.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: save(path) and save() run saveCommand(Some(path)) or saveCommand(None) through runCommand, so the write is executed eagerly as a command.

nodes.name: saveCommand
nodes.summary: Builds the plan for save. It rejects a conflicting path option and the hive provider, asserts the writer is not bucketed, and looks up a V2 provider. With V2: Append builds AppendData.byName and Overwrite builds OverwriteByExpression.byName (table loaded via SupportsCatalogOptions or getTable, falling back to the V1 path when BATCH_WRITE is unsupported); the other modes build CreateTableAsSelect (ErrorIfExists or Ignore) or fail for plain TableProviders. Without a V2 provider it calls saveToV1SourceCommand.

nodes.name: assertSchemaEvolutionNotEnabledForV1Write
nodes.summary: Throws schemaEvolutionNotSupportedForV1TableWriteError when withSchemaEvolution was requested for a V1 write.

nodes.name: getOptionsWithPath
nodes.summary: Returns extraOptions, adding the path option when a save path is given.

nodes.name: saveToV1SourceCommand
nodes.summary: V1 path of save: encodes partitioning and clustering columns into the options, then returns DataSource(session, source, partitionColumns, options).planForWriting(curmode, df.logicalPlan), so SaveMode is interpreted by the V1 DataSource.

nodes.name: insertInto
nodes.summary: Runs insertIntoCommand(tableName) through runCommand.

nodes.name: insertIntoCommand
nodes.summary: Builds the insertInto plan across three overloads. Asserts not bucketed and rejects partitionBy, parses the table name, then picks a catalog. For a V2 catalog and table it builds AppendData.byPosition (Append, ErrorIfExists, Ignore), or for Overwrite OverwritePartitionsDynamic.byPosition (dynamic partition overwrite mode) or OverwriteByExpression.byPosition; V1 tables become an InsertIntoStatement with overwrite = (curmode == Overwrite).

nodes.name: getWritePrivileges
nodes.summary: Returns INSERT and DELETE privileges for Overwrite, otherwise INSERT only.

nodes.name: getBucketSpec
nodes.summary: Calls isBucketed() for validation and, if a bucket count is set, returns BucketSpec(numBuckets, bucketColumnNames, sortColumnNames).

nodes.name: hasCustomSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: True when SQLConf.V2_SESSION_CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION is not the builtin value.

nodes.name: saveAsTable
nodes.summary: Runs saveAsTableCommand(tableName) through runCommand.

nodes.name: saveAsTableCommand
nodes.summary: Builds the saveAsTable plan across two overloads. Resolves the table name to a V2 catalog (non-session catalog, or the session catalog when V2 is usable) or a V1 TableIdentifier. For V2: an existing V1Table falls back to saveAsV1TableCommand; Append on an existing table builds AppendData.byName; Overwrite builds ReplaceTableAsSelect with orCreate = true; other cases build CreateTableAsSelect with ignoreIfExists for SaveMode.Ignore.

nodes.name: saveAsV1TableCommand
nodes.summary: Builds a CatalogTable (EXTERNAL when a location is set, else MANAGED; provider, partition columns, bucket spec, cluster-by property) and returns SaveAsV1TableCommand(tableDesc, curmode, df.logicalPlan).

nodes.name: partitioningAsV2
nodes.summary: Converts partitionBy, bucketBy and clusterBy settings to a Seq of V2 Transforms (IdentityTransform, bucket transform, ClusterByTransform).

nodes.name: checkPartitioningMatchesV2Table
nodes.summary: Requires that user-provided V2 partitioning or clustering equals the existing table's partitioning; an empty provided partitioning is accepted.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.summary: Wraps the command plan in a new QueryExecution (sharing the dataset's tracker and a shuffle cleanup mode) and calls assertCommandExecuted() to execute it eagerly.

nodes.name: lookupV2Provider
nodes.summary: Calls DataSource.lookupDataSourceV2(source, conf) and ignores FileDataSourceV2 so file sources use the V1 write path (TODO SPARK-28396).

nodes.name: DataFrameWriterV2
nodes.summary: Final classic implementation of the api DataFrameWriterV2, constructed from a table name and a Dataset. Builder methods (using, option(s), tableProperty, partitionedBy, clusterBy) store state; each terminal action builds a V2 logical plan against the parsed multipart table name and runs it with runCommand.

nodes.name: PartitionTransform
nodes.summary: Private helper object that defines extractors for the partitioning functions hours, days, months, years and bucket, used by partitionedBy to recognise unresolved function expressions.

nodes.name: ExtractTransform
nodes.summary: Extractor class whose unapply matches an UnresolvedFunction with the given name and returns its argument expressions.

nodes.name: using
nodes.summary: Sets the table provider (data source name) used in the table spec.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one write option to the mutable options map.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds all entries of a Scala map (or java.util.Map converted with asScala) to the options map.

nodes.name: tableProperty
nodes.summary: Adds a table property that ends up in UnresolvedTableSpec.properties.

nodes.name: partitionedBy
nodes.summary: Converts Column expressions into V2 Transforms: years/months/days/hours/bucket function calls (via PartitionTransform) or a plain attribute as identity; invalid bucket counts or other expressions raise errors; then calls validatePartitioning.

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Stores a ClusterByTransform over the given columns and calls validatePartitioning.

nodes.name: validatePartitioning
nodes.summary: Throws clusterByWithPartitionedBy when both partitioning and clustering were set.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Runs createCommand() through runCommand.

nodes.name: createCommand
nodes.summary: Rejects schema evolution and returns CreateTableAsSelect(UnresolvedIdentifier(tableName), partitioning ++ clustering, logicalPlan, buildTableSpec(), options, ignoreIfExists = false).

nodes.name: buildTableSpec
nodes.summary: Builds an UnresolvedTableSpec from the properties, provider and options; the location comes from the path option unless LEGACY_DF_WRITER_V2_IGNORE_PATH_OPTION is set.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Calls internalReplace(orCreate = false).

nodes.name: createOrReplace
nodes.summary: Calls internalReplace(orCreate = true).

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Runs appendCommand() through runCommand.

nodes.name: appendCommand
nodes.summary: Returns AppendData.byName over an UnresolvedRelation that requires INSERT privilege, with the stored options and the schema evolution flag.

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Runs overwriteCommand(condition) through runCommand.

nodes.name: overwriteCommand
nodes.summary: Returns OverwriteByExpression.byName over an UnresolvedRelation that requires INSERT and DELETE privileges, with the converted condition expression.

nodes.name: overwritePartitions
nodes.summary: Runs overwritePartitionsCommand() through runCommand.

nodes.name: overwritePartitionsCommand
nodes.summary: Returns OverwritePartitionsDynamic.byName over an UnresolvedRelation that requires INSERT and DELETE privileges.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.summary: Wraps the command in a QueryExecution (sharing the dataset's tracker and a shuffle cleanup mode) and calls assertCommandExecuted() to run it eagerly.

nodes.name: internalReplace
nodes.summary: Runs replaceCommand(orCreate) through runCommand.

nodes.name: replaceCommand
nodes.summary: Rejects schema evolution and returns ReplaceTableAsSelect(UnresolvedIdentifier(tableName), partitioning ++ clustering, logicalPlan, buildTableSpec(), writeOptions, orCreate).

nodes.name: Dataset.scala
nodes.summary: Classic (non-Connect) implementation of the Scala Dataset/DataFrame API. A Dataset wraps a QueryExecution (a LogicalPlan plus its analysis, optimization and physical planning) and an Encoder; transformations build a new LogicalPlan and wrap it in a new Dataset, while actions run the executed plan inside SQLExecution.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a private[sql] companion object (Dataset.apply, Dataset.ofRows) and a large class that extends the abstract sql.Dataset; many overrides at the end only narrow return types to the classic classes.

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.summary: Classic Dataset[T]: holds a QueryExecution and an Encoder generator, exposes the analyzed logical plan as logicalPlan, and implements relational and typed transformations by wrapping new logical operators with withPlan, withTypedPlan or withSameTypedPlan. Actions go through withAction/SQLExecution. The companion object (lines 74-141) provides apply and ofRows.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends sql.Dataset[T] from sql/api. The constructor eagerly runs assertAnalyzed on the QueryExecution unless lazy analysis is enabled, so most analysis errors surface when a Dataset is created.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory for typed Datasets (two overloads: implicit Encoder, or an encoder generator). Builds a Dataset from a LogicalPlan and eagerly touches resolvedEnc so the Encoder is checked against the plan schema, skipping the check for Row encoders because it requires running the whole Analyzer.

nodes.name: ofRows
nodes.summary: Companion factory (three overloads) that turns a LogicalPlan into a DataFrame: creates a QueryExecution (via sessionState.executePlan or new QueryExecution, optionally with a QueryPlanningTracker and shuffle cleanup mode), calls assertAnalyzed unless analysis is lazy, and wraps it with a RowEncoder derived from the analyzed schema.

nodes.name: queryExecution
nodes.summary: Constructor val holding the QueryExecution that owns this Dataset's logical, analyzed, optimized and physical plans. Marked DeveloperApi, Unstable and transient.

nodes.name: sparkSession
nodes.summary: Lazy val returning the SparkSession of the QueryExecution; throws a driver-only error if the QueryExecution or its session is null (for example when used on executors).

nodes.name: logicalPlan
nodes.summary: Computes the Dataset's logical plan: the unanalyzed logical plan when analysis is lazy, otherwise queryExecution.commandExecuted, tagged with this Dataset's id when FAIL_AMBIGUOUS_SELF_JOIN_ENABLED is set so ambiguous self joins can be detected.

nodes.name: exprEnc
nodes.summary: Lazy ExpressionEncoder obtained with encoderFor(encoder); used for actual (de)serialization and for binding Aggregator inputs.

nodes.name: resolvedEnc
nodes.summary: Lazy encoder resolved and bound to the output of queryExecution.commandExecuted with the session analyzer; used to turn collected rows back into objects of type T.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves a quoted column name against the analyzed plan with the analyzer's resolver, throwing an unresolved-column error that lists the schema field names if nothing matches.

nodes.name: showString
nodes.summary: Builds the text table used by show: fetches rows with getRows, computes column widths (using half-width string length), pads and truncates cells, and supports a vertical record layout and an 'only showing top N rows' footer.

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: toDF() reuses the same QueryExecution under a RowEncoder for the schema (a cheap re-typing to DataFrame). The toDF(colNames*) overload at lines 531-533 instead builds an UnresolvedSubqueryColumnAliases plan via withPlan to rename columns.

nodes.name: as
nodes.summary: as[U: Encoder] re-types the Dataset to another Encoder by calling Dataset[U](sparkSession, logicalPlan), which re-validates the encoder against the plan schema. The as(alias) overload at lines 950-952 wraps the plan in a SubqueryAlias.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns the analyzed plan's schema inside sparkSession.withActive.

nodes.name: explain
nodes.summary: Prints queryExecution.explainString for the requested ExplainMode, rather than going through ExplainCommand, so the output matches the Dataset's own plans.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Runs an action named isEmpty on a select().limit(1) query and returns whether executeTake(1) is empty.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Core of checkpoint/localCheckpoint: runs the physical plan inside withAction, copies rows into an RDD, checkpoints or locally checkpoints (optionally persisting first, eagerly if requested), and returns a new Dataset over a LogicalRDD built from this Dataset.

nodes.name: withWatermark
nodes.summary: Defines an event-time watermark by wrapping the plan in EventTimeWatermark with a parsed delay threshold (must not be negative).

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Join transformations: join(right) builds an inner Join node; the using-columns overload first analyzes the Join so the analyzer disambiguates self joins, then rebuilds it as a UsingJoin. The Column condition overload at lines 699-703 delegates to resolveSelfJoinCondition.

nodes.name: crossJoin
nodes.summary: Wraps this plan and the right plan in a Join node with the Cross join type and no condition.

nodes.name: joinWith
nodes.summary: Typed join returning Dataset[(T, U)]: analyzes a Join first (resolving the condition and self joins), builds a tuple ProductEncoder from both encoders and uses JoinWith.typedJoinWith to produce the plan.

nodes.name: lateralJoin
nodes.summary: Lateral join support: the private overload wraps this plan and the right plan (as LateralSubquery) in a LateralJoin node, and the public overloads pick Inner or a parsed LateralJoinType, with or without a join expression.

nodes.name: resolveSelfJoinCondition
nodes.summary: Helper that applies the SPARK-6231 self-join hack: analyzes the Join so the analyzer clones one side, and when both sides share attributes, resolves trivially true conditions to the two sides through JoinWith.resolveSelfJoinCondition (also handling a Project added over the Join).

nodes.name: col
nodes.summary: Resolves a column by name: '*' becomes a ResolvedStar over the analyzed output, regex-quoted names go to colRegex when configured, otherwise the resolved attribute is tagged with the dataset id.

nodes.name: colRegex
nodes.summary: Selects columns by regex: an escaped identifier becomes an UnresolvedRegex (optionally qualified), any other name falls back to resolve plus the dataset-id tag.

nodes.name: select
nodes.summary: Untyped select(cols*) builds a Project over logicalPlan (rejecting TypedColumns that still need an input type) and returns a DataFrame via withPlan; the typed select[U1](TypedColumn) overload applies withInputType and flattens struct results into a new Dataset with the resulting encoder.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: filter(Column) builds a Filter node over logicalPlan with the condition expression and keeps the same Encoder via withSameTypedPlan. Function-based overloads at lines 1464-1471 use TypedFilter.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Replaces top-level integer literals with UnresolvedOrdinal when groupByOrdinal is enabled and returns a RelationalGroupedDataset over toDF() with the GroupByType.

nodes.name: groupByKey
nodes.summary: Typed grouping: wraps the plan in AppendColumns with the key function, executes that plan to get a QueryExecution, and returns a classic KeyValueGroupedDataset over it with the new key columns.

nodes.name: unpivot
nodes.summary: Wide-to-long reshape: builds an Unpivot logical node over the plan from id columns, optional value columns and the variable and value column names (two overloads).

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Adds a CollectMetrics node (named metrics over the plan, keyed by this Dataset's id); the Observation overload first registers the Observation with sparkSession.observationManager.

nodes.name: limit
nodes.summary: Wraps the plan in a Limit with a literal row count, keeping the same Encoder.

nodes.name: combineUnions
nodes.summary: Flattens nested adjacent Union nodes (including distinct-like Distinct/Deduplicate over Union) with transformDownWithPruning; the comment notes this breaks caching but suits unioning many files.

nodes.name: flattenUnion
nodes.summary: Merges children of directly nested Union (or Distinct/Deduplicate-wrapped Union) nodes into the parent Union when byName and allowMissingCol match, copying tags onto the new Union.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Unions this and another Dataset by position: builds a Union node, flattens with combineUnions and wraps through withSetOperator.

nodes.name: unionByName
nodes.summary: Unions by column name: first resolves the by-name Union with executePlan(...).analyzed (needed to combine adjacent resolved Unions), then applies combineUnions inside withSetOperator.

nodes.name: withColumns
nodes.summary: Adds or replaces columns with a Project containing UnresolvedStarWithColumns; requires the name and column counts to match.

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: drop(names) keeps the columns whose names do not match using the analyzer resolver (returning toDF() if nothing is dropped, else select); drop(Column, ...) builds a DataFrameDropColumns node.

nodes.name: dropDuplicates
nodes.summary: Deduplicates on the given column names: resolves them to attributes of the analyzed output and wraps the plan in a Deduplicate node.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Typed map: wraps the plan in a MapElements node for the user function and creates a Dataset[U] using the implicit Encoder (a MapFunction overload exists at 1479-1482).

nodes.name: mapPartitions
nodes.summary: Typed per-partition transformation: builds a MapPartitions node over the plan and returns a new Dataset[U] using the implicit Encoder.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Action returning an Array[T]: runs withAction('collect', queryExecution) with collectFromPlan.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Action that runs groupBy().count() inside withAction and reads the single long result from executeCollect().

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Repartitions into numPartitions with a shuffle by wrapping the plan in Repartition(shuffle = true).

nodes.name: repartitionByExpression
nodes.summary: Repartitions by expressions via RepartitionByExpression; rejects SortOrder expressions with an error pointing to repartitionByRange.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Reduces partitions without a shuffle by wrapping the plan in Repartition(shuffle = false).

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Caches this Dataset through sparkSession.sharedState.cacheManager.cacheQuery with the given StorageLevel (cache() and persist() default to the configured defaultCacheStorageLevel).

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Removes this Dataset from the cache via cacheManager.uncacheQuery (cascade = false, optional blocking).

nodes.name: rdd
nodes.summary: Lazy RDD view of the Dataset: runs materializedRdd (the deserialized plan executed via rddQueryExecution.toRdd) inside withNewRDDExecutionId('rdd').

nodes.name: createTempView
nodes.summary: Registers the Dataset as a local or global temporary view: parses the multipart name, rejects multi-part names unless allowed, and runs a CreateViewCommand built from the logical plan via withPlan.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Returns a classic DataFrameWriter for this Dataset, failing analysis with CALL_ON_STREAMING_DATASET_UNSUPPORTED if the Dataset is streaming.

nodes.name: sameSemantics
nodes.summary: Developer API that compares the analyzed plans of two Datasets with sameResult.

nodes.name: withNewRDDExecutionId
nodes.summary: Wraps an RDD-based action in SQLExecution.withNewExecutionId on rddQueryExecution and resets the executed plan's metrics before running the body.

nodes.name: withAction
nodes.summary: Central wrapper for plan-based actions: runs the body inside SQLExecution.withNewExecutionId, qe.withQueryExecutionId and QueryExecution.withInternalError after resetting executedPlan metrics, passing the executed SparkPlan to the action.

nodes.name: collectFromPlan
nodes.summary: Collects a SparkPlan with executeCollect() and maps each row to T using the deserializer of resolvedEnc.

nodes.name: sortInternal
nodes.summary: Shared sorting logic: converts column expressions to SortOrder (replacing integer literals with UnresolvedOrdinal when orderByOrdinal is enabled) and wraps the plan in a Sort node, global or per partition.

nodes.name: withPlan
nodes.summary: Wraps a new LogicalPlan as a DataFrame by calling Dataset.ofRows; the standard helper for untyped transformations.

nodes.name: withTypedPlan
nodes.summary: Wraps a new LogicalPlan as a Dataset[U] with an implicit Encoder by calling Dataset.apply.

nodes.name: withSameTypedPlan
nodes.summary: Wraps a new LogicalPlan as a Dataset[T] reusing this Dataset's encoderGenerator, for transformations that keep the element type.

nodes.name: withSetOperator
nodes.summary: Wraps a set-operation plan: for untyped Datasets it uses ofRows (since set operators can widen types and the Row encoder cannot be reused), otherwise Dataset.apply with the encoder.

nodes.name: KeyValueGroupedDataset.scala
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of KeyValueGroupedDataset[K, V], the result of Dataset.groupByKey. It keeps the grouping QueryExecution plus data and grouping attributes and builds object-style logical operators (MapGroups, FlatMapGroupsWithState, TransformWithState, CoGroup, Aggregate) over its analyzed plan.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala; most methods build a logical operator and wrap it with Dataset[U](sparkSession, plan) using implicit Encoders; the tail of the file only overrides return types to the classic Dataset.

nodes.name: KeyValueGroupedDataset
nodes.summary: A Dataset logically grouped by a user key. Created only via Dataset.groupByKey, it holds the key and value Encoders, the QueryExecution of the plan that appended the grouping columns, and the data and grouping attributes. Its logicalPlan is queryExecution.analyzed.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends sql.KeyValueGroupedDataset[K, V]; the constructor is private[sql].

nodes.name: keyAs
nodes.summary: Returns a new KeyValueGroupedDataset over the same QueryExecution and attributes but with a different key Encoder.

nodes.name: mapValues
nodes.summary: Appends a mapped value column with AppendColumns, projects the new columns plus grouping attributes, executes that plan and returns a new KeyValueGroupedDataset with the new value Encoder.

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Returns the distinct keys as a Dataset[K]: Distinct over a Project of the grouping attributes.

nodes.name: flatMapSortedGroups
nodes.summary: Builds a MapGroups node with sorted groups from the sort expressions and the user function, wrapped in Dataset[U].

nodes.name: mapGroupsWithState
nodes.summary: Stateful per-group mapping (three overloads: default, with timeout, with timeout and initial state): wraps the function to return a single-element iterator and builds a FlatMapGroupsWithState node with isMapGroupsWithState = true and Update output mode.

nodes.name: flatMapGroupsWithState
nodes.summary: Stateful per-group flat mapping (with and without initial state): validates that the output mode is Append or Update and builds a FlatMapGroupsWithState node with isMapGroupsWithState = false.

nodes.name: transformWithState
nodes.summary: Arbitrary stateful processing (four overloads: processor or processor with initial state, each with a TimeMode or an event-time column name): builds a TransformWithState logical node over the grouping and data attributes, and for the event-time variants updates the event time column afterwards.

nodes.name: updateEventTimeColumnAfterTransformWithState
nodes.summary: Creates a Dataset from the TransformWithState plan and then wraps its plan in UpdateEventTimeWatermarkColumn for the named event-time column.

nodes.name: reduceGroups
nodes.summary: Reduces values per key by building a ReduceAggregator from the function and the value Encoder and running it through agg.

nodes.name: aggUntyped
nodes.summary: Typed aggregation core: applies withInputType to each TypedColumn, builds the key column with aggKeyColumn, creates an Aggregate grouped by the grouping attributes and returns a Dataset with a tuple encoder of key plus result encoders.

nodes.name: cogroupSorted
nodes.summary: Co-groups this and another KeyValueGroupedDataset by key with optional sort expressions on each side by building a CoGroup node over both logical plans, wrapped in Dataset[R].

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Builds a string such as 'KeyValueGroupedDataset: [key: [...], value: [...]]' from the key and value encoder schemas, showing at most two fields each.

nodes.name: ObservationManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ObservationManager, the per-session registry of Observation objects waiting for a query to finish. It maps (name, dataFrameId) to an Observation and completes it with the metrics collected by CollectMetrics nodes of a finished QueryExecution.

nodes.name: ObservationManager
nodes.summary: Keeps a ConcurrentHashMap keyed by (observation name, dataframe id). register adds Observations (rejecting streaming Datasets), getOrNewObservation creates one on demand, and tryComplete fills and notifies observations from a finished QueryExecution's observed metrics.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Two overloads: register(observation, ds) throws IllegalArgumentException for streaming Datasets and otherwise delegates with ds.id; register(observation, dataFrameId) marks the Observation registered and stores it with putIfAbsent under (name, id).

nodes.name: getOrNewObservation
nodes.summary: Returns the Observation for (name, dataFrameId), creating and marking registered a new Observation with computeIfAbsent when none exists.

nodes.name: tryComplete
nodes.summary: Walks qe.logical (including subqueries, pruned by the COLLECT_METRICS tree pattern) for CollectMetrics nodes, removes the matching registered Observation and calls setMetricsAndNotify with the metrics from qe.observedMetrics (or an empty Row if none were collected), evaluated lazily inside a Try.

nodes.name: SQLImplicits.scala
nodes.summary: Classic SQLImplicits (implicit conversions from local Seq and RDD to DatasetHolder, used by 'import spark.implicits._') and the classic DatasetHolder that exposes toDS and toDF.

nodes.name: SQLImplicits
nodes.summary: Abstract class extending sql.SQLImplicits that implements localSeqToDatasetHolder and rddToDatasetHolder by calling session.createDataset and wrapping the result in a DatasetHolder.

nodes.name: DatasetHolder
nodes.summary: Classic DatasetHolder[U] over a Dataset[U]: toDS returns it, and toDF() or toDF(colNames) delegate to the Dataset.

nodes.name: localSeqToDatasetHolder
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion from a local Seq[T] (with an Encoder) to a DatasetHolder built from session.createDataset(s).

nodes.name: rddToDatasetHolder
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion from an RDD[T] (with an Encoder) to a DatasetHolder built from session.createDataset(rdd).

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: toDF() returns ds.toDF() and toDF(colNames*) returns ds.toDF(colNames: _*), converting the wrapped Dataset to a DataFrame (with optional column names).

nodes.name: Catalog.scala
nodes.summary: Classic (non-Connect) implementation of the user-facing Catalog API. It answers every metadata and cache request by building a logical plan (ShowTables, UnresolvedTableOrView, CreateTable, DropTable, ...), running it through sparkSession.sessionState.executePlan, and wrapping the result rows as a Dataset of Table/Column/Database/Function objects.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a private[sql] companion object; many public methods are overloads that share one internal helper, and the SessionCatalog (Hive-style) path is kept first for Spark 3.3 backward compatibility.

nodes.name: Catalog
nodes.summary: Implements org.apache.spark.sql.catalog.Catalog on top of a classic SparkSession. It mixes the legacy SessionCatalog (used first for backward compatibility with Spark 3.3 and prior) with the multi-catalog CatalogManager / TableCatalog API, resolving names into three-part identifiers and delegating DDL, listing and cache operations to analyzed commands and the shared CacheManager. The companion object (line 1107) adds makeDataset to turn lists of Table/Column/etc. into local Datasets.

nodes.name: parseIdent
nodes.summary: Parses a name into multipart identifier parts with the session SQL parser; optionally falls back to the original name when parsing fails with a ParseException.

nodes.name: qualifyV1Ident
nodes.summary: Turns a 1 or 2 part name into a full identifier by prepending the session catalog name (CatalogManager.SESSION_CATALOG_NAME) and, for a single part, the current database from the session catalog.

nodes.name: currentDatabase
nodes.summary: Returns the current namespace of the CatalogManager as a quoted string.

nodes.name: setCurrentDatabase
nodes.summary: Sets the current namespace on the CatalogManager from the parsed name; the name is not assumed to carry a catalog prefix.

nodes.name: listDatabases
nodes.summary: Public overloads that list databases, with or without a name pattern; both delegate to listDatabasesInternal.

nodes.name: listDatabasesInternal
nodes.summary: Runs a ShowNamespacesCommand plan, finds the resolved catalog, builds a Database object per returned row with makeDatabase and returns them as a Dataset via Catalog.makeDataset.

nodes.name: listTables
nodes.summary: Public overloads that list tables and views in the current or a given database, optionally filtered by a pattern (the name can be qualified with a catalog); temporary views are included.

nodes.name: listTablesInternal
nodes.summary: Resolves the namespace and builds a ShowTables plan, then hands it to makeTablesDataset.

nodes.name: makeTablesDataset
nodes.summary: Executes a ShowTables plan, determines the owning catalog from the analyzed plan (or the v2 session catalog for the V1 command) and maps each row to a Table through resolveTable.

nodes.name: resolveTable
nodes.summary: Builds a Table for one SHOW TABLES row. Temp views get no catalog prefix; if resolution fails with a non-fatal error for a persistent table it logs a warning and returns a partial Table, and a missing table returns None.

nodes.name: makeTable
nodes.summary: Analyzes an UnresolvedTableOrView plan and converts the ResolvedTable, ResolvedPersistentView or ResolvedTempView result into a catalog.Table (EXTERNAL or MANAGED, VIEW, or TEMPORARY); throws tableOrViewNotFound otherwise.

nodes.name: listFunctions
nodes.summary: Public overloads listing functions in the current or a given database, optionally matching a pattern; built-in and temporary functions are included.

nodes.name: listFunctionsInternal
nodes.summary: Lists built-in functions with a system-scope ShowFunctions plan (names are looked up as single parts) and then user functions in the resolved namespace, building a Function for each via makeFunction.

nodes.name: toFunctionIdent
nodes.summary: Parses a function name; for backward compatibility with Spark 3.3 it checks the session catalog for a persistent non-temporary function first and then qualifies the name with the session catalog.

nodes.name: makeFunction
nodes.summary: Analyzes an UnresolvedFunctionName plan and converts a persistent or non-persistent resolved function into a catalog.Function, reading the class name from V1Function info; otherwise throws unresolvedRoutineError with the SQL resolution search path.

nodes.name: listColumns
nodes.summary: Overloads that list columns of a table, view or temp view. The name-only overload first checks the session catalog for compatibility, then a private overload resolves the table via UnresolvedTableOrView and derives partition, bucket and clustering columns from the V2 table partitioning.

nodes.name: schemaToColumns
nodes.summary: Maps each StructField to a catalog.Column with comment, simple type string, nullability and partition/bucket/cluster flags supplied by predicate functions.

nodes.name: getDatabase
nodes.summary: Returns the Database for a name by delegating to makeDatabase with no explicit catalog.

nodes.name: makeDatabase
nodes.summary: Resolves a namespace with UnresolvedNamespace (fetchMetadata = true) and builds a Database from the ResolvedNamespace comment and location properties; falls back to a bare Database otherwise.

nodes.name: resolveNamespace
nodes.summary: Treats the name as a single database in the session catalog when it exists there (prefixing the session catalog name), otherwise parses it as a qualified catalog/namespace.

nodes.name: toTableIdent
nodes.summary: Parses a table name and, if it is not a temp view and the session catalog (Hive Metastore) has the table, qualifies it with the session catalog; otherwise keeps the parsed parts.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Overloads returning a Table or view; global temp views are looked up directly while other db-qualified names always go to the session catalog.

nodes.name: getFunction
nodes.summary: Overloads returning a Function; the db-qualified form always looks in the session catalog.

nodes.name: databaseExists
nodes.summary: Returns true if getDatabase succeeds and false when NoSuchNamespaceException is thrown.

nodes.name: tableExists
nodes.summary: Public overloads checking whether a table, view or temp view exists. They delegate to a private variant (line 246) that analyzes an UnresolvedTableOrView plan and treats TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND as false.

nodes.name: functionExists
nodes.summary: Public overloads checking whether a function exists. A private variant (line 366) analyzes an UnresolvedFunctionName plan and treats UNRESOLVED_ROUTINE as false.

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: Family of createTable overloads. All funnel into the five-argument version, which builds an UnresolvedTableSpec and a CreateTable plan (MANAGED, or EXTERNAL when a path/location is given), runs it with executePlan(...).toRdd and returns sparkSession.table(tableName). The path-only overload uses spark.sql.sources.default.

nodes.name: dropTempView
nodes.summary: If the local temp view exists, uncaches it with uncacheView and then drops it from the session catalog; returns whether it existed.

nodes.name: dropGlobalTempView
nodes.summary: Same as dropTempView for global temporary views.

nodes.name: uncacheView
nodes.summary: Uncaches a view definition through the CacheManager, cascading when the view has view text (SPARK-33142); non-fatal errors are ignored.

nodes.name: recoverPartitions
nodes.summary: Executes a RecoverPartitions plan over an UnresolvedTable so the catalog picks up partitions found in the table directory; only works for partitioned tables, not temp views.

nodes.name: isCached
nodes.summary: Returns true when CacheManager.lookupCachedData finds cached data for the named table or view (a protected overload at line 887 does the same for a Dataset).

nodes.name: cacheTable
nodes.summary: Overloads that cache a table or view through CacheManager.cacheQuery; the no-level overload uses the configured default cache storage level.

nodes.name: uncacheTable
nodes.summary: Uncaches a table or view: a local or global temp view goes through uncacheView, anything else is resolved and removed with CommandUtils.uncacheTableOrView (cascade = true).

nodes.name: clearCache
nodes.summary: Removes all cached tables and views by calling CacheManager.clearCache on the shared state.

nodes.name: refreshTable
nodes.summary: Fully refreshes a table or view: refreshes the analyzed relation, invalidates the matching relation cache entry (session catalog or V2 catalog) and re-caches the plan with CommandUtils.recacheTableOrView so dependents are cleared.

nodes.name: resolveRelation
nodes.summary: Returns the analyzed logical plan of sparkSession.table(tableName).

nodes.name: refreshByPath
nodes.summary: Refreshes cache entries and metadata for datasets containing the given data source path via CacheManager.recacheByPath (prefix matching).

nodes.name: currentCatalog
nodes.summary: Returns the name of the CatalogManager's current catalog.

nodes.name: setCurrentCatalog
nodes.summary: Sets the current catalog on the CatalogManager.

nodes.name: listCatalogs
nodes.summary: Overloads listing catalogs known to the CatalogManager (optionally filtered by pattern) as CatalogMetadata objects via makeCatalog.

nodes.name: dropTable
nodes.summary: Runs a DropTable plan for the parsed identifier (temp views allowed) with the given ifExists and purge flags.

nodes.name: dropView
nodes.summary: Runs a DropView plan for the parsed identifier with the ifExists flag.

nodes.name: createDatabase
nodes.summary: Runs a CreateNamespace plan using the parsed name and the given properties map.

nodes.name: dropDatabase
nodes.summary: Runs a DropNamespace plan with ifExists and cascade flags.

nodes.name: listPartitions
nodes.summary: Runs ShowPartitions for the table and returns the first column of each row as a TablePartition Dataset.

nodes.name: listViews
nodes.summary: Overloads listing views in the current or a given database, optionally by pattern, using listViewsInternal.

nodes.name: listViewsInternal
nodes.summary: Builds a ShowViews plan for the given namespace plan and pattern and passes it to makeViewsDataset.

nodes.name: makeViewsDataset
nodes.summary: Executes a ShowViews plan, finds the catalog and maps rows to Table objects via resolveTable.

nodes.name: getTableProperties
nodes.summary: Runs ShowTableProperties and collects the key/value rows into a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: getCreateTableString
nodes.summary: Runs ShowCreateTable (optionally as serde) and returns the first row as a string, or an empty string.

nodes.name: truncateTable
nodes.summary: Runs a TruncateTable plan on the resolved table identifier.

nodes.name: analyzeTable
nodes.summary: Runs an AnalyzeTable plan with an empty partition spec and the noScan flag to compute table statistics.

nodes.name: makeCatalog
nodes.summary: Creates a CatalogMetadata with a name and a null description.

nodes.name: makeDataset
nodes.summary: Companion object helper: encodes a Seq of DefinedByConstructorParams objects with an ExpressionEncoder, builds a LocalRelation, runs executePlan and returns a Dataset over it.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions.scala
