nodes.summary: Classic implementation of DataFrame statistic functions (approxQuantile, cov, corr, crosstab, freqItems, sampleBy). It forwards to the execution.stat helpers StatFunctions and FrequentItems, and implements stratified sampling directly with rand and a UDF filter.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions
nodes.summary: Final class extending the shared sql.DataFrameStatFunctions API and wrapping a classic DataFrame. Most methods run inside withOrigin and call StatFunctions or FrequentItems; the overloads taking Array/Java Map arguments only re-dispatch to the parent trait.

nodes.name: approxQuantile
nodes.summary: Selects the given columns and calls StatFunctions.multipleApproxQuantiles with the probabilities and relative error; a second private[spark] overload accepts Lists and returns java Lists for Python-friendly calls.

nodes.name: cov
nodes.summary: Computes the sample covariance of two columns with StatFunctions.calculateCov.

nodes.name: corr
nodes.summary: Computes the correlation of two columns with StatFunctions.pearsonCorrelation; requires method to be pearson, since only the Pearson coefficient is supported.

nodes.name: crosstab
nodes.summary: Builds a contingency table of two columns through StatFunctions.crossTabulate.

nodes.name: freqItems
nodes.summary: The Seq-based freqItems finds frequent items in a single pass via FrequentItems.singlePassFreqItems; the other overloads re-dispatch to the parent trait.

nodes.name: sampleBy
nodes.summary: Stratified sampling overloads. The Column/Scala-Map version validates that fractions are in [0, 1], draws rand(seed) and filters with a UDF that compares the random value to the fraction of each stratum; the others delegate to the parent trait.

nodes.name: DataStreamWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Classic builder for starting a streaming write. It collects the sink format, output mode, trigger, options, partitioning/clustering columns and foreach/foreachBatch writers, then start/toTable create a sink and launch a StreamingQuery through sessionState.streamingQueryManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala final class (with companion object holding source-name constants) using this.type return types for fluent builder chaining.

nodes.name: DataStreamWriter
nodes.summary: Implements streaming.DataStreamWriter over a classic Dataset. The builder methods only store state in private vars (default format is spark.sql.sources.default, output mode Append, trigger ProcessingTime(0)). start/toTable then pick a sink: MemorySink, ForeachWriterTable, ForeachBatchSink, a DSv2 SupportsWrite table, or a V1 sink from DataSource.createSink. The companion object (line 460) defines the source-name constants and which sources allow one-time queries with a temporary checkpoint location.

nodes.name: outputMode
nodes.summary: Sets the output mode, either from an OutputMode value or by parsing a string with InternalOutputModes; returns this for chaining.

nodes.name: trigger
nodes.summary: Stores the Trigger that controls how often the streaming query runs (default is Trigger.ProcessingTime(0)).

nodes.name: queryName
nodes.summary: Records the query name as the queryName option; it is later read back in startQuery and is required by the memory sink.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Validates the sink name with validateSinkName and stores it in sinkName for the later startQuery call.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Sets the output source / data source name used to choose the sink.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Stores the partitioning columns and checks that they are not combined with clusterBy.

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Stores the clustering columns and checks that they are not combined with partitionBy.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one key/value entry to the case-insensitive extraOptions map; the typed Boolean/Long/Double overloads are covariant forwards (line 421).

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds all entries of a Scala or Java map to extraOptions.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the streaming query. The path overload rejects a path option set together with a path argument (unless the legacy path option behavior is on); both overloads call startInternal.

nodes.name: toTable
nodes.summary: Starts the query writing into a catalog table. It parses the name, rejects temp views, creates the table with a CreateTable plan (with partitioning or ClusterByTransform) when it does not exist, loads it and starts a DSv2 streaming write, or falls back to a V1 write after checking the provider matches the source and the table is not a view.

nodes.name: startInternal
nodes.summary: Core of start(): rejects the Hive source, then picks a sink by source name: memory (needs a queryName, registers a temp view of the memory sink), foreach, foreachBatch (not allowed with a continuous trigger), or a looked-up data source that is used as a DSv2 TableProvider with STREAMING_WRITE support or else as a V1 sink. It always ends with startQuery.

nodes.name: startQuery
nodes.summary: Builds and starts the StreamingQuery by calling sessionState.streamingQueryManager.startQuery with query name, sink name, checkpoint location, output mode, trigger and optional catalog identifiers. For a RealTimeTrigger it first checks the sink against RealTimeModeAllowlist, and sources in SOURCES_ALLOW_ONE_TIME_QUERY may use a temporary checkpoint location.

nodes.name: createV1Sink
nodes.summary: Creates a V1 Sink by building a DataSource with the source name, options (clustering columns re-encoded from the normalized columns) and normalized partition columns, then calling createSink(outputMode).

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Registers a ForeachWriter by calling foreachImplementation.

nodes.name: foreachImplementation
nodes.summary: Sets the source to foreach, stores the cleaned writer (throws IllegalArgumentException when it is null) and optionally replaces the encoder.

nodes.name: foreachBatch
nodes.summary: Sets the source to foreachBatch and stores the user function (a null function throws IllegalArgumentException); a Java VoidFunction2 overload is forwarded to the parent at line 431.

nodes.name: normalizedParCols
nodes.summary: Returns the partition columns normalized to the real names in the dataset output.

nodes.name: normalizedClusteringCols
nodes.summary: Returns the clustering columns normalized to the real names in the dataset output.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Finds the dataset output column that matches the given name using the analyzer resolver (so case-insensitivity is handled once) or throws columnNotFoundInExistingColumnsError.

nodes.name: assertNotPartitioned
nodes.summary: Throws operationNotSupportPartitioningError if partitionBy was used with a sink that does not support it.

nodes.name: validatePartitioningAndClustering
nodes.summary: Throws clusterByWithPartitionedBy if both clusterBy and partitionBy were set.

nodes.name: SparkSession.scala
nodes.summary: Classic (non-Connect) SparkSession: the entry point of the Dataset and DataFrame API in the JVM. The class holds the SparkContext, lazily creates SharedState and SessionState, and builds DataFrames; its companion object holds the Builder, getOrCreate logic and the active/default session registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a private constructor plus a companion object; lazy vals defer creation of sharedState and sessionState until first use.

nodes.name: SparkSession
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of the abstract sql.SparkSession API. It wraps a SparkContext, an optional existing SharedState and an optional parent SessionState, and exposes sql, table, range, createDataFrame, read/readStream, udf, streams, newSession and more. The same id also covers the companion object (lines 931-1301), which holds the Builder, active/default session helpers and session-state instantiation.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one id. The class range starts at the class declaration and the range here ends at the end of the companion object.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Builder for SparkSession (SparkSession.builder()). It collects options and extensions, then build() reuses the thread active session or the global default session if one exists, otherwise creates a SparkContext via SparkContext.getOrCreate and a new SparkSession.

nodes.name: implicits
nodes.summary: Object exposing the implicit conversions of SQLImplicits (such as toDF and encoder implicits) bound to this session, supplied by overriding the protected session member with self.

nodes.name: sharedState
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the SharedState: returns the existingSharedState if one was passed in (for example by newSession) and otherwise creates a new SharedState from the SparkContext and initial session options.

nodes.name: sqlConf
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the session SQLConf. With a parent session state it clones the parent conf (optionally merging the SparkConf); otherwise it builds a new SQLConf merged from the shared state conf, SparkContext non-static SQL configs and initial session options. It is initialized before sessionState so SQLConf.get cannot recurse during state creation.

nodes.name: sessionState
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the SessionState: when a parent state exists it is cloned for this session, otherwise instantiateSessionState reflectively builds a SessionState (or Hive variant, chosen by sessionStateClassName) from the shared state conf. This is why a new session pays the state construction cost only on first use.

nodes.name: sqlContext
nodes.summary: Val holding the SQLContext wrapper, created as new SQLContext(this) for backward compatibility with the Spark 1.x entry point.

nodes.name: udf
nodes.summary: Returns the UDFRegistration from sessionState.udfRegistration, used for registering user-defined functions in this session.

nodes.name: streams
nodes.summary: Returns the StreamingQueryManager from sessionState.streamingQueryManager, used to manage active streaming queries of this session.

nodes.name: catalog
nodes.summary: Lazy val creating the classic Catalog (new Catalog(self)) for working with databases, tables and functions.

nodes.name: newSession
nodes.summary: Creates a new SparkSession that shares the SparkContext and the shared state of this session but has no parent session state, so its SQL configuration, temporary views and UDFs start independent.

nodes.name: cloneSession
nodes.summary: Creates a copy of the session sharing the SparkContext and shared state while copying the session state, the artifact manager and the managed job tags. Forces sessionState, artifactManager and managedJobTags to initialize so the copy happens eagerly.

nodes.name: emptyDataFrame
nodes.summary: Lazy val for an empty DataFrame built with Dataset.ofRows over an empty LocalRelation.

nodes.name: emptyDataset
nodes.summary: Creates an empty Dataset[T] with a LocalRelation whose schema comes from the implicit Encoder of T.

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Group of createDataFrame overloads that build DataFrames from RDD[Product], Seq[Product], RDD[Row] plus a schema, java Lists and Java bean classes. They wrap data as ExternalRDD, LocalRelation or LogicalRDD plans and call Dataset.ofRows, running inside withActive.

nodes.name: baseRelationToDataFrame
nodes.summary: Wraps a data source BaseRelation into a DataFrame via Dataset.ofRows over a LogicalRelation.

nodes.name: createDataset
nodes.summary: Group of createDataset overloads. For a Seq it serializes each element with the Encoder into a LocalRelation; for an RDD it uses ExternalRDD; for a java List it delegates to the Seq overload.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Group of range overloads that produce a Dataset[java.lang.Long]. The short forms fill defaults (start 0, step 1, numPartitions from leafNodeDefaultParallelism) and the full form builds a logical Range plan with Encoders.LONG.

nodes.name: internalCreateDataFrame
nodes.summary: Internal helper that wraps an RDD[InternalRow] and a schema in a LogicalRDD plan and returns a DataFrame through Dataset.ofRows. Used by createDataFrame and by the PySpark helper applySchemaToPythonRDD.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame for a table or view: the public overload delegates to read.table(tableName), and the internal overload builds Dataset.ofRows over an UnresolvedRelation for a TableIdentifier.

nodes.name: resolveAndValidateParameters
nodes.summary: Resolves and validates SQL parameter expressions: wraps them in a fake Project over OneRowRelation, runs the analyzer, checks them with ParameterizedQueryArgumentsValidator, runs the optimizer to constant-fold, and returns a map of names to Literals (INVALID_SQL_ARG if one is not folded).

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Group of sql overloads (positional args, named args, unified args with names, and plain sql(sqlText)). Each runs inside withActive, converts args to literal expressions with lit, resolves them through resolveAndValidateParameters, parses with sessionState.sqlParser.parsePlanWithParameters inside a QueryPlanningTracker PARSING phase, optionally wraps the plan in a ParameterizedQuery in legacy mode, and returns Dataset.ofRows(self, plan, tracker). Commands run eagerly in Dataset.ofRows while SELECT queries stay lazy.

nodes.name: executeCommand
nodes.summary: Runs a command through a named external runner by wrapping an ExternalCommandExecutor plan in Dataset.ofRows.

nodes.name: addArtifact
nodes.summary: Group of addArtifact overloads (path string, URI, bytes with a target path, source and target) that build Artifact objects and register them with artifactManager.addLocalArtifacts. The addArtifacts varargs form is defined right below at lines 752-754.

nodes.name: addTag
nodes.summary: Adds a managed job tag after validation by SparkContext.throwIfInvalidTag, storing a real tag that includes the session UUID and thread UUID so tags of different threads and sessions do not clash.

nodes.name: interruptTag
nodes.summary: Interrupts running operations carrying the given managed tag by mapping it to the real tag and calling doInterruptTag.

nodes.name: doInterruptTag
nodes.summary: Cancels jobs with a tag through SparkContext.cancelJobsWithTagWithFuture, waits up to 60 seconds, and returns the SQL execution root ids from the cancelled jobs.

nodes.name: interruptOperation
nodes.summary: Interrupts a SQL operation given its execution id string (must parse as a Long) using the execution id job tag; throws IllegalArgumentException for a non-numeric id.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Returns a new DataFrameReader bound to this session for loading data sources.

nodes.name: readStream
nodes.summary: Returns a new DataStreamReader bound to this session for streaming sources.

nodes.name: tvf
nodes.summary: Returns a new TableValuedFunction helper bound to this session.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Stops the underlying SparkContext (the AutoCloseable close implementation).

nodes.name: applySchemaToPythonRDD
nodes.summary: Applies a schema (given as JSON string or StructType) to an RDD of Array[Any] produced by Python, converting each value with EvaluatePython.makeFromJava and creating a DataFrame through internalCreateDataFrame. Marked in the source as used by PySpark only.

nodes.name: getSchema
nodes.summary: Infers a Catalyst schema for a java bean class with JavaTypeInference.inferDataType and converts the struct fields to AttributeReferences.

nodes.name: leafNodeDefaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns the default parallelism for leaf nodes from the LEAF_NODE_DEFAULT_PARALLELISM SQL conf or the SparkContext default parallelism.

nodes.name: converter
nodes.summary: Serializable ColumnNodeToExpressionConverter for this session that parses SQL with sessionState.sqlParser and reads configuration from sessionState.conf. It backs the expression and toRichColumn methods inherited from ColumnConversions.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Creates a new SparkSession.Builder.

nodes.name: getActiveSession
nodes.summary: Returns the thread-local active session by delegating to the SparkSessionCompanion implementation.

nodes.name: getDefaultSession
nodes.summary: Returns the global default session by delegating to the SparkSessionCompanion implementation.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Returns the active session, falling back to the default session, via the SparkSessionCompanion implementation.

nodes.name: tryCastToImplementation
nodes.summary: Casts a generic sql.SparkSession to the classic implementation, returning None when called inside a running Spark task.

nodes.name: applyModifiableSettings
nodes.summary: Applies builder options to an already existing session: only options that differ from the current conf are considered, runtime SQL configs are set with setConfString, and a warning is logged when static or non-modifiable settings are ignored.

nodes.name: getOrCloneSessionWithConfigsOff
nodes.summary: Returns the original session when all listed boolean configs are already off, otherwise clones the session and disables those configs in the clone.

nodes.name: registerContextListener
nodes.summary: Registers a SparkListener once per context that clears the default and active sessions when the application ends.

nodes.name: sessionStateClassName
nodes.summary: Chooses the session state builder class name from the catalog implementation conf: the Hive builder for "hive" and SessionStateBuilder for "in-memory".

nodes.name: assertOnDriver
nodes.summary: Throws an internal error if a TaskContext exists, enforcing that SparkSession is only created and accessed on the driver.

nodes.name: instantiateSessionState
nodes.summary: Reflectively builds the SessionState: loads the builder class by name, calls its constructor with the session and None, casts to BaseSessionStateBuilder and calls build(); any failure is rethrown as IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: hiveClassesArePresent
nodes.summary: Checks whether the Hive session state builder and HiveConf classes can be loaded.

nodes.name: cleanupAnyExistingSession
nodes.summary: Stops and clears any leftover active or default session, logging a warning with its creation site (used to tidy up leaked sessions).

nodes.name: applyAndLoadExtensions
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkSessionExtensions, applies the classes named in StaticSQLConf and optionally loads providers from the classpath depending on LOAD_SESSION_EXTENSIONS_FROM_CLASSPATH.

nodes.name: applyExtensions
nodes.summary: Instantiates each extension class listed in the SPARK_SESSION_EXTENSIONS conf and applies it to the extensions object, logging a warning when a class is missing or of the wrong type.

nodes.name: loadExtensions
nodes.summary: Loads SparkSessionExtensionsProvider implementations through ServiceLoader and applies each to the extensions, logging failures instead of aborting.

nodes.name: sparkContext
nodes.summary: Sets a user supplied SparkContext to reuse instead of creating one in build.

nodes.name: handleBuilderConfig
nodes.summary: Intercepts builder options: warns that the connect remote and api mode keys are not supported in Classic mode, and when the catalog implementation is hive requires Hive classes (and disables artifact session isolation) or throws.

nodes.name: withExtensions
nodes.summary: Lets the caller register SparkSessionExtensions on the builder.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Core of getOrCreate and create. Unless forceCreate, it returns the thread active session or the global default (applying modifiable settings); otherwise it gets or creates a SparkContext from the options, applies extensions, constructs the SparkSession, sets it as default and active, and registers a context listener.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Returns an existing session or creates one: build(forceCreate = false).

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Always creates a new session: build(forceCreate = true).

nodes.name: StreamingQueryManager.scala
nodes.summary: Classic StreamingQueryManager that tracks all active StreamingQuery instances of a SparkSession. It creates and starts MicroBatchExecution, AsyncProgressTrackingMicroBatchExecution or ContinuousExecution queries, enforces name and id uniqueness across sessions, and lets callers await termination.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryManager
nodes.summary: Manages the streaming queries of one SparkSession. Its constructor registers listeners from STREAMING_QUERY_LISTENERS and the shared status listener, keeps an activeQueries map guarded by a lock shared across sessions through SharedState, and tracks the last terminated query exception for awaitAnyTermination.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Returns the currently active queries as an array while holding the shared lock.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up an active query by UUID (returns null if absent) or by a string id parsed to a UUID.

nodes.name: awaitAnyTermination
nodes.summary: Blocks (polling the termination lock every 10 ms) until any query terminates, rethrowing the failure of the last failed query; the timed overload returns whether a termination was seen before the timeout.

nodes.name: resetTerminated
nodes.summary: Clears the remembered last-terminated-query state so awaitAnyTermination waits for new terminations.

nodes.name: addListener
nodes.summary: Registers a StreamingQueryListener on the StreamingQueryListenerBus.

nodes.name: postListenerEvent
nodes.summary: Posts a StreamingQueryListener event to the listener bus.

nodes.name: useAsyncProgressTracking
nodes.summary: Reads the ASYNC_PROGRESS_TRACKING_ENABLED option (default false) from the extra options to decide on async progress tracking.

nodes.name: createQuery
nodes.summary: Builds a StreamingQueryWrapper: asserts the DataFrame is analyzed, checks the real-time trigger minimum batch duration, creates a WriteToStreamStatement, analyzes it to a WriteToStream, then picks ContinuousExecution, AsyncProgressTrackingMicroBatchExecution (rejecting real-time triggers and sink evolution) or MicroBatchExecution.

nodes.name: startQuery
nodes.summary: Creates the query, then under the shared lock rejects a duplicate active name and handles a duplicate active id (stopping the old run when STREAMING_STOP_ACTIVE_RUN_ON_RESTART is true, otherwise throwing), registers it in activeQueries and shared state, and finally calls streamingQuery.start() outside any lock.

nodes.name: notifyQueryTermination
nodes.summary: Called when a query terminates: unregisters it, records its exception for awaiters, notifies waiting threads and deactivates its state store coordinator instances.

nodes.name: unregisterTerminatedStream
nodes.summary: Removes a terminated query from shared-state activeStreamingQueries and the local activeQueries map under the shared lock.

nodes.name: TableValuedFunction.scala
nodes.summary: Classic TableValuedFunction exposed by SparkSession.tvf. Each builtin table-valued function (explode, inline, stack, json_tuple, ...) becomes a DataFrame over an UnresolvedTableValuedFunction plan, while range delegates to SparkSession.range.

nodes.name: TableValuedFunction
nodes.summary: Implements sql.TableValuedFunction for a SparkSession: range overloads call sparkSession.range and every other method calls the private fn helper with the function name and its Column arguments.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Four range overloads (end; start and end; with step; with numPartitions) that each forward to the matching SparkSession.range.

nodes.name: fn
nodes.summary: Private helper that converts the Column arguments to expressions with sparkSession.expression and wraps UnresolvedTableValuedFunction(name, args) in Dataset.ofRows.

nodes.name: explode
nodes.summary: Calls fn("explode", Seq(collection)); explode_outer, posexplode and posexplode_outer follow the same pattern.

nodes.name: json_tuple
nodes.summary: Calls fn("json_tuple", input +: fields).

nodes.name: stack
nodes.summary: Calls fn("stack", n +: fields).

nodes.name: UDFRegistration.scala
nodes.summary: Classic UDFRegistration reached through SparkSession.udf. It registers Scala UDFs, aggregators, UDAFs, Python UDFs and Java UDF classes into a FunctionRegistry as temporary functions.

nodes.name: UDFRegistration
nodes.summary: Implements sql.UDFRegistration for a session and its FunctionRegistry. Each register path builds an expression builder (ScalaUDAF, ScalaAggregator or ScalaUDF via toScalaUDF, or a PythonUDF builder) and stores it with createOrReplaceTempFunction.

nodes.name: registerPython
nodes.summary: Logs the UserDefinedPythonFunction details at debug level and registers its builder as a temporary function with source "python_udf".

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a deprecated UserDefinedAggregateFunction as ScalaUDAF, and (in the protected overload) a UserDefinedFunction: UserDefinedAggregator becomes ScalaAggregator, a SparkUserDefinedFunction becomes ScalaUDF via toScalaUDF, optionally validating the argument count and raising wrongNumArgsError.

nodes.name: registerJavaUDAF
nodes.summary: Loads a Java UDAF class by name through the artifact manager class loader, checks it implements UserDefinedAggregateFunction, instantiates it and registers it.

nodes.name: registerJava
nodes.summary: Loads a Java UDF class, finds its single UDFn interface, infers the return type with JavaTypeInference when none is given, and dispatches on the number of type arguments (UDF0 to UDF22) to the matching register overload.

nodes.name: columnNodeSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Bridges the API-level ColumnNode tree and Catalyst expressions in both directions. ColumnNodeToExpressionConverter turns a ColumnNode into a Catalyst Expression, while ExpressionColumnNode and ColumnNodeExpression wrap an Expression inside a Column and a ColumnNode inside an Expression.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala pattern matching over the ColumnNode case classes; the trait and its companion object share one class id.

nodes.name: ColumnNodeToExpressionConverter
nodes.summary: Trait (with a default companion object) that is a function ColumnNode => Expression. apply pattern matches every ColumnNode kind (literals, attributes, stars, regexes, functions, aliases, casts, SQL strings, sort orders, windows, lambdas, CASE WHEN, user-defined functions, subqueries, wrapped expressions) and builds the matching Catalyst expression. The object parses with the active session parser and uses SQLConf.get.

nodes.name: ExpressionColumnNode
nodes.summary: ColumnNode wrapper for a Catalyst Expression so an Expression can live inside a Column. normalize strips column reference metadata used for ambiguous self join detection; its companion apply unwraps a ColumnNodeExpression instead of double wrapping.

nodes.name: ColumnNodeExpression
nodes.summary: Unevaluable placeholder Expression (nullable, NullType, no children) that carries a ColumnNode inside an expression tree; the converter later replaces it by converting the node. The companion apply unwraps an ExpressionColumnNode instead.

nodes.name: ExpressionUtils
nodes.summary: Helpers that create a Column from an Expression, an Expression from a Column, give an Expression a name (toNamed) and generate default aliases.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Converts a ColumnNode to an Expression inside SQLConf.withExistingConf and CurrentOrigin.withOrigin. One case per node kind produces the Catalyst equivalent; unsupported nodes raise an internal error.

nodes.name: convertUnresolvedNamedLambdaVariable
nodes.summary: Converts an API lambda variable to a Catalyst UnresolvedNamedLambdaVariable.

nodes.name: convertSortOrder
nodes.summary: Maps API sort direction and null ordering to Catalyst Ascending/Descending and NullsFirst/NullsLast and builds a Catalyst SortOrder.

nodes.name: convertWindowFrameBoundary
nodes.summary: Maps a window frame boundary (current row, unbounded preceding or following, or a value node) to the Catalyst expression.

nodes.name: convertUnresolvedAttribute
nodes.summary: Creates an UnresolvedAttribute and, when present, tags it with the plan id and the metadata column flag.

nodes.name: convertUnresolvedRegex
nodes.summary: Creates a quoted UnresolvedAttribute for a regex column and tags it with the plan id when given.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Rewrites AttributeReferences with DetectAmbiguousSelfJoin.stripColumnReferenceMetadata and returns a copy with no origin.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: returns the inner node when given a ColumnNodeExpression, otherwise a new ExpressionColumnNode.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: returns the inner expression when given an ExpressionColumnNode, otherwise a new ColumnNodeExpression.

nodes.name: column
nodes.summary: Creates a Column backed by ExpressionColumnNode(e).

nodes.name: expression
nodes.summary: Creates a ColumnNodeExpression for a Column, intended only for expressions that will build another Column.

nodes.name: toNamed
nodes.summary: Returns a NamedExpression: keeps existing named expressions, uses an empty MultiAlias for generators, tries a better alias for a top-level Cast, and otherwise wraps in an UnresolvedAlias with a generated name.

nodes.name: generateAlias
nodes.summary: Generates an alias string: toString for a typed aggregate, toPrettySQL for other expressions.

nodes.name: conversions.scala
nodes.summary: Implicit conversions for the classic implementation: ClassicConversions casts API interfaces (SparkSession, Dataset, RelationalGroupedDataset, KeyValueGroupedDataset, SQLContext) to their classic classes, and ColumnConversions / RichColumn convert a Column into a Catalyst Expression.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala implicit defs and implicit classes; traits come with companion objects of the same name.

nodes.name: ClassicConversions
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait (plus an object extending it) of implicit castToImpl conversions from the sql.* API types to the classic implementations, and an implicit class that builds a Column from an Expression. Offered as a trait so extension authors can shim it across Spark versions.

nodes.name: ColumnConstructorExt
nodes.summary: Implicit class adding Column(expression) to the Column companion by calling ExpressionUtils.column.

nodes.name: ColumnConversions
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait (with an object using the global ColumnNodeToExpressionConverter) that converts a Column to an Expression with expression(column) and offers an implicit toRichColumn. SparkSession mixes in this trait.

nodes.name: RichColumn
nodes.summary: Wraps a Column and a ColumnNodeToExpressionConverter to provide the expr and named methods, reinstating the pre-Spark 4 Column functionality.

nodes.name: castToImpl
nodes.summary: Overloaded implicit conversions that cast sql.SparkSession, Dataset, RelationalGroupedDataset, KeyValueGroupedDataset and SQLContext to their classic classes with asInstanceOf.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds a Column from an Expression via ExpressionUtils.column.

nodes.name: expression
nodes.summary: Converts a Column to an Expression by applying the converter to column.node.

nodes.name: toRichColumn
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion that wraps a Column in a RichColumn bound to the converter.

nodes.name: expr
nodes.summary: Returns the Expression for the column by applying the converter to column.node.

nodes.name: named
nodes.summary: Returns the expression as a NamedExpression using ExpressionUtils.toNamed.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of df.na: drop, fill and replace for missing data. Each operation resolves columns against the DataFrame and rebuilds it with select or filter using Column expressions such as coalesce, nanvl, CaseKeyWhen and AtLeastNNonNulls.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions
nodes.summary: Final class implementing sql.DataFrameNaFunctions for a DataFrame. The core logic is in drop0, fillValue, fillMap and replace0; the many drop/fill/replace overloads at the end only forward to the parent implementation with super.

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: Protected drop overloads that remove rows by delegating to drop0 with either all output attributes or the resolved named columns.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Public fill overloads for Long, Double, String and Boolean values, with or without a column list, which delegate to fillValue (all output attributes or the given columns converted by toAttributes).

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Replaces values using a map: "*" applies to all output columns, otherwise each column must resolve to an Attribute (nested fields raise nestedFieldUnsupportedError), then replace0 is called.

nodes.name: replace0
nodes.summary: Builds the replacement: numeric keys and values are converted to double, the target column type comes from the first key (Double, Boolean or String), matching columns are projected through replaceCol and the result is df.select(projections).

nodes.name: fillMap
nodes.summary: Validates a column-to-value map (column must resolve to an Attribute, value must be a number, boolean or string) and projects each mapped column through a typed fillCol call.

nodes.name: fillCol
nodes.summary: Two overloads building the filling Column: for Double and Float it first applies nanvl(expr, null), then coalesce(value, lit(replacement).cast(dataType)) aliased to the column name.

nodes.name: replaceCol
nodes.summary: Returns a Column using CaseKeyWhen over the replacement map branches (targets cast to the attribute type), with the attribute itself as the fallback.

nodes.name: convertToDouble
nodes.summary: Converts Float, Double, Long and Int values to Double and throws IllegalArgumentException for other types.

nodes.name: toAttributes
nodes.summary: Resolves column names with df.col(name).expr and keeps those that are Attributes.

nodes.name: outputAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the analyzed plan output attributes of the DataFrame.

nodes.name: drop0
nodes.summary: Filters the DataFrame with an AtLeastNNonNulls predicate that keeps rows having at least minNonNulls non-null, non-NaN values over the given columns.

nodes.name: fillValue
nodes.summary: Fills values of a given type into the selected columns: the target type is NumericType, StringType or BooleanType based on the value, and only columns of a matching type and in the column list are filled with fillCol; others pass through.

nodes.name: RelationalGroupedDataset.scala
nodes.summary: Classic RelationalGroupedDataset returned by groupBy, rollup, cube, groupingSets and pivot. Its toDF turns aggregate columns into an Aggregate or Pivot logical plan, and it also hosts the internal grouped-map entry points used by the Python and R integrations (flatMapGroupsIn*, applyInPandasWithState, transformWithState*).
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one class id; the companion holds the GroupType case objects and helpers.

nodes.name: RelationalGroupedDataset
nodes.summary: Holds the DataFrame, the grouping expressions and a GroupType. The agg, count, mean, max, avg, min and sum methods are overrides that forward to the parent, which calls toDF; toDF builds Aggregate (group by), Aggregate over Rollup, Cube or GroupingSets, or Pivot depending on the GroupType. The companion object (lines 632-722) holds the GroupType values and helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Range covers the class (54-630) and its companion object (632-722).

nodes.name: GroupType
nodes.summary: Trait for the grouping kind with a toString derived from the class name (strips "$" and "Type").

nodes.name: GroupByType
nodes.summary: Marker object for a plain GROUP BY.

nodes.name: CubeType
nodes.summary: Marker object for CUBE.

nodes.name: RollupType
nodes.summary: Marker object for ROLLUP.

nodes.name: GroupingSetsType
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the list of grouping sets for GROUPING SETS.

nodes.name: PivotType
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the pivot column expression and pivot value expressions for PIVOT.

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: Converts aggregate Columns to expressions (adding the input type for typed aggregators), prepends the grouping expressions when dataFrameRetainGroupColumns is set, aliases everything, and builds the plan by GroupType: Aggregate, Aggregate over Rollup or Cube, GroupingSets, or Pivot; wrapped in Dataset.ofRows.

nodes.name: selectNumericColumns
nodes.summary: Returns Columns for the named columns after checking they are numeric, or all numeric columns of the DataFrame when no name is given.

nodes.name: as
nodes.summary: Creates a KeyValueGroupedDataset by resolving the grouping expressions with handleGroupingExpression and passing the key and value encoders.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Agg overloads (string pairs, maps, Columns) that forward to the parent implementation, which ends in toDF.

nodes.name: pivot
nodes.summary: Pivot overloads. The Column and Seq version turns values into Literal or Column expressions and creates a new RelationalGroupedDataset with a PivotType (only allowed right after a plain group by; repeated pivot or pivot after rollup/cube raises errors). The Column-only overload first gets the distinct values with collectPivotValues.

nodes.name: flatMapGroupsInR
nodes.summary: Internal: applies a serialized R function to each group by selecting the grouping columns and creating a FlatMapGroupsInR plan.

nodes.name: flatMapGroupsInPandas
nodes.summary: Internal: checks the column is a grouped-map Pandas UDF with a StructType return type, projects grouping columns in front, and creates a FlatMapGroupsInPandas plan.

nodes.name: flatMapGroupsInArrow
nodes.summary: Internal: the Arrow-UDF counterpart of flatMapGroupsInPandas that creates a FlatMapGroupsInArrow plan.

nodes.name: flatMapCoGroupsInPandas
nodes.summary: Internal: cogroups two grouped datasets, requiring the same number of keys and a cogrouped-map Pandas UDF, and creates a FlatMapCoGroupsInPandas plan from the two analyzed projections.

nodes.name: flatMapCoGroupsInArrow
nodes.summary: Internal: the Arrow-UDF counterpart of flatMapCoGroupsInPandas that creates a FlatMapCoGroupsInArrow plan.

nodes.name: applyInPandasWithState
nodes.summary: Internal: builds a FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithState plan after validating that the output mode is append or update.

nodes.name: transformWithStateInPySpark
nodes.summary: Internal: calls _transformWithStateInPySpark with the PYTHON_ROW user-facing data type.

nodes.name: transformWithStateInPandas
nodes.summary: Internal: calls _transformWithStateInPySpark with the PANDAS user-facing data type.

nodes.name: _transformWithStateInPySpark
nodes.summary: Builds a TransformWithStateInPySpark plan (with or without an initial state dataset) over the grouping-projected child, then optionally updates the event time column through updateEventTimeColumnAfterTransformWithState.

nodes.name: updateEventTimeColumnAfterTransformWithState
nodes.summary: Wraps the transformWithState plan in an UpdateEventTimeWatermarkColumn node for the named event time column.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Describes the dataset: up to two grouping fields with types, a count of remaining ones, the DataFrame and the group type.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory creating a RelationalGroupedDataset.

nodes.name: handleGroupingExpression
nodes.summary: Analyzes grouping expressions in a dummy Project over a LocalRelation with the session analyzer, adds grouping expressions missing from the DataFrame, and returns a QueryExecution with the grouping attributes.

nodes.name: alias
nodes.summary: Wraps an expression as a NamedExpression: keeps named ones, uses an UnresolvedAlias with generateAlias for aggregates, an UnresolvedAlias for unresolved ones, and otherwise an Alias with a pretty SQL name.

nodes.name: collectPivotValues
nodes.summary: Collects the sorted distinct values of the pivot column (limit dataFramePivotMaxValues + 1) and raises an error if the limit is exceeded; streaming DataFrames are rejected.

nodes.name: SQLContext.scala
nodes.summary: Classic SQLContext, the Spark 1.x entry point kept for backward compatibility. Since Spark 2.0 it is a thin wrapper over SparkSession: nearly every method forwards to the session or to the parent implementation. The companion object offers getOrCreate and bean-to-InternalRow helpers.

nodes.name: SQLContext
nodes.summary: Class (lines 59-384) extending sql.SQLContext(sparkSession) with sessionState, sharedState, read, readStream, streams, udf and forwarding overloads for createDataFrame, createDataset, range, sql, table, load, jdbc and the deprecated applySchema/jsonFile/jsonRDD/parquetFile methods. The companion object (lines 386-443) extends sql.SQLContextCompanion.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one class id.

nodes.name: implicits
nodes.summary: Object exposing SQLImplicits for this SQLContext, supplying the session through the protected session member.

nodes.name: sessionState
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.sessionState.

nodes.name: sharedState
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.sharedState.

nodes.name: conf
nodes.summary: Deprecated accessor returning sessionState.conf.

nodes.name: setConf
nodes.summary: Sets SQL configuration from Properties or a ConfigEntry on sessionState.conf.

nodes.name: experimental
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.experimental.

nodes.name: udf
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.udf (the UDFRegistration).

nodes.name: internalCreateDataFrame
nodes.summary: Forwards to sparkSession.internalCreateDataFrame to create a DataFrame from an RDD[InternalRow].

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.read.

nodes.name: readStream
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.readStream.

nodes.name: registerDataFrameAsTable
nodes.summary: Registers a DataFrame as a temporary view via createOrReplaceTempView.

nodes.name: streams
nodes.summary: Returns sparkSession.streams, the StreamingQueryManager.

nodes.name: newSession
nodes.summary: Creates a new session with sparkSession.newSession() and returns its sqlContext.

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Overloads for creating DataFrames (from RDD[Product], Seq, RDD[Row] with a schema, Java RDDs and lists, bean classes) that call super.createDataFrame, which uses the session. The createDataset overloads at lines 181-188 sit inside this span.

nodes.name: createExternalTable
nodes.summary: Deprecated createExternalTable overloads forwarding to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Range overloads returning Dataset[Row], forwarding to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL query by calling super.sql(sqlText), which uses the session.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame for a table with super.table.

nodes.name: applySchema
nodes.summary: Deprecated applySchema overloads (RDD or JavaRDD with schema or bean class) forwarding to the parent.

nodes.name: jsonRDD
nodes.summary: Deprecated jsonRDD overloads; the unschematized forms call read.json(json) and the others forward to the parent.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Deprecated load overloads forwarding to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Deprecated jdbc overloads forwarding to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Companion method returning newSparkSessionBuilder().sparkContext(sparkContext).getOrCreate().sqlContext.

nodes.name: beansToRows
nodes.summary: Converts an iterator of Java Beans to InternalRows using bean read methods and Catalyst type converters, handling nested structs recursively.

nodes.name: getSQLProperties
nodes.summary: Extracts all spark.sql* entries from a SparkConf into a Properties object.

nodes.name: DataStreamReader.scala
nodes.summary: Classic builder for reading a streaming source. It records format, schema, options and an optional source name, and load/table/changes wrap an unresolved logical plan (UnresolvedDataSource, UnresolvedRelation or RelationChanges) in a NamedStreamingRelation and turn it into a streaming DataFrame with Dataset.ofRows.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala final class using this.type return types for fluent chaining; covariant overrides at the bottom just forward to the shared parent implementation.

nodes.name: DataStreamReader
nodes.summary: Implements streaming.DataStreamReader for a classic SparkSession. Builder calls only fill private vars (source defaults to spark.sql.sources.default); loading is lazy and produces a streaming plan that the analyzer resolves later. The schema setter rejects CHAR/VARCHAR types and the table/changes paths build UnresolvedRelation with isStreaming = true.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Sets the input data source name used by load().

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Stores a user-specified schema after CharVarcharUtils.failIfHasCharVarchar rejects CHAR/VARCHAR types; a null schema is ignored.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one entry to the case-insensitive extraOptions map.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds all entries of a map to extraOptions.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Experimental: validates the source name with validateSourceName and stores it so that the resulting NamedStreamingRelation carries a user-provided name.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads a streaming DataFrame from a path. It throws setPathOptionAndCallWithPathParameterError when a path option is already set (unless the legacy behavior flag is on) and then calls loadInternal; the no-argument load() at line 79 calls loadInternal(None).

nodes.name: loadInternal
nodes.summary: Creates an UnresolvedDataSource (source, schema, options, isStreaming = true, path), wraps it with NamedStreamingRelation.withUserProvidedName and returns Dataset.ofRows over the plan.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Streams from a table: parses the multipart name, builds an UnresolvedRelation with isStreaming = true and the reader options, wraps it in a NamedStreamingRelation and returns a DataFrame.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Streams the change feed of a table: rejects a user-specified schema, builds a changelog context from the options and session time zone, wraps an UnresolvedRelation in RelationChanges and a NamedStreamingRelation.

nodes.name: assertNoSpecifiedSchema
nodes.summary: Throws userSpecifiedSchemaUnsupportedError if a schema was set for an operation that does not allow one.

nodes.name: validateJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Runs checkJsonSchema on the user-specified schema, if any.

nodes.name: validateXmlSchema
nodes.summary: Runs checkXmlSchema on the user-specified schema, if any.

nodes.name: RuntimeConfig.scala
nodes.summary: Classic runtime configuration interface exposed as SparkSession.conf. It reads and writes the session's SQLConf, and set/unset first reject static configs and, optionally, Spark core configs that are not SQL configs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a default constructor argument (new SQLConf) and several private[sql] overloads that take typed ConfigEntry arguments.

nodes.name: RuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Implements sql.RuntimeConfig on top of a SQLConf instance. Reads and writes go straight to the SQLConf (setConfString, getConfString, getAllConfs, unset, isModifiable), and the write paths (set, unset) validate the key with requireNonStaticConf first.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets a config value after requireNonStaticConf(key); the string overload calls sqlConf.setConfString and the private[sql] ConfigEntry overload calls sqlConf.setConf.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Reads a config as a string from sqlConf.getConfString, throwing NoSuchElementException when the key is unset and has no default, or returning the supplied default (overloads at lines 68-77 do the same for ConfigEntry).

nodes.name: getAll
nodes.summary: Returns all configs from sqlConf.getAllConfs as a Scala Map.

nodes.name: getAllAsJava
nodes.summary: Returns getAll converted to a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: getOption
nodes.summary: Returns Some(value) or None, turning the NoSuchElementException from get into None.

nodes.name: unset
nodes.summary: Removes a config key after requireNonStaticConf(key) via sqlConf.unsetConf.

nodes.name: isModifiable
nodes.summary: Reports whether the key can be modified, delegating to sqlConf.isModifiable.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether the key is set in the underlying SQLConf.

nodes.name: requireNonStaticConf
nodes.summary: Validation gate used by set and unset. spark.default.parallelism is allowed through (kept for SPARK-48773 behavior compatibility); a static SQL config key throws cannotModifyValueOfStaticConfigError; and when setCommandRejectsSparkCoreConfs is on, a Spark core ConfigEntry that is not a SQL config throws cannotModifyValueOfSparkConfigError.

nodes.name: SchedulerBackendUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds SchedulerBackendUtils, a helper object that computes the initial target number of executors, either from the dynamic allocation settings or from the executor instances setting.

nodes.name: SchedulerBackendUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with the default executor count (2) and getInitialTargetExecutorNumber, used when a backend needs to know how many executors to start with.

nodes.name: getInitialTargetExecutorNumber
nodes.summary: Returns the initial executor target: with dynamic allocation enabled, the configured initial executor count after checking it lies between the min and max; otherwise the requested executor instances, falling back to the supplied default.

nodes.name: AccumulableInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AccumulableInfo, the developer-facing case class that describes an accumulator modified during a task or stage (id, name, partial update, total value, internal flag).

nodes.name: AccumulableInfo
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the id, optional name, optional partial update, optional total value and internal/countFailedValues flags of an accumulator. Used to report accumulator state for a task or stage; its update and value types are lost (cast to strings) once JSON serialized for the event log.

nodes.name: AsyncEventQueue.scala
nodes.summary: Implements AsyncEventQueue, a bounded queue that delivers posted listener events to its child listeners on a dedicated daemon thread, dropping events when full and exposing queue metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Private Scala class with a companion object holding the POISON_PILL sentinel and the dropped-event logging interval.

nodes.name: AsyncEventQueue
nodes.summary: SparkListenerBus subclass with a LinkedBlockingQueue sized by configuration. Events posted to it are dispatched to its listeners in a separate thread started by start(); stop() enqueues a poison pill and waits for the queue to drain. Overflowing events are dropped and counted. The companion object defines POISON_PILL and LOGGING_INTERVAL.

nodes.name: capacity
nodes.summary: Reads the queue capacity from a per-queue config key, falling back to the default listener bus capacity, and asserts it is positive.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Loop run on the dispatch thread: takes events from the queue until the poison pill, posts each to all listeners while timing it, and decrements the in-flight event count.

nodes.name: getTimer
nodes.summary: Returns the metrics timer associated with a listener class from LiveListenerBusMetrics.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the dispatch thread once, remembering the SparkContext so it can be stopped if dispatching fails; throws if already started.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the queue by enqueuing the poison pill and joining the dispatch thread (up to the configured exit timeout); new events are dropped afterwards.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Offers an event to the queue; when the queue is full it drops the event, increments the dropped counters, and logs an error once plus rate-limited warnings.

nodes.name: waitUntilEmpty
nodes.summary: Testing helper that polls until all queued events are fully processed or a deadline passes.

nodes.name: removeListenerOnError
nodes.summary: Handles a listener that failed unrecoverably by removing it from the whole LiveListenerBus.

nodes.name: BarrierJobAllocationFailed.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the exception hierarchy thrown when a job with barrier stages fails a pre-submission check, plus the shared error message constants.

nodes.name: BarrierJobAllocationFailed
nodes.summary: Base SparkException for barrier-stage submission check failures. Its companion object holds the error messages for unsupported RDD chains, dynamic allocation being enabled, and a barrier stage needing more slots than the cluster has.

nodes.name: BarrierJobUnsupportedRDDChainException
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a barrier stage contains an unsupported RDD chain pattern; uses the matching message constant.

nodes.name: BarrierJobRunWithDynamicAllocationException
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a barrier stage is run with dynamic resource allocation enabled.

nodes.name: BarrierJobSlotsNumberCheckFailed
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a barrier stage requires more concurrent task slots than the cluster currently has; exposes the required and maximum concurrent task counts.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics Source for the DAGScheduler, registering gauges for stages and jobs and a timer for event loop message processing.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source named DAGScheduler. Registers gauges for failed, running and waiting stages and for total and active jobs read from the DAGScheduler, and exposes a timer for the time spent processing its event loop messages.

nodes.name: EventLoggingListener.scala
nodes.summary: Implements EventLoggingListener, a SparkListener that serializes scheduler events to JSON and writes them to the event log, with redaction of sensitive properties.

nodes.name: EventLoggingListener
nodes.summary: SparkListener that logs events as JSON through an EventLogFileWriter. It flushes on key events, optionally tracks per-stage executor metric peaks, can log block updates, and redacts sensitive properties. The companion object has the default log dir, the driver stage key and redactEvent.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the log writer and writes the initial log-start event.

nodes.name: initEventLog
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerLogStart event carrying the Spark version as the first log entry.

nodes.name: logEvent
nodes.summary: Converts an event to a JSON string via JsonProtocol and writes it, optionally flushing; keeps a copy when testing.

nodes.name: onStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: Logs the stage-submitted event with redacted properties and starts tracking executor metric peaks for the stage when enabled.

nodes.name: onTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Logs the task-end event and folds the task executor metrics into per-executor peaks for its stage.

nodes.name: onEnvironmentUpdate
nodes.summary: Logs the environment update event after redacting sensitive entries.

nodes.name: onStageCompleted
nodes.summary: Emits the per-executor peak stage metrics events for the completed stage, clears earlier attempts, then logs the stage-completed event with a flush.

nodes.name: onJobStart
nodes.summary: Logs the job-start event with redacted properties and flushes.

nodes.name: onBlockUpdated
nodes.summary: Logs block update events only when block update logging is enabled.

nodes.name: onExecutorMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Logs driver metrics updates and records executor metric peaks for the matching or all active stages.

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: Logs events of other types when they declare themselves loggable.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the underlying event log writer.

nodes.name: redactProperties
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of properties where those that are Spark conf keys are passed through Utils.redact and local properties are kept unchanged.

nodes.name: redactEvent
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that redacts sensitive values in each environment detail group of an environment update event, except the classpath entries.

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommissionInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the message and driver-side state describing an executor that is being decommissioned.

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommissionInfo
nodes.summary: Case class giving detail about an executor decommission: a human readable message and an optional worker host, set when the host itself is decommissioned (used to infer possible shuffle data loss).

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommissionState
nodes.summary: Case class holding decommission state kept by the TaskSchedulerImpl: the driver-clock start time and optional worker host. Kept separate from the info message so the two can evolve independently.

nodes.name: ExecutorFailuresInTaskSet.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a small helper that tracks task failures on one executor within one task set, for exclusion purposes.

nodes.name: ExecutorFailuresInTaskSet
nodes.summary: Tracks, for one executor in one task set, a map from task index to failure count and most recent failure time. Used for exclusion decisions.

nodes.name: updateWithFailure
nodes.summary: Records a failure for a task index by incrementing its count and keeping the latest failure time.

nodes.name: numUniqueTasksWithFailures
nodes.summary: Returns the number of distinct task indexes that have failed on this executor.

nodes.name: getNumTaskFailures
nodes.summary: Returns how many times the given task index has failed on this executor, or 0.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the unique failed task count and the failure map as a string.

nodes.name: ExecutorLossReason.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ExecutorLossReason hierarchy that explains why an executor or process was lost, exited, was killed or is being decommissioned.

nodes.name: ExecutorLossReason
nodes.summary: Serializable base class holding a message that explains an executor or whole process failing or exiting.

nodes.name: ExecutorExited
nodes.summary: Loss reason for an executor exit, with the exit code, whether the app caused it, and a reason. The companion apply fills the reason using ExecutorExitCode.explainExitCode.

nodes.name: ExecutorLossMessage
nodes.summary: Holder object for a shared loss message string used when decommissioning finished.

nodes.name: ExecutorKilled
nodes.summary: Singleton loss reason meaning the executor was killed by the driver.

nodes.name: LossReasonPending
nodes.summary: Singleton loss reason meaning the cause is not yet known. The task scheduler uses it to remove executor state without yet failing the tasks that ran there.

nodes.name: ExecutorProcessLost
nodes.summary: Loss reason for a lost executor process, with an optional worker host (set when the host is confirmed lost) and a flag for whether the app caused it (true by default).

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommission
nodes.summary: Loss reason meaning the executor is marked for decommissioning; the message is a fixed prefix plus the reason. Used by the task scheduler to remove executor state without failing running tasks yet.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorResourceInfo, which holds the name and addresses of one resource type on an executor.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceInfo
nodes.summary: Extends ResourceInformation and mixes in ResourceAllocator to hold a resource name and its addresses on an executor. Managed by the SchedulerBackend, and the TaskScheduler uses it to schedule tasks on idle executors.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourcesAmounts.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorResourcesAmounts, a temporary per-executor view of how much of each custom resource address (such as GPU or FPGA indices) is still free, plus a companion that builds it from ExecutorResourceInfo. The doc comment says it is used while offering resources to tasks in the TaskSchedulerImpl.
nodes.languageNotes: Resource amounts are stored as Long internal values through ResourceAmountUtils so fractional amounts (for example 0.2 of a GPU) avoid floating point errors.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourcesAmounts
nodes.summary: Holds a mutable copy of the available amount of every resource address on one executor (resource name to address to internal Long amount). Offers acquire, release and assignAddressesCustomResources so addresses can be reserved for a task set under a ResourceProfile; the companion object adds empty and apply(Map[String, ExecutorResourceInfo]) factories.

nodes.name: availableResources
nodes.summary: Converts the internal Long amounts back into fractional Double amounts per resource and address; documented as being for testing.

nodes.name: acquire
nodes.summary: Subtracts the assigned amounts from the matching resource addresses and throws a SparkException if the resource or address is unknown or the remaining amount would go below zero.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Adds previously assigned amounts back to the matching resource addresses and throws a SparkException if the resource or address is unknown or a total would exceed one entire resource.

nodes.name: assignAddressesCustomResources
nodes.summary: Looks at the custom task resources of a ResourceProfile and tries to pick addresses in sorted order that satisfy each request (whole addresses for amounts of 1 or more, a partial share for amounts below 1). Returns None if any requested resource cannot be met, otherwise the chosen addresses and amounts.

nodes.name: empty
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates an ExecutorResourcesAmounts with no resources.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds an ExecutorResourcesAmounts from a map of resource name to ExecutorResourceInfo by taking each info's resourcesAmounts.

nodes.name: ExternalClusterManager.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ExternalClusterManager trait, the plugin interface through which an external cluster manager supplies a TaskScheduler and SchedulerBackend for a given master URL.

nodes.name: ExternalClusterManager
nodes.summary: Trait that an external scheduler plugin implements: it says whether it can handle a master URL, creates the TaskScheduler and SchedulerBackend for a SparkContext, and then initializes the two together.

nodes.name: canCreate
nodes.summary: Returns true if this cluster manager can create scheduler components for the given master URL.

nodes.name: createTaskScheduler
nodes.summary: Creates the TaskScheduler responsible for task handling for the given SparkContext and master URL.

nodes.name: createSchedulerBackend
nodes.summary: Creates the SchedulerBackend that works with the task scheduler; called after createTaskScheduler.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Initializes the task scheduler and backend after both have been created.

nodes.name: HealthTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HealthTracker, which records task failures per executor and per node and excludes problem executors and nodes for an application for a limited time, plus its companion config helpers and the ExcludedExecutor record. Per its doc comment it works together with the exclusion logic in TaskSetManagers and its callers hold a lock on the TaskSchedulerImpl.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala structured logging (log interpolator with MDC) and posts both legacy Blacklisted and newer Excluded listener events to keep backwards compatibility.

nodes.name: HealthTracker
nodes.summary: Tracks failures across successful task sets and fetch failures, excludes executors and nodes when thresholds are reached, expires exclusions after a timeout, and optionally kills or decommissions excluded executors through an ExecutorAllocationClient. It posts listener events on the LiveListenerBus. It is not thread-safe except excludedNodeList; the companion object holds config validation and timeout helpers.

nodes.name: ExecutorFailureList
nodes.summary: Inner class that keeps the task failures (stage, attempt, task index and expiry time) seen on one executor within successful task sets, with a tracked minimum expiry so old entries can be dropped quickly.

nodes.name: ExcludedExecutor
nodes.summary: Private case class pairing the node of an excluded executor with the time its exclusion expires.

nodes.name: applyExcludeOnFailureTimeout
nodes.summary: Removes executors and nodes whose exclusion expiry time has passed, posts the matching unexcluded/unblacklisted events and refreshes the cached excluded node list and next expiry time.

nodes.name: updateNextExpiryTime
nodes.summary: Recomputes the earliest expiry time over excluded executors and nodes so applyExcludeOnFailureTimeout can skip work when nothing has expired.

nodes.name: killExecutor
nodes.summary: Kills or decommissions one executor through the allocation client (depending on configuration) and logs when no allocation client is defined.

nodes.name: killExcludedExecutor
nodes.summary: Kills the excluded executor when the kill-on-exclusion setting is enabled.

nodes.name: killExcludedIdleExecutor
nodes.summary: Kills an excluded idle executor, used when tasks are unschedulable and a new executor should be acquired.

nodes.name: killExecutorsOnExcludedNode
nodes.summary: Kills or decommissions all executors on an excluded host through the allocation client when the kill setting is enabled, logging failures.

nodes.name: updateExcludedForFetchFailure
nodes.summary: On a fetch failure, excludes the whole node if the external shuffle service is enabled, otherwise excludes only the failing executor, posting events and optionally killing executors.

nodes.name: updateExcludedForSuccessfulTaskSet
nodes.summary: Adds the failures from a successful task set to each executor's failure list, excludes executors that reach the failure limit, and excludes a node when enough of its executors are excluded.

nodes.name: isExecutorExcluded
nodes.summary: Returns whether an executor is currently excluded.

nodes.name: excludedNodeList
nodes.summary: Returns the immutable set of excluded nodes from an AtomicReference; the one thread-safe method of the class.

nodes.name: isNodeExcluded
nodes.summary: Returns whether a node is currently excluded.

nodes.name: handleRemovedExecutor
nodes.summary: Drops the failure list of a removed executor while intentionally keeping its exclusion records so node-level exclusion can still be decided.

nodes.name: addFailures
nodes.summary: Records each failed task of a task set with its expiry time and updates the minimum expiry.

nodes.name: numUniqueTaskFailures
nodes.summary: Returns the number of unique task failures still tracked for this executor.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Returns true when no failures are tracked.

nodes.name: dropFailuresWithTimeoutBefore
nodes.summary: Removes tracked failures whose expiry is before the given time so isolated old failures do not cause exclusion.

nodes.name: isExcludeOnFailureEnabled
nodes.summary: Decides whether application-level exclusion is on by checking the application-level setting, the general setting, then the legacy timeout setting, defaulting to off.

nodes.name: getExcludeOnFailureTimeout
nodes.summary: Returns the exclusion timeout in milliseconds from the new setting, the legacy setting, or a one hour default.

nodes.name: validateExcludeOnFailureConfs
nodes.summary: Checks that the exclusion related settings are positive and that the per-node attempt limit is below the task failure limit, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise.

nodes.name: InputFormatInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DeveloperApi class InputFormatInfo, which validates a Hadoop InputFormat class and path and computes preferred host locations (SplitInfo) from the input splits, with a companion that aggregates them into a host to splits map.

nodes.name: InputFormatInfo
nodes.summary: Holds a Hadoop configuration, an InputFormat class and an input path; on construction it checks the class implements either the mapreduce or mapred InputFormat API. It can then list the splits and turn them into SplitInfo values, and the companion object groups them by host to compute preferred locations.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Determines whether the input format class belongs to the mapreduce or mapred Hadoop API and throws IllegalArgumentException if it is neither or cannot be found.

nodes.name: prefLocsFromMapreduceInputFormat
nodes.summary: Creates the mapreduce InputFormat by reflection, reads its splits for the path and converts them to a set of SplitInfo.

nodes.name: prefLocsFromMapredInputFormat
nodes.summary: Creates the mapred InputFormat by reflection, reads its splits for the path and converts them to a set of SplitInfo.

nodes.name: findPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Chooses the mapreduce or mapred path according to the validated flags and returns the SplitInfo set.

nodes.name: computePreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Companion method that runs findPreferredLocations for each InputFormatInfo and groups the resulting SplitInfo values by host location.

nodes.name: JobListener.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the JobListener trait, the callback interface notified when tasks of a submitted job succeed or when the job fails.

nodes.name: JobListener
nodes.summary: Trait with taskSucceeded(index, result) and jobFailed(exception), notified after a job is submitted to the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: taskSucceeded
nodes.summary: Called each time a task of the job succeeds, with the task index and its result.

nodes.name: jobFailed
nodes.summary: Called when the whole job fails, after which no more taskSucceeded calls happen.

nodes.name: JobResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed JobResult type with its two DeveloperApi outcomes, JobSucceeded and JobFailed(exception).

nodes.name: JobResult
nodes.summary: Sealed trait representing the result of a job in the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: JobSucceeded
nodes.summary: Case object marking a job that finished successfully.

nodes.name: JobFailed
nodes.summary: Case class marking a failed job, carrying the Exception that caused the failure.

nodes.name: JobWaiter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JobWaiter, a JobListener that lets a caller wait for a DAGScheduler job, forwarding each task result to a handler function and exposing completion as a Future.

nodes.name: JobWaiter
nodes.summary: JobListener implementation tied to one jobId. It passes each task result to a (possibly non thread safe) result handler under a lock, completes a Promise when all tasks have finished (immediately if there are zero tasks), fails it on jobFailed, and can ask the DAGScheduler to cancel the job.

nodes.name: jobFinished
nodes.summary: Returns whether the completion promise has been completed.

nodes.name: completionFuture
nodes.summary: Returns the Future that completes when the job finishes or fails.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Asks the DAGScheduler to cancel the job with an optional reason; a no-argument overload at line 61 calls it with None. Cancellation is handled asynchronously.

nodes.name: taskSucceeded
nodes.summary: Calls the result handler under a lock and completes the promise once the number of finished tasks equals the total.

nodes.name: jobFailed
nodes.summary: Fails the completion promise with the exception, or logs a warning if the promise was already completed.

nodes.name: LiveListenerBus.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LiveListenerBus, which buffers and then asynchronously delivers scheduler events to registered SparkListeners through named queues, plus LiveListenerBusMetrics that exposes event counts and per-listener timers as a metrics source.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object holding queue-name constants and a DynamicVariable used to detect calls made from the listener thread.

nodes.name: LiveListenerBus
nodes.summary: Asynchronously passes SparkListenerEvents to registered listeners. Events posted before start() are buffered, listeners are grouped into independent named queues (shared, appStatus, executorManagement, eventLog) each with its own delivery thread, and events posted after stop() are dropped. The companion object (lines 250-261) defines the queue names and the withinListenerThread flag.

nodes.name: LiveListenerBusMetrics
nodes.summary: Metrics Source named LiveListenerBus that counts events posted to the bus and lazily creates per-listener-class processing-time timers, limited by the configured maximum number of timed listener classes.

nodes.name: addToSharedQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a listener to the queue shared by all non-internal listeners.

nodes.name: addToManagementQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a listener to the executor management queue.

nodes.name: addToStatusQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a listener to the application status queue.

nodes.name: addToEventLogQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a listener to the event log queue.

nodes.name: addToQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a listener to a named queue, creating and starting a new AsyncEventQueue if none with that name exists yet; throws if the bus has already been stopped.

nodes.name: removeListener
nodes.summary: Removes a listener from every queue it was added to and stops and removes any queue that becomes empty.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Posts an event to all queues, buffering it if the bus has not started yet and dropping it if the bus is stopped; increments the posted-events counter.

nodes.name: postToQueues
nodes.summary: Iterates over all queues and posts the event to each of them.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts every queue, replays the events buffered before startup, clears the buffer and registers the bus metrics with the metrics system. May be called only once.

nodes.name: waitUntilEmpty
nodes.summary: Waits until all queues are drained or a deadline passes, throwing a timeout error if any queue is still non-empty.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the bus after queued events are processed, then stops and clears all queues; further events are dropped.

nodes.name: getTimerForListenerClass
nodes.summary: Returns a timer for the given listener class, creating it on first use unless the configured maximum number of timed classes has been reached.

nodes.name: MergeStatus.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MergeStatus, the scheduler-side record of a merged shuffle partition for push-based shuffle (merger location, merge id, bitmap of merged map outputs, total size), together with helpers that split a MergeStatuses message into per-partition MergeStatus objects.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object providing factory and conversion helpers; the class is Externalizable and keeps its state in private[this] vars.

nodes.name: MergeStatus
nodes.summary: Status of merging shuffle partition blocks for one shuffle partition, kept by the scheduler inside the MapOutputTracker and served to reducers fetching push-merged blocks. It stores the merger BlockManagerId, shuffle merge id, a RoaringBitmap of merged mappers and the merged size, and is Externalizable. The companion object (lines 85-116) holds a dummy reduce-count constant, the apply factory and the MergeStatuses converter.

nodes.name: getNumMissingMapOutputs
nodes.summary: Counts the map outputs among the first numMaps that are not present in the merged bitmap.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Serializes the location, shuffle merge id, mapper bitmap and size to an ObjectOutput.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Restores the location, shuffle merge id, mapper bitmap and size from an ObjectInput.

nodes.name: convertMergeStatusesToMergeStatusArr
nodes.summary: Splits a MergeStatuses message received from an external shuffle service into (reduceId, MergeStatus) pairs, using the supplied merger location with the shuffle-merger identifier.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs a MergeStatus from a location, merge id, bitmap and size.

nodes.name: MiscellaneousProcessDetails.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the DeveloperApi class MiscellaneousProcessDetails (since 3.2.0), a serializable holder for a miscellaneous process's host and port, core count and log URL map that the scheduler passes to SparkListeners.

nodes.name: MiscellaneousProcessDetails
nodes.summary: Serializable value class carrying hostPort, cores and logUrlInfo of a miscellaneous process so that the scheduler can hand them to SparkListeners.

nodes.name: OutputCommitCoordinator.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the output commit coordination protocol: a driver-side authority that applies a first-committer-wins policy to decide which task attempt may commit output, the RPC messages it uses, and the endpoint that serves executors' requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a private sealed trait and case classes for RPC messages, a class with nested private case classes, and a companion object holding the RPC endpoint.

nodes.name: OutputCommitCoordinationMessage
nodes.summary: Private sealed serializable trait that is the base of the messages exchanged with the output commit coordinator endpoint.

nodes.name: StopCoordinator
nodes.summary: Case object message telling the driver's coordinator endpoint to stop.

nodes.name: AskPermissionToCommitOutput
nodes.summary: Case class message carrying stage, stage attempt, partition and attempt number, sent by a task asking to commit its output.

nodes.name: OutputCommitCoordinator
nodes.summary: Decides whether tasks may commit output using a first-committer-wins policy. It exists on both drivers and executors: executors forward canCommit requests over RPC to the driver, where per-stage state tracks the authorized committer for each partition and attempts known to have failed. The DAGScheduler drives stageStart, stageEnd and taskCompleted.

nodes.name: TaskIdentifier
nodes.summary: Private case class identifying a committer by stage attempt and task attempt, since the same task can run in two attempts of a stage at once.

nodes.name: StageState
nodes.summary: Private per-stage state holding the authorized committer of each partition and a map of failed attempts per partition.

nodes.name: OutputCommitCoordinatorEndpoint
nodes.summary: RpcEndpoint nested in the OutputCommitCoordinator object that runs on the driver; it stops on StopCoordinator and answers AskPermissionToCommitOutput by calling the coordinator's handleAskPermissionToCommit.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Returns whether the coordinator's internal stage state map is empty.

nodes.name: canCommit
nodes.summary: Called by tasks to ask whether they may commit; sends an AskPermissionToCommitOutput message to the coordinator endpoint and waits for the answer, returning false (with an error log) if the coordinator was stopped.

nodes.name: stageStart
nodes.summary: Called by the DAGScheduler when a stage starts; creates the stage state, or reuses the existing state from a previous attempt.

nodes.name: stageEnd
nodes.summary: Called by the DAGScheduler when a stage ends; removes the stage state.

nodes.name: taskCompleted
nodes.summary: Called by the DAGScheduler on task completion; for failures other than success or commit denial it records the attempt as failed and releases the commit lock if that attempt held it.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: On the driver, tells the endpoint to stop, clears the endpoint reference and the stage states.

nodes.name: handleAskPermissionToCommit
nodes.summary: Driver-side handler of a commit request: denies if the attempt already failed, grants and records the committer if the partition has none, and denies if another attempt holds it or the stage has completed.

nodes.name: attemptFailed
nodes.summary: Checks whether the given stage attempt and task attempt are recorded as failed for the partition.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles one-way messages: on StopCoordinator logs and stops the endpoint.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
