nodes.summary: Handles AskPermissionToCommitOutput by replying with the coordinator's decision.

nodes.name: ReplayListenerBus.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ReplayListenerBus, a SparkListenerBus that re-posts events read from serialized JSON event log data to its registered listeners, together with HaltReplayException and a companion holding the replay filter type. Used when event logs are replayed.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing a class, a companion object with a type alias and a default filter value, and a private[spark] exception class.

nodes.name: ReplayListenerBus
nodes.summary: SparkListenerBus that replays events from serialized event data. Its companion object defines the ReplayEventsFilter type alias (a String => Boolean) and SELECT_ALL_FILTER, a filter that accepts every line.

nodes.name: replay
nodes.summary: Replays events from an event log, one JSON-encoded SparkListenerEvent per line. The InputStream overload (lines 54-61) reads UTF-8 lines and delegates to this iterator overload, which applies the events filter, parses each line with JsonProtocol and posts it to all listeners; it skips unrecognized events and properties with a one-time warning, tolerates a truncated last line when maybeTruncated is set, and returns false if replay was halted or an error occurred.

nodes.name: isIgnorableException
nodes.summary: Overrides the bus hook so that a HaltReplayException thrown by a listener is treated as ignorable.

nodes.name: HaltReplayException
nodes.summary: Exception that listeners can throw to stop an event log replay. It is handled only by ReplayListenerBus and causes errors with other bus implementations.

nodes.name: SchedulingAlgorithm.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SchedulingAlgorithm trait and its two implementations, FIFOSchedulingAlgorithm and FairSchedulingAlgorithm, which provide the comparators that order Schedulable entries.

nodes.name: SchedulingAlgorithm
nodes.summary: Trait for the sort algorithm between Schedulables: its single method, comparator, says whether the first Schedulable sorts before the second. Per its comment, FIFO orders TaskSetManagers and FS orders Pools, with FIFO or FS inside pools.

nodes.name: FIFOSchedulingAlgorithm
nodes.summary: SchedulingAlgorithm that orders by priority first and then by stageId, with the smaller value sorting first.

nodes.name: comparator
nodes.summary: Compares two Schedulables by the sign of the priority difference, falling back to the stageId difference on a tie, and returns true when the first sorts before the second.

nodes.name: FairSchedulingAlgorithm
nodes.summary: SchedulingAlgorithm implementing fair ordering: a Schedulable running fewer tasks than its minShare is needy and goes first, needy ones are compared by running-tasks to minShare ratio, others by running-tasks to weight ratio, and ties break by name.

nodes.name: comparator
nodes.summary: Computes minShare and weight based ratios of running tasks for both Schedulables and decides ordering: needy before non-needy, then by the relevant ratio, then by name.

nodes.name: SchedulingMode.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the SchedulingMode enumeration with the values FAIR, FIFO and NONE.

nodes.name: SchedulingMode
nodes.summary: Enumeration (with a SchedulingMode type alias for Value) whose FAIR and FIFO values pick the policy used to order tasks among a Schedulable's sub-queues, and NONE is used when a Schedulable has no sub-queues.

nodes.name: SparkListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the scheduler event case classes (stage, task, job, executor, node, block manager, application and resource profile events), the SparkListenerInterface trait with one callback per event, and the no-op SparkListener base class. Listeners extend SparkListener to receive these events.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file of many case classes extending a common SparkListenerEvent trait; several are deprecated blacklist variants kept alongside the newer exclude variants.

nodes.name: SparkListenerStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: Event posted when a stage is submitted; carries the StageInfo and the job Properties (default null). Delivered to listeners through onStageSubmitted.

nodes.name: SparkListenerStageCompleted
nodes.summary: Event posted when a stage completes successfully or fails; carries the StageInfo. Delivered through onStageCompleted.

nodes.name: SparkListenerTaskStart
nodes.summary: Event posted when a task starts; carries the stage id, stage attempt id and TaskInfo. Delivered through onTaskStart.

nodes.name: SparkListenerTaskGettingResult
nodes.summary: Event posted when a task begins remotely fetching its result; carries the TaskInfo. Not posted for tasks that do not need to fetch the result remotely.

nodes.name: SparkListenerSpeculativeTaskSubmitted
nodes.summary: Event posted when a speculative task is submitted; carries stage id and attempt id, plus a taskIndex and partitionId (default -1) that a secondary constructor sets, kept for compatibility with older versions of the event that did not store the task index.

nodes.name: SparkListenerTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Event posted when a task ends; carries stage ids, task type, the TaskEndReason, TaskInfo, executor metrics and the TaskMetrics, which may be null if the task failed.

nodes.name: SparkListenerJobStart
nodes.summary: Event posted when a job starts; carries job id, time, the StageInfos and Properties, and exposes stageIds derived from the StageInfos for compatibility with older versions that stored only stage ids.

nodes.name: SparkListenerJobEnd
nodes.summary: Event posted when a job ends; carries job id, time and the JobResult.

nodes.name: SparkListenerEnvironmentUpdate
nodes.summary: Event posted when environment properties are updated; carries a map from category name to sequences of key/value pairs.

nodes.name: SparkListenerBlockManagerAdded
nodes.summary: Event posted when a new block manager joins; carries time, BlockManagerId, total max memory and optional on-heap and off-heap maxima.

nodes.name: SparkListenerBlockManagerRemoved
nodes.summary: Event posted when an existing block manager is removed; carries time and BlockManagerId.

nodes.name: SparkListenerUnpersistRDD
nodes.summary: Event posted when an RDD is manually unpersisted by the application; carries the RDD id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Event posted when the driver registers a new executor; carries time, executor id and ExecutorInfo.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorRemoved
nodes.summary: Event posted when the driver removes an executor; carries time, executor id and the removal reason.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorBlacklisted
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerExecutorExcluded: event for an executor excluded for the application; carries time, executor id and task failure count.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorExcluded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when the driver excludes an executor for the application; carries time, executor id and task failure count.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorBlacklistedForStage
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerExecutorExcludedForStage: event for an executor excluded for a stage; carries time, executor id, failure count, stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorExcludedForStage
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when the driver excludes an executor for a stage; carries time, executor id, failure count, stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeBlacklistedForStage
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerNodeExcludedForStage: event for a node excluded for a stage; carries time, host id, executor failure count, stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeExcludedForStage
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when the driver excludes a node for a stage; carries time, host id, executor failure count, stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorUnblacklisted
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerExecutorUnexcluded: event for re-enabling a previously excluded executor; carries time and executor id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorUnexcluded
nodes.summary: Event posted when the driver re-enables a previously excluded executor; carries time and executor id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeBlacklisted
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerNodeExcluded: event for a node excluded for the application; carries time, host id and executor failure count.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeExcluded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when the driver excludes a node for the application; carries time, host id and executor failure count.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeUnblacklisted
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 3.1.0 in favor of SparkListenerNodeUnexcluded: event for re-enabling a previously excluded node; carries time and host id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerNodeUnexcluded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when the driver re-enables a previously excluded node; carries time and host id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerUnschedulableTaskSetAdded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when a task set becomes unschedulable due to excludeOnFailure while dynamic allocation is enabled; carries stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerUnschedulableTaskSetRemoved
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when an unschedulable task set becomes schedulable again while dynamic allocation is enabled; carries stage id and attempt id.

nodes.name: SparkListenerBlockUpdated
nodes.summary: Event posted when the driver receives a block update; carries the BlockUpdatedInfo.

nodes.name: SparkListenerMiscellaneousProcessAdded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.2.0) announcing a miscellaneous process; carries time, process id and MiscellaneousProcessDetails.

nodes.name: SparkListenerExecutorMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Periodic update from an executor delivered via heartbeat; carries executor id, a sequence of (taskId, stageId, stageAttemptId, accumulator updates) and per-(stage, attempt) executor metrics.

nodes.name: SparkListenerStageExecutorMetrics
nodes.summary: Peak executor-level metric values for an executor and stage, written to the history log at stage completion; only seen when reading an event log, never in a live application.

nodes.name: SparkListenerApplicationStart
nodes.summary: Event posted when the application starts; carries app name, optional app id and attempt id, time, Spark user and optional driver logs and attributes.

nodes.name: SparkListenerApplicationEnd
nodes.summary: Event posted when the application ends; carries time and an optional exit code.

nodes.name: SparkListenerLogStart
nodes.summary: Internal event describing the metadata of an event log; carries the Spark version string.

nodes.name: SparkListenerResourceProfileAdded
nodes.summary: Event (since 3.1.0) posted when a ResourceProfile is added to the manager; carries the ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: SparkListenerInterface
nodes.summary: Internal trait (private[spark]) declaring one callback per scheduler event, for example onStageCompleted, onTaskEnd, onJobStart, onExecutorAdded and onApplicationEnd, plus onOtherEvent for events such as SQL-specific ones. It is the listener type consumed by the listener bus.

nodes.name: SparkListener
nodes.summary: Developer API abstract class implementing SparkListenerInterface with no-op bodies for every callback, so applications can extend it and override only the events they care about.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the empty package object for org.apache.spark.scheduler; its comment describes the package as Spark's scheduling components, including DAGScheduler and the lower level TaskScheduler.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedClusterMessage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed CoarseGrainedClusterMessage trait and the CoarseGrainedClusterMessages object holding every RPC message exchanged between the driver, executors and the cluster manager. Covers driver-to-executor commands, executor-to-driver reports, driver-internal control messages and executor allocation requests.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedClusterMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed marker trait that all coarse-grained cluster messages extend; it only adds Serializable so messages can be sent over RPC.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedClusterMessages
nodes.summary: Container object that groups all message case classes and case objects sent between driver, executors and the cluster manager (for example in Yarn, between the driver and the AM).

nodes.name: RetrieveSparkAppConfig
nodes.summary: Message carrying a resourceProfileId, used to ask for the Spark application configuration for that resource profile.

nodes.name: SparkAppConfig
nodes.summary: Message holding the Spark properties, optional IO encryption key, optional Hadoop delegation credentials, the ResourceProfile and optional log level that make up an application config.

nodes.name: RetrieveLastAllocatedExecutorId
nodes.summary: Case object message that asks for the last allocated executor id.

nodes.name: LaunchTask
nodes.summary: Driver-to-executor message wrapping a SerializableBuffer with the serialized task to launch.

nodes.name: KillTask
nodes.summary: Driver-to-executor message asking to kill a task, giving its task id, executor, whether to interrupt the thread, and a reason.

nodes.name: KillExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Message that asks to kill all executors running on a given host.

nodes.name: UpdateExecutorsLogLevel
nodes.summary: Message carrying a log level string to apply to executors (plural form).

nodes.name: UpdateExecutorLogLevel
nodes.summary: Message carrying a log level string to apply to an executor (singular form).

nodes.name: DecommissionExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Message that asks to decommission all executors on a given host.

nodes.name: UpdateDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Message carrying a byte array of delegation tokens to push to the receiver.

nodes.name: RegisterExecutor
nodes.summary: Executor-to-driver registration message with executor id, RPC ref, hostname, cores, log URLs, attributes, resources and resource profile id.

nodes.name: LaunchedExecutor
nodes.summary: Executor-to-driver message carrying the executor id of an executor that has launched.

nodes.name: StatusUpdate
nodes.summary: Executor-to-driver message reporting a task state change, with executor id, task id, state, a SerializableBuffer of data, task cpus and per-resource assignments. Its companion object adds an apply factory that takes a plain ByteBuffer.

nodes.name: ShufflePushCompletion
nodes.summary: Message carrying shuffleId, shuffleMergeId and mapIndex, reporting that a shuffle push has completed.

nodes.name: ReviveOffers
nodes.summary: Driver-internal case object message that triggers re-offering of resources.

nodes.name: StopDriver
nodes.summary: Driver-internal case object message that stops the driver endpoint.

nodes.name: StopExecutor
nodes.summary: Case object message that tells a single executor to stop.

nodes.name: StopExecutors
nodes.summary: Case object message that tells the executors to stop.

nodes.name: RemoveExecutor
nodes.summary: Driver-internal message carrying an executor id and an ExecutorLossReason, used to remove an executor.

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommissioning
nodes.summary: Message sent from executor to driver to say the executor has started decommissioning, used when decommission is triggered at the executor (for example on K8S).

nodes.name: DecommissionExecutor
nodes.summary: Object message sent from driver to executor to decommission it, used for Standalone cases where decommission is triggered at MasterWebUI or Worker.

nodes.name: ExecutorDecommissionSigReceived
nodes.summary: Object message sent to the executor itself when it receives a signal, indicating that it starts to decommission.

nodes.name: RemoveWorker
nodes.summary: Message carrying workerId, host and a message string, used to remove a worker.

nodes.name: SetupDriver
nodes.summary: Message carrying the driver RpcEndpointRef so the receiver can set up its link to the driver.

nodes.name: AddWebUIFilter
nodes.summary: Message exchanged between the driver and the AM in Yarn client mode, carrying a filter name, filter params and proxy base for the web UI.

nodes.name: RegisterClusterManager
nodes.summary: Message carrying the cluster manager (AM) RpcEndpointRef, used in executor allocation exchanges between the driver and the cluster manager.

nodes.name: MiscellaneousProcessAdded
nodes.summary: Message sent to the driver to report a miscellaneous process, with a timestamp, process id and MiscellaneousProcessDetails.

nodes.name: RetrieveDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Object message used by YARN's client mode AM to retrieve the current set of delegation tokens.

nodes.name: RequestExecutors
nodes.summary: Message that requests executors by giving the new total per ResourceProfile (including pending and running ones), locality-aware task counts, host-to-local task counts and excluded nodes.

nodes.name: GetExecutorLossReason
nodes.summary: Message used to check whether an executor was force-killed for a reason unrelated to its running tasks, for instance preemption.

nodes.name: KillExecutors
nodes.summary: Message carrying a sequence of executor ids to kill.

nodes.name: Shutdown
nodes.summary: Message used internally by executors to shut themselves down, with an exit code that defaults to 0.

nodes.name: IsExecutorAlive
nodes.summary: Message that checks whether CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend thinks the given executor is alive.

nodes.name: TaskThreadDump
nodes.summary: Message carrying a taskId, used to request a thread dump for that task.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Alternate factory on the StatusUpdate companion that takes a ByteBuffer, wraps it in a SerializableBuffer and delegates to the main StatusUpdate constructor.

nodes.name: ExecutorData.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorData, the per-executor record CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend keeps for each registered executor.

nodes.name: ExecutorData
nodes.summary: Cluster-private subclass of ExecutorInfo that groups an executor's RpcEndpointRef, RPC address, host, free and total cores, log URLs, attributes, resource info, resource profile id, registration timestamp and request time for use by CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend. It adds a mutable freeCores field to the inherited ExecutorInfo state.

nodes.name: ExecutorInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the public DeveloperApi class ExecutorInfo that carries executor details from the scheduler to SparkListeners.

nodes.name: ExecutorInfo
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi class that stores information about an executor (host, total cores, log URL map, attributes, resources info, resource profile id, registration and request time) to pass from the scheduler to SparkListeners. It has several auxiliary constructors that default the missing fields, and equality that ignores the registration and request times.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares two ExecutorInfo objects by host, total cores, log URL map, attributes, resources info and resource profile id, guarded by canEqual.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Computes a hash by folding the hash codes of the non-null compared fields with a multiplier of 31.

nodes.name: ExecutorMonitor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorMonitor, the listener ExecutorAllocationManager uses to track executor activity and detect idle or timed-out executors for dynamic allocation.

nodes.name: ExecutorMonitor
nodes.summary: SparkListener and CleanerListener that monitors executor activity for ExecutorAllocationManager. It tracks running tasks, cached RDD blocks and shuffle data per executor, computes idle timeouts, marks executors pending removal or decommissioning, and counts how executors were removed in the ExecutorAllocationManagerSource metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes in the SparkListener, CleanerListener and Logging traits; keeps mutable state in ConcurrentHashMap and AtomicLong for cross-thread safety.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears the tracked executors, the per-resource-profile counts and the next-timeout and timed-out state.

nodes.name: timedOutExecutors
nodes.summary: Returns the sorted list of executors and their ResourceProfile id that are currently timed out. When the next timeout has passed it rescans executors that are not pending removal, decommissioning or holding active shuffle data, and updates the next timeout; meant to be called from the EAM thread.

nodes.name: executorsKilled
nodes.summary: Marks the given executors as pending removal (covering kills and decommissions) and forces the timed-out list to be recomputed on the next EAM callback.

nodes.name: executorsDecommissioned
nodes.summary: Marks the given executors as decommissioning and forces the timed-out list to be recomputed on the next EAM callback.

nodes.name: getResourceProfileId
nodes.summary: Returns the resource profile id of a tracked executor, or UNKNOWN_RESOURCE_PROFILE_ID if it is not tracked; marked as for testing.

nodes.name: pendingRemovalCountPerResourceProfileId
nodes.summary: Counts executors with the given resource profile id that are pending removal.

nodes.name: decommissioningPerResourceProfileId
nodes.summary: Counts executors with the given resource profile id that are decommissioning.

nodes.name: onJobStart
nodes.summary: Listener callback that, when shuffle tracking is enabled, records which stages and shuffle ids belong to the job and marks executors holding data for re-used shuffles as active again.

nodes.name: onJobEnd
nodes.summary: Listener callback that, when shuffle tracking is enabled, removes the job from active shuffle bookkeeping and updates executors whose shuffle data is no longer in use by any active job.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Listener callback that, if the executor is still active, ensures it is tracked and increments its running task count; guards against late task start events.

nodes.name: onTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Listener callback that records the executor as holding shuffle data when a successful task belongs to a shuffle stage, then decrements the executor's running task count.

nodes.name: onExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Listener callback that starts tracking a newly registered executor with its resource profile id and logs the new total.

nodes.name: decrementExecResourceProfileCount
nodes.summary: Decrements the executor count for a resource profile id and drops the entry when it reaches zero.

nodes.name: onExecutorRemoved
nodes.summary: Listener callback that stops tracking a removed executor, updates the resource profile count, increments the metric matching how it was removed (graceful decommission, unfinished decommission, driver kill or unexpected exit), logs the statistics and requests a timeout recompute.

nodes.name: onBlockUpdated
nodes.summary: Listener callback that updates tracking when a block changes: shuffle data blocks add the shuffle when tracking is enabled, and RDD blocks are added to or removed from the executor's cached blocks, refreshing its timeout when the cached state changes.

nodes.name: onUnpersistRDD
nodes.summary: Listener callback that removes the unpersisted RDD from every executor's cached blocks and refreshes the timeout of executors left with no cached blocks.

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: Listener callback that handles the internal ShuffleCleanedEvent by cleaning up the related shuffle state.

nodes.name: shuffleCleaned
nodes.summary: CleanerListener callback that posts a ShuffleCleanedEvent to the listener bus (only when shuffle tracking is enabled) so the state is updated on the event thread.

nodes.name: isExecutorIdle
nodes.summary: Returns whether a tracked executor is idle, throwing a SparkCoreErrors error if the executor is not tracked; visible for testing.

nodes.name: executorsPendingToRemove
nodes.summary: Returns the set of executor ids that are pending removal; visible for testing.

nodes.name: executorsDecommissioning
nodes.summary: Returns the set of executor ids that are decommissioning; visible for testing.

nodes.name: ensureExecutorIsTracked
nodes.summary: Returns the Tracker for an executor, creating it and updating resource profile counts when new, and fixing up an unknown resource profile id when the real one arrives. It guards against a task start event arriving before the block manager added event (SPARK-4951).

nodes.name: updateNextTimeout
nodes.summary: Lowers the shared next-timeout value with a compare-and-set loop so that concurrent updates never raise it.

nodes.name: cleanupShuffle
nodes.summary: Removes a shuffle from the active-job map and from every executor's tracked shuffle ids.

nodes.name: Tracker
nodes.summary: Inner class holding per-executor state: resource profile id, timeout deadline, pending removal and decommissioning flags, running task count, cached RDD blocks and shuffle ids. It computes the executor's idle timeout from the idle, storage and shuffle timeouts.

nodes.name: ShuffleCleanedEvent
nodes.summary: Private listener event carrying a shuffle id; ExecutorMonitor posts it to the listener bus so shuffle cleanup is handled on the event thread, and it is not logged.

nodes.name: ExecutorIdCollector
nodes.summary: Private helper that collects up to ten executor ids for debug messages and counts the excess, to avoid overly long log lines.

nodes.name: isIdle
nodes.summary: Returns true when the executor has an idle start time and no active shuffle.

nodes.name: updateRunningTasks
nodes.summary: Adjusts the running task count by a delta (not below zero), resets the idle start time and recomputes the timeout.

nodes.name: updateTimeout
nodes.summary: Recomputes the executor's timeout deadline as the idle start plus the maximum of the idle, storage and shuffle timeouts, and asks for a timed-out list refresh if a timed-out executor got a later deadline.

nodes.name: addShuffle
nodes.summary: Records a shuffle id as held by this executor and marks it as having an active shuffle.

nodes.name: removeShuffle
nodes.summary: Removes a shuffle id and, when none remain, clears the active shuffle flag and refreshes the timeout if the executor is idle.

nodes.name: updateActiveShuffles
nodes.summary: Recomputes whether any of the executor's shuffles are in the given active set and refreshes the timeout if the executor stopped having active shuffles while idle.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds an executor id when debug logging is on, keeping at most ten ids and counting the rest as excess.

nodes.name: BlockException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockException, a package-private exception type carrying a BlockId and a message, for signalling block-related failures inside the storage package.

nodes.name: BlockException
nodes.summary: Case class extending Exception with the BlockId involved and an error message. Thrown to report a failure tied to a specific block.

nodes.name: BlockManagerDecommissioner.scala
nodes.summary: Implements block migration for a decommissioning BlockManager: background threads move cached RDD blocks and shuffle blocks to peer block managers (or to a fallback storage) with retry handling.

nodes.name: BlockManagerDecommissioner
nodes.summary: Handles block manager decommissioning retries. start() submits a single-thread RDD-block migration loop and a shuffle-block refresh loop, per-peer ShuffleMigrationRunnable threads run in a cached pool, and lastMigrationInfo() reports the last migration time and whether everything was migrated. The two loops are kept in private Runnable vals (rddBlockMigrationRunnable calls decommissionRddCacheBlocks, shuffleBlockMigrationRefreshRunnable calls refreshMigratableShuffleBlocks), which have no separate nodes.

nodes.name: ShuffleMigrationRunnable
nodes.summary: Private inner Runnable bound to one peer BlockManagerId that consumes shuffle blocks from the shared migration queue and uploads them to that peer (or copies them to the fallback storage). It stops for the peer on certain failures and requeues blocks with a retry count.

nodes.name: allowRetry
nodes.summary: Decides whether a failed shuffle block goes back on the migration queue: if the failure count is below the configured maximum it re-adds the block with the new count and logs it, otherwise it logs that it gives up and returns false.

nodes.name: nextShuffleBlockToMigrate
nodes.summary: Polls the shared shufflesToMigrate queue, sleeping one second when it is empty, until a block and its retry count is available. Throws an interrupted error if the thread is interrupted.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main loop of the per-peer migration thread. Takes a block from the queue, resolves its sub-blocks via the migratable resolver, uploads them through the block transfer service (or copies to fallback storage when the peer is the fallback id), and on IOException or SparkException decides between skipping a deleted block, falling back, stopping because the target is decommissioned, or retrying. Counts migrated shuffles and stops on interruption or error.

nodes.name: refreshMigratableShuffleBlocks
nodes.summary: Refreshes the shuffle migration state: queues locally stored shuffles not yet seen (sorted by shuffle id and map id), starts a ShuffleMigrationRunnable in the pool for each new live peer, stops threads for peers that disappeared, gives up if no peer is running, and returns true if blocks remain to be migrated.

nodes.name: stopMigratingShuffleBlocks
nodes.summary: Sets keepRunning to false on every per-peer runnable and shuts down the shuffle migration thread pool immediately.

nodes.name: decommissionRddCacheBlocks
nodes.summary: Gets the migratable RDD blocks from the BlockManager and migrates each one, returning true if any block failed replication (so another round is needed) and false when nothing is left or all succeeded.

nodes.name: migrateBlock
nodes.summary: Replicates one ReplicateBlock via BlockManager.replicateBlock using the decommission failure limit, and removes the local block when replication succeeds. Returns whether replication succeeded.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts block migration by submitting the RDD block loop and the shuffle block refresh loop to their executors when those are enabled.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Marks the decommissioner stopped (idempotent) and shuts down the RDD migration executor, the shuffle refresh executor and the shuffle migration pool, logging any errors.

nodes.name: lastMigrationInfo
nodes.summary: Returns a pair of the last migration timestamp (the minimum over the active RDD and shuffle migrations, or Long.MaxValue when finished) and a flag telling whether all blocks have been migrated.

nodes.name: BlockManagerId.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockManagerId, the externalizable unique identifier of a BlockManager (executor id, host, port, optional topology info), plus a companion object that creates and de-duplicates ids through a bounded cache.

nodes.name: BlockManagerId
nodes.summary: Developer API class identifying a BlockManager by executor id, host, port and optional topology info. Its constructors are private so instances come from the companion apply methods, which de-duplicate through a Guava cache; it serializes via Externalizable and resolves back to the cached instance on read. The companion object holds apply, the cache, getCachedBlockManagerId and the constants SHUFFLE_MERGER_IDENTIFIER and INVALID_EXECUTOR_ID.

nodes.name: hostPort
nodes.summary: Returns the host and port joined as host:port after checking the host name and that the port is positive.

nodes.name: isDriver
nodes.summary: Returns whether this id belongs to the driver by delegating to SparkContext.isDriver with the executor id.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Writes executor id, host, port and, only when present, the topology info to an ObjectOutput.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Reads executor id, host, port and the optional topology info from an ObjectInput back into the fields.

nodes.name: readResolve
nodes.summary: Deserialization hook that replaces a freshly read instance with the cached BlockManagerId for the same value.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Value equality comparing executor id, port, host and topology info.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a BlockManagerId from executor id, host, port and optional topology info and returns the cached instance. A second overload reads an id from an ObjectInput and also returns the cached instance.

nodes.name: getCachedBlockManagerId
nodes.summary: Looks the given id up in the bounded cache (maximum 10000 entries) and returns the canonical instance.

nodes.name: BlockManagerManagedBuffer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockManagerManagedBuffer, a ManagedBuffer wrapper around BlockData that ties the block read lock to the buffer's reference count.

nodes.name: BlockManagerManagedBuffer
nodes.summary: Wraps a BlockData retrieved from the BlockManager so the block's read lock is released when the buffer's references are released. If dispose is true the data is disposed when the reference count reaches zero. It bridges the BlockManager read-lock model and the network layer retain/release counts.

nodes.name: retain
nodes.summary: Increments the reference count and takes an additional non-blocking read lock on the block, asserting the lock was obtained.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Unlocks the block when unlockOnDeallocate is set, decrements the reference count, and disposes the BlockData when the count reaches zero and dispose is true.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMaster.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockManagerMaster, the client-side facade that sends messages to the driver's block manager master endpoint for registration, block location lookup, block removal and status queries, plus the endpoint name constants.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMaster
nodes.summary: Wraps the driver endpoint and heartbeat endpoint references and exposes block manager operations (register, update block info, locations, peers, removal of RDDs, shuffles and broadcasts, memory and storage status, decommission) as RPC asks. Its companion object defines DRIVER_ENDPOINT_NAME and DRIVER_HEARTBEAT_ENDPOINT_NAME. Used by every BlockManager and on the driver to stop the master endpoints.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Removes a dead executor from the driver endpoint by sending RemoveExecutor through tell and logging the result. Only called on the driver side.

nodes.name: decommissionBlockManagers
nodes.summary: Asks the driver endpoint, without blocking, to decommission the block managers of the given executor ids.

nodes.name: getReplicateInfoForRDDBlocks
nodes.summary: Synchronously asks the driver endpoint for the ReplicateBlock information of all RDD blocks stored in the given block manager.

nodes.name: removeExecutorAsync
nodes.summary: Requests removal of a dead executor from the driver endpoint without waiting for the reply.

nodes.name: registerBlockManager
nodes.summary: Registers a BlockManagerId with the driver along with its local dirs, on-heap and off-heap memory sizes and storage endpoint, and returns the updated id (with topology info) from the master. Logs a failed re-registration when the returned executor id is the invalid id.

nodes.name: updateBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Sends UpdateBlockInfo with the storage level and memory and disk sizes of a block to the driver and returns the boolean result.

nodes.name: getLocationsAndStatus
nodes.summary: Asks the driver for the locations and status of a block given the requester host, returning an Option of BlockLocationsAndStatus.

nodes.name: getLocations
nodes.summary: Asks the driver for the block manager locations of a block. A second overload takes an array of BlockIds and returns the locations for each one (this node uses the range of the multi-block overload).

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether the master knows at least one location for the block, only for blocks reported to the master.

nodes.name: getPeers
nodes.summary: Gets the ids of the other block managers in the cluster from the driver.

nodes.name: getShufflePushMergerLocations
nodes.summary: Gets unique shuffle service locations where an executor registered earlier for block push/merge with push based shuffle, filtered by hosts and the number of mergers needed.

nodes.name: removeShufflePushMergerLocation
nodes.summary: Sends a non-blocking request to remove a host from the candidate list of shuffle push mergers, triggered for example by a FetchFailedException on that host.

nodes.name: removeBlock
nodes.summary: Asks the driver to remove a block from the storage endpoints that have it, for blocks the driver knows about.

nodes.name: removeRdd
nodes.summary: Asks the driver to remove all blocks of an RDD, logs a warning if the returned future fails, and optionally waits on it with the removal timeout.

nodes.name: removeShuffle
nodes.summary: Asks the driver to remove all blocks of a shuffle, logs a warning if the returned future fails, and optionally waits on it with the removal timeout.

nodes.name: removeBroadcast
nodes.summary: Asks the driver to remove all blocks of a broadcast (optionally also from the master), logs a warning if the future fails, and optionally waits on it.

nodes.name: getMemoryStatus
nodes.summary: Returns a map from each block manager id to its maximum and remaining memory, or an empty map when there is no driver endpoint.

nodes.name: getStorageStatus
nodes.summary: Returns the StorageStatus array from the driver, or an empty array when there is no driver endpoint.

nodes.name: getBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Collects the status of a block on all block managers by asking the driver for a map of futures and awaiting their sequence, to avoid blocking the master endpoint. Throws if the combined result is null. Documented as expensive and intended for testing.

nodes.name: getMatchingBlockIds
nodes.summary: Asks the driver for the ids of existing blocks matching a filter, optionally querying the storage endpoints, and awaits the returned future. Documented as expensive and intended for testing.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the driver endpoint and the heartbeat endpoint on the driver node, sets the endpoint references to null, and logs a warning if the heartbeat endpoint could not be stopped.

nodes.name: tell
nodes.summary: Private helper that sends a message to the driver endpoint and throws an error if the reply is not true.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMasterHeartbeatEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RPC endpoint that answers block manager heartbeats on the driver. It is kept separate from the main master endpoint for performance and shares the same block manager info map.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMasterHeartbeatEndpoint
nodes.summary: Thread-safe RPC endpoint that handles BlockManagerHeartbeat and StopBlockManagerMaster messages. It looks up the sender in a shared map of BlockManagerInfo and refreshes its last-seen time, and tells unknown block managers to re-register.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Pattern-matches incoming messages: replies to a heartbeat with the result of heartbeatReceived, stops the endpoint and replies true on StopBlockManagerMaster, and ignores anything else.

nodes.name: heartbeatReceived
nodes.summary: Returns true when the driver knows the block manager (after updating its last-seen time), otherwise returns true only for the driver block manager in non-local mode. A false result tells the block manager to re-register.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMessages.scala
nodes.summary: Declares every RPC message exchanged between the block manager master on the driver and the block manager storage endpoints on executors. Messages are grouped into two sealed traits by direction.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMessages
nodes.summary: Private object that namespaces all block manager RPC messages as case classes and case objects. It has one sealed hierarchy for master-to-storage-endpoint commands and one for storage-endpoint-to-master requests.

nodes.name: ToBlockManagerMasterStorageEndpoint
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that marks all messages sent from the master to storage endpoints (remove, replicate, decommission, thread dump and similar commands).

nodes.name: ToBlockManagerMaster
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that marks all messages sent from storage endpoints to the master (registration, block updates, location queries, heartbeats and similar requests).

nodes.name: RemoveBlock
nodes.summary: Master-to-storage-endpoint message asking a block manager to remove one block; only valid for blocks the master knows about.

nodes.name: ReplicateBlock
nodes.summary: Message asking a block manager to replicate a block, carrying the existing replica locations and a maximum replica count; used to replace blocks lost to executor failure.

nodes.name: DecommissionBlockManager
nodes.summary: Case object telling a block manager to decommission itself.

nodes.name: RemoveRdd
nodes.summary: Message asking a block manager to remove all blocks that belong to the given RDD id.

nodes.name: RemoveShuffle
nodes.summary: Message asking a block manager to remove all blocks of the given shuffle id.

nodes.name: RemoveBroadcast
nodes.summary: Message asking a block manager to remove all blocks of a broadcast; the removeFromDriver flag defaults to true.

nodes.name: MarkRDDBlockAsVisible
nodes.summary: Message asking a block manager to mark an RDD block as visible.

nodes.name: TriggerThreadDump
nodes.summary: Driver-to-executor case object that triggers a thread dump.

nodes.name: TriggerHeapHistogram
nodes.summary: Driver-to-executor case object that requests a heap histogram.

nodes.name: RegisterBlockManager
nodes.summary: Request that registers a block manager with the master, carrying its id, local directories, on-heap and off-heap memory limits, its endpoint reference and a re-registration flag.

nodes.name: UpdateBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Request reporting a change in a block status (storage level, memory size and disk size) for a block manager. It is Externalizable, with a no-arg constructor for deserialization, and writeExternal and readExternal serialize the fields by hand.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Serializes the block manager id, block name, storage level and the two sizes to the output.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Restores the fields from the input by reading the block manager id, block id name, storage level and the two sizes.

nodes.name: UpdateRDDBlockTaskInfo
nodes.summary: Request linking an RDD block to the task id that computed it.

nodes.name: UpdateRDDBlockVisibility
nodes.summary: Request that sets the visibility of the RDD blocks produced by a task id.

nodes.name: GetRDDBlockVisibility
nodes.summary: Request asking whether an RDD block is visible.

nodes.name: GetLocations
nodes.summary: Request asking the master for the block managers that hold a block.

nodes.name: GetLocationsAndStatus
nodes.summary: Request asking for the locations and status of a block, given the host of the requester.

nodes.name: BlockLocationsAndStatus
nodes.summary: Reply to GetLocationsAndStatus holding the block locations, the block status and optional local directories when the data is on disk on the requester host. It asserts that the location list is non-empty.

nodes.name: GetLocationsMultipleBlockIds
nodes.summary: Request asking for the locations of several blocks at once.

nodes.name: GetPeers
nodes.summary: Request asking for the peer block managers of the given block manager.

nodes.name: GetExecutorEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Request asking for the endpoint reference of an executor by id.

nodes.name: RemoveExecutor
nodes.summary: Request to remove an executor from the master by id.

nodes.name: StopBlockManagerMaster
nodes.summary: Case object asking the block manager master to stop.

nodes.name: GetMemoryStatus
nodes.summary: Case object asking the master for the memory status of the block managers.

nodes.name: GetStorageStatus
nodes.summary: Case object asking the master for the storage status of the block managers.

nodes.name: DecommissionBlockManagers
nodes.summary: Request to decommission the block managers of the given executor ids.

nodes.name: GetReplicateInfoForRDDBlocks
nodes.summary: Request asking for replication information about the RDD blocks of a block manager.

nodes.name: GetBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Request asking for the status of a block, optionally asking the storage endpoints; the flag defaults to true.

nodes.name: GetMatchingBlockIds
nodes.summary: Request asking for all block ids that match a filter function, optionally asking the storage endpoints.

nodes.name: BlockManagerHeartbeat
nodes.summary: Heartbeat request carrying the block manager id of the sender.

nodes.name: IsExecutorAlive
nodes.summary: Request asking whether the executor with the given id is alive.

nodes.name: GetShufflePushMergerLocations
nodes.summary: Request asking for locations of shuffle push mergers, given the number needed and a set of hosts to filter out.

nodes.name: RemoveShufflePushMergerLocation
nodes.summary: Request to remove a shuffle push merger location by host.

nodes.name: BlockManagerSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics source that exposes block manager memory and disk usage as gauges. The gauges are computed from the storage status reported by the block manager master.

nodes.name: BlockManagerSource
nodes.summary: Metrics source named "BlockManager" that registers gauges (in MB) for maximum, remaining and used memory (total, on-heap and off-heap) and for disk space used. Each gauge reads the storage status from the master of the given BlockManager.

nodes.name: registerGauge
nodes.summary: Registers a gauge under the given name whose value is the result of a function of the block manager master, converted from bytes to megabytes.

nodes.name: BlockManagerStorageEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the executor-side RPC endpoint that executes commands sent by the block manager master. Block-removal commands run asynchronously on a dedicated thread pool.

nodes.name: BlockManagerStorageEndpoint
nodes.summary: RPC endpoint that takes commands from the master and applies them to the local BlockManager: remove block, RDD, shuffle or broadcast, decommission, status queries, replicate block, thread dump, heap histogram and marking RDD blocks visible. Slow removal operations are run asynchronously on a daemon thread pool that is shut down on stop.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Dispatches each master command to the local BlockManager, using doAsync for remove operations and replying directly for the rest. For shuffle removal it unregisters the shuffle with the map output tracker and the shuffle manager when they exist.

nodes.name: doAsync
nodes.summary: Runs the given body in a Future on the endpoint thread pool, replies with the result on success and sends the failure to the caller on error, logging both outcomes.

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the asynchronous thread pool when the endpoint stops.

nodes.name: BlockNotFoundException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the exception thrown when a block with a given id cannot be found.

nodes.name: BlockNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Exception taking a block id string and carrying the message "Block <id> not found".

nodes.name: BlockReplicationPolicy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable policy for choosing peers when replicating blocks, plus a random-sampling helper and two policies: a random one and a rack-aware one that follows HDFS behavior.

nodes.name: BlockReplicationPolicy
nodes.summary: Developer API trait whose prioritize method orders candidate peers for replicating a block. BlockManager replicates to each returned peer in order until the replication target is reached, and calls prioritize again after a failure.

nodes.name: prioritize
nodes.summary: Abstract method that takes the local block manager id, peers, peers already replicated to, the block id and the replica count, and returns a prioritized list of peers of at most the needed size.

nodes.name: BlockReplicationUtils
nodes.summary: Public helper object with random sampling used by the replication policies.

nodes.name: getSampleIds
nodes.summary: Draws m unique random indices out of n using the sampling algorithm by Robert Floyd, and returns them as zero-based indices.

nodes.name: getRandomSample
nodes.summary: Returns a random sample of size m from a sequence, or a shuffled copy of the whole sequence when it has no more than m elements.

nodes.name: RandomBlockReplicationPolicy
nodes.summary: Basic policy that seeds a random generator with the block id hash and picks a random sample of peers, aiming to place blocks on different hosts when possible. It logs a warning when fewer peers than replicas are available.

nodes.name: prioritize
nodes.summary: Returns a random sample of peers when there are more peers than replicas, otherwise a shuffled list of all peers.

nodes.name: BasicBlockReplicationPolicy
nodes.summary: Policy that mimics HDFS block replication: it picks one peer in the same rack, one outside the rack and the rest at random, using the topology info of the block manager ids. Without topology info it falls back to random sampling.

nodes.name: prioritize
nodes.summary: Checks from peersReplicatedTo whether in-rack and out-of-rack replication are done, then chooses one in-rack peer, one out-of-rack peer and a random sample of remaining peers, in that order. It randomly samples directly when topology info is missing or all replicas are placed.

nodes.name: BlockSavedOnDecommissionedBlockManagerException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the exception for saving a block on an executor that is already decommissioned.

nodes.name: BlockSavedOnDecommissionedBlockManagerException
nodes.summary: Exception whose message states that the given block id cannot be saved on a decommissioned executor.

nodes.name: BlockUpdatedInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the developer API case class that records the status of a block in a block manager, plus a companion factory from the UpdateBlockInfo message.

nodes.name: BlockUpdatedInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding a block manager id, block id, storage level and memory and disk sizes. Its companion object adds an apply that converts an UpdateBlockInfo message into this class.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that copies the five fields of an UpdateBlockInfo message into a BlockUpdatedInfo.

nodes.name: FallbackStorage.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the fallback storage used during storage decommissioning: shuffle files are copied to a configured Hadoop file system path and read back from there. It also provides a placeholder RPC endpoint reference and cleanup of the fallback location.

nodes.name: FallbackStorage
nodes.summary: Class that copies shuffle index and data files of a block to the fallback path and reports their block status to the master. Its companion object also holds the fallback block manager id, the lookup, registration, cleanup and read helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: The class and its companion object share one id; object methods are listed as FallbackStorage.<name>.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Copies the index file and, if present, the data file of a shuffle map output into the fallback path under app, shuffle id and hash folders, then reports their block status. It logs a warning when the block resolver is not an IndexShuffleBlockResolver.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a file of the given shuffle id exists in the fallback file system.

nodes.name: FallbackStorageRpcEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Placeholder RpcEndpointRef registered for the fallback block manager. It has no address, ignores sends, and answers every ask with true after cleaning up the fallback files when the message is RemoveShuffle.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: On a RemoveShuffle message calls FallbackStorage.cleanUp for that shuffle id, ignores other messages, and returns a future completed with true.

nodes.name: getFallbackStorage
nodes.summary: Returns a new FallbackStorage when the fallback path is configured, otherwise None.

nodes.name: registerBlockManagerIfNeeded
nodes.summary: When a fallback path is configured, registers the fallback block manager id with the block manager master using a FallbackStorageRpcEndpointRef.

nodes.name: cleanUp
nodes.summary: Deletes the fallback directory of this application, or of one shuffle id when given, if a path is set, cleanup is enabled and the app id is known. It logs success or failure.

nodes.name: reportBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Reports a block of the given length as disk-only on the fallback block manager id through the block manager master.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads a shuffle block or block batch from the fallback storage: it parses the index file for offsets, then reads the byte range from the data file and returns it as an NioManagedBuffer. Other block id types raise an internal error.

nodes.name: FileSegment.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileSegment, a small value class that references a byte range of a file by file, offset and length. Used wherever storage code needs to point at part of a file without copying it.

nodes.name: FileSegment
nodes.summary: References a particular segment of a file (possibly the whole file) via a File, an offset and a length. The constructor requires non-negative offset and length, and toString prints the file name, offset and length.

nodes.name: SparkListenerBus.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the SparkListenerBus trait, the ListenerBus specialization that dispatches each SparkListenerEvent to the matching callback of a SparkListenerInterface listener.

nodes.name: SparkListenerBus
nodes.summary: A ListenerBus for SparkListenerEvent that relays events to its SparkListenerInterface listeners. It only supplies doPostEvent and is mixed into the concrete buses that post scheduler events.

nodes.name: doPostEvent
nodes.summary: Pattern-matches an event on its concrete SparkListenerEvent type and calls the corresponding onXxx method of the listener (stage, job, task, executor, block manager, exclusion/blacklist, resource profile and other events). Unrecognized events fall through to listener.onOtherEvent.

nodes.name: SplitInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SplitInfo, a developer-API class describing one input split (input format class, host, path, length and the underlying split object), plus a companion that builds SplitInfo lists from old and new Hadoop-style splits.

nodes.name: SplitInfo
nodes.summary: Holds information about one split instance, with the input format class, host location, path, length and the underlying split. It overrides toString, hashCode and equals, and the companion object converts splits into one SplitInfo per host location.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Computes a hash code from the input format class, host location, path and the low 31 bits of the length, ignoring the underlying split.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares host location, input format class, path, length and underlying split. The source comment notes it is mostly useless because most split implementations lack equals, so it only succeeds with identity equality.

nodes.name: toSplitInfo
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates one SplitInfo for every location of a mapred InputSplit, sharing the split length. An overload at lines 75-83 does the same for a mapreduce InputSplit.

nodes.name: StatsReportListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StatsReportListener, a SparkListener that logs summary statistics (percentile distributions of task runtime, shuffle and result sizes, time percentages) when a stage completes, plus its companion helpers and the private RuntimePercentage case class.

nodes.name: StatsReportListener
nodes.summary: Simple developer-API SparkListener that collects (TaskInfo, TaskMetrics) pairs from task-end events and, when a stage completes, logs percentile distributions for task runtime, shuffle bytes written, fetch wait time, remote bytes read, result size and time percentages. The companion object holds the formatting and distribution helpers.

nodes.name: RuntimePercentage
nodes.summary: Private case class holding the executor, fetch-wait and other fraction of a task's total time, with a companion apply that derives them from the task duration and TaskMetrics.

nodes.name: onTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Appends the (TaskInfo, TaskMetrics) pair of a finished task to the buffer when both are non-null.

nodes.name: onStageCompleted
nodes.summary: Logs the stage status and prints distributions of task runtime, shuffle bytes written, fetch wait time, remote bytes read, task result size and the executor/fetch/other time percentages, then clears the buffered task metrics.

nodes.name: getStatusDetail
nodes.summary: Builds a one-line description of a StageInfo: stage id and attempt, name, status string with optional failure reason, task count and elapsed milliseconds.

nodes.name: extractDoubleDistribution
nodes.summary: Maps the task metrics through a Double-valued metric function and builds an Option of Distribution.

nodes.name: extractLongDistribution
nodes.summary: Like extractDoubleDistribution for Long-valued metric functions, converting values to Double.

nodes.name: showDistribution
nodes.summary: Logs a heading, the summary statistics and the quantiles of a Distribution using the supplied number formatter. Other overloads (lines 120-138) accept an Option, a printf-style format string, or a metric function plus task metrics.

nodes.name: showBytesDistribution
nodes.summary: Logs a distribution of a Long metric formatted as human-readable byte sizes via Utils.bytesToString. Overloads at lines 147-153 take an Option[Distribution] or a Distribution.

nodes.name: showMillisDistribution
nodes.summary: Logs a distribution of a Long metric formatted as time using millisToString. An overload at lines 155-158 takes an Option[Distribution].

nodes.name: millisToString
nodes.summary: Reformats a millisecond interval as hours, min, s or ms with one decimal place depending on its size.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Computes the fetch-wait, executor (run time minus fetch wait) and remaining fractions of the total task time from TaskMetrics.

nodes.name: StructuredStreamingIdAwareSchedulerLogging.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a Logging mix-in for scheduler components that prefixes log messages with the structured streaming query ID and batch ID read from task Properties, plus a companion object with the helpers that build those log entries.

nodes.name: StructuredStreamingIdAwareSchedulerLogging
nodes.summary: Scheduler-private logging trait that overrides logInfo, logWarning, logDebug, logError and logTrace (message and LogEntry variants, with and without Throwable) so each message is wrapped by the companion's constructStreamingLogEntry. Implementors supply the task properties, an enable flag and the query-id length; identifiers come from Properties because streaming sets them as thread-local properties that the scheduler threads cannot see.

nodes.name: constructStreamingLogEntry
nodes.summary: Wraps a lazily evaluated message in a LogEntry that prepends the query and batch IDs and fills the log context map, or returns a plain entry when disabled or the properties are null. An overload at lines 184-203 does the same for an existing LogEntry.

nodes.name: constructStreamingContext
nodes.summary: Builds the log context HashMap with lowercase query-id and batch-id keys from the available identifiers.

nodes.name: formatMessage
nodes.summary: Prepends [queryId = ...] and [batchId = ...] markers to a LogEntry using MDC keys and returns a MessageWithContext. An overload at lines 241-247 formats a plain string message.

nodes.name: getStreamingProperties
nodes.summary: Reads the query ID (optionally truncated to a given length, where -1 means no truncation) and batch ID from Properties, ignoring empty values.

nodes.name: SupportsDelegationToken.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the SupportsDelegationToken mix-in trait that lets a scheduler backend create, start and stop a Hadoop delegation token manager when security is enabled.

nodes.name: SupportsDelegationToken
nodes.summary: Mix-in trait for SchedulerBackend that holds an optional HadoopDelegationTokenManager and drives its lifecycle. Subclasses override createTokenManager and implement updateDelegationTokens to receive new tokens.

nodes.name: createTokenManager
nodes.summary: Hook that creates the token manager for the application; called once at scheduler backend start when Hadoop security is enabled. The default returns None.

nodes.name: updateDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Abstract callback invoked when a new set of serialized delegation tokens is sent to the driver.

nodes.name: setupTokenManager
nodes.summary: If Hadoop security is enabled, creates the token manager and either starts it (when renewal is enabled) or obtains tokens once into the current credentials and serializes them, then passes non-null tokens to updateDelegationTokens.

nodes.name: stopTokenManager
nodes.summary: Stops the delegation token manager if one was created.

nodes.name: TaskDescription.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskDescription, the message describing a task that is sent to an executor, and its companion object with hand-written encode/decode routines that serialize it compactly.

nodes.name: TaskDescription
nodes.summary: Describes a task passed to executors: task id, attempt number, executor id, name, index, partition id, job artifacts, properties, cpus, resources and the already serialized task. Instances are usually created by TaskSetManager.resourceOffer; the companion encodes and decodes them manually so the executor can read artifacts and properties before deserializing the task.

nodes.name: serializeStringLongMap
nodes.summary: Writes the size of a String-to-Long map followed by each key as UTF and each value as a long.

nodes.name: serializeResources
nodes.summary: Writes the nested resource map (resource name to address to amount) with counts and UTF/long entries.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Serializes a TaskDescription into a ByteBuffer: header fields, artifacts, properties (values written as length-prefixed UTF-8 bytes to avoid writeUTF limits), cpus, resources, then the already serialized task bytes.

nodes.name: deserializeOptionString
nodes.summary: Reads a boolean flag and, if set, a UTF string, returning an Option.

nodes.name: deserializeArtifacts
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a JobArtifactSet by reading the optional state (uuid and REPL class directory URI) and the jars, files and archives maps.

nodes.name: serializeOptionString
nodes.summary: Writes a boolean presence flag and the UTF string when defined.

nodes.name: serializeArtifacts
nodes.summary: Writes the optional artifact state (uuid and REPL class directory URI) and the jars, files and archives maps of a JobArtifactSet.

nodes.name: deserializeStringLongMap
nodes.summary: Reads a size-prefixed sequence of UTF key and long value pairs into a mutable HashMap.

nodes.name: deserializeResources
nodes.summary: Reads the nested resource map (resource type to address to amount) and returns an immutable map.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Reads a TaskDescription back from a ByteBuffer by mirroring encode, then slices the remaining bytes as the serialized task to be deserialized later.

nodes.name: TaskInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskInfo, the developer-facing record of one task attempt inside a TaskSet, with launch and finish times, executor, host, locality and accumulable updates.

nodes.name: TaskInfo
nodes.summary: Holds the state of a single task attempt: index, attempt number, partition id, launch time, executor, host, locality and speculative flag. It also tracks getting-result and finish times plus failed, killed and launching flags, and exposes derived status values such as running, finished, successful and a status string. It is cloneable and carries the accumulable updates for the attempt.

nodes.name: cloneWithEmptyAccumulables
nodes.summary: Clones this TaskInfo and clears the accumulables on the copy.

nodes.name: markFinished
nodes.summary: Records the finish time (asserted to be positive) and sets the failed and killed flags from the given task state.

nodes.name: status
nodes.summary: Returns a status string: GET RESULT or RUNNING while unfinished, otherwise FAILED, KILLED, SUCCESS or UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: duration
nodes.summary: Returns finish time minus launch time, and throws an error obtained from SparkCoreErrors if the task has not finished.

nodes.name: TaskLocality.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TaskLocality enumeration (PROCESS_LOCAL, NODE_LOCAL, NO_PREF, RACK_LOCAL, ANY) and a helper that checks whether a locality satisfies a constraint.

nodes.name: TaskLocality
nodes.summary: Enumeration of data locality levels a task can be launched at, ordered from PROCESS_LOCAL to ANY. The source notes that PROCESS_LOCAL is expected to be used only within TaskSetManager for now.

nodes.name: isAllowed
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given locality condition is at least as local as the constraint, using the enumeration ordering.

nodes.name: TaskLocation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed TaskLocation trait and its three case classes (executor cache, host, and HDFS cache location) plus a companion that parses location strings.

nodes.name: TaskLocation
nodes.summary: Sealed trait describing a place where a task should run, either a host or a host plus executor id. Its companion object holds the string tags for executor and in-memory (cache) locations and the apply factories that build a location from a host and executor id or parse a string from getPreferredLocations.

nodes.name: ExecutorCacheTaskLocation
nodes.summary: Case class for a location with both a host and an executor id on that host; the executor is preferred and executors on the same host are the next level of preference. Its toString uses the executor location tag.

nodes.name: HostTaskLocation
nodes.summary: Case class for a task location that names only a host; toString returns the host.

nodes.name: HDFSCacheTaskLocation
nodes.summary: Case class for a host location where the data is cached by HDFS; toString prefixes the host with the in-memory location tag.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a location string (executor_host_execid, host, or hdfs_cache_host) into the matching TaskLocation case class and rejects malformed executor strings. An overload at lines 61-63 builds an ExecutorCacheTaskLocation from a host and executor id.

nodes.name: TaskResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TaskResult hierarchy: an indirect result that points to a block, and a direct result that carries the serialized value, accumulator updates and executor metric peaks.

nodes.name: TaskResult
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the result of a task, which also carries accumulator updates and executor metric peaks.

nodes.name: IndirectTaskResult
nodes.summary: Case class referencing a DirectTaskResult that was stored in the worker BlockManager, holding the block id and its size. Used when a result is fetched later instead of being sent with the status update.

nodes.name: DirectTaskResult
nodes.summary: TaskResult that holds the task return value as a chunked byte buffer, the accumulator updates and the metric peaks. It is Externalizable, and lazily deserializes the value on the first call to value().

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Writes the value buffer, the number of accumulator updates with each update, and the metric peaks to the output.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Reads the value buffer, accumulator updates and metric peaks back from the input and resets the deserialized flag.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Returns the task value, deserializing it from the byte buffer on first use with the given serializer instance or the one from SparkEnv. The comment warns that this can be slow and should not run while holding a lock.

nodes.name: TaskResultGetter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskResultGetter, which runs a thread pool on the driver that deserializes successful and failed task results and fetches indirect results from the block manager.

nodes.name: TaskResultGetter
nodes.summary: Driver-side helper owning a daemon thread pool (size from spark.resultGetter.threads, default 4) that handles finished tasks. It deserializes direct results, fetches indirect results from the block manager, enforces the result size limit, patches the result-size accumulator, and reports back to the TaskSchedulerImpl. It also deserializes failure reasons and forwards partition completion notifications.

nodes.name: enqueueSuccessfulTask
nodes.summary: Submits a job that deserializes the TaskResult. It kills the task if the result exceeds the size limit, fetches and removes an indirect result block, reports a lost result when the block is gone, sets the result-size accumulator, and then calls handleSuccessfulTask. Failures abort the TaskSetManager.

nodes.name: enqueueFailedTask
nodes.summary: Submits a job that deserializes the TaskFailedReason (falling back to UnknownReason) and always calls handleFailedTask, even if deserialization fails. A rejected execution is ignored when the SparkEnv is stopped.

nodes.name: enqueuePartitionCompletionNotification
nodes.summary: Asynchronously calls handlePartitionCompleted on the scheduler so the DAGScheduler does not call the synchronized method directly.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the result getter thread pool immediately.

nodes.name: TaskSetExcludeList.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskSetExcludelist, the per-taskset helper that tracks task failures and excludes executors and nodes (per task or for the whole taskset), plus a companion check for whether the feature is enabled.

nodes.name: TaskSetExcludelist
nodes.summary: Helper of TaskSetManager that records task failures per executor and decides when a task, executor or node is excluded within one taskset. It posts excluded-for-stage events to the listener bus and keeps failure data for application-level exclusion by HealthTracker. In dry-run mode it stores information only and never excludes. It must be called with the TaskScheduler lock held. The companion object reads the config to decide whether exclusion on failure is enabled.

nodes.name: updateExcludedForFailedTask
nodes.summary: Records a failed task attempt for an executor, excludes the task from a host once its attempts across that host exceed the per-node limit, and excludes the executor for the stage when enough unique tasks failed on it. It then checks whether the node should be excluded too, logging and posting both the deprecated blacklisted and the excluded events.

nodes.name: getLatestFailureReason
nodes.summary: Returns the most recent failure reason recorded for this TaskSet.

nodes.name: isExecutorExcludedForTask
nodes.summary: Returns true if the executor has failed the given task index at least the configured maximum attempts per executor; always false in dry-run mode.

nodes.name: isNodeExcludedForTask
nodes.summary: Returns true if the node is excluded for the given task index; always false in dry-run mode.

nodes.name: isExecutorExcludedForTaskSet
nodes.summary: Returns true if the executor is excluded for the whole taskset; deliberately ignores application-level exclusion for speed.

nodes.name: isNodeExcludedForTaskSet
nodes.summary: Returns true if the node is excluded for the whole taskset; always false in dry-run mode.

nodes.name: isExcludeOnFailureEnabled
nodes.summary: Companion helper that checks the taskset-level config first, then the overall exclusion config, and defaults to false.

nodes.name: WorkerOffer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerOffer, a case class describing the free resources of one executor offered to the scheduler.

nodes.name: WorkerOffer
nodes.summary: Case class representing free resources on an executor: executor id, host, free cores, an optional host:port address, available executor resources and the resource profile id. It is the unit passed to the scheduler when resources are offered.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMasterEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side RPC endpoint that tracks every registered block manager, where each block lives and how much memory each manager has. Also defines BlockStatus, BlockStatusPerBlockId and BlockManagerInfo, the per-block and per-manager records it keeps.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a message-handling receiveAndReply partial function and futures used to keep slow removals off the endpoint thread.

nodes.name: BlockManagerMasterEndpoint
nodes.summary: Master-node endpoint that records which block managers are registered, which blocks each holds, and memory use per manager. It answers location, peer, status and merger-location queries, orchestrates removal of RDD, shuffle, broadcast and single blocks, and posts block manager events to the listener bus.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Dispatches each block manager message (register, update block info, get locations, remove RDD/shuffle/broadcast/block, decommission, RDD block visibility and others) to the matching private method and replies to the caller. For UpdateBlockInfo it posts SparkListenerBlockUpdated only when the update succeeds.

nodes.name: isRDDBlockVisible
nodes.summary: Tells whether an RDD block is visible: when visibility tracking is on, the block must have locations and not be in the invisible set; when it is off, always true.

nodes.name: updateRDDBlockVisibility
nodes.summary: Called after a task finishes. If the task succeeded, removes its RDD blocks from the invisible set and asks the holding storage endpoints to mark them visible; always forgets the task id. Does nothing when visibility tracking is disabled. (updateRDDBlockTaskInfo, a short sibling that records which task produced a block, is not given its own node.)

nodes.name: handleBlockRemovalFailure
nodes.summary: Builds a recover handler for block removal futures: IOException is logged and the default value returned; TimeoutException is swallowed only if the driver reports the executor as lost, otherwise rethrown.

nodes.name: removeRdd
nodes.summary: Removes all blocks of an RDD from the master metadata, from each block manager, and, where RDD fetch through the external shuffle service is enabled, from shuffle services whose original executor is gone. Returns a future of the removed-block counts.

nodes.name: removeShuffle
nodes.summary: Removes a shuffle from all storage endpoints, deletes shuffle blocks of deallocated executors through the external shuffle service, and removes merged shuffle data from push-based merger locations. Returns a combined future of boolean results.

nodes.name: removeBroadcast
nodes.summary: Sends RemoveBroadcast to every block manager (skipping the driver unless removeFromDriver is true) because the master may not know of all broadcast blocks. Failures fall back to a zero count.

nodes.name: removeBlockManager
nodes.summary: Drops a block manager from the master tables and deletes it from the location set of each block it held. Blocks with no replicas left are deregistered; with proactive replication, an RDD or test block gets a ReplicateBlock request sent to a randomly chosen remaining location. Posts SparkListenerBlockManagerRemoved.

nodes.name: addMergerLocation
nodes.summary: Records the host of a newly registered non-driver block manager as a shuffle merger location, evicting the oldest entry once the retained-locations limit is reached.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Looks up the block manager of an executor id and removes it, logging the start and completion.

nodes.name: getReplicateInfoForRDDBlocks
nodes.summary: Builds a ReplicateBlock message for each RDD block held by a block manager, using the other known locations; returns an empty list if the block manager no longer exists.

nodes.name: removeBlockFromWorkers
nodes.summary: Sends RemoveBlock to every block manager known to hold the block, without waiting for confirmation, using the shared failure handler for errors.

nodes.name: blockStatus
nodes.summary: Returns, per block manager, a future of the status of one block. It either asks each storage endpoint or reads the master record asynchronously, so the endpoint thread is never blocked. Documented as expensive and for testing.

nodes.name: getMatchingBlockIds
nodes.summary: Collects the ids of blocks matching a filter across all block managers, either by asking storage endpoints or from the master records, and flattens the results into one future.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a block manager: adds topology information, stores its local dirs, replaces an older manager on the same executor, creates a BlockManagerInfo, adds merger location when push-based shuffle is on and posts SparkListenerBlockManagerAdded. Rejects re-registration from a lost executor by returning an id with the invalid executor id.

nodes.name: updateShuffleBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Handles block updates for shuffle blocks: an index block triggers MapOutputTracker.updateMapOutput inside a Future (to avoid a deadlock noted in the source), a data block is ignored, and anything else returns false.

nodes.name: updateBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Applies a block update from a block manager to the per-manager info and to the master block-locations map, handling RDD cache visibility, external shuffle service locations for disk-persisted RDD blocks, and dropping blocks with no locations. Returns false for an unknown manager.

nodes.name: getLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the block manager ids holding a block, or an empty sequence if none are known.

nodes.name: getLocationsAndStatus
nodes.summary: Finds the best location and status for a block for a requesting host, preferring the external shuffle service on the same host for RDD blocks when enabled, then disk-persisted copies on the same host, then any active location. Adds the executor local dirs when the block is on disk on the requester host.

nodes.name: getPeers
nodes.summary: Returns the other non-driver, non-decommissioning block managers that can be used as replication peers for a given block manager.

nodes.name: getShufflePushMergerLocations
nodes.summary: Chooses merger locations for push-based shuffle: hosts of active executors first (minus filtered hosts), then, if more are needed, a random selection from previously seen merger hosts.

nodes.name: getExecutorEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Returns the storage endpoint reference for the block manager registered for an executor id, if any.

nodes.name: BlockStatus
nodes.summary: Case class holding the storage level, in-memory size and on-disk size of one block, with isCached true when the total size is above zero. The companion object offers an empty status with StorageLevel.NONE. Marked as a developer API.

nodes.name: BlockStatusPerBlockId
nodes.summary: Map of block id to BlockStatus that releases its backing hash map when the last block is removed, so idle external shuffle service entries use no memory.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Stores a block status, creating the backing hash map on first use. (get, a null-safe lookup, is not given its own node.)

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a block entry and sets the backing map to null when it becomes empty.

nodes.name: BlockManagerInfo
nodes.summary: Master-side record for one block manager: ids, max on-heap and off-heap memory, remaining memory, last-seen time, storage endpoint and the status of each block it holds. Created in BlockManagerMasterEndpoint on registration.
