nodes.name: updateBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Updates the block map and remaining-memory counter when a block is added, changed or dropped, depending on its storage level (memory, disk or invalid), and keeps the external shuffle service block statuses in sync. Writes debug logs for each case.

nodes.name: removeBlock
nodes.summary: Deletes a block from the info, returns its memory size to the remaining memory and removes it from the external shuffle service status map.

nodes.name: TimeTrackingOutputStream.java
nodes.summary: Defines TimeTrackingOutputStream, an OutputStream wrapper that times its write, flush and close calls and adds the elapsed time to shuffle write metrics.

nodes.name: TimeTrackingOutputStream
nodes.summary: Final OutputStream decorator that intercepts write calls on a delegate stream and tracks the total time spent writing so it can update shuffle write metrics. Not thread safe.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a byte range to the delegate stream and reports the elapsed nanoseconds through incWriteTime. Overloads write(int) at lines 42-47 and write(byte[]) at lines 49-54 do the same.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Flushes the delegate stream and reports the elapsed nanoseconds through incWriteTime.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the delegate stream and reports the elapsed nanoseconds through incWriteTime.

nodes.name: UnmanagedMemoryConsumer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the identifier case class and the trait for components that use memory outside Spark's unified memory management. Implementers expose an id, a memory mode and a current byte count so the memory tracking system can poll them.

nodes.name: UnmanagedMemoryConsumerId
nodes.summary: Case class identifying an unmanaged memory consumer by a component type string and an instance key. For shared memory consumers the key should be common across instances to avoid double counting.

nodes.name: UnmanagedMemoryConsumer
nodes.summary: Trait for components that allocate memory outside Spark's unified memory management and want it tracked. It requires an id, the memory mode (ON_HEAP or OFF_HEAP) and getMemBytesUsed, which a polling mechanism calls periodically; returning -1 removes the consumer from tracking.

nodes.name: RowBasedChecksum.scala
nodes.summary: Scala file defining the abstract RowBasedChecksum class and its companion object. It computes an order-independent checksum over (key, value) pairs by combining the XOR and the SUM of per-row checksums.
nodes.languageNotes: Lives under src/main/java in the core module but is a Scala source file.

nodes.name: RowBasedChecksum
nodes.summary: Abstract class that accumulates a checksum over input (key, value) pairs independent of their order. Subclasses supply calculateRowChecksum; the class XORs and sums the row checksums, mixes them with a left rotation in getValue, and reports 0 if any error occurred. The companion object folds an array of checksums into one aggregated value.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Returns the final checksum as the XOR value combined with the left-rotated SUM value, or the default 0 if an error was seen during computation.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Updates the checksum with one (key, value) pair by computing the row checksum and folding it into the XOR and SUM accumulators. Not thread safe; on a non-fatal error it logs the error and marks the checksum as failed.

nodes.name: calculateRowChecksum
nodes.summary: Abstract protected hook that computes the checksum value for a single (key, value) pair.

nodes.name: rotateLeft
nodes.summary: Private helper that rotates a Long left by 27 bit positions, used to mix the SUM accumulator before combining it with the XOR.

nodes.name: getAggregatedChecksumValue
nodes.summary: Companion object method that folds an array of RowBasedChecksum instances into one Long (acc * 31 + value), returning 0 for a null array.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the package-level documentation for org.apache.spark.memory and declares an empty package object. The doc comment describes the JVM-wide MemoryManager, the per-task TaskMemoryManager, MemoryConsumers and MemoryPools.

nodes.name: memory
nodes.summary: Empty package object for org.apache.spark.memory. Its scaladoc explains the memory management design: MemoryManager divides memory between storage and execution, TaskMemoryManager serves individual tasks, MemoryConsumers request memory from it, and UnifiedMemoryManager is the one MemoryManager implementation.

nodes.name: LogBlockIdGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LogBlockIdGenerator trait that creates unique LogBlockIds for log blocks, plus a concrete generator for python worker log blocks.

nodes.name: LogBlockIdGenerator
nodes.summary: Trait responsible for generating unique LogBlockIds. Subclasses declare their log block type and implement genUniqueBlockId; the final nextBlockId checks that the generated id has the expected log block type and throws an internal error otherwise.

nodes.name: nextBlockId
nodes.summary: Generates a new LogBlockId from the last log time and executor id and validates that its log block type matches the generator's type, throwing an internal error on mismatch.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogBlockIdGenerator
nodes.summary: LogBlockIdGenerator for the PYTHON_WORKER log block type. It builds a PythonWorkerLogBlockId from the last log time, executor id, session id and worker id given at construction. genUniqueBlockId and logBlockType are its one-line overrides.

nodes.name: LogBlockWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LogBlockWriter, which writes log lines to a temporary local file and saves the result as a disk-only block in the BlockManager.

nodes.name: LogBlockWriter
nodes.summary: Writes log entries directly to a temporary file on local disk through a counting, buffered, serialization stream and saves the file as a block in BlockManager if any log was written. Callers must call save or close to release resources; it does not support concurrent writes and closes itself when a write or save fails.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates the temp file in the local directory, wraps it in buffered and counting output streams, and opens a block serialization stream for the log line class of the block type; closes the writer and rethrows on failure.

nodes.name: bytesWritten
nodes.summary: Returns the byte count of the counting stream while it is open, otherwise the total recorded when the block was saved.

nodes.name: writeLog
nodes.summary: Serializes one LogLine to the block stream and marks that records were written. Throws if the writer is already closed or the write fails, leaving the caller to deal with possible corrupted data.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Validates the block id type, flushes and closes the serialization stream and, if records were written, saves the temp file as a block via saveToBlockManager. Always closes the writer in a finally block.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Idempotently releases resources: closes the serialization stream, deletes the temp file if it exists, nulls the streams and marks the writer closed. Cleanup failures are logged as warnings.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Test-only method that flushes the serialization stream if it is open.

nodes.name: saveToBlockManager
nodes.summary: Saves the temp file as a DISK_ONLY block with the given id and size by building a TempFileBasedBlockStoreUpdater on the BlockManager and calling save; returns whether it succeeded.

nodes.name: LogLine.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LogLine trait with its companion object and two case-class implementations, one for tests and one for python worker logs. These are the record types written to and read from log blocks.

nodes.name: LogLine
nodes.summary: Base trait for a log line with an event time in milliseconds, a sequence id and a message. The companion object maps a log block type to the ClassTag of the matching LogLine subclass.

nodes.name: getClassTag
nodes.summary: Companion method returning the ClassTag of TestLogLine for the TEST block type and of PythonWorkerLogLine for PYTHON_WORKER; any other block type throws a RuntimeException.

nodes.name: TestLogLine
nodes.summary: Case class implementation of LogLine (event time, sequence id, message) used for the TEST log block type.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogLine
nodes.summary: Case class implementation of LogLine (event time, sequence id, message) used for the PYTHON_WORKER log block type.

nodes.name: PushBasedFetchHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PushBasedFetchHelper, a helper for ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator that holds the push-based shuffle logic: fetching push-merged block metadata, tracking shuffle chunk bitmaps, reading push-merged local blocks and falling back to the original blocks on failure.

nodes.name: PushBasedFetchHelper
nodes.summary: Private helper class owned by a ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator that encapsulates push-based fetching. A push-merged block holds several shuffle chunks, each merging blocks of one reduce partition. It keeps a map of chunk bitmaps, requests merged block metadata from the shuffle client, reads push-merged local blocks, and starts fallback fetches of the original blocks through the map output tracker when a merged block or chunk fails.

nodes.name: isPushMergedShuffleBlockAddress
nodes.summary: Returns true if the block manager address belongs to the shuffle merger, i.e. its executor id equals SHUFFLE_MERGER_IDENTIFIER.

nodes.name: isRemotePushMergedBlockAddress
nodes.summary: Returns true if the address is a push-merged block address on a host different from the local block manager's host.

nodes.name: isLocalPushMergedBlockAddress
nodes.summary: Returns true if the address is a push-merged block address on the same host as the local block manager.

nodes.name: removeChunk
nodes.summary: Removes a shuffle chunk's bitmap from the chunk metadata map; run by the task thread when the iterator processes a SuccessFetchResult.

nodes.name: addChunk
nodes.summary: Stores the bitmap of a shuffle chunk in the chunk metadata map; run by the task thread when the iterator processes a PushMergedLocalMetaFetchResult.

nodes.name: getRoaringBitMap
nodes.summary: Looks up the RoaringBitmap recorded for a given ShuffleBlockChunkId, if any.

nodes.name: getShuffleChunkCardinality
nodes.summary: Returns the number of map blocks in a shuffle chunk, taken from its bitmap cardinality or 0 when no bitmap is known.

nodes.name: createChunkBlockInfosFromMetaResponse
nodes.summary: Turns the chunk bitmaps of a push-merged block into fetchable ShuffleBlockChunkIds with an approximate chunk size, registering each bitmap and returning the (block id, size, map index) tuples to fetch.

nodes.name: sendFetchMergedStatusRequest
nodes.summary: Asks the shuffle client for the metadata of each push-merged block in a FetchRequest, using a MergedBlocksMetaListener. On success it queues a PushMergedRemoteMetaFetchResult with the chunk bitmaps; on a parse error or failure it queues a PushMergedRemoteMetaFailedFetchResult.

nodes.name: fetchAllPushMergedLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Entry point run by the task thread at iterator initialization that fetches all outstanding push-merged local blocks when there are any and a host-local dir manager is available.

nodes.name: fetchPushMergedLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Fetches push-merged local blocks using cached merged directories when present, otherwise asynchronously retrieves them from the external shuffle service. If getting the directories fails it queues FallbackOnPushMergedFailureResult for each block so the original blocks are fetched.

nodes.name: fetchPushMergedLocalBlock
nodes.summary: Reads the local merged block metadata for one block and queues a PushMergedLocalMetaFetchResult; on any exception it queues a FallbackOnPushMergedFailureResult instead of reporting a fetch failure.

nodes.name: initiateFallbackFetchForPushMergedBlock
nodes.summary: Starts fetching the original blocks for a push-merged block or shuffle chunk that failed. It adjusts the iterator's block counts, asks the map output tracker for the original map sizes, for a failed remote chunk also falls back all pending chunks of the same host by merging their bitmaps, then calls the iterator's fallbackFetch.

nodes.name: RDDInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RDDInfo developer-API class describing an RDD (id, name, partitions, storage level, call site, cached sizes) and its companion that builds one from an RDD.

nodes.name: RDDInfo
nodes.summary: Developer API class holding descriptive and cache-status information about an RDD: id, name, partition count, storage level, barrier flag, parent ids, call site, operation scope and output deterministic level. It also tracks the number of cached partitions and the memory and disk sizes, is ordered by id, and its companion object creates an RDDInfo from an RDD.

nodes.name: isCached
nodes.summary: Returns true when the RDD has cached bytes in memory or on disk and at least one cached partition.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the RDD name, id, storage level, cached and total partition counts, and memory and disk sizes as a readable string.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Orders RDDInfo instances by RDD id (Ordered implementation).

nodes.name: fromRdd
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds an RDDInfo from an RDD: uses the RDD name or its formatted class name, collects parent ids from dependencies, and picks the long or short call site form depending on the event log call site configuration.

nodes.name: RollingLogWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RollingLogWriter, which writes log entries through LogBlockWriters and rolls over to a new log block when the current one reaches a size limit.

nodes.name: RollingLogWriter
nodes.summary: Writes log entries to log blocks in a rolling manner, splitting blocks by a size limit (default 32MB). It lazily gets a LogBlockWriter from the BlockManager, rolls over after a write once the size limit is reached, and on rollOver or close saves the current block under a new id from the LogBlockIdGenerator.

nodes.name: shouldRollOver
nodes.summary: Private check that returns true when a current block writer exists and its written byte count has reached the rolling size.

nodes.name: writeLog
nodes.summary: Writes a log entry, creating a new block writer if none exists and recording the entry's event time. On failure it optionally closes the current block without saving, then rethrows; after a successful write it rolls over if the size limit is reached.

nodes.name: rollOver
nodes.summary: Saves the current log block and resets the current writer so the next entry starts a new block.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Saves the current block and resets the writer and the last log time.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Test-only method that flushes the current block writer if one exists.

nodes.name: saveCurrentBlock
nodes.summary: Generates the next block id from the last log time and the executor id, logs the save with the approximate size, and calls save on the current block writer.

nodes.name: ShuffleManagerNotInitializedException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the exception raised when a shuffle migration request reaches an executor whose ShuffleManager is not yet initialized. The message reports the timeout in milliseconds, and the sender is expected to retry later.

nodes.name: ShuffleManagerNotInitializedException
nodes.summary: Exception subclass built from a timeout in milliseconds, with the message 'ShuffleManager not initialized within <timeoutMs>ms.'. Thrown when a shuffle migration request arrives before the target executor has a ShuffleManager, so the sender can retry after a short delay.

nodes.name: StorageUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds StorageStatus, which tracks per-BlockManager block statuses and memory and disk usage, and the StorageUtils helper object that disposes of mapped buffers and resolves the external shuffle service port.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file combining a stateful class with a helper object; StorageUtils uses the Sun Unsafe cleaner to free buffers eagerly.

nodes.name: StorageStatus
nodes.summary: Storage information for one BlockManager: it keeps RDD blocks grouped by RDD id and non-RDD blocks in separate maps, plus cached per-RDD and non-RDD memory and disk totals. Offers lookups of blocks and on-heap, off-heap, memory and disk usage and remaining space; an auxiliary constructor (lines 57-65) seeds it with initial blocks. Accesses are documented as not thread-safe.

nodes.name: RddStorageInfo
nodes.summary: Private case class holding the memory usage, disk usage and storage level aggregated for one RDD inside a StorageStatus.

nodes.name: NonRddStorageInfo
nodes.summary: Private case class with mutable on-heap, off-heap and disk usage counters for all non-RDD blocks of a StorageStatus.

nodes.name: blocks
nodes.summary: Returns all blocks of this block manager by concatenating the non-RDD blocks with the RDD blocks; the source notes this clones the maps and is expensive.

nodes.name: rddBlocks
nodes.summary: Returns all RDD blocks of this block manager by flattening the per-RDD block maps; documented as expensive because it copies maps.

nodes.name: addBlock
nodes.summary: Adds or overwrites a block: first updates the cached storage info, then stores the status in the per-RDD map for an RDDBlockId or in the non-RDD map otherwise.

nodes.name: getBlock
nodes.summary: Looks up one block status in O(1) by routing RDD block ids through the per-RDD map and other ids through the non-RDD map.

nodes.name: onHeapMemRemaining
nodes.summary: Computes remaining on-heap memory as the on-heap maximum minus the on-heap memory used, or None when either is not defined.

nodes.name: offHeapMemRemaining
nodes.summary: Computes remaining off-heap memory as the off-heap maximum minus the off-heap memory used, or None when either is not defined.

nodes.name: onHeapCacheSize
nodes.summary: Sums the memory usage of cached RDDs whose storage level does not use off-heap memory, when an on-heap maximum is defined.

nodes.name: offHeapCacheSize
nodes.summary: Sums the memory usage of cached RDDs whose storage level uses off-heap memory, when an off-heap maximum is defined.

nodes.name: diskUsedByRdd
nodes.summary: Returns the disk space used by a given RDD in this block manager in O(1) time, or 0 when the RDD has no stored info.

nodes.name: updateStorageInfo
nodes.summary: Applies a new block status to the cached usage totals: computes the memory and disk change against the previous status, then updates or removes the per-RDD entry, or the on-heap/off-heap and disk counters for non-RDD blocks. Totals are clamped at zero and an RDD whose usage drops to zero is removed.

nodes.name: StorageUtils
nodes.summary: Private helper object for storage code. It builds a Sun Unsafe based cleaner used by dispose, and resolves the external shuffle service port from the Spark or Yarn configuration.

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.summary: Frees a memory-mapped ByteBuffer eagerly through the Unsafe cleaner (logging a trace message); direct buffers and null are left alone. The source warns that reading a disposed buffer causes errors.

nodes.name: externalShuffleServicePort
nodes.summary: Reads the shuffle service port through Utils.getSparkOrYarnConfig; when the Yarn config holds port 0 it falls back to the value in the Spark configuration, otherwise it returns the value found.

nodes.name: TopologyMapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TopologyMapper developer API that maps a host name to topology information used when choosing executors for block replication, together with a default mapper that reports no topology and a mapper that reads a properties file.

nodes.name: TopologyMapper
nodes.summary: Abstract developer API constructed from a SparkConf with one abstract method, getTopologyForHost, that returns topology information (possibly nested with a delimiter, e.g. a rack path) for a host without the host name itself. Used to tell apart executors on different racks during block replication.

nodes.name: getTopologyForHost
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the optional topology string for a host name; implementations may return None or an empty string when topology information is unavailable, which implies the same rack.

nodes.name: DefaultTopologyMapper
nodes.summary: TopologyMapper that assumes all nodes are in the same rack: it logs a debug message for each request and always returns None.

nodes.name: getTopologyForHost
nodes.summary: Logs the requested host at debug level and returns None, so every host is treated as being in the same rack.

nodes.name: FileBasedTopologyMapper
nodes.summary: TopologyMapper backed by a properties file whose path comes from the STORAGE_REPLICATION_TOPOLOGY_FILE setting (spark.storage.replication.topologyFile). Requires the file to be configured, loads it with Utils.getPropertiesFromFile, and looks hosts up in the loaded map; selected through spark.storage.replication.topologyMapper.

nodes.name: getTopologyForHost
nodes.summary: Looks the host up in the loaded properties map and returns the match; when no entry exists it logs a warning that the host has no topology information and returns None.

nodes.name: SparkOutOfMemoryError.java
nodes.summary: Declares SparkOutOfMemoryError, the error thrown when a task cannot acquire memory from the memory manager, so that only the task is killed instead of the executor.

nodes.name: SparkOutOfMemoryError
nodes.summary: Final error class extending OutOfMemoryError and implementing SparkThrowable, with an error class, message parameters and an optional SQL state. Thrown when a task cannot get memory from the memory manager, so that the current task is killed rather than the executor; its message is built through SparkThrowableHelper.getMessage.

nodes.name: SparkOutOfMemoryError
nodes.summary: Constructor taking an error class, message parameters and an SQL state; builds the message through SparkThrowableHelper.getMessage and stores the three fields. The overload without a SQL state (lines 36-38) delegates to it with null.

nodes.name: getMessageParameters
nodes.summary: Returns the message parameters map held by the error.

nodes.name: getCondition
nodes.summary: Returns the error class (the condition) of this error.

nodes.name: getSqlState
nodes.summary: Returns the stored SQL state, or the SparkThrowable default SQL state when none was provided.

nodes.name: TooLargePageException.java
nodes.summary: Declares TooLargePageException, a runtime exception reporting that a page of a requested size cannot be allocated.

nodes.name: TooLargePageException
nodes.summary: Package-visible runtime exception whose constructor takes a size in bytes and sets the message 'Cannot allocate a page of <size> bytes.'. Signals an allocation request for a page that is too large.

nodes.name: ShuffleDataIO.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ShuffleDataIO root interface of the shuffle storage plugin system, which hands out the executor-side and driver-side shuffle components.

nodes.name: ShuffleDataIO
nodes.summary: Private interface that is the root of a plugin system for storing and reading temporary shuffle data in the sort-based shuffle. One instance is loaded per process; the default implementation uses the executor's local disks, and alternatives can be chosen with spark.shuffle.sort.io.plugin.class.

nodes.name: executor
nodes.summary: Called once on executor processes to bootstrap the shuffle data storage modules that only run on executors; returns the ShuffleExecutorComponents.

nodes.name: driver
nodes.summary: Called once on the driver process to bootstrap the shuffle metadata modules maintained by the driver; returns the ShuffleDriverComponents.

nodes.name: ShuffleDriverComponents.java
nodes.summary: Declares ShuffleDriverComponents, the driver-side part of the shuffle storage plugin: application bootstrap and cleanup, per-shuffle registration and removal, and a reliable-storage capability flag.

nodes.name: ShuffleDriverComponents
nodes.summary: Private interface for building shuffle support modules on the driver. It initializes the module once per application (returning extra configuration for executors), cleans up at application end, and has default no-op hooks for registering and removing shuffles and a default of false for reliable storage support.

nodes.name: initializeApplication
nodes.summary: Called once in the driver before executor requests are submitted; prepares the module (for example registering with external services) and returns extra configuration settings the executor components need.

nodes.name: cleanupApplication
nodes.summary: Called once at the end of the application to clean up any remaining shuffle state.

nodes.name: registerShuffle
nodes.summary: Default no-op hook called once per shuffle id when it is first generated for a shuffle stage.

nodes.name: removeShuffle
nodes.summary: Default no-op hook that removes shuffle data for the given shuffle id, optionally blocking until deletion finishes.

nodes.name: supportsReliableStorage
nodes.summary: Default method returning false; implementations return true when shuffle data lives in storage external to the executor host lifecycle.

nodes.name: ShuffleExecutorComponents.java
nodes.summary: Declares ShuffleExecutorComponents, the executor-side part of the shuffle storage plugin: per-executor initialization and creation of map output writers.

nodes.name: ShuffleExecutorComponents
nodes.summary: Private interface (since 3.0.0) for building shuffle support on executors. It initializes with the application and executor ids plus extra configs from the driver components, creates a map output writer per map task, and optionally creates a single-file map output writer.

nodes.name: initializeExecutor
nodes.summary: Called once per executor to bootstrap the module with the application id, executor id and extra configs returned by ShuffleDriverComponents.initializeApplication.

nodes.name: createMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Called once per map task to create the writer that persists all partitioned bytes written by that task, given the shuffle id, map task id and number of partitions.

nodes.name: createSingleFileMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Default method returning Optional.empty(); implementations may override it to supply a writer that optimizes transferring a single partition file as a map task's whole result.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapOutputWriter.java
nodes.summary: Declares ShuffleMapOutputWriter, the per-map-task writer interface that hands out partition writers and commits or aborts all writes atomically.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Private interface (since 3.0.0) for a top-level writer that returns child writers for persisting a map task's output and commits all writes as one atomic operation. Partition writers are requested with strictly increasing reduce partition ids, and commit returns a message with per-partition byte counts and optional metadata.

nodes.name: getPartitionWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a ShufflePartitionWriter for a given reduce partition id; called at most once per partition, with increasing ids, and not necessarily for empty partitions.

nodes.name: commitAllPartitions
nodes.summary: Commits all writes of the partition writers, makes them available to downstream reduce tasks, and returns a MapOutputCommitMessage with the bytes written per partition; checksums are passed in when shuffle checksum is enabled.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts all writes done by the partition writers, invalidating the written bytes and cleaning up resources; invoked before propagating an exception thrown by commitAllPartitions.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionWriter.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ShufflePartitionWriter interface, which a map task uses to open an output stream or an optional byte channel for the bytes of one (mapper, reducer) shuffle block.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionWriter
nodes.summary: Private interface for persisting the bytes of a single shuffle partition to a backing data store. The map task obtains it from a ShuffleMapOutputWriter, opens a stream (or a channel wrapper), writes the partition and then asks how many bytes were written.

nodes.name: openStream
nodes.summary: Opens and returns the OutputStream used to write the partition bytes; called once per partition writer and closed by the map task after the block is written or on failure.

nodes.name: openChannelWrapper
nodes.summary: Default method returning Optional.empty(); implementations may return a WritableByteChannelWrapper so spill file bytes can be transferred without copying through memory.

nodes.name: getNumBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Returns the number of bytes written through the stream or channel, which can differ from the bytes supplied by the caller (for example when compressed or encrypted).

nodes.name: SingleSpillShuffleMapOutputWriter.java
nodes.summary: Declares the optional SingleSpillShuffleMapOutputWriter interface for handing a single already-formatted spill file to the backing store.

nodes.name: SingleSpillShuffleMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Private optional extension for partition writing that is optimized for transferring one file holding the bytes of all partitions of a map task to the backing store.

nodes.name: transferMapSpillFile
nodes.summary: Transfers a file containing the bytes of all partitions written by this map task, together with the partition lengths and checksums.

nodes.name: WritableByteChannelWrapper.java
nodes.summary: Declares WritableByteChannelWrapper, a closeable thin wrapper around a WritableByteChannel used by shuffle partition writers.

nodes.name: WritableByteChannelWrapper
nodes.summary: Private interface that wraps a WritableByteChannel, mainly so the local disk shuffle implementation can provide a FileChannel that stays open across partition writes.

nodes.name: channel
nodes.summary: Returns the underlying channel that bytes are written into.

nodes.name: MapOutputCommitMessage.java
nodes.summary: Defines MapOutputCommitMessage, the immutable result object returned when a shuffle map task commits its output.

nodes.name: MapOutputCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Final class holding the partition lengths of the blocks written by a map task and optional MapOutputMetadata. Created through static of factory methods when all partitions are committed; lengths let downstream readers size buffers.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Static factory with two overloads: one takes only partition lengths (metadata empty), the other also takes a MapOutputMetadata; this node covers both, using the wider range.

nodes.name: getPartitionLengths
nodes.summary: Returns the array of per-partition block lengths.

nodes.name: getMapOutputMetadata
nodes.summary: Returns the optional metadata tag attached to the commit message.

nodes.name: ShuffleChecksumSupport.java
nodes.summary: Defines the ShuffleChecksumSupport interface with default helpers to create per-partition checksums and read their values.

nodes.name: ShuffleChecksumSupport
nodes.summary: Interface with default methods that shuffle writers mix in: one creates per-partition Checksum objects when the shuffle checksum configuration is enabled (otherwise an empty array), the other converts checksums to long values.

nodes.name: createPartitionChecksums
nodes.summary: Reads the shuffle checksum enabled and algorithm settings from SparkConf; returns checksums for each partition from ShuffleChecksumHelper when enabled, otherwise ShuffleChecksumHelper.EMPTY_CHECKSUM.

nodes.name: getChecksumValues
nodes.summary: Loops over the given Checksum array and returns their getValue results as a long array.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleDataIO.java
nodes.summary: Defines LocalDiskShuffleDataIO, the default ShuffleDataIO implementation that provides local disk based executor and driver shuffle components.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleDataIO
nodes.summary: Implementation of the ShuffleDataIO plugin that replicates the historic local shuffle storage and index file behavior. Holds the SparkConf and hands out local disk executor and driver components.

nodes.name: executor
nodes.summary: Creates a LocalDiskShuffleExecutorComponents from the stored SparkConf.

nodes.name: driver
nodes.summary: Creates a new LocalDiskShuffleDriverComponents.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleDriverComponents.java
nodes.summary: Defines LocalDiskShuffleDriverComponents, the driver side shuffle components of the local disk shuffle implementation.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleDriverComponents
nodes.summary: Driver components for local disk shuffle. It keeps the BlockManagerMaster from SparkEnv after initialization and delegates shuffle removal to it; there is no application level cleanup.

nodes.name: initializeApplication
nodes.summary: Looks up the BlockManagerMaster through SparkEnv.get().blockManager().master() and returns an empty map of extra configs.

nodes.name: cleanupApplication
nodes.summary: Does nothing; local disk shuffle needs no application level cleanup.

nodes.name: removeShuffle
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalStateException if not initialized, otherwise asks the BlockManagerMaster to remove the given shuffle, optionally blocking.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleExecutorComponents.java
nodes.summary: Defines LocalDiskShuffleExecutorComponents, the executor side shuffle components that create local disk map output writers.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleExecutorComponents
nodes.summary: Executor components for local disk shuffle. After initialization it builds an IndexShuffleBlockResolver from the BlockManager and creates LocalDiskShuffleMapOutputWriter and LocalDiskSingleSpillMapOutputWriter instances for map tasks. A second constructor marked VisibleForTesting injects the BlockManager and resolver directly.

nodes.name: initializeExecutor
nodes.summary: Takes the BlockManager from SparkEnv (throws IllegalStateException if missing) and creates the IndexShuffleBlockResolver used by the writers.

nodes.name: createMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Requires an initialized resolver and returns a new LocalDiskShuffleMapOutputWriter for the shuffle, map task and partition count.

nodes.name: createSingleFileMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Requires an initialized resolver and returns an Optional holding a new LocalDiskSingleSpillMapOutputWriter.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleMapOutputWriter.java
nodes.summary: Implements the local disk ShuffleMapOutputWriter: writes the partitions of a map task into one temporary data file and commits it with an index file through the block resolver.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShuffleMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Writes shuffle map output to a single local data file (temp file, then committed with index and checksum metadata by IndexShuffleBlockResolver). Partitions must be requested in increasing order; each partition is written either through a buffered stream or through a FileChannel, and the partition lengths are recorded for the commit message.

nodes.name: getPartitionWriter
nodes.summary: Rejects non-increasing partition ids, lazily creates the temp file through the block resolver, records the current channel position and returns a new LocalDiskShufflePartitionWriter.

nodes.name: commitAllPartitions
nodes.summary: Verifies the channel position equals the bytes written (raising an IOException mentioning a transferTo kernel bug otherwise), closes streams, writes the metadata file and commits via the block resolver, and returns a MapOutputCommitMessage with the partition lengths.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Closes open streams and deletes the temporary shuffle file, logging a warning if deletion fails.

nodes.name: cleanUp
nodes.summary: Closes the buffered stream, file channel and file stream if they were opened.

nodes.name: initStream
nodes.summary: Lazily opens the temp file in append mode as a FileOutputStream wrapped in a BufferedOutputStream of the configured size.

nodes.name: initChannel
nodes.summary: Lazily opens the temp file channel in append mode to work around a Linux kernel transferTo bug.

nodes.name: LocalDiskShufflePartitionWriter
nodes.summary: Inner ShufflePartitionWriter for one reduce partition; allows either a stream or a channel for the partition (not both) and reports the bytes written.

nodes.name: openStream
nodes.summary: Initializes the buffered stream and returns a single PartitionWriterStream; throws IllegalStateException if a channel was already requested.

nodes.name: openChannelWrapper
nodes.summary: Initializes the file channel and returns an Optional holding a single PartitionWriterChannel; throws IllegalStateException if a stream was already requested.

nodes.name: getNumBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Returns the count from the channel or stream wrapper, or 0 for an empty partition.

nodes.name: PartitionWriterStream
nodes.summary: Inner OutputStream that writes to the shared buffered file stream, counts bytes, rejects writes after close, and on close records the partition length and adds to the merged file byte count.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Overloaded write (single byte, and byte array range); this node uses the array overload range. Verifies the stream is open, writes to the buffered stream and increments the count.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Marks the stream closed and stores the byte count as the partition length without closing the shared file stream.

nodes.name: verifyNotClosed
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalStateException when writing to a closed block output stream.

nodes.name: PartitionWriterChannel
nodes.summary: Inner WritableByteChannelWrapper over the shared output FileChannel; computes the bytes written as the channel position delta and records the partition length on close.

nodes.name: getCount
nodes.summary: Returns the channel position minus the position at the start of this partition.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Records the partition length from the channel position delta and adds it to the merged file byte count, leaving the channel open.

nodes.name: LocalDiskSingleSpillMapOutputWriter.java
nodes.summary: Implements the local disk single-spill map output writer that moves one finished spill file into place as the shuffle data file.

nodes.name: LocalDiskSingleSpillMapOutputWriter
nodes.summary: SingleSpillShuffleMapOutputWriter for local disk shuffle: since the spill file already has the final format, it is moved directly to the data file location and committed with its index and checksums through IndexShuffleBlockResolver.

nodes.name: transferMapSpillFile
nodes.summary: Moves the map spill file to a temp file derived from the resolver data file path (no merging), then calls writeMetadataFileAndCommit with the partition lengths and checksums.

nodes.name: MapOutputMetadata.java
nodes.summary: Declares MapOutputMetadata, an opaque serializable marker interface for metadata attached to a committed shuffle map output.

nodes.name: MapOutputMetadata
nodes.summary: Empty Serializable interface acting as an opaque metadata tag for registering the result of committing a map task output; implementations must be serializable because it is sent from executors to the driver.

nodes.name: PackedRecordPointer.java
nodes.summary: Defines PackedRecordPointer, a package-private helper that packs a partition id and a memory record pointer into one 8-byte long.

nodes.name: PackedRecordPointer
nodes.summary: Wrapper around an 8-byte word holding a 24-bit partition number, a 13-bit page number and a 27-bit offset in page (so pages are at most 128 MB). It provides a static packing method and instance getters that decode the partition id and record pointer.

nodes.name: packPointer
nodes.summary: Static method that asserts the partition id fits in 24 bits, compresses the TaskMemoryManager page number and offset to 40 bits and ORs in the partition id shifted by 40.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Stores the packed long to decode.

nodes.name: getPartitionId
nodes.summary: Extracts the upper 24 bits as the partition id.

nodes.name: getRecordPointer
nodes.summary: Reconstructs the original record pointer from the packed page number and offset bits.

nodes.name: BroadcastFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the BroadcastFactory trait, the interface that every broadcast implementation provides so that SparkContext can instantiate a particular broadcast for a whole job.

nodes.name: BroadcastFactory
nodes.summary: Private trait describing how broadcast variables are created and removed: initialize, newBroadcast, unbroadcast and stop. It lets multiple broadcast implementations be plugged in behind one interface.

nodes.name: newBroadcast
nodes.summary: Abstract method that creates a new broadcast variable from a value, a local-mode flag, a unique id and a serializedOnly flag (which skips caching the unserialized value on the driver), returning a Broadcast.

nodes.name: TorrentBroadcastFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the BroadcastFactory implementation that creates TorrentBroadcast variables, which transfer broadcast data to executors with a BitTorrent-like protocol.

nodes.name: TorrentBroadcastFactory
nodes.summary: BroadcastFactory that builds a TorrentBroadcast for each new broadcast and delegates removal of persisted state to TorrentBroadcast.unpersist. Its initialize and stop methods do nothing.

nodes.name: newBroadcast
nodes.summary: Creates a new TorrentBroadcast from the given value, id and serializedOnly flag; the isLocal argument is ignored.

nodes.name: unbroadcast
nodes.summary: Removes all persisted state of the torrent broadcast with the given id by calling TorrentBroadcast.unpersist, optionally also on the driver and optionally blocking.

nodes.name: ExecutorClassLoader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ClassLoader an executor uses to load classes generated by the REPL, fetching class files from a Hadoop FileSystem or over a Spark RPC endpoint, plus the helper that rewrites REPL wrapper constructors and a special error type for remote loading failures.

nodes.name: ExecutorClassLoader
nodes.summary: ClassLoader (with a null parent) that reads class files from a Hadoop FileSystem or from the driver through an RPC channel when the URI scheme is spark. It honors a userClassPathFirst flag, delegates resource lookup to a ParentClassLoader, and rewrites REPL wrapper classes on load. Used to load classes defined by the interpreter on executors.

nodes.name: getResourceAsStream
nodes.summary: Returns a resource stream, trying the locally fetched class file first when userClassPathFirst is set, otherwise the parent loader first, so dynamically generated class files can be read as resources.

nodes.name: getClassResourceAsStreamLocally
nodes.summary: For names ending in .class, opens the class file through the configured fetch function and maps ClassNotFoundException to a null result, following ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream semantics.

nodes.name: findClass
nodes.summary: Finds a class either locally first (userClassPathFirst) or by trying the parent loader and then falling back to findClassLocally, wrapping unexpected failures in RemoteClassLoaderError and raising ClassNotFoundException when the class is absent.

nodes.name: getClassFileInputStreamFromSparkRPC
nodes.summary: Opens an RPC channel to the class server under the class URI and wraps it in a stream that converts 'Stream was not found' errors into ClassNotFoundException and other failures into RemoteClassLoaderError.

nodes.name: getClassFileInputStreamFromFileSystem
nodes.summary: Opens a class file under the configured directory on the given Hadoop FileSystem, converting FileNotFoundException into ClassNotFoundException.

nodes.name: findClassLocally
nodes.summary: Fetches the class file for a name, transforms it and defines the class, returning None when the class is not found; other failures are logged and either rethrown or, with userClassPathFirst, treated as not found. Always closes the input stream.

nodes.name: readAndTransformClass
nodes.summary: Reads class bytes from a stream. For REPL wrapper classes named line*$iw$ it rewrites the constructor with ConstructorCleaner so initialization code is skipped; other classes are passed through unchanged.

nodes.name: urlEncode
nodes.summary: URL-encodes each path segment of a string with UTF-8 while preserving slashes.

nodes.name: ConstructorCleaner
nodes.summary: ASM ClassVisitor that replaces each instance constructor with a minimal one that only calls the Object constructor and returns, so REPL wrapper objects do not run their initialization code on load.

nodes.name: visitMethod
nodes.summary: Visits each method; for the non-static <init> constructor it emits a stripped-down body and returns null, otherwise it returns the method visitor unchanged.

nodes.name: RemoteClassLoaderError
nodes.summary: Error raised when a class cannot be loaded because of an exception while contacting the class source. It is neither a LinkageError nor a ClassNotFoundException so the JVM retries loading the class later.

nodes.name: ExecutorExitCode.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the exit codes executors use to report specific failures to the cluster manager, and a function that turns an exit code into a readable explanation.

nodes.name: ExecutorExitCode
nodes.summary: Object holding executor exit code constants for disk store directory failure, external block store failures, heartbeat failure, TaskReaper kill and block manager re-registration failure. The values are chosen to avoid clashing with natural JVM or signal exit statuses.

nodes.name: explainExitCode
nodes.summary: Maps an exit code to a human-readable message, covering the executor-specific codes and the shared uncaught-exception and OOM codes; unknown codes above 128 are annotated as possibly caused by a signal.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsPoller.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the poller that samples executor metrics and tracks their peak values per task and per stage, feeding executor heartbeats and task results.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsPoller
nodes.summary: Polls executor metrics (on its own scheduled thread or from the heartbeater) and keeps peak values per running task and per (stage, attempt) in concurrent maps. Per-stage peaks are returned as executor updates for heartbeats and reset each time; per-task peaks are returned at task end. One instance exists per executor.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsPoller.TCMP
nodes.summary: Private case class pairing the running task count of a stage with its array of executor metric peaks.

nodes.name: poll
nodes.summary: Reads the latest executor metrics, pushes them to the optional ExecutorMetricsSource, and raises the peak of every metric for each active stage and each running task.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the scheduled polling task at the configured interval when a polling thread exists.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Registers a task: creates its metric peaks array and creates or increments the task count for its stage and attempt.

nodes.name: onTaskCompletion
nodes.summary: Decrements the stage's running task count and removes the task's metric peaks entry.

nodes.name: getTaskMetricPeaks
nodes.summary: Returns the recorded metric peaks for a task, or an array of zeros if the task is unknown or was killed before onTaskStart.

nodes.name: getExecutorUpdates
nodes.summary: Collects per-stage metric peaks since the last call as ExecutorMetrics, resets those peaks, and removes stage entries whose task count is zero. Used by the heartbeat report.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the polling thread and waits up to 10 seconds for termination.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics Source that exposes executor metric values as gauges in the metrics system, using a cached snapshot to avoid expensive repeated collection.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsSource
nodes.summary: Source that holds a volatile snapshot of executor metric values, updated by the metrics poller, and registers one gauge per metric type in its registry before registering itself with a MetricsSystem. Caching avoids gathering costly memory and procfs metrics on every read.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetricsSource.ExecutorMetricGauge
nodes.summary: Private Gauge that returns the snapshot value at a fixed metric index.

nodes.name: updateMetricsSnapshot
nodes.summary: Replaces the cached metrics snapshot with a new array of values; called by ExecutorMetricsPoller.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Creates a gauge for each executor metric type, registers them under their metric names in the registry, and registers this source with the given MetricsSystem.

nodes.name: ExecutorSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics Source for an executor, exposing thread pool gauges, per-scheme file system statistics gauges and a set of counters for task metrics.

nodes.name: ExecutorSource
nodes.summary: Source that registers gauges for the executor thread pool (active, completed, started tasks and pool sizes) and for file system read/write bytes and operations per scheme, and defines counters for task level metrics such as run time, GC time, shuffle read and write, input and output, and spill. Created per executor.

nodes.name: fileStats
nodes.summary: Looks up the Hadoop FileSystem statistics object for a scheme.

nodes.name: registerFileSystemStat
nodes.summary: Registers a gauge named after the scheme and statistic that reads a value from the scheme's file system statistics, falling back to a default when none exist.

nodes.name: InputMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataReadMethod enumeration and the InputMetrics class that tracks bytes and records read from external systems with accumulators.

nodes.name: DataReadMethod
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the ways input data was read: Memory, Disk, Hadoop and Network (a remote block manager). Marked as a developer API and not thread-safe.

nodes.name: InputMetrics
nodes.summary: Developer API class holding two LongAccumulators for bytes read and records read, with public getters and spark-private increment and set methods. Used to report metrics about reading data from external systems.

nodes.name: GenericAvroSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Kryo serializer for generic Avro containers, which sends either a schema fingerprint or a compressed schema with each datum and caches schemas, readers and writers.

nodes.name: GenericAvroSerializer
nodes.summary: Kryo Serializer for GenericContainer subtypes. If the schema was registered ahead of time, only its 64-bit fingerprint is written; otherwise the compressed schema is written. It memoizes compressed schemas, parsed schemas, fingerprints and datum readers and writers because these operations are expensive. The compression codec is created lazily from SparkEnv.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Compresses a schema's string form with the configured codec, memoizing the result per schema.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Decompresses schema bytes and parses them into a Schema, caching results by buffer.

nodes.name: serializeDatum
nodes.summary: Writes a datum: first a flag and either the registered fingerprint or the length and compressed schema, then the Avro binary encoding using a cached datum writer. The overriding write method delegates here.

nodes.name: deserializeDatum
nodes.summary: Reads the schema (by fingerprint lookup in the registered schemas or by decompressing it, throwing a SparkException for an unknown fingerprint) and decodes the datum with a cached reader. The overriding read method delegates here.

nodes.name: JavaSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Java-serialization based Serializer: JavaSerializer (the public entry point), its per-use JavaSerializerInstance, and the stream wrappers that write and read objects through ObjectOutputStream and ObjectInputStream. It is used wherever Spark serializes data with plain Java serialization.

nodes.name: JavaSerializationStream
nodes.summary: SerializationStream that writes objects with an ObjectOutputStream. It resets the stream every counterReset objects so the stream does not leak memory, and when extraDebugInfo is on it rewraps NotSerializableException through SerializationDebugger.

nodes.name: JavaDeserializationStream
nodes.summary: DeserializationStream that reads objects from an ObjectInputStream whose resolveClass uses the supplied ClassLoader and falls back to primitive type names. Its companion object (lines 98-111, private) holds the primitiveMappings map from primitive names to classes.

nodes.name: DummyInvocationHandler
nodes.summary: Object implementing InvocationHandler whose invoke always throws UnsupportedOperationException. It is the handler used when resolving a deserialized dynamic proxy class.

nodes.name: JavaSerializerInstance
nodes.summary: SerializerInstance for Java serialization. It serializes to and from ByteBuffers via ByteBufferOutputStream and ByteBufferInputStream and creates the Java serialization and deserialization streams.

nodes.name: JavaSerializer
nodes.summary: Public DeveloperApi Serializer that uses Java's built-in serialization. It reads the stream reset interval and extra-debug-info settings from SparkConf, is Externalizable so the settings travel with it, and creates JavaSerializerInstance objects with the default or context class loader.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Writes the object to the ObjectOutputStream, rewraps NotSerializableException with extra debug info when enabled, and resets the stream after every counterReset objects.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Flushes the underlying ObjectOutputStream.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying ObjectOutputStream.

nodes.name: resolveClass
nodes.summary: Anonymous ObjectInputStream override that loads the class by name through the configured ClassLoader and falls back to primitiveMappings when the class is not found.

nodes.name: resolveProxyClass
nodes.summary: Anonymous ObjectInputStream override that loads the proxy interfaces with the configured ClassLoader and returns the class of a proxy built with DummyInvocationHandler.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Reads the next object from the ObjectInputStream and casts it to the requested type.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying ObjectInputStream.

nodes.name: invoke
nodes.summary: Throws UnsupportedOperationException for any proxy method call.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes one object into a ByteBuffer by writing it through a serialization stream over a ByteBufferOutputStream.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Deserializes one object from a ByteBuffer using the default class loader. An overload (lines 133-137) does the same with an explicit ClassLoader.

nodes.name: serializeStream
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaSerializationStream over the given OutputStream with the configured reset interval and debug flag.

nodes.name: deserializeStream
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaDeserializationStream over the given InputStream with the default class loader. An overload (lines 147-149) takes an explicit ClassLoader.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaSerializerInstance using the serializer's default class loader or the thread context class loader.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable hook that writes counterReset and extraDebugInfo so the settings survive shipping the serializer.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable hook that restores counterReset and extraDebugInfo from the stream.

nodes.name: KryoSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the Kryo-based Serializer: KryoSerializer builds and configures Kryo instances (registered classes, Avro, user registrators, pooling), KryoSerializerInstance borrows and releases them, and the stream classes plus Input/Output bridges adapt Kryo to the stream interfaces. It is the alternative to Java serialization selected by configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing a configurable class with a private companion object that lists the Spark classes registered up front (lines 530-660), plus a few private helper classes.

nodes.name: KryoSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer backed by Kryo. It validates the buffer-size settings, builds Kryo instances in newKryo (registering common Spark classes, Avro containers, configured classes and user registrators), optionally pools them, and hands out KryoSerializerInstance objects. Its companion object (lines 530-660) lists the always-registered classes and the SQL/ML classes loaded by name.

nodes.name: PoolWrapper
nodes.summary: Private KryoPool wrapper that delegates borrow, release and run to a soft-reference pool built from the Kryo factory, and can rebuild that pool via reset after the class loader changes.

nodes.name: KryoSerializationStream
nodes.summary: SerializationStream that writes class-tagged objects to a Kryo output over an OutputStream, using a Kryo instance borrowed from the owning KryoSerializerInstance and released on close.

nodes.name: KryoDeserializationStream
nodes.summary: DeserializationStream that reads class-tagged objects from a Kryo input, maps Kryo's buffer-underflow error to EOFException, and exposes iterators over values and key-value pairs that stop at end of input.

nodes.name: KryoSerializerInstance
nodes.summary: SerializerInstance for Kryo. It borrows Kryo from a pool or a single cached instance, serializes to and from ByteBuffers (turning buffer overflow into a SparkException), creates the stream wrappers and reports whether Kryo auto-reset is on.

nodes.name: KryoRegistrator
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait that clients implement to register their own classes with Kryo through registerClasses; it is loaded by name from the user-registrator configuration in KryoSerializer.newKryo.

nodes.name: KryoInputObjectInputBridge
nodes.summary: Bridge that wraps a Kryo input as both an InputStream and an ObjectInput, forwarding each read method to Kryo and reading objects via readClassAndObject. readLine is unsupported.

nodes.name: KryoOutputObjectOutputBridge
nodes.summary: Bridge that wraps a Kryo output as both an OutputStream and an ObjectOutput, forwarding each write method to Kryo and writing objects via writeClassAndObject. writeChars is unsupported.

nodes.name: JavaIterableWrapperSerializer
nodes.summary: Private Kryo serializer for results of asJavaIterable: it writes the underlying Scala Iterable of the wrapper class and converts a Scala Iterable back to a Java Iterable on read. Its companion object (lines 745-759) finds the wrapper class and its underlying method by reflection.

nodes.name: newKryoOutput
nodes.summary: Creates a KryoOutput (unsafe variant when configured) with the initial buffer size and the larger of buffer size and max buffer size.

nodes.name: newKryo
nodes.summary: Builds a configured Kryo: sets registration and reference tracking, registers common Spark classes, serializers for Java-serialized and Avro types, configured classes and user registrators, Chill's Scala registrations, extra array types and loadable SQL/ML classes, then sets the class loader.

nodes.name: setDefaultClassLoader
nodes.summary: Overrides the base method to set the default class loader and rebuild the Kryo pool so new instances use it.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a KryoSerializerInstance with the unsafe and pool settings.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Writes the object with its class to the Kryo output.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Flushes the Kryo output, throwing IOException if the stream is already closed.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the output and then always releases the borrowed Kryo instance back to the serializer instance.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Checks the Kryo input for end of data and closes the stream when it is exhausted.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Reads one class-tagged object from the Kryo input and converts a buffer-underflow KryoException into EOFException.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the Kryo input and always releases the borrowed Kryo instance.

nodes.name: asIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a NextIterator over the remaining values that ends at end of input or EOFException and closes the stream when finished.

nodes.name: asKeyValueIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a NextIterator over key-value pairs read with readKey and readValue that ends at end of input or EOFException.

nodes.name: borrowKryo
nodes.summary: Borrows a Kryo from the pool, the cached instance or a fresh newKryo call, and resets it before use.

nodes.name: releaseKryo
nodes.summary: Returns a Kryo to the pool or stores it as the cached instance if none is cached; otherwise the extra instance is discarded.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes an object into a ByteBuffer using a borrowed Kryo and reports buffer overflow as a SparkException that names the max-buffer-size setting.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Deserializes an object from a ByteBuffer with a given ClassLoader, temporarily setting it on the borrowed Kryo. An overload (lines 464-477) does the same without changing the class loader.

nodes.name: serializeStream
nodes.summary: Creates a KryoSerializationStream over the given OutputStream.

nodes.name: deserializeStream
nodes.summary: Creates a KryoDeserializationStream over the given InputStream.

nodes.name: getAutoReset
nodes.summary: Reads the private autoReset field of Kryo by reflection on a borrowed instance to tell whether auto-reset is on.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the underlying Scala Iterable when the object is the asJavaIterable wrapper class, otherwise writes the object itself.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads an object and returns it as a Java Iterable, converting a Scala Iterable with asJava.

nodes.name: SerializationDebugger.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SerializationDebugger, a helper that finds the chain of fields and objects that leads to a non-serializable object and appends it to a NotSerializableException message. It walks objects with reflection on private ObjectStreamClass members and is switched off when the JVM extended debug info flag is on.

nodes.name: SerializationDebugger
nodes.summary: Singleton holding the serialization debugging logic: improveException decorates a NotSerializableException with a serialization stack, and an inner class does the object graph traversal. The enableDebugging flag depends on the JDK version and the sun.io.serialization.extendedDebugInfo property, and the reflection holder is null when the JVM internals cannot be accessed.

nodes.name: SerializationDebugger
nodes.summary: Private traversal class created for each find call. It keeps a visited set to avoid cycles and visits primitives, arrays, Externalizable and Serializable objects, returning the path to the first non-serializable object.

nodes.name: ListObjectOutput
nodes.summary: Dummy ObjectOutput that discards primitive writes and records every object passed to writeObject, so the objects written by an Externalizable.writeExternal call can be collected through outputArray.

nodes.name: NullOutputStream
nodes.summary: OutputStream that drops every byte, acting like /dev/null. Used as the target of ListObjectOutputStream.

nodes.name: ListObjectOutputStream
nodes.summary: ObjectOutputStream subclass that enables replaceObject and records each object being serialized while writing the bytes to a NullOutputStream. Used to capture the objects a custom writeObject method writes.

nodes.name: ObjectStreamClassMethods
nodes.summary: Implicit value class that adds methods to ObjectStreamClass (slot descriptors, write-object and write-replace checks, field counts and values) by delegating to private JDK methods through the reflection holder.

nodes.name: ObjectStreamClassReflection
nodes.summary: Holder of the java.lang.reflect Method and Field handles for private ObjectStreamClass members such as getClassDataLayout and invokeWriteReplace. Constructing it throws on a JVM whose internals differ, which leaves the debugger disabled.

nodes.name: improveException
nodes.summary: Returns a NotSerializableException whose message is extended with the serialization stack found by find. If debugging is disabled, reflection is unavailable, or the debugger itself fails, the original exception is returned.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Creates a new traversal instance and returns the path leading to a not serializable object, or an empty list. Handles primitives, arrays, Serializable, Externalizable and writeReplace.

nodes.name: visit
nodes.summary: Visits an object, skipping nulls and already visited objects. It dispatches on the kind of object (primitive, string, array, Externalizable, Serializable) and returns the stack of path elements when a non-serializable object is found.

nodes.name: visitArray
nodes.summary: Visits each element of an object array and returns the first non-empty child stack.

nodes.name: visitExternalizable
nodes.summary: Calls writeExternal on a ListObjectOutput to capture the objects the instance would write, then visits each captured object.

nodes.name: visitSerializable
nodes.summary: Visits a Serializable object slot by slot, using the ObjectStreamClass descriptors to find the fields of each class in the hierarchy. It follows writeReplace results and delegates to a captured-write approach for slots that define writeObject.

nodes.name: visitSerializableWithWriteObjectMethod
nodes.summary: Writes the object into a ListObjectOutputStream to collect the objects a custom writeObject emits. If an IOException occurs it visits the captured objects, otherwise it marks them all as visited.

nodes.name: findObjectAndDescriptor
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive lookup of the object to serialize and its ObjectStreamClass, repeatedly applying writeReplace until the replacement has the same class as the input.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Appends the written object to the internal buffer so it can be returned later by outputArray.

nodes.name: replaceObject
nodes.summary: Records each object seen by the stream and returns it unchanged.

nodes.name: getSlotDescs
nodes.summary: Invokes getClassDataLayout reflectively and maps each class data slot to its ObjectStreamClass descriptor.

nodes.name: Serializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable serialization API: Serializer, SerializerInstance, SerializationStream and DeserializationStream. A Serializer creates per-thread SerializerInstance objects, which in turn create the streams used to write and read objects.

nodes.name: Serializer
nodes.summary: Abstract base for serializers. It creates SerializerInstance objects through newInstance, lets callers set a default class loader for deserialization, and has a private flag saying whether serialized objects can be relocated. Implementations need a zero-arg constructor or one taking a SparkConf.

nodes.name: SerializerInstance
nodes.summary: Single-thread serializer handle that serializes and deserializes values to and from a ByteBuffer and creates serialization and deserialization streams. Multiple streams may be created from one instance if they are used within the same thread.

nodes.name: SerializationStream
nodes.summary: Abstract Closeable stream for writing serialized objects, with writeObject as the general method and writeKey, writeValue and writeAll built on it.

nodes.name: DeserializationStream
nodes.summary: Abstract Closeable stream for reading serialized objects. readKey and readValue delegate to readObject, and asIterator and asKeyValueIterator expose the content as one-shot iterators that stop on EOFException.

nodes.name: setDefaultClassLoader
nodes.summary: Stores the given class loader as the default for deserialization and returns this serializer.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Abstract factory method that creates a new SerializerInstance.

nodes.name: supportsRelocationOfSerializedObjects
nodes.summary: Private flag, false by default, telling whether reordering serialized bytes is equivalent to reordering the objects before serializing them.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Abstract method that serializes a value to a ByteBuffer.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Abstract method that deserializes a value from a ByteBuffer, with an overload at line 116 that also takes a class loader.

nodes.name: serializeStream
nodes.summary: Abstract method that wraps an OutputStream in a SerializationStream.

nodes.name: deserializeStream
nodes.summary: Abstract method that wraps an InputStream in a DeserializationStream.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Abstract general-purpose method that writes one object to the stream.

nodes.name: writeKey
nodes.summary: Writes the key of a key-value pair by calling writeObject.

nodes.name: writeValue
nodes.summary: Writes the value of a key-value pair by calling writeObject.

nodes.name: writeAll
nodes.summary: Writes every element of an iterator with writeObject and returns the stream.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Abstract general-purpose method that reads one object from the stream.

nodes.name: readKey
nodes.summary: Reads the key of a key-value pair by calling readObject.

nodes.name: readValue
nodes.summary: Reads the value of a key-value pair by calling readObject.

nodes.name: asIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a one-shot iterator over the remaining objects, built on NextIterator. It ends when readObject throws EOFException and closes the stream on close.

nodes.name: asKeyValueIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a one-shot iterator over key-value pairs by reading a key then a value on each step, ending on EOFException.

nodes.name: SerializerManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SerializerManager, which picks a serializer for blocks and shuffles and wraps streams with encryption and compression depending on the block type and configuration.

nodes.name: SerializerManager
nodes.summary: Configures serialization, compression and encryption for Spark components. It holds a default serializer and a KryoSerializer, selects Kryo automatically for primitives, primitive arrays and strings, and wraps block streams with encryption (when a key is set) and compression (by block id type).

nodes.name: setDefaultClassLoader
nodes.summary: Sets the default class loader on the internal KryoSerializer.

nodes.name: canUseKryo
nodes.summary: Returns true when the class tag is a primitive, a primitive array or a String, which are the types for which Kryo is picked automatically.

nodes.name: getSerializer
nodes.summary: Returns the Kryo serializer when auto-pick is on and the class tag allows it, else the default serializer. An overload taking key and value class tags does the same for shuffles of key-value pairs (lines 102 to 108).

nodes.name: shouldCompress
nodes.summary: Tells whether a block id type should be compressed by matching it against shuffle, broadcast, RDD and temporary block ids and returning the matching compression setting.

nodes.name: wrapStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an input or output stream first for encryption and then for compression. Two overloads cover InputStream and OutputStream.

nodes.name: wrapForEncryption
nodes.summary: Wraps an input or output stream with a crypto stream when an encryption key is defined, otherwise returns the stream unchanged. Two overloads cover both directions.

nodes.name: wrapForCompression
nodes.summary: Wraps an input or output stream with the compression codec when the block id type should be compressed. Two overloads cover both directions.

nodes.name: dataSerializeStream
nodes.summary: Serializes an iterator of values into an output stream through a buffered stream and the block serialization stream.

nodes.name: dataSerialize
nodes.summary: Serializes values into a ChunkedByteBuffer using the implicit class tag.

nodes.name: dataSerializeWithExplicitClassTag
nodes.summary: Serializes values into a ChunkedByteBuffer using an explicit class tag, with compression applied and auto-pick disabled for stream blocks.

nodes.name: dataDeserializeStream
nodes.summary: Deserializes an input stream into an iterator of values, applying decompression for the block type.

nodes.name: blockSerializationStream
nodes.summary: Creates a SerializationStream for a block, applying compression for the block type and choosing the serializer from the class tag.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the empty package object for org.apache.spark.serializer, which carries scaladoc describing the package as pluggable serializers for RDD and shuffle data.

nodes.name: serializer
nodes.summary: Empty package object of org.apache.spark.serializer used only to attach package-level documentation that points to the Serializer class.

nodes.name: MigratableResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the experimental MigratableResolver trait that lets a shuffle block resolver list, receive and hand out shuffle blocks for block migration.

nodes.name: MigratableResolver
nodes.summary: Experimental trait, since 3.1.0, that lets Spark migrate shuffle blocks. Implementations report the locally stored shuffles, accept a block as a stream, and return the blocks to migrate for a shuffle and map.

nodes.name: getStoredShuffles
nodes.summary: Returns the shuffle ids stored locally as ShuffleBlockInfo values, for use in block migrations.

nodes.name: addShuffleToSkip
nodes.summary: Marks a shuffle that should not be migrated. The default implementation does nothing.

nodes.name: putShuffleBlockAsStream
nodes.summary: Writes a provided shuffle block through a stream callback during block migration. It takes a BlockId and a SerializerManager, and support for the remote shuffle maximum disk setting is left to the implementation.

nodes.name: getMigrationBlocks
nodes.summary: Returns the list of block ids with managed buffers to migrate for a particular shuffle and map.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the experimental ShuffleBlockInfo case class that carries a shuffle id and map id for shuffle block migration.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Experimental case class holding a shuffleId and mapId in a type safe way, used by MigratableResolver. Its toString renders migrate_shuffle_<shuffleId>_<mapId>.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockPusher.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the executor-side pusher that sends a map task's shuffle blocks to remote shuffle services when push-based shuffle is enabled. Groups contiguous blocks of the shuffle data file into PushRequests, throttles them by bytes, requests and blocks in flight, and notifies the driver when the push finishes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object that holds the shared daemon thread pool, the PushRequest and PushResult case classes, and a stop() method.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockPusher
nodes.summary: Pushes the blocks of one finished shuffle map output to remote shuffle services. It is created after the shuffle writer finishes writing the shuffle file, converts the data file into PushRequests, sends them from a shared thread pool within in-flight limits, drops addresses that are unreachable, and tells the driver once all pushes are done. The companion object (lines 479-522) holds the pool and the PushRequest and PushResult case classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id.

nodes.name: PushRequest
nodes.summary: Case class describing one request to push blocks to a remote shuffle service: the target BlockManagerId, the list of block ids with their sizes, and a ManagedBuffer holding the contiguous data chunk. Its size field is the sum of the block sizes.

nodes.name: PushResult
nodes.summary: Private case class carrying the outcome of one block push: the block id string and the failure exception, which is null when the push succeeded.

nodes.name: createErrorHandler
nodes.summary: Builds a BlockPushErrorHandler whose shouldRetryError returns false when the cause is a FileNotFoundException or when the failure is a non-fatal push failure with a no-retry error code. Marked visible for testing.

nodes.name: initiateBlockPush
nodes.summary: Entry point for pushing a mapper's output. Creates a transport conf, records shuffle id, merge id and map index, builds PushRequests for the data file, randomizes their order and queues them, then either notifies the driver of completion (no requests) or submits a task to start pushing.

nodes.name: tryPushUpToMax
nodes.summary: Calls pushUpToMax and logs a warning instead of propagating any non-fatal exception, stopping the push on failure.

nodes.name: submitTask
nodes.summary: Executes a task on the block pusher thread pool if the pool exists and is not shut down. Kept as a separate method so tests can override it.

nodes.name: pushUpToMax
nodes.summary: Synchronized method that first drains deferred push requests and then regular push requests while the in-flight bytes, request and per-address block limits allow it, deferring requests whose target address is maxed out. Contains the local helpers isRemoteBlockPushable and isRemoteAddressMaxedOut.

nodes.name: sendRequest
nodes.summary: Sends one PushRequest: updates the in-flight counters, slices the request buffer into per-block buffers, randomizes block order, and calls pushBlocks on the block store client with a BlockPushingListener. The listener hands success and failure results back to the push thread pool so the next batch can be pushed.

nodes.name: sliceReqBufferIntoBlockBuffers
nodes.summary: Loads the request's ManagedBuffer into memory and slices it into one NioManagedBuffer per block using the block sizes, so only one copy of the data is kept in memory. A single-block request is returned as is.

nodes.name: updateStateAndCheckIfPushMore
nodes.summary: Synchronized method that updates bytes, requests and per-address block counters after a push result. On a ConnectException it drops queued requests for that address once, and it notifies the driver when nothing is left. Returns true when more blocks should be pushed.

nodes.name: notifyDriverAboutPushCompletion
nodes.summary: Tells the driver, through the executor backend, that all blocks of the current map task have been pushed so shuffle merge can be finalized early. Only CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend supports it; other backends log a warning. Runs at most once per pusher.

nodes.name: prepareBlockPushRequests
nodes.summary: Converts the mapper's shuffle data file into PushRequests by grouping contiguous non-empty blocks that map to the same merger location, respecting the max batch size, max blocks per address and max block size to push. Zero-length and oversized blocks are skipped.

nodes.name: createRequestBuffer
nodes.summary: Creates a FileSegmentManagedBuffer for a range of the shuffle data file. Overridable so tests can substitute it.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Companion-object method that shuts down the shared block pusher thread pool if it was created.

nodes.name: ShuffleChecksumUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds helper functions for shuffle checksum files: derives the checksum file name for a shuffle data block and verifies per-partition checksums against the data and index files.

nodes.name: ShuffleChecksumUtils
nodes.summary: Public object with utilities that work on shuffle checksum files. getChecksumFileName maps a ShuffleDataBlockId to its checksum file name, and compareChecksums recomputes each partition's checksum from the data and index files and compares it with the stored values.

nodes.name: getChecksumFileName
nodes.summary: Returns the checksum file name for a ShuffleDataBlockId (built from a ShuffleChecksumBlockId and the algorithm), or null for any other block id.

nodes.name: compareChecksums
