nodes.summary: Reads the expected per-partition checksums, then reads the data file through the index file offsets with a CheckedInputStream and returns false at the first partition whose computed checksum differs. Closes all streams in finally blocks.

nodes.name: ShuffleDataIOUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the key prefix for shuffle plugin configs passed from driver to executor and loads the configured ShuffleDataIO plugin class.

nodes.name: ShuffleDataIOUtils
nodes.summary: Private object that holds SHUFFLE_SPARK_CONF_PREFIX, the prefix of config keys passed from the driver to the executor, and loadShuffleDataIO, which instantiates the shuffle IO plugin named by the configuration.

nodes.name: loadShuffleDataIO
nodes.summary: Reads the configured shuffle IO plugin class, loads it through Utils.loadExtensions as a ShuffleDataIO, and fails with a requirement error if no valid plugin results.

nodes.name: metrics.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ShuffleReadMetricsReporter and ShuffleWriteMetricsReporter traits, the single-threaded interfaces through which shuffle read and write code reports its counters.

nodes.name: ShuffleReadMetricsReporter
nodes.summary: Trait listing the increment methods for shuffle read metrics (remote and local blocks and bytes, fetch wait time, records read, merged block and chunk counts, request durations). Implementations are assumed to be called from a single thread.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriteMetricsReporter
nodes.summary: Trait listing the increment and decrement methods for shuffle write metrics: bytes written, records written and write time. Implementations are assumed to be called from a single thread.

nodes.name: ExecutorLogUrlHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Rewrites executor log URLs using a user-supplied pattern with {{ATTRIBUTE}} placeholders, falling back to the original URLs when required attributes are missing.

nodes.name: ExecutorLogUrlHandler
nodes.summary: Takes an optional log URL pattern and, given the original log URLs and executor attributes, produces custom log URLs by substituting placeholders (and expanding {{FILE_NAME}} over the LOG_FILES attribute). If attributes are missing it logs the failure once and returns the original URLs. The companion object (lines 94-96) defines the placeholder regex.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id.

nodes.name: applyPattern
nodes.summary: Public entry point: applies the pattern when one is configured, otherwise returns the given log URLs unchanged.

nodes.name: doApplyPattern
nodes.summary: Finds the placeholders in the pattern, checks that the needed attributes (and LOG_FILES for FILE_NAME) exist, then substitutes them to build either one 'log' URL or one URL per log file name.

nodes.name: logFailToRenewLogUrls
nodes.summary: Logs once, guarded by an AtomicBoolean, that the log URLs could not be renewed, giving the reason, the required placeholders and the available attributes.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorMetrics, the serializable array-backed holder for executor and driver metric values sent in heartbeats, and a companion helper that reads current values from the metric getters.

nodes.name: ExecutorMetrics
nodes.summary: Developer API class holding one value per executor metric type in a long array indexed by ExecutorMetricType.metricToOffset. It supports lookup by name, an isSet check, construction from arrays, atomic arrays or maps, and updating peak values. The companion object (lines 90-109) provides getCurrentMetrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id; auxiliary constructors are private[spark].

nodes.name: getMetricValue
nodes.summary: Returns the stored value for a named executor metric by looking up its offset.

nodes.name: compareAndUpdatePeakValues
nodes.summary: Compares another ExecutorMetrics with this one and raises any value where the other is larger. Returns true if any metric got a new peak.

nodes.name: getCurrentMetrics
nodes.summary: Companion-object method that collects current metric values from every ExecutorMetricType getter using the given MemoryManager and returns them as one array.

nodes.name: SerializerHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Provides helpers to serialize an object into a ChunkedByteBuffer and to deserialize one back using a SerializerInstance.

nodes.name: SerializerHelper
nodes.summary: Private object with two generic helpers: serializeToChunkedBuffer writes an object into a ChunkedByteBuffer sized from an estimated size, and deserializeFromChunkedBuffer reads an object back from one.

nodes.name: serializeToChunkedBuffer
nodes.summary: Chooses a chunk size from the estimated size, writes the object through the instance's serialization stream into a ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream and returns the resulting ChunkedByteBuffer.

nodes.name: deserializeFromChunkedBuffer
nodes.summary: Opens a deserialization stream over the buffer's input stream, reads one object, closes the stream and returns the object.

nodes.name: DummySerializerInstance.java
nodes.summary: Java class providing a no-op SerializerInstance singleton that exists only so a DiskBlockObjectWriter can be constructed on the shuffle write path.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class extending a Scala abstract class; uses an anonymous inner SerializationStream.

nodes.name: DummySerializerInstance
nodes.summary: Final singleton SerializerInstance (INSTANCE) used as a placeholder because DiskBlockObjectWriter needs a serializer instance even though the shuffle write path writes through OutputStream methods. Only the returned stream's flush and close do real work (delegating to the wrapped OutputStream); all other methods throw UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: serializeStream
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous SerializationStream that forwards flush and close to the given OutputStream (rethrowing IOException via Platform.throwException) and throws UnsupportedOperationException from writeObject.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Throws UnsupportedOperationException because this dummy instance does not serialize objects.

nodes.name: deserializeStream
nodes.summary: Throws UnsupportedOperationException because this dummy instance does not deserialize streams.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Throws UnsupportedOperationException. Two overloads exist (with and without a ClassLoader, lines 84-86 and 89-91); both throw.

nodes.name: ShuffleSortDataFormat.java
nodes.summary: Defines the SortDataFormat used to sort shuffle record pointers stored as longs in a LongArray, reusing a single PackedRecordPointer as the key object. It is used by the sort-based shuffle's in-memory sorter.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class parameterized by key type PackedRecordPointer and buffer type LongArray.

nodes.name: ShuffleSortDataFormat
nodes.summary: SortDataFormat over a LongArray of packed record pointers. It reads keys into a reused PackedRecordPointer, swaps and copies 8-byte entries, and allocates by returning the single preallocated buffer after checking that it is large enough.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Loads the long at the position into the supplied reusable PackedRecordPointer and returns it. The two-argument overload (lines 33-36) throws UnsupportedOperationException because keys are reused.

nodes.name: newKey
nodes.summary: Creates a new PackedRecordPointer to be used as a reusable key.

nodes.name: swap
nodes.summary: Swaps two long entries in the LongArray through a temporary value.

nodes.name: copyElement
nodes.summary: Copies one long entry from a source LongArray to a destination LongArray.

nodes.name: copyRange
nodes.summary: Copies a range of entries between LongArrays with Platform.copyMemory using 8-byte element offsets.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Returns the preallocated buffer, asserting that it is at least as large as the requested length.

nodes.name: SpillInfo.java
nodes.summary: Package-private holder for the metadata of one spill file written by the shuffle external sorter: per-partition lengths, the file and its temp shuffle block id.

nodes.name: SpillInfo
nodes.summary: Final class with partitionLengths (sized by the partition count), the spill File and the TempShuffleBlockId; the constructor only allocates and assigns these fields. The class documentation names ShuffleExternalSorter as the writer.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object for org.apache.spark.broadcast that exists only to carry the package documentation about broadcast variables, which send immutable datasets to all nodes.

nodes.name: CommitDeniedException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the exception thrown when a task tries to commit output but the driver denies it, with a conversion to the TaskCommitDenied failure reason.

nodes.name: CommitDeniedException
nodes.summary: Private exception carrying a message plus the job id, split id and attempt number of a denied commit. It is used by the executor side when the driver refuses a task's commit.

nodes.name: toTaskCommitDeniedReason
nodes.summary: Builds a TaskCommitDenied failure reason from the job id, split id and attempt number.

nodes.name: OutputMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataWriteMethod enumeration and the OutputMetrics class that exposes bytes and records written through accumulators.

nodes.name: DataWriteMethod
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi Enumeration naming the method by which output data was written; its only value is Hadoop.

nodes.name: OutputMetrics
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi collection of two LongAccumulators for the total bytes and records written to external systems. The values are exposed through read accessors and package-restricted setters.

nodes.name: bytesWritten
nodes.summary: Returns the sum of the bytes-written accumulator.

nodes.name: recordsWritten
nodes.summary: Returns the sum of the records-written accumulator.

nodes.name: setBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Sets the bytes-written accumulator to the given value.

nodes.name: setRecordsWritten
nodes.summary: Sets the records-written accumulator to the given value.

nodes.name: NioBufferedFileInputStream.java
nodes.summary: Java InputStream that reads a file through a direct ByteBuffer and a FileChannel, avoiding the extra copy between Java and native memory that BufferedInputStream incurs. A Cleaner releases the channel and the buffer when the stream is closed or collected.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses java.lang.ref.Cleaner with a private record (ResourceCleaner) as the cleanup action instead of finalizers.

nodes.name: NioBufferedFileInputStream
nodes.summary: Final InputStream subclass that buffers a file in a direct ByteBuffer filled from a FileChannel. Implements read, bulk read, available, skip and close, with skip able to move the channel position past the buffered data. Constructors take a File and an optional buffer size (default 8192 bytes).

nodes.name: refill
nodes.summary: Private helper that refills the byte buffer from the file channel when it has no remaining bytes; returns false at end of file.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Bulk read into a byte array after bounds checking, refilling the buffer first and copying at most the remaining buffered bytes. The single-byte read() overload (lines 81-86) also uses refill.

nodes.name: skip
nodes.summary: Skips n bytes, using only the buffer when it holds enough data and otherwise discarding the buffer and moving the file channel position for the rest.

nodes.name: skipFromFileChannel
nodes.summary: Private helper that advances the file channel position by n bytes, capped at the end of the file, and returns the number of bytes skipped.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the stream by running the registered Cleaner action, and rethrows the cause of an UncheckedIOException as the original IOException.

nodes.name: ResourceCleaner
nodes.summary: Private record implementing Runnable that closes the file channel and disposes the direct byte buffer; registered with the Cleaner for the stream.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Closes the file channel (wrapping IOException in UncheckedIOException) and always disposes the byte buffer via StorageUtils.dispose.

nodes.name: ProcfsMetricsGetter.scala
nodes.summary: Reads per-process memory statistics from the procfs directory for the current JVM process and its descendants, summing virtual and resident memory for JVM, Python and other processes. Used to report process tree metrics when the corresponding executor setting is enabled.

nodes.name: ProcfsMetrics
nodes.summary: Private[spark] case class holding the summed virtual memory and resident set size totals for JVM, Python and other processes.

nodes.name: ProcfsMetricsGetter
nodes.summary: Class (with companion object holding a shared pTreeInfo instance) that computes ProcfsMetrics for the process tree of the current process by parsing each process stat file under a procfs directory (default /proc/). Becomes unavailable and reports zeros if procfs is missing, the page size cannot be determined, or a stat file cannot be read.

nodes.name: computePageSize
nodes.summary: Determines the memory page size by running `getconf PAGESIZE` (4096 under tests); on failure it marks the getter unavailable and returns 0.

nodes.name: addProcfsMetricsFromOneProcess
nodes.summary: Parses the stat file of one pid (handling spaces inside the parenthesized comm field), takes virtual and resident memory, and adds them to the JVM, Python or other bucket of the given ProcfsMetrics depending on the process name. Rethrows IOException.

nodes.name: computeProcessTree
nodes.summary: Returns the pid of the current process plus all descendant pids, or an empty set when procfs metrics are unavailable.

nodes.name: computeAllMetrics
nodes.summary: Aggregates ProcfsMetrics over every pid in the process tree; returns all zeros if unavailable or if any process cannot be read, to avoid reporting partial values.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriteMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the public DeveloperApi ShuffleWriteMetrics class, a set of accumulators for bytes written, records written and write time of a task shuffle output.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriteMetrics
nodes.summary: Collection of three LongAccumulators (bytes written, records written, write time in nanoseconds) exposed through read accessors and updated through the ShuffleWriteMetricsReporter inc/dec methods. Not thread-safe.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the package object for org.apache.spark.executor, whose scaladoc describes the package as executor components used with various cluster managers and points to Executor.

nodes.name: executor
nodes.summary: Empty package object that exists to hold the package-level scaladoc for org.apache.spark.executor.

nodes.name: RpcAddress.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcAddress, the host and port address of an RPC environment, together with its companion factory methods for building one from a URI or a spark:// URL.

nodes.name: RpcAddress
nodes.summary: Case class holding a host and port with hostPort and toSparkURL ("spark://host:port") helpers. The companion object normalizes the host in apply and offers fromUrlString and fromSparkURL parsers.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds an RpcAddress after normalizing the host with Utils.normalizeIpIfNeeded.

nodes.name: fromUrlString
nodes.summary: Parses a URI string and returns the RpcAddress made of its host and port.

nodes.name: fromSparkURL
nodes.summary: Extracts host and port from a "spark://host:port" URL using Utils.extractHostPortFromSparkUrl and returns the RpcAddress.

nodes.name: CryptoStreamUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Utility object for IO encryption: wraps output/input streams and byte channels with encrypting or decrypting streams, writes and reads a random initialization vector, and generates encryption keys from Spark configuration.

nodes.name: CryptoStreamUtils
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object that creates encrypted OutputStream/WritableByteChannel and decrypted InputStream/ReadableByteChannel wrappers (the IV is written first and read back first), builds the crypto Properties from the spark.io.encryption.commons.config. prefix, and creates keys using the configured key size and algorithm.

nodes.name: createCryptoOutputStream
nodes.summary: Writes a fresh initialization vector to the given OutputStream and returns a CryptoOutputStream that encrypts everything written after it.

nodes.name: createWritableChannel
nodes.summary: Wraps a WritableByteChannel in a CryptoHelperChannel, writes the initialization vector, and returns an encrypting CryptoOutputStream over it.

nodes.name: createCryptoInputStream
nodes.summary: Reads the initialization vector from the start of the InputStream and returns a CryptoInputStream that decrypts the rest.

nodes.name: createReadableChannel
nodes.summary: Reads the initialization vector from the ReadableByteChannel and returns a CryptoInputStream that decrypts the remaining data.

nodes.name: toCryptoConf
nodes.summary: Converts the SparkConf entries under the spark.io.encryption.commons.config. prefix into a Properties object via CryptoUtils.toCryptoConf.

nodes.name: createKey
nodes.summary: Creates a new encryption key using the configured key size in bits and key generation algorithm.

nodes.name: createInitializationVector
nodes.summary: Generates a 16-byte initialization vector with a secure random and logs a warning if creating it takes over 2000 ms.

nodes.name: CryptoHelperChannel
nodes.summary: Private WritableByteChannel wrapper that loops until all bytes of a buffer are written to the underlying channel; a workaround for CRYPTO-125 as stated in the source.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the whole source buffer to the sink channel, repeating until no bytes remain, and returns the byte count.

nodes.name: CryptoParams
nodes.summary: Private holder that derives the AES SecretKeySpec, cipher transformation and crypto Properties from a key and a SparkConf.

nodes.name: HadoopDelegationTokenProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the DeveloperApi trait HadoopDelegationTokenProvider, the extension point through which a service supplies delegation tokens and renewal times.

nodes.name: HadoopDelegationTokenProvider
nodes.summary: Trait with a unique serviceName, a delegationTokensRequired check (by default tied to whether Hadoop security is enabled) and obtainDelegationTokens, which adds tokens to Credentials and returns the next renewal time if renewable.

nodes.name: serviceName
nodes.summary: Abstract name of the service providing delegation tokens; must be unique and is used internally to tell providers apart.

nodes.name: delegationTokensRequired
nodes.summary: Abstract check for whether delegation tokens are required for this service given the Spark and Hadoop configuration.

nodes.name: obtainDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Abstract method that obtains delegation tokens for the service, adds them to the given Credentials, and returns the next renewal time as an Option[Long].

nodes.name: SocketAuthHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Implements a simple shared-secret authentication protocol for sockets: one side sends the secret, the other compares it and replies "ok" or "err". Used by the socket servers that talk to external processes.

nodes.name: SocketAuthHelper
nodes.summary: Class holding the SparkConf, the generated auth secret and the unix-domain-socket settings. Provides authClient (server side checks the client secret), authToServer (client side sends the secret and checks the reply) and length-prefixed UTF-8 socket read/write helpers. Closes the socket on failure.

nodes.name: authClient
nodes.summary: Server-side check on a Socket: sets a 10 second timeout, reads the client secret, compares it in constant time, replies "ok" or "err", and closes the socket if authentication fails. The SocketChannel overload (lines 56-59) returns immediately for unix domain sockets and otherwise delegates here.

nodes.name: authToServer
nodes.summary: Client-side authentication: writes the secret to the socket and expects "ok" in reply, throwing IllegalArgumentException and closing the socket otherwise; skipped for unix domain sockets.

nodes.name: readUtf8
nodes.summary: Reads a length-prefixed UTF-8 string from the socket input stream.

nodes.name: writeUtf8
nodes.summary: Writes a UTF-8 string with a leading int length to the socket output stream and flushes.

nodes.name: SocketAuthServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a one-connection authenticated socket server run in a daemon thread, a variant that runs a user function on the connection, and a convenience for serving data written to an output stream. Used to exchange data with external processes.

nodes.name: SocketAuthServer
nodes.summary: Abstract class (with companion object) that opens a loopback TCP or unix domain server socket on construction, accepts a single connection within a configured timeout, authenticates it with SocketAuthHelper and calls handleConnection, delivering the result or error through a Promise read by getResult. The companion provides serveToStream.

nodes.name: startServer
nodes.summary: Private method run during construction: binds a unix domain or loopback server channel, sets the accept timeout, starts a daemon thread that accepts, authenticates and handles one connection, then closes the server; returns the connection info (path or port) and the secret.

nodes.name: handleConnection
nodes.summary: Abstract hook, called after the client is authenticated; any error cleans up the connection and server and is propagated to getResult.

nodes.name: getResult
nodes.summary: Blocks (indefinitely, or up to the given Duration in the second overload) for handleConnection to finish and returns its result, using ThreadUtils.awaitResult on the promise future.

nodes.name: SocketFuncServer
nodes.summary: SocketAuthServer subclass whose handleConnection simply runs a supplied function on the authenticated SocketChannel.

nodes.name: serveToStream
nodes.summary: Companion helper that starts a SocketFuncServer whose handler wraps the socket in a BufferedOutputStream, runs the caller writeFunc, and closes the stream; returns an array of connection info, secret and the server object.

nodes.name: RpcCallContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RpcCallContext trait, the callback an RpcEndpoint uses to reply to a message sender with a response or a failure, and to read the sender address. It is thread-safe and can be called from any thread.

nodes.name: RpcCallContext
nodes.summary: Trait with reply(response), sendFailure(e) and senderAddress; handed to RpcEndpoint.receiveAndReply so the endpoint can answer an ask or report an error. Safe to call from any thread.

nodes.name: RpcEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the endpoint side of the RPC layer: the RpcEnvFactory trait, the RpcEndpoint trait with its life cycle callbacks, and the ThreadSafe, Isolated and IsolatedThreadSafe endpoint variants.

nodes.name: RpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Base trait for a message-handling RPC endpoint. Defines receive, receiveAndReply and the onError, onConnected, onDisconnected, onNetworkError, onStart and onStop callbacks, with the lifecycle constructor -> onStart -> receive* -> onStop. Receive may be called concurrently unless ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint is used.

nodes.name: RpcEnvFactory
nodes.summary: Trait for a factory that creates an RpcEnv from an RpcEnvConfig. Implementations must have an empty constructor so they can be created by reflection.

nodes.name: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Marker trait extending RpcEndpoint that requires RpcEnv to deliver messages thread-safely: processing of one message happens before the next for the same endpoint, though not necessarily on the same thread.

nodes.name: IsolatedRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Endpoint trait that uses a dedicated thread pool for message delivery; threadCount declares how many threads to use, and more than one means messages can arrive concurrently and out of order.

nodes.name: IsolatedThreadSafeRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Isolated endpoint that fixes threadCount at 1 so messages are handled one at a time, giving thread-safe handling on a dedicated thread.

nodes.name: self
nodes.summary: Final accessor returning this endpoint RpcEndpointRef by asking rpcEnv.endpointRef(this); valid only after onStart and null after onStop.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles one-way messages sent through RpcEndpointRef.send or RpcCallContext.reply. The default throws a SparkException for any message.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles messages sent through RpcEndpointRef.ask. The default replies to the sender with a failure through the RpcCallContext.

nodes.name: onError
nodes.summary: Invoked when an exception is thrown while handling a message; by default rethrows the cause and lets RpcEnv deal with it.

nodes.name: onConnected
nodes.summary: Callback invoked when a remote address connects to the current node; does nothing by default.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: Callback invoked when a remote address is lost; does nothing by default.

nodes.name: onNetworkError
nodes.summary: Callback invoked on a network error in the connection with a remote address; does nothing by default.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Callback invoked before the endpoint starts handling any message; does nothing by default.

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Callback invoked when the endpoint is stopping; self is null at this point so it cannot be used to send or ask. Does nothing by default.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Final convenience method that stops this endpoint by calling rpcEnv.stop with its own reference if self is not null.

nodes.name: threadCount
nodes.summary: Final override of threadCount returning 1 so the dedicated pool has a single thread.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointAddress.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcEndpointAddress, the address identifier of an RPC endpoint (RpcAddress plus endpoint name), and its companion factories including the parser for spark:// URLs.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointAddress
nodes.summary: Case class holding a nullable RpcAddress and a required endpoint name; toString renders spark://name@host:port or spark-client://name when the address is null (client-only connection). The companion object builds instances from host, port and name or by parsing a Spark URL.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a spark://name@host:port URL with java.net.URI into an RpcEndpointAddress and throws a SparkException when the scheme, host, port, name, path, fragment or query are invalid. An overload apply(host, port, name) at lines 49-51 builds the address directly.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointNotFoundException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the RpcEndpointNotFoundException, a SparkException thrown when an endpoint cannot be found for a given URI.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Package-private SparkException subclass with the message "Cannot find endpoint: <uri>", used when an endpoint lookup fails.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointRef.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcEndpointRef, the serializable, thread-safe handle for sending one-way or request-reply messages to a remote RpcEndpoint, and AbortableRpcFuture, a Future wrapper with an abort hook.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Abstract, serializable, thread-safe reference to an RpcEndpoint with send (fire-and-forget), ask (returns a Future), askAbortable and blocking askSync. It reads a default ask timeout from SparkConf via RpcUtils.askRpcTimeout, and each ask sends the message once without retry.

nodes.name: AbortableRpcFuture
nodes.summary: Wraps a Future and an onAbort callback and exposes abort(t); used for long-running RPCs that may need to be cancelled.

nodes.name: askAbortable
nodes.summary: Sends a message to receiveAndReply and returns an AbortableRpcFuture; the default implementation throws UnsupportedOperationException and subclasses override it.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Asks the endpoint and returns a Future using the default ask timeout (the abstract ask(message, timeout) overload is at line 64). The message is sent once and never retried.

nodes.name: askSync
nodes.summary: Blocking ask with an explicit RpcTimeout: calls ask and waits for the reply with timeout.awaitResult, throwing on failure. The overload at line 85 uses the default ask timeout. Should not be called in an endpoint message loop.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts the RPC by invoking the onAbort callback with the given throwable.

nodes.name: RpcEnv.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcEnv, the RPC environment where endpoints register and from which endpoint references are obtained, plus the RpcEnvFileServer trait for serving files, jars and directories, the RpcEnvConfig case class, and the RpcEnv.create entry points.

nodes.name: RpcEnv
nodes.summary: Abstract RPC environment: endpoints register by name with setupEndpoint, and RpcEnv routes messages from endpoint references or remote nodes to them, using RpcCallContext.sendFailure for uncaught errors. It also resolves endpoint refs by name or URI, stops endpoints, shuts down, deserializes objects holding refs and opens file channels. The companion object creates a NettyRpcEnv through NettyRpcEnvFactory.

nodes.name: RpcEnvFileServer
nodes.summary: Trait for a server that RpcEnv uses to serve files, jars and directories to other processes of the application; declares addFile, addJar, addDirectory, addDirectoryIfAbsent, removeFile and removeJar and provides validateDirectoryUri.

nodes.name: RpcEnvConfig
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the settings needed to build an RpcEnv: SparkConf, name, bind and advertise addresses, port, SecurityManager, usable core count and client mode flag.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Factory in the companion object that builds an RpcEnvConfig and creates the RpcEnv through a new NettyRpcEnvFactory. An overload at lines 37-45 takes a single host and delegates here with numUsableCores 0.

nodes.name: setupEndpointRefByURI
nodes.summary: Blocking lookup of an endpoint ref by URI: waits on asyncSetupEndpointRefByURI using defaultLookupTimeout.

nodes.name: setupEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Blocking lookup of an endpoint ref by RpcAddress and endpoint name, built by rendering an RpcEndpointAddress as a URI and calling setupEndpointRefByURI.

nodes.name: validateDirectoryUri
nodes.summary: Normalizes a base URI for served directories to a form with a single leading slash and no trailing slash, and rejects /files and /jars.

nodes.name: RpcEnvStoppedException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares RpcEnvStoppedException, an IllegalStateException with message "RpcEnv already stopped." signalling that an operation hit a stopped RpcEnv.

nodes.name: RpcEnvStoppedException
nodes.summary: Package-private IllegalStateException subclass used to report that the RpcEnv was already stopped; Dispatcher creates it when a message is posted after shutdown.

nodes.name: RpcTimeout.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcTimeout, a timeout duration paired with the configuration property that controls it, and RpcTimeoutException, so timeout failures mention which property to adjust. The companion object builds timeouts from SparkConf.

nodes.name: RpcTimeout
nodes.summary: Serializable class holding a FiniteDuration and its config property name. awaitResult waits on a Future and rewrites any TimeoutException into an RpcTimeoutException naming the property; the companion apply methods read the timeout from SparkConf (single key, key with default, or prioritized key list).

nodes.name: RpcTimeoutException
nodes.summary: TimeoutException subclass that wraps the original TimeoutException as its cause and carries the amended message mentioning the controlling config property.

nodes.name: createRpcTimeoutException
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps a TimeoutException into an RpcTimeoutException with ". This timeout is controlled by <property>" appended.

nodes.name: addMessageIfTimeout
nodes.summary: PartialFunction usable as a Future recover callback: rethrows an existing RpcTimeoutException and converts any other TimeoutException into one with the property description.

nodes.name: awaitResult
nodes.summary: Waits for a Future up to this timeout via ThreadUtils.awaitResult, and on TimeoutException throws an RpcTimeoutException naming the controlling property.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory taking a prioritized list of property keys: uses the first one set in SparkConf, otherwise the default value with the first key, and builds the RpcTimeout. Two simpler overloads (lines 91-94 and 105-108) read a single property with or without a default.

nodes.name: Dispatcher.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Dispatcher, the message router of the netty RPC implementation: it registers endpoints by name, runs them on shared or dedicated message loops, and posts local, remote, one-way and broadcast messages to them.

nodes.name: Dispatcher
nodes.summary: Per-NettyRpcEnv router holding name-to-MessageLoop and endpoint-to-ref maps. It registers endpoints (isolated ones get a DedicatedMessageLoop, others share one SharedMessageLoop), wraps incoming requests into InboxMessages with a call context, posts them to the target loop, and bounces messages with an error once stopped.

nodes.name: registerRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Registers an endpoint under a name: builds its NettyRpcEndpointRef, records it before the loop starts, and assigns the endpoint to a DedicatedMessageLoop (for IsolatedRpcEndpoint) or the shared loop, rolling back on failure. Throws if stopped or the name is taken.

nodes.name: getRpcEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Returns the registered RpcEndpointRef for an endpoint, or null.

nodes.name: removeRpcEndpointRef
nodes.summary: Removes the endpoint-to-ref mapping; called later from the Inbox so in-flight messages can still resolve the ref.

nodes.name: unregisterRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: Idempotently removes an endpoint name from the loop map and unregisters it from its MessageLoop, leaving endpointRefs to be cleaned later.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the whole dispatcher: marks it stopped, unregisters all endpoints, stops dedicated loops and the shared loop, then releases awaitTermination. An overload at lines 106-114 stops a single endpoint by its ref name.

nodes.name: postToAll
nodes.summary: Posts an InboxMessage to every registered endpoint, logging a debug or warning message when delivery fails; used to announce network events to all endpoints.

nodes.name: postRemoteMessage
nodes.summary: Wraps a request from a remote endpoint with a RemoteNettyRpcCallContext into an RpcMessage and posts it to the target endpoint, failing the response callback on error.

nodes.name: postLocalMessage
nodes.summary: Wraps a request from a local endpoint with a LocalNettyRpcCallContext tied to a Promise into an RpcMessage and posts it, failing the promise on error.

nodes.name: postOneWayMessage
nodes.summary: Posts a one-way message to the target endpoint; if delivery fails because the RpcEnv or SparkEnv is stopped it logs and drops the message, otherwise rethrows.

nodes.name: postMessage
nodes.summary: Looks up the endpoint loop under the lock and posts the message to it, or calls the failure callback with RpcEnvStoppedException (dispatcher stopped) or a SparkException (endpoint not found).

nodes.name: awaitTermination
nodes.summary: Blocks on the shutdown latch until stop() completes.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Returns whether an endpoint with the given name is registered.

nodes.name: Inbox.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Inbox that queues messages for one RpcEndpoint and delivers them thread-safely, plus the sealed InboxMessage hierarchy (one-way, request-reply, start, stop and remote connection events). It is used by the netty Dispatcher message loops to feed endpoints.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait with private[netty] case classes and case objects as the message ADT; the Inbox guards its state with synchronized blocks.

nodes.name: InboxMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that is the common parent of every message stored in an Inbox.

nodes.name: OneWayMessage
nodes.summary: Inbox message carrying a fire-and-forget payload and the sender address; delivered to the endpoint's receive handler.

nodes.name: RpcMessage
nodes.summary: Inbox message carrying a payload, the sender address and a NettyRpcCallContext; delivered to the endpoint's receiveAndReply handler so it can answer.

nodes.name: OnStart
nodes.summary: Case object message that triggers the endpoint's onStart; it is always the first message added to a new Inbox.

nodes.name: OnStop
nodes.summary: Case object message that triggers the endpoint's onStop; Inbox.stop appends it as the last message.

nodes.name: RemoteProcessConnected
nodes.summary: Inbox message telling an endpoint that a remote process has connected; handled by calling onConnected.

nodes.name: RemoteProcessDisconnected
nodes.summary: Inbox message telling an endpoint that a remote process has disconnected; handled by calling onDisconnected.

nodes.name: RemoteProcessConnectionError
nodes.summary: Inbox message telling an endpoint that a network error happened with a remote address; handled by calling onNetworkError.

nodes.name: Inbox
nodes.summary: Stores messages for one RpcEndpoint and posts them to it thread-safely. It tracks stopped state and the number of active threads, allows concurrent processing only for endpoints that are not ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint, and guarantees OnStop is the last message.

nodes.name: process
nodes.summary: Polls and handles messages for the endpoint in a loop: dispatches each InboxMessage subtype to the matching RpcEndpoint callback, replies with sendFailure on errors, and manages numActiveThreads and enableConcurrent so that only allowed threads process at once.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Adds a message to the queue, or drops it through onDrop when the inbox is already stopped.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Marks the inbox stopped, disables concurrent processing and appends OnStop so it is the last message; a no-op if already stopped.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Returns whether the message queue is empty, under the inbox lock.

nodes.name: onDrop
nodes.summary: Logs a warning that a message is dropped because the endpoint is stopped; exposed so test cases can override it.

nodes.name: safelyCall
nodes.summary: Runs an action and routes non-fatal exceptions to the endpoint's onError, ignoring errors from onError itself; fatal errors decrement the active thread count, are logged and rethrown.

nodes.name: getNumActiveThreads
nodes.summary: Returns the number of threads currently processing this inbox, under the inbox lock; exposed only for testing.

nodes.name: MessageLoop.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the message loops the netty Dispatcher uses to deliver Inbox messages to endpoints: an abstract MessageLoop that owns the active-inbox queue and receive loop, a SharedMessageLoop that serves many endpoints on a shared pool, and a DedicatedMessageLoop for a single isolated endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed abstract class with private subclasses; MessageLoop.PoisonPill in the companion object is a sentinel Inbox used to stop worker threads.

nodes.name: MessageLoop
nodes.summary: Abstract base for dispatcher message loops. It holds a queue of inboxes with pending messages, runs a receive loop in every pool thread that takes an inbox and calls its process, and stops by enqueueing a PoisonPill inbox and shutting down the pool. The companion object defines PoisonPill (lines 95-98).

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the loop once by enqueueing the PoisonPill, shutting down the thread pool, then waiting for termination.

nodes.name: receiveLoop
nodes.summary: Worker loop that takes an active inbox from the queue and processes it, requeues the PoisonPill and exits when it sees it, logs non-fatal errors, and resubmits itself on fatal throwables before rethrowing.

nodes.name: SharedMessageLoop
nodes.summary: MessageLoop that serves many RPC endpoints from one shared dispatcher thread pool, sized from the Netty dispatcher thread configuration or the available cores. It keeps a map from endpoint name to Inbox.

nodes.name: getNumOfThreads
nodes.summary: Computes the pool size from usable cores, the dispatcher numThreads setting, and a driver or executor specific numThreads setting when an executor id is configured.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Looks up the inbox registered for the endpoint name, posts the message to it and marks the inbox active.

nodes.name: unregister
nodes.summary: Removes the endpoint's inbox, stops it and marks it active so the OnStop message is handled.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Creates an Inbox for the endpoint, stores it by name and marks it active so the OnStart message is handled.

nodes.name: DedicatedMessageLoop
nodes.summary: MessageLoop dedicated to a single IsolatedRpcEndpoint with its own Inbox and its own pool sized by the endpoint's threadCount. It starts the receive loops on construction, using execute rather than submit so uncaught exceptions are not swallowed.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Requires the endpoint name to match, posts the message to the single inbox and marks it active.

nodes.name: unregister
nodes.summary: Stops the inbox, marks it active for OnStop, enqueues the PoisonPill and shuts down the dedicated thread pool.

nodes.name: NettyRpcCallContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines NettyRpcCallContext and its two implementations, which let an RpcEndpoint reply to or fail a request. The local variant completes a Promise when sender and receiver are in the same process; the remote variant serializes the reply and sends it through an RpcResponseCallback.

nodes.name: NettyRpcCallContext
nodes.summary: Abstract RpcCallContext for the netty RPC layer. reply and sendFailure both go through the abstract send method; failures are wrapped in an RpcFailure.

nodes.name: reply
nodes.summary: Sends the response through the abstract send method.

nodes.name: sendFailure
nodes.summary: Wraps the throwable in an RpcFailure and sends it through the abstract send method.

nodes.name: LocalNettyRpcCallContext
nodes.summary: Call context for a sender and receiver in the same process; the reply is delivered by completing a scala Promise.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Completes the Promise successfully with the message.

nodes.name: RemoteNettyRpcCallContext
nodes.summary: Call context for a remote sender; serializes the reply with the NettyRpcEnv and sends it through an RpcResponseCallback.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Serializes the message using NettyRpcEnv.serialize and passes the bytes to callback.onSuccess.

nodes.name: NettyRpcEnv.scala
nodes.summary: Netty-based implementation of the RPC environment: the env itself, its endpoint reference, request message wire format, server-side handler and factory. Used by Spark processes to register endpoints, send one-way messages, ask for replies and download files over a transport client.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a class plus companion object, nested private classes and several package-private helper classes sharing one file.

nodes.name: NettyRpcEnv
nodes.summary: RpcEnv implementation built on a transport context. It owns the Dispatcher for local endpoints, a map of Outbox objects per remote RpcAddress for non-blocking send and ask, a server, client factories (plus a separate one for file downloads), a timeout scheduler and a connection thread pool. The companion object holds the currentEnv and currentClient dynamic variables used during deserialization of endpoint references.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object (lines 468-487) shares this node id; it defines the DynamicVariable fields currentEnv and currentClient.

nodes.name: FileDownloadChannel
nodes.summary: ReadableByteChannel over the source end of a pipe used by openChannel. An error from the RPC thread is stored with setError and rethrown from read, so remote failures reach the reading thread instead of pipe-close exceptions.

nodes.name: FileDownloadCallback
nodes.summary: StreamCallback that writes received stream data into the sink end of the download pipe, closes the sink on completion, and on failure records the cause on the FileDownloadChannel before closing the sink.

nodes.name: NettyRpcEnvFactory
nodes.summary: RpcEnvFactory that creates a NettyRpcEnv with a JavaSerializer instance. Unless in client mode it starts the server on the configured port through startServiceOnPort, and shuts the env down if that fails.

nodes.name: NettyRpcEndpointRef
nodes.summary: RpcEndpointRef used by NettyRpcEnv. On the owning node it wraps an RpcEndpointAddress; after deserialization on another node it remembers the TransportClient that delivered it, so messages can go back over that connection. Its address can be null when the endpoint host does not listen.

nodes.name: RequestMessage
nodes.summary: Message sent from a sender to a NettyRpcEndpointRef receiver, carrying the sender address, receiver and content. serialize writes the addresses and endpoint name manually to keep the size small; the companion apply rebuilds a message (with a receiver ref bound to the client) from received bytes.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object (lines 630-658) shares this node id.

nodes.name: RpcFailure
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping a Throwable, used as a reply that signals a failure on the receiver side. askAbortable turns a received RpcFailure into a failed promise.

nodes.name: NettyRpcHandler
nodes.summary: RpcHandler that receives requests from transport clients and forwards them to the Dispatcher. It tracks remote RpcEnv addresses per client connection, posts connect, disconnect and connection-error events to all endpoints, and removes the Outbox of a closed connection.

nodes.name: createClientBootstraps
nodes.summary: Returns an auth client bootstrap list when authentication is enabled, otherwise an empty list. Used for both the main and the file download client factories.

nodes.name: removeOutbox
nodes.summary: Removes the Outbox for an address from the outbox map and stops it.

nodes.name: startServer
nodes.summary: Creates the transport server (with auth bootstrap when enabled) and registers the RpcEndpointVerifier endpoint on the dispatcher.

nodes.name: asyncSetupEndpointRefByURI
nodes.summary: Builds an endpoint ref from a URI and asks the remote RpcEndpointVerifier whether that endpoint name exists. The future succeeds with the ref or fails with RpcEndpointNotFoundException.

nodes.name: postToOutbox
nodes.summary: Sends an outbox message either directly over the receiver ref client, or through the Outbox of the receiver address (created atomically with putIfAbsent). If the env is already stopped it removes and stops the outbox instead.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: One-way send of a RequestMessage. Local receivers get the message posted straight to the dispatcher; remote receivers get the serialized message wrapped in a OneWayOutboxMessage.

nodes.name: askAbortable
nodes.summary: Implements ask with a promise: local receivers use postLocalMessage, remote ones use an RpcOutboxMessage in an outbox. It schedules a timeout failure, cancels it on completion, and returns an AbortableRpcFuture whose abort callback fails the promise and removes the pending RPC request.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Deserializes bytes with the Java serializer instance while the given TransportClient is bound to currentClient. The overload deserialize(action) at lines 353-357 binds this env to currentEnv around any deserialization action.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Idempotent shutdown: marks the env stopped, stops all outboxes, the timeout scheduler, dispatcher, server, client factories, connection executor, file download factory and transport context.

nodes.name: openChannel
nodes.summary: Opens a ReadableByteChannel for a remote file URI by creating a pipe, streaming the path from a download client into the sink, and returning a FileDownloadChannel on the source. On failure it closes both pipe ends.

nodes.name: downloadClient
nodes.summary: Lazily creates (double-checked locking) a separate client factory for file downloads, copying spark.rpc.io settings into the spark.files.io namespace when missing, then returns a client for the host and port.

nodes.name: setError
nodes.summary: Stores an error from RPC threads so that the reading thread can rethrow it; it deliberately does not close the source because of a race with read.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads from the pipe source but rethrows the stored RPC error, if any, in preference to exceptions caused by the pipe being closed.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a NettyRpcEnv from an RpcEnvConfig; when not in client mode it starts the server on the requested port (retrying through startServiceOnPort) and shuts the env down on non-fatal errors.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Java deserialization hook that restores the transient env and client fields from NettyRpcEnv.currentEnv and currentClient.

nodes.name: askAbortable
nodes.summary: Wraps the message in a RequestMessage from the local env address and delegates to NettyRpcEnv.askAbortable. The ask method at lines 564-566 returns its future.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Requires a non-null message and sends it one-way through NettyRpcEnv.send.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Writes sender address, receiver address, receiver endpoint name and the Java-serialized content into a byte buffer.

nodes.name: writeRpcAddress
nodes.summary: Writes a presence flag, then host and port, for an RpcAddress (or only false for null).

nodes.name: readRpcAddress
nodes.summary: Reads the presence flag and, if set, host and port to rebuild an RpcAddress; returns null otherwise.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory in the companion object: reads the sender and receiver addresses and endpoint name from the bytes, builds a NettyRpcEndpointRef bound to the client, and deserializes the remaining bytes as the message content.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles a request that expects a reply by converting the bytes with internalReceive and posting the message to the dispatcher with the callback. The overload at lines 693-697 handles one-way messages via postOneWayMessage.

nodes.name: internalReceive
nodes.summary: Decodes a RequestMessage, fills in the client socket address when the sender is unknown, and on the first message from a listening remote env posts RemoteProcessConnected for its address.

nodes.name: exceptionCaught
nodes.summary: Posts RemoteProcessConnectionError for the client address (and for the remote env address when known), or logs an error if the channel closed before connecting.

nodes.name: channelActive
nodes.summary: Posts RemoteProcessConnected for the new client socket address to all endpoints.

nodes.name: channelInactive
nodes.summary: Removes the outbox for the closed client address and posts RemoteProcessDisconnected for it and for the remote env address, if one was recorded.

nodes.name: Outbox.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the outgoing message side of the Netty RPC env: the OutboxMessage hierarchy (one-way and RPC-with-reply messages) and the per-address Outbox queue that connects lazily and drains messages. Used by NettyRpcEnv for non-blocking send and ask to remote addresses.

nodes.name: OutboxMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for messages queued in an Outbox, with sendWith (send over a TransportClient) and onFailure (notify the sender) operations.

nodes.name: OneWayOutboxMessage
nodes.summary: Outbox message for fire-and-forget sends: sendWith calls client.send on the serialized content, and failures are logged (at debug level for RpcEnvStoppedException, otherwise as a warning).

nodes.name: RpcOutboxMessage
nodes.summary: Outbox message for ask calls. It sends through client.sendRpc, remembers the client and request id, acts as the RpcResponseCallback that forwards success and failure to supplied functions, and can remove the pending request on timeout or abort.

nodes.name: Outbox
nodes.summary: Per-remote-address queue of OutboxMessages with a lazily established TransportClient. It connects in the env connection executor, ensures only one thread drains the queue at a time, fails queued messages when the connection fails or it is stopped, and removes itself from NettyRpcEnv on network failure.
nodes.languageNotes: State fields are annotated with GuardedBy("this") and protected with synchronized blocks; the self alias "outbox" is used inside the anonymous Callable.

nodes.name: onFailure
nodes.summary: Logs a failed one-way send: debug for RpcEnvStoppedException, warning for any other throwable.

nodes.name: sendWith
nodes.summary: Stores the client and sends the content with sendRpc, keeping the returned request id.

nodes.name: removeRpcRequest
nodes.summary: Removes the pending request from the client by request id, or logs an error when the ask ended before a client was connected.

nodes.name: onTimeout
nodes.summary: Called when the ask times out; removes the pending RPC request.

nodes.name: onAbort
nodes.summary: Called when the ask is aborted; removes the pending RPC request.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Adds a message to the queue and starts draining, or, if the Outbox is stopped, fails the message with a SparkException.

nodes.name: drainOutbox
nodes.summary: Drains the queue: returns if stopped, connecting or already draining; launches a connect task when no client exists; otherwise sends queued messages one by one and handles network failures.

nodes.name: launchConnectTask
nodes.summary: Submits a task to the client connection executor that creates the client for the address, stores it, and then drains the queue; on a non-fatal error it clears the future and handles the network failure.

nodes.name: handleNetworkFailure
nodes.summary: Marks the Outbox stopped, drops the client, removes it from NettyRpcEnv so later messages get a new Outbox, and fails every remaining message with the cause.

nodes.name: closeClient
nodes.summary: Sets the client to null without closing it so the connection can be reused.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the Outbox, cancels any pending connect task, drops the client and fails remaining messages with a SparkException.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointVerifier.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RpcEndpointVerifier, an endpoint registered on each server env so remote envs can ask whether a named endpoint exists. Used while setting up a remote endpoint reference.

nodes.name: RpcEndpointVerifier
nodes.summary: RpcEndpoint that answers CheckExistence(name) messages by replying with the result of Dispatcher.verify. The companion object defines the well-known endpoint NAME "endpoint-verifier".
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object (lines 35-40) shares this node id.

nodes.name: CheckExistence
nodes.summary: Case class message asking the remote RpcEndpointVerifier whether an endpoint with the given name exists.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles CheckExistence by replying to the caller with whether the dispatcher knows the endpoint name.

nodes.name: ReadAheadInputStream.java
nodes.summary: Defines ReadAheadInputStream, an InputStream wrapper that reads ahead from an underlying stream on a background thread using two swapped buffers so that readers are not blocked on disk I/O.

nodes.name: ReadAheadInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream that keeps an active buffer for read() calls and a read ahead buffer filled asynchronously by a single daemon 'read-ahead' thread; when the active buffer is exhausted the two buffers are swapped. State is guarded by a ReentrantLock and a condition, and read failures are captured and rethrown to the reader.

nodes.name: checkReadException
nodes.summary: Rethrows the exception captured by the background read (IOException, Error or RuntimeException as is, anything else wrapped in an IOException) when a read was aborted.

nodes.name: readAsync
nodes.summary: Schedules an asynchronous fill of the read ahead buffer on the single-thread executor, unless the stream is at end of stream or a read is already running. The task records end of stream or the captured exception, signals waiting readers, and may close the underlying stream if close() was requested meanwhile.

nodes.name: closeUnderlyingInputStreamIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Clears the reading flag after a background read and closes the underlying stream if close() was called while the read was in progress, logging any IOException.

nodes.name: signalAsyncReadComplete
nodes.summary: Wakes all waiters on the asyncReadComplete condition while holding the state lock.

nodes.name: waitForAsyncReadComplete
nodes.summary: Blocks the reader until no async read is in progress, marking that a reader is waiting so the background read can return early, then checks for a captured read exception. Interrupts are converted to InterruptedIOException.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads up to len bytes into an array after validating the arguments. When the active buffer is empty it waits for the pending async read, triggers the first read if needed, swaps buffers and starts the next async read. The single-byte overload read() has a fast path from the active buffer, delegates to this method, and shares this id.

nodes.name: swapBuffers
nodes.summary: Exchanges the active buffer and the read ahead buffer references.

nodes.name: available
nodes.summary: Returns the bytes remaining in both buffers, capped at Integer.MAX_VALUE, under the state lock.

nodes.name: skip
nodes.summary: Skips n bytes, using only the active buffer when it has enough data and otherwise taking the lock and delegating to skipInternal.

nodes.name: skipInternal
nodes.summary: Skips bytes with the state lock held: waits for the async read, skips within the two buffers when available data suffices, otherwise empties both buffers and skips on the underlying stream, then restarts the async read.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Marks the stream closed, shuts down the read-ahead executor and waits for it to terminate, and closes the underlying stream unless a running background read will close it instead.

nodes.name: ShuffleReadMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffleReadMetrics, the per-task set of accumulators describing shuffle read activity, and TempShuffleReadMetrics, a plain-variable holder used per shuffle dependency and merged into the former.

nodes.name: ShuffleReadMetrics
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi class holding LongAccumulator fields for remote and local blocks fetched, bytes read, fetch wait time, records read and merged block/chunk statistics. It exposes read accessors, private[spark] increment and set methods, and setMergeValues to combine temporary metrics. Operations are documented as not thread-safe.

nodes.name: TempShuffleReadMetrics
nodes.summary: Private[spark] ShuffleReadMetricsReporter that stores the same shuffle read counters in simple local vars with increment overrides and getters. One is used per shuffle dependency and all are merged into ShuffleReadMetrics at the end.

nodes.name: setMergeValues
nodes.summary: Resets every accumulator to zero and then adds the corresponding value of each given TempShuffleReadMetrics into this object.

nodes.name: NettyStreamManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines NettyStreamManager, the StreamManager used by a NettyRpcEnv to serve registered files, jars and directories as streams.

nodes.name: NettyStreamManager
nodes.summary: StreamManager and RpcEnvFileServer implementation that keeps concurrent maps of files, jars and directories and serves them through openStream. It backs file and jar registration, while getChunk is unsupported.

nodes.name: getChunk
nodes.summary: Always throws UnsupportedOperationException because only streaming via openStream is supported.

nodes.name: openStream
nodes.summary: Parses a stream id of the form /type/name, looks the file up in the files map, the jars map or a registered directory, and returns a FileSegmentManagedBuffer over the whole file, or null if the file is missing or not a regular file.

nodes.name: addFile
nodes.summary: Registers a file under its name in the files map (rejecting a different path with the same name) and returns its /files URL on the RpcEnv address.

nodes.name: addJar
nodes.summary: Registers a jar file under its name in the jars map (rejecting a conflicting path) and returns its /jars URL on the RpcEnv address.

nodes.name: addDirectory
nodes.summary: Validates the base URI, registers the directory and fails if the URI is already registered, then returns the URL for the directory.

nodes.name: addDirectoryIfAbsent
nodes.summary: Validates the base URI and registers the directory only if absent, returning the URL for the directory.

nodes.name: GroupMappingServiceProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the GroupMappingServiceProvider trait, the abstraction that maps a user name to the set of groups the user belongs to.

nodes.name: GroupMappingServiceProvider
nodes.summary: Trait with a single method getGroups(userName) returning a set of group names, empty for an invalid user. Per its documentation, the SecurityManager asks the provider configured by spark.user.groups.mapping for a user's groups when access control checks are enabled with spark.acls.enable.

nodes.name: getGroups
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns the set of groups the given user belongs to, empty in case of an invalid user.

nodes.name: SecurityConfigurationLock.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the SecurityConfigurationLock object, used as a lock when global JVM security configuration must be modified.

nodes.name: SecurityConfigurationLock
nodes.summary: Empty private[spark] object that serves as a synchronization monitor, so that changes to global JVM security configuration do not race.

nodes.name: ShellBasedGroupsMappingProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Declares ShellBasedGroupsMappingProvider, a GroupMappingServiceProvider that finds a user's groups by running the Unix id command.

nodes.name: ShellBasedGroupsMappingProvider
nodes.summary: Private[spark] GroupMappingServiceProvider (with Logging) for Unix environments that locates the id command via which and runs it with -Gn to fetch the groups of a user. It does not cache results because calls are expected to be infrequent.

nodes.name: getGroups
nodes.summary: Implements getGroups by calling getUnixGroups, logging the user and groups at debug level, and returning the groups.

nodes.name: getUnixGroups
nodes.summary: Runs the id command with the -Gn option and the user name through Utils.executeAndGetOutput, strips the trailing line end, and splits the output on spaces into a set.

nodes.name: WholeTextFileRecordReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Configurable mixin, a record reader that returns one whole text file as a single key-value pair, and a combine-file record reader that forwards the Hadoop Configuration to its per-file readers. Used when many small text files are read into one split.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait that adapts the Hadoop Configurable interface and is mixed into several readers.

nodes.name: Configurable
nodes.summary: Private trait that implements the Hadoop Configurable interface by storing the Configuration passed to setConf and returning it from getConf. Mixed into the readers in this file so they can receive the Hadoop Configuration.

nodes.name: WholeTextFileRecordReader
nodes.summary: RecordReader for one file inside a CombineFileSplit: the key is the file path and the value is the entire file content as Text. It produces exactly one record, tracks a processed flag, and reads the bytes through HadoopCodecStreams so compressed files are decoded.

nodes.name: nextKeyValue
nodes.summary: On the first call opens the file with HadoopCodecStreams.createInputStream, reads all bytes into the value Text, closes the stream, marks the file processed and returns true; later calls return false.

nodes.name: ConfigurableCombineFileRecordReader
nodes.summary: CombineFileRecordReader that passes the Hadoop Configuration on to the Configurable record readers it creates for each file in a combined split. It re-applies the configuration whenever a new inner reader is initialised or the configuration is set.

nodes.name: initNextRecordReader
nodes.summary: Delegates to the parent to create the next per-file reader and, when a Configuration is available, sets it on that reader.

nodes.name: setConf
nodes.summary: Stores the Configuration through the parent and also pushes it to the current inner reader if one exists.

nodes.name: FixedLengthBinaryInputFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Input format for flat binary files made of fixed-size records, with the record length taken from a Hadoop configuration property. It aligns split sizes to whole records so every split starts and ends on a record boundary.

nodes.name: FixedLengthBinaryInputFormat
nodes.summary: FileInputFormat producing (LongWritable, BytesWritable) pairs from fixed-length binary records; the companion object holds the record-length property name and a lookup helper. It forces split sizes to be multiples of the record length and creates a FixedLengthBinaryRecordReader for each split.

nodes.name: getRecordLength
nodes.summary: Companion object helper that reads the record length property from the Hadoop configuration of the given job context and converts it to an Int.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Lazily loads the record length on first use and reports that a file can be split only when the record length is positive, logging a debug message otherwise.

nodes.name: computeSplitSize
nodes.summary: Computes the default split size and rounds it down to a multiple of the record length (or raises it to one record) so splits contain only whole records.

nodes.name: createRecordReader
nodes.summary: Returns a new FixedLengthBinaryRecordReader for the given split.

nodes.name: PortableDataStream.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the input formats and record readers used to read whole files as streams, plus the serializable PortableDataStream handle that defers opening a file until it is read. Used for APIs that return one stream or byte array per file.
nodes.languageNotes: The PortableDataStream class serializes the split and configuration into byte arrays and rebuilds them lazily after deserialization.

nodes.name: StreamFileInputFormat
nodes.summary: Abstract CombineFileInputFormat keyed by path that never splits files and offers setMinPartitions to derive the maximum split size from user-requested partitions, default parallelism and the configured file open cost.

nodes.name: setMinPartitions
nodes.summary: Sums the sizes of the listed files plus the open cost, divides by the larger of default parallelism and minPartitions, and sets the max split size (lowering per-node and per-rack minimums if needed) to keep behaviour compatible with the old Hadoop API.

nodes.name: StreamBasedRecordReader
nodes.summary: Abstract RecordReader that emits one record per file: it wraps the file in a PortableDataStream, hands it to the subclass parseStream, and uses the file path as the key.

nodes.name: nextKeyValue
nodes.summary: On the first call builds a PortableDataStream for the file, parses it through parseStream, sets the key to its path and marks it processed; returns false afterwards.

nodes.name: StreamRecordReader
nodes.summary: StreamBasedRecordReader whose parseStream returns the PortableDataStream unchanged, so the value is the stream handle itself.

nodes.name: StreamInputFormat
nodes.summary: StreamFileInputFormat for PortableDataStream values; its createRecordReader wraps StreamRecordReader in a CombineFileRecordReader.

nodes.name: createRecordReader
nodes.summary: Creates a CombineFileRecordReader over the combined split using StreamRecordReader as the per-file reader class.

nodes.name: PortableDataStream
nodes.summary: Serializable handle to a file inside a CombineFileSplit that stores the Hadoop Configuration and the split as byte arrays and rebuilds them lazily, so the stream is only opened when the user calls open or toArray. Exposes the path and configuration.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Opens the file at the split index through its FileSystem and returns a DataInputStream; the caller must close it.

nodes.name: toArray
nodes.summary: Opens the stream, reads all bytes into an array and closes the stream in a finally block.

nodes.name: getPath
nodes.summary: Returns the file path computed lazily from the split, without opening the file.

nodes.name: PluginContextImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the PluginContext handed to plugins, giving them a metric registry and message passing to the driver plugin endpoint. Used when plugins are initialised by Spark.

nodes.name: PluginContextImpl
nodes.summary: PluginContext implementation holding the plugin name, RpcEnv, metrics system, conf, executor id and resources. It lazily creates a driver endpoint reference, sends or asks PluginMessage values to the driver, and registers plugin metrics as a metrics source.

nodes.name: PluginMetricsSource
nodes.summary: Inner metrics Source that exposes the plugin MetricRegistry under the source name plugin.<pluginName>.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Sends a one-way PluginMessage with the plugin name to the driver endpoint, throwing IllegalStateException if the endpoint reference is not known.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Sends a PluginMessage to the driver endpoint and waits synchronously for the reply, unwrapping the cause of a SparkException and failing if the endpoint is unknown.

nodes.name: registerMetrics
nodes.summary: If the plugin registry holds any metrics, creates a PluginMetricsSource and registers it with the metrics system.

nodes.name: PluginEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PluginMessage and the driver-side RPC endpoint that routes plugin messages to the DriverPlugin registered under the matching name.

nodes.name: PluginMessage
nodes.summary: Case class carrying a plugin name and an arbitrary message object, used to address driver plugin RPC messages.

nodes.name: PluginEndpoint
nodes.summary: Isolated thread-safe RPC endpoint on the driver that holds a map of plugin names to DriverPlugin instances and dispatches incoming PluginMessage values to the right plugin, either as a one-way message or as a request with a reply.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles a one-way PluginMessage: looks up the plugin by name, calls its receive, logs a warning if a reply is returned or an exception is thrown, and throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown plugin.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles a PluginMessage that expects an answer: calls the named plugin receive and replies to the RpcCallContext with its result, or throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown plugin.

nodes.name: CompressionCodec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CompressionCodec trait and its companion factory, plus the LZ4, LZF, Snappy and Zstandard implementations used to compress block, shuffle and similar streams. Codec choice comes from the io compression configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object of the CompressionCodec trait acts as a factory that instantiates codecs reflectively by short or full class name.

nodes.name: CompressionCodec
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait with compressedOutputStream and compressedInputStream (and continuous variants that default to the normal ones) for wrapping streams with a compression algorithm. Its companion object (lines 60-118) holds the short codec names, the default fallback and the factory methods; the wire protocol is not guaranteed across versions.

nodes.name: supportsConcatenationOfSerializedStreams
nodes.summary: Returns true when the codec is a Snappy, LZF, LZ4 or Zstandard codec, meaning serialized streams compressed by it can be concatenated.

nodes.name: createCodec
nodes.summary: Resolves a codec name (short name or class name) to a class, builds it with a constructor taking SparkConf, and throws a codec-not-available error if it cannot be found. The overloads at lines 82-84 pick the name from the configuration.

nodes.name: getShortName
nodes.summary: Returns the lowercase short codec name for a given short or fully qualified class name, or throws SparkIllegalArgumentException (CODEC_SHORT_NAME_NOT_FOUND) if unknown.

nodes.name: LZ4CompressionCodec
nodes.summary: LZ4 implementation of CompressionCodec using LZ4 block streams with an xxHash checksum and a block size from configuration. It caches the LZ4 and xxHash factories lazily to avoid repeated JNI load attempts.

nodes.name: LZFCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: LZF implementation of CompressionCodec that uses a parallel LZF output stream when the parallel compression option is enabled, otherwise a regular LZF output stream.

nodes.name: SnappyCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Snappy implementation of CompressionCodec with a configurable block size; its constructor checks that the native Snappy library loads and wraps load errors in IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: ZStdCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Zstandard implementation of CompressionCodec configured with buffer size, level, strategy, worker count and optional buffer pooling. It wraps streams in buffered streams to cut JNI overhead and has continuous variants that can read and write open frames.

nodes.name: compressedOutputStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an OutputStream in an LZ4BlockOutputStream with the configured block size, fast compressor and xxHash32 checksum, without sync flush.

nodes.name: compressedInputStream
nodes.summary: Builds an LZ4BlockInputStream with a safe decompressor and xxHash32 checksum that does not stop on empty blocks.

nodes.name: compressedOutputStream
nodes.summary: Returns a PLZFOutputStream when parallel compression is on, otherwise an LZFOutputStream that finishes the block on flush.

nodes.name: compressedOutputStream
nodes.summary: Creates a Zstandard output stream with the configured level, workers and optional strategy, wrapped in a BufferedOutputStream.

nodes.name: compressedContinuousOutputStream
nodes.summary: Creates a Zstandard output stream with closeFrameOnFlush enabled so readers of a continuous stream are not stuck on an open frame, wrapped in a BufferedOutputStream.

nodes.name: compressedInputStream
nodes.summary: Wraps a Zstandard input stream in a BufferedInputStream to reduce JNI call overhead on small reads.

nodes.name: compressedContinuousInputStream
nodes.summary: Wraps a Zstandard input stream with the continuous flag set so reading from open frames (for example a live event log) does not fail with a truncation error.

nodes.name: HadoopCodecStreams.scala
nodes.summary: Utility for opening Hadoop file input streams with the right decompression codec, including Zstandard and Gzip fallbacks for non-standard extensions and a fallback to the Spark Zstandard codec.

nodes.name: HadoopCodecStreams
nodes.summary: Object that finds a Hadoop compression codec from a file name, creates decompressing input streams and, when Hadoop lacks Zstandard support, falls back to the Spark Zstandard codec. It also recognizes the .zstd and .gzip extensions.

nodes.name: getDecompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Looks up a Hadoop codec by file name through CompressionCodecFactory and, if none matches, maps the .zstd and .gzip extensions to the Zstandard and Gzip codecs.

nodes.name: createZstdInputStream
nodes.summary: For files ending in .zstd or .zst, creates a Spark Zstandard codec from the current SparkEnv conf (or a new SparkConf) and returns its decompressing stream; returns None for other files.

nodes.name: createInputStream
nodes.summary: Opens the file through its FileSystem and wraps it with the codec found for its name; if the Hadoop codec throws a RuntimeException it tries the Spark Zstandard stream, and with no codec returns the raw stream.

nodes.name: MutableCheckedOutputStream.scala
nodes.summary: Output stream wrapper that updates a checksum while writing, where the checksum can be swapped at runtime.

nodes.name: MutableCheckedOutputStream
nodes.summary: Variant of CheckedOutputStream that wraps an OutputStream and updates a Checksum for every byte written. setChecksum can change the calculator at runtime, and writes assert that a checksum has been set.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Asserts a checksum is set, updates it with the given byte range and writes the range to the wrapped stream. The single-byte overload at lines 34-38 does the same for one byte.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object declaration for org.apache.spark.io whose documentation points to CompressionCodec as the main IO compression API.

nodes.name: io
nodes.summary: Empty package object for org.apache.spark.io, present to carry the package documentation about IO codecs used for compression.

nodes.name: WholeTextFileInputFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the input format that reads whole text files as (path, content) pairs, combining small files into splits.

nodes.name: WholeTextFileInputFormat
nodes.summary: CombineFileInputFormat subclass for reading whole text files: each file is one record whose key is the file path and value is the entire content. Files are never split, and the number of splits is steered through a user-supplied minimum partition count.

nodes.name: createRecordReader
nodes.summary: Builds a ConfigurableCombineFileRecordReader over WholeTextFileRecordReader and passes the current configuration to it.

nodes.name: setMinPartitions
nodes.summary: Converts a requested minimum partition count into a maximum split size (total file length divided by the count) and lowers the per-node and per-rack minimum split sizes if they exceed it. Keeps compatibility with the old Hadoop API.

nodes.name: PluginContainer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the container that loads the configured Spark plugins and runs their driver-side or executor-side lifecycle (init, metrics registration, task callbacks, shutdown).

nodes.name: PluginContainer
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class declaring shutdown, registerMetrics and the task start/success/failure callbacks. Its companion object (lines 189-220) loads the plugins named in the PLUGINS config and returns a driver or executor container, or None when no plugin is configured.

nodes.name: DriverPluginContainer
nodes.summary: Driver-side container: initializes each plugin driver component with a PluginContextImpl, stores the extra conf it returns in the SparkConf, registers a PluginEndpoint when any driver plugin exists, and forwards metrics registration and shutdown. Task callbacks throw IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: ExecutorPluginContainer
nodes.summary: Executor-side container: initializes each plugin executor component with its extra conf and a PluginContextImpl, then forwards task start, success, failure and shutdown callbacks, logging and swallowing exceptions. registerMetrics throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Private apply that loads SparkPlugin extensions from the PLUGINS config for either a SparkContext (driver) or a SparkEnv (executor) and builds the matching container. Two public overloads (lines 193-197 and 199-203) wrap it with Left or Right.

nodes.name: registerMetrics
nodes.summary: Calls registerMetrics on every driver plugin and then on its PluginContextImpl.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down each driver plugin, logging any exception instead of propagating it.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down each executor plugin, logging any exception instead of propagating it.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Invokes onTaskStart on every executor plugin, logging failures.

nodes.name: onTaskSucceeded
