nodes.summary: Sets the stopped flag, interrupts the cleaning thread only inside a synchronized block so a running task finishes first, joins the thread and shuts down the periodic GC service.

nodes.name: registerRDDForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers an RDD so that CleanRDD(rdd.id) runs when the RDD is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerAccumulatorForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers an AccumulatorV2 so that CleanAccum runs when the accumulator is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerShuffleForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers a ShuffleDependency so that CleanShuffle runs when it is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerBroadcastForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers a Broadcast so that CleanBroadcast runs when it is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerRDDCheckpointDataForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers an RDD so that CleanCheckpoint for the given parent id runs when the RDD is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerSparkListenerForCleanup
nodes.summary: Registers a listener owner object so that CleanSparkListener removes the listener once the owner is garbage collected.

nodes.name: registerForCleanup
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps the object and its cleanup task in a CleanupTaskWeakReference and adds it to the reference buffer so the reference is kept alive until handled.

nodes.name: keepCleaning
nodes.summary: Loop run by the cleaning thread until stopped: takes references from the queue with a poll timeout, removes them from the buffer and dispatches each CleanupTask to the matching doCleanup method, logging errors without stopping.

nodes.name: doCleanupRDD
nodes.summary: Unpersists the RDD through the SparkContext, notifies listeners with rddCleaned and logs errors.

nodes.name: doCleanupShuffle
nodes.summary: If the map output tracker still contains the shuffle, removes it via ShuffleDriverComponents, unregisters it from the tracker and notifies listeners with shuffleCleaned; otherwise logs that it is already gone.

nodes.name: doCleanupBroadcast
nodes.summary: Unbroadcasts the broadcast through the broadcast manager and notifies listeners with broadcastCleaned.

nodes.name: doCleanupAccum
nodes.summary: Removes the accumulator from AccumulatorContext and notifies listeners with accumCleaned.

nodes.name: doCleanCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Removes checkpoint files written to reliable storage via ReliableRDDCheckpointData.cleanCheckpoint and notifies listeners with checkpointCleaned; local checkpoints are handled by RDD cleanup.

nodes.name: doCleanSparkListener
nodes.summary: Removes the listener from the SparkContext's listener bus.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationClient.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutorAllocationClient trait, the interface through which Spark asks a cluster manager to add, kill or decommission executors. The doc comment says it is currently supported only in Kubernetes and YARN mode.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationClient
nodes.summary: Private trait describing requests sent to the cluster manager: listing active executors, requesting a total or additional number of executors, killing executors by id or host, and decommissioning executors by id or host. Concrete kill/decommission helpers are built on killExecutors and decommissionExecutors.

nodes.name: getExecutorIds
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the ids of the currently active executors.

nodes.name: isExecutorActive
nodes.summary: Abstract method telling whether the executor with the given id can currently be used to execute tasks for submitted jobs.

nodes.name: requestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Abstract method that tells the cluster manager the desired executor count per ResourceProfile id plus locality-aware task counts and per-host task counts, and returns whether the request was acknowledged.

nodes.name: requestExecutors
nodes.summary: Abstract method requesting additional executors for the default ResourceProfile; returns whether the cluster manager acknowledged the request.

nodes.name: killExecutors
nodes.summary: Abstract method asking the cluster manager to kill the given executors, with flags for adjusting the target executor count, counting task failures, and forcing the kill of busy executors; returns the ids acknowledged for removal.

nodes.name: decommissionExecutors
nodes.summary: Asks the cluster manager to decommission executors given as (id, ExecutorDecommissionInfo) pairs. The default implementation just delegates to killExecutors with countFailures set to false; schedulers supporting graceful decommissioning override it.

nodes.name: decommissionExecutor
nodes.summary: Final helper that decommissions a single executor by wrapping it in an array and calling decommissionExecutors; returns true only if the first returned id equals the requested executor id.

nodes.name: decommissionExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Abstract method requesting decommission of every executor on the given host.

nodes.name: killExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Abstract method requesting that every executor on the given host be killed.

nodes.name: killExecutor
nodes.summary: Kills one executor by calling killExecutors with adjustTargetNumExecutors true and countFailures false; returns true only if the first acknowledged id equals the requested one.

nodes.name: FutureAction.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FutureAction, a cancellable extension of the Scala Future for the result of a Spark action, together with its single-job implementation (SimpleFutureAction), a multi-job implementation (ComplexFutureAction), the JobSubmitter handle, and a wrapper exposing a FutureAction as a Java future.

nodes.name: FutureAction
nodes.summary: Trait extending Scala Future with cancel, isCancelled, get (blocking with an infinite wait) and jobIds. It re-declares Future methods so that the documentation refers to actions.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: No-argument cancel that calls cancel(None); the abstract overload cancel(reason: Option[String]) at line 44 shares this node id.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Blocks until the action finishes and returns its result by awaiting this future with an infinite duration; declared to throw SparkException.

nodes.name: jobIds
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a snapshot of the job ids run by the underlying async operation; operations running several jobs can return different lists on different calls.

nodes.name: SimpleFutureAction
nodes.summary: FutureAction for actions that trigger a single job (the doc names count, collect and reduce). It wraps a JobWaiter and a by-name result function, and tracks a volatile cancelled flag.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Sets the cancelled flag and cancels the underlying JobWaiter with the optional reason.

nodes.name: ready
nodes.summary: Waits on the JobWaiter completion future for up to the given duration and returns this action.

nodes.name: result
nodes.summary: Waits for the JobWaiter completion future, asserts a value is defined, and returns the computed result or rethrows the failure.

nodes.name: onComplete
nodes.summary: Registers a callback on the JobWaiter completion future that invokes the supplied function with this action value.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Maps the JobWaiter completion future value to the result function, so the result is computed lazily once the job has succeeded. transform (152-153) and transformWith (155-156) apply the same mapping and are not given separate nodes.

nodes.name: JobSubmitter
nodes.summary: Developer API trait handed to the run function of a ComplexFutureAction; its submitJob wraps SparkContext job submission so that cancellation is supported.

nodes.name: submitJob
nodes.summary: Abstract method that submits a job for an RDD with a partition function, partitions and a result handler, and returns a FutureAction holding the result.

nodes.name: ComplexFutureAction
nodes.summary: FutureAction for actions that may trigger several jobs (the doc names take and takeSample). Cancellation sets a flag, fails the internal promise with a SparkException and cancels every sub-action submitted so far.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Synchronized cancel that marks the action cancelled, fails the promise with "Action has been cancelled" and cancels all submitted sub-actions.

nodes.name: jobSubmitter
nodes.summary: Builds the JobSubmitter given to the run function. Its submitJob is synchronized and throws a SparkException if cancelled, otherwise it submits through the RDD SparkContext and prepends the resulting job to subActions.

nodes.name: ready
nodes.summary: Waits on the internal promise future for up to the given duration and returns this action.

nodes.name: result
nodes.summary: Returns the result of the internal promise future after waiting up to the given duration.

nodes.name: onComplete
nodes.summary: Delegates the completion callback registration to the internal promise future.

nodes.name: JavaFutureActionWrapper
nodes.summary: Private wrapper that adapts a FutureAction[S] and a converter function to the JavaFutureAction[T] interface, mapping failures to CancellationException or ExecutionException as java.util.Future expects.

nodes.name: isDone
nodes.summary: Returns true if the wrapped action is cancelled or completed, following the java.util.Future contract.

nodes.name: jobIds
nodes.summary: Converts the wrapped action job ids to a java.util.List of Integer.

nodes.name: getImpl
nodes.summary: Waits for the wrapped action with a timeout, then converts the successful value or throws CancellationException (if cancelled) or ExecutionException wrapping the failure.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Timed get that converts the timeout and unit to a Duration and calls getImpl; the no-argument get() at line 289 calls getImpl with an infinite duration and shares this node id.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Synchronized cancel that returns false if already done, otherwise cancels the wrapped FutureAction and returns true; the mayInterruptIfRunning flag is not used.

nodes.name: Heartbeater.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Heartbeater, a small private class that runs a caller-supplied reportHeartbeat function on a daemon scheduled thread at a fixed interval.

nodes.name: Heartbeater
nodes.summary: Wraps a single-thread daemon scheduled executor named by the caller. start schedules reportHeartbeat at a fixed rate after a randomized initial delay, doReportHeartbeat invokes it directly, and stop shuts the executor down waiting up to 10 seconds.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Schedules the heartbeat task with an initial delay of intervalMs plus a random amount up to intervalMs so heartbeats do not stay in sync; the task runs reportHeartbeat inside Utils.logUncaughtExceptions.

nodes.name: doReportHeartbeat
nodes.summary: Calls the reportHeartbeat function once on the current thread.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the heartbeat executor and waits up to 10 seconds for termination.

nodes.name: InternalAccumulator.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the string constants naming internal task-level metric accumulators, all prefixed with "internal.metrics.", grouped for shuffle read, shuffle write, output and input metrics.

nodes.name: InternalAccumulator
nodes.summary: Private object defining the metric name prefixes and the names of internal task metrics such as executor run time, GC time, result size, spill bytes and peak execution memory, plus nested objects for shuffle read, shuffle write, output and input metric names.

nodes.name: shuffleRead
nodes.summary: Nested object with the names of shuffle read metrics (remote and local blocks and bytes, fetch wait time, records read) and the shuffle push read metrics for merged blocks and chunks.

nodes.name: shuffleWrite
nodes.summary: Nested object with the names of the shuffle write metrics: bytes written, records written and write time.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Nested object with the names of the output metrics: bytes written and records written.

nodes.name: input
nodes.summary: Nested object with the names of the input metrics: bytes read and records read.

nodes.name: InterruptibleIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines InterruptibleIterator, a developer API iterator wrapper that lets a running task be killed by checking the TaskContext interrupted state on each hasNext call.

nodes.name: InterruptibleIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps a delegate iterator and a TaskContext. hasNext first calls context.killTaskIfInterrupted() and then delegates, so task killing takes effect during iteration; next simply delegates.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Calls context.killTaskIfInterrupted() before delegating hasNext; a code comment notes that checking Thread.interrupted instead is a possible optimization because the context flag is volatile and costs a read fence.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns delegate.next().

nodes.name: JobArtifactSet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JobArtifactState and JobArtifactSet, which carry the per-session jars, files and archives (and an optional client uuid and REPL class directory URI) for a job, plus a companion object that tracks the active client state in a thread-local.

nodes.name: JobArtifactState
nodes.summary: Private case class holding the artifact state for the current client: a uuid (usually from a Spark Connect client) and an optional REPL class directory URI.

nodes.name: JobArtifactSet
nodes.summary: Serializable class storing session-specific jars, files and archives (each a map to a long) and an optional JobArtifactState, with equals/hashCode over those fields. The companion object (lines 65-122) provides empty and default sets, a thread-local client state, and getActiveOrDefault.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Computes the hash from the state and the jars, files and archives converted to sequences.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares another JobArtifactSet by class, state and the sequence forms of jars, files and archives; the match has no fallback case, so a non-JobArtifactSet argument raises a MatchError.

nodes.name: defaultJobArtifactSet
nodes.summary: Marked "For testing". Returns getActiveOrDefault for the active SparkContext if there is one, otherwise the empty set.

nodes.name: getCurrentJobArtifactState
nodes.summary: Returns the artifact state stored in the current thread-local, if any.

nodes.name: withActiveJobArtifactState
nodes.summary: Runs a block with the given JobArtifactState set in the thread-local (recording it as the last seen state) and restores the previous state in a finally clause.

nodes.name: getActiveOrDefault
nodes.summary: Builds a JobArtifactSet from the SparkContext: if a client state exists it fills the REPL class URI from spark.repl.class.uri and takes that uuid jars, files and archives, otherwise it uses all added jars, files and archives of the context.

nodes.name: MapOutputStatistics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapOutputStatistics, a small private class carrying the shuffle id and approximate output bytes per map output partition of a map stage.

nodes.name: MapOutputStatistics
nodes.summary: Holds shuffleId and bytesByPartitionId (an array of approximate output bytes per map output partition, possibly inexact because compressed map statuses are used). The doc says it may become a DeveloperApi in the future.

nodes.name: PartitionEvaluator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PartitionEvaluator trait, a developer API (since 3.5.0) for computing one RDD partition on the executor side.

nodes.name: PartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Trait with a single method eval(partitionIndex, inputs*) returning an iterator. Spark serializes and sends a PartitionEvaluatorFactory to executors, which creates the evaluator there.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates the RDD partition at the given index over one or more input iterators (more than one if the RDD was zipped from multiple RDDs) and returns the output iterator.

nodes.name: PartitionEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the serializable PartitionEvaluatorFactory trait, a developer API (since 3.5.0) used to create a PartitionEvaluator on the executor side.

nodes.name: PartitionEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable trait with createEvaluator(), which Spark calls on executors after shipping the factory; each RDD partition creates its own evaluator instance, so one evaluator is used by only one thread.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Abstract method creating a PartitionEvaluator for one partition; one instance is used by one thread only.

nodes.name: SSLOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SSLOptions, a case class holding the SSL settings of one configuration namespace (key store, trust store, passwords, protocol, ciphers), and its companion that parses them from SparkConf and Hadoop configuration, with name constants for RPC SSL password configs and environment variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class with default arguments plus a companion object; passwords are masked in toString.

nodes.name: SSLOptions
nodes.summary: Container for SSL configuration of a namespace such as spark.ssl or spark.ssl.rpc. Can build a Jetty server SSL context factory or a ConfigProvider from its settings, and its companion object parses the options from SparkConf with fallback to defaults, Hadoop credential passwords and RPC SSL environment variables.

nodes.name: createJettySslContextFactoryServer
nodes.summary: Builds an optional Jetty SslContextFactory.Server from the key store, trust store, protocol and supported ciphers; returns None when SSL is disabled.

nodes.name: createConfigProvider
nodes.summary: Copies all SparkConf entries into a map, adds the SSL settings of this object under its namespace (default spark.ssl) and returns a MapConfigProvider over it.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Companion method that resolves an SSLOptions from SparkConf and Hadoop configuration for a namespace, using optional default options, Hadoop credential providers and RPC SSL password environment variables as fallbacks; returns disabled options when SSL is off.

nodes.name: SecurityManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SecurityManager, the class that holds Spark security configuration: authentication secret handling, view/modify/admin ACLs for users and groups, network encryption and RPC SSL options, plus constants for the auth secret config and environment variable.
nodes.languageNotes: Class with a companion object; mutable ACL sets are initialized in the constructor in a required order (admin ACLs first).

nodes.name: SecurityManager
nodes.summary: Spark class responsible for security. Normally created by SparkEnv, it reads the auth, ACL, encryption and SSL settings from SparkConf, answers permission checks for the UI and for modify actions, creates or looks up the authentication secret, and exposes RPC SSL options and the password environment for subprocesses. Also acts as the SecretKeyHolder with a single shared secret.

nodes.name: getSSLOptions
nodes.summary: Parses SSLOptions for the namespace spark.ssl.<module>, using the default spark.ssl options as fallback, and logs the result.

nodes.name: setViewAcls
nodes.summary: Sets the view ACL set to admin ACLs plus the default users plus the allowed users. Overload at line 128 takes a single default user string.

nodes.name: setViewAclsGroups
nodes.summary: Sets the view ACL groups to admin ACL groups plus the allowed groups; admin groups must be set first.

nodes.name: getViewAcls
nodes.summary: Returns the view ACLs as a comma separated string, or the wildcard "*" when it is present.

nodes.name: setModifyAcls
nodes.summary: Sets the modify ACL set to admin ACLs plus the default users plus the allowed users.

nodes.name: setModifyAclsGroups
nodes.summary: Sets the modify ACL groups to admin ACL groups plus the allowed groups.

nodes.name: getModifyAcls
nodes.summary: Returns the modify ACLs as a comma separated string, or the wildcard "*" when it is present.

nodes.name: setAdminAcls
nodes.summary: Replaces the admin ACL set; view and modify ACLs must be set again afterwards to pick up the change.

nodes.name: checkAdminPermissions
nodes.summary: Checks whether a user is an admin by testing the admin ACLs and groups; admins get view and modify rights and may impersonate users in UI requests.

nodes.name: checkUIViewPermissions
nodes.summary: Checks whether a user may view the UI against the view ACLs and groups; all users pass when ACLs are disabled, the user is null or a wildcard is set.

nodes.name: checkModifyPermissions
nodes.summary: Checks whether a user may modify the application against the modify ACLs and groups, with the same open-access rules as the view check.

nodes.name: isEncryptionEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether network encryption is enabled from the network crypto or SASL encryption configs, and turns it off with a warning when RPC SSL is enabled.

nodes.name: getSecretKey
nodes.summary: Returns the authentication secret when authentication is on, looking in the current user credentials, the local secretKey field, the environment, SparkConf and the secret file in that order, and failing if none is set. Overload at line 421 takes an app id and delegates to it.

nodes.name: initializeAuth
nodes.summary: Initializes the authentication secret: does nothing when auth is disabled, and for yarn, local and Kubernetes masters creates or reads a secret, storing it in the user credentials except on Kubernetes; for other masters it requires the secret in the configuration.

nodes.name: secretKeyFromFile
nodes.summary: Reads the secret key from the configured secret file and base64-encodes it, only permitted when the master is Kubernetes.

nodes.name: isUserInACL
nodes.summary: Private check used by the permission methods: grants access if the user is null, ACLs are disabled, a wildcard or the user is in the user set, otherwise tests whether the user belongs to an allowed group.

nodes.name: getEnvironmentForSslRpcPasswords
nodes.summary: When RPC SSL is enabled, returns a map of environment variable names to the key, private key, key store and trust store passwords so they can be passed to executors or other subprocesses.

nodes.name: SerializableWritable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SerializableWritable, a developer API wrapper that makes a Hadoop Writable usable with Java serialization.

nodes.name: SerializableWritable
nodes.summary: Developer API wrapper around a Hadoop Writable value. It marks the value transient and implements custom Java write and read hooks that write and read it through a Hadoop ObjectWritable, so the value can travel with serialized closures or RDDs.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook that writes the default fields and then the wrapped Writable through an ObjectWritable, inside tryOrIOException.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Java deserialization hook that reads the default fields, then rebuilds the wrapped Writable from an ObjectWritable created with an empty Hadoop Configuration.

nodes.name: SparkFileAlreadyExistsException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkFileAlreadyExistsException, a Hadoop file-already-exists exception that carries a Spark error class.

nodes.name: SparkFileAlreadyExistsException
nodes.summary: Hadoop FileAlreadyExistsException subclass that builds its message from an error class and message parameters through SparkThrowableHelper, and implements SparkThrowable accessors for the parameters, condition and optional SQL state. Used when an existing file blocks an operation.

nodes.name: SparkFiles.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the public SparkFiles object that resolves local paths of files added through SparkContext.addFile.

nodes.name: SparkFiles
nodes.summary: Public singleton that resolves paths to files added with SparkContext.addFile. It uses the root directory from SparkEnv and, when a job artifact state exists, a per-session UUID subdirectory.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the absolute path of an added file, prefixing the file name with the current job artifact UUID directory unless it is the default.

nodes.name: getRootDirectory
nodes.summary: Returns the root directory of added files, taken from the SparkEnv driver temporary directory or "." if none is set.

nodes.name: SparkStatusTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkStatusTracker, the low-level status API that reads job, stage and executor information from the AppStatusStore with weak consistency guarantees.

nodes.name: SparkStatusTracker
nodes.summary: Low-level, weakly consistent API for monitoring job and stage progress. It queries an AppStatusStore for jobs by group or tag, active stage and job ids, job and stage info, and executor info, returning only recent data limited by the retained jobs and stages settings.

nodes.name: getJobIdsForGroup
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of known jobs in a job group (or without a group when null), in any order and in any state.

nodes.name: getJobIdsForTag
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of known jobs that carry a given job tag, in any order and in any state.

nodes.name: getActiveStageIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all stages whose status is ACTIVE.

nodes.name: getActiveJobIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all jobs whose execution status is RUNNING.

nodes.name: getJobInfo
nodes.summary: Returns a SparkJobInfo (job id, stage ids, status) for a job id, or None when it is missing or garbage collected.

nodes.name: getStageInfo
nodes.summary: Returns a SparkStageInfo for the latest attempt of a stage (name, task counts, submission time), or None when it is missing or garbage collected.

nodes.name: getExecutorInfos
nodes.summary: Returns SparkExecutorInfo for the driver and all known executors, with host, port, cached memory, running task count and on-heap and off-heap storage memory metrics.

nodes.name: StatusAPIImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the private plain-data implementations of the SparkJobInfo, SparkStageInfo and SparkExecutorInfo interfaces. Instances carry the job, stage and executor status values handed out by the status API.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala classes with only constructor vals that implement Java interfaces.

nodes.name: SparkJobInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Private immutable implementation of SparkJobInfo holding the job id, its stage ids and its JobExecutionStatus.

nodes.name: SparkStageInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Private immutable implementation of SparkStageInfo holding the stage id, current attempt id, submission time, name and task counters (total, active, completed, failed).

nodes.name: SparkExecutorInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Private immutable implementation of SparkExecutorInfo holding host, port, cache size, running task count and used and total on-heap and off-heap storage memory.

nodes.name: TaskEndReason.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed hierarchy of reasons why a task ended (success, fetch failure, exception, kill, commit denial, executor loss, unknown). Each failure reason has an error string for the UI and a flag telling whether it counts toward the task failure limit.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed trait with case objects and case classes; a header note says new reasons must also be serialized in util.JsonProtocol.

nodes.name: TaskEndReason
nodes.summary: Sealed root trait of all task end reasons. It is a developer API type reported back by the task scheduler.

nodes.name: Success
nodes.summary: Case object meaning the task succeeded.

nodes.name: TaskFailedReason
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for all failure reasons. It requires toErrorString for the web UI and provides countTowardsTaskFailures (default true), which says whether the failure counts toward the maximum allowed task failures before the stage is aborted.

nodes.name: Resubmitted
nodes.summary: Case object for a ShuffleMapTask that finished earlier but must run again on another executor because the executor was lost before the stage completed.

nodes.name: FetchFailed
nodes.summary: Case class for a task that could not fetch shuffle data from a remote block manager, carrying the block manager address, shuffle id, map id and index, reduce id and message. It does not count toward task failures because the earlier stage that produced the data must be rerun.

nodes.name: ExceptionFailure
nodes.summary: Case class for a task that failed with a runtime exception (the most common failure, includes user program exceptions). It stores the class name, description, stack traces, an optional serializable wrapper of the exception, accumulator updates and metric peaks, and has helper constructors and withAccums and withMetricPeaks setters.

nodes.name: ThrowableSerializationWrapper
nodes.summary: Private[spark] Serializable wrapper holding a Throwable from user task code. If the Throwable cannot be deserialized, the field becomes null and a warning is logged, so the stack trace and message are still preserved elsewhere.

nodes.name: TaskResultLost
nodes.summary: Case object for a task that finished successfully but whose result was lost from the executor's block manager before it was fetched.

nodes.name: TaskKilled
nodes.summary: Case class for a task that was killed intentionally and must be rescheduled. It has a reason, accumulator updates and metric peaks, and does not count toward task failures.

nodes.name: TaskCommitDenied
nodes.summary: Case class for a task whose request to the driver to commit its output was denied. It does not count toward task failures, to avoid spurious stage failures when many speculative tasks are denied.

nodes.name: ExecutorLostFailure
nodes.summary: Case class for a task that failed because its executor was lost, with an optional reason and a flag saying whether the exit was caused by the running application. Only app-caused exits count toward task failures.

nodes.name: UnknownReason
nodes.summary: Case object for a task that ended for an unknown reason, for example a ClassNotFound error when deserializing the task result.

nodes.name: toErrorString
nodes.summary: Builds the error string for a fetch failure, printing the block manager address (or null), shuffle id, map index (Unknown when Int.MinValue), map id, reduce id and message.

nodes.name: toErrorString
nodes.summary: Returns the full stack trace string when present, otherwise falls back to the older exceptionString format for backward compatibility.

nodes.name: exceptionString
nodes.summary: Private helper that formats class name, description and an indented stack trace into a string, handling null values. It omits the exception causes and is kept for backward compatibility.

nodes.name: withAccums
nodes.summary: Sets the accumulators on this failure and returns it, used to attach accumulators after construction.

nodes.name: withMetricPeaks
nodes.summary: Sets the metric peaks on this failure and returns it.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Custom Java deserialization hook that reads the Throwable and, if that fails with an Exception, logs a warning and leaves the field unchanged.

nodes.name: toErrorString
nodes.summary: Builds an error string stating whether the executor exit was caused by a running task or unrelated to it, plus the optional reason.

nodes.name: TaskKilledException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares TaskKilledException, thrown when a task is explicitly killed so that the task failure is expected.

nodes.name: TaskKilledException
nodes.summary: Developer API RuntimeException carrying a kill reason, with an auxiliary constructor that uses the reason 'unknown reason'. Thrown when a task is explicitly killed.

nodes.name: TaskNotSerializableException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the exception thrown when a task cannot be serialized.

nodes.name: TaskNotSerializableException
nodes.summary: Private[spark] Exception wrapping the underlying error, thrown when a task cannot be serialized.

nodes.name: TaskOutputFileAlreadyExistException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the exception thrown when a task cannot write its output file because the file already exists.

nodes.name: TaskOutputFileAlreadyExistException
nodes.summary: Private[spark] Exception wrapping the underlying error, thrown when a task cannot write to its output file because it already exists.

nodes.name: SparkJobInfo.java
nodes.summary: Java interface exposing information about Spark jobs: job id, stage ids and execution status.
nodes.languageNotes: Java interface extending Serializable; the doc says it is not designed to be implemented outside Spark.

nodes.name: SparkJobInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable public interface with jobId, stageIds and status accessors, used to report job information. It is not meant to be implemented outside Spark because methods may be added.

nodes.name: SparkStageInfo.java
nodes.summary: Java interface exposing information about Spark stages: ids, name, submission time and task counters.
nodes.languageNotes: Java interface extending Serializable; the doc says it is not designed to be implemented outside Spark.

nodes.name: SparkStageInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable public interface with stageId, currentAttemptId, submissionTime, name and counters for total, active, completed and failed tasks. It is not meant to be implemented outside Spark because methods may be added.

nodes.name: HeartbeatReceiver.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the driver-side endpoint that receives executor heartbeats, forwards task metric updates to the task scheduler, and expires and replaces executors that stop sending heartbeats. It also defines the heartbeat message types.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing case-class messages with an RPC endpoint that is also a SparkListener.

nodes.name: Heartbeat
nodes.summary: Private[spark] message sent from an executor to the driver, carrying the executor id, per-task accumulator updates, the block manager id and executor metric peaks per (stage, attempt). It conveys liveness and progress of running tasks.

nodes.name: TaskSchedulerIsSet
nodes.summary: Case object event used by SparkContext to tell HeartbeatReceiver that its task scheduler has been created.

nodes.name: ExpireDeadHosts
nodes.summary: Case object message that triggers the check for executors without recent heartbeats.

nodes.name: ExecutorRegistered
nodes.summary: Private case class message telling the receiver that an executor was added.

nodes.name: ExecutorRemoved
nodes.summary: Private case class message telling the receiver that an executor was removed.

nodes.name: HeartbeatResponse
nodes.summary: Private[spark] reply to a heartbeat holding a flag saying whether the executor's block manager should re-register.

nodes.name: HeartbeatReceiver
nodes.summary: Driver-side class that is both a SparkListener and an isolated RPC endpoint. It records the last heartbeat time per executor, forwards heartbeat data to the TaskScheduler on a single-thread executor, replies with a HeartbeatResponse, and periodically removes and replaces executors whose heartbeat timed out. The companion object defines the endpoint name constant.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Schedules a fixed-rate task that asks the endpoint itself to run ExpireDeadHosts every check-timeout interval.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles local messages (executor registered or removed, scheduler set, expire dead hosts) and executor Heartbeat messages. For a known executor it updates the last-seen time and passes the update to the scheduler on the event loop thread; for an unknown executor or a scheduler that is not ready it replies with a HeartbeatResponse.

nodes.name: addExecutor
nodes.summary: Asks the endpoint with ExecutorRegistered and returns None if the receiver is stopped. Documented as for tests; also called by the listener hook.

nodes.name: onExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Listener callback that registers a newly added executor with the receiver.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Asks the endpoint with ExecutorRemoved and returns None if the receiver is stopped.

nodes.name: onExecutorRemoved
nodes.summary: Listener callback that tells the receiver an executor was removed, after the actual removal, to avoid noisy errors from in-flight heartbeats.

nodes.name: expireDeadHosts
nodes.summary: Finds executors whose last heartbeat is older than the timeout, logs a warning, and on a separate thread kills and replaces the executor and, for the coarse-grained backend, sends RemoveExecutor with ExecutorProcessLost. Throws for unknown backend types and forgets the executor.

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Cancels the timeout checking task and shuts down the event loop and kill-executor threads.

nodes.name: TaskState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TaskState enumeration with the task lifecycle values LAUNCHING, RUNNING, FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED and LOST, plus helpers to classify a state.

nodes.name: TaskState
nodes.summary: Spark-private Enumeration of the states a task can be in. It keeps a set of terminal states (FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED, LOST) and offers isFailed and isFinished checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala Enumeration object; the TaskState type alias is Value.

nodes.name: isFailed
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given state is LOST or FAILED.

nodes.name: isFinished
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given state is one of the terminal states FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED or LOST.

nodes.name: JavaDoubleRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Java-friendly wrapper around an RDD of Scala doubles. Exposes the common RDD operations and double-specific statistics (sum, mean, variance, histogram, approximate results) returning Java types.

nodes.name: JavaDoubleRDD
nodes.summary: Wraps an RDD[scala.Double] (srdd) and presents it as an RDD of java.lang.Double for Java callers. It delegates transformations such as distinct, filter, coalesce, subtract, sample and union to the underlying RDD and re-wraps the result, and offers numeric actions like sum, min, max, stats, mean, variance, stdev, histogram and approximate mean and sum. The companion object provides fromRDD and an implicit toRDD conversion.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object; both share one node. Many overloads (distinct, coalesce, subtract, sample, unpersist, histogram, meanApprox, sumApprox) delegate to srdd.

nodes.name: wrapRDD
nodes.summary: Wraps an RDD of java.lang.Double into a new JavaDoubleRDD by unboxing each element back to a Scala double.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Sets the storage level of the underlying RDD so values persist across operations, and returns a JavaDoubleRDD.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD as non-persistent and removes its blocks; this overload takes a blocking flag, while the no-argument overload (line 63) blocks until blocks are deleted.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Returns a new JavaDoubleRDD containing only the elements for which the given Java function returns true.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Returns a JavaDoubleRDD reduced into numPartitions partitions, optionally with a shuffle; another overload (line 96) takes only numPartitions.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Returns a JavaDoubleRDD with exactly numPartitions partitions, using a shuffle to redistribute data.

nodes.name: subtract
nodes.summary: Returns the elements of this RDD that are not in another JavaDoubleRDD, using a given Partitioner; overloads at lines 121 and 127 use the default partitioning or a partition count.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Returns a sampled subset of this RDD with or without replacement and a given seed; the overload at line 139 draws a random seed from Utils.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Returns the union of this JavaDoubleRDD and another one; identical elements appear multiple times.

nodes.name: intersection
nodes.summary: Returns the intersection of this JavaDoubleRDD and another one without duplicates; performs a shuffle internally.

nodes.name: min
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum element of the RDD using the natural ordering comparator.

nodes.name: max
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum element of the RDD using the natural ordering comparator.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Returns a StatCounter that captures the mean, variance and count of the RDD's elements in one pass.

nodes.name: meanApprox
nodes.summary: Returns a PartialResult holding an approximate mean within a timeout at a given confidence; the overload at line 227 omits the confidence.

nodes.name: sumApprox
nodes.summary: Returns a PartialResult holding an approximate sum within a timeout at a given confidence; the overload at line 238 omits the confidence.

nodes.name: histogram
nodes.summary: Computes a histogram using bucketCount evenly spaced buckets between the minimum and maximum, returning bucket boundaries and counts. Overloads at lines 270 and 274 take explicit bucket arrays (the latter with an evenBuckets flag).

nodes.name: setName
nodes.summary: Assigns a name to the underlying RDD and returns this JavaDoubleRDD.

nodes.name: fromRDD
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a JavaDoubleRDD from an RDD[scala.Double].

nodes.name: toRDD
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion from JavaDoubleRDD to its underlying RDD[scala.Double] (srdd).

nodes.name: JavaHadoopRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Java-friendly pair RDD wrapper around a HadoopRDD, adding mapPartitionsWithInputSplit so Java callers can see the InputSplit behind each partition.

nodes.name: JavaHadoopRDD
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi subclass of JavaPairRDD[K, V] that wraps a HadoopRDD. Its one extra method maps over a partition while exposing the org.apache.hadoop.mapred.InputSplit that was the base of that partition, using Java function and iterator types.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes implicit ClassTags for K and V as overriding vals.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithInputSplit
nodes.summary: Applies a Java Function2 over each partition's input split and iterator, converting between Java and Scala iterators, and returns a JavaRDD of the results. It delegates to HadoopRDD.mapPartitionsWithInputSplit.

nodes.name: JavaNewHadoopRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Java-friendly pair RDD wrapper around a NewHadoopRDD, adding mapPartitionsWithInputSplit so Java callers can see the InputSplit behind each partition.

nodes.name: JavaNewHadoopRDD
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi subclass of JavaPairRDD[K, V] that wraps a NewHadoopRDD. Its one extra method maps over a partition while exposing the org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.InputSplit that was the base of that partition, using Java function and iterator types.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes implicit ClassTags for K and V as overriding vals.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithInputSplit
nodes.summary: Applies a Java Function2 over each partition's input split and iterator, converting between Java and Scala iterators, and returns a JavaRDD of the results. It delegates to NewHadoopRDD.mapPartitionsWithInputSplit.

nodes.name: JavaPairRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JavaPairRDD, the Java-friendly wrapper around a Scala RDD of key-value pairs, plus its companion object with conversion helpers and implicit adapters. It exposes pair-RDD operations (joins, cogroup, aggregation by key, sorting, Hadoop output) with Java function types and Java collections.

nodes.name: wrapRDD
nodes.summary: Override of the abstract wrap hook from the shared Java RDD trait: wraps a Scala RDD of pairs into a new JavaPairRDD by delegating to the companion fromRDD.

nodes.name: cache
nodes.summary: Persists this RDD with the default storage level (MEMORY_ONLY) and returns the result as a JavaPairRDD.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Sets the storage level of the wrapped RDD so its values persist across operations after first computation, returning a new JavaPairRDD.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD as non-persistent and removes its blocks from memory and disk. Overloaded with a blocking flag version (line 82) that controls whether the call waits for deletion.

nodes.name: distinct
nodes.summary: Returns a new JavaPairRDD with the distinct elements. Overloaded: a no-arg version (line 89) and one taking a number of partitions (this node).

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Keeps only the pairs for which the Java Function predicate returns true, adapting the Java function to a Scala predicate.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Reduces the RDD to the given number of partitions, optionally with a shuffle. Overloaded: a one-argument version (line 106) and this two-argument version.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD with exactly the requested number of partitions by delegating to the Scala repartition, which uses a shuffle.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Returns a sampled subset of the RDD with or without replacement. Overloaded: the two-argument version (line 128) draws a random seed and calls this three-argument version.

nodes.name: sampleByKey
nodes.summary: Stratified sampling by key: converts a Java map of per-key fractions into a Scala map and delegates to the Scala sampleByKey. Overloaded with a version (line 164) that picks a random seed.

nodes.name: sampleByKeyExact
nodes.summary: Stratified sampling by key that makes extra passes to get an exact sample size per stratum, converting Java fractions into a Scala map. Overloaded with a version (line 199) that picks a random seed.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Returns the union of this RDD and another JavaPairRDD of the same type; identical elements appear multiple times.

nodes.name: intersection
nodes.summary: Returns the intersection of this RDD and another one without duplicates; the source notes it performs a shuffle internally.

nodes.name: first
nodes.summary: Override of first() so the generated bytecode returns a Tuple2 rather than Object, avoiding NoSuchMethodError at runtime (explained in the source comment).

nodes.name: combineByKey
nodes.summary: Generic per-key combine using createCombiner, mergeValue and mergeCombiners Java functions with an explicit partitioner, map-side combine flag and serializer. Other overloads (lines 281, 292, 537) default the partitioner, serializer and map-side combine.

nodes.name: reduceByKey
nodes.summary: Merges values per key with an associative, commutative Java reduce function, using the default partitioner. Overloads take an explicit partitioner (line 303) or a partition count (line 406).

nodes.name: reduceByKeyLocally
nodes.summary: Merges values per key like reduceByKey but returns the result immediately to the driver as a serializable Java Map.

nodes.name: countByKey
nodes.summary: Counts elements per key and returns the counts to the driver as a Java Map of Long values.

nodes.name: countByKeyApprox
nodes.summary: Approximate countByKey that can return a PartialResult if it does not finish within a timeout. The overload at line 322 omits the confidence argument, while this one takes it with default 0.95.

nodes.name: aggregateByKey
nodes.summary: Aggregates values per key with a zero value, a sequence function and a combine function, allowing a result type different from the value type. Overloads take a partition count (line 357) or neither (line 371).

nodes.name: foldByKey
nodes.summary: Merges values per key using an associative function and a neutral zero value. Overloads accept a partition count (line 390) or use the default partitioning (line 398).

nodes.name: groupByKey
nodes.summary: Groups values per key into a single Java Iterable, converting the Scala result with groupByResultToJava. Overloads take a partition count (line 428) or none (line 562); the doc recommends reduceByKey or combineByKey for aggregations.

nodes.name: subtract
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD with the elements of this one that are not in the other. Overloads take a partition count (line 443) or a partitioner (line 449).

nodes.name: subtractByKey
nodes.summary: Returns the pairs of this RDD whose keys are not present in the other JavaPairRDD. Overloads accept a partition count (line 466) or a partitioner (line 474).

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the RDD partitioned with the given partitioner.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Inner join on keys, returning (k, (v1, v2)) tuples, with an explicit partitioner. Overloads use the default hash join (line 570) or a partition count (line 578).

nodes.name: leftOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Left outer join with an explicit partitioner; maps each Scala Option into a Java Optional with JavaUtils.optionToOptional. Overloads at lines 587 and 598 use the default partitioning or a partition count.

nodes.name: rightOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Right outer join with an explicit partitioner; maps Scala Options to Java Optional. Overloads at lines 610 and 621 use default partitioning or a partition count.

nodes.name: fullOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Full outer join with an explicit partitioner; both sides become Java Optional values. Overloads at lines 636 and 651 use default partitioning or a partition count.

nodes.name: JavaPairRDD
nodes.summary: Java-friendly RDD of (K, V) pairs that wraps a Scala RDD and extends AbstractJavaRDDLike. Each method adapts Java functions and collections to the Scala RDD, PairRDDFunctions and OrderedRDDFunctions APIs and wraps results back into a JavaPairRDD. The companion object (lines 1035 to 1084, sharing this node id) holds fromRDD, fromJavaRDD, result-conversion helpers and implicit function adapters.

nodes.name: collectAsMap
nodes.summary: Returns the key-value pairs to the driver as a serializable Java Map; the source warns it should only be used for small results.

nodes.name: mapValues
nodes.summary: Transforms each value with a Java Function while keeping keys and the original partitioning.

nodes.name: flatMapValues
nodes.summary: Expands each value through a FlatMapFunction (a Java iterator converted to Scala) while keeping keys and partitioning.

nodes.name: cogroup
nodes.summary: Groups the values for each key across this RDD and up to three others into tuples of Java Iterables. Many overloads (lines 691 to 767) cover one, two or three other RDDs combined with a partitioner or a partition count; this node is the widest one (three others plus a partitioner).

nodes.name: groupWith
nodes.summary: Alias for cogroup over three other RDDs (this node) with Java Iterable results. Other overloads (lines 770 and 774) take one or two other RDDs.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Returns the values for a key as a Java List, searching only one partition when the RDD has a known partitioner.

nodes.name: saveAsHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD to a Hadoop-supported file system with the old mapred OutputFormat API. Overloads at lines 802 and 811 omit the JobConf or add a compression codec.

nodes.name: saveAsNewAPIHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD to a Hadoop-supported file system using the new mapreduce OutputFormat API with a Configuration. A second overload at line 839 omits the Configuration.

nodes.name: saveAsNewAPIHadoopDataset
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD to any Hadoop-supported storage system described by a Configuration object.

nodes.name: saveAsHadoopDataset
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD to a Hadoop-supported storage system configured by a JobConf that sets the OutputFormat and any output paths.

nodes.name: repartitionAndSortWithinPartitions
nodes.summary: Repartitions with the given partitioner and sorts records by key within each partition, pushing the sort into the shuffle. Uses a Comparator as the implicit ordering; the overload at line 864 uses a natural ordering comparator.

nodes.name: sortByKey
nodes.summary: Sorts the RDD by key so each partition holds a sorted range, using a Comparator, a direction flag and a partition count. Several overloads (lines 889 to 930) default the comparator, direction or partition count.

nodes.name: filterByRange
nodes.summary: Keeps only elements whose keys lie in the inclusive range lower to upper using a Comparator; can scan only matching partitions when range partitioned. The overload at line 952 uses natural ordering. Marked since 3.1.0.

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Returns a JavaRDD with the key of each tuple.

nodes.name: values
nodes.summary: Returns a JavaRDD with the value of each tuple.

nodes.name: countApproxDistinctByKey
nodes.summary: Approximates the number of distinct values per key (HyperLogLog based, as the source documents) with a given relative accuracy and a partitioner. Overloads take a partition count (line 1009) or only the accuracy (line 1024).

nodes.name: setName
nodes.summary: Assigns a name to the wrapped RDD and returns this JavaPairRDD for chaining.

nodes.name: groupByResultToJava
nodes.summary: Companion helper (private[spark]) that converts the Scala Iterable values of a grouped RDD into Java Iterables via mapValues.

nodes.name: cogroupResultToJava
nodes.summary: Companion helper (private[spark]) that converts a two-way cogroup result of Scala Iterables into Java Iterables.

nodes.name: cogroupResult2ToJava
nodes.summary: Companion helper (private[spark]) that converts a three-way cogroup result of Scala Iterables into Java Iterables.

nodes.name: cogroupResult3ToJava
nodes.summary: Companion helper (private[spark]) that converts a four-way cogroup result of Scala Iterables into Java Iterables.

nodes.name: fromRDD
nodes.summary: Companion factory that wraps a Scala RDD of key-value pairs in a JavaPairRDD; used throughout the class to wrap results.

nodes.name: toRDD
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion from a JavaPairRDD back to the Scala RDD it wraps, so Java-wrapped RDDs can be passed to Scala RDD methods.

nodes.name: toScalaFunction2
nodes.summary: Private[spark] implicit that adapts a Java Function2 to a Scala Function2 by calling its call method.

nodes.name: toScalaFunction
nodes.summary: Private[spark] implicit that adapts a Java Function to a Scala one-argument function.

nodes.name: pairFunToScalaFun
nodes.summary: Private[spark] implicit that adapts a Java PairFunction to a Scala function returning a tuple.

nodes.name: fromJavaRDD
nodes.summary: Converts a JavaRDD of key-value tuples into a JavaPairRDD, using fake class tags for key and value types.

nodes.name: JavaRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JavaRDD, the Java-friendly wrapper of RDD with its companion object. Used as the main Java-facing RDD type, returned by transformations throughout the Java API.

nodes.name: JavaRDD
nodes.summary: Java-friendly wrapper around a Scala RDD (class plus companion). It adds caching, partitioning, sampling, sorting and set-style transformations that return JavaRDD, on top of the shared JavaRDDLike operations. The companion provides implicit conversions to and from RDD and helpers to build a JavaRDD from a file or input stream of byte arrays.

nodes.name: wrapRDD
nodes.summary: Wraps a Scala RDD into a JavaRDD by delegating to the companion JavaRDD.fromRDD; this is the hook the shared JavaRDDLike operations use to build their results.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Persists the underlying RDD at the given storage level and returns it wrapped as a JavaRDD.

nodes.name: withResources
nodes.summary: Sets a ResourceProfile on the underlying RDD (needs a supporting cluster manager and dynamic allocation, per its doc comment) and returns the wrapped result.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Returns a JavaRDD with only the elements for which the Java Function predicate returns true, by calling filter on the underlying RDD.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Reduces the RDD to a given number of partitions, optionally with a shuffle; the numPartitions-only overload at line 101 is a one-line variant sharing this id.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Returns a sampled subset of the RDD using a user-supplied seed; the overload at lines 132-133 draws a random seed from Utils.random and delegates here.

nodes.name: randomSplit
nodes.summary: Randomly splits the RDD by the given weights and seed and wraps each piece as a JavaRDD; the overload at lines 159-160 picks a random seed and delegates here.

nodes.name: subtract
nodes.summary: Returns the elements of this RDD that are not in another RDD, with an explicit partition count; sibling overloads (lines 194 and 205-206) use the default partitioning or a given Partitioner.

nodes.name: setName
nodes.summary: Assigns a name to the underlying RDD and returns this JavaRDD.

nodes.name: sortBy
nodes.summary: Sorts the RDD by a key function given as a Java Function. It builds a natural Guava ordering and a fake ClassTag, then calls sortBy on the underlying RDD.

nodes.name: fromRDD
nodes.summary: Implicit companion conversion that wraps a Scala RDD into a JavaRDD given a ClassTag.

nodes.name: toRDD
nodes.summary: Implicit companion conversion that unwraps a JavaRDD back to its underlying Scala RDD.

nodes.name: readRDDFromFile
nodes.summary: Opens the named file and builds a JavaRDD of byte arrays from it with the requested parallelism; package-private helper in the api package.

nodes.name: readRDDFromInputStream
nodes.summary: Reads length-prefixed byte arrays from an input stream until EOF, then parallelizes them into a JavaRDD with the given parallelism and closes the stream.

nodes.name: JavaRDDLike.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JavaRDDLike trait with its AbstractJavaRDDLike workaround class: the shared transformations and actions for the Java RDD wrappers (JavaRDD, JavaPairRDD, JavaDoubleRDD). Each method adapts Java functions and collections to the underlying Scala RDD.

nodes.name: AbstractJavaRDDLike
nodes.summary: Private dummy abstract class that extends JavaRDDLike. Per its comment it works around a Scala compiler issue, so implementations such as JavaRDD extend it instead of the trait directly.

nodes.name: JavaRDDLike
nodes.summary: Trait defining the operations common to the Java RDD wrappers, each delegating to the underlying Scala RDD. It covers transformations, actions, checkpointing, ordering and async actions, converting between Scala and Java collections and types. Not intended to be implemented by user code.

nodes.name: partitions
nodes.summary: Returns the RDD partitions as a Java List by converting the underlying array.

nodes.name: partitioner
nodes.summary: Returns the RDD partitioner as a Java Optional, via JavaUtils.optionToOptional.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Computes or reads from cache the elements of one partition and returns them as a Java Iterator. The doc comment marks it as internal, for implementers of custom RDD subclasses.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Applies a Java Function to every element and returns a JavaRDD of the results.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithIndex
nodes.summary: Applies a Java Function2 to each partition together with its index, keeping the partition index of the original; preservesPartitioning defaults to false.

nodes.name: mapToDouble
nodes.summary: Maps each element to a double with a DoubleFunction and returns a JavaDoubleRDD.

nodes.name: mapToPair
nodes.summary: Maps each element to a key/value pair with a PairFunction and returns a JavaPairRDD.

nodes.name: flatMap
nodes.summary: Applies a FlatMapFunction to each element and flattens the resulting iterators into a JavaRDD.

nodes.name: flatMapToDouble
nodes.summary: Flat-maps each element with a DoubleFlatMapFunction into a JavaDoubleRDD.

nodes.name: flatMapToPair
nodes.summary: Flat-maps each element with a PairFlatMapFunction into a JavaPairRDD of key/value pairs.

nodes.name: mapPartitions
nodes.summary: Applies a FlatMapFunction over each partition iterator, with a preservesPartitioning flag; the overload at lines 152-157 omits the flag.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsToDouble
nodes.summary: Applies a DoubleFlatMapFunction per partition, with preservesPartitioning, and returns a JavaDoubleRDD; the overload at lines 174-179 omits the flag.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsToPair
nodes.summary: Applies a PairFlatMapFunction per partition, with preservesPartitioning, and returns a JavaPairRDD; the overload at lines 184-190 omits the flag.

nodes.name: foreachPartition
nodes.summary: Applies a VoidFunction to the iterator of each partition for side effects.

nodes.name: glom
nodes.summary: Coalesces the elements of each partition into a Java List, producing a JavaRDD of lists.

nodes.name: cartesian
nodes.summary: Returns the Cartesian product with another JavaRDDLike as a JavaPairRDD of all element pairs.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Groups elements by a key function, with a given partition count, into a JavaPairRDD of key and Iterable; the overload at lines 240-245 uses default partitioning. Uses implicit fake ClassTags and groupByResultToJava.

nodes.name: pipe
nodes.summary: Pipes elements to a forked external process and returns its output lines as a JavaRDD of strings. This is the widest of five overloads (command as String or List, optional env, working dir flag, buffer size, encoding).

nodes.name: zip
nodes.summary: Zips this RDD with another one into key/value pairs; assumes both have the same number of partitions and elements per partition.

nodes.name: zipPartitions
nodes.summary: Zips the partitions of this RDD with those of another using a FlatMapFunction2, returning a JavaRDD; both must have the same number of partitions.

nodes.name: zipWithUniqueId
nodes.summary: Zips elements with generated unique Long ids without triggering a job; ids may have gaps.

nodes.name: zipWithIndex
nodes.summary: Zips elements with their Long index, ordered by partition and then position; may trigger a job when there is more than one partition.

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Applies a VoidFunction to every element for side effects, calling foreach on the underlying RDD.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Returns all elements as a Java List; the doc warns to use it only when the result is small, since it is loaded into driver memory.

nodes.name: toLocalIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a Java Iterator over all elements, consuming memory up to the size of the largest partition.

nodes.name: collectPartitions
nodes.summary: Collects the elements of selected partitions as an array of Java Lists by running a job through the SparkContext. A comment says it helps implement take for other language frontends.

nodes.name: reduce
nodes.summary: Reduces the elements with a commutative, associative Java Function2 via the underlying RDD.

nodes.name: treeReduce
nodes.summary: Reduces elements in a multi-level tree with a suggested depth; the overload at line 400 uses depth 2.

nodes.name: fold
nodes.summary: Folds the elements of each partition and then the partition results using a zero value and an associative function.

nodes.name: aggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregates with a zero value, a per-partition seqOp and a combOp; the result type U may differ from the element type.

nodes.name: treeAggregate
nodes.summary: Tree-style aggregation with depth and an option to do the final aggregation on the executor; the overloads at lines 436-442 (with depth) and 447-452 (depth 2) are simpler forms.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of elements in the RDD.

nodes.name: countApprox
nodes.summary: Approximate count that returns a possibly incomplete PartialResult with error bounds within a timeout and confidence; the overload at lines 495-496 omits the confidence.

nodes.name: countByValue
nodes.summary: Counts each unique value and returns a serializable Java Map of value to count, using JavaUtils.mapAsSerializableJavaMap.

nodes.name: countByValueApprox
nodes.summary: Approximate countByValue returning a PartialResult of a Java Map of bounded values; the overload at lines 530-531 omits confidence.

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Returns the first num elements as a Java List, scanning partitions one by one.

nodes.name: takeSample
nodes.summary: Returns a fixed-size random sample as a Java List with a given seed; the overload at lines 544-545 draws a random seed.

nodes.name: first
nodes.summary: Returns the first element of the RDD.

nodes.name: saveAsTextFile
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD as a compressed text file using a CompressionCodec class; the overload at lines 564-566 writes uncompressed text.

nodes.name: saveAsObjectFile
nodes.summary: Saves the RDD as a SequenceFile of serialized objects.

nodes.name: keyBy
nodes.summary: Creates key/value tuples by applying a key function to each element, returning a JavaPairRDD.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD for checkpointing; it must be called before any job runs on the RDD.

nodes.name: getCheckpointFile
nodes.summary: Returns the checkpoint file name as a Java Optional.

nodes.name: toDebugString
nodes.summary: Returns a debugging description of the RDD and its recursive dependencies.

nodes.name: top
nodes.summary: Returns the top k elements using natural ordering via a Guava ordering; the overload at lines 630-632 takes a Comparator.

nodes.name: takeOrdered
nodes.summary: Returns the k smallest elements using natural ordering; the overload at lines 658-660 takes a Comparator.

nodes.name: max
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum element as defined by a Comparator.

nodes.name: min
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum element as defined by a Comparator.

nodes.name: countApproxDistinct
nodes.summary: Returns the approximate number of distinct elements for a given relative accuracy.

nodes.name: countAsync
nodes.summary: Asynchronous count that returns a JavaFutureAction wrapping the underlying future in a JavaFutureActionWrapper.

nodes.name: collectAsync
nodes.summary: Asynchronous collect returning a JavaFutureAction of a Java List.

nodes.name: takeAsync
nodes.summary: Asynchronous take returning a JavaFutureAction of the first num elements.

nodes.name: foreachAsync
nodes.summary: Asynchronous foreach that applies a VoidFunction to all elements and returns a JavaFutureAction of Void.

nodes.name: foreachPartitionAsync
nodes.summary: Asynchronous foreachPartition returning a JavaFutureAction of Void.

nodes.name: JavaSparkContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JavaSparkContext, a Java-friendly wrapper around SparkContext that returns JavaRDDs and works with Java collections, plus its companion object with implicit conversions and JAR lookup helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with several auxiliary constructors and many overloaded delegating methods that hide ClassTags from Java callers.

nodes.name: JavaSparkContext
nodes.summary: Java-friendly version of SparkContext: wraps a SparkContext (field sc) and exposes RDD creation (parallelize, textFile, Hadoop input), broadcast, file and JAR distribution, job group and tag control, and stop/close. Its companion object adds implicit conversions to and from SparkContext, jarOfClass, jarOfObject and fakeClassTag. Auxiliary constructors build the underlying SparkContext from a SparkConf or from master, app name, Spark home, JARs and environment. Most methods are thin delegations; overloads of the same name share one node.

nodes.name: statusTracker
nodes.summary: Returns a new JavaSparkStatusTracker built over the wrapped SparkContext.

nodes.name: parallelize
nodes.summary: Distributes a Java list to form a JavaRDD using a faked ClassTag and SparkContext.parallelize. The overload without numSlices (lines 149-150) uses defaultParallelism.

nodes.name: emptyRDD
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaRDD with no partitions or elements by wrapping a new EmptyRDD.

nodes.name: parallelizePairs
nodes.summary: Distributes a Java list of Tuple2 to form a JavaPairRDD, supplying faked key and value ClassTags. The overload at lines 161-162 uses defaultParallelism.

nodes.name: parallelizeDoubles
nodes.summary: Distributes a Java list of Doubles to form a JavaDoubleRDD by unboxing the values. The overload at lines 169-170 uses defaultParallelism.

nodes.name: textFile
nodes.summary: Reads a text file (UTF-8) from any Hadoop-supported file system into a JavaRDD of Strings. The single-argument overload at lines 177 omits minPartitions.

nodes.name: wholeTextFiles
nodes.summary: Reads a directory of text files as a JavaPairRDD of (path, content), one record per file. The overload at lines 231-232 uses the default minPartitions.

nodes.name: binaryFiles
nodes.summary: Reads a directory of binary files as a JavaPairRDD of (path, PortableDataStream). The overload at lines 297-298 uses defaultMinPartitions.

nodes.name: binaryRecords
nodes.summary: Loads a flat binary file with constant-length records as a JavaRDD of byte arrays.

nodes.name: sequenceFile
nodes.summary: Gets a JavaPairRDD for a Hadoop SequenceFile with the given key and value classes, building ClassTags from the classes. The overload at lines 336-341 omits minPartitions.

nodes.name: objectFile
nodes.summary: Loads an RDD previously saved as a SequenceFile of serialized objects, returning a JavaRDD. The overload at lines 362-365 omits minPartitions.

nodes.name: hadoopRDD
nodes.summary: Gets a JavaPairRDD for a Hadoop dataset described by a JobConf and InputFormat, wrapping the result in a JavaHadoopRDD. The overload at lines 416-426 omits minPartitions.

nodes.name: hadoopFile
nodes.summary: Gets a JavaPairRDD for a Hadoop file with an arbitrary old-API InputFormat, wrapped in JavaHadoopRDD. The overload at lines 457-467 omits minPartitions.

nodes.name: newAPIHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Gets a JavaPairRDD for a file with an arbitrary new-API InputFormat and extra Configuration, wrapped in JavaNewHadoopRDD.

nodes.name: newAPIHadoopRDD
nodes.summary: Gets a JavaPairRDD for a Hadoop Configuration and new-API InputFormat, wrapped in JavaNewHadoopRDD.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Builds the union of JavaPairRDDs (varargs). Overloads for JavaRDD (lines 520-524) and JavaDoubleRDD (538-541) share this node; all require a non-empty argument list and delegate to SparkContext.union.

nodes.name: broadcast
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a read-only value to the cluster and returns the Broadcast handle, using a faked ClassTag.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the underlying SparkContext. The overload at lines 566-568 also passes an exit code that is forwarded to the scheduler backend.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closeable implementation that simply calls stop().

nodes.name: getSparkHome
nodes.summary: Returns the Spark home location as a Java Optional, converting the Scala Option through JavaUtils.

nodes.name: addFile
nodes.summary: Adds a file to be downloaded with the job on every node. The overload at lines 602-604 adds a recursive flag for directories.

nodes.name: addJar
nodes.summary: Adds a JAR dependency for all tasks run on this context in the future.

nodes.name: hadoopConfiguration
nodes.summary: Returns the Hadoop Configuration shared by all Hadoop RDDs created from this context.

nodes.name: setCheckpointDir
nodes.summary: Sets the directory under which RDDs are checkpointed.

nodes.name: getCheckpointDir
nodes.summary: Returns the checkpoint directory as a Java Optional.

nodes.name: checkpointFile
nodes.summary: Protected helper that reads a checkpointed RDD from a path as a JavaRDD with a faked ClassTag.

nodes.name: getConf
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the SparkConf of the wrapped context.

nodes.name: getReadOnlyConf
nodes.summary: Returns a read-only view of the Spark configuration.

nodes.name: setLocalProperty
nodes.summary: Sets a local property (for example a fair scheduler pool) that affects jobs submitted from this thread and is inherited by child threads.

nodes.name: getLocalProperty
nodes.summary: Returns a thread-local property value, or null if it is missing.

nodes.name: setLogLevel
nodes.summary: Overrides the log level of the wrapped context using a level name such as INFO or WARN.

nodes.name: setJobGroup
nodes.summary: Assigns a group ID and description to all jobs started by this thread, optionally interrupting on cancel. The two-argument overload at line 730 sets interruptOnCancel to false.

nodes.name: addJobTag
nodes.summary: Adds a tag to all jobs started by this thread; removeJobTag, getJobTags and clearJobTags (lines 765-779) are sibling delegations.

nodes.name: cancelJobGroup
nodes.summary: Cancels active jobs of a group with a reason. The overload at line 798 omits the reason.

nodes.name: cancelJobsWithTag
nodes.summary: Cancels active jobs carrying a tag, with a reason. The overload at line 817 omits the reason.

nodes.name: cancelAllJobs
nodes.summary: Cancels all scheduled or running jobs.

nodes.name: getPersistentRDDs
nodes.summary: Returns a Java map of the JavaRDDs that have been marked persistent, converting each RDD with JavaRDD.fromRDD.

nodes.name: fromSparkContext
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion in the companion object that wraps a SparkContext in a new JavaSparkContext.

nodes.name: toSparkContext
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion in the companion object that unwraps the sc field of a JavaSparkContext.

nodes.name: jarOfClass
nodes.summary: Finds the JAR a class was loaded from, as an array, via SparkContext.jarOfClass.

nodes.name: jarOfObject
nodes.summary: Finds the JAR containing the class of an object, as an array, via SparkContext.jarOfObject.

nodes.name: fakeClassTag
nodes.summary: Produces a ClassTag[T] that is really ClassTag.AnyRef cast, keeping ClassTags out of the Java API. Used by most RDD-creating methods; may cost primitive specialization at runtime.

nodes.name: PythonHadoopUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the Converter trait and its helper implementations that translate between Hadoop Writable objects and plain Java objects, plus PythonHadoopUtil with Configuration and RDD conversion helpers. Used when RDDs are read from or written to Hadoop formats through a Python-facing API.

nodes.name: Converter
nodes.summary: Trait Converter[-T, +U] with a single convert method, meant to be implemented to add custom transformation when reading or writing custom classes. Its companion object getInstance loads a converter class by name through reflection, logging success or failure, and falls back to a default converter when no class is named.

nodes.name: getInstance
nodes.summary: Instantiates the converter class named in an Option via Utils.classForName and its no-argument constructor, logging the load or rethrowing on failure; returns the supplied default converter if no class name is given.

nodes.name: WritableToJavaConverter
nodes.summary: Converter that turns common Hadoop Writable objects (ints, doubles, longs, text, bytes, arrays, maps and so on) into primitives, Strings, byte arrays, arrays or Java maps, cloning other Writables with the broadcast Hadoop configuration. Non-Writable inputs pass through unchanged.

nodes.name: convertWritable
nodes.summary: Pattern-matches a Writable and returns the underlying primitive, String, copied byte array, converted object array, or Java HashMap built recursively from a MapWritable; unknown Writables are cloned with WritableUtils.clone.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Converter entry point: applies convertWritable to Writable inputs and returns any other object unchanged.

nodes.name: JavaToWritableConverter
nodes.summary: Converter that turns common Java types (boxed numbers, String, Boolean, byte arrays, null, Java maps, object arrays) into Hadoop Writables. Existing Writables pass through, and unsupported types raise a SparkException.

nodes.name: convertToWritable
nodes.summary: Pattern-matches a Java object and builds the matching Writable, recursing into maps and arrays and throwing a SparkException for unsupported types.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Converter entry point: returns Writable inputs as is and otherwise delegates to convertToWritable.

nodes.name: PythonHadoopUtil
nodes.summary: Utility object with helpers for moving data between Python-facing objects and Hadoop-related objects: building a Hadoop Configuration from a Java map, merging two configurations, and applying key and value Converters over an RDD of pairs.

nodes.name: mapToConf
nodes.summary: Copies the entries of a Java map into a new Hadoop Configuration created without default resources.

nodes.name: mergeConfs
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the left Configuration with every entry of the right one set on top, so right-hand keys win.

nodes.name: convertRDD
nodes.summary: Maps an RDD of key-value pairs to an RDD of (Any, Any) by applying the key Converter and value Converter to each pair.

nodes.name: PythonPartitioner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonPartitioner, a Partitioner for long-valued keys whose equality includes the id of the Python-side partition function. It is used by the Python API to decide which partition a key belongs to.

nodes.name: PythonPartitioner
nodes.summary: Partitioner subclass that stores numPartitions and the unique id() of the Python partitioning function so the id takes part in equals and hashCode. Keys are mapped to a partition with a non-negative modulo, and null keys go to partition 0.

nodes.name: getPartition
nodes.summary: Maps a key to a partition: null goes to 0, Long keys use the int value, and other keys use hashCode, always through Utils.nonNegativeMod with numPartitions because the Python partition function is not trusted to return valid ids.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two PythonPartitioner instances are equal when both numPartitions and pyPartitionFunctionId match.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Computes a hash from numPartitions and the hash of pyPartitionFunctionId, consistent with equals.

nodes.name: JavaSparkStatusTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JavaSparkStatusTracker, a thin wrapper over the SparkContext status tracker that exposes job, stage and executor status to Java callers. Missing information is returned as null instead of Option.

nodes.name: JavaSparkStatusTracker
nodes.summary: Low-level status reporting API for monitoring job and stage progress, with weak consistency semantics and information limited to recent jobs and stages. Every method delegates to sc.statusTracker and converts Option results to null.

nodes.name: getJobIdsForGroup
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all known jobs in a job group (or those without a group when the argument is null), delegating to the status tracker.

nodes.name: getActiveStageIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all active stages, with no ordering guarantee.

nodes.name: getActiveJobIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all active jobs, with no ordering guarantee.

nodes.name: getJobInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the SparkJobInfo for a job id, or null if it is missing or was garbage collected.

nodes.name: getStageInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the SparkStageInfo for a stage id, or null if it is missing or was garbage collected.

nodes.name: getExecutorInfos
nodes.summary: Returns information on all known executors including the driver (host, port, cacheSize, numRunningTasks and memory metrics).

nodes.name: JavaUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds JavaUtils, a private[spark] helper object for Java interop: converting Scala Option to the Java Optional type and wrapping a Scala Map as a serializable java.util.AbstractMap view.
nodes.languageNotes: The wrapper reimplements a Scala map-wrapper class so that it can implement java.io.Serializable; the comment cites SPARK-3926 / SI-8911 as the reason.

nodes.name: JavaUtils
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object with Java interop helpers: optionToOptional and mapAsSerializableJavaMap, plus the nested SerializableMapWrapper class.

nodes.name: optionToOptional
nodes.summary: Converts a Scala Option into the Java Optional type, using Optional.of for a defined value and Optional.empty otherwise.

nodes.name: mapAsSerializableJavaMap
nodes.summary: Wraps a Scala collection.Map in a SerializableMapWrapper (a workaround for SPARK-3926 / SI-8911).

nodes.name: SerializableMapWrapper
nodes.summary: java.util.AbstractMap view over a Scala collection.Map that also implements java.io.Serializable. It delegates size, containsKey and get to the underlying map, and its entrySet iterator supports remove only when the underlying map is mutable.
