nodes.languageNotes: Copied from the Scala library map wrapper because that class has no no-arg constructor and cannot just be subclassed to add Serializable.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the size of the underlying Scala map.

nodes.name: containsKey
nodes.summary: Delegates the key lookup to the underlying map instead of iterating the key set, and returns false when the key has the wrong type (ClassCastException).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the underlying map, returning null when it is absent or the key has the wrong type.

nodes.name: entrySet
nodes.summary: Builds the AbstractSet entry view over the underlying map. Its iterator returns Map.Entry objects whose setValue calls put on the wrapper, and its remove removes the last returned key if the underlying map is mutable, otherwise it throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object for org.apache.spark.api.java, which is empty and exists only to carry the package documentation "Spark Java programming APIs".

nodes.name: java
nodes.summary: Empty package object whose only purpose is the package-level doc comment for the Spark Java programming APIs.

nodes.name: Py4JServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Py4JServer, which creates and controls the Py4J server used by the Python side to talk to the JVM. The server type is picked from the PYSPARK_PIN_THREAD environment variable.

nodes.name: Py4JServer
nodes.summary: Wrapper around either a Py4J ClientServer (thread pinning, the default) or a GatewayServer, bound to the loopback address on an ephemeral port with a secret auth token created from the SparkConf. It offers start, getListeningPort and shutdown that dispatch on the server type.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the underlying ClientServer or GatewayServer, and throws an unexpected-server error for any other type.

nodes.name: getListeningPort
nodes.summary: Returns the port the underlying server listens on, handling both server types.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down the underlying server, handling both server types.

nodes.name: PythonErrorUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonErrorUtils, an object of accessors that read structured error metadata from a SparkThrowable, because Py4J does not work with default methods.

nodes.name: PythonErrorUtils
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object whose static-style methods forward to SparkThrowable accessors (condition, SQL state, message parameters, query context and others), so that the Python side can call them through Py4J.

nodes.name: getCondition
nodes.summary: Returns the error condition of the throwable.

nodes.name: getErrorClass
nodes.summary: Returns the error condition (same value as getCondition, kept under the older error class name).

nodes.name: getSqlState
nodes.summary: Returns the SQLSTATE of the throwable.

nodes.name: isInternalError
nodes.summary: Tells whether the throwable is an internal error.

nodes.name: getBreakingChangeInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the BreakingChangeInfo of the throwable.

nodes.name: getMessageParameters
nodes.summary: Returns the message parameters as a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: getDefaultMessageTemplate
nodes.summary: Returns the default message template of the throwable.

nodes.name: getQueryContext
nodes.summary: Returns the array of QueryContext entries of the throwable.

nodes.name: PythonGatewayServer.scala
nodes.summary: Entry point of the JVM process that hosts a Py4J server for a Python driver. It publishes the bound port and auth secret to a file and exits when the Python driver closes stdin.

nodes.name: PythonGatewayServer
nodes.summary: Private[spark] main object launched via SparkSubmit by the Python driver (the source names java_gateway.py). It starts a Py4JServer on an ephemeral port, writes the port and secret to the file named by _PYSPARK_DRIVER_CONN_INFO_PATH through a temp file and rename, and then blocks reading System.in so that it exits when the Python driver dies.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates a Py4JServer from a new SparkConf, starts it, and exits with status 1 if binding failed. It then writes the port, secret length and secret bytes to the connection-info file, and loops on System.in.read until EOF before exiting with 0.

nodes.name: TestUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Test helper utilities kept in the main codebase because several projects use them: building jars, asserting spills, HTTP helpers, a local HTTP server, listener helpers, log4j2 test config and temp file creation. Also defines the private SpillListener.
nodes.languageNotes: Lives in main sources (the file TODO says to move it to test code once project test dependencies allow it).

nodes.name: TestUtils
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object extending SparkTestUtils with helpers for tests: jar creation, spill assertions, exception message assertions, Python availability checks, executable lookup, HTTP request helpers and a test HTTP server, listener scoping, executor waiting, log4j2 configuration, and temp JSON/script file creation.

nodes.name: createJarWithClasses
nodes.summary: Creates a jar of compiled classes with the given names (optionally with base classes and extra classpath URLs) in a temp directory, and returns its URL. Class names should be unique when used in class loader tests.

nodes.name: createJarWithFiles
nodes.summary: Creates a jar from a map of entry names to string contents, in the given or a temp directory, and returns its URL.

nodes.name: createJar
nodes.summary: Writes the given files into a jar (optionally under a directory prefix and with a Main-Class manifest entry) and returns the jar URL.

nodes.name: assertSpilled
nodes.summary: Runs a code body with a SpillListener installed and asserts that at least one stage spilled.

nodes.name: assertNotSpilled
nodes.summary: Runs a code body with a SpillListener installed and asserts that no stage spilled.

nodes.name: assertExceptionMsg
nodes.summary: Asserts that some exception in the cause chain contains a message (optionally ignoring case), and, when a type parameter is given, that the matching exception is of that subtype.

nodes.name: testCommandAvailable
nodes.summary: Tells whether a command is available, by delegating to Utils.checkCommandAvailable.

nodes.name: isPythonVersionAvailable
nodes.summary: Checks whether python3 at or above minimumPythonSupportedVersion is available.

nodes.name: isPythonVersionAtLeast
nodes.summary: Runs python3 through a shell (cmd.exe on Windows, sh otherwise) to test whether its version is at least major.minor.reversion, returning false on failure.

nodes.name: getAbsolutePathFromExecutable
nodes.summary: Resolves the absolute path of an executable, checking the current directory for bare names and otherwise searching the PATH entries.

nodes.name: httpResponseCode
nodes.summary: Returns the response code of an HTTP(S) request made through withHttpConnection.

nodes.name: redirectUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the Location header of an HTTP(S) response made through withHttpConnection.

nodes.name: httpResponseMessage
nodes.summary: Returns the body of an HTTP(S) response as text, read through withHttpConnection.

nodes.name: withHttpConnection
nodes.summary: Opens an HttpURLConnection with the given method and headers, disables certificate and host name validation for HTTPS, runs the supplied function and always disconnects.

nodes.name: withListener
nodes.summary: Adds a SparkListener to the SparkContext, runs the body, then waits until the listener bus is empty and removes the listener.

nodes.name: withHttpServer
nodes.summary: Starts an embedded Jetty server on a random port serving files from a base directory, passes its URL to the body, and stops the server afterwards.

nodes.name: waitUntilExecutorsUp
nodes.summary: Polls the status tracker until more than numExecutors executors are listed, and throws TimeoutException when the timeout elapses first.

nodes.name: configTestLog4j2
nodes.summary: Reconfigures log4j2 with a console appender writing to stderr at the given root level, for test suites.

nodes.name: recursiveList
nodes.summary: Lists the files and directories under a directory recursively.

nodes.name: listDirectory
nodes.summary: Lists file paths under a path recursively, skipping files whose names start with a dot or underscore (as MapReduce does).

nodes.name: createTempJsonFile
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON value to a new temp file in the given directory and returns its path.

nodes.name: createTempScriptWithExpectedOutput
nodes.summary: Creates an executable temp bash script that prints the given output with a here-document and returns its path.

nodes.name: SpillListener
nodes.summary: Private SparkListener that records task metrics per stage and, when a stage completes, marks the stage as spilled if the summed memoryBytesSpilled is above zero. Used by assertSpilled and assertNotSpilled.

nodes.name: numSpilledStages
nodes.summary: Returns, under the listener lock, the number of stages that were found to spill.

nodes.name: onTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Stores the finished task metrics under the task stage id.

nodes.name: onStageCompleted
nodes.summary: On stage completion, sums memoryBytesSpilled over the stage task metrics and records the stage id as spilled when the sum is positive.

nodes.name: JavaFutureAction.java
nodes.summary: Java interface JavaFutureAction, a java.util.concurrent.Future that also reports the ids of the jobs run by the underlying async operation.

nodes.name: JavaFutureAction
nodes.summary: Generic interface extending Future<T> with jobIds(), which returns a snapshot of the job ids run by the async operation. Some operations run several jobs, so later calls can return different lists.

nodes.name: jobIds
nodes.summary: Returns the current snapshot of the job ids run by the underlying async operation.

nodes.name: Optional.java
nodes.summary: Defines a final, serializable Optional container for a value that may be absent, offering a subset of the java.util.Optional and Guava Optional APIs.

nodes.name: Optional
nodes.summary: Work-alike clone of Optional used by Spark's Java API in preference to returning null. It holds a single value or none, with factories empty, of, ofNullable, absent and fromNullable and accessors get, orElse, or, orNull and isPresent. Its source states it exists because java.util.Optional was not used at the time and the Guava Optional caused library version conflicts.
nodes.languageNotes: Final generic class implementing Serializable; equals uses pattern matching on instanceof.

nodes.name: empty
nodes.summary: Returns the shared empty Optional instance cast to the requested type.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Wraps a non-null value in an Optional and throws NullPointerException for null.

nodes.name: ofNullable
nodes.summary: Wraps a possibly null value, returning empty() when it is null and of(value) otherwise.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the wrapped value and throws NullPointerException if the Optional is empty.

nodes.name: orElse
nodes.summary: Returns the wrapped value if present, otherwise the supplied default.

nodes.name: isPresent
nodes.summary: Returns true when the Optional holds a value.

nodes.name: absent
nodes.summary: Guava-style alias that returns an empty Optional by calling empty().

nodes.name: fromNullable
nodes.summary: Guava-style alias for ofNullable.

nodes.name: or
nodes.summary: Guava-style accessor returning the value if present, otherwise the supplied default.

nodes.name: orNull
nodes.summary: Returns the value if present, or null when empty.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares two Optionals by their wrapped values using Objects.equals.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Returns 0 for an empty Optional, otherwise the hash code of the value.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns "Optional.empty" or "Optional[value]".

nodes.name: StorageLevels.java
nodes.summary: Exposes commonly used StorageLevel constants (NONE, DISK_ONLY, MEMORY_ONLY, MEMORY_AND_DISK, OFF_HEAP and their serialized and replicated variants) for Java callers, with a create factory.

nodes.name: StorageLevels
nodes.summary: Holder of public static StorageLevel constants built through its create method, so Java code can pick a storage level without calling the Scala companion directly.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a StorageLevel from useDisk, useMemory, useOffHeap, deserialized and replication arguments by calling StorageLevel.apply.

nodes.name: DriverPlugin.java
nodes.summary: Declares the DriverPlugin interface, the driver-side component of a SparkPlugin, with lifecycle hooks init, registerMetrics, receive and shutdown.

nodes.name: DriverPlugin
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi interface for the driver component of a plugin, with default implementations. init runs early in driver startup and returns a map handed to the executor plugin; registerMetrics runs later once the app ID is known; receive handles RPC messages sent by the executor component; shutdown is called when the application stops.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes the plugin early in driver startup, before the task scheduler exists, and returns a map of configuration passed to ExecutorPlugin init; the default returns an empty map.

nodes.name: registerMetrics
nodes.summary: Called later in startup, after the application ID is known, so the plugin can register metrics with the registry from its PluginContext; the default does nothing.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles an RPC message sent by the executor-side component and returns an optional reply; the default throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Informs the plugin that the application is shutting down; the default does nothing.

nodes.name: ExecutorPlugin.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ExecutorPlugin interface, the executor-side component of a SparkPlugin, with hooks for init, shutdown and per-task start, success and failure.

nodes.name: ExecutorPlugin
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi interface for the executor component of a plugin. init and shutdown run during executor start and stop and block them; onTaskStart, onTaskSucceeded and onTaskFailed run on the task thread for every task and their exceptions are caught and suppressed.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Called during executor initialization with the PluginContext and extra configuration returned by the driver component; metrics should be registered here.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Cleans up the plugin during executor shutdown and blocks shutdown until it returns.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Runs before each task on the task's thread; exceptions are logged and suppressed, so it should stay cheap.

nodes.name: onTaskSucceeded
nodes.summary: Runs after a task completes without exceptions, even if onTaskStart failed.

nodes.name: onTaskFailed
nodes.summary: Runs after a task fails, receiving the TaskFailedReason.

nodes.name: PluginContext.java
nodes.summary: Declares the PluginContext interface passed to plugins at initialization, giving access to the metric registry, SparkConf, executor ID, hostname, resources and messaging to the driver component.

nodes.name: PluginContext
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi interface that is plugin-specific: metrics and messages are tied to one plugin. It exposes the metric registry, the application configuration, the executor ID, the hostname and the allocated custom resources, and lets a plugin send a one-way message or ask the driver component and wait for a reply.

nodes.name: metricRegistry
nodes.summary: Returns the registry where the plugin registers its metrics.

nodes.name: conf
nodes.summary: Returns the SparkConf of the application.

nodes.name: executorID
nodes.summary: Returns the executor ID of the process; on the driver it identifies the driver.

nodes.name: hostname
nodes.summary: Returns the host name the Spark process uses for communication.

nodes.name: resources
nodes.summary: Returns the custom resources (such as GPUs or FPGAs) allocated to the driver or executor, keyed by name.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Sends a serializable message to the plugin's driver-side component without waiting for a reply; returns once enqueued.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Sends an RPC to the driver-side component and blocks until a reply arrives or the RPC ask timeout elapses; driver errors are rethrown.

nodes.name: SparkPlugin.java
nodes.summary: Declares the SparkPlugin interface, the entry point of a dynamically loadable plugin that supplies optional driver and executor components.

nodes.name: SparkPlugin
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi interface for a plugin loaded by adding its class name to Spark configuration. It has two optional parts: one driver-side DriverPlugin per application and one ExecutorPlugin per executor; returning null means a component is not needed.

nodes.name: driverPlugin
nodes.summary: Returns the plugin's driver-side component, or null if none is needed.

nodes.name: executorPlugin
nodes.summary: Returns the plugin's executor-side component, or null if none is needed.

nodes.name: ResourceDiscoveryPlugin.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ResourceDiscoveryPlugin interface that lets a plugin control how custom resource addresses are discovered.

nodes.name: ResourceDiscoveryPlugin
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi interface for pluggable discovery of custom resources. Plugins can be chained so different plugins handle different resource types; one that does not handle a resource returns an empty Optional so other plugins and finally the default discovery script plugin are tried.

nodes.name: discoverResource
nodes.summary: Discovers the addresses of the requested resource, called early in executor, driver or worker initialization, and returns an Optional ResourceInformation. Spark fails if too few addresses are returned.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PythonWorkerUtils singleton, which holds the helpers the JVM uses to write setup data (UTF strings, byte arrays, task context, Spark files, broadcasts, functions, conf) to a Python worker stream and to read strings, bytes and accumulator updates back. Each writer notes the worker-side function that consumes the data.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object marked private[spark]; mixes in Logging and exposes an implicit json4s Formats value.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton object with static-style helpers that define the wire format between the JVM and a Python worker: length-prefixed UTF-8 strings and byte arrays, a JSON task context, Spark file directory and includes, broadcast variable updates, serialized Python functions and conf key-value pairs. It also reads accumulator updates sent back by the worker.

nodes.name: writeUTF
nodes.summary: Encodes a string as UTF-8 bytes and writes it with writeBytes, to be read by UTF8Deserializer.loads on the Python side.

nodes.name: writeBytes
nodes.summary: Writes a 4-byte length followed by the byte array, matching FramedSerializer._read_with_length on the Python side.

nodes.name: writePythonVersion
nodes.summary: Writes the driver-side Python version string so the worker can check it with worker_util.check_python_version.

nodes.name: writeTaskContext
nodes.summary: Serializes task context information (barrier flag, connection info, secret, stage, partition and attempt ids, cpus, resources, local properties) to JSON and writes it for worker_util.setup_task_context.

nodes.name: writeSparkFiles
nodes.summary: Writes the Spark files root directory (scoped by job artifact UUID when present) and the number and names of Python includes (zip and egg files) for worker_util.setup_spark_files.

nodes.name: writeBroadcasts
nodes.summary: Computes which broadcast variables to remove from and add to the worker, then writes the changes. When serializer encryption is enabled and new broadcasts exist, it starts an EncryptedPythonBroadcastServer and sends its connection info; otherwise it sends the broadcast ids and paths directly.

nodes.name: writePythonFunction
nodes.summary: Writes the command bytes of a PythonFunction to the worker.

nodes.name: writeConf
nodes.summary: Writes the number of conf entries followed by each key and value as UTF strings.

nodes.name: readUTF
nodes.summary: Reads a UTF-8 string of a given byte length (the overload without a length reads the length from the stream first, at lines 209-211).

nodes.name: readBytes
nodes.summary: Reads a byte array of a given length with readFully, returning an empty array for zero length (the overload without a length reads the length first, at lines 223-225).

nodes.name: receiveAccumulatorUpdates
nodes.summary: Reads the number of accumulator updates sent by worker_util.send_accumulator_updates and adds each byte update to the optional PythonAccumulator.

nodes.name: BaseRRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BaseRRunner, the abstract driver for running R code in a worker process: it opens a local server socket, launches an R worker (through a shared daemon on non-Windows systems when enabled), authenticates two connections and streams input and output. The file also holds the reader and writer helper classes, protocol constants and the stderr-capturing thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with an abstract generic class that declares nested abstract classes ReaderIterator and WriterThread; the companion object keeps the daemon state in synchronized fields.

nodes.name: BaseRRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract class that runs R UDFs: compute opens a localhost ServerSocket, starts an R worker, accepts one connection for input (served by a writer thread) and one for output (read through a ReaderIterator). Subclasses supply newReaderIterator and newWriterThread. Its companion object (lines 257-360) launches R processes and manages the daemon channel.

nodes.name: ReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract nested iterator that pulls the next output object from the R worker stream through the abstract read method and marks end-of-stream with eos. Its handleException turns exceptions into a SparkException that includes the lines captured from the R process.

nodes.name: WriterThread
nodes.summary: Abstract nested thread named 'writer for R' that sends the partition index, serializer names, package names, function, broadcast variables, partition count, mode, optional column names and a has-data flag to the R process, then calls writeIteratorToStream. Errors are logged and the output stream is closed at the end.

nodes.name: SpecialLengths
nodes.summary: Singleton holding the marker value TIMING_DATA (-1) that the R worker sends in place of a data length to signal timing information.

nodes.name: RRunnerModes
nodes.summary: Singleton with the integer mode constants RDD, DATAFRAME_DAPPLY and DATAFRAME_GAPPLY that tell the R worker how it is being used.

nodes.name: BufferedStreamThread
nodes.summary: Thread that reads lines from an input stream, logs each one and keeps the most recent errBufferSize lines in a circular buffer. getLines returns the buffered lines so they can be attached to failure messages.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Starts a timing clock, opens a ServerSocket on localhost, creates the R worker, accepts and authenticates the input and output sockets, starts the writer thread on the input socket and returns a reader iterator over the output socket. The server socket is closed once both connections are accepted.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns true when a buffered object exists or when read() produces another one before end of stream.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the buffered object and clears it, or fails with an empty iterator error when no more data is available.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Sets the SparkEnv and TaskContext for the thread and writes the full R request header and data to the stream, using SerDe for strings and column names. Exceptions are logged and the output is closed in the finally block.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Reads every line from the stream, stores it in the circular buffer under synchronization and logs it.

nodes.name: getLines
nodes.summary: Returns the buffered lines in order, oldest first, joined with newlines.

nodes.name: startStdoutThread
nodes.summary: Creates a daemon BufferedStreamThread of 100 lines on the process input stream, starts it and returns it.

nodes.name: getROptions
nodes.summary: Runs the R command with --version, parses the version number and returns --no-restore for R 4.2 or later, otherwise --vanilla (also the fallback on any failure).

nodes.name: createRProcess
nodes.summary: Builds and starts the R process for a given script (daemon.R or worker.R) from the SparkR worker directory, sets the SPARKR_* environment variables including the port and secret, merges stderr into stdout and returns the reader thread.

nodes.name: createRWorker
nodes.summary: Launches an R worker for a given port. Unless running on Windows or the daemon is disabled, it lazily starts a single daemon process, authenticates it and sends the port over the daemon channel (resetting state if the daemon died); otherwise it starts worker.R directly.

nodes.name: RRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RDD classes backed by R functions (BaseRRDD, PairwiseRRDD, RRDD, StringRRDD), the RRDD companion with helpers that create the SparkContext and RDDs from R data, and RParallelizeServer for receiving R data over an authenticated socket.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file where the class RRDD and the object RRDD share one node id; the classes are private to the package.

nodes.name: BaseRRDD
nodes.summary: Private abstract RDD subclass that keeps the parent partitions and, in compute, creates an RRunner and runs it on the parent's iterator for the partition. The concrete RRDD types differ in their serializer and element type.

nodes.name: PairwiseRRDD
nodes.summary: RDD of (Int, Array[Byte]) pairs formed from key-value pairs returned by R, used by SparkR shuffle operations; it passes the BYTE serialization format and exposes a JavaPairRDD view.

nodes.name: RRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that stores serialized R objects as Array[Byte] and exposes a JavaRDD view. The companion object (lines 106-172) provides the creation helpers used from R.

nodes.name: StringRRDD
nodes.summary: RDD of R objects represented as strings; it passes the STRING serialization format and exposes a JavaRDD view.

nodes.name: RParallelizeServer
nodes.summary: SocketAuthServer named sparkr-parallelize-server that reads R data over an authenticated socket and builds a JavaRDD[Array[Byte]]; used instead of a temporary file when encryption is enabled.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Creates an RRunner with the RDD's R settings, obtains the first parent's iterator for the partition and runs the runner on it, returning the resulting iterator.

nodes.name: createSparkContext
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkConf from the app name, Spark home, master (falling back to local), environment maps and executor env, sets the derby error log property when requested, then creates a JavaSparkContext and adds the given jars.

nodes.name: createRDDFromArray
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaRDD of byte arrays by parallelizing the given array of arrays, one slice per element; used when parallelize is called from R.

nodes.name: createRDDFromFile
nodes.summary: Creates a JavaRDD of byte arrays from a temporary file on the driver with the given parallelism; used when parallelize is called on large R objects.

nodes.name: serveToStream
nodes.summary: Runs a write function on a stream served through SocketAuthServer, authenticated with a RAuthHelper built from the current SparkEnv conf.

nodes.name: handleConnection
nodes.summary: Wraps the accepted socket channel in an input stream and reads the RDD data from it with JavaRDD.readRDDFromInputStream.

nodes.name: RRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RRunner, the concrete BaseRRunner used for RDD and DataFrame R UDFs. It reads results from the R worker as byte arrays, strings or shuffled (key, bytes) pairs, logs timing data, and writes input elements in the BYTE, ROW or STRING format.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class that instantiates anonymous subclasses of the nested abstract ReaderIterator and WriterThread; default constructor arguments select RDD mode.

nodes.name: RRunner
nodes.summary: Concrete runner that extends BaseRRunner with default arguments for plain RDD use (numPartitions -1, no DataFrame, mode RRunnerModes.RDD). It supplies the reader iterator that decodes worker output and the writer thread that encodes input, and is created by BaseRRDD.compute.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Returns a ReaderIterator that picks a reader by numPartitions and serializer (shuffled pairs, string data, or byte arrays). Its read method handles the TIMING_DATA marker by logging boot, init, broadcast, input, compute and output times, returns data when the length is positive and sets eos at length zero.

nodes.name: newWriterThread
nodes.summary: Returns a WriterThread whose writeIteratorToStream writes each element by the deserializer format (length-prefixed bytes, raw row bytes, or a printed string), handling (key, iterator) and (key, value) tuples and writing an 'r' byte as a group boundary after the inner elements.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogCapture.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonWorkerLogCapture, which wraps a Python worker output stream, strips out lines carrying a logging marker and routes the JSON payload to per-worker rolling log writers.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogCapture
nodes.summary: Manages Python UDF log capture: parses worker (or daemon) output, writes marked lines as PythonWorkerLogLine records to a RollingLogWriter kept per worker id, and passes all other output through unchanged. Works for both daemon and non-daemon modes.

nodes.name: CaptureWorkerLogsInputStream
nodes.summary: Private InputStream that reads the wrapped stream line by line in ISO-8859-1, hands lines containing the log marker to processLogLine and serves the remaining bytes to the caller; closes all log writers at end of stream or on close.

nodes.name: wrapInputStream
nodes.summary: Returns a CaptureWorkerLogsInputStream around the given stream so that Python log lines are captured while other output flows through.

nodes.name: removeAndCloseWorkerLogWriter
nodes.summary: Removes the log writer registered for a worker id and closes it, logging a warning if closing fails.

nodes.name: closeAllWriters
nodes.summary: Closes every active per-worker log writer (warning on failures) and clears the writer map.

nodes.name: getOrCreateLogWriter
nodes.summary: Atomically gets or creates the (RollingLogWriter, sequence counter) pair for a worker id, creating the writer through the block manager with a PythonWorkerLogBlockIdGenerator for the session and worker.

nodes.name: processLogLine
nodes.summary: Splits a line at the log marker: an empty JSON payload closes that worker's writer, otherwise the payload is written as a PythonWorkerLogLine with timestamp and sequence id. Returns the text before the marker, or the whole line plus a line separator when no marker is present.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Serves bytes from an internal buffer; when empty it reads the next line, processes marker lines, refills the buffer, and closes all writers at end of stream. The single-byte read() overload (lines 155-163) delegates to it.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying reader and always closes all log writers afterwards.

nodes.name: SerDeUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the SerDeUtil object with helpers that pickle JVM objects and RDDs for Python and unpickle Python-serialized RDDs back into JVM objects, including adaptive batching.

nodes.name: SerDeUtil
nodes.summary: Utility object for serialization and deserialization between Python and Java using Pickle: registers a bytearray constructor, converts RDDs of Java objects to pickled byte arrays (auto-batched), converts pickled RDDs back to Java objects, and handles key-value pair RDDs.

nodes.name: ByteArrayConstructor
nodes.summary: Unpickler constructor that returns an empty byte array when called with no arguments (an empty byte array pickled by Python 3) and otherwise defers to the parent constructor.

nodes.name: AutoBatchedPickler
nodes.summary: Iterator that pickles elements in batches whose size doubles while the pickled size is under 1M and halves when it is over 10M, so batches stay in a reasonable size range.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Synchronized, once-only registration of ByteArrayConstructor for bytearray and bytes style pickle names; must run before unpickling array.array from Python (and in cluster mode inside closures).

nodes.name: toJavaArray
nodes.summary: Maps an RDD of Java lists or arrays to an RDD of arrays, without recursive conversion; used only by the SQL Python layer.

nodes.name: javaToPython
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD of Java objects into an RDD of pickled byte arrays by wrapping each partition iterator in AutoBatchedPickler.

nodes.name: pythonToJava
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD of pickled byte arrays into an RDD of JVM objects by unpickling each row, flattening batched rows into their elements when batched is true.

nodes.name: checkPickle
nodes.summary: Tries to pickle a sample key and value and returns flags telling which of them failed, logging a warning that toString will be used as fallback.

nodes.name: pairRDDToPython
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD of key-value pairs into pickled byte arrays, probing the first element with checkPickle and falling back to toString for keys or values that cannot be pickled; uses AutoBatchedPickler when batchSize is 0, otherwise fixed-size groups.

nodes.name: pythonToPairRDD
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD of pickled Python tuples into an RDD[(K, V)], checking the first element is a two-element array (or the RDD is empty) and throwing SparkException otherwise.

nodes.name: StreamingPythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingPythonRunner (with its companion factory) that launches a Python worker for streaming functions, sends the version, session id and serialized function, and exposes stop and status checks.

nodes.name: StreamingPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Starts a dedicated Python worker through PythonWorkerFactory for a streaming function, passes environment variables (local dirs, buffer size, auth timeout, Spark Connect URL), performs an initialization handshake with a temporary 5 minute timeout on TCP sockets, and returns the data streams. The companion object (lines 32-41) provides an apply factory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object whose apply method is the factory; the three exception classes are defined as inner classes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that constructs a StreamingPythonRunner from the function, connect URL, session id and worker module.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Prepares the worker environment, creates a simple blocking-mode worker, writes the Python version, optional session id and the function, flushes, reads an integer response, restores the socket timeout and throws on a nonzero response; returns the (DataOutputStream, DataInputStream) pair.

nodes.name: StreamingPythonRunnerInitializationCommunicationException
nodes.summary: SparkPythonException with error class STREAMING_PYTHON_RUNNER_INITIALIZATION_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE, raised when initialization fails with a generic exception.

nodes.name: StreamingPythonRunnerInitializationTimeoutException
nodes.summary: SparkPythonException with error class STREAMING_PYTHON_RUNNER_INITIALIZATION_TIMEOUT_FAILURE, raised when the initialization socket read times out.

nodes.name: StreamingPythonRunnerInitializationException
nodes.summary: SparkPythonException with error class STREAMING_PYTHON_RUNNER_INITIALIZATION_FAILURE carrying the nonzero response code and the error message sent back by Python.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the Python worker and its factory if they were started, logging an error on exception.

nodes.name: isWorkerStopped
nodes.summary: Returns Some(true/false) from the factory when both worker and factory exist, otherwise None.

nodes.name: RAuthHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RAuthHelper, a SocketAuthHelper variant that reads and writes the authentication handshake strings with the R serialization format.

nodes.name: RAuthHelper
nodes.summary: Socket authentication helper for the R backend: disables Unix domain sockets and implements readUtf8 and writeUtf8 with SerDe.readString and SerDe.writeString so the secret exchange matches the R wire format.

nodes.name: readUtf8
nodes.summary: Reads a string from the socket input stream using SerDe.readString.

nodes.name: writeUtf8
nodes.summary: Writes a string to the socket output stream with SerDe.writeString and flushes.

nodes.name: RBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Netty-based RBackend server and its main entry point, which binds a local port for R to call into the JVM, publishes connection details to R through a temp file and shuts down when R disconnects.

nodes.name: RBackend
nodes.summary: Netty-based backend server used for communication between R and Java: builds a pipeline (length-prefixed frames, read timeout, auth handler, RBackendHandler), binds to localhost on a random port, owns a JVMObjectTracker and can run and close. The companion object (lines 108-195) holds the main method.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one id; the companion extends Logging.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Creates the event loop, RBackendHandler and RAuthHelper, configures the ServerBootstrap pipeline, binds to localhost on an ephemeral port and returns the port with the auth helper.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Blocks until the server channel closes.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the server channel (waiting up to 10 seconds), shuts down the boss and child groups and clears the JVM object tracker.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point: starts the backend, opens an auth-protected control server socket, writes ports, R package path, timeout and secret to a temp file renamed to the given path, and starts a daemon thread that waits for R to connect (up to 10 failed auth attempts) then exits the JVM when that connection ends.

nodes.name: RBackendHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Netty channel handler for the R backend: receives serialized method-call requests from a client, dispatches them by reflection onto JVM objects or classes, and writes back the serialized result or error.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses java.lang.reflect to select a method or constructor by matching decoded arguments against parameter types.

nodes.name: RBackendHandler
nodes.summary: Sharable Netty SimpleChannelInboundHandler[Array[Byte]] created with an RBackend server. Each message is decoded (isStatic flag, object id, method name, argument count), handled either as a built-in SparkRHandler command (echo, stopBackend, rm) or as a reflective call on a tracked JVM object, and the reply is written back to the channel.

nodes.name: channelRead0
nodes.summary: Decodes one request message and, for the special SparkRHandler object, runs the echo, stopBackend or rm commands. For any other object it starts a keep-alive scheduled executor that sends heartbeat replies (code +1) at a fixed interval, calls handleMethodCall, then writes the reply bytes to the context.

nodes.name: channelReadComplete
nodes.summary: Flushes the channel context after a read batch completes.

nodes.name: exceptionCaught
nodes.summary: Ignores ReadTimeoutException with a warning; for any other exception prints the stack trace and closes the connection.

nodes.name: handleMethodCall
nodes.summary: Resolves the target class (static class name or tracked object), reads the arguments, picks a matching method or constructor (methodName "<init>") via findMatchedSignature, invokes it reflectively and writes status 0 plus the result; on failure logs and writes status -1 with the cause message.

nodes.name: readArgs
nodes.summary: Reads numArgs serialized objects from the input stream using SerDe and the server JVM object tracker.

nodes.name: findMatchedSignature
nodes.summary: Searches an array of parameter-type arrays (methods or constructors of the same name) for the first signature that accepts the given arguments, widening primitives to wrapper types and converting a Java array to an immutable Seq when the parameter is a Seq. Returns the index as an Option.

nodes.name: RUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Utility object for locating the SparkR package and checking whether R or SparkR is installed, plus small helpers on JavaSparkContext.

nodes.name: RUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton with helpers that compute SparkR package paths for driver and executors in different deploy modes (including YARN cluster and client), test whether R or SparkR is installed, and expose the encryption flag and job tags of a JavaSparkContext.

nodes.name: localSparkRPackagePath
nodes.summary: Builds the SparkR library path (SPARK_HOME or spark.test.home, then R/lib) as an Option.

nodes.name: isSparkRInstalled
nodes.summary: Returns true when the SparkR directory exists under the local R library path; used before running tests that need SparkR.

nodes.name: sparkRPackagePath
nodes.summary: Returns the SparkR package path plus an optional extra R packages path, depending on master and deploy mode: archives named sparkr and rpkg in the current directory for YARN cluster (or YARN client executors), otherwise the local path; throws SparkException when SPARK_HOME is unset.

nodes.name: isRInstalled
nodes.summary: Checks that R is available by launching "R --version" and testing for exit code 0; any exception yields false.

nodes.name: isEncryptionEnabled
nodes.summary: Reads the IO encryption flag from the configuration of a JavaSparkContext.

nodes.name: getJobTags
nodes.summary: Returns the job tags of a JavaSparkContext as a String array.

nodes.name: ConsoleSink.scala
nodes.summary: Metrics sink that periodically prints all registered metrics to the console.

nodes.name: ConsoleSink
nodes.summary: Sink built from a Properties object and a MetricRegistry. Reads the "period" (default 10) and "unit" (default SECONDS) properties, validates them with MetricsSystem.checkMinimalPollingPeriod and builds a ConsoleReporter that converts durations to milliseconds and rates to seconds.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the console reporter with the configured period and unit.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the console reporter.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Triggers an immediate one-off report of all metrics through the console reporter.

nodes.name: CsvSink.scala
nodes.summary: Metrics sink that periodically writes registered metrics to CSV files in a directory.

nodes.name: CsvSink
nodes.summary: Sink built from a Properties object and a MetricRegistry. Reads "period" (default 10), "unit" (default SECONDS) and "directory" (default /tmp/), validates the polling period with MetricsSystem.checkMinimalPollingPeriod and builds a CsvReporter using the US locale that writes into the directory.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the CSV reporter with the configured period and unit.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the CSV reporter.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Triggers an immediate one-off report of all metrics through the CSV reporter.

nodes.name: GraphiteSink.scala
nodes.summary: Metrics sink that periodically sends registered metrics to a Graphite server over TCP or UDP.

nodes.name: GraphiteSink
nodes.summary: Sink built from a Properties object and a MetricRegistry. Requires "host" and "port" (throwing a SparkCoreErrors error if missing), reads period, unit, prefix, protocol (tcp or udp) and an optional regex filter on metric names, and builds a GraphiteReporter with the chosen Graphite or GraphiteUDP connection.

nodes.name: propertyToOption
nodes.summary: Looks up a property by name and wraps the possibly null value in an Option.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the Graphite reporter with the configured period and unit.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the Graphite reporter.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Triggers an immediate one-off report of all metrics through the Graphite reporter.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceRequests.scala
nodes.summary: Public builder-style API for assembling a set of executor resource requests (memory, off-heap memory, overhead, pyspark memory, cores and custom resources) to use with a ResourceProfile at stage level.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Serializable, @Evolving class since 3.1.0 that stores executor resource requests in a ConcurrentHashMap keyed by resource name. Each setter creates an ExecutorResourceRequest, stores it and returns this for chaining; memory strings are converted to MiB.

nodes.name: requests
nodes.summary: Returns all stored executor resource requests as an immutable Scala Map.

nodes.name: requestsJMap
nodes.summary: Java-friendly view of requests as a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: memory
nodes.summary: Adds a "memory" request; the amount string is parsed and converted to MiB.

nodes.name: offHeapMemory
nodes.summary: Adds an off-heap memory request in MiB, which only takes effect when off-heap memory is enabled.

nodes.name: memoryOverhead
nodes.summary: Adds a memory overhead request in MiB.

nodes.name: pysparkMemory
nodes.summary: Adds a "pyspark.memory" request in MiB.

nodes.name: cores
nodes.summary: Adds a request for the number of cores per executor.

nodes.name: resource
nodes.summary: Adds a request for a custom resource (for example a GPU) with amount, optional discovery script and optional vendor; empty strings stand for "not specified".

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Renders the stored requests as a descriptive string.

nodes.name: ResourceAllocator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines fixed-point resource amount helpers and a single-threaded trait that tracks per-address availability of a resource so executors or workers can acquire and release fractions of it.

nodes.name: ResourceAmountUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton that avoids floating-point precision loss by scaling fractional resource amounts with ONE_ENTIRE_RESOURCE (10^16) into longs, with conversions in both directions.

nodes.name: isOneEntireResource
nodes.summary: True when the long amount equals one entire resource.

nodes.name: toInternalResource
nodes.summary: Converts a fractional Double amount to the internal scaled Long.

nodes.name: toFractionalResource
nodes.summary: Converts an internal scaled Long amount back to a fractional Double.

nodes.name: ResourceAllocator
nodes.summary: Trait for executors and workers that manages a map from resource address to remaining (scaled) amount. It lists available and assigned addresses and offers acquire and release that throw SparkException for unknown addresses or invalid amounts. Documented as intended for single-threaded use.

nodes.name: resourcesAmounts
nodes.summary: Returns the current scaled amounts per address as an immutable Map.

nodes.name: availableAddrs
nodes.summary: Returns the sorted addresses whose remaining amount is greater than zero.

nodes.name: assignedAddrs
nodes.summary: Returns the sorted addresses that are at least partly assigned (amount below one entire resource).

nodes.name: acquire
nodes.summary: Subtracts the requested amount from each address, throwing SparkException if an address does not exist or not enough remains; used when a task is launched.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Adds the given amount back to each address, throwing SparkException if the address does not exist or the total would exceed one entire resource; used when a task finishes.

nodes.name: ResourceDiscoveryScriptPlugin.scala
nodes.summary: Default resource discovery plugin that runs a user-provided discovery script and parses its JSON output into ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: ResourceDiscoveryScriptPlugin
nodes.summary: @DeveloperApi plugin since 3.0.0 that is loaded by default to discover custom resources by executing the discovery script from the request. As the last plugin it throws if the resource is not discovered or the script is missing.

nodes.name: discoverResource
nodes.summary: Validates that a discovery script is specified and exists, runs it, parses the JSON output with ResourceInformation.parseJson, and checks that the returned resource name matches the requested one before wrapping the result in an Optional; throws SparkException otherwise.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceRequest.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutorResourceRequest value class, which describes one executor-level resource (name, amount, optional discovery script and vendor) for use with a ResourceProfile at stage level.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceRequest
nodes.summary: Serializable request for an executor resource such as a GPU, carrying resource name, amount, an optional discovery script and an optional vendor. It mirrors the spark.executor.resource.{resourceName}.* configs and is built through ExecutorResourceRequests or consumed by ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares two requests by runtime class, resource name, amount, discovery script and vendor.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hashes a Seq of resource name, amount, discovery script and vendor, consistent with equals.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the request as name, amount, script and vendor text.

nodes.name: ResourceInformation.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the ResourceInformation class (resource name plus an array of address strings) and its JSON helpers. Used wherever Spark passes discovered or allocated resources such as GPUs, including parsing them from JSON.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object and the private case class ResourceInformationJson use json4s Extraction and DefaultFormats for JSON conversion.

nodes.name: ResourceInformation
nodes.summary: Serializable description of one type of resource (for example a GPU): its name and an array of resource-specific address strings. The companion object parses it from a JSON string or JValue and the instance can render itself back to JSON.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the resource as "[name: ..., addresses: ...]" with comma-joined addresses.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares by runtime class, name and the addresses converted to immutable sequences.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hashes a Seq of the name and the addresses as an immutable sequence, consistent with equals.

nodes.name: toJson
nodes.summary: Converts this resource to a json4s JValue through the private ResourceInformationJson case class.

nodes.name: parseJson
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string into a ResourceInformation and, on failure, throws a SparkException that includes a correct JSON example. An overload at lines 84-92 does the same from a JValue.

nodes.name: ResourceInformationJson
nodes.summary: Private case class used only to simplify JSON serialization and extraction of ResourceInformation (name and addresses as a Seq).

nodes.name: toJValue
nodes.summary: Decomposes this case class into a JValue using json4s Extraction with DefaultFormats.

nodes.name: toResourceInformation
nodes.summary: Builds a ResourceInformation from the name and the addresses converted to an array.

nodes.name: ResourceProfileBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ResourceProfileBuilder, the public builder that collects executor and task resource requests and produces a ResourceProfile to associate with an RDD, so resource needs can change between stages.

nodes.name: ResourceProfileBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder that accumulates executor and task resource requests in concurrent maps and builds a ResourceProfile. It is used to specify per-stage resource requirements for an RDD.

nodes.name: taskResources
nodes.summary: Returns an immutable Scala Map snapshot of the task resource requests collected so far.

nodes.name: executorResources
nodes.summary: Returns an immutable Scala Map snapshot of the executor resource requests collected so far.

nodes.name: taskResourcesJMap
nodes.summary: Java-specific view of the task resource requests as a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: executorResourcesJMap
nodes.summary: Java-specific view of the executor resource requests as a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: require
nodes.summary: Adds all requests from an ExecutorResourceRequests object to the builder and returns the builder for chaining. An overload at lines 74-77 does the same for TaskResourceRequests.

nodes.name: clearExecutorResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Removes every executor resource request from the builder and returns it.

nodes.name: clearTaskResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Removes every task resource request from the builder and returns it.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the executor and task resource requests as "name=request" text.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates a TaskResourceProfile when no executor resources were requested, otherwise a full ResourceProfile from the executor and task resources.

nodes.name: TaskResourceRequests.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskResourceRequests, a fluent container of TaskResourceRequest entries used with a ResourceProfile to declare task-level cpu and custom resource needs for an RDD at stage level.

nodes.name: TaskResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Serializable set of task resource requests keyed by resource name, with convenience methods for cpus and custom resources (GPU, FPGA and so on). It feeds ResourceProfileBuilder.

nodes.name: requests
nodes.summary: Returns an immutable Scala Map snapshot of all task resource requests.

nodes.name: requestsJMap
nodes.summary: Java-specific view of all task resource requests as a java.util.Map.

nodes.name: cpus
nodes.summary: Adds a cpus TaskResourceRequest with the given integer amount per task and returns this object.

nodes.name: resource
nodes.summary: Adds a named custom resource request with a Double amount, which can be fractional (at most 0.5) so several tasks share one resource address.

nodes.name: addRequest
nodes.summary: Adds an existing TaskResourceRequest to the set, keyed by its resource name.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats the underlying request map as "Task resource requests: ...".

nodes.name: ResourceUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Resource configuration and discovery layer: resource identifiers, requests, requirements and allocations, plus the ResourceUtils object that parses spark.<component>.resource.* configs, reads resources files, runs discovery plugins and warns about wasted resources.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses implicit json4s Formats for extracting ResourceAllocation from a resources file and structured logging with MDC keys.

nodes.name: ResourceID
nodes.summary: Identifier for a resource, made of a component name (spark.driver, spark.executor or spark.task) and a resource name such as gpu. It builds the matching config key prefixes for amount, discovery script and vendor.

nodes.name: ResourceRequest
nodes.summary: Resource request parsed from configuration, holding the ResourceID, an integer amount and optional discovery script and vendor. It is passed to discovery plugins when resources are discovered.

nodes.name: ResourceRequirement
nodes.summary: Private case class for the requirement of a component: resource name, whole amount and numParts (how many ways a whole resource is split, for fractional task amounts).

nodes.name: ResourceAllocation
nodes.summary: Private case class pairing a ResourceID with allocated addresses. A cluster manager serializes it to JSON to pass allocated resources to the driver and executors, and it converts to ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: ResourceUtils
nodes.summary: Internal utility object for resource handling. It parses resource configs into requests and requirements, loads allocations from a resources file, discovers resources via plugins, checks allocations against requests or a ResourceProfile, and logs warnings when resources would be wasted.

nodes.name: parseResourceRequest
nodes.summary: Reads the amount, optional discovery script and vendor configs for one ResourceID and returns a ResourceRequest, throwing a SparkException when the amount is missing.

nodes.name: listResourceIds
nodes.summary: Lists the distinct ResourceIDs configured under spark.<component>.resource. and throws a SparkException for a key without a sub-config such as amount.

nodes.name: parseAllResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Parses a ResourceRequest for every configured resource of a component and keeps only those with amount greater than zero.

nodes.name: calculateAmountAndPartsForFraction
nodes.summary: Splits a possibly fractional task amount into an integer amount and the number of slots per address (0.5 gives 1 and 2). Amounts above 1.0 must be whole numbers, otherwise a SparkException is thrown.

nodes.name: addTaskResourceRequests
nodes.summary: Copies non-zero task resource amounts from the spark.task.resource configs into the given TaskResourceRequests.

nodes.name: parseResourceRequirements
nodes.summary: Turns configured resource amounts of a component into ResourceRequirements; only tasks may use fractional amounts, others throw a SparkException.

nodes.name: executorResourceRequestToRequirement
nodes.summary: Maps ExecutorResourceRequests to ResourceRequirements with a whole amount and one part.

nodes.name: resourcesMeetRequirements
nodes.summary: Returns true if the free amount of every required resource is at least the required amount.

nodes.name: withResourcesJson
nodes.summary: Reads a resources file as text and applies an extractor to it, wrapping non-fatal errors in a SparkException that names the file.

nodes.name: parseAllocatedFromJsonFile
nodes.summary: Parses a resources JSON file into a Seq of ResourceAllocation using json4s DefaultFormats.

nodes.name: parseAllocated
nodes.summary: Returns the allocations from an optional resources file whose component name matches the given component.

nodes.name: parseAllocatedOrDiscoverResources
nodes.summary: Combines allocations from the resources file with resources found by running discovery for configured resources not in the file and with amount above zero.

nodes.name: assertResourceAllocationMeetsRequest
nodes.summary: Requires that an allocation has the same ResourceID as the request and at least the requested number of addresses.

nodes.name: assertAllResourceAllocationsMeetRequests
nodes.summary: Checks every ResourceRequest against the allocation of the same ID.

nodes.name: assertAllResourceAllocationsMatchResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Requires each executor request of a ResourceProfile to be present in the allocations with enough addresses.

nodes.name: getOrDiscoverAllResources
nodes.summary: Returns resource name to ResourceInformation for a component, using the resources file first and discovery from Spark configs for the rest, after verifying the amounts requested.

nodes.name: emptyStringToOptional
nodes.summary: Converts an empty string to an empty Optional and any other string to a present Optional.

nodes.name: getOrDiscoverAllResourcesForResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Like getOrDiscoverAllResources but takes custom executor resources from a ResourceProfile for those not in the resources file, runs discovery for them and validates the result against the profile.

nodes.name: logResourceInfo
nodes.summary: Logs, between separator lines, the custom resources configured for a component or a message that none are configured.

nodes.name: discoverResource
nodes.summary: Loads configured discovery plugins plus ResourceDiscoveryScriptPlugin as the last one and returns the first ResourceInformation any of them provides, otherwise throws a SparkException.

nodes.name: validateTaskCpusLargeEnough
nodes.summary: Throws a SparkException if cores per executor are fewer than cpus per task, otherwise returns true.

nodes.name: warnOnWastedResources
nodes.summary: Computes the limiting resource and tasks per executor for a ResourceProfile and logs a warning (or throws when the testing flag is set) when cores or custom resources would be wasted.

nodes.name: ResourceProfile.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ResourceProfile (immutable set of executor and task resource requests), the task-only TaskResourceProfile subclass, and the ResourceProfile companion with built-in resource names, default profile creation, and executor sizing for cluster managers. Used when a stage-level resource request or the application default profile has to be created and sized.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class plus companion object; mutable private vars cache the computed slot and limiting-resource values behind synchronized access.

nodes.name: ResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Immutable description of executor and task resource requirements, keyed by resource name, that is applied to an RDD stage. Each instance gets a unique id, validates fractional task amounts, and lazily computes the limiting resource, max tasks per executor and slots per resource address from the requests and the SparkConf.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Asserts that every task resource amount is either at most 0.5 or a whole number. Called from the class constructor and overridden as a no-op in TaskResourceProfile.

nodes.name: getCustomExecutorResources
nodes.summary: Returns the executor resources whose names are not one of the built-in executor resources (for example accelerator-style custom resources). Overridden in TaskResourceProfile.

nodes.name: getSchedulerTaskResourceAmount
nodes.summary: Returns the whole-number amount of a named task resource that the scheduler should reserve, treating any fractional amount below 1 as 1 and throwing a SparkException when the resource is not in the profile.

nodes.name: getNumSlotsPerAddress
nodes.summary: Returns how many tasks can share one address of the named resource, computing the cached per-resource slot map first if needed. Throws a SparkException when the resource is not part of the profile.

nodes.name: maxTasksPerExecutor
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum number of tasks that fit on one executor of this profile, based on the limiting resource. Triggers the calculation on first use and caches the result.

nodes.name: limitingResource
nodes.summary: Returns the name of the resource that yields the fewest task slots per executor, computing it on first use. May be an empty string when executor cores are unknown and there are no other resources.

nodes.name: shouldCheckExecutorCores
nodes.summary: Decides whether executor cores can be used in the slot calculation: true if the executor cores config is set, the master is Kubernetes, or the master is yarn.

nodes.name: calculateTasksAndLimitingResource
nodes.summary: Computes the number of tasks per executor, the limiting resource and the slots per resource address by comparing task requests with executor resources (and cores when known). Throws if a task resource has no executor resource, warns about unused executor resources, and stores the results in private fields under synchronization.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Equality for profiles: same class, same id, same task resources and same executor resources.

nodes.name: resourcesEqual
nodes.summary: Compares only the task and executor resources (and class) of two profiles, ignoring their ids. Used to find an already registered equivalent profile.

nodes.name: TaskResourceProfile
nodes.summary: ResourceProfile that holds only task resources. It supports stage-level task scheduling when dynamic allocation is disabled (tasks run on executors of the default profile) and requests new executors based on the default executor resources when dynamic allocation is enabled.

nodes.name: getCustomExecutorResources
nodes.summary: Returns the custom executor resources: when no SparkEnv is available or dynamic allocation is enabled it uses the base behavior, otherwise it takes them from the default profile.

nodes.name: getOrCreateDefaultProfile
nodes.summary: Returns the application default ResourceProfile, creating it under a lock from the default task and executor resources of the SparkConf on first call and marking it with the default profile id.

nodes.name: getDefaultProfileExecutorResources
nodes.summary: Returns the recorded DefaultProfileExecutorResources, creating the default profile first if it has not been built.

nodes.name: getDefaultTaskResources
nodes.summary: Builds the default task resource map from the cpus-per-task setting plus any task resource requests found in the configuration.

nodes.name: getDefaultExecutorResources
nodes.summary: Builds the default executor resource map from the configuration (cores, memory, overhead, pyspark memory, off-heap memory and custom resource requests), with different handling of cores and memory for standalone and local-cluster masters, and records the DefaultProfileExecutorResources as a side effect.

nodes.name: reInitDefaultProfile
nodes.summary: Clears and recreates the default profile; intended for tests only.

nodes.name: clearDefaultProfile
nodes.summary: Resets the cached default profile and its executor resources under the default profile lock.

nodes.name: getTaskCpusOrDefaultForProfile
nodes.summary: Returns the cpus per task from the given profile, or the configured cpus-per-task value when the profile does not set it.

nodes.name: executorOffHeapMemorySizeAsMb
nodes.summary: Gets the off-heap memory size in MiB from an executor resource request by delegating to Utils.checkOffHeapEnabled, which returns 0 when off-heap memory is disabled.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourcesOrDefaults
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the final executor sizing (cores, executor, off-heap, pyspark and overhead memory, total memory and custom resources) handed to a cluster manager.

nodes.name: DefaultProfileExecutorResources
nodes.summary: Case class recording the executor resource values that were derived from the application configuration for the default profile.

nodes.name: calculateOverHeadMemory
nodes.summary: Returns the configured overhead memory if present, otherwise the larger of overheadFactor times executor memory and the configured minimum overhead.

nodes.name: getResourcesForClusterManager
nodes.summary: Resolves the full set of executor resources a cluster manager needs to request a container for a profile id. Starts from default profile values, overrides them with values in a non-default profile, maps custom resource names, adds pyspark memory only for Python apps, and returns an ExecutorResourcesOrDefaults with the total memory.

nodes.name: ResourceProfileManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ResourceProfileManager, the single registry that stores ResourceProfile objects by id so other components can pass only the id. It checks which cluster setups support non-default profiles, decides whether a task profile can run on an executor profile, and announces new profiles on the listener bus.

nodes.name: ResourceProfileManager
nodes.summary: Keeps every ResourceProfile in an id-keyed map guarded by a read-write lock (profiles are never removed). Created with a SparkConf and LiveListenerBus, it registers the default profile on construction and is used to add, look up, deduplicate and validate profiles.

nodes.name: defaultResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Returns the default ResourceProfile created from the application level configs.

nodes.name: isSupported
nodes.summary: Checks whether a profile is allowed for the current master and dynamic allocation setting, throwing a SparkException when TaskResourceProfiles or custom profiles are used in an unsupported mode (skipped in unit tests unless a test flag is set). Also logs a warning for standalone or local-cluster with dynamic allocation when no executor cores are set. Always returns true when it does not throw.

nodes.name: canBeScheduled
nodes.summary: Returns true when the task and executor profile ids are equal, or when dynamic allocation is off and the task profile is a TaskResourceProfile (which may use default-profile executors).

nodes.name: addResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Validates support and adds a profile to the map under the write lock if its id is new. For a new profile it precomputes the limiting resource and posts a SparkListenerResourceProfileAdded event to the listener bus outside the lock.

nodes.name: resourceProfileFromId
nodes.summary: Looks up a ResourceProfile by id under the read lock and throws a SparkException if the id is unknown.

nodes.name: getEquivalentProfile
nodes.summary: Returns an already registered profile whose task and executor resources equal the given profile (ignoring id), or None.

nodes.name: TaskResourceRequest.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskResourceRequest, a serializable pair of resource name and amount used with a ResourceProfile to state what each task needs at the stage level. Amounts above 1.0 must be whole numbers; fractions express several tasks per resource address.

nodes.name: TaskResourceRequest
nodes.summary: Immutable request for one task resource (name and Double amount) that asserts the amount is at most 1.0 or a whole number. Provides value-based equals, hashCode and toString, and is the element type of ResourceProfile task resource maps.

nodes.name: JVMObjectTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JVMObjectId and JVMObjectTracker, a thread-safe registry that assigns string ids to JVM objects handed to R so they can be referenced later in RPC calls. Both types are private to the api.r package.

nodes.name: JVMObjectId
nodes.summary: Private case class wrapping the string id of a tracked JVM object; requires the id to be non-null.

nodes.name: JVMObjectTracker
nodes.summary: Concurrent map from JVMObjectId to object with an atomic counter. It adds objects and returns new ids, looks them up or removes them, reports its size and can be cleared.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the tracked object for an id as an Option, None if absent.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the tracked object for an id or throws NoSuchElementException when the id is not tracked.

nodes.name: addAndGetId
nodes.summary: Stores an object under a new id taken from an incrementing counter and returns that id.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the object for an id as an Option, None if it was not tracked.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the number of objects currently tracked.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes all tracked objects.

nodes.name: RBackendAuthHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RBackendAuthHandler, a Netty inbound handler that authenticates a connection from the R process by comparing the received secret with the expected one. On success it removes itself from the pipeline and replies "ok"; on failure it replies "err" and closes the channel.

nodes.name: RBackendAuthHandler
nodes.summary: Private SimpleChannelInboundHandler for byte arrays constructed with the expected secret. It is used as the first handler on connections from the R process.

nodes.name: channelRead0
nodes.summary: Decodes the client secret (dropping the trailing null terminator written by R), compares it with the expected secret using MessageDigest.isEqual, then removes the handler and replies "ok" or logs the failure, replies "err" and closes the context.

nodes.name: writeReply
nodes.summary: Serializes a reply string with SerDe.writeString into a byte array and writes and flushes it to the channel.

nodes.name: SerDe.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SerDe object that reads and writes values on data streams using a one-byte type tag, and the SerializationFormats constants. Used to move values between the R side and the JVM side, including references to JVM objects kept by a tracker.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object with Java-to-R and R-to-Java type mapping documented in comments; uses pattern matching on type tags.

nodes.name: SerDe
nodes.summary: Singleton utility that deserializes typed objects from a DataInputStream and serializes JVM objects to a DataOutputStream. Each value is prefixed by a type character (for example 'i' integer, 'c' string, 'l' list, 'j' JVM object reference); unknown types are delegated to optional SQL read/write hooks, and non-primitive objects are written as references through a JVMObjectTracker.

nodes.name: SerDe.readObjectType
nodes.summary: Reads one byte from the stream and returns it as the type character.

nodes.name: SerDe.readObject
nodes.summary: Reads a type tag and then delegates to readTypedObject to read a value of that type.

nodes.name: SerDe.readTypedObject
nodes.summary: Reads a value according to the given type character: null, int, double, boolean, string, map, bytes, array, list, date, time or a JVM object looked up in the tracker. For unknown types it uses the registered SQL read hook and throws IllegalArgumentException if none can read it.

nodes.name: SerDe.readBytes
nodes.summary: Reads a length-prefixed byte array from the stream.

nodes.name: SerDe.readStringBytes
nodes.summary: Reads len bytes, asserts the last byte is a terminating zero, and decodes the rest as a UTF-8 string.

nodes.name: SerDe.readString
nodes.summary: Reads an int length and then the string bytes using readStringBytes.

nodes.name: SerDe.readDate
nodes.summary: Reads a date as a string, returning null for the value "NA" and a java.sql.Date otherwise.

nodes.name: SerDe.readTime
nodes.summary: Reads a double of seconds since epoch and converts it to a Timestamp with nanoseconds, returning null for NaN.

nodes.name: SerDe.readArray
nodes.summary: Reads an array whose elements all share one type tag read first from the stream (int, string, double, boolean, JVM object, bytes, nested array or list). Unknown element types go through the SQL read hook, and an invalid type raises IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: SerDe.readList
nodes.summary: Reads a length-prefixed list where each element carries its own type tag, returning an Array[Object].

nodes.name: SerDe.readMap
nodes.summary: Reads a map as a string-key array followed by a list of values, converting them to a java.util.Map with Utils.toJavaMap; returns an empty HashMap when the length is zero.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeType
nodes.summary: Writes the one-byte type tag for a type name such as void, character, double, integer, logical, date, time, raw, array, list, map or jobj, and throws IllegalArgumentException for other names.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeKeyValue
nodes.summary: Writes one map entry: validates that the key is a non-null String, then writes the key string and the value object.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeObject
nodes.summary: Main serialization entry point. Writes void for null and otherwise matches on the runtime type to write strings, numbers, booleans, dates, times, byte and primitive arrays, object arrays, Properties, Java and Scala maps; anything else is first offered to the SQL write hook and then written as a JVM object reference.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeDate
nodes.summary: Writes a java.sql.Date as its string form.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeTime
nodes.summary: Writes a Timestamp as seconds since epoch as a double including nanoseconds. A second overload accepts java.sql.Time and writes milliseconds divided by 1000 as a double (lines 434-436).

nodes.name: SerDe.writeString
nodes.summary: Writes a string as a UTF-8 byte array prefixed with its int length.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeBytes
nodes.summary: Writes a byte array prefixed with its int length.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeJObj
nodes.summary: Registers the object with the JVMObjectTracker and writes the resulting id string, so the other side can refer to the object.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeIntArr
nodes.summary: Writes an integer type tag, the array length and each int.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeDoubleArr
nodes.summary: Writes a double type tag, the array length and each double.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeBooleanArr
nodes.summary: Writes a logical type tag, the array length and each boolean.

nodes.name: SerDe.writeStringArr
nodes.summary: Writes a character type tag, the array length and each string.

nodes.name: SerializationFormats
nodes.summary: Singleton holding the string constants BYTE ("byte"), STRING ("string") and ROW ("row") that name serialization formats used with the R serialization layer.

nodes.name: JmxSink.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JmxSink, a metrics Sink that publishes a MetricRegistry through a JMX reporter. Used when the metrics system is configured with this sink.

nodes.name: JmxSink
nodes.summary: Sink implementation built from a Properties object and a MetricRegistry. It creates a JmxReporter for the registry, starts and stops that reporter on start and stop, and does nothing on report.

nodes.name: JmxSink.start
nodes.summary: Starts the JmxReporter so that the registry metrics are exposed over JMX.

nodes.name: JmxSink.stop
nodes.summary: Stops the JmxReporter.

nodes.name: JmxSink.report
nodes.summary: No-op implementation of Sink.report.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the empty package object org.apache.spark.metrics.source, documented as holding the sources used in Spark's metrics system. It contains no members; it only anchors the package.

nodes.name: source
nodes.summary: Empty package object for org.apache.spark.metrics.source (documented as 'Sources used in Spark's metrics system'). It declares no members.

nodes.name: Deploy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the standalone-deploy (master side) configuration entries under the spark.deploy.* prefix, plus spark.dead.worker.persistence: recovery mode, application/driver retention, executor placement and ID patterns.

nodes.name: Deploy
nodes.summary: Singleton object Deploy holding ConfigBuilder entries for the standalone cluster master. Recovery group: spark.deploy.recoveryMode (default "NONE"), spark.deploy.recoveryMode.factory (""), spark.deploy.recoveryDirectory (""), spark.deploy.recoveryCompressionCodec (optional, doc lists none, lz4, lzf, snappy, zstd; only FILESYSTEM mode), spark.deploy.recoveryTimeout (seconds, must be positive, optional; doc says default follows the worker timeout), spark.deploy.zookeeper.url and spark.deploy.zookeeper.dir (both optional, used with ZOOKEEPER recovery mode). Retention and liveness group: spark.deploy.retainedApplications (200), spark.deploy.retainedDrivers (200), spark.dead.worker.persistence (15), spark.deploy.maxExecutorRetries (10). Scheduling group: spark.deploy.spreadOutDrivers (true), spark.deploy.spreadOutApps (true, alternative key spark.deploy.spreadOut), spark.deploy.workerSelectionPolicy (upper-cased, validated against WorkerSelectionPolicy, default CORES_FREE_DESC), spark.deploy.defaultCores (must be positive, default Int.MaxValue), spark.deploy.maxDrivers (positive, default Int.MaxValue). Identifier group: spark.deploy.appNumberModulo (optional, must be >= 1000), spark.deploy.driverIdPattern (default "driver-%s-%04d") and spark.deploy.appIdPattern (default "app-%s-%04d"), both rejecting whitespace.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: WorkerSelectionPolicy
nodes.summary: Enumeration nested in Deploy listing the allowed values of spark.deploy.workerSelectionPolicy: CORES_FREE_ASC, CORES_FREE_DESC, MEMORY_FREE_ASC, MEMORY_FREE_DESC and WORKER_ID. Used to validate that config's value.

nodes.name: History.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the History Server configuration entries under spark.history.* (filesystem log scanning, cleaner, local/hybrid store, UI, Kerberos, custom executor log URL).

nodes.name: History
nodes.summary: Singleton object History with ConfigBuilder entries for the History Server; DEFAULT_LOG_DIR is "file:/tmp/spark-events".
