Log directory and scan group: spark.history.fs.logDirectory (default DEFAULT_LOG_DIR, at least one non-empty directory, comma-separated list allowed), spark.history.fs.logDirectory.names (optional display names, since 4.2.0), spark.history.fs.safemodeCheck.interval (5s), spark.history.fs.update.interval (10s), spark.history.fs.update.batchSize (default Int.MaxValue, must be positive), spark.history.fs.update.scanDisabledPathPatterns (list, default Nil), spark.history.fs.numReplayThreads and spark.history.fs.numCompactThreads (both default to ceil(availableProcessors/4)), spark.history.fs.inProgressOptimization.enabled (true), spark.history.fs.endEventReparseChunkSize (1m). Cleaner group: spark.history.fs.cleaner.enabled (false), spark.history.fs.cleaner.interval (1d), spark.history.fs.cleaner.maxAge (7d), spark.history.fs.cleaner.maxNum (Int.MaxValue), driver log cleaner keys spark.history.fs.driverlog.cleaner.enabled/maxAge/interval that fall back to the event log cleaner ones, and rolling event log keys spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.maxFilesToRetain, spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.compaction.score.threshold (internal, 0.7) and spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.onDemandLoadEnabled (true). Store group: spark.history.store.path (optional), spark.history.store.serializer (JSON by default, or PROTOBUF), spark.history.store.maxDiskUsage (10g), spark.history.store.hybridStore.enabled (false), spark.history.store.hybridStore.maxMemoryUsage (2g), spark.history.store.hybridStore.diskBackend (ROCKSDB by default, or LEVELDB). UI and security group: spark.history.ui.title ("History Server"), spark.history.ui.port (18080), spark.history.ui.acls.enable (false), spark.history.ui.admin.acls and spark.history.ui.admin.acls.groups (lists), spark.history.ui.maxApplications, spark.history.retainedApplications (50), spark.history.provider (default "org.apache.spark.deploy.history.FsHistoryProvider"), spark.history.kerberos.enabled/principal/keytab, spark.history.custom.executor.log.url and its applyIncompleteApplication flag (true).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: LocalStoreSerializer
nodes.summary: Enumeration nested in History with the values JSON and PROTOBUF; it validates spark.history.store.serializer.

nodes.name: HybridStoreDiskBackend
nodes.summary: Enumeration nested in History with the values LEVELDB and ROCKSDB; it validates spark.history.store.hybridStore.diskBackend.

nodes.name: Kryo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Kryo serializer configuration entries under spark.kryo.* and spark.kryoserializer.*.

nodes.name: Kryo
nodes.summary: Singleton object Kryo with ConfigBuilder entries. Class registration: spark.kryo.registrationRequired (false), spark.kryo.registrator (list, default Nil), spark.kryo.classesToRegister (list, default Nil). Behavior flags: spark.kryo.unsafe (true), spark.kryo.pool (true), spark.kryo.referenceTracking (true). Buffer sizes: spark.kryoserializer.buffer (default "64k", KiB) and spark.kryoserializer.buffer.max (default "64m", MiB).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: Network.scala
nodes.summary: Defines network and RPC configuration entries under spark.network.* and spark.rpc.*.

nodes.name: Network
nodes.summary: Singleton object Network with ConfigBuilder entries. Network group: spark.network.crypto.saslFallback (true), spark.network.crypto.enabled (false), spark.network.remoteReadNioBufferConversion (false), spark.network.timeout (default "120s"), spark.network.timeoutInterval (default taken from STORAGE_BLOCKMANAGER_TIMEOUTINTERVAL, in milliseconds). RPC group: spark.rpc.askTimeout and spark.rpc.lookupTimeout (optional strings), spark.rpc.connect.threads (64), spark.rpc.io.numConnectionsPerPeer (1), spark.rpc.io.threads (optional), spark.rpc.message.maxSize (128), spark.rpc.netty.dispatcher.numThreads (optional).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: Python.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Python worker related configuration entries under spark.python.*, spark.executor.python.* and spark.executor.pyspark.*.

nodes.name: Python
nodes.summary: Singleton object Python with ConfigBuilder entries. Worker lifecycle: spark.python.worker.reuse (true), spark.python.use.daemon (true), spark.python.daemon.module and spark.python.worker.module (optional), spark.python.task.killTimeout (default "2s"), spark.python.factory.idleWorkerMaxPoolSize (optional, must be > 0), spark.python.daemon.killWorkerOnFlushFailure (true). Timeouts and diagnostics: spark.python.worker.idleTimeoutSeconds (default 0, no timeout), spark.python.worker.killOnIdleTimeout (false), spark.python.worker.tracebackDumpIntervalSeconds (0, disabled), spark.python.worker.faulthandler.enabled (false), spark.executor.python.worker.log.details (false), spark.python.authenticate.socketTimeout (internal, "15s"). Resources: spark.executor.pyspark.memory (optional, MiB). Unix domain socket: spark.python.unix.domain.socket.enabled (default true only if env PYSPARK_UDS_MODE is "true") and spark.python.unix.domain.socket.dir (internal, optional, path length limited so the socket path stays under 104 characters).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: R.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the R backend configuration entries under spark.r.* and spark.sparkr.*.

nodes.name: R
nodes.summary: Singleton object R with ConfigBuilder entries: spark.r.backendConnectionTimeout (6000), spark.r.numRBackendThreads (2), spark.r.heartBeatInterval (100), spark.sparkr.r.command (default "Rscript") and spark.r.command (optional).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object whose vals are ConfigBuilder(...) entries; the object itself has no methods.

nodes.name: SparkConfigProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkConfigProvider, a ConfigProvider backed by a Java map that only serves keys starting with "spark.".

nodes.name: SparkConfigProvider
nodes.summary: Config provider over a java.util.Map[String, String] that only reads Spark config keys (those starting with "spark."), also honoring deprecated names via SparkConf.

nodes.name: get

nodes.name: Status.scala

nodes.languageNotes: Package object (not a class): the vals are accessed as org.apache.spark.internal.config.<NAME>.

nodes.name: MetricsServlet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MetricsServlet sink, which serves the contents of a metric registry as JSON over an HTTP servlet instead of pushing it anywhere.

nodes.name: MetricsServlet
nodes.summary: Sink that reads a "path" property (and an optional "sample" flag, default false) and exposes the registry as JSON through a servlet handler. start, stop and report do nothing because metrics are only produced when the servlet is requested.

nodes.name: getHandlers
nodes.summary: Builds a single servlet context handler at the configured path that answers requests with the JSON snapshot as text/json.

nodes.name: getMetricsSnapshot
nodes.summary: Serializes the whole metric registry to a JSON string using the Jackson object mapper configured with the metrics module.

nodes.name: PrometheusServlet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PrometheusServlet sink, which renders a metric registry as plain text in Prometheus format and serves it over an HTTP servlet.

nodes.name: PrometheusServlet
nodes.summary: Developer API sink that reads a "path" property and exposes gauges, counters, histograms, meters and timers of the registry as Prometheus-style text lines with a type label. It is used by the Spark metrics system internally and by the Spark K8s operator, according to its doc comment.

nodes.name: getHandlers
nodes.summary: Builds one servlet context handler at the configured path that responds with the Prometheus text snapshot as text/plain.

nodes.name: getMetricsSnapshot
nodes.summary: Iterates over gauges, counters, histograms, meters and timers in the registry and appends one line per statistic (counts, min/max/mean, percentiles, rates) with a type label; string-valued gauges are skipped. A request-taking overload at line 56 simply delegates to this no-argument version, which is marked Since 4.0.0.

nodes.name: normalizeKey
nodes.summary: Turns a metric name into a Prometheus-safe prefix by replacing every non-alphanumeric character with an underscore and wrapping it as "metrics_<name>_".

nodes.name: Slf4jSink.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Slf4jSink, which periodically writes the metric registry to the logs through a Slf4j reporter.

nodes.name: Slf4jSink
nodes.summary: Sink configured by "period" (default 10) and "unit" (default SECONDS) properties that validates the polling period and wraps a Slf4j reporter converting durations to milliseconds and rates to seconds. start, stop and report delegate to that reporter.

nodes.name: StatsdSink.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StatsdSink and its companion constants, a sink that sends metrics to a StatsD server on a schedule.

nodes.name: StatsdSink
nodes.summary: Sink (class plus companion object of property keys and defaults: host 127.0.0.1, port 8125, period 10, unit SECONDS, prefix, regex) that builds an optional regex metric filter, validates the polling period and drives a StatsdReporter. start and stop log through the Logging trait.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the underlying StatsdReporter at the configured period and unit and logs the metric prefix in use. The stop and report methods are one-line delegations to the reporter.

nodes.name: StatsdReporter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StatsdReporter, a scheduled reporter that sends metrics as StatsD datagrams over UDP, plus the StatsD metric type codes.

nodes.name: StatsdMetricType
nodes.summary: Object holding the StatsD metric type codes used when formatting packets: counter "c", gauge "g", timer "ms" and set "s".

nodes.name: StatsdReporter
nodes.summary: Scheduled reporter that, on each run, opens a UDP socket to the configured host and port and sends every gauge, counter, histogram, meter and timer as "name:value|type" packets, then closes the socket. Send failures are logged at debug level.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Creates a datagram socket (logging a warning on failure), reports all gauges, counters, histograms, meters and timers through the helper methods, and closes the socket, swallowing and logging send errors.

nodes.name: reportGauge
nodes.summary: Sends a gauge value as a StatsD gauge if the value is numeric.

nodes.name: reportCounter
nodes.summary: Sends a counter count as a StatsD counter packet.

nodes.name: reportHistogram
nodes.summary: Sends a histogram count as a gauge and its max, mean, min, standard deviation and percentile snapshot values as timer packets.

nodes.name: reportMetered
nodes.summary: Sends a meter count as a gauge and its one, five, fifteen minute and mean rates, converted to the rate unit, as timer packets.

nodes.name: reportTimer
nodes.summary: Sends a timer snapshot (max, mean, min, standard deviation, percentiles) converted to the duration unit, then reports its metered rates.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Builds a "name:value|type" string, sanitizes whitespace, wraps it in a UTF-8 datagram packet and sends it on the socket.

nodes.name: fullName
nodes.summary: Joins the configured prefix and the given name parts into a dotted metric name.

nodes.name: sanitize
nodes.summary: Replaces runs of whitespace with a dash so a packet stays one token.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Formats a value to a string, returning an empty string when it is not numeric.

nodes.name: formatAny
nodes.summary: Formats floats, doubles and big decimals with two decimals and other numbers via toString, returning None for non-numeric values.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object declaration for org.apache.spark.metrics.sink, documented as the sinks used in the metrics system; it contains no members.

nodes.name: StaticSources.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the static metric sources (code generation and Hive external catalog metrics) that can be reported to from any class without a SparkEnv.

nodes.name: StaticSources
nodes.summary: Object holding the list of all static sources, CodegenMetrics and HiveCatalogMetrics, which may be reported to from any class including static ones.

nodes.name: CodegenMetrics
nodes.summary: Metrics source named "CodeGenerator" holding histograms for source code length, compilation time, generated class bytecode size and generated method bytecode size.

nodes.name: HiveCatalogMetrics
nodes.summary: Metrics source named "HiveExternalCatalog" holding counters for fetched partitions, discovered files, file cache hits, Hive client calls and parallel listing jobs, with increment helpers that let clients avoid classloader issues with the metrics classes.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Decrements every counter by its current value so all metrics return to zero; documented as useful in tests. The increment* methods at lines 105-109 are one-line wrappers over the counters.

nodes.name: AccumulatorSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines metric sources that report the values of long and double accumulators as gauges and register themselves with the metrics system.

nodes.name: AccumulatorSource
nodes.summary: Base metrics source named "AccumulatorSource" that registers each accumulator under its name as a gauge returning the accumulator value. It is restricted to long and double accumulators, excluding collection accumulators.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a gauge for every named accumulator in the metric registry, with each gauge returning the current accumulator value.

nodes.name: LongAccumulatorSource
nodes.summary: Empty subclass of AccumulatorSource for long accumulators, plus a companion object whose register method creates the source and registers it with the metrics system. Driver side only, per its doc comment.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Creates a LongAccumulatorSource, registers the given named long accumulators in it and adds it to the metrics system of the SparkContext environment.

nodes.name: DoubleAccumulatorSource
nodes.summary: Empty subclass of AccumulatorSource for double accumulators, plus a companion object whose register method creates the source and registers it with the metrics system. Driver side only, per its doc comment.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Creates a DoubleAccumulatorSource, registers the given named double accumulators in it and adds it to the metrics system of the SparkContext environment.

nodes.name: JVMCPUSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a metrics source exposing the JVM process CPU time as a gauge.

nodes.name: JVMCPUSource
nodes.summary: Metrics source named "JVMCPU" that registers a "jvmCpuTime" gauge reading the ProcessCpuTime attribute of the operating system MBean, in nanoseconds, or -1 when it cannot be read.

nodes.name: JvmSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JvmSource metrics source that exposes standard JVM garbage collection, memory usage and buffer pool metrics.

nodes.name: JvmSource
nodes.summary: Metrics source named "jvm" whose registry is filled with garbage collector, memory usage and buffer pool metric sets, the latter built from the platform MBean server.

nodes.summary: Defines the configuration entries for the Spark web UI and its security settings, all built with ConfigBuilder as vals of the private[spark] object UI. Key groups: (1) core UI switches: spark.ui.enabled (default true), spark.ui.port (4040), spark.ui.killEnabled (true), spark.ui.showConsoleProgress (false), spark.ui.consoleProgress.update.interval (200 ms), spark.ui.filters (empty list), spark.ui.threadDumpsEnabled and spark.ui.threadDump.flamegraphEnabled (true), spark.ui.heapHistogramEnabled (true), spark.ui.prometheus.enabled (true, internal), spark.ui.showErrorStacks (true), spark.ui.groupSQLSubExecutionEnabled (true); (2) reverse proxy: spark.ui.reverseProxy (false), spark.ui.reverseProxyUrl (optional, rejects URLs containing the words proxy or history), spark.ui.proxyRedirectUri; (3) HTTP security headers and Jetty: spark.ui.xXssProtection ("1; mode=block"), spark.ui.xContentTypeOptions.enabled (true), spark.ui.strictTransportSecurity, spark.ui.contentSecurityPolicy.enabled (false), spark.ui.requestHeaderSize ("8k"), spark.ui.jetty.sniHostCheckEnabled (false, internal), spark.ui.jetty.stopTimeout ("30s", internal, alternative key spark.ui.jettyStopTimeout); (4) timeline limits: spark.ui.timelineEnabled (true), spark.ui.timeline.tasks.maximum (1000), jobs.maximum (500), stages.maximum (500), executors.maximum (250); (5) ACLs: spark.acls.enable (false), spark.ui.view.acls, spark.ui.view.acls.groups, spark.admin.acls, spark.admin.acls.groups, spark.modify.acls, spark.modify.acls.groups (all empty lists by default), spark.user.groups.mapping (default org.apache.spark.security.ShellBasedGroupsMappingProvider); (6) Master UI and logs: spark.master.ui.decommission.allow.mode (LOCAL, one of ALLOW, LOCAL, DENY), spark.master.ui.title, spark.master.ui.visibleEnvVarPrefixes, spark.ui.custom.executor.log.url. Contains no methods.

nodes.name: UI
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object that groups every web UI related configuration entry as a ConfigEntry val (booleanConf, intConf, stringConf, timeConf, bytesConf builders with defaults, version tags and docs). Other Spark code reads these entries through the config API instead of using raw key strings. See the file node for the key groups and the most important keys.

nodes.name: Worker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the configuration entries for the standalone Worker process, built with ConfigBuilder as vals of the private[spark] object Worker. Key groups: (1) identity and resources: SPARK_WORKER_PREFIX = "spark.worker", spark.worker.resourcesFile (internal, optional, JSON array of ResourceAllocation), spark.worker.idPattern (internal, default "worker-%s-%s-%d", validated to produce no whitespace); (2) liveness and registration: spark.worker.timeout (60), spark.worker.initialRegistrationRetries (6, internal, must be positive), spark.worker.maxRegistrationRetries (16, internal, must be positive), spark.worker.preferConfiguredMasterAddress (false), spark.worker.driverTerminateTimeout ("10s"); (3) cleanup: spark.worker.cleanup.enabled (true), spark.worker.cleanup.interval (30 minutes in seconds, 60 * 30), spark.worker.cleanup.appDataTtl (7 days in seconds); (4) worker UI: spark.worker.ui.port (optional), spark.worker.ui.retainedExecutors (1000), spark.worker.ui.retainedDrivers (1000), spark.worker.ui.compressedLogFileLengthCacheSize (100); (5) decommission: spark.worker.decommission.signal ("PWR"). Contains no methods.

nodes.name: Worker
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object that groups the standalone Worker configuration entries as ConfigEntry vals plus the SPARK_WORKER_PREFIX constant. Read by worker side code through the config API. See the file node for the key groups and the most important keys.

nodes.name: DependencyUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object used when submitting applications to resolve Ivy/Maven coordinates, expand glob paths, download remote jars and files to a local temp directory and add local jars to a class loader. Also defines the IvyProperties case class carrying the Ivy settings read from system properties.

nodes.name: IvyProperties
nodes.summary: Case class holding five Ivy related settings (package exclusions, packages, repositories, Ivy repo path, Ivy settings path) as plain strings; produced by DependencyUtils.getIvyProperties.

nodes.name: DependencyUtils
nodes.summary: Object with the dependency handling helpers: resolving ivy:// URIs and package lists through MavenUtils, resolving and downloading comma separated jar/file lists (local and local: schemes are returned as is, other schemes are fetched with Utils.doFetchFile), expanding Hadoop file system globs, merging file lists and adding local jars to a MutableURLClassLoader.

nodes.name: getIvyProperties
nodes.summary: Reads the Ivy related system properties (keys of JAR_PACKAGES_EXCLUSIONS, JAR_PACKAGES, JAR_REPOSITORIES, JAR_IVY_REPO_PATH, JAR_IVY_SETTING_PATH) and returns them as an IvyProperties instance, with null for unset values.

nodes.name: resolveMavenDependencies
nodes.summary: Overload taking explicit transitive flag, exclusions, packages, repositories, Ivy repo path and optional settings file: builds or loads the IvySettings through MavenUtils and calls MavenUtils.resolveMavenCoordinates, returning the resolved jar paths. The other overload (lines 69-95) takes an ivy:// URI, validates that its authority has the form org:module:version, merges the repositories from system properties with those in the URI query via MavenUtils.parseQueryParams and delegates to this overload.

nodes.name: resolveAndDownloadJars
nodes.summary: Expands globs in a comma separated jar list, drops the entry matching the user jar name, downloads the rest into a new temp directory with downloadFileList and returns the local list, or null when nothing remains.

nodes.name: addJarsToClassPath
nodes.summary: Splits a comma separated jar list and adds each jar to the given MutableURLClassLoader through addJarToClasspath; does nothing for null.

nodes.name: downloadFileList
nodes.summary: Downloads every entry of a comma separated file list with downloadFile into the target directory and returns the resulting comma separated local list; requires a non-null list.

nodes.name: downloadFile
nodes.summary: Returns the path unchanged for file and local schemes; for other schemes fetches the file into the target directory with Utils.doFetchFile and returns its local URI string. For http, https and ftp under Utils.isTesting it returns a dummy path instead of downloading.

nodes.name: resolveGlobPaths
nodes.summary: Resolves each path of a comma separated list into concrete files using resolveGlobPath, keeping a #fragment name when present and throwing a SparkException when a path with a fragment resolves to several files.

nodes.name: addJarToClasspath
nodes.summary: Adds a local jar (file or local scheme) to the class loader when it exists, logging a warning if the file is missing; remote jars are skipped with a warning.

nodes.name: mergeFileLists
nodes.summary: Merges several comma separated file lists, ignoring blank or null ones, into one comma separated string, or null when the result is empty.

nodes.name: splitOnFragment
nodes.summary: Private helper that resolves a path to a URI and splits it into the URI without its fragment and the optional fragment string.

nodes.name: resolveGlobPath
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns local, http, https and ftp URIs untouched and otherwise expands the URI with FileSystem.globStatus, keeping only files and falling back to the original URI when there is no match.

nodes.name: Utils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the large Utils object, the general utility toolbox of Spark core (file fetching, local directories, host and port parsing, unit conversions, process execution, error handling helpers, thread dumps, log level control, redaction, extension loading). Also defines CallSite, CallerContext, RedirectThread and CircularBuffer.
nodes.languageNotes: Utils is a Scala object mixing in several util traits (SparkClassUtils, SparkErrorUtils, SparkFileUtils and others) that live in common/utils. Methods such as classForName, getContextOrSparkClassLoader, getSparkClassLoader, tryOrIOException, tryWithResource, tryWithSafeFinally, createDirectory, stringToSeq, resolveURI, copyStream and closeQuietly are NOT defined in this file; they are inherited from those traits.

nodes.name: Utils
nodes.summary: The private[spark] Utils object: Spark's catch-all utility toolbox, mixing in Logging and the SparkClassUtils, SparkEnvUtils, SparkErrorUtils, SparkFileUtils, SparkSerDeUtils, SparkStreamUtils, SparkStringUtils and SparkSystemUtils traits. It is used from almost every module. Methods grouped by theme (line ranges): serialization and buffers (deserializeLongValue 133-143, serializeViaNestedStream 146-157, deserializeViaNestedStream 160-171, weakIntern 174-176, writeByteBufferImpl 191-210, clone 1686-1688); class loader scoping (withContextClassLoader 181-189); temp dirs and permissions (chmod700 232-239, createTempDir 245-251, createExecutorLocalTempDir 260-267, tempFileWith 2696-2698); URI and file name encoding (encodeFileNameToURIRawPath 319-325, encodeRelativeUnixPathToURIRawPath 330-336, decodeFileNameInURI 342-346, validateURL 716-729, isLocalUri 3022-3024, getUriBuilder 3027-3038); file fetching and archives (fetchFile 365-441, unpack 448-468, doFetchFile 638-678, fetchHcfsFile 685-709, downloadFile 515-535, copyFile 553-598, unzipFilesFromFile 3112-3116, symlink 1865-1873, isInDirectory 2551-2562); local dirs (getLocalDir 744-753, getOrCreateLocalRootDirs 775-784, getConfiguredLocalDirs 791-808, clearLocalRootDirs 855-857, isInRunningSparkTask 763); host and port handling (findLocalInetAddress 888-926, setCustomHostname 933-937, localCanonicalHostName 942-944, localHostName 950-952, localHostNameForURI 957-959, checkHost 991-998, checkHostPort 1000-1008, parseHostPort 1014-1046, extractHostPortFromSparkUrl 2456-2475, startServiceOnPort 2264-2340, isBindCollision 2345-2361, userPort 2256-2258, portMaxRetries 2242-2250); unit conversion and formatting (timeStringAsMs 1092-1094, timeStringAsSeconds 1100-1102, byteStringAsBytes/Kb/Mb/Gb 1109-1138, memoryStringToMb 1143-1147, bytesToString 1156-1174, msDurationToString 1179-1195, megabytesToString 1200-1202, getUsedTimeNs 1052-1054, timeTakenMs 494-499, stringHalfWidth 3000-3002); process execution (executeCommand 1207-1224, executeAndGetOutput 1229-1247, processStreamByLine 1252-1266, terminateProcess 1921-1941, getStderr 1947-1954, checkCommandAvailable 3182-3194, splitCommandString 1699-1751); error handling wrappers (tryOrExit 1274-1281, tryOrStopSparkContext 1291-1309, tryLogNonFatalError 1312-1320, tryWithSafeFinallyAndFailureCallbacks 1333-1367, doTryWithCallerStacktrace 1405-1432, getTryWithCallerStacktrace 1448-1471, logUncaughtExceptions 1961-1972, tryLog 1975-1987, isFatalError 1990-2001, exceptionString 2108-2117, stringifyException 3245-3251); call sites (getCallSite 1496-1550, withDummyCallSite 2533-2545); log file length and offsets (getFileLength 1574-1580, offsetBytes 1609-1681); numeric and iterator helpers (nonNegativeMod 1757-1760, nonNegativeHash 1765-1776, times 1792-1798, timeIt 1809-1826, getIteratorSize 1831-1841, getIteratorZipWithIndex 1847-1857, randomize 864-866, randomizeInPlace 872-880, median 3169-3177); Hadoop helpers (getHadoopFileSystem 1878-1887, uploadFileToHadoopCompatibleFS 1892-1904, isFileSplittable 3041-3044, buildLocationMetadata 3060-3078); properties and config (resolveURIs 2004-2010, nonLocalPaths 2013-2027, loadDefaultSparkProperties 2035-2046, getPropertiesFromFile 2073-2092, getDefaultPropertiesFile 2095-2102, getSparkOrYarnConfig 2437-2445, sparkJavaOpts 2230-2237, cloneProperties 3047-3054, getUserJars 2748-2750, getLocalUserJarsForShell 2757-2760); thread and heap diagnostics (threadInfoOrdering 2130-2153, getThreadDump 2156-2161, getHeapHistogram 2164-2177, getThreadDumpForThread 2179-2188, getProcessName 2704-2706); log level and logging setup (setLogLevel 2366-2373, setLogLevelIfNeeded 2376-2380, getLogLevel 2390-2393, initDaemon 2712-2715, resetStructuredLogging 2722-2741); environment and mode checks (libraryPathEnvName 2398-2406, libraryPathEnvPrefix 2413-2427, isLocalMaster 2569-2572, isClientMode 3017-3019, isPushBasedShuffleEnabled 2581-2616, isDynamicAllocationEnabled 2653-2657, isStreamingDynamicAllocationEnabled 2659-2663, getDynamicAllocationInitialExecutors 2668-2691, parseStandaloneMasterUrls 2517-2519, responseFromBackup 2525-2527, checkAndGetK8sMasterUrl 2915-2942); users and secrets (getCurrentUserName 2482-2491, getCurrentUserGroups 2496-2511, createSecret 2966-2972, redact overloads 2768-2843, redactCommandLineArgs 2845-2854); reflection and extensions (instantiateSerializerOrShuffleManager 2620-2639, instantiateSerializerFromConf 2643-2648, loadExtensions 2868-2908); string substitution (substituteAppNExecIds 2948-2950, substituteAppId 2955-2957, substituteSparkVersion 2962-2964, sanitizeDirName 3004-3006, nameForAppAndAttempt 3008-3015); memory settings (executorOffHeapMemorySizeAsMb 3083-3086, checkOffHeapEnabled 3091-3099); GC detection (isSerialGC 3199, isParallelGC 3204, isG1GC 3209, isZGC 3214, isShenandoahGC 3219, checkUseGC 3221-3223, getVMOptionValue 3230-3240); misc (createFailedToGetTokenMessage 3102-3106, createResourceUninterruptiblyIfInTaskThread 3156-3160, copyStreamUpTo 282-311). Function nodes below cover the most important of these; the remaining one-liners and private fields are summarized only here. Overloads share one function node (writeByteBuffer, bytesToString, offsetBytes, getHadoopFileSystem, startServiceOnPort, resetStructuredLogging, redact, getUriBuilder).

nodes.name: CallSite
nodes.summary: Case class holding a short and a long description of the place in user code that created an RDD or ran an operation; its companion object defines the local property keys 'callSite.short' and 'callSite.long' and an empty instance. Produced by Utils.getCallSite and read or reset by Utils.withDummyCallSite.

nodes.name: OriginalTryStackTraceException
nodes.summary: Exception nested in Utils that preserves the original stack trace before stitching; on later accesses it is attached as a suppressed exception so the original failure location stays visible. Used by doTryWithCallerStacktrace and getTryWithCallerStacktrace.

nodes.name: TryStackTraceWrapper
nodes.summary: Internal exception wrapper nested in Utils that carries an original exception, the number of stack frames to preserve, and the OriginalTryStackTraceException; it is used only for stack trace stitching and never exposed to users.

nodes.name: Lock
nodes.summary: Private implicit class in Utils that adds a lockString method to LockInfo, labelling a lock as Monitor(...) or Lock(...); used when converting ThreadInfo into a ThreadStackTrace.

nodes.name: CallerContext
nodes.summary: Utility class (with a private[util] companion object that reads hadoop.caller.context.enabled) that builds a 'SPARK_<from>_<appId>_...' caller context string, truncates it to the Hadoop maximum size, and sets it as the Hadoop caller context and audit context when enabled. Used so storage and cluster audit logs can show which Spark job issued a request.

nodes.name: RedirectThread
nodes.summary: Daemon thread that copies bytes from an input stream to an output stream, flushing after each chunk, and optionally closes the output at end of stream. Used to redirect a child process's stdout or stderr.

nodes.name: CircularBuffer
nodes.summary: OutputStream that keeps only the last N bytes (10 KiB by default) written to it in a circular buffer; toString returns the retained bytes in write order. Useful for capturing the tail of a process's output.

nodes.name: deserializeLongValue
nodes.summary: Decodes eight big-endian bytes into a Long; documented as used for the Python partitioner.

nodes.name: serializeViaNestedStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an OutputStream in a serializer stream, runs the supplied writer function against it, and always closes the serialization stream.

nodes.name: deserializeViaNestedStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an InputStream in a deserialization stream with the given serializer, runs the supplied reader function, and always closes the stream.

nodes.name: withContextClassLoader
nodes.summary: Runs a block with the given context class loader set on the current thread and restores the old loader afterwards.

nodes.name: writeByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Writes a ByteBuffer to a DataOutput (this overload) or an OutputStream (overload at 222-224, same node id) via writeByteBufferImpl, avoiding a copy when the buffer is array-backed.

nodes.name: writeByteBufferImpl
nodes.summary: Private helper that writes a ByteBuffer through a writer function: uses the backing array directly when present, otherwise copies in chunks through a thread-local buffer and restores the buffer position.

nodes.name: chmod700
nodes.summary: JDK equivalent of chmod 700: restricts read, write and execute access of a file to its owner and reports whether all changes succeeded.

nodes.name: createTempDir
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary directory under the given root (default java.io.tmpdir, prefix 'spark') and registers it for deletion at JVM shutdown. Overrides the inherited trait method.

nodes.name: createExecutorLocalTempDir
nodes.summary: Creates a temp directory that is cleaned up when the executor stops: uses the default java tmp dir inside a YARN container, otherwise a directory under Spark's local dir.

nodes.name: copyStreamUpTo
nodes.summary: Copies the first maxSize bytes of an InputStream into an in-memory chunked buffer, mainly to detect corruption early, and returns a stream that replays the buffered data followed by the rest of the original stream.

nodes.name: encodeFileNameToURIRawPath
nodes.summary: Converts a file name that may contain URI-invalid characters (for example a space) into a raw URI path; rejects names containing slashes.

nodes.name: encodeRelativeUnixPathToURIRawPath
nodes.summary: Encodes a relative UNIX path into a raw URI path using a dummy scheme and host so URI does not misparse it, then strips the leading slash.

nodes.name: decodeFileNameInURI
nodes.summary: Returns the decoded file name from the last segment of a URI's raw path.

nodes.name: fetchFile
nodes.summary: Downloads a file or directory into a target directory over HTTP, a Hadoop-compatible filesystem or the local filesystem. With useCache it first fetches into a lock-protected local cache shared by executors of the same application, then copies; it optionally untars .tar/.tgz files (legacy behavior), makes the file executable and fixes read permission on Windows.

nodes.name: unpack
nodes.summary: Unpacks a .jar, .zip, .tar.gz, .tgz or .tar archive into a destination directory (copying it unchanged for other types), mirroring Hadoop's distributed cache behavior.

nodes.name: unTarUsingJava
nodes.summary: Private helper that untars a file by invoking Hadoop FileUtil's Java-based unTar implementation through reflection, rethrowing the underlying cause.

nodes.name: timeTakenMs
nodes.summary: Runs a block and returns its result together with the elapsed time in milliseconds.

nodes.name: downloadFile
nodes.summary: Private helper that downloads an InputStream to a temp file next to the destination, then moves it to the destination via copyFile, deleting the temp file if anything fails.

nodes.name: copyFile
nodes.summary: Private helper that copies or moves a file to a destination: no-op if the existing destination matches, throws SparkException if it differs and overwrite is disabled, otherwise deletes and replaces it.

nodes.name: filesEqualRecursive
nodes.summary: Private helper that compares two files or two directory trees for equal content, matching directory entries by sorted name.

nodes.name: copyRecursive
nodes.summary: Private helper that copies a file or recursively copies a directory tree to a destination path.

nodes.name: doFetchFile
nodes.summary: Downloads a file or directory to a target directory, dispatching on the URL scheme: spark (RPC channel from the active SparkEnv), http/https/ftp (with a configurable timeout), file (local copy), and anything else through a Hadoop-compatible filesystem.

nodes.name: fetchHcfsFile
nodes.summary: Fetches a file, or recursively a directory, from a Hadoop-compatible filesystem into the target directory.

nodes.name: validateURL
nodes.summary: Checks that an http, https or ftp URI can be turned into a URL, rethrowing MalformedURLException with a clearer message.

nodes.name: getLocalDir
nodes.summary: Returns one randomly chosen local directory from the (cached) set Spark can write to, honoring YARN, SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS, spark.local.dir and java.io.tmpdir in that order; throws IOException if none could be created.

nodes.name: isRunningInYarnContainer
nodes.summary: Returns true when the CONTAINER_ID environment variable (set by YARN) is present.

nodes.name: getOrCreateLocalRootDirs
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches the local root directories for the application using double-checked locking; later calls with different configuration return the same directories.

nodes.name: getConfiguredLocalDirs
nodes.summary: Returns the configured local directories without creating them: YARN's LOCAL_DIRS (shuffled) in a YARN container, SPARK_EXECUTOR_DIRS or SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS if set, otherwise spark.local.dir or java.io.tmpdir.

nodes.name: getOrCreateLocalRootDirsImpl
nodes.summary: Private implementation that warns about URI-looking directories, then for each configured root creates the directory if needed, makes a restricted (chmod 700) temp subdirectory in it, and skips roots that fail.

nodes.name: getYarnLocalDirs
nodes.summary: Private helper that reads YARN's LOCAL_DIRS environment variable and fails if it is empty.

nodes.name: randomize
nodes.summary: Returns a new randomly ordered sequence of the elements using a local random generator (avoids the inter-thread contention of scala.util.Random.shuffle).

nodes.name: randomizeInPlace
nodes.summary: Shuffles an array in place with a Fisher-Yates style loop and returns the same array.

nodes.name: findLocalInetAddress
nodes.summary: Private method that determines the local IP: uses SPARK_LOCAL_IP when set, otherwise the local host address, and if that is a loopback address scans network interfaces for a non-loopback, non-link-local address (preferring IPv4), logging warnings.

nodes.name: setCustomHostname
nodes.summary: Validates and stores a custom host name that overrides the detected one in localHostName and related methods.

nodes.name: localCanonicalHostName
nodes.summary: Returns the local machine's fully qualified domain name (or the custom host name), bracketed when it is an IPv6 address.

nodes.name: localHostName
nodes.summary: Returns the local host address (or the custom host name), bracketed when it is an IPv6 address.

nodes.name: localHostNameForURI
nodes.summary: Returns the local host name in a form suitable for use inside a URI, bracketing IPv6 addresses.

nodes.name: addBracketsIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Wraps an address containing a colon in square brackets unless it is already bracketed.

nodes.name: normalizeIpIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Normalizes a string that looks like an IPv6 address (digits and colons, optionally bracketed) to its canonical bracketed form and leaves other hosts unchanged.

nodes.name: checkHost
nodes.summary: Asserts that a string is a host name or IP without a port; IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.

nodes.name: checkHostPort
nodes.summary: Asserts that a string contains both a host and a port, handling bracketed IPv6 hosts.

nodes.name: parseHostPort
nodes.summary: Splits a 'host:port' string (including bracketed IPv6 hosts) into a (host, port) tuple, using port 0 when no port is given, and caches results in a concurrent map.

nodes.name: getUsedTimeNs
nodes.summary: Returns a string such as '12 ms' telling how long has passed since a System.nanoTime start timestamp.

nodes.name: deleteRecursively
nodes.summary: Deletes a file or directory tree through the inherited implementation and then removes the path from the shutdown-hook deletion registry.

nodes.name: doesDirectoryContainAnyNewFiles
nodes.summary: Returns true if any file or subdirectory in a directory tree was modified within the last cutoff seconds.

nodes.name: timeStringAsMs
nodes.summary: Converts a time string such as '50s', '100ms' or '250us' to milliseconds (no suffix means ms) by delegating to the Java network utils class. Sibling timeStringAsSeconds (1100-1102) returns seconds.

nodes.name: byteStringAsBytes
nodes.summary: Converts a size string such as '50b', '100k' or '250m' to bytes by delegating to the Java network utils class. Siblings byteStringAsKb, byteStringAsMb and byteStringAsGb (1118-1138) convert to larger units.

nodes.name: memoryStringToMb
nodes.summary: Converts a JVM memory size such as '300m' or '1g' (as passed to -Xmx) to mebibytes, converting through bytes so that a bare number is treated as bytes.

nodes.name: bytesToString
nodes.summary: Formats a byte count as a human-readable string such as '4.0 MiB'. The Long overload (1156-1160) picks the unit; the BigInt overload (1162-1174) handles values beyond 64 bits and uses scientific notation when huge. Both share this node id.

nodes.name: msDurationToString
nodes.summary: Formats a millisecond duration as ms, seconds, minutes or hours text.

nodes.name: megabytesToString
nodes.summary: Formats a megabyte quantity as a human-readable string by converting to bytes and calling bytesToString.

nodes.name: executeCommand
nodes.summary: Starts an external command in a working directory with extra environment variables and returns the Process; optionally logs its stderr line by line on a daemon thread.

nodes.name: executeAndGetOutput
nodes.summary: Runs a command, collects its stdout on a daemon thread, waits for exit and returns the output, throwing SparkException (after logging the output) when the exit code is not 0.

nodes.name: processStreamByLine
nodes.summary: Starts and returns a daemon thread that reads an InputStream line by line and passes each line to a callback.

nodes.name: tryOrExit
nodes.summary: Runs a Unit block and forwards any uncaught throwable (except control-flow throwables) to Spark's uncaught exception handler; meant for Spark-started JVM processes.

nodes.name: tryOrStopSparkContext
nodes.summary: Runs a Unit block and, on an uncaught throwable, logs it and stops the SparkContext in a new thread; rethrows fatal errors. Meant for driver-side components that must not kill the user's JVM.

nodes.name: tryLogNonFatalError
nodes.summary: Runs a Unit block, logging non-fatal errors and letting fatal ones propagate.

nodes.name: tryWithSafeFinallyAndFailureCallbacks
nodes.summary: Runs a block with a catch callback and a finally callback, marking the current task failed on error, and appends exceptions thrown by the callbacks as suppressed exceptions on the original so the first failure is not masked.

nodes.name: doTryWithCallerStacktrace
nodes.summary: Wraps a code block in a Try; on failure wraps the exception with metadata (frame depth and original stack trace) so that getTryWithCallerStacktrace can later stitch the stack trace of whoever reads the result.

nodes.name: getTryWithCallerStacktrace
nodes.summary: Unwraps a Try produced by doTryWithCallerStacktrace: on failure rewrites the exception's stack trace to join the original lower frames with the current caller's, adds the original trace as a suppressed exception on repeat access, and rethrows; on success returns the value.

nodes.name: sparkInternalExclusionFunction
nodes.summary: Private default filter for getCallSite: returns true for class names that belong to Spark's core or SQL packages or to Scala, so those frames are skipped when looking for user code.

nodes.name: getCallSite
nodes.summary: Walks the current thread's stack trace to find the last Spark method and the first user-code file and line, and returns a CallSite with a short form such as 'method at file:line' and a long form made of the stack (depth from spark.callstack.depth). Used to tell users where an RDD was created.

nodes.name: getCompressedLogFileLengthCache
nodes.summary: Private method that lazily builds a size-bounded Guava loading cache mapping gzip file paths to their uncompressed length.

nodes.name: getFileLength
nodes.summary: Returns a file's length; for .gz files returns the cached uncompressed length so repeated decompression is avoided.

nodes.name: getCompressedFileLength
nodes.summary: Private method that determines the uncompressed size of a gzip file by reading it fully, logging and rethrowing errors.

nodes.name: offsetBytes
nodes.summary: Returns the text between byte offsets start and end across an ordered list of files (and their lengths), treating them as one concatenated stream; the single-file overload (1609-1627) reads part of one file, optionally gzip-compressed, and shares this node id.

nodes.name: splitCommandString
nodes.summary: Splits a command-line string into arguments the way a shell would, honoring single quotes, double quotes and backslash escapes inside double quotes.

nodes.name: nonNegativeMod
nodes.summary: Computes x modulo mod and adds mod when the raw remainder is negative so the result is never negative.

nodes.name: nonNegativeHash
nodes.summary: Returns the absolute value of an object's hashCode (0 for null and for Int.MinValue); kept in sync with the Java network utils version.

nodes.name: getSystemProperties
nodes.summary: Returns an immutable map snapshot of all system properties, including defaults, safe to iterate.

nodes.name: times
nodes.summary: Repeats a Unit block a given number of times with a while loop so the JVM can optimize it, unlike a for comprehension.

nodes.name: timeIt
nodes.summary: Times numIters runs of a block in nanoseconds, optionally running a prepare step before each iteration whose time is excluded.

nodes.name: getIteratorSize
nodes.summary: Counts the elements of an iterator, using knownSize when available and otherwise consuming it.

nodes.name: getIteratorZipWithIndex
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator pairing each element with a Long index starting at startIndex, avoiding the Int overflow of Scala's zipWithIndex.

nodes.name: symlink
nodes.summary: Creates a symbolic link from a relative destination to an absolute source, throwing IOException if the path kinds are wrong.

nodes.name: getHadoopFileSystem
nodes.summary: Returns the Hadoop FileSystem for the scheme in a path; the URI overload (1878-1880) calls FileSystem.get directly and the String overload (this range) converts to URI first. Both share this node id.

nodes.name: uploadFileToHadoopCompatibleFS
nodes.summary: Copies a local file to a Hadoop-compatible filesystem, optionally deleting the source and overwriting, wrapping IOException in SparkException.

nodes.name: terminateProcess
nodes.summary: Politely destroys a process, waits up to a timeout, then forcibly kills it if needed; returns the exit value or None if it could not be terminated.

nodes.name: getStderr
nodes.summary: Waits up to a timeout for a process to terminate and returns its stderr text, or None if it is still running.

nodes.name: logUncaughtExceptions
nodes.summary: Runs a block, logging any uncaught exception (except control-flow throwables) with the thread name and rethrowing it.

nodes.name: tryLog
nodes.summary: Runs a block and returns a Try, logging uncaught exceptions as Failure rather than throwing them (control-flow throwables still propagate).

nodes.name: isFatalError
nodes.summary: Returns true for throwables that are fatal, treating NonFatal ones plus InterruptedException, NotImplementedError, ControlThrowable and LinkageError as not fatal.

nodes.name: resolveURIs
nodes.summary: Resolves each entry of a comma-separated path list to a URI string using resolveURI and re-joins them.

nodes.name: nonLocalPaths
nodes.summary: Returns the entries of a comma-separated path list whose resolved URI scheme is not local, file or a Windows drive letter.

nodes.name: loadDefaultSparkProperties
nodes.summary: Loads spark.* settings from a given or default properties file into a SparkConf and the JVM system properties when not already set, and returns the file path used.

nodes.name: trimExceptCRLF
nodes.summary: Trims leading and trailing characters at or below the space character like String.trim, but keeps carriage returns and newlines that were explicitly escaped in a properties file.

nodes.name: getPropertiesFromFile
nodes.summary: Loads a Java properties file as a string map (UTF-8, values trimmed with trimExceptCRLF), requiring that it exists and is a regular file and wrapping IOException in SparkException.

nodes.name: getDefaultPropertiesFile
nodes.summary: Finds spark-defaults.conf under SPARK_CONF_DIR or SPARK_HOME/conf and returns its absolute path, or null if it is missing.

nodes.name: exceptionString
nodes.summary: Returns the full printStackTrace text of an exception including causes, or an empty string for null.

nodes.name: getThreadDump
nodes.summary: Returns stack traces of all live threads as ThreadStackTrace objects, filtering out null entries and sorting with threadInfoOrdering (task threads and Connect execute threads first). Used to capture dumps for the web UI.

nodes.name: getHeapHistogram
nodes.summary: Returns the JVM class histogram as lines by invoking the in-process DiagnosticCommand MBean (gcClassHistogram), avoiding a jmap subprocess whose output pipe could block.

nodes.name: getThreadDumpForThread
nodes.summary: Returns the full stack trace of one thread by id as an Option, or None for a non-positive id or a missing thread.

nodes.name: threadInfoToThreadStackTrace
nodes.summary: Private converter from a JMX ThreadInfo to a ThreadStackTrace, annotating stack frames with blocked/waiting/locked lock information and collecting lock owner, synchronizers and thread flags.

nodes.name: sparkJavaOpts
nodes.summary: Converts the properties of a Spark conf (optionally filtered by key) into a sequence of '-Dkey=value' Java options.

nodes.name: portMaxRetries
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum number of port-bind retries from spark.port.maxRetries, defaulting to 16 (100 when testing).

nodes.name: userPort
nodes.summary: Computes the port to try for a given base and retry offset, wrapping around and skipping privileged ports below 1024.

nodes.name: startServiceOnPort
nodes.summary: Starts a service on a given port, retrying with port+1 on bind collisions up to a maximum and raising BindException with a hint on failure; port 0 means a random free port. The overload taking a conf (2264-2270) reads the retry count from portMaxRetries and shares this node id.

nodes.name: isBindCollision
nodes.summary: Returns true if an exception or any of its causes indicates an address/port bind collision (BindException, native bind failure, or Netty-style 'Failed to bind' errors).

nodes.name: setLogLevel
nodes.summary: Sets the root logger level in the log4j configuration and clears the spark-shell threshold level.

nodes.name: setLogLevelIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Sets the root log level only when it differs from the current level.

nodes.name: getLogLevel
nodes.summary: Returns the name of the current root logger level.

nodes.name: libraryPathEnvName
nodes.summary: Returns the library path environment variable name for the OS: PATH on Windows, DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH on macOS, LD_LIBRARY_PATH otherwise.

nodes.name: libraryPathEnvPrefix
nodes.summary: Builds a command prefix that appends the given library paths to the platform library path variable, for example LD_LIBRARY_PATH="path1:path2:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH".

nodes.name: getSparkOrYarnConfig
nodes.summary: Returns a config value from SparkConf if set; otherwise, only when the master is yarn, from the Hadoop YarnConfiguration; otherwise the default.

nodes.name: extractHostPortFromSparkUrl
nodes.summary: Parses a 'spark://host:port' master URL into (host, port), throwing SparkException if the URL has any other component or a different scheme.

nodes.name: getCurrentUserName
nodes.summary: Returns the current user name, preferring SPARK_USER over the Hadoop UserGroupInformation short name, and falling back to the user.name system property if the subject lookup is unsupported.

nodes.name: getCurrentUserGroups
nodes.summary: Returns the groups of a user using the configured GroupMappingServiceProvider class (instantiated by name), or an empty set when none is configured or lookup fails.

nodes.name: parseStandaloneMasterUrls
nodes.summary: Splits a comma-delimited standalone master URL string such as 'spark://abc,def' into full 'spark://' URLs.

nodes.name: responseFromBackup
nodes.summary: Returns true if a response message starts with the marker text used by standby (backup) masters.

nodes.name: withDummyCallSite
nodes.summary: Runs a body with empty call-site local properties set on the SparkContext so RDD creation does not call getCallSite each time, then restores the previous values.

nodes.name: isInDirectory
nodes.summary: Returns true if the first file is a directory that is an ancestor of (or equal to) the child, walking up the child's parents.

nodes.name: isLocalMaster
nodes.summary: Returns true when spark.master is 'local' or starts with 'local['.

nodes.name: isPushBasedShuffleEnabled
nodes.summary: Decides whether push-based shuffle can be enabled: requires the setting on, YARN with the external shuffle service (or testing), IO encryption off, and a serializer that supports relocation; logs a warning when requested but not possible.

nodes.name: instantiateSerializerOrShuffleManager
nodes.summary: Loads a class by name and instantiates it with a (SparkConf, isDriver) constructor, falling back to a SparkConf-only constructor and then a no-arg constructor.

nodes.name: instantiateSerializerFromConf
nodes.summary: Instantiates the serializer class named by a config entry by delegating to instantiateSerializerOrShuffleManager.

nodes.name: isDynamicAllocationEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns true when dynamic allocation is enabled and Spark is not in local mode (unless the testing flag allows it).

nodes.name: isStreamingDynamicAllocationEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns true when streaming dynamic allocation is enabled and Spark is not in local mode (unless the testing flag allows it).

nodes.name: getDynamicAllocationInitialExecutors
nodes.summary: Computes the initial executor count as the maximum of the minimum-executors, initial-executors and executor-instances settings, warning when the latter two are below the minimum.

nodes.name: tempFileWith
nodes.summary: Returns a new path in the same directory as the given file with a random UUID suffix.

nodes.name: getProcessName
nodes.summary: Returns this JVM's runtime name, typically 'pid@hostname'.

nodes.name: initDaemon
nodes.summary: Called early in main() of daemons: logs the process name and registers signal logging.

nodes.name: resetStructuredLogging
nodes.summary: Enables or disables structured logging based on a system property (this overload, usable before SparkConf exists); the overload at 2735-2741 uses a ReadOnlySparkConf and shares this node id.

nodes.name: getUserJars
nodes.summary: Returns the non-empty entries of the spark.jars setting.

nodes.name: redact
nodes.summary: Private overload that replaces the value of a key/value pair with '*********(redacted)' when the redaction regex matches the key or the value. Public overloads (2768-2843) redact a conf's pairs, an optional regex over pairs or text, and a string map; all share this node id.

nodes.name: redactCommandLineArgs
nodes.summary: Redacts the values of '-Dkey=value' command-line arguments whose key or value matches the configured redaction pattern.

nodes.name: loadExtensions
nodes.summary: Creates instances of extension classes by name, requiring them to be subclasses of a base class and to have a no-arg or SparkConf constructor; an UnsupportedOperationException from a constructor means the extension opts out and is skipped.

nodes.name: checkAndGetK8sMasterUrl
nodes.summary: Validates a Kubernetes master URL beginning with k8s://, defaults a missing scheme to https, warns for http, rejects other schemes and returns the resolved k8s:// URL.

nodes.name: createSecret
nodes.summary: Generates a random hex-encoded secret of the configured bit length using SecureRandom.

nodes.name: nameForAppAndAttempt
nodes.summary: Builds a directory-safe name from an application id and optional attempt id using sanitizeDirName (3004-3006, which replaces spaces, colons, slashes and special characters).

nodes.name: isFileSplittable
nodes.summary: Returns true if a path has no compression codec or a splittable one.

nodes.name: cloneProperties
nodes.summary: Creates a new Properties object with the same entries as the given one (null stays null).

nodes.name: buildLocationMetadata
nodes.summary: Builds a '(N paths)[...]' string from a list of paths, stopping to append paths once the string exceeds a length threshold and adding an ellipsis.

nodes.name: executorOffHeapMemorySizeAsMb
nodes.summary: Returns the configured off-heap memory size in MB, or 0 when off-heap memory is disabled.

nodes.name: checkOffHeapEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns the off-heap size when off-heap memory is enabled (requiring it to be positive) and 0 when it is disabled.

nodes.name: createFailedToGetTokenMessage
nodes.summary: Builds a structured log message about a failed delegation token request and how to disable the service's credential provider.

nodes.name: unzipFilesFromFile
nodes.summary: Unzips a zip file read from a Hadoop filesystem into a local directory and returns the extracted files.

nodes.name: unzipFilesFromInputStream
nodes.summary: Extracts the file entries of a zip stream into a local directory (flat, using only entry file names) and returns the created files, closing streams quietly.

nodes.name: createResourceUninterruptiblyIfInTaskThread
nodes.summary: Creates a closeable resource uninterruptibly via the TaskContext when called in a task thread, otherwise creates it normally, so resources are not leaked on task cancellation.

nodes.name: median
nodes.summary: Returns the median of a long array (sorting it unless already sorted), never less than 1.

nodes.name: checkCommandAvailable
nodes.summary: Checks whether a command exists on the PATH by running 'where' on Windows or 'command -v' elsewhere and testing for exit code 0.

nodes.name: checkUseGC
nodes.summary: Returns true if the named HotSpot boolean VM option (for example UseG1GC) is set to true; backs the lazy isSerialGC, isParallelGC, isG1GC, isZGC and isShenandoahGC flags.

nodes.name: getVMOptionValue
nodes.summary: Reads a HotSpot VM option value through the HotSpotDiagnosticMXBean via reflection, returning None if it cannot be read.

nodes.name: stringifyException
nodes.summary: Returns the printStackTrace output of a throwable as a string.

nodes.name: prepareContext
nodes.summary: Private method that truncates the caller context string to the Hadoop maximum size (hadoop.caller.context.max.size, default 128), logging a warning when truncated.

nodes.name: setCurrentContext
nodes.summary: When caller context is enabled, sets the built context as the Hadoop caller context and as the 'spark' entry of the audit context.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Copies bytes from the input stream to the output stream in 1 KiB chunks, flushing each time, and closes the output at the end if propagateEof is set; IOExceptions are ignored.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Stores one byte at the current position and advances it with wrap-around, remembering when the buffer has filled.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns the buffered bytes in write order as a UTF-8 string, re-ordering the wrapped buffer when it is full.

nodes.name: ExposedBufferByteArrayOutputStream.java
nodes.summary: Defines a final ByteArrayOutputStream subclass that exposes the protected internal byte array through getBuf(). Lets callers read the written bytes without the copy made by toByteArray().

nodes.name: ExposedBufferByteArrayOutputStream
nodes.summary: Final ByteArrayOutputStream subclass created with an initial size. Its getBuf() method returns the underlying buffer directly instead of a copy.

nodes.name: getBuf
nodes.summary: Returns the protected buf array of the parent ByteArrayOutputStream without copying.

nodes.name: BlockingThreadPoolExecutorService.scala
nodes.summary: Provides an ExecutorService that throttles task submission with a semaphore sized to threads plus queue slots. Submissions acquire a permit and finished tasks release it, so callers block when the pool is saturated.

nodes.name: BlockingThreadPoolExecutorService
nodes.summary: ExecutorService wrapping a fixed-size ThreadPoolExecutor with a bounded LinkedBlockingQueue and a Semaphore. submit and execute block until a permit is free; the invokeAll and invokeAny methods throw UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: RunnableWithPermitRelease
nodes.summary: Private inner Runnable that runs a wrapped Runnable and releases the semaphore permit in a finally block.

nodes.name: CallableWithPermitRelease
nodes.summary: Private inner Callable that calls a wrapped Callable and releases the semaphore permit in a finally block.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Delegates shutdown to the underlying ThreadPoolExecutor.

nodes.name: shutdownNow
nodes.summary: Delegates shutdownNow to the underlying ThreadPoolExecutor and returns the pending tasks.

nodes.name: isShutdown
nodes.summary: Reports whether the underlying ThreadPoolExecutor has been shut down.

nodes.name: isTerminated
nodes.summary: Reports whether the underlying ThreadPoolExecutor has terminated.

nodes.name: awaitTermination
nodes.summary: Delegates awaitTermination with the given timeout and unit to the underlying ThreadPoolExecutor.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Acquires a permit, then submits a Callable wrapped to release the permit when done. If the wait is interrupted it re-sets the interrupt flag and returns a failed future. Two overloads (submit(Runnable, result) at lines 69-76 and submit(Runnable) at lines 78-85) do the same with a Runnable.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Acquires a permit (restoring the interrupt flag if interrupted) and executes the command wrapped to release the permit when done.

nodes.name: invokeAll
nodes.summary: Unsupported: throws UnsupportedOperationException. The overload without a timeout is at lines 95-97.

nodes.name: invokeAny
nodes.summary: Unsupported: throws UnsupportedOperationException. The overload without a timeout is at lines 104-105.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs the wrapped Runnable and releases a permit in a finally block.

nodes.name: call
nodes.summary: Calls the wrapped Callable and releases a permit in a finally block.

nodes.name: BoundedPriorityQueue.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a bounded priority queue that keeps only the top K elements according to an implicit Ordering. Useful where a fixed number of best elements should be retained while streaming over values.

nodes.name: BoundedPriorityQueue
nodes.summary: Serializable Iterable and Growable that wraps a java.util.PriorityQueue and retains at most maxSize elements. Once full, a new element replaces the lowest one only if it is greater under the ordering.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns the underlying queue's iterator converted to a Scala Iterator.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the number of elements currently held in the underlying queue.

nodes.name: addAll
nodes.summary: Adds every element of the given collection through the bounded add path and returns this queue.

nodes.name: addOne
nodes.summary: Offers the element when the queue is below maxSize, otherwise tries to replace the current lowest element.

nodes.name: poll
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the head of the underlying priority queue.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Empties the underlying priority queue.

nodes.name: maybeReplaceLowest
nodes.summary: Compares the new element with the queue head and, if it is greater, removes the head and inserts the new element.

nodes.name: ByteBufferInputStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines an InputStream that reads data from a ByteBuffer. It drops its reference to the buffer once the buffer is exhausted.

nodes.name: ByteBufferInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream over a ByteBuffer with single-byte, array and skip reads. When the buffer runs out or is skipped to its end, it sets the buffer to null.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads up to length bytes from the buffer into dest at offset and returns -1 when exhausted. Overloads read() at lines 30-37 and read(dest) at lines 39-41 read one byte or delegate to this one.

nodes.name: skip
nodes.summary: Advances the buffer position by up to the requested bytes and cleans up if the buffer becomes empty.

nodes.name: cleanUp
nodes.summary: Sets the buffer reference to null so it can be released.

nodes.name: ByteBufferOutputStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a ByteArrayOutputStream subclass that converts its contents to a ByteBuffer without copying. It rejects writes after close and allows toByteBuffer only after close.

nodes.name: ByteBufferOutputStream
nodes.summary: ByteArrayOutputStream with a closed flag and a default capacity of 32. Writes and resets fail with require after close, and toByteBuffer wraps the internal buffer.

nodes.name: getCount
nodes.summary: Returns the number of valid bytes in the internal buffer.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a byte range after requiring the stream is not closed. The single-byte overload at lines 34-37 does the same check.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets the stream after requiring it is not closed.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the parent stream once and marks this stream as closed.

nodes.name: toByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Requires the stream to be closed, then wraps the internal buffer for the valid count in a ByteBuffer without copying.

nodes.name: CausedBy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CausedBy extractor object used in pattern matches to obtain the root cause of a Throwable. If the error has no cause it yields the error itself.

nodes.name: CausedBy
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply walks the cause chain recursively and returns the deepest cause, for use in catch clauses.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Recursively follows getCause and returns the last throwable in the chain, or the input if it has no cause.

nodes.name: Clock.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Clock trait, an abstraction over time so that time can be mocked in unit tests, and SystemClock, its implementation backed by the System API.

nodes.name: Clock
nodes.summary: Trait that represents a clock with getTimeMillis, nanoTime and waitTillTime so that it can be mocked out in unit tests.

nodes.name: SystemClock
nodes.summary: Serializable Clock implementation using System.currentTimeMillis and System.nanoTime. Its waitTillTime polls with sleeps until the target time is reached.

nodes.name: getTimeMillis
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the current system time in milliseconds.

nodes.name: nanoTime
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a high resolution time source in nanoseconds, intended for computing time intervals.

nodes.name: waitTillTime
nodes.summary: Abstract method that waits until the wall clock reaches at least the given time.

nodes.name: getTimeMillis
nodes.summary: Returns System.currentTimeMillis().

nodes.name: nanoTime
nodes.summary: Returns System.nanoTime().

nodes.name: waitTillTime
nodes.summary: Blocks by repeatedly sleeping for the smaller of the remaining time and a poll time (at least minPollTime) until the current time reaches the target, then returns the current time.

nodes.name: CollectionsUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a helper that builds a binary search function for arrays, using natural ordering for primitive key types and an Ordering comparator otherwise.

nodes.name: CollectionsUtils
nodes.summary: Private object holding makeBinarySearch.

nodes.name: makeBinarySearch
nodes.summary: Matches on the ClassTag of the key type and returns an (Array, key) => Int function backed by java.util.Arrays.binarySearch, specialized for Float, Double, Byte, Char, Short, Int and Long, with a comparator-based fallback.

nodes.name: CommandLineUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines traits with basic command line support: a main entry method plus message printing and an exit function that can be replaced in tests.

nodes.name: CommandLineUtils
nodes.summary: Trait that extends CommandLineLoggingUtils and declares an abstract main(args) method.

nodes.name: CommandLineLoggingUtils
nodes.summary: Trait with an overridable exit function, a configurable print stream (default System.err), and helpers to print messages and print an error then exit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Abstract entry point that takes the command line arguments.

nodes.name: printMessage
nodes.summary: Prints a string to the configured print stream.

nodes.name: printErrorAndExit
nodes.summary: Prints an error message and a hint about --help and --verbose, then calls exitFn with code 1.

nodes.name: DirectByteBufferOutputStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DirectByteBufferOutputStream, an OutputStream that writes into a growable direct (off-heap) ByteBuffer. Used where serialized bytes should be collected in a direct buffer that can be handed out as a ByteBuffer and freed eagerly.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class extending java.io.OutputStream; the buffer field is set to null on close, and every public method guards against use after close.

nodes.name: DirectByteBufferOutputStream
nodes.summary: OutputStream that appends bytes to a direct byte buffer allocated through Platform.allocateDirectBuffer, starting at the given capacity (32 by default) and doubling it on demand up to the 2GB limit. close frees the buffer eagerly via StorageUtils.dispose instead of waiting for GC.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Appends a range of a byte array to the buffer after checking the stream is open and ensuring capacity. An overload at lines 37-41 writes a single byte the same way.

nodes.name: ensureCapacity
nodes.summary: Throws an internal error if the requested size would exceed Int.MaxValue (2GB), and calls grow when the request is larger than the current buffer capacity.

nodes.name: grow
nodes.summary: Allocates a new direct buffer of at least the requested capacity (normally double the old one), copies the existing content over, and disposes the old buffer with StorageUtils.dispose. Earlier references to the old buffer become invalid.

nodes.name: checkNotClosed
nodes.summary: Throws an internal error if the buffer has already been released by close.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears the buffer so that writing restarts from position zero, reusing the allocated memory.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the number of bytes written so far (the buffer position).

nodes.name: toByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Returns a flipped duplicate of the internal buffer holding the written bytes. The result is invalidated by later close, write or reset calls.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Frees the direct buffer immediately through StorageUtils.dispose and sets the reference to null, so later calls fail the closed check.

nodes.name: BestEffortLazyVal.java
nodes.summary: Defines BestEffortLazyVal, a lock-free lazily initialized value that may run its compute function more than once under contention but keeps a single result. Useful to avoid deadlocks when exactly-once computation is not required.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class taking a scala.Function0; uses a VarHandle compare-and-set on a volatile field for lock-free publication.

nodes.name: BestEffortLazyVal
nodes.summary: Holds a compute function and a volatile cached value. The cached value is serialized with the object, and the compute function must not return null; failures are not cached.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the cached value if present; otherwise runs the compute function, stores the result with compareAndSet on a VarHandle, clears the function so the closure can be garbage collected, and returns the stored value.

nodes.name: ChildFirstURLClassLoader.java
nodes.summary: Defines ChildFirstURLClassLoader, a mutable class loader that looks in its own URLs before the parent when loading classes and resources. Used when child classes must take precedence over those of the parent loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class that passes null (or the grandparent) as the real parent and keeps the actual parent in a ParentClassLoader field, which inverts the usual lookup order.

nodes.name: ChildFirstURLClassLoader
nodes.summary: MutableURLClassLoader that tries its own URLs first and falls back to a wrapped ParentClassLoader on ClassNotFoundException. The two-argument constructor (lines 38-41) passes null as the real parent; a second constructor (lines 47-50) takes a grandparent for the order grandparent, child URLs, parent.

nodes.name: loadClass
nodes.summary: Tries to load the class from this loader's own URLs and, on ClassNotFoundException, delegates to the wrapped parent loader.

nodes.name: getResources
nodes.summary: Returns an enumeration of the resources found through this loader's URLs followed by those from the parent loader.

nodes.name: getResource
nodes.summary: Returns the resource from this loader's URLs if found, otherwise asks the parent loader.

nodes.name: EnumUtil.java
nodes.summary: Defines EnumUtil, a small internal helper that parses an enum constant from a string without regard to case.
nodes.languageNotes: Java static helper with a generic bound on Enum types, annotated @Private.

nodes.name: EnumUtil
nodes.summary: Private utility class with a static parseIgnoreCase method for any enum type and a helper that lists the valid constant names for error messages.

nodes.name: parseIgnoreCase
nodes.summary: Returns the enum constant whose name matches the string ignoring case, null for a null input, and throws IllegalArgumentException listing the supported values otherwise.

nodes.name: joinToString
nodes.summary: Joins the names of all enum constants with a comma and space; used to build the error message.

nodes.name: TransientBestEffortLazyVal.java
nodes.summary: Defines TransientBestEffortLazyVal, a lock-free lazy value like BestEffortLazyVal whose cached result is never serialized: the compute function is always serialized and the value is recomputed after deserialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Differs from BestEffortLazyVal by marking the cached field transient and resetting it in readObject.

nodes.name: TransientBestEffortLazyVal
nodes.summary: Lazy value holder with a volatile compute function and a transient volatile cached field, published with compareAndSet on a VarHandle. The compute function must not return null and failures are not cached.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the cached value if set; otherwise calls the compute function (which is kept, not cleared), stores the result with compareAndSet and returns it.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Custom deserialization hook that reads the default fields and then resets the cached value to null so it is recomputed.

nodes.name: ParentClassLoader.java
nodes.summary: Defines ParentClassLoader, a ClassLoader wrapper that makes findClass and loadClass public. It is used by ChildFirstURLClassLoader to delegate lookups to the parent loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class whose only purpose is to widen the visibility of protected ClassLoader methods.

nodes.name: ParentClassLoader
nodes.summary: ClassLoader subclass that wraps a parent loader and overrides findClass and loadClass so they can be called from outside the class hierarchy. Registered as parallel capable.

nodes.name: findClass
nodes.summary: Public override that forwards to ClassLoader.findClass.

nodes.name: loadClass
nodes.summary: Public override that forwards to ClassLoader.loadClass(name, resolve).

nodes.name: MutableURLClassLoader.java
nodes.summary: Defines MutableURLClassLoader, a URLClassLoader that exposes addURL so jars can be added at runtime. It is the base class of ChildFirstURLClassLoader.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class widening addURL from protected to public.

nodes.name: MutableURLClassLoader
nodes.summary: URLClassLoader subclass that makes addURL public so callers can add URLs after construction. Registered as parallel capable.

nodes.name: addURL
nodes.summary: Public override that calls URLClassLoader.addURL to add a URL to the search path.

nodes.name: Distribution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Distribution, an in-memory helper that sorts a small sample of doubles and reports quantiles and summary statistics, plus a companion object with a factory returning an Option. Meant for small data sets only.

nodes.name: Distribution
nodes.summary: Sorts a slice of a double array on construction and exposes quantile lookup (getQuantiles), printing of the min/25%/50%/75%/max row, a StatCounter over the slice, and a combined summary printer. nodes.name: getQuantiles
nodes.summary: Returns the data values at the requested probabilities (0 to 1, defaulting to 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) by indexing the sorted array through closestIndex.

nodes.name: closestIndex
nodes.summary: Private helper that maps a probability to an index in the sorted slice, clamped to the last element of the slice.

nodes.name: showQuantiles
nodes.summary: Prints a min/25%/50%/75%/max header and the default quantile values to the given PrintStream. The companion object has an overload (lines 84-90) that prints an arbitrary iterable of quantile values; both share this id.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Prints the StatCounter for the data and then the quantile row to the given PrintStream (System.out by default).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that returns Some(new Distribution(data)) when the input is non-empty and None otherwise.

nodes.name: IdGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines IdGenerator, a thin wrapper around an AtomicInteger that hands out unique increasing ids. The doc comment cites BlockManager naming its RpcEndpoints with it.

nodes.name: IdGenerator
nodes.summary: Holds a private AtomicInteger and exposes next, which increments and returns it, giving thread-safe unique ids per generator instance.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns id.incrementAndGet, the next unique integer for this generator.

nodes.name: IntParam.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the IntParam extractor object that parses a string into an Int for pattern matching.

nodes.name: IntParam
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply returns Some(int) when the string parses and None on NumberFormatException, so it can be used in pattern matches over string arguments.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Tries str.toInt and returns Some of the result, or None when a NumberFormatException is thrown.

nodes.name: KeyLock.scala
nodes.summary: Defines KeyLock, a per-key mutual exclusion helper built on a ConcurrentHashMap, so that only one function body runs at a time for any given key.

nodes.name: KeyLock
nodes.summary: Keeps a ConcurrentHashMap of key to lock object. withLock acquires the key (blocking on the existing lock object while another holder owns the key), runs the function, and releases in a finally block, notifying waiters. Keys must implement equals and hashCode correctly.

nodes.name: LastAttemptAccumulator

nodes.name: setValueIfOnDriverSide

nodes.name: lastAttemptValueForRDDIds

nodes.name: lastAttemptValueForRDDId

nodes.name: lastAttemptValueForAllRDDs

nodes.summary: Visible-for-testing accessor returning how many RDDs have recorded updates.

nodes.name: getValid
nodes.summary: Visible-for-testing accessor returning whether the accumulator has not been invalidated.

nodes.name: removeListenerOnError
nodes.summary: Hook called when a listener is interrupted while handling an event; by default just removes the listener, and subclasses can add cleanup.

nodes.name: ManualClock.scala
