nodes.name: waitTillTime
nodes.summary: Blocks (waiting in 10 ms steps) until the clock time is at least the target, then returns the current time.

nodes.name: MemoryParam.scala

nodes.name: MutablePair.scala

nodes.summary: Handles an incoming signal: temporarily reinstalls the previous handler, runs every registered action, escalates to the previous handler if all return false, then reinstalls itself.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the package object for org.apache.spark.util with only a scaladoc comment ('Spark utilities'); it defines no members.

nodes.name: util
nodes.summary: Empty package object for org.apache.spark.util that exists to carry the package-level documentation comment.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JsonProtocol object that converts SparkListenerEvents and the classes they depend on to and from JSON (the event log format), plus the JsonProtocolOptions helper. By theme: event serialization (lines 77-422), serialization of dependent classes (424-863: stage, task, accumulable, task metrics, executor metrics, task end reason, block manager id, job result, RDD info, storage level, block status, executor info, resource requests), serialization utilities (865-907), event deserialization (910-1193), deserialization of dependent classes (1195-1616), deserialization utilities (1618-1658) and private JSON helpers (1660-1704). Documents the compatibility rules: never delete JSON fields, make new fields optional.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object using the Jackson streaming JsonGenerator for writing and JsonNode tree reads with an implicit class for type-checked field extraction.

nodes.name: JsonProtocolOptions
nodes.summary: Holds configuration for JsonProtocol (whether task metrics accumulators are included, read once from the event log config) so that SparkConf need not be re-parsed on each use.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol
nodes.summary: Singleton that serializes SparkListener events to JSON and reads them back, extending JsonUtils. Writers are named xxxToJson (sparkEventToJsonString is the entry point) and readers xxxFromJson (sparkEventFromJson is the entry point). Small members without their own node: executorResourceRequestToJson, executorResourceRequestMapToJson, taskResourceRequestToJson and taskResourceRequestMapToJson (lines 829-863) with their FromJson counterparts (1074-1086), UUIDToJson (881-886) and UUIDFromJson (1637-1641). The extractElements, extractBoolean, extractInt, extractLong, extractDouble and extractString helpers live in the JsonNodeImplicits class.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.SPARK_LISTENER_EVENT_FORMATTED_CLASS_NAMES
nodes.summary: Private object that holds the formatted class name of each supported SparkListener event, used as the Event field when writing and as match keys when reading.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.TASK_END_REASON_FORMATTED_CLASS_NAMES
nodes.summary: Private object that holds formatted class names of the TaskEndReason variants, used by taskEndReasonFromJson to select a reason.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.JOB_RESULT_FORMATTED_CLASS_NAMES
nodes.summary: Private object that holds formatted class names of JobSucceeded and JobFailed, used by jobResultFromJson.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.JsonNodeImplicits
nodes.summary: Private implicit class adding type-checked extractors (elements, boolean, int, long, double, string) to JsonNode, so parsing fails on unexpected types instead of silently using defaults.

nodes.name: sparkEventToJsonString
nodes.summary: Entry point that serializes a SparkListenerEvent to a JSON string. The one-argument overload (lines 82-84, for tests only) uses default JsonProtocolOptions; the two-argument overload (lines 86-90) wraps writeSparkEventToJson in toJsonString.

nodes.name: writeSparkEventToJson
nodes.summary: Dispatches a SparkListenerEvent to the matching xxxToJson writer by pattern match on the concrete event type (stage, task, job, environment, block manager, application, executor, log start, metrics, block update, resource profile). Unknown event types fall back to the Jackson mapper.

nodes.name: stageSubmittedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerStageSubmitted as a JSON object with the event name, the stage info (without accumulables, per SPARK-42205) and optional properties.

nodes.name: stageCompletedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerStageCompleted as JSON, including the stage info with its accumulables.

nodes.name: taskStartToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerTaskStart as JSON with stage id, stage attempt id and the task info (accumulables omitted per SPARK-42205).

nodes.name: taskGettingResultToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerTaskGettingResult as JSON holding only the task info, without accumulables.

nodes.name: taskEndToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerTaskEnd as JSON: stage ids, task type, end reason, task info with accumulables, executor metrics and, when present, task metrics.

nodes.name: jobStartToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerJobStart as JSON with job id, submission time, stage infos (accumulables deliberately included), stage ids and optional properties.

nodes.name: jobEndToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerJobEnd as JSON with job id, completion time and the serialized job result.

nodes.name: environmentUpdateToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerEnvironmentUpdate as JSON with the JVM, Spark, Hadoop, system and metrics properties and the classpath entries as map fields.

nodes.name: blockManagerAddedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerBlockManagerAdded as JSON with the block manager id, maximum memory, timestamp and optional on-heap and off-heap maximums.

nodes.name: blockManagerRemovedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerBlockManagerRemoved as JSON with the block manager id and timestamp.

nodes.name: unpersistRDDToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerUnpersistRDD as JSON holding the RDD id.

nodes.name: applicationStartToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerApplicationStart as JSON: app name, optional app id, timestamp, user, optional attempt id, driver logs and driver attributes.

nodes.name: applicationEndToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerApplicationEnd as JSON with the timestamp and an optional exit code.

nodes.name: resourceProfileAddedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerResourceProfileAdded as JSON with the profile id and its executor and task resource request maps (written by executorResourceRequestMapToJson at lines 838-847 and taskResourceRequestMapToJson at lines 856-863).

nodes.name: executorAddedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerExecutorAdded as JSON with timestamp, executor id and executor info.

nodes.name: executorRemovedToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerExecutorRemoved as JSON with timestamp, executor id and removal reason.

nodes.name: logStartToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerLogStart as JSON carrying the current SPARK_VERSION.

nodes.name: executorMetricsUpdateToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerExecutorMetricsUpdate as JSON: per-task accumulator updates and per-stage executor metrics for one executor.

nodes.name: stageExecutorMetricsToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerStageExecutorMetrics as JSON with executor id, stage ids and the executor metrics.

nodes.name: blockUpdateToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a SparkListenerBlockUpdated as JSON wrapping the block updated info.

nodes.name: stageInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes a StageInfo (ids, name, task count, RDD infos, parent ids, details, times, failure reason, resource profile id, shuffle push settings and, only when includeAccumulables is true, accumulables; otherwise an empty array).

nodes.name: taskInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes a TaskInfo (ids, launch and finish times, executor, host, locality, speculative, failed and killed flags, optionally accumulables).

nodes.name: accumulablesToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a collection of AccumulableInfo as a JSON array sorted by id, skipping excluded accumulators (updated block statuses, collect-metrics) and optionally the task metric accumulators.

nodes.name: accumulableInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes one AccumulableInfo with id, name, update, value, internal flag, count-failed-values flag and metadata, delegating value encoding to accumValueToJson.

nodes.name: accumValueToJson
nodes.summary: Writes an accumulator value: internal task metric accumulators (name starting with the metrics prefix) are written as numbers or as arrays of block id and status, other accumulators as strings. Must stay consistent with accumValueFromJson.

nodes.name: taskMetricsToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes TaskMetrics into a JSON object with executor times, memory peaks, result sizes, spill bytes and nested objects for shuffle read (including push-based), shuffle write, input, output and updated blocks, using local helper writers.

nodes.name: executorMetricsToJson
nodes.summary: Writes an ExecutorMetrics as a JSON object with one numeric field per metric listed in ExecutorMetricType.metricToOffset.

nodes.name: taskEndReasonToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes a TaskEndReason: writes the formatted class name as Reason, then extra fields for FetchFailed, ExceptionFailure, TaskCommitDenied, ExecutorLostFailure and TaskKilled; other reasons carry no extra fields.

nodes.name: blockManagerIdToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a BlockManagerId as a JSON object with executor id, host and port.

nodes.name: jobResultToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a JobResult: the formatted class name as Result, plus the serialized exception when the result is JobFailed.

nodes.name: rddInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes an RDDInfo (id, name, optional scope JSON, callsite, parent ids, storage level, barrier flag, deterministic level, partition counts and sizes).

nodes.name: storageLevelToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a StorageLevel as a JSON object with use-disk, use-memory, use-off-heap, deserialized and replication fields.

nodes.name: blockStatusToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a BlockStatus as a JSON object with storage level, memory size and disk size.

nodes.name: executorInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Serializes an ExecutorInfo: host, cores, log URLs, attributes, resources (each written as raw JSON taken from ResourceInformation), resource profile id and optional registration and request times.

nodes.name: blockUpdatedInfoToJson
nodes.summary: Writes a BlockUpdatedInfo as JSON with block manager id, block id, storage level and sizes.

nodes.name: writeMapField
nodes.summary: Utility that writes a Map[String,String] as a named JSON object field.

nodes.name: propertiesToJson
nodes.summary: Utility that writes a java.util.Properties object as a JSON object of string fields.

nodes.name: stackTraceToJson
nodes.summary: Utility that writes a stack trace array as a JSON array of objects with declaring class, method name, file name and line number.

nodes.name: exceptionToJson
nodes.summary: Utility that writes an Exception as a JSON object with its message and stack trace.

nodes.name: sparkEventFromJson
nodes.summary: Entry point that parses a SparkListenerEvent from a JSON string (lines 937-939) or a JsonNode (lines 941-974). It switches on the Event field against the formatted class names and calls the matching xxxFromJson reader; an unknown name is loaded as a class and read through the Jackson mapper if it is a SparkListenerEvent, otherwise a SparkException is thrown.

nodes.name: stageSubmittedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerStageSubmitted from JSON (stage info and optional properties).

nodes.name: stageCompletedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerStageCompleted from JSON (stage info).

nodes.name: taskStartFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerTaskStart from JSON; the stage attempt id defaults to 0 when absent.

nodes.name: taskGettingResultFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerTaskGettingResult from JSON (task info only).

nodes.name: executorMetricsFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads an ExecutorMetrics from JSON; metrics missing (for example in logs from very old versions) default to zero.

nodes.name: taskEndFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerTaskEnd from JSON: ids, task type, end reason, task info, executor metrics and task metrics.

nodes.name: jobStartFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerJobStart from JSON; when the Stage Infos field (added in Spark 1.2.0) is absent, placeholder StageInfo objects are built from the stage ids.

nodes.name: jobEndFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerJobEnd from JSON; completion time defaults to -1 when absent.

nodes.name: resourceProfileAddedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerResourceProfileAdded from JSON by rebuilding a ResourceProfile from its executor and task request maps (read by executorResourceRequestMapFromJson at lines 1081-1086 and taskResourceRequestMapFromJson at lines 1074-1079) and setting its id.

nodes.name: executorResourceRequestFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads an ExecutorResourceRequest from JSON (name, amount, discovery script, vendor).

nodes.name: taskResourceRequestFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a TaskResourceRequest from JSON (name and amount).

nodes.name: environmentUpdateFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerEnvironmentUpdate from JSON; the Hadoop and Metrics Properties fields default to empty for older logs.

nodes.name: blockManagerAddedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerBlockManagerAdded from JSON; the timestamp defaults to -1 and the on-heap and off-heap maximums are optional.

nodes.name: blockManagerRemovedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerBlockManagerRemoved from JSON; the timestamp defaults to -1.

nodes.name: unpersistRDDFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerUnpersistRDD from JSON.

nodes.name: applicationStartFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerApplicationStart from JSON with optional app id, attempt id, driver logs and driver attributes.

nodes.name: applicationEndFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerApplicationEnd from JSON with an optional exit code.

nodes.name: executorAddedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerExecutorAdded from JSON (time, executor id, executor info).

nodes.name: executorRemovedFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerExecutorRemoved from JSON (time, executor id, reason).

nodes.name: logStartFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerLogStart (the Spark version) from JSON.

nodes.name: executorMetricsUpdateFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerExecutorMetricsUpdate from JSON: task accumulator updates plus an optional map of per-stage executor metrics.

nodes.name: stageExecutorMetricsFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerStageExecutorMetrics from JSON.

nodes.name: blockUpdateFromJson
nodes.summary: Reads a SparkListenerBlockUpdated from JSON.

nodes.name: stageInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a StageInfo from JSON, defaulting fields added in later versions (attempt id, parent ids, details, shuffle push settings, resource profile id) and restoring times, failure reason and accumulables.

nodes.name: taskInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a TaskInfo from JSON with defaults for older logs (attempt, partition id, speculative, killed) and restores timing, failure flags and accumulables.

nodes.name: accumulableInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an AccumulableInfo from JSON, decoding update and value with accumValueFromJson.

nodes.name: accumValueFromJson
nodes.summary: Decodes an accumulator value: metrics-prefixed accumulators come back as longs or as a java list of (BlockId, BlockStatus) pairs, others as strings. Mirrors accumValueToJson.

nodes.name: taskMetricsFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds TaskMetrics from JSON, tolerating missing or older fields: scalar timings and sizes, shuffle read (including push-based), shuffle write, output, input and updated block statuses. Returns empty metrics for null JSON.

nodes.name: taskEndReasonFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a TaskEndReason by matching the Reason field against formatted class names (Success, Resubmitted, FetchFailed, ExceptionFailure, TaskResultLost, TaskKilled, TaskCommitDenied, ExecutorLostFailure, UnknownReason), supplying defaults for fields missing in older logs.

nodes.name: blockManagerIdFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a BlockManagerId from JSON, returning null for null JSON and interning executor id and host.

nodes.name: jobResultFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a JobResult (JobSucceeded or JobFailed with an exception) from the Result field.

nodes.name: rddInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an RDDInfo from JSON with defaults for fields added later (barrier flag, deterministic level, callsite, parent ids).

nodes.name: storageLevelFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a StorageLevel from JSON; the Use Off Heap field defaults to false for older logs.

nodes.name: blockStatusFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a BlockStatus from JSON (storage level, memory and disk sizes).

nodes.name: executorInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an ExecutorInfo from JSON, defaulting fields added later (attributes, resources, resource profile id, registration and request time).

nodes.name: blockUpdatedInfoFromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a BlockUpdatedInfo from JSON.

nodes.name: resourcesMapFromJson
nodes.summary: Parses the Resources JSON object into a map of ResourceInformation, asserting that the node is an object.

nodes.name: mapFromJson
nodes.summary: Utility that reads a JSON object into a Map[String,String].

nodes.name: propertiesFromJson
nodes.summary: Utility that reads optional JSON into a Properties object, or null when absent.

nodes.name: stackTraceFromJson
nodes.summary: Utility that reads a JSON array into an Array[StackTraceElement], empty when absent.

nodes.name: exceptionFromJson
nodes.summary: Utility that rebuilds an Exception with its message and stack trace from JSON.

nodes.name: jsonOption
nodes.summary: Private helper that turns null or NullNode into None so optional fields can be read with defaults.

nodes.name: SizeEstimator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SizeEstimator object, which estimates how many bytes of JVM heap a Java object and everything it references occupy, and the KnownSizeEstimation trait that lets a class report its own size. Used for memory-aware caches, for example to size deserialized cached data or broadcast variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object with a mutable initialization phase that detects 64-bit, compressed-oops and compact-object-header settings, then walks object graphs with an explicit stack and reflection.

nodes.name: KnownSizeEstimation
nodes.summary: Trait with a single estimatedSize member. When an object extends it, SizeEstimator uses the returned value as that object's size instead of walking its fields.

nodes.name: SizeEstimator
nodes.summary: Singleton that estimates the heap size of an object graph. It caches per-class field layout information, samples large arrays instead of visiting every element, and adapts object and pointer sizes to the detected JVM settings. Extends Logging.

nodes.name: SearchState
nodes.summary: Private helper holding the state of one estimation run: a stack of objects still to visit, an identity map of visited objects and the running size total.

nodes.name: ClassInfo
nodes.summary: Private cache entry for one class: its shell size (non-static fields plus Object size) and the list of pointer fields to follow.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Runs one estimation: enqueues the root object and visits objects from the stack until none remain, returning the accumulated size. A public overload at line 67 creates a fresh IdentityHashMap and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Sets the 64-bit flag, compressed-oops and compact-object-header flags, the object size and pointer size from the JVM, then resets the class info cache with an entry for Object.

nodes.name: getIsCompactObjectHeaders
nodes.summary: Decides whether compact object headers are in use: a test system property override first, then false for JVMs older than version 24, otherwise the UseCompactObjectHeaders VM option.

nodes.name: getIsCompressedOops
nodes.summary: Decides whether compressed object pointers are in use: a test property override, the vendor VM info for IBM and OpenJ9, then the UseCompressedOops VM option, falling back to a guess from max heap below 32 GB with a warning.

nodes.name: visitSingleObject
nodes.summary: Adds the size of one object: arrays go to visitArray, scala.reflect objects, class loaders and Class objects are ignored, KnownSizeEstimation objects use their own estimate, and other objects use cached class info and enqueue their pointer fields.

nodes.name: visitArray
nodes.summary: Adds the size of an array. Primitive arrays are computed from length, small object arrays have every element enqueued, and arrays longer than 400 elements are estimated by sampling twice and extrapolating from the smaller sample.

nodes.name: sampleArray
nodes.summary: Draws 100 distinct random indices from an array and sums the estimated sizes of the non-null elements, sharing the visited map with the outer run.

nodes.name: primitiveSize
nodes.summary: Returns the byte size of a primitive class, and throws IllegalArgumentException for a non-primitive class.

nodes.name: getClassInfo
nodes.summary: Gets or computes the ClassInfo of a class. It starts from the superclass layout, counts declared non-static fields by size, simulates field placement and alignment, records accessible pointer fields and caches the result.

nodes.name: alignSize
nodes.summary: Rounds a size up to the 8-byte object alignment boundary.

nodes.name: alignSizeUp
nodes.summary: Rounds a size up to the next multiple of a power-of-two alignment using bit masking. The result is wrong if the alignment is not a power of two.

nodes.name: enqueue
nodes.summary: Marks a non-null, not yet visited object as visited and pushes it on the stack.

nodes.name: isFinished
nodes.summary: Returns true when the stack of objects to visit is empty.

nodes.name: dequeue
nodes.summary: Pops and returns the last object on the stack.

nodes.name: SparkClosureCleaner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SparkClosureCleaner object, a Spark-specific wrapper around ClosureCleaner that also checks the cleaned closure can be serialized with the closure serializer. Used to make a closure serializable before it is shipped.

nodes.name: SparkClosureCleaner
nodes.summary: Private[spark] singleton exposing clean, which cleans a closure and optionally verifies it by serializing it with the closure serializer of the current SparkEnv.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Cleans a closure in place through ClosureCleaner, then, when checkSerializable is set and a SparkEnv exists, serializes the result and throws SparkException with the message 'Task not serializable' on failure. Returns the cleaned closure, or the original if nothing was cleaned.

nodes.name: SparkExitCode.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SparkExitCode object holding named integer process exit codes such as success, failure, uncaught exception, out of memory, class not found and driver timeout. Used by Spark processes when they terminate.

nodes.name: SparkExitCode
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object of exit code constants: EXIT_SUCCESS 0, EXIT_FAILURE 1, ERROR_MISUSE_SHELL_BUILTIN 2, ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND 3, EXCEED_MAX_EXECUTOR_FAILURES 11, UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION 50, UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_TWICE 51, OOM 52, CLASS_NOT_FOUND 101, DRIVER_TIMEOUT 124 and ERROR_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND 127.

nodes.name: SparkUncaughtExceptionHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkUncaughtExceptionHandler, the default uncaught exception handler for Spark daemons. It logs the exception and terminates the process with an exit code that depends on the kind of error.

nodes.name: SparkUncaughtExceptionHandler
nodes.summary: Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler that exits the process for any Error and, when exitOnUncaughtException is true, for any Exception. It searches the cause chain up to the configured depth for OutOfMemoryError or KilledByTaskReaperException, and halts the runtime if logging itself fails. Extends Logging.

nodes.name: uncaughtException
nodes.summary: Logs the uncaught exception (marking it when the container is shutting down) and, if not in shutdown, walks the cause chain to exit with the OOM or task reaper code, else with UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION when enabled. On an error while handling it halts the runtime with OOM or UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_TWICE. A one-argument overload at line 116 delegates here using the current thread.

nodes.name: StatCounter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StatCounter, a serializable accumulator of count, mean, variance, max and min for a stream of doubles, with support for merging two counters. Used to compute summary statistics in a single pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object; uses Welford and Chan style running-variance updates and several overloaded merge methods.

nodes.name: StatCounter
nodes.summary: Serializable class tracking count, mean, variance numerator, max and min of doubles in a numerically robust way, built from an initial collection of values. The companion object (lines 156-162) offers apply factories from an IterableOnce or varargs.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another StatCounter into this one, combining count, mean, variance numerator, max and min with a weighted formula that favors numerical stability. If merging with itself it merges a copy. Overloads at lines 43-51 (single value) and 54-57 (collection of values) update one value at a time.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Returns a new StatCounter holding the same internal statistics.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of values seen.

nodes.name: mean
nodes.summary: Returns the running mean.

nodes.name: sum
nodes.summary: Returns the sum, computed as count times mean.

nodes.name: max
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum value seen.

nodes.name: min
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum value seen.

nodes.name: variance
nodes.summary: Returns the population variance by delegating to popVariance.

nodes.name: popVariance
nodes.summary: Returns the population variance (second moment divided by count), or NaN when there are no values.

nodes.name: sampleVariance
nodes.summary: Returns the sample variance (divided by n minus 1), or NaN when there are fewer than two values.

nodes.name: stdev
nodes.summary: Returns the population standard deviation by delegating to popStdev.

nodes.name: popStdev
nodes.summary: Returns the square root of the population variance.

nodes.name: sampleStdev
nodes.summary: Returns the square root of the sample variance.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Formats count, mean, stdev, max and min as a string.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a StatCounter from variable-length double arguments. An overload at line 158 takes an IterableOnce of doubles.

nodes.name: StubClassLoader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StubClassLoader and its companion, a ClassLoader that generates empty stub classes for missing classes selected by a predicate. Used so lambdas whose capturing class refers to unknown but unneeded classes can still be loaded.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class and companion object; generates class bytes through the ASM ClassWriter API.

nodes.name: StubClassLoader
nodes.summary: ClassLoader subclass (extends Logging) whose findClass defines a generated stub when the class name is accepted by shouldStub, and throws ClassNotFoundException otherwise. The companion object (lines 43-96) builds an instance from name prefixes and generates the stub bytecode.

nodes.name: findClass
nodes.summary: Throws ClassNotFoundException unless the name should be stubbed; otherwise generates stub bytes and defines the class.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a StubClassLoader which stubs any class whose name starts with one of the given prefixes.

nodes.name: generateStub
nodes.summary: Generates bytecode for an empty public class with the given name whose constructor calls Object's constructor and then throws ClassNotFoundException saying the class is stubbed and the artifact must be added by calling session.addArtifact.

nodes.name: ThreadUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ThreadUtils object: helpers that create named daemon thread pools, scheduled executors and a ForkJoinPool, run code in a new thread with an adjusted stack trace, await futures with exception wrapping, shut executors down, and run a function over a collection in parallel (parmap).

nodes.name: ThreadUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton holding thread and executor helper methods. It builds thread factories and pools with daemon, named threads, wraps Await-style calls so errors are rethrown as SparkException, and offers parmap for interruptible parallel mapping.

nodes.name: sameThreadExecutorService
nodes.summary: Builds an ExecutorService (an AbstractExecutorService subclass) that runs each submitted command in the calling thread. It tracks running tasks and shutdown state under a ReentrantLock, rejects execute after shutdown, and supports awaitTermination. Used to create the shared sameThread execution context.

nodes.name: namedThreadFactory
nodes.summary: Creates a ThreadFactory that gives threads a prefix-based name and marks them as daemon.

nodes.name: newDaemonCachedThreadPool
nodes.summary: Creates a cached thread pool of daemon threads named by a prefix. The overload with maxThreadNumber (lines 139-151, chosen as widest) builds a ThreadPoolExecutor with a LinkedBlockingQueue, a keep-alive time and core thread timeout; the one-argument overload (lines 130-133) wraps Executors.newCachedThreadPool.

nodes.name: newDaemonFixedThreadPool
nodes.summary: Creates a fixed-size thread pool whose threads are daemon threads named with a prefix.

nodes.name: newDaemonSingleThreadExecutor
nodes.summary: Creates a single-thread fixed pool with one daemon thread using the given thread name format.

nodes.name: newDaemonSingleThreadExecutorWithRejectedExecutionHandler
nodes.summary: Creates a single daemon thread ThreadPoolExecutor backed by an ArrayBlockingQueue of the given capacity and a caller-supplied RejectedExecutionHandler.

nodes.name: newDaemonBlockingThreadPoolExecutorService
nodes.summary: Creates a BlockingThreadPoolExecutorService with a bounded work queue, so task submission blocks when the queue is full, using a named daemon thread factory.

nodes.name: newDaemonSingleThreadScheduledExecutor
nodes.summary: Creates a one-thread ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with daemon threads and enables removal of cancelled tasks from the queue.

nodes.name: newSingleThreadScheduledExecutor
nodes.summary: Creates a one-thread ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with non-daemon threads and enables removal of cancelled tasks from the queue.

nodes.name: newDaemonThreadPoolScheduledExecutor
nodes.summary: Creates a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with a given number of daemon threads named with a prefix, and enables removal of cancelled tasks from the queue.

nodes.name: runInNewThread
nodes.summary: Runs a block of code in a new thread, joins it and returns the result. If the body threw a non-fatal exception, it is rethrown in the caller thread with an adjusted stack trace produced by wrapCallerStacktrace.

nodes.name: wrapCallerStacktrace
nodes.summary: Combines the stack trace of an exception thrown in another thread with the caller thread's stack trace, separated by a placeholder element, and returns the same exception. Used so that rethrown exceptions show both where they occurred and who called.

nodes.name: newForkJoinPool
nodes.summary: Creates a ForkJoinPool with a given max parallelism whose worker threads are named with a prefix through a custom worker thread factory.

nodes.name: awaitResult
nodes.summary: Preferred alternative to Await.result. There are four overloads: two for Awaitable (lines 358-368) that delegate to SparkThreadUtils.awaitResult, and two for java.util.concurrent.Future (lines 372-403, widest range chosen here). The Future version calls get (with a timeout unless the duration is infinite), unwraps SparkFatalException, optionally rethrows a cause that carries a SparkThrowable condition, and wraps other non-timeout errors in a SparkException.

nodes.name: awaitReady
nodes.summary: Preferred alternative to Await.ready. Calls ready on the awaitable and wraps non-fatal, non-timeout exceptions in a SparkException.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down an ExecutorService, waits for the grace period (default 30 seconds) for termination and then forces shutdownNow if the executor is still not shut down.

nodes.name: parmap
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each element of a sequence in parallel on a freshly created ForkJoinPool and returns the results, awaiting a combined future. Unlike parallel collections it can be interrupted. A three-argument overload (lines 437-439) delegates here with preserveSparkThrowable set to false.

nodes.name: UninterruptibleThread.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UninterruptibleThread, a Thread subclass that can run a block of code without being interrupted; interrupts that arrive meanwhile are deferred until the block returns.

nodes.name: UninterruptibleThread
nodes.summary: A Thread with runUninterruptibly, which runs code without Thread.interrupt() setting the interrupted status; the interrupt is deferred until runUninterruptibly returns. runUninterruptibly must be called only from this thread. An inner UninterruptibleLock coordinates the state flags.

nodes.name: UninterruptibleLock
nodes.summary: Private inner monitor class holding the uninterruptible, shouldInterruptThread and awaitInterruptThread flags. Its synchronized methods coordinate runUninterruptibly and interrupt so that a pending interrupt is recorded and replayed after the uninterruptible zone ends.

nodes.name: getAndSetUninterruptible
nodes.summary: Sets the uninterruptible flag to the given value and returns the previous value.

nodes.name: isInterruptPending
nodes.summary: Clears any set interrupted status into the shouldInterruptThread flag and reports whether an interrupt call is still awaited (awaitInterruptThread set and no interrupt seen yet).

nodes.name: recoverInterrupt
nodes.summary: Resets the uninterruptible flag to false and, if an interrupt was deferred, calls the real Thread.interrupt to restore the interrupted status.

nodes.name: isInterruptible
nodes.summary: Decides whether it is safe to interrupt the thread now. Returns true, and marks awaitInterruptThread, only when the thread is not in an uninterruptible zone and no other interrupt is in flight; otherwise the interrupt is deferred.

nodes.name: runUninterruptibly
nodes.summary: Runs the given by-name block in this thread without allowing interrupts. It checks it is called from the owning thread, runs directly if already in an uninterruptible zone, otherwise waits for any in-flight interrupt, runs the block, and recovers a deferred interrupt in a finally.

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Overrides Thread.interrupt: it calls the real interrupt only when the lock says the thread is currently interruptible, then clears the awaitInterruptThread flag; otherwise the interrupt is deferred.

nodes.name: UninterruptibleThreadRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UninterruptibleThreadRunner, which runs code on a dedicated single UninterruptibleThread executor unless the caller is already such a thread.

nodes.name: UninterruptibleThreadRunner
nodes.summary: Owns a single-thread executor whose thread is an UninterruptibleThread (daemon). runUninterruptibly runs the body directly if the current thread is already an UninterruptibleThread, otherwise submits it as a Future and awaits the result with ThreadUtils.awaitResult. The source cites Kafka consumer usage as an example.

nodes.name: runUninterruptibly
nodes.summary: Runs the body directly when already inside an UninterruptibleThread, otherwise runs it on the runner's executor and blocks for the result.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down the underlying single-thread executor.

nodes.name: taskListeners.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the task listener traits (completion, failure, interrupt) and the TaskCompletionListenerException used to report errors from completion callbacks.

nodes.name: TaskCompletionListener
nodes.summary: Developer API trait for a listener with onTaskCompletion(context), invoked when a task's execution completes.

nodes.name: TaskFailureListener
nodes.summary: Developer API trait for a listener with onTaskFailure(context, error), invoked when a task's execution hits an error. Implementations must be idempotent because the callback can run multiple times.

nodes.name: TaskInterruptListener
nodes.summary: Developer API trait for a listener with onTaskInterrupted(context, reason), invoked when a task's execution is interrupted.

nodes.name: TaskCompletionListenerException
nodes.summary: RuntimeException thrown when a TaskCompletionListener callback fails. It holds the listener error messages and an optional previous task error, and getMessage combines them with the previous exception's message and stack trace.

nodes.name: getMessage
nodes.summary: Builds the message: a single listener error message as is, or numbered messages for several, followed by the previous task exception's message and stack trace when present.

nodes.name: RadixSort.java
nodes.summary: Implements least-significant-digit radix sort over long arrays held in off-heap or on-heap memory, with variants for plain long arrays and for key-prefix arrays (pairs of longs sorted on the second).

nodes.name: RadixSort
nodes.summary: Public class of static methods that sort long data in a LongArray using LSD radix sort, supporting ascending/descending and signed/unsigned order and a byte range. Both sort entry points return the start index of the sorted data, since results may end up in the second half of the array.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Sorts numRecords longs in a LongArray by the byte range [startByteIndex, endByteIndex] with radix sort. It needs free space equal to the record count, ping-pongs between the two halves via sortAtByte for each byte that varies, and returns the start index of the sorted data.

nodes.name: sortAtByte
nodes.summary: Does one counting-sort pass for a byte position: converts counts to output offsets and copies each long into its bucket's destination.

nodes.name: getCounts
nodes.summary: Computes a 256-bucket histogram for each byte index in range, skipping byte positions where all values are identical (found by a bitwise min/max pre-pass); skipped positions are left null.

nodes.name: transformCountsToOffsets
nodes.summary: Converts byte-value counts in place into output memory offsets for the chosen order (ascending or descending, signed ordering puts negatives first) and record size.

nodes.name: sortKeyPrefixArray
nodes.summary: Key-prefix variant of sort: each record is two longs, only the second is sorted on, and sorting starts from a startIndex. Uses getKeyPrefixArrayCounts and sortKeyPrefixArrayAtByte per varying byte and returns the start index of the result.

nodes.name: getKeyPrefixArrayCounts
nodes.summary: Key-prefix specialization of getCounts: builds byte histograms over the second long of each 16-byte record, skipping bytes that do not vary.

nodes.name: sortKeyPrefixArrayAtByte
nodes.summary: Key-prefix specialization of sortAtByte: moves each (key, prefix) pair of longs to its bucket destination based on one byte of the prefix.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillReader.java
nodes.summary: Defines UnsafeSorterSpillReader, an iterator that reads back the sorted records of one spill file written by UnsafeSorterSpillWriter, one record at a time, and closes the file after the last record.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class in the Scala-based core module that reaches Scala config entries through package$.MODULE$.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillReader
nodes.summary: Final class that extends UnsafeSorterIterator and implements Closeable. It opens a spill file through a buffered file stream, optionally with read-ahead, wraps it with the serializer manager and, per loadNext call, reads the record length, key prefix and record bytes into a reusable byte array. It closes the stream when the last record has been read and registers a task completion listener to close it too.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillReader
nodes.summary: Constructor: opens the spill file with NioBufferedFileInputStream (buffer size from config or its default), wraps it with ReadAheadInputStream when read-ahead is enabled and the stream from SerializerManager.wrapStream, reads the record count from the first int, and registers a task completion listener that closes the reader.

nodes.name: getNumRecords
nodes.summary: Returns the total number of records stored in the spill file, read from the file header.

nodes.name: getCurrentPageNumber
nodes.summary: Always throws UnsupportedOperationException, because spill-file records do not live in a memory page.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns true while records remain to be read from the spill file.

nodes.name: loadNext
nodes.summary: Advances to the next record: kills the task if it was interrupted, reads the record length and key prefix, grows the buffer if the record is larger, reads the record bytes, and closes the reader once the last record has been consumed.

nodes.name: getBaseObject
nodes.summary: Returns the byte array that holds the current record data.

nodes.name: getBaseOffset
nodes.summary: Returns the byte array base offset of the Platform class, the offset at which the current record starts in the buffer.

nodes.name: getRecordLength
nodes.summary: Returns the length in bytes of the current record.

nodes.name: getKeyPrefix
nodes.summary: Returns the sort key prefix of the current record.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying input stream (if still open) and nulls the stream references; safe to call more than once.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillWriter.java
nodes.summary: Defines UnsafeSorterSpillWriter, which spills a list of already sorted records to a temporary local block file in the format [record count][len][key prefix][data]..., and hands out an UnsafeSorterSpillReader to read that file back.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class that copies record bytes out of managed memory through Platform.copyMemory into a reusable byte buffer before writing.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillWriter
nodes.summary: Final class that creates a temp local block file through the block manager, writes a header with the expected record count, and then writes each record as its length, key prefix and bytes, staging the bytes through a byte buffer of the configured disk write buffer size. It throws if more records are written than announced, and produces an UnsafeSorterSpillReader for the file via getReader.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillWriter
nodes.summary: Constructor: creates a temp local block and file with the disk block manager, obtains a DiskBlockObjectWriter with a dummy serializer instance, and writes the record count as the 4-byte file header.

nodes.name: writeLongToBuffer
nodes.summary: Writes a long into the write buffer at a given offset as 8 big-endian bytes, mirroring DataOutputStream.writeLong.

nodes.name: writeIntToBuffer
nodes.summary: Writes an int into the write buffer at a given offset as 4 big-endian bytes, mirroring DataOutputStream.writeInt.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one record to the spill file: puts the length and key prefix into the buffer, copies the record bytes from the base object and offset into the buffer in chunks that fit its free space, flushes each chunk to the disk writer, and calls recordWritten. Throws IllegalStateException if more records than announced are written.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Commits and closes the disk writer and releases the writer and write buffer references.

nodes.name: getFile
nodes.summary: Returns the spill file this writer writes to.

nodes.name: getReader
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeSorterSpillReader for the spill file using the given serializer manager and the block id of the file.

nodes.name: recordsSpilled
nodes.summary: Returns how many records have been written to the spill file so far.

nodes.name: BitSet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BitSet, a simple fixed-size bit set backed by an array of longs, with set algebra (and, or, xor, and-not, union, intersects), bit iteration and counting, and no bounds checking for speed.

nodes.name: BitSet
nodes.summary: Serializable fixed-size bit set (created with a bit count) that stores bits in an Array[Long]. It supports set, unset, get, range set and clear, nextSetBit based iteration, cardinality, and bit-wise operations that return new sets, and its equals and hashCode are based on the word array. The class skips safety and bound checks to be fast.

nodes.name: capacity
nodes.summary: Returns the number of bits the set can represent (number of words times 64).

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Clears all set bits by filling the word array with zeros.

nodes.name: setUntil
nodes.summary: Sets all bits below a given index: fills whole words with ones and applies a mask to the last partial word.

nodes.name: clearUntil
nodes.summary: Clears all bits below a given index: zeroes whole words and masks the last partial word.
Returns a new BitSet holding the bit-wise AND of this set and another, sized to the larger capacity.
Returns a new BitSet holding the bit-wise OR of this set and another, copying the leftover words of the longer set.
Returns a new BitSet holding the symmetric difference (bit-wise XOR) of this set and another.

nodes.name: andNot
nodes.summary: Returns a new BitSet holding the bits that are in this set but not in the other (AND-NOT).

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets the bit at the given index to true using word index and mask arithmetic.

nodes.name: unset
nodes.summary: Clears the bit at the given index.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns whether the bit at the given index is set.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an Iterator[Int] over the indices of set bits, driven by nextSetBit.

nodes.name: cardinality
nodes.summary: Counts the number of bits set to true by summing the bit count of each word.

nodes.name: nextSetBit
nodes.summary: Returns the index of the first set bit at or after a start index, or -1 if there is none; checks the current word first and then scans the following words.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: In-place union: ORs another BitSet into this one, requiring this set to have no more words than the other.

nodes.name: intersects
nodes.summary: Returns true if the intersection with another BitSet of the same word count is non-empty.

nodes.name: bit2words
nodes.summary: Private helper that computes how many longs are needed to hold a given number of bits.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Equality override: two BitSets are equal when their word arrays are equal.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Hash code override computed from the word array.

nodes.name: ImmutableBitSet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ImmutableBitSet, a BitSet subclass whose bits are set once in the constructor and whose mutating methods throw, plus a private ErrorMessage object holding the error text.

nodes.name: ErrorMessage
nodes.summary: Private object holding the constant message 'mutable operation is not supported' that ImmutableBitSet uses when a mutating method is called.

nodes.name: ImmutableBitSet
nodes.summary: BitSet subclass built from a bit count and a list of bit indices; the constructor sets those bits through the parent set method. It overrides clear, clearUntil, set, setUntil, unset and union to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the set cannot change after construction.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: clearUntil
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: setUntil
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: unset
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Override that always throws UnsupportedOperationException with the shared error message, blocking mutation of the immutable set.

nodes.name: CompactBuffer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CompactBuffer, an append-only Seq that keeps up to two elements in fields and only allocates an array for more, plus its companion object with apply factories; it saves memory for small groups such as in groupBy.

nodes.name: CompactBuffer
nodes.summary: Spark-private append-only buffer that extends Seq and Serializable. The first two elements live in fields, the rest in an Array that doubles in size up to a maximum, avoiding the overhead of ArrayBuffer for small buffers. The companion object (lines 154-161) provides apply() for an empty buffer and apply(value) for a single-element buffer; ++= has a fast path when merging another CompactBuffer.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one id; the companion apply overloads (lines 155 and 157-160) are not separate nodes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the element at a position (fields for 0 and 1, array otherwise) and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException when out of range. The companion object's apply() and apply(value) factory overloads share this node id.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Private method that replaces the element at a position, with the same bounds check as apply.
Appends one value: stores it in a field for the first two elements, otherwise grows the backing array and stores it there; returns the buffer.

Appends all values of another collection; when the argument is a CompactBuffer it grows once and copies fields and array directly (used for cogroup and groupByKey merging), otherwise it appends each element.

nodes.name: length
nodes.summary: Returns the current number of elements.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the elements by position, throwing NoSuchElementException when exhausted.

nodes.name: growToSize
nodes.summary: Private method that sets the size and enlarges the backing array (start 8, doubling, capped at the maximum rounded array length); throws UnsupportedOperationException if the buffer would exceed that maximum.

nodes.name: ExternalAppendOnlyMap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExternalAppendOnlyMap, an append-only map that merges values into combiners and spills sorted contents to temporary disk files when memory is insufficient, then reads the spills back with a hash-ordered sort-merge. Also holds its private nested iterator classes and a companion object with a hash helper and a hash-based key comparator.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with private inner classes that close over the enclosing map's type parameters K, V and C, plus a companion object holding the hash helpers.

nodes.name: ExternalAppendOnlyMap
nodes.summary: Developer API append-only map from keys K to combiners C, built from createCombiner, mergeValue and mergeCombiners functions. It holds a size-tracking in-memory map, spills it sorted by key hash to temp files through the disk block manager when the Spillable memory check says so (or when forced), and exposes a destructive iterator that sort-merges the in-memory data with all spills. The companion object (lines 614-633) provides the hash helper and the HashComparator; the secondary constructor at lines 75-82 keeps binary compatibility.

nodes.name: ExternalIterator
nodes.summary: Private iterator created by iterator when at least one spill exists. It builds a priority queue of StreamBuffers, one per input stream (the sorted in-memory data plus every spilled map), and on each next call takes the lowest key hash, merges the combiners of equal keys across streams with mergeCombiners, and refills the buffers.

nodes.name: StreamBuffer
nodes.summary: Private class holding a buffered stream iterator and the pairs that currently share the lowest key hash in that stream. It is Comparable by minimum key hash, in descending order so the max-oriented priority queue yields the smallest hash first.

nodes.name: DiskMapIterator
nodes.summary: Private iterator that reads (K, C) pairs back from one spill file. It splits the file by the recorded batch sizes, opens a deserialization stream limited to one batch at a time through the serializer manager, and deletes the file on exhaustion or at task completion.

nodes.name: SpillableIterator
nodes.summary: Private iterator wrapping an upstream iterator so the map can force-spill the remaining in-memory data to disk while a reader is consuming it. spill swaps the upstream for a disk iterator under a lock, and toCompletionIterator frees the map when iteration finishes.

nodes.name: HashComparator
nodes.summary: Private comparator in the companion object that orders arbitrary keys by their hash code, using the null-safe hash helper. The map sorts in-memory data with it before spilling.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a single key and value by wrapping them in a one-element iterator and calling insertAll.

nodes.name: insertAll
nodes.summary: Inserts every entry of an iterator: it tracks the peak estimated size, asks maybeSpill whether to spill, replaces the in-memory map after a spill, and merges each value with createCombiner or mergeValue via changeValue. It fails if the map was already iterated. An Iterable overload (lines 179-181) delegates to this one and shares this id.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Override of the Spillable hook that sorts the current in-memory map by key hash with a destructive sorted iterator and spills it to a new disk map iterator kept in the spilled-maps buffer.

nodes.name: forceSpill
nodes.summary: Override called when the task memory manager needs memory back. It spills through the active reading iterator if one exists (clearing the in-memory map on success), otherwise spills a non-empty current map and replaces it, and returns whether anything was spilled.

nodes.name: spillMemoryIteratorToDisk
nodes.summary: Writes the pairs of an in-memory iterator to a temp local block file in serializer-sized batches using a disk writer, tracking batch sizes and bytes spilled, and reverting or deleting the file on failure. Returns a DiskMapIterator over the new file.

nodes.name: destructiveIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps an in-memory iterator in a SpillableIterator, remembers it as the reading iterator so forceSpill can reach it, and returns it as a completion iterator.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Override of Iterable.iterator. It throws if the map was already consumed, returns the destructive in-memory iterator when nothing spilled, and otherwise returns a new ExternalIterator that merges memory and spills.

nodes.name: freeCurrentMap
nodes.summary: Private method that drops the reference to the in-memory map so it can be garbage collected and calls releaseMemory.

nodes.name: hashKey
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns the hash of the key of a (K, C) pair through the companion object's hash.

nodes.name: readNextHashCode
nodes.summary: Fills a buffer with the next run of pairs from a buffered iterator that share the same key hash, so streams are consumed one hash code at a time.

nodes.name: mergeIfKeyExists
nodes.summary: Scans a StreamBuffer for the given key, removes that pair if found and returns the base combiner merged with it through mergeCombiners; otherwise returns the base combiner unchanged.

nodes.name: removeFromBuffer
nodes.summary: Removes an element from an ArrayBuffer in constant time by moving the last element into its slot and dropping the tail, which is valid because buffer order does not matter.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Dequeues the buffer with the lowest key hash, takes one pair, merges in matching keys from other buffers with the same minimum hash, then refills and re-enqueues the visited buffers. Throws NoSuchElementException when the heap is empty.

nodes.name: minKeyHash
nodes.summary: Returns the key hash of the first pair in the buffer, asserting that the buffer is not empty.

nodes.name: compareTo
nodes.summary: Compares buffers by minimum key hash in descending order, because the mutable priority queue dequeues the maximum.

nodes.name: nextBatchIterator
nodes.summary: Closes the previous batch streams, then opens the spill file at the next batch offset, limits the stream to that batch, wraps it with the serializer manager and returns a key-value iterator over it. When no batches remain it calls cleanup and returns null.

nodes.name: readNextItem
nodes.summary: Returns the next pair from the current batch iterator and moves to the next batch once serializerBatchSize objects have been read.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Initializes the batch iterator lazily on first use and reports whether the current batch iterator has more elements.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next pair via readNextItem, throwing NoSuchElementException if hasNext is false.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Marks all batches as consumed, closes the deserialization and file streams and deletes the spill file, logging a warning if the delete fails. It is also registered as a task completion listener.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Under a lock, spills the remaining upstream elements to disk once (logging the task attempt and memory released), asserts the old upstream is drained and switches upstream to the disk iterator. Returns false if it already spilled.

nodes.name: destroy
nodes.summary: Frees the in-memory map and replaces the upstream with an empty iterator.

nodes.name: toCompletionIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps this iterator in a CompletionIterator that runs destroy when iteration completes.

nodes.name: readNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next upstream element under the spill lock, or returns null when the upstream is exhausted.

nodes.name: hash
nodes.summary: Companion object helper returning 0 for null and the object's hashCode otherwise.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares two keys by their null-safe hash codes and returns -1, 0 or 1.

nodes.name: TimSort.java
nodes.summary: Java port of the Android TimSort (a stable, adaptive, iterative mergesort) generalized to sort through a SortDataFormat instead of a plain array, so buffers such as alternating key/value arrays can be sorted. The class is package private and is meant to be used through the Scala Sorter wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Kept in Java with the original Android style so it stays easy to compare against the source it was ported from. Uses a generic key type K and an opaque Buffer type accessed only through the SortDataFormat.

nodes.name: TimSort
nodes.summary: Generic stable sort over a Buffer of keys of type K, read and moved through a SortDataFormat. sort() uses binary insertion sort for short ranges, otherwise finds natural runs, extends short runs to a minimum length and merges them on a stack of pending runs. Used when a collection sorts data that is not a simple per-element array.

nodes.name: SortState
nodes.summary: Inner class that holds the state of one ongoing TimSort: the buffer, comparator, temporary merge storage, the minGallop threshold and the stack of pending runs. It implements run merging (mergeCollapse, mergeAt, mergeLo, mergeHi) and the galloping binary searches.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Entry point of the sort over the range [lo, hi). Returns immediately for fewer than 2 elements, uses countRunAndMakeAscending plus binarySort for ranges below MIN_MERGE, and otherwise loops over natural runs, extends short ones with binarySort, pushes them on a SortState and merges via mergeCollapse, finishing with mergeForceCollapse.

nodes.name: binarySort
nodes.summary: Sorts a range with binary insertion sort, assuming the part before start is already sorted. It copies each pivot element aside, finds its position by binary search after any equal elements (keeping stability) and shifts elements using SortDataFormat copy operations.

nodes.name: countRunAndMakeAscending
nodes.summary: Returns the length of the run starting at lo and reverses it in place if it is strictly descending, so the run is ascending on return. Used by sort() to find natural runs.

nodes.name: reverseRange
nodes.summary: Reverses the elements in [lo, hi) of the buffer by swapping pairs through the SortDataFormat.

nodes.name: minRunLength
nodes.summary: Computes the minimum acceptable run length for an array of length n, based on MIN_MERGE. Natural runs shorter than this are extended with binarySort.

nodes.name: SortState
nodes.summary: Constructor of SortState. Stores the buffer, comparator and length, allocates the initial temporary merge storage via the SortDataFormat, and allocates the pending-run stack with a length chosen from the array length.

nodes.name: pushRun
nodes.summary: Pushes a run (its base index and length) onto the pending-run stack.

nodes.name: mergeCollapse
nodes.summary: Merges adjacent pending runs until the TimSort stack invariants on run lengths hold again. Called each time a new run is pushed.

nodes.name: mergeForceCollapse
nodes.summary: Merges all remaining runs on the stack until only one remains. Called once at the end of sort() to complete the sort.

nodes.name: mergeAt
nodes.summary: Merges the two runs at stack indices i and i+1. It first uses gallopRight and gallopLeft to trim elements already in place, then calls mergeLo when the first run is not longer than the second, otherwise mergeHi.

nodes.name: gallopLeft
nodes.summary: Locates the insertion point of a key in a sorted range, returning the index of the leftmost equal element if one exists. It gallops outward from a hint with exponentially growing offsets and then finishes with a binary search.

nodes.name: gallopRight
nodes.summary: Like gallopLeft, but when the range contains elements equal to the key it returns the index after the rightmost equal element. Uses exponential galloping from a hint followed by binary search.

nodes.name: mergeLo
nodes.summary: Merges two adjacent runs in place and stably by copying the first run to temporary storage and merging forward. It switches to galloping mode when one run keeps winning, adapts minGallop, and throws IllegalArgumentException if the comparator violates its contract. Used when len1 <= len2.

nodes.name: mergeHi
nodes.summary: Mirror image of mergeLo: copies the second run to temporary storage and merges backward from the end, with the same galloping logic and contract-violation check. Used when len1 >= len2.

nodes.name: ensureCapacity
nodes.summary: Ensures the temporary merge storage can hold at least minCapacity elements, reallocating through the SortDataFormat with exponential growth (capped at half the array length) when needed.

nodes.name: PrefixComparator.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract PrefixComparator class used in prefix sort to compare 8-byte key prefixes, with type-specific comparisons supplied by subclasses. It is annotated @Private.

nodes.name: PrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Abstract comparator over two long values that hold 8-byte key prefixes. Subclasses implement the single compare(long, long) method for a given key type, for example lexicographic comparison for strings.

nodes.name: PrefixComparators.java
nodes.summary: Holds the shared PrefixComparator constants for string, binary, long and double sort keys, in ascending and descending order with nulls first or last. It also has helpers that turn a string, byte array or double into an 8-byte sort prefix, and the nested comparators that compare prefixes as signed or unsigned longs.
nodes.languageNotes: Java file with a private constructor, static comparator constants and many small final nested classes. The descending comparators swap their parameters before comparing.

nodes.name: PrefixComparators
nodes.summary: Utility class that cannot be instantiated. It exposes ready-made PrefixComparator constants (STRING, BINARY, LONG, DOUBLE, each with _DESC, _NULLS_LAST and _DESC_NULLS_FIRST variants) and groups the nested prefix computation helpers and comparator implementations.

nodes.name: StringPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Holder for computePrefix, which maps a UTF8String to its long prefix and uses 0 for null.

nodes.name: BinaryPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Holder for computePrefix, which maps a byte array to its long prefix.

nodes.name: DoublePrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Holder for computePrefix, which converts a double into a long that orders correctly when compared as an unsigned value.

nodes.name: RadixSortSupport
nodes.summary: Abstract PrefixComparator that adds sortDescending, sortSigned and nullsFirst. A comparator extending it signals that its ordering can be used by radix sort.

nodes.name: UnsignedPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Ascending, nulls-first comparator that compares prefixes as unsigned longs.

nodes.name: UnsignedPrefixComparatorNullsLast
nodes.summary: Ascending, nulls-last comparator that compares prefixes as unsigned longs.

nodes.name: UnsignedPrefixComparatorDescNullsFirst
nodes.summary: Descending, nulls-first comparator that compares prefixes as unsigned longs by swapping the arguments.

nodes.name: UnsignedPrefixComparatorDesc
nodes.summary: Descending, nulls-last comparator that compares prefixes as unsigned longs by swapping the arguments.

nodes.name: SignedPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Ascending, nulls-first comparator that compares prefixes as signed longs.

nodes.name: SignedPrefixComparatorNullsLast
nodes.summary: Ascending, nulls-last comparator that compares prefixes as signed longs.

nodes.name: SignedPrefixComparatorDescNullsFirst
nodes.summary: Descending, nulls-first comparator that compares prefixes as signed longs by swapping the arguments.

nodes.name: SignedPrefixComparatorDesc
nodes.summary: Descending, nulls-last comparator that compares prefixes as signed longs by swapping the arguments.

nodes.name: computePrefix
nodes.summary: Returns the prefix of a UTF8String via getPrefix, or 0 when the value is null.

nodes.name: computePrefix
nodes.summary: Returns the prefix of a byte array via ByteArray.getPrefix.

nodes.name: computePrefix
nodes.summary: Normalizes -0.0 to 0.0, takes the double bits and flips them (all bits for negatives, only the sign bit otherwise) so the result sorts correctly as an unsigned long.

nodes.name: RecordComparator.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract RecordComparator used to order two records in the unsafe sorter. It is consulted after the prefixes compare equal, and may simply return 0 when the whole key fits in the 8-byte prefix.

nodes.name: RecordComparator
nodes.summary: Abstract class with one compare method that takes the base object, offset and length of each of two records and returns a negative, zero or positive int.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Abstract method that compares two records, each given as a base object, offset and length, and returns the usual negative, zero or positive result.

nodes.name: RecordPointerAndKeyPrefix.java
nodes.summary: Defines a small mutable pair of a record pointer and a key prefix. It is the key object the sorter reuses while sorting the (pointer, prefix) entries.

nodes.name: RecordPointerAndKeyPrefix
nodes.summary: Final class with two public long fields: recordPointer (an address encoded as described in TaskMemoryManager) and keyPrefix (used for comparisons).

nodes.name: UnsafeSortDataFormat.java
nodes.summary: Teaches the generic sorter how to read, swap and copy entries in a LongArray that stores (record pointer, key prefix) pairs. It is used by UnsafeInMemorySorter, and it always allocates from the single buffer it was given.

nodes.name: UnsafeSortDataFormat
nodes.summary: Final SortDataFormat over RecordPointerAndKeyPrefix keys and a LongArray. Entry i keeps its pointer at position 2i and its 8-byte key prefix at 2i+1, and keys are reused instead of allocated per read.

nodes.name: UnsafeSortDataFormat
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores the LongArray buffer later returned by allocate.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Fills the reusable RecordPointerAndKeyPrefix with the pointer and prefix at the given position and returns it. The overload without a reuse object (lines 41-44) throws UnsupportedOperationException because keys are always reused.

nodes.name: newKey
nodes.summary: Creates a new empty RecordPointerAndKeyPrefix to be reused as a key.

nodes.name: swap
nodes.summary: Swaps the two long slots (pointer and prefix) of the entries at two positions.

nodes.name: copyElement
nodes.summary: Copies one entry (pointer and prefix) from a source array position to a destination array position.

nodes.name: copyRange
nodes.summary: Copies a range of entries between two LongArrays with Platform.copyMemory, using 16 bytes per entry.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Asserts that the buffer holds at least 2 * length longs and returns the existing buffer instead of allocating a new one.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterBoundedSpillMerger.java
nodes.summary: Performs a multi-round k-way merge of spill files in which at most mergeFactor readers are open at a time, writing intermediate spill files for the early rounds. It bounds memory use during the merge phase of the external sort at the cost of extra disk I/O.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private final Java class. Logging uses SparkLogger with MDC keys from LogKeys.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterBoundedSpillMerger
nodes.summary: Merges spill writers in rounds of at most mergeFactor files, deleting consumed files eagerly, then does a final merge (optionally including an in-memory iterator) with UnsafeSorterSpillMerger. It tracks intermediate files so they can be cleaned up if the merge fails, and is created by UnsafeExternalSorter.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterBoundedSpillMerger
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores the merge factor, the record and prefix comparators, the block manager, the serializer manager and the file buffer size.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: While there are more spill writers than the merge factor, partitions them into groups, merges each group into one intermediate spill file and deletes the consumed files. It then builds a final UnsafeSorterSpillMerger over the remaining writers plus the optional in-memory iterator and returns its sorted iterator. If a round makes no progress it logs a warning and falls back to an unbounded final merge.

nodes.name: partitionWriters
nodes.summary: Splits writers into groups limited by both the merge factor and a total of Integer.MAX_VALUE records, so the record count of a merged spill file cannot overflow an int.

nodes.name: mergeGroupToSpill
nodes.summary: Opens a reader on each writer of a group, merges them with an UnsafeSorterSpillMerger and writes every record in sorted order to a new UnsafeSorterSpillWriter. It records the new file as an intermediate file and throws if the total record count exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE.

nodes.name: deleteConsumedFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes the spill files of the given writers if they exist and logs a warning when a delete fails.

nodes.name: getIntermediateRoundsCompleted
nodes.summary: Returns how many intermediate merge rounds have been completed.

nodes.name: cleanupIntermediateFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes every tracked intermediate spill file that still exists and clears the set. It is a safety net called during resource cleanup.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterIterator.java
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract UnsafeSorterIterator, the common iterator type over sorted records in the unsafe sorter. A record is advanced with loadNext and then read through accessors for its base object, offset, length and key prefix.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract class with hasNext, loadNext and accessors for the current record (base object, base offset, record length, key prefix), plus the total number of records and the current page number. Subclasses in this wave include a merged iterator and spill readers.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Abstract method that reports whether another record is available.

nodes.name: loadNext
nodes.summary: Abstract method that advances to the next record and makes it readable through the accessors. It may throw IOException.

nodes.name: getBaseObject
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the base object of the current record.

nodes.name: getBaseOffset
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the base offset of the current record.

nodes.name: getRecordLength
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the length of the current record.

nodes.name: getKeyPrefix
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the key prefix of the current record.

nodes.name: getNumRecords
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the number of records in the iterator.

nodes.name: getCurrentPageNumber
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for the page number of the current record.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillMerger.java
nodes.summary: Merges several sorted UnsafeSorterIterators (spill readers) into one sorted iterator using a priority queue ordered by key prefix and then by record comparator. It opens all given readers at once and is used for single-round merges and for the final round of the bounded merger.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private final Java class. getSortedIterator returns an anonymous UnsafeSorterIterator subclass.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillMerger
nodes.summary: Holds a PriorityQueue of non-empty UnsafeSorterIterators ordered by prefix comparison with a record comparison as tie-breaker, and a running record count. getSortedIterator returns an iterator that repeatedly yields the smallest current record.

nodes.name: UnsafeSorterSpillMerger
nodes.summary: Constructor that builds the comparator (prefix first, record comparator when prefixes are equal) and creates the priority queue sized for numSpills iterators.

nodes.name: addSpillIfNotEmpty
nodes.summary: Adds a spill iterator to the queue only if it has records: it loads its first record, enqueues it and adds its record count. Empty readers are skipped so hasNext of the merged iterator stays correct.

nodes.name: getSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous UnsafeSorterIterator that, on each loadNext, re-enqueues the previously returned reader (if it has more records) and removes the smallest reader from the queue. Its accessors delegate to that reader, and getCurrentPageNumber is unsupported. The accessor overrides are not given separate nodes.

nodes.name: SparkCoreErrors.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkCoreErrors, a single object that builds the exceptions (mostly SparkException with a named error class and message parameters) thrown by core code for checkpoint, barrier stage, block manager, shuffle, memory, add-file and codec failures.

nodes.name: SparkCoreErrors
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object grouping factory methods for core error values. Each method returns a Throwable (SparkException, SparkIllegalArgumentException, IOException, barrier job exceptions, FetchFailedException, SparkOutOfMemoryError and so on) so callers throw a uniform, named error. Only the more substantial methods have their own nodes; many other one-statement error builders (for example emptyRDDError, emptyCollectionError, interruptedError, noSuchElementError) are not listed individually.

nodes.name: eofExceptionWhileReadPortNumberError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3001) for hitting end of stream while reading a daemon port number, optionally appending the daemon exit code.

nodes.name: rddBlockNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3003) reporting that a block for a given RDD id was not found.

nodes.name: pathNotSupportedError
nodes.summary: Builds an IOException saying a path is a directory, which the record reader does not support when recursive input is disabled.

nodes.name: checkpointRDDBlockIdNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (CHECKPOINT_RDD_BLOCK_ID_NOT_FOUND) for a missing checkpoint RDD block id.

nodes.name: checkpointRDDHasDifferentNumberOfPartitionsFromOriginalRDDError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3019) reporting a checkpointed RDD whose partition count differs from the original RDD, with both ids and lengths as parameters.

nodes.name: checkpointFailedToSaveError
nodes.summary: Builds an IOException stating that a task failed to save its checkpoint output and the final output path does not exist.

nodes.name: sparkJobCancelled
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (SPARK_JOB_CANCELLED) with the job id and a reason, carrying an optional cause.

nodes.name: sparkJobCancelledAsPartOfJobGroupError
nodes.summary: Builds a job-cancelled SparkException whose reason says the job belongs to a cancelled job group.

nodes.name: barrierStageWithRDDChainPatternError
nodes.summary: Creates a BarrierJobUnsupportedRDDChainException for an unsupported RDD chain pattern in a barrier stage.

nodes.name: barrierStageWithDynamicAllocationError
nodes.summary: Creates a BarrierJobRunWithDynamicAllocationException for running a barrier job with dynamic allocation.

nodes.name: numPartitionsGreaterThanMaxNumConcurrentTasksError
nodes.summary: Creates a BarrierJobSlotsNumberCheckFailed when a barrier stage needs more partitions than the maximum number of concurrent tasks.

nodes.name: failToSerializeTaskError
nodes.summary: Wraps a Throwable in a TaskNotSerializableException for a task that could not be serialized.

nodes.name: unrecognizedBlockIdError
nodes.summary: Creates an UnrecognizedBlockId exception for a block name that cannot be parsed.

nodes.name: taskHasNotLockedBlockError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3030) saying the current task attempt has not locked the given block.

nodes.name: cannotSaveBlockOnDecommissionedExecutorError
nodes.summary: Creates a BlockSavedOnDecommissionedBlockManagerException for a block saved on a decommissioned block manager.

nodes.name: unableToRegisterWithExternalShuffleServerError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3033) with the cause message when registering with the external shuffle server fails.

nodes.name: unexpectedShuffleBlockWithUnsupportedResolverError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3035) naming a block id and the shuffle block resolver of the given ShuffleManager that cannot handle it.

nodes.name: failToStoreBlockOnBlockManagerError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3036) when a block cannot be stored on a given block manager.

nodes.name: blockNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Creates a BlockNotFoundException from the string form of a block id.

nodes.name: failToCreateDirectoryError
nodes.summary: Builds an IOException reporting that a directory with permission 770 could not be created after a number of attempts.

nodes.name: fetchFailedError
nodes.summary: Creates a FetchFailedException from the block manager address, shuffle id, map id and index, reduce id, message and optional cause.

nodes.name: failToGetNonShuffleBlockError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3042) with a cause for failing to get a non-shuffle block.

nodes.name: graphiteSinkInvalidProtocolError
