nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (GRAPHITE_SINK_INVALID_PROTOCOL) for an invalid protocol value.

nodes.name: graphiteSinkPropertyMissingError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (GRAPHITE_SINK_PROPERTY_MISSING) for a missing required property.

nodes.name: outOfMemoryError
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkOutOfMemoryError (UNABLE_TO_ACQUIRE_MEMORY) carrying the requested and received byte counts as parameters.

nodes.name: failedRenameTempFileError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (FAILED_RENAME_TEMP_FILE) giving the source and destination paths of a failed rename.

nodes.name: addLocalDirectoryError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (UNSUPPORTED_ADD_FILE.LOCAL_DIRECTORY) for adding a local directory as a file.

nodes.name: addDirectoryError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkException (UNSUPPORTED_ADD_FILE.DIRECTORY) for adding a directory as a file.

nodes.name: codecNotAvailableError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkIllegalArgumentException (CODEC_NOT_AVAILABLE.WITH_CONF_SUGGESTION) that names the missing codec and suggests setting the IO_COMPRESSION_CODEC configuration to the fallback codec.

nodes.name: tooManyArrayElementsError
nodes.summary: Builds a SparkIllegalArgumentException (COLLECTION_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.INITIALIZE) reporting the requested element count and the maximum rounded array length.

nodes.name: quoteByDefault
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps a string in double quotes.

nodes.name: toConf
nodes.summary: Quotes a configuration key for use in an error message parameter.

nodes.name: toConfVal
nodes.summary: Quotes a configuration value for use in an error message parameter.

nodes.name: SparkPath.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkPath, a canonical, URL-encoded string wrapper for file paths, with conversions to and from Hadoop Path, FileStatus and java URI.
nodes.languageNotes: Case class with a private constructor plus a companion object holding the public factories.

nodes.name: SparkPath
nodes.summary: Case class (private constructor) and companion object that give type safety to path handling: it stores the URL-encoded string and exposes urlEncoded, toUri and toPath, while the companion creates instances from Hadoop Path strings, Paths, FileStatus, URL strings or URIs. Used where Spark must not mix Hadoop Path.toString and URI.toString representations.

nodes.name: toUri
nodes.summary: Parses the stored string into a java URI.

nodes.name: toPath
nodes.summary: Builds a Hadoop Path from the URI form of this path.

nodes.name: fromPathString
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkPath from a Hadoop Path string by building a Path and delegating to fromPath; the caller must be sure of the encoding.

nodes.name: fromPath
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkPath from a Hadoop Path via its URI.

nodes.name: fromFileStatus
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkPath from the path of a Hadoop FileStatus.

nodes.name: fromUrlString
nodes.summary: Wraps an already URL-encoded string in a SparkPath without validating it.

nodes.name: fromUri
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkPath from a java URI using its string form.

nodes.name: OpenHashMap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OpenHashMap, a fast open-addressing hash map for nullable keys that supports insert and update but not deletion, built on OpenHashSet.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @specialized value types and a separate slot for the null key.

nodes.name: OpenHashMap
nodes.summary: Private[spark] map class (an Iterable of key/value pairs, Serializable) that stores keys in an OpenHashSet and values in a parallel array, handling the null key separately. It supports contains, apply, get, update, changeValue and iteration, grows its value array when the key set rehashes, and is described in the source as about 5X faster than java.util.HashMap.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the key set size, plus one when a null-key value is present.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Tests whether a key has a binding, using the null flag for null keys and the key set position otherwise.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the value for a key, or a null/zero default value when the key is absent.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the value for a key as an Option, None when absent.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Sets the value for a key (null key handled separately), adds the key without resizing, then rehashes the key set if needed.

nodes.name: changeValue
nodes.summary: Sets a default value when the key is new, or replaces the old value with mergeValue(oldValue); returns the new value.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over (key, value) pairs, yielding the null-key pair first and then the occupied key set positions.

nodes.name: grow
nodes.summary: Callback passed to rehashIfNeeded that saves the old value array and allocates a larger one.

nodes.name: move
nodes.summary: Callback passed to rehashIfNeeded that copies a value from its old position to its new position.

nodes.name: Utils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the collection Utils object with helpers to take the smallest K elements, merge sorted iterators, convert sequences of Options, and build Scala or Java maps from key and value collections.

nodes.name: Utils
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object extending SparkCollectionUtils that provides takeOrdered, mergeOrdered, sequenceToOption, toMap and toJavaMap. The ordering helpers wrap an implicit Ordering in a Guava Ordering.

nodes.name: takeOrdered
nodes.summary: Returns the first num elements of an iterator under an implicit Ordering, keeping the order, using Guava leastOf.

nodes.name: mergeOrdered
nodes.summary: Merges several already sorted iterators into one sorted iterator without removing duplicates, using Guava mergeSorted; inputs must share the same ordering.

nodes.name: sequenceToOption
nodes.summary: Returns Some(flattened values) only if every Option in the sequence is defined, otherwise None.

nodes.name: toMap
nodes.summary: Builds an immutable Map from parallel key and value collections, equivalent to keys.zip(values).toMap but faster.

nodes.name: toJavaMap
nodes.summary: Builds an unmodifiable java.util.Map from parallel key and value collections, equivalent to keys.zip(values).toMap.asJava but faster.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the package object for org.apache.spark.util.random, documented as utilities for random number generation; the object body is empty.

nodes.name: random
nodes.summary: Empty package object for org.apache.spark.util.random with only a doc comment about random number generation utilities.

nodes.name: OpenHashSet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OpenHashSet, a fast insertion-only open-addressing hash set with specialized storage for Long, Int, Double and Float, plus its companion object holding capacity constants and primitive hashers. It serves as a building block for higher level hash structures.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala @specialized on Long, Int, Double and Float so primitive keys are stored without boxing.

nodes.name: OpenHashSet
nodes.summary: Insertion-only hash set (keys are never removed) backed by a data array and a BitSet of occupied slots, with a power-of-2 capacity, quadratic probing and a load factor below 1.0. It exposes position-based access and allocate and move callbacks so that higher level structures can keep parallel arrays in sync when the table grows. The companion object (lines 282-322) holds MAX_CAPACITY, INVALID_POS, NONEXISTENCE_MASK, POSITION_MASK and the Hasher classes; the auxiliary constructors this(initialCapacity) and this() default the load factor to 0.7 and the capacity to 64.
nodes.languageNotes: Members are protected rather than private so the specialized subclasses generated by the compiler can reach them.

nodes.name: Hasher
nodes.summary: Sealed base hasher whose hash method returns o.hashCode(); it is the generic fallback used by OpenHashSet for non-primitive keys and is specialized for Long, Int, Double and Float.

nodes.name: LongHasher
nodes.summary: Hasher for Long keys that folds the high 32 bits into the low 32 bits without boxing.

nodes.name: IntHasher
nodes.summary: Hasher for Int keys that returns the value itself as the hash code.

nodes.name: DoubleHasher
nodes.summary: Hasher for Double keys that hashes the raw long bits from doubleToLongBits by folding the high half into the low half.

nodes.name: FloatHasher
nodes.summary: Hasher for Float keys that uses floatToIntBits as the hash code.

nodes.name: getBitSet
nodes.summary: Returns the BitSet that marks which slots of the data array hold a key.

nodes.name: size
nodes.summary: Returns the number of elements currently in the set.

nodes.name: capacity
nodes.summary: Returns the capacity of the set, that is the length of the underlying array.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Returns true if the key is present, by checking that getPos is not INVALID_POS.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds an element via addWithoutResize and then grows and rehashes the table through rehashIfNeeded if it is over capacity.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Adds every element of another OpenHashSet to this set and returns this set.

nodes.name: keyExistsAtPos
nodes.summary: Private check that compares the stored key at a position using equals (object equality) so values such as 0.0 and -0.0 or NaN are handled consistently.

nodes.name: addWithoutResize
nodes.summary: Inserts a key using quadratic probing without triggering a rehash and returns the slot position, with the high bit (NONEXISTENCE_MASK) set when the key was not previously present. The caller must call rehashIfNeeded afterwards.

nodes.name: rehashIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Calls rehash with the given allocate and move callbacks when the size exceeds the grow threshold.

nodes.name: getPos
nodes.summary: Returns the array position of a key found by quadratic probing, or INVALID_POS when it is absent.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Returns the value stored at the given array position.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an Iterator over all stored elements by walking the occupied positions with nextPos and getValue.

nodes.name: getValueSafe
nodes.summary: Returns the value at a position after asserting that the bitset marks that slot as occupied.

nodes.name: nextPos
nodes.summary: Returns the next occupied position at or after the given one by delegating to BitSet.nextSetBit.

nodes.name: rehash
nodes.summary: Private method that doubles the capacity, calls the allocate callback, reinserts every key into a new array and bitset using probing, calls the move callback for each key, and then swaps in the new structures and recomputes the grow threshold.

nodes.name: hashcode
nodes.summary: Private re-hash of a hash code using a Murmur3 32-bit hash, to cope with hash functions that differ little in the lower bits.

nodes.name: nextPowerOf2
nodes.summary: Private helper that rounds a requested capacity up to the next power of 2 (returning 1 for 0).

nodes.name: PairsWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the PairsWriter trait, an abstraction of a consumer of key-value pairs.

nodes.name: PairsWriter
nodes.summary: Trait for a consumer of key-value pairs, used when persisting partitioned data, either through the shuffle writer plugins or via DiskBlockObjectWriter. It declares a single abstract write(key, value) method.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Abstract method that accepts one key and one value to be written.

nodes.name: SizeTrackingVector.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SizeTrackingVector, an append-only PrimitiveVector that also tracks its estimated size in bytes.

nodes.name: SizeTrackingVector
nodes.summary: Append-only buffer that extends PrimitiveVector and mixes in SizeTracker so its size in bytes can be estimated. It reports every append to the tracker and resets the size samples when the vector is resized.
Appends a value through PrimitiveVector and then calls afterUpdate so the size estimate can be sampled.

nodes.name: resize
nodes.summary: Resizes the underlying vector through PrimitiveVector and then calls resetSamples, returning this vector.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBuffer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ChunkedByteBuffer, a read-only byte buffer stored as several ByteBuffer chunks, its companion factory methods, and ChunkedByteBufferInputStream for reading it as an InputStream.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Read-only byte buffer physically stored as multiple ByteBuffer chunks instead of one contiguous array, so it can hold more than 2 GB. It can write itself to a channel in fixed-size slices, serialize through Externalizable, convert to an array, a ByteBuffer, an InputStream or a Netty file region, copy itself and dispose its chunks. The companion object (lines 220-271) provides fromManagedBuffer, fromFile and estimateBufferChunkSize; the auxiliary constructors take no chunks or a single ByteBuffer.

nodes.name: writeFully
nodes.summary: Writes all chunks to a WritableByteChannel in slices no larger than the configured write chunk size, to avoid caching a large temporary direct buffer.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable write that stores the chunk count, each chunk limit and then the chunk data using Utils.writeByteBuffer.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Externalizable read that rebuilds the chunks as on-heap ByteBuffers from the stored chunk sizes and recomputes the total size.

nodes.name: toNetty
nodes.summary: Wraps this buffer in a ChunkedByteBufferFileRegion so data larger than 2 GB can be transferred.

nodes.name: toNettyForSsl
nodes.summary: Wraps this buffer in a Netty ChunkedStream over toInputStream so it can be sent in a way compatible with SSL encryption.

nodes.name: toArray
nodes.summary: Copies the buffer into a new byte array by writing it to a ByteArrayWritableChannel, and throws UnsupportedOperationException if the size exceeds the maximum array size.

nodes.name: toByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Returns a duplicate of the single chunk when there is one, otherwise copies all data into a new ByteBuffer via toArray.

nodes.name: toInputStream
nodes.summary: Creates a ChunkedByteBufferInputStream over this buffer, optionally disposing the buffer at the end of the stream.

nodes.name: getChunks
nodes.summary: Returns duplicates of the backing ByteBuffers so callers can read them without changing the originals.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Makes a deep copy of this buffer into new chunks obtained from the given allocator function.

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.summary: Disposes every chunk through StorageUtils.dispose once, cleaning up direct or memory-mapped buffers.

nodes.name: fromManagedBuffer
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a ChunkedByteBuffer from a ManagedBuffer, reading a file segment, converting an EncryptedManagedBuffer's block data, or wrapping the nio buffer otherwise.

nodes.name: fromFile
nodes.summary: Companion factory that reads a file (or an offset and length range of it, via a private overload; the public overload only passes the whole file) into a ChunkedByteBuffer using a ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream without memory mapping the file.

nodes.name: estimateBufferChunkSize
nodes.summary: Companion helper that estimates a chunk size between a minimum of 1024 bytes and 1 MB (the default when the size is unknown).

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBufferInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream that reads from the chunks of a ChunkedByteBuffer, skipping empty chunks and moving to the next chunk as each is consumed. When created with dispose set, it disposes the buffer on close.

nodes.name: available
nodes.summary: Returns the remaining bytes in the current chunk, advancing to the next chunk when needed.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads bytes into an array from the current chunk (the single-byte read() overload is at lines 305-315); on exhaustion it closes the stream and returns -1.

nodes.name: skip
nodes.summary: Skips up to the number of bytes remaining in the current chunk and moves on to the next chunk or closes the stream when exhausted.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Disposes the underlying ChunkedByteBuffer when dispose was requested and clears the stream's references.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream, an OutputStream that writes into fixed-size byte buffer chunks and can produce a ChunkedByteBuffer once closed.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream
nodes.summary: OutputStream that accumulates written bytes in fixed-size chunks obtained from an allocator function, allocating a new chunk when the last one is full. After close, toChunkedByteBuffer returns the data as a ChunkedByteBuffer (callable once), trimming the last chunk to the written length.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Marks the stream closed once, calling the OutputStream close.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a byte array range into the current chunk, allocating new chunks as needed (the single-byte write(Int) overload is at lines 63-69); both require the stream to be open.

nodes.name: allocateNewChunkIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Private helper that allocates a new chunk with the allocator when the current chunk is full.

nodes.name: toChunkedByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Builds a ChunkedByteBuffer from the written chunks after close; it flips the full chunks, copies the partly filled last chunk into a right-sized buffer, disposes the old one with StorageUtils.dispose, and can only be called once.

nodes.name: LauncherBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract LauncherBackend, which lets an application talk to a launcher server, plus a private companion holding a thread factory.

nodes.name: LauncherBackend
nodes.summary: Abstract class that connects to a launcher server over a loopback socket using a port and secret from the SparkConf or environment, sends a Hello and later app id and state updates, and reacts to Stop messages by running onStopRequest on a new thread. Subclasses implement onStopRequest and may override onDisconnected. The private companion object (lines 125-129) creates the named thread factory.

nodes.name: BackendConnection
nodes.summary: Private inner class extending LauncherConnection that handles incoming messages: a Stop message triggers fireStopRequest and any other message type raises IllegalArgumentException. Its close clears the connected flag and calls onDisconnected.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Reads the launcher port and secret from the conf or environment and, if both are present, opens a loopback socket, sends a Hello with the secret and Spark version, and starts the connection thread.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the connection if one exists and waits for the client thread to finish.

nodes.name: setAppId
nodes.summary: Sends a SetAppId message to the launcher when connected.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Sends a SetState message to the launcher when connected and the state has changed since the last one sent.

nodes.name: isConnected
nodes.summary: Returns whether the launcher handle is still connected to this backend.

nodes.name: onStopRequest
nodes.summary: Abstract callback implemented by subclasses to stop the application as gracefully as possible.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: Overridable callback invoked when the launcher handle disconnects; the default does nothing.

nodes.name: fireStopRequest
nodes.summary: Private method that runs onStopRequest on a new thread from the named factory, logging non-fatal errors.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Dispatches an incoming message: Stop calls fireStopRequest, any other message throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Sets the connected flag to false, closes the connection and always calls onDisconnected.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitArgumentsParser.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkSubmitArgumentsParser, a thin abstract class that exposes SparkSubmitOptionParser to code outside the launcher package.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitArgumentsParser
nodes.summary: Abstract class extending SparkSubmitOptionParser. It exists only to make that parser visible to code outside the launcher package, since Java has no equivalent of private[spark] and the parser class should not be public.

nodes.name: PercentileHeap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PercentileHeap, a structure that tracks a chosen percentile of inserted numbers using two priority queues.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class that stores negated values in a plain PriorityQueue to emulate a max-heap and avoid comparator call overhead.

nodes.name: PercentileHeap
nodes.summary: Keeps a small heap of values below the target percentile and a large heap of values above it, so the percentile can be read in O(1) and inserts cost O(log n). The percentage must be strictly between 0 and 1 (default 0.5).

nodes.name: percentile
nodes.summary: Returns the percentile of the inserted elements, equal to sorted(p) with p = (length * percentage).toInt, by peeking the large heap. Throws NoSuchElementException when empty.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a number and rebalances the two heaps (moving the top element across them when needed) so the large heap top stays at the target percentile.

nodes.name: SizeTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SizeTracker trait that lets a collection keep a cheap running estimate of its size in bytes by sampling SizeEstimator with exponential back-off.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with a private companion object holding the Sample case class.

nodes.name: SizeTracker
nodes.summary: Trait for collections that track their estimated size in bytes. It samples SizeEstimator at growing intervals (growth rate 1.1), keeps only the last two samples, and extrapolates between samples so estimateSize is O(1). Implementers call afterUpdate after each change and resetSamples after a dramatic size change.

nodes.name: Sample
nodes.summary: Private case class in the SizeTracker companion that records one size sample as (size in bytes, number of updates at sampling time).

nodes.name: resetSamples
nodes.summary: Resets the update counters, clears the sample queue and takes a fresh sample. Intended to be called after the collection changes size dramatically.

nodes.name: afterUpdate
nodes.summary: Callback invoked after every insertion or update; increments the update counter and takes a new sample when the next sampling point is reached.

nodes.name: takeSample
nodes.summary: Estimates the current size with SizeEstimator, enqueues the sample (keeping only the last two), recomputes the bytes-per-update slope (never negative) and schedules the next sample point using the growth rate.

nodes.name: estimateSize
nodes.summary: Returns the estimated collection size in bytes in O(1) time, as the last sample plus bytes-per-update times the updates made since that sample.

nodes.name: DriverLogger.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DriverLogger, which attaches a log4j file appender to the root logger for the driver and can continuously copy that local log file to a DFS directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a nested Runnable (DfsAsyncWriter) and a companion object holding constants and an Option-returning factory.

nodes.name: DriverLogger
nodes.summary: Adds a file appender named _DriverLogAppender to the root logger, writing the driver log to a local file (driver.log under a configured or local directory). When asked via startSync it uploads that file to DFS through a DfsAsyncWriter; stop removes the appender and deletes the local directory. The companion object holds the file and appender name constants and an apply factory.

nodes.name: DfsAsyncWriter
nodes.summary: Runnable that opens the local driver log and a DFS output file, then every 5 seconds copies new bytes (in 1 MB chunks) from the local file to DFS and flushes. closeWriter writes the remaining bytes, closes both streams and shuts down its scheduler thread.

nodes.name: addLogAppender
nodes.summary: Builds a pattern layout (configured or default) and a non-appending file appender on the local log file, adds it to the root logger and starts it.

nodes.name: startSync
nodes.summary: Creates a DfsAsyncWriter for the sanitized application id so the local log file is continuously moved to DFS; logs an error instead of failing if it cannot be created.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Removes and stops the log appender, closes the DFS writer if present, and finally deletes the local driver log directory, logging any errors.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Validates that the DFS root directory exists, opens the local log input stream and the DFS output file with restricted permissions, and schedules the periodic upload task on a daemon single-thread scheduler.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Copies all currently available bytes from the local log stream to the DFS output stream in chunks and syncs the DFS stream when data was written; errors are logged.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Writes any remaining bytes by calling run, then marks the writer closed and closes the input and output streams, logging close errors.

nodes.name: closeWriter
nodes.summary: Submits close to the scheduler thread, shuts the scheduler down and waits up to one minute for it to terminate.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory on the companion object. Creates a DriverLogger when local logging or persist-to-DFS in client mode is configured; returns Some only when a DFS directory is configured, otherwise None (a local-only logger is still started for the driver log UI). Logs and returns None on failure.

nodes.name: FileAppender.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileAppender, which runs a daemon thread that copies an input stream into a file, plus a companion factory that picks a plain or rolling appender from the executor log rolling settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with protected template methods (appendToFile, openFile, closeFile) that RollingFileAppender overrides or reuses.

nodes.name: FileAppender
nodes.summary: Starts a daemon thread on construction that reads chunks from an input stream and appends them to a file until the stream ends or stop is called, optionally closing the input stream afterwards. The companion object creates the right appender (plain, time-based rolling or size-based rolling) from SparkConf.

nodes.name: appendStreamToFile
nodes.summary: Main loop of the appender thread: opens the file, reads buffers from the input stream until stop is requested or EOF, appends non-empty reads, ignores IOException after a stop request, and always closes the file (and the stream if configured).

nodes.name: appendToFile
nodes.summary: Writes the given number of bytes to the file output stream, opening the file first if it is not yet open. Overridden by RollingFileAppender.

nodes.name: openFile
nodes.summary: Opens the target file in append mode as a FileOutputStream.

nodes.name: closeFile
nodes.summary: Flushes and closes the file output stream.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that reads the executor log rolling strategy, size and time interval from SparkConf and returns a plain FileAppender (no or illegal strategy), a time-based RollingFileAppender (daily, hourly, minutely or a number of seconds) or a size-based RollingFileAppender. Warns on illegal values and falls back to a plain appender. Contains the local helpers createTimeBasedAppender and createSizeBasedAppender.

nodes.name: RollingFileAppender.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RollingFileAppender, a FileAppender that rolls the active log file over according to a RollingPolicy, optionally gzips rolled files and deletes the oldest ones beyond a retention limit.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala subclass of FileAppender with a companion object that lists rolled-over files in order.

nodes.name: RollingFileAppender
nodes.summary: Extends FileAppender: before each write it asks the RollingPolicy whether to roll over, then closes and renames the active file (adding a policy-generated suffix, gzipping if enabled), reopens it and prunes old rolled files beyond the configured maximum. The companion object holds the default buffer size, the .gz suffix and getSortedRolledOverFiles.

nodes.name: appendToFile
nodes.summary: Overrides FileAppender.appendToFile: rolls the file over first when the policy says so, then writes the bytes via the parent and reports the byte count to the policy.

nodes.name: rollover
nodes.summary: Closes the active file, moves it to its rolled-over name, reopens a fresh file, and deletes old files when a retention limit is set; errors are logged rather than thrown.

nodes.name: rotateFile
nodes.summary: Moves the active file to the rollover file name, or when compression is enabled copies it into a gzip file with a .gz suffix and deletes the original.

nodes.name: rolloverFileExist
nodes.summary: Returns true if the given rollover file, or its .gz variant, already exists.

nodes.name: moveFile
nodes.summary: Computes the rollover file name from the policy suffix and rotates the active file there; if that name already exists it tries numbered alternative names (up to 10000) and logs a warning.

nodes.name: deleteOldFiles
nodes.summary: Lists files in the log directory that start with the active file name, sorts them and deletes the oldest so only the configured number of rolled files is retained.

nodes.name: getSortedRolledOverFiles
nodes.summary: Companion helper that returns the rolled-over files of a directory sorted by name (ignoring a .gz suffix) followed by the active file if it exists.

nodes.name: RandomSampler.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RandomSampler trait and its companion constants, plus the concrete samplers BernoulliCellSampler, BernoulliSampler and PoissonSampler, and the internal GapSampling and GapSamplingReplacement helpers that skip ahead between sampled items. Used to take random samples of iterators, with or without replacement.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait plus companion object; samplers are Cloneable and Serializable so they can be copied per partition.

nodes.name: RandomSampler
nodes.summary: Trait for a pseudorandom sampler that turns an iterator of T into an iterator of U. Its companion object (lines 55-86, merged into this node) holds the default RNG factory and the default gap-sampling fraction and epsilon constants.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Overloaded sample: the iterator form (lines 41-42) filters items by calling the abstract sample(): Int (line 48), which returns how many times the next item is sampled and 0 if not sampled.

nodes.name: newDefaultRNG
nodes.summary: Companion factory returning the default random number generator used by samplers, a new XORShiftRandom.

nodes.name: BernoulliCellSampler
nodes.summary: Sampler that accepts an item when a random draw falls in the range [lb, ub), or outside it when complement is true; used to partition a data sequence. It validates the bounds in its constructor and owns an XORShiftRandom.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Draws a uniform value and returns 1 if it falls in [lb, ub) (flipped when complement is set), else 0; an empty range returns 1 or 0 depending on complement.

nodes.name: BernoulliSampler
nodes.summary: Sampler based on Bernoulli trials with a fixed sampling fraction. It returns 0 or 1 for the extremes, switches to gap sampling when the fraction is at or below the default maximum gap fraction, and otherwise compares a uniform draw against the fraction.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Chooses between constant results, the lazily created GapSampling helper, or a direct uniform draw compared to the fraction, depending on the fraction value.

nodes.name: PoissonSampler
nodes.summary: Sampler for sampling with replacement that draws the number of copies of each item from a Poisson distribution, optionally using GapSamplingReplacement when the fraction is low. Has an auxiliary one-argument constructor that enables gap sampling.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Iterator form of sample (the widest of two overloads; the no-argument form is at lines 212-221): returns an empty iterator for a non-positive fraction, otherwise flatMaps each item into the sampled number of copies.

nodes.name: GapSampling
nodes.summary: Package-private helper that implements Bernoulli sampling by drawing how many items to drop from a geometric distribution, so that the RNG is not called for every item. Used by BernoulliSampler for small fractions.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Returns 0 while a countdown of items to drop is positive, otherwise advances to the next gap and returns 1.

nodes.name: advance
nodes.summary: Draws a uniform value bounded below by epsilon and sets the number of elements to skip from a geometric distribution using log(u) / log(1 - f).

nodes.name: GapSamplingReplacement
nodes.summary: Package-private helper for sampling with replacement that skips items with replication factor zero using a geometric draw and samples a Poisson value conditioned to be at least 1 for the others. Used by PoissonSampler for small fractions.

nodes.name: poissonGE1
nodes.summary: Samples from a Poisson distribution conditioned on the result being at least 1, by starting from one simulated iteration and continuing the standard multiplication loop.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Returns 0 while the drop countdown is positive; otherwise draws a conditioned Poisson count, advances to the next gap and returns the count.

nodes.name: advance
nodes.summary: Sets the number of elements to skip from a geometric distribution with q = e^(-f), using a uniform draw bounded below by epsilon.

nodes.name: SamplingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds sampling helpers: reservoir sampling that also returns the input size, a function that computes an inflated sampling fraction to reach a target sample size with high probability, and the Poisson and Binomial bound calculators it relies on.
nodes.languageNotes: Three private[spark] singleton objects.

nodes.name: SamplingUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton object with reservoirSampleAndCount and computeFractionForSampleSize. Used when a fixed-size sample must be drawn from an iterator or when a fraction must be chosen to get at least a given number of items.

nodes.name: reservoirSampleAndCount
nodes.summary: Fills a reservoir with the first k items of the input and then replaces entries with probability k/l using an XORShiftRandom; returns the samples (trimmed if input is shorter than k) and the total input count.

nodes.name: computeFractionForSampleSize
nodes.summary: Returns a sampling rate that yields at least the lower-bound sample size with about 99.99% probability, using PoissonBounds for sampling with replacement and BinomialBounds otherwise.

nodes.name: PoissonBounds
nodes.summary: Singleton with lower and upper bounds on a Poisson lambda that make tail probabilities small, based on a step function of the number of standard deviations. Used for sampling with replacement.

nodes.name: getLowerBound
nodes.summary: Returns a lambda for which the probability of exceeding s is very small, floored at 1e-15.

nodes.name: getUpperBound
nodes.summary: Returns a lambda for which the probability of falling below s is very small, floored at 1e-10.

nodes.name: numStd
nodes.summary: Private helper choosing the number of standard deviations (12, 9 or 6) from the sample size s; has a TODO to make it tighter.

nodes.name: BinomialBounds
nodes.summary: Singleton with lower and upper thresholds for the success rate of Bernoulli trials, used to guarantee an exact sample size with high confidence when sampling without replacement. Defines minSamplingRate of 1e-10.

nodes.name: getLowerBound
nodes.summary: Computes a threshold p such that n Bernoulli trials with rate p are unlikely to give more than fraction * n successes.

nodes.name: getUpperBound
nodes.summary: Computes a threshold p such that n Bernoulli trials with rate p are unlikely to give fewer than fraction * n successes, clamped between minSamplingRate and 1.

nodes.name: StratifiedSamplingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Auxiliary functions and data structures for stratified sampling by key. When an exact sample size is needed it makes extra passes over the RDD to compute a per-stratum acceptance threshold using a waitlist, then builds per-partition sampling functions with and without replacement.
nodes.languageNotes: Private nested class RandomDataGenerator and a private[random] AcceptanceResult class support the seqOp/combOp aggregation.

nodes.name: StratifiedSamplingUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton (extends Logging) that collects per-stratum acceptance statistics with an aggregation over the RDD, computes exact thresholds, and returns the per-partition functions used for sampling by key with or without replacement. The file comment says it supports the sampleByKey method in PairRDDFunctions.

nodes.name: getAcceptanceResults
nodes.summary: Runs mapPartitionsWithIndex over the RDD, folding each partition with the seqOp (seeded by seed + partition) into a map of AcceptanceResult per key, then reduces the partition maps with the combOp. Only invoked when exact sample size is required.

nodes.name: getSeqOp
nodes.summary: Returns the function that updates a per-key AcceptanceResult for each item: with replacement it uses Poisson bounds and counts, without replacement it uses streaming Binomial bounds; it counts accepted items and fills the waitlist with random values.

nodes.name: getCombOp
nodes.summary: Returns the function that merges per-partition AcceptanceResult maps over the union of their keys, merging entries into the second map.

nodes.name: computeThresholdByKey
nodes.summary: For each stratum computes the target sample size and picks the acceptance threshold: the accept bound if too many were pre-accepted, the waitlist bound if the waitlist is too short, otherwise the sorted waitlist value at the needed index. Logs warnings in the two edge cases.

nodes.name: getBernoulliSamplingFunction
nodes.summary: Returns the per-partition function for sampling without replacement; when exact is set it first computes thresholds from the acceptance results, then filters items by comparing a uniform draw to the per-key rate with a seed of seed + partition index.

nodes.name: getPoissonSamplingFunction
nodes.summary: Returns the per-partition function for sampling with replacement; the exact branch first counts items per key, computes thresholds and replays the same RNG call pattern, the non-exact branch draws a Poisson count per item.

nodes.name: RandomDataGenerator
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps an XORShiftRandom for uniform values and a cache of Poisson distributions keyed by mean, seeded together. Used by the sampling functions and the seqOp.

nodes.name: reSeed
nodes.summary: Reseeds the uniform generator, stores the Poisson seed and clears the Poisson distribution cache.

nodes.name: nextPoisson
nodes.summary: Returns a Poisson sample for the given mean, creating and seeding a PoissonDistribution on first use and caching it.

nodes.name: AcceptanceResult
nodes.summary: Serializable per-stratum record of item count, instantly accepted count, waitlist values, and the accept and waitlist bounds. Used by the seqOp and combOp of StratifiedSamplingUtils.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another optional AcceptanceResult into this one by appending its waitlist and adding its accepted and item counts.

nodes.name: XORShiftRandom.scala
nodes.summary: Implements a XORShift random number generator that extends java.util.Random and avoids thread safety overhead. Used as the default RNG by the samplers and other random utilities in this package.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object hashes the seed with MurmurHash3 so that seed bits are spread out.

nodes.name: XORShiftRandom
nodes.summary: Random number generator subclass of java.util.Random that overrides next(bits) with the xorshift steps and keeps a plain Long seed; the companion object (lines 57-67, merged into this node) provides hashSeed. Has an auxiliary no-argument constructor seeded by nanoTime.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Overrides Random.next(bits): applies the three xor-shift steps to the seed and returns the low bits as an Int; all other nextXxx methods build on it.

nodes.name: setSeed
nodes.summary: Overrides setSeed to store the hashed seed.

nodes.name: hashSeed
nodes.summary: Companion method that hashes a Long seed twice with MurmurHash3 over its bytes and combines the results so the seed has 0/1 bits throughout.

nodes.name: PartitionedPairBuffer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines an append-only buffer of key-value pairs tagged with partition IDs that estimates its own size in bytes. It stores keys and values in one array so it can be sorted in place by partition and optionally key.

nodes.name: PartitionedPairBuffer
nodes.summary: Growable array buffer implementing WritablePartitionedPairCollection and SizeTracker. It holds (partition, key) tuples and values in an interleaved array, supports up to MAXIMUM_CAPACITY elements (defined in the private companion object, merged into this node), and sorts in place with KVArraySortDataFormat.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Appends a (partition, key) entry and value, growing the array first if full, then notifies the size tracker through afterUpdate.

nodes.name: growArray
nodes.summary: Doubles the array capacity (capped at MAXIMUM_CAPACITY), copies the data, and resets the size samples; throws IllegalStateException if already at the maximum.

nodes.name: partitionedDestructiveSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Sorts the buffer in place with a Sorter and KVArraySortDataFormat, using the partition comparator or a partition-then-key comparator, and returns an iterator over the sorted data.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Private method returning an iterator that reads the (partition, key) tuple and value from consecutive array slots.

nodes.name: PrimitiveVector.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PrimitiveVector, an append-only, non-threadsafe, array-backed vector specialized for primitive types. Used where a growable array of Long, Int or Double values is needed without boxing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @specialized(Long, Int, Double) with a ClassTag context bound; the array is assigned after declaration to avoid a duplicate array in the specialized parent.

nodes.name: PrimitiveVector
nodes.summary: Growable array-backed vector with append (+=), indexed access, iterator, trim, resize and toArray. It doubles its backing array when full.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the element at index after checking it is below the current element count.
Appends a value, doubling the backing array first when it is full.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the stored elements that throws NoSuchElementException when exhausted.

nodes.name: resize
nodes.summary: Replaces the backing array with a copy of the new length and shrinks the element count if the new length is smaller; returns this.

nodes.name: toArray
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the backing array trimmed to the current size.

nodes.name: copyArrayWithLength
nodes.summary: Private helper that allocates an array of the given length and copies the current contents into it.

nodes.name: SizeTrackingAppendOnlyMap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SizeTrackingAppendOnlyMap, an append-only hash map that also tracks its estimated size in bytes. It reports each update to the size tracker and resets the size samples when the table grows.

nodes.name: SizeTrackingAppendOnlyMap
nodes.summary: Append-only map that extends AppendOnlyMap and mixes in SizeTracker. After every update or changeValue it calls afterUpdate so that the size estimate stays current, and it resets its samples when the table grows.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Delegates to AppendOnlyMap.update and then calls afterUpdate so the size tracker records the change.

nodes.name: changeValue
nodes.summary: Delegates to AppendOnlyMap.changeValue, calls afterUpdate, and returns the new value.

nodes.name: growTable
nodes.summary: Grows the underlying table through the parent implementation and then resets the size samples, since the old samples no longer reflect the new table.

nodes.name: SortDataFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SortDataFormat abstraction that lets a sorter work on an arbitrary buffer (key lookup, swap, copy, allocate), plus KVArraySortDataFormat for arrays that alternate keys and values.

nodes.name: SortDataFormat
nodes.summary: Abstract class describing how to sort an arbitrary buffer: how to get the sort key for an index, swap elements, copy single elements or ranges, and allocate a new buffer. A sorter is parameterized by an instance of it.

nodes.name: newKey
nodes.summary: Creates a new mutable key for reuse; defaults to null and should be implemented when the reuse variant of getKey is overridden.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Returns the sort key at a position, optionally reusing the given key; the default ignores the reuse parameter and calls the two-argument getKey (which is the protected abstract overload declared at line 47).

nodes.name: swap
nodes.summary: Abstract method that swaps the elements at two positions of the buffer.

nodes.name: copyElement
nodes.summary: Abstract method that copies one element from a source buffer position to a destination buffer position.

nodes.name: copyRange
nodes.summary: Abstract method that copies a range of elements from a source buffer to a destination buffer, allowing overlapping ranges.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Abstract method that allocates a buffer able to hold the given number of elements, whose contents are invalid until data is copied in.

nodes.name: KVArraySortDataFormat
nodes.summary: SortDataFormat for a flat array whose elements alternate between keys and values, as used by AppendOnlyMap. Positions are doubled to address the key and the value of each pair.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Returns the key stored at index 2 * pos of the alternating key-value array.

nodes.name: swap
nodes.summary: Swaps two key-value pairs by exchanging both the key and the value slots.

nodes.name: copyElement
nodes.summary: Copies one key-value pair (two array slots) from source to destination.

nodes.name: copyRange
nodes.summary: Copies a range of key-value pairs using System.arraycopy over twice the element count.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Allocates an array with 2 * length slots so it can hold the requested number of key-value pairs.

nodes.name: Sorter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Sorter, a thin wrapper that makes the package-private Java TimSort usable from the rest of Spark for buffers described by a SortDataFormat.

nodes.name: Sorter
nodes.summary: Wraps TimSort, which is package private in Java, and exposes a sort method over a range [lo, hi) of a buffer using a SortDataFormat and a comparator.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Sorts the buffer within the range [lo, hi) by delegating to the wrapped TimSort with the given comparator.

nodes.name: WritablePartitionedPairCollection.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the interface for size-tracking key-value collections that carry a partition per pair, can be iterated in partition then key order, and can be drained through a WritablePartitionedIterator. Also contains the partition comparators and the iterator class.

nodes.name: WritablePartitionedPairCollection
nodes.summary: Trait (with companion object) for collections of key-value pairs that have an associated partition, a memory-efficient destructive sorted iterator, and a way to write contents directly to a writer. The companion object supplies the partition-only and partition-then-key comparators.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Abstract method that inserts a key-value pair under a partition id.

nodes.name: partitionedDestructiveSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning an iterator over ((partition, key), value) in partition order then by the optional key comparator; it may destroy the underlying collection.

nodes.name: destructiveSortedWritablePartitionedIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps the destructive sorted iterator in a WritablePartitionedIterator so the records can be written out instead of returned.

nodes.name: partitionComparator
nodes.summary: Companion object method returning a comparator on (Int, K) pairs that orders by partition id only.

nodes.name: partitionKeyComparator
nodes.summary: Companion object method returning a comparator that orders (Int, K) pairs by partition id and breaks ties with the supplied key comparator.

nodes.name: WritablePartitionedIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator wrapper that writes each element to a PairsWriter instead of returning it, while exposing the partition id of the current element.

nodes.name: writeNext
nodes.summary: Writes the current key and value to the given PairsWriter and advances to the next element or null.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns true while a current element is available.

nodes.name: nextPartition
nodes.summary: Returns the partition id of the current element.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBufferFileRegion.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ChunkedByteBufferFileRegion, which exposes a ChunkedByteBuffer as a netty FileRegion so that more than 2 GB can be sent in a single netty message even though the data is not backed by a file.

nodes.name: ChunkedByteBufferFileRegion
nodes.summary: Package-private AbstractFileRegion implementation over a ChunkedByteBuffer. It tracks the bytes transferred and the current chunk, and writes chunks to a channel in pieces of at most ioChunkSize, stopping when the channel accepts a partial write.

nodes.name: transferTo
nodes.summary: Writes the remaining chunks to the target channel in ioChunkSize pieces, stops on a short write as netty expects, and returns the bytes written while updating the transferred counter.

nodes.name: RollingPolicy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RollingPolicy trait that decides when and how rolling log files are rolled over, with a time-based and a size-based implementation and their companion constants.

nodes.name: RollingPolicy
nodes.summary: Trait that defines the policy used by RollingFileAppender: whether to roll over now, notifications that a rollover or a write happened, and the suffix of the rolled-over file name.

nodes.name: shouldRollover
nodes.summary: Abstract method telling whether a rollover should start, given the number of bytes about to be written.

nodes.name: rolledOver
nodes.summary: Abstract notification that a rollover has occurred.

nodes.name: bytesWritten
nodes.summary: Abstract notification that the given number of bytes has been written.

nodes.name: generateRolledOverFileSuffix
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the desired name suffix of the rolled-over file.

nodes.name: TimeBasedRollingPolicy
nodes.summary: RollingPolicy that rolls files over at a fixed interval. It raises intervals below the 60 second minimum (with a warning), computes the next rollover time on the interval grid, and formats the file suffix from a configurable date pattern. The companion object holds MINIMUM_INTERVAL_SECONDS.

nodes.name: shouldRollover
nodes.summary: Returns true when the current time has passed the next rollover time.

nodes.name: rolledOver
nodes.summary: Recomputes the next rollover time after a rollover and logs it at debug level.

nodes.name: bytesWritten
nodes.summary: No-op, since the time-based policy ignores bytes written.

nodes.name: calculateNextRolloverTime
nodes.summary: Computes the next rollover time by rounding the current time up to the next multiple of the rollover interval.

nodes.name: generateRolledOverFileSuffix
nodes.summary: Formats the current time with the configured suffix pattern to name the rolled-over file.

nodes.name: SizeBasedRollingPolicy
nodes.summary: RollingPolicy that rolls files over once a size limit is reached. It enforces a minimum size (ten times RollingFileAppender.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE, with a warning), counts bytes written since the last rollover, and names files with a timestamp suffix. The companion object holds MINIMUM_SIZE_BYTES.

nodes.name: shouldRollover
nodes.summary: Returns true when the bytes about to be written plus the bytes written since the last rollover would exceed the size limit.

nodes.name: rolledOver
nodes.summary: Resets the counter of bytes written since the last rollover.

nodes.name: bytesWritten
nodes.summary: Adds the given bytes to the counter for the current file.

nodes.name: generateRolledOverFileSuffix
nodes.summary: Formats the current time as a timestamp suffix for the rolled-over file name.

nodes.name: Pseudorandom.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Pseudorandom trait, a developer API marker for classes with pseudorandom behavior that can have their random seed set.

nodes.name: Pseudorandom
nodes.summary: Developer API trait declaring setSeed(seed: Long), implemented by classes whose pseudorandom behavior can be re-seeded.

nodes.name: setSeed
nodes.summary: Abstract method that sets the random seed.

nodes.name: ApplicationDescription.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ApplicationDescription case class that a standalone application client sends to the Master when it registers. It carries the application name, core limit, launch Command, UI URL, default resource profile and event log settings.

nodes.name: ApplicationDescription
nodes.summary: Case class describing an application submitted to a standalone cluster: name, optional maximum cores, the executor launch Command, the application UI URL, the default ResourceProfile, optional event log directory and codec, optional initial executor limit and the user name. It derives per-executor memory, cores and custom resource requirements from the default profile.

nodes.name: memoryPerExecutorMB
nodes.summary: Returns the executor memory in MB from the default resource profile, falling back to 1024 when the profile does not define it.

nodes.name: coresPerExecutor
nodes.summary: Returns the optional executor core count from the default resource profile.

nodes.name: resourceReqsPerExecutor
nodes.summary: Converts the custom executor resource requests of the default profile, sorted by resource name, into a sequence of ResourceRequirement through ResourceUtils.

nodes.name: Client.scala
nodes.summary: Standalone cluster driver client: ClientEndpoint is an RPC endpoint that submits or kills a driver on the Master(s) and polls its status, Client is the deprecated main entry, and ClientApp is the SparkApplication that wires up the RpcEnv and the endpoint.

nodes.name: ClientEndpoint
nodes.summary: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint used by the standalone client to relay messages to the driver. On start it sends RequestSubmitDriver (launch) or RequestKillDriver (kill) to every Master, then polls RequestDriverStatus on a schedule, handles the replies, and exits the JVM on failure, on a terminal driver state, or when not configured to wait for completion. There is no retry if submission fails.

nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: Deprecated executable object for starting and terminating drivers in a standalone cluster. Its main prints a deprecation warning unless SPARK_SUBMIT is set, then runs a ClientApp.

nodes.name: ClientApp
nodes.summary: SparkApplication that parses ClientArguments, sets the RPC ask timeout default to 10s and the root log level, creates the driverClient RpcEnv, sets up endpoint refs for all master URLs and registers a ClientEndpoint named client, then blocks until the RpcEnv terminates.

nodes.name: getProperty
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the JVM system properties first and then in the SparkConf.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: For the launch command builds the DriverWrapper Command from driver class path, library path and Java options and a DriverDescription, and sends RequestSubmitDriver; for kill sends RequestKillDriver. Then schedules monitorDriverStatus at a fixed rate.

nodes.name: asyncSendToMasterAndForwardReply
nodes.summary: Asks every master endpoint the given message and forwards each successful reply to the endpoint itself, logging a warning on failure.

nodes.name: monitorDriverStatus
nodes.summary: Sends RequestDriverStatus for the submitted driver id when one is set.

nodes.name: reportDriverStatus
nodes.summary: Handles a driver status reply: logs the state once, exits the JVM with -1 on an exception or an unrecognized driver, with 0 when the driver finished, failed, errored or was killed, or when not waiting for application completion; otherwise keeps monitoring.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles SubmitDriverResponse, KillDriverResponse and DriverStatusResponse messages; records the active master and submitted driver id, exits with -1 on a failed response not coming from a backup master, and delegates status replies to reportDriverStatus.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: Remembers a lost master address and exits the JVM with -1 once every master has been lost.

nodes.name: onNetworkError
nodes.summary: Logs a network error for a master, records it as lost and exits the JVM with -1 when all masters are lost.

nodes.name: onError
nodes.summary: Logs the error and exits the JVM with -1.

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the scheduled executor used to forward messages.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Prints a deprecation warning pointing to spark-submit when SPARK_SUBMIT is not set and runs new ClientApp().start with a fresh SparkConf.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Builds the driverClient RpcEnv from ClientArguments, creates endpoint refs for the masters, registers the ClientEndpoint and awaits termination.

nodes.name: DriverDescription.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DriverDescription case class that describes a driver to launch on a standalone worker.

nodes.name: DriverDescription
nodes.summary: Case class holding the jar URL, memory, cores, supervise flag, launch Command and resource requirements of a driver submitted to a standalone cluster. It is carried by RequestSubmitDriver and LaunchDriver and its toString shows the main class of the command.

nodes.name: ExecutorDescription.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorDescription, the on-the-wire summary of an executor sent from Worker to Master.

nodes.name: ExecutorDescription
nodes.summary: Serializable class sent from a Worker to the Master with an executor's app id, executor id, resource profile id, cores, memory in MB and ExecutorState. This is enough state for the Master to rebuild its internal data structures during failover.

nodes.name: ExecutorFailureTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Tracks executor failure timestamps per host and overall, and computes the default maximum number of executor failures from configuration.

nodes.name: ExecutorFailureTracker
nodes.summary: Records the time of each executor failure, both overall and per host, and counts failures that are still inside the configured validity interval (expired entries are dequeued). The companion object computes the maximum allowed number of executor failures: the configured value, or twice the effective executor count with a minimum of 3.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id.

nodes.name: updateAndCountFailures
nodes.summary: Drops failure timestamps older than the validity interval from the head of the queue (when the interval is positive) and returns the remaining count.

nodes.name: numFailedExecutors
nodes.summary: Returns the number of recent executor failures across all hosts.

nodes.name: registerFailureOnHost
nodes.summary: Records a failure timestamp both in the overall queue and in the queue of the given host, creating the host queue if needed.

nodes.name: registerExecutorFailure
nodes.summary: Records a failure timestamp in the overall queue only.

nodes.name: numFailuresOnHost
nodes.summary: Returns the number of recent failures on one host, or 0 when the host has none.

nodes.name: maxNumExecutorFailures
nodes.summary: Returns the configured MAX_EXECUTOR_FAILURES, or by default max(3, 2 * the effective executor count) where the count comes from streaming dynamic allocation max, dynamic allocation max, or the executor instances setting, guarding against integer overflow.

nodes.name: ExternalShuffleService.scala
nodes.summary: Standalone external shuffle service: a server that lets executors' shuffle files be read through a block handler even after executors are stopped, plus a main object to run it as a process.

nodes.name: ExternalShuffleService
nodes.summary: Provides a TransportServer, backed by an ExternalBlockHandler, from which executors' shuffle files can be read, so the files stay available when executors are turned off or killed. It optionally uses SASL authentication, can persist registered executors in a DB under the local dirs, and exposes metrics through a source. The companion object holds the main entry that builds the service, starts it, installs a shutdown hook and blocks until terminated.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id; the object has a public main and a private[spark] main overload that accepts a custom service factory.

nodes.name: findRegisteredExecutorsDBFile
nodes.summary: Resolves the file for the registered executors DB inside the first spark.local.dir entry that already contains it (or the first entry); warns and returns null when spark.local.dir is not set.

nodes.name: getBlockHandler
nodes.summary: Returns the ExternalBlockHandler of this service.

nodes.name: newShuffleBlockHandler
nodes.summary: Creates the ExternalBlockHandler with the configured local dirs, using an on-disk registered executors DB when the shuffle service DB option and the service are both enabled. Factored out so subclasses can override it.

nodes.name: startIfEnabled
nodes.summary: Calls start when the shuffle service is enabled in the configuration.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the transport server on the configured port, adding an AuthServerBootstrap when authentication is enabled, then registers the server and block handler metrics and starts the metrics system.

nodes.name: applicationRemoved
nodes.summary: Cleans up all shuffle files of an application that has exited, including its local dirs.

nodes.name: executorRemoved
nodes.summary: Cleans up the non-shuffle files associated with an executor that has exited.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the transport server and transport context and clears the references.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point for the process: loads default Spark properties, resets logging, forces the shuffle service enabled flag, builds the service through the supplied factory, starts it, adds a shutdown hook that stops it and blocks on a latch. The one-argument main (lines 162-164) delegates here with the default factory.

nodes.name: DeployMessage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines every RPC message exchanged between the standalone Master, Workers, application clients, driver clients and the Master and Worker web UIs, all grouped inside the DeployMessages object under a sealed DeployMessage trait.

nodes.name: DeployMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed serializable marker trait extended by most standalone deploy messages.

nodes.name: DeployMessages
nodes.summary: Container object holding the message case classes and case objects of the standalone deploy protocol, grouped by direction: Worker to Master, Master to Worker, worker internal, AppClient to Master, Master to AppClient, DriverClient and Master, Master to MasterWebUI, WorkerWebUI and Worker, and liveness checks.

nodes.name: RegisterWorker
nodes.summary: Worker to Master registration request with the worker id, host, port, endpoint ref, cores, memory, web UI URL, the master address it used and its resources. It validates the host and requires a positive port.

nodes.name: DecommissionWorkers
nodes.summary: Internal message used by the Master itself to handle a DecommissionWorkersOnHosts request from MasterWebUI asynchronously, carrying the worker ids to decommission.

nodes.name: DecommissionWorker
nodes.summary: Case object sent from Master to Worker to decommission it, used when decommission is triggered at MasterWebUI; all executors on that Worker are decommissioned too.

nodes.name: WorkerDecommissionSigReceived
nodes.summary: Case object the Worker sends to itself when it receives a signal indicating that it should start decommissioning.

nodes.name: WorkerDecommissioning
nodes.summary: Message from Worker to Master telling it that the Worker has started decommissioning, used when decommission is triggered at the Worker.

nodes.name: ExecutorStateChanged
nodes.summary: Worker to Master message reporting that an executor of an application changed state, with the optional message and exit status.

nodes.name: DriverStateChanged
nodes.summary: Worker to Master message reporting that a driver changed state, with an optional exception.

nodes.name: WorkerExecutorStateResponse
nodes.summary: Pairs an ExecutorDescription with the resources assigned to that executor, as part of a worker's scheduler state response.

nodes.name: WorkerDriverStateResponse
nodes.summary: Pairs a driver id with the resources assigned to that driver, as part of a worker's scheduler state response.

nodes.name: WorkerSchedulerStateResponse
nodes.summary: Worker's scheduler state: a list of executor responses and a sequence of driver responses, identified by worker id.

nodes.name: WorkerLatestState
nodes.summary: Message a Worker sends to the Master when it registers, listing its executors and driver ids. The Master compares them with its own records and tells the worker to kill unknown executors and drivers.

nodes.name: Heartbeat
nodes.summary: Worker to Master heartbeat carrying the worker id and the worker endpoint ref.

nodes.name: DecommissionWorkersOnHosts
nodes.summary: Used by MasterWebUI to ask the Master to decommission all active workers on any of the given hostnames (hostnames without ports).

nodes.name: RegisterWorkerResponse
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the possible Master responses to a worker registration: RegisteredWorker, RegisterWorkerFailed and MasterInStandby.

nodes.name: RegisteredWorker
nodes.summary: Master to Worker response confirming registration, with the master ref, the master web UI URL, the master address and a flag for duplicate registration requests.

nodes.name: RegisterWorkerFailed
nodes.summary: Master to Worker response saying that registration failed, with a message.

nodes.name: MasterInStandby
nodes.summary: Case object response meaning the contacted Master is in standby and cannot register the worker.

nodes.name: ReconnectWorker
nodes.summary: Master to Worker message telling the worker to reconnect to the given master URL.

nodes.name: KillExecutor
nodes.summary: Master to Worker request to kill the executor with the given app id and executor id.

nodes.name: LaunchExecutor
nodes.summary: Master to Worker request to launch an executor for an application, with the ApplicationDescription, resource profile id, cores, memory and assigned resources.

nodes.name: LaunchDriver
nodes.summary: Master to Worker request to launch a driver, with its DriverDescription and assigned resources.

nodes.name: KillDriver
nodes.summary: Master to Worker request to kill the driver with the given id.

nodes.name: ApplicationFinished
nodes.summary: Message carrying the id of an application that has finished.

nodes.name: WorkDirCleanup
nodes.summary: Case object sent to the Worker endpoint periodically to clean up application folders.

nodes.name: ReregisterWithMaster
nodes.summary: Case object used when a worker attempts to reconnect to a master.

nodes.name: RegisterApplication
nodes.summary: AppClient to Master request to register an application, with its ApplicationDescription and the driver endpoint ref.

nodes.name: UnregisterApplication
nodes.summary: AppClient to Master message to unregister the application with the given id.

nodes.name: MasterChangeAcknowledged
nodes.summary: AppClient to Master acknowledgement for the given app id after a master change.

nodes.name: RequestExecutors
nodes.summary: AppClient to Master request for the total number of executors wanted per ResourceProfile for an application.

nodes.name: KillExecutors
nodes.summary: AppClient to Master request to kill the listed executor ids of an application.

nodes.name: RegisteredApplication
nodes.summary: Master to AppClient response confirming registration, with the assigned app id and the master ref.

nodes.name: ExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Master to AppClient notification that an executor was added on a worker, with host and port, cores and memory; it validates the host and port.

nodes.name: ExecutorUpdated
nodes.summary: Master to AppClient notification of an executor state change, with an optional message, exit status and the worker host when that host is lost or decommissioned.

nodes.name: ApplicationRemoved
nodes.summary: Master to AppClient notification that the application was removed, with a message.

nodes.name: WorkerRemoved
nodes.summary: Master to AppClient notification that a worker was removed, with its id, host and a message.

nodes.name: RequestSubmitDriver
nodes.summary: DriverClient to Master request to submit a driver described by a DriverDescription.

nodes.name: SubmitDriverResponse
nodes.summary: Master reply to a driver submission with the master ref, a success flag, an optional driver id and a message.

nodes.name: RequestKillDriver
nodes.summary: DriverClient to Master request to kill the driver with the given id.

nodes.name: KillDriverResponse
nodes.summary: Master reply to a kill driver request with the master ref, driver id, success flag and message.

nodes.name: RequestKillAllDrivers
nodes.summary: Case object request to kill all drivers.

nodes.name: KillAllDriversResponse
nodes.summary: Master reply to a request to kill all drivers, with the master ref, success flag and message.

nodes.name: RequestDriverStatus
nodes.summary: DriverClient to Master request for the status of the driver with the given id.

nodes.name: DriverStatusResponse
nodes.summary: Master reply to a driver status request: whether the driver was found, its optional state, worker id, worker host and port, and an optional exception.

nodes.name: RequestClearCompletedDriversAndApps
nodes.summary: Case object request to clear the Master's completed drivers and applications.

nodes.name: RequestReadyz
nodes.summary: Case object readiness check request to the Master.

nodes.name: StopAppClient
nodes.summary: Case object internal to the AppClient used to stop it.

nodes.name: MasterChanged
nodes.summary: Master to Worker and AppClient message announcing a new master ref and its web UI URL.

nodes.name: RequestMasterState
nodes.summary: Case object sent from MasterWebUI to the Master to request its state.

nodes.name: MasterStateResponse
nodes.summary: Master reply to MasterWebUI with host, port, optional REST port, arrays of WorkerInfo, active and completed ApplicationInfo, active and completed DriverInfo and the master recovery state. It validates host and port and builds spark:// URIs for the master and the REST port.

nodes.name: RequestWorkerState
nodes.summary: Case object sent from WorkerWebUI to the Worker to request its state.

nodes.name: WorkerStateResponse
nodes.summary: Worker reply to WorkerWebUI with host, port, worker id, running and finished ExecutorRunner and DriverRunner lists, master URL, cores and memory totals and use, web UI URL and resources. It validates host and port.

nodes.name: SendHeartbeat
nodes.summary: Case object used for liveness checks in various places.

nodes.name: ExecutorState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutorState enumeration used for standalone executor lifecycle states and a helper that tells which states are finished.

nodes.name: ExecutorState
nodes.summary: Enumeration with the states LAUNCHING, RUNNING, KILLED, FAILED, LOST, EXITED and DECOMMISSIONED, plus the type alias ExecutorState. DECOMMISSIONED is not counted as finished because the executor still exists on the worker but should get no new tasks.

nodes.name: isFinished
nodes.summary: Returns true when the state is one of KILLED, FAILED, LOST or EXITED.

nodes.name: FaultToleranceTest.scala
nodes.summary: Standalone-mode fault tolerance test harness that starts Master and Worker processes in Docker containers, kills leaders and checks that the cluster recovers. Run by hand via spark-class, since it needs a working Docker installation and a ZooKeeper-based recovery mode.

nodes.name: FaultToleranceTest
nodes.summary: Application object holding the fault tolerance scenarios (sanity-basic, single-master-halt, rolling-outage and others) for the standalone Master. It tracks the started Master and Worker containers, creates a SparkContext client against them, and asserts that exactly one Master is ALIVE and all workers are registered.

nodes.name: afterEach
nodes.summary: Cleanup run after each scenario: stops the SparkContext, terminates all containers and recursively deletes the spark_leader and master_status ZooKeeper directories for speed between tests.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Runs one named scenario body, counts it as passed or failed, logs the outcome (exiting the JVM with status 1 on failure) and then calls afterEach.

nodes.name: addMasters
nodes.summary: Starts the requested number of Master containers through SparkDocker and appends them to the tracked master list.

nodes.name: addWorkers
nodes.summary: Starts the requested number of Worker containers pointed at the current master URLs and appends them to the tracked worker list.

nodes.name: createClient
nodes.summary: Stops any previous SparkContext, resets the driver port property and creates a new SparkContext against the current masters, which exercises the standalone client.

nodes.name: getMasterUrls
nodes.summary: Builds the comma separated spark:// URL string (port 7077) for a sequence of test masters.

nodes.name: getLeader
nodes.summary: Returns the single master whose recovery state is ALIVE, asserting that exactly one such master exists.

nodes.name: killLeader
nodes.summary: Refreshes the state of all masters, finds the current leader, removes it from the tracked list and kills its container.

nodes.name: terminateCluster
nodes.summary: Kills every Master and Worker container and clears both tracking lists.

nodes.name: assertUsable
nodes.summary: Checks the cluster can run a small parallelize/collect job on the SparkContext, waiting up to two minutes (the client retry logic may make this slow while the cluster recovers).

nodes.name: assertValidClusterState
nodes.summary: Asserts the cluster is usable and then polls master state until all expected workers are live, exactly one master is ALIVE, the others are STANDBY and at least one application is live; fails after two minutes with diagnostic logging.

nodes.name: assertTrue
nodes.summary: Throws an IllegalStateException with the given message when the condition is false.

nodes.name: TestMasterInfo
nodes.summary: Test-side handle for one Master container (IP, Docker id, log file). It reads the Master JSON status page over HTTP to track the recovery state, live worker IPs and live application count, and can kill its container.

nodes.name: readState
nodes.summary: Fetches http://<ip>:8080/json, parses it, and updates the live worker IPs (taken from webuiaddress), the number of active apps and the master recovery state; exceptions are logged and ignored.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Kills this master container through Docker.kill.

nodes.name: TestWorkerInfo
nodes.summary: Test-side handle for one Worker container (IP, Docker id, log file) that can kill its container.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Kills this worker container through Docker.kill.

nodes.name: SparkDocker
nodes.summary: Helper object that launches Master and Worker containers by building a docker run command and waiting for the container to print its IP address.

nodes.name: startMaster
nodes.summary: Starts a spark-test-master container with the given mount directory and wraps the result in a TestMasterInfo.

nodes.name: startWorker
nodes.summary: Starts a spark-test-worker container with the given master URLs and mount directory and wraps the result in a TestWorkerInfo.

nodes.name: startNode
nodes.summary: Runs a docker command, captures its output into a temp log file, waits up to 30 seconds for the CONTAINER_IP= line, and returns the IP, the last container id and the log file.

nodes.name: DockerId
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around a Docker container id string whose toString returns the id.

nodes.name: Docker
nodes.summary: Helper object that builds docker run commands, kills containers and looks up the id of the most recently started container using the docker command line.

nodes.name: makeRunCmd
nodes.summary: Builds a docker run command string for an image tag with optional arguments and volume mount, logs it and converts it to a ProcessBuilder.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Runs docker kill for the given container id.

nodes.name: getLastProcessId
nodes.summary: Runs docker ps -l -q and returns the id of the latest container as a DockerId.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JSON serialization of standalone cluster state (workers, applications, drivers, executors, master and worker state) as json4s objects.

nodes.name: JsonProtocol
nodes.summary: Object with write* methods that convert WorkerInfo, ApplicationInfo, ApplicationDescription, ExecutorRunner, DriverInfo, MasterStateResponse and WorkerStateResponse into json4s JObjects with fixed lowercase field names, plus a cluster utilization summary. Private to the deploy package.

nodes.name: writeResourcesInfo
nodes.summary: Converts a map of resource name to ResourceInformation into a JObject by calling toJson on each entry.

nodes.name: writeResourceRequirement
nodes.summary: Converts a ResourceRequirement into a JSON object with name and amount fields.

nodes.name: writeWorkerInfo
nodes.summary: Exports a WorkerInfo as JSON with id, host, port, web UI address, cores, memory and resource usage (total, used, free), state and last heartbeat.

nodes.name: writeApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Exports an ApplicationInfo as JSON with id, start time, name, cores, user, per-executor memory and resources (also under the deprecated perslave names), submit date, state and duration.

nodes.name: writeApplicationDescription
nodes.summary: Exports an ApplicationDescription as JSON, redacting secret-bearing environment and Java options in the command using the configured redaction regex.

nodes.name: writeExecutorRunner
nodes.summary: Exports an ExecutorRunner as JSON with executor id, memory, resources, app id and the nested application description.

nodes.name: writeDriverInfo
nodes.summary: Exports a DriverInfo as JSON with id, start time, state, cores, memory, resources, submit date, worker id and main class.

nodes.name: writeMasterState
nodes.summary: Exports a MasterStateResponse as JSON (url, workers, alive workers, cores and memory totals over alive workers, active and completed apps and drivers, status), or only the single requested field when one is given.

nodes.name: writeWorkerState
nodes.summary: Exports a WorkerStateResponse as JSON with worker id, master URL and web UI URL, cores, memory, resources and the running and finished executors.

nodes.name: writeClusterUtilization
nodes.summary: Computes cluster utilization from a MasterStateResponse: number of waiting (SUBMITTED) drivers, cores and memory totals and used amounts over alive workers, and the utilization percentages (100 when the total is zero).

nodes.name: LocalSparkCluster.scala
nodes.summary: Testing helper that runs a standalone Master and several Workers inside one JVM, while executors still run in separate JVMs.

nodes.name: LocalSparkCluster
