nodes.summary: Class (with companion object) that starts a Master and a configurable number of Workers in the same JVM with their own RpcEnvs, exposes the master web UI port and worker log files for tests, and shuts everything down in worker-then-master order. The companion object keeps the most recently created instance and its apply method creates it.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the Master (REST server disabled and shuffle service off unless configured otherwise) and then the requested number of Workers, using temp work directories when testing; returns the master URL array.

nodes.name: workerLogfiles
nodes.summary: Lists all files ending in .log under the temporary worker directories (test only).

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down worker RpcEnvs before master RpcEnvs, waits for termination, clears the tracking buffers and clears the companion singleton.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a LocalSparkCluster, stores it as the current local cluster and returns it.

nodes.name: PythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonRunner, the main class that launches a Python application as a subprocess, starts a Py4J gateway server for it to connect back to the JVM, and builds its PYTHONPATH and environment variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object with a main method; also holds path-formatting helpers that are reused by other launchers.

nodes.name: PythonRunner
nodes.summary: Singleton main class used to launch Python applications. It runs python as a subprocess, optionally starts a Py4J gateway server, passes configuration through environment variables, redirects the child output and throws SparkUserAppException on a non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Picks the Python executable, formats the file paths, starts the Py4J gateway server (unless a remote is configured in connect mode), builds PYTHONPATH and the environment, runs the Python process, waits for it and shuts the gateway down.

nodes.name: formatPath
nodes.summary: Converts a local Python file path (possibly with a file or local URI scheme) into a plain path suitable for PYTHONPATH, rejecting non-local paths and malformed paths and stripping the leading slash before a Windows drive letter.

nodes.name: formatPaths
nodes.summary: Splits a comma-delimited list of Python file paths, drops empty entries and formats each one with formatPath.

nodes.name: resolvePyFiles
nodes.summary: Replaces local .py files with a temporary directory containing copies of them, because PYTHONPATH expects directories rather than single files; other entries are kept and the result is de-duplicated.

nodes.name: RPackageUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RPackageUtils, which detects R source code inside a jar through a manifest key, extracts it, installs it with an R command and zips built R libraries for distribution to the cluster.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala private[deploy] object mixing in Logging; uses MDC log interpolators for structured messages.

nodes.name: RPackageUtils
nodes.summary: Private deploy-package utility object for building R packages that ship inside jars. It looks for the Spark-HasRPackage manifest entry, extracts the R/pkg folder to a temporary directory, runs the R install command, and bundles built libraries into a zip file.

nodes.name: print
nodes.summary: Logs a message either to the given PrintStream (used in tests, with an optional stack trace) or to the logger at the level that matches the supplied java.util.logging level.

nodes.name: checkManifestForR
nodes.summary: Returns true if the jar manifest exists and its main attributes contain Spark-HasRPackage set to true, meaning the jar bundles R source code.

nodes.name: rPackageBuilder
nodes.summary: Runs the R CMD INSTALL command on the extracted R/pkg folder into the given library directory, with SparkR package paths and profile set in the environment, and returns whether the process exited with 0.

nodes.name: extractRFolder
nodes.summary: Copies every jar entry located under R/pkg into a new temporary directory, creating directories and files as needed, and returns that directory.

nodes.name: checkAndBuildRPackage
nodes.summary: For each comma-separated jar path that exists, checks the manifest for R code and, when present, extracts and builds the R package into the shared R packages directory, printing the layout documentation on failure and cleaning up afterward.

nodes.name: listFilesRecursively
nodes.summary: Recursively lists all files under a directory, skipping names that contain any of the given exclude patterns.

nodes.name: zipRLibraries
nodes.summary: Creates a fresh zip file named by the caller inside the directory, containing all non-zip files below it with relative paths that always use forward slashes, and returns the zip file.

nodes.name: RRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RRunner, the main class used by spark-submit to launch an R application: it starts an RBackend server thread, runs R as a subprocess that connects back to it, and propagates the R exit code.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object with a single main method that coordinates a backend thread with a semaphore.

nodes.name: RRunner
nodes.summary: Singleton main class for launching SparkR applications. It starts an RBackend in a separate thread, waits for it to initialize, launches the R command with connection settings in the environment, redirects output and fails when the backend does not start or R exits with a non-zero code.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Resolves the R file and command from system properties, starts the backend thread and waits up to a timeout for it to initialize, then runs R with backend port, secret and package directories in the environment, and throws SparkUserAppException on failure or SparkException on a backend timeout.

nodes.name: RedirectConsolePlugin.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a built-in plugin that redirects stdout and stderr of the driver and executors to the logging system, together with the PrintStream and line-buffer helpers that implement the redirection.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a SparkPlugin class and companion object, driver and executor plugin classes, and private[spark] helper classes.

nodes.name: RedirectConsolePlugin
nodes.summary: SparkPlugin that supplies a driver-side and an executor-side plugin for redirecting console output to logging. Its companion object holds the helpers that replace System.out and System.err with logging print streams.

nodes.name: DriverRedirectConsolePlugin
nodes.summary: Driver plugin that reads the configured driver console outputs and redirects stdout and/or stderr to the logging system during init.

nodes.name: ExecRedirectConsolePlugin
nodes.summary: Executor plugin that reads the configured executor console outputs and redirects stdout and/or stderr to the logging system during init.

nodes.name: LoggingPrintStream
nodes.summary: PrintStream that writes into a LineBuffer and, after every write, forwards each completed line to a callback such as a logger method.

nodes.name: LineBuffer
nodes.summary: ByteArrayOutputStream that accumulates bytes and yields a line when a line separator is seen or when a size threshold is reached; its companion object caches the line separator bytes.

nodes.name: redirectStdoutToLog
nodes.summary: Replaces System.out with a LoggingPrintStream that sends each line to the info level of the stdout logger.

nodes.name: redirectStderrToLog
nodes.summary: Replaces System.err with a LoggingPrintStream that sends each line to the error level of the stderr logger.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Redirects the driver stdout and stderr to logging according to the driver redirect-console-outputs configuration and returns an empty map of extra configuration.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Redirects the executor stdout and stderr to logging according to the executor redirect-console-outputs configuration.

nodes.name: tryLogCurrentLine
nodes.summary: Synchronized helper that asks the underlying LineBuffer for a completed line and passes it to the redirect callback.

nodes.name: tryGenerateContext
nodes.summary: Returns the buffered text as a line when the buffer ends with the line separator (without the separator) or when the maximum size is reached, resetting the buffer; otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: isLineEnded
nodes.summary: Checks whether the last bytes in the buffer match the platform line separator, with a fast path for a single-byte separator.

nodes.name: SparkApplication.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SparkApplication trait, the entry-point abstraction for a Spark application, and JavaMainApplication, which adapts a plain Java class with a static main method to that trait.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait plus a private[deploy] implementation that uses reflection to find and invoke main.

nodes.name: SparkApplication
nodes.summary: Private[spark] trait describing the entry point of a Spark application: implementations provide a no-argument constructor and a start method taking arguments and a SparkConf.

nodes.name: JavaMainApplication
nodes.summary: SparkApplication that wraps a standard class with a static main method. Configuration is passed through system properties, so running several in one JVM can leak configuration.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Looks up the static main method of the wrapped class by reflection (failing if it is not static), copies all SparkConf entries into system properties and invokes main with the arguments.

nodes.name: SparkCuratorUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Provides helpers for creating a Curator ZooKeeper client from Spark configuration and for creating and recursively deleting ZooKeeper paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala private[spark] singleton object that mixes in Logging and holds timeout and retry constants.

nodes.name: SparkCuratorUtil
nodes.summary: Private[spark] utility object for ZooKeeper access through Curator: it builds and starts a client with fixed session and connection timeouts and an exponential backoff retry, and offers mkdir and recursive delete helpers.

nodes.name: newClient
nodes.summary: Reads the ZooKeeper URL from the given configuration key (default is the standard ZooKeeper URL setting), creates a Curator client with the object timeouts and retry policy, starts it and returns it.

nodes.name: mkdir
nodes.summary: Creates the path including missing parents when it does not exist, ignoring a node-already-exists race.

nodes.name: deleteRecursive
nodes.summary: If the path exists, deletes each of its children and then the path itself.

nodes.name: SparkHadoopUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkHadoopUtil and its companion object, the helpers Spark uses to interact with Hadoop: building Hadoop Configuration from SparkConf and environment AWS variables, authenticating as the Spark user, serializing delegation tokens, tracking FileSystem byte statistics, and listing or globbing paths.

nodes.name: SparkHadoopUtil
nodes.summary: Class and companion object that bundle helpers for talking to Hadoop from Spark: building Hadoop Configuration objects from SparkConf, running code as the Spark user, moving delegation tokens, reading FileSystem statistics and globbing or listing paths. Its companion object (line 347 onward) holds the lazily created singleton returned by get plus constants naming where each configuration option came from.

nodes.name: runAsSparkUser
nodes.summary: Runs a no-argument function inside doAs of the UserGroupInformation produced by createSparkUser, so HDFS and YARN calls use the Spark user identity.

nodes.name: createSparkUser
nodes.summary: Creates a remote-user UserGroupInformation for the current user name and copies the current user credentials into it.

nodes.name: transferCredentials
nodes.summary: Adds the credentials of a source UserGroupInformation to a destination one.

nodes.name: appendS3AndSparkHadoopHiveConfigurations
nodes.summary: Companion-object version (the class has a public delegating overload): when the conf is non-null, copies S3 credentials from environment variables, hive-site.xml entries, spark.hadoop.* and spark.hive.* entries, and the spark buffer size into a Hadoop Configuration.

nodes.name: appendSparkHadoopConfigs
nodes.summary: Companion-object version for ReadOnlySparkConf: strips the spark.hadoop. prefix from matching keys into the Hadoop Configuration and sets defaults for the output committer algorithm version and the s3a syncable exception downgrade unless the user set them. The class has two further public overloads (one for SparkConf, one copying between maps) that share this id.

nodes.name: appendSparkHiveConfigs
nodes.summary: Copies keys starting with spark.hive. from a map into a destination map as hive.* keys. The companion object has a private overload for ReadOnlySparkConf and Hadoop Configuration that shares this id.

nodes.name: newConfiguration
nodes.summary: Instance method that builds a Hadoop Configuration from a SparkConf through the companion object and then adds the gateway Hadoop conf file as a resource. The companion object has an overload taking ReadOnlySparkConf that shares this id and only applies the Spark settings.

nodes.name: loginUserFromKeytab
nodes.summary: Logs in to Kerberos with the given principal and keytab, throwing a SparkException if the keytab file does not exist.

nodes.name: addDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Resets the Hadoop configuration, deserializes the given token bytes into Credentials, logs the tokens and adds them to the current user.

nodes.name: getFSBytesReadOnThreadCallback
nodes.summary: Returns a callback giving the bytes read from Hadoop FileSystems since the call was made, summing per-thread statistics so child threads and the parent task thread are both counted.

nodes.name: getFSBytesWrittenOnThreadCallback
nodes.summary: Returns a callback giving the bytes written to Hadoop FileSystems by the calling thread since the call was made.

nodes.name: listLeafStatuses
nodes.summary: Recursively lists FileStatus objects for all files under a base status, or returns the status itself when it is a file. A second overload takes a Path and shares this id.

nodes.name: isGlobPath
nodes.summary: Returns true if the path string contains any glob character such as braces, brackets, star, question mark or backslash.

nodes.name: globPath
nodes.summary: Expands a glob pattern through FileSystem.globStatus into qualified paths, returning an empty sequence when nothing matches. An overload taking only a Path obtains the FileSystem from the conf and shares this id.

nodes.name: globPathIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Globs the pattern only if it contains glob characters, otherwise returns it unchanged as a single path. An overload taking a FileSystem shares this id.

nodes.name: substituteHadoopVariables
nodes.summary: Replaces ${hadoopconf-...} placeholders in a string with values looked up in a Hadoop Configuration, recursing until no more placeholders resolve.

nodes.name: dumpTokens
nodes.summary: Maps the tokens of a Credentials object to printable strings, or returns an empty collection when the credentials are null.

nodes.name: tokenToString
nodes.summary: Formats a Hadoop token for logging; for abstract delegation token identifiers it appends renewer, issue date and maximum date in readable form, and logs at debug if decoding fails.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes a Credentials object to a byte array using writeTokenStorageToStream.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Reads a Credentials object back from a byte array of serialized token storage.

nodes.name: appendS3CredentialsFromEnvironment
nodes.summary: When both access key ID and secret key are non-null, sets the s3, s3n and s3a credential options on the Hadoop Configuration (plus endpoint and session token when given) with a source string that includes the local host name.

nodes.name: appendHiveConfigs
nodes.summary: Copies every entry from the lazily loaded hive-site.xml key list into the Hadoop Configuration, labelled with the hive-site source string.

nodes.name: propertySources
nodes.summary: Returns the comma-joined origins recorded for a configuration key in a Hadoop Configuration, or an empty string when none are known.

nodes.name: createFile
nodes.summary: Creates an output stream on a file system; when erasure coding is not allowed it creates parent directories and uses the builder API with replicate() for HDFS builders, otherwise it calls fs.create directly.

nodes.name: isFile
nodes.summary: Returns whether a path is a file, treating FileNotFoundException as false.

nodes.name: SparkPipelines.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the SparkPipelines object, the outer launcher of the spark-pipelines command line interface that routes spark-submit arguments to SparkSubmit and passes pipeline-specific arguments on to the inner CLI file.

nodes.name: SparkPipelines
nodes.summary: Outer command line entry point for the spark-pipelines tool. It splits incoming arguments into spark-submit options and pipeline-specific options, forces the Spark Connect API mode, and calls SparkSubmit.main with the pipelines CLI file followed by the pipeline arguments.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Takes the pipelines CLI file from the first argument, builds the spark-submit argument list from the rest and invokes SparkSubmit.main.

nodes.name: constructSparkSubmitArgs
nodes.summary: Splits the arguments and returns the spark-submit arguments, then the CLI file, then the pipeline arguments as one sequence.

nodes.name: splitArgs
nodes.summary: Uses an anonymous SparkSubmitArgumentsParser to separate arguments: --remote is captured, --class and any spark.api.mode other than connect are rejected, --name/-h/--help and unknown options go to the pipeline args, and the rest go to spark-submit. It then appends the connect API mode conf and the remote value (default local).

nodes.name: StandaloneResourceUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StandaloneResourceUtils with the MutableResourceInfo and StandaloneResourceAllocation case classes, the routine that persists allocated resources to a JSON file for a driver or executor, and string formatters of resource data for the UI.

nodes.name: StandaloneResourceUtils
nodes.summary: Object of helpers for resource handling in Standalone mode: writing allocated resources to a JSON file for a driver or executor, converting resource maps to mutable form, and formatting resource information as strings for the UI.

nodes.name: MutableResourceInfo
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a resource name with a mutable set of addresses, with + and - operators that add or remove addresses of a ResourceInformation (asserting the names match) and a conversion back to ResourceInformation.
Adds the addresses of another MutableResourceInfo (or, in a second overload sharing this id, a ResourceInformation) after asserting the resource names match.
Removes the addresses of a ResourceInformation from this set after asserting the resource names match.

nodes.name: toResourceInformation
nodes.summary: Converts to an immutable ResourceInformation using the name and an array of the addresses.

nodes.name: StandaloneResourceAllocation
nodes.summary: Case class recording the resource allocations assigned to a worker or client driver process id, used only in Standalone mode.

nodes.name: toResourceInformationMap
nodes.summary: Converts the allocations into a map from resource name to ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: prepareResourcesFile
nodes.summary: Returns None for empty resources; otherwise writes the allocations as JSON to a temp file in the directory and renames it to a resource-<component>-*.json file, wrapping write failures in a SparkException. Used for a cluster-mode driver or an executor in Standalone mode.

nodes.name: writeResourceAllocationJson
nodes.summary: Serializes a sequence of allocations to compact JSON and writes it to the given file.

nodes.name: toMutable
nodes.summary: Converts a map of ResourceInformation into a map of MutableResourceInfo holding hash sets of addresses.

nodes.name: formatResourcesDetails
nodes.summary: Formats per-resource free and used addresses as a single string for the UI.

nodes.name: formatResourcesAddresses
nodes.summary: Formats each resource name with its address list as a comma-separated string for the UI.

nodes.name: formatResourcesUsed
nodes.summary: Formats used over total counts per resource name as a string for the UI.

nodes.name: formatResourceRequirements
nodes.summary: Formats resource requirements as amount and name pairs joined with commas, used for the UI.

nodes.name: Utils.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the deploy module Utils object that renders portions of stderr, stdout or out log files for a web UI /log endpoint, with offset and length handling.

nodes.name: Utils
nodes.summary: Private utility object of the deploy module that serves log file contents over a web UI: it attaches a /log handler and reads a byte range of stderr, stdout or out logs from the log directory.

nodes.name: addRenderLogHandler
nodes.summary: Attaches a /log servlet handler to a WebUI page whose response is produced by renderLog.

nodes.name: renderLog
nodes.summary: Reads logType, offset and byteLength request parameters (default 100 KB) and the SPARK_LOG_DIR environment variable, calls getLog and returns a header line with the byte range followed by the log text.

nodes.name: getLog
nodes.summary: Returns a window of a log as text plus start, end and total length: validates the log type against stderr, stdout and out, finds the sorted rolled-over files, computes the clamped offset range and reads those bytes, returning an error message tuple on failure.

nodes.name: ApplicationInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the master-side record of one registered standalone application, tracking its state, granted cores, executors and per-resource-profile executor targets.

nodes.name: ApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable master-side bookkeeping object for one application: holds start time, id, description, driver reference, state, executors, removed executors and retry count. Also tracks target executor counts and executor resource descriptions per resource profile id, and is used by the master when scheduling executors for the application.
nodes.languageNotes: Transient mutable fields are re-created by init() on construction and again in readObject during deserialization.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Custom deserialization hook that reads default fields and then calls init() to rebuild the transient state.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Resets all transient state: sets state to WAITING, creates empty executor collections, builds the application source, registers the default resource profile and its executor resource description, and sets the initial executor limit for the default profile.

nodes.name: getOrUpdateExecutorsForRPId
nodes.summary: Returns the set of executor ids for a resource profile id, creating an empty set when none exists.

nodes.name: getTargetExecutorNumForRPId
nodes.summary: Returns the target executor count recorded for a resource profile id, defaulting to 0.

nodes.name: getRequestedRPIds
nodes.summary: Returns the sorted ids of all resource profiles requested by this application.

nodes.name: createResourceDescForResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Builds and stores an ExecutorResourceDescription for a resource profile, falling back to the application description's cores and memory per executor when the profile does not set them, and adding custom executor resource requirements.

nodes.name: getResourceDescriptionForRpId
nodes.summary: Looks up the executor resource description for a resource profile id, used when scheduling.

nodes.name: requestExecutors
nodes.summary: Records new target executor totals per resource profile, creating resource descriptions and registering profiles not yet known.

nodes.name: getResourceProfileById
nodes.summary: Returns the stored resource profile for a given id.

nodes.name: newExecutorId
nodes.summary: Returns the next executor id, or reuses a supplied id while advancing the counter past it.

nodes.name: addExecutor
nodes.summary: Creates an ExecutorDesc on a worker with the given cores, memory and resources, registers it under its resource profile, and adds its cores to the granted total.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Moves an executor from the active map to the removed list, drops it from its resource profile set and subtracts its cores.

nodes.name: coresLeft
nodes.summary: Computes cores still wanted by the application as requested cores minus granted cores.

nodes.name: incrementRetryCount
nodes.summary: Increments and returns the application's retry counter.

nodes.name: markFinished
nodes.summary: Sets the final application state and records the end time.

nodes.name: isFinished
nodes.summary: Returns true when the state is neither WAITING nor RUNNING.

nodes.name: getExecutorLimit
nodes.summary: Sums the target executor counts across all resource profiles.

nodes.name: duration
nodes.summary: Returns elapsed milliseconds from the start time to the end time, or to now when the application has not ended.

nodes.name: ApplicationState.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the Enumeration of lifecycle states an application can be in on the standalone master.

nodes.name: ApplicationState
nodes.summary: Enumeration object, private to the master package, with the values WAITING, RUNNING, FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED and UNKNOWN. Used by the master-side application record to hold and test application state.

nodes.name: ApplicationSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics source exposing one application's status, runtime and granted cores on the master.

nodes.name: ApplicationSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source for a single ApplicationInfo. Its source name combines 'application', the application name and the creation time, and it registers gauges named status, runtime_ms and cores that read the application's state, duration and granted cores.

nodes.name: ClientArguments.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the command-line argument parser (and its defaults) for the standalone driver client, supporting 'launch' and 'kill' commands.

nodes.name: ClientArguments
nodes.summary: Parses driver client arguments into a command ('launch' or 'kill'), master URLs, jar URL, main class, cores, memory, supervise flag, log level, driver options and driver id; prints usage and exits on invalid input. The companion object holds the default cores, memory and supervise values and the jar URL validity check.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object shares the class id; the line range spans both.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive pattern match over the argument list handling --cores, --memory, --supervise, --help, --verbose, 'launch' and 'kill'; any other input prints usage and exits.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Builds the usage text with the default values, writes it to standard error and exits the JVM with the given code.

nodes.name: isValidJarUrl
nodes.summary: Checks that a string parses as a URI with a scheme and a path ending in .jar; returns false on a syntax error. Defined in the companion object.

nodes.name: DriverTimeoutPlugin.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a built-in plugin that terminates the driver JVM after a configured number of minutes.

nodes.name: DriverTimeoutPlugin
nodes.summary: Plugin entry class: returns a DriverTimeoutDriverPlugin as its driver plugin and null (no-op) as its executor plugin.

nodes.name: DriverTimeoutDriverPlugin
nodes.summary: Driver-side plugin that owns a daemon single-thread scheduled executor; on init it reads the driver timeout setting and, unless it is 0, schedules a task that logs a warning and calls System.exit with the driver timeout exit code. Shutdown stops the scheduler.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Reads the driver timeout from the SparkContext configuration; warns and does nothing when 0, otherwise schedules the JVM-terminating task after that many minutes. Returns an empty extra-configuration map. (The one-line shutdown override is not given its own node.)

nodes.name: Command.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Command case class describing a process to launch: main class, arguments, environment and class path, library path and Java options.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Private[spark] case class holding mainClass, arguments, environment map, classPathEntries, libraryPathEntries and javaOpts. Used as a plain description of a command to run; the worker command builder in this wave consumes it.

nodes.name: ExternalShuffleServiceSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metrics source for the external shuffle service.

nodes.name: ExternalShuffleServiceSource
nodes.summary: Thread-safe metrics Source named 'shuffleService' with its own metric registry; registerMetricSet adds all metrics of a given MetricSet to that registry.

nodes.name: registerMetricSet
nodes.summary: Registers all metrics from the given MetricSet into this source's registry.

nodes.name: StandaloneAppClientListener.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the listener trait whose callbacks the standalone deploy client invokes on cluster events.

nodes.name: StandaloneAppClientListener
nodes.summary: Trait of callbacks invoked when the deploy client connects, disconnects, dies, is given or loses an executor, has an executor decommissioned, or has a worker removed. Implementations must not block inside the callbacks. Methods are abstract so none get their own node.

nodes.name: WorkerCommandBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a command builder that turns a Command, a Spark home and a memory size into a Java launch command line.

nodes.name: WorkerCommandBuilder
nodes.summary: Extends AbstractCommandBuilder (in the launcher package, not linked here) to build a worker's Java command: copies the Command's environment into the child environment, sets the Spark home variable, and builds the Java command with the class path entries, -Xmx memory option and Java options. Lives in the launcher package to reach package-private APIs, and is used by CommandUtils per its class comment.

nodes.name: buildCommand
nodes.summary: Builds the Java command list from the class path entries, adds the -Xmx option and the Java options, and returns it. A second no-argument overload (line 45) calls this one with an empty map.

nodes.name: DriverInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DriverInfo, the master-side record of one submitted driver (start time, id, DriverDescription, submit date) with its state, last launch exception, assigned worker and allocated resources. It is Serializable and resets its transient fields on deserialization.

nodes.name: DriverInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable holder for a driver that was submitted to the standalone master. It keeps transient state (initially DriverState.SUBMITTED), an optional launch exception, the most recent WorkerInfo and a map of resource name to ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Java deserialization hook that reads the default fields and then calls init to reset the transient state.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Resets the transient fields: state to DriverState.SUBMITTED, worker and exception to None.

nodes.name: withResources
nodes.summary: Stores the map of resources (resource name to ResourceInformation) allocated to this driver; the matching resources accessor returns it.

nodes.name: DriverState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DriverState enumeration listing the lifecycle states of a driver in the standalone master.

nodes.name: DriverState
nodes.summary: Enumeration with the values SUBMITTED, RUNNING, FINISHED, RELAUNCHING, UNKNOWN, KILLED, FAILED and ERROR. Source comments describe them, for example UNKNOWN is a state temporarily not known due to master failure recovery and ERROR is an unrecoverable error such as a missing jar file.

nodes.name: ExecutorDesc.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorDesc, the master-side description of one executor assigned to an application on a worker.

nodes.name: ExecutorDesc
nodes.summary: Records an executor by id, owning ApplicationInfo, WorkerInfo, cores, memory, allocated resources and resource profile id, and tracks a mutable ExecutorState starting at LAUNCHING. Equality is based on fullId, worker id, cores and memory.

nodes.name: copyState
nodes.summary: Copies the state from an on-the-wire ExecutorDescription into this executor.

nodes.name: fullId
nodes.summary: Returns the executor identifier formed as application id, a slash and the executor id.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Considers two ExecutorDesc equal when fullId, worker id, cores and memory match.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceDescription.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutorResourceDescription case class describing per-executor resource requirements of a resource profile.

nodes.name: ExecutorResourceDescription
nodes.summary: Case class holding optional cores per executor, memory in MB per executor and a sequence of custom ResourceRequirement entries (default empty). Documented as describing resource requirements for different resource profiles, used for executor scheduling.

nodes.name: FileSystemPersistenceEngine.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileSystemPersistenceEngine, a PersistenceEngine that stores each persisted object as a serialized file in one directory.

nodes.name: FileSystemPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: PersistenceEngine that keeps one file per application and worker in a directory (created if missing, including through a symbolic link), using a Serializer and an optional CompressionCodec. Files are deleted when the entries are removed.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Persists an object under the given name by writing it to a new file in the directory.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Deletes the file with the given name and logs a warning if the delete fails.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Lists files in the directory whose names start with the prefix and deserializes each into a sequence of T.

nodes.name: serializeIntoFile
nodes.summary: Creates a new file (failing if it exists or cannot be created), wraps the stream with the codec when set, and writes the object with a serializer instance, closing streams in a safe finally block.

nodes.name: deserializeFromFile
nodes.summary: Opens a file, applies the codec if present, and reads one object with a serializer instance, closing the streams afterwards.

nodes.name: LeaderElectionAgent.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LeaderElectionAgent and LeaderElectable traits for master leader election, plus MonarchyLeaderAgent, the single-node implementation.

nodes.name: LeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait for agents that track the current master. It exposes the LeaderElectable masterInstance and a default no-op stop method, and is the common interface for election agents.

nodes.name: LeaderElectable
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait implemented by a master candidate, with electedLeader and revokedLeadership callbacks invoked by an election agent.

nodes.name: MonarchyLeaderAgent
nodes.summary: Single-node LeaderElectionAgent that treats the given LeaderElectable as always the leader, calling electedLeader immediately on construction.

nodes.name: MasterArguments.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MasterArguments, the command-line parser for the standalone master.

nodes.name: MasterArguments
nodes.summary: Parses master command-line options (--host/-h, --port/-p, --webui-port, --properties-file, --help) into host, port, webUiPort and propertiesFile. Defaults are read from SPARK_MASTER_HOST, SPARK_MASTER_PORT and SPARK_MASTER_WEBUI_PORT environment variables, then it loads default Spark properties into the SparkConf and lets the MASTER_UI_PORT config override the web UI port.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive pattern match over the argument list that sets host, port, webUiPort or propertiesFile and prints usage and exits on --help or unknown arguments.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Prints the master usage text to stderr and exits the JVM with the given exit code.

nodes.name: MasterMessages.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MasterMessages sealed trait and its companion object of case objects and case classes for messages seen only by the Master and its associated entities.

nodes.name: MasterMessages
nodes.summary: Sealed Serializable trait with a private[master] companion object that holds the messages seen only by the Master and its associated entities: leader election notices, self-sent timeout and recovery messages, and bound-port requests.

nodes.name: ElectedLeader
nodes.summary: Case object sent from the LeaderElectionAgent to the Master when it is elected leader.

nodes.name: RevokedLeadership
nodes.summary: Case object sent from the LeaderElectionAgent to the Master when leadership is revoked.

nodes.name: CheckForWorkerTimeOut
nodes.summary: Case object the Master sends to itself to check for timed-out workers.

nodes.name: BeginRecovery
nodes.summary: Case class the Master sends to itself to begin recovery, carrying the stored ApplicationInfo and WorkerInfo sequences.

nodes.name: CompleteRecovery
nodes.summary: Case object the Master sends to itself to complete recovery.

nodes.name: BoundPortsRequest
nodes.summary: Case object requesting the ports the master is bound to.

nodes.name: BoundPortsResponse
nodes.summary: Case class reply carrying the RPC endpoint port, web UI port and optional REST port.

nodes.name: MasterSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MasterSource, the metrics Source for the standalone master.

nodes.name: MasterSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source named "master" that registers gauges on a MetricRegistry for the number of workers, alive workers, applications and waiting applications, read from the given Master.

nodes.name: PersistenceEngine.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract PersistenceEngine, which the standalone Master uses to persist and read back applications, drivers and workers for failure recovery, plus a no-op BlackHolePersistenceEngine. The concrete storage mechanism is left to subclasses.

nodes.name: PersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Abstract base class that lets the Master persist name-object pairs needed to recover from a failure. Final helper methods store and remove ApplicationInfo, WorkerInfo and DriverInfo objects under app_, worker_ and driver_ prefixed names; subclasses define persist, unpersist and read.

nodes.name: BlackHolePersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Master-private PersistenceEngine whose persist and unpersist do nothing and whose read returns Nil, so no state is kept and nothing is recovered. Its three one-line overrides are not given separate nodes.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Abstract method that defines how an object is serialized and persisted under a name; implementation depends on the store used.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Abstract method that defines how the object referred to by its name is removed from the store.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns all stored objects whose name matches a prefix, deserialized back to type T.

nodes.name: addApplication
nodes.summary: Persists an ApplicationInfo under the name app_ plus its id.

nodes.name: removeApplication
nodes.summary: Removes the persisted ApplicationInfo stored under app_ plus its id.

nodes.name: addWorker
nodes.summary: Persists a WorkerInfo under the name worker_ plus its id.

nodes.name: removeWorker
nodes.summary: Removes the persisted WorkerInfo stored under worker_ plus its id.

nodes.name: addDriver
nodes.summary: Persists a DriverInfo under the name driver_ plus its id.

nodes.name: removeDriver
nodes.summary: Removes the persisted DriverInfo stored under driver_ plus its id.

nodes.name: readPersistedData
nodes.summary: Reads all persisted applications, drivers and workers by their prefixes inside rpcEnv.deserialize and returns them as a tuple; ids imply creation-time ordering. Used when the Master recovers.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Default no-op hook that subclasses override to release their store resources.

nodes.name: RecoveryModeFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable StandaloneRecoveryModeFactory API and its built-in FileSystem, RocksDB and ZooKeeper implementations. Each factory creates the PersistenceEngine and the LeaderElectionAgent that the standalone Master uses for its recovery mode.

nodes.name: StandaloneRecoveryModeFactory
nodes.summary: Abstract DeveloperApi factory, constructed from a SparkConf and a Serializer, that can be plugged in as an alternative recovery mode for standalone mode. It creates the PersistenceEngine and the LeaderElectionAgent.

nodes.name: FileSystemRecoveryModeFactory
nodes.summary: Factory for filesystem recovery: builds a FileSystemPersistenceEngine on the configured recovery directory (with an optional compression codec) and a MonarchyLeaderAgent, whose leader is forever leader since recovery restores from the filesystem.

nodes.name: RocksDBRecoveryModeFactory
nodes.summary: Factory for RocksDB recovery: builds a RocksDBPersistenceEngine on the configured recovery directory and a MonarchyLeaderAgent, so the leader is a no-op and recovery restores from RocksDB.

nodes.name: ZooKeeperRecoveryModeFactory
nodes.summary: Factory for ZooKeeper recovery: builds a ZooKeeperPersistenceEngine and a ZooKeeperLeaderElectionAgent so the Master can recover state and elect a leader through ZooKeeper.

nodes.name: createPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Abstract method that creates the PersistenceEngine defining how worker, driver and other information is handled for recovery.

nodes.name: createLeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: Abstract method that creates the LeaderElectionAgent deciding who is elected master for a given LeaderElectable.

nodes.name: createPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Logs the recovery directory, optionally creates a compression codec from the recovery codec setting, and returns a FileSystemPersistenceEngine.

nodes.name: createLeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: Returns a MonarchyLeaderAgent for the given master.

nodes.name: createPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Reads the recovery directory setting, logs it and returns a RocksDBPersistenceEngine.

nodes.name: createLeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: Returns a MonarchyLeaderAgent for the given master.

nodes.name: createPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: Returns a ZooKeeperPersistenceEngine built from the conf and serializer.

nodes.name: createLeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: Returns a ZooKeeperLeaderElectionAgent for the given master and conf.

nodes.name: RecoveryState.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the RecoveryState enumeration listing the Master states STANDBY, ALIVE, RECOVERING and COMPLETING_RECOVERY, aliased as MasterState. It is visible inside the deploy package.

nodes.name: RecoveryState
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the lifecycle states of a Master: STANDBY, ALIVE, RECOVERING and COMPLETING_RECOVERY, with a MasterState type alias.

nodes.name: RocksDBPersistenceEngine.scala
nodes.summary: Implements a PersistenceEngine backed by RocksDB for the standalone Master. It opens a database in a given directory with a bloom filter, ZSTD and LZ4 compression, and stores serialized objects keyed by name.

nodes.name: RocksDBPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: PersistenceEngine that stores serialized objects in a RocksDB database under a directory it creates if missing (following a symbolic link if needed). Configured with a full bloom filter, ZSTD at the bottommost level and LZ4 elsewhere; used by the RocksDB recovery mode.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Serializes the object with the serializer and puts the bytes into the database under the UTF-8 name, copying out of the buffer when it has no backing array.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Deletes the entry stored under the given name from RocksDB.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Seeks a RocksDB iterator to the name prefix and deserializes every consecutive value whose key starts with it, closing the iterator afterwards.

nodes.name: WorkerState.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the WorkerState enumeration with values ALIVE, DEAD, DECOMMISSIONED and UNKNOWN, private to the master package.

nodes.name: WorkerState
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the states the Master tracks for a worker: ALIVE, DEAD, DECOMMISSIONED and UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: WorkerInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Master-side bookkeeping for a standalone worker: WorkerInfo tracks its cores, memory, executors, drivers, state, heartbeat and custom resources, and WorkerResourceInfo allocates whole resource addresses. Used by the Master when scheduling and during recovery.

nodes.name: WorkerResourceInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable case class pairing a resource name with its addresses and mixing in ResourceAllocator. Its acquire(amount) hands out whole available addresses as a ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: WorkerInfo
nodes.summary: Serializable object the Master keeps for each worker: id, host, port, cores, memory, RPC endpoint, web UI address and resource map. It tracks transient executors, drivers, used cores and memory, state and last heartbeat, and re-runs init after deserialization.

nodes.name: acquire
nodes.summary: Takes the requested number of available addresses (asserting enough exist), acquires them as entire resources through the ResourceAllocator and returns a ResourceInformation for them. Another acquire overload comes from ResourceAllocator.

nodes.name: coresFree
nodes.summary: Returns the cores not yet used (cores minus coresUsed).

nodes.name: memoryFree
nodes.summary: Returns the memory not yet used (memory minus memoryUsed).

nodes.name: resourcesAmountFree
nodes.summary: Maps each resource name to the number of its currently available addresses.

nodes.name: resourcesInfo
nodes.summary: Maps each resource name to a ResourceInformation holding all of its addresses.

nodes.name: resourcesInfoFree
nodes.summary: Maps each resource name to a ResourceInformation holding only its available addresses.

nodes.name: resourcesInfoUsed
nodes.summary: Maps each resource name to a ResourceInformation holding only its assigned addresses.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Custom Java deserialization hook that reads default fields and then calls init to restore the transient state.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes transient state: empty executor and driver maps, ALIVE state, zero used cores and memory, and the current time as last heartbeat.

nodes.name: hostPort
nodes.summary: Returns the host and port joined as host:port after asserting the port is positive.

nodes.name: addExecutor
nodes.summary: Records an executor by its full id and adds its cores and memory to the used totals.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: If the executor is known, removes it, subtracts its cores and memory and releases its resources.

nodes.name: hasExecutor
nodes.summary: Returns true when any executor on this worker belongs to the given application.

nodes.name: addDriver
nodes.summary: Records a driver by id and adds its memory and cores to the used totals.

nodes.name: removeDriver
nodes.summary: Removes a driver by id, subtracts its memory and cores and releases its resources.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Sets the worker state.

nodes.name: isAlive
nodes.summary: Returns true when the worker state is ALIVE.

nodes.name: acquireResources
nodes.summary: Acquires the amounts named in each ResourceRequirement from the matching WorkerResourceInfo and returns the acquired ResourceInformation by resource name.

nodes.name: recoverResources
nodes.summary: Used during master recovery: re-acquires the expected addresses as entire resources on the matching resources.

nodes.name: releaseResources
nodes.summary: Releases the previously allocated addresses of a driver or executor back to the matching resources.

nodes.name: ZooKeeperLeaderElectionAgent.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the ZooKeeper-based leader election agent for the standalone Master. It uses a Curator LeaderLatch under a configured ZooKeeper directory and notifies the Master when leadership is gained or lost.

nodes.name: ZooKeeperLeaderElectionAgent
nodes.summary: LeaderElectionAgent and LeaderLatchListener that starts a Curator client and leader latch on construction and tracks a LEADER or NOT_LEADER status. It calls electedLeader or revokedLeadership on the LeaderElectable master when status changes.

nodes.name: LeadershipStatus
nodes.summary: Private enumeration inside the agent with the values LEADER and NOT_LEADER.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Logs startup, creates a ZooKeeper client from the conf, creates a LeaderLatch on the leader_election path, registers this agent as listener and starts the latch.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the leader latch and the ZooKeeper client.

nodes.name: isLeader
nodes.summary: Listener callback: under synchronization, if the latch still holds leadership, logs it and updates the status to leader.

nodes.name: notLeader
nodes.summary: Listener callback: under synchronization, if leadership is not held, logs the loss and updates the status to not leader.

nodes.name: updateLeadershipStatus
nodes.summary: Moves status between NOT_LEADER and LEADER and calls electedLeader or revokedLeadership on the master instance on a real transition.

nodes.name: ZooKeeperPersistenceEngine.scala
nodes.summary: Implements a PersistenceEngine that stores the Master's recovery state as ZooKeeper nodes under a master_status directory. Objects are serialized into node data and read back by name prefix.

nodes.name: ZooKeeperPersistenceEngine
nodes.summary: PersistenceEngine that uses a Curator ZooKeeper client to create, delete and read persistent nodes under the configured directory plus /master_status. Unreadable nodes are logged and deleted while reading; used by the ZooKeeper recovery mode.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Serializes the object into a ZooKeeper node at the working directory plus the given name.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Deletes the ZooKeeper node stored under the given name.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Lists the children of the working directory, keeps those starting with the prefix and deserializes each one.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the ZooKeeper client.

nodes.name: serializeIntoFile
nodes.summary: Serializes a value with the serializer and creates a persistent ZooKeeper node at the path holding the bytes.

nodes.name: deserializeFromFile
nodes.summary: Reads a node's data and deserializes it; on an exception it logs a warning, deletes the node and returns None.

nodes.name: ApplicationPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the standalone Master web UI page that shows details of one application: its settings, state, links to its UI or history, and tables of current and removed executors. It reads application data from the Master by RPC.

nodes.name: ApplicationPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage mounted at the path app for the Master UI. It asks the master endpoint for its state, finds the application by the appId request parameter among active and completed apps, and renders the application summary plus executor and removed-executor tables.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Looks up the app by appId through a RequestMasterState call; returns a Not Found page when missing. Otherwise builds the application detail list (cores, executor limit, memory, resources, dates, state, UI or history link) and executor tables, wrapped in a Spark page.

nodes.name: executorRow
nodes.summary: Renders one table row for an ExecutorDesc: id, worker link, cores, memory, resource profile id, resources, state and stdout and stderr log links.

nodes.name: EnvironmentPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the master web UI Environment page for the standalone master. It is attached by MasterWebUI and also served at the /environment path.

nodes.name: EnvironmentPage
nodes.summary: Master UI page (WebUIPage named Environment) that shows runtime information, Spark, Hadoop, system and metrics properties, classpath entries and selected environment variables of the master process, as collapsible sorted tables. Created in MasterWebUI.initialize with the master SparkConf.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Collects environment details through SparkEnv.environmentDetails, redacts the sensitive property groups, filters environment variables by the configured visible prefixes, builds one listing table per group and returns the page wrapped by UIUtils.basicSparkPage. Small private helpers (propertyHeader, classPathHeader, headerClasses, headerClassesNoSortValues, jvmRowDataPre, propertyRow, classPathRow) supply table headers and rows.

nodes.name: LogPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the log viewer page of the standalone master web UI.

nodes.name: LogPage
nodes.summary: Master UI page (WebUIPage named logPage) that shows a chunk of a master log file from the SPARK_LOG_DIR directory (default logs/), with Load More and Load New buttons driven by a generated onload script. Attached in MasterWebUI.initialize.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Reads the logType, offset and byteLength request parameters, fetches the log text with the deploy Utils.getLog helper, builds the byte range label, buttons and script, and returns the page through UIUtils.basicSparkPage. It also uses UIUtils.encodeLogParam and CspNonce.get.

nodes.name: MasterWebUI.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the web UI server of the standalone master and wires its pages, static resources, kill and decommission handlers and proxy support.

nodes.name: MasterWebUI
nodes.summary: Web UI server for the standalone master (a WebUI subclass named MasterUI). On construction it calls initialize to attach ApplicationPage, LogPage, EnvironmentPage and MasterPage, static resources, the log render handler, optional kill handlers for applications and drivers, and an optional workers/kill decommission servlet. The companion object (lines 133-135) only holds the private STATIC_RESOURCE_DIR taken from SparkUI.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates MasterPage, ApplicationPage, LogPage and EnvironmentPage and attaches them, registers the /environment servlet, static handler and log render handler. When kill is enabled it adds POST redirect handlers for /app/kill and /driver/kill. When decommission is enabled it adds a /workers/kill servlet that checks modify permissions and the allow mode, asks the master to decommission the requested hosts and maps the removed worker count to an HTTP status.

nodes.name: addProxy
nodes.summary: Creates a proxy handler from idToUiAddress and attaches it, so worker and application UIs can be reached through the master.

nodes.name: idToUiAddress
nodes.summary: Asks the master for its state and looks up the UI address of a worker or an active application by id, preferring the worker address.

nodes.name: isLocal
nodes.summary: Returns true when an address is a wildcard, loopback or local network interface address, treating a SocketException as not local.

nodes.name: isDecommissioningRequestAllowed
nodes.summary: Applies the configured decommission allow mode: ALLOW permits every request, LOCAL permits only requests whose remote address is local, anything else is rejected.

nodes.name: MasterPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the index page of the standalone master web UI, listing workers, applications and drivers, and its JSON and kill-request handling.

nodes.name: MasterPage
nodes.summary: Index page (WebUIPage with an empty prefix) of the master UI. It renders cluster totals and tables of workers, running and completed applications and drivers, serves the same state as JSON (including a cluster utilization view), and handles the application and driver kill requests registered by MasterWebUI.

nodes.name: getMasterState
nodes.summary: Asks the master endpoint for a MasterStateResponse by sending RequestMasterState and waiting for the reply.

nodes.name: renderJson
nodes.summary: Serves the JSON view: with no path field it writes the whole master state, for clusterutilization it writes the cluster utilization, otherwise it writes the master state restricted to the requested field, all through JsonProtocol.

nodes.name: handleAppKillRequest
nodes.summary: Handles an application kill request by looking up the application by id and removing it from the master with state KILLED, via handleKillRequest.

nodes.name: handleDriverKillRequest
nodes.summary: Handles a driver kill request by asking the master endpoint with RequestKillDriver for the given id, via handleKillRequest.

nodes.name: handleKillRequest
nodes.summary: Shared kill logic: runs the given action only when kill is enabled, the user has modify permissions, and the request has an id and terminate=true, then sleeps 100 ms.

nodes.name: formatWorkerResourcesDetails
nodes.summary: Formats a worker's used and free resource info as text with StandaloneResourceUtils.formatResourcesDetails.

nodes.name: formatMasterResourcesInUse
nodes.summary: Sums per-resource address counts over all alive workers (total and used) and formats them with StandaloneResourceUtils.formatResourcesUsed.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the master index page: fetches the master state, prepares header lists and sorted worker, application and driver data, builds listing tables, composes the summary list (URLs, worker counts, cores, memory, resources, applications, drivers, status) and collapsible sections, and wraps them with UIUtils.basicSparkPage using the configured title or a default.

nodes.name: workerRow
nodes.summary: Returns the function that renders one worker table row: id (linked to the worker UI when alive), host and port, state, cores, memory and an optional resources column.

nodes.name: appRow
nodes.summary: Renders one application table row with id, optional kill form, name or link, cores, memory per executor, resource requirements, submit date, user, state and duration. The kill form is shown only when kill is enabled and the application is running or waiting.

nodes.name: driverRow
nodes.summary: Renders one driver table row with id, optional kill form, submit date, worker link, state, cores, memory, resources, main class and optionally the duration. activeDriverRow and completedDriverRow (one-liners) call it with showDuration true and false.

nodes.name: RestSubmissionClient.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the REST client side of the standalone application submission protocol: RestSubmissionClient posts create, kill, killall, clear, readyz and status requests as HTTP calls to a RestSubmissionServer, and RestSubmissionClientApp wraps it as a SparkApplication entry point. Used when an application is submitted to a spark:// master over the REST protocol.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a class, its companion object (constants and helpers) and a second SparkApplication class; blocking HTTP via HttpURLConnection with a 10 second Await on a Future.

nodes.name: RestSubmissionClient
nodes.summary: Client that submits applications to a RestSubmissionServer over HTTP using the v1 URL scheme /v1/submissions/[action]. Tries each configured master in turn, posts JSON for create and plain POST/GET for kill, killall, clear, readyz and status, and tracks masters that lost contact. Its companion object (lines 529-552) holds supportedMasterPrefixes, PROTOCOL_VERSION, filterSystemEnvironment and supportsRestClient.

nodes.name: createSubmission
nodes.summary: Submits an application described by a CreateSubmissionRequest. For each master it posts the request as JSON; on a successful CreateSubmissionResponse it reports and polls the submission status, otherwise it logs the unexpected response. Rethrows a connection error when all masters are lost.

nodes.name: killSubmission
nodes.summary: Asks the master to kill the submission with the given id by POSTing to the kill URL, trying each master until one that is not a backup answers with a KillSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: killAllSubmissions
nodes.summary: Asks the master to kill all submissions by POSTing to the killall URL, skipping responses that come from a backup master.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Asks the master to clear all submissions and applications by POSTing to the clear URL and handling a ClearResponse.

nodes.name: readyz
nodes.summary: Checks whether the master is ready by sending a GET to the readyz URL and handling a ReadyzResponse; starts from an ErrorResponse so a result exists if no master answers.

nodes.name: requestSubmissionStatus
nodes.summary: Requests the status of a submission with a GET to the status URL. When quiet is false the successful SubmissionStatusResponse is logged; used both directly and by the status polling loop.

nodes.name: constructSubmitRequest
nodes.summary: Builds and validates a CreateSubmissionRequest from the app resource, main class, arguments, Spark properties and environment variables, stamping the client Spark version.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Opens an HttpURLConnection to the URL with method GET and returns the parsed response via readResponse.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Opens an HttpURLConnection to the URL with method POST (no body) and returns the parsed response via readResponse.

nodes.name: postJson
nodes.summary: Sends a POST with the given JSON as the UTF-8 request body and Content-Type application/json, converts a ConnectException into a SubmitRestConnectionException, then reads the response.

nodes.name: readResponse
nodes.summary: Reads the HTTP response in a Future awaited for up to 10 seconds. Non-200 codes become an ErrorResponse (carrying the highest protocol version on an unknown-version code); 200 bodies are parsed with SubmitRestProtocolMessage.fromJson and validated. Maps socket, JSON, protocol and timeout failures to connection or protocol exceptions. Exposed for testing.

nodes.name: getSubmitUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for creating a submission (base URL plus /create).

nodes.name: getKillUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for killing a submission (base URL plus /kill/[submissionId]).

nodes.name: getKillAllUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for killing all submissions (base URL plus /killall).

nodes.name: getClearUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for clearing all submissions and applications (base URL plus /clear).

nodes.name: getReadyzUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for the readyz API (base URL plus /readyz).

nodes.name: getStatusUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the REST URL for a submission status request (base URL plus /status/[submissionId]).

nodes.name: getBaseUrl
nodes.summary: Strips a supported master prefix and trailing slash and returns http://[host:port]/v1/submissions, the base of all REST URLs.

nodes.name: validateMaster
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalArgumentException unless the master URL starts with one of the supported prefixes.

nodes.name: reportSubmissionStatus
nodes.summary: Logs the outcome of a create response; on success with a submission id it starts polling the submission state, and logs an error if the id is missing or the submission failed.

nodes.name: pollSubmissionStatus
nodes.summary: Polls the submission status up to a fixed number of tries, sleeping between attempts, and logs the driver state, worker location and any error message once the master recognizes the driver.

nodes.name: handleRestResponse
nodes.summary: Logs the message type and JSON of a response received from the server.

nodes.name: handleUnexpectedRestResponse
nodes.summary: Logs an error saying the server answered with a message of an unexpected type.

nodes.name: handleConnectionException
nodes.summary: Records a master as lost and returns true when all masters are lost. Does not account for masters recovering later (see SPARK-6443 in the comment).

nodes.name: filterSystemEnvironment
nodes.summary: Companion helper that keeps only environment variables starting with SPARK_ while excluding SPARK_ENV_LOADED, SPARK_HOME and SPARK_CONF_DIR, which are usually wrong on the remote machine.

nodes.name: supportsRestClient
nodes.summary: Companion helper returning true when the master URL starts with a supported prefix (spark://), meaning the REST client can handle it.

nodes.name: RestSubmissionClientApp
nodes.summary: SparkApplication adapter that turns command line arguments (app resource, main class, app args) and a SparkConf into a REST submission: it reads spark.master, creates a RestSubmissionClient and submits. Used as the entry point when a REST submission is requested.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Submits a request to run the application and returns the response: requires spark.master in the conf, builds a RestSubmissionClient, constructs the submit request from the conf properties and env, and calls createSubmission. Visible for testing.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: SparkApplication entry point: validates that at least an app resource and main class are given, filters the process environment to SPARK_ variables via filterSystemEnvironment, and calls run.

nodes.name: RestSubmissionServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the server side of the REST submission protocol: the abstract RestSubmissionServer starts a Jetty server mapping /v1/submissions/[create|kill|killall|status|clear|readyz] to servlets, and an abstract servlet per action (plus a default ErrorServlet) parses requests, delegates to abstract handle* methods and sends validated JSON responses. Used by a master to accept submissions from RestSubmissionClient.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with abstract servlet classes whose handle* hooks are implemented elsewhere, and a private companion object holding the protocol version and the 468 status code.

nodes.name: RestSubmissionServer
nodes.summary: Abstract HTTP server for the REST submission protocol. Declares one servlet member per action, maps URL prefixes under /v1/submissions to them (with ErrorServlet as default), and starts or stops an embedded Jetty server on a requested port with optional configured filters. Its companion object (lines 159-162) holds PROTOCOL_VERSION and SC_UNKNOWN_PROTOCOL_VERSION (468).

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the server on the requested port through Utils.startServiceOnPort using doStart, remembers the Jetty Server and returns the bound port.

nodes.name: doStart
nodes.summary: Builds the Jetty server: a daemon QueuedThreadPool sized by configuration (optionally using a virtual thread executor on Java 21 and later), a connector that hides server version and X-Powered-By headers, a ServletContextHandler with each prefix mapped to its servlet, and the configured filters; starts it and returns the server with its bound port.

nodes.name: addFilters
nodes.summary: Adds the filter classes named by the master REST server filter setting to the handler, passing init parameters read from spark.[filter].param. prefixed settings, for all dispatcher types on /*.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the underlying Jetty server if it was started.

nodes.name: RestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet base for all REST submission servlets. Provides shared helpers to send a validated JSON response, find unknown fields in a client request by diffing JSON, format exceptions, build ErrorResponse messages and parse the submission id from a request path.

nodes.name: sendResponse
nodes.summary: Validates the response message, then writes its JSON to the servlet response with content type application/json and utf-8 encoding.

nodes.name: findUnknownFields
nodes.summary: Returns the names of fields present in the client request JSON but not in the server-side re-serialized message, found by diffing the two parsed JSON documents.

nodes.name: formatException
nodes.summary: Returns a human readable string made of the exception and its tab-indented stack trace.

nodes.name: handleError
nodes.summary: Builds an ErrorResponse carrying the server Spark version and the given message.

nodes.name: parseSubmissionId
nodes.summary: Extracts the submission id as the first path segment of the request path (for example /[id]/rest), returning None for a null, empty or id-less path.

nodes.name: validateResponse
nodes.summary: Validates a response message; when validation throws it sets HTTP 500 and returns an ErrorResponse describing the internal error instead.

nodes.name: KillRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for kill requests. Its doPost parses the submission id from the URL and delegates to the abstract handleKill, or answers 400 with an error when the id is missing.

nodes.name: doPost
nodes.summary: Handles a kill POST: parses the submission id from the path info, calls handleKill for it, or sets HTTP 400 and returns an error saying the id is missing; then sends the response.

nodes.name: KillAllRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for killAll requests. Its doPost calls the abstract handleKillAll and sends the response.

nodes.name: doPost
nodes.summary: Handles a killall POST by calling handleKillAll and sending its KillAllSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: ClearRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for clear requests (clearing completed drivers and apps). Its doPost calls the abstract handleClear and sends the response.

nodes.name: doPost
nodes.summary: Handles a clear POST by calling handleClear and sending its ClearResponse.

nodes.name: ReadyzRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for readyz requests. Its doGet calls the abstract handleReadyz and answers 200 with the response if successful, otherwise 503 with a 'Master is not ready.' error.

nodes.name: doGet
nodes.summary: Handles a readyz GET: sets HTTP 200 and returns the ReadyzResponse when it is successful, otherwise sets HTTP 503 and returns an error response; then sends the response.

nodes.name: StatusRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for status requests. Its doGet parses the submission id from the URL and delegates to the abstract handleStatus, or answers 400 when the id is missing.

nodes.name: doGet
nodes.summary: Handles a status GET: parses the submission id from the path info and calls handleStatus, or sets HTTP 400 with an error saying the id is missing; then sends the response.

nodes.name: SubmitRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Abstract servlet for submit requests. Its doPost reads the JSON body, parses and validates the message, and delegates to the abstract handleSubmit; malformed JSON or protocol errors produce a 400 error response.

nodes.name: doPost
nodes.summary: Handles a create POST: reads the request body, parses it with SubmitRestProtocolMessage.fromJson, validates it and calls handleSubmit; on JsonProcessingException or SubmitRestProtocolException sets HTTP 400 and returns a 'Malformed request' error; then sends the response.

nodes.name: ErrorServlet
nodes.summary: Default servlet mapped to /* that handles any request not matched by another servlet. It explains what part of the path is wrong (missing version, missing /submissions, missing action, unknown version) and answers 400, or 468 with the highest supported protocol version on a version mismatch.

nodes.name: service
nodes.summary: Overrides service to inspect the request path and build a descriptive error message, then returns HTTP 468 plus highestProtocolVersion on an unknown protocol version or 400 otherwise, and sends the error response.

nodes.name: HadoopDelegationTokenManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HadoopDelegationTokenManager, which loads delegation token providers and obtains, renews and distributes delegation tokens for long-running applications, plus a companion helper for per-service enable flags.

nodes.name: HadoopDelegationTokenManager
nodes.summary: Manager that obtains delegation tokens from configured providers and, when renewal is enabled, logs in with a keytab or ticket cache, periodically fetches fresh tokens and sends them to the driver endpoint. Its companion object decides whether a service provider is enabled.

nodes.name: renewalEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether token renewal is enabled, based on the configured credentials source (keytab with a principal, or a ticket cache with Kerberos credentials).

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the token renewer: requires renewal and a scheduler endpoint, creates the renewal executor, schedules TGT relogin for keytab logins and fetches the first set of tokens.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the renewal executor if it was created.

nodes.name: obtainDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Public method that logs in, obtains tokens as the fresh user and adds them to the given Credentials when Kerberos credentials are available. A private no-argument overload (lines 165-177) queries every enabled provider and returns the credentials with the earliest next renewal time.

nodes.name: isProviderLoaded
nodes.summary: Returns whether a provider with the given service name was loaded; marked as visible for testing.

nodes.name: scheduleRenewal
nodes.summary: Schedules updateTokensTask to run after the given delay (clamped to zero) on the renewal executor.

nodes.name: updateTokensTask
nodes.summary: Logs in, obtains new tokens, serializes them and sends an UpdateDelegationTokens message to the scheduler endpoint; on failure it logs a warning and reschedules a retry.

nodes.name: obtainTokensAndScheduleRenewal
nodes.summary: Obtains tokens as the given user and schedules the next renewal using the configured renewal interval ratio and the earliest next renewal time.

nodes.name: doLogin
nodes.summary: Logs in from the principal and keytab, from the ticket cache, or returns the current user when it is a proxy user.

nodes.name: loadProviders
nodes.summary: Loads HadoopDelegationTokenProvider implementations through the service loader, ignoring load failures, and keeps only providers whose service is enabled, keyed by service name.

nodes.name: isServiceEnabled
nodes.summary: Companion object method that reads the per-service enabled flag, warns about deprecated keys that are set, and falls back to the deprecated flags (default true) when the new key is unset.

nodes.name: StandaloneRestServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the REST submission server embedded in the standalone Master and the servlets that translate REST kill, killAll, status, clear, readyz and submit requests into messages sent to the Master endpoint.

nodes.name: StandaloneRestServer
nodes.summary: Server used in cluster mode only that responds to requests from the REST submission client. It extends RestSubmissionServer and wires each request kind to a Standalone servlet that talks to the Master endpoint.

nodes.name: StandaloneKillRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles kill requests by asking the Master endpoint to kill a driver and returning a KillSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: StandaloneKillAllRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles killAll requests by asking the Master endpoint to kill all drivers and returning a KillAllSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: StandaloneStatusRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles status requests by asking the Master endpoint for a driver status and mapping it into a SubmissionStatusResponse.

nodes.name: StandaloneClearRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles clear requests by asking the Master endpoint to clear completed drivers and applications.

nodes.name: StandaloneReadyzRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles readyz requests by asking the Master endpoint whether it is ready and returning a ReadyzResponse.

nodes.name: StandaloneSubmitRequestServlet
nodes.summary: Servlet that handles submit requests: it builds a DriverDescription from a CreateSubmissionRequest, sends it to the Master endpoint and replies with a CreateSubmissionResponse, or an error for unexpected message types.

nodes.name: handleKill
nodes.summary: Sends RequestKillDriver for the submission id to the Master endpoint and copies the reply into a KillSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: handleKillAll
nodes.summary: Sends RequestKillAllDrivers to the Master endpoint and copies the reply into a KillAllSubmissionResponse.

nodes.name: handleStatus
nodes.summary: Sends RequestDriverStatus to the Master endpoint and fills a SubmissionStatusResponse with driver state, worker id, worker host and port, and an exception message when present.

nodes.name: handleClear
nodes.summary: Sends RequestClearCompletedDriversAndApps to the Master endpoint and returns a ClearResponse carrying the boolean result.

nodes.name: handleReadyz
nodes.summary: Sends RequestReadyz to the Master endpoint and returns a ReadyzResponse carrying the boolean result.

nodes.name: replacePlaceHolder
nodes.summary: Replaces a value of the form {{NAME}} with the environment variable NAME when it is set, otherwise returns the value unchanged.

nodes.name: buildDriverDescription
nodes.summary: Builds a DriverDescription from a submit request: validates required fields, resolves placeholders and driver settings, assembles the java options, constructs the DriverWrapper Command and parses driver resource requirements.

nodes.name: handleSubmit
nodes.summary: Handles a validated submit request: for a CreateSubmissionRequest it builds the driver description, asks the Master to submit it and returns a CreateSubmissionResponse with any unknown fields; otherwise sets 400 and returns an error.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolException.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the exception types of the REST submission protocol: a general protocol exception, a missing-field exception and a connection exception raised when the client cannot reach the server.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolException
nodes.summary: Base exception thrown in the REST application submission protocol, carrying a message and an optional cause.

nodes.name: SubmitRestMissingFieldException
nodes.summary: Exception thrown when a field is missing from a SubmitRestProtocolMessage.

nodes.name: SubmitRestConnectionException
nodes.summary: Exception thrown when the REST client cannot reach the REST server.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolMessage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract SubmitRestProtocolMessage base for requests and responses in the REST submission protocol, with JSON serialization, validation helpers, and a companion object that parses JSON back into the right message type.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with Jackson annotations; the companion object holds a shared ObjectMapper configured with the Scala module.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolMessage
nodes.summary: Abstract message exchanged in the REST submission protocol, with the common action, message fields, toJson and validation. Its companion object parses the action from JSON and deserializes into the matching message class.

nodes.name: toJson
nodes.summary: Validates the message and serializes it to indented JSON with the shared object mapper.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Runs doValidate and wraps any exception into a SubmitRestProtocolException that names the message type.

nodes.name: doValidate
nodes.summary: Base validation hook that throws SubmitRestMissingFieldException when the action field is null; subclasses override it to add checks.

nodes.name: assertFieldIsSet
nodes.summary: Throws SubmitRestMissingFieldException naming the field and message type when the given value is null.

nodes.name: assert
nodes.summary: Throws SubmitRestProtocolException with the given message when the condition is false.

nodes.name: parseAction
nodes.summary: Parses JSON and returns the value of its action field, throwing SubmitRestMissingFieldException when it is absent.

nodes.name: fromJson
