nodes.summary: Constructs a message from JSON by reading the action, loading the class of that name in this package and deserializing into it. A second overload (lines 143-145) deserializes JSON into a caller-supplied class.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolRequest.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the request side of the REST submission protocol: the abstract SubmitRestProtocolRequest that requires a client version and CreateSubmissionRequest, which carries the application resource, main class, arguments, Spark properties and environment variables.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolRequest
nodes.summary: Abstract request sent by the client in the REST submission protocol; it adds a clientSparkVersion field and validates that it is set.

nodes.name: CreateSubmissionRequest
nodes.summary: Request to launch a new application. It carries the app resource, main class, arguments, Spark properties and environment variables, and validates that the boolean, numeric and memory properties parse.

nodes.name: doValidate
nodes.summary: Calls the base validation and then asserts that clientSparkVersion is set.

nodes.name: doValidate
nodes.summary: Validates that Spark properties and appResource are set and that the supervise, driver cores, max cores, driver memory and executor memory properties have well-formed values.

nodes.name: assertProperty
nodes.summary: Applies a conversion function to a Spark property if present and throws SubmitRestProtocolException describing the expected value type when the conversion fails.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolResponse.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the response side of the REST submission protocol: the abstract SubmitRestProtocolResponse and its concrete submit, kill, killAll, clear, readyz, status and error responses.

nodes.name: SubmitRestProtocolResponse
nodes.summary: Abstract response sent by the server; it adds serverSparkVersion, success and unknownFields and validates that the server version is set.

nodes.name: CreateSubmissionResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a CreateSubmissionRequest, carrying the submission id and requiring the success field.

nodes.name: KillSubmissionResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a kill request, carrying the submission id and requiring both submissionId and success.

nodes.name: KillAllSubmissionResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a killAll request that requires the success field.

nodes.name: ClearResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a clear request that requires the success field.

nodes.name: ReadyzResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a readyz request that requires the success field.

nodes.name: SubmissionStatusResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a status request, carrying the submission id, driver state, worker id and worker host and port; requires submissionId and success.

nodes.name: ErrorResponse
nodes.summary: Error response used in the protocol; it records the highest protocol version the server knows about and requires a message.

nodes.name: ApplicationCache.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the history server cache of loaded application UIs, together with its key, entry, metrics, operations trait and the servlet filter that triggers refresh checks for incomplete applications.

nodes.name: ApplicationCache
nodes.summary: Cache of application UIs backed by a size-bounded loading cache keyed by app id and attempt id. Loads a UI through ApplicationCacheOperations, attaches it, registers a refresh-check filter for incomplete applications, and detaches the UI when an entry is evicted.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up the cache entry for an app id and optional attempt id, unwrapping execution exceptions so the underlying cause is thrown.

nodes.name: withSparkUI
nodes.summary: Runs a closure while holding the read lock of an application UI, retrying with invalidate and reload until a valid entry is locked, so the UI data store is not closed during use.

nodes.name: loadApplicationEntry
nodes.summary: Loads the SparkUI via operations.getAppUI, registers the check filter if the application is incomplete, attaches the UI, and returns a new CacheEntry; detaches the UI and rethrows if initialization fails.

nodes.name: registerFilter
nodes.summary: Creates an ApplicationCacheCheckFilter for the given key and UI and adds it to every handler of the SparkUI for all paths.

nodes.name: invalidate
nodes.summary: Invalidates the cache entry for the given key.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Dumps retained application count, clock time, all cache entries and the metrics into a string for tests and diagnostics.

nodes.name: CacheEntry
nodes.summary: Final class holding a cached LoadedAppUI and a flag saying whether the application has completed and so needs no refreshing.

nodes.name: CacheKey
nodes.summary: Final case class key made of application id and optional attempt id, used to index the application cache.

nodes.name: CacheMetrics
nodes.summary: Metrics source for the application cache holding counters for lookups, lookup failures, evictions and loads plus a load timer, exposed under the source name ApplicationCache.

nodes.name: ApplicationCacheOperations
nodes.summary: Trait describing the cache event API: getAppUI to load a UI, and attachSparkUI and detachSparkUI to connect or disconnect it from the web UI. Implemented by the component that owns the web UI.

nodes.name: ApplicationCacheCheckFilter
nodes.summary: Servlet filter put in front of an incomplete application UI. If the UI is no longer valid it invalidates the cache entry and sends a 302 redirect to the same URL, otherwise it passes the request along the chain.

nodes.name: doFilter
nodes.summary: Takes the UI read lock, forwards the request when the UI is valid, and otherwise invalidates the cache entry and redirects the caller to the current URL (with query string).

nodes.name: EventLogFileCompactor.scala
nodes.summary: Implements compaction of rolled event log files into a single compact file by replaying them with event filter builders and filters, and defines the compaction result types and the writer used for the compact file.

nodes.name: EventLogFileCompactor
nodes.summary: Compacts old event log files into one compact file in two replay phases: builders gather information to create event filters, then the filters decide which events are rewritten. Computes a score from filter statistics (rate of filtered-out task events) and skips compaction when it is too low.

nodes.name: compact
nodes.summary: Entry point: checks preconditions, selects the files to compact, builds filters, and if the minimum score reaches the threshold rewrites the files and deletes the compacted ones; returns a CompactionResult with SUCCESS, NOT_ENOUGH_FILES or LOW_SCORE_FOR_COMPACTION.

nodes.name: assertPrecondition
nodes.summary: Requires that at most one compact file exists in the list and that it is placed first.

nodes.name: initializeBuilders
nodes.summary: Loads all EventFilterBuilder implementations via ServiceLoader and replays the given event log files through a ReplayListenerBus so the builders can collect information.

nodes.name: calculateScore
nodes.summary: Computes the fraction of tasks that would be filtered out (total minus live tasks over total) from filter statistics.

nodes.name: rewrite
nodes.summary: Writes a compact file containing only events accepted by the filters using a CompactedEventLogFileWriter; unidentified lines are copied as they are. Returns the path of the compact file.

nodes.name: cleanupCompactedFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes each compacted event log file from the file system and logs a warning when a file cannot be removed.

nodes.name: findFilesToCompact
nodes.summary: Selects all but the last maxFilesToRetain files for compaction, returning nothing when only a compact file would be compacted.

nodes.name: CompactionResult
nodes.summary: Case class describing the outcome of compaction: a result code and the index of the compact file when successful.

nodes.name: CompactionResultCode
nodes.summary: Enumeration of compaction result codes: SUCCESS, NOT_ENOUGH_FILES and LOW_SCORE_FOR_COMPACTION.

nodes.name: CompactedEventLogFileWriter
nodes.summary: Private writer extending SingleEventLogFileWriter that only uses the original file path to derive the path of the compact file by appending the compacted suffix.

nodes.name: EventLogFileReaders.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the readers that expose information about event log files for an application: an abstract EventLogFileReader with a factory object, a reader for a single log file, and a reader for rolled multi-file logs.

nodes.name: EventLogFileReader
nodes.summary: Abstract base reader for event log file(s) declaring last index, sizes, completion, modification time, zipping, file listing, compression codec and total size. Its companion object creates the right reader for a path or status and opens a (possibly compressed) event log as an input stream.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this node: lines 35-98 are the abstract class, lines 100-165 are the companion object with the factory and openEventLog.

nodes.name: fileSizeForDFS
nodes.summary: Opens the path and returns the file length when the wrapped stream is a DFSInputStream, otherwise None.

nodes.name: addFileAsZipEntry
nodes.summary: Copies the file at the given path into the zip stream as a new entry with the given name.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory taking a FileStatus: returns a single-file reader for a plain file, a rolling reader for a directory holding event log and appstatus files, or None. Overloads: apply(fs, path, lastIndex) chooses a reader from lastIndex, and apply(fs, path) resolves the status first (this node covers the widest overload).

nodes.name: openEventLog
nodes.summary: Opens an event log through a buffered stream and wraps it with the compression codec chosen from the file name (codecs cached in a map), closing the stream on failure; returns a stream of one JSON record per line.

nodes.name: isSingleEventLog
nodes.summary: Treats a non-directory whose name does not start with a dot as a single event log file.

nodes.name: SingleFileEventLogFileReader
nodes.summary: Reader for one event log file. Fetches the file status once on demand, so it may not reflect a file that changes concurrently; completion is derived from the in-progress suffix in the file name.

nodes.name: completed
nodes.summary: Reports the log as completed when the file name (after stripping the compacted suffix) does not end with the in-progress suffix.

nodes.name: fileSizeForLastIndexForDFS
nodes.summary: Returns the known size when completed, otherwise asks the DFS stream for the file length.

nodes.name: zipEventLogFiles
nodes.summary: Adds the single event log file to the zip stream under its own name.

nodes.name: RollingEventLogFilesFileReader
nodes.summary: Reader for a directory of rolled event log files plus an appstatus file. Lists files once, sorts them by index (compact file placed after a normal file of the same index), drops files before the last compact file and verifies there are no missing indices.

nodes.name: eventLogFiles
nodes.summary: Lazy value that filters event log files, sorts them by index, drops files before the last compact file, and requires consecutive indices.

nodes.name: completed
nodes.summary: Reports completion when the appstatus file name does not end with the in-progress suffix.

nodes.name: fileSizeForLastIndexForDFS
nodes.summary: Returns the known size of the last file when completed, otherwise the DFS length of the last event log file.

nodes.name: zipEventLogFiles
nodes.summary: Writes a directory entry and then adds every file in the log directory as a zip entry under it.

nodes.name: dropBeforeLastCompactFile
nodes.summary: Drops event log files that precede the last compacted file in the list.

nodes.name: EventLogFileWriters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the event log writer hierarchy: an abstract EventLogFileWriter base with shared compression, buffering, flushing and rename logic, a single-file writer, and a rolling writer that splits events across several files in a per-application directory. Used to persist application event logs, with the companion object choosing the implementation from configuration.

nodes.name: EventLogFileWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract base class (with companion object) for writers that write JSON event lines into event log files. It reads the compress, codec, overwrite, buffer size and excluded-pattern settings from SparkConf, opens the output stream (a plain FileOutputStream for local paths, a Hadoop stream otherwise), and offers writeLine, closeWriter and renameFile helpers. The companion defines the .inprogress and .compact suffixes, the file permissions, and an apply factory that returns a rolling or single-file writer.

nodes.name: SingleEventLogFileWriter
nodes.summary: Writer that stores all events of an application in one file. It writes to a .inprogress path and renames the file to its final name on stop. Its companion getLogPath encodes app id, attempt id and the compression codec name into the file name.

nodes.name: RollingEventLogFilesWriter
nodes.summary: Writer that rolls over to a new event file when the configured maximum size is reached, keeping each application in its own directory named eventlog_v2_<appId>. It tracks uncompressed bytes with a CountingOutputStream and marks completion through a zero-byte appstatus file; the companion object holds the name prefixes and helpers to build and recognise those paths.

nodes.name: requireLogBaseDirAsDirectory
nodes.summary: Checks that the log base directory is a directory and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise.

nodes.name: initLogFile
nodes.summary: Prepares an event log file for writing: optionally deletes an existing file, opens a local FileOutputStream or a Hadoop stream, wraps it with the codec and a buffer, sets file permissions and installs the PrintWriter produced by the supplied function. Closes the raw stream if setup fails.

nodes.name: writeLine
nodes.summary: Writes one event line unless it starts with an excluded pattern, and optionally flushes the writer and the Hadoop stream.

nodes.name: closeWriter
nodes.summary: Flushes and closes the current writer, logging errors found by checkError and closing the Hadoop stream as a best effort when closing fails.

nodes.name: renameFile
nodes.summary: Renames a log file to its destination, deleting an existing destination when overwrite is set or throwing IOException otherwise, then touches the modification time.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory in the companion object that returns a RollingEventLogFilesWriter when rolling is enabled in the configuration and a SingleEventLogFileWriter otherwise.

nodes.name: codecName
nodes.summary: Extracts the compression codec name from a log file name after stripping the .compact and .inprogress suffixes.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Validates the base directory and opens the .inprogress log file with a UTF-8 PrintWriter.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the writer and renames the .inprogress file to the final log path.

nodes.name: getLogPath
nodes.summary: Builds the file-system-safe log file path for an application from the base dir, app id, attempt id and optional codec name.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Creates the per-application directory (failing if it exists unless overwrite is set), creates the in-progress app status file and rolls to the first event file.

nodes.name: writeEvent
nodes.summary: Rolls to a new event file when the bytes written plus the new event would exceed the maximum size, then writes the event line.

nodes.name: rollEventLogFile
nodes.summary: Closes the current event file, increments the index and opens the next events_<index>_<app> file with a counting output stream. Exposed to the history package for tests.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the writer and renames the in-progress app status file to its completed name.

nodes.name: createAppStatusFile
nodes.summary: Creates the zero-byte app status file (in progress or completed) with the log file permissions.

nodes.name: getAppEventLogDirPath
nodes.summary: Returns the per-application event log directory path (eventlog_v2_ prefix plus app and attempt name).

nodes.name: getAppStatusFilePath
nodes.summary: Returns the app status file path, adding the .inprogress suffix while the application is running.

nodes.name: getEventLogFilePath
nodes.summary: Returns the path of an events_<index>_<app> file, appending the codec name as an extension when given.

nodes.name: getEventLogFileIndex
nodes.summary: Parses the numeric index out of an event log file name and requires that the name is an event log file.

nodes.name: HBaseDelegationTokenProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Delegation token provider for HBase, with the service name hbase. It looks up HBase classes by reflection so HBase is not a compile-time dependency, fetches an authentication token and adds it to the credentials.

nodes.name: HBaseDelegationTokenProvider
nodes.summary: Package-private HadoopDelegationTokenProvider for HBase that obtains tokens through reflective calls to the HBase TokenUtil, first with the older Configuration-based API and, on failure, with a Connection created from ConnectionFactory. Tokens are required only when hbase.security.authentication is kerberos.

nodes.name: obtainDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Tries to obtain an HBase token via TokenUtil.obtainToken(Configuration) and add it to the credentials; on a non-fatal error it logs a warning and retries with the connection-based method. Always returns None since no renewal time is known.

nodes.name: obtainDelegationTokensWithHBaseConn
nodes.summary: Obtains an HBase token through a Connection created by ConnectionFactory and TokenUtil.obtainToken(Connection), adds it to the credentials and closes the connection in a finally block. Used for HBase versions where the Configuration-based call is no longer available.

nodes.name: delegationTokensRequired
nodes.summary: Returns true when the HBase configuration sets hbase.security.authentication to kerberos.

nodes.name: hbaseConf
nodes.summary: Creates an HBase configuration from the Hadoop configuration via HBaseConfiguration.create by reflection, falling back to the original configuration if HBase classes cannot be loaded.

nodes.name: HadoopFSDelegationTokenProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Delegation token provider for Hadoop file systems, with the service name hadoopfs. It fetches tokens for the default, configured and (for yarn masters) staging file systems and computes when the tokens next need renewal.

nodes.name: HadoopFSDelegationTokenProvider
nodes.summary: Provider that obtains file system delegation tokens, working out the renewer, excluding configured hosts from renewal, and caching the token renewal interval from the first call. The companion object hadoopFSsToAccess collects the file systems that need tokens. Tokens are required when Hadoop security is enabled.

nodes.name: obtainDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Fetches delegation tokens for the file systems to access, determines the renewal interval once, and returns the earliest next renewal time (issue date plus interval) over the fetched tokens; logs a warning and returns None on non-fatal errors.

nodes.name: delegationTokensRequired
nodes.summary: Returns whether Hadoop security is enabled for the current user group information.

nodes.name: getTokenRenewer
nodes.summary: Chooses the token renewer: the master principal when spark.master contains yarn, otherwise the current user name; throws SparkException if it is empty.

nodes.name: fetchDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Adds delegation tokens for each file system to the credentials, using an empty renewer for hosts excluded from renewal and the given renewer for the rest.

nodes.name: getTokenRenewalInterval
nodes.summary: Fetches temporary tokens with the logged-in user as renewer, renews each to measure its renewal interval, cancels it, and returns the smallest interval found (or None).

nodes.name: getIssueDate
nodes.summary: Returns a token's issue date, logging warnings and using the current time when the date is unset or in the future.

nodes.name: hadoopFSsToAccess
nodes.summary: Returns the set of file systems needing tokens: those listed in the Kerberos file systems setting, the staging directory file system when the master contains yarn, and the default file system.

nodes.name: CommandUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Utilities used by the worker for launching commands that run with the Spark classpath: building a ProcessBuilder from a Command, substituting arguments, adding library path and secret environment variables, and redirecting process output to files.

nodes.name: CommandUtils
nodes.summary: Package-private singleton with helpers that turn a deploy Command into a runnable ProcessBuilder and redirect process streams to files. It is used by the worker side when launching drivers and executors.

nodes.name: buildProcessBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a ProcessBuilder for a Command: localizes the command (placeholders, class paths, environment), prepends the java command line, and copies the environment into the builder. The env argument exists for testing.

nodes.name: buildCommandSeq
nodes.summary: Creates the full command line by running WorkerCommandBuilder and appending the main class and its arguments.

nodes.name: buildLocalCommand
nodes.summary: Returns a new Command adapted to the local machine: merges library path entries into the environment, adds the auth secret and SSL password variables when security requires them, substitutes arguments, appends class paths, and filters secret options out of the java options.

nodes.name: redirectStream
nodes.summary: Starts a thread that copies an input stream into a file opened in append mode, logging when the redirection closes with an IOException.

nodes.name: DriverRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DriverRunner, which manages the execution of one driver on a standalone worker (including restarting it on failure), plus the small Sleeper and ProcessBuilderLike traits that make the retry loop testable. Used only in standalone cluster deploy mode.

nodes.name: DriverRunner
nodes.summary: Manages the execution of one driver, including automatically restarting the driver on failure (per the class comment, only used in standalone cluster deploy mode). It prepares the driver directory and user jar, builds the process, redirects its output to stdout and stderr files, runs it in a thread, and reports the final DriverState to the worker RPC endpoint.

nodes.name: setClock
nodes.summary: Replaces the Clock used by the retry loop; the source comment says it is decoupled for testing.

nodes.name: setSleeper
nodes.summary: Replaces the Sleeper used for back-off waits between driver relaunches; decoupled for testing.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts a thread named "DriverRunner for <driverId>" that registers a shutdown hook, runs prepareAndRunDriver, sets finalState to FINISHED, KILLED or FAILED from the exit code and kill flag (or ERROR with the exception), removes the hook, and finally sends DriverStateChanged to the worker.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Marks the runner as killed and, under the lock, terminates the driver process with the configured timeout; logs a warning that the process will likely be orphaned if termination fails.

nodes.name: createWorkingDirectory
nodes.summary: Creates the per-driver directory under workDir and throws an IOException if it cannot be created.

nodes.name: downloadUserJar
nodes.summary: Fetches the user jar named by the driver description into the driver directory (skipping the copy if the file already exists) and returns its absolute local path; throws if the jar is missing after the copy.

nodes.name: prepareAndRunDriver
nodes.summary: Creates the working directory, downloads the user jar, writes the driver resources file, builds the process builder with placeholder substitution for {{WORKER_URL}} and {{USER_JAR}}, adds driver log URLs to the environment, and calls runDriver. Defines a local substituteVariables helper.

nodes.name: runDriver
nodes.summary: Sets the process directory, defines a local initialize callback that redirects stdout and stderr to files in the base directory (writing a redacted launch command header to stderr), and delegates to runCommandWithRetry.

nodes.name: runCommandWithRetry
nodes.summary: Starts the command and waits for it; if supervise is set and the exit code is nonzero and the runner was not killed, relaunches it after a sleep that doubles each time (reset when a run lasts longer than 5 seconds). Returns the last exit code.

nodes.name: Sleeper
nodes.summary: Package-private trait with a single method sleep(seconds), used by DriverRunner to wait between relaunch attempts so that tests can substitute their own sleeper. The default instance in DriverRunner sleeps in one-second steps and stops early once the runner is killed.

nodes.name: ProcessBuilderLike
nodes.summary: Trait (with companion object) that exposes start() and command of a process builder. The source comment says it is needed because ProcessBuilder is a final class and cannot be mocked; the companion apply wraps a real ProcessBuilder. Used by DriverRunner.runCommandWithRetry.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that wraps a ProcessBuilder in an anonymous ProcessBuilderLike whose start and command delegate to the builder.

nodes.name: WorkerArguments.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerArguments, the command-line parser for the standalone worker process. It reads defaults from environment variables, parses options, and validates worker memory.

nodes.name: WorkerArguments
nodes.summary: Command-line parser for the worker. Its constructor sets host, port, web UI port, cores, memory, masters, work dir and properties file from defaults and SPARK_WORKER_* environment variables, parses the arguments, loads default Spark properties into the conf, resets logging, applies the configured UI port and checks the memory value.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive pattern match over the argument list handling --host, --port, --cores, --memory, --work-dir, --webui-port, --properties-file, --help and a single positional master URL list; prints usage and exits on bad or missing input.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Prints the worker usage text to stderr and exits the JVM with the given exit code.

nodes.name: inferDefaultCores
nodes.summary: Returns the number of processors available to the JVM as the default core count.

nodes.name: inferDefaultMemory
nodes.summary: Reads total physical memory through the operating system MXBean (falling back to 2 GB on failure), leaves out 1 GB for the operating system and returns the larger of that and Utils.DEFAULT_DRIVER_MEM_MB.

nodes.name: checkWorkerMemory
nodes.summary: Throws an IllegalStateException if the configured worker memory is zero or negative.

nodes.name: WorkerSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerSource, a metrics Source named "worker" that exposes gauges for the worker executor count and used and free cores and memory.

nodes.name: WorkerSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source with sourceName "worker". It registers gauges named executors, coresUsed, memUsed_MB, coresFree and memFree_MB that read the corresponding values from the Worker it is given.

nodes.name: WorkerWatcher.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerWatcher, an RPC endpoint that connects to a worker and terminates the JVM when that connection is severed, giving fate sharing between a worker and its child processes.

nodes.name: WorkerWatcher
nodes.summary: RpcEndpoint which connects to a worker process and terminates the JVM if the connection is severed (fate sharing between a worker and its child processes). It ignores connection events from other addresses, and in testing mode records the shutdown in isShutDown instead of calling System.exit.

nodes.name: isWorker
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given RpcAddress equals the address parsed from the worker URL.

nodes.name: exitNonZero
nodes.summary: In testing mode sets isShutDown; otherwise, the first time only (guarded by an AtomicBoolean), starts a separate thread that calls System.exit(-1), to avoid the dead lock described in the source comment.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles any received message by logging a warning about an unexpected message.

nodes.name: onConnected
nodes.summary: Logs a successful connection when the remote address is the watched worker.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: When the watched worker disconnects, logs an error and calls exitNonZero.

nodes.name: onNetworkError
nodes.summary: When a network error comes from the watched worker address, logs the failure to initialize the connection and calls exitNonZero.

nodes.name: LogPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LogPage, the worker web UI page named "logPage" that shows and serves stdout, stderr and out logs of executors, drivers or the worker itself.

nodes.name: LogPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage registered as "logPage" in the worker UI. Given appId and executorId, a driverId, or the self flag, it resolves the log directory under the work dir, checks it is inside that directory, reads a byte range from the rolled-over log files and renders it as HTML (render) or plain text (renderLog).

nodes.name: renderLog
nodes.summary: Reads appId, executorId, driverId, self, logType, offset and byteLength request parameters, selects the log directory, and returns the requested log bytes as text prefixed with a "Bytes start-end of length" header. Throws if the identifiers do not match a supported combination.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the HTML log page: resolves the log directory and URL-encoded query parameters, fetches the log slice, and assembles Back to Master link, byte range, Load More and Load New buttons, the log text and an onload script from UIUtils.logPageOnloadScript.

nodes.name: getLog
nodes.summary: Returns (text, startByte, endByte, totalLength) for a log type in a directory: rejects unsupported log types and directories outside the work dir, finds the sorted rolled-over files, clamps the offset and extracts the byte range; on exceptions it logs and returns an error message.

nodes.name: WorkerPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerPage, the main page of the standalone worker web UI, listing worker details and its running and finished executors and drivers.

nodes.name: WorkerPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage mounted at the root of the worker UI. It asks the worker endpoint for a WorkerStateResponse and renders worker id, master URL, cores, memory and resources, plus collapsible tables of running and finished executors and drivers; renderJson returns the same state as JSON.

nodes.name: renderJson
nodes.summary: Asks the worker endpoint for its WorkerStateResponse and serializes it with JsonProtocol.writeWorkerState.

nodes.name: formatWorkerResourcesDetails
nodes.summary: Computes free resource addresses (total minus used, per resource name) from the worker state and formats used and free resource details for display.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Fetches the worker state and builds the page: worker detail list, then collapsible tables for running executors, running drivers, finished executors and finished drivers (driver and finished sections shown only when non-empty), wrapped by UIUtils.basicSparkPage.

nodes.name: executorRow
nodes.summary: Renders one table row for an ExecutorRunner: id, state, cores, memory, resources, application id/name/user (with a link to the application UI when running) and stdout/stderr log links.

nodes.name: driverRow
nodes.summary: Renders one table row for a DriverRunner: driver id, main class, state (RUNNING if no final state), cores, memory, resources, stdout/stderr log links and any final exception.

nodes.name: WorkerWebUI.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WorkerWebUI, the web UI server for the standalone worker, which attaches the log page, the worker page, static resources and a /log servlet handler.

nodes.name: WorkerWebUI
nodes.summary: Web UI server for the standalone worker (name "WorkerUI"), built from the worker, its work dir and a requested port, using the worker security manager and conf. It calls initialize at construction. The companion object WorkerWebUI defines STATIC_RESOURCE_BASE as SparkUI.STATIC_RESOURCE_DIR.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates a LogPage and a WorkerPage and attaches them, adds the static resource handler, and attaches a servlet handler at "/log" that returns LogPage.renderLog output.

nodes.name: DriverWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DriverWrapper launcher object used to start a driver program in standalone cluster mode so that it shares fate with the Worker process.

nodes.name: DriverWrapper
nodes.summary: Utility object that launches driver programs so they share fate with the Worker process; used in standalone cluster mode only. It keeps its argument ordering stable because the application submission gateway uses it to launch the driver.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point taking <workerUrl> <userJar> <driverMainClass> [options]. It creates a "Driver" RpcEnv, registers a "workerWatcher" endpoint, installs a child-first or mutable URL class loader holding the user jar depending on a driver class-path-first property, sets up dependencies, invokes the user main class by reflection and shuts the RpcEnv down; with fewer arguments it prints a usage message and exits with -1.

nodes.name: setupDependencies
nodes.summary: Private helper that resolves Maven coordinates from Ivy properties, merges them with the configured jars list, downloads the jars locally and adds them to the given class loader.

nodes.name: ApplicationHistoryProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Declares LoadedAppUI, a loaded Spark UI with a read/write lock and a validity flag, and the abstract ApplicationHistoryProvider contract that the History Server uses to list applications, load their UIs and serve event logs.

nodes.name: LoadedAppUI
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping a loaded Spark UI together with a ReentrantReadWriteLock and a volatile valid flag. The provider invalidates it under the write lock when the underlying app data changes; the ApplicationCache holds read locks while using it, and an invalidated UI stays in memory until the cache sees it or evicts it.

nodes.name: invalidate
nodes.summary: Marks the loaded UI as no longer valid while holding the write lock, signalling the cache that it should not serve new requests.

nodes.name: ApplicationHistoryProvider
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for history providers backing the History Server. It declares listing of applications, loading an application UI, writing event logs to a zip stream, application info lookup and UI view permission checks, with default no-op implementations for start, stop, config, last-updated time and pending event log count.

nodes.name: getEventLogsUnderProcess
nodes.summary: Returns the count of application event logs the provider is still processing so the UI can indicate more applications may appear; defaults to 0 for providers without such a notion.

nodes.name: getLastUpdatedTime
nodes.summary: Returns the time in millis that the provider last updated its application history, or 0 when undefined or unsupported (default).

nodes.name: getListing
nodes.summary: Abstract listing method returning an iterator of ApplicationInfo. There are two overloads: a no-argument one returning all known applications (line 100) and one taking a max count and a predicate (line 109) that returns matching applications up to the maximum.

nodes.name: getAppUI
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the LoadedAppUI for an application id and optional attempt id, or None when the application or attempt is not found.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Hook called when the server is shutting down; default is a no-op.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Hook called when the server is starting up so the provider can initialize and start background threads after construction; default is a no-op.

nodes.name: getConfig
nodes.summary: Returns the configuration map shown on the History Server home page, in map order; defaults to an empty map.

nodes.name: writeEventLogs
nodes.summary: Abstract method that writes the application event logs, compressed into a single zip file, to the given ZipOutputStream; declared to throw SparkException if the logs for the app id cannot be found.

nodes.name: getApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the ApplicationInfo for an app id if it exists.

nodes.name: getEmptyListingHtml
nodes.summary: Returns the html text to display when the application list is empty; defaults to an empty sequence.

nodes.name: onUIDetached
nodes.summary: Hook called when an application UI is unloaded from the history server; default is a no-op.

nodes.name: checkUIViewPermissions
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning whether the given user may view the UI of the given application attempt; documented to throw NoSuchElementException if the attempt does not exist.

nodes.name: BasicEventFilterBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the basic event filter used for event log compaction: BasicEventFilterBuilder tracks live jobs, stages, tasks, RDDs and executors from listener events, and BasicEventFilter (built on JobEventFilter) rejects events for finished jobs and dead executors.

nodes.name: BasicEventFilterBuilder
nodes.summary: SparkListener and EventFilterBuilder that tracks live jobs, stages, tasks, RDDs and executors plus total job, stage and task counters, and passes them to a BasicEventFilter so finished jobs (with their stages, tasks and RDDs) and dead executors can be rejected.

nodes.name: onJobStart
nodes.summary: Counts the job and its stages and records the job id mapped to its stage ids as live.

nodes.name: onJobEnd
nodes.summary: Removes the finished job from the live set and drops the job stages from the live task and RDD maps.

nodes.name: onStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: Records the RDD ids of the submitted stage and prepares an empty live task set for it.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Counts the task and adds its task id to the live task set of its stage if that stage is tracked.

nodes.name: onExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Adds the executor id to the live executor set.

nodes.name: onExecutorRemoved
nodes.summary: Removes the executor id from the live executor set.

nodes.name: createFilter
nodes.summary: Builds FilterStatistics from the total and live counters and returns a new BasicEventFilter holding the live jobs, stages, tasks, RDDs and executors.

nodes.name: JobEventFilter
nodes.summary: Abstract EventFilter that handles only job related events. Its protected acceptFnForJobEvents partial function returns false for events (stage, task, job, unpersist RDD, executor metrics update and speculative task events) that do not belong to live jobs, stages, tasks or RDDs, and true otherwise.

nodes.name: BasicEventFilter
nodes.summary: Concrete JobEventFilter that additionally rejects executor and block manager events for executors that are no longer live; events unrelated to jobs and executors are left unmatched ("Dont mind").

nodes.name: acceptBlockManagerEvent
nodes.summary: Private helper that accepts a block manager event when the block manager belongs to the driver or to a live executor.

nodes.name: acceptFn
nodes.summary: Overrides acceptFn to combine the executor and block manager partial function with the inherited job event partial function using orElse.

nodes.name: EventFilter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the event filtering abstractions for event log compaction: the EventFilterBuilder and EventFilter traits, the FilterStatistics case class, and EventFilter.applyFilterToFile which replays an event log through filters and routes each line to accepted, rejected or unidentified callbacks.

nodes.name: EventFilterBuilder
nodes.summary: Trait extending SparkListenerInterface that gathers information from received events and creates an EventFilter that uses it to decide whether an event is accepted.

nodes.name: createFilter
nodes.summary: Abstract method creating a new EventFilter from the information gathered so far.

nodes.name: EventFilter
nodes.summary: Trait deciding whether a given event is accepted or rejected, via statistics() (used to score compaction) and acceptFn() (a partial function left unmatched for events the filter has no opinion on). The companion object (lines 62-109) holds FilterStatistics and applyFilterToFile.

nodes.name: statistics
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning optional FilterStatistics used to measure the compaction score; None if the filter does not track job related events.

nodes.name: acceptFn
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a partial function mapping an event to true (accept) or false (reject) for events the filter can decide on, leaving others unmatched.

nodes.name: FilterStatistics
nodes.summary: Case class holding total and live counts of jobs, stages and tasks, used to measure how much compaction would filter out.

nodes.name: applyFilterToFile
nodes.summary: Opens an event log, parses each line into a Spark event and applies the filters: an event is rejected only if at least one filter has an opinion and all opinions are false. Calls onAccepted, onRejected or onUnidentified (for unparsable lines) and logs and rethrows on malformed lines.

nodes.name: HistoryAppStatusStore.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HistoryAppStatusStore, an AppStatusStore used by the History Server that rewrites executor log URLs using a configured custom pattern.

nodes.name: HistoryAppStatusStore
nodes.summary: Subclass of AppStatusStore built over a KVStore for a replayed application. At construction it decides whether a custom executor log URL pattern applies (only for completed applications, or incomplete ones if the matching option is set) and, if so, replaces the log URLs in executor summaries it returns.

nodes.name: executorList
nodes.summary: Overrides AppStatusStore.executorList; returns the executor summaries with their log URLs rewritten when a custom URL pattern is configured, otherwise the unchanged list.

nodes.name: executorSummary
nodes.summary: Overrides AppStatusStore.executorSummary; returns one executor's summary with rewritten log URLs when a custom URL pattern is configured.

nodes.name: replaceLogUrls
nodes.summary: Applies the log URL handler's pattern to an executor summary's logs and attributes and returns a copy of the summary carrying the new log map.

nodes.name: replaceExecutorLogs
nodes.summary: Builds a new ExecutorSummary by copying every field of the source summary except the executor logs map, which is replaced by the given one.

nodes.name: HistoryPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HistoryPage, the History Server landing page that lists applications, provider configuration and links to incomplete applications and the server log.

nodes.name: HistoryPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage mounted at the root of the History Server. It renders the provider's config entries, a note about event logs being processed, the last update time, and the application table (loaded by static JavaScript), with a toggle between completed and incomplete applications.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the full landing page XML for a request: reads the showIncomplete parameter, queries the HistoryServer for config, update time and event logs in progress, and assembles script tags, the application list placeholder and page links into a basic Spark page.

nodes.name: shouldDisplayApplications
nodes.summary: Returns true if the History Server holds at least one application whose completed state differs from the requested incomplete flag.

nodes.name: makePageLink
nodes.summary: Builds the base-URI-prefixed link to the root page with the showIncomplete query parameter set to the given value.

nodes.name: isApplicationCompleted
nodes.summary: Returns true when an application has at least one attempt and its first listed attempt is completed.

nodes.name: HistoryServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the HistoryServer web server that renders Spark UIs of completed applications from an ApplicationHistoryProvider, plus its companion object holding the daemon entry point.

nodes.name: HistoryServer
nodes.summary: WebUI subclass (also a UIRoot and ApplicationCacheOperations) that serves completed applications' UIs. It delegates listings and UI loading to an ApplicationHistoryProvider, caches loaded UIs in an ApplicationCache, attaches the history page, log page, REST API and a servlet that loads an application's UI on first request and redirects to it. The companion object provides main, security setup and the attempt URI helper.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this node; the object (main, createSecurityManager, initSecurity, getAttemptURI) spans lines 299-370.

nodes.name: withSparkUI
nodes.summary: Runs a function against the cached SparkUI of an application attempt by delegating to the ApplicationCache.

nodes.name: checkUIViewPermissions
nodes.summary: Asks the history provider whether a user may view the UI of the given application attempt.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Attaches the history page, log page, REST API handler, static resources, render-log handler and the application loader servlet context at the history path prefix.

nodes.name: bind
nodes.summary: Binds the HTTP server by calling the parent implementation.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the web server and then stops the history provider.

nodes.name: attachSparkUI
nodes.summary: Adds the handlers of a reconstructed SparkUI to the bound server; asserts that the server was bound first.

nodes.name: detachSparkUI
nodes.summary: Removes the handlers of a SparkUI from the bound server and tells the provider the UI was detached.

nodes.name: getAppUI
nodes.summary: Asks the provider to load the application UI for an app and attempt id, returning it with its completed state if found.

nodes.name: getApplicationList
nodes.summary: Returns the provider's listing of known applications, in descending order of end time.

nodes.name: getEventLogsUnderProcess
nodes.summary: Returns the number of event logs the provider is currently processing.

nodes.name: getLastUpdatedTime
nodes.summary: Returns the time at which the provider last updated its listing.

nodes.name: getApplicationInfoList
nodes.summary: Returns up to max applications matching a filter from the provider (UIRoot implementation). A no-argument overload at lines 223-225 returns getApplicationList().

nodes.name: getApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Looks up an application's info by id through the provider.

nodes.name: writeEventLogs
nodes.summary: Writes the event logs of an application attempt to a zip stream by delegating to the provider.

nodes.name: emptyListingHtml
nodes.summary: Returns the provider's HTML to show when the application list is empty.

nodes.name: getProviderConfig
nodes.summary: Returns the provider's configuration map shown on the listing page.

nodes.name: loadAppUi
nodes.summary: Forces the application cache to load an application's UI; returns false if a NoSuchElementException shows it does not exist.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns a multi-line description of the server, its provider and its cache for diagnostics.

nodes.name: loaderServlet.doGet
nodes.summary: GET handler of the anonymous loader servlet (field loaderServlet, lines 77-132). Parses app and attempt ids from the path, tries to load the UI as a single-attempt and then multi-attempt application, answers 404 if not found, and otherwise redirects to the requested URI keeping the query string. doTrace in the same servlet rejects TRACE.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Daemon entry point of the History Server: parses arguments, sets up security, instantiates the configured provider by reflection, builds and binds the server, starts the provider, registers a shutdown hook and blocks forever.

nodes.name: createSecurityManager
nodes.summary: Turns off authentication and the generic ACL switch in the given conf (logging that only the History Server ACL setting is used), then creates a SecurityManager so the server can run in a secured cluster.

nodes.name: initSecurity
nodes.summary: When Kerberos is enabled in the History configuration, reads the principal and keytab (failing if missing) and logs in from the keytab.

nodes.name: getAttemptURI
nodes.summary: Builds the UI path for an application and optional attempt id under the history path prefix.

nodes.name: HistoryServerArguments.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the command-line argument parser for the History Server, handling --help and --properties-file and printing usage built from History config entries.

nodes.name: HistoryServerArguments
nodes.summary: Command-line parser for the HistoryServer. At construction it parses the arguments, loads default Spark properties (plus an optional properties file) into the SparkConf, re-initializes structured logging, and prints usage listing the History config entries then exits on --help or bad options.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive parser over the argument list: --help or -h prints usage and exits 0, --properties-file stores the path, an empty list ends parsing, and anything else prints an error with usage and exits 1.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Reflects over the fields of the History config object to collect every ConfigEntry, formats them (split into History Server options and FsHistoryProvider options, with wrapped docs and defaults) to stderr, and exits with the given code.

nodes.name: HistoryServerDiskManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HistoryServerDiskManager, which tracks and bounds local disk usage of the History Server's per-application stores, with leases, eviction of idle stores and a persisted ApplicationStoreInfo record.

nodes.name: HistoryServerDiskManager
nodes.summary: Keeps track of disk usage of application stores under an apps directory and temp directory, persisting per-store info in a listing KVStore. It leases space ahead of writing a store, evicts the least recently accessed idle stores when space runs short, marks stores as active when opened, and releases or deletes them; usage may temporarily exceed the configured maximum.

nodes.name: Lease
nodes.summary: Handle for space leased to write an application store in a temporary directory. commit moves the finished store to its final location and updates accounting (marking it active); rollback deletes the temp directory and returns the leased space.

nodes.name: ApplicationStoreInfo
nodes.summary: Private case class persisted in the listing store describing one on-disk application store: its path, last access time, app id, optional attempt id and size. The path and lastAccess fields are KV index parameters used to look up and order stores for eviction.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Start-up step: sets usage from the apps directory size, deletes leftover temp stores, removes listing entries whose store directory no longer exists, corrects recorded sizes that drifted from the real directory size, and logs the resulting usage.

nodes.name: lease
nodes.summary: Reserves space for a new store sized as an approximation of the event log size, evicting idle stores if needed, creates a restricted temp directory for it and returns a Lease; may let usage exceed the maximum and logs when it does.

nodes.name: openStore
nodes.summary: Returns the directory of an application's store if it exists, marking it active so it is not evicted, and records its current size and access time in the listing.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Marks an application's store as no longer in use: removes it from the active map and deducts its size, then either deletes the store (when requested) or re-measures it and updates the listing and usage accounting.

nodes.name: approximateSize
nodes.summary: Estimates the disk store size from the event log size: twice the log size for compressed logs, half for uncompressed ones.

nodes.name: free
nodes.summary: Returns the remaining space under the maximum usage (never negative), counting leased space as used.

nodes.name: committed
nodes.summary: Returns the amount of committed disk space.

nodes.name: deleteStore
nodes.summary: Deletes a store directory recursively and removes its ApplicationStoreInfo from the listing.

nodes.name: makeRoom
nodes.summary: If free space is below the requested size, walks stores in last-access order, picks idle ones to evict until enough space is covered, deletes them, updates usage and logs the result or a warning if nothing could be freed.

nodes.name: appStorePath
nodes.summary: Computes the store directory for an app id and optional attempt id, using a file extension chosen from the hybrid store disk backend setting.

nodes.name: updateApplicationStoreInfo
nodes.summary: Writes an ApplicationStoreInfo with the current clock time and the given size for an application's store into the listing.

nodes.name: updateUsage
nodes.summary: Atomically adjusts the current usage (and committed usage when requested) by a delta, throwing if either counter goes negative.

nodes.name: sizeOf
nodes.summary: Returns the size of a directory (marked visible for testing).

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Finishes a lease: replaces any existing store at the destination, releases the leased amount, measures the temp store, makes room, renames it into place, updates committed usage and listing, warns if the maximum is exceeded and marks the app active. Fails if the app is already active.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: Abandons a lease: returns the leased space to the accounting and deletes the temporary directory.

nodes.name: HistoryServerMemoryManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private HistoryServerMemoryManager, which tracks how much memory the in-memory stores used by the history server are leasing against a configured maximum.

nodes.name: HistoryServerMemoryManager
nodes.summary: Keeps an AtomicLong of current usage and a map of per-application (appId, attemptId) leases. Callers lease an estimate of memory before building a hybrid store and release it afterwards; a lease that would exceed the configured maximum fails.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Logs the current and maximum memory usage when the manager starts.

nodes.name: lease
nodes.summary: Estimates the memory needed for an event log from its size and codec, throws a RuntimeException if adding it would exceed the maximum, otherwise records the lease for the app and attempt and adds it to current usage.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Removes the lease recorded for an app and attempt and subtracts its size from current usage, logging the release; does nothing if no lease exists.

nodes.name: approximateMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Maps an event log size to an estimated in-memory size: 10x for the ZSTD codec, 4x for any other codec, and half the size when there is no codec.

nodes.name: LogPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the history server LogPage, a WebUIPage named logPage that renders a slice of a log file with Load More and Load New buttons.

nodes.name: LogPage
nodes.summary: A package-private WebUIPage registered as logPage. Its render method reads the logType, offset and byteLength request parameters, fetches the log text with deploy Utils.getLog, and builds the HTML and onload script for incremental log loading.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the log page for the history server: reads request parameters, calls getLog, assembles the byte-range header, buttons, log text and a nonce-marked onload script, and wraps them with UIUtils.basicSparkPage.

nodes.name: CspNonce.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CspNonce object, a thread-local holder for the per-request Content Security Policy nonce used to mark inline scripts as trusted.

nodes.name: CspNonce
nodes.summary: A private[spark] object wrapping a ThreadLocal[String]. HttpSecurityFilter generates a nonce per request and clears it afterwards, and UI pages read it with get to put on inline script tags.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Creates a random UUID string, stores it in the current thread's nonce slot and returns it.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the nonce stored for the current thread, that is, for the current request.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes the nonce from the current thread once the request has completed.

nodes.name: DriverLogPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the live driver log UI: DriverLogPage renders and serves slices of the driver log files, and DriverLogTab attaches it as a logs tab of SparkUI.

nodes.name: DriverLogPage
nodes.summary: A WebUIPage that requires a configured local driver log directory. It serves the supported log types (the driver log file, stderr and stdout) as an HTML page via render and as plain text via renderLog, reading rolled-over files through a private getLog.

nodes.name: DriverLogTab
nodes.summary: A SparkUITab named logs that creates a DriverLogPage for the parent SparkUI's conf, attaches it and exposes it through getPage.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the driver log HTML page: reads logType, offset and byteLength, gets the log slice, creates the header, Load More and Load New buttons and a nonce-marked onload script, and wraps them with UIUtils.headerSparkPage.

nodes.name: renderLog
nodes.summary: Returns the requested log slice as plain text, prefixed with a line stating the byte range, total length and location.

nodes.name: getLog
nodes.summary: Validates the log type, lists the sorted rolled-over files, computes start and end byte indexes from the offset and requested length, and reads that range; returns an error text and zero offsets for an unsupported type or on exception.

nodes.name: GraphUIData.scala
nodes.summary: Defines GraphUIData, which generates HTML and JavaScript for timeline, histogram and area-stack graphs, and JsCollector, which gathers the JavaScript statements and module imports emitted for a page.

nodes.name: GraphUIData
nodes.summary: A private[spark] helper holding the div ids, data points, axis bounds, Y unit and optional batch interval of a graph. Each generate method adds JavaScript to a JsCollector and returns the div element where the graph is drawn.

nodes.name: JsCollector
nodes.summary: A private[spark] collector of JavaScript variable names, prepared statements, statements and module imports for one request. toHtml renders them all as one nonce-marked module script that runs when the DOM is ready.

nodes.name: generateDataJs
nodes.summary: Serializes the (x, y) data points to a JavaScript array literal, assigns it to a fresh variable name from the collector and registers the declaration as a prepared statement.

nodes.name: generateTimelineHtml
nodes.summary: Registers the timeline imports, a registerTimeline call and a drawTimeline call (with the batch interval when defined), and returns the timeline div.

nodes.name: generateHistogramHtml
nodes.summary: Registers the histogram imports, a registerHistogram call and a drawHistogram call over the Y values (with the batch interval when defined), and returns the histogram div.

nodes.name: generateAreaStackHtmlWithData
nodes.summary: Pads the per-label duration data, serializes the values and sorted labels to JavaScript variables, registers a drawAreaStack call and returns the timeline div.

nodes.name: nextVariableName
nodes.summary: Increments a counter and returns the next unused JavaScript variable name of the form v<N>.

nodes.name: addPreparedStatement
nodes.summary: Appends a JavaScript statement that runs before the regular statements.

nodes.name: addStatement
nodes.summary: Appends a JavaScript statement that runs after the prepared statements.

nodes.name: addImports
nodes.summary: Adds a module import line for the given source file and function names, formatted with UIUtils.formatImportJavaScript. An overload at lines 163-165 adds a ready-made import string directly.

nodes.name: toHtml
nodes.summary: Builds a module script element, tagged with the CSP nonce, that contains the imports and runs the prepared statements and statements in a document ready handler.

nodes.name: HttpSecurityFilter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the servlet filter HttpSecurityFilter, which applies access control, a CSP nonce and security response headers to each UI request, and XssSafeRequest, which sanitizes request parameters.

nodes.name: HttpSecurityFilter
nodes.summary: A private servlet Filter that, for every request, sets cache and security headers, checks doAs impersonation and UI view permissions through SecurityManager, and passes on the request wrapped in XssSafeRequest.

nodes.name: XssSafeRequest
nodes.summary: A private HttpServletRequestWrapper that returns the effective user as the remote user and exposes request parameter names and values stripped of newlines and single quotes and HTML-escaped.

nodes.name: doFilter
nodes.summary: Sets Cache-Control, generates the CSP nonce and optionally the Content-Security-Policy header, enforces doAs admin checks and UI view permissions (sending 403 on failure), sets X-Frame-Options and related headers, runs the chain with a sanitized request, and always clears the nonce.

nodes.name: getParameterNames
nodes.summary: Returns an Enumeration over the sanitized parameter names.

nodes.name: getParameter
nodes.summary: Returns the first sanitized value of the named parameter, or null if it is absent.

nodes.name: stripXSS
nodes.summary: Removes newlines, URL-encoded newlines and single quotes with a regex and then HTML-escapes the string; null stays null.

nodes.name: JWSFilter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JWSFilter, an optional servlet filter that lets a request through only if its Authorization Bearer header carries a JWS signed with a configured secret key.

nodes.name: JWSFilter
nodes.summary: A private servlet Filter enabled through spark.ui.filters with a secretKey parameter. It rejects requests with a missing, malformed or invalid Bearer token with HTTP 403.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Decodes the base64url secretKey init parameter and builds the HMAC SecretKey; it fails if the parameter is missing or the key is too weak.

nodes.name: doFilter
nodes.summary: Sets Cache-Control, reads the Authorization header, verifies a Bearer token's signature and continues the chain, or sends 403 for a missing header, a malformed header or a JwtException.

nodes.name: EnvironmentPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Environment tab of the Spark UI: EnvironmentPage renders a tabbed shell for runtime, Spark, resource profile, Hadoop, system, metrics and classpath information, and EnvironmentTab attaches it.

nodes.name: EnvironmentPage
nodes.summary: A WebUIPage that embeds a JSON map of known config default values and a tab layout with a loading spinner per section, then loads utils.js and environmentpage.js so the browser fills the panes.

nodes.name: EnvironmentTab
nodes.summary: A SparkUITab named environment that creates an EnvironmentPage for the parent SparkUI's conf and the AppStatusStore and attaches it.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Collects the default value strings of all known config entries into a JSON string (escaping closing tags), builds the tab navigation and spinner panes with two module script tags, and wraps them with UIUtils.headerSparkPage using DataTables.

nodes.name: ExecutorHeapHistogramPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutorHeapHistogramPage, a UI page named heapHistogram that shows a table of an executor's heap histogram.

nodes.name: ExecutorHeapHistogramPage
nodes.summary: A WebUIPage that, for the executorId request parameter, asks the optional SparkContext for the executor's heap histogram, parses each line with a regex into rank, instances, bytes, class name and module columns, and renders a sortable table.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalArgumentException if executorId is missing, fetches the histogram, turns matching lines into table rows (ignoring header and total lines), shows an error text if none was returned, and wraps the result with UIUtils.headerSparkPage.

nodes.name: ConsoleProgressBar.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ConsoleProgressBar, which draws a one-line text progress bar for active stages on the console. Used by the driver to give terminal feedback while stages run.

nodes.name: ConsoleProgressBar
nodes.summary: Polls the status store for active stages on a fixed-rate daemon timer and prints a carriage-return-overwritten progress bar to stderr, showing at most three stages in one line and only after a stage has run at least 500 ms. Created with a SparkContext and torn down with stop() because the timer thread would otherwise retain the context.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Timer callback that skips if a finish happened within the delay window, filters active stages older than 500 ms from the status store, and shows up to three of them.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Builds the progress text for each stage as header, '=' and '>' bar and a (complete + active) / total tail sized to the terminal width, then prints it only if it changed or a minute has passed.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Overwrites the current progress line with spaces and resets the cached bar if one was shown.

nodes.name: finishAll
nodes.summary: Clears the progress bar and records the finish time so the bar does not interleave with job output.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Cancels the refresh timer future and shuts down the timer executor so the thread does not retain the SparkContext.

nodes.name: ExecutorThreadDumpPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the executor thread dump page of the web UI, which lists an executor's threads with their states, locks and stack traces and optionally a flame graph. It belongs to the executors tab.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds HTML using Scala XML literals; the page is registered under the path threadDump.

nodes.name: ExecutorThreadDumpPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage for the path threadDump that reads an executorId request parameter, asks the SparkContext for that executor's thread dump and renders a summary table, an optional flame graph and a sortable per-thread table with a search box and download link. Shows an error text if the dump cannot be fetched.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Decodes the executorId parameter (throwing IllegalArgumentException when missing), fetches the thread dump from the SparkContext, builds table rows with blocked-by links and held locks, and wraps the content in the standard Spark page header.

nodes.name: drawExecutorFlamegraph
nodes.summary: Emits the flame graph section: embeds the JSON from FlamegraphNode in a hidden div, loads the stylesheet and scripts under /static and adds an inline module script (with a CSP nonce) that calls drawFlamegraph and toggleFlamegraph.

nodes.name: threadDumpSummary
nodes.summary: Builds a collapsible summary table counting threads per thread state with percentages of the total.

nodes.name: FlamegraphNode.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FlamegraphNode, a tree node that aggregates thread stack traces into flame graph data and serializes it as JSON. Used by the executor thread dump page.

nodes.name: FlamegraphNode
nodes.summary: Case class (with companion object) representing a named node with a sample count and child nodes keyed by frame name. The case class is lines 25-33 and the companion object is lines 35-50; toJsonString renders a node and its children as a JSON string, and the companion apply builds a tree from an array of thread stack traces.

nodes.name: toJsonString
nodes.summary: Recursively renders this node as a JSON object with its name, value and children array.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory taking an Array of ThreadStackTrace: builds a root node and, for each thread, walks its stack frames in reversed order, creating or reusing child nodes (names JSON-escaped) and incrementing their counts.

nodes.name: AllStagesPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AllStagesPage, the landing page of the Stages tab listing active, pending, completed, skipped and failed stages and fair scheduler pools.

nodes.name: AllStagesPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage with an empty path under the StagesTab that shows a summary list of stage counts per status, an optional pool table when the fair scheduler is used, and one collapsible StageTableBase per non-empty status. Pool data is only available in live UIs.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Collects pools from the SparkContext (live UIs only) with their stored PoolData, reads all stages and the app summary from the store, builds per-status summaries and tables, and renders them under the title 'Stages for All Jobs'.

nodes.name: summaryAndTableForStatus
nodes.summary: For one StageStatus filters the stages (failed ones reversed), and returns None for both parts when empty, otherwise a summary list item and a collapsible StageTableBase table with kill support only for active stages.

nodes.name: statusName
nodes.summary: Maps a StageStatus to its lowercase label used in anchors and table tags.

nodes.name: summaryContent

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Builds the summary list item linking to a status section, adding the id completed-summary for the completed status.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Wraps a stage table in a collapsible section with a header showing the status and its count.

nodes.name: JobDataUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JobDataUtil helper object that computes and formats a job's duration and submission time for UI display.

nodes.name: JobDataUtil
nodes.summary: Object with helpers over the JobData API type: raw duration in milliseconds (using the current time for running jobs) and formatted duration and submission time strings, with 'Unknown' when no submission time exists.

nodes.name: getDuration
nodes.summary: Returns the elapsed milliseconds between submission and completion, or until now if not completed; None when never submitted.

nodes.name: getFormattedDuration

nodes.name: getFormattedSubmissionTime
nodes.summary: Formats the job submission time through UIUtils.formatDate, or returns 'Unknown'.

nodes.name: PoolPage.scala

nodes.name: PoolTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PoolTable, which renders an HTML table of fair scheduler pools. Used by the all-stages page and the pool page.

nodes.name: PoolTable
nodes.summary: Takes a map from Schedulable to PoolData and a StagesTab and produces a table with pool name link, minimum share, weight, active stage count, running tasks and scheduling mode.

nodes.name: toNodeSeq
nodes.summary: Renders the table header with tooltips and one row per pool.

nodes.name: poolRow
nodes.summary: Renders one pool row, linking the pool name to the stages/pool page with a URL-encoded poolname parameter.

nodes.name: StageDataUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StageDataUtil helper object that computes and formats a stage's duration and submission time for UI display.

nodes.name: StageDataUtil
nodes.summary: Public object with helpers over the StageData API type: raw duration in milliseconds (using the current time for running stages) and formatted duration and submission time strings, with 'Unknown' when no submission time exists.

nodes.name: getDuration
nodes.summary: Returns the elapsed milliseconds between submission and completion, or until now if not completed; None when never submitted.

nodes.name: getFormattedDuration
nodes.summary: Formats getDuration through UIUtils.formatDuration, or returns 'Unknown'.

nodes.name: getFormattedSubmissionTime
nodes.summary: Formats the stage submission time through UIUtils.formatDate, or returns 'Unknown'.
