nodes.summary: Defines TaskThreadDumpPage, the web UI page that shows the current thread dump of one running task on an executor.

nodes.name: TaskThreadDumpPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage under the path taskThreadDump that reads executorId and taskId request parameters, asks the SparkContext for that task's thread dump and renders the thread's id, name, state, locks and full text. Shows a message if the task finished or the dump failed.

nodes.name: executorThreadDumpUrl
nodes.summary: Builds the link to the executors page for an executor, anchored at the blocking thread id.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Decodes the required executorId and taskId parameters (throwing IllegalArgumentException when missing), fetches the task thread dump from the SparkContext and renders a one-row thread table with a blocked-by link and the dump text.

nodes.name: FsHistoryProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FsHistoryProvider, the ApplicationHistoryProvider implementation that scans configured event log directories, replays logs to build a listing store of applications, and creates per-attempt UI stores on demand. Also holds the listing store entity types (LogInfo, AttemptInfoWrapper, ApplicationInfoWrapper) and AppListingListener used to extract listing data from event logs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a private[history] class, companion object, an Enumeration and several Jackson/KVIndex annotated store entities.

nodes.name: FsHistoryProvider
nodes.summary: Provides application history from event logs stored in file systems. It periodically scans one or more log directories for new or grown event logs (comparing log size), replays them into a listing KVStore, cleans expired logs and driver logs, and on request rebuilds a per-attempt status store (disk, hybrid or in-memory) to render a SparkUI. The companion object (lines 1742-1758) holds the event name prefixes used to filter replayed events and CURRENT_LISTING_VERSION.

nodes.name: isScanDisabled
nodes.summary: Checks whether scanning is disabled for a directory by matching its fully qualified path against the configured disabled-path regex patterns.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Starts polling immediately if the file system is not in safe mode; otherwise starts a safe mode check thread and returns it.

nodes.name: startSafeModeCheckThread
nodes.summary: Spawns a daemon thread that waits until the file system leaves safe mode and then starts polling, so the history UI can still be shown while the file system is unavailable. A failure in the thread logs an error and exits the process unless an error handler is supplied.

nodes.name: startPolling
nodes.summary: Initializes the disk and memory managers, validates the log directories (failing only if none is valid) and, outside tests, schedules periodic tasks for checkForLogs, cleanLogs and cleanDriverLogs on the single-thread pool.

nodes.name: getListing
nodes.summary: Returns the application listing in descending end time order from the listing store. Two overloads exist: one returns all entries and one returns up to max entries matching a predicate.

nodes.name: getApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Loads one application from the listing store and returns it as an ApplicationInfo, or None when it is not found.

nodes.name: getAppUI
nodes.summary: Builds the SparkUI for an application attempt. It loads the listing entry (optionally from a fallback rolling log location), creates a security manager, loads a disk or in-memory status store, creates the UI with a HistoryAppStatusStore, attaches plugin tabs and records it as an active UI.

nodes.name: loadFromFallbackLocation
nodes.summary: Used for on-demand loading of a rolling event log that is not yet in the listing: resolves the log path across all directories, merges its listing data immediately and then loads the application.

nodes.name: getConfig
nodes.summary: Returns the key-value configuration shown in the history UI: event log directories with display names, safe mode state and the driver log directory when configured.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Sets the caller context to HISTORY and runs initialize, remembering the returned init thread.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Interrupts the init thread, shuts down the scheduling and replay and compaction executors, closes all active UI stores and closes the listing store.

nodes.name: onUIDetached
nodes.summary: Removes a UI from the active set when it is detached, closes its store under the write lock and releases its disk store, deleting the files if the UI is no longer valid.

nodes.name: checkUIViewPermissions
nodes.summary: Checks whether a user may view an attempt's UI by building a security manager from the attempt's ACLs; throws NoSuchElementException when the attempt is missing.

nodes.name: checkForLogs
nodes.summary: Periodic scan that checks every non-disabled log directory for new or updated event logs, then removes listing entries for logs that disappeared (excluding processing entries and scan-disabled directories) and records the new scan time.

nodes.name: FsHistoryProviderMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class carrying the listing database version, UI version and log directory.

nodes.name: LogType
nodes.summary: Enumeration with the values DriverLogs and EventLogs, used to tag LogInfo entries by the kind of log file they track.

nodes.name: LogInfo
nodes.summary: Case class stored in the listing store that tracks an event log or driver log file: path, last processed time, log type, app and attempt ids, file size, last index and compaction state. Tracks valid and invalid logs so the cleaner knows which files are safe to delete.

nodes.name: AttemptInfoWrapper
nodes.summary: Listing store wrapper around ApplicationAttemptInfo that adds the log path, file size, last index, admin and view ACLs and the log source name and full path of an attempt.

nodes.name: ApplicationInfoWrapper
nodes.summary: Listing store entity pairing an ApplicationInfo with its list of AttemptInfoWrapper values. It exposes KVIndex-annotated id, endTime and oldestAttempt accessors and converts back to an ApplicationInfo with attempts via toApplicationInfo.

nodes.name: AppListingListener
nodes.summary: SparkListener used while replaying an event log to collect the application id, name, attempt times, user, Spark version and UI ACLs into an ApplicationInfoWrapper. It can throw HaltReplayException once the application id and first environment update have been seen, so replay stops early.

nodes.name: MutableApplicationInfo
nodes.summary: Private helper in AppListingListener holding the mutable application id and name and building an ApplicationInfoWrapper in toView.

nodes.name: MutableAttemptInfo
nodes.summary: Private helper in AppListingListener holding mutable attempt fields (times, user, completion, Spark version, ACLs) and building an AttemptInfoWrapper, including the log source name and path from the provider, in toView.

nodes.name: checkForLogsInDir
nodes.summary: Scans one log directory: lists readers, skips inaccessible and in-progress entries, sorts by modification time, decides which logs need reparsing (size change, new entry, expired entry deletion, fast in-progress parsing) and submits merge tasks to the replay executor for them.

nodes.name: shouldReloadLog
nodes.summary: Decides whether an event log must be re-read by comparing completion state, last index and file size against the stored LogInfo, with an extra DFS length check for in-progress logs.

nodes.name: cleanAppData
nodes.summary: Removes an attempt (or the whole application) from the listing store when its log file is stale, then invalidates and closes any active UI and releases its disk store.

nodes.name: writeEventLogs
nodes.summary: Writes the event log files of an application (one attempt or all attempts) into a zip stream by resolving each log path and delegating to the reader's zipEventLogFiles; closes the stream at the end.

nodes.name: resolveLogPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the file system and full path for a log file name, trying the known source directory first, then scanning all log directories and finally falling back to the first directory.

nodes.name: logDirForPath
nodes.summary: Finds the configured log directory string that contains a path, using normalized path matching first and string prefix matching second, defaulting to the first directory.

nodes.name: getLogDirInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the display name and full path of the configured log directory that contains a given log path, falling back to the first directory on failure.

nodes.name: isDescendantOf
nodes.summary: Returns true when a path equals an ancestor path or has it among its parents.

nodes.name: mergeApplicationListing
nodes.summary: Task body run on the replay executor: reads the previous compaction evaluation, merges the log into the listing, runs the age-based log check when the cleaner is enabled, handles permission and missing-file errors, and on success submits a compaction task.

nodes.name: doMergeApplicationListing
nodes.summary: Visible-for-testing entry point that replays a log file and saves the application in the listing store by delegating to doMergeApplicationListingInternal.

nodes.name: doMergeApplicationListingInternal
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive routine that replays a log with an AppListingListener and an events filter for application start, end, log start and environment update events, optionally skips to near the end of the file to find the end event, then writes the application and LogInfo to the listing store or re-parses the whole log when the end event was not found.

nodes.name: compact
nodes.summary: Runs rolling event log compaction for a reader if its last index has not been evaluated yet, using the compactor for the log's directory, and records the evaluated index in LogInfo.

nodes.name: invalidateUI
nodes.summary: Marks the active UI of an app attempt (if any) as invalid and closes its store.

nodes.name: checkAndCleanLog
nodes.summary: Deletes a single log if it is an invalid or corrupt log older than the max log age, and deletes expired attempts of its application.

nodes.name: cleanLogs
nodes.summary: Periodic cleaner: deletes attempts older than the max log age, deletes invalid logs without an application, trims completed attempts when the number of logs exceeds the configured maximum and clears expired entries from the inaccessible list.

nodes.name: deleteAttemptLogs
nodes.summary: Rewrites or deletes the listing entry for an application and deletes the log files and app data of the attempts to delete; returns how many logs were deleted.

nodes.name: cleanDriverLogs
nodes.summary: Periodic cleaner for driver logs in the configured DFS directory: tracks new files in the listing, refreshes entries whose size or modification time changed, deletes files past the max driver log age and removes stale driver log entries.

nodes.name: rebuildAppStore
nodes.summary: Rebuilds an application status store from its event log by replaying events through an AppStatusListener (and plugin listeners) on a tracking store with async updates disabled.

nodes.name: parseAppEventLogs
nodes.summary: Replays each event log file through a ReplayListenerBus, stopping early when the bus reports an error or a halt.

nodes.name: isFsInSafeMode
nodes.summary: Checks whether any distributed file system of the log directories is in safe mode; an overload takes a single DistributedFileSystem and queries only active name nodes.

nodes.name: addListing
nodes.summary: Writes an application to the listing store under the listing lock, merging its attempt into any existing application entry and sorting attempts by start time.

nodes.name: loadDiskStore
nodes.summary: Loads a disk-based status store for an attempt: tries to open an existing store, otherwise (when enabled) tries to create a hybrid store and finally falls back to creating a disk store by replaying the event log.

nodes.name: createHybridStore
nodes.summary: Creates a HybridStore by leasing memory, rebuilding the app store in memory (retrying once on IOException), leasing disk space and starting a background switch to a disk store, with commit or rollback handled by a switch listener.

nodes.name: createDiskStore
nodes.summary: Creates a disk store by leasing disk space, rebuilding the app store into it from the event log (retrying once on IOException) and committing the lease.

nodes.name: createInMemoryStore
nodes.summary: Creates an in-memory store by rebuilding the app store from the event log, retrying once on IOException.

nodes.name: deleteLog
nodes.summary: Deletes a log path recursively unless it is marked inaccessible, logging permission and IO errors; returns whether the delete happened.

nodes.name: submitLogProcessTask
nodes.summary: Marks a path as being processed and submits a task to the given executor; if submission fails it logs an error and ends processing for the path.

nodes.name: createSecurityManager
nodes.summary: Builds a SecurityManager for an attempt, enabling ACLs per configuration and applying the history-wide and per-attempt admin and view ACLs and groups.

nodes.name: onApplicationStart
nodes.summary: Records application id, name, attempt id, start time, last updated time and Spark user from the start event, then checks whether replay can halt.

nodes.name: onApplicationEnd
nodes.summary: Records end time, last updated time from the reader's modification time, duration and completion from the application end event.

nodes.name: onEnvironmentUpdate
nodes.summary: On the first environment update only, reads the UI view and admin ACLs and ACL groups from the Spark properties, then checks whether replay can halt.

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: Captures the Spark version from SparkListenerLogStart events.

nodes.name: applicationInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the collected ApplicationInfoWrapper when an application id was seen, otherwise None.

nodes.name: checkProgress
nodes.summary: Throws HaltReplayException once, if halting is enabled and both the application id and the environment update have been read.

nodes.name: toView
nodes.summary: Builds an ApplicationInfoWrapper from the collected id and name and a single attempt view.

nodes.name: toView
nodes.summary: Builds an AttemptInfoWrapper from the collected fields, asking the provider for the log source name and full path.

nodes.name: HybridStore.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HybridStore, a KVStore for the history server that first holds data in an InMemoryStore while event logs are replayed and then dumps it to a disk-based store in a background thread. Also defines the SwitchToDiskStoreListener callback trait in its companion object.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class implementing a Java KVStore interface; the companion object only holds the listener trait.

nodes.name: HybridStore
nodes.summary: KVStore implementation that speeds up loading of event logs by writing to an InMemoryStore first and, once the app store is restored, copying all written classes to a disk-based store (LevelDB or RocksDB) in a daemon thread and then switching reads and writes to the disk store. Tracks written classes in klassMap, forbids delete and removeAllByIndexValues once switching has started, and its companion object holds the SwitchToDiskStoreListener trait.

nodes.name: getMetadata
nodes.summary: Delegates getMetadata to the store currently in use (in-memory or disk).

nodes.name: setMetadata
nodes.summary: Delegates setMetadata to the store currently in use.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads a value by class and natural key from the store currently in use.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a value to the current store and, while the background thread has not started, records the value's class in klassMap so it will be dumped to disk later.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Deletes an entry from the current store, but throws IllegalStateException once the background thread has started switching to the disk store.

nodes.name: view
nodes.summary: Returns a KVStoreView of the given class from the store currently in use.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Counts entries of a class, optionally for an indexed value, in the store currently in use. Two overloads (lines 93-95 and 97-99) share this id.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Marks the store closed, waits for a running background thread to finish, then closes the in-memory store and the disk store if one was set.

nodes.name: removeAllByIndexValues
nodes.summary: Removes all entries matching the given index values from the current store, but throws IllegalStateException once switching to the disk store has begun.

nodes.name: setDiskStore
nodes.summary: Sets the disk-based KVStore that the in-memory data will be dumped to.

nodes.name: switchToDiskStore
nodes.summary: Starts a daemon thread that copies every class in klassMap from the in-memory store to the LevelDB or RocksDB disk store via writeAll, then notifies the listener of success, turns off the in-memory flag and closes the in-memory store. On any exception it reports failure through the listener; it returns immediately if the store is already closed.

nodes.name: getStore
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory store while the use-in-memory flag is set, otherwise the disk store. Used by all delegating methods and visible for testing.

nodes.name: HybridStore.SwitchToDiskStoreListener
nodes.summary: Trait declared in the HybridStore companion object. Implementations receive a callback when the background dump to the disk store succeeds or fails.

nodes.name: onSwitchToDiskStoreSuccess
nodes.summary: Callback invoked after all data has been written to the disk store.

nodes.name: onSwitchToDiskStoreFail
nodes.summary: Callback invoked with the exception when dumping data to the disk store fails.

nodes.name: AppHistoryServerPlugin.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the AppHistoryServerPlugin trait, the interface through which modules outside core supply history listeners and UI setup to the history server.

nodes.name: AppHistoryServerPlugin
nodes.summary: Private trait describing a history-server plugin: createListeners builds listeners that replay event logs into an ElementTrackingStore, setupUI attaches the plugin tabs to a SparkUI, and displayOrder (default Integer.MAX_VALUE) orders plugin tabs.

nodes.name: AppStatusSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the appStatus metrics source with counters for jobs, stages, tasks and excluded executors, plus a gauge for job duration.

nodes.name: JobDuration
nodes.summary: Gauge[Long] that reports the current value of an AtomicLong, used to expose the job duration metric.

nodes.name: AppStatusSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source named "appStatus" that registers a job duration gauge and counters for failed, skipped and completed stages, succeeded and failed jobs, and completed, failed, killed and skipped tasks, plus executor exclusion counters (with deprecated blacklist variants). The companion object builds counters and creates the source only when the app status source config flag is enabled.

nodes.name: getCounter
nodes.summary: Companion helper that returns a Counter registered in the implicit MetricRegistry under the given prefix and name.

nodes.name: createSource
nodes.summary: Returns Some(new AppStatusSource) when the configuration flag for the app status source is true, otherwise None.

nodes.name: AppStatusUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds helper functions that compute scheduler delay, getting-result time and quantile values from task data for the status API.

nodes.name: AppStatusUtils
nodes.summary: Private object with time-derivation helpers for tasks (scheduler delay and getting-result time, each with a TaskData overload and a raw-values overload) and a function that picks quantile values from a sorted sequence.

nodes.name: schedulerDelay
nodes.summary: Returns the scheduler delay of a finished task using its metrics and duration, or 0 while the task is still running. The overload at lines 45-54 takes raw timing values and returns max(0, duration - runTime - deserializeTime - serializeTime - gettingResultTime).

nodes.name: gettingResultTime
nodes.summary: Computes the time spent fetching a task result from fetchStart, the launch time and the duration, using the current time when the task has no duration. The overload at lines 41-43 takes a TaskData.

nodes.name: fetchStart
nodes.summary: Private helper returning the result fetch start time in milliseconds of a task, or -1 if it is not defined.

nodes.name: getQuantilesValue
nodes.summary: Returns the values at the requested quantile positions of an indexed sequence, or zeros when the sequence is empty.

nodes.name: ApplicationListResource.scala
nodes.summary: REST resource that lists applications, filtered by status and by start and end date windows.

nodes.name: ApplicationListResource
nodes.summary: Jersey resource producing JSON whose GET method returns the applications matching the status, date range and limit query parameters; an application counts as running if its latest attempt is not completed.

nodes.name: appList

nodes.summary: Serializes an ApplicationEnvironmentInfoWrapper into protobuf bytes.

nodes.summary: Builds the protobuf ApplicationEnvironmentInfo from runtime info, the property pair lists and the resource profiles.

nodes.summary: Rebuilds an ApplicationEnvironmentInfo from its protobuf form, reading optional string fields and mapping property pairs to tuples.

nodes.name: getBarrierClusters

nodes.name: getIndeterminateNodes

nodes.name: makeOperationGraph

nodes.name: makeDotFile

nodes.name: makeDotNode

nodes.name: makeDotSubgraph

nodes.name: PrometheusResource.scala

nodes.languageNotes: Class spans lines 37-109 (annotations from line 37) and the companion object spans lines 111-121.

nodes.name: executors
nodes.summary: GET handler at path prometheus that writes a spark_info line with the Spark version and revision, then for each executor from the status store emits labeled lines for block, memory, disk, core, task, GC, input, shuffle read and write values, optional storage memory metrics and peak memory metrics. Returns the assembled text.

nodes.name: getServletHandler
nodes.summary: Companion object method that creates a ServletContextHandler with context path /metrics, registers a Jersey ServletContainer scanning the org.apache.spark.status.api.v1 package, stores the given UIRoot in the servlet context and maps it to /*.

nodes.name: SimpleDateParam.scala
nodes.summary: Holds a small request parameter class that parses a date string from a REST query into a millisecond timestamp.

nodes.name: SimpleDateParam
nodes.summary: Wraps the original string value of a date query parameter and eagerly computes its timestamp in milliseconds. It first tries the pattern yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSz, then falls back to yyyy-MM-dd interpreted in GMT, and otherwise throws a WebApplicationException with a 400 Bad Request response saying the date could not be parsed.

nodes.name: StagesResource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the REST resource for stages: listing stages, fetching stage or stage attempt data, task summaries, task lists and a server-side paginated and searchable task table, all backed by the application status store.
nodes.languageNotes: JAX-RS annotations (@GET, @Path, @QueryParam, @DefaultValue) drive routing; every handler wraps its work in withUI.

nodes.name: StagesResource
nodes.summary: JAX-RS resource producing JSON for stage endpoints. It extends BaseAppResource and reads stage and task data from the UI's status store, with helpers for quantile parsing, server-side pagination and task search.

nodes.name: stageList
nodes.summary: GET handler listing stages filtered by status, with optional details, summaries, quantiles and task status filters. When details and a task status filter are given it keeps only stages with at least one task in the requested state.

nodes.name: stageData
nodes.summary: GET handler at {stageId} returning all attempts of a stage; throws NotFoundException (unknown stage) when the result is empty.

nodes.name: oneAttemptData
nodes.summary: GET handler at {stageId}/{stageAttemptId} returning one attempt. On NoSuchElementException it builds a message that lists the found attempts or says the stage is unknown, and throws NotFoundException.

nodes.name: taskSummary
nodes.summary: GET handler at taskSummary returning task metric distributions for a stage attempt at the requested quantiles (default 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95); throws NotFoundException if no tasks reported metrics yet.

nodes.name: taskList
nodes.summary: GET handler at taskList returning tasks of a stage attempt with offset, length, sort order and status filters, delegating to the store.

nodes.name: taskTable
nodes.summary: GET handler at taskTable used by the stages page data table. It decodes query parameters, detects a search value, loads the page of tasks through doPagination, optionally filters and slices them with filterTaskList, and returns a map with aaData, recordsTotal and recordsFiltered.

nodes.name: doPagination
nodes.summary: Reads sort column, order, start and length from the query parameters (sorting by Logs falls back to Index) and fetches the matching tasks from the store; when a search is active it fetches all rows so the search covers the whole table.

nodes.name: filterTaskList
nodes.summary: Returns the tasks for which any displayed field or formatted task metric (durations, byte sizes, record counts, shuffle values) contains the lower-cased search string.

nodes.name: parseQuantileString
nodes.summary: Splits a comma separated string into doubles and throws BadParameterException naming the quantiles parameter if any entry is not a number.

nodes.name: PagedTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the generic paging support for UI tables: a data source that slices rows per page, a page result holder, and a PagedTable trait that renders an HTML table with page navigation, sortable headers and request parameter helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala XML literals to build HTML directly in code.

nodes.name: PagedDataSource
nodes.summary: Abstract data source parameterized by row type and page size. Subclasses supply the total data size and a slice of rows; pageData clamps the requested page number and returns the rows of that page.

nodes.name: PageData
nodes.summary: Case class holding the total number of pages and the rows of one page, returned by PagedDataSource.pageData.

nodes.name: PagedTable
nodes.summary: Trait for tables that render one page of rows as HTML plus page navigation. Implementors define the table id, CSS class, form field names, data source, headers and row rendering; the trait provides table, pageNavigation, header rows with sort links, and parameter parsing helpers.

nodes.name: pageData
nodes.summary: Computes the total page count (one page holds everything when pageSize is zero or less), clamps the requested page into range, slices the corresponding rows and returns them as PageData.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Renders the table for one page: top and bottom page navigation around the headers and rows. If an IndexOutOfBoundsException occurs it shows navigation for page 1 and an alert with the exception string.

nodes.name: pageNavigation
nodes.summary: Builds the page navigation: groups of 10 page numbers with previous and next page and group links, the current page disabled, and a form with hidden fields from the current query string for jumping to a page and setting the page size.

nodes.name: getParameterOtherTable
nodes.summary: Returns the request parameters whose names do not start with the given table tag, joined as name=value pairs with ampersands, so other tables on the page keep their state.

nodes.name: getTableParameters
nodes.summary: Reads the sort column, descending flag and page size for a table tag from the request, defaulting to the given sort column (descending when it equals the default) and a page size of 100.

nodes.name: isSortColumnValid
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalArgumentException (Unknown column) unless the sort column is among the sortable headers of the header info.

nodes.name: headerRow
nodes.summary: Builds the thead row from header info: the active sort column gets a link that flips direction with an arrow, other sortable columns get sort links, and non-sortable columns are plain; each header is wrapped in a tooltip span.

nodes.name: ToolTips.scala
nodes.summary: Collects the tooltip help strings shown in the web UI for task and stage metrics, timelines, DAG visualizations, executor limits and stage duration.

nodes.name: ToolTips
nodes.summary: Singleton object of string constants such as SCHEDULER_DELAY, TASK_DESERIALIZATION_TIME, SHUFFLE_READ, GC_TIME, PEAK_EXECUTION_MEMORY, JOB_TIMELINE, STAGE_DAG, APPLICATION_EXECUTOR_LIMIT and DURATION, each holding the explanatory text for a UI column or section.
nodes.languageNotes: A separate ToolTips object exists in the ui/storage package; this one is in org.apache.spark.ui.

nodes.name: UIWorkloadGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Provides a command line tool that keeps submitting a mix of jobs to a SparkContext to exercise the web UI, used as an internal testing tool.

nodes.name: UIWorkloadGenerator
nodes.summary: Singleton object with a main method that runs job sets against a given master and scheduling mode (FIFO or FAIR). The job mix covers count, cache and count, a single shuffle, entirely and partially failed phases, and jobs with delays.
nodes.languageNotes: Usage text in the source: ./bin/spark-class org.apache.spark.ui.UIWorkloadGenerator [master] [FIFO|FAIR] [#job set (4 jobs per set)].

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Validates three arguments (master, scheduling mode, number of job sets), creates a SparkContext named Spark UI tester, then for every job set starts each job on its own thread with a description property (and pool property under FAIR), waits 5 seconds between launches, waits on a semaphore for all threads and stops the context. Nested helper setProperties is not a separate node.

nodes.name: RDDPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Web UI page that shows storage details for a single RDD (storage level, partition counts, memory and disk sizes), a per-executor data distribution table and a paged table of the RDD blocks. Also holds the row data, data source and paged table classes used to list and sort the blocks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala XML literals are used to build the HTML directly; the helper classes are private[ui].

nodes.name: RDDPage
nodes.summary: Web UI page (prefix "rdd") that renders storage info for the RDD named by the "id" request parameter. Shows summary fields, a worker table and a block table, or an "RDD Not Found" page if the RDD is unknown.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Reads the "id" and "block.page" parameters, loads the RDD storage info, builds the worker table and the BlockPagedTable, and returns the full page through UIUtils.headerSparkPage. Falls back to an "RDD Not Found" page on NoSuchElementException and shows an alert if the block table parameters are invalid.

nodes.name: workerRow
nodes.summary: Renders one HTML table row for an RDD data distribution entry: address, on-heap and off-heap memory used and remaining, and disk usage. (The one-line private workerHeader helper has no node.)

nodes.name: BlockTableRowData
nodes.summary: Private case class holding one rendered row of the RDD block table: block name, storage level, memory used, disk used and the executors string.

nodes.name: BlockDataSource
nodes.summary: Paged data source for the RDD block table. Converts RDDPartitionInfo entries into BlockTableRowData rows, resolving executor ids to host:port addresses, and sorts them by the requested column and direction.

nodes.name: sliceData
nodes.summary: Returns the requested slice of the sorted block rows for the current page.

nodes.name: blockRow
nodes.summary: Maps one RDDPartitionInfo to a BlockTableRowData, translating executor ids to addresses, sorting and joining them with spaces.

nodes.name: ordering
nodes.summary: Builds an Ordering over BlockTableRowData for a column name ("Block Name", "Storage Level", "Size in Memory", "Size on Disk", "Executors"), reversed when descending. Throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown column.

nodes.name: BlockPagedTable
nodes.summary: Paged HTML table of RDD blocks. Reads sort column, direction and page size from the request, builds a BlockDataSource, and renders headers, rows and page links under the "block" tag.

nodes.name: pageLink
nodes.summary: Builds the URL of a given page of the block table, carrying the page number, URL-encoded sort column, sort direction and page size.

nodes.name: goButtonFormPath
nodes.summary: Builds the form path used by the page-size "Go" button, including the encoded sort column and direction.

nodes.name: headers
nodes.summary: Builds the sortable header row for the block table (Block Name, Storage Level, Size in Memory, Size on Disk, Executors) after validating the sort column.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Renders one HTML table row for a BlockTableRowData, formatting memory and disk sizes as readable byte strings.

nodes.name: StoragePage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Storage tab landing page that lists all persisted RDDs and, when present, aggregated and per-block tables for streaming receiver blocks. Includes a small private summary class aggregating stream blocks per executor.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala XML literals build the HTML; rddTable, receiverBlockTables and streamBlockStorageLevelDescriptionAndSize are private[storage].

nodes.name: StoragePage
nodes.summary: Web UI page (empty prefix) listing RDDs currently stored, with links to each RDD page, plus tables of receiver stream blocks grouped by executor and by block id.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the Storage page by concatenating the RDD table and receiver block tables and wrapping them with UIUtils.headerSparkPage.

nodes.name: rddTable
nodes.summary: Builds the collapsible "RDDs" table with ID, name, storage level, cached partitions, fraction cached and sizes; returns Nil when no RDD is persisted.

nodes.name: rddRow
nodes.summary: Renders one RDD row with a link to the RDD detail page, cached partition count, percentage cached and byte sizes.

nodes.name: receiverBlockTables
nodes.summary: Builds the "Receiver Blocks" section from stream blocks, grouped by name, combining the executor metrics table and the block table; returns Nil if there are no blocks.

nodes.name: executorMetricsTable
nodes.summary: Groups stream blocks by executor id into ExecutorStreamSummary objects and renders them as the aggregated per-executor table.

nodes.name: executorMetricsTableRow
nodes.summary: Renders one row of the per-executor stream block table: executor id, address, total memory and disk size and stream block count.

nodes.name: streamBlockTable
nodes.summary: Renders the "Blocks" listing table of stream blocks, or Nil when empty.

nodes.name: streamBlockTableRow
nodes.summary: Renders all rows for one block id, with a first subrow plus one subrow per additional replication.

nodes.name: streamBlockTableSubrow

nodes.name: streamBlockStorageLevelDescriptionAndSize

nodes.name: ExecutorStreamSummary

nodes.name: StorageTab.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Storage tab of the Spark Web UI, which attaches the StoragePage and the RDDPage when it is created.

nodes.name: StorageTab

nodes.name: ApplicationInfoWrapperSerializer
nodes.summary: Package-private ProtobufSerDe implementation for ApplicationInfoWrapper. serialize builds a StoreTypes.ApplicationInfoWrapper and returns its bytes; deserialize parses bytes back into an ApplicationInfoWrapper, mapping optional fields through Utils helpers.

nodes.summary: Serializes an ApplicationInfoWrapper into protobuf bytes by building the nested ApplicationInfo message and setting it as info.

nodes.summary: Builds a StoreTypes.ApplicationInfo from an ApplicationInfo, setting id and name as strings, copying the optional core and memory settings when present, and adding each attempt.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Parses protobuf bytes into a StoreTypes.CachedQuantile and constructs a CachedQuantile with every metric field passed by name.

nodes.name: ExecutorStageSummarySerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object that converts the API-level ExecutorStageSummary to and from its StoreTypes protobuf message. Reused by the ExecutorStageSummaryWrapper serializer.

nodes.name: JobDataWrapperSerializer.scala

nodes.name: serializeJobData
nodes.summary: Builds a StoreTypes.JobData from a JobData, copying task and stage counters, the status, optional description, times and group, stage ids, job tags and the killed tasks summary map.

nodes.name: ToolTips.scala
nodes.summary: Holds tooltip text constants for the column headers of the Storage tab (RDD name, storage level, cached partitions, fraction cached, size in memory, size on disk).

nodes.name: ToolTips
nodes.summary: Package-private object in the ui.storage package with six string constants describing the Storage page columns, to be shown as header tooltips.

nodes.name: BytesToBytesMap.java
nodes.summary: Defines BytesToBytesMap, an append-only hash map whose keys and values are contiguous byte regions stored in memory pages, plus its iterator classes and the Location handle. Used where records must be hashed and then optionally handed to the external sorter in place.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class built on raw memory offsets; keys and values are addressed through a base object plus offset rather than Java objects.

nodes.name: BytesToBytesMap
nodes.summary: Append-only hash map extending MemoryConsumer, backed by a power-of-2 long array that uses quadratic probing with triangular numbers. Keys and values are copied into data pages obtained from the TaskMemoryManager. The map can grow and rehash, can spill pages through a destructive iterator, and holds up to 2^29 keys.

nodes.name: MapIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over all entries of the map that returns the same Location object on each next() call. In destructive mode it frees each data page as it moves on and can spill pages to disk, after which it reads the remaining records back from spill files.

nodes.name: MapIteratorWithKeyIndex
nodes.summary: Iterator that walks the key slots of the map's long array and then the values of each key, so the key index is preserved in the Location. The class comment says it is NOT thread-safe.

nodes.name: Location
nodes.summary: Handle returned by lookup and iterators describing one key and value position (base object, offsets, lengths). Its append method writes a new value for the key into the current data page, links values of the same key, and triggers growth of the table when the threshold is reached.

nodes.name: BytesToBytesMap
nodes.summary: Constructor taking the task memory manager, block manager, serializer manager, initial capacity, load factor and page size; validates the capacity and page size and allocates the initial table. A second overload (lines 205-217) takes fewer arguments, reads the block manager and serializer manager from SparkEnv and fixes the load factor at 0.5.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns a non-destructive MapIterator over all values of the map; every next() call returns the same Location object.

nodes.name: destructiveIterator
nodes.summary: Updates the peak memory figure and returns a destructive MapIterator that frees each page as it advances. The map must not be used after this call.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Looks up a key by hashing it with Murmur3 (seed 42) and returns the shared Location handle. An overload at lines 513-516 takes a precomputed hash instead.

nodes.name: safeLookup
nodes.summary: Probes the long array with quadratic probing, comparing the stored 32-bit hash and then the key bytes, and fills the provided Location with either the matching entry or the empty slot. It counts lookups and probes and can be used by several threads because the Location is passed in.

nodes.name: acquireNewPage
nodes.summary: Allocates a new data page for the required size and makes it the current page, resetting the page cursor; returns false if memory cannot be acquired.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: MemoryConsumer spill hook: if another consumer triggered it and a destructive iterator exists, delegates to that iterator's spill; otherwise releases nothing.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Allocates and zeroes the long array for a capacity rounded up to a power of 2 (at least 64, at most MAX_CAPACITY) and sets the growth threshold and the hash mask.

nodes.name: free
nodes.summary: Frees the long array, all data pages and any spill files owned by the map; it can be called more than once.

nodes.name: getTotalMemoryConsumption
nodes.summary: Returns the total bytes used by all data pages plus the long array.

nodes.name: updatePeakMemoryUsed
nodes.summary: Raises the recorded peak memory use if the current total consumption is higher.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets the map to its initial state: frees the array and all pages, reallocates the table at the initial capacity and clears the counters and page pointers.

nodes.name: growAndRehash
nodes.summary: Allocates a larger table using the growth strategy, then re-inserts every entry by masking its stored 32-bit hash (no rehashing of keys), and frees the old array.

nodes.name: MapIterator
nodes.summary: Private constructor; in destructive mode registers itself as the map's destructive iterator and releases the long array right away.

nodes.name: advanceToNextPage
nodes.summary: Moves to the next data page (removing and freeing the previous one when destructive, outside the lock to avoid a deadlock) or, when pages are exhausted, switches to reading records from the first spill file.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns whether records remain; when none remain it deletes a leftover spill file.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the Location for the next record, either from the current in-memory page or from the spill reader, advancing pages when needed.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Synchronized spill used by a destructive iterator: writes whole data pages (except the current one) to spill files through UnsafeSorterSpillWriter and frees them until the requested number of bytes is released.

nodes.name: handleFailedDelete
nodes.summary: Removes the first spill writer's file from disk and logs an error if the file cannot be deleted.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next Location: either the next value of the current key or the next occupied slot of the long array, keeping the key index.

nodes.name: updateAddressesAndSizes
nodes.summary: Decodes the record header at a base object and offset to set the key and value offsets and lengths. An overload (lines 585-589) first resolves a page and offset from an encoded address.

nodes.name: with
nodes.summary: Points the Location at a table slot with its hash code and defined flag, and decodes the stored record if the key is defined. Overloads at lines 615-619 (page and offset, for iteration) and 625-635 (base, offset and length, for spill reading) set it for other cases.

nodes.name: nextValue
nodes.summary: Follows the 8-byte pointer at the end of the record to the next value stored under the same key; returns false at the end of the chain.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Appends a key and value (both 8-byte aligned) to the current data page, links it at the head of the value chain, updates the table slot and counters, and grows the table when the threshold is reached. Returns false if the key limit is hit or memory cannot be acquired.

nodes.summary: Defines every Spark SQL configuration entry: the SQLConf companion object registers roughly 720 buildConf/buildStaticConf entries (lines 253-7420) plus the deprecated and removed config maps (7446-7560), and the SQLConf class (7572-8974) exposes typed getters over a per-session settings map. Entry groups by theme with line ranges: registry and active-conf lookup (62-252: buildConf, buildStaticConf, withExistingConf, get); analyzer incl. single-pass resolver (253-535, spark.sql.analyzer.*); optimizer rules, plan-change logging and validation (536-692: spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules, planChangeLog.level); dynamic partition pruning and runtime bloom filters (693-835); in-memory columnar cache (836-899); joins and shuffle (900-1040: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, spark.sql.shuffle.partitions); adaptive execution (1041-1335: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled, adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled, adaptive.skewJoin.enabled, adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes); collation settings (1157-1206); subexpression elimination and parser caches (1335-1484); Parquet (1485-1784: spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown, parquet.mergeSchema, parquet.outputTimestampType), ORC (1785-1853), Hive metastore pruning (1854-1950); data source V2 pushdown and default source (2037-2100: spark.sql.sources.default); bucketing and V2 bucketing (2137-2299); caching, ordinals, commit protocol, partition discovery and function path resolution (2300-2552); whole-stage codegen (2553-2705: spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage, codegen.factoryMode, codegen.fallback); file source partitioning and corrupt-file handling (2706-2777: spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes, files.ignoreCorruptFiles); exchange and subquery reuse (2778-2839); structured streaming state store, checkpoint and file sink/source (2840-3550 and 3740-4001); variable substitution, codegen aggregate/join switches and view behaviour (3551-3739); statistics and CBO (4002-4152: spark.sql.cbo.enabled, cbo.joinReorder.enabled); session time zone (4157: spark.sql.session.timeZone); window, session-window, join and shuffle-dependency spill thresholds (4166-4363); Arrow and Python UDF execution (4364-4893: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled, execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch); decimal, redaction, SQL scripting and continuous streaming (4894-5030); insert and store-assignment policy (5084-5190: spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode, spark.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy); ANSI mode and default columns (5180-5300: spark.sql.ansi.enabled, ansi.enforceReservedKeywords, defaultColumn.enabled); nested schema pruning and subquery decorrelation (5313-5510: spark.sql.optimizer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled); CSV, REPL eager eval, artifact isolation, Avro (5520-5657); legacy flags and string limits (5658-5846: spark.sql.legacy.*); timestamp type, catalog and CTE settings (5848-6030: spark.sql.timestampType, spark.sql.defaultCatalog); JDBC dialect legacy mappings (6034-6148); filter pushdown, JSON and Variant (6149-6282); datetime rebase modes (6283-6424); bucket coalescing, char/varchar, PySpark inference and misc legacy (6425-6830); local relation limits (6827-6893); pipelines and late additions (6894-7420). The file also holds nine nested Enumeration/holder objects, DeprecatedConfig and RemovedConfig.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with one big companion object of config vals declared through a builder DSL (doc, version, internal, typed conf, createWithDefault); a class of typed accessors follows.

nodes.name: SQLConf
nodes.summary: Single id for both the SQLConf companion object (lines 62-7561) and the SQLConf class (7572-8974). The object is the registry: buildConf(key) and buildStaticConf(key) create ConfigBuilder entries and register them in a copy-on-write map, so duplicate keys fail; static keys are tracked separately (isStaticConfigKey) and cannot be changed by sessions; SQLConf.get returns the active conf (thread-local fallback, withExistingConf scope, ReadOnlySQLConf inside tasks, error in the scheduler event loop thread). Entry groups with ranges are listed in the file summary. Key literal names by area. Optimizer: spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules (562), optimizer.maxIterations (571), optimizer.inSetConversionThreshold (578), optimizer.dynamicPartitionPruning.enabled (693), optimizer.runtime.bloomFilter.enabled (739), optimizer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled (5326), spark.sql.cbo.enabled (4091), cbo.joinReorder.enabled (4105). Adaptive execution: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled (1050, default true), adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes (1093), adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled (1101), adaptive.skewJoin.enabled (1230), adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled (1221), adaptive.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (1280). Shuffle partitions and joins: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (1000, default 200), spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (949, default 10MB), spark.sql.join.preferSortMergeJoin (900), spark.sql.shuffledHashJoinFactor (956). Codegen: spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage (2553, default true), codegen.factoryMode (2607), codegen.fallback (2619), codegen.hugeMethodLimit (2644), codegen.maxFields (2599). ANSI mode: spark.sql.ansi.enabled (5180, key from SqlApiConfHelper, default true unless env SPARK_ANSI_SQL_MODE is false), ansi.enforceReservedKeywords (5191), ansi.doubleQuotedIdentifiers (5199), spark.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy (5151). File sources: spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes (2706, default 128MB), files.openCostInBytes (2714), files.ignoreCorruptFiles (2745), spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown (1565), parquet.mergeSchema (1495), parquet.enableVectorizedReader (1665), spark.sql.orc.filterPushdown (1832), spark.sql.sources.default (2073), spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode (5088). Arrow: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled (4405), execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch (4580), execution.arrow.localRelationThreshold (4441), execution.arrow.compression.codec (4639). Session and misc: spark.sql.session.timeZone (4157), spark.sql.caseSensitive (1384), spark.sql.timestampType (5852), spark.sql.defaultCatalog (5903), spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy (6004). Also 7446-7560: deprecatedSQLConfigs (warns on use of old keys) and removedSQLConfigs (rejects non-default values). The class holds a synchronized settings map and a ConfigReader; its ~480 accessors (7583-8752) wrap getConf(entry) per setting, with a few computed ones (numShufflePartitions, resolver, canonicalize, defaultPathOrder). Methods 8757-8974: setConf, setConfString (validates value via the registered entry), getConf overloads, getConfString, getAllConfs, getAllDefinedConfs (public entries with key, value, doc, version), redactOptions, contains, setConfWithCheck (warns on deprecated keys, rejects removed keys with non-default value), unsetConf, clear, clone, copy (tests), isModifiable. Overload note: getConf has three overloads (8797, 8806, 8815) and setConf two; one function node each is given.
