nodes.summary: Enumeration with EXCEPTION and LAST_WIN; the value type of spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy (line 5932), the policy for duplicate map keys in builtin map-building functions.

nodes.name: SQLConf.DeprecatedConfig
nodes.summary: Case class (key, version, comment) describing a deprecated SQL config; toDeprecationString builds the warning text. Used by the deprecatedSQLConfigs map (7452) and logged by SQLConf.setConfWithCheck and unsetConf.

nodes.name: SQLConf.RemovedConfig
nodes.summary: Case class (key, version, defaultValue, comment) describing a removed SQL config; its body throws an internal error if the version string is not a valid major.minor.patch. Used by removedSQLConfigs (7513) and checked by SQLConf.requireDefaultValueOfRemovedConf.

nodes.name: buildConf
nodes.summary: Creates a ConfigBuilder for the given key and registers the finished entry in the SQLConf entry map (via onCreate(register)); every non-static SQL config val in the object is declared through it.

nodes.name: buildStaticConf
nodes.summary: Like buildConf, but when the entry is created it also records the key as a static config key, so the setting cannot be changed after the first session and shared state are initialized.

nodes.name: mergeNonStaticSQLConfigs
nodes.summary: Copies the given config map into a SQLConf with setConfString, skipping keys registered as static; used so that later-created sessions respect static configs and only change non-static ones.

nodes.name: withExistingConf
nodes.summary: Runs a block with a given SQLConf installed in a thread-local, restoring the previous value afterwards; SQLConf.get prefers this conf, which matters for tasks and for the scheduler event loop thread.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the active SQLConf: inside a running task it returns the withExistingConf value or a new ReadOnlySQLConf from the task context; on the DAGScheduler event loop thread it requires withExistingConf (error when testing); otherwise the thread-local or the registered confGetter (the active session's conf or the fallback).

nodes.name: numShufflePartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the shuffle partition count: when adaptive execution and partition coalescing are both enabled it uses the optional initial partition number setting, falling back to spark.sql.shuffle.partitions; otherwise the plain default.

nodes.name: resolver
nodes.summary: Returns the case-sensitive or case-insensitive name resolver from the catalyst analysis package, depending on caseSensitiveAnalysis.

nodes.name: defaultPathOrder
nodes.summary: Orders the given persistent catalog path entries together with the system.session and system.builtin namespaces according to sessionFunctionResolutionOrder (first, second or last).

nodes.name: setConfString
nodes.summary: Sets a config by string key and value: rejects null, validates the value with the registered entry's valueConverter when the key is registered, then stores it through setConfWithCheck.

nodes.name: getConf
nodes.summary: Reads a typed config entry from the settings map or its default. Overloads: getConf(entry, defaultValue) at 8797, getConf(entry) at 8806, getConf(OptionalConfigEntry) at 8815; all require the entry to be registered. This node uses the first overload's range.

nodes.name: getConfString
nodes.summary: Returns the string value of a key or the supplied default, following FallbackConfigEntry parents and validating the default via the registered entry; the one-argument overload at 8783 throws if the key is unknown. This node uses the two-argument overload's range.

nodes.name: getAllDefinedConfs
nodes.summary: Loads the static and Hive-module configs, then returns key, display value, doc and version for every public registered entry; used to list all defined SQL configs.

nodes.name: redactOptions
nodes.summary: Applies the SQL options redaction pattern and the secret redaction pattern to a sequence of key-value options via Utils.redact; the Map overload at 8895 delegates to it. This node uses the sequence overload's range.

nodes.name: setConfWithCheck
nodes.summary: Stores a key and value in the settings map after logging a deprecation warning for deprecated keys and rejecting non-default values for removed configs.

nodes.name: isModifiable
nodes.summary: Returns true when the key is a registered config and is not a static config key, i.e. a session may change it.

nodes.name: StaticSQLConf.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the object of static SQL configuration entries, which are cross-session and immutable: users can read them through SparkSession.conf but cannot set or unset them. Entries live in lines 35-316 and are grouped as: catalog and warehouse (35-63: spark.sql.warehouse.dir, spark.sql.catalogImplementation, spark.sql.globalTempDatabase), metastore and cache sizing (71-96, 276-286: spark.sql.sources.schemaStringLengthThreshold, spark.sql.filesourceTableRelationCacheSize, spark.sql.metadataCacheTTLSeconds), codegen and debug (89-114: spark.sql.codegen.cache.maxEntries, spark.sql.codegen.comments, spark.sql.debug), extensions, cache serializer and listeners (116-171: spark.sql.extensions, spark.sql.cache.serializer, spark.sql.queryExecutionListeners), UI and event settings (173-178, 222-228, 253-298), thread thresholds (180-220), and legacy or misc flags (230-251, 300-316).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file whose single object builds typed config entries with the buildStaticConf builder imported from SQLConf.

nodes.name: StaticSQLConf
nodes.summary: Object holding about 30 static SQL config entries, each created with SQLConf.buildStaticConf and a fluent chain of doc, version, type (intConf, stringConf, booleanConf, timeConf), checkValue and createWithDefault or createOptional. Static means shared by all sessions and not changeable by users. Groups: (1) Catalog and warehouse, lines 35-63: WAREHOUSE_PATH = spark.sql.warehouse.dir (default resolves 'spark-warehouse'), CATALOG_DEFAULT_DATABASE = spark.sql.catalog.<session catalog name>.defaultDatabase (default 'default'), CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION = spark.sql.catalogImplementation (allowed values hive or in-memory, default in-memory), GLOBAL_TEMP_DATABASE = spark.sql.globalTempDatabase (lowercased, default global_temp). (2) Metastore schema and cache sizing, lines 71-96 and 276-286: SCHEMA_STRING_LENGTH_THRESHOLD = spark.sql.sources.schemaStringLengthThreshold (default 4000), FILESOURCE_TABLE_RELATION_CACHE_SIZE = spark.sql.filesourceTableRelationCacheSize (default 1000), CODEGEN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = spark.sql.codegen.cache.maxEntries (default 100), METADATA_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = spark.sql.metadataCacheTTLSeconds (default -1). (3) Codegen and debug, lines 98-114: CODEGEN_COMMENTS = spark.sql.codegen.comments, DEBUG_MODE = spark.sql.debug. (4) Extensions, serializer and listeners, lines 116-171: HIVE_THRIFT_SERVER_SINGLESESSION = spark.sql.hive.thriftServer.singleSession, SPARK_SESSION_EXTENSIONS = spark.sql.extensions, LOAD_SESSION_EXTENSIONS_FROM_CLASSPATH = spark.sql.extensions.test.loadFromCp, SPARK_CACHE_SERIALIZER = spark.sql.cache.serializer (default DefaultCachedBatchSerializer class name), QUERY_EXECUTION_LISTENERS = spark.sql.queryExecutionListeners, STREAMING_QUERY_LISTENERS = spark.sql.streaming.streamingQueryListeners. (5) UI and events, lines 173-178, 222-228, 253-298: UI_RETAINED_EXECUTIONS = spark.sql.ui.retainedExecutions (1000), SQL_EVENT_TRUNCATE_LENGTH = spark.sql.event.truncate.length, STREAMING_UI_ENABLED = spark.sql.streaming.ui.enabled, STREAMING_UI_RETAINED_PROGRESS_UPDATES = spark.sql.streaming.ui.retainedProgressUpdates, STREAMING_UI_RETAINED_QUERIES = spark.sql.streaming.ui.retainedQueries, ENABLED_STREAMING_UI_CUSTOM_METRIC_LIST = spark.sql.streaming.ui.enabledCustomMetricList. (6) Thread thresholds, lines 180-220: SHUFFLE_EXCHANGE_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD = spark.sql.shuffleExchange.maxThreadThreshold (1024), BROADCAST_EXCHANGE_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD = spark.sql.broadcastExchange.maxThreadThreshold (128), SUBQUERY_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD = spark.sql.subquery.maxThreadThreshold (16), RESULT_QUERY_STAGE_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD = spark.sql.resultQueryStage.maxThreadThreshold (1024). (7) Legacy and misc, lines 230-251, 300-316: SQL_LEGACY_SESSION_INIT_WITH_DEFAULTS = spark.sql.legacy.sessionInitWithConfigDefaults, DEFAULT_URL_STREAM_HANDLER_FACTORY_ENABLED = spark.sql.defaultUrlStreamHandlerFactory.enabled, DISABLED_JDBC_CONN_PROVIDER_LIST = spark.sql.sources.disabledJdbcConnProviderList, DATA_FRAME_DEBUGGING_ENABLED = spark.python.sql.dataFrameDebugging.enabled (default true).

nodes.name: BaseSessionStateBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BaseSessionStateBuilder, the abstract builder that wires every component of a SessionState (conf, function registries, catalog, parser, analyzer, optimizer, planner, listeners, artifact manager) and builds it, plus SparkUDFExpressionBuilder for turning UserDefinedAggregateFunction classes into expressions. Used when a SparkSession creates its session state or clones one from a parent state; hooks let extensions add analyzer, optimizer and planner rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file relying on lazy vals for shared components and anonymous subclasses of Analyzer, SparkOptimizer and SparkPlanner to inject custom rules.

nodes.name: BaseSessionStateBuilder
nodes.summary: Abstract @Unstable builder that coordinates construction of a new SessionState for a SparkSession, optionally cloning pieces (conf, functionRegistry, experimentalMethods, catalog) from a parentState. Shared components (functionRegistry, tableFunctionRegistry, dataSourceManager, experimentalMethods, sqlParser, resourceLoader, catalog, v2SessionCatalog, catalogManager) are lazy vals so they are created once; analyzer, optimizer, planner and the managers are defs used by build. Custom hooks (customResolutionRules, customHintResolutionRules, customPostHocResolutionRules, customCheckRules, customOperatorOptimizationRules, customEarlyScanPushDownRules, customPreCBORules, customPlanningStrategies) pull rules from SparkSessionExtensions. The build method passes everything to the SessionState constructor; subclasses must supply newBuilder.

nodes.name: newBuilder
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns a function creating a new builder for a given SparkSession and optional parent SessionState; subclasses must override it so createClone can build clones.

nodes.name: functionRegistry
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the scalar FunctionRegistry: clones the parent state's registry if present, otherwise clones the builtin registry and lets extensions register functions.

nodes.name: tableFunctionRegistry
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the TableFunctionRegistry: cloned from the parent state or from the builtin one with extension-registered table functions.

nodes.name: dataSourceManager
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the DataSourceManager that manages user-registered data sources; cloned from the parent state or newly created.

nodes.name: sqlParser
nodes.summary: Lazy val for the ParserInterface: wraps a new SparkSqlParser through extensions.buildParser so extension parsers can take part.

nodes.name: catalog
nodes.summary: Lazy val that creates the SessionCatalog from the shared external catalog, global temp view manager, function registries, Hadoop conf, parser, resource loader and a SparkUDFExpressionBuilder; copies state (temp tables and current database) from the parent state's catalog.

nodes.name: catalogManager
nodes.summary: Lazy val that builds a DefaultCatalogManager over the V2SessionCatalog and the V1 SessionCatalog and copies the session path from the parent state.

nodes.name: analyzer
nodes.summary: Creates the Analyzer as an anonymous subclass that overrides hint resolution rules, single-pass resolver extensions and post-hoc rules and checks, extendedResolutionRules (data source, file source, session catalog, write-to-stream, procedures, execute immediate and others), postHocResolutionRules (table creation and insertion preprocessing, DataSourceAnalysis, char padding) and extendedCheckRules (PreWriteCheck, PreReadCheck, TableCapabilityCheck, CommandCheck and others), appending the custom rules from extensions.

nodes.name: customResolutionRules
nodes.summary: Returns extra resolution rules for the Analyzer built from extensions.buildResolutionRules.

nodes.name: customPostHocResolutionRules
nodes.summary: Returns extra post-hoc resolution rules for the Analyzer built from extensions.buildPostHocResolutionRules.

nodes.name: customCheckRules
nodes.summary: Returns extra check rules for the Analyzer built from extensions.buildCheckRules.

nodes.name: optimizer
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkOptimizer as an anonymous subclass that appends custom early scan push down rules, pre-CBO rules and operator optimization rules to the defaults.

nodes.name: planner
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkPlanner as an anonymous subclass whose extraPlanningStrategies adds customPlanningStrategies from extensions.

nodes.name: adaptiveRulesHolder
nodes.summary: Builds an AdaptiveRulesHolder from the query stage prep, runtime optimizer, query stage optimizer and query post planner strategy rules supplied by extensions.

nodes.name: planNormalizationRules
nodes.summary: Returns plan normalization rules: NormalizeCTEIds followed by the rules from extensions.buildPlanNormalizationRules.

nodes.name: createQueryExecution
nodes.summary: Returns the function that creates a QueryExecution for a plan and CommandExecutionMode, passing a shuffle cleanup mode taken from QueryExecution.determineShuffleCleanupMode.

nodes.name: listenerManager
nodes.summary: Creates the ExecutionListenerManager: clones the parent state's manager for the session and conf, otherwise creates a new one that loads extensions.

nodes.name: artifactManager
nodes.summary: Creates the ArtifactManager, cloning the parent state's manager for the new session or creating a new one.

nodes.name: createClone
nodes.summary: Returns a function that clones a session state by creating a new builder through newBuilder with the old state as parent and calling build.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the SessionState by passing conf, registries, data source components, lazily evaluated catalog, analyzer, optimizer and streaming managers, listener manager, query execution factory, clone function, columnar rules, adaptive rules holder, plan normalization rules and artifact manager to its constructor.

nodes.name: SparkUDFExpressionBuilder
nodes.summary: FunctionExpressionBuilder passed to the SessionCatalog by BaseSessionStateBuilder to turn a registered class into an Expression. Its only method, makeExpression, supports UserDefinedAggregateFunction classes via ScalaUDAF and rejects other classes.

nodes.name: makeExpression
nodes.summary: Builds an expression for a registered function class: if the class is a UserDefinedAggregateFunction it instantiates it through its no-arg constructor and wraps it in a ScalaUDAF named after the function, checking that the number of input types matches the argument count (wrongNumArgsError otherwise); any other class raises QueryCompilationErrors.noHandlerForUDAFError.

nodes.name: ReadOnlySQLConf.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ReadOnlySQLConf, a read-only SQLConf created by tasks on the executor side from the local properties propagated from the driver, and TaskContextConfigProvider, the provider that reads config values from a TaskContext's local properties. Both classes are small (67 lines in total).

nodes.name: ReadOnlySQLConf
nodes.summary: SQLConf subclass used on the executor side: settings is the task's local properties map and the reader is a ConfigReader over a TaskContextConfigProvider. All mutating methods throw: setConfWithCheck, unsetConf (by key and by ConfigEntry) and clear raise QueryExecutionErrors.cannotMutateReadOnlySQLConfError, while clone and copy raise cannotCloneOrCopyReadOnlySQLConfError.

nodes.name: TaskContextConfigProvider
nodes.summary: ConfigProvider whose get(key) returns Option(context.getLocalProperty(key)) for the wrapped TaskContext, so configs are looked up in the task's local properties.

nodes.name: NonClosableMutableURLClassLoader.java
nodes.summary: Java file defining a MutableURLClassLoader whose close method does nothing, so the loader cannot be closed.

nodes.name: NonClosableMutableURLClassLoader
nodes.summary: Public MutableURLClassLoader subclass created with an empty URL array and a given parent loader; a static block registers the class as parallel capable and its close method is an empty override, so closing it has no effect.

nodes.name: Artifact.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private[sql] Artifact class (a relative path plus a local payload) and its companion object with factories for jar, class and cache artifacts and for parsing file: and ivy: URIs. Used by the SQL client side to describe files that are to be uploaded as session artifacts.

nodes.name: Artifact
nodes.summary: Class holds a relative target path and a LocalData storage, rejects absolute paths with require, and exposes a lazy size taken from the storage. The companion object (lines 37-157) holds the prefixes classes, jars and cache, the factory methods and the LocalData payload types.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a private constructor; all instances are created through the companion object factories.

nodes.name: LocalData
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for a payload stored on the local machine. It requires a stream (InputStream) and a size in bytes.

nodes.name: LocalFile
nodes.summary: LocalData backed by a file path: size comes from Files.size and stream from Files.newInputStream.

nodes.name: InMemory
nodes.summary: LocalData backed by a byte array: size is the array length and stream is a ByteArrayInputStream over the bytes.

nodes.name: newArtifactFromExtension
nodes.summary: Chooses a jar or class artifact from the file name suffix (.jar or .class) and throws UnsupportedOperationException for any other file name.

nodes.name: parseArtifacts
nodes.summary: Turns a URI into artifacts: a file: scheme gives one artifact based on the file extension and a LocalFile, an ivy: scheme is resolved through newIvyArtifacts, and any other scheme throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: newJarArtifact
nodes.summary: Creates an artifact under the jars prefix and requires the target file name to end in .jar.

nodes.name: newClassArtifact
nodes.summary: Creates an artifact under the classes prefix and requires the target file name to end in .class.

nodes.name: newCacheArtifact
nodes.summary: Creates an artifact under the cache prefix whose path is the given id and which has no suffix requirement.

nodes.name: newIvyArtifacts
nodes.summary: Resolves an ivy: URI of the form org:module:version: validates the authority, reads transitive, exclusions and repository query parameters, builds Ivy settings, resolves the Maven coordinates to jar files and wraps each jar as a LocalFile jar artifact.

nodes.name: newArtifact
nodes.summary: Private helper that checks the target path suffix with require and builds an Artifact whose path is the prefix joined with the target path using ArtifactUtils.concatenatePaths.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract DataFrameNaFunctions class (the df.na API) for handling missing data: drop rows with null or NaN, fill nulls with constants or per-column maps, and replace values. The protected drop(Option[Int]) and drop(Option[Int], Seq) methods, the fill variants without a default body, fillMap and the Scala Map replace variants are left to subclasses.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions
nodes.summary: Stable abstract class for missing-data functionality on a DataFrame. The many drop overloads all end in two protected abstract drop methods (with a minimum non-null count, optionally with column names) after how = "any" or "all" is mapped to a count by toMinNonNulls. The fill overloads replace nulls (and NaN in numeric columns) in numeric, string and boolean columns, or by a column-to-value map via the protected abstract fillMap. The replace overloads replace matching values in named columns or "*" using a Map or a java.util.Map; the Java-friendly variants delegate to the Scala ones.

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: Group of public drop overloads (span lines 39-112; other overloads at 49, 57, 65, 76, 87, 95, 103 and 112) that build a new DataFrame without rows that have too many null or NaN values, by how (any or all), by minimum non-null count, and for all or the given columns. Array variants convert to Seq and everything funnels into the protected abstract drop(minNonNulls) and drop(minNonNulls, cols).

nodes.name: toMinNonNulls
nodes.summary: Private helper that maps how to an optional minimum non-null count: "any" gives None, "all" gives Some(1), and any other value throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Group of fill overloads (span lines 131-256) that replace null (and NaN for numeric) values with a Long, Double, String or Boolean value, for all columns or the given columns (Array variants delegate to Seq), plus fill(java.util.Map) and fill(Map) that delegate to fillMap. The fill variants for a single value and for Seq columns are abstract.

nodes.name: fillMap
nodes.summary: Protected abstract method that fills nulls from a sequence of (column name, replacement value) pairs; the Map based fill overloads convert their argument to a Seq and call it.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Group of replace overloads (span lines 285-360) that replace values matching the keys of a replacement map, for one column, a list of columns or "*". The java.util.Map variants convert to a Scala Map and delegate; the Scala Map variants are abstract.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract DataFrameStatFunctions class (the df.stat API) with statistics helpers on a DataFrame: approximate quantiles, covariance, correlation, crosstab, frequent items, stratified sampling, and Count-min sketch and Bloom filter construction.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions
nodes.summary: Stable abstract class of statistic functions. The multi-column approxQuantile, cov, corr (with method), crosstab, freqItems(Seq, support) and sampleBy(Column, ...) are abstract, while convenience overloads implement the Array, String and java.util.Map variants. The countMinSketch and bloomFilter methods are implemented here: they run an aggregate over the protected df and read the resulting binary value back into a CountMinSketch or a BloomFilter.

nodes.name: approxQuantile
nodes.summary: Approximate quantiles of numeric columns (a variation of the Greenwald-Khanna algorithm with a relative error bound). The single column overload (lines 74-79) takes the head of the result of the multi-column abstract overload (lines 104-107); null and NaN values are ignored.

nodes.name: cov
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the sample covariance of two numeric columns.

nodes.name: corr
nodes.summary: Correlation of two columns: the abstract overload takes a method name (only Pearson is supported) and the two-column overload (lines 169-171) calls it with "pearson".

nodes.name: crosstab
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns a pair-wise frequency (contingency) table of two columns as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: freqItems
nodes.summary: Frequent items per column, possibly with false positives. Array overloads convert to Seq, the overloads without support use 0.01, and freqItems(Seq, support) (line 309) is abstract.

nodes.name: sampleBy
nodes.summary: Stratified sample without replacement from a per-stratum fraction map and seed. String-named column and java.util.Map overloads delegate to the abstract overload that takes a Column (line 415).

nodes.name: countMinSketch
nodes.summary: Builds a CountMinSketch over a column. Overloads accept depth and width or eps and confidence; the depth/width form derives eps = 2.0 / width and confidence = 1 - 1 / 2^depth. The eps/confidence form (lines 516-521) selects count_min_sketch on df as BinaryEncoder, takes the head and reads it with CountMinSketch.readFrom.

nodes.name: bloomFilter
nodes.summary: Builds a BloomFilter over a column. A false-positive-probability overload computes the bit count with BloomFilter.optimalNumOfBits, and the numBits overload (lines 580-584) runs the internal bloom_filter_agg aggregate, reads the binary result and calls BloomFilter.readFrom.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriterV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the v2 write API for Datasets: the abstract DataFrameWriterV2 class (append, overwrite, overwritePartitions and optional schema evolution) and two builder traits, WriteConfigMethods (write options) and CreateTableWriter (create, replace, createOrReplace, partitioning, clustering, provider and table properties).

nodes.name: DataFrameWriterV2
nodes.summary: Experimental abstract writer for external storage through the v2 API. It extends CreateTableWriter, keeps a private[sql] _withSchemaEvolution flag set by withSchemaEvolution, narrows the inherited builder methods to return this.type (option overloads for Boolean, Long and Double delegate to the String overload), and adds append, overwrite(condition) and overwritePartitions, which are abstract and declared to throw NoSuchTableException when the table does not exist.

nodes.name: WriteConfigMethods
nodes.summary: Trait parameterised by the builder type R with the common write option methods: option(key, String) and options(Map) in Scala and Java map forms are abstract, and the Boolean, Long and Double option overloads convert the value to a string and call the String overload.

nodes.name: CreateTableWriter
nodes.summary: Trait that restricts a writer to create and replace operations. It declares create (fails with TableAlreadyExistsException), replace (fails with CannotReplaceMissingTableException), createOrReplace, partitionedBy, clusterBy, using (provider) and tableProperty, and extends WriteConfigMethods with itself as builder type.

nodes.name: withSchemaEvolution
nodes.summary: Experimental method (since 4.2.0) that sets the _withSchemaEvolution flag to true and returns this; the target table must declare the AUTOMATIC_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION capability.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Abstract: append the DataFrame contents to the output table after validating compatibility; fails with NoSuchTableException when the table is missing.

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Abstract: overwrite the rows matching a Column filter condition with the DataFrame contents; fails with NoSuchTableException when the table is missing.

nodes.name: overwritePartitions
nodes.summary: Abstract: dynamically overwrite every partition for which the DataFrame has at least one row; fails with NoSuchTableException when the table is missing.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Abstract: create a new table from the DataFrame contents using the writer configuration; fails with TableAlreadyExistsException when it exists.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Abstract: replace an existing table with the DataFrame contents and writer configuration; fails with CannotReplaceMissingTableException when it does not exist.

nodes.name: createOrReplace
nodes.summary: Abstract: create the table, or replace its configuration and data if it already exists.

nodes.name: partitionedBy
nodes.summary: Abstract varargs builder method that sets the partitioning columns or transforms of the table created by create, createOrReplace or replace.

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Abstract varargs builder method (since 4.0.0) that clusters the stored output by the given column names.

nodes.name: DatasetHolder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract DatasetHolder container that wraps a Dataset so that Scala implicit conversions (via import spark.implicits._) can offer toDS and toDF on local collections and similar values.

nodes.name: DatasetHolder
nodes.summary: Abstract container for a Dataset used by implicit conversions in Scala. It declares toDS() to get a Dataset[T], toDF() to get a DataFrame, and toDF(colNames) to get a DataFrame with renamed columns; the no-argument forms are declared with parentheses so the compiler does not treat rdd.toDS("1") as a call followed by apply. Concrete implementations are supplied elsewhere.

nodes.name: toDS
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns the wrapped data as a Dataset[T]; declared with parentheses on purpose.

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns the wrapped data as a DataFrame. Overloaded: toDF() at line 42 keeps the default column names and toDF(colNames: String*) at line 44 assigns the given names.

nodes.name: ForeachWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract ForeachWriter class, the user hook for writing the rows of a query (typically a streaming query) to arbitrary storage one partition at a time.

nodes.name: ForeachWriter
nodes.summary: Serializable abstract class for custom per-partition output logic. One instance handles one partition of the data of a task, and each task gets its own deserialized copy. The lifecycle is open(partitionId, epochId), then process(value) for each row if open returned true, then close(errorOrNull). The class docs say (partitionId, epochId) cannot be used for deduplication and point to foreachBatch for that.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Abstract hook called when starting to process one partition; returns true if the partition and epoch should be processed and false to skip it.

nodes.name: process
nodes.summary: Abstract hook called on the executor side for each value, only if open returned true.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Abstract hook called when processing of a partition stops, with the error seen (or null). It is called whether open returned true or false, except when the JVM crashes or open throws.

nodes.name: DataSourceRegistration.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DataSourceRegistration, the helper behind SparkSession.dataSource that registers user-defined (Python) data sources with the DataSourceManager after checking for name clashes.

nodes.name: DataSourceRegistration
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class with functions for registering user-defined data sources; reached through SparkSession.dataSource. registerPython logs the new source (name, command, envVars, pythonIncludes, pythonExec), calls checkDataSourceExists, and then hands it to DataSourceManager.registerDataSource. checkDataSourceExists lets user-defined sources be re-registered but raises dataSourceAlreadyExists when a built-in or Scala/Java source with that name can be loaded or when lookup fails for any reason other than DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.name: registerPython
nodes.summary: Registers a UserDefinedPythonDataSource under the given name: logs its details at debug level, validates the name with checkDataSourceExists, then calls DataSourceManager.registerDataSource.

nodes.name: checkDataSourceExists
nodes.summary: Returns quietly if the manager already knows a user-defined source with the name; otherwise tries DataSource.lookupDataSource and throws QueryCompilationErrors.dataSourceAlreadyExists if it resolves or fails with an unexpected error, accepting only DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.name: ExperimentalMethods.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExperimentalMethods, the holder reachable as spark.experimental that exposes mutable lists of extra planner strategies and extra optimizer rules.

nodes.name: ExperimentalMethods
nodes.summary: Experimental and unstable holder (no binary or source compatibility guarantee) with two volatile vars: extraStrategies (Seq[Strategy]) for strategies injected into the query planner at runtime, and extraOptimizations (Seq[Rule[LogicalPlan]]) for extra optimizer rules. clone() copies both lists into a new instance. Example in the docs: spark.experimental.extraStrategies += ...

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Creates a new ExperimentalMethods and copies extraStrategies and extraOptimizations into it.

nodes.name: ExtendedExplainGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExtendedExplainGenerator trait that a session extension implements to add extra information to explain output for a SparkPlan.

nodes.name: ExtendedExplainGenerator
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait (since 4.0.0) for session extensions that provide additional explain plan information. It requires a title and a generateExtendedInfo(plan: SparkPlan) method that returns the extra text.

nodes.name: title
nodes.summary: Abstract member returning the title under which the extended information is shown.

nodes.name: generateExtendedInfo
nodes.summary: Abstract method that takes a SparkPlan and returns the extra explain text as a String.

nodes.name: SparkSessionExtensions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkSessionExtensions, the experimental holder of injection points (analyzer, optimizer, planner, parser, function, columnar and adaptive-execution rule builders) that users register through SparkSession.Builder.withExtensions or the spark.sql.extensions setting.

nodes.name: SparkSessionExtensions
nodes.summary: Collects builders injected by user code and later turned into rules for a SparkSession. Public inject* methods store builders in buffers (injectResolutionRule, injectHintResolutionRule, injectPostHocResolutionRule, injectCheckRule, injectPlanNormalizationRule, injectOptimizerRule, injectPreCBORule, injectPlannerStrategy, injectParser, injectFunction, injectTableFunction, injectColumnar, injectQueryPostPlannerStrategyRule, injectQueryStagePrepRule, injectRuntimeOptimizerRule, injectQueryStageOptimizerRule). Matching build* methods apply the builders to a session and return the rules; buildParser stacks parsers with foldLeft; registerFunctions and registerTableFunctions put injected functions into the registries as built-in identifiers. The docs warn that builders must not assume the session is fully initialized. Defines type aliases RuleBuilder, CheckRuleBuilder, StrategyBuilder, ParserBuilder, FunctionDescription, TableFunctionDescription, ColumnarRuleBuilder and the three query stage builder types (lines 110-119). It has about 32 methods, mostly one-line inject/build pairs, so only the non-trivial ones and a representative set of inject methods have function nodes.

nodes.name: injectColumnar
nodes.summary: Registers a builder for a ColumnarRule that can override columnar execution of an executor; later read by buildColumnarRules.

nodes.name: injectResolutionRule
nodes.summary: Registers an analyzer resolution Rule builder to run in the resolution phase of analysis; read back by buildResolutionRules.

nodes.name: injectOptimizerRule
nodes.summary: Registers an optimizer Rule builder executed during the operator optimization batch; such rules must not change the query result.

nodes.name: injectPlannerStrategy
nodes.summary: Registers a planner Strategy builder used to convert a LogicalPlan into an executable SparkPlan.

nodes.name: buildParser
nodes.summary: Applies the injected parser builders in order with foldLeft, each one receiving the session and the previous parser, so injected parsers are stacked on the initial one.

nodes.name: injectParser
nodes.summary: Registers a custom parser builder that gets the session and the initial parser, allowing a partial parser that delegates to the underlying one.

nodes.name: registerFunctions
nodes.summary: Registers every injected function description into the given FunctionRegistry as a built-in identifier, but only for unqualified names (no database or catalog part); multi-part names are ignored.

nodes.name: registerTableFunctions
nodes.summary: Same as registerFunctions but for injected table function descriptions and a TableFunctionRegistry; only unqualified names are registered.

nodes.name: injectFunction
nodes.summary: Adds a (FunctionIdentifier, ExpressionInfo, FunctionBuilder) description to be registered into the FunctionRegistry for all sessions.

nodes.name: injectTableFunction
nodes.summary: Adds a table function description to be registered into the TableFunctionRegistry for all sessions.

nodes.name: SparkSessionExtensionsProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SparkSessionExtensionsProvider trait, the base type for extension classes that receive a SparkSessionExtensions and inject rules or functions; documented with an example registering an "age" function.

nodes.name: SparkSessionExtensionsProvider
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait (since 3.2.0) that extends Function1[SparkSessionExtensions, Unit]. An implementation overrides apply to call inject* methods on the given SparkSessionExtensions. The docs list three ways to enable it: withExtensions on SparkSession.Builder, the spark.sql.extensions config, or java.util.ServiceLoader with a META-INF/services file named after this trait.

nodes.name: TableArg.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TableArg, the wrapper around a table subquery argument expression that lets a DataFrame passed to a table-valued function be partitioned, ordered or confined to a single partition.

nodes.name: TableArg
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class that represents a table argument for table-valued functions (since 4.0.0). It holds a FunctionTableSubqueryArgumentExpression and a classic SparkSession. partitionBy(cols*) sets partitionByExpressions, orderBy(cols*) wraps each column expression in an ascending SortOrder unless it already is one, and withSinglePartition() sets the single-partition flag. Each returns a new TableArg built with expression.copy(...). Calls are rejected with IllegalArgumentException when partitioning is repeated or when orderBy comes before partitionBy or withSinglePartition.

nodes.name: isPartitioned
nodes.summary: Private check that is true when partitionByExpressions is non-empty or withSinglePartition is set on the wrapped expression.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Returns a new TableArg partitioned by the given columns; throws IllegalArgumentException if partitionBy or withSinglePartition was already called.

nodes.name: orderBy
nodes.summary: Returns a new TableArg ordered by the given columns (non-SortOrder expressions become ascending SortOrder); throws IllegalArgumentException unless partitionBy or withSinglePartition was called first.

nodes.name: withSinglePartition
nodes.summary: Returns a new TableArg whose input is processed in a single partition; throws IllegalArgumentException if partitioning was already set.

nodes.name: UDTFRegistration.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UDTFRegistration, the helper behind SparkSession.udtf that registers Python user-defined table functions as temporary functions in the TableFunctionRegistry.

nodes.name: UDTFRegistration
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class (since 3.5.0) with functions for registering user-defined table functions; reached through SparkSession.udtf. registerPython logs the function details (name, command, envVars, pythonIncludes, pythonExec, returnType, udfDeterministic) and then calls tableFunctionRegistry.createOrReplaceTempFunction with a builder that uses the active session sqlParser and the source label "python_udtf".

nodes.name: registerPython
nodes.summary: Registers a UserDefinedPythonTableFunction under the given name via createOrReplaceTempFunction, building the function with the sqlParser of the active SparkSession and marking its source as python_udtf.

nodes.name: DataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DataSource, the case class that turns a data source description (provider class name, paths, optional schema, partition columns, bucket spec, options, catalog table) into a concrete implementation, plus its companion object with provider lookup and path helpers. It is used when reading or writing through the reader and writer APIs, CREATE TABLE USING, and streaming sources and sinks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class plus companion object sharing one class id. The instance method and the companion method named checkAndGlobPathIfNecessary are overloads that share one function id.

nodes.name: DataSource
nodes.summary: Case class (lines 97-607) and companion object (lines 609-893) representing a pluggable data source. The class resolves its provider through providingClass/providingInstance, infers schema and partitioning (getOrInferFileFormatSchema), creates streaming sources and sinks (createSource, createSink, sourceSchema), resolves a BaseRelation for reading (resolveRelation), and builds write plans or writes and reads back (planForWriting, writeAndRead, planForWritingFileFormat). The companion object holds backwardCompatibilityMap (old provider names such as org.apache.spark.sql.parquet mapped to current classes, plus the literal names com.databricks.spark.csv and com.databricks.spark.xml), spark2RemovedClasses, GLOB_PATHS_KEY ("__globPaths__"), lookupDataSource, lookupDataSourceV2, checkAndGlobPathIfNecessary, buildStorageFormatFromOptions and validateSchema. Extends SessionStateHelper and Logging.
nodes.languageNotes: The lineRange covers both the case class and its companion object, which share this id.

nodes.name: DataSource.SourceInfo
nodes.summary: Nested case class (name, schema, partitionColumns) returned by sourceSchema and exposed through the lazy sourceInfo field. It describes a streaming source: its display name, schema and partition column names.

nodes.name: providingClass
nodes.summary: Lazy value that calls DataSource.lookupDataSource for className and instantiates it; when the instance is a FileDataSourceV2 it returns that source's fallbackFileFormat so catalog tables keep using the FileFormat path.

nodes.name: providingInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a new instance of providingClass through its no-arg constructor; used by the read, write and streaming methods to pattern match on the provider type.

nodes.name: makeQualified
nodes.summary: Qualifies a Hadoop Path against its file system URI and working directory using the Hadoop configuration built from the session and options.

nodes.name: globPaths
nodes.summary: Returns whether paths should be globbed, read from the __globPaths__ option and defaulting to true.

nodes.name: getOrInferFileFormatSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the (data schema, partition schema) pair for a FileFormat: uses userSpecifiedSchema when present, otherwise infers the data schema with format.inferSchema over the file index files, and infers or casts partition columns (the SPARK-18510 behaviour). Logs a warning when data and partition schemas share column names.

nodes.name: sourceSchema
nodes.summary: Computes the SourceInfo for a streaming source. Handles StreamSourceProvider directly; for a FileFormat it checks the path exists (unless globbed), requires a schema when streaming schema inference is disabled (except text or single variant column), infers schema through getOrInferFileFormatSchema, and applies the force-nullable setting.

nodes.name: createSource
nodes.summary: Creates a streaming Source: delegates to StreamSourceProvider.createSource, or builds a FileStreamSource for a FileFormat using sourceInfo schema and partition columns; throws for other provider types.

nodes.name: createSink
nodes.summary: Creates a streaming Sink: delegates to StreamSinkProvider.createSink, or builds a FileStreamSink for a FileFormat (Append output mode only); throws for other provider types.

nodes.name: resolveRelation
nodes.summary: Resolves a BaseRelation for reading or writing. Dispatches on RelationProvider / SchemaRelationProvider (and the user schema), on FileFormat sources that have a streaming metadata log (MetadataLogFileIndex), and on ordinary file sources (CatalogFileIndex when partitions are tracked in the catalog, otherwise InMemoryFileIndex built from globbed paths), returning a HadoopFsRelation. Afterwards it checks for duplicate column names and verifies the schema with DataSourceUtils.

nodes.name: planForWritingFileFormat
nodes.summary: Builds an InsertIntoHadoopFsRelationCommand for writing to a FileFormat: requires exactly one output path, qualifies it, validates partition columns and picks up the existing file index of the catalog table when present.

nodes.name: writeAndRead
nodes.summary: Writes a LogicalPlan to this data source and returns a BaseRelation for reading it back. A CreatableRelationProvider is called directly after checking data type support; a FileFormat runs the write command via QueryExecution.runCommand and then resolves the relation with the written schema.

nodes.name: planForWriting
nodes.summary: Returns a LogicalPlan for writing to this data source: SaveIntoDataSourceCommand for a CreatableRelationProvider, or the InsertIntoHadoopFsRelationCommand plan for a FileFormat after schema validation and an interval type check.

nodes.name: createInMemoryFileIndex
nodes.summary: Creates an InMemoryFileIndex over the given globbed paths using the session FileStatusCache; used to list files and read the partition schema.

nodes.name: disallowWritingIntervals
nodes.summary: Throws an unsupported data type error when an output column has an interval type that the target format cannot write.

nodes.name: lookupDataSource
nodes.summary: Companion method that looks up the class for a provider name: applies backwardCompatibilityMap and ORC/Avro special cases, then searches DataSourceRegister services by short name, falls back to loading the fully qualified class or its DefaultSource, and picks the internal org.apache.spark source when several are registered. Falls back to PythonDataSourceV2 for user-defined data sources and raises specific errors for missing ORC, Avro, Kafka and removed Spark 2 classes.

nodes.name: lookupDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Companion method that returns an optional TableProvider for a provider name: loads the class with lookupDataSource, instantiates it, and returns None when the provider is listed in the USE_V1_SOURCE_LIST setting or is not a TableProvider; sets the short name on PythonDataSourceV2.

nodes.name: checkAndGlobPathIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Companion method that qualifies path strings, splits them into glob and non glob paths, expands globs in parallel with ThreadUtils.parmap, optionally checks that paths and glob results exist, and logs ignored paths. Returns all resulting Paths. A short instance method of the same name in the DataSource class (lines 588-594) merges the path option with paths and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: buildStorageFormatFromOptions
nodes.summary: Companion method that builds a CatalogStorageFormat from options, treating the path option as the table location and keeping the remaining options as storage properties.

nodes.name: validateSchema
nodes.summary: Companion method that validates that a schema to be written is not empty (including nested struct fields) unless ALLOW_EMPTY_SCHEMAS_FOR_WRITES is set; used before writing to file based sources.

nodes.name: HiveSerDe.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the HiveSerDe case class (input format, output format and serde class names) and its companion object with a table mapping short file format names to Hive SerDe settings. Used to translate between Spark data source names and Hive storage descriptors when building catalog storage formats.

nodes.name: HiveSerDe
nodes.summary: Case class (lines 26-29, three optional strings: inputFormat, outputFormat, serde) with companion object (lines 31-166). The object holds serdeMap for sequencefile, rcfile, orc, parquet, textfile and avro, and serdeInverseMap (reverse mapping, skipping sequencefile and rcfile and naming textfile as "text"). sourceToSerDe maps a source abbreviation or class name (for example org.apache.spark.sql.parquet, orcfile, parquetfile, avrofile) to a HiveSerDe, serdeToSource does the reverse lookup, buildStorageFormat creates a CatalogStorageFormat from an optional location and SerdeInfo (using STORED AS, formatClasses or serde properties) and throws a caller supplied error for an unknown STORED AS format, and getDefaultStorage builds the default CatalogStorageFormat from the hive.default.fileformat setting (falling back to textfile).
nodes.languageNotes: Case class and companion object share this id; the range covers both.

nodes.name: SessionStateHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SessionStateHelper trait and its companion object, small accessors that fetch the SparkConf, SQLConf and Hadoop Configuration from a SparkSession. Mixed into classes such as DataSource that need session configuration.

nodes.name: SessionStateHelper
nodes.summary: Trait (lines 29-55) with a companion object (line 57) offering sessionState (protected), getSparkConf (from the SparkContext), getSqlConf (from sessionState.conf) and two getHadoopConf overloads: one using sessionState.newHadoopConf(), and one using newHadoopConfWithOptions(options). The companion object extends the trait so the helpers can be called statically.

nodes.name: SessionState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SessionState (the holder of all session-specific state of a SparkSession), its companion object, SessionStateBuilder (the concrete builder) and SessionResourceLoader (loads jars, files and archives for function resources). Used each time a session is created or cloned.

nodes.name: SessionState
nodes.summary: Class (lines 71-144, private[sql]) with companion object (lines 146-152) that holds session specific state: SQLConf, ExperimentalMethods, function and table function registries, UDF/UDTF registrations, DataSourceManager, SparkPlanner, ExecutionListenerManager, columnar rules, adaptive rules holder, plan normalization rules, and builder functions for the SessionCatalog (catalog), Analyzer (analyzer), Optimizer (optimizer), SessionResourceLoader, StreamingQueryManager, StreamingCheckpointManager and ArtifactManager, all exposed as lazy values so heavy objects are created only when needed. Methods: catalogManager (analyzer.catalogManager), newHadoopConf (copies the Hadoop configuration and overlays SQL conf entries), newHadoopConfWithOptions (adds non-null options except path and paths), clone (calls createClone), and executePlan (creates a QueryExecution through createQueryExecution with a CommandExecutionMode). The companion's newHadoopConf(hadoopConf, sqlConf) does the actual overlay.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id; range covers both.

nodes.name: SessionStateBuilder
nodes.summary: Concrete BaseSessionStateBuilder that takes a SparkSession and an optional parent SessionState and overrides newBuilder to return another SessionStateBuilder; marked Unstable.

nodes.name: SessionResourceLoader
nodes.summary: Session shared FunctionResourceLoader (Unstable). loadResource adds a jar, file or archive to the SparkContext depending on the resource type; resolveJars expands ivy URIs into Maven dependency paths; addJar resolves the URI, registers the jar with the SparkContext and the shared jarClassLoader, and sets the thread context classloader.

nodes.name: newHadoopConf
nodes.summary: Returns a Hadoop Configuration for the session by passing the SparkContext Hadoop configuration and the SQLConf to the companion helper, which copies the configuration and overlays all non-null SQL conf entries.

nodes.name: newHadoopConfWithOptions
nodes.summary: Creates a new Hadoop Configuration from newHadoopConf and sets every non-null option except path and paths.

nodes.name: executePlan
nodes.summary: Creates a QueryExecution for a LogicalPlan with a CommandExecutionMode (default ALL) by calling the createQueryExecution function.

nodes.name: loadResource
nodes.summary: Loads a function resource by matching its type: JarResource goes to addJar, FileResource to SparkContext.addFile, ArchiveResource to SparkContext.addArchive.

nodes.name: resolveJars
nodes.summary: Resolves a jar URI: ivy URIs go through DependencyUtils.resolveMavenDependencies, other URIs are returned as their string form.

nodes.name: addJar
nodes.summary: Adds a jar path to the SparkContext and to the shared jarClassLoader (converting local paths to URLs), then sets the thread context classloader.

nodes.name: SharedState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SharedState, the holder of everything shared across all sessions of one SQLContext (cache manager, status store, external catalog, global temp views, jar class loader), and its companion object that resolves and qualifies the warehouse path. Used when the first SparkSession is created to build the session-independent state.

nodes.name: SharedState
nodes.summary: Class SharedState (lines 51-198) holds state shared across sessions: it clones the Spark and Hadoop conf (applying initial session configs and the resolved warehouse path), and exposes cacheManager, relationCache, activeStreamingQueries guarded by activeQueriesLock, statusStore (SQL listener, store and SQLTab), a lazy streamingQueryStatusListener (only when the streaming UI is enabled), a lazy externalCatalog (built by reflection, creates the default database if missing, forwards catalog events to the listener bus), globalTempViewManager (fails if the global temp database name already exists in the catalog) and a jarClassLoader. The companion object SharedState (lines 200-314) provides the static helpers: resolveWarehousePath, qualifyWarehousePath, setWarehousePathConf, plus private helpers to pick the catalog class (hive or in-memory), instantiate it by reflection and install the Hadoop URL stream handler factory once. Both share this node.

nodes.name: externalCatalog
nodes.summary: Lazy val that builds the external catalog: instantiates the catalog class named by the catalog implementation setting via SharedState.reflect, creates the default database with ignoreIfExists when it is missing (or throws if the configured default database is not named 'default'), wraps it in ExternalCatalogWithListener and posts catalog events to the SparkContext listener bus.
nodes.languageNotes: Defined as a lazy val, so it is created on first use and not at SharedState construction.

nodes.name: statusStore
nodes.summary: Val that creates the SQL status store: it takes the ElementTrackingStore from the SparkContext, registers a SQLAppStatusListener on the status queue of the listener bus, builds a SQLAppStatusStore on top of it and attaches a SQLTab to the web UI when a UI exists.
nodes.languageNotes: Defined as a val, so it runs once at SharedState construction.

nodes.name: setFsUrlStreamHandlerFactory
nodes.summary: Private helper in the companion object that, once per JVM and only when DEFAULT_URL_STREAM_HANDLER_FACTORY_ENABLED is set, registers a Hadoop FsUrlStreamHandlerFactory via URL.setURLStreamHandlerFactory (double-checked under synchronized) and logs a warning on failure.

nodes.name: externalCatalogClassName
nodes.summary: Private helper that maps the CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION setting to a class name: 'hive' gives HiveExternalCatalog, 'in-memory' gives the canonical name of InMemoryCatalog.

nodes.name: reflect
nodes.summary: Private generic helper that loads a class by name, finds a constructor taking two given argument types (via ClassTags), constructs it and casts to T; any failure is rethrown as IllegalArgumentException 'Error while instantiating'.

nodes.name: resolveWarehousePath
nodes.summary: Decides the warehouse path from spark.sql.warehouse.dir in the initial session configs, then in the SparkConf, then hive.metastore.warehouse.dir in the Hadoop conf, then the default; warns if the Hive key is set in session options, removes the Hive key from the SparkConf, and returns the resolved path.

nodes.name: qualifyWarehousePath
nodes.summary: Qualifies the warehouse path with the file system of the given Hadoop conf (makeQualified) and logs the result.

nodes.name: setWarehousePathConf
nodes.summary: Writes the warehouse path to the SparkConf under spark.sql.warehouse.dir and to the Hadoop conf under hive.metastore.warehouse.dir.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the package object org.apache.spark.sql.internal, whose only content is a scaladoc stating that all classes in this package are an internal API subject to change between minor releases.

nodes.name: internal
nodes.summary: Empty package object 'internal' in org.apache.spark.sql (lines 20-24). It has no members; its scaladoc warns that every class in the internal package is internal API and may change between minor releases.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the package object org.apache.spark.sql.sources with a scaladoc describing the package as a set of APIs for adding data sources to Spark SQL.

nodes.name: sources
nodes.summary: Empty package object 'sources' in org.apache.spark.sql (lines 19-22). It has no members; its scaladoc says the package holds the APIs for adding data sources to Spark SQL.

nodes.name: VariableSubstitution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines VariableSubstitution, a helper that expands ${var}, ${system:var} and ${env:var} references in query text when SQLConf.variableSubstituteEnabled is on.

nodes.name: VariableSubstitution
nodes.summary: Class VariableSubstitution (lines 29-54) extends SQLConfHelper. It builds a ConfigReader over a ConfigProvider that reads values from the session conf via getConfString and redacts them with redactOptions, binds the prefixes spark, sparkconf, hivevar and hiveconf to that provider, and exposes substitute(input), which returns the input expanded by the reader if variableSubstituteEnabled is true and unchanged otherwise.

nodes.name: substitute
nodes.summary: Given a query string, runs the ConfigReader substitution when conf.variableSubstituteEnabled is true and otherwise returns the input unchanged.

nodes.name: KeyValueGroupedDataset.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract KeyValueGroupedDataset API, a Dataset logically grouped by a user-specified key (obtained through groupByKey on a Dataset). It covers key and value mapping, mapGroups and flatMapGroups (optionally with sorted iterators), stateful mapGroupsWithState, flatMapGroupsWithState and transformWithState, reduceGroups, typed agg for one to eight columns, count and cogroup. Java-friendly overloads delegate to the Scala versions through ToScalaUDF.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with context bounds (U: Encoder) and many Java-specific overloads that wrap Java functional interfaces with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: KeyValueGroupedDataset
nodes.summary: Abstract, serializable class for a Dataset grouped by a key of type K with values of type V; users call groupByKey on a Dataset instead of constructing it. Main methods: keyAs, mapValues, keys, flatMapGroups, flatMapSortedGroups, mapGroups, mapGroupsWithState, flatMapGroupsWithState, transformWithState, reduceGroups, agg (up to 8 typed columns), count, cogroup and cogroupSorted. Concrete subclasses supply the abstract members.

nodes.name: keyAs
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a KeyValueGroupedDataset whose key is mapped to another type L using an Encoder, following the same rules as `as` on Dataset.

nodes.name: mapValues
nodes.summary: Applies a function to the values of each group and keeps the key unchanged. The Scala overload (line 54) is abstract; this Java overload (MapFunction plus Encoder, lines 69-71) wraps the function with ToScalaUDF and delegates.

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a Dataset of each unique key, equivalent to mapping out the keys and applying distinct.

nodes.name: flatMapGroups
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each group, passing the key and an iterator over the group's elements, and returns a Dataset of the produced elements. The Scala overload (lines 99-101) delegates to flatMapSortedGroups with no sort expressions; this Java overload (lines 121-123) wraps FlatMapGroupsFunction with ToScalaUDF. Does not support partial aggregation, so all data is shuffled.

nodes.name: flatMapSortedGroups
nodes.summary: Same as flatMapGroups but the iterator given to the function is sorted by the supplied sort expressions. The Scala overload (lines 149-150) is abstract; this Java overload (lines 176-182) converts the Array of Columns and wraps the function with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: mapGroups
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each group that returns one element per group. The Scala overload (lines 202-204) delegates to flatMapGroups via UDFAdaptors.mapGroupsToFlatMapGroups; the Java overload (lines 224-226) wraps MapGroupsFunction with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: mapGroupsWithState
nodes.summary: Applies a function per group while keeping user-defined per-group state (GroupState), invoked once per group for batch data and every trigger for streaming data. Several overloads (lines 247-405) differ by timeoutConf and initialState; the Scala overloads are abstract and the Java overloads wrap MapGroupsWithStateFunction with ToScalaUDF. This node covers the widest overload (lines 397-405).

nodes.name: flatMapGroupsWithState
nodes.summary: Like mapGroupsWithState but the function returns an iterator of outputs and takes an OutputMode and GroupStateTimeout. Overloads (lines 430-548) add initialState; Scala versions are abstract and Java versions wrap FlatMapGroupsWithStateFunction with ToScalaUDF. This node covers the widest overload (lines 538-548).

nodes.name: transformWithState
nodes.summary: Invokes methods of a StatefulProcessor (arbitrary state API v2) for each group, with a TimeMode or an eventTimeColumnName, an OutputMode and optionally an initial state. Overloads (lines 569-806) include abstract Scala versions and Java versions taking explicit output and initial-state encoders that delegate to them. This node covers one of the widest overloads (lines 754-764).

nodes.name: reduceGroups
nodes.summary: Reduces the elements of each group with a binary function that must be commutative and associative. The Scala overload (line 815) is abstract; the Java overload (lines 824-826) wraps ReduceFunction with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: aggUntyped
nodes.summary: Protected abstract helper that builds typed aggregations returning tuples without using the type system; the public agg overloads cast its result.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Computes one to eight TypedColumn aggregations per key and returns a Dataset of tuples of the key and the results. Each overload (lines 841-941) calls aggUntyped and casts the result; this node covers the widest (8 columns, lines 931-941).

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Returns a Dataset of (key, count) tuples by calling agg with functions.count(lit(1)) encoded as a primitive Long.

nodes.name: cogroup
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each cogrouped key, passing the key and iterators over the elements from this and another KeyValueGroupedDataset. The Scala overload (lines 959-962) delegates to cogroupSorted with no sort expressions; the Java overload (lines 972-977) wraps CoGroupFunction with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: cogroupSorted
nodes.summary: Same as cogroup but the two iterators are sorted by the given expressions. The Scala overload (lines 994-995) is abstract; the Java overload (lines 1012-1021) converts the Column arrays and wraps CoGroupFunction with ToScalaUDF.

nodes.name: MergeIntoWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MergeIntoWriter, the abstract builder for merge operations, and the case classes WhenMatched, WhenNotMatched and WhenNotMatchedBySource that choose the action (update, delete, insert) for each kind of row. The writer collects actions through protected callbacks and runs them when merge() is called.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class plus three case classes with private[sql] constructors; the case classes forward to protected[sql] callbacks of the writer.

nodes.name: MergeIntoWriter
nodes.summary: Experimental abstract class that defines and runs merge actions for a Dataset. whenMatched, whenNotMatched and whenNotMatchedBySource (each with or without a Column condition) create the action holders; withSchemaEvolution turns on schema evolution (off by default); merge() executes the operation. Subclasses implement the protected[sql] callbacks insertAll, insert, updateAll, update and delete.

nodes.name: whenMatched
nodes.summary: Creates a WhenMatched action for rows where a source row matches a target row on the merge condition. The no-argument overload (lines 52-54) has no extra condition; this overload (lines 73-75) adds a Column condition.

nodes.name: whenNotMatched
nodes.summary: Creates a WhenNotMatched action for source rows that match no target row. The no-argument overload (lines 91-93) has no extra condition; this overload (lines 111-113) adds a Column condition.

nodes.name: whenNotMatchedBySource
nodes.summary: Creates a WhenNotMatchedBySource action for target rows that match no source row. The no-argument overload (lines 130-132) has no extra condition; this overload (lines 152-154) adds a Column condition.

nodes.name: withSchemaEvolution
nodes.summary: Turns on the schemaEvolution flag for this merge operation and returns the same writer.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Abstract method that executes the merge operation with the configured actions.

nodes.name: insertAll
nodes.summary: Protected[sql] abstract callback invoked by WhenNotMatched.insertAll to register an insert-all action with an optional condition.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Protected[sql] abstract callback invoked by WhenNotMatched.insert to register an insert action with a column assignment map and an optional condition.

nodes.name: updateAll
nodes.summary: Protected[sql] abstract callback invoked by WhenMatched and WhenNotMatchedBySource to register an update-all action; the notMatchedBySource flag selects which kind of rows it applies to.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Protected[sql] abstract callback invoked by WhenMatched and WhenNotMatchedBySource to register an update action with a column assignment map; the notMatchedBySource flag selects the row kind.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Protected[sql] abstract callback invoked by WhenMatched and WhenNotMatchedBySource to register a delete action; the notMatchedBySource flag selects the row kind.

nodes.name: WhenMatched
nodes.summary: Case class holding a MergeIntoWriter and an optional condition for rows that match on the merge condition. Its updateAll, update(Map) and delete methods call the writer's callbacks with notMatchedBySource set to false and return the writer.

nodes.name: updateAll
nodes.summary: Registers an update-all action on the writer for matched rows by calling MergeIntoWriter.updateAll with notMatchedBySource = false.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Registers an update action with the given column assignment map for matched rows by calling MergeIntoWriter.update with notMatchedBySource = false.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Registers a delete action for matched rows by calling MergeIntoWriter.delete with notMatchedBySource = false.

nodes.name: WhenNotMatched
nodes.summary: Case class holding a MergeIntoWriter and an optional condition for source rows that match no target row. Its insertAll and insert(Map) methods call the writer's insert callbacks and return the writer.

nodes.name: insertAll
nodes.summary: Registers an insert-all action for non-matched rows by calling MergeIntoWriter.insertAll with the stored condition.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Registers an insert action with the given column assignment map for non-matched rows by calling MergeIntoWriter.insert.

nodes.name: WhenNotMatchedBySource
nodes.summary: Case class holding a MergeIntoWriter and an optional condition for target rows that have no match in the source. Its updateAll, update(Map) and delete methods call the writer's callbacks with notMatchedBySource set to true and return the writer.

nodes.name: updateAll
nodes.summary: Registers an update-all action for target rows not matched by the source by calling MergeIntoWriter.updateAll with notMatchedBySource = true.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Registers an update action with the given column assignment map for target rows not matched by the source by calling MergeIntoWriter.update with notMatchedBySource = true.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Registers a delete action for target rows not matched by the source by calling MergeIntoWriter.delete with notMatchedBySource = true.

nodes.name: Observation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Observation helper class and its companion object, used with Dataset.observe to collect named metrics while the first action runs on the observed Dataset. get blocks until the metrics are available; an Observation can be registered with a Dataset only once.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class backed by a Promise[Row] and an AtomicBoolean; the companion object provides apply factories.

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.summary: Collects observed metrics for a Dataset. A promise holds the metrics Row, set through setMetricsAndNotify. get returns them as a Scala Map (getAsJava as a Java Map) after waiting for the first action to finish; markRegistered enforces single use; the name must be non-empty and a random UUID name is used when none is given. Not supported for streaming Datasets. Companion object (lines 148-159) offers apply() and apply(name).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Waits for the observed Dataset's first action and returns the observed metrics as a Map[String, Any]; returns an empty Map when the row or its schema is null. Calls getRow.

nodes.name: getAsJava
nodes.summary: Java-specific variant of get that returns the metrics as a java.util.Map by converting the result of get.

nodes.name: markRegistered
nodes.summary: Marks the Observation as registered using an atomic compareAndSet and throws IllegalArgumentException if it was already used with a Dataset.

nodes.name: setMetricsAndNotify
nodes.summary: Completes the internal promise with the observed metrics Try[Row], which wakes waiting threads; returns whether the completion succeeded.

nodes.name: getRow
nodes.summary: Waits on the future with SparkThreadUtils.awaitResult and unwraps the cause of a SparkException so the root cause is thrown.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion object factory that creates a named Observation; the no-argument overload (line 153) creates an anonymous one with a random name.

nodes.name: RelationalGroupedDataset.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract RelationalGroupedDataset, the result of groupBy, cube, rollup or pivot on a DataFrame. Provides agg in several forms and shortcut aggregates (count, mean, max, avg, min, sum) plus pivot overloads; concrete classes supply df, toDF, selectNumericColumns, as and the Column pivot methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with Scala-only and Java-specific agg overloads; varargs methods are annotated with scala.annotation.varargs.

nodes.name: RelationalGroupedDataset
nodes.summary: Stable abstract class for aggregations on a DataFrame after groupBy, cube, rollup or pivot; named GroupedData in Spark 1.x. agg accepts column/method pairs, a Map, a Java Map or Column expressions; count, mean, max, avg, min and sum aggregate numeric columns; pivot turns column values into columns, optionally with an explicit value list. Subclasses provide df, toDF, selectNumericColumns, as and the Column-based pivot.

nodes.name: toDF
nodes.summary: Protected abstract method that builds the aggregation DataFrame from the grouping and the given aggregate Columns.

nodes.name: selectNumericColumns
nodes.summary: Protected abstract method that selects the numeric columns among the given column names as Columns.

nodes.name: toAggCol
nodes.summary: Private helper that turns a (column name, method name) pair into an aggregate Column: avg/average/mean, stddev/std and count/size map to the functions avg, stddev and count, any other name is applied with Column.fn.

nodes.name: aggregateNumericColumns
nodes.summary: Private helper that applies a Column => Column aggregate function to the selected numeric columns and builds the result through toDF.

nodes.name: as
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning a KeyValueGroupedDataset grouped by the current grouping expressions, with Encoders for key and value types.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Computes aggregates and keeps grouping columns in the output. Overloads take (String, String) pairs (lines 89-90), a Scala Map (line 107), a Java Map (lines 122-124, this node, which converts to a Scala Map and calls the Map overload) or Column expressions (lines 157-158).

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Counts rows per group by aggregating functions.count(functions.lit(1)) aliased as count.

nodes.name: mean
nodes.summary: Computes the average of numeric columns per group (documented as an alias for avg) through aggregateNumericColumns with functions.avg.

nodes.name: max
nodes.summary: Computes the maximum of numeric columns per group through aggregateNumericColumns with functions.max.

nodes.name: avg
nodes.summary: Computes the average of numeric columns per group through aggregateNumericColumns with functions.avg.

nodes.name: min
nodes.summary: Computes the minimum of numeric columns per group through aggregateNumericColumns with functions.min.

nodes.name: sum
nodes.summary: Computes the sum of numeric columns per group through aggregateNumericColumns with functions.sum.

nodes.name: pivot
nodes.summary: Pivots a column and applies an aggregation. Overloads (lines 237-358) take a column name or Column, optionally with an explicit list of values (Seq or Java List) to avoid eagerly computing distinct values; the String versions delegate to the Column versions, and the Column versions (lines 338 and 358) are abstract. This node covers pivot(String, Seq) at lines 271-272.

nodes.name: RuntimeConfig.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract RuntimeConfig interface for reading and changing Spark SQL runtime configuration, reached through SparkSession.conf. Options set here are propagated to the Hadoop configuration during I/O.

nodes.name: RuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Stable abstract class with set (string, Boolean, Long and ConfigEntry overloads), get and getOption lookups (with or without a user default), getAll, unset, isModifiable and a private[sql] contains check. The Boolean and Long set overloads delegate to the String version; concrete implementations provide the storage.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets a configuration property. Overloads take a String value (line 37, abstract), a Boolean (lines 44-46, this node, which calls the String version with value.toString), a Long (lines 53-55, same approach) and a typed ConfigEntry (line 60, private[sql]).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the value of a configuration key, throwing NoSuchElementException if it is unset and has no built-in default. Overloads add a user default (line 82) and typed ConfigEntry/OptionalConfigEntry lookups (lines 88-89, 95, 101).

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: private[sql] abstract method returning whether a particular key is set.

nodes.name: getAll
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning all properties set in this configuration as a Map.

nodes.name: getOption
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning Some of the value (or its built-in default) for a key, or None when neither exists.

nodes.name: unset
nodes.summary: Abstract method that resets the configuration property for the given key.

nodes.name: isModifiable
nodes.summary: Abstract method telling whether a key can be modified in the current session; static SQL, Spark Core, non-existent and other non-modifiable keys return false.
