nodes.languageNotes: Annotated @Stable. Many names have a deprecated camelCase form (approxCountDistinct, sumDistinct, monotonicallyIncreasingId, toDegrees, shiftLeft, bitwiseNOT) next to the snake_case SQL name.

nodes.name: functions.partitioning
nodes.summary: Nested object partitioning (lines 11831-11880) holding the Scala-specific partition transform functions years, months, days, hours and bucket (bucket has an Int and a Column numBuckets overload). Each builds a Column with Column.internalFn(name, ...) and is used when declaring table partitioning on timestamp, date or hashed columns. A TODO in the source says it exists until a static annotation lets Java reach the same API, after which the top-level functions.years, months, days, hours and bucket are to be deprecated.

nodes.name: col
nodes.summary: Returns a Column for the given column name, as Column(colName). column is an alias; used wherever a column is referenced by name.

nodes.name: lit
nodes.summary: Creates a literal Column: returns the argument unchanged if it is already a Column, converts a Scala Symbol to a ColumnName, and otherwise builds Column(internal.Literal(literal)) directly to avoid the costly reflection that typedlit uses.

nodes.name: typedlit
nodes.summary: Creates a literal Column that can handle parameterized Scala types such as List, Seq and Map. Same handling of Column and Symbol as lit, otherwise it infers the data type with ScalaReflection.schemaFor[T] (wrapped in Try) and builds internal.Literal(literal, dataType). typedLit (131-141) is an alias that calls it.

nodes.name: expr
nodes.summary: Parses a SQL expression string into a Column by wrapping it in internal.SqlExpression, similar to selectExpr; the doc example is groupBy(expr("length(word)")).

nodes.name: broadcast
nodes.summary: Marks a Dataset as small enough to broadcast in a join by returning df.hint("broadcast") cast back to df.type.

nodes.name: when
nodes.summary: Starts a conditional expression: evaluates a condition and returns a value, built as internal.CaseWhenOtherwise from the (condition, lit(value)) pair.

nodes.name: window
nodes.summary: Time window grouping function for streaming and batch aggregation. The overloads (tumbling, sliding with slideDuration, and with startTime) delegate to the four-argument form (line 8277), which calls Column.fn("window", timeColumn, lit(windowDuration), lit(slideDuration), lit(startTime)). window_time and session_window follow it.

nodes.name: transform
nodes.summary: Higher-order function that applies a lambda to each element of an array column. Two overloads: f: Column => Column and f: (Column, Column) => Column (element and index). Both call Column.fn("transform", column, createLambda(f)).

nodes.name: createLambda
nodes.summary: Private helper (three overloads for 1, 2 and 3 argument Scala lambdas, widest range shown) that creates UnresolvedNamedLambdaVariable x, y, z, applies the Scala function to Columns over those variables, and wraps the resulting node in internal.LambdaFunction. Used by transform and the other higher-order functions.

nodes.name: explode
nodes.summary: Generator function that returns a new row for each element of an array or map column, using default column names col, key and value; built as Column.fn("explode", e). Related: explode_outer, posexplode, posexplode_outer, inline, inline_outer.

nodes.name: from_json
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string column into a struct, array or map using a schema. About 11 overloads take the schema as StructType, DataType, String or Column and options as Scala Map or java.util.Map; they funnel into a private from_json (line 9536) that calls Column.fnWithOptions("from_json", options, e, schema).

nodes.name: to_json
nodes.summary: Converts a struct, array or map column into a JSON string. Overloads accept a Scala Map or a java.util.Map of options (converted with asScala), or no options (an empty Map), and delegate to the same expression builder.

nodes.name: call_function
nodes.summary: Calls a SQL function by name, which may be quoted or qualified, with column arguments: Column(internal.UnresolvedFunction(funcName, cols.map(_.node), isUserDefinedFunction = true)). call_udf (line 11803) delegates to it; callUDF (line 11786) is the older name.

nodes.name: udf
nodes.summary: Defines a UserDefinedFunction. Scala overloads (11329-11594) take closures Function0 to Function10 with TypeTags and call SparkUserDefinedFunction(f, typeTag); Java overloads (11595-11776) take UDF0 to UDF10 plus a returnType and call SparkUserDefinedFunction(ToScalaUDF(f), returnType, arity); the deprecated udf(f: AnyRef, dataType) throws CompilationErrors.usingUntypedScalaUDFError() unless SqlApiConf.get.legacyAllowUntypedScalaUDFs is set.

nodes.name: udaf
nodes.summary: Wraps a typed Aggregator[IN, BUF, OUT] as a UserDefinedFunction usable in untyped DataFrame aggregation. The overload with a TypeTag infers the input encoder with ScalaReflection.encoderFor[IN]; the overload with an explicit Encoder[IN] (for Java) returns UserDefinedAggregator(agg, inputEncoder).

nodes.name: columnNodes.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ColumnNode AST used to build Column expressions independently of the execution backend: literals, attribute and star references, function calls, aliases, casts, sort orders, window specs and frames, lambdas, extract/update field, CASE WHEN, inline UDF calls, lazy and subquery expressions. Each node can normalize itself and render a SQL-like string; a backend converts the AST to its own form.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file of sealed hierarchies and case classes; most definitions are private[sql] and extend the ColumnNode trait.

nodes.name: ColumnNode
nodes.summary: private[sql] trait extending ColumnNodeLike for the Column AST: declares origin, a lazy normalized form (stripped of dataset context, used for Column equality and hash code) and a SQL-like sql string. Its companion object (lines 89-108) holds NO_ORIGIN and helpers normalize, argumentsToSql, textArgumentsToSql, elementsToSql and optionToSql.

nodes.name: ColumnNodeLike
nodes.summary: Base trait for anything that behaves like a node in the Column AST: normalize, sql and children, plus foreach (visit this node and all descendants) and collect (gather results of a partial function).

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Applies a function to this node and then recursively to every child node.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Walks the tree with foreach and gathers the results of a partial function into a Seq.

nodes.name: elementsToSql
nodes.summary: Companion helper that renders a sequence of nodes as a comma-separated string with an optional prefix, or an empty string when the sequence is empty. Other helpers in the object: normalize (lines 91-94), argumentsToSql, textArgumentsToSql and optionToSql.

nodes.name: Literal
nodes.summary: Case class node for a literal value with an optional DataType; sql renders null, strings, longs, floats, doubles and shorts with toSQLValue and other values with toString, and normalize clears the origin.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders the literal: NULL for null, quoted values through toSQLValue for String, Long, Float, Double and Short, and toString for everything else.

nodes.name: UnresolvedAttribute
nodes.summary: Case class node referencing an attribute produced by one of the underlying DataFrames, by name parts, optional plan id and a metadata-column flag. Its companion object (lines 164-186) adds apply overloads that parse an unparsed identifier with AttributeNameParser.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that parses an unparsed identifier into name parts with AttributeNameParser.parseAttributeName. Overloads (lines 165-185) default planId, isMetadataColumn and origin (CurrentOrigin.get).

nodes.name: UnresolvedStar
nodes.summary: Case class node referencing all columns in a namespace (global, a DataFrame or a nested struct); sql renders target.* or *.

nodes.name: UnresolvedFunction
nodes.summary: Case class node for calling a function by name (built-in, UDF or catalog-registered) with argument nodes, with flags for distinct, user-defined and internal; sql renders name(args).

nodes.name: SqlExpression
nodes.summary: Case class node holding SQL expression text to be evaluated; sql returns the text unchanged.

nodes.name: Alias
nodes.summary: Case class node that names a child column and optionally attaches Metadata; sql renders child AS name, with a parenthesized list for multi-part names.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders the alias as child.sql AS name; a single name is used as is and several names are rendered as an argument list.

nodes.name: Cast
nodes.summary: Case class node that casts a child to a DataType with an optional evaluation mode; sql renders the mode prefix, CAST(child AS type). Its companion object (lines 306-313) defines the EvalMode values Legacy, Ansi and Try.

nodes.name: EvalMode
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for the cast evaluation mode, a ColumnNodeLike whose sql is the mode prefix (empty by default) and which has no children.

nodes.name: Legacy
nodes.summary: Object for the legacy cast evaluation mode (no sql prefix).

nodes.name: Ansi
nodes.summary: Object for the ANSI cast evaluation mode (no sql prefix).

nodes.name: Try
nodes.summary: Object for the try cast evaluation mode; its sql prefix is TRY_.

nodes.name: UnresolvedRegex
nodes.summary: Case class node referencing all columns in the global namespace whose names match a regex; sql returns the regex.

nodes.name: SortOrder
nodes.summary: Case class node that sorts a child column by a SortDirection and NullOrdering; sql renders child, direction and null ordering. Its companion object (lines 358-369) defines Ascending, Descending, NullsFirst and NullsLast.

nodes.name: SortDirection
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for the sort direction, carrying its sql keyword and no children.

nodes.name: Ascending
nodes.summary: Object for ascending order, sql ASC.

nodes.name: Descending
nodes.summary: Object for descending order, sql DESC.

nodes.name: NullOrdering
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for null placement in sorting, carrying its sql keyword and no children.

nodes.name: NullsFirst
nodes.summary: Object for nulls first, sql NULLS FIRST.

nodes.name: NullsLast
nodes.summary: Object for nulls last, sql NULLS LAST.

nodes.name: Window
nodes.summary: Case class node that evaluates a function node within a WindowSpec; sql renders function OVER (spec).

nodes.name: WindowSpec
nodes.summary: Case class (a ColumnNodeLike) describing a window by partition columns, sort columns and an optional frame; sql joins PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and the frame parts that are not empty.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Builds the window clause by rendering partition columns with PARTITION BY, sort columns with ORDER BY and the frame, dropping empty parts and joining with spaces.

nodes.name: WindowFrame
nodes.summary: Case class (a ColumnNodeLike) for a window frame with a frame type and lower and upper boundaries; sql renders type BETWEEN lower AND upper. Its companion object (lines 427-454) defines FrameType (Row, Range), FrameBoundary (CurrentRow, UnboundedPreceding, UnboundedFollowing, Value) and value factories.

nodes.name: FrameType
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for the frame type, carrying its sql keyword and no children.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: Object for a row-based frame, sql ROWS.

nodes.name: Range
nodes.summary: Object for a range-based frame, sql RANGE.

nodes.name: FrameBoundary
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for a frame boundary; normalize returns itself and it has no children.

nodes.name: CurrentRow
nodes.summary: Object for the CURRENT ROW boundary.

nodes.name: UnboundedPreceding
nodes.summary: Object for the UNBOUNDED PRECEDING boundary.

nodes.name: UnboundedFollowing
nodes.summary: Object for the UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING boundary.

nodes.name: Value
nodes.summary: Case class boundary holding a ColumnNode value (an offset); sql is the value's sql and its child is the value.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Companion factory creating a Value boundary from an Int (line 452) or a Long (line 453) by wrapping it in a Literal typed IntegerType or LongType.

nodes.name: LambdaFunction
nodes.summary: Case class node for a lambda function with bound UnresolvedNamedLambdaVariable arguments, typically passed as an argument to another function; sql renders args -> body. Its companion object (lines 486-489) offers an apply that fills the origin from CurrentOrigin.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders the lambda: a single argument is shown bare, several arguments as an argument list, followed by -> and the body.

nodes.name: UnresolvedNamedLambdaVariable
nodes.summary: Case class node for a variable used in a LambdaFunction; sql is the variable name. Its companion object (lines 509-526) generates unique names with an AtomicLong counter and has a resetIdGenerator for tests.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that appends a unique counter value to the variable name, because names such as x, y or z are reused.

nodes.name: resetIdGenerator
nodes.summary: private[sql] method that sets the id counter back to 0; documented as for testing purposes only.

nodes.name: UnresolvedExtractValue
nodes.summary: Case class node that extracts a value from a complex type (struct field, map value or array element) using an extraction node; sql renders child[extraction].

nodes.name: UpdateFields
nodes.summary: Case class node that updates or drops a field of a struct; sql renders update_field(...) when a new value is given and drop_field(...) otherwise.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders update_field(struct, field, value) when a value expression exists and drop_field(struct, field) when it is None.

nodes.name: CaseWhenOtherwise
nodes.summary: Case class node for CASE WHEN branches (condition and value pairs) with an optional otherwise value; requires at least one branch and renders CASE ... END.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders CASE with a WHEN ... THEN ... entry per branch, an optional ELSE and END.

nodes.name: children
nodes.summary: Returns the flattened condition and value nodes of all branches followed by the otherwise node, if any.

nodes.name: InvokeInlineUserDefinedFunction
nodes.summary: Case class node that invokes an inline user-defined function (a UserDefinedFunctionLike) with argument nodes; sql renders function name and arguments.

nodes.name: UserDefinedFunctionLike
nodes.summary: private[sql] trait for user-defined functions whose default name is the formatted class name from SparkClassUtils.

nodes.name: LazyExpression
nodes.summary: Case class marker node that triggers lazy analysis in the Spark Classic DataFrame for its child; sql renders lazy(child).

nodes.name: SubqueryType
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the kind of subquery in a SubqueryExpression; its companion object (lines 658-662) defines SCALAR, EXISTS and IN(values).

nodes.name: SCALAR
nodes.summary: Case object for a scalar subquery.

nodes.name: EXISTS
nodes.summary: Case object for an EXISTS subquery.

nodes.name: IN
nodes.summary: Case class for an IN subquery that carries the list of value nodes tested for membership.

nodes.name: SubqueryExpression
nodes.summary: Public case class node that wraps a Dataset used as a subquery together with its SubqueryType; sql renders the subquery as (ds), a membership test for IN or the type followed by (ds).

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Renders the subquery: ($ds) for SCALAR, (values) IN ($ds) for IN, and the type followed by ($ds) otherwise.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the org.apache.spark.sql package object: the DataFrame type alias for Dataset[Row] and private[sql] constants for file metadata keys (Spark version, session time zone, legacy datetime, legacy INT96).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala package object; DataFrame is a type alias, not a class, so it has no node of its own.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Package object of org.apache.spark.sql. Declares type DataFrame = Dataset[Row] and the private[sql] string constants SPARK_VERSION_METADATA_KEY (org.apache.spark.version), SPARK_TIMEZONE_METADATA_KEY (org.apache.spark.timeZone), SPARK_LEGACY_DATETIME_METADATA_KEY (org.apache.spark.legacyDateTime) and SPARK_LEGACY_INT96_METADATA_KEY (org.apache.spark.legacyINT96), used as keys in written file metadata.

nodes.name: SQLContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract SQLContext, the Spark 1.x style entry point kept for backward compatibility that now wraps a SparkSession, together with the SQLContextCompanion trait and the SQLContext companion object. Most methods simply delegate to the wrapped session (configuration, createDataFrame/createDataset, range, sql, table listing) and a block of deprecated loaders (jsonFile, jsonRDD, load, jdbc, parquetFile) delegates to the reader.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class whose concrete members forward to sparkSession; the abstract members (newSession, setConf(props), listenerManager, experimental, udf, implicits, read, readStream, streams) are supplied by subclasses.

nodes.name: SQLContext
nodes.summary: Abstract wrapper around a SparkSession that keeps the old SQLContext API alive (annotated Stable). Provides config access (setConf, getConf, getAllConfs), table cache calls (isCached, cacheTable, uncacheTable, clearCache), DataFrame and Dataset creation (createDataFrame, createDataset, baseRelationToDataFrame, emptyDataFrame, range), sql, table, tables and tableNames, and a deprecated section (applySchema, parquetFile, jsonFile, jsonRDD, load, jdbc, createExternalTable, dropTempTable). It extends Logging and Serializable; the companion object SQLContext (lines 1022-1030, extending SQLContextCompanion) shares this node id and offers getOrCreate.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract members newSession, setConf(Properties), listenerManager, experimental, udf, implicits, read, readStream and streams are left to subclasses.

nodes.name: SQLContextCompanion
nodes.summary: Private trait holding the shared companion behaviour of SQLContext: an abstract type SQLContextImpl, an abstract deprecated getOrCreate(sparkContext), and setActive and clearActive, which forward to SparkSession.setActiveSession and SparkSession.clearActiveSession. Used by the SQLContext companion object.

nodes.name: setConf
nodes.summary: Sets one Spark SQL configuration key/value by calling sparkSession.conf.set. An abstract overload setConf(Properties) is declared at line 83 and left to subclasses.

nodes.name: getConf
nodes.summary: Returns the value of a configuration key through sparkSession.conf.get; a second overload at lines 112-114 takes a default value for keys that are not set.

nodes.name: getAllConfs
nodes.summary: Returns all configuration properties that were explicitly set (not defaults) as an immutable Map copy, via sparkSession.conf.getAll.

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrame from an RDD of Rows plus a StructType schema (annotated DeveloperApi) by calling sparkSession.createDataFrame. Overloads at lines 227, 237, 363, 377, 389, 401 and 413 take an RDD or Seq of Products, a JavaRDD or java List of Rows with a schema, or an RDD, JavaRDD or List with a bean class.

nodes.name: createDataset
nodes.summary: Creates a Dataset from a local Seq with an implicit Encoder by calling sparkSession.createDataset. Overloads at lines 329-331 (RDD input) and 349-351 (java List input) work the same way.

nodes.name: createExternalTable
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 2.2.0; creates a table from a source, schema and options by calling sparkSession.catalog.createTable. Five other overloads (lines 448-525) cover path-only, path plus source, and source with java or Scala option maps, with or without a schema.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrame of ids from start to end with a step and number of partitions by calling sparkSession.range(...).toDF(). Overloads at lines 547, 556 and 565 provide the shorter argument lists.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Executes a SQL query string through sparkSession.sql and returns the result as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns the named table or view as a DataFrame by calling sparkSession.table.

nodes.name: tables
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame listing the tables of the current database by passing sparkSession.catalog.listTables() to mapTableDatasetOutput. The overload at lines 619-621 takes a database name.

nodes.name: mapTableDatasetOutput
nodes.summary: Private helper that reshapes the catalog Table Dataset into the old tables() layout: columns namespace (first namespace element or empty string), tableName and isTemporary, using when/coalesce so the columns come out non-nullable.

nodes.name: tableNames
nodes.summary: Returns the names of the tables in the given database as an Array[String], by selecting the name column of sparkSession.catalog.listTables and collecting it with Encoders.STRING. The no-argument overload at lines 651-653 uses the current database.

nodes.name: applySchema
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.3.0 alias that forwards to createDataFrame; three more overloads (lines 688-709) accept JavaRDD input or a bean class.

nodes.name: parquetFile
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.4.0; loads Parquet files as a DataFrame with read.parquet(paths), returning emptyDataFrame when no path is given.

nodes.name: jsonFile
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.4.0; loads JSON files with read.json, with optional schema (read.schema(schema).json) or samplingRatio option variants at lines 738-740, 750-753 and 760-763.

nodes.name: jsonRDD
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.4.0; loads an RDD or JavaRDD of JSON strings into a DataFrame via read.json, optionally with a schema or a samplingRatio option. Six overloads span lines 774-837.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.4.0; loads data using read.format(source).schema(schema).options(options).load(). Other overloads (lines 848-914) take a path, a path with source, or a source with options, using Java or Scala maps.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Deprecated since 1.4.0; reads a JDBC table partitioned on columnName between lowerBound and upperBound with read.jdbc. Overloads at lines 924-927 (url and table) and 967-970 (explicit partition predicates) use Properties defaults.

nodes.name: setActive
nodes.summary: Deprecated; sets the SQLContext active for the current thread by calling SparkSession.setActiveSession on its session.

nodes.name: clearActive
nodes.summary: Deprecated; clears the active SQLContext for the current thread by calling SparkSession.clearActiveSession.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Deprecated; the companion object implementation that builds a session with SparkSession.builder().sparkContext(sparkContext).getOrCreate() and returns its sqlContext. The abstract declaration is in SQLContextCompanion at line 996.

nodes.name: SQLImplicits.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the implicit conversions and implicit Encoders that let Scala values become Datasets: the abstract SQLImplicits class (string-context $ column syntax, Seq and RDD to DatasetHolder, Symbol to ColumnName), the EncoderImplicits trait with encoders for primitives, boxed types, dates and times, Seq, Map, Set and Array types, and LowPrioritySQLImplicits with the product encoder. Used when users write import spark.implicits._.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala implicit classes, implicit defs and a low priority trait to resolve ambiguity between Seq and Product encoders.

nodes.name: SQLImplicits
nodes.summary: Abstract class (Serializable, extends EncoderImplicits) of session-bound implicit conversions: the nested StringToColumn class for the $"name" syntax, the abstract localSeqToDatasetHolder and rddToDatasetHolder conversions that build a DatasetHolder from a Seq or RDD, symbolToColumn (Symbol to ColumnName), and the protected abstract session accessor.

nodes.name: StringToColumn
nodes.summary: Implicit class wrapping a StringContext so that $"col name" produces a ColumnName; its $ method builds new ColumnName(sc.s(args: _*)).

nodes.name: EncoderImplicits
nodes.summary: Trait that supplies implicit Encoder instances without needing a SparkSession: primitives (newIntEncoder to newBooleanEncoder, newStringEncoder), decimals, Geometry, Geography, java.sql and java.time dates and times, boxed primitives, Seq encoders (newSequenceEncoder plus deprecated newIntSeqEncoder and similar vals), Map and Set encoders (newMapEncoder, newSetEncoder), Java enum encoders, and Array encoders (newIntArrayEncoder, newProductArrayEncoder, etc.). Extends LowPrioritySQLImplicits and Serializable.
nodes.languageNotes: Many encoders are implicit vals or defs delegating to Encoders.* or ScalaReflection.encoderFor; private helpers newSeqEncoder and newArrayEncoder build AgnosticEncoders.

nodes.name: LowPrioritySQLImplicits
nodes.summary: Low priority implicit holder for conflicting implicits; it contains newProductEncoder, placed here so that List values (both Seq and Product) resolve to the Seq encoder.
Builds a ColumnName from the interpolated string using sc.s(args: _*); this is what enables $"col name" column syntax.

nodes.name: symbolToColumn
nodes.summary: Implicit conversion that turns a Scala Symbol into a ColumnName using the symbol name.

nodes.name: newJavaEnumEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for Java enum types, obtained from ScalaReflection.encoderFor[A].

nodes.name: newSeqEncoder
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps an element AgnosticEncoder into an IterableEncoder for Seq[E], passing the element nullability and lenient serialization settings. Used by the deprecated Seq val encoders.

nodes.name: newProductSeqEncoder
nodes.summary: Deprecated (use newSequenceEncoder) encoder for Seq of Product types, built with newSeqEncoder(ScalaReflection.encoderFor[A]).

nodes.name: newSequenceEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for any Seq subtype, derived with ScalaReflection.encoderFor[T].

nodes.name: newMapEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for Map types, derived with ScalaReflection.encoderFor[T].

nodes.name: newSetEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for Set types; sets are serialized as Catalyst arrays, so duplicates in the array are removed when decoding back to a Set.

nodes.name: newArrayEncoder
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps an element AgnosticEncoder into an ArrayEncoder, passing the element nullability. Used by the primitive and string array encoder vals.

nodes.name: newProductArrayEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for Array of Product types, built by newArrayEncoder(ScalaReflection.encoderFor[A]).

nodes.name: newProductEncoder
nodes.summary: Implicit encoder for Product types (case classes, tuples) via Encoders.product[T]; kept at low priority to disambiguate List values.

nodes.name: TableValuedFunction.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract TableValuedFunction interface of Spark SQL (since 4.0.0): methods that each return a Dataset from a table-valued call, namely range, the explode and inline generator families, json_tuple, stack, collations, sql_keywords, the variant_explode pair and python_worker_logs. Concrete implementations live in other files.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with only abstract members; @scala.annotation.varargs on json_tuple and stack.

nodes.name: TableValuedFunction
nodes.summary: Abstract interface for invoking table-valued functions: range overloads (Dataset[Long] column id), generators explode, explode_outer, posexplode, posexplode_outer, inline, inline_outer, json_tuple, stack, plus collations, sql_keywords, variant_explode, variant_explode_outer and python_worker_logs, each returning a Dataset (mostly Dataset[Row]). It has no implementation here.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Abstract range producing a Dataset[Long] with a single LongType column named id from 0 or start to end (exclusive) with a step; overloads at lines 35, 44, 53 and 62 add start, step and numPartitions.

nodes.name: explode
nodes.summary: Abstract; creates a DataFrame with one row per element of an array or map column, using default column names col, or key and value.

nodes.name: explode_outer
nodes.summary: Abstract; like explode but produces a null row when the array or map is null or empty.

nodes.name: inline
nodes.summary: Abstract; creates a DataFrame with one row per element of an array of structs.

nodes.name: inline_outer
nodes.summary: Abstract; like inline but produces null for each nested column when the array is null or empty.

nodes.name: json_tuple
nodes.summary: Abstract varargs method; creates a DataFrame with a new row for a JSON column according to the given field names.

nodes.name: posexplode
nodes.summary: Abstract; like explode but also returns the element position, with default column names pos, col, or key and value.

nodes.name: posexplode_outer
nodes.summary: Abstract; like posexplode but produces the row (null, null) when the array or map is null or empty.

nodes.name: stack
nodes.summary: Abstract varargs method; separates col1 to colk into n rows, with default column names col0, col1 and so on.

nodes.name: collations
nodes.summary: Abstract; returns all Spark SQL string collations as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: sql_keywords
nodes.summary: Abstract; returns the Spark SQL keywords as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: variant_explode
nodes.summary: Abstract; separates a variant object or array into rows with schema struct<pos int, key string, value variant>, ignoring non-variant-array/object input.

nodes.name: variant_explode_outer
nodes.summary: Abstract; like variant_explode but produces NULL when the variant is not an array or object.

nodes.name: python_worker_logs
nodes.summary: Abstract; returns a DataFrame of logs collected from Python workers (since 4.1.0).

nodes.name: UDFRegistration.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract UDFRegistration (since 4.0.0), the object behind SparkSession.udf for registering user-defined functions by name. It has a few hand-written members (registerJava, register for UserDefinedFunction and the deprecated UserDefinedAggregateFunction, private helpers, and a protected abstract register) followed by generated overloads: register for Scala closures of 0 to 22 arguments (lines 168-1131) and register for Java UDF0 to UDF22 instances (lines 1141-1363).
nodes.languageNotes: Overloads for arities 0-22 were generated by the script shown in the comment at lines 128-165; each Scala overload is a thin call to registerScalaUDF with implicit TypeTags, each Java overload calls registerJavaUDF(name, ToScalaUDF(f), returnType, n).

nodes.name: UDFRegistration
nodes.summary: Abstract class for registering UDFs by name. registerJava registers a Java UDF class by class name; register(name, UserDefinedFunction) registers a UDF built with the Dataset API; register(name, UserDefinedAggregateFunction) is deprecated since 3.0.0; Scala-closure overloads with 0 to 22 arguments and Java UDF0 to UDF22 overloads validate parameter counts and delegate to the protected abstract register(name, udf, source, validateParameterCount), which concrete subclasses implement.

nodes.name: registerJava
nodes.summary: Abstract; registers a Java UDF class by fully qualified class name with an optional return data type (inferred by reflection when null). The class must implement one of the UDF interfaces of the api.java package; noted as not supported in Spark Connect.

nodes.name: registerScalaUDF
nodes.summary: Private helper that wraps a Scala closure and its TypeTags into SparkUserDefinedFunction and registers it through the protected register with source "scala_udf" and validateParameterCount = true.

nodes.name: registerJavaUDF
nodes.summary: Private helper that rejects char/varchar return types via SparkCharVarcharUtils.failIfHasCharVarchar, wraps the function and cardinality in SparkUserDefinedFunction, and registers it with source "java_udf" and parameter-count validation.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Representative node for the many overloads named register: the 22-argument Scala closure version (lines 1057-1131, widest) forwards to registerScalaUDF with 23 implicit TypeTags. Other overloads: register(name, UserDefinedFunction) at 79-81 (source "scala_udf", no parameter count validation), the deprecated UDAF version at 101, the protected abstract register(name, udf, source, validateParameterCount) at 122-126, Scala closures of 0 to 21 arguments (lines 168-1054), and Java UDF0 to UDF22 versions (lines 1141-1363) calling registerJavaUDF(name, ToScalaUDF(f), returnType, n).

nodes.name: base.proto
nodes.summary: Protobuf definitions of the Spark Connect session API: Plan, user context, analyze, execute, config, artifact, interrupt, reattach, release, error detail, clone session and status messages, plus the SparkConnectService gRPC service that exposes them as RPCs. Defines 99 top-level and nested messages, enums and services.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol Buffers proto3 file in package spark.connect with java_multiple_files and java_package org.apache.spark.connect.proto.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.summary: The top-level unit sent to the server; a oneof (op_type) holding a root Relation, a Command or a compressed operation. Fields: root, command, compressed_operation. Oneof op_type: root, command, compressed_operation.

nodes.name: Plan.CompressedOperation
nodes.summary: A compressed relation or command: the compressed bytes, the operation type and the compression codec. Fields: data, op_type, compression_codec.

nodes.name: Plan.CompressedOperation.OpType
nodes.summary: Enum of what a compressed operation holds: unspecified, relation or command. Values: OP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, OP_TYPE_RELATION, OP_TYPE_COMMAND.

nodes.name: CompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Enum of compression codecs for compressed operations: unspecified and zstd. Values: COMPRESSION_CODEC_UNSPECIFIED, COMPRESSION_CODEC_ZSTD.

nodes.name: UserContext
nodes.summary: Identifies the user of a request (user id and name) and carries extension Any messages. Fields: user_id, user_name, extensions.

nodes.name: AnalyzePlanRequest
nodes.summary: Request to analyze a plan without executing it; carries session id, user context, client type and a oneof (analyze) selecting schema, explain, tree string, is local, is streaming, input files, spark version, DDL parse, same semantics, semantic hash, persist, unpersist, get storage level or JSON to DDL. Fields: session_id, client_observed_server_side_session_id, user_context, client_type, schema, explain, tree_string, is_local, is_streaming, input_files, spark_version, ddl_parse, same_semantics, semantic_hash, persist, unpersist, get_storage_level, json_to_ddl. Oneof analyze: schema, explain, tree_string, is_local, is_streaming, input_files, spark_version, ddl_parse, same_semantics, semantic_hash, persist, unpersist, get_storage_level, json_to_ddl.

nodes.name: AnalyzePlanRequest.Schema
nodes.summary: Asks for the schema of a plan. Fields: plan.

nodes.name: AnalyzePlanRequest.Explain
nodes.summary: Asks for the explain string of a plan in a chosen explain mode. Fields: plan, explain_mode.

nodes.name: AnalyzePlanRequest.Explain.ExplainMode

nodes.summary: Result of defining an output, carrying its resolved identifier. Fields: resolved_identifier.

nodes.name: PipelineCommandResult.DefineFlowResult
nodes.summary: Result of defining a flow, carrying its resolved identifier. Fields: resolved_identifier.

nodes.name: OutputType
nodes.summary: Enum of pipeline output types: unspecified, materialized view, table, temporary view and sink. Values: OUTPUT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, MATERIALIZED_VIEW, TABLE, TEMPORARY_VIEW, SINK.

nodes.name: PipelineEventResult
nodes.summary: A response that carries one event emitted during a pipeline run. Fields: event.

nodes.name: PipelineEvent
nodes.summary: A pipeline event with a timestamp and an optional message. Fields: timestamp, message.

nodes.name: SourceCodeLocation
nodes.summary: Source code location (file name, line number, definition path and extensions) of a dataset or flow. Fields: file_name, line_number, definition_path, extension.

nodes.name: PipelineQueryFunctionExecutionSignal
nodes.summary: Signal from the server asking the client to execute the query function for one or more flows (by name and identifier). Fields: flow_names, flow_identifiers.

nodes.name: PipelineAnalysisContext
nodes.summary: Metadata giving pipeline context (graph id, definition path, flow name and identifier) during query analysis. Fields: dataflow_graph_id, definition_path, flow_name, flow_identifier, extension.

nodes.name: AggregatingAccumulator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AggregatingAccumulator, an AccumulatorV2 that computes a global aggregate over InternalRow input using declarative, imperative and typed imperative aggregate functions. Used by CollectMetricsExec to gather named metrics from a query.

nodes.name: AggregatingAccumulator
nodes.summary: Accumulator that keeps one aggregation buffer (a SpecificInternalRow) and updates it with row input via update projections and imperative aggregates, merges buffers from other accumulators, and produces a result row through result projections. The companion object's apply builds an instance from aggregate expressions and the input attributes. Used on executors to add rows and on the driver to merge and read the value.

nodes.name: createBuffer
nodes.summary: Builds a fresh SpecificInternalRow buffer, fills it from the initial value expressions with an interpreted projection (not generated code, as stated in the comment) and initializes imperative and typed imperative aggregates.

nodes.name: getOrCreateBuffer
nodes.summary: Lazily creates the buffer on first use and sets up the JoinedRow whose left side is the buffer.

nodes.name: withSQLConf
nodes.summary: Runs a body under the stored SQLConf when present (driver side), directly when it may run on an executor, or returns a default value otherwise; needed because the DAGScheduler thread has no SQL configuration.

nodes.name: copyAndReset
nodes.summary: Creates a new AggregatingAccumulator with the same expressions and aggregates but no buffer state.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds one input row: applies the update projection to the buffer joined with the row, then calls update on every imperative and typed imperative aggregate.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another AggregatingAccumulator into this one using the merge projection and the merge methods of imperative aggregates; typed imperatives use merge on the driver (serialized buffers) and mergeBuffersObjects otherwise. Throws a cannot-merge error for other accumulator types. The copy method (lines 133-137) calls copyAndReset then merge.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Returns the result row by applying the result projection to the current buffer, or to a temporary buffer when the accumulator is still zero so its state is not changed.

nodes.name: withBufferSerialized
nodes.summary: Serializes the buffers of all typed imperative aggregates in place; asserts it runs on the executor side.

nodes.name: setState
nodes.summary: Copies the buffer and joined row of another accumulator into this one so state is published only when a task completes; CollectMetricsExec is named as the example user.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: walks the given aggregate expressions, collects buffer attributes, initial, update and merge expressions for declarative aggregates, binds imperative aggregates (inserting NoOp placeholders to stay aligned), builds result expressions, and returns a new AggregatingAccumulator.

nodes.name: AliasAwareOutputExpression.scala
nodes.summary: Defines two physical-plan traits for unary operators that propagate child partitioning and ordering through aliases in their output expressions. Used by projecting operators so aliased columns still satisfy distribution and ordering requirements.

nodes.name: PartitioningPreservingUnaryExecNode
nodes.summary: Trait for unary exec nodes that compute outputPartitioning from the child's partitioning, rewriting expressions through aliases (hasAlias, projectExpression, capped by aliasCandidateLimit) or keeping only partitionings that reference output attributes. Falls back to UnknownPartitioning when nothing remains and wraps several results in a PartitioningCollection.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Computes the node's output partitioning: with aliases it projects each child partitioning expression, dedupes by canonicalized form and limits the number of candidates; without aliases it keeps partitionings whose references are in the output set. Returns UnknownPartitioning, a single partitioning, or a PartitioningCollection.

nodes.name: flattenPartitioning
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens nested PartitioningCollection values into a flat sequence of partitionings.

nodes.name: OrderPreservingUnaryExecNode
nodes.summary: Trait that mixes UnaryExecNode with AliasAwareQueryOutputOrdering so a unary operator keeps the child's output ordering through aliased output expressions.

nodes.name: BaseScriptTransformationExec.scala
nodes.summary: Base support for script transformation in physical plans: runs an external script through bash, feeds it input rows through a writer thread and parses the script's output lines back into rows. Also holds the ScriptTransformationIOSchema that carries row format and serde properties.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with a lazy per-column converter list built by pattern matching on Catalyst data types.

nodes.name: BaseScriptTransformationExec
nodes.summary: Trait for a unary exec node that pipes child rows through an external script. doExecute maps each partition, skips launching the script when the partition is empty, and calls the abstract processIterator. It provides initProc (starts /bin/bash -c with the script, sets PATH and OMP_NUM_THREADS, drains stderr into a CircularBuffer), createOutputIteratorWithoutSerde (reads output lines and converts fields), checkFailureAndPropagate (waits for the process and raises an error on nonzero exit) and outputFieldWriters (string-to-type converters).

nodes.name: BaseScriptTransformationWriterThread
nodes.summary: Abstract daemon thread that writes the input rows to the script's output stream. It records any exception for the reader side, destroys the process on write failure, closes the stream and waits for the process in run, and offers processRowsWithoutSerde for the default text format.

nodes.name: ScriptTransformationIOSchema
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping the input and output row formats, serde classes and properties, record reader and writer classes and the schemaLess flag. The companion object supplies defaultFormat (field, line and null tokens), defaultIOSchema and an apply that converts a ScriptInputOutputSchema.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the child, and for each non-empty partition calls processIterator with a broadcast Hadoop configuration and projects results to UnsafeProjection rows; empty partitions return an empty iterator without starting the script.

nodes.name: initProc
nodes.summary: Starts the script with /bin/bash -c in the SparkFiles root directory, appends that directory to PATH, sets OMP_NUM_THREADS from spark.task.cpus when unset, and starts a RedirectThread that copies stderr into a 2048-size CircularBuffer to avoid deadlocks. Returns the output stream, process, input stream and stderr buffer.

nodes.name: createOutputIteratorWithoutSerde
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator that reads script output lines, splits them with the output field token and converts each field with outputFieldWriters (or takes the first two string columns in schema-less mode). On errors or end of input it calls checkFailureAndPropagate.

nodes.name: checkFailureAndPropagate
nodes.summary: Rethrows an exception captured by the writer thread, waits for the process up to the script transformation exit timeout setting, and throws a subprocess-exited error with the stderr buffer when the exit code is nonzero.

nodes.name: outputFieldWriters
nodes.summary: Lazy value that builds, per output attribute, a function converting a text field to the Catalyst value for string, boolean, numeric, decimal, date, timestamp, interval, complex (via JsonToStructs) and user-defined types; unsupported types raise an error. Conversions are wrapped by wrapperConvertException.

nodes.name: processRowsWithoutSerde
nodes.summary: Writes each input row to the script as a text line, joining fields with the field token, writing the null token for nulls and ending with the line token.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Thread body: sets the task context, runs processRows, stores any Throwable and destroys the process, then closes the output stream, waits for the process and logs stderr when it exits nonzero.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a ScriptTransformationIOSchema from a catalyst ScriptInputOutputSchema by copying its fields.

nodes.name: CoGroupedIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CoGroupedIterator, which merges two key-ordered grouped iterators into one iterator of (key, left rows, right rows). Used where two grouped inputs must be processed together by grouping key.

nodes.name: CoGroupedIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over two iterators of (key, rows) pairs that assumes both are ordered by the grouping key. It compares keys with a generated ordering and emits the pair with the smaller key alone (other side empty) or, for equal keys, both row iterators together.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Pulls the next group from each side when the current slot is empty and reports whether either side still has data.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next cogrouped tuple: right only, left only, or both when keys are equal; otherwise compares keys with the generated ordering and consumes the smaller side.

nodes.name: leftOnly
nodes.summary: Emits the current left group with an empty right iterator and clears the left slot.

nodes.name: rightOnly
nodes.summary: Emits the current right group with an empty left iterator and clears the right slot.

nodes.name: CollectMetricsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CollectMetricsExec, a pass-through unary operator that computes named metrics over its child's rows with an AggregatingAccumulator, plus a helper to gather all collected metrics from a plan tree.

nodes.name: CollectMetricsExec
nodes.summary: Case class unary exec node that leaves child rows, output, partitioning and ordering unchanged while feeding each row to an AggregatingAccumulator built from the metric expressions. Exposes collectedMetrics as a Row converted from the accumulator value. The companion object defines ACCUMULATOR_NAME and collect, which walks a plan (including subqueries and cached in-memory table scans) and returns a Map from metric name to Row.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps child partitions through a task-local copy of the accumulator, adds every row to it, and on task completion either sets the shared accumulator's state or merges into it, so partial updates are not visible during heartbeats.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Companion method that recursively collects metrics from a plan tree, using collectWithSubqueries to find CollectMetricsExec nodes and following InMemoryTableScanExec relations into their cached plans, and merges the maps.

nodes.name: collectedMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the accumulator value converted to a Row of the metrics schema.

nodes.name: Columnar.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the columnar plugin hook (ColumnarRule), the row-to-columnar and columnar-to-row transition operators (RowToColumnarExec, ColumnarToRowExec) with their tag traits, the RowToColumnConverter that appends InternalRow data to writable column vectors, and the ApplyColumnarRulesAndInsertTransitions rule that places the transitions in a physical plan. Used when a physical plan has operators that support columnar execution.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source file.

nodes.name: ColumnarRule
nodes.summary: Holds user-defined rules for injecting columnar implementations of operators. preColumnarTransitions can replace SparkPlan nodes with columnar versions before Spark inserts transitions, and postColumnarTransitions runs afterwards to replace the transitions or clean up the plan. Both default to identity rules.

nodes.name: ColumnarToRowTransition
nodes.summary: Tag trait for unary plan nodes that transition from columns to rows, so plugins can replace ColumnarToRowExec with an optimized version and plan walkers still recognize the transition.

nodes.name: ColumnarToRowExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator that turns an RDD of ColumnarBatch into an RDD of InternalRow, inserted whenever a columnar-to-row transition is needed. doExecute builds a ColumnarToRowEvaluatorFactory (either via mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or per-partition evaluators), and doProduce generates whole-stage code that iterates the batches and emits one row per batch row, with numOutputRows and numInputBatches metrics and limit/stop checks.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Creates a ColumnarToRowEvaluatorFactory from the child output and the two metrics, and applies it to the child columnar RDD either through mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or a per-partition evaluator, depending on conf.usePartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: genCodeColumnVector
nodes.summary: Generates the ExprCode that reads a single column value (and null flag when nullable) from a ColumnVector at a row ordinal, for the parent operator to consume as a row.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Produces the generated Java source that loops over ColumnarBatch inputs: it declares batch, batchIdx and column vector fields, adds a nextBatch function that updates the metrics, then emits a per-row loop calling the parent consume, with a shouldStop check and batch cleanup.

nodes.name: inputRDDs
nodes.summary: Returns the child columnar RDD cast to RDD[InternalRow] (a type-erasure workaround) as the single input of the codegen stage.

nodes.name: RowToColumnConverter
nodes.summary: Serializable helper (with its companion object) that appends InternalRow fields to an array of WritableColumnVector. The class builds one TypeConverter per schema field and convert() applies them to a row. The companion object picks converters by data type in getConverterForType (primitive, string, binary, interval, variant, array, struct, decimal and map types) and wraps them in null-handling converters when the field is nullable. Private singleton converters exist for Binary, Boolean, Byte, Short, Int, Float, Long, Double, String, BinaryView, Calendar and Variant.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Appends each field of an InternalRow to the matching WritableColumnVector by calling the per-field converter in order.

nodes.name: getConverterForType
nodes.summary: Maps a Catalyst DataType to a TypeConverter (recursing for arrays, structs and maps), throws an unsupported-type error for unknown types, and wraps the result in a basic or struct null-handling converter when the column is nullable.

nodes.name: TypeConverter
nodes.summary: Private abstract serializable base class of all converters, with a single append(row, column, vector) method that writes one value into a WritableColumnVector.

nodes.name: BasicNullableTypeConverter
nodes.summary: Wraps another converter and appends a null to the vector when the row value is null, otherwise delegates.

nodes.name: StructNullableTypeConverter
nodes.summary: Wraps another converter and appends a null struct (appendStruct(true)) when the row value is null, otherwise delegates; used for struct, calendar interval and variant columns.

nodes.name: ArrayConverter
nodes.summary: Appends an array value by calling appendArray and then the element converter for every element.

nodes.name: StructConverter
nodes.summary: Appends a struct value by appending a struct and running one child converter per field on the child vectors.

nodes.name: DecimalConverter
nodes.summary: Appends a decimal as an int, a long or the unscaled big-integer bytes depending on whether the precision fits Decimal.MAX_INT_DIGITS or MAX_LONG_DIGITS.

nodes.name: MapConverter
nodes.summary: Appends a map value by appending an array of the given size and converting keys and values with the key and value converters into the two child vectors.

nodes.name: RowToColumnarTransition
nodes.summary: Tag trait for unary plan nodes that transition from rows to columns, so plugins can replace RowToColumnarExec with an optimized version and plan walkers still recognize it.

nodes.name: RowToColumnarExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator that converts an RDD of InternalRow from the child into an RDD of ColumnarBatch (supportsColumnar is true). doExecuteColumnar builds a RowToColumnarEvaluatorFactory using conf.offHeapColumnVectorEnabled and conf.columnBatchSize, with numInputRows and numOutputBatches metrics; the row execute path simply delegates to the child.

nodes.name: doExecuteColumnar
nodes.summary: Creates a RowToColumnarEvaluatorFactory and applies it to the child row RDD via mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or per-partition evaluators, depending on conf.usePartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: ApplyColumnarRulesAndInsertTransitions
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] that runs the preColumnarTransitions of the given ColumnarRules, inserts RowToColumnarExec and ColumnarToRowExec where adjacent operators disagree on row versus columnar output, and then runs the postColumnarTransitions rules in reverse order. Private helpers ensureOutputsColumnar, ensureOutputsRowBased and insertTransitions walk the plan; planned V1 writes via DataWritingCommandExec are handled specially.

nodes.name: ensureOutputsColumnar
nodes.summary: Makes the plan produce columnar output: wraps a non-columnar plan in RowToColumnarExec over a row-based child, otherwise recurses into the children unless the node is already a RowToColumnarTransition.

nodes.name: ensureOutputsRowBased
nodes.summary: Makes the plan produce row output: adds ColumnarToRowExec over a columnar-only plan, otherwise recurses into the children and decides per node (including DataWritingCommandExec with a V1WriteCommand under planned write) whether the children should output columnar.

nodes.name: insertTransitions
nodes.summary: Dispatches to ensureOutputsColumnar or ensureOutputsRowBased according to the outputsColumnar flag.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Applies each rule preColumnarTransitions, inserts the transitions, then applies each rule postColumnarTransitions in reverse order and returns the resulting plan.

nodes.name: ColumnarEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the two PartitionEvaluatorFactory implementations used by the columnar transition operators: ColumnarToRowEvaluatorFactory (batches to unsafe rows) and RowToColumnarEvaluatorFactory (rows to reusable ColumnarBatch instances). Each factory creates a per-partition evaluator whose eval method does the conversion and updates the SQL metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source file.

nodes.name: ColumnarToRowEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory[ColumnarBatch, InternalRow]; createEvaluator returns a private evaluator that, for every input batch, increments numInputBatches and numOutputRows and lazily iterates the batch rows through an UnsafeProjection built from the child output. Used by ColumnarToRowExec.

nodes.name: ColumnarToRowEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private PartitionEvaluator whose eval asserts a single input iterator and flat-maps each ColumnarBatch to unsafe rows.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeProjection for the child output and returns the flat-mapped row iterator over the input batches while updating the batch and row metrics.

nodes.name: RowToColumnarEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, ColumnarBatch] configured with an off-heap flag, the batch row count, the schema and two metrics. Its evaluator builds a ColumnarBatch of on-heap or off-heap column vectors once per partition and refills it with up to numRows rows per next() call. Used by RowToColumnarExec.

nodes.name: RowToColumnarEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private PartitionEvaluator that returns an iterator of ColumnarBatch, lazily allocating converters, vectors and the batch and closing the batch via a task completion listener.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator that, on each next(), resets the vectors, converts up to numRows input rows with RowToColumnConverter, sets the row count on the shared ColumnarBatch, and updates numInputRows and numOutputBatches.

nodes.name: CommandResultExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CommandResultExec, the leaf physical plan node that holds the already-computed rows of an executed command. Used so that a command result can be returned, collected, taken or shown in EXPLAIN without re-running the command.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source file.

nodes.name: CommandResultExec
nodes.summary: Leaf SparkPlan (also InputRDDCodegen) that stores the command output attributes, the command physical plan (transient, only for displaying the plan tree in EXPLAIN as an inner child) and the result rows (transient, may not be serializable). It lazily converts the rows to unsafe rows, parallelizes them into an RDD (empty RDD if no rows, slices bounded by session.leafNodeDefaultParallelism), and overrides executeCollect, executeToIterator, executeTake and executeTail to return the local rows directly while posting the numOutputRows driver metric.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps the cached RDD of rows, incrementing the numOutputRows metric for each row.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Adds the row count to numOutputRows, sends the driver metrics and returns the local unsafe rows without running a job.

nodes.name: executeTake
nodes.summary: Returns the first limit unsafe rows from the local array, updating numOutputRows and sending driver metrics.

nodes.name: executeTail
nodes.summary: Returns the last limit unsafe rows from the local array, updating numOutputRows and sending driver metrics.

nodes.name: sendDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Reads the SQL execution id from the local properties of the SparkContext (SQLExecution.EXECUTION_ID_KEY) and posts the driver metric updates through SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricUpdates.

nodes.name: EmptyRelationExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines EmptyRelationExec, a leaf physical node used for an empty relation produced by propagating empty relations; it keeps the eliminated logical plan so it can still be shown in the plan tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source file.

nodes.name: EmptyRelationExec
nodes.summary: Leaf SparkPlan (also InputRDDCodegen) wrapping a transient logical plan that was eliminated as an empty relation (the plan may be partially executed, i.e. contain LogicalQueryStage). It returns an empty RDD for row and columnar execution, empty arrays for executeCollect, executeTake and executeTail, appends the wrapped logical plan under itself in generateTreeString, and canonicalizes to a LocalRelation of its output.

nodes.name: generateTreeString
nodes.summary: Calls the parent generateTreeString and then, if the logical plan is present, prints the logical plan as the last child one level deeper.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Copies the node with a logical plan replaced by the canonicalized LocalRelation of its output, so the original logical plan does not affect plan equality.

nodes.name: ExistingRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines logical and physical plan nodes that scan existing RDDs: ExternalRDD and ExternalRDDScanExec for RDDs of arbitrary objects, LogicalRDD and RDDScanExec for RDDs of InternalRow (with optional statistics, constraints, partitioning, ordering and stream), and OneRowRelationExec for queries without a FROM clause.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source file.

nodes.name: ExternalRDD
nodes.summary: Case class (with companion object) that is a logical LeafNode scanning an RDD of objects. The companion apply creates the node with a generated object attribute and wraps it with CatalystSerde.serialize. It is a MultiInstanceRelation (newInstance renews the output attribute) and its computeStats returns the default size in bytes from the session conf.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: builds an ExternalRDD over the RDD using a generated object attribute and returns CatalystSerde.serialize of it using the implicit Encoder.

nodes.name: ExternalRDDScanExec
nodes.summary: Physical leaf node that scans an RDD of objects: doExecute wraps each object into a row with ObjectOperator.wrapObjectToRow while counting numOutputRows. The node name is Scan plus the RDD name.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps the partitions of the RDD, converting each value to a row via ObjectOperator.wrapObjectToRow and incrementing numOutputRows.

nodes.name: LogicalRDD
nodes.summary: Case class (with companion object) that is a logical LeafNode scanning an RDD[InternalRow] with explicit output, partitioning and ordering, optional streaming source, and optional originStats and originConstraints in a second parameter list so rules do not rewrite them. newInstance rewrites attributes in the partitioning, ordering, stats and constraints; computeStats uses the original stats or the default size; constraints drop subquery predicates. The companion offers fromDataset, buildOutputAssocForRewrite, buildOutputAssocForRewriteWithNewOutput, rewriteStatsAndConstraints, rewriteStatistics and rewriteConstraints.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a copy with fresh attribute instances and rewrites the partitioning, ordering, stats and constraints to the new attributes.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Returns originStats if present, otherwise Statistics with the default size in bytes from the session conf.

nodes.name: withStream
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the node with the given SparkDataStream set.

nodes.name: fromDataset
nodes.summary: Companion method that creates a LogicalRDD from an RDD and an origin Dataset, using the first leaf of the executed plan partitioning, its ordering, and statistics and constraints rewritten from the optimized plan.

nodes.name: buildOutputAssocForRewrite
nodes.summary: Builds an attribute map from source to destination output when names and data types match for all columns, otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: buildOutputAssocForRewriteWithNewOutput
nodes.summary: Same as buildOutputAssocForRewrite but compares only data types, so the new output may have different names.

nodes.name: rewriteStatsAndConstraints
nodes.summary: Rewrites the optimized plan stats and constraints to the logical plan output attributes; logs a warning and returns (None, None) when the outputs cannot be matched.

nodes.name: rewriteStatistics
nodes.summary: Returns Statistics with attribute stats keys replaced through the column rewrite map.

nodes.name: rewriteConstraints
nodes.summary: Transforms every constraint expression, replacing attributes through the column rewrite map.

nodes.name: RDDScanExec
nodes.summary: Physical leaf node scanning an RDD[InternalRow]: doExecute converts each row to an UnsafeRow with an UnsafeProjection while counting numOutputRows. It exposes the optional stream, uses a "Scan <name>" node name, and ignores the stream when canonicalizing.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps partitions with index, initializing an UnsafeProjection for the schema and projecting each row while incrementing numOutputRows.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes via the parent and copies the node with stream set to None.

nodes.name: OneRowRelationExec
nodes.summary: Physical leaf node for a OneRowRelation (queries with no FROM clause): it builds a one-partition RDD that yields one empty unsafe row, outputs no attributes and counts numOutputRows. It deliberately does not extend RDDScanExec to avoid TreeNode.makeCopy reflection complexity.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps the single-row RDD, incrementing numOutputRows for each row.

nodes.name: ExpandExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExpandExec, the physical operator that applies several projection lists to each input row, producing multiple output rows per input row, with both interpreted and whole-stage code generation paths.

nodes.name: ExpandExec
nodes.summary: Case class unary exec node taking projections (Seq of expression lists), output attributes and a child. For every input row it emits one row per projection, with unknown partitioning and a numOutputRows metric. doExecute builds UnsafeProjections per partition; doProduce and doConsume generate code with a loop and switch over projection indexes, computing columns that are identical across projections once and splitting large switch-case bodies into methods when code exceeds the method split threshold.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted path: for each partition builds one initialized UnsafeProjection per projection list and, for each input row, emits one projected row per group while incrementing numOutputRows.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Delegates code production to the child, which must support code generation, passing this operator as the consumer.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for the consume side: finds columns with identical expressions across projections, declares output variables, builds a switch-case per projection to fill the varying columns (splitting into helper functions when the code length exceeds the split threshold), then loops over all projections incrementing the output metric and consuming each row.

nodes.name: ExplainMode.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed ExplainMode trait with five case-object modes (simple, extended, codegen, cost, formatted) and a parser from string names. Used to choose what explain output shows for a DataFrame.

nodes.name: ExplainMode
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with a name member for the explain mode; its companion object offers fromString, which lowercases the input and maps it to one of the five modes or throws an IllegalArgumentException listing the accepted names.

nodes.name: SimpleMode
nodes.summary: Case object for the "simple" explain mode. Prints only the physical plan to the console.

nodes.name: ExtendedMode
nodes.summary: Case object for the "extended" explain mode. Prints both logical and physical plans.

nodes.name: CodegenMode
nodes.summary: Case object for the "codegen" explain mode. Prints the physical plan and, if available, the generated code.

nodes.name: CostMode
nodes.summary: Case object for the "cost" explain mode. Prints the logical plan and, if available, plan node statistics.

nodes.name: FormattedMode
nodes.summary: Case object for the "formatted" explain mode. Splits the output into a physical plan outline and node details.

nodes.name: fromString
nodes.summary: Converts a mode name (case-insensitive) to the matching ExplainMode object, else throws IllegalArgumentException naming the accepted modes.

nodes.name: basicPhysicalOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the basic physical plan operators of Spark SQL: ProjectExec, FilterExec, SampleExec, RangeExec, UnionExec, CoalesceExec, and the subquery wrappers BaseSubqueryExec, SubqueryExec and ReusedSubqueryExec. Most of them mix in CodegenSupport so they can take part in whole-stage code generation, and each also has a plain doExecute path that builds RDDs.

nodes.name: ProjectExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for Project. It extends UnaryExecNode with CodegenSupport, SafeForKWayMerge, PartitioningPreservingUnaryExecNode and OrderPreservingUnaryExecNode. The output is projectList turned into attributes. doConsume binds the project expressions to the child output and emits code (with subexpression elimination when the conf allows it) that evaluates them and calls consume. usedInputs keeps only attributes used more than once. doExecute builds a ProjectEvaluatorFactory and runs it with mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal, preserving partition sizes.

nodes.name: usedInputs
nodes.summary: Returns the input attributes that must be evaluated before this operator: only those that appear at least twice in projectList, so other evaluation can be deferred until the output attribute is used.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates the Java code for the consume side of whole-stage codegen: binds projectList to child.output, optionally applies subexpression elimination, evaluates non-deterministic expressions eagerly, and calls consume with the result variables.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution path: creates a ProjectEvaluatorFactory and applies it to the child RDD, through mapPartitionsWithEvaluator if conf.usePartitionEvaluator is set, otherwise through mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal.

nodes.name: GeneratePredicateHelper
nodes.summary: Trait extending PredicateHelper (with a CodegenSupport self type) that generates Java code for filter predicates. generatePredicateCode splits the condition into IsNotNull checks and other predicates, then emits each predicate in order, loading attributes lazily and placing each IsNotNull check before the predicate that needs it so evaluation short-circuits. The method is overloaded: one version takes the condition expression and splits it, the other takes the already split predicate lists. Used by FilterExec.

nodes.name: generatePredicateCode
nodes.summary: Generates the filter predicate code from pre-split notNullPreds and otherPreds. For each other predicate it first emits the matching IsNotNull checks, then the predicate itself, and finally the remaining IsNotNull checks, using 'continue' to skip rows that fail. The overload at lines 132-146 takes only the condition, splits it with splitConjunctivePredicates, and delegates to this version.

nodes.name: FilterExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for Filter. It splits the condition into IsNotNull predicates and other predicates, treats the columns checked by IsNotNull as non-nullable in its output, and keeps child ordering and partitioning. doConsume emits do/while(false) code that counts numOutputRows; when subexpression elimination and the FilterExec-specific subexpression elimination conf are on and a non-cheap common subexpression exists (per CollapseProject.isCheap), it uses a CSE path with ordering invariants, else it falls back to generatePredicateCode. doExecute uses FilterEvaluatorFactory.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates filter code for whole-stage codegen. Chooses between the common-subexpression-elimination path (interleaving IsNotNull checks, CSE state computation and each predicate so short-circuiting is kept) and the plain generatePredicateCode path, resets isNull to false for the not-null columns, wraps the checks in 'do { } while (false)', adds one to numOutputRows and calls consume.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution path: builds a FilterEvaluatorFactory with the condition, child output and numOutputRows metric and applies it per partition, via mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal.

nodes.name: SampleExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for sampling the dataset with lowerBound, upperBound, withReplacement and an optional seed (a random seed is chosen if none is given). doExecute uses PartitionwiseSampledRDD with a PoissonSampler when sampling with replacement, otherwise randomSampleWithRange. doConsume generates code with a PoissonSampler or BernoulliCellSampler held as mutable state, seeded per partition. needCopyResult is true when sampling with replacement.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based sampling: with replacement it wraps the child RDD in a PartitionwiseSampledRDD using a PoissonSampler (gap sampling disabled), without replacement it calls randomSampleWithRange; each emitted row increments numOutputRows.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates sampling code for whole-stage codegen. With replacement it creates a PoissonSampler state initialized per partition index and loops consume that many times per row; without replacement it creates a BernoulliCellSampler seeded with the seed plus the partition index and consumes the row only when sample() is non-zero.

nodes.name: RangeExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for range (generating a range of 64 bit numbers), wrapping a logical Range. It is a LeafExecNode with CodegenSupport. outputPartitioning is SinglePartition, RangePartitioning or UnknownPartitioning(0) depending on numElements and numSlices. doProduce emits batched loops (batch size 1000) with BigInteger-safe partition start and end computation and periodic metric updates. doExecute is the non-codegen path that builds an iterator over UnsafeRows per partition with overflow detection, wrapped in an InterruptibleIterator. An empty range uses EmptyRDD.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Returns SinglePartition for one slice, RangePartitioning over the output ordering for several slices, and UnknownPartitioning(0) when the range has no elements.

nodes.name: inputRDDs
nodes.summary: Returns an EmptyRDD for an empty range, otherwise an RDD of numSlices slice indexes built with sparkContext.parallelize, used as the input of the generated code.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Generates the produce-side Java code. It adds mutable state (initRange, nextIndex, batchEnd, numElementsTodo, TaskContext, InputMetrics), an initRange helper that computes each partition's start and number of elements with BigInteger, and an outer loop over batches with an inner for loop that consumes each value, with optional shouldStop check and limit checks. Metrics are updated at the end of each batch.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Non-codegen execution: for each of numSlices partitions it computes a safe (overflow-clamped) start and end, then iterates numbers by step, detects overflow, updates numOutputRows and input metrics, and returns reused UnsafeRows wrapped in an InterruptibleIterator.

nodes.name: UnionExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for unioning two or more plans without a distinct, which is UNION ALL in SQL; the companion object (lines 1186-1217) holds codegen eligibility helpers. Output attributes get merged nullability and data types. It can keep a known output partitioning when all children agree and UNION_OUTPUT_PARTITIONING is set, using SQLPartitioningAwareUnionRDD; otherwise doExecute calls sparkContext.union. supportCodegen is decided by supportCodegenFailureReason (disabled conf, partitioning-aware, nested union, multi-rdd child, partition-index-dependent child, too many children, columnar, type mismatch). In the fused path unionedInputRDD builds a UnionRDD, doProduce emits a switch over children with a helper method per child, and doConsume projects the child row to the union output through perChildProjections.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes the union output: for each column position it takes the first child's attribute, marks it nullable if any child is nullable, and merges the data types with StructType.unionLikeMerge (rebuilding the AttributeReference if the type changed).

nodes.name: prepareOutputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Returns the children's output partitionings, with the attributes of the other children rewritten to the first child's attributes at the same position, so they can be compared.

nodes.name: comparePartitioning
nodes.summary: Returns true when both partitionings are SinglePartition or are equal hash partitionings; range partitionings are never treated as equal because their bounds may differ.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: When UNION_OUTPUT_PARTITIONING is set and all children have the same partitioning, returns that partitioning mapped to the union's output attributes; otherwise falls back to the default.

nodes.name: supportCodegen
nodes.summary: Returns true when supportCodegenFailureReason (lazy val at lines 979-1000) is empty; otherwise logs the skip reason and returns false. The reasons checked include the union-codegen conf, partitioning-aware unions, nested unions, children with several input RDDs, partition-index-dependent children, WHOLESTAGE_UNION_MAX_CHILDREN, columnar support and type mismatch.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Generates the fused union code: records for each UnionRDD partition its owning child and local index, wraps each child's produced code in its own helper method, rebinds currentPartitionIndexVar to the child-local index, and emits a switch on the child index that calls the right helper. The per-pass state (numOutputRowsTerm, currentEmittingChild) is kept in ThreadLocals.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Called while a child's code is being produced: binds that child's projection to the child output, generates the projection code, adds one to the shared numOutputRows metric and calls consume with the projected expressions.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution: for a plain union calls sparkContext.union on the children's RDDs; for a union with a known partitioning builds an SQLPartitioningAwareUnionRDD from the non-empty child RDDs.

nodes.name: isKnownMultiInputRDDCodegen
nodes.summary: Companion helper: true for codegen operators that return more than one RDD from inputRDDs (SortMergeJoinExec and ShuffledHashJoinExec), which fused union cannot handle.

nodes.name: hasPartitionIndexDependentCodegen
nodes.summary: Companion helper: true if any expression in the plan subtree is Nondeterministic other than InputFileName, InputFileBlockStart and InputFileBlockLength, since such expressions may embed the raw partitionIndex that would be wrong under fused union.

nodes.name: CoalesceExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan that returns exactly numPartitions partitions through a narrow dependency (coalesce without shuffle); if more partitions are requested, the current number stays. Output partitioning is SinglePartition for one partition, else UnknownPartitioning. doExecute returns an empty RDD with one partition when numPartitions is 1 and the child has none, otherwise rdd.coalesce(numPartitions, shuffle = false). The companion object defines EmptyRDDWithPartitions and EmptyPartition.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Coalesces the child RDD to numPartitions without a shuffle, and uses EmptyRDDWithPartitions to avoid returning an RDD with zero partitions while claiming SinglePartition.

nodes.name: EmptyRDDWithPartitions
nodes.summary: Nested class in the CoalesceExec companion: an RDD of InternalRow with no data but the given number of partitions. getPartitions creates EmptyPartition(i) for each index and compute returns an empty iterator.

nodes.name: EmptyPartition
nodes.summary: Nested case class in the CoalesceExec companion: a Partition identified only by its index, used by EmptyRDDWithPartitions.

nodes.name: BaseSubqueryExec
nodes.summary: Abstract parent class for the subquery plans, extending SparkPlan. It declares name and child, passes output, outputPartitioning and outputOrdering through from the child, and overrides generateTreeString so that in EXPLAIN FORMATTED mode (printNodeId true) subquery plans are left out of the main plan tree.

nodes.name: generateTreeString
nodes.summary: Delegates to super.generateTreeString only when printNodeId is false, so subqueries are excluded from the main plan in EXPLAIN FORMATTED and printed separately.

nodes.name: SubqueryExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan for a subquery (companion object at lines 1390-1400). It collects the child's rows on a separate thread through a lazy relationFuture started in doPrepare, with a limit given by maxNumRows, and records the 'dataSize' and 'collectTime' metrics.
