It must be used through executeCollect, which waits for the future; doExecute, executeTake and executeTail throw an internal error. The companion has a daemon thread pool sized by SUBQUERY_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD and createForScalarSubquery, which asks for at most 2 rows.

nodes.name: relationFuture
nodes.summary: Lazy val that runs child.executeCollect (or executeTake(maxNumRows)) in another thread with the SQL execution id and thread-local state captured, measures collect time and data size, posts the driver metric updates, and returns the rows.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Waits for relationFuture with ThreadUtils.awaitResult and returns the collected rows; this is the only supported way to run a SubqueryExec.

nodes.name: createForScalarSubquery
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a SubqueryExec with maxNumRows = Some(2), enough rows to detect a scalar subquery returning more than one row without collecting everything.

nodes.name: ReusedSubqueryExec
nodes.summary: Wrapper for a reused BaseSubqueryExec. It is a LeafExecNode that forwards name, output, ordering, partitioning, canonicalization, prepare, doExecute and executeCollect to the wrapped child, so a subquery that appears twice is computed once.

nodes.name: captured.py
nodes.summary: Converts JVM exceptions raised through Py4J into Python exception classes. Defines CapturedException and one subclass per JVM exception type (AnalysisException, ParseException, IllegalArgumentException and others), the SQLQueryContext and DataFrameQueryContext wrappers, and the helpers convert_exception, capture_sql_exception, unwrap_spark_exception and install_exception_handler that patch py4j get_return_value.
nodes.languageNotes: Each concrete class combines CapturedException with the matching class from pyspark.errors.exceptions.base (imported under a Base prefix) through multiple inheritance.

nodes.name: CapturedException
nodes.summary: Base class of all Python exceptions built from a captured JVM Py4JJavaError. It keeps a description, the JVM stack trace, the converted cause and the original Java error, and answers getCondition, getMessageParameters, getSqlState, getMessage and getQueryContext by asking the JVM PythonErrorUtils when the origin is a SparkThrowable. __str__ appends the JVM stack trace when the SQL conf pysparkJVMStacktraceEnabled is on.

nodes.name: convert_exception
nodes.summary: Converts a Py4JJavaError into the matching Python CapturedException through _convert_exception, then lets recover_python_exception rebuild an original Python exception when one was wrapped.

nodes.name: _convert_exception
nodes.summary: Chooses the Python exception class for a Py4J Java exception by checking the JVM class with is_instance_of in a fixed order (ParseException before AnalysisException, NumberFormatException before IllegalArgumentException), and falls back to UnknownException built from the string form and the stack trace.

nodes.name: capture_sql_exception
nodes.summary: Wraps a callable with a decorator that catches Py4JJavaError, converts it with convert_exception and re-raises the converted exception without the JVM chain, unless the result is an UnknownException (then the original error is re-raised).

nodes.name: unwrap_spark_exception
nodes.summary: Context manager that catches a Py4JJavaError whose Java exception is a SparkException and raises the converted cause instead, unless the cause converts to UnknownException; other errors are re-raised.

nodes.name: install_exception_handler
nodes.summary: Hooks the capture_sql_exception wrapper into py4j by replacing get_return_value in py4j.java_gateway, so JVM errors become Python exceptions with the same message. It is idempotent because it always wraps the original py4j.protocol.get_return_value.

nodes.name: AnalysisException
nodes.summary: Failed to analyze a SQL query plan. Python counterpart of the JVM AnalysisException, produced by _convert_exception.

nodes.name: ParseException
nodes.summary: Failed to parse a SQL command. Subclass of AnalysisException, matching the JVM rule that the parser exception inherits the analysis exception.

nodes.name: IllegalArgumentException
nodes.summary: Passed an illegal or inappropriate argument. Captured form of java.lang.IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryException
nodes.summary: Exception that stopped a streaming query. Captured form of the JVM StreamingQueryException.

nodes.name: QueryExecutionException
nodes.summary: Failed to execute a query. Captured form of the JVM QueryExecutionException.

nodes.name: PythonException
nodes.summary: Exceptions thrown from Python workers. Its __str__ builds the text from the msg and traceback message parameters when both are present, otherwise it falls back to the base string.

nodes.name: ArithmeticException
nodes.summary: Arithmetic exception. Captured form of java.lang.ArithmeticException.

nodes.name: UnsupportedOperationException
nodes.summary: Unsupported operation exception. Captured form of java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
nodes.summary: Array index out of bounds exception. Captured form of java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

nodes.name: DateTimeException
nodes.summary: Datetime exception. Captured form of java.time.DateTimeException.

nodes.name: NumberFormatException
nodes.summary: Number format exception. Subclass of the captured IllegalArgumentException because the JVM NumberFormatException inherits IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: SparkRuntimeException
nodes.summary: Runtime exception. Captured form of the JVM SparkRuntimeException.

nodes.name: SparkUpgradeException
nodes.summary: Exception thrown because of a Spark upgrade. Captured form of the JVM SparkUpgradeException.

nodes.name: SparkNoSuchElementException
nodes.summary: No such element exception. Captured form of the JVM SparkNoSuchElementException.

nodes.name: UnknownException
nodes.summary: None of the other exceptions. Fallback class used by _convert_exception when the JVM exception type is not recognized; its callers re-raise the original Py4J error instead of the converted one.

nodes.name: SQLQueryContext
nodes.summary: Query context of a SQL text error, wrapping a JVM context object. Its methods contextType (always SQL), objectType, objectName, startIndex, stopIndex, fragment, callSite and summary read the corresponding values from the wrapped JVM object.

nodes.name: DataFrameQueryContext
nodes.summary: Query context of a DataFrame API error, wrapping a JVM context object. Its methods contextType (always DataFrame), objectType, objectName, startIndex, stopIndex, fragment, callSite and summary read the corresponding values from the wrapped JVM object.

nodes.name: CapturedException.__init__
nodes.summary: Builds the exception either from a description plus stack trace or from the original Java error (the two forms are mutually exclusive), converts the optional cause with convert_exception, and logs the exception.

nodes.name: CapturedException.__str__
nodes.summary: Returns the description, adding the JVM stacktrace when the SQL conf flag pysparkJVMStacktraceEnabled is on (default true if the conf cannot be read).

nodes.name: CapturedException.getCondition
nodes.summary: Returns the error condition from PythonErrorUtils when the origin is a SparkThrowable, otherwise None.

nodes.name: CapturedException.getErrorClass
nodes.summary: Deprecated alias that warns and returns getCondition().

nodes.name: CapturedException.getMessageParameters
nodes.summary: Returns the error message parameters as a dict from PythonErrorUtils when the origin is a SparkThrowable, otherwise None.

nodes.name: CapturedException.getSqlState
nodes.summary: Returns the SQL state from PythonErrorUtils when the origin is a SparkThrowable, otherwise None.

nodes.name: CapturedException.getMessage
nodes.summary: Formats the error message from the condition and message parameters through the JVM SparkThrowableHelper when the origin is a SparkThrowable, otherwise returns an empty string.

nodes.name: CapturedException.getQueryContext
nodes.summary: Returns the list of query contexts of a SparkThrowable origin, wrapping each JVM context as SQLQueryContext (type SQL) or DataFrameQueryContext.

nodes.name: PythonException.__str__
nodes.summary: Builds the message as msg, a colon and the stripped traceback from the message parameters, or defers to the base __str__ when they are missing.

nodes.name: types.proto
nodes.summary: Protobuf definitions of the Spark Connect DataType message and its nested type messages (boolean, numeric, string, date and time, interval, char, varchar, decimal, struct, array, map, variant, UDT, geometry, geography, unparsed and time types). DataType only describes a type and carries no value.
nodes.languageNotes: Protobuf 3 file in package spark.connect; all type messages are nested inside DataType, selected by its kind oneof.

nodes.name: DataType
nodes.summary: Describes the logical data type of something without carrying a value. The kind oneof selects one of the nested type messages (primitive, string, date and time, interval, complex, UDT, geospatial, unparsed and time types); the nested messages are defined inside it. Oneof kind alternatives: null, binary, boolean, byte, short, integer, long, float, double, decimal, string, char, var_char, date, timestamp, timestamp_ntz, calendar_interval, year_month_interval, day_time_interval, array, struct, map, variant, udt, geometry, geography, unparsed, time.

nodes.name: DataType.Boolean
nodes.summary: Boolean type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Byte
nodes.summary: Byte (tiny integer) type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Short
nodes.summary: Short integer type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Integer
nodes.summary: Integer type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Long
nodes.summary: Long integer type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Float
nodes.summary: Float type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Double
nodes.summary: Double type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.String
nodes.summary: String type, with an optional collation name. Fields: type_variation_reference, collation.

nodes.name: DataType.Binary
nodes.summary: Binary type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.NULL
nodes.summary: Null type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Timestamp
nodes.summary: Timestamp type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Date
nodes.summary: Date type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.TimestampNTZ
nodes.summary: Timestamp without time zone type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Time
nodes.summary: Time type with an optional precision. Fields: precision, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.CalendarInterval
nodes.summary: Calendar interval type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.YearMonthInterval
nodes.summary: Year-month interval type with optional start and end fields. Fields: start_field, end_field, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.DayTimeInterval
nodes.summary: Day-time interval type with optional start and end fields. Fields: start_field, end_field, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Char
nodes.summary: Fixed length character type. Fields: length, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.VarChar
nodes.summary: Variable length character type with a maximum length. Fields: length, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Decimal
nodes.summary: Decimal type with optional scale and precision. Fields: scale, precision, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.StructField
nodes.summary: One field of a struct type: name, DataType, nullability and optional metadata string. Fields: name, data_type, nullable, metadata.

nodes.name: DataType.Struct
nodes.summary: Struct type: a list of StructField. Fields: fields, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Array
nodes.summary: Array type: element DataType and whether elements may be null. Fields: element_type, contains_null, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Map
nodes.summary: Map type: key and value DataType and whether values may be null. Fields: key_type, value_type, value_contains_null, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Geometry
nodes.summary: Geometry type identified by an SRID. Fields: srid, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Geography
nodes.summary: Geography type identified by an SRID. Fields: srid, type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.Variant
nodes.summary: Variant type. Fields: type_variation_reference.

nodes.name: DataType.UDT
nodes.summary: User defined type: type name, optional JVM class (Scala/Java UDT), optional Python class and serialized Python class (Python UDT) and optional underlying sql type. Fields: type, jvm_class, python_class, serialized_python_class, sql_type.

nodes.name: DataType.Unparsed
nodes.summary: Data type given as an unparsed data type string. Fields: data_type_string.

nodes.name: relations.proto
nodes.summary: Protobuf definitions of the Spark Connect relation messages: the Relation container with its large rel_type oneof, and one message per relational operator (read, project, filter, join, set operation, sort, limit, aggregate, sample, range, repartition, rename and column messages, NA and statistic functions, user defined function carriers, as-of, lateral and nearest-by joins, ML relations). Operators reference their input Relation and Expression, DataType, Catalog, Origin and ML messages defined in the other Connect proto files.
nodes.languageNotes: Protobuf 3 file in package spark.connect with java_multiple_files; messages are listed with their nested messages and enums as Outer.Inner classes.

nodes.name: MlRelation
nodes.summary: Relation that represents the ML world: either a Transform (apply a cached model or a new transformer to an input) or a Fetch (read an attribute from a server-side object that yields a relation). Can carry an optional dataset used to restore the model summary. Fields: model_summary_dataset. Oneof ml_type alternatives: transform, fetch.

nodes.name: MlRelation.Transform
nodes.summary: Nested relation that represents transform(input) of an ML operator, where the operator is either an object reference to a cached model or an ML transformer such as VectorAssembler. Carries the input dataframe and the operator specific parameters. Fields: input, params. Oneof operator alternatives: obj_ref, transformer.

nodes.name: Fetch
nodes.summary: Message for fetching an attribute from an object on the server side. It can be a relation (for example model.summary.roc returns a DataFrame) or a ML command (for example model.coefficients returns a literal). Holds an object reference and a chain of method calls. Fields: obj_ref, methods.

nodes.name: Fetch.Method
nodes.summary: One method call in a Fetch chain: the method name and its optional arguments. Fields: method, args.

nodes.name: Fetch.Method.Args
nodes.summary: One argument of a Fetch method call, which is either a literal value or an input relation (args_type oneof). Oneof args_type alternatives: param, input.

nodes.name: Unknown
nodes.summary: Empty relation message used for testing purposes only. Has no fields.

nodes.name: RelationCommon
nodes.summary: Common metadata shared by all relations: a deprecated source_info string, an optional per-client globally unique plan_id for the connect plan, and an Origin that keeps the origin information such as a stack trace. Fields: source_info, plan_id, origin.

nodes.name: SQL
nodes.summary: Relation that uses a SQL query to generate its output. Parameters can be passed as deprecated literal maps or lists (args, pos_args) or as expressions (named_arguments, pos_arguments), and named and positional forms cannot coexist. Fields: query, args, pos_args, named_arguments, pos_arguments.

nodes.name: WithRelations
nodes.summary: Relation holding a root plan and one or more referenced plans that the root plan uses. References are made by name (through a subquery alias) or by plan_id (RelationCommon.plan_id). Can be used to implement CTEs, describe DAGs or reduce tree depth; references must not form cycles. Fields: root, references.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Relation that reads from a file, table or other data source and has no additional inputs. The read_type oneof selects a named table or a data source, and is_streaming marks a streaming read. Fields: is_streaming. Oneof read_type alternatives: named_table, data_source.

nodes.name: Read.NamedTable
nodes.summary: Read of a named table identified by an unparsed identifier, with case-insensitive options. Fields: unparsed_identifier, options.

nodes.name: Read.DataSource
nodes.summary: Read of a data source: optional format (parquet, orc, text, json, csv, avro and so on; the default comes from the SQL conf spark.sql.sources.default), optional DDL or JSON schema, options, file system paths, JDBC partition predicates and an optional user-provided streaming source name used in checkpoint metadata. Fields: format, schema, options, paths, predicates, source_name.

nodes.name: RelationChanges
nodes.summary: Reads Change Data Capture changes for a named table (the changes() API of the batch and streaming readers). CDC specific settings such as startingVersion, endingVersion and deduplicationMode are passed in the options map. Fields: unparsed_identifier, options, is_streaming.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Projection of a bag of expressions over an optional input relation. The input is optional (for example SELECT ABS(-1) has no input) and at least one expression is required. Fields: input, expressions.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.summary: Relation that applies a boolean condition expression to each row of the input relation to produce the output. Fields: input, condition.

nodes.name: Join
nodes.summary: Join of a left and a right relation with an optional join condition, a join type and optional using_columns (the condition and using_columns do not coexist). Also carries an optional JoinDataType used only by joinWith. Fields: left, right, join_condition, join_type, using_columns, join_data_type.

nodes.name: Join.JoinType
nodes.summary: Enum of join types: unspecified, inner, full outer, left outer, right outer, left anti, left semi and cross. Values: JOIN_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, JOIN_TYPE_INNER, JOIN_TYPE_FULL_OUTER, JOIN_TYPE_LEFT_OUTER, JOIN_TYPE_RIGHT_OUTER, JOIN_TYPE_LEFT_ANTI, JOIN_TYPE_LEFT_SEMI, JOIN_TYPE_CROSS.

nodes.name: Join.JoinDataType
nodes.summary: Used by joinWith only: records whether the left and the right side data types are structs. Fields: is_left_struct, is_right_struct.

nodes.name: SetOperation
nodes.summary: Set operation (intersect, union, except) between a left and a right input relation, with optional flags for is_all (keep duplicates), by_name and allow_missing_columns (only UNION supports the last two). Fields: left_input, right_input, set_op_type, is_all, by_name, allow_missing_columns.

nodes.name: SetOperation.SetOpType
nodes.summary: Enum of set operation types: unspecified, intersect, union and except. Values: SET_OP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, SET_OP_TYPE_INTERSECT, SET_OP_TYPE_UNION, SET_OP_TYPE_EXCEPT.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.summary: Relation that limits the number of rows taken from the input relation. Fields: input, limit.

nodes.name: Offset
nodes.summary: Relation that reads rows starting from an offset on the input relation. Fields: input, offset.

nodes.name: Tail
nodes.summary: Relation that fetches a given number of rows from the end of the input relation. Fields: input, limit.

nodes.name: Aggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregation over an input relation: grouping type, grouping expressions, aggregate expressions, an optional pivot and optional grouping sets. It describes how a relational grouped dataset was built. Fields: input, group_type, grouping_expressions, aggregate_expressions, pivot, grouping_sets.

nodes.name: Aggregate.GroupType
nodes.summary: Enum of group types: unspecified, groupby, rollup, cube, pivot and grouping sets. Values: GROUP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GROUP_TYPE_GROUPBY, GROUP_TYPE_ROLLUP, GROUP_TYPE_CUBE, GROUP_TYPE_PIVOT, GROUP_TYPE_GROUPING_SETS.

nodes.name: Aggregate.Pivot
nodes.summary: Pivot specification of an aggregate: the pivot column and the optional literal values that become output columns (if empty, the server runs a job to collect the distinct values). Fields: col, values.

nodes.name: Aggregate.GroupingSets
nodes.summary: One grouping set of an aggregate, expressed as a list of grouping expressions. Fields: grouping_set.

nodes.name: Sort
nodes.summary: Sort of the input relation by a list of sort order expressions, optionally global. Fields: input, order, is_global.

nodes.name: Drop
nodes.summary: Drops columns from the input relation, given either as column expressions or as column names. Fields: input, columns, column_names.

nodes.name: Deduplicate
nodes.summary: Removes duplicate rows of the input relation, based on a list of column names or on all columns (the two options are not used together), optionally within the time range of the watermark. Fields: input, column_names, all_columns_as_keys, within_watermark.

nodes.name: LocalRelation
nodes.summary: Relation holding local data that does not need to be qualified by name. The data is Arrow IPC streaming bytes that contain the schema; an optional DDL or JSON schema string updates column names and types and is required when no data is given. Fields: data, schema.

nodes.name: CachedLocalRelation
nodes.summary: Local relation that has already been cached on the server, identified by the sha-256 hash of the serialized LocalRelation. It does not support local relations over 2GB; the userId and sessionId fields are reserved and removed because the server must always use the active session and user. Fields: hash.

nodes.name: ChunkedCachedLocalRelation
nodes.summary: Cached local relation stored as several chunks: a list of sha-256 hashes, one per cached Arrow IPC batch of LocalRelation.data, and an optional hash of the schema. Fields: dataHashes, schemaHash.

nodes.name: CachedRemoteRelation
nodes.summary: Relation that refers to a remote relation cached on the server by the relation id assigned by the service. Fields: relation_id.

nodes.name: Sample
nodes.summary: Sampling of a fraction of the input relation between a lower and an upper bound, with optional replacement and a seed, plus a deterministic_order flag that is true when randomSplit is used. Fields: input, lower_bound, upper_bound, with_replacement, seed, deterministic_order.

nodes.name: Range
nodes.summary: Relation that generates a sequence of integers from start (default 0) to end with a step, and an optional number of partitions. Fields: start, end, step, num_partitions.

nodes.name: SubqueryAlias
nodes.summary: Gives an alias, with an optional qualifier, to the input relation. Fields: input, alias, qualifier.

nodes.name: Repartition
nodes.summary: Repartitions the input relation into a positive number of partitions, with an optional shuffle flag. Fields: input, num_partitions, shuffle.

nodes.name: ShowString
nodes.summary: Composes the string that represents rows for output by invoking Dataset.showString: number of rows, truncation width and vertical printing. Fields: input, num_rows, truncate, vertical.

nodes.name: HtmlString
nodes.summary: Composes the HTML string that represents rows for output by invoking Dataset.htmlString: number of rows and truncation width. Fields: input, num_rows, truncate.

nodes.name: StatSummary
nodes.summary: Computes specified statistics (count, mean, stddev, min, max, percentiles, count_distinct, approx_count_distinct) for numeric and string columns by invoking Dataset.summary. Fields: input, statistics.

nodes.name: StatDescribe
nodes.summary: Computes basic statistics (count, mean, stddev, min, max) for numeric and string columns; all such columns if none are named. Fields: input, cols.

nodes.name: StatCrosstab
nodes.summary: Computes a pair-wise frequency table (contingency table) of two columns by invoking Dataset.stat.crosstab. Fields: input, col1, col2.

nodes.name: StatCov
nodes.summary: Calculates the sample covariance of two numerical columns by invoking Dataset.stat.cov. Fields: input, col1, col2.

nodes.name: StatCorr
nodes.summary: Calculates the correlation of two columns (only the Pearson coefficient is supported) by invoking Dataset.stat.corr. Fields: input, col1, col2, method.

nodes.name: StatApproxQuantile
nodes.summary: Calculates approximate quantiles of numerical columns for a list of probabilities and a relative error, by invoking Dataset.stat.approxQuantile. Fields: input, cols, probabilities, relative_error.

nodes.name: StatFreqItems
nodes.summary: Finds frequent items for columns, possibly with false positives, with an optional minimum support, by invoking Dataset.stat.freqItems. Fields: input, cols, support.

nodes.name: StatSampleBy
nodes.summary: Returns a stratified sample without replacement based on a sampling fraction for each stratum, with a strata column and a seed. Fields: input, col, fractions, seed.

nodes.name: StatSampleBy.Fraction
nodes.summary: Sampling fraction for one stratum: the stratum literal and the fraction value in [0, 1]. Fields: stratum, fraction.

nodes.name: NAFill
nodes.summary: Replaces null values by invoking Dataset.na.fill: one value for all compatible columns, one value for named columns, or one value per named column. Supported value types are bool, long, double and string. Fields: input, cols, values.

nodes.name: NADrop
nodes.summary: Drops rows containing null values by invoking Dataset.na.drop, with optional columns to consider and an optional minimum number of non-null and non-NaN values required to keep a row. Fields: input, cols, min_non_nulls.

nodes.name: NAReplace
nodes.summary: Replaces old values with new values by invoking Dataset.na.replace, for optional columns and a list of replacements. Fields: input, cols, replacements.

nodes.name: NAReplace.Replacement
nodes.summary: One replacement pair of an NAReplace: the old literal value and the new literal value of the same data type. Fields: old_value, new_value.

nodes.name: ToDF
nodes.summary: Renames all columns of the input relation by a list of new names of the same length. Fields: input, column_names.

nodes.name: WithColumnsRenamed
nodes.summary: Renames columns of the input relation, through a deprecated name-to-name map or through a list of Rename pairs. Fields: input, rename_columns_map, renames.

nodes.name: WithColumnsRenamed.Rename
nodes.summary: One column rename: the existing column name and the new column name. Fields: col_name, new_col_name.

nodes.name: WithColumns
nodes.summary: Adds columns or replaces existing columns of the same name by applying aliased expressions to the input relation; duplicated names in the mapping are an error. Fields: input, aliases.

nodes.name: WithWatermark
nodes.summary: Defines a watermark on the input relation: the event time column name and the delay threshold. Fields: input, event_time, delay_threshold.

nodes.name: Hint
nodes.summary: Applies a named hint with optional parameters over a relation. Join hints include BROADCAST, MERGE, SHUFFLE_HASH and SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL; partitioning hints include COALESCE, REPARTITION and REPARTITION_BY_RANGE. Fields: input, name, parameters.

nodes.name: Unpivot
nodes.summary: Unpivots a DataFrame from wide to long format: id columns, optional value columns, and the names of the variable and value output columns. Fields: input, ids, values, variable_column_name, value_column_name.

nodes.name: Unpivot.Values
nodes.summary: Wrapper holding the list of value expressions to unpivot. Fields: values.

nodes.name: Transpose
nodes.summary: Transposes a DataFrame, switching rows to columns: the values of the index column become the new columns (only a single index column is supported now). Fields: input, index_columns.

nodes.name: UnresolvedTableValuedFunction
nodes.summary: Relation that calls a table valued function by name (or unparsed name for a user defined function) with a list of argument expressions, resolved later on the server. Fields: function_name, arguments.

nodes.name: ToSchema
nodes.summary: Applies a user provided schema (a DataType) to the input relation; the server updates the dataframe with that schema. Fields: input, schema.

nodes.name: RepartitionByExpression
nodes.summary: Repartitions the input relation by partitioning expressions, with an optional positive number of partitions. Fields: input, partition_exprs, num_partitions.

nodes.name: MapPartitions
nodes.summary: Relation for mapPartitions equivalent APIs (mapInPandas, mapInArrow): input relation, a user defined function, and optional barrier mode and resource profile id. Fields: input, func, is_barrier, profile_id.

nodes.name: GroupMap
nodes.summary: Relation for group map APIs (apply, applyInPandas): input, grouping expressions and a user defined function, with optional sorting expressions, initial state input and grouping, map/flatMap-groups-with-state settings (output mode, timeout conf, state schema) and TransformWithState info. Fields: input, grouping_expressions, func, sorting_expressions, initial_input, initial_grouping_expressions, is_map_groups_with_state, output_mode, timeout_conf, state_schema, transform_with_state_info.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInfo
nodes.summary: Additional input parameters of the TransformWithState operator: time mode, optional event time column name and optional output schema (only used for the pandas flavor). Fields: time_mode, event_time_column_name, output_schema.

nodes.name: CoGroupMap
nodes.summary: Relation for the co-group map API (applyInPandas): two input relations with their grouping expressions, a user defined function, and optional sorting expressions for each side. Fields: input, input_grouping_expressions, other, other_grouping_expressions, func, input_sorting_expressions, other_sorting_expressions.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithState
nodes.summary: Relation for applyInPandasWithState: input, grouping expressions, user defined function, output schema, state schema, output mode and timeout conf. Fields: input, grouping_expressions, func, output_schema, state_schema, output_mode, timeout_conf.

nodes.name: CommonInlineUserDefinedTableFunction
nodes.summary: Inline user defined table function: name, determinism flag, argument expressions, and the function type chosen in the oneof (a PythonUDTF). Fields: function_name, deterministic, arguments. Oneof function alternatives: python_udtf.

nodes.name: PythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Python user defined table function: optional return type, eval type, encoded command bytes and the Python version used in the client. Fields: return_type, eval_type, command, python_ver.

nodes.name: CommonInlineUserDefinedDataSource
nodes.summary: Inline user defined data source: a name and the data source type chosen in the oneof (a PythonDataSource). Fields: name. Oneof data_source alternatives: python_data_source.

nodes.name: PythonDataSource
nodes.summary: Python data source: encoded command bytes and the Python version used in the client. Fields: command, python_ver.

nodes.name: CollectMetrics
nodes.summary: Collects arbitrary named metrics from a dataset: input relation, metrics name and a sequence of metric expressions. Fields: input, name, metrics.

nodes.name: Parse
nodes.summary: Parses a single text column of the input relation as CSV, JSON or XML, with an optional schema (inferred if not set) and case-insensitive parser options. Fields: input, format, schema, options.

nodes.name: Parse.ParseFormat
nodes.summary: Enum of text formats for Parse: unspecified, CSV, JSON and XML. Values: PARSE_FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED, PARSE_FORMAT_CSV, PARSE_FORMAT_JSON, PARSE_FORMAT_XML.

nodes.name: AsOfJoin
nodes.summary: As-of join of a left and a right relation: as-of columns on both sides, optional join expression or using_columns, join type, optional tolerance, allow_exact_matches flag and search direction. Fields: left, right, left_as_of, right_as_of, join_expr, using_columns, join_type, tolerance, allow_exact_matches, direction.

nodes.name: LateralJoin
nodes.summary: Lateral join of a left and a right relation with an optional join condition and a Join.JoinType. Fields: left, right, join_condition, join_type.

nodes.name: NearestByJoin
nodes.summary: For each left row, returns up to num_results rows from the right relation ranked by a ranking expression. Join type, mode and direction are strings (as for AsOfJoin) and are validated server side at planning time. Fields: left, right, ranking_expression, num_results, join_type, mode, direction.

nodes.name: Relation
nodes.summary: The main relation message of the Connect protocol: a typed container that holds exactly one explicit relation type (the rel_type oneof) plus shared metadata in RelationCommon. Every new relation type has to be registered in this oneof. Used wherever a plan or an input dataset is described. Fields: common. Oneof rel_type alternatives: read, project, filter, join, set_op, sort, limit, aggregate, sql, local_relation, sample, offset, deduplicate, range, subquery_alias, repartition, to_df, with_columns_renamed, show_string, drop, tail, with_columns, hint, unpivot, to_schema, repartition_by_expression, map_partitions, collect_metrics, parse, group_map, co_group_map, with_watermark, apply_in_pandas_with_state, html_string, cached_local_relation, cached_remote_relation, common_inline_user_defined_table_function, as_of_join, common_inline_user_defined_data_source, with_relations, transpose, unresolved_table_valued_function, lateral_join, chunked_cached_local_relation, relation_changes, nearest_by_join, fill_na, drop_na, replace, summary, crosstab, describe, cov, corr, approx_quantile, freq_items, sample_by, catalog, ml_relation, extension, unknown.

nodes.name: ExplainUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Builds the text of a physical-plan explain: gives every operator a unique id, prints the operator tree with those ids, then a verbose block per operator, then the subqueries and any adaptively optimized out exchanges. Used to produce the explain output of a plan.

nodes.name: ExplainUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton (extends AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper) that renders a physical plan into explain text. Its public entry points are processPlan (assigns operator ids, prints the main plan, then each subquery under a "Subqueries" header and each adaptively optimized out exchange under its own header), getOpId (looks up the id of an operator) and generateFieldString (delegates to QueryPlan). Private helpers generate operator ids bottom-up, collect operators that have an id, set whole-stage codegen id tags, and gather subquery plans. Ids live in a thread-local identity map (localIdMap) that is restored after each call.

nodes.name: processPlanSkippingSubqueries
nodes.summary: For one plan, sets whole-stage codegen ids, appends the operator tree with operator ids, then appends the verbose string of each operator not yet collected. Subqueries are skipped (handled by processPlan); an AnalysisException is appended as text.

nodes.name: processPlan
nodes.summary: Main entry: installs a fresh identity id map, numbers all operators (including those inside subqueries), finds ReusedExchange nodes whose child got no id and numbers those subtrees too, prints the main plan, then prints each subquery (skipping ReusedSubqueryExec) and each adaptively optimized out exchange, and finally restores the previous id map.

nodes.name: generateOperatorIDs
nodes.summary: Walks a plan bottom-up and records an incrementing id for each operator in the id map, skipping WholeStageCodegenExec, InputAdapter and subqueries. Recurses into the executed and initial plans of an AdaptiveSparkPlanExec, the plan of a QueryStageExec and the innerChildren of other plans; collects ReusedExchangeExec nodes. Returns the last id used.

nodes.name: collectOperatorsWithID
nodes.summary: Walks a plan bottom-up and appends every operator that has an id (and has not been collected yet, tracked in a BitSet) to the output buffer, skipping subqueries, WholeStageCodegenExec and InputAdapter and descending into adaptive plans, query stages and innerChildren.

nodes.name: generateWholeStageCodegenIds
nodes.summary: Walks a plan top-down and tags each operator under a WholeStageCodegenExec with that stage's codegen id (QueryPlan.CODEGEN_ID_TAG); InputAdapter resets the id. Descends into adaptive plans, query stages and innerChildren; subqueries are skipped.

nodes.name: generateFieldString
nodes.summary: Public helper that formats a named field and its value for explain output by delegating to QueryPlan.generateFieldString.

nodes.name: getSubqueries
nodes.summary: Collects (hosting SparkPlan, hosting expression, BaseSubqueryExec) tuples for every PlanExpression whose plan is a subquery, recursing into the subquery plan and into adaptive plans and query stages.

nodes.name: getOpId
nodes.summary: Returns the operator id of a plan from the thread-local id map as a string, or "unknown" when the plan has no id.

nodes.name: ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray.scala
nodes.summary: Defines an append-only array of UnsafeRow that stays in an in-memory buffer until a row-count or byte-size threshold is hit, then moves to an UnsafeExternalSorter that can spill to disk. Used by operators that need to buffer rows without sorting them.

nodes.name: ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray
nodes.summary: Append-only row buffer (the companion object at lines 265-267 holds DefaultInitialSizeOfInMemoryBuffer = 128). Rows are copied into an ArrayBuffer until numRowsInMemoryBufferThreshold or sizeInBytesInMemoryBufferThreshold is reached; after that all rows move permanently into an UnsafeExternalSorter created without comparators, which spills after numRowsSpillThreshold or sizeInBytesSpillThreshold. Main methods: add, clear, length, isEmpty, spillSize and generateIterator (from a start index, invalidated by later add or clear calls through a modification counter). An auxiliary constructor takes only the four thresholds and reads the task and environment services.

nodes.name: ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArrayIterator
nodes.summary: Private abstract base for the array iterators. It remembers the modification count seen at creation, exposes isModified and throwExceptionIfModified (closes the iterator and raises a concurrent modification error), and a no-op closeIfNeeded hook.

nodes.name: InMemoryBufferIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over the in-memory ArrayBuffer from a start index; hasNext is false once the array was modified, and next fails if it was modified.

nodes.name: SpillableArrayIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over the UnsafeExternalSorter-backed storage. It reuses one UnsafeRow instance that is pointed at each loaded record, and closes the underlying sorter iterator when it is Closeable.

nodes.name: spillSize
nodes.summary: Returns the total bytes spilled to disk so far: bytes from earlier cleared sorters plus the current sorter's spill size.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Releases the backing storage: cleans up the sorter (after adding its spill size to the running total) or clears the in-memory buffer, resets the counters and bumps the modification count to invalidate iterators.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Appends a row. While below both in-memory thresholds the row is copied into the buffer; otherwise it creates an UnsafeExternalSorter (logging that it reached the spill threshold), moves the buffered rows into it and inserts the new row there. Increments the row and modification counts.

nodes.name: generateIterator
nodes.summary: Creates an iterator starting at a given index (validating it with QueryExecutionErrors) over either the in-memory buffer or the sorter. A no-argument overload (line 207) starts at index 0.

nodes.name: FileRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the FileRelation trait for relations backed by files.

nodes.name: FileRelation
nodes.summary: Interface for relations backed by files. Its single method inputFiles returns the list of url-encoded file paths read when scanning the relation; those paths are what a user gets from inputPaths on a DataFrame that queries the relation.

nodes.name: FilterEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the partition evaluator factory used to apply a filter condition to the rows of one partition while counting output rows.

nodes.name: FilterEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory for row filtering. Constructed from the filter condition, the child output attributes and a numOutputRows metric; createEvaluator returns a FilterPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: FilterPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Nested evaluator whose eval method expects exactly one input iterator, builds a Predicate from the condition and child output, initializes it with the partition index and returns only rows for which the predicate is true, incrementing numOutputRows for each kept row.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Returns a new FilterPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Filters the single input iterator with a freshly created, partition-initialized predicate and counts the rows that pass.

nodes.name: GenerateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical operator that applies a Generator (such as an explode-style expression) to each input row, plus the lazy iterator used to run the generator's terminate step at the end of a partition.

nodes.name: LazyIterator
nodes.summary: Private sealed case class iterator that defers calling a function returning rows until the first hasNext or next. GenerateExec uses it so generator.terminate() runs only after all rows of the partition were consumed.

nodes.name: GenerateExec
nodes.summary: Unary physical operator that applies a Generator to each input row and joins the generated rows with the required child columns, like a flatMap. With outer = true each input row appears at least once, with a null generator row when the generator yields nothing. doExecute runs the interpreted path per partition and converts results to unsafe rows; whole-stage code generation (doProduce, doConsume, codeGenCollection, codeGenIterableOnce, codeGenAccessor) is supported when generator.supportCodegen is true, with loops over array or map data for CollectionGenerator and over an iterator otherwise. Tracks a numOutputRows metric.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted execution: per partition it initializes nondeterministic parts of the bound generator, evaluates the generator on every row, joins output with the (pruned) required child output, handles the outer case with a null row, appends the lazy terminate() output, converts rows with an UnsafeProjection and counts numOutputRows.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Codegen consume step: maps the required child columns to generated input code and emits either collection-based loop code or iterator-based loop code depending on whether the bound generator is a CollectionGenerator.

nodes.name: codeGenCollection
nodes.summary: Generates Java source that loops over the array or map produced by a CollectionGenerator, supporting inline struct arrays, optional position output and the outer case (the index starts at -1 for empty input so the loop runs once), then calls consume for each element.

nodes.name: codeGenIterableOnce
nodes.summary: Generates Java source that iterates over the rows returned by a regular generator expression of array of struct type, with a separate loop shape for outer = true that guarantees one iteration for empty input.

nodes.name: codeGenAccessor
nodes.summary: Generates the code that reads one value (and its null flag) from array data or an internal row at an index, combining extra null checks and returning an ExprCode.

nodes.name: GroupedIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines GroupedIterator, which walks a presorted row iterator and yields each group's key together with a lazy iterator over that group's rows.

nodes.name: GroupedIterator
nodes.summary: Companion object (lines 26-37) and class (lines 68-169). The apply factory returns Iterator.empty for empty input, otherwise a GroupedIterator (its constructor is private; empty input is not handled by the class). The class iterates a presorted InternalRow iterator and returns pairs of the group key row (from a generated unsafe projection) and a lazily built iterator over the group's rows; keys are compared with a generated ordering. Full groups are never materialized, and the previous group's iterator must be consumed before hasNext moves to the next group.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory in the companion object: returns an empty iterator when the input is empty, otherwise wraps the buffered input in a new GroupedIterator.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: True if the next group's iterator is already prepared or fetching one succeeds.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the key projection of the current group together with the iterator over its rows, then clears the stored iterator.

nodes.name: fetchNextGroupIterator
nodes.summary: Skips any unread rows of the current group, detects the first row of the next group by comparing keys with the generated ordering, and creates the next group's iterator; returns false when no rows remain.

nodes.name: createGroupValuesIterator
nodes.summary: Builds the inner iterator over the current group's rows. It peeks the next input row with head and continues only while the key matches the current group, so it never consumes rows of the next group.

nodes.name: HiveResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HiveResult, which runs a physical plan and formats the collected result rows as Hive compatible tab-delimited strings, including nested values, dates, timestamps, intervals and binary.

nodes.name: HiveResult
nodes.summary: Singleton (extends SQLConfHelper) that turns query results into Hive style strings. hiveResultString strips a root CommandResultExec and special-cases DESCRIBE commands (name, type, comment padded to 20 chars), SHOW TABLES and SHOW VIEWS (names only); other plans are collected and each value is formatted with toHiveString and joined by tabs. Also provides getTimeFormatters, getBinaryFormatter (sets BINARY_OUTPUT_STYLE to UTF8 when unset) and the BinaryFormatter type alias. Used by tests and by SparkSQLDriver for command line applications (per its comment).

nodes.name: TimeFormatters
nodes.summary: Case class bundling the date, time and timestamp formatters used while formatting values.

nodes.name: getTimeFormatters
nodes.summary: Creates the DateFormatter, a FractionTimeFormatter and a fraction TimestampFormatter for the session local time zone and returns them as a TimeFormatters.

nodes.name: getBinaryFormatter
nodes.summary: Returns a function formatting byte arrays; if the BINARY_OUTPUT_STYLE setting is empty it first sets it to UTF8 to keep legacy behavior, then uses ToStringBase.getBinaryFormatter.

nodes.name: stripRootCommandResult
nodes.summary: Unwraps a CommandResultExec at the root of a plan and returns its inner plan, otherwise returns the plan unchanged.

nodes.name: hiveResultString
nodes.summary: Executes the plan and returns Hive compatible result lines: DESCRIBE output is padded, SHOW TABLES and SHOW VIEWS return only the name column, and all other results are formatted value by value with toHiveString and tab-joined.

nodes.name: formatDescribeTableOutput
nodes.summary: Formats DESCRIBE rows as name, data type and comment (empty if null), each padded to 20 characters and joined by tabs.

nodes.name: toHiveString
nodes.summary: Public formatter for one (value, DataType) pair: prints NULL (or null when nested) for nulls, tries the type's external formatter from TypeApiOps first, and otherwise falls back to toHiveStringDefault.

nodes.name: toHiveStringDefault
nodes.summary: Default value formatting by data type: booleans, dates, times, timestamps, binary, decimals (plain string), numerics, strings (quoted when nested), calendar and year-month or day-time intervals in Hive style, variants, geometry and geography as EWKT, user-defined types, and arrays, maps (sorted entries) and structs formatted recursively.

nodes.name: InsertSortForLimitAndOffset.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical rule InsertSortForLimitAndOffset. For a GlobalLimitExec that sits on a single-partition ShuffleExchangeExec, it re-adds a local SortExec after the shuffle so that the order of an earlier global sort is kept for LIMIT and OFFSET.

nodes.name: InsertSortForLimitAndOffset
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] gated by SQLConf.ORDERING_AWARE_LIMIT_OFFSET. apply matches GlobalLimitExec over a ShuffleExchangeExec(SinglePartition) whose child has a logical link, finds the ordering of a global SortExec below, then puts a non-global SortExec (and a ProjectExec restoring the original output if needed) on top of the shuffle and sets logical links so AQE re-optimization keeps them.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan: for each GlobalLimitExec over a single-partition shuffle, builds the new SortExec (global = false) and optional ProjectExec on top of the shuffle and rebuilds the limit with it as child; returns the plan unchanged if the config is off.

nodes.name: extractOrderingAndPropagateOrderingColumns
nodes.summary: Walks down through a global SortExec, LocalLimitExec, WholeStageCodegenExec, FilterExec, EvalPythonExec and ProjectExec to find the sort order. When a ProjectExec drops ordering columns it adds the missing columns to its project list so the sort can run after the shuffle. Returns the ordering and the rewritten child, or None.

nodes.name: LocalTableScanExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LocalTableScanExec, the physical leaf operator that scans an in-memory sequence of InternalRow values. It turns the rows into UnsafeRows, serves them through an RDD or directly for collect, take and tail, and reports a numOutputRows metric.

nodes.name: LocalTableScanExec
nodes.summary: Case class LocalTableScanExec(output, rows, stream) extends LeafExecNode with StreamSourceAwareSparkPlan and InputRDDCodegen. It lazily converts rows to UnsafeRows (unsafeRows), builds an RDD with parallelize capped by leafNodeDefaultParallelism (or emptyRDD when empty), counts rows in doExecute, and short-circuits executeCollect, executeTake and executeTail on the driver while posting driver metric updates (sendDriverMetrics). doCanonicalize drops the stream, and getStream returns it.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Returns the lazily built RDD of rows, incrementing the numOutputRows metric for every row.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Adds the row count to numOutputRows, sends driver metrics and returns all unsafe rows without running a job.

nodes.name: executeTake
nodes.summary: Takes the first limit rows from the local unsafe rows, updates numOutputRows and posts driver metrics.

nodes.name: executeTail
nodes.summary: Takes the last limit rows from the local unsafe rows, updates numOutputRows and posts driver metrics.

nodes.name: sendDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Reads the SQL execution id from the SparkContext local property and posts the operator metric values with SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricUpdates.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the plan and clears the stream field so the stream is ignored when comparing plans.

nodes.name: MultiResultExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MultiResultExec, a physical node holding several child plans where only the last child determines the output and the result.

nodes.name: MultiResultExec
nodes.summary: Case class MultiResultExec(children) extends SparkPlan. Its output is the output of the last child (or empty), doExecute executes the last child RDD (or an empty RDD), and withNewChildrenInternal copies the node with new children.

nodes.name: ProjectEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ProjectEvaluatorFactory, a PartitionEvaluatorFactory that evaluates a project list over each partition's rows with an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: ProjectEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Class ProjectEvaluatorFactory(projectList, childOutput) extends PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow]. createEvaluator returns a nested ProjectPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: ProjectPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Nested PartitionEvaluator whose eval asserts a single input iterator, creates an UnsafeProjection from the project list and child output, initializes it with the partition index and maps every input row through it.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Returns a new ProjectPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Builds an UnsafeProjection for the partition, initializes it with the partition index and applies it to each input row.

nodes.name: OptimizeMetadataOnlyQuery.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical rule OptimizeMetadataOnlyQuery, which answers aggregate queries that read only partition columns by replacing the table scan with a LocalRelation of partition values taken from file listing or the catalog.

nodes.name: OptimizeMetadataOnlyQuery
nodes.summary: Case class OptimizeMetadataOnlyQuery(catalog: SessionCatalog) extends Rule[LogicalPlan]. When conf.optimizerMetadataOnly is on, apply rewrites an Aggregate over a PhysicalOperation on a partitioned relation, if only partition attributes are referenced and all aggregates are DISTINCT or Max, Min, First, Last, so the scan becomes a LocalRelation of partition values. It logs a warning that results may be wrong when partition metadata exists but data files are empty. Supports HadoopFsRelation tables (via location.listFiles) and HiveTableRelation tables (via the catalog or already pruned partitions).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rewrites matching Aggregate nodes: checks that project list and filters only reference partition attributes, that every aggregate is distinct or a Max/Min/First/Last, logs a warning, and swaps the scan via replaceTableScanWithPartitionMetadata. Returns the plan unchanged when the config is off.

nodes.name: getPartitionAttrs
nodes.summary: Maps partition column names to the relation output attributes by lower-cased name, throwing cannotFindColumnInRelationOutputError when a column is missing.

nodes.name: replaceTableScanWithPartitionMetadata
nodes.summary: Normalizes partition filters and replaces the relation in the child plan with a LocalRelation of partition values: for HadoopFsRelation it lists files with the filters, for HiveTableRelation it uses pruned partitions or the catalog (listPartitionsByFilter or listPartitions) and casts partition spec values to the column types; any other relation raises an internal error.

nodes.name: PartitionedRelation
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply finds a partitioned LogicalRelationWithTable(HadoopFsRelation) or HiveTableRelation and returns the set of partition attributes together with the relation node, or None.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches partitioned file-source and Hive table relations and returns their partition AttributeSet and the relation.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantProjects.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical rule RemoveRedundantProjects, which drops ProjectExec nodes whose output equals their child output (with ordering checks) to simplify the final physical plan.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantProjects
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] gated by SQLConf.REMOVE_REDUNDANT_PROJECTS_ENABLED. It walks the plan with a requireOrdering flag: a ProjectExec is removed when its output matches the child output (same attribute order when ordering is required, else sorted by exprId, and no tightening of nullability) and its logical link is empty or equal to the child's. Special cases: TakeOrderedAndProjectExec under AQE, BaseAggregateExec in Final or PartialMerge mode, and pass-through nodes (FilterExec, BaseJoinExec, WindowExec, ExpandExec). DataSourceV2ScanExecBase without columnar support keeps its project.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Entry point: returns the plan as is when the config is off, otherwise calls removeProject(plan, true).

nodes.name: removeProject
nodes.summary: Recursive rewrite that removes redundant ProjectExec nodes and keeps the logical link of the child, while choosing the requireOrdering flag passed down for TakeOrderedAndProjectExec, BaseAggregateExec and other nodes.

nodes.name: canPassThrough
nodes.summary: True for FilterExec, BaseJoinExec, WindowExec and ExpandExec, which inherit the ordering requirement from their parent.

nodes.name: checkNullability
nodes.summary: Checks that no project output attribute is non-nullable while the matching child attribute is nullable.

nodes.name: isRedundant
nodes.summary: Decides whether a project equals its child output by exprId (ordered or sorted) plus nullability; returns false for non-columnar DataSourceV2ScanExecBase children, also under a FilterExec.

nodes.name: canRemove
nodes.summary: Allows removal only when the project logical link is empty or equals the child logical link (SPARK-36020), so AQE can map physical nodes to logical ones.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantSorts.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical rule RemoveRedundantSorts, which removes SortExec nodes when the child already provides the required ordering and satisfies the required distribution.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantSorts
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] gated by SQLConf.REMOVE_REDUNDANT_SORTS_ENABLED. removeSorts replaces a SortExec by its child when SortOrder.orderingSatisfies(child.outputOrdering, orders) and the child outputPartitioning satisfies the sort required child distribution, so both local and global sorts can be dropped.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged when the config is off, otherwise calls removeSorts.

nodes.name: removeSorts
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan and replaces each SortExec whose child already satisfies the ordering and the required distribution with that child.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantWindowGroupLimits.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical rule RemoveRedundantWindowGroupLimits, which removes a partial WindowGroupLimitExec under a final one when the partitioning already satisfies the final node distribution.

nodes.name: RemoveRedundantWindowGroupLimits
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] whose apply matches a Final WindowGroupLimitExec over a Partial WindowGroupLimitExec and, if the partial node child outputPartitioning satisfies the outer node required child distribution, rebuilds the outer node directly on that child.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan, dropping the partial WindowGroupLimitExec below a final one when the child partitioning satisfies the final node required distribution.

nodes.name: ReplaceHashWithSortAgg.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical rule ReplaceHashWithSortAgg, which swaps hash-based aggregates for SortAggregateExec when the child is already sorted by the grouping keys.

nodes.name: ReplaceHashWithSortAgg
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] gated by SQLConf.REPLACE_HASH_WITH_SORT_AGG_ENABLED. It converts a HashAggregateExec or ObjectHashAggregateExec with grouping keys to a sort aggregate (toSortAggregate) in two cases: a partial and final pair whose partial child satisfies the required sort order (the pair becomes one Complete-mode SortAggregate), or a single hash aggregate whose child satisfies it. Partial and final aggregates are paired only if the modes match and their logical links have the same result.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged when the config is off, otherwise calls replaceHashAgg.

nodes.name: replaceHashAgg
nodes.summary: transformDown over the plan: for hash-based aggregates with keys, builds the sort aggregate and returns it (merged with a matching partial child as Complete mode, or alone) only when the child outputOrdering satisfies the required child ordering; otherwise keeps the hash aggregate.

nodes.name: isPartialAgg
nodes.summary: Checks that all expressions of one aggregate are Partial, all of the other are Final, and both logical links give sameResult.

nodes.name: isHashBasedAggWithKeys
nodes.summary: True when the aggregate is a HashAggregateExec or ObjectHashAggregateExec with non-empty grouping expressions.

nodes.name: SQLExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLExecution, the object that tags Spark jobs with a SQL execution id, root execution id and query id, posts SparkListenerSQLExecutionStart and End events around a query, and propagates SQL configs, session job tags and thread-local state to other threads. Also holds SQLExecutionThreadLocalCaptured, a case class that restores captured thread locals on another thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object with by-name block parameters (body: => T) used as scoped wrappers.

nodes.name: SQLExecutionThreadLocalCaptured
nodes.summary: Case class holding the SparkSession, a cloned set of SparkContext local properties and the JobArtifactState captured on an originating thread. Its runWith method applies them on another thread, runs a block, then restores the original active session and local properties. Created by SQLExecution.captureThreadLocals.

nodes.name: runWith
nodes.summary: Runs the given body with the captured active job artifact state, active session and local properties applied (and session tags via SQLExecution.withSessionTagsApplied), then puts back the previous local properties and active session, or clears the active session if there was none.

nodes.name: SQLExecution
nodes.summary: Object (extends Logging) that connects Spark jobs to SQL executions. It defines the keys spark.sql.execution.id, spark.sql.execution.root.id and spark.sql.execution.query.id, hands out execution ids from an AtomicLong, and keeps a map from execution id to QueryExecution. Main methods: withNewExecutionId and withNewExecutionIdOnError start an execution, post start and end events, clean up shuffles and observations; withExecutionId reuses a known id on another thread; withSQLConfPropagated copies SQL confs into job local properties; withSessionTagsApplied adds session job tags; captureThreadLocals and withThreadLocalCaptured forward thread locals to an executor service.

nodes.name: checkSQLExecutionId
nodes.summary: In tests only, throws an internal error if the SparkContext has no spark.sql.execution.id local property, meaning an action started a query without calling withNewExecutionId.

nodes.name: extractShuffleIds
nodes.summary: Returns the shuffle ids of a physical plan: for an AdaptiveSparkPlanExec the keys of its context shuffleIds, otherwise the shuffleId of every ShuffleExchangeLike node found by collect.

nodes.name: withNewExecutionId0
nodes.summary: Core wrapper that runs a body (a Right function or a Left error) as a new SQL execution. It sets the execution id, query id and root execution id local properties, builds the description and redacted modified configs, posts SparkListenerSQLExecutionStart (with SparkPlanInfo and the explain string), runs the body, then in finally removes shuffle files or skips migration according to shuffleCleanupMode, posts SparkListenerSQLExecutionEnd with duration and error message, cleans up DAGScheduler query jobs, completes observations and restores the old local properties.

nodes.name: withNewExecutionId
nodes.summary: Public entry point that runs a by-name body as a new SQL execution for the given QueryExecution, with an optional execution name, by delegating to withNewExecutionId0 with a Right function.

nodes.name: withNewExecutionIdOnError
nodes.summary: Posts the execution start event for a QueryExecution and rethrows the given Throwable, by calling withNewExecutionId0 with a Left error, so that failures before execution still show up as an execution.

nodes.name: withExecutionId
nodes.summary: Runs a body with a known execution id string set as the spark.sql.execution.id local property (restored afterwards), with SQL confs and session tags applied, so jobs on another thread are linked to the original execution, for example in broadcast exchange futures.

nodes.name: withSessionTagsApplied
nodes.summary: Adds the session managed job tags and the session job tag to the SparkContext for the duration of a block and removes them afterwards.

nodes.name: withSQLConfPropagated
nodes.summary: Copies every SQL conf whose key starts with "spark" into SparkContext local properties so that executors can see them, runs the body, and restores the original local property values in finally.

nodes.name: captureThreadLocals
nodes.summary: Creates a SQLExecutionThreadLocalCaptured from the session, a clone of the SparkContext local properties and the current JobArtifactState (or the session artifact manager state when none is set).

nodes.name: withThreadLocalCaptured
nodes.summary: Captures thread locals on the calling thread and runs the body on the given ExecutorService through CompletableFuture.supplyAsync, applying the captured state with runWith.

nodes.name: SQLExecutionRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLExecutionRDD, an RDD wrapper that captures the SQLConf at creation time and re-applies it while computing a partition when no tracked SQL execution is active.

nodes.name: SQLExecutionRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[InternalRow] that wraps a sqlRDD and takes a snapshot of the SQLConf (getAllConfs). It reuses the parent partitioner and partitions. In compute, if the task has no spark.sql.execution.id local property it rebuilds a SQLConf from the snapshot and runs the parent iterator inside SQLConf.withExistingConf; otherwise it simply returns the parent iterator. Configs set after creation of the RDD and before its execution are missed.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the partitions of the first parent RDD unchanged.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Computes a partition: when the task has no SQL execution id local property it runs the parent iterator with the captured SQLConf applied through SQLConf.withExistingConf, otherwise it calls the parent iterator directly.

nodes.name: SafeForKWayMerge.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the marker trait SafeForKWayMerge for execution nodes that can be used with SortedMergeCoalescedRDD.

nodes.name: SafeForKWayMerge
nodes.summary: Marker trait with no members. Execution nodes that implement it promise to keep no per-partition mutable state in shared plan-node fields, with all per-partition state captured inside the partition iterator closure (for example through the PartitionEvaluatorFactory pattern), so they are safe for the concurrent k-way merge in SortedMergeCoalescedRDD.

nodes.name: ScanFileListing.scala
nodes.summary: Declares ScanFileListing, the trait that represents selected and dynamically selected partitions during file listing, together with the ListingPartition case class used when iterating them.

nodes.name: ListingPartition
nodes.summary: Case class holding the partition values (InternalRow), the number of files and an iterator of FileStatusWithMetadata for one listed partition. Returned by ScanFileListing.filePartitionIterator.

nodes.name: ScanFileListing
nodes.summary: Trait that defines the contract for a representation of selected partitions during file listing, placed at the package root so other packages can use it. It declares partitionCount, totalFileSize, totalNumberOfFiles, filterAndPruneFiles (static predicate then dynamic file filters), toPartitionArray (Array[PartitionedFile]), calculateTotalPartitionBytes, filePartitionIterator (lazy iterator over ListingPartition) and bucketsContainSingleFile.

nodes.name: filterAndPruneFiles
nodes.summary: Abstract method that filters partitions with a bound static predicate and then prunes files of the surviving partitions with the dynamic file filters, returning a new ScanFileListing.

nodes.name: SortPrefixUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SortPrefixUtils, helpers that choose prefix comparators and build prefix computers for sort orders, used to speed up sorting on a fixed-size sort prefix.

nodes.name: SortPrefixUtils
nodes.summary: Object with helpers for prefix-based sorting. getPrefixComparator picks a PrefixComparator for a SortOrder by data type, direction and null ordering (string, binary, long-like types, double-like types, otherwise a no-op comparator); an overload builds one for the first field of a StructType. canSortFullyWithPrefix says whether a key can be fully sorted with a radix sort on the prefix. createPrefixGenerator builds an UnsafeExternalRowSorter.PrefixComputer for the first schema field.

nodes.name: NoOpPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Private object extending PrefixComparator whose compare always returns 0, used when no prefix comparison can be generated for a SortOrder.

nodes.name: getPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Returns the PrefixComparator for a SortOrder based on its data type: string, binary, long-like types (boolean, integral, date, timestamp, time, interval, small decimals), double-like types (float, double, large decimals), otherwise the no-op comparator. An overload at lines 111-118 does the same for the first field of a StructType in ascending order.

nodes.name: stringPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Private helper that picks the string PrefixComparator variant from PrefixComparators for the sort direction (ascending or descending) and null ordering (nulls first or last) of a SortOrder.

nodes.name: binaryPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Private helper that picks the binary PrefixComparator variant from PrefixComparators for the sort direction (ascending or descending) and null ordering (nulls first or last) of a SortOrder.

nodes.name: longPrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Private helper that picks the long PrefixComparator variant from PrefixComparators for the sort direction (ascending or descending) and null ordering (nulls first or last) of a SortOrder.

nodes.name: doublePrefixComparator
nodes.summary: Private helper that picks the double PrefixComparator variant from PrefixComparators for the sort direction (ascending or descending) and null ordering (nulls first or last) of a SortOrder.

nodes.name: canSortFullyWithPrefix
nodes.summary: Returns true when a SortOrder data type (boolean, integral, date, timestamp, time, float, double, interval, or decimal that fits in a long) can be fully sorted by a radix sort on the prefix. An overload at lines 139-141 accepts a StructField.

nodes.name: createPrefixGenerator
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeExternalRowSorter.PrefixComputer for the first field of a schema: it projects a SortPrefix of the bound reference and writes the null flag and long value into a reusable Prefix object. Returns a function giving an empty prefix when the schema is empty.

nodes.name: SparkPlanInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkPlanInfo, the DeveloperApi class that stores node name, simple string, children, metadata and metrics of a SQL plan, plus its private companion that converts a SparkPlan (or LogicalPlan) tree into SparkPlanInfo.

nodes.name: SparkPlanInfo
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi class (lines 34-52) with nodeName, simpleString, children, metadata and metrics (Seq of SQLMetricInfo); equality compares nodeName, simpleString and children, and hashCode uses simpleString. The private[execution] companion object (lines 54-105) holds fromSparkPlan, fromLogicalPlan and the lazy EMPTY instance. It is used when SQLExecution posts the execution start event.

nodes.name: fromLogicalPlan
nodes.summary: Private companion method that converts a LogicalPlan into a SparkPlanInfo. Children come from the physical plan of a LogicalQueryStage, the wrapped plan of an EmptyRelation, or the plan children plus subqueries; metadata and metrics are left empty.

nodes.name: fromSparkPlan
nodes.summary: Converts a SparkPlan tree into a SparkPlanInfo tree. It looks through ReusedExchangeExec, ReusedSubqueryExec, AdaptiveSparkPlanExec (executed plan), QueryStageExec, InMemoryTableScanExec (cached plan) and EmptyRelationExec, builds SQLMetricInfo entries from the node metrics, adds file scan metadata for FileSourceScanLike, and recurses into SparkPlan or LogicalPlan children.

nodes.name: SparkScriptTransformationExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkScriptTransformationExec, the physical operator that pipes input rows through an external script process, and its writer thread SparkScriptTransformationWriterThread.

nodes.name: SparkScriptTransformationExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator (extends BaseScriptTransformationExec) that transforms its child output by forking and running a script. processIterator starts the process with initProc, projects input rows with an InterpretedProjection, starts a SparkScriptTransformationWriterThread to feed the process input stream, and returns an output iterator that reads the script output and checks for failures. withNewChildInternal copies the node with a new child.

nodes.name: processIterator
nodes.summary: Runs the script for one partition: launches the process, builds the input projection, starts a writer thread that writes the projected rows to the process, and returns the iterator over the process output created by createOutputIteratorWithoutSerde.

nodes.name: SparkScriptTransformationWriterThread
nodes.summary: Case class extending BaseScriptTransformationWriterThread that writes the input rows to the script process output stream. Its processRows simply calls processRowsWithoutSerde, so rows are written without a serde.

nodes.name: StreamSourceAwareSparkPlan.scala
nodes.summary: Declares StreamSourceAwareSparkPlan, a mixin trait for physical source nodes that expose the stream they read.

nodes.name: StreamSourceAwareSparkPlan
nodes.summary: Trait extending SparkPlan, mixed into physical source nodes created from source logical nodes that inherit StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan. Its single method getStream returns Option[SparkDataStream]; implementers should report numOutputRows in their metrics.

nodes.name: SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec, the non-executable intermediate physical plan for dynamic partition pruning subquery filters when adaptive execution and DPP are both enabled.

nodes.name: SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec
nodes.summary: Case class (BaseSubqueryExec with UnaryExecNode) holding name, indices, onlyInBroadcast, the transient build logical plan, buildKeys and child. It stores the initial physical plan of DPP subquery filters; doExecute always throws an unsupported-code-path error. After the build side runs, the node is replaced by SubqueryBroadcastExec with the child optimized to use the build side ReusedExchange. doCanonicalize normalizes buildKeys against the child output and renames the node "dpp".

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Always throws QueryExecutionErrors.executeCodePathUnsupportedError("SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec"), because the node is only an intermediate plan.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the node by normalizing the build keys against the child output with QueryPlan.normalizeExpressions, setting the name to "dpp" and canonicalizing the child.

nodes.name: SubqueryBroadcastExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan SubqueryBroadcastExec, which collects the join key values from the build side of a broadcast join and returns them as rows for an in-subquery based filter. A companion object holds the thread pool used to wait for the broadcast.

nodes.name: SubqueryBroadcastExec
nodes.summary: Case class (with companion object) that executes a custom subquery over the BroadcastExchange or broadcast query stage of the build side of a join. In a background future it fetches the broadcast HashedRelation, extracts the requested key columns (by bit operations for a LongHashedRelation, otherwise by BoundReference), projects them to UnsafeRows, de-duplicates them if keys are not unique, and records collectTime, numOutputRows and dataSize metrics. It is only used together with InSubqueryExec; doExecute is unsupported and executeCollect awaits the future. The companion object owns the daemon thread pool named dynamicpruning, sized by BROADCAST_EXCHANGE_MAX_THREAD_THRESHOLD.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Builds the output attributes, one AttributeReference per requested index, named after the build key (or key_<idx> when the key is not a named expression), so that InSubqueryExec can tell single-column from multi-column mode.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Returns a canonical copy named dpp with the build keys normalized against the child output and the child canonicalized.

nodes.name: relationFuture
nodes.summary: Lazy transient future that runs on the dynamicpruning thread pool: it captures the SQL execution id, executes the child broadcast to get the HashedRelation, extracts and projects the key expressions, de-duplicates non-unique keys, updates the metrics and posts driver metric updates.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Blocks on relationFuture with an infinite duration and returns the collected key rows; this is how InSubqueryExec obtains the broadcast keys.

nodes.name: limit.scala
nodes.summary: Physical operators for LIMIT, OFFSET, TAIL and top-K: the LimitExec trait, CollectLimitExec, CollectTailExec, the BaseLimitExec trait (with code generation), LocalLimitExec, GlobalLimitExec and TakeOrderedAndProjectExec. They take a bounded number of rows per partition or globally, often via a shuffle to a single partition.

nodes.name: LimitExec
nodes.summary: Trait for unary physical operators that take a limited number of rows from the child; declares the abstract limit value.

nodes.name: CollectLimitExec
nodes.summary: Takes the first limit rows, collects them to a single partition and drops the first offset rows. Used when a logical Limit or Offset is the final operator, i.e. results are being collected to the driver. executeCollect uses executeTake or executeCollect on the child; doExecute locally limits partitions, shuffles to SinglePartition with an UnsafeRowSerializer and applies slice, take or drop.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Collects on the driver: executeTake(limit) on the child (then drop offset) when a limit is set, otherwise executeCollect().drop(offset).

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds the RDD: empty single partition if the child has no partitions or limit is 0; otherwise locally takes limit rows per partition, shuffles them to a single partition through ShuffleExchangeExec.prepareShuffleDependency and ShuffledRowRDD, then applies slice(offset, limit), take(limit) or drop(offset).

nodes.name: CollectTailExec
nodes.summary: Takes the last limit rows and collects them to a single partition. Used when a logical Tail is the final operator and results go back to the driver. executeCollect calls child.executeTail; doExecute keeps the last rows per partition via takeRight, shuffles to SinglePartition and applies takeRight again.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds the RDD for tail: empty for no partitions or limit 0, otherwise applies takeRight per partition, shuffles to a single partition, and applies takeRight again.

nodes.name: takeRight
nodes.summary: Keeps only the last limit rows of an iterator using a HybridRowQueue (rows are copied as UnsafeRows, the oldest removed once the count reaches limit) and registers a task completion listener to close the queue.

nodes.name: BaseLimitExec
nodes.summary: Trait (with companion object BaseLimitExec that hands out unique counter names such as _limit_counter_<id>) shared by LocalLimitExec and GlobalLimitExec.
