It passes through child output, partitioning and ordering, executes by taking limit rows per partition, and supports whole-stage code generation by adding a counter mutable state, a limitNotReachedChecks condition and an if-check in doConsume.

nodes.name: newLimitCountTerm
nodes.summary: Companion object method returning a fresh counter variable name _limit_counter_<n> from a shared AtomicInteger.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Registers the limit counter as an inlined Java int mutable state in the codegen context and asks the child to produce rows into this operator.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that increments the counter and consumes the row only while the counter is below limit.

nodes.name: LocalLimitExec
nodes.summary: Takes the first limit rows of each child partition without collecting or shuffling them.

nodes.name: GlobalLimitExec
nodes.summary: Takes the first limit rows and then drops the first offset rows of the child's single output partition; requires AllTuples distribution. Overrides doExecute with slice or drop when offset > 0, and doConsume with a skip counter (rowsSkipped) plus the limit counter in generated code.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: With offset > 0 applies slice(offset, limit) or drop(offset) per partition; otherwise defers to BaseLimitExec.doExecute.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: With offset > 0 generates code that first skips offset rows (rowsSkipped counter) and then consumes up to limit - offset rows; otherwise defers to BaseLimitExec.doConsume.

nodes.name: TakeOrderedAndProjectExec
nodes.summary: Takes the first limit rows by the given sortOrder, drops offset rows and projects projectList; logically a Limit/Offset after a SortExec (optionally with a ProjectExec in between). executeCollect uses takeOrdered with a LazilyGeneratedOrdering; doExecute computes local top-K per partition (skipping the sort when the child ordering already satisfies sortOrder), shuffles to a single partition and applies the final top-K, offset and projection.

nodes.name: executeCollect
nodes.summary: Driver-side path: takes the top limit rows with takeOrdered, using a per-partition take when the child ordering already satisfies sortOrder, drops offset and projects with an UnsafeProjection if projectList differs from the child output.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds the RDD: computes local top-K per partition (take or Utils.takeOrdered), shuffles to SinglePartition, then applies final takeOrdered, offset drop and optional projection per partition.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Returns the one-line plan description TakeOrderedAndProject(limit=..., offset=..., orderBy=[...], output=[...]) with truncated lists.

nodes.name: objects.scala
nodes.summary: Physical operators that work on user-defined objects (typed Dataset operations): object producer and consumer traits, DeserializeToObjectExec, SerializeFromObjectExec, ObjectOperator helpers, map and group-map operators, append-column operators, R based operators (dapply, gapply, with and without Arrow) and CoGroupExec.

nodes.name: ObjectProducerExec
nodes.summary: Trait for physical operators that output a single object field (outputObjAttr); defines output, producedAttributes and outputObjectType. Physical version of ObjectProducer.

nodes.name: ObjectConsumerExec
nodes.summary: Trait for unary physical operators whose child outputs exactly one object column (asserted); exposes inputObjectType and mixes in ReferenceAllColumns. Physical version of ObjectConsumer.

nodes.name: DeserializeToObjectExec
nodes.summary: Turns each child row into an object using the deserializer expression; the output is a single-field safe row holding the object. Supports whole-stage code generation (doConsume binds the deserializer to the child output) and an interpreted path using GenerateSafeProjection.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generated-code path: binds the deserializer to the child output, generates its code and passes the resulting object variable to the parent.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted path: per partition, generates a safe projection from the deserializer and maps each input row through it.

nodes.name: SerializeFromObjectExec
nodes.summary: Takes the input object from the child (a single-field row) and turns it into an unsafe row using the serializer expressions; output is the serializer attributes. Supports whole-stage code generation and an interpreted path with UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generated-code path: binds each serializer expression to the child output and consumes the resulting variables.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted path: per partition, creates an UnsafeProjection from the serializer and maps each row through it.

nodes.name: ObjectOperator
nodes.summary: Object with helper functions used by operators that work with user-defined objects: deserializeRowToObject (two overloads), serializeObjectToRow, wrapObjectToRow (object to a one-field InternalRow) and unwrapObjectFromRow (read field 0 of a row).

nodes.name: deserializeRowToObject
nodes.summary: Returns a function InternalRow => Any that uses a generated safe projection of the deserializer (with an input schema; the overload without a schema is at lines 155-158) and reads field 0.

nodes.name: serializeObjectToRow
nodes.summary: Returns a function Any => UnsafeRow that stores the object in a one-field SpecificInternalRow and applies a generated unsafe projection of the serializer expressions.

nodes.name: wrapObjectToRow
nodes.summary: Returns a function that writes an object into a reused one-field SpecificInternalRow of the given type.

nodes.name: unwrapObjectFromRow
nodes.summary: Returns a function that reads field 0 of an InternalRow with the given object type.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsExec
nodes.summary: Applies a user function to the iterator of input objects of each partition; child must output a single object field. Unwraps rows to objects, runs func and wraps the results back.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: unwraps input rows to objects with ObjectOperator.unwrapObjectFromRow, applies func to the iterator and wraps outputs with ObjectOperator.wrapObjectToRow.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsInRWithArrowExec
nodes.summary: Runs an R function over partitions using Arrow record batches in both directions. Input rows are batched with BatchIterator (arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch), sent through an ArrowRRunner in DATAFRAME_DAPPLY mode, and returned columnar batches are checked against the expected output types (an arrowDataTypeMismatchError is thrown for dapply()) and converted to rows. The source calls it similar to MapPartitionsExec and ArrowEvalPythonExec.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: batches the input iterator, runs ArrowRRunner.compute, validates the data types of every returned batch against the output schema and projects the rows with an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: MapElementsExec
nodes.summary: Applies a function (a MapFunction or a Scala function) to each input object; child outputs a single object field. A safe analogue of ProjectExec because the output is a custom object. In code generation it builds an Invoke on the function object; in the interpreted path it calls the function per row.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Generated-code path: chooses the function class and method name (MapFunction.call or via FunctionUtils.getFunctionOneName), wraps func in a Literal and an Invoke expression, binds it and consumes the result.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted path: resolves func to Any => Any and applies it to each unwrapped input object, wrapping the result into an output row.

nodes.name: AppendColumnsExec
nodes.summary: Applies a function to each input row (deserialized by the deserializer) and appends the encoded result as new columns at the end of the row, joined with GenerateUnsafeRowJoiner.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: deserializes each row, applies func, serializes the result to an unsafe row and joins it to the original row with an UnsafeRowJoiner.

nodes.name: AppendColumnsWithObjectExec
nodes.summary: Optimized version of AppendColumnsExec that works directly on the deserialized object from the child; it serializes both the original object (inputSerializer) and the function result (newColumnsSerializer) and joins them.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: unwraps the child object, applies func, serializes input object and new columns separately and joins the two unsafe rows.

nodes.name: MapGroupsExec
nodes.summary: Groups input rows by groupingAttributes and calls func with each key and an iterator over the group's values (sorted by dataOrder if given); results are flattened. Requires ClusteredDistribution on the grouping attributes and ascending sort on them. The companion object apply builds an instance from a function that also takes a LogicalGroupState, creating a batch GroupStateImpl with the given timeout and whether an event-time watermark is present.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: groups rows with GroupedIterator, deserializes key and values, calls func and wraps each result into an output row.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: wraps a function taking a LogicalGroupState into a two-argument function by supplying GroupStateImpl.createForBatch(timeoutConf, watermarkPresent), where watermarkPresent is true if any child output attribute has the event-time watermark delay metadata key.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInRExec
nodes.summary: Groups input rows by key and calls an R function with each group (gapply on the R side), flattening the results. Rows are converted to R bytes, executed by an RRunner in DATAFRAME_GAPPLY mode, and the output bytes are converted back to rows or kept as serialized R data when outputSchema equals SERIALIZED_R_DATA_SCHEMA.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Chooses the R serialization format from outputSchema, then per partition groups rows, converts keys and rows to R bytes, runs RRunner.compute, and converts the returned bytes back to rows (or wraps raw bytes).

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInRWithArrowExec
nodes.summary: Arrow variant of FlatMapGroupsInRExec: groups rows, sends them as Arrow record batches through an ArrowRRunner (DATAFRAME_GAPPLY) that additionally writes the serialized group keys, and validates returned batch types (arrowDataTypeMismatchError for gapply()). Source comments describe the step-by-step JVM and R exchange, and relate it to FlatMapGroupsInPandasExec.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Per partition: groups rows and records each key as R bytes, runs an ArrowRRunner subclass that overrides bufferedWrite to also write the keys, then validates batch data types and projects rows to the output.

nodes.name: CoGroupExec
nodes.summary: Co-groups the left and right children by key and calls func with the key and two iterators of group elements; results are flattened. Requires ClusteredDistribution on each side and sorting by group attributes plus leftOrder/rightOrder; doExecute zips partitions and uses GroupedIterator and CoGroupedIterator.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Zips left and right partitions, groups each side with GroupedIterator, merges groups by key with CoGroupedIterator, deserializes key and both sides, calls func and wraps results.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object file for org.apache.spark.sql.execution; the package object has no members and only carries the scaladoc describing the physical execution component of Spark SQL as a private package whose classes are internal API.

nodes.name: execution
nodes.summary: Empty package object execution whose documentation states that it is the physical execution component of Spark SQL, a private package whose classes are internal API subject to change between minor releases.

nodes.name: subquery.scala
nodes.summary: Physical (executable) subquery expressions: ExecSubqueryExpression base class, ScalarSubquery and InSubqueryExec, plus the PlanSubqueries rule that turns logical scalar and IN subqueries inside a SparkPlan into these physical expressions backed by SubqueryExec plans.

nodes.name: ExecSubqueryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract base class (with companion object) for subquery expressions that live in a SparkPlan and hold a BaseSubqueryExec plan. Declares updateResult to fill the expression with the collected result of the executed plan, and withNewPlan. The companion hasSubquery tests whether an expression tree contains any ExecSubqueryExpression.

nodes.name: hasSubquery
nodes.summary: Companion helper: returns true when the expression tree contains an ExecSubqueryExpression.

nodes.name: ScalarSubquery
nodes.summary: Physical copy of the scalar subquery: a subquery returning one row and one column. updateResult runs plan.executeCollect, fails with multipleRowScalarSubqueryError if more than one row comes back, stores the first column of the single row (or null when no rows) and marks the expression updated. eval returns the stored value; code generation and toLiteral turn the result into a Literal.

nodes.name: updateResult
nodes.summary: Collects the subquery plan, raises multipleRowScalarSubqueryError for more than one row, asserts a single field, stores the value (null if no row) and sets the updated flag.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Returns the stored scalar result after requiring that updateResult has run.

nodes.name: doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates code by converting the finished result to a Literal and delegating to Literal.doGenCode.

nodes.name: toLiteral
nodes.summary: Builds a Literal of the subquery data type from the stored result, requiring that the subquery has finished.

nodes.name: InSubqueryExec
nodes.summary: Physical node of an IN subquery. updateResult collects the plan, keeping the rows themselves for multi-column plans or the first column otherwise, and broadcasts the result unless isDynamicPruning (the pruning case happens on the driver, so no broadcast). eval and doGenCode first call prepareResult (loading the broadcast value if needed) and delegate to an InSet built from the result; values() exposes the raw result for pruning.

nodes.name: updateResult
nodes.summary: Collects the subquery plan; stores all rows for multi-column output or the first column converted to the child data type, and broadcasts the result through the session SparkContext when not used for dynamic pruning.

nodes.name: prepareResult
nodes.summary: Requires that a result or broadcast exists and restores the result from the broadcast value when the local result is null.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Calls prepareResult and evaluates the InSet predicate on the input row.

nodes.name: doGenCode
nodes.summary: Calls prepareResult and delegates code generation to the InSet predicate.

nodes.name: PlanSubqueries
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] that finds logical ScalarSubquery and InSubquery (ListQuery) expressions in a plan (pruned by SCALAR_SUBQUERY and IN_SUBQUERY patterns) and replaces them with physical ScalarSubquery over SubqueryExec.createForScalarSubquery, or InSubqueryExec over SubqueryExec with isDynamicPruning = false. Multi-value IN keys are wrapped in a named struct with fields col_<index>. Subquery plans are prepared with QueryExecution.prepareExecutedPlan.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms all expressions of the plan: logical scalar subqueries become physical ScalarSubquery over a SubqueryExec of the prepared executed plan; IN subqueries become InSubqueryExec (single value, or named struct for multiple values) over a SubqueryExec.

nodes.name: UnionLoopExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the UnionLoopExec physical operator that executes a recursive CTE written with UNION ALL by repeatedly running the recursive term against the previous iteration result.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class extending a leaf physical node; uses a driver-side while loop that builds a new logical plan per iteration.

nodes.name: UnionLoopExec
nodes.summary: Leaf physical node for recursion (only UNION ALL is supported). Takes a loopId, a transient anchor plan, a transient recursion plan, output attributes, and optional limit and maxDepth. Exposes the metrics numOutputRows, numIterations and numAnchorOutputRows, runs the anchor first, then substitutes each UnionLoopRef with the previous iteration result and runs the recursion until it yields no rows, the limit is reached, or the level or row limit from the config is exceeded (errors RECURSION_LEVEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and RECURSION_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). Also overrides innerChildren, doCanonicalize and verboseStringWithOperatorId. Used when the planner turns a recursive CTE (UnionLoop) into a physical plan.

nodes.name: executeAndCacheAndCount
nodes.summary: Executes a plan (wrapped in a LocalLimit when a limit is set) as a Dataset and returns the resulting dataframe with its row count. Small results are converted to a LocalRelation (anchor row limit config) so later iterations can be folded in the optimizer; otherwise the result is repartitioned and materialized.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Main recursion loop: runs the anchor, then repeatedly rewrites the recursion plan (re-seeding non-deterministic expressions and replacing UnionLoopRef nodes with the previous result), enforces level and row limits, updates metrics, and finally unions all iteration plans, coalesces them to the anchor partition count and returns the RDD.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the node by also canonicalizing the anchor and recursion plans.

nodes.name: verboseStringWithOperatorId
nodes.summary: Builds the verbose explain string showing the loop id, output attributes and limit.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the shuffle serializer for UnsafeRow records: rows are already bytes, so they are written as a 4-byte length followed by the row bytes and read back into a single reused UnsafeRow.
nodes.languageNotes: The serializer instance builds anonymous SerializationStream and DeserializationStream subclasses inline.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for UnsafeRows used during shuffle, parameterized by the number of fields and an optional data size SQLMetric. newInstance returns an UnsafeRowSerializerInstance and supportsRelocationOfSerializedObjects is true.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowSerializerInstance
nodes.summary: Private serializer instance that implements only the methods used by shuffle. serializeStream writes length-prefixed row bytes and adds row sizes to the data size metric; deserializeStream reads rows into a reused byte buffer and UnsafeRow (asKeyValueIterator, readValue, readKey returns a dummy). serialize, deserialize, writeAll, writeObject, readObject and asIterator throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeRowSerializerInstance for the configured field count and data size metric.

nodes.name: serializeStream
nodes.summary: Returns a SerializationStream over a buffered DataOutputStream; writeValue records the row size in the metric and writes the size followed by the row bytes, writeKey only asserts the key is null or an Int.

nodes.name: deserializeStream
nodes.summary: Returns a DeserializationStream whose asKeyValueIterator and readValue read length-prefixed rows into a growing buffer and point a single reused UnsafeRow at it, releasing the buffers after the last row.

nodes.name: WholeStageCodegenEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the partition evaluator factory used by whole-stage codegen: it compiles the generated source and iterates the generated BufferedRowIterator for each partition.

nodes.name: WholeStageCodegenEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory for InternalRow input and output. Holds the generated code (broadcast or direct), a duration SQLMetric and the references array, and createEvaluator returns a WholeStageCodegenPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: WholeStageCodegenPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Inner PartitionEvaluator whose eval compiles the cleaned source, builds a BufferedRowIterator, initializes it with the partition index and input iterators, and wraps it in an iterator that adds the generated code duration to the metric when exhausted.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Creates a new WholeStageCodegenPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Resolves the source (from the broadcast or directly), compiles it with CodeGenerator.compile, generates a BufferedRowIterator, initializes it for the partition and returns an iterator that updates durationMs at the end.

nodes.name: AnalyzeColumnCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ANALYZE ... FOR COLUMNS command that gathers column-level statistics for a table, temp view or cached view and stores them in the catalog.

nodes.name: AnalyzeColumnCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command taking a table identifier, optional column names and an allColumns flag (exactly one of the two must be given). run dispatches on the identifier: global temp views and temp views are analyzed through the cache manager (error if not cached), catalog tables compute row count and column stats and write new CatalogStatistics via alterTableStats, and catalog views are only supported if cached. Column types are checked by supportsType (integral, decimal, double, float, boolean, datetime, binary, string; char and varchar are rejected).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates the arguments and routes to temp view or catalog analysis based on the table identifier and global temp database; returns no rows.

nodes.name: analyzeColumnInCachedData
nodes.summary: Looks up the cached data for a plan and asks the cache manager to analyze the selected columns of the cached query; returns whether cached data was found.

nodes.name: analyzeColumnInTempView
nodes.summary: Analyzes a temp view through its cached data, throwing a compilation error if the view is not cached.

nodes.name: getColumnsToAnalyze
nodes.summary: Resolves the requested column names (or all output attributes) against a relation using the configured resolver and rejects columns whose types do not support statistics.

nodes.name: analyzeColumnInCatalog
nodes.summary: Analyzes a catalog table: computes size, row count and column stats through CommandUtils, merges them over existing stats and writes them back; for views it falls back to cached-data analysis.

nodes.name: supportsType
nodes.summary: Returns true when column statistics can be gathered for the given data type.

nodes.name: AnalyzePartitionCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ANALYZE ... PARTITION command that computes per-partition statistics (size, and optionally row count) and updates the metastore.

nodes.name: AnalyzePartitionCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command with a table identifier, a partition spec (partition column to optional value) and a noscan flag (default true, only size is computed). run rejects views, lists the matching partitions, optionally counts rows per partition via CommandUtils, computes new partition stats and calls alterPartitions on the catalog when they changed. An empty spec means all partitions; an unknown partition or a spec that is not a prefix of the partition columns raises an error.

nodes.name: getPartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Normalizes the user partition spec against the table partition schema, checks that specified columns form a prefix of the partition columns, and returns only the specified values (None when empty).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Resolves the table, lists partitions matching the spec, computes row counts (unless noscan) and per-partition stats, and writes changed partitions back to the catalog.

nodes.name: AnalyzeTableCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ANALYZE TABLE command that computes table-level statistics by delegating to CommandUtils.

nodes.name: AnalyzeTableCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command with a table identifier and a noScan flag (default true); run calls CommandUtils.analyzeTable and returns no rows.

nodes.name: AnalyzeTablesCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the command that analyzes every table in a database to generate statistics, logging a warning for tables that fail.

nodes.name: AnalyzeTablesCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command with an optional database name (current database by default) and a noScan flag. run lists the tables of the database and calls CommandUtils.analyzeTable for each one, catching non-fatal errors and logging a warning with the table, database and error.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Iterates over the tables of the target database and analyzes each, logging a warning instead of failing when one table cannot be analyzed.

nodes.name: CommandCheck.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CommandCheck, an analyzer-side check over logical plans that validates execution commands.

nodes.name: CommandCheck
nodes.summary: Object that is a function from LogicalPlan to Unit and mixes in SQLConfHelper. apply walks the plan and, for each AnalyzeColumnCommand with explicit column names, checks the names for duplicates using the case sensitivity setting.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Traverses the plan and rejects duplicate column names in AnalyzeColumnCommand column lists via SchemaUtils.checkColumnNameDuplication.

nodes.name: CommandUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds CommandUtils, a set of helpers shared by table-level commands: computing table and partition sizes on the file system, building column statistics (including optional equi-height histograms) with aggregate queries, analyzing a table, and uncaching or recaching tables and views. It also defines PathFilterIgnoreNonData, a path filter that skips staging directories and non-data files when summing sizes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object with many small helpers; several private methods build Catalyst aggregate expressions for column statistics.

nodes.name: PathFilterIgnoreNonData
nodes.summary: A serializable Hadoop PathFilter whose accept method rejects any file whose name starts with the given staging directory name or that is not a data file according to DataSourceUtils.isDataFile. It is used when listing leaf files to compute total directory sizes in parallel.

nodes.name: CommandUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object (with Logging) used by commands that change data or compute statistics. Main methods: updateTableStats refreshes or clears catalog statistics after a data change; calculateTotalSize and calculatePartitionStats sum file sizes per table or partition; analyzeTable implements ANALYZE TABLE for tables and cached views; computeColumnStats runs an Aggregate query to produce ColumnStat values (ndv, min, max, null count, lengths, optional histogram); uncacheTableOrView and recacheTableOrView keep the cache manager consistent; calculateRowCountsPerPartition counts rows per partition.

nodes.name: updateTableStats
nodes.summary: Called after a command changes table data. If automatic size update is enabled it recomputes the total size and partition stats and alters the catalog statistics only when they changed; otherwise it clears existing stats or refreshes the table relation cache.

nodes.name: calculateTotalSize
nodes.summary: Returns the total size of a table and the partitions whose stats changed. For an unpartitioned table it sums the table location; for a partitioned table it delegates to calculatePartitionStats over the listed partitions, and it logs the time taken.

nodes.name: calculatePartitionStats
nodes.summary: Computes the sizes of all given partition locations and, with optional per-partition row counts, builds updated partitions whose statistics differ from the old ones using compareAndGetNewStats. Returns the summed size and the changed partitions.

nodes.name: calculateSingleLocationSize
nodes.summary: Sums the size of all data files below one table location by recursively listing the file system, skipping Hive staging directories (config hive.exec.stagingdir, default .hive-staging). Failures are logged as warnings and give size 0.

nodes.name: calculateMultipleLocationSizes
nodes.summary: Computes sizes of several locations, either in a Spark job via calculateMultipleLocationSizesInParallel when the parallel file listing setting is on, or one by one with calculateSingleLocationSize.

nodes.name: calculateMultipleLocationSizesInParallel
nodes.summary: Launches a job through InMemoryFileIndex.bulkListLeafFiles to list leaf files of the defined paths with a PathFilterIgnoreNonData filter, then returns a size per input path (0 for undefined paths).

nodes.name: compareAndGetNewStats
nodes.summary: Compares old catalog statistics with a new total size and row count and returns new CatalogStatistics only if something changed; row count is only recorded when it was computed and differs.

nodes.name: analyzeTable
nodes.summary: Implements the work of ANALYZE TABLE: for a view it only works when the view is cached (counts it unless noScan) and otherwise raises an error; for a table it computes total size, optional partition row counts and table row count, and writes new table and partition stats to the catalog.

nodes.name: computeColumnStats
nodes.summary: Computes the row count and a ColumnStat per column by running one Aggregate query (executedPlan.executeTake) over the relation, using percentiles first when histograms are enabled. Private to the sql package.

nodes.name: computePercentiles
nodes.summary: Runs an ApproximatePercentile aggregate for each histogram-capable column when histograms are enabled, and returns an AttributeMap of percentile arrays used as bin boundaries for equi-height histograms.

nodes.name: supportsHistogram
nodes.summary: Returns true for integral, decimal, double, float and datetime column types, the types for which a histogram can be gathered.

nodes.name: statExprs
nodes.summary: Builds the CreateNamedStruct expression that computes distinct count, min, max, null count, average length, max length and interval ndvs for one column; string and binary columns skip min, max and histogram, and unsupported types raise an error. Must stay in sync with rowToColumnStat.

nodes.name: rowToColumnStat
nodes.summary: Converts the struct row produced by statExprs back into a ColumnStat, and builds an equi-height Histogram from the interval ndvs and percentile endpoints when they are present.

nodes.name: isDataPath
nodes.summary: Private check that a path is not under the staging directory and is a data path according to DataSourceUtils.isDataPath.

nodes.name: uncacheTableOrView
nodes.summary: Uncaches a table or view. Overloads: one takes a ResolvedIdentifier, one a TableIdentifier (both cascade), one a LogicalPlan plus cascade flag (this widest one is the node range), and a private one taking name parts that calls CacheManager.uncacheTableOrView. A DSv2 relation without time travel is uncached by name, other plans by plan via uncacheQuery.

nodes.name: recacheTableOrView
nodes.summary: Recaches entries that reference a relation: by name for a DSv2 relation without time travel (CacheManager.recacheTableOrView), otherwise by plan (CacheManager.recacheByPlan).

nodes.name: calculateRowCountsPerPartition
nodes.summary: Counts rows per partition by filtering the table with an optional partition spec, grouping by partition columns and collecting the counts. Null partition values map to the default partition name.

nodes.name: CreateSQLFunctionCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateSQLFunctionCommand, the DDL command behind CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMPORARY] FUNCTION for SQL scalar and table functions. When run it parses the parameters and RETURNS clause, validates and analyzes the function body, derives determinism and SQL data access, and registers the function as a temporary function or stores it in the catalog.
nodes.languageNotes: Large case class command; the run method is a single long method of about 230 lines.

nodes.name: CreateSQLFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Case class (a CreateUserDefinedFunctionCommand) with the parsed pieces of a CREATE FUNCTION statement: name, input parameter text, return type text, expression or query text, comment, collation, determinism, CONTAINS SQL flag, table function flag, temp, ignoreIfExists and replace. run builds a SQLFunction, builds an input plan from the parameters (including default values), analyzes the scalar body or the table body (via a LateralJoin), checks it, and then registers or creates the function. Private helpers check cyclic references, aggregate/window/generator use, temporary object references, SQL data access and generate stored properties.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes the command: parses parameters and return type, builds the SQLFunction, builds the input plan, analyzes a scalar (Project) or table (LateralJoin) body, runs the validation checks, infers the return type if none is declared, verifies temp objects, generates properties, derives determinism and CONTAINS SQL, then registers a temp function or drops (when replacing) and creates a persistent one in the catalog. Returns an empty Seq.

nodes.name: checkFunctionBodyAnalysis
nodes.summary: Runs the analyzer's checkAnalysis on a SQLFunctionNode wrapping the function and its body to verify the body can be analyzed.

nodes.name: checkFunctionSignatures
nodes.summary: When replacing an existing function, checks via lookupFunctionInfo that it is a SQL function, and otherwise throws CANNOT_REPLACE_NON_SQL_UDF_WITH_SQL_UDF.

nodes.name: collectTemporaryObjectsInUnresolvedPlan
nodes.summary: Walks the unresolved plan (including CTEs and subquery expressions) and returns the temporary view names and temporary function names it references.

nodes.name: verifyTemporaryObjectsNotExists
nodes.summary: For a non-temporary function, throws an error if the body references a temp view, temp function or temp variable (found with ViewHelper.collectTemporaryVariables).

nodes.name: checkCyclicFunctionReference
nodes.summary: Follows references from the plan to other SQL scalar and table functions (through subqueries and expressions) and raises cyclicFunctionReference when the chain leads back to the function being created.

nodes.name: checkAggOrWindowOrGeneratorExpr
nodes.summary: Throws CANNOT_CONTAIN_COMPLEX_FUNCTIONS if the resolved body contains window, generator or aggregate expressions.

nodes.name: deriveSQLDataAccess
nodes.summary: Determines whether the body reads SQL data (views, real relations, or nested functions declared as reading data) and throws INVALID_SQL_FUNCTION_DATA_ACCESS if the function was declared CONTAINS SQL but reads data. Returns whether it reads SQL data.

nodes.name: generateFunctionProperties
nodes.summary: Builds the property map stored with the function: SQL configs captured at creation, current catalog and namespace, names of referred temp views/functions/variables, and the serialized resolution path from CatalogManager.pathEntriesForPersistence.

nodes.name: CreateUserDefinedFunctionCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract base class CreateUserDefinedFunctionCommand and its companion object. The companion's apply factory picks the concrete command for a routine language (only SQL is supported, giving CreateSQLFunctionCommand) and the object holds shared validation helpers for parameter names, RETURNS column names, trailing defaults and NOT NULL.

nodes.name: CreateUserDefinedFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Abstract class extending LeafRunnableCommand with CapturesConfig, the base type of CREATE FUNCTION commands (class at lines 31-32, companion object at 35-175). The companion apply builds a CreateSQLFunctionCommand for LanguageSQL and throws unsupportedUserDefinedFunction for any other language; checkParameterNameDuplication, checkReturnsColumnDuplication, checkDefaultsTrailing and checkParameterNotNull are the fail-early checks used while registering a function.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that asserts the language is not null and returns a CreateSQLFunctionCommand for LanguageSQL; any other routine language raises unsupportedUserDefinedFunction.

nodes.name: checkParameterNameDuplication
nodes.summary: Fails early if the input parameter names contain duplicates (case-insensitive unless case-sensitive analysis is on), reporting the duplicated names.

nodes.name: checkReturnsColumnDuplication
nodes.summary: Fails if the RETURNS TABLE columns contain duplicate names, using the same case rule as the parameter check.

nodes.name: checkDefaultsTrailing
nodes.summary: Checks that once a parameter has a default value all later parameters also have one, otherwise throws NOT_A_VALID_DEFAULT_PARAMETER_POSITION.

nodes.name: checkParameterNotNull
nodes.summary: Throws if any parameter or returned column is declared NOT NULL, which is not allowed for function parameters.

nodes.name: DataWritingCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataWritingCommand trait, a Command that writes data out and exposes write metrics, and its companion object with helpers: output attribute renaming, metric propagation between commands, and a check that a CTAS target directory is empty.

nodes.name: DataWritingCommand
nodes.summary: Trait (a UnaryCommand with CTEInChildren) for commands that write the output of an analyzed query plan. It makes the query the child, exposes outputColumnNames and outputColumns, provides lazy write metrics taken from BasicWriteJobStatsTracker, a basicWriteJobStatsTracker factory, and an abstract run(sparkSession, child: SparkPlan). The companion object has logicalPlanOutputWithNames, propogateMetrics (copies metrics from an inner write command and posts driver metric updates) and assertEmptyRootPath (CTAS must not target a non-empty directory unless allowed by config).

nodes.name: basicWriteJobStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Wraps a Hadoop Configuration in a SerializableConfiguration and returns a BasicWriteJobStatsTracker bound to this command's metrics.

nodes.name: logicalPlanOutputWithNames
nodes.summary: Returns the query's output attributes renamed with the provided names; asserts both lists have equal length.

nodes.name: propogateMetrics
nodes.summary: Copies metric values from a write command to the metrics of the command that triggered it (used for CTAS) and posts driver metric updates for the current SQL execution id. The name is spelled 'propogateMetrics' in the source.

nodes.name: assertEmptyRootPath
nodes.summary: For SaveMode.ErrorIfExists, throws createTableAsSelectWithNonEmptyDirectoryError if the table path is a non-empty directory and allowNonEmptyLocationInCTAS is off.

nodes.name: DescribeProcedureCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DescribeProcedureCommand, the runnable command behind the SQL statement DESC PROCEDURE procedure_name. It turns a resolved procedure into formatted text rows.

nodes.name: DescribeProcedureCommand
nodes.summary: Case class command that implements DESC PROCEDURE. Its run method matches the child plan against ResolvedProcedure with an UnboundProcedure (any other child raises an internal error) and calls describeV2Procedure, which builds a list of key/value pairs for 'Procedure:', 'Description:' and, for a SimpleProcedure, a 'Parameters:' block (or '()' when there are none). Parameter lines show mode, name, data type, optional DEFAULT and optional comment, padded into aligned columns by formatProcedureParameters and tabulate. The single output column is procedure_desc (a non-null string).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes DESC PROCEDURE: if the child is a ResolvedProcedure holding an UnboundProcedure it returns the described rows, otherwise it throws SparkException.internalError with the child class name.

nodes.name: describeV2Procedure
nodes.summary: Builds the description rows: procedure name, description and, for SimpleProcedure, the formatted parameter list; keys are padded to the same width and joined with the values into one Row per line.

nodes.name: formatProcedureParameters
nodes.summary: Formats each ProcedureParameter as mode, name, data type SQL string, optional DEFAULT value and optional quoted comment, padding mode, name and type columns to the longest entry.

nodes.name: tabulate
nodes.summary: Pads every input string to the length of the longest one so that keys line up in the output.

nodes.name: DescribeRelationJsonCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DescribeRelationJsonCommand, the runnable command for DESCRIBE ... AS JSON. It renders table, view, column, clustering, bucket, storage and partition metadata as a single JSON string row.

nodes.name: DescribeRelationJsonCommand
nodes.summary: Case class command for DESCRIBE ... AS JSON, with a single non-null string output column json_metadata. run matches the child plan: a ResolvedTempView (partition spec not allowed, identifier under system.session), a ResolvedPersistentView (converted to a CatalogTable through V1View or V1Table.toCatalogTable, also adds the view creation SQL configs), or a ResolvedTable with V1Table (adds columns, clustering info and either partition info or formatted table info). Anything else raises describeAsJsonNotSupportedForV2TablesError. Results go into a LinkedHashMap of JValue through addKeyValueToMap, which lower-cases and underscores keys, renames inputformat/outputformat, formats created_time and last_access as UTC timestamps, and skips duplicate or excluded keys (catalog, schema, database, table). A default 'collation' of UTF8_BINARY is added last and the map is rendered with json4s compact(render(...)). jsonType converts a DataType recursively into JSON with extra fields for array, map, struct, decimal, varchar, char, timestamp_ltz, intervals and string collation.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the resolved child (temp view, persistent view or V1 table), fills the ordered JSON map through the describe* helpers, appends the default collation and returns one Row holding the compact JSON text.

nodes.name: addKeyValueToMap
nodes.summary: Adds a key/value pair to the JSON map after normalizing the key (lower case, spaces to underscores, renames for input_format and output_format), formatting created_time and last_access epoch values as UTC strings, and ignoring keys already present or in the excluded set.

nodes.name: describeIdentifier
nodes.summary: Writes table_name, catalog_name, namespace and (when a namespace exists) schema_name entries from the qualified name parts.

nodes.name: jsonType
nodes.summary: Recursively converts a DataType to its JSON description, adding element_nullable, key/value types, struct fields with comments and defaults, decimal precision and scale, char and varchar length, timestamp_ltz, interval start and end units and string collation.

nodes.name: describeColsJson
nodes.summary: Builds the columns entry by running jsonType on the schema as a struct and extracting its fields array.

nodes.name: describeViewSqlConfsJson
nodes.summary: Adds view_creation_spark_configuration, a JSON object with the SQL configs saved when the view was created.

nodes.name: describeClusteringInfoJson
nodes.summary: For tables with a clusterBySpec, adds clustering_columns as quoted dotted names after asserting each column exists in the table schema.

nodes.name: describeFormattedTableInfoJson
nodes.summary: Adds bucket spec, storage format and general table information (each through its toJsonLinkedHashMap) to the JSON map.

nodes.name: describePartitionInfoJson
nodes.summary: Handles DESCRIBE with a PARTITION clause: rejects views, verifies the partition provider is hive, normalizes the partition spec, fetches the partition from the session catalog and adds partition, table, bucket and storage details (partition details first so they win for duplicate keys).

nodes.name: InsertIntoDataSourceDirCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines InsertIntoDataSourceDirCommand, the command that writes a query result to a directory for INSERT OVERWRITE DIRECTORY ... USING format.

nodes.name: InsertIntoDataSourceDirCommand
nodes.summary: Case class command (storage, provider, query, overwrite) used for INSERT OVERWRITE DIRECTORY with USING format OPTIONS. run asserts that a directory path and a provider are present, builds a DataSource with the storage properties plus a path option, requires that the provider class is a FileFormat (otherwise throws onlySupportDataSourcesProvidingFileFormatError), picks SaveMode.Overwrite or ErrorIfExists, executes dataSource.planForWriting on the query and logs and rethrows AnalysisException failures. It also implements withCTEDefs by wrapping the query in WithCTE.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates the directory and provider, creates the DataSource, checks it is a file format, then plans and executes the write of the query with the chosen SaveMode and returns no rows.

nodes.name: cache.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ClearCacheCommand, the command that removes all cached data from the in-memory cache.

nodes.name: ClearCacheCommand
nodes.summary: Case object leaf command that clears all cached data by calling sparkSession.catalog.clearCache() in run and returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls sparkSession.catalog.clearCache() and returns an empty Row sequence.

nodes.name: commands.scala
nodes.summary: Core command abstractions of the SQL execution layer: the RunnableCommand traits, the physical ExecutedCommandExec and DataWritingCommandExec operators that run commands once, the EXPLAIN commands, and ExternalCommandExecutor for running a string command on an external runner.

nodes.name: RunnableCommand
nodes.summary: Trait for a logical command executed for its side effects. It has no children, holds a lazy metrics map of SQLMetric (empty by default) that is handed to ExecutedCommandExec, and declares run(sparkSession): Seq[Row].

nodes.name: LeafRunnableCommand
nodes.summary: Trait combining RunnableCommand with LeafLike for commands without child plans.

nodes.name: UnaryRunnableCommand
nodes.summary: Trait combining RunnableCommand with UnaryLike for commands that have exactly one child plan.

nodes.name: ExecutedCommandExec
nodes.summary: Physical leaf operator that runs a RunnableCommand. Its lazy sideEffectResult calls cmd.run once, converts the Rows to InternalRows with a Catalyst converter, and all execute variants (executeCollect, executeToIterator, executeTake, executeTail, doExecute via a one-partition parallelize) read that cached result so the command is never run twice. It shares the command's metrics and uses 'Execute ' + cmd.nodeName as its node name.

nodes.name: DataWritingCommandExec
nodes.summary: Physical unary operator that runs a DataWritingCommand against its child SparkPlan. Like ExecutedCommandExec it caches the converted result of cmd.run(session, child) in sideEffectResult and serves collect, take, tail and doExecute from it; it reuses the command's metrics, output and argString and implements withNewChildInternal by copying with a new child.

nodes.name: ExplainCommand
nodes.summary: Case class for EXPLAIN (EXTENDED | CODEGEN | COST | FORMATTED) on a logical plan, with a single nullable string column plan. run stages the plan (replacing ExecutableDuringAnalysis nodes via stageForExplain), builds a QueryExecution with CommandExecutionMode.SKIP and returns qe.explainString(mode); on a non-fatal error it returns the message 'Error occurred during query planning' split into rows. It optimizes the plan but does not execute it, and implements SupervisingCommand through withTransformedSupervisedPlan.

nodes.name: StreamingExplainCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf command that explains how a streaming batch is executed. It holds an IncrementalExecution and returns its full toString when extended is true, otherwise its simpleString, with the same error-to-rows fallback as ExplainCommand.

nodes.name: ExternalCommandExecutor
nodes.summary: Command that runs an arbitrary string command inside an external execution engine through an ExternalCommandRunner and returns its lines in one column command_output. The case class wraps (runner, command, options); its companion object apply looks up the runner by name through DataSource.lookupDataSource and instantiates it if it is an ExternalCommandRunner, otherwise throws commandExecutionInRunnerUnsupportedError. The companion object shares this node.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Stages the logical plan for explain, creates a QueryExecution with CommandExecutionMode.SKIP and returns its explainString for the requested mode as one Row; planning errors are returned as rows of text.

nodes.name: stageForAnalysis
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan, replacing every ExecutableDuringAnalysis node with its stageForExplain form so explain does not execute it.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Returns the IncrementalExecution text (full toString when extended, else simpleString) as one Row, with errors returned as text rows.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Runs the command on the external runner with the options as a CaseInsensitiveStringMap and returns the resulting lines.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: finds the data source class named runner, creates an instance if it is an ExternalCommandRunner and wraps it in an ExternalCommandExecutor, otherwise throws commandExecutionInRunnerUnsupportedError.

nodes.name: createDataSourceTables.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateDataSourceTableCommand and CreateDataSourceTableAsSelectCommand, the commands that create data source tables (with or without a query result) and register them in the session catalog.

nodes.name: CreateDataSourceTableCommand
nodes.summary: Case class command (table, ignoreIfExists) for CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] ... USING format OPTIONS (...). run returns early or fails when the table already exists, then resolves a relation from the DataSource (without checking files exist, honoring the FILE_SOURCE_INSERT_ENFORCE_NOT_NULL setting) to validate arguments and infer schema and partition columns when none were given. It stores the inferred schema, or an empty schema with a warning when data and partition columns overlap in a HadoopFsRelation, sets tracksPartitionsInCatalog from manageFilesourcePartitions, and calls catalog.createTable. Not intended for temporary tables.

nodes.name: CreateDataSourceTableAsSelectCommand
nodes.summary: Case class command (table, mode, query, outputColumnNames) for CREATE TABLE ... USING format AS SELECT. If the table exists it errors, returns, or appends according to the SaveMode; otherwise it validates the location, picks the default path for managed tables, writes the query through saveDataIntoTable, creates the table with the schema of the written relation and, for partitioned HadoopFsRelation tables with partition management on, runs RepairTableCommand to register partitions. It ends by updating table statistics with CommandUtils.updateTableStats. withCTEDefs wraps the query in WithCTE.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the data source table: checks existence, resolves the relation to validate options and infer schema and partitions, decides which schema and partition columns to store, and registers the table in the session catalog.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes CTAS: handles an existing table by SaveMode, otherwise writes the query data, creates the table entry with the written relation's schema and repairs partitions when needed, then updates table stats.

nodes.name: saveDataIntoTable
nodes.summary: Builds a DataSource for the table (with a path option from the given location) and calls writeAndRead with the query and output column names, logging and rethrowing AnalysisException.

nodes.name: ddl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the runnable DDL commands of the Spark SQL v1 session catalog path: create, drop, alter and describe database, drop table or view, drop temp view, alter table properties, column, serde, location and partitions, MSCK REPAIR TABLE, and the SaveAsV1TableCommand. It also holds the DDLUtils helper object (hive versus datasource table checks, partition provider and alter type verification, column name checks, read path overwrite check). Each command extends LeafRunnableCommand and acts through sparkSession.sessionState.catalog.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file of case classes that all extend LeafRunnableCommand and implement run(sparkSession): Seq[Row]; the file ends with a utility object (DDLUtils).

nodes.name: CreateDatabaseCommand
nodes.summary: Command for CREATE DATABASE or SCHEMA. Its run method builds a CatalogDatabase (comment defaults to empty, location defaults to the catalog default DB path) and calls catalog.createDatabase with the ifNotExists flag; an existing database is an error unless ifNotExists is true.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the database in the session catalog from the name, optional location, comment and properties, honoring ifNotExists, and returns no rows.

nodes.name: DropDatabaseCommand
nodes.summary: Command for DROP DATABASE [IF EXISTS] [RESTRICT|CASCADE]. Its run method simply calls catalog.dropDatabase(databaseName, ifExists, cascade); cascade drops dependent objects first, otherwise a non-empty database cannot be dropped.

nodes.name: AlterDatabasePropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER DATABASE SET DBPROPERTIES. Its run method reads the existing database metadata and calls catalog.alterDatabase with the new key-value pairs merged into the old properties.

nodes.name: AlterDatabaseSetLocationCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER DATABASE SET LOCATION. Its run method copies the database metadata with a new locationUri and calls catalog.alterDatabase.

nodes.name: DescribeDatabaseCommand
nodes.summary: Command for DESCRIBE DATABASE [EXTENDED]. Its run method returns rows for catalog name, database name, comment, location, owner and (if present) collation; in extended mode it adds a Properties row with the redacted, sorted properties minus the reserved namespace properties.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the DESCRIBE DATABASE result rows from the database metadata; when extended is true it appends the non-reserved properties with sensitive options redacted.

nodes.name: DropTableCommand
nodes.summary: Command for DROP TABLE and DROP VIEW (not temp views, which DropTempViewCommand handles). Its run method checks that a view is dropped with DROP VIEW and a table with DROP TABLE (metric views count as views), uncaches the table through the cache manager, refreshes it, then calls catalog.dropTable; a missing table is an error unless ifExists is true.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates table versus view command type, uncaches the query (logging non-fatal failures), refreshes the table in the catalog and drops it with the purge flag; raises noSuchTableError when absent and ifExists is false.

nodes.name: DropTempViewCommand
nodes.summary: Command that drops a local or global temporary view identified by a multi-part Identifier. Its run method validates the namespace shape (empty, one part, or system.session), uncaches the view, refreshes it, and calls dropTempView or dropGlobalTempView depending on the namespace; a missing view is an error unless ifExists is true.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Looks up the raw local or global temp view, uncaches it and refreshes it, then drops it from the local or global temp view registry according to the identifier namespace.

nodes.name: AlterTableSetPropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE or ALTER VIEW SET TBLPROPERTIES. Its run method merges the new properties into the table properties (updating the CatalogTable comment when the comment property is set), calls catalog.alterTable and invalidates the cached table.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Overrides old properties with the given ones, keeps the table comment in sync, persists via catalog.alterTable and invalidates the cached table.

nodes.name: AlterTableUnsetPropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE or ALTER VIEW UNSET TBLPROPERTIES. Its run method removes the given keys from the table properties (resetting the comment if the comment key is removed), calls catalog.alterTable and invalidates the cached table.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Filters the listed property keys out of the table properties, clears the comment when its key is unset, then persists via catalog.alterTable and invalidates the cache.

nodes.name: AlterTableChangeColumnCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE CHANGE COLUMN. It currently only supports changing the comment, default value or collation (recursively through nested types) of a non-partition column; its run method checks the table type, rejects partition columns, collation changes on bucket columns and any rename or incompatible type change, rebuilds the data schema and calls catalog.alterTableDataSchema. Private helpers find the column by name, change type, add a comment, add a default value, compare names and check type evolution.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Refreshes the table, verifies it is not a view and the column is not a partition or bucket column in an invalid way, checks the new type only differs in collation, then rewrites the matching StructField with the new type, comment and current default metadata and stores the new data schema.

nodes.name: findColumnByName
nodes.summary: Finds the column in the schema with the table resolver and throws cannotFindColumnError when it does not exist.

nodes.name: canEvolveType
nodes.summary: Returns true when the two data types are equal except for compatible collation differences (DataType.equalsIgnoreCompatibleCollation without complex type checks).

nodes.name: AlterTableSerDePropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE [PARTITION] SET SERDE / SET SERDEPROPERTIES. It requires at least one of serde class or properties, rejects the operation on datasource tables, and updates either the table storage or one partition storage in the catalog.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Without a partition spec it updates the table storage serde and properties via catalog.alterTable; with a partition spec it copies the partition and calls catalog.alterPartitions; datasource tables are rejected.

nodes.name: AlterTableAddPartitionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE ADD [IF NOT EXISTS] PARTITION. Its run method normalizes partition specs, creates the partitions in batches sized by SQLConf.ADD_PARTITION_BATCH_SIZE, refreshes the table and then updates table statistics (incrementally by added size when auto size update is on, otherwise through CommandUtils.updateTableStats).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Verifies the partition provider is hive, normalizes each spec and location, adds partitions in metastore-friendly batches, refreshes the table and adjusts its size statistics.

nodes.name: AlterTableRenamePartitionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE PARTITION spec1 RENAME TO PARTITION spec2. Its run method normalizes both specs against the partition schema and calls catalog.renamePartitions, then refreshes the table.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Normalizes old and new partition specs, renames the partition in the catalog and refreshes the table.

nodes.name: AlterTableDropPartitionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE DROP [IF EXISTS] PARTITION ... [PURGE]. Its run method normalizes the specs, calls catalog.dropPartitions (honoring ifExists, purge and retainData), refreshes the table and updates table statistics through CommandUtils.updateTableStats.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Normalizes the partition specs, drops them in the catalog, refreshes the table and recomputes its statistics.

nodes.name: PartitionStatistics
nodes.summary: Small case class holding the fast statistics (numFiles and totalSize) gathered for a partition directory during RepairTableCommand.

nodes.name: RepairTableCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE RECOVER PARTITIONS and MSCK REPAIR TABLE [ADD|DROP|SYNC PARTITIONS]. Its run method scans the table directory tree for key=value partition directories (in parallel through a fork-join pool), optionally gathers fast file stats (numFiles, totalSize, transient_lastDdlTime) in a Spark job when many partitions exist, adds missing partitions to the catalog in batches, drops partitions whose directory no longer exists, marks the table as tracking partitions in the catalog and refreshes it. Helpers: getPathFilter (skips _SUCCESS, _temporary and dot files), scanPartitions, gatherPartitionStats, addPartitions, dropPartitions.

nodes.name: getPathFilter
nodes.summary: Returns a Hadoop PathFilter built from the configured input path filter that also excludes _SUCCESS, _temporary and hidden (dot) names.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates the table is partitioned and has a location, drops stale partitions and/or scans and adds new ones (with optional fast stats), sets tracksPartitionsInCatalog on the table and refreshes it, logging counts of added and dropped partitions.

nodes.name: scanPartitions
nodes.summary: Recursively lists the directory tree one partition column level at a time, parsing key=value directory names into partition specs (parallelizing the listing with ParVector when the level is wide) and ignoring entries that do not match the expected column.

nodes.name: gatherPartitionStats
nodes.summary: Computes numFiles and totalSize per partition location; when the partition count exceeds the threshold it runs a Spark job over the locations, otherwise it lists them sequentially.

nodes.name: addPartitions
nodes.summary: Registers the discovered partitions in the catalog in batches (sequentially, because the Hive client is not thread safe), attaching the fast stats as partition parameters when available.

nodes.name: dropPartitions
nodes.summary: Finds catalog partitions whose location no longer exists on the file system (in parallel) and drops them with ignoreIfNotExists and retainData set; returns the number dropped.

nodes.name: AlterTableSetLocationCommand
nodes.summary: Command for ALTER TABLE [PARTITION spec] SET LOCATION. With a partition spec it updates that partition storage location; otherwise it changes the table storage location. It then refreshes the table and recomputes statistics through CommandUtils.updateTableStats.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Applies the new location to either one normalized partition or to the table itself, refreshes the table and updates its stats.

nodes.name: SaveAsV1TableCommand
nodes.summary: Private command that saves a query as a V1 table for the given SaveMode. If the table exists it ignores, errors, or (for Overwrite) first checks the target is not read by the query, drops the table and runs a CreateTable command with the query; otherwise it runs CreateTable directly. A small private runCommand helper executes the plan and asserts it ran.

nodes.name: runCommand
nodes.summary: Executes the given logical plan through the session state and asserts that the command has been executed.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Qualifies the table identifier and dispatches on (tableExists, SaveMode): ignore, error, overwrite after refusing to overwrite a table being read, or plain CreateTable with the query.

nodes.name: DDLUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object for DDL commands: provider checks (isHiveTable, isDatasourceTable, HIVE_PROVIDER = "hive"), readHiveTable, verifyPartitionProviderIsHive, verifyAlterTableType, checkTableColumns and checkDataColNames (column name validation for hive-orc/parquet/avro and orc, parquet, avro providers, rejecting ANSI intervals in hive tables), and verifyNotReadPath (refuses to overwrite a path that the query reads).

nodes.name: isHiveTable
nodes.summary: Returns true when the optional provider name equals "hive" ignoring case. An overload at lines 1041-1043 takes a CatalogTable and delegates to this one with table.provider.

nodes.name: isDatasourceTable
nodes.summary: Returns true when the table has a provider that is not "hive", i.e. it is a datasource table.

nodes.name: readHiveTable
nodes.summary: Builds a HiveTableRelation for a table using its data and partition schemas converted to nullable attributes.

nodes.name: verifyPartitionProviderIsHive
nodes.summary: Throws a standard compilation error when an action needs the hive partition provider but a datasource table has filesource partition management disabled or does not store partition metadata in the catalog.

nodes.name: verifyAlterTableType
nodes.summary: Throws when ALTER VIEW targets a table or ALTER TABLE targets a view-like object; temporary views are allowed for both.

nodes.name: checkTableColumns
nodes.summary: Validates column names and types by provider: hive tables reject ANSI intervals and check names per ORC, Parquet or Avro serde; orc, parquet and avro providers check names directly. The single-argument overload (lines 1105-1107) delegates here with the table data schema.

nodes.name: checkDataColNames
nodes.summary: Looks up the data source for the provider and, for a FileFormat or a FileDataSourceV2 fallback file format, calls DataSourceUtils.checkFieldNames on the schema; lookup failures are logged and ignored.

nodes.name: verifyNotReadPath
nodes.summary: Collects the root paths of HadoopFsRelations read by the query and throws a compilation error when the output path is one of them (naming the table when one is given).

nodes.name: functions.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the runnable SQL commands for functions: CREATE FUNCTION (temporary or permanent), DESCRIBE FUNCTION (including SQL user-defined functions with input, returns, body and stored SQL path), DROP FUNCTION, SHOW FUNCTIONS with LIKE patterns, and REFRESH FUNCTION. Every command extends LeafRunnableCommand and works through the session catalog and function registry.

nodes.name: CreateFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMPORARY] FUNCTION name AS className [USING JAR|FILE ...]. For a temporary function it loads the resources and registers the function in the registry; for a permanent one it stores metadata in the external catalog (or alters it on replace) without loading the UDF class right away.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Registers a temporary function after loading its resources (error if it exists and replace is false), or creates or alters the permanent function metadata in the catalog.

nodes.name: DescribeFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for DESCRIBE FUNCTION [EXTENDED]. For ordinary functions it returns Function, Class and Usage rows (plus Extended Usage); for SQL functions it returns an aligned Function, Type, Input, Returns and, in extended mode, Comment, Collation, Deterministic, Data Access, Configs, Owner, Create Time, Body and the persisted SQL Path. Private helpers append key-value pairs, pad strings to equal width (tabulate), and format parameters with defaults and comments.

nodes.name: tabulate
nodes.summary: Pads every input string with spaces to the length of the longest one so that keys or parameter names line up.

nodes.name: formatParameters
nodes.summary: Formats a StructType of function parameters as aligned "name type" lines, adding DEFAULT values and comments only in extended mode.

nodes.name: describeSQLFunction
nodes.summary: Builds the DESCRIBE FUNCTION rows for a SQL function parsed from ExpressionInfo: name, type (scalar or table), input, returns, and in extended mode comment, collation, determinism, data access, configs, owner, creation time, body and stored SQL path.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Qualifies the function identifier and either delegates to describeSQLFunction for SQL functions or returns Function, Class and Usage rows (and Extended Usage when requested).

nodes.name: DropFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for DROP [TEMPORARY] FUNCTION [IF EXISTS]. A temporary drop validates the session or system.session namespace, refuses to drop a builtin function when no temporary one exists, and calls dropTempFunction; a permanent drop calls catalog.dropFunction.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops a temporary function (after namespace and builtin checks) or a permanent function, honoring ifExists.

nodes.name: ShowFunctionsCommand
nodes.summary: Command for SHOW FUNCTIONS [LIKE pattern]. Its run method lists catalog functions matching the pattern, keeps USER or SYSTEM ones according to the flags, and for system functions also adds the builtin operators from FunctionRegistry.builtinOperators that match, returning the sorted names.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists matching functions from the session catalog, filters by user or system, appends builtin operator names when system functions are shown, and returns them sorted as rows.

nodes.name: RefreshFunctionCommand
nodes.summary: Command for REFRESH FUNCTION name. Its run method re-registers a persistent function from catalog metadata (overriding the cached one); for a non-persistent function it unregisters any cached entry and throws noSuchFunctionError.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Reloads the permanent function into the function registry, or clears the cached entry and fails when the function is not persistent.

nodes.name: metricViewCommands.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateMetricViewCommand (creates a metric view in the session catalog from a YAML body), the AlterMetricViewCommand placeholder, and the MetricViewHelper object that analyzes the metric view text and collects direct table or view dependencies of an analyzed plan.

nodes.name: CreateMetricViewCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command that creates a metric view. It requires the child to be a ResolvedIdentifier in the session catalog (otherwise an internal error), analyzes the view text with MetricViewHelper, validates user specified column counts, merges the metric view descriptor properties into the user properties and calls catalog.createTable with a prepared view table marked as a metric view.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the child: a ResolvedIdentifier of the session catalog goes to createMetricViewInSessionCatalog, anything else throws an internal error.

nodes.name: validateUserColumns
nodes.summary: Throws cannotCreateViewNotEnoughColumnsError or cannotCreateViewTooManyColumnsError when the user specified column list length differs from the analyzed plan output.

nodes.name: createMetricViewInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Analyzes the metric view YAML, validates user columns, merges the descriptor properties (metric_view.*) into the given properties and creates the view table through ViewHelper.prepareTable and catalog.createTable, honoring allowExisting.

nodes.name: AlterMetricViewCommand
nodes.summary: Case class placeholder (child plan and original text) for ALTER of a metric view; it has no run logic in this file.

nodes.name: MetricViewHelper
nodes.summary: Helper object for metric view commands. analyzeMetricViewText plans and analyzes a metric view YAML body and returns the analyzed plan with the parsed MetricView descriptor; collectTableDependencies walks an analyzed plan (including subquery expressions) to gather direct table and view dependencies as multi-part names, normalizing v1 names to [spark_catalog, db, table] through qualifyV1.

nodes.name: collectTableDependencies
nodes.summary: Traverses the analyzed plan and returns distinct direct dependencies: persistent views, v2 relations (catalog plus namespace plus name), Hive table relations and catalog backed logical relations, descending through children and subquery plans but not through those leaves.

nodes.name: qualifyV1
nodes.summary: Normalizes 1, 2 or 3 part v1 table names to the 3 part form [spark_catalog, db, table], using the default database for one part names and passing other arities through.

nodes.name: analyzeMetricViewText
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic CatalogTable identifier from the name parts, calls MetricViewPlanner.planWrite to get the placeholder plan and the parsed MetricView, runs the analyzer on it, checks temporary objects via ViewHelper.verifyTemporaryObjectsNotExists, and returns the analyzed plan with the descriptor.

nodes.name: SetCatalogCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetCatalogCommand, the runnable command behind SET CATALOG, which evaluates a catalog name expression and switches the session's current catalog.

nodes.name: SetCatalogCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SET CATALOG xxx. It holds a catalogNameExpr that may be a declared session variable, a plain identifier, a string literal, the identifier() function or another foldable expression such as CAST or CONCAT. getCatalogName evaluates it and run sets the current catalog on the session's catalog manager. It produces no output rows.

nodes.name: getCatalogName
nodes.summary: Evaluates the catalog name expression through IdentifierResolution.evalIdentifierExpr and returns the single name part. It throws multipartCatalogNameNotAllowed when the evaluated name has more than one part.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls getCatalogName and sets the result as the current catalog on sessionState.catalogManager, then returns no rows.

nodes.name: SetCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetCommand (SET key=value, SET -v, SET) and ResetCommand (RESET), the runnable commands that read, write and reset SQL configuration for the current session.

nodes.name: SetCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SET key = value, SET -v and plain SET. At construction it matches the optional key/value pair to pick an output schema and a run function. Cases: the deprecated mapred.reduce.tasks and the replaced mapreduce.job.reduces are converted to the shuffle partitions config with a warning; hivevar: names are set directly; an ordinary key/value is set after checking that the key is not a declared SQL variable and warning about hive.* keys with the Hive catalog; no argument lists all session configs with redaction; SET -v lists every defined config with default, doc and since-version; a single key query falls back to the shared Hadoop conf. The companion object defines the VariableName regex for hivevar:.

nodes.name: keyValueOutput
nodes.summary: Builds the two column (key, value) string output schema as attributes, shared by most SET variants.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes the run function selected at construction time against the given session. The matching logic itself sits in the class body (lines 51-200).

nodes.name: ResetCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for RESET and RESET key. With a key it unsets that config and restores the value from the initial session options or the shared initial configs. Without a key it clears the session conf and merges the initial Spark conf and the non static initial session options back in.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Resets one config key or the whole session SQLConf to the values captured at session start, using SQLConf.mergeSparkConf and SQLConf.mergeNonStaticSQLConfigs, and returns no rows.

nodes.name: SetNamespaceCollation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetNamespaceCollationCommand, which implements ALTER DATABASE/SCHEMA/NAMESPACE ... DEFAULT COLLATION by setting the collation property on a namespace.

nodes.name: SetNamespaceCollationCommand
nodes.summary: Unary runnable command for ALTER (DATABASE|SCHEMA|NAMESPACE) ... DEFAULT COLLATION. Its child is the resolved namespace plan. run builds a NamespaceChange.setProperty for the collation property and applies it through the namespace catalog's alterNamespace. withNewChildInternal copies the command with a new child.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Unpacks the ResolvedNamespace child, creates a set-property change for PROP_COLLATION and calls alterNamespace on the catalog. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: SetNamespaceCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetNamespaceCommand, the runnable command for USE NAMESPACE that changes the session's current namespace.

nodes.name: SetNamespaceCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for USE NAMESPACE xxx. run calls setCurrentNamespace on the session's catalog manager with the namespace parts and returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Sets the current namespace of the session catalog manager from the namespace parts.

nodes.name: SetPathCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetPathCommand, the runnable command for SET PATH = element, ... that sets the internal session path used for resolution.

nodes.name: SetPathCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SET PATH = pathElement (, pathElement)*. run fails with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.SET_PATH_WHEN_DISABLED when the PATH_ENABLED conf is off. Otherwise it expands shortcut elements at run time, validates there are no static duplicates (honoring case sensitivity) and sets or clears the session path on the catalog manager. The PathElement AST lives in catalyst so the same grammar parses the DEFAULT_PATH conf.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Checks that the path feature is enabled, expands and validates the path elements, then calls setSessionPath or clearSessionPath on the catalog manager when the expanded list is empty.

nodes.name: ShowCatalogsCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowCatalogsCommand, the runnable command for SHOW CATALOGS.

nodes.name: ShowCatalogsCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SHOW CATALOGS with an optional name pattern. It outputs a single non-null string column named catalog, and run returns one row per catalog from the catalog manager's listCatalogs(pattern).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists catalogs matching the optional pattern from sessionState.catalogManager and wraps each name in a Row.

nodes.name: ShowCollationsCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowCollationsCommand, the runnable command for SHOW COLLATIONS that lists available collations with their metadata.

nodes.name: ShowCollationsCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SHOW COLLATIONS with an optional pattern. Its output columns are NAME, LANGUAGE, COUNTRY, ACCENT_SENSITIVITY, CASE_SENSITIVITY, PAD_ATTRIBUTE and ICU_VERSION. run loads every collation's metadata from CollationFactory, filters names with StringUtils.filterPattern and renders accent and case sensitivity as text labels.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists collations via CollationFactory.listCollations and loadCollationMeta, applies the optional name pattern and builds one row per collation.

nodes.name: ShowCurrentNamespaceCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowCurrentNamespaceCommand, the runnable command for SHOW CURRENT NAMESPACE.

nodes.name: ShowCurrentNamespaceCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for SHOW CURRENT NAMESPACE. It outputs the columns catalog and namespace, and run returns one row with the current catalog name and the quoted current namespace from the session catalog manager.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Reads currentCatalog.name and the quoted currentNamespace from the catalog manager and returns them as one row.

nodes.name: ShowNamespacesCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowNamespacesCommand and its companion, the runnable command for SHOW NAMESPACES (and legacy SHOW DATABASES) that lists namespaces of a resolved catalog namespace.

nodes.name: ShowNamespacesCommand
nodes.summary: Unary runnable command for SHOW NAMESPACES with an optional pattern. run unpacks the ResolvedNamespace child, lists namespaces from the catalog (nested under the given namespace if non-empty), quotes names unless the legacy single column databaseName output is used, and filters by the pattern using StringUtils.filterPattern. The companion object's output picks databaseName when the legacy output schema conf is set and namespace otherwise.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists namespaces of the resolved catalog, formats names (unquoted for legacy databaseName output), applies the pattern filter and returns rows.

nodes.name: output
