nodes.summary: Companion object method that returns the single column output schema: databaseName when SQLConf.legacyOutputSchema is true, otherwise namespace.

nodes.name: ShowProceduresCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowProceduresCommand, the runnable command for SHOW PROCEDURES [(IN|FROM) namespace] that lists procedures in a catalog namespace.

nodes.name: ShowProceduresCommand
nodes.summary: Unary runnable command for SHOW PROCEDURES. If no namespace is given the current one is used. Output columns are catalog, namespace (array of strings), schema and procedure_name. run matches the ResolvedNamespace child, gets the catalog as a procedure catalog, lists procedures for the namespace and emits one row each, using the last namespace part as the schema.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists procedures through asProcedureCatalog.listProcedures for the resolved namespace and maps each to a row of catalog name, namespace, schema and procedure name.

nodes.name: UnsetNamespacePropertiesCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UnsetNamespacePropertiesCommand, which implements ALTER (DATABASE|SCHEMA|NAMESPACE) ... UNSET (DBPROPERTIES|PROPERTIES) by removing property keys from a namespace.

nodes.name: UnsetNamespacePropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Unary runnable command that unsets namespace properties given a list of keys. run maps each key to a NamespaceChange.removeProperty and applies them in one alterNamespace call; removing a missing property still succeeds. The child plan is the ident parameter and withNewChildInternal copies the command with a new ident.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds removeProperty changes for each key and calls alterNamespace on the resolved namespace's catalog, returning no rows.

nodes.name: resources.scala
nodes.summary: Defines runnable commands for session resources: ADD JAR, ADD FILE, ADD ARCHIVE and the LIST FILES, LIST JARS and LIST ARCHIVES commands.

nodes.name: AddJarsCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command that adds each given jar path to the current session through sessionState.resourceLoader.addJar so it can be used for UDFs or serdes. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls resourceLoader.addJar for every path and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: AddFilesCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command that adds files to the session via SparkContext.addFile. The recursive flag is the negation of the addSingleFileInAddFile conf. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Reads the addSingleFileInAddFile conf, then calls sparkContext.addFile(path, recursive) for each path.

nodes.name: AddArchivesCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command that adds archives to the session via SparkContext.addArchive. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls sparkContext.addArchive for each path and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: ListFilesCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for LIST FILES. It outputs a single Results column. With no arguments it returns every file registered in the SparkContext; with file paths it resolves each URI (local and file schemes to canonical file URIs) and returns only those that were added.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Gets sparkContext.listFiles and returns all of them, or filters them against the canonicalized requested paths.

nodes.name: ListJarsCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for LIST JARS. Single Results column. With no arguments it returns all jars from sparkContext.listJars; with names it returns the registered jar paths that contain the given jar file name.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists jars from the SparkContext and optionally filters by matching the last path segment of each requested jar.

nodes.name: ListArchivesCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf runnable command for LIST ARCHIVES. Single Results column. With no arguments it returns all archives from sparkContext.listArchives; with names it returns the registered archive paths that contain the given archive file name.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists archives from the SparkContext and optionally filters by matching the last path segment of each requested archive.

nodes.name: tables.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the runnable table-level DDL and inspection commands of the SQL execution layer: CREATE TABLE (LIKE), ALTER TABLE RENAME and ADD COLUMNS, LOAD DATA, TRUNCATE TABLE, the DESCRIBE family (table, query, column), SHOW TABLES, TBLPROPERTIES, COLUMNS, PARTITIONS, SHOW CREATE TABLE (Spark DDL and AS SERDE) and REFRESH TABLE. Each is a case class whose run(sparkSession) calls the session catalog and returns rows. A TODO at line 146 says the remaining table commands of ddl.scala should move here.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case classes extending LeafRunnableCommand or UnaryRunnableCommand; DESCRIBE and SHOW CREATE TABLE commands share behaviour through the DescribeCommandBase and ShowCreateTableCommandBase traits.

nodes.name: CreateTableLikeCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for CREATE TABLE t1 LIKE t2 [USING provider | STORED AS hiveFormat]. run() reads the source table metadata (temp view or permanent), decides the new provider and storage (validating a given provider via data source lookup), chooses MANAGED or EXTERNAL from the location, copies schema, partition columns, bucket spec and catalog partition tracking (comment is dropped), and creates the target table in the session catalog.

nodes.name: CreateTableLikeCommand.run
nodes.summary: Builds the new CatalogTable from the source table (provider, storage, managed or external type, raw schema, partitions, bucket spec) and creates it in the catalog.

nodes.name: CreateTableCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command that creates a table from a CatalogTable definition via the session catalog. The source notes it is currently used only for creating Hive tables and not for temporary tables.

nodes.name: CreateTableCommand.run
nodes.summary: Creates the table in the session catalog with the ignoreIfExists flag.

nodes.name: AlterTableRenameCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for ALTER TABLE/VIEW ... RENAME TO. A temp view is simply renamed. For a real table it verifies the alter type, remembers the cached storage level, uncaches the table, refreshes it, renames it and then re-caches the new name with the previous storage level.

nodes.name: AlterTableRenameCommand.run
nodes.summary: Renames a temp view directly, or for a real table uncaches, refreshes, renames and re-caches with the original storage level.

nodes.name: AlterTableAddColumnsCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS. run() checks the table is eligible (verifyAlterTableAddColumn rejects views and data source tables whose format is not CSV, JSON, Parquet or ORC), validates default values, duplicate column names and collations in map keys, uncaches and refreshes the table, then alters the catalog schema by appending the new columns to the data schema before the partition schema.

nodes.name: AlterTableAddColumnsCommand.run
nodes.summary: Verifies the table, validates default values, column names and collations, then alters the catalog schema with the added columns.

nodes.name: AlterTableAddColumnsCommand.verifyAlterTableAddColumn
nodes.summary: Returns the table metadata after rejecting views and data source tables whose file format is not CSV, JSON, Parquet or ORC.

nodes.name: LoadDataCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for LOAD DATA [LOCAL] INPATH ... [OVERWRITE] INTO TABLE ... [PARTITION (...)] on Hive tables. run() validates the partition spec against the table, rejects data source tables, resolves the input path (local or relative to /user/<name> with fs.defaultFS), checks that the path exists, calls catalog loadTable or loadPartition, refreshes the table and updates table stats. The companion object (lines 402-433) has makeQualified, a path qualification helper ported from the Hadoop Path class (the companion shares this class id).

nodes.name: LoadDataCommand.run
nodes.summary: Validates the target table and partition spec, resolves and checks the input path, then loads data into the table or partition and refreshes caches and stats.

nodes.name: LoadDataCommand.makeQualified
nodes.summary: Companion object helper (private[sql]) that qualifies a Path with a default URI scheme and authority and a working directory; ported from the Hadoop Path class per its comment.

nodes.name: TruncateTableCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for TRUNCATE TABLE ... [PARTITION (...)]. It rejects external tables and partition specs on unpartitioned tables, collects the table or partition locations, and for each location records the permission and ACL (unless ignored by config), deletes and recreates the directory, restores permission and ACL, then refreshes the table and updates table stats. Has a private newAclEntry helper that builds an AclEntry.

nodes.name: TruncateTableCommand.run
nodes.summary: Truncates data by deleting and recreating each table or partition directory while restoring permissions and ACLs, then refreshes the table and updates stats.

nodes.name: TruncateTableCommand.newAclEntry
nodes.summary: Builds a Hadoop AclEntry from a scope, type and permission.

nodes.name: ResolvedChildHelper
nodes.summary: Helper object whose getTableMetadata extracts the CatalogTable from the resolved child plan (temp view, persistent V1 view, V1 table) and otherwise looks it up in the session catalog. Used by ShowColumnsCommand and DescribeTableCommand.

nodes.name: ResolvedChildHelper.getTableMetadata
nodes.summary: Matches the resolved child plan (temp view, V1 view, V1 table) to return its CatalogTable, falling back to the catalog lookups.

nodes.name: DescribeCommandBase
nodes.summary: Trait with shared output helpers for the DESCRIBE commands. describeSchema appends one row per column (name, simple data type string, comment) with an optional header row, and append adds a single row to the buffer.

nodes.name: DescribeCommandBase.describeSchema
nodes.summary: Appends a header row (when requested) and one row per schema column with name, data type string and comment.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for DESCRIBE [EXTENDED|FORMATTED] table_name [partitionSpec]. run() resolves table metadata with ResolvedChildHelper, restores raw char/varchar types, prints the schema, partition information, clustering information, then either detailed partition info (when a partition spec is given) or the formatted table info (when extended), and finally column default values. Private describe* helpers produce each section.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.run
nodes.summary: Produces the DESCRIBE output: schema, partition and clustering info, detailed partition or formatted table info, and default column values.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.describePartitionInfo
nodes.summary: Appends the partition columns section when the table is partitioned.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.describeClusteringInfo
nodes.summary: Appends the clustering columns section from the clusterBySpec, asserting each column exists in the schema.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.describeFormattedTableInfo
nodes.summary: Appends the detailed table information rows, excluding partition columns and schema.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.describeDetailedPartitionInfo
nodes.summary: Validates that the target is not a view and has a Hive partition provider, normalizes the spec and looks up the partition for detailed output.

nodes.name: DescribeTableCommand.describeFormattedDetailedPartitionInfo
nodes.summary: Appends database, table, partition, bucket and storage information rows for a partition.

nodes.name: DescribeQueryCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for DESCRIBE [QUERY] statement. It only needs the schema, so it executes the plan with CommandExecutionMode.SKIP and prints the analyzed schema. It supports CTE definitions via withCTEDefs and supervised plan transformation via withTransformedSupervisedPlan.

nodes.name: DescribeQueryCommand.run
nodes.summary: Executes the plan in SKIP mode and describes the analyzed schema.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for DESCRIBE [EXTENDED|FORMATTED] table_name column_name. run() resolves the column (rejecting nested columns), prints col_name, data_type and comment, and for the extended form adds column statistics (min, max, num_nulls, distinct_count, avg_col_len, max_col_len), a histogram description and the default value. Private helpers format timestamp stats in the session time zone and describe histograms.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnCommand.run
nodes.summary: Resolves the column and returns its name, type and comment, plus stats, histogram and default value when extended.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnCommand.toZoneAwareExternalString
nodes.summary: Converts a stored timestamp stat string to internal form and reformats it in the session local time zone; other types pass through unchanged.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnCommand.histogramDescription
nodes.summary: Formats a histogram as a header row plus one row per bin with lower bound, upper bound and distinct count.

nodes.name: ShowTablesCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for SHOW TABLES [IN db] [LIKE pattern] and SHOW TABLE EXTENDED ... [PARTITION(spec)]. Without a partition spec it lists tables of the database (database, table name, isTemporary and, if extended, the table information string); with a partition spec it returns the information of that single partition.

nodes.name: ShowTablesCommand.run
nodes.summary: Lists tables of a database (with optional pattern and extended info) or returns the information of one partition.

nodes.name: ShowTablePropertiesCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for SHOW TBLPROPERTIES table_name[('key')]. Returns nothing for temp views; otherwise returns one redacted property value, or all properties (excluding those starting with the view prefix) sorted by key.

nodes.name: ShowTablePropertiesCommand.run
nodes.summary: Returns one redacted table property or all non view-prefixed properties sorted by key.

nodes.name: ShowColumnsCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable unary command for SHOW COLUMNS (FROM | IN) table [(FROM | IN) database]. Resolves the table metadata through ResolvedChildHelper and returns one row per schema column name.

nodes.name: ShowColumnsCommand.run
nodes.summary: Looks up the table (optionally in the given database) and returns its column names.

nodes.name: ShowPartitionsCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for SHOW PARTITIONS table [PARTITION(spec)]. Fails for non partitioned tables, verifies the partition provider is Hive, normalizes the optional spec and returns the partition names from the catalog.

nodes.name: ShowPartitionsCommand.run
nodes.summary: Validates the table is partitioned with a Hive provider, normalizes the spec and lists partition names.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase
nodes.summary: Trait (extends SQLConfHelper) with the shared builders for SHOW CREATE TABLE output: location, comment, collation, TBLPROPERTIES, multi-line concatenation, and the full CREATE VIEW body (view columns, properties, schema binding, view text). Mixed into ShowCreateTableCommand and ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase.showTableLocation
nodes.summary: Appends a LOCATION clause for external tables.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase.showTableProperties
nodes.summary: Appends a sorted, redacted TBLPROPERTIES clause when properties exist.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase.showCreateView
nodes.summary: Appends the CREATE VIEW body: columns, comment, collation, properties, schema binding and view text.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase.showViewDataColumns
nodes.summary: Appends the view column list with optional comments and without data types.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommandBase.showViewProperties
nodes.summary: Appends TBLPROPERTIES for a view, skipping view-prefixed and collation properties.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for SHOW CREATE TABLE [db.]table that emits Spark DDL. Rejects temp views and metric views, converts Hive serde tables to a data source provider when a mapping exists (convertTableMetadata, using HiveSerDe) or errors for unsupported features, then writes CREATE VIEW or CREATE TABLE with columns, USING/OPTIONS, PARTITIONED BY, CLUSTERED BY, comment, collation, location and properties.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.run
nodes.summary: Generates the Spark DDL string for a table or view, rejecting temp views, metric views and unsupported Hive features, converting Hive serde tables when possible.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.convertTableMetadata
nodes.summary: Maps a Hive serde table to a Spark data source via HiveSerDe.serdeToSource, or throws with the serde, input and output formats if unmapped.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.showDataSourceTableDataColumns
nodes.summary: Appends the column definitions as DDL using raw char/varchar types and explicit UTF8_BINARY collation.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.showDataSourceTableOptions
nodes.summary: Appends the USING provider line and redacted OPTIONS.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.showDataSourceTableNonDataColumns
nodes.summary: Appends PARTITIONED BY and CLUSTERED BY / SORTED BY / INTO BUCKETS clauses.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableCommand.showCreateDataSourceTable
nodes.summary: Composes the data source table DDL from columns, options, partitioning, comment, collation, location and properties.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for SHOW CREATE TABLE table_identifier AS SERDE. Rejects Spark data source tables and generates Hive style DDL (header columns, PARTITIONED BY, CLUSTERED BY, ROW FORMAT SERDE with SERDEPROPERTIES, STORED AS input/output formats, location and properties) for external, managed or view tables.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.run
nodes.summary: Returns the Hive style DDL for a non data source table and errors for Spark data source tables.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.showCreateHiveTable
nodes.summary: Builds the CREATE [EXTERNAL] TABLE or VIEW string for a Hive table, erroring on unsupported features or unknown table types.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.showHiveTableHeader
nodes.summary: Appends the non partition column definitions.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.showHiveTableNonDataColumns
nodes.summary: Appends PARTITIONED BY and CLUSTERED BY / SORTED BY / INTO BUCKETS clauses in Hive style.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand.showHiveTableStorageInfo
nodes.summary: Appends ROW FORMAT SERDE with SERDEPROPERTIES and STORED AS INPUTFORMAT / OUTPUTFORMAT clauses.

nodes.name: RefreshTableCommand
nodes.summary: Runnable command for REFRESH TABLE [db.]table that refreshes all cached entries of the table through the catalog API; a cached InMemoryRelation is dropped and recached lazily.

nodes.name: RefreshTableCommand.run
nodes.summary: Refreshes the table through the catalog API.

nodes.name: CloseCursorExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node CloseCursorExec that executes the CLOSE cursor command inside a SQL script.

nodes.name: CloseCursorExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for closing a cursor. It moves the cursor from the Opened or Fetching state to Closed and raises CURSOR_NOT_FOUND or CURSOR_NOT_OPEN when the cursor is missing, declared only, or already closed. Used when a SQL script runs CLOSE on a cursor.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Casts the cursor expression to a CursorReference, fetches the scripting context and the cursor state, checks the state is open, then updates the state to CursorClosed and returns no rows. The output override (line 67) is trivial and returns Nil.

nodes.name: CreateVariableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateVariableExec, the physical plan node for DECLARE of one or more variables, either session variables or local variables inside a script.

nodes.name: CreateVariableExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node that creates variables from resolved identifiers and a default value expression, with an optional OR REPLACE flag. It evaluates the default expression once, normalizes names when analysis is case insensitive, and registers the variables in the scripting variable manager (when the catalog is FakeLocalCatalog) or in the session temporary variable manager. Used when a DECLARE statement executes.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Evaluates the default expression into a Literal, builds a VariableDefinition per identifier, picks the scripting or temp variable manager, rejects duplicate names inside one DECLARE (DUPLICATE_VARIABLE_NAME_INSIDE_DECLARE) and existing names without OR REPLACE (VARIABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS), then creates each variable. stringArgs (lines 41-42) and output (line 108) are trivial overrides.

nodes.name: CursorCommandUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds CursorCommandUtils, a package-private helper object shared by the cursor command nodes to reach the SQL scripting execution context.

nodes.name: CursorCommandUtils
nodes.summary: Package-private utility object for cursor commands. Its method getScriptingContext returns the current SqlScriptingExecutionContext and throws CURSOR_OUTSIDE_SCRIPT when no scripting context manager exists. Used by the declare, open, fetch and close cursor nodes.

nodes.name: getScriptingContext
nodes.summary: Looks up SqlScriptingContextManager and returns its context cast to SqlScriptingExecutionContext, or throws AnalysisException CURSOR_OUTSIDE_SCRIPT with the quoted cursor name.

nodes.name: DeclareCursorExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DeclareCursorExec, the physical plan node that registers a new cursor in the current script scope.

nodes.name: DeclareCursorExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for DECLARE CURSOR. It stores a CursorDefinition (normalized name and the original SQL text) in the current scope and sets the state to CursorDeclared; the query is not parsed or analyzed until OPEN. Throws CURSOR_ALREADY_EXISTS if the name is already used in the scope.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Gets the scripting context and current scope, normalizes the cursor name by case sensitivity, rejects duplicates, then puts the CursorDefinition into scope.cursors and CursorDeclared into scope.cursorStates. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: DropVariableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DropVariableExec, the physical plan node that removes a session variable.

nodes.name: DropVariableExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node that drops a session variable. It removes the variable from the session temporary variable manager (name lowercased when analysis is case insensitive) and throws VARIABLE_NOT_FOUND unless ifExists is set.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Normalizes the name, calls remove on the temp variable manager, and raises VARIABLE_NOT_FOUND (with the system catalog and session namespace in the quoted name) when nothing was removed and ifExists is false.

nodes.name: FetchCursorExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FetchCursorExec, the physical plan node that implements FETCH from an open cursor into variables, with ANSI casting.

nodes.name: FetchCursorExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for FETCH cursor INTO variables. It reads the next row from the iterator created at OPEN (moving Opened to Fetching on the first fetch), then assigns columns to the target VariableReferences using ANSI store assignment casts. Main helpers: shouldFetchIntoStruct, fetchIntoVariables, fetchIntoStruct, applyCastIfNeeded and assignToVariable. Throws CURSOR_NOT_FOUND, CURSOR_NOT_OPEN, CURSOR_NO_MORE_ROWS and ASSIGNMENT_ARITY_MISMATCH.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Resolves the cursor state, obtains the iterator and schema (transitioning CursorOpened to CursorFetching), errors if the cursor is not open or has no more rows, takes the next row and dispatches to fetchIntoStruct or fetchIntoVariables. Returns no rows; output (line 264) is a trivial override.

nodes.name: shouldFetchIntoStruct
nodes.summary: True when there is exactly one target variable of struct type and the row has more than one column (the SQL standard special case).

nodes.name: fetchIntoVariables
nodes.summary: Checks that the number of targets equals the number of columns (ASSIGNMENT_ARITY_MISMATCH otherwise), then casts each column and assigns it to its variable one to one.

nodes.name: applyCastIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Returns the value unchanged when types match, otherwise evaluates an ANSI-enabled Cast to the target type using the session local time zone.

nodes.name: assignToVariable
nodes.summary: Chooses the scripting variable manager for FakeLocalCatalog or the temp variable manager for FakeSystemCatalog (with internal or unresolved-variable errors otherwise), builds a VariableDefinition holding the value as a Literal and sets the variable.

nodes.name: fetchIntoStruct
nodes.summary: Fetches all columns of the row into one STRUCT variable: validates the field count, builds a Literal or ANSI Cast per field, evaluates a CreateStruct and assigns it through assignToVariable.

nodes.name: OpenCursorExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OpenCursorExec, the physical plan node that opens a declared cursor and starts executing its query.

nodes.name: OpenCursorExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for OPEN cursor [USING args]. It checks the cursor is Declared or Closed (else CURSOR_ALREADY_OPEN), parses and analyzes the stored query text through ParameterizedQueryExecutor with the USING arguments and names, builds a Dataset and calls executeToIterator immediately so file lists and snapshots are captured, then stores CursorOpened with the iterator and output schema.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates cursor state, calls executeParameterizedQuery on the cursor definition query text, creates a Dataset with ofRows, obtains the result iterator from the executed plan and updates the cursor state to CursorOpened. Returns no rows; output (line 98) is a trivial override.

nodes.name: ParameterBindingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParameterBindingUtils, shared logic that turns USING clause expressions into parameter values and names.

nodes.name: ParameterBindingUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object that is the single place for USING clause parameter binding, shared by EXECUTE IMMEDIATE and OPEN CURSOR. buildUnifiedParameters produces parallel arrays of values and names (from Alias nodes or pre-extracted names), and evaluateParameterExpression evaluates a variable reference or foldable expression to a Literal.

nodes.name: buildUnifiedParameters
nodes.summary: Builds (values, names) arrays from the argument expressions. Uses pre-extracted names when given (must match args length), otherwise reads names from Alias nodes with an empty name for positional parameters, and evaluates each parameter expression.

nodes.name: evaluateParameterExpression
nodes.summary: Evaluates a VariableReference or any foldable expression to a typed Literal, and throws unsupportedParameterExpression for non-foldable expressions such as column references.

nodes.name: ParameterizedQueryExecutor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ParameterizedQueryExecutor trait that parses and analyzes SQL text with optional bound parameters.

nodes.name: ParameterizedQueryExecutor
nodes.summary: Trait shared by EXECUTE IMMEDIATE and OPEN CURSOR to run query text with optional USING parameters. It requires a session and provides executeParameterizedQuery, which returns the analyzed logical plan.

nodes.name: executeParameterizedQuery
nodes.summary: When arguments are present, binds them through ParameterBindingUtils.buildUnifiedParameters and calls sql(queryText, values, names), otherwise calls sql(queryText); returns the analyzed plan of the resulting Dataset.

nodes.name: SetVariableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetVariableExec, the physical plan node that runs the SET VAR assignment: it executes the child query, takes at most one row and stores the values into session variables or scripting local variables.

nodes.name: SetVariableExec
nodes.summary: Physical command node (V2CommandExec with UnaryLike) for setting variables. run() calls query.executeCollect(): zero rows set every target variable to null, more than one row throws ROW_SUBQUERY_TOO_MANY_ROWS, and exactly one row assigns column i to variable i. setVariable picks the variable manager from the VariableReference catalog (FakeLocalCatalog uses the scripting variable manager, FakeSystemCatalog uses the session temp variable manager), lower-cases the name parts unless analysis is case sensitive, and writes a VariableDefinition holding the new Literal. output is empty and withNewChildInternal copies the node with a new query.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Collects the child query result and assigns it: no rows gives null for every variable, more than one row raises ROW_SUBQUERY_TOO_MANY_ROWS, one row maps column index to variable index. Returns an empty row sequence.

nodes.name: setVariable
nodes.summary: Stores one value in a variable. Adjusts the name parts for case sensitivity, selects the scripting or session variable manager from the variable catalog (raising internal or unresolved-variable errors for inconsistent states), and calls set with a new VariableDefinition built from a Literal of the value.

nodes.name: V2CommandStrategy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines V2CommandStrategy, a planner strategy that turns variable and cursor logical commands into their physical Exec nodes.

nodes.name: V2CommandStrategy
nodes.summary: Planner strategy object (extends Strategy, which is the classic alias of SparkStrategy). Its apply method pattern matches on logical plans: CreateVariable becomes CreateVariableExec (only when all identifiers are ResolvedIdentifier), DropVariable becomes DropVariableExec, SetVariable becomes SetVariableExec wrapping planLater(query), DeclareCursor, OpenCursor, FetchCursor and CloseCursor become DeclareCursorExec, OpenCursorExec, FetchCursorExec and CloseCursorExec, and anything else returns Nil. A TODO notes that non data source v2 commands should be moved here.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Maps a LogicalPlan to a Seq[SparkPlan]: matches the variable commands (create, drop, set) and cursor commands (declare, open, fetch, close) and builds the matching Exec node, otherwise returns an empty sequence.

nodes.name: AggregatePushDownUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object used when aggregates are pushed down to file sources: it builds the schema of a pushed aggregation, compares aggregations, converts the aggregate result row into a one-row ColumnarBatch and reorders partition values to match group by columns.

nodes.name: AggregatePushDownUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object documented as "aggregate push down to Parquet and ORC". Methods: getSchemaForPushedAggregation (returns None when data filters exist, or group by columns differ from partition columns, or an aggregate is unsupported; accepts Max, Min on boolean, byte, short, int, long, float, double, date non-partition columns, non-distinct Count and CountStar), equivalentAggregations, convertAggregatesRowToBatch, getSchemaWithoutGroupingExpression, reOrderPartitionCol and the private extractColName.

nodes.name: getSchemaForPushedAggregation
nodes.summary: Builds the StructType of a pushed down aggregation or returns None if it cannot be pushed down. Rejects any data filter, group by columns that are not exactly the partition columns, partition column min/max, and non-primitive min/max types (comments cite undefined INT96 order and truncated binary min/max). Output fields are group by columns followed by names like max(col), min(col), count(col) and count(*).

nodes.name: equivalentAggregations
nodes.summary: Checks whether two Aggregation objects are equal by sorting the aggregate and group by expressions by hashCode and comparing them element by element.

nodes.name: convertAggregatesRowToBatch
nodes.summary: Converts the aggregate result held in an InternalRow into a one-row ColumnarBatch for the columnar reader, allocating on-heap or off-heap column vectors and filling them with a RowToColumnConverter.

nodes.name: getSchemaWithoutGroupingExpression
nodes.summary: Returns the aggregate schema without the leading group by columns by dropping as many fields as there are group by expressions.

nodes.name: reOrderPartitionCol
nodes.summary: Reorders partition values to follow the order of the group by columns when partition schema order differs; asserts that the column counts match and builds a new GenericInternalRow.

nodes.name: extractColName
nodes.summary: Private helper returning the single field name of a V2 FieldReference, or None for other expressions.

nodes.name: views.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the v1 (session catalog) view commands CREATE VIEW, ALTER VIEW AS, ALTER VIEW SCHEMA BINDING and SHOW VIEWS, the shared ViewHelper object that builds view properties and temporary view definitions, and the CheckViewReferences post-analysis check for v2 view commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case classes extending RunnableCommand; ViewHelper is an object mixing in SQLConfHelper, Logging and CapturesConfig.

nodes.name: CreateViewCommand
nodes.summary: Logical RunnableCommand (also AnalysisOnlyCommand, CTEInChildren and CreateTempView) for CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMPORARY|GLOBAL TEMPORARY] VIEW. run() requires the plan to be analyzed, checks user column count against plan output, verifies a permanent view references no temporary objects or auto-generated aliases, then creates a local temp view, global temp view (in the global temp database) or persistent view; for an existing view it applies allowExisting, rejects non-views, or on replace checks for cycles, uncaches, drops and recreates it. markAsAnalyzed captures referred temp function names; withNewChildrenInternal, childrenToAnalyze and withCTEDefs adapt the plan child. The comment states v2 checks live in CheckViewReferences.

nodes.name: AlterViewAsCommand
nodes.summary: RunnableCommand (also AnalysisOnlyCommand and CTEInChildren) for ALTER VIEW ... AS query. run() decides whether the name is a temp view, runs the temp object and auto-alias checks, and calls alterTemporaryView (rebuilds the TemporaryViewRelation and alters the temp view definition) or alterPermanentView (detects cyclic references, uncaches, regenerates view properties and updates the stored CatalogTable with the new schema and text). markAsAnalyzed, childrenToAnalyze, withNewChildrenInternal and withCTEDefs manage the query child.

nodes.name: AlterViewSchemaBindingCommand
nodes.summary: LeafRunnableCommand for ALTER VIEW ... WITH SCHEMA binding. run() throws if the view is temporary, otherwise alterPermanentView uncaches the view and rewrites its properties through generateViewProperties with captureNewPath = false and the new ViewSchemaMode, then calls alterTable.

nodes.name: ShowViewsCommand
nodes.summary: LeafRunnableCommand for SHOW VIEWS [(IN|FROM) db] [LIKE pattern]. run() lists views from the session catalog (pattern or "*") and returns rows of namespace, view name and an isTemp flag.

nodes.name: ViewHelper
nodes.summary: Shared helper object for views (SQLConfHelper, Logging, CapturesConfig). Public methods: generateViewProperties (builds the stored properties: query output column names, current catalog and namespace, captured SQL configs, referred temp view/function/variable names, schema mode, frozen resolution path), checkCyclicViewReference, verifyAutoGeneratedAliasesNotExists, verifyTemporaryObjectsNotExists, collectTemporaryVariables, createTemporaryViewRelation, prepareTable and aliasPlan. Private helpers cover removing old properties (removeQueryColumnNames, removeSQLConfigs, removeResolutionPath, removeReferredTempNames), generateQueryColumnNames, viewSchemaModeToProps, referredTempNamesToProps, collectTemporaryViews, prepareTemporaryViewPlan, needsToUncache, prepareTemporaryView and prepareTemporaryViewStoringAnalyzedPlan.

nodes.name: CheckViewReferences
nodes.summary: Post-analysis check (LogicalPlan => Unit) for v2 CREATE VIEW and ALTER VIEW AS. For an analyzed CreateView it first requires a ViewCatalog (MISSING_CATALOG_ABILITY.VIEWS), then verifies no temporary objects or auto-generated aliases and, on replace, no cycles; for an analyzed AlterViewAs it runs the same checks without the capability check. Private helpers catalogAndIdent, fullIdentFor and requireViewCatalog extract the catalog and identifier from ResolvedIdentifier or ResolvedPersistentView.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes CREATE VIEW: validates analysis state and column list, checks temp object references and auto aliases, then creates a local or global temp view, or creates, skips, replaces (after cycle check, uncache and drop) or rejects a persistent view depending on allowExisting, replace and whether the existing object is a view. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: markAsAnalyzed
nodes.summary: Returns a copy with isAnalyzed = true and the referred temporary function names collected from the AnalysisContext.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs ALTER VIEW AS: checks temp object references and auto aliases, validates collations in the query schema, and dispatches to alterTemporaryView or alterPermanentView depending on whether the name is a temp view.

nodes.name: markAsAnalyzed
nodes.summary: Returns a copy marked as analyzed with the referred temporary function names taken from the AnalysisContext.

nodes.name: alterTemporaryView
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the TemporaryViewRelation for a local or global temp view (chosen by whether the name has a database) with replace = true and installs it with alterTempViewDefinition.

nodes.name: alterPermanentView
nodes.summary: Alters a persisted view: detects cyclic view references, uncaches the view, regenerates view properties from the new query output, and calls alterTable with the new raw schema, properties and view text.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Throws an error for temporary views, otherwise calls alterPermanentView to apply the new schema binding mode. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: alterPermanentView
nodes.summary: Uncaches the view and rewrites its properties with the new ViewSchemaMode (keeping the stored resolution path via captureNewPath = false), then updates the catalog table.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists views in the given database matching the optional pattern and maps each to a Row of quoted namespace, view name and temporary flag.

nodes.name: generateQueryColumnNames
nodes.summary: Builds the property map holding the number of view query output columns and each column name under a prefixed key.

nodes.name: viewSchemaModeToProps
nodes.summary: Converts a ViewSchemaMode to a property map; nothing is stored for SchemaUnsupported (for backward compatibility).

nodes.name: referredTempNamesToProps
nodes.summary: Serializes referred temporary view, function and variable names to JSON strings stored under the VIEW_REFERRED_TEMP_* property keys.

nodes.name: generateViewProperties
nodes.summary: Produces the property map stored with a view: removes old query column, SQL config, temp name and resolution path properties, then adds current catalog and namespace, captured SQL configs, query output column names (skipped for SCHEMA EVOLUTION), referred temp names, schema mode and the serialized resolution path. Checks the field names for duplicates first.

nodes.name: checkCyclicViewReference
nodes.summary: Walks the logical plan (including subquery expressions) and throws a recursive view error if the altered view appears again in the reference path.

nodes.name: verifyAutoGeneratedAliasesNotExists
nodes.summary: For a permanent view, throws an error if an output attribute carries the __autoGeneratedAlias metadata and the conf does not allow auto generated aliases.

nodes.name: verifyTemporaryObjectsNotExists
nodes.summary: For a permanent view, throws if the plan references temporary views, referred temporary functions or temporary variables.

nodes.name: collectTemporaryViews
nodes.summary: Collects the distinct name parts of all temporary views referenced in a plan, including those inside subquery expressions.

nodes.name: collectTemporaryVariables
nodes.summary: Collects the distinct original name parts of VariableReference expressions in a plan, descending into subqueries.

nodes.name: createTemporaryViewRelation
nodes.summary: Builds the TemporaryViewRelation for a temp view: decides whether the old view must be uncached (checking cycles when the analyzed plan is not stored), resolves the default collation, and either stores the original text with generated properties or stores the analyzed plan (rewriting DataSourceV2 relations to table references).

nodes.name: prepareTemporaryViewPlan
nodes.summary: Rewrites DataSourceV2Relation nodes that have a catalog and identifier and no time travel spec into V2TableReference nodes for the temp view.

nodes.name: needsToUncache
nodes.summary: Returns true unless the stored temp view plan gives the same result as the new aliased plan.

nodes.name: prepareTemporaryView
nodes.summary: Creates the CatalogTable (type VIEW) for a temp view that stores its original SQL text, with properties generated from the collected temp views, functions and variables.

nodes.name: prepareTemporaryViewStoringAnalyzedPlan
nodes.summary: Creates the CatalogTable for a temp view that stores the analyzed plan, marking it with the VIEW_STORING_ANALYZED_PLAN property.

nodes.name: prepareTable
nodes.summary: Creates the CatalogTable saved for a persistent view (type VIEW or METRIC_VIEW) with the aliased raw schema, generated properties, original text and comment; throws if the view was created through the Dataset API without original text.

nodes.name: aliasPlan
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged when no user columns are given, otherwise projects the plan output with Alias names and optional comment metadata (optionally retaining existing attribute metadata) and analyzes the projection.

nodes.name: catalogAndIdent
nodes.summary: Extracts the catalog and identifier from a ResolvedIdentifier or ResolvedPersistentView and throws an internal error for any other shape.

nodes.name: fullIdentFor
nodes.summary: Returns the full multipart identifier: catalog name followed by the identifier parts.

nodes.name: requireViewCatalog
nodes.summary: Throws the views-ability error if the resolved catalog is not a ViewCatalog.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Traverses the plan and, for each analyzed CreateView or AlterViewAs, runs the catalog capability, temp object, auto alias and (when replacing or altering) cycle checks against the full identifier.

nodes.name: ApplyCharTypePadding.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ApplyCharTypePadding optimizer-side rule that right-pads CHAR(N) values on read and in string comparisons, delegating the actual rewriting to ApplyCharTypePaddingHelper.

nodes.name: ApplyCharTypePadding
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] object. If conf.charVarcharAsString is set it returns the plan unchanged. When conf.readSideCharPadding is on it applies readSidePadding to LogicalRelation, DataSourceV2Relation and HiveTableRelation (cleaning char/varchar metadata from their output) and then pads string comparisons with padCharCol = false; otherwise it only pads comparisons, with padCharCol depending on SQLConf.LEGACY_NO_CHAR_PADDING_IN_PREDICATE.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Applies read-side padding to the three relation kinds and string comparison padding to the plan, or skips everything when char/varchar is treated as string.

nodes.name: BasicWriteStatsTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the basic write statistics classes for file writes: per-task stats (partitions, files, bytes, rows), the task-side tracker that measures them, and the job-side tracker that aggregates them into SQL metrics.

nodes.name: BasicWriteTaskStats
nodes.summary: Case class holding the simple metrics of one write task (partitions as InternalRows, numFiles, numBytes, numRows); it extends WriteTaskStats and is what BasicWriteTaskStatsTracker returns and BasicWriteJobStatsTracker aggregates.

nodes.name: BasicWriteTaskStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Task-side WriteTaskStatsTracker with Logging. It records new partitions, submitted files and row counts; on closeFile it looks up the file size through the Hadoop FileSystem (for zero-byte files it also tries the magic-committer extended attribute header) and adds to the file and byte totals. getFinalStats reports bytes and records written to the task output metrics, warns if the number of files seen differs from submitted files, adds the task commit time to the optional SQLMetric, and returns a BasicWriteTaskStats.

nodes.name: BasicWriteJobStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Serializable job-side WriteJobStatsTracker (range includes its companion object). newTaskInstance creates BasicWriteTaskStatsTracker instances for executors, and processStats sums the BasicWriteTaskStats and updates the driver side metrics (files, output bytes, output rows, dynamic partitions, job commit time) and posts them with SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricUpdates. An auxiliary constructor splits a metrics map into driver metrics and the task commit time metric. The companion object holds the metric keys (numFiles, numOutputBytes, numOutputRows, numParts, taskCommitTime, jobCommitTime), FILE_LENGTH_XATTR and the metrics factory.

nodes.name: getFileSize
nodes.summary: Returns the size of a written file or None if it is not found. Uses getFileStatus length when positive; for zero-byte files tries the XAttr FILE_LENGTH_XATTR header, parsing a non-negative length and ignoring parse or unsupported-operation failures. An overload at lines 71-75 takes a String path and resolves the FileSystem from hadoopConf.

nodes.name: closeFile
nodes.summary: Updates the file statistics for the closed file and removes it from the set of submitted files.

nodes.name: updateFileStats
nodes.summary: Adds the size of the file (when found) to numBytes and increments numFiles.

nodes.name: getFinalStats
nodes.summary: Publishes bytes and records written to the TaskContext output metrics, logs a warning if numSubmittedFiles differs from numFiles, adds the task commit time to the metric, and returns the BasicWriteTaskStats.

nodes.name: newTaskInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a BasicWriteTaskStatsTracker from the serializable Hadoop configuration and the task commit time metric.

nodes.name: processStats
nodes.summary: Casts the task stats to BasicWriteTaskStats, sums files, bytes, rows and the set of partitions, adds them with the job commit time to the driver side metrics, and posts the metric updates for the current SQL execution id.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Companion method creating the SQLMetrics map: number of written files, written output (size), number of output rows, number of dynamic parts, task commit time and job commit time.

nodes.name: BucketingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BucketingUtils, helpers for the bucket id embedded in bucketed file names and for computing bucket ids from values.

nodes.name: BucketingUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object. It holds a regex that finds the bucket id after the last underscore of a file name (before an optional extension), the reserved option name __hive_compatible_bucketed_table_insertion__ and four methods: getBucketId (file name to Option[Int]), getBucketIdFromValue (hash partitioning bucket id of a value), canBucketOn (false when the type has a non UTF8 binary collation) and bucketIdToString (formats the id as _ followed by five digits).

nodes.name: getBucketId
nodes.summary: Extracts the bucket id from a bucketed file name using the underscore-number pattern; returns None when the name does not match.

nodes.name: getBucketIdFromValue
nodes.summary: Computes the bucket id of one value: puts it in a SpecificInternalRow and evaluates the partitionIdExpression of HashPartitioning(bucketColumn, numBuckets) through an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: canBucketOn
nodes.summary: Returns true when the data type has no non UTF8 binary collation, using SchemaUtils.hasNonUTF8BinaryCollation.

nodes.name: bucketIdToString
nodes.summary: Formats a bucket id as the file name suffix, an underscore followed by the id zero padded to five digits.

nodes.name: VariableAssignmentUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines VariableAssignmentUtils, a helper shared by the SET and FETCH commands for assigning a value to a SQL variable that is either a scripting local variable or a session variable.

nodes.name: VariableAssignmentUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with the single method assignVariable. It chooses the variable manager from the VariableReference catalog (FakeLocalCatalog means the scripting context manager, FakeSystemCatalog means the session temp variable manager), validates that the variable exists, and stores a new VariableDefinition holding a Literal of the value.

nodes.name: assignVariable
nodes.summary: Assigns value to varRef: lower-cases the name parts unless the SQLConf is case sensitive, picks the scripting or session VariableManager, raises internal errors for missing scripting manager, missing local variable or unexpected catalog and an unresolved-variable error for a missing session variable, then calls set with the new VariableDefinition.

nodes.name: CatalogFileIndex.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CatalogFileIndex, the FileIndex used for a metastore catalog table; it lists partitions through the catalog and delegates file listing to an InMemoryFileIndex.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: CatalogFileIndex
nodes.summary: FileIndex for a metastore catalog table, built from a SparkSession, the CatalogTable metadata and the table size in bytes. It reports the partition schema and root path from the table, shares a global FileStatusCache, and implements filterPartitions (asks the catalog for partitions matching the pruning filters and returns an InMemoryFileIndex over just those partition paths, or over the table root when the table is not partitioned), listFiles, refresh (invalidates the status cache), inputFiles, and equals/hashCode keyed on the table identifier so it can be part of a cache key.

nodes.name: CatalogFileIndex.filterPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns an InMemoryFileIndex restricted to the partitions that match the given partition-pruning filters. For a partitioned table it lists partitions via ExternalCatalogUtils.listPartitionsByFilter, builds qualified PartitionPath entries and a PartitionSpec, and records the metadata operation time; otherwise it indexes the table root path.

nodes.name: CatalogFileIndex.listFiles
nodes.summary: Lists files by first calling filterPartitions with the partition filters and then listing the resulting InMemoryFileIndex with the data filters.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CodecStreams object with helpers that open compressed or plain input and output streams for data source files.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: CodecStreams
nodes.summary: Utility object for file streams. It creates input streams (optionally closed on task completion), creates output streams that apply the compression codec configured in the Hadoop JobContext or inferred from the file extension, builds an OutputStreamWriter, and reports the compression file extension.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.createInputStream
nodes.summary: Opens an input stream for a path by delegating to HadoopCodecStreams.createInputStream.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.createInputStreamWithCloseResource
nodes.summary: Creates an input stream and registers a task completion listener on the current TaskContext so the stream is closed when the task finishes.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.getCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns the compression codec: the configured output compressor class (default GzipCodec) if output compression is enabled, otherwise the codec matched from the file path extension, if any.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.createOutputStream
nodes.summary: Creates a new file (failing if it exists) and wraps the stream with the compression codec when one applies.

nodes.name: CodecStreams.createOutputStreamWriter
nodes.summary: Wraps createOutputStream in an OutputStreamWriter with a charset (UTF-8 by default).

nodes.name: CodecStreams.getCompressionExtension
nodes.summary: Returns the default file extension of the active compression codec, or an empty string when none is used.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DataSourceManager, a registry of user-defined Python data sources looked up by case-insensitive name, plus its companion that discovers static ones.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager
nodes.summary: Manager for user-defined data sources (class at lines 35-90, companion object at 93-134). The class registers a data source builder under a lowercased name (warning when it replaces an earlier one), looks it up by name (runtime registrations take precedence over static ones, and a missing name raises dataSourceDoesNotExist), checks existence, and clones itself with the runtime registrations. The companion lazily loads static Python data sources by calling UserDefinedPythonDataSource.lookupAllDataSourcesInPython when a Python executable is available, and tolerates lookup failures.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.registerDataSource
nodes.summary: Registers a data source builder under a normalized (lowercase) name and logs a warning if it replaces a runtime or static registration.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.lookupDataSource
nodes.summary: Returns the builder for a name or throws QueryCompilationErrors.dataSourceDoesNotExist.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.dataSourceExists
nodes.summary: Returns whether a data source with the given name exists, case-insensitively.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.getDataSource
nodes.summary: Private lookup that checks runtime registrations first and falls back to static ones.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.clone
nodes.summary: Creates a new DataSourceManager and re-registers every runtime data source into it.

nodes.name: DataSourceManager.initialStaticDataSourceBuilders
nodes.summary: Companion method that, when the default Python executable is available, loads Python data sources once (synchronized), logging and ignoring failures, and returns them as a lowercase-name map; returns an empty map otherwise.

nodes.name: DataSourceMetricsMixin.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataSourceMetricsMixin trait for data sources that expose SQL metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: DataSourceMetricsMixin
nodes.summary: Trait with one abstract method, getMetrics, returning a sequence of (name, SQLMetric) pairs. Data sources mix it in to publish their own metrics.

nodes.name: DataSourceResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DataSourceResolver, a ResolverExtension that resolves unresolved catalog relations by reusing FindDataSourceTable.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: DataSourceResolver
nodes.summary: ResolverExtension for nodes in the datasources package, kept as an extension to avoid cyclic dependencies between the resolver and datasources packages. Its resolveOperator handles UnresolvedCatalogRelation by delegating to FindDataSourceTable.resolveUnresolvedCatalogRelation, throws ExplicitlyUnsupportedResolverFeature when the result is a StreamingRelation or StreamingRelationV2, and returns None for any other operator.

nodes.name: DataSourceResolver.resolveOperator
nodes.summary: Resolves an UnresolvedCatalogRelation through FindDataSourceTable and rejects streaming relations with ExplicitlyUnsupportedResolverFeature; returns None for operators it does not handle.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataSourceUtils object with shared helpers for data sources: option and Hadoop conf handling, schema checks, datetime rebase logic, and partition/data filter splitting.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object extending PredicateHelper. Groups: (1) option helpers: mergeWriteOptionsIntoHadoopConf, setConfIfAbsent, generateDatasourceOptions, encode/decodePartitioningColumns and the keys __partition_columns, partitionOverwriteMode and __clustering_columns (lines 48-106, 292-314); (2) driver-side checks: checkFieldNames and verifySchema (112-141); (3) path and pushdown predicates: isDataPath, isDataFile, supportNestedPredicatePushdown, containsFiltersWithCollation (143-162, 355-366); (4) calendar rebase for Parquet and Avro: datetimeRebaseSpec, int96RebaseSpec, newRebaseExceptionInRead/Write and the createDateRebaseFunc and createTimestampRebaseFunc builders (164-290); (5) getPartitionFiltersAndDataFilters overloads (316-353); and shouldIgnoreCorruptFileException.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.mergeWriteOptionsIntoHadoopConf
nodes.summary: Copies non-null write options into a Hadoop Configuration, skipping the keys "path" and "paths" and using the original key casing when the map is case-insensitive.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.setConfIfAbsent
nodes.summary: Sets a Hadoop conf key to a by-name value only when the key is not already set, so per-write options win over session defaults.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.encodePartitioningColumns
nodes.summary: Serializes a sequence of partition column names to a JSON string using json4s Serialization.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.decodePartitioningColumns
nodes.summary: Parses the JSON string produced by encodePartitioningColumns back into column names.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.checkFieldNames
nodes.summary: Recursively checks that every field name in a schema (including nested structs) is supported by the FileFormat, throwing invalidColumnNameAsPathError otherwise. Meant to run on the driver.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.verifySchema
nodes.summary: Fails on unsupported data types and checks every field against FileFormat.supportDataType (or supportReadDataType when read-only), throwing dataTypeUnsupportedByDataSourceError.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.supportNestedPredicatePushdown
nodes.summary: Returns true when the relation is a HadoopFsRelation whose name is in the NESTED_PREDICATE_PUSHDOWN_FILE_SOURCE_LIST setting.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.getRebaseSpec
nodes.summary: Private helper deciding the datetime rebase policy: forces CORRECTED in tests when spark.test.forceNoRebase is true; otherwise uses the file writer version and a legacy metadata key to choose LEGACY or CORRECTED, falling back to the configured mode. Returns a RebaseSpec that carries the file time zone for LEGACY.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.datetimeRebaseSpec
nodes.summary: Builds the RebaseSpec for date and timestamp values using minimum version 3.0.0 and the legacy datetime metadata key.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.int96RebaseSpec
nodes.summary: Builds the RebaseSpec for INT96 timestamps using minimum version 3.1.0 and the legacy INT96 metadata key.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.newRebaseExceptionInRead
nodes.summary: Creates the SparkUpgradeException for ancient dates read from Parquet INT96, Parquet or Avro, naming the matching config key and option.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.newRebaseExceptionInWrite
nodes.summary: Creates the SparkUpgradeException for ancient dates written as Parquet INT96, Parquet or Avro, naming the matching config key.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.shouldIgnoreCorruptFileException
nodes.summary: Returns true for RuntimeException, IOException or InternalError, the failures that may be skipped when ignoring corrupt files.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.createDateRebaseFuncInRead
nodes.summary: Returns an Int-to-Int function for date days on read: throws for pre-switch days in EXCEPTION mode, rebases Julian to Gregorian in LEGACY mode, identity in CORRECTED mode.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.createDateRebaseFuncInWrite
nodes.summary: Returns an Int-to-Int function for date days on write: throws for pre-switch days in EXCEPTION mode, rebases Gregorian to Julian in LEGACY mode, identity in CORRECTED mode.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.createTimestampRebaseFuncInRead
nodes.summary: Returns a Long-to-Long function for timestamp microseconds on read, following the RebaseSpec mode and its time zone.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.createTimestampRebaseFuncInWrite
nodes.summary: Returns a Long-to-Long function for timestamp microseconds on write, using the session local time zone in LEGACY mode.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.generateDatasourceOptions
nodes.summary: Merges the extra read options with table storage properties and the table location as "path". Unless the legacy extra-options behavior is on, it fails when an extra option conflicts with a table property and drops case-insensitive duplicates.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.getPartitionFiltersAndDataFilters
nodes.summary: Splits normalized filters into partition filters and data filters, by schema column names or by attribute ExprIds (three overloads: two public at 322 and 338, one private at 344); also adds extra partition predicates extracted from data filters using PredicateHelper.

nodes.name: DataSourceUtils.containsFiltersWithCollation
nodes.summary: Recursively checks a sources.Filter tree (And, Or, Not) for a CollatedFilter.

nodes.name: DaysWritable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DaysWritable, a DateWritable that keeps Gregorian and Julian day counts and rebases when reading and writing.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: DaysWritable
nodes.summary: DateWritable subclass that stores days in both the Gregorian calendar and the Julian calendar. Dates are exposed as Julian days (getDays, get) and written and read as Julian VInt values, which keeps files compatible with Spark 2.4 and earlier for dates before 1582-10-15. It has constructors from no arguments, Gregorian days, or another DateWritable, and set and readFields recompute the other calendar value with the rebase functions.

nodes.name: DaysWritable.set
nodes.summary: Sets the Gregorian days and recomputes the Julian days by rebasing.

nodes.name: DaysWritable.write
nodes.summary: Writes the Julian days as a variable-length int to the output.

nodes.name: DaysWritable.readFields
nodes.summary: Reads Julian days as a variable-length int and derives the Gregorian days by rebasing.

nodes.name: ExternalEngineDatasourceRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExternalEngineDatasourceRDD marker trait for relations that read from an external database engine.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: ExternalEngineDatasourceRDD
nodes.summary: Trait to be implemented by relations that access external database engines; it declares getExternalEngineQuery, which returns the query string sent to the engine.

nodes.name: FallBackFileSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FallBackFileSourceV2 rule that rewrites inserts into file source V2 tables to use the V1 FileFormat.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: FallBackFileSourceV2
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] that replaces a File source V2 table inside an InsertIntoStatement with a LogicalRelation over a HadoopFsRelation built from the table fallback FileFormat, because a view over a file V2 source has no physical plan for inserts. The source calls it a temporary hack until catalog support for file data source V2 is finished.

nodes.name: FallBackFileSourceV2.apply
nodes.summary: Resolves operators in the plan: for each InsertIntoStatement targeting a FileTable it instantiates the fallback FileFormat, builds a HadoopFsRelation from the table file index and schema, and replaces the target with a LogicalRelation.

nodes.name: FileFormatDataWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the per-task data writers used when Spark writes file-based data sources: an abstract base writer, an empty-directory writer, a single-directory writer, two dynamic partition/bucket writers (single and concurrent), plus the shared WriteJobDescription, WriterBucketSpec and result/summary case classes. Used by FileFormatWriter on executors to turn InternalRows into output files and report commit results.

nodes.name: FileFormatDataWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for writing data out in a single Spark task. It extends DataWriter[InternalRow], keeps the current OutputWriter, the set of updated partitions and the stats trackers, wraps writes with error enrichment and custom metric updates (writeWithMetrics, writeWithIterator), and on commit() releases resources, commits the task through the FileCommitProtocol and returns a WriteTaskResult. abort() releases resources and aborts the task.

nodes.name: EmptyDirectoryDataWriter
nodes.summary: Task writer used for empty partitions. Its write() does nothing, so the task only goes through the commit path of the base writer.

nodes.name: SingleDirectoryDataWriter
nodes.summary: Writes rows to a single directory (non-dynamic-partition writes). It opens a new OutputWriter through newOutputWriter, which asks the FileCommitProtocol for a temp file named with a -cNNN counter, and rolls to a new file once maxRecordsPerFile records have been written.

nodes.name: BaseDynamicPartitionDataWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract base with the common logic of dynamic partition or bucket writes. It builds projections for partition values, the partition path string (col=val/col=val), the bucket id and the output data row, and provides renewCurrentWriter (opens a new file for a partition and bucket, using custom partition locations when present), renewCurrentWriterIfTooManyRecords and writeRecord. It asserts that the data is partitioned or bucketed.

nodes.name: DynamicPartitionDataSingleWriter
nodes.summary: Dynamic partition writer that keeps only one writer open at a time. It requires input sorted on partition and/or bucket columns, opens a new file when the partition or bucket changes, and starts a new file when the record limit per file is reached.

nodes.name: DynamicPartitionDataConcurrentWriter
nodes.summary: Dynamic partition writer that keeps several writers open at once in a map keyed by partition and bucket. When the number of concurrent writers reaches the maxWriters threshold (config SQLConf.MAX_CONCURRENT_OUTPUT_FILE_WRITERS) it falls back to sorting the remaining rows and writing them sequentially. Callers use writeWithIterator instead of write.

nodes.name: WriterIndex
nodes.summary: Private case class used as the key of the concurrent writer map: a mutable pair of optional partition values and optional bucket id.

nodes.name: WriterStatus
nodes.summary: Private class holding the state of one concurrent writer: its OutputWriter, the number of records in the current file and the file counter.

nodes.name: releaseCurrentWriter
nodes.summary: Closes the current OutputWriter, tells the stats trackers the file is closed, and clears the reference even if closing fails.

nodes.name: releaseResources
nodes.summary: Releases all resources of the task writer; by default only the current writer. Subclasses with more writers override it.

nodes.name: enrichWriteError
nodes.summary: Runs a block and converts failures: FetchFailedException is rethrown, FileAlreadyExistsException becomes TaskOutputFileAlreadyExistException when fast-fail is on, any other Throwable becomes taskFailedWhileWritingRowsError for the given path.

nodes.name: writeWithMetrics
nodes.summary: Writes one record under enrichWriteError and refreshes custom metrics every CustomMetrics.NUM_ROWS_PER_UPDATE rows.

nodes.name: writeWithIterator
nodes.summary: Writes all records of an iterator through writeWithMetrics and updates the custom metrics at the end.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Releases resources, commits the task with the FileCommitProtocol while timing it, collects the final stats of each tracker and returns a WriteTaskResult with an ExecutedWriteSummary containing the updated partitions.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Releases resources and then aborts the task through the FileCommitProtocol.

nodes.name: newOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Resets the record count, releases resources, asks the committer for a new task temp file with a -cNNN counter and the format file extension, creates the OutputWriter from the OutputWriterFactory and registers the new file with the stats trackers.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Rolls to a new file when maxRecordsPerFile is reached, then writes the row to the current writer and notifies the stats trackers.

nodes.name: renewCurrentWriter
nodes.summary: Opens a new OutputWriter for a partition and/or bucket: optionally closes the old one, records the partition directory as updated, builds the file name prefix and suffix from the bucket id and file counter, picks the committer temp path (absolute custom path when a custom partition location exists) and registers the file with stats trackers.

nodes.name: renewCurrentWriterIfTooManyRecords
nodes.summary: Increments the file counter, asserts it is below the maximum, and renews the current writer after the per-file record limit was exceeded.

nodes.name: writeRecord
nodes.summary: Projects the input row to the data columns, writes it to the current writer, notifies stats trackers and counts the record.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Compares the partition values and bucket id of the incoming row with the current ones; on a change it resets the file counter and renews the writer, otherwise it renews it only when the record limit is hit; then writes the record.

nodes.name: releaseResources
nodes.summary: Closes every writer held in the concurrent writers map, tells the stats trackers, and clears the map.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Switches the current writer when the partition or bucket changes (keeping it in the map unless already in sorted fallback mode), sets up the writer from the map, renews it when the record limit is hit, and writes the record.

nodes.name: writeWithIterator
nodes.summary: Writes records with concurrent writers until the sorted fallback is triggered; remaining rows are then sorted with the sorter from ConcurrentOutputWriterSpec and written one by one.

nodes.name: updateCurrentWriterStatusInMap
nodes.summary: Stores the current writer, record count and file counter back into the status entry of the concurrent writers map.

nodes.name: setupCurrentWriterUsingMap
nodes.summary: Takes the current writer from the map or creates a new one, asserts the writer count limits and logs and switches to sorted mode when the max concurrent writers threshold is reached.

nodes.name: clearCurrentWriterStatus
nodes.summary: Saves the current writer status to the map if it has a partition or bucket, then resets the current writer id, writer and counters.

nodes.name: WriterBucketSpec
nodes.summary: Case class with the bucketing specification used by all write tasks: the bucketIdExpression that computes a bucket id from the bucket columns, and bucketFileNamePrefix, a function from bucket id to the output file name prefix.

nodes.name: WriteJobDescription
nodes.summary: Serializable job description shared by all write tasks: uuid, Hadoop conf, OutputWriterFactory, all/data/partition columns, optional WriterBucketSpec, output path, custom partition locations, maxRecordsPerFile, time zone and the WriteJobStatsTracker list. It asserts that all columns equal partition plus data columns.

nodes.name: WriteTaskResult
nodes.summary: Case class returned by a successful write task: the TaskCommitMessage plus the ExecutedWriteSummary. It extends WriterCommitMessage.

nodes.name: ExecutedWriteSummary
nodes.summary: Case class with the metrics of a write task: the set of updated partitions (valid for dynamic partitions) and one WriteTaskStats per WriteJobStatsTracker.

nodes.name: FileIndexOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the option names that the file index understands (ignoreMissingFiles, ignoreInvalidPartitionPaths, the time zone option, recursiveFileLookup, basePath, modifiedbefore, modifiedafter, pathglobfilter).

nodes.name: FileIndexOptions
nodes.summary: Object extending DataSourceOptions that registers the file index option names with newOption: IGNORE_MISSING_FILES, IGNORE_INVALID_PARTITION_PATHS, TIME_ZONE, RECURSIVE_FILE_LOOKUP, BASE_PATH_PARAM, MODIFIED_BEFORE, MODIFIED_AFTER and PATH_GLOB_FILTER.

nodes.name: FileResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Resolver extension that resolves unresolved relations created out of files by reusing the ResolveSQLOnFile rule.

nodes.name: FileResolver
nodes.summary: ResolverExtension that resolves an UnresolvedRelation created out of a file path by reusing the ResolveSQLOnFile rule. It is an extension to avoid cyclic dependencies between the resolver and datasources packages; resolveOperator returns the resolved plan or None.

nodes.name: UnresolvedRelationResolution
nodes.summary: Nested extractor object whose unapply runs ResolveSQLOnFile's UnresolvedRelationResolution inside AnalysisHelper.allowInvokingTransformsInAnalyzer, because that path calls the analyzer again on a leaf node.

nodes.name: resolveOperator
nodes.summary: Matches the operator with UnresolvedRelationResolution and returns the resolved relation, or None when it does not apply.

nodes.name: HadoopFileLinesReader.scala
nodes.summary: Adapter that turns a PartitionedFile into an iterator of Text lines using a Hadoop line record reader.

nodes.name: HadoopFileLinesReader
nodes.summary: Iterator[Text] and Closeable over all lines of a part of a file (PartitionedFile). It builds a FileSplit and a task attempt context, picks HadoopLineRecordReader or LineRecordReader depending on SQLConf hadoopLineRecordReaderEnabled, passes an optional line separator, and wraps the reader in a RecordReaderIterator. With no separator it covers CR, CRLF and LF.

nodes.name: HadoopFileWholeTextReader.scala
nodes.summary: Adapter that turns a PartitionedFile into an iterator of Text holding whole-file content through WholeTextFileRecordReader.

nodes.name: HadoopFileWholeTextReader
nodes.summary: Iterator[Text] and Closeable over the content of a PartitionedFile. It wraps the file in a CombineFileSplit, builds a task attempt context, initializes a WholeTextFileRecordReader and exposes it through a RecordReaderIterator.

nodes.name: InsertIntoDataSourceCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the command that inserts query results into a data source relation implementing InsertableRelation.

nodes.name: InsertIntoDataSourceCommand
nodes.summary: Case class LeafRunnableCommand (with CTEInChildren) that inserts the result of a query into a LogicalRelation whose relation is an InsertableRelation. run() builds a Dataset from the query, calls relation.insert(data, overwrite), then re-caches cached plans referring to the relation. withCTEDefs wraps the query in WithCTE.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates a Dataset from the query, inserts it into the InsertableRelation with the overwrite flag, recaches plans that refer to the relation and returns no rows.

nodes.name: withCTEDefs
nodes.summary: Returns a copy whose query is wrapped in WithCTE with the given CTE definitions.

nodes.name: InsertIntoHadoopFsRelationCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the V1 write command that writes a query to a HadoopFsRelation path, handling save modes, static and dynamic partition overwrite, catalog partition updates and cache refresh.

nodes.name: InsertIntoHadoopFsRelationCommand
nodes.summary: Case class V1WriteCommand for writing data to a HadoopFsRelation; supports append, overwrite and dynamic partition writes. run() validates column names, finds partitions tracked by the catalog and their custom locations, creates a FileCommitProtocol, applies the SaveMode (ErrorIfExists, Overwrite, Append, Ignore), calls FileFormatWriter.write, then updates catalog partitions, refreshes the FileIndex, recaches data and updates table stats. dynamicPartitionOverwrite is true for DYNAMIC overwrite mode with fewer static partitions than partition columns; requiredOrdering comes from V1WritesUtils.getSortOrder.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main execution: checks duplicate column names and map-key collations, resolves the output path and catalog partitions, creates the committer, decides whether to insert based on SaveMode and existing path, runs FileFormatWriter.write with a basic stats tracker, then refreshes catalog partitions (add and drop), the FileIndex and cached data, and updates table stats.

nodes.name: deleteMatchingPartitions
nodes.summary: Deletes partition files matching the static partition prefix and all custom partition locations through committer.deleteWithJob, failing with an error if clearing fails.

nodes.name: getCustomPartitionLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the partitions whose catalog location differs from the default k=v/k=v location, as a map from partition spec to custom location.

nodes.name: LogicalRelationResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Resolver extension that accepts already-built LogicalRelation nodes as resolved.

nodes.name: LogicalRelationResolver
nodes.summary: ResolverExtension that completes resolution of LogicalRelation nodes: resolveOperator returns the relation unchanged when the operator is a LogicalRelation, otherwise None.

nodes.name: resolveOperator
nodes.summary: Returns Some(relation) for a LogicalRelation operator and None for anything else.

nodes.name: OutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OutputWriterFactory and OutputWriter, the abstractions used to persist rows of a HadoopFsRelation into files.

nodes.name: OutputWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable abstract factory created on the driver for each write job to a HadoopFsRelation and shipped to executors. getFileExtension returns the file extension and newInstance creates an OutputWriter for a path, data schema and Hadoop task context.

nodes.name: OutputWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract writer for one output file on the executor side. Subclasses implement write(row) to persist a row, close() to finish the file before task commit, and path() for the file path; they must have a zero-argument constructor.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Abstract method called by each task on the executor to create a new OutputWriter for a file path, data schema and task context.

nodes.name: PartitioningUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Partition discovery helpers for file based sources: parses directory paths like a=1/b=hello into typed partition values and a PartitionSpec, infers and widens partition column types, converts raw strings to catalyst values, and validates or merges partition schemas. Defines PartitionPath, PartitionSpec and the PartitioningUtils object (lines 48-668).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object mixing in SQLConfHelper; parsePartitions is overloaded (time zone id string or ZoneId).

nodes.name: PartitionPath
nodes.summary: Companion object and case class pairing a directory Path with the partition values (an InternalRow) found in it. The companion apply(values, path: String) builds one from a string path. Before scanning, the files under the path must still be enumerated.

nodes.name: PartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Case class holding the partition column StructType and the list of PartitionPath entries of a partitioned file dataset. The companion object defines emptySpec, used when the dataset is not partitioned.

nodes.name: PartitioningUtils
nodes.summary: Object (extends SQLConfHelper) holding the partition discovery logic: parsePartitions and parsePartition read column names and values out of paths, parsePathFragment and getPathFragment convert between a=1/b=2 fragments and specs, resolvePartitions and findWiderTypeForPartitionColumn settle type conflicts across paths, inferPartitionColumnValue guesses a type from a string, castPartValueToDesiredType converts it, and validatePartitionColumn, canPartitionOn, partitionColumnsSchema and mergeDataAndPartitionSchema check and combine schemas. Also defines timePartitionPattern and timestampPartitionPattern.
