nodes.name: TypedPartValue
nodes.summary: Case class holding a raw partition string value together with the DataType chosen for it. Used while resolving type conflicts between partitions.

nodes.name: PartitionValues
nodes.summary: Case class pairing the partition column names of one path with their TypedPartValue entries. It requires both sequences to have the same size.

nodes.name: parsePartitions
nodes.summary: Parses a group of qualified paths into a PartitionSpec. Parses each path with parsePartition, throws a conflicting directory structure error if base paths differ (unless invalid paths are ignored), resolves type conflicts with resolvePartitions, builds the nullable partition column StructType (honouring user specified names and types) and casts values with castPartValueToDesiredType. An overload at lines 104-115 takes a time zone id string and delegates here.

nodes.name: parsePartition
nodes.summary: Parses one path by walking up its parents, collecting name=value segments via parsePartitionColumn until a base path or the root is reached or a segment cannot be parsed. Returns the partition values and the path where discovery stopped, and ignores _temporary directories.

nodes.name: parsePartitionColumn
nodes.summary: Parses a single path segment such as a=1 into a column name and TypedPartValue. Fails on an empty name or value, uses the user supplied data type when present, otherwise infers the type with inferPartitionColumnValue.

nodes.name: parsePathFragment
nodes.summary: Parses a partition path fragment like fieldOne=1/fieldTwo=2 into a TablePartitionSpec map by calling parsePathFragmentAsSeq.

nodes.name: parsePathFragmentAsSeq
nodes.summary: Splits a partition path fragment on slash and equals signs and unescapes names and values, returning a sequence of string pairs.

nodes.name: getPathFragment
nodes.summary: Inverse of parsePathFragment: builds the escaped name=value path fragment for a partition spec following the partition schema order, stripping leading zeros of numeric values. An overload at lines 375-377 accepts a sequence of Attributes.

nodes.name: removeLeadingZerosFromNumberTypePartition
nodes.summary: For numeric data types, casts the partition string to the type and back to a string so leading zeros disappear; other types are returned unchanged.

nodes.name: resolvePartitions
nodes.summary: Checks that all paths have the same partition column names (case sensitivity optional), raising a conflicting partition columns error otherwise, then unifies the type of each column across paths with resolveTypeConflicts.

nodes.name: conflictingPartitionColumnsError
nodes.summary: Builds the SparkRuntimeException listing the distinct partition column name lists and the suspicious paths, used by resolvePartitions.

nodes.name: inferPartitionColumnValue
nodes.summary: Infers the DataType of a raw partition value string. With type inference on, tries Integer, Long, Decimal (scale <= 0), Double, timestamp, date and time in that order, falling back to String, or NullType for the default partition name. Without inference it returns String or NullType. The doc comment holds the conflict resolution table.

nodes.name: castPartValueToDesiredType
nodes.summary: Converts a partition value string into the catalyst internal value for a desired data type (numeric, decimal, string, date, time, timestamp, interval, binary, boolean). Returns null for the default partition name and throws an internal error for unsupported types.

nodes.name: validatePartitionColumn
nodes.summary: Validates partition columns for a write: checks duplicates, that each column exists and has a partitionable type, and that not all columns are used for partitioning.

nodes.name: canPartitionOn
nodes.summary: Returns whether a data type can be a partition column: only binary ordered strings and atomic types other than variant.

nodes.name: partitionColumnsSchema
nodes.summary: Looks up the given partition column names in a schema (using the configured resolver) and returns them as a nullable StructType, failing if a column is not in the schema.

nodes.name: mergeDataAndPartitionSchema
nodes.summary: Merges data and partition schemas. Overlapping columns keep the data schema position but take the partition schema data type; returns the full schema and the map of overlapping partition columns.

nodes.name: getColName
nodes.summary: Returns a field name as is when case sensitive, otherwise lower cased.

nodes.name: resolveTypeConflicts
nodes.summary: Reduces the data types of a column's typed values with findWiderTypeForPartitionColumn and applies the widest type to all values.

nodes.name: findWiderTypeForPartitionColumn
nodes.summary: Function value widening two partition column types: double with decimal or long falls back to String to avoid precision loss; other pairs use TypeCoercion.findWiderTypeForTwo, else String.

nodes.name: PushVariantIntoScan.scala
nodes.summary: Optimizer rule that pushes variant field extraction into Parquet scans: variant columns are rewritten to structs of requested fields (annotated with VariantMetadata) and variant_get or cast expressions become struct field accesses. Contains VariantMetadata, RequestedVariantField, StructPath, VariantInRelation and the PushVariantIntoScan rule.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses extractor objects (unapply) for pattern matching on expression trees and a case-class metadata encoding stored in StructField metadata.

nodes.name: VariantMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class (path, failOnError, timeZoneId) describing one variant extraction, stored as StructField metadata under the key __VARIANT_METADATA_KEY. toMetadata writes it, fromMetadata reads it back, parsedPath parses the JSON path, and the companion isVariantStruct tells whether a struct has all fields annotated with this metadata (a 'variant struct').

nodes.name: RequestedVariantField
nodes.summary: Case class of a VariantMetadata path and target DataType that the scan must produce for one variant extraction. The companion offers fullVariant (path $, type VariantType) and apply overloads building it from a VariantGet or a Cast.

nodes.name: StructPath
nodes.summary: Extractor object: matches an expression that is an Attribute or nested GetStructField accesses on one, returning the root ExprId and the sequence of field ordinals (empty for plain attribute access).

nodes.name: VariantInRelation
nodes.summary: Tracks all eligible variant columns of a relation (those at the root or nested only in structs) in a mapping from root attribute id to struct path to requested fields. Usage order: addVariantFields, collectRequestedFields over dependent expressions, rewriteType for the new schema, rewriteExpr to turn variant extractions into struct accesses.

nodes.name: StructPathToVariant
nodes.summary: Nested extractor that matches a StructPath whose target is a tracked variant in the mapping and returns its map of requested fields.

nodes.name: PushVariantIntoScan
nodes.summary: Optimizer Rule[LogicalPlan] that, when SQLConf.PUSH_VARIANT_INTO_SCAN is on, finds project/filter over a Parquet HadoopFsRelation (via PhysicalOperation and LogicalRelationWithTable) and rewrites variant columns into structs of requested fields, rewriting the plan expressions to read struct fields. Skips correlated subqueries and returns the plan unchanged when no variant is eligible.

nodes.name: toMetadata
nodes.summary: Encodes this VariantMetadata as a Spark Metadata with one entry under METADATA_KEY holding path, failOnError and timeZoneId.

nodes.name: parsedPath
nodes.summary: Parses the path into a VariantPathSegment array with VariantPathParser, throwing an invalid variant get path error (named variant_get or try_variant_get) on failure.

nodes.name: isVariantStruct
nodes.summary: Companion helper returning true when a StructType is non-empty and every field carries the variant metadata key; the overload at 74-77 accepts any DataType.

nodes.name: fromMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads a VariantMetadata back from a Metadata produced by toMetadata.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Overloaded companion factories creating a RequestedVariantField from a VariantGet (foldable path) or from a Cast (path $, failOnError unless TRY mode); both overloads share this node.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Extractor method returning the root ExprId and ordinal path for attribute or GetStructField chains, otherwise None.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Looks up the StructPath of an expression in the mapping and returns the requested field map for that variant, if tracked.

nodes.name: addVariantFields
nodes.summary: Recursively registers variant leaves (with null default value) found at root or inside non-variant structs into the mapping, recording their struct ordinal path.

nodes.name: rewriteType
nodes.summary: Produces the new data type for a column: each tracked variant becomes a struct of its requested fields (field names are ordinals, metadata is the VariantMetadata), using a placeholder field when none was requested; structs are rewritten recursively.

nodes.name: addField
nodes.summary: Adds a RequestedVariantField to a variant's map, giving it the next ordinal if not already present.

nodes.name: collectRequestedFields
nodes.summary: Visits an expression to record variant_get and cast accesses as requested fields, full variant accesses as the fullVariant field, ignores IsNull and IsNotNull, and removes variants whose enclosing struct is used directly (not eligible).

nodes.name: rewriteExpr
nodes.summary: Rewrites expressions using transformDown so variant_get, cast and full variant uses become GetStructField accesses on the rewritten attribute, and other attributes map to the new AttributeReferences.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: leaves correlated subqueries and plans alone when the PUSH_VARIANT_INTO_SCAN config is off, otherwise transformDown matching Parquet HadoopFsRelation scans under projects and filters and calls rewritePlan.

nodes.name: rewritePlan
nodes.summary: Builds a VariantInRelation for the relation schema (using existence default values), collects requested fields from project and filter expressions, rewrites the schema, relation, filter and project list (wrapping non-named results in Alias), and returns the original plan when nothing is eligible.

nodes.name: RecordReaderIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Adaptor that exposes a Hadoop RecordReader as a Scala Iterator over the values it returns, closing the reader early at end of input. Used by file format readers to iterate rows or column batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns Objects rather than InternalRow because column batches are passed as if they were rows via type erasure.

nodes.name: RecordReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Generic class RecordReaderIterator[T] that extends Iterator[T] with Closeable over a Hadoop RecordReader[_, T]. hasNext advances the reader with nextKeyValue and closes it once exhausted, next returns getCurrentValue (or throws an end of stream error), map wraps the iterator while keeping it Closeable, and close releases the reader exactly once.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Calls nextKeyValue on the reader when no pair is buffered; on end of input marks finished and closes the reader early to release resources.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the reader's current value after checking hasNext, throwing an end of stream error when exhausted.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Returns a mapped Iterator that is still Closeable and delegates hasNext, next and close to this iterator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying RecordReader once and nulls the reference, safe to call repeatedly.

nodes.name: SaveIntoDataSourceCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SaveIntoDataSourceCommand, the runnable command that writes the result of a query through a CreatableRelationProvider and then refreshes cached data for the resulting relation.

nodes.name: SaveIntoDataSourceCommand
nodes.summary: Case class (query, dataSource, options, mode) extending LeafRunnableCommand with CTEInChildren. run calls CreatableRelationProvider.createRelation with a Dataset of the query, rewrites some data source exceptions into a friendlier error, then recaches by plan through the CacheManager. It differs from InsertIntoDataSourceCommand, which uses InsertableRelation.insert. simpleString redacts options, clone keeps the options map, withCTEDefs wraps the query in WithCTE.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the relation through dataSource.createRelation (mapping NullPointerException, MatchError and ArrayIndexOutOfBounds into an external data source error, passing SparkThrowable through), then tries to recache plans referring to the new LogicalRelation, ignoring non fatal failures. Returns an empty Seq of rows.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Renders the command string with the data source, redacted options and save mode.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Recreates the command with a cloned query so the options map is kept as is (default clone would turn a CaseInsensitiveMap into a normal map).

nodes.name: withCTEDefs
nodes.summary: Copies the command with the query wrapped in WithCTE using the given CTE definitions.

nodes.name: SchemaMergeUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Provides SchemaMergeUtils.mergeSchemasInParallel, which merges Parquet or ORC file schemas by running a Spark job over file path and length pairs and then merging the partial results on the driver.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around non-serializable FileStatus by shipping only path and length and recreating fake FileStatus objects on executors.

nodes.name: SchemaMergeUtils
nodes.summary: Object (extends Logging) with one method, mergeSchemasInParallel. The caller passes a schemaReader function that reads schemas from a list of files; the object distributes the file info, merges per partition and then on the driver, raising a failed merging schema error on conflict.

nodes.name: mergeSchemasInParallel
nodes.summary: Serializes the Hadoop conf, keeps only (path, length) of each FileStatus, parallelizes them with a bounded partition count, and inside withSQLConfPropagated reads schemas per partition with the supplied reader (honouring ignoreCorruptFiles and ignoreMissingFiles) and merges them. Merges the partial schemas on the driver and returns None when there are no files.

nodes.name: ddl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines three plan nodes of the datasources package: CreateTable (an unresolved logical plan describing a table to create, optionally with data), CreateTempViewUsing (a runnable command that creates a local or global temporary view on a data source) and RefreshResource (a command that refreshes cached data for a path). Analysis rules replace or run them later.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case classes; CreateTable is a LogicalPlan that always reports itself as unresolved, the other two extend LeafRunnableCommand.

nodes.name: CreateTable
nodes.summary: Logical plan that carries a CatalogTable description, a SaveMode and an optional query for CREATE TABLE and CTAS. It asserts a provider is set, only allows ErrorIfExists or Ignore when there is no query, has the query as its only child, no output and is always unresolved, so it must be replaced by concrete implementations during analysis. Method locationQualifiedOrAbsent tells whether the table location is absolute or missing; rules.scala refers to this class under the alias CreateTableV1.

nodes.name: locationQualifiedOrAbsent
nodes.summary: Returns true when the table storage location is absolute or not set, false otherwise; used to detect locations that still need to be qualified.

nodes.name: CreateTempViewUsing
nodes.summary: Runnable command that creates or replaces a local or global temporary view backed by a data source given by provider, optional user schema and options. It rejects a database qualifier in the view name at construction; run refuses the Hive provider, resolves the source (a DataSourceV2 table provider if one is found, else a DataSource relation), analyzes the plan and registers it as a temp or global temp view in the session catalog. argString renders the command for plan display with options redacted.

nodes.name: argString
nodes.summary: Builds the display string of the command from table identifier, optional schema, replace flag, provider and redacted options.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes the command: loads the data source (V2 provider first, otherwise a DataSource relation wrapped in LogicalRelation), analyzes it, and creates a global temp view in the configured global temp database or a local temp view, returning no rows.

nodes.name: RefreshResource
nodes.summary: Runnable command holding a path; its run method calls the session catalog's refreshByPath for that path and returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Refreshes cached data and metadata for the stored path through sparkSession.catalog.refreshByPath and returns an empty row sequence.

nodes.name: pathFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the path filter strategies that file data sources use to skip files while listing: a glob filter, and modifiedBefore and modifiedAfter filters on file modification time, plus PathFilterFactory that builds the active filters from the read options.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala traits with companion objects acting as builders; each filter class has a companion object extending StrategyBuilder.

nodes.name: PathFilterStrategy
nodes.summary: Serializable trait with a single method accept(FileStatus) that decides whether a file should be kept.

nodes.name: StrategyBuilder
nodes.summary: Trait with create(parameters) that returns an optional PathFilterStrategy built from case-insensitive read options.

nodes.name: PathGlobFilter
nodes.summary: Filter that wraps a Hadoop GlobFilter built from a pattern and accepts files whose path matches it. Its companion object is a StrategyBuilder that creates the filter when the option FileIndexOptions.PATH_GLOB_FILTER is present.

nodes.name: accept
nodes.summary: Accepts a file when the glob filter matches the file status path.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builder method in the companion object: creates a PathGlobFilter if the path glob filter option is set, else None.

nodes.name: ModifiedDateFilter
nodes.summary: Abstract base of the time based filters. It declares timeZoneId and a protected localTime that converts microseconds with DateTimeUtils.fromUTCTime. Its companion object has getTimeZoneId (reads the timeZone option or the session local time zone) and toThreshold (parses a timestamp string, throwing a compilation error for an invalid value). The scaladoc shows modifiedAfter and modifiedBefore reader option examples.

nodes.name: getTimeZoneId
nodes.summary: Returns the time zone id from the read options or falls back to the session local time zone from SQLConf.

nodes.name: toThreshold
nodes.summary: Parses a timestamp string in the given time zone into a microsecond threshold, failing with an invalid-timestamp error naming the strategy.

nodes.name: ModifiedBeforeFilter
nodes.summary: Filter that keeps files whose modification time, converted to microseconds and local time, is before a threshold. Its companion object builds it from the option FileIndexOptions.MODIFIED_BEFORE.

nodes.name: accept
nodes.summary: Accepts a file if the threshold minus the local modification time in microseconds is positive.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builder method in the companion object: if the modifiedBefore option is set, parses it with toThreshold and returns a ModifiedBeforeFilter.

nodes.name: ModifiedAfterFilter
nodes.summary: Filter that keeps files whose modification time, converted to microseconds and local time, is after a threshold. Its companion object builds it from the option FileIndexOptions.MODIFIED_AFTER.

nodes.name: accept
nodes.summary: Accepts a file if the local modification time in microseconds minus the threshold is positive.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builder method in the companion object: if the modifiedAfter option is set, parses it with toThreshold and returns a ModifiedAfterFilter.

nodes.name: PathFilterFactory
nodes.summary: Holds the list of strategy builders (PathGlobFilter, ModifiedBeforeFilter, ModifiedAfterFilter); its create method returns the filters that apply to the given read options.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Calls create on every registered strategy builder and flattens the results into the sequence of active path filters.

nodes.name: rules.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the analyzer rules and plan checks for data source tables: ResolveSQLOnFile (direct queries on files), PreprocessTableCreation (normalizes and validates CREATE TABLE and append to existing tables), PreprocessTableInsertion (aligns INSERT queries with the target schema and partitions), QualifyLocationWithWarehouse, and the check objects HiveOnlyCheck, PreReadCheck, PreWriteCheck and ViewSyncSchemaToMetaStore.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala Rule[LogicalPlan] classes and objects using partial-function pattern matching on plan nodes; the check objects extend LogicalPlan => Unit.

nodes.name: ResolveSQLOnFile
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that replaces an UnresolvedRelation with a LogicalRelation when the plan is a direct query on files (identifier of two parts, provider then path) and the runSQLonFile setting allows it. A time travel query on such a path-based table fails, a missing provider class leaves the plan unchanged, and non-file or Hive sources and empty locations raise analysis errors. Nested object UnresolvedRelationResolution does the matching and stores the resolved relation in the single-pass resolver bridge state.

nodes.name: UnresolvedRelationResolution
nodes.summary: Extractor object inside ResolveSQLOnFile whose unapply turns an UnresolvedRelation that looks like a file query into a LogicalRelation, converting errors as described in the enclosing rule, and records the result in the AnalysisContext single-pass resolver bridge state.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches an UnresolvedRelation that passes maybeSQLFile, resolves its DataSource and returns Some(LogicalRelation); maps unsupported-operation errors to analysis failures, class-not-found to None and other errors to a direct query failure; registers the result with the bridge state.

nodes.name: maybeSQLFile
nodes.summary: True when conf.runSQLonFile is on and the relation identifier has exactly two parts.

nodes.name: resolveDataSource
nodes.summary: Builds a DataSource from the identifier (provider is the first part, path the last) and fails analysis if the provider is not a FileFormat, is the Hive provider, or the path is empty.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry: rewrites plans with resolveOperators, failing time travel on path-based tables and replacing file queries through UnresolvedRelationResolution.

nodes.name: PreprocessTableCreation
nodes.summary: Case class rule taking a SessionCatalog that preprocesses CreateTable (aliased CreateTableV1) and V2 create table plans. For CREATE TABLE without schema it forbids bucketing and partitioning; for append to an existing table it checks provider, location, column count, partition columns, bucketing and clustering against the existing table and reorders the query columns; otherwise it normalizes partition, bucket and sort columns (duplicates, existence, types, partition columns moved to the end). For V2 plans it checks duplicate column and partition names and normalizes partition references. Helpers: fallBackV2ToV1, normalizeCatalogTable, normalizePartitionColumns, normalizeBucketSpec, failAnalysis.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry with four cases: schema-less create (rejects bucket or partition specs), append to an existing table (consistency checks and column reordering via TableOutputResolver.resolveOutputColumns), create with normalized columns (CTAS or plain), and V2CreateTablePlan normalization of schema and partitioning.

nodes.name: fallBackV2ToV1
nodes.summary: Instantiates the given provider class and returns its fallbackFileFormat if it is a FileDataSourceV2, else the class itself, so V2 and V1 providers can be compared.

nodes.name: normalizeCatalogTable
nodes.summary: Checks schema column name duplication and map key collations, normalizes partition columns and bucket spec, rejects bucket or sort columns that are partition columns, and adds cluster-by properties to the copied table.

nodes.name: normalizePartitionColumns
nodes.summary: Normalizes partition column names against the schema, rejects duplicates, using every column as partition column, and partition columns whose type PartitioningUtils.canPartitionOn rejects.

nodes.name: normalizeBucketSpec
nodes.summary: Normalizes a bucket spec with CatalogUtils.normalizeBucketSpec, rejects duplicate bucket or sort columns, non-orderable sort column types and bucket columns that BucketingUtils.canBucketOn rejects.

nodes.name: failAnalysis
nodes.summary: Throws an AnalysisException with the legacy error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3072 carrying the given message.

nodes.name: PreprocessTableInsertion
nodes.summary: Rule object (extends ResolveInsertionBase) that preprocesses InsertIntoStatement on Hive table relations, HadoopFsRelation and InsertableRelation targets. It rejects schema evolution and replace criteria, normalizes the static partition spec, can restore nullability from the catalog schema, resolves the query output columns by name or position (turning arity mismatches with static partitions into a dedicated error), and fills dynamic partition columns.

nodes.name: preprocess
nodes.summary: Core of the insert rule: validates the statement, computes expected columns (optionally restoring catalog nullability when FILE_SOURCE_INSERT_ENFORCE_NOT_NULL is set), checks empty partition values, resolves output columns with TableOutputResolver and returns the insert with a new query and a full partition spec.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry: for a resolved InsertIntoStatement it dispatches on the table type (HiveTableRelation, LogicalRelationWithTable over HadoopFsRelation, or over InsertableRelation) to preprocess; other targets are unchanged.

nodes.name: restoreDataTypeNullability
nodes.summary: Recursively copies nullability flags from an original data type into the resolved type for structs, arrays and maps, keeping the resolved structure.

nodes.name: HiveOnlyCheck
nodes.summary: Check object (a LogicalPlan => Unit function) that throws when a Hive table CREATE or INSERT OVERWRITE DIRECTORY with Hive format appears in a plan, since those need Hive support.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Walks the plan and raises ddlWithoutHiveSupportEnabledError for CreateTable on a Hive table and for InsertIntoDir with a Hive provider.

nodes.name: PreReadCheck
nodes.summary: Check object that verifies the expressions InputFileName, InputFileBlockStart and InputFileBlockLength are not used over more than one file based input source in a plan (a union counts its children as one).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Traverses every operator and, for each InputFileName, InputFileBlockLength or InputFileBlockStart expression, runs checkNumInputFileBlockSources.

nodes.name: checkNumInputFileBlockSources
nodes.summary: Counts file based sources below an operator (Hive table or HadoopFsRelation counts 1, other leaf 0, union at most 1) and fails analysis with MULTI_SOURCES_UNSUPPORTED_FOR_EXPRESSION when more than one is found.

nodes.name: PreWriteCheck
nodes.summary: Check object run before writing into a data source table: rejects inserts that read from the same relation they write, inserts into non-file relations with partition specs or not allowed relations, and inserts into RDD based, Range, OneRowRelation or LocalRelation targets.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Matches InsertIntoStatement nodes and throws UNSUPPORTED_INSERT errors (READ_FROM, NOT_PARTITIONED, NOT_ALLOWED, RDD_BASED) per the checks of the enclosing object.

nodes.name: QualifyLocationWithWarehouse
nodes.summary: Case class rule taking a SessionCatalog that qualifies a relative table location of a CreateTable plan with the warehouse path before catalog operations and reads and writes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: For CreateTable plans whose location is not qualified or absent, qualifies the identifier, builds the full table path with makeQualifiedTablePath and returns a copy with the new location.

nodes.name: ViewSyncSchemaToMetaStore
nodes.summary: Check object that, for persisted views with WITH SCHEMA TYPE EVOLUTION or SCHEMA EVOLUTION, compares the view schema with its query schema and updates the catalog entry when types, nullability, comments or names differ, wrapping failures in FAILED_UPDATE_VIEW_SCHEMA.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Finds View operators with an evolution schema mode, decides if the stored schema must be redone, builds the new schema (keeping field metadata for type evolution), checks name duplication and calls alterTable on the session catalog.

nodes.name: FileFormatWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FileFormatWriter helper object that writes the output of a physical plan out through a FileFormat: driver side job setup, an executor side write task per RDD partition, task and job commit or abort through a FileCommitProtocol, and statistics processing. Also holds the OutputSpec and ConcurrentOutputWriterSpec case classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object extending Logging with a long parameter list on write (scalastyle argcount is switched off around it) and structured logging via MDC keys.

nodes.name: FileFormatWriter
nodes.summary: Helper object for writing FileFormat data to a location. write sets up a Hadoop Job, merges write options, computes data columns, bucket spec and required ordering, builds a WriteJobDescription, calls committer.setupJob, then runs executeWrite (one variant for WriteFiles plans, one that adds a projection and sort itself) and aborts the job on any failure. Further methods: writeAndCommit, createSortPlan, createConcurrentOutputWriterSpec, executeTask (one Spark task) and processStats. It keeps two test-only variables, outputOrderingMatched and executedPlan.

nodes.name: OutputSpec
nodes.summary: Case class describing where output files go: outputPath, customPartitionLocations per partition spec and the outputColumns.

nodes.name: ConcurrentOutputWriterSpec
nodes.summary: Case class describing concurrent output writers: maxWriters and a createSorter function that creates an UnsafeExternalRowSorter.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Runs a whole write job: creates the Hadoop Job, merges options, derives data, bucket and sort columns, calls prepareWrite on the FileFormat for the output writer factory, builds a WriteJobDescription, determines the required ordering, calls committer.setupJob before any adaptive plan is materialized, checks whether the plan ordering matches, and executes the write; on any Throwable it logs and calls abortJob. Returns the set of updated partition paths. The scaladoc lists the five workflow steps.

nodes.name: executeWrite
nodes.summary: Variant for plans without WriteFiles: converts empty strings to null in partition columns, adds a sort (or concurrent writers) when ordering does not match, executes the plan RDD (adding a one-partition dummy RDD for zero partitions) and runs a job with executeTask per partition, committing each task result. A second overload (lines 301-335) takes a WriteFilesSpec and calls planForWrites.executeWrite, collecting WriteTaskResult commit messages; both are wrapped by writeAndCommit.

nodes.name: writeAndCommit
nodes.summary: Evaluates the supplied write block to get task results, commits the job through committer.commitJob while timing it, processes statistics and returns the union of updated partition paths.

nodes.name: createSortPlan
nodes.summary: Binds the required ordering (ascending SortOrder on each expression) to the output columns and returns a non-global SortExec over the plan; binds early to avoid attribute id mismatch after optimization.

nodes.name: createConcurrentOutputWriterSpec
nodes.summary: Returns a ConcurrentOutputWriterSpec with the configured maxConcurrentOutputFileWriters and a sorter factory when concurrent writers are enabled (max writers above zero and no sort columns), else None.

nodes.name: executeTask
nodes.summary: Writes the rows of one partition in a Spark task: builds job, task and attempt ids and a TaskAttemptContext, calls committer.setupTask, picks a data writer (EmptyDirectoryDataWriter, SingleDirectoryDataWriter, DynamicPartitionDataConcurrentWriter or DynamicPartitionDataSingleWriter), writes with the iterator and commits; on failure aborts the writer or task, and always closes the writer. Returns a WriteTaskResult.

nodes.name: processStats
nodes.summary: Checks every task returned one WriteTaskStats per tracker, transposes the per-task stats into per-tracker lists and calls processStats on each WriteJobStatsTracker with the job commit duration.

nodes.name: SQLHadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLHadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol, a commit protocol for file-based writes that lets the Hadoop output committer be chosen through a SQL configuration entry.

nodes.name: SQLHadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol
nodes.summary: Variant of HadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol (constructed with jobId, path and dynamicPartitionOverwrite) that lets the actual Hadoop OutputCommitter be set with the option SQLConf.OUTPUT_COMMITTER_CLASS. Its only override, setupCommitter, reads that class from the task configuration and instantiates it; it is used when file data sources commit their written output.

nodes.name: setupCommitter
nodes.summary: Starts from the parent committer, then looks up the committer class configured under SQLConf.OUTPUT_COMMITTER_CLASS. If it is a FileOutputCommitter subclass it is built with the (Path, TaskAttemptContext) constructor, using the staging directory when dynamic partition overwrite is on; otherwise the no-argument constructor is used. Logs the chosen committer class.

nodes.name: SchemaPruning.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SchemaPruning optimizer rule that prunes unneeded nested columns from data source relations (Parquet and ORC v1) and unneeded file-source metadata columns, rewriting the plan to read only the required physical fields.

nodes.name: SchemaPruning
nodes.summary: Catalyst Rule[LogicalPlan] that matches a ScanOperation over a LogicalRelation backed by a HadoopFsRelation, works out which root and nested fields are really requested by the projects and filters, and replaces the relation with one holding a pruned data schema and pruned metadata schema. Main methods: apply (plan transformDown), prunePhysicalColumns (decides whether pruning helps), canPruneDataSchema (Parquet or ORC with the nested schema pruning setting on), pruneMetadataSchema, buildNewProjection, buildPrunedRelation, getPrunedOutput and countLeaves (counts leaf fields to detect that something was removed).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: transforms the plan top-down, and for each ScanOperation over a HadoopFsRelation-backed LogicalRelation calls prunePhysicalColumns, building a pruned HadoopFsRelation (copy with the pruned dataSchema) when pruning applies; otherwise keeps the original operator.

nodes.name: prunePhysicalColumns
nodes.summary: Normalizes attribute names, identifies the requested root fields from projects and filters, and if any nested field is requested prunes the data schema and the metadata schema. Returns None when nothing nested is required or the leaf count does not shrink; otherwise builds the pruned relation and the rewritten projection.

nodes.name: canPruneDataSchema
nodes.summary: Returns true when the nested schema pruning setting is enabled and the relation file format is a ParquetFileFormat or an OrcFileFormat.

nodes.name: pruneMetadataSchema
nodes.summary: Prunes the file-source metadata struct by dropping sibling sub-attributes that are not requested; kept sub-attributes keep their original data types because the extractor yields a complete value.

nodes.name: normalizeAttributeRefNames
nodes.summary: Rewrites AttributeReference names in the given expressions to the names used by the logical relation output, so attributes and schema fields can be compared by name.

nodes.name: buildNewProjection
nodes.summary: Builds the new Project over the pruned leaf node: original filters are rewritten with ProjectionOverSchema and stacked as Filter nodes over the leaf, and projections are rewritten likewise with original output names restored.

nodes.name: buildPrunedRelation
nodes.summary: Copies the LogicalRelation with the pruned base relation and a pruned output derived from the merged data and metadata schema, and copies tags from the original relation.

nodes.name: getPrunedOutput
nodes.summary: Converts the required schema to attributes, reusing the original output attributes by name with their data types updated so existing references stay valid.

nodes.name: countLeaves
nodes.summary: Recursively counts the leaf (non-complex) fields in a DataType by descending into arrays, maps and structs; used to check whether pruning removed anything.

nodes.name: SourceOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SourceOptions, a small serializable holder of two table-level data source flags read from case-insensitive option maps, together with its companion object of option names and defaults.

nodes.name: SourceOptions
nodes.summary: Serializable wrapper over a CaseInsensitiveMap[String] (an auxiliary constructor accepts a plain Map). Exposes two vals: skipHiveMetadata (option "skipHiveMetadata", default false, disables saving table metadata in a Hive compatible way) and respectSparkSchema (option "respectSparkSchema", default false, always uses the schema restored from table properties). The companion object SourceOptions holds the option-name and default-value constants.

nodes.name: V1Writes.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the V1WriteCommand trait, the V1Writes optimizer rule that injects WriteFiles and a required sort below V1 write commands, and the V1WritesUtils helpers for bucketing, sort order and empty-string-to-null handling.

nodes.name: V1WriteCommand
nodes.summary: Trait extending DataWritingCommand for write commands whose provider is a FileFormat. It declares the members a V1 write must expose: fileFormat, partitionColumns, staticPartitions, bucketSpec, options and requiredOrdering (FileFormatWriter adds a SortExec if the required ordering is empty).

nodes.name: V1Writes
nodes.summary: Optimizer Rule[LogicalPlan] that, when the planned write setting is enabled, rewrites each V1WriteCommand whose child is not already a WriteFiles: it prepares the query (empty to null for partition columns, plus a local Sort for the required ordering), wraps it in a WriteFiles node and remaps attribute expression ids. Main methods: apply and prepareQuery.

nodes.name: V1WritesUtils
nodes.summary: Helper object for V1 writes. Methods: getWriterBucketSpec (bucket id expression and file name prefix, Hive-compatible hash when the Hive bucket write option is "true", otherwise HashPartitioning), getBucketSortColumns, getSortOrder (dynamic partition columns, then bucket id, then sort columns), convertEmptyToNull, hasEmptyToNull, eliminateFoldableOrdering, isOrderingMatched and getWriteFilesOpt.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: if planned write is enabled, transforms the plan bottom-up; for each V1WriteCommand without a WriteFiles child it prepares the query, builds WriteFiles with the command spec, and rewrites attribute ids in both the new child and the command so references stay consistent.

nodes.name: prepareQuery
nodes.summary: Adds a Project that converts empty strings to null for partition columns when needed, rewrites the required ordering to the new output, removes foldable orderings, and adds a non-global Sort unless the existing output ordering already matches.

nodes.name: getWriterBucketSpec
nodes.summary: Builds an optional WriterBucketSpec from the BucketSpec: Hive-compatible tables use HiveHash with a bitwise-and and Pmod plus a "%05d_0_" file name prefix, other tables use the HashPartitioning partition id expression and no prefix.

nodes.name: getBucketSortColumns
nodes.summary: Resolves the bucket spec sort column names to attributes among the data columns.

nodes.name: getSortOrder
nodes.summary: Computes the ascending sort order for a write: dynamic partition columns first, then the bucket id expression, then bucket sort columns; returns empty when concurrent output writers are enabled and there are no sort columns.

nodes.name: convertEmptyToNull
nodes.summary: Returns a projection list that wraps nullable string partition columns in Empty2Null aliases, or Nil if no column needs the conversion.

nodes.name: hasEmptyToNull
nodes.summary: Checks whether any of the given expressions contains an Empty2Null node.

nodes.name: eliminateFoldableOrdering
nodes.summary: Builds a temporary Sort over the query and applies FoldablePropagation and EliminateSorts to drop foldable sort expressions from the required ordering.

nodes.name: isOrderingMatched
nodes.summary: Returns true when the required ordering is a prefix satisfied by the output ordering, ignoring sort direction and null ordering.

nodes.name: getWriteFilesOpt
nodes.summary: Finds the first WriteFilesExecBase node in a physical plan, if any.

nodes.name: WriteFiles.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical WriteFiles operator and the physical WriteFilesExec operator used by planned V1 writes, plus the WriteFilesSpec that carries the write job description, commit protocol and concurrent writer spec.

nodes.name: WriteFilesSpec
nodes.summary: Case class holding everything a V1WriteCommand with a FileFormat provider needs to run its write: the WriteJobDescription, the FileCommitProtocol committer, and a function from SparkPlan to an optional ConcurrentOutputWriterSpec.

nodes.name: WriteFiles
nodes.summary: Logical UnaryNode injected by V1Writes between a V1WriteCommand and its query; it must be the root plan as child of the command. It carries the child, fileFormat, partitionColumns, bucketSpec, options and staticPartitions; its output is the child output, and it implements withNewChildInternal via copy.

nodes.name: WriteFilesExecBase
nodes.summary: Trait for physical write-files nodes extending UnaryExecNode: output is empty and doExecute throws an internal error because only the doExecuteWrite path is supported.

nodes.name: WriteFilesExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator responsible for writing files. Its doExecuteWrite takes a WriteFilesSpec, executes the child, and on every partition calls FileFormatWriter.executeTask to write rows, returning an RDD of WriterCommitMessage; withNewChildInternal and stringArgs support plan copying and display.

nodes.name: doExecuteWrite
nodes.summary: Runs the child plan, substitutes a single empty partition when the RDD has zero partitions so at least one write task sets up metadata, then maps each partition with mapPartitionsInternal, calling FileFormatWriter.executeTask with the job description, tracker id, stage, partition and attempt numbers, committer and iterator.

nodes.name: WriteStatsTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the traits used to collect statistics during file writes: WriteTaskStats, WriteTaskStatsTracker (per task, on executors) and WriteJobStatsTracker (per job, on the driver).

nodes.name: WriteTaskStats
nodes.summary: Marker trait extending Serializable for statistics objects produced by a write task; instances are gathered on the driver from all executors.

nodes.name: WriteTaskStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Trait for per-task collectors of write statistics in FileFormatWriter (one per executor task). Callbacks: newPartition(partitionValues), newFile(filePath), closeFile(filePath), newRow(filePath, row) (called per row so it must be light) and getFinalStats(taskCommitTime), which returns a WriteTaskStats and may be called only once.

nodes.name: WriteJobStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Serializable trait holding the parameters needed to create a WriteTaskStatsTracker on every executor (newTaskInstance) and to process the stats from all successful tasks on the driver (processStats(stats, jobCommitTime)), for example aggregating or saving them.

nodes.name: OpenedParquetFooter.java
nodes.summary: Defines the OpenedParquetFooter Java record that bundles a read Parquet footer with its input file and an optional still-open input stream.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record: accessors footer(), inputFile() and inputStreamOpt() are generated by the compiler.

nodes.name: OpenedParquetFooter
nodes.summary: Public record with components footer (ParquetMetadata), inputFile (HadoopInputFile) and inputStreamOpt (Optional of SeekableInputStream). Adds inputStream(), which returns the stream with Optional.get() and so fails if no stream was kept open.

nodes.name: inputStream
nodes.summary: Returns the contained SeekableInputStream by calling get() on the Optional, which throws if it is empty.

nodes.name: ParquetCompressionCodec.java
nodes.summary: Defines the ParquetCompressionCodec enum that maps the compression codec names accepted by Spark to Parquet CompressionCodecName values.

nodes.name: ParquetCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Enum with constants NONE, UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY, GZIP, LZO, BROTLI, LZ4, LZ4_RAW and ZSTD, each wrapping a Parquet CompressionCodecName (NONE maps to UNCOMPRESSED). Offers getCompressionCodec(), fromString(s) (upper-case lookup with Locale.ROOT), lowerCaseName() backed by an EnumMap, and the static list availableCodecs (UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY, GZIP, ZSTD, LZ4, LZ4_RAW).

nodes.name: fromString
nodes.summary: Static factory that upper-cases the given name with Locale.ROOT and returns the matching enum constant via valueOf.

nodes.name: lowerCaseName
nodes.summary: Returns the lower-case name of the codec from a precomputed EnumMap.

nodes.name: ParquetColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines the package-private ParquetColumnVector class, which ties a Parquet column to its Spark writable vector, repetition and definition level vectors and children, and assembles arrays, maps, structs and variants from the levels.

nodes.name: ParquetColumnVector
nodes.summary: Holds the information for one Parquet column, primitive or nested: the ParquetColumn, a list of child ParquetColumnVector objects, the WritableColumnVector for values, repetition and definition level vectors (allocated for leaf columns and shared upward), and the VectorizedColumnReader for primitive columns. The constructor handles missing columns (default values, row index, setMissing) and variant columns. Main methods: getLeaves, assemble (builds collections, structs or variants from levels), reset, setColumnReader, assembleCollection, assembleStruct, getNextCollectionStart and getCollectionSize; plus simple getters for the column, value vector, level vectors and reader.

nodes.name: ParquetColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor (id covers the only constructor). For a missing column it either returns early (row index), marks the vector missing, or fills it with the default value as a constant. For variant file types it builds a content child and variant schema; for primitive columns it reserves repetition and definition level vectors; for nested columns it recursively builds children, reuses levels from a non-missing child and marks the struct missing if all children are missing.

nodes.name: getChildren
nodes.summary: Returns the child ParquetColumnVector list of this column.

nodes.name: getLeaves
nodes.summary: Collects all primitive (leaf) column vectors under this one in depth-first order by calling getLeavesHelper.

nodes.name: getLeavesHelper
nodes.summary: Static recursive helper that adds primitive vectors to the result list and descends into children of non-primitive vectors.

nodes.name: assemble
nodes.summary: Assembles this column recursively after levels are read: variant columns assemble their content child and build variant batches; array and map columns assemble children then call assembleCollection; struct and variant types call assembleStruct; it does nothing for primitive or all-null columns.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets the value vector, repetition and definition level vectors and all children recursively, unless the column vector is all null.

nodes.name: setColumnReader
nodes.summary: Sets the VectorizedColumnReader; throws IllegalStateException when called on a non-primitive column.

nodes.name: assembleCollection
nodes.summary: Walks the definition levels of an array or map to fill null flags, offsets and lengths in the vector, handling the four definition level cases (defined, null, missing due to a null parent, nested element) and skipping offsets for null or empty collections.

nodes.name: assembleStruct
nodes.summary: Walks the definition and repetition levels and marks each struct row null or not null in the vector, skipping entries that belong to nested repeated elements.

nodes.name: getNextCollectionStart
nodes.summary: Given a collection element index, returns the index where the next collection starts by scanning repetition levels up to the max repetition level.

nodes.name: getCollectionSize
nodes.summary: Counts the top-level elements of the collection starting at an index by scanning repetition levels, counting only those at the current collection depth (documented with a nested list example).

nodes.name: ParquetDictionary.java
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetDictionary, the adapter that lets Spark's vectorized columns decode dictionary ids through a Parquet column dictionary, optionally transforming values of unsigned integer columns.

nodes.name: ParquetDictionary
nodes.summary: Final class implementing the vectorized Dictionary interface on top of an org.apache.parquet.column.Dictionary. It forwards decodeToInt, decodeToLong, decodeToFloat, decodeToDouble and decodeToBinary to the Parquet dictionary. When needTransform is true, decodeToLong reads the stored signed int and widens it with Integer.toUnsignedLong (unsigned int32), and decodeToBinary reads the stored signed long and returns the bytes of a BigInteger built from Long.toUnsignedString (unsigned int64 as decimal(20, 0)). Used when a Parquet column chunk is dictionary encoded and the values are decoded lazily.

nodes.name: decodeToInt
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to an int; with needTransform set it narrows the long returned by decodeToLong, otherwise it calls the Parquet dictionary decodeToInt directly.

nodes.name: decodeToLong
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to a long; with needTransform set it reads the stored signed int32 and converts it to an unsigned long, otherwise it calls the Parquet dictionary decodeToLong.

nodes.name: decodeToBinary
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to bytes; with needTransform set it turns the stored signed int64 into the big-endian bytes of the unsigned value, otherwise it returns the Parquet binary via getBytesUnsafe. decodeToFloat and decodeToDouble are plain one-line forwards and have no own node.

nodes.name: ParquetFooterReader.java
nodes.summary: Utility class with static helpers for reading the footer of a Parquet file: building the metadata filter for a file split, reading a footer from an input file, and opening a file while optionally keeping its input stream open.

nodes.name: ParquetFooterReader
nodes.summary: Utility class that encapsulates helper methods for reading a Parquet footer. buildFilter returns SKIP_ROW_GROUPS when row groups are skipped, otherwise a range filter built from the PartitionedFile start and length. readFooter reads the footer of a HadoopInputFile with a given metadata filter. openFileAndReadFooter opens the file and returns an OpenedParquetFooter, keeping the SeekableInputStream open (detached from the file reader) only when keepInputStreamOpen is true, which the vectorized reader uses so that the file is not opened twice.

nodes.name: buildFilter
nodes.summary: Builds the Parquet metadata filter for a file split: skips row group metadata when skipRowGroup is true, otherwise restricts to the byte range of the PartitionedFile.

nodes.name: readFooter
nodes.summary: Reads the ParquetMetadata footer of an input file with the given metadata filter, opening and closing a stream via ParquetFileReader.readFooter.

nodes.name: openFileAndReadFooter
nodes.summary: Opens the Parquet file, reads its footer using buildFilter (row groups are read only when keepInputStreamOpen is true) and returns an OpenedParquetFooter, carrying the detached input stream only in the keep-open case.

nodes.name: ParquetReadState.java
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetReadState, the package-private holder of intermediate state while a column chunk is read, including row range tracking for column-index based row skipping.

nodes.name: ParquetReadState
nodes.summary: Package-private final helper that stores state while reading a Parquet column chunk: max repetition and definition levels, whether the column is required, the current row id, value and level offsets in the batch, remaining values in the page and rows in the batch, plus fields used for repeated values (lastListCompleted, numBatchedDefLevels, shouldSkip). From row indexes it builds an iterator of row ranges (constructRanges), with sentinel ranges MAX_ROW_RANGE (no row indexes, keep all rows) and END_ROW_RANGE (all ranges consumed). resetForNewBatch and resetForNewPage reset counters, currentRangeStart and currentRangeEnd expose the active range and nextRange advances it.

nodes.name: RowRange
nodes.summary: Private record holding an inclusive row index range [start, end] used by ParquetReadState.

nodes.name: constructRanges
nodes.summary: Converts the PrimitiveIterator of row indexes into an iterator of contiguous RowRange values (for example [0,1,2,4,5,7,8,9] becomes [0-2], [4-5], [7-9]); returns null when no row indexes are given.

nodes.name: resetForNewBatch
nodes.summary: Resets offsets, the rows left to read in the batch, the repeated-value flags and counters; called at the start of reading a new batch.

nodes.name: resetForNewPage
nodes.summary: Sets the number of values left in the page and the row id of the first row of the page; called at the start of reading a new page.

nodes.name: nextRange
nodes.summary: Advances currentRange to the next row range, using MAX_ROW_RANGE when there are no row ranges and END_ROW_RANGE once the ranges are exhausted. currentRangeStart and currentRangeEnd are one-line accessors with no own node.

nodes.name: ParquetVectorUpdater.java
nodes.summary: Declares the ParquetVectorUpdater interface, the per-type strategy used by the vectorized Parquet reader to read, skip and dictionary-decode values into a WritableColumnVector.

nodes.name: ParquetVectorUpdater
nodes.summary: Public interface for updating a WritableColumnVector from a VectorizedValuesReader. readValues reads a batch of values at an offset, skipValues skips a batch, readValue reads a single value, decodeDictionaryIds (default method) fills non-null slots of a batch from dictionary ids, and decodeSingleDictionaryId decodes one dictionary id with a Parquet Dictionary. Implementations are the nested updater classes in ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory, chosen by the Parquet physical type and the requested Spark type.

nodes.name: readValues
nodes.summary: Abstract method: reads total values from the values reader into the vector, starting at offset.

nodes.name: skipValues
nodes.summary: Abstract method: skips total values in the values reader.

nodes.name: readValue
nodes.summary: Abstract method: reads a single value from the values reader into the vector at offset.

nodes.name: decodeDictionaryIds
nodes.summary: Default method that loops over total slots from offset and, for each non-null slot, calls decodeSingleDictionaryId to fill it from the dictionary ids vector.

nodes.name: decodeSingleDictionaryId
nodes.summary: Abstract method: decodes the dictionary id at offset in the ids vector using the Parquet dictionary and writes the value into the destination vector.

nodes.name: ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory.java
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory, which picks the right ParquetVectorUpdater for a Parquet column from its physical type, logical type annotation, the requested Spark type and the datetime and INT96 rebase settings, and holds 38 small nested updater classes (one per supported type conversion) plus the rebase and decimal-compatibility helpers they share.
nodes.languageNotes: Java switch with arrow cases and pattern-matching instanceof; the nested updaters are private static classes that all implement the same four-method interface, so the file is long but very regular.

nodes.name: ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory
nodes.summary: Public factory created with the logical type annotation, an optional convertTz, and the rebase mode and time zone for datetimes and INT96. Its getUpdater method maps a ColumnDescriptor plus a Spark DataType to one of the nested updater classes, throwing SchemaColumnConvertNotSupportedException for invalid or unsupported combinations. It also holds helpers: isTimestampTypeMatched, isTimeTypeMatched, isUnsignedIntTypeMatched, shouldConvertTimestamps, the rebaseDays, rebaseMicros and rebaseInt96 functions, and the decimal checks canReadAsIntDecimal, canReadAsLongDecimal, canReadAsBinaryDecimal, canReadAsDecimal, isDecimalTypeMatched and isSameDecimalScale. Nested updaters, grouped by theme: simple copies (NullTypeUpdater, BooleanUpdater, IntegerUpdater, LongUpdater, FloatUpdater, DoubleUpdater, BinaryUpdater, ByteUpdater, ShortUpdater), widening or narrowing (IntegerToLongUpdater, IntegerToDoubleUpdater, FloatToDoubleUpdater, DowncastLongUpdater), unsigned ints (UnsignedIntegerUpdater, UnsignedLongUpdater), dates and timestamps with and without rebase (DateToTimestampNTZUpdater, IntegerWithRebaseUpdater, LongWithRebaseUpdater, LongAsMicrosUpdater, LongAsMicrosRebaseUpdater, LongAsNanosUpdater), INT96 timestamps (BinaryToSQLTimestamp*Updater, four variants), geospatial (GeometryUpdater, GeographyUpdater), fixed-length byte arrays (FixedLenByteArray*Updater) and decimals (DecimalUpdater and its four subclasses, IntegerToBinaryUpdater, LongToBinaryUpdater).

nodes.name: getUpdater
nodes.summary: Selects the ParquetVectorUpdater for a column: it switches on the Parquet physical type (BOOLEAN, INT32, INT64, FLOAT, DOUBLE, INT96, BINARY, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY) and checks the requested Spark type, the logical type annotation and the rebase modes ('CORRECTED' or 'EXCEPTION' versus legacy rebase) to return the matching nested updater. If the combination is not supported it throws the exception built by constructConvertNotSupportedException.

nodes.name: isTimestampTypeMatched
nodes.summary: True when the logical type annotation is a timestamp annotation with the given time unit.

nodes.name: isTimeTypeMatched
nodes.summary: True when the logical type annotation is a time annotation with the given time unit.

nodes.name: isUnsignedIntTypeMatched
nodes.summary: True when the logical type annotation is an unsigned int annotation with the given bit width.

nodes.name: rebaseDays
nodes.summary: Rebases a Julian day number to the Gregorian calendar with RebaseDateTime, or throws DataSourceUtils.newRebaseExceptionInRead for dates before the calendar switch when failIfRebase is true.

nodes.name: rebaseTimestamp
nodes.summary: Rebases Julian microseconds to the Gregorian calendar in the given time zone, or throws a rebase exception naming the format when failIfRebase is true and the value is before the switch.

nodes.name: rebaseMicros
nodes.summary: Calls rebaseTimestamp with the format name 'Parquet' to rebase timestamp microseconds.

nodes.name: rebaseInt96
nodes.summary: Calls rebaseTimestamp with the format name 'Parquet INT96' to rebase INT96 timestamp microseconds.

nodes.name: shouldConvertTimestamps
nodes.summary: True when a convertTz was given and it is not UTC, meaning INT96 timestamps need a time zone shift.

nodes.name: constructConvertNotSupportedException
nodes.summary: Builds a SchemaColumnConvertNotSupportedException from the column path, the Parquet physical type name and the Spark catalog string, used for unsupported type combinations.

nodes.name: canReadAsIntDecimal
nodes.summary: True when the Spark type is a 32-bit decimal and the Parquet decimal type and scale match.

nodes.name: canReadAsLongDecimal
nodes.summary: True when the Spark type is a 64-bit decimal and the Parquet decimal type and scale match.

nodes.name: canReadAsBinaryDecimal
nodes.summary: True when the Spark type is a byte-array decimal and the Parquet decimal type and scale match.

nodes.name: canReadAsDecimal
nodes.summary: True when the Spark type is a DecimalType and the Parquet type is compatible (scale equality is not required).

nodes.name: isLongDecimal
nodes.summary: True when the Spark type is decimal(20, 0), the type used for unsigned 64-bit integers.

nodes.name: isDateTypeMatched
nodes.summary: True when the column's logical type annotation is a date annotation.

nodes.name: isSignedIntAnnotation
nodes.summary: True when the annotation is an int annotation that is signed.

nodes.name: isDecimalTypeMatched
nodes.summary: Decides whether the requested DecimalType can hold the Parquet column: for decimal annotations the scale may grow if precision grows by at least as much, and for signed or un-annotated INT32 and INT64 columns the integer digits must fit the int or long decimal precision.

nodes.name: isSameDecimalScale
nodes.summary: True when the Parquet decimal scale equals the requested Spark scale; signed or un-annotated integers count as scale 0.

nodes.name: NullTypeUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for Parquet columns of unknown logical type read as NullType. Every method (readValues, skipValues, readValue, decodeSingleDictionaryId) throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException, because it must never be called when all values are null.

nodes.name: BooleanUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for BOOLEAN columns read as BooleanType: readBooleans and skipBooleans on the values reader, putBoolean for a single value. decodeSingleDictionaryId throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3186) since booleans have no dictionary.

nodes.name: IntegerUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT32 values stored as int: readIntegers, skipIntegers, putInt and dictionary decodeToInt. Used for IntegerType, 32-bit decimals, year-month intervals and for dates when rebasing is CORRECTED.

nodes.name: IntegerToLongUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 values and widens each to a long with putLong, for LongType and decimals stored in a long. Skips with skipIntegers; dictionary ids use decodeToInt.

nodes.name: IntegerToDoubleUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 values and writes them as doubles with putDouble (INT32 requested as DoubleType).

nodes.name: DateToTimestampNTZUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 dates (days) and converts each to microseconds at UTC with DateTimeUtils.daysToMicros, for TimestampNTZType read from a Parquet date column when no rebase is needed.

nodes.name: DateToTimestampNTZWithRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: Like DateToTimestampNTZUpdater but first rebases the Julian day number to the Gregorian calendar with rebaseDays, failing instead when failIfRebase is true.

nodes.name: UnsignedIntegerUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for unsigned INT32 (UINT32) columns read as long: readUnsignedIntegers on the batch path, Integer.toUnsignedLong for single values and dictionary ids.

nodes.name: ByteUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 values into a ByteType vector: readBytes and skipBytes, putByte, and a (byte) cast on dictionary values.

nodes.name: ShortUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 values into a ShortType vector: readShorts and skipShorts, putShort, and a (short) cast on dictionary values.

nodes.name: IntegerWithRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT32 date values that need Julian to Gregorian rebasing. The batch path uses readIntegersWithRebase; single values and dictionary values go through rebaseDays. Holds a failIfRebase flag.

nodes.name: LongUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT64 values stored as long: readLongs, skipLongs, putLong and dictionary decodeToLong. Used for LongType, 64-bit decimals, TimestampType in micros under CORRECTED rebase, TimestampNTZ micros and day-time intervals.

nodes.name: DowncastLongUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT64 columns read into a 32-bit decimal: each long is cast to int and written with putInt (also for dictionary values, since the long data array is not allocated for such decimals).

nodes.name: UnsignedLongUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for unsigned INT64 (UINT64) columns read as decimal(20, 0): readUnsignedLongs on the batch path, and for single values the unsigned value is built with BigInteger from Long.toUnsignedString and stored via putByteArray.

nodes.name: LongWithRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT64 timestamps in micros that need Julian to Gregorian rebasing: readLongsWithRebase on the batch path and rebaseMicros for single and dictionary values, with failIfRebase and a time zone string.

nodes.name: LongAsMicrosUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT64 timestamp values in milliseconds and converts each to microseconds with DateTimeUtils.millisToMicros, for TimestampType or TimestampNTZType with millisecond unit.

nodes.name: LongAsMicrosRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: Like LongAsMicrosUpdater but also rebases the converted microseconds from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar using rebaseMicros and the configured time zone, failing when failIfRebase is true.

nodes.name: LongAsNanosUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT64 values and converts them with DateTimeUtils.microsToNanos, used when the requested Spark type is TimeType.

nodes.name: FloatUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for FLOAT columns read as FloatType: readFloats, skipFloats, putFloat and dictionary decodeToFloat.

nodes.name: FloatToDoubleUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads FLOAT values and writes them as doubles (FLOAT requested as DoubleType).

nodes.name: DoubleUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for DOUBLE columns read as DoubleType: readDoubles, skipDoubles, putDouble and dictionary decodeToDouble.

nodes.name: BinaryUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for BINARY columns read as string, binary or byte-array decimal: readBinary and skipBinary on the values reader, and dictionary values stored with putByteArray from getBytesUnsafe.

nodes.name: GeometryUpdater
nodes.summary: Final updater for BINARY columns read as GeometryType: the values reader's readGeometry fills the vector, single reads delegate to readValues with total 1, and dictionary values are converted from WKB bytes with WKBToGeometryConverter using the srid of the vector's GeometryType.

nodes.name: GeographyUpdater
nodes.summary: Final updater for BINARY columns read as GeographyType: the values reader's readGeography fills the vector, single reads delegate to readValues with total 1, and dictionary values are converted from WKB bytes with WKBToGeographyConverter using the srid of the vector's GeographyType.

nodes.name: IntegerToBinaryUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT32 values and stores each as the BigInteger byte array of the value (INT32 read as a byte-array decimal).

nodes.name: LongToBinaryUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads INT64 values and stores each as the BigInteger byte array of the value (INT64 read as a byte-array decimal).

nodes.name: BinaryToSQLTimestampUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for INT96 timestamps: reads 12 bytes per value and converts them to microseconds with ParquetRowConverter.binaryToSQLTimestamp (no rebase, no time zone conversion). Skips with skipFixedLenByteArray(total, 12).

nodes.name: BinaryToSQLTimestampConvertTzUpdater
nodes.summary: INT96 timestamp updater that, after converting the 12 bytes to microseconds, shifts the time from the given convertTz to UTC with DateTimeUtils.convertTz.

nodes.name: BinaryToSQLTimestampRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: INT96 timestamp updater that rebases the converted microseconds from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar with rebaseInt96, using failIfRebase and a time zone string.

nodes.name: BinaryToSQLTimestampConvertTzRebaseUpdater
nodes.summary: INT96 timestamp updater that does both: rebases with rebaseInt96 and then shifts from convertTz to UTC with DateTimeUtils.convertTz.

nodes.name: FixedLenByteArrayUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater for FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY columns read as byte arrays (binary or byte-array decimals): reads arrayLen bytes per value with readBinary(arrayLen) and stores them with putByteArray.

nodes.name: FixedLenByteArrayAsIntUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads fixed-length byte arrays of arrayLen bytes and converts them to an int via ParquetRowConverter.binaryToUnscaledLong, for decimals stored in an int vector.

nodes.name: FixedLenByteArrayAsLongUpdater
nodes.summary: Updater that reads fixed-length byte arrays of arrayLen bytes and converts them to a long via ParquetRowConverter.binaryToUnscaledLong, for decimals stored in a long vector.

nodes.name: DecimalUpdater
nodes.summary: Private abstract base of the decimal updaters. It keeps the target DecimalType, implements readValues as a loop over readValue, and offers writeDecimal, which sets the scale of a BigDecimal to the Spark scale with RoundingMode.UNNECESSARY and writes an int, a long or a byte array depending on whether the Spark type is a 32-bit, 64-bit or larger decimal.

nodes.name: IntegerToDecimalUpdater
nodes.summary: Decimal updater for INT32 columns: builds a BigDecimal from the int and the Parquet scale (taken from the DecimalLogicalTypeAnnotation, 0 when absent) and writes it through writeDecimal.

nodes.name: LongToDecimalUpdater
nodes.summary: Decimal updater for INT64 columns: builds a BigDecimal from the long and the Parquet scale (0 when no decimal annotation) and writes it through writeDecimal.

nodes.name: BinaryToDecimalUpdater
nodes.summary: Decimal updater for BINARY columns: reads the bytes into the vector, builds a BigDecimal from the BigInteger and the Parquet scale, and writes it through writeDecimal. Dictionary values are decoded from the binary dictionary the same way.

nodes.name: FixedLenByteArrayToDecimalUpdater
nodes.summary: Decimal updater for FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY columns: reads arrayLen bytes, builds a BigDecimal from the BigInteger and the Parquet scale, and writes it through writeDecimal.

nodes.name: SpecificParquetRecordReaderBase.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract base RecordReader used by Parquet readers that materialize rows directly. It holds the file path, schemas, row count and row group reader, and is initialized from a Hadoop split, from a plain path (for tests) or from explicit schemas.
nodes.languageNotes: Java

nodes.name: SpecificParquetRecordReaderBase
nodes.summary: Abstract generic RecordReader<Void, T> base class for custom Parquet readers. Its initialize overloads open a ParquetFileReader for the split range, parse the writer version, run a ReadSupport to get the requested Parquet schema, convert it to a Spark StructType through ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter and compute the total filtered row count. Another overload initializes from a path and optional column list, and a third from supplied schemas and a row group reader. close() releases the row group reader. Subclasses use the protected fields (file, fileSchema, requestedSchema, sparkSchema, parquetColumn, totalRowCount, reader).

nodes.name: ParquetRowGroupReader
nodes.summary: Package-private interface (extends Closeable) with readNextRowGroup(), which returns the next PageReadStore or null when no row group is left. It lets tests supply their own row group source.

nodes.name: ParquetRowGroupReaderImpl
nodes.summary: Private static implementation of ParquetRowGroupReader that wraps a ParquetFileReader. readNextRowGroup() returns reader.readNextFilteredRowGroup() and close() closes the wrapped reader.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Main initialization: opens a ParquetFileReader (reusing a supplied input file, footer and stream when all are defined), sets file schema, writer version, requested schema, Spark schemas and total row count, and in tests updates a NumRowGroupsAcc accumulator. Overloads share this id: initialize(InputSplit, TaskAttemptContext) at 93-96 delegates with empty options, initialize(String path, List columns) at 168-211 is the test-oriented path based init, and initialize(MessageType, MessageType, ParquetRowGroupReader, int) at 214-233 takes explicit schemas.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the row group reader if it is set and clears the field.

nodes.name: toSetMultiMap
nodes.summary: Converts a Map<K,V> of file key-value metadata into an unmodifiable Map<K, Set<V>> with single-element sets, the shape the ReadSupport InitContext expects.

nodes.name: getReadSupportClass
nodes.summary: Looks up the configured ReadSupport class from the Hadoop configuration using ParquetInputFormat.READ_SUPPORT_CLASS.

nodes.name: getReadSupportInstance
nodes.summary: Instantiates a ReadSupport class through its no-argument constructor and wraps reflection failures in a BadConfigurationException.

nodes.name: VectorizedColumnReader.java
nodes.summary: Implements the per-column decoder for the vectorized Parquet reader. It reads pages of one column chunk, picks the right values reader for each page encoding and fills WritableColumnVectors in batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Java

nodes.name: VectorizedColumnReader
nodes.summary: Decoder that returns values from a single Parquet column. It holds the optional dictionary, the definition and repetition level readers (VectorizedRleValuesReader), a ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory and a ParquetReadState. readBatch(total, column, repetitionLevels, definitionLevels) loops over pages, reading either dictionary ids (lazily set as a ParquetDictionary when allowed, otherwise decoded eagerly) or plain values via the page's values reader. Page reading handles DataPageV1 and DataPageV2 and chooses PLAIN, DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY, DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY, DELTA_BINARY_PACKED or RLE readers.

nodes.name: VectorizedColumnReader
nodes.summary: Constructor: obtains the PageReader for the column descriptor, builds the ParquetReadState and ParquetVectorUpdaterFactory, reads the dictionary page if present (marking pages as dictionary encoded) and checks that the page has values and that rebase modes are LEGACY, EXCEPTION or CORRECTED.

nodes.name: isLazyDecodingSupported
nodes.summary: Decides per physical type (INT32, INT64, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BINARY) and Spark type whether dictionary values can be decoded lazily. It returns false when upcasting, datetime rebasing, decimal scale rebasing or geometry/geography types require extra processing.

nodes.name: needsDecimalScaleRebase
nodes.summary: Returns true when both the Parquet column and the Spark type are decimals with different scale.

nodes.name: readBatch
nodes.summary: Reads total rows into a column vector. For each page it resets the read state, then for dictionary encoded pages reads dictionary ids and either sets a ParquetDictionary on the vector for lazy decoding or decodes ids with the updater; for other pages it decodes values with the definition level reader (or the repeated variants when the column is repeated), decoding earlier dictionary ids first if encodings are mixed.

nodes.name: readPage
nodes.summary: Reads the next data page (returning -1 when none is left), records the first row index of the page and dispatches to readPageV1 or readPageV2 through a DataPage.Visitor.

nodes.name: initDataReader
nodes.summary: Creates the values reader for a page: a VectorizedRleValuesReader for dictionary encodings (only PLAIN_DICTIONARY and RLE_DICTIONARY are supported) or the result of getValuesReader otherwise, initializes it from the page stream, and passes the previous reader along when sequential reads are required for corrupt delta byte arrays.

nodes.name: getValuesReader
nodes.summary: Maps an Encoding to a vectorized reader: PLAIN to VectorizedPlainValuesReader, DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY, DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY and DELTA_BINARY_PACKED to the matching Vectorized delta readers, and RLE (booleans only) to VectorizedRleValuesReader; other encodings raise SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: readPageV1
nodes.summary: Reads a V1 data page: validates the definition level encoding, creates the repetition and definition level readers from the page bytes, then initializes the data reader. Returns the page value count.

nodes.name: readPageV2
nodes.summary: Reads a V2 data page: creates the repetition and definition level readers from their separate byte ranges (without length prefix) and initializes the data reader from the page data. Returns the page value count.

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaBinaryPackedReader.java
nodes.summary: Vectorized decoder for the Parquet DELTA_BINARY_PACKED encoding, used for INT32 and INT64 columns. It reads the page header and then expands bit-packed deltas into column vectors.
nodes.languageNotes: Java

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaBinaryPackedReader
nodes.summary: Extends VectorizedReaderBase. initFromPage reads the block size, mini block count, total value count and first value; readValues walks blocks and mini blocks (reading the min delta and bit widths, unpacking 8 values at a time) and hands each decoded long to an IntegerOutputWriter lambda. The public methods readBytes, readShorts, readIntegers, readLongs, readUnsignedIntegers, readUnsignedLongs, readIntegersWithRebase and readLongsWithRebase differ only in the lambda they pass, and the skip methods use a no-op writer. The single-value readByte/readShort/readInteger/readLong (5-line wrappers) and skipBytes/skipShorts/skipIntegers/skipLongs get no separate nodes.

nodes.name: initFromPage
nodes.summary: Reads the DELTA_BINARY_PACKED header (block size, mini block count, total value count, zig-zag first value), checks the mini block size is a multiple of 8 and allocates the bit width and unpack buffers.

nodes.name: readIntegersWithRebase
nodes.summary: Reads integer (date) values and rebases days before the last Julian/Gregorian switch day from Julian to Gregorian, or throws a rebase exception when failIfRebase is true.

nodes.name: readLongsWithRebase
nodes.summary: Reads long (timestamp micros) values and rebases values before the last Julian switch timestamp from Julian to Gregorian in the given time zone, or throws a rebase exception when failIfRebase is true.

nodes.name: readValues
nodes.summary: Core loop: checks the requested count against the total, emits the first value on the first read, then repeatedly loads mini blocks into the output through the given IntegerOutputWriter. Wraps IO errors in ParquetDecodingException.

nodes.name: loadMiniBlockToOutput
nodes.summary: Reads the block header and unpacks a mini block when needed, then computes values as last value plus min delta plus unpacked delta and writes up to the remaining count. Returns the number of values written.

nodes.name: readBlockHeader
nodes.summary: Reads the min delta of the next block, reads the mini block bit widths and resets the block and mini block counters.

nodes.name: unpackMiniBlock
nodes.summary: Unpacks one mini block of bit-packed delta values (8 at a time) into the long buffer using a little-endian BytePackerForLong for the current bit width.

nodes.name: readBitWidthsForMiniBlocks
nodes.summary: Reads one bit width byte per mini block of the current block from the input stream.

nodes.name: skipValues
