nodes.summary: Skips values by running readValues with a no-op output writer and a null vector.

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaByteArrayReader.java
nodes.summary: Vectorized decoder for the Parquet DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY encoding for binary, string and geo columns. It combines a prefix length reader and a suffix reader and rebuilds each value from the previous value plus the suffix.
nodes.languageNotes: Java

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaByteArrayReader
nodes.summary: Extends VectorizedReaderBase and implements VectorizedValuesReader and RequiresPreviousReader. initFromPage reads the prefix lengths with a VectorizedDeltaBinaryPackedReader into an int vector and hands the remaining stream to a VectorizedDeltaLengthByteArrayReader for suffixes. readBinary/readValues append prefix (taken from the previous value) plus suffix to the column's array data; readGeometry and readGeography do the same and then convert WKB bytes; skipBinary rebuilds values without producing output. setPreviousReader copies the last value of the previous page's reader to support files written with the PARQUET-246 bug.

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaByteArrayReader
nodes.summary: Package-private constructor creating the prefix length reader, the suffix reader and two one-row OnHeapColumnVector temporaries for binary values.

nodes.name: initFromPage
nodes.summary: Reads all prefix lengths into an int OnHeapColumnVector via the prefix length reader, then initializes the suffix reader on the same input stream.

nodes.name: readBinary
nodes.summary: Reads one binary value (readBinary(int len) returning a Parquet Binary). The overload readBinary(int total, WritableColumnVector c, int rowId) at 101-103 reads many values by calling readValues. Overloads share this id.

nodes.name: readValues
nodes.summary: For each row, takes the prefix length and suffix, appends prefix bytes copied from the previous value and the suffix bytes to the vector's array data, stores the array range and remembers the new value as previous. It uses the prefix length even for the first value of a page because of PARQUET-246.

nodes.name: readGeometry
nodes.summary: Asserts the vector type is GeometryType and reads WKB values converted with WKBToGeometryConverter using the type's srid.

nodes.name: readGeography
nodes.summary: Asserts the vector type is GeographyType and reads WKB values converted with WKBToGeographyConverter using the type's srid.

nodes.name: readGeoData
nodes.summary: Rebuilds each WKB value from prefix and suffix, converts it to the physical geo representation with the given WKBConverterStrategy, appends it to the array data and keeps the WKB bytes as the previous value.

nodes.name: setPreviousReader
nodes.summary: Copies the last value of the previous page's reader so the first value of a page can be read from a delta of the previous page's last value (workaround for PARQUET-246 corrupt files).

nodes.name: skipBinary
nodes.summary: Skips total values by rebuilding each value into alternating temporary vectors so the previous value stays correct, without writing to an output vector.

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaLengthByteArrayReader.java
nodes.summary: Vectorized decoder for the Parquet DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY encoding. It decodes all value lengths first, then slices the byte stream per value to fill binary, string or geo column vectors.
nodes.languageNotes: Java

nodes.name: VectorizedDeltaLengthByteArrayReader
nodes.summary: Extends VectorizedReaderBase and implements VectorizedValuesReader. initFromPage reads the lengths with a VectorizedDeltaBinaryPackedReader into an int vector and keeps the remaining stream. readBinary slices each value from the stream and writes it with ByteBufferOutputWriter; readGeometry and readGeography convert WKB bytes to the physical geo form. getBytes(rowId) returns a slice for a row (also used by VectorizedDeltaByteArrayReader for suffixes), and skipBinary skips the bytes of the next values.

nodes.name: initFromPage
nodes.summary: Reads all value lengths into an int OnHeapColumnVector via the length reader and keeps the remaining input stream for value bytes.

nodes.name: readBinary
nodes.summary: For each value, looks up its length, slices that many bytes from the stream and writes them into the column vector with ByteBufferOutputWriter.writeArrayByteBuffer; raises ParquetDecodingException on EOF.

nodes.name: readGeometry
nodes.summary: Asserts the vector type is GeometryType and reads values through readGeoData with WKBToGeometryConverter and the type's srid.

nodes.name: readGeography
nodes.summary: Asserts the vector type is GeographyType and reads values through readGeoData with WKBToGeographyConverter and the type's srid.

nodes.name: readGeoData
nodes.summary: Reads each WKB value from the stream, converts it with the WKBConverterStrategy and srid, and writes the physical bytes to the column vector.

nodes.name: getBytes
nodes.summary: Returns a ByteBuffer slice of the stream holding the value for the given row (length from the lengths vector); raises ParquetDecodingException on EOF.

nodes.name: skipBinary
nodes.summary: Skips the bytes of the next total values in the input stream using their decoded lengths and advances the current row.

nodes.name: ParquetRowConverter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the converters that turn Parquet records read by parquet-mr into Catalyst InternalRows (non-vectorized read path). It holds the updater traits, the ParquetRowConverter class with its nested converters for strings, geometries, geographies, decimals, arrays, maps, variants and repeated fields, and a companion object with INT96 and decimal binary helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a large recursive pattern match in newConverter and many private nested final classes that extend Parquet PrimitiveConverter and GroupConverter.

nodes.name: ParentContainerUpdater
nodes.summary: Trait used by a Parquet converter to hand converted values to its parent container (an InternalRow cell or an ArrayBuffer). It has start and end hooks plus set and typed setters (setBoolean, setByte, setShort, setInt, setLong, setFloat, setDouble) that default to set.

nodes.name: NoopUpdater
nodes.summary: Object that extends ParentContainerUpdater and does nothing. It is passed to the root converter, which has no parent container, and to fields that are read only for their levels.

nodes.name: HasParentContainerUpdater
nodes.summary: Trait that exposes the ParentContainerUpdater of a converter through an abstract updater member.

nodes.name: ParquetGroupConverter
nodes.summary: Abstract convenience base class for Parquet group converters that carry a ParentContainerUpdater. It extends GroupConverter and mixes in HasParentContainerUpdater.

nodes.name: ParquetPrimitiveConverter
nodes.summary: Converter for Parquet primitive types that forwards addBoolean, addInt, addLong, addFloat, addDouble and addBinary (as unsafe bytes) to the parent updater. It is subclassed with overrides for types that need conversion, such as BYTE, SHORT, unsigned ints, dates and timestamps.

nodes.name: ParquetRowConverter
nodes.summary: Converts Parquet records into Catalyst InternalRows; it can be the root converter (with NoopUpdater) or a nested struct converter. For each Parquet field it matches a Catalyst field by field id (when enabled and present) or by name (case sensitive or not per SQLConf), and builds a field converter with newConverter, writing into a shared SpecificInternalRow through RowUpdater. It also applies existence default values for missing columns, rebases dates, timestamps and INT96 values, and handles legacy list layouts. The companion object (lines 1111-1142) provides binaryToUnscaledLong and binaryToSQLTimestamp.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object shares this class id. Constructor takes ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter, Parquet GroupType, Catalyst StructType, optional ZoneId, two RebaseSpec values and a ParentContainerUpdater.

nodes.name: currentRecord
nodes.summary: Returns the InternalRow converted from the current Parquet record, after applying existence default values to the row using the precomputed bitmask.

nodes.name: end
nodes.summary: Called when a record ends: calls end on every field updater and then sets the filled current row into the parent updater.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Called when a record starts: sets every cell of the current row to null and calls start on every field updater.

nodes.name: newConverter
nodes.summary: Builds the converter for a Parquet type and a Spark SQL data type by pattern matching on the Catalyst type and the Parquet physical and logical type. It covers null, integer widening, byte, short, decimals backed by INT32, INT64, binary or fixed bytes, strings, geometry, geography, timestamps (micros, millis, INT96, NTZ), dates, time, arrays (repeated or LIST), maps, structs (copying the row for map or array parents), and variants; unsupported combinations throw QueryExecutionErrors.

nodes.name: canReadAsTimestampNTZ
nodes.summary: Returns true when the Parquet type carries a timestamp logical type annotation, which is the condition used to read it as TimestampNTZ.

nodes.name: binaryToUnscaledLong
nodes.summary: Companion helper that reads big-endian bytes of a Parquet Binary into a sign-extended unscaled Long for decimals, using the backing byte array without copying.

nodes.name: binaryToSQLTimestamp
nodes.summary: Companion helper that decodes a 12-byte INT96 value (time of day in nanoseconds plus Julian day, little endian) into Spark microseconds with DateTimeUtils.fromJulianDay; asserts the length is 12.

nodes.name: RowUpdater
nodes.summary: Private updater that writes each converted field value into the ordinal-th cell of a shared InternalRow, using the typed setters (setBoolean, setByte, setShort, setInt, setLong, setDouble, setFloat) to avoid boxing.

nodes.name: ParquetStringConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for string columns. It expands the Parquet dictionary into UTF8String values in setDictionary, returns them in addValueFromDictionary, and in addBinary wraps the heap byte array of the Binary as a UTF8String without copying.

nodes.name: ParquetGeometryConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for geometry columns that decodes WKB binaries to geometry values with the column srid, with a dictionary cache (setDictionary, addValueFromDictionary) and an addBinary path that uses the heap array when available.

nodes.name: ParquetGeographyConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for geography columns that decodes WKB binaries to geography values with the column srid, using the same dictionary-expansion approach as the geometry converter.

nodes.name: ParquetDecimalConverter
nodes.summary: Abstract converter for fixed-precision decimals. It handles INT32 and INT64 values through decimalFromLong, and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY or BINARY values through decimalFromBinary (unscaled Long when precision fits, otherwise BigInteger), and serves dictionary values from expandedDictionary.

nodes.name: ParquetIntDictionaryAwareDecimalConverter
nodes.summary: Decimal converter whose dictionary holds INT32 values; setDictionary decodes each entry with decodeToInt into a Decimal.

nodes.name: ParquetLongDictionaryAwareDecimalConverter
nodes.summary: Decimal converter whose dictionary holds INT64 values; setDictionary decodes each entry with decodeToLong into a Decimal.

nodes.name: ParquetBinaryDictionaryAwareDecimalConverter
nodes.summary: Decimal converter whose dictionary holds binary values; setDictionary decodes each entry with decodeToBinary and decimalFromBinary.

nodes.name: ParquetArrayConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for Spark arrays stored as Parquet lists. It decides, by converting the repeated field to a Catalyst type and checking legacy LIST layouts through the schema converter, whether the repeated field is the element itself (2-level layout) or only the syntactic group of the standard 3-level layout (then it uses the nested ElementConverter). On end it sets a GenericArrayData into the parent.

nodes.name: ElementConverter
nodes.summary: Group converter for the single element field inside the standard 3-level LIST layout; it stores the converted element and appends it to the enclosing array buffer on end.

nodes.name: ParquetMapConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for Spark maps stored as Parquet maps. It collects keys and values in two buffers through a KeyValueConverter and on end sets an ArrayBasedMapData built from them; duplicate or null keys have undefined behavior as noted in the code.

nodes.name: KeyValueConverter
nodes.summary: Group converter for the key and value pair inside a Parquet map; it holds one converter for keys and one for values, resets them on start and appends the pair to the map buffers on end.

nodes.name: ParquetUnshreddedVariantConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for the legacy unshredded Variant layout, used when spark.sql.variant.allowReadingShredded is false. It requires exactly two required binary fields named value and metadata (otherwise throws QueryCompilationErrors) and on end builds a VariantVal from them.

nodes.name: ParquetVariantConverter
nodes.summary: Final converter for Variant columns, shredded or not. It maps the Parquet type to a Spark struct, builds a variant schema, reads the file data with an inner ParquetRowConverter, and on end assembles either a Variant or a struct of extracted fields through SparkShreddingUtils.

nodes.name: RepeatedConverter
nodes.summary: Private trait that supplies newArrayUpdater, an updater that buffers repeated values and sets a GenericArrayData into the parent on end.

nodes.name: RepeatedPrimitiveConverter
nodes.summary: Primitive converter for an unannotated repeated primitive field, interpreted as a required array of required elements; it forwards all add calls and dictionary support to an element converter created by newConverter.

nodes.name: RepeatedGroupConverter
nodes.summary: Group converter for an unannotated repeated group field, interpreted as a required array of required structs; it delegates getConverter, start and end to the element converter.

nodes.name: decimalFromBinary
nodes.summary: Converts a Parquet Binary to a Decimal, using an unscaled Long when the precision is at most Decimal.MAX_LONG_DIGITS and a BigInteger otherwise.

nodes.name: addBinary
nodes.summary: Wraps the heap array backing the Binary as a UTF8String without copying and sets it into the updater.

nodes.name: addBinary
nodes.summary: Decodes a WKB geometry from the Binary (using the backing array slice when available, else getBytesUnsafe) with the column srid and sets it into the updater.

nodes.name: addBinary
nodes.summary: Decodes a WKB geography from the Binary (using the backing array slice when available, else getBytesUnsafe) with the column srid and sets it into the updater.

nodes.name: InferVariantShreddingSchema.scala
nodes.summary: Defines InferVariantShreddingSchema, which looks at a sample of buffered rows and works out the typed schema that each top-level or struct-nested VariantType column should be shredded into when writing Parquet.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with private helpers that recurse over Variant values and Spark DataTypes; uses pattern matching on type pairs to merge schemas.

nodes.name: InferVariantShreddingSchema
nodes.summary: Given the original StructType (no shredding), finds the index paths to every VariantType field that is not nested in an array or map (getPathsToVariant). Its public method inferSchema(rows) folds the sample rows into one merged schema per Variant path (schemaOf, mergeSchema), drops rare fields, widens integers to LongType, caps the number of shredded fields and depth using SQLConf.VARIANT_SHREDDING_MAX_SCHEMA_WIDTH and VARIANT_SHREDDING_MAX_SCHEMA_DEPTH, then calls SparkShreddingUtils to build the shredding schema and returns the full schema with each Variant replaced. Used by ParquetOutputWriterWithVariantShredding.

nodes.name: MaxFields
nodes.summary: Private case class holding one mutable Int, remaining, used as a shared budget of shredded fields across a file. finalizeSimpleSchema decrements it and stops adding fields once it reaches zero.

nodes.name: getPathsToVariant
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a StructType and returns the index paths (Seq of Int) of every VariantType field at the top level or nested in struct fields. Variants inside arrays or maps are not included.

nodes.name: getValueAtPath
nodes.summary: Follows an index path through an InternalRow, descending into child structs, and returns the VariantVal as an Option. Returns None when the Variant or any containing struct is null. Tail recursive.

nodes.name: schemaOf
nodes.summary: Computes a candidate Spark DataType for one Variant value (depth limited by maxDepth). Objects become StructTypes whose fields carry a COUNT metadata of 1 and are checked to be sorted by name (MALFORMED_VARIANT otherwise), arrays merge their element schemas, longs become the smallest DecimalType that fits, and UUID is left as VariantType.

nodes.name: mergeDecimal
nodes.summary: Merges two DecimalTypes with possibly different scales by taking the larger scale and the larger integer range. Falls back to VariantType if the result would exceed DecimalType.MAX_PRECISION.

nodes.name: mergeDecimalWithLong
nodes.summary: Merges a DecimalType with LongType: an integer-like decimal (scale 0, precision up to 18) becomes LongType, otherwise it is merged with Decimal(19, 0) through mergeDecimal.

nodes.name: mergeSchema
nodes.summary: Merges two inferred DataTypes. NullType yields the other side, decimals and long/decimal pairs use the decimal merge helpers, two StructTypes are merged field by field in name order summing the COUNT metadata (capped at 1000 fields), arrays merge their elements, identical scalar types are kept, and any other mismatch becomes VariantType.

nodes.name: updateSchema
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of a StructType in which every VariantType field (found by index path) is replaced by its inferred shredding schema from the supplied map, recursing into nested structs. Asserts that each Variant path has a replacement.

nodes.name: finalizeSimpleSchema
nodes.summary: Finalizes a merged Variant schema: widens integer types to LongType, turns empty structs into VariantType, drops struct fields below a minimum count, and consumes the shared MaxFields budget, returning VariantType when it runs out. Narrow decimals become Decimal(18, s) or Decimal(38, s).

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Public entry point. For each Variant path, folds the rows into a merged schema, uses a minimum cardinality of about 10 percent of non-null values, finalizes it, converts it with SparkShreddingUtils.variantShreddingSchema and addWriteShreddingMetadata, and finally rewrites the whole schema through updateSchema.

nodes.name: ParquetOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetOptions, the class that resolves the options of the Parquet data source (compression, schema merging, datetime rebase modes, variant shredding inference) against SQLConf defaults, plus its companion object holding the option names.

nodes.name: ParquetOptions
nodes.summary: Class (lines 32-94) extending FileSourceOptions, built from a case-insensitive option map and a SQLConf (an auxiliary constructor accepts a plain Map). Vals: compressionCodecClassName (precedence compression, then parquet.compression, then SQLConf.parquetCompressionCodec; throws QueryExecutionErrors.codecNotAvailableError for an unknown codec), mergeSchema (option mergeSchema or SQLConf.isParquetSchemaMergingEnabled), inferShreddingForVariant (needs SQLConf.VARIANT_WRITE_SHREDDING_ENABLED and then the option or SQLConf.VARIANT_INFER_SHREDDING_SCHEMA). Defs: datetimeRebaseModeInRead and int96RebaseModeInRead. The companion object (lines 97-123) extends DataSourceOptions and defines the option names MERGE_SCHEMA ("mergeSchema"), PARQUET_COMPRESSION (ParquetOutputFormat.COMPRESSION), COMPRESSION ("compression"), DATETIME_REBASE_MODE ("datetimeRebaseMode"), INT96_REBASE_MODE ("int96RebaseMode"), and the lookup of short codec names built from ParquetCompressionCodec.

nodes.name: datetimeRebaseModeInRead
nodes.summary: Returns the rebase mode for DATE and TIMESTAMP values on read: the datetimeRebaseMode option if present, otherwise SQLConf.PARQUET_REBASE_MODE_IN_READ as a string.

nodes.name: int96RebaseModeInRead
nodes.summary: Returns the rebase mode for INT96 timestamps on read: the int96RebaseMode option if present, otherwise SQLConf.PARQUET_INT96_REBASE_MODE_IN_READ as a string.

nodes.name: getParquetCompressionCodecName
nodes.summary: Companion object helper that maps a lower case short codec name to the name of the corresponding compression codec, using the private table built from ParquetCompressionCodec.values().

nodes.name: ParquetOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetOutputWriter, the OutputWriter that writes InternalRows to a single Parquet file on the executor side.

nodes.name: ParquetOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Executor-side OutputWriter constructed with a file path and a Hadoop TaskAttemptContext. It creates a RecordWriter from an anonymous ParquetOutputFormat whose getDefaultWorkFile returns the given path; write sends each InternalRow to that record writer and close closes it. Not serializable by design.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one InternalRow to the underlying Parquet RecordWriter (key is null).

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying Parquet RecordWriter using the task attempt context.

nodes.name: ParquetOutputWriterWithVariantShredding.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetOutputWriterWithVariantShredding, a wrapper writer that buffers the first rows so a shredding schema for Variant columns can be inferred before the real Parquet writer is created.

nodes.name: ParquetOutputWriterWithVariantShredding
nodes.summary: OutputWriter built from a path, a TaskAttemptContext, an InferVariantShreddingSchema helper and an isShreddingSchemaForced flag. Rows are buffered (up to maxBufferRows = 4096 rows or maxBufferSize = 64 MB, copying each row as UnsafeRow) until stopBuffering says to stop; then finalizeSchemaAndFlush infers the schema (unless it is forced), stores it with ParquetWriteSupport.setShreddingSchema, creates a ParquetOutputWriter and replays the buffered rows. Later rows go straight to the inner writer, and close flushes any buffered rows first. Executor side only.

nodes.name: finalizeSchemaAndFlush
nodes.summary: Infers the shredding schema from the buffered rows (skipped when the schema is forced) and sets it in the Hadoop configuration, creates the inner ParquetOutputWriter, writes all buffered rows to it, then clears the buffer.

nodes.name: stopBuffering
nodes.summary: Decides whether the current row ends the buffering phase: true when the buffered row count would reach maxBufferRows or the accumulated size in bytes would exceed maxBufferSize. Updates bufferedSize as a side effect.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a row. While no inner writer exists it converts the row to UnsafeRow if needed and buffers a copy, flushing when stopBuffering fires; once the inner writer exists it forwards rows directly.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the writer: if no row threshold was reached it first calls finalizeSchemaAndFlush, then closes and drops the inner ParquetOutputWriter in a finally block.

nodes.name: ParquetSchemaConverter.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the converters between Parquet schemas and Spark SQL schemas: ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter (MessageType to StructType or ParquetColumn), SparkToParquetSchemaConverter (StructType to MessageType) and the ParquetSchemaConverter object with shared helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Large pattern matches over Parquet logical type annotations and Spark DataTypes; includes legacy Spark 1.4 list/map and decimal write formats and backward-compatible LIST reading rules.

nodes.name: ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter
nodes.summary: Converts a Parquet MessageType into a Spark StructType (convert) or into a ParquetColumn tree that also carries repetition and definition levels and column descriptors (convertParquetColumn). Constructor flags control binary-as-string, INT96-as-timestamp, case sensitivity, timestamp NTZ inference, nanos-as-long, field-id matching, ignoring the Variant annotation and respecting unknown logical types; auxiliary constructors build it from a SQLConf or a Hadoop Configuration. Handles primitive types by logical annotation (convertPrimitiveField), groups for LIST, MAP and Variant (convertGroupField, convertVariantField), uses an optional Spark read schema to keep narrower types, and applies the LIST backward-compatibility rules in isElementType.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Builds a ColumnIO for the Parquet MessageType, converts it and returns just the Spark StructType.

nodes.name: convertParquetColumn
nodes.summary: Converts a Parquet MessageType into a ParquetColumn, optionally guided by a Spark read schema so that types such as tinyint or smallint that Parquet stores as int are preserved.

nodes.name: convertInternal
nodes.summary: Converts the children of a GroupColumnIO into a struct ParquetColumn. Matches each child to a read-schema field by normalized name, falling back to field id when enabled, treats a bare REPEATED field as a required array of required elements, and builds StructFields with nullability from OPTIONAL or REQUIRED.

nodes.name: convertField
nodes.summary: Converts one ColumnIO to a ParquetColumn. Dispatches primitives to convertPrimitiveField, handles Variant targets (reading shredded files when SQLConf.VARIANT_ALLOW_READING_SHREDDED is set, otherwise convertVariantField), variant struct targets, and other groups to convertGroupField. User defined types in the read type are replaced by their sqlType.

nodes.name: convertPrimitiveField
nodes.summary: Maps a primitive Parquet column to a Spark type by primitive type name and logical annotation: BOOLEAN, FLOAT, DOUBLE, INT32 (int, date, decimal, unsigned widening), INT64 (long, decimal, unsigned 64 as Decimal(20,0), timestamps, time), INT96 (needs the timestamp assumption), BINARY (string, binary, decimal, geometry, geography), FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY (decimal, binary). Unsupported or illegal combinations raise QueryCompilationErrors; a Spark read type takes priority.

nodes.name: convertGroupField
nodes.summary: Converts a group column by its logical annotation: a Variant-annotated group, a LIST (3-level or legacy 2-level, using isElementType), or a MAP / MAP_KEY_VALUE, validating the structure with checkConversionRequirement. Groups without annotation become structs through convertInternal; other annotations throw unrecognizedParquetTypeError.

nodes.name: convertVariantField
nodes.summary: Converts a Variant group that has exactly two required BINARY children named value and metadata into a ParquetColumn of VariantType, throwing the invalidVariant* compilation errors otherwise.

nodes.name: isElementType
nodes.summary: Implements the Parquet LIST backward-compatibility rules: decides whether the repeated type is itself the list element (primitive repeated type, group with more than one field, group named array, or group named <parent>_tuple).

nodes.name: SparkToParquetSchemaConverter
nodes.summary: Converts a Spark StructType into a Parquet MessageType (convert) and a single StructField into a Parquet Type (convertField). Constructor flags choose the legacy Spark 1.4 format, the output timestamp type (INT96, TIMESTAMP_MICROS or TIMESTAMP_MILLIS), whether to write field ids and whether to annotate Variant groups; auxiliary constructors read them from a SQLConf or Hadoop Configuration. The private convertField matches on the DataType: atomic types, decimals (legacy fixed-length bytes, or INT32, INT64 and fixed-length by precision in standard mode), arrays and maps in legacy and standard layouts, VariantType and variant shredding structs, structs, user defined types and NullType.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.summary: Builds a Parquet MessageType named spark_schema from a Spark StructType by converting every field with convertField (inShredded = false).

nodes.name: convertField
nodes.summary: Converts a StructField to a Parquet Type with an explicit repetition and an inShredded flag, by matching on the DataType. The public overload convertField(field, inShredded) at lines 634-641 picks OPTIONAL or REQUIRED from nullability and attaches a field id when useFieldId is on and ParquetUtils.hasFieldId holds. This node covers the large private overload; timestamps inside shredded Variants always use INT64 microseconds.

nodes.name: ParquetSchemaConverter
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with shared constants and helpers: SPARK_PARQUET_SCHEMA_NAME ("spark_schema"), EMPTY_MESSAGE (an empty MessageType with that name), checkConversionRequirement (throws AnalysisException with error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3071 when a condition fails) and isComplexType (true for ArrayType, MapType and StructType). Used by both converter classes.

nodes.name: checkConversionRequirement
nodes.summary: Takes a by-name boolean and a message; throws an AnalysisException (error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3071) carrying the message when the condition is false.

nodes.name: isComplexType
nodes.summary: Returns true only for ArrayType, MapType and StructType, so types such as CalendarIntervalType count as not complex.

nodes.name: VectorizedPlainValuesReader.java
nodes.summary: Defines the Parquet PLAIN decoder with the vectorized interface: it reads batches of booleans, integers, longs, floats, doubles, byte arrays and geometry/geography values from a page stream straight into a WritableColumnVector. It is the value reader used for pages that are PLAIN encoded.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class with many final read/skip methods; hot loops branch on ByteBuffer.hasArray() to use bulk little-endian copy methods of the column vector.

nodes.name: VectorizedPlainValuesReader
nodes.summary: Implements the PLAIN encoding decoder. It keeps a ByteBufferInputStream (set by initFromPage), slices little-endian buffers for batches (getBuffer), and offers readBooleans/readIntegers/readLongs/readFloats/readDoubles/readBytes/readShorts/readBinary plus matching skip methods, rebase variants for dates and timestamps, unsigned int/long variants, and readGeometry/readGeography that convert WKB values. Booleans are bit-unpacked using bitOffset and currentByte. Used when a Parquet data page is PLAIN encoded.

nodes.name: updateCurrentByte
nodes.summary: Reads one byte from the input stream into currentByte, wrapping an IOException in a ParquetDecodingException. Used by the boolean readers when the bit cursor needs a new byte.

nodes.name: readBooleans
nodes.summary: Reads total bit-packed booleans into the column vector. It first finishes a partly used byte using bitOffset, then batch-reads all full bytes with one getBuffer call, then reads a trailing partial byte.

nodes.name: skipBooleans
nodes.summary: Skips total boolean values by advancing the bit cursor, skipping whole bytes with skipFully and reading one more byte for a trailing partial group.

nodes.name: getBuffer
nodes.summary: Returns a little-endian slice of length bytes from the input stream, throwing ParquetDecodingException on IOException. All batch readers use it to get their raw bytes.

nodes.name: readIntegers
nodes.summary: Reads total 4-byte little-endian ints into the vector; uses putIntsLittleEndian when the buffer has a backing array, otherwise reads int by int.

nodes.name: readUnsignedIntegers
nodes.summary: Reads total 4-byte ints and stores each as an unsigned value widened to long via Integer.toUnsignedLong.

nodes.name: readIntegersWithRebase
nodes.summary: Variant of readIntegers for date values: a first pass checks whether any value is below RebaseDateTime.lastSwitchJulianDay; if so it either throws (failIfRebase, via DataSourceUtils.newRebaseExceptionInRead) or rebases each value from Julian to Gregorian days, otherwise it takes the fast bulk path.

nodes.name: readLongs
nodes.summary: Reads total 8-byte little-endian longs into the vector, using putLongsLittleEndian for array-backed buffers.

nodes.name: readUnsignedLongs
nodes.summary: Reads total 8-byte values as unsigned 64-bit numbers and stores each as big-endian BigInteger-compatible bytes through putLittleEndianBytesAsBigInteger, reusing a 9-byte scratch buffer.

nodes.name: putLittleEndianBytesAsBigInteger
nodes.summary: Converts 8 little-endian bytes into the minimal big-endian two's-complement byte array that BigInteger expects (adds a 0x00 sign byte when bit 7 is set, writes [0x00] for zero) and puts it into the column vector with putByteArray.

nodes.name: readLongsWithRebase
nodes.summary: Variant of readLongs for timestamp values: checks in a first pass whether any value is below RebaseDateTime.lastSwitchJulianTs, then either throws, rebases with rebaseJulianToGregorianMicros using the given time zone, or takes the fast bulk path.

nodes.name: readBytes
nodes.summary: Reads total byte values; PLAIN stores each as a 4-byte little-endian int, so it takes the first byte of every 4 bytes.

nodes.name: readShorts
nodes.summary: Reads total short values stored as 4-byte ints, using putShortsFromIntsLittleEndian for array-backed buffers or casting each int otherwise.

nodes.name: readBoolean
nodes.summary: Reads a single boolean from the current bit position, loading a new byte when bitOffset is 0.

nodes.name: readBinary
nodes.summary: Reads total length-prefixed binary values into the vector with putByteArray, avoiding an intermediate array for direct buffers. A second overload readBinary(int len) at lines 493-504 returns a Parquet Binary of the given length.

nodes.name: skipBinary
nodes.summary: Skips total length-prefixed binary values by reading each length and skipping that many bytes.

nodes.name: readGeometry
nodes.summary: Reads total geometry values: asserts the vector type is GeometryType, takes its srid and delegates to readGeoData with WKBToGeometryConverter.INSTANCE.

nodes.name: readGeography
nodes.summary: Reads total geography values: asserts the vector type is GeographyType, takes its srid and delegates to readGeoData with WKBToGeographyConverter.INSTANCE.

nodes.name: readGeoData
nodes.summary: Reads length-prefixed WKB values, converts each with the given WKBConverterStrategy, records (offset, length) with putArray, collects the converted bytes in a ByteBufferOutputStream and appends them to the child array data in a single appendBytes call.

nodes.name: VectorizedReaderBase.java
nodes.summary: Base class for VectorizedValuesReader implementations. Every read and skip method throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException, so concrete readers only override the types they support.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class in which about 30 methods are one-line throwers, so no per-method nodes are emitted.

nodes.name: VectorizedReaderBase
nodes.summary: Base class that extends the Parquet ValuesReader and implements VectorizedValuesReader. skip(), readByte, readShort, readBinary(len), all batch read methods (readBooleans, readBytes, readShorts, readIntegers, readIntegersWithRebase, readUnsignedIntegers, readUnsignedLongs, readLongs, readLongsWithRebase, readFloats, readDoubles, readBinary, readGeometry, readGeography) and all skip methods (skipBooleans, skipBytes, skipShorts, skipIntegers, skipLongs, skipFloats, skipDoubles, skipBinary, skipFixedLenByteArray) throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException. It avoids duplicating those throwing methods in concrete readers.

nodes.name: VectorizedRleValuesReader.java
nodes.summary: Parquet run-length / bit-packed hybrid decoder with the vectorized interface. It decodes definition and repetition levels, dictionary ids and DataPageV2 booleans, and drives the batch reading of values together with levels, nulls, row-index ranges and a ParquetVectorUpdater.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class using switch expressions over a private MODE enum; PACKED-branch decoding is extracted to separate methods so the RLE fast path stays small for the JIT, as noted in its comments.

nodes.name: VectorizedRleValuesReader
nodes.summary: Reader for Parquet's run-length encoded and bit-packed data. Constructors choose fixed or variable bit width; initFromPage binds the page stream; readNextGroup reads a group header and loads either an RLE run or 8-value bit-packed groups. readBatch reads definition levels and values for non-repeated columns, readBatchRepeated and readIntegersRepeated do the same with repetition levels for nested columns, and skipValues skips levels plus the matching non-null values. As a VectorizedValuesReader it also decodes dictionary ids (readIntegers) and booleans (readBooleans); other read and skip methods throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException. Used for definition/repetition levels, dictionary ids and V2 boolean pages.

nodes.name: MODE
nodes.summary: Private enum with two values, RLE and PACKED, that records whether the current group is a run-length run or a bit-packed buffer.

nodes.name: DefLevelProcessor
nodes.summary: Private static helper used by readBatchRepeatedInternal. It batches consecutive definition levels and, using the ParquetReadState flag shouldSkip, flushes them either by reading values (reader.readValues) or by skipping them (reader.skipValues). Methods: readValues(n), skipValues(n) and finish().

nodes.name: initFromPage
nodes.summary: Binds the page input stream. For fixed-width readers it optionally reads a 4-byte length and slices the stream; otherwise it reads the bit width from the first byte. A bit width of 0 is treated as one RLE run of valueCount zeros.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Validates that bitWidth is between 0 and 32 and sets bitWidth, bytesWidth and the little-endian BytePacker.

nodes.name: readInteger
nodes.summary: Returns the next decoded int, loading a new group when the current one is used up; returns currentValue in RLE mode or the next entry of currentBuffer in PACKED mode.

nodes.name: readBatch
nodes.summary: Public entry point to read a batch of definition levels and values for a non-repeated column; it calls readBatchInternal when no defLevels vector is given and readBatchInternalWithDefLevels otherwise.

nodes.name: readIntegers
nodes.summary: VectorizedValuesReader implementation that decodes dictionary ids (RLE or PACKED) into a column vector. An overload at lines 184-197 takes a ParquetReadState, a nulls vector and def levels, and decodes ids together with nulls using IntegerUpdater.

nodes.name: readBatchInternal
nodes.summary: Core loop for reading values with definition levels but without storing the levels. It walks RLE/PACKED groups, honours the row ranges in ParquetReadState (skipping or reading), writes nulls for levels below the max definition level and calls updater.readValues for non-null runs.

nodes.name: readPackedBatch
nodes.summary: PACKED-branch of readBatchInternal: scans runs of max-definition-level (non-null) and null entries, reads non-null runs via updater.readValue/readValues and writes nulls row by row. Split out to keep the RLE path small for the JIT.

nodes.name: readBatchInternalWithDefLevels
nodes.summary: Same loop as readBatchInternal but it also writes the definition levels into the defLevels vector, delegating the reading to readValuesN.

nodes.name: readBatchRepeated
nodes.summary: Public entry point to read repetition levels, definition levels and values for repeated (list/array) columns; delegates to readBatchRepeatedInternal with valuesReused set to true.

nodes.name: readIntegersRepeated
nodes.summary: Repeated-column variant for dictionary ids: calls readBatchRepeatedInternal with a separate nulls vector and an IntegerUpdater.

nodes.name: readBatchRepeatedInternal
nodes.summary: Reads repetition levels from this reader until the batch of top-level rows is full or the page is drained. It honours row-index ranges, appends repetition levels, and uses a DefLevelProcessor to batch the matching definition-level and value reads or skips.

nodes.name: readValues
nodes.summary: Private method that reads the next total definition levels from this reader and the corresponding values via valueReader, reserving space in the vectors and updating appended-element counts. Only used for repeated values.

nodes.name: readValuesN
nodes.summary: Reads n entries from the current group: in RLE mode it writes values or nulls in one call and puts the definition level, in PACKED mode it delegates to readPackedBatchWithDefLevels.

nodes.name: readPackedBatchWithDefLevels
nodes.summary: PACKED-branch of readValuesN: groups entries by exact definition level value, reads non-null runs in batch, writes nulls and definition levels per row.

nodes.name: skipValues
nodes.summary: Skips n levels from this reader and the matching non-null values from the values reader through updater.skipValues. A second overload skipValues(int n) at lines 1028-1040 just advances the group state.

nodes.name: readBooleans
nodes.summary: Decodes total booleans from RLE runs (putBooleans) or PACKED buffers (putByte of 0/1) into the column vector.

nodes.name: readUnsignedVarInt
nodes.summary: Reads the next varint-encoded int from the input stream; used for group headers.

nodes.name: readIntLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Reads the next 4 bytes as a little-endian int.

nodes.name: readIntLittleEndianPaddedOnBitWidth
nodes.summary: Reads an RLE run value that is stored in bytesWidth (0 to 4) little-endian bytes.

nodes.name: readNextGroup
nodes.summary: Reads the next group header and sets mode and currentCount; for RLE it reads the repeated value, for PACKED it unpacks groups of 8 values with the BytePacker into currentBuffer. Returns false when the stream is empty.

nodes.name: readValues
nodes.summary: Called for a run of kept rows: if the batch was in skip mode it flushes the pending skipped levels through reader.skipValues and starts a new read batch, otherwise it extends the pending count.

nodes.name: skipValues
nodes.summary: Called for a run of skipped rows: if the batch was in read mode it flushes pending levels via reader.readValues and switches to skip mode, otherwise it extends the pending count.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Flushes the remaining batched definition levels by reading or skipping them, then resets numBatchedDefLevels.

nodes.name: VectorizedValuesReader.java
nodes.summary: Interface for vectorized (batched) Parquet value decoding. It declares single-value reads, batch reads into a WritableColumnVector, batch skips, and two nested functional interfaces for writing output.
nodes.languageNotes: Java interface with nested @FunctionalInterface interfaces; ByteBufferOutputWriter has two static helper methods.

nodes.name: VectorizedValuesReader
nodes.summary: Interface implemented by the Parquet value decoders. Single-value methods: readBoolean, readByte, readShort, readInteger, readLong, readFloat, readDouble, readBinary(len). Batch read methods fill total values into c starting at rowId: readBooleans, readBytes, readShorts, readIntegers, readIntegersWithRebase, readUnsignedIntegers, readUnsignedLongs, readLongs, readLongsWithRebase, readFloats, readDoubles, readBinary, readGeometry, readGeography. Skip methods: skipBooleans, skipBytes, skipShorts, skipIntegers, skipLongs, skipFloats, skipDoubles, skipBinary, skipFixedLenByteArray. Implemented by the PLAIN, RLE and base readers.

nodes.name: IntegerOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Functional interface with write(outputColumnVector, rowId, val) that writes a long value into a given row of a WritableColumnVector.

nodes.name: ByteBufferOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Functional interface with write(c, rowId, ByteBuffer val, length). It provides static helpers writeArrayByteBuffer (copies the buffer's array into the vector with putByteArray) and skipWrite (does nothing).

nodes.name: writeArrayByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Static helper that writes length bytes of the buffer's backing array (from arrayOffset plus position) into the column vector row with putByteArray.

nodes.name: WKBConverterStrategy.java
nodes.summary: Defines the WKBConverterStrategy interface and two singleton enums that turn WKB bytes plus an srid into the physical byte representation of a geometry or a geography value. Used by the PLAIN reader when decoding geospatial Parquet columns.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private interface and enums share one Java file; the enums use the single INSTANCE constant pattern.

nodes.name: WKBConverterStrategy
nodes.summary: Package-private strategy interface with convert(byte[] wkb, int srid) returning the converted physical bytes.

nodes.name: WKBToGeometryConverter
nodes.summary: Singleton enum (INSTANCE) implementing the strategy; convert calls STUtils.stGeomFromWKB(wkb, srid) and returns its bytes.

nodes.name: WKBToGeographyConverter
nodes.summary: Singleton enum (INSTANCE) implementing the strategy; convert calls STUtils.stGeogFromWKB(wkb, srid) and returns its bytes.

nodes.name: ParquetColumn.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetColumn, a case class that pairs a Parquet column with its Spark SQL type, and its companion apply methods that build one from a Parquet PrimitiveColumnIO or GroupColumnIO.

nodes.name: ParquetColumn
nodes.summary: Case class (lines 31-44) holding sparkType, an optional ColumnDescriptor (set only for primitive columns), repetition and definition levels, required flag, field path, child columns and an optional variantFileType used when the column should produce a Spark variant. isPrimitive is true when a descriptor exists. The companion object (lines 46-58) has two apply methods: one for a PrimitiveColumnIO and one for a GroupColumnIO with children.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a group ParquetColumn (no descriptor) from a GroupColumnIO and child columns. A sibling overload at lines 47-51 builds a primitive column from a PrimitiveColumnIO, taking its ColumnDescriptor.

nodes.name: ParquetRecordMaterializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetRecordMaterializer, the Parquet RecordMaterializer that builds Catalyst InternalRow records through a root ParquetRowConverter in the row-based (non-vectorized) read path.

nodes.name: ParquetRecordMaterializer
nodes.summary: Package-private RecordMaterializer for InternalRow. It creates a root ParquetRowConverter from the Parquet schema, Catalyst schema, schema converter, optional time zone and the datetime and INT96 rebase specs, using NoopUpdater as parent updater. getRootConverter returns that converter and getCurrentRecord returns its current record.

nodes.name: ParquetRowIndexUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Helpers for producing a row index column when reading Parquet files. It provides a RowIndexGenerator for the vectorized reader and a RecordReader wrapper that fills the row index into InternalRows for the non-vectorized (parquet-mr) reader, plus functions to locate and recognize the temporary row index column.

nodes.name: ParquetRowIndexUtil
nodes.summary: Object holding the row index support for Parquet reads. Main methods: createGeneratorIfNeeded (returns a RowIndexGenerator when the schema has the row index column, else null), addRowIndexToRecordReaderIfNeeded (wraps a ParquetRecordReader when needed), findRowIndexColumnIndexInSchema (finds the column named by ParquetFileFormat.ROW_INDEX_TEMPORARY_COLUMN_NAME and checks it is LongType) and isRowIndexColumn.

nodes.name: RowIndexGenerator
nodes.summary: Generates row indexes for vectorized readers. initFromPageReadStore sets the iterator from the row group offset, either over the rows selected by page skipping or over all rows of the group (throws IOException when no offset is present); populateRowIndex writes the next numRows indexes into a WritableColumnVector or into the row index column of an array of ParquetColumnVector.

nodes.name: RecordReaderWithRowIndexes
nodes.summary: Private RecordReader wrapper around a ParquetRecordReader of InternalRow. It delegates every call to the parent and, in getCurrentValue, sets the row index column of the returned row to the parent current row index. Used with the non-vectorized Parquet reader.

nodes.name: createGeneratorIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Looks up the row index column in the Spark schema and returns a new RowIndexGenerator for it, or null when the column is absent.

nodes.name: addRowIndexToRecordReaderIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Wraps the given ParquetRecordReader in RecordReaderWithRowIndexes when the schema has a row index column; otherwise returns the reader unchanged.

nodes.name: findRowIndexColumnIndexInSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the position of the field named ParquetFileFormat.ROW_INDEX_TEMPORARY_COLUMN_NAME in the schema, -1 when absent, and throws a RuntimeException when the field is not LongType.

nodes.name: isRowIndexColumn
nodes.summary: Returns true when a ParquetColumn is a top-level column (path length 1) whose name is the temporary row index column name.

nodes.name: initFromPageReadStore
nodes.summary: Initializes the row index iterator from a PageReadStore: starts at the row group index offset and iterates either the selected row indexes (page skipping) shifted by that offset or all rows of the group; throws IOException when no offset is available.

nodes.name: populateRowIndex
nodes.summary: Writes the next numRows row indexes into a WritableColumnVector with putLong. An overload (lines 57-59) takes an array of ParquetColumnVector and fills the row index column.

nodes.name: getCurrentValue
nodes.summary: Gets the current InternalRow from the parent reader and sets the row index column to the parent current row index before returning it.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcFileFormat, the file format behind the "orc" data source. It infers schemas, prepares writes, decides whether columnar reads are possible, and builds the per-file reader that handles column pruning, filter push-down and partition values.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat
nodes.summary: ORC implementation of FileFormat, registered under the short name "orc" and serializable. inferSchema delegates to OrcUtils, prepareWrite sets the compression codec and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates OrcOutputWriter instances, supportBatch and supportDataType say what the vectorized path and the format can handle, and buildReaderWithPartitionValues returns the function that reads one PartitionedFile as either columnar batches or deserialized rows. Also overrides shortName, toString, hashCode and equals.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the schema of the given ORC files by calling OrcUtils.inferSchema.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Builds OrcOptions from the write options and SQL conf, stores the compression codec in the Hadoop configuration, and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates OrcOutputWriter instances and picks the file extension (compression suffix plus ".orc") from the configured codec.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.supportBatch
nodes.summary: Returns true when the vectorized ORC reader is enabled and every field of the schema supports columnar reads (through OrcUtils.supportColumnarReads, optionally including nested columns).

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.isSplitable
nodes.summary: Always returns true: ORC files can be split.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues
nodes.summary: Returns a function that reads one PartitionedFile. It resolves the requested column ids against the file schema, pushes filters down as an ORC search argument, then either uses the vectorized OrcColumnarBatchReader (batch mode, with a task completion listener to close it) or the row-based OrcInputFormat reader with OrcDeserializer and a generated unsafe projection, appending partition values when present. Requires FileFormat.OPTION_RETURNING_BATCH.

nodes.name: OrcFileFormat.supportDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively decides which data types ORC can store: atomic types are supported; variant, geometry and geography are not; struct, array, map and user-defined types are supported when their component types are.

nodes.name: OrcFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Converts Spark source Filters into an ORC SearchArgument for predicate push-down. It first trims the filters to the convertible part, then builds the argument in a single pass with one builder.

nodes.name: OrcFilters
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object extending OrcFiltersBase that builds ORC SearchArguments. createFilter ANDs all convertible filters and builds one argument; convertibleFilters trims filters (partial push-down is only allowed under AND, not under OR or NOT); getPredicateLeafType maps Spark types to ORC PredicateLeaf types; castLiteralValue normalizes literals (longs, doubles, HiveDecimalWritable, dates, timestamps, intervals); buildSearchArgument and buildLeafSearchArgument emit the actual builder calls for And, Or, Not, EqualTo, EqualNullSafe, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, IsNull, IsNotNull and In. Used by OrcFileFormat when filter push-down is enabled.

nodes.name: OrcFilters.createFilter
nodes.summary: Entry point: builds the searchable column type map for the schema, trims the filters to the convertible ones, combines them into one AND tree, and builds the ORC SearchArgument (None when nothing is convertible).

nodes.name: OrcFilters.convertibleFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the part of the filter list that can safely be converted. AND may drop one unconvertible side only when partial push-down is still allowed, OR needs both sides, and NOT disables partial push-down for its child; leaves are tested by trying buildLeafSearchArgument.

nodes.name: OrcFilters.getPredicateLeafType
nodes.summary: Maps a Spark DataType to the ORC PredicateLeaf.Type (boolean, long, float, string, date, timestamp, decimal) and throws for unsupported types.

nodes.name: OrcFilters.castLiteralValue
nodes.summary: Casts a filter literal into the representation the ORC SearchArgument builder accepts (long, double, HiveDecimalWritable, java Date or Timestamp, interval as months or microseconds).

nodes.name: OrcFilters.buildSearchArgument
nodes.summary: Recursively adds a fully convertible filter to the builder, using startAnd, startOr and startNot with end(), and delegating leaves to buildLeafSearchArgument; throws if a leaf is not convertible.

nodes.name: OrcFilters.buildLeafSearchArgument
nodes.summary: Adds one leaf predicate to the builder wrapped in the required parent (equals, nullSafeEquals, lessThan, lessThanEquals, isNull, in; greater-than and not-null are expressed through startNot). Returns None for unsupported filters or unknown columns.

nodes.name: OrcFiltersBase.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the OrcFiltersBase trait with the filter helpers shared by ORC filter conversion: building a balanced AND tree and computing the map of pushable columns.

nodes.name: OrcFiltersBase
nodes.summary: Trait with methods meant to be shared when upgrading the built-in Hive. buildTree folds a filter sequence into a balanced tree of And filters; getSearchableTypeMap returns the columns that can be pushed down. Also holds the nested case class OrcPrimitiveField. Mixed into OrcFilters.

nodes.name: OrcPrimitiveField
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a (possibly dotted and quoted) ORC field name with its Spark DataType.

nodes.name: OrcFiltersBase.buildTree
nodes.summary: Combines a sequence of filters into one filter by recursively splitting it in half and joining the halves with And; returns None for an empty sequence.

nodes.name: OrcFiltersBase.getSearchableTypeMap
nodes.summary: Returns a map from column name to OrcPrimitiveField for atomic, non-binary columns, descending into structs with dot-separated quoted names and ignoring binary, user-defined, array and map columns. In case-insensitive mode it skips names that collide after lowercasing and wraps the result in a CaseInsensitiveMap.

nodes.name: OrcOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcOutputWriter, the OutputWriter that writes Spark InternalRows to one ORC file.

nodes.name: OrcOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Private[sql] OutputWriter for ORC. On construction it creates an OrcSerializer for the schema and an ORC writer for the given path (schema from OrcUtils.orcTypeDescription, Spark version stored as user metadata), wrapped in a record writer with a batch size. write serializes each row and hands it to the record writer; close closes it. Created by the factory returned from OrcFileFormat.prepareWrite.

nodes.name: OrcOutputWriter.write
nodes.summary: Serializes one InternalRow to an OrcStruct with OrcSerializer and writes it through the record writer.

nodes.name: OrcOutputWriter.close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying record writer with the task attempt context.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcShimUtils, small helpers that isolate the Hive-based types (DateWritable, HiveDecimalWritable, VectorizedRowBatch, SearchArgument) used by ORC code so they can change when the built-in Hive is upgraded.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with type aliases Operator and SearchArgument and conversion helpers: getGregorianDays turns a DateWritable into Gregorian days, getDecimal turns a HiveDecimalWritable into a Spark Decimal, getDateWritable returns a getter-to-DateWritable function (reusing one object when asked), and getHiveDecimalWritable returns a getter-to-HiveDecimalWritable function for a precision and scale.

nodes.name: VectorizedRowBatchWrap
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper class holding a Hive VectorizedRowBatch in a public val named batch.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils.getGregorianDays
nodes.summary: Converts a DateWritable value to Gregorian days through DaysWritable.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils.getDecimal
nodes.summary: Converts a HiveDecimalWritable value to a Spark Decimal keeping its precision and scale.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils.getDateWritable
nodes.summary: Returns a function that reads an int day count from a SpecializedGetters and returns a DaysWritable; with reuseObj it updates a single shared DaysWritable instead of allocating one per call.

nodes.name: OrcShimUtils.getHiveDecimalWritable
nodes.summary: Returns a function that reads a Decimal of the given precision and scale from a SpecializedGetters and wraps it in a HiveDecimalWritable.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the OrcUtils object, the central helper for ORC reads and writes: listing files, reading and merging file schemas, converting between ORC and Catalyst types, mapping requested columns to file columns, and answering aggregate push-down from file footer statistics.

nodes.name: OrcUtils
nodes.summary: Object (extends Logging) with the ORC helper functions: listOrcFiles, readSchema, toCatalystSchema, readOrcSchemasInParallel, inferSchema, requestedColumnIds, addSparkVersionMetadata, getOrcSchemaString, orcTypeDescription, orcResultSchemaString, supportColumnarReads and createAggInternalRowFromFooter. Also holds extensionsForCompressionCodecNames (codec name to file suffix such as ".snappy", ".zlib", ".zstd", ".lz4", ".lzo", ".brotli") and CATALYST_TYPE_ATTRIBUTE_NAME ("spark.sql.catalyst.type"), an ORC type attribute used to keep the original Spark type. Used by OrcFileFormat, OrcOutputWriter and the aggregate push-down path.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.listOrcFiles
nodes.summary: Lists the leaf files under a path, skipping directories and names that start with "_" or ".".

nodes.name: OrcUtils.readSchema
nodes.summary: Reads the ORC TypeDescription of one file (None for an empty schema). Missing files can be skipped when ignoreMissingFiles is set, corrupt files when ignoreCorruptFiles is set (otherwise it throws), and the reader is closed even if the thread was interrupted, with the interrupt status restored. Overload at lines 179-188 takes a SparkSession, files and options, and returns the Catalyst schema of the first readable file.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.toCatalystSchema
nodes.summary: Converts an ORC TypeDescription into a Spark StructType, recursing through struct, list and map categories and using the "spark.sql.catalyst.type" attribute when present, otherwise parsing the ORC type string; CHAR and VARCHAR are replaced with STRING.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.readOrcSchemasInParallel
nodes.summary: Reads the schemas of many ORC files with ThreadUtils.parmap using the pool name "readingOrcSchemas" and 8 threads, returning the Catalyst schemas; visible for testing and used for schema merging.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the ORC schema: when OrcOptions.mergeSchema is set it merges the schemas of all files in parallel through SchemaMergeUtils, otherwise it uses the first readable file.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.requestedColumnIds
nodes.summary: Maps the required schema fields to column positions in the ORC file and returns them with a flag that says whether column pruning is allowed (None for an empty file). It rejects timestamp versus timestamp-without-time-zone mismatches, maps by position for files with "_col" names or forced positional evolution, and otherwise maps by name (case-sensitively or case-insensitively, failing on ambiguous matches); missing columns get -1.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.addSparkVersionMetadata
nodes.summary: Adds the Spark version as user metadata under SPARK_VERSION_METADATA_KEY to an ORC Writer.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.getOrcSchemaString
nodes.summary: Renders a Spark DataType as an ORC schema string (struct, array, map recursively; day-time interval, timestamp without time zone and time as bigint; year-month interval as int; otherwise the catalog string).

nodes.name: OrcUtils.orcTypeDescription
nodes.summary: Builds an ORC TypeDescription from a Spark DataType, recursing through struct, array and map; for interval, timestamp, time and string types it sets the "spark.sql.catalyst.type" attribute so the original Spark type can be restored.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.orcResultSchemaString
nodes.summary: Chooses the result schema string for a read (pruned result schema, or the full data schema plus partition schema), stores it in the Hadoop configuration as the ORC mapred input schema, and returns it.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.supportColumnarReads
nodes.summary: Returns true when a data type can be read in columnar mode: atomic types always, and struct, array and map types only when nested column support is enabled and their children qualify.

nodes.name: OrcUtils.createAggInternalRowFromFooter
nodes.summary: Computes pushed-down Max, Min, Count and CountStar results from the column statistics in the ORC file footer instead of reading data, deserializes them into an InternalRow with OrcDeserializer, and prepends re-ordered partition values via a JoinedRow when there are group-by columns. Throws a SparkException suggesting to disable "spark.sql.orc.aggregatePushdown" if the statistics cannot be read.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetWriteSupport, the Parquet WriteSupport that writes Catalyst InternalRows through a Parquet RecordConsumer, in standard or legacy format, plus its companion with schema-setting helpers.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport
nodes.summary: Class (with companion object) implementing Parquet WriteSupport[InternalRow]. init reads the row schema (and an optional variant shredding schema) from the Hadoop configuration, builds one ValueWriter per field, converts the schema to a Parquet message type, and returns a WriteContext with metadata (Spark version, Spark row schema, and legacy date/time or INT96 rebase markers with the session time zone when the rebase mode is LEGACY). write emits each row as a message. makeWriter creates per-type writers (boolean, integers, intervals, float, double, string, timestamp as INT96, micros or millis, time, binary, geometry and geography as WKB, decimals, variants, structs, arrays, maps, user-defined types); makeDecimalWriter, makeArrayWriter and makeMapWriter handle the layout differences between standard mode ("list"/"element", "key_value") and legacy mode ("bag"/"array", "map", two-level arrays). The companion object holds the configuration keys SPARK_ROW_SCHEMA ("org.apache.spark.sql.parquet.row.attributes") and SPARK_VARIANT_SHREDDING_SCHEMA, with setSchema and setShreddingSchema. Read side counterpart is ParquetReadSupport.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.init
nodes.summary: Initializes the write support from the Hadoop configuration: loads the schema and optional shredding schema, requires the legacy-format and output timestamp type settings to be present, creates the root field writers, converts the schema with SparkToParquetSchemaConverter, and returns a WriteContext with the message type and metadata.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.prepareForWrite
nodes.summary: Stores the RecordConsumer that all later writes go to.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.write
nodes.summary: Writes one InternalRow as a Parquet message by wrapping writeFields in consumeMessage.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.writeFields
nodes.summary: Writes every non-null field of a row, each inside startField/endField, using the matching ValueWriter.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.makeWriter
nodes.summary: Returns the ValueWriter for a Spark DataType. Dates use the rebase function; timestamps are written as INT96, TIMESTAMP_MICROS or TIMESTAMP_MILLIS depending on the output timestamp type (always INT64 micros inside a shredded variant); variants are written as a group with "value" and "metadata" binaries; shredding structs are filled via SparkShreddingUtils; other structs, arrays, maps, decimals and user-defined types recurse. Unsupported types raise an internal error.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.makeDecimalWriter
nodes.summary: Builds the decimal ValueWriter: standard mode writes INT32 for precision up to 9 and INT64 up to 18; legacy mode writes a fixed-length byte array from the unscaled long up to precision 18; larger precisions use a fixed-length byte array from the unscaled BigInteger bytes with sign padding.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.makeArrayWriter
nodes.summary: Builds the array ValueWriter: three-level "list"/"element" layout in standard mode, three-level "bag"/"array" layout in legacy mode with nullable elements, and a two-level repeated "array" layout in legacy mode without null elements. Repeated fields are only created for non-empty arrays and null elements are skipped.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.makeMapWriter
nodes.summary: Builds the map ValueWriter, writing a repeated key/value group named "key_value" in standard mode or "map" in legacy mode, with a required "key" and an optional "value" (skipped when null).

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.consumeMessage
nodes.summary: Runs a block between startMessage and endMessage on the RecordConsumer.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.consumeGroup
nodes.summary: Runs a block between startGroup and endGroup on the RecordConsumer.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.consumeField
nodes.summary: Runs a block between startField and endField for a named field and index on the RecordConsumer.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.setSchema
nodes.summary: Companion helper: stores the row schema JSON under SPARK_ROW_SCHEMA in the configuration and sets the Parquet writer version to PARQUET_1_0 if unset.

nodes.name: ParquetWriteSupport.setShreddingSchema
nodes.summary: Companion helper: stores the variant shredding schema JSON under SPARK_VARIANT_SHREDDING_SCHEMA in the configuration.

nodes.name: OrcOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcOptions, the option holder for the ORC data source (compression codec and schema merging), and its companion with the option names.

nodes.name: OrcOptions
nodes.summary: Class (with companion object) extending FileSourceOptions that parses ORC data source options. compressionCodec resolves the codec by precedence "compression", then "orc.compress", then the SQL conf orcCompressionCodec, lowercases it, and throws a codec-not-available error if it is not among the known short names. mergeSchema reads the "mergeSchema" option, falling back to the SQL conf isOrcSchemaMergingEnabled. The companion (extending DataSourceOptions) defines MERGE_SCHEMA, ORC_COMPRESSION, COMPRESSION, the short-name map built from OrcCompressionCodec, and getORCCompressionCodecName. Used by OrcFileFormat.prepareWrite and OrcUtils.inferSchema.

nodes.name: OrcOptions.getORCCompressionCodecName
nodes.summary: Companion method: returns the ORC compression kind name for a lowercase codec short name.

nodes.name: SparkShreddingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Scala support code for reading and writing shredded Parquet variant columns. It defines the schema-building helpers in SparkShreddingUtils (variantShreddingSchema, buildVariantSchema, castShredded, assembleVariant, assembleVariantStruct and their batch forms), a family of ParquetVariantReader subclasses that turn typed_value/value structs into Spark values, the ScalarCastHelper expression, and small adapters to the variant library. It is used when a Parquet variant column is scanned, either rebuilt into a full variant or read as a struct of extracted fields.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing case classes, private[this] final reader subclasses, a case object with helpers and Java-codegen string templates.

nodes.name: SparkShreddedRow
nodes.summary: Case class that wraps a SpecializedGetters row and implements ShreddingUtils.ShreddedRow so the variant library can read Spark rows. Each getter (isNullAt, getInt, getDecimal, getString, getStruct, getArray and so on) delegates to the wrapped row; getUuid always throws malformedVariant because UUIDs are not shredded. Used by ParquetVariantReader.rebuildVariant and SparkShreddingUtils.assembleVariant.

nodes.name: SchemaPathSegment
nodes.summary: Case class holding the result of looking up one VariantPathSegment in a VariantSchema: the raw path, whether it is an object or array step, the typed_value index (negative when absent) and the field or array index to extract. Built in SparkShreddingUtils.getFieldsToExtract and consumed by extractField.

nodes.name: FieldToExtract
nodes.summary: Case class pairing an array of SchemaPathSegment with a ParquetVariantReader; it describes one field of a variant struct that the scan must produce by extracting from the variant column. Returned by SparkShreddingUtils.getFieldsToExtract.

nodes.name: ScalarCastHelper
nodes.summary: Unary expression (with its companion object) that casts a non-nullable scalar typed_value into a target data type, with its own error reporting instead of the normal Cast. doGenCode generates Java code: custom casts for long/decimal to timestamp and decimal to string call VariantGet helpers inside try/catch, other combinations use a TRY-mode Cast, and unsupported ones always yield null, optionally raising an invalid variant cast error depending on castArgs.failOnError. The object adds throwInvalidVariantCast, callable from generated code. Used only by ScalarReader.

nodes.name: doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for the cast: picks a custom VariantGet cast method for long/decimal to timestamp or decimal to string, otherwise uses a TRY-mode Cast, otherwise a constant null, and appends code that throws an invalid variant cast error when castArgs.failOnError is set.

nodes.name: ParquetVariantReader
nodes.summary: Base class (with companion object) for reading a Parquet variant value, shredded or not, into a Spark value of targetType. read checks typed_value and value: if typed_value is absent it casts the binary value with VariantGet.cast, otherwise it calls readFromTyped, which subclasses override. Protected helpers rebuildVariant and invalidCast rebuild the variant or throw/return null on a bad cast. The companion apply picks the concrete reader by target type (struct, array, string-keyed map, variant or atomic type), or returns a plain container when the extraction path is missing from the schema.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads one row holding a variant: throws MALFORMED_VARIANT when both typed_value and value are null, casts value with VariantGet.cast when typed_value is null, else delegates to readFromTyped.

nodes.name: rebuildVariant
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a binary-format Variant from a shredded Parquet variant row by calling ShreddingUtils.rebuild with a VariantBuilder.

nodes.name: invalidCast
nodes.summary: Handles an impossible cast: throws invalidVariantCast with the rebuilt variant's JSON when castArgs.failOnError is true, otherwise returns null.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates the reader matching targetType: StructReader, ArrayReader, MapReader (string keys only), VariantReader or ScalarReader; returns a bare ParquetVariantReader when schema is null. Throws an unreachable error for other types.

nodes.name: StructReader
nodes.summary: Reader that produces a Spark struct from a variant. It maps each target field to a field of the object typed_value (fieldInputIndices, fieldReaders), reads shredded fields through child readers, and takes remaining fields from the unshredded object stored in value via getFieldByKey and VariantGet.cast. Shredded fields must not be null; a non-object value raises malformedVariant.

nodes.name: ArrayReader
nodes.summary: Reader that produces a Spark array from the array typed_value of a variant. It uses one element reader built from schema.arraySchema and throws malformedVariant for null elements; returns an invalid cast when the schema has no array part.

nodes.name: MapReader
nodes.summary: Reader that produces a Spark map with string keys from a variant object. It combines shredded fields (valueReaders, shreddedFieldNames) with fields found in the unshredded object in value, and raises malformedVariant if value repeats a shredded key, to avoid duplicate map keys. Arrays are shrunk when some shredded fields are missing.

nodes.name: VariantReader
nodes.summary: Reader whose target type is variant. If the column is top-level unshredded it wraps the binary value directly in a VariantVal, otherwise it rebuilds the variant from the shredded layout.

nodes.name: ScalarReader
nodes.summary: Reader for atomic target types. It builds a MutableProjection around ScalarCastHelper over the scalar typed_value and applies it in readFromTyped; when there is no scalar schema, a string target is built from the rebuilt variant JSON and other types give an invalid cast.

nodes.name: readFromTyped
nodes.summary: Reads the shredded object typed_value of a variant into a GenericInternalRow, filling missing fields from the unshredded object in value.

nodes.name: readFromTyped
nodes.summary: Reads the array typed_value into a GenericArrayData by running the element reader on each struct element.

nodes.name: readFromTyped
nodes.summary: Builds key and value arrays from shredded and unshredded object fields and returns an ArrayBasedMapData.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Returns a VariantVal, reusing the binary value when top-level unshredded and rebuilding otherwise.

nodes.name: readFromTyped
nodes.summary: Runs the cast projection on the row and returns the value, or null; handles the no-scalar-schema case.

nodes.name: SparkShreddingUtils
nodes.summary: Case object holding the entry points of Parquet variant shredding in Spark. It names the fields value, typed_value and metadata; derives shredding schemas (variantShreddingSchema, addWriteShreddingMetadata, isVariantShreddingStruct); converts a shredding StructType into a VariantSchema (buildVariantSchema) and back for scalars (scalarSchemaToSparkType); converts a Parquet type to a Spark type (parquetTypeToSparkType); shreds a Variant (castShredded); computes extraction paths (getFieldsToExtract, extractField); and assembles variants or variant structs from Parquet rows, singly or for a whole WritableColumnVector (assembleVariant, assembleVariantStruct, assembleVariantBatch, assembleVariantStructBatch).

nodes.name: buildVariantSchema
nodes.summary: Converts a Spark StructType that is a valid shredding schema into a VariantSchema, recording indexes of typed_value, value and metadata and building object, array or scalar sub-schemas recursively; rejects empty, duplicate or malformed layouts with invalidVariantShreddingSchema. A public overload (lines 455-460) accepts a DataType and requires a StructType.

nodes.name: variantShreddingSchema
nodes.summary: Given the expected schema of a variant, returns the shredding schema with value and typed_value fields inserted at each level (plus metadata at the top), for arrays, structs, variant, numeric/string/binary/datetime types; other types raise an error.

nodes.name: addWriteShreddingMetadata
nodes.summary: Adds a marker metadata key to every top-level field of a shredding schema so writers recognize it.

nodes.name: isVariantShreddingStruct
nodes.summary: Returns true when the struct is non-empty and every field carries the write-shredding marker.

nodes.name: scalarSchemaToSparkType
nodes.summary: Maps a VariantSchema.ScalarType to the matching Spark DataType (string, integral sizes, float, double, boolean, binary, decimal, date, timestamp, timestamp without time zone).

nodes.name: parquetTypeToSparkType
nodes.summary: Converts a Parquet type to a Spark DataType by wrapping it in a message type and using ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter with ignoreVariantAnnotation enabled.

nodes.name: castShredded
nodes.summary: Shreds an input Variant according to a VariantSchema using VariantShreddingWriter and returns the resulting InternalRow.

nodes.name: getFieldsToExtract
nodes.summary: Returns the FieldToExtract array for a variant struct target type (null for plain variant): resolves each parsed variant path against the file's VariantSchema into SchemaPathSegment entries and creates a ParquetVariantReader with VariantCastArgs.

nodes.name: extractField
nodes.summary: Walks a Parquet variant row along a SchemaPathSegment path, stepping into typed_value structs or arrays, falls back to the binary value for the remainder when the path is not shredded, then reads the result with the field's ParquetVariantReader.

nodes.name: assembleVariant
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a VariantVal from a shredded Parquet row with ShreddingUtils.rebuild.

nodes.name: assembleVariantStruct
nodes.summary: Builds an InternalRow whose fields are extracted from a Parquet variant row using extractField; requires non-null metadata.

nodes.name: assembleVariantBatch
nodes.summary: Batch version of assembleVariant: fills an output WritableColumnVector with value and metadata child columns for every row of the input vector.

nodes.name: assembleVariantStructBatch
nodes.summary: Batch version of assembleVariantStruct: converts each assembled struct into the output vector using a RowToColumnConverter.

nodes.name: SparkShreddedResult
nodes.summary: Private class implementing VariantShreddingWriter.ShreddedResult by storing results in a GenericInternalRow sized to the schema. addArray, addObject, addScalar, addVariantValue and addMetadata write into the typed_value, value or metadata slot; addScalar converts strings and decimals to Spark's UTF8String and Decimal.

nodes.name: SparkShreddedResultBuilder
nodes.summary: Private builder implementing VariantShreddingWriter.ShreddedResultBuilder: createEmpty returns a SparkShreddedResult and allowNumericScaleChanges returns true.

nodes.name: SecureConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract SecureConnectionProvider for JDBC drivers that use a Kerberos keytab and principal, and a JDBCConfiguration helper. The provider handles a connection only when keytab and principal are set and the driver class matches; before connecting it installs a JAAS login configuration for the driver's application entry.

nodes.name: SecureConnectionProvider
