nodes.summary: Abstract JDBC provider (with companion object) for secured connections. It extends BasicConnectionProvider; subclasses supply driverClass and appEntry. canHandle requires non-null keytab and principal and a matching driverClass; getConnection first calls setAuthenticationConfig and then the basic getConnection. setAuthenticationConfig wraps the current JAAS Configuration in a JDBCConfiguration and installs it with Configuration.setConfiguration.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Returns true when keytab and principal are set in the JDBC options and the configured driver class equals this provider's driverClass (case-insensitive).

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Sets the authentication configuration for the driver and then delegates to the basic connection logic.

nodes.name: setAuthenticationConfig
nodes.summary: Reads the current JAAS configuration, wraps it in a JDBCConfiguration for appEntry with the keytab and principal, and sets it as the active configuration.

nodes.name: JDBCConfiguration
nodes.summary: JAAS Configuration subclass that returns a Krb5 login module entry (keytab, principal, useKeyTab, refreshKrb5Config) for the requested application entry and delegates every other name to the parent configuration. The module name comes from SecurityUtils.getKrb5LoginModuleName.

nodes.name: getAppConfigurationEntry
nodes.summary: Returns the Kerberos entry when the name equals appEntry, otherwise asks the parent configuration.

nodes.name: DriverRegistry.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DriverRegistry object, which registers JDBC drivers loaded from user-supplied jars through a thin DriverWrapper so java.sql.DriverManager can use them, and looks registered drivers up by class name.

nodes.name: DriverRegistry
nodes.summary: Singleton registry of wrapped JDBC drivers. The object first touches DriverManager.getDrivers to avoid initialization races. register(className) loads the class with the context or Spark class loader and, unless it came from the bootstrap loader or is already wrapped, creates a DriverWrapper and registers it with DriverManager under a lock. get(className) finds a registered driver, unwrapping DriverWrapper, or throws an internal error if none matches.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a driver class by name: skips bootstrap-loaded classes and existing wrappers, otherwise instantiates it, wraps it in a DriverWrapper and registers it with DriverManager.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the registered Driver whose class canonical name equals className, looking through DriverWrapper, or throws an internal error.

nodes.name: ConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ConnectionProviderBase and the ConnectionProvider object, which load JdbcConnectionProvider implementations with ServiceLoader, drop those disabled in SQLConf, and select one to create a JDBC connection for a given driver and options.

nodes.name: ConnectionProviderBase
nodes.summary: Protected abstract class that holds the list of loaded JdbcConnectionProvider instances. loadProviders reads providers through ServiceLoader (logging and skipping failures) and removes names listed in SQLConf.disabledJdbcConnectionProviders. create filters providers by canHandle, picks one by the optional provider name or requires exactly one match, and calls getConnection; when the provider modifiesSecurityContext it does so inside SecurityConfigurationLock and restores the original JAAS configuration afterwards.

nodes.name: loadProviders
nodes.summary: Loads all JdbcConnectionProvider services, tolerating load failures, and filters out providers disabled by the SQL configuration.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Selects a connection provider for the driver, options and optional name (error if none or several match) and returns its connection, guarding security-context changes with SecurityConfigurationLock.

nodes.name: ConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Private[sql] singleton extending ConnectionProviderBase with no extra members; it is the shared instance used to create JDBC connections.

nodes.name: OrcArrayColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Column vector adapter for Spark ArrayType backed by an ORC ListColumnVector; created by OrcColumnVectorUtils for list columns.

nodes.name: OrcArrayColumnVector
nodes.summary: OrcColumnVector subclass for ArrayType. It keeps the child OrcColumnVector holding all elements, and getArray(rowId) returns a ColumnarArray built from the ListColumnVector offsets and lengths for that row. All other typed getters (getBoolean, getInt, getUTF8String, getMap, getChild and so on) throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: getArray
nodes.summary: Returns the array value of a row as a ColumnarArray over the child data vector, using the offset and length stored in the ORC ListColumnVector.

nodes.name: OrcAtomicColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Column vector adapter for Spark atomic types backed by ORC long, double, bytes, decimal or timestamp column vectors; created by OrcColumnVectorUtils for non-nested columns.

nodes.name: OrcAtomicColumnVector
nodes.summary: OrcColumnVector subclass for atomic types. The constructor picks which one of LongColumnVector, DoubleColumnVector, BytesColumnVector, DecimalColumnVector or TimestampColumnVector is populated (otherwise it throws) and records whether the Spark type is a date or timestamp. Getters (getBoolean, getByte, getShort, getInt, getLong, getFloat, getDouble, getDecimal, getUTF8String, getBinary) read from that vector via getRowIndex; getInt rebases Julian days to Gregorian for dates and getLong converts a timestamp with DateTimeUtils.fromJavaTimestamp. Array, map and child access throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: OrcAtomicColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor that wraps the given ORC ColumnVector into exactly one typed field (long, double, bytes, decimal or timestamp) and sets the isDate and isTimestamp flags from the Spark DataType; throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException for other vector classes.

nodes.name: getInt
nodes.summary: Reads an int from the long vector; for DateType it rebases the value from Julian to Gregorian days with RebaseDateTime.rebaseJulianToGregorianDays.

nodes.name: getLong
nodes.summary: Reads a long; for TimestampType it converts the ORC timestamp via DateTimeUtils.fromJavaTimestamp, otherwise it reads the long vector.

nodes.name: getDecimal
nodes.summary: Returns the Decimal at a row from the decimal vector with the requested precision and scale, or null when the row is null.

nodes.name: getUTF8String
nodes.summary: Returns the string at a row as a UTF8String over the bytes vector (start and length), or null when the row is null.

nodes.name: getBinary
nodes.summary: Copies the bytes at a row out of the bytes vector into a new byte array, or null when the row is null.

nodes.name: OrcColumnStatistics.java
nodes.summary: Defines OrcColumnStatistics, a tree wrapper that turns the flat array of ORC ColumnStatistics from the file footer into a nested structure following the data types. Used for aggregate push down in ORC.

nodes.name: OrcColumnStatistics
nodes.summary: Holds one ORC ColumnStatistics and a list of child OrcColumnStatistics for the sub-fields of struct, map and array columns (the flat footer array is in pre-order of the type tree). Provides getStatistics(), get(ordinal) for a child (throws IndexOutOfBoundsException when out of range) and add(child).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the child statistics at the given ordinal, throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException with a formatted message when the ordinal is out of range.

nodes.name: OrcColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract OrcColumnVector, which adapts Hive's ColumnVector to Spark's vectorized ColumnVector so ORC batches can be wrapped in a ColumnarBatch without copying.

nodes.name: OrcColumnVector
nodes.summary: Abstract base class extending Spark's vectorized ColumnVector and holding the wrapped Hive ColumnVector (baseData) and the current batch size. Implements hasNull, numNulls (handles repeating and no-null vectors), isNullAt and close (no-op), exposes setBatchSize, and provides the protected getRowIndex helper that maps a row id to 0 when the vector is repeating. Subclasses in this directory are OrcAtomicColumnVector, OrcArrayColumnVector, OrcMapColumnVector and OrcStructColumnVector.

nodes.name: numNulls
nodes.summary: Counts null entries in the batch: batchSize or 0 for a repeating vector depending on the first null flag, 0 if there are no nulls, otherwise a scan of isNull over the batch size.

nodes.name: isNullAt
nodes.summary: Returns whether the row is null in the wrapped vector, mapping the row id through getRowIndex.

nodes.name: setBatchSize
nodes.summary: Records the number of valid rows in the current ORC batch; called by the batch reader after each batch is read.

nodes.name: getRowIndex
nodes.summary: Helper returning 0 when the wrapped vector isRepeating, otherwise the given row id.

nodes.name: OrcColumnVectorUtils.java
nodes.summary: Package-private utility that converts a Hive ColumnVector tree into the matching OrcColumnVector wrapper tree for a Spark DataType.

nodes.name: OrcColumnVectorUtils
nodes.summary: Utility class with the static toOrcColumnVector method. It wraps long, double, bytes, decimal and timestamp vectors in OrcAtomicColumnVector, and recursively builds OrcStructColumnVector, OrcArrayColumnVector and OrcMapColumnVector for struct, list and map vectors; it throws IllegalArgumentException for other combinations.

nodes.name: toOrcColumnVector
nodes.summary: Recursive factory choosing the OrcColumnVector wrapper from the runtime class of the Hive ColumnVector and the Spark DataType (struct fields, array element type, map key and value types).

nodes.name: OrcDeserializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcDeserializer, which converts ORC structs (OrcStruct and the Hadoop Writable values inside them) into Spark InternalRow objects, plus small updater helpers that write into rows or array data. Used by the ORC read path when rows are read without the vectorized reader.

nodes.name: OrcDeserializer
nodes.summary: Builds, for a required schema and the requested ORC column ids, one writer function per column and reuses a single SpecificInternalRow as the result. deserialize(orcStruct) and deserializeFromValues(orcValues) fill that row (null for missing values) and then apply existence default values for columns that are absent from the file (column id -1). It maps each Catalyst type (primitives, string, binary, date, timestamp, decimal, struct, array, map, user defined types) to the matching Writable type.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Converts one OrcStruct to the reused InternalRow: for each target column that has a writer it reads the field at the requested ORC column id, sets null or runs the writer, then applies existence default values using the bitmask.

nodes.name: deserializeFromValues
nodes.summary: Same as deserialize but takes a sequence of already extracted ORC Writable values instead of an OrcStruct.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Recursive factory that returns a function writing an ORC Writable value into a CatalystDataUpdater at an ordinal, chosen by the Catalyst DataType. Handles each primitive, string, binary, date (via OrcShimUtils.getGregorianDays), timestamp, decimal (via OrcShimUtils.getDecimal), struct (copies the row when nested in an array or map), array, map and user defined type, and throws an internal error for unsupported types.

nodes.name: createArrayData
nodes.summary: Allocates the ArrayData used for ORC lists and map keys/values: an UnsafeArrayData backed by a primitive array for boolean, byte, short, int, long, float, double and interval types, otherwise a GenericArrayData.

nodes.name: CatalystDataUpdater
nodes.summary: Sealed trait giving a uniform way to set values (set, setNullAt, setBoolean, setByte, setShort, setInt, setLong, setDouble, setFloat) inside either an InternalRow or an ArrayData; the typed setters default to set.

nodes.name: RowUpdater
nodes.summary: CatalystDataUpdater implementation that forwards every set call to an InternalRow.

nodes.name: ArrayDataUpdater
nodes.summary: Final CatalystDataUpdater implementation that forwards every set call to an ArrayData; used for array elements and map keys and values.

nodes.name: OrcSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcSerializer, which converts Spark InternalRow objects into ORC structs made of Hadoop Writable values. Used by the ORC write path to produce the records handed to the ORC output writer.

nodes.name: OrcSerializer
nodes.summary: Given a data schema, derives the ORC TypeDescription (OrcUtils.orcTypeDescription), allocates one reusable OrcStruct and builds one converter per column. serialize(row) fills that struct, writing null for null columns. Converters map each Catalyst type to the matching Writable (BooleanWritable, IntWritable, Text, BytesWritable, OrcTimestamp, OrcList, OrcMap, nested OrcStruct, and others) and reuse the Writable object for primitives where possible.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Converts one InternalRow to the shared OrcStruct by running the per-column converters and setting null fields for null values; returns the same OrcStruct instance on every call.

nodes.name: newConverter
nodes.summary: Recursive factory that returns a converter from a SpecializedGetters value at an ordinal to an ORC Writable, selected by Catalyst DataType and ORC TypeDescription. The reuseObj flag decides whether a single Writable is reused (it is false for array elements and map keys and values, which are stored in lists). Date and decimal use OrcShimUtils.getDateWritable and getHiveDecimalWritable; unsupported types raise an internal error.

nodes.name: OrcColumnarBatchReader.java
nodes.summary: Defines OrcColumnarBatchReader, a record reader that returns ColumnarBatch objects from ORC files so vectorized execution (whole-stage codegen) can consume them.

nodes.name: OrcColumnarBatchReader
nodes.summary: Hadoop RecordReader<Void, ColumnarBatch> over an ORC file split. initialize creates the ORC Reader and row reader (optionally with a pre-read OrcTail), then initBatch builds the ColumnarBatch: partition columns become ConstantColumnVector values, columns missing from the file become on-heap or off-heap vectors filled with null or the existence default, and file columns are wrapped through OrcColumnVectorUtils.toOrcColumnVector. nextKeyValue/nextBatch read the next ORC batch and set the row count; close releases the batch and reader.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Opens the ORC file for the split (path, max file length, filesystem, optional OrcTail), builds reader options for the split range and creates the row reader; the two-argument overload (lines 123-127) delegates here with a null OrcTail. initBatch must be called afterwards.

nodes.name: initBatch
nodes.summary: Creates the ORC VectorizedRowBatch of the configured capacity and the ColumnarBatch of wrappers: constant vectors for partition columns, constant null/default vectors for missing columns (throwing IllegalArgumentException if the default cannot be assigned), and OrcColumnVector wrappers for columns present in the file.

nodes.name: nextBatch
nodes.summary: Reads the next ORC batch into the row batch, returns false at end of data, otherwise sets the number of rows on the ColumnarBatch and the batch size on each wrapped OrcColumnVector.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the ColumnarBatch and the ORC record reader and clears both references.

nodes.name: OrcCompressionCodec.java
nodes.summary: Defines the OrcCompressionCodec enum mapping Spark's ORC compression codec names to ORC CompressionKind values.

nodes.name: OrcCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Enum with the constants NONE, UNCOMPRESSED (both CompressionKind.NONE), ZLIB, SNAPPY, LZO, LZ4, ZSTD and BROTLI. getCompressionKind returns the ORC CompressionKind and lowerCaseName returns the lower-case codec name from a static EnumMap. Used where a Spark compression option has to be translated to an ORC codec.

nodes.name: OrcFooterReader.java
nodes.summary: Java utility class with static helpers that read column statistics from an ORC file footer and convert them to Spark's OrcColumnStatistics tree.

nodes.name: OrcFooterReader
nodes.summary: Utility class for reading ORC file footers. readStatistics takes an ORC Reader, converts its schema with OrcUtils.toCatalystSchema and returns the nested statistics; the private convertStatistics consumes a queue of ORC ColumnStatistics in pre-order and recurses through struct fields, map key and value types and array element types.

nodes.name: readStatistics
nodes.summary: Static method that reads the schema and column statistics of an ORC file and returns them as an OrcColumnStatistics tree matching the Spark schema.

nodes.name: convertStatistics
nodes.summary: Recursively builds an OrcColumnStatistics by removing one ORC statistic from the queue and adding children for struct fields, map key and value, or array element.

nodes.name: OrcMapColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Java column vector for Spark MapType over an ORC MapColumnVector, built from a keys vector and a values vector.

nodes.name: OrcMapColumnVector
nodes.summary: Column vector for map columns read from ORC. It keeps child OrcColumnVector instances for keys and values; getMap reads the offset and length of the row from the underlying MapColumnVector and returns a ColumnarMap over the child vectors. All other typed getters (getBoolean through getArray) and getChild throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: getMap
nodes.summary: Returns a ColumnarMap for the given row using offset and length from the ORC MapColumnVector and the key and value child vectors.

nodes.name: OrcStructColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Java column vector for Spark StructType over an ORC vector, holding one OrcColumnVector per struct field.

nodes.name: OrcStructColumnVector
nodes.summary: Column vector for struct columns read from ORC. It stores an array of field vectors; getChild(ordinal) returns the field vector at that ordinal. The scalar getters, getArray and getMap throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: BasicConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BasicConnectionProvider, the default JDBC connection provider that connects without Kerberos by passing the JDBC options as connection properties to the driver.

nodes.name: BasicConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Default, non-secure JdbcConnectionProvider named "basic". canHandle is true when keytab or principal is missing; getConnection builds a Properties object (from getAdditionalProperties plus the JDBC options), logs the redacted URL and calls driver.connect; modifiesSecurityContext returns false. Subclasses override getAdditionalProperties.

nodes.name: getAdditionalProperties
nodes.summary: Returns an empty Properties object; hook for subclasses to add driver-specific properties (data source properties take precedence).

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: True when the options have no keytab or no principal.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Merges additional properties with the JDBC connection properties and opens the connection with driver.connect on the JDBC URL.

nodes.name: modifiesSecurityContext
nodes.summary: Always returns false because the basic provider does not change the security context.

nodes.name: DB2ConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DB2ConnectionProvider, a Kerberos-enabled JDBC provider for the DB2 driver.

nodes.name: DB2ConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Secure JDBC provider named "db2" for driver class com.ibm.db2.jcc.DB2Driver with JAAS entry "JaasClient". getConnection sets the authentication configuration, logs in from the keytab with Hadoop UserGroupInformation and connects inside doAs; getAdditionalProperties sets securityMechanism to 11 (Kerberos) and KerberosServerPrincipal.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Installs the JAAS configuration, logs in the principal from its keytab and runs the parent getConnection as that user.

nodes.name: getAdditionalProperties
nodes.summary: Returns properties that switch the DB2 driver to Kerberos (securityMechanism 11) and set the server principal.

nodes.name: MSSQLConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MSSQLConnectionProvider, a Kerberos-enabled JDBC provider for the SQL Server driver that also finds the JAAS configuration name from the JDBC URL.

nodes.name: MSSQLConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Secure JDBC provider named "mssql" for driver class com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver. appEntry looks up the jaasConfigurationName property (default SQLJDBCDriver) by calling the driver's private parseAndMergeProperties method by reflection, or by splitting the URL on ';' and '=' if the method is missing. getConnection logs in from the keytab and connects inside doAs; getAdditionalProperties sets integratedSecurity=true and authenticationScheme=JavaKerberos.

nodes.name: appEntry
nodes.summary: Determines the JAAS application entry from the URL or driver parser, falling back to the default name SQLJDBCDriver.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Installs the JAAS configuration, logs in from the keytab and calls the parent getConnection inside doAs.

nodes.name: getAdditionalProperties
nodes.summary: Returns properties enabling integrated Kerberos security in the SQL Server driver.

nodes.name: MariaDBConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MariaDBConnectionProvider, a minimal Kerberos-enabled JDBC provider for the MariaDB driver.

nodes.name: MariaDBConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Secure JDBC provider named "mariadb" for driver class org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver; its only behavior is the JAAS entry name "Krb5ConnectorContext" returned by appEntry, the rest is inherited from SecureConnectionProvider.

nodes.name: OracleConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OracleConnectionProvider, a Kerberos-enabled JDBC provider for the Oracle driver.

nodes.name: OracleConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Secure JDBC provider named "oracle" for driver class oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver with JAAS entry "kprb5module". getConnection logs in from the keytab and connects inside doAs; getAdditionalProperties sets oracle.net.authentication_services to (KERBEROS5).

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Installs the JAAS configuration, logs in from the keytab and calls the parent getConnection inside doAs.

nodes.name: getAdditionalProperties
nodes.summary: Returns the property that turns on Kerberos authentication in the Oracle driver.

nodes.name: PostgresConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PostgresConnectionProvider, a Kerberos-enabled JDBC provider for the PostgreSQL driver.

nodes.name: PostgresConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Secure JDBC provider named "postgres" for driver class org.postgresql.Driver. appEntry calls the driver's parseURL method by reflection and returns the jaasApplicationName property, defaulting to "pgjdbc".

nodes.name: appEntry
nodes.summary: Finds the JAAS application name from the parsed JDBC URL via reflection on parseURL, default pgjdbc.

nodes.name: JDBCRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JDBC data source relation: JDBCRelation (a scannable, insertable relation over a JDBC table) and its companion object, which computes per-partition WHERE clauses from the partitionColumn, lowerBound, upperBound and numPartitions options and resolves the table schema.

nodes.name: JDBCPartitioningInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding the validated partitioning instructions for a JDBC read: the partition column, its data type, long-valued lower and upper bounds, and the requested number of partitions. It is produced inside JDBCRelation.columnPartition and consumed there to build the partition WHERE clauses.

nodes.name: JDBCRelation
nodes.summary: Covers both the JDBCRelation companion object (lines 50-268) and the JDBCRelation case class (lines 270-348). The object computes partition WHERE clauses (columnPartition), resolves the remote schema with an optional custom schema (getSchema) and builds a relation with a timed schema fetch (apply). The class is a BaseRelation that supports pruned and filtered scans and inserts: it reports which filters the dialect cannot compile (unhandledFilters), builds JDBCRDD scans with pushed-down predicates, aggregates, sample, sort, limit and offset (two buildScan overloads), writes a DataFrame through the JDBC writer (insert), and prints a credential-free description (toString).

nodes.name: columnPartition
nodes.summary: Companion-object method that turns the partitionColumn, lowerBound, upperBound and numPartitions options into an array of JDBCPartition objects, each carrying a WHERE clause. It validates the options, converts bounds to longs, shrinks the partition count when the bound range is smaller than it, computes a stride with fixed-point decimals to avoid overflow, centers the first and last partitions, adds an 'is null' predicate to the first partition, and falls back to a single partition when no partitioning is requested.

nodes.name: verifyAndGetNormalizedPartitionColumn
nodes.summary: Private helper that finds the partition column in the resolved schema (matching either the raw or dialect-quoted name), rejects columns that are not numeric, date or timestamp, and returns the dialect-quoted column name with its data type.

nodes.name: toInternalBoundValue
nodes.summary: Private helper that parses a string bound option into a long: numeric types use toLong, dates and timestamps are parsed with the session time zone, and a failure raises an IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: toBoundValueInWhereClause
nodes.summary: Private helper that renders a long partition bound as text for a WHERE clause: numbers as plain text, dates and timestamps as quoted formatted strings using the given time zone.

nodes.name: getSchema
nodes.summary: Resolves the Catalyst schema of the JDBC table through JDBCRDD.resolveTable and, when a customSchema option is set, replaces column types using JdbcUtils.getCustomSchema.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory taking partitions and JDBCOptions plus a SparkSession. It creates a schema-fetch SQL metric, resolves the schema inside a timing block, and returns a JDBCRelation holding the metric under schemaFetchKey.

nodes.name: unhandledFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the filters the JDBC dialect cannot compile to its SQL syntax, so Spark evaluates them itself; when predicate push down is disabled it returns all filters.

nodes.name: buildScan
nodes.summary: Two overloads share this id. The first (lines 293-309) is the PrunedFilteredScan entry point: it converts filters to V2 predicates when push down is enabled and calls JDBCRDD.scanTable. The second (this range) accepts final schema, predicates, group-by columns, table sample clause, limit, sort orders and offset for aggregate, sample and limit push down and passes them all to JDBCRDD.scanTable, casting the result back to RDD[Row].

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Implements InsertableRelation by writing the DataFrame with the JDBC writer in Overwrite or Append mode using the url, table-or-query and properties from the options.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Builds the plan description 'JDBCRelation(prepareQuery+tableOrQuery)' with the partition count, deliberately leaving out credentials.

nodes.name: JdbcRelationProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Registers the 'jdbc' data source: JdbcRelationProvider creates JDBCRelation instances for reads and, for writes, applies the SaveMode semantics (overwrite with truncate or drop-and-recreate, append, error-if-exists, ignore) before returning a relation over the written table.

nodes.name: JdbcRelationProvider
nodes.summary: Data source provider with short name 'jdbc'. The read createRelation builds JDBCOptions, fetches the schema with a timing metric, computes partitions via JDBCRelation.columnPartition and returns a JDBCRelation. The write createRelation checks whether the table exists, then handles Overwrite (truncate and load when truncate is on and the dialect does not cascade, else drop, create and save), Append, ErrorIfExists and Ignore, creates and saves the table when missing, closes the connection and finally returns a read relation. Two createRelation overloads exist; the write one is widest.

nodes.name: createRelation
nodes.summary: Write-path overload (lines 52-99, widest; the read overload is lines 32-50). Opens a connection from the dialect, branches on table existence and SaveMode, uses JdbcUtils helpers (tableExists, truncateTable, dropTable, createTable, saveTable, getSchemaOption, isCascadingTruncateTable), and returns the read relation for the written table.

nodes.name: JdbcUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JdbcUtils object, the shared helper layer for Spark's JDBC data source: converting ResultSets to Spark rows and schemas, writing DataFrame partitions with batched inserts and transactions, generating table DDL, and running schema, table and index operations through a JdbcDialect. Used by the JDBC relation, the JDBC catalog code and the write path.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object with private type aliases JDBCValueGetter and JDBCValueSetter (functions between a ResultSet/PreparedStatement and a row); per-type behavior is built by pattern matching on the Catalyst DataType and returning closures.

nodes.name: JdbcUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton of utility functions for JDBC tables, used by the JDBC read and write paths. Read side: getSchemaOption and getSchema (ResultSet metadata to StructType, through getCatalystType and the dialect), getCustomSchema (customSchema option), resultSetToRows and resultSetToSparkInternalRows (ResultSet to Row/InternalRow with makeGetters/makeGetter), createSchemaFetchMetric. Write side: getInsertStatement, saveTable and savePartition (batched inserts with transaction isolation handling and task interrupt closing of the connection), makeSetter (Row field to PreparedStatement parameter), schemaString and createTable, getCommonJDBCType and getJdbcType. DDL helpers that mostly delegate to the JdbcDialect: tableExists, dropTable, truncateTable, isCascadingTruncateTable, renameTable, alterTable, createSchema, schemaExists, listSchemas, alterSchemaComment, removeSchemaComment, dropSchema, createIndex, indexExists, dropIndex, listIndexes (all via executeStatement where they run SQL). Also processIndexProperties, containsIndexTypeIgnoreCase, getSupportedIndexTypeList, checkIfIndexExists, executeQuery, classifyException and withConnection. Looks up the dialect with JdbcDialects.get(options.url) in nearly every method.

nodes.name: tableExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether the target table exists by preparing and running the dialect's table-exists query, treating an object-not-found SQLException (as decided by the dialect) as false and rethrowing any other failure.

nodes.name: truncateTable
nodes.summary: Truncates the target table using the dialect's truncate query, passing the cascade option only when it was set in the write options.

nodes.name: getInsertStatement
nodes.summary: Builds the INSERT statement for a row via the dialect. When the existing table schema is known, it keeps the DataFrame column order but uses the table's column names (resolved with the session resolver) so case-sensitive databases receive the right names.

nodes.name: getCommonJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps a Catalyst DataType (integral, floating, boolean, string, binary, char, varchar, timestamp, timestamp NTZ, date, decimal) to a default JdbcType (database type name plus java.sql.Types code); returns None for unsupported types so a dialect can decide.

nodes.name: getJdbcType
nodes.summary: Resolves the JdbcType for a Catalyst type by asking the dialect first and falling back to getCommonJDBCType; throws a query execution error when neither knows the type. Used when creating tables, setting nulls and creating arrays.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Default mapping from a java.sql.Types code (with type name, precision, scale, signedness and the NTZ preference) to a Catalyst type, including decimal handling and char/varchar. Called only when the dialect returns no type; unknown codes raise an unrecognized SQL type error.

nodes.name: getSchemaOption
nodes.summary: Returns the Catalyst schema of the table or query in the options if it can be queried, running the dialect's schema query and delegating to getSchema; returns None when a SQLException occurs.

nodes.name: getSchema
nodes.summary: Converts a ResultSet's metadata into a StructType. Per column it reads label, type, precision, scale, signedness and nullability, records metadata flags (logical_time_type, rowid, isSigned, isTimestampNTZ, scale, jdbcClientType), lets the dialect update metadata and supply the Catalyst type, and falls back to getCatalystType.

nodes.name: resultSetToRows
nodes.summary: Converts a ResultSet into an iterator of external Rows using a dialect: builds an input metrics holder from the current task (or a fresh one), gets internal rows from resultSetToSparkInternalRows and maps them through an ExpressionEncoder deserializer. The overload without a dialect passes NoopDialect.

nodes.name: resultSetToSparkInternalRows
nodes.summary: Wraps a ResultSet in a NextIterator of InternalRow that reuses one mutable row, applies the per-column getters, counts records read in the input metrics, optionally times fetch and conversion with a SQLMetric, and closes the ResultSet when finished.

nodes.name: createSchemaFetchMetric
nodes.summary: Creates a nano-timing SQLMetric named by JDBCRelation.schemaFetchName for measuring the schema fetch time.

nodes.name: makeGetters
nodes.summary: Creates one JDBCValueGetter per field of the schema (after replacing char/varchar with string) by calling makeGetter with the field's type and metadata.

nodes.name: makeGetter
nodes.summary: Builds the function that copies one ResultSet column into an InternalRow field, with a case per Catalyst type: primitives, decimal with fixed precision and scale, dates and timestamps via dialect conversions, time-of-day, binary-as-long, row ids, intervals, PostgreSQL bit arrays, nested arrays and null. Unsupported types raise an unsupported JDBC type error.

nodes.name: makeSetter
nodes.summary: Builds the function that writes one Row field into a PreparedStatement parameter, with a case per Catalyst type: primitives, string, binary, timestamp and date (java.time or java.sql depending on the Java 8 API setting), timestamp NTZ via the dialect, decimal and arrays created with Connection.createArrayOf. Other types raise an error.

nodes.name: savePartition
nodes.summary: Writes one partition of rows to the database with batched inserts. It opens a connection from the dialect, registers a task interrupt listener that closes it, picks a usable transaction isolation level, sets nulls and values using the setters, executes batches every batchSize rows, commits or rolls back, and records the number of rows written in the task output metrics.

nodes.name: isolationLevelString
nodes.summary: Converts a java.sql.Connection transaction isolation constant into a readable name such as NONE, READ_COMMITTED or SERIALIZABLE for log messages.

nodes.name: schemaString
nodes.summary: Builds the column definition list for CREATE TABLE from a schema: each column is a quoted name, a type (a user-specified type from createTableColumnTypes or the JdbcType definition) and NOT NULL when not nullable.

nodes.name: parseUserSpecifiedCreateTableColumnTypes
nodes.summary: Parses the createTableColumnTypes option as a table schema string, checks for duplicate names and for names missing from the DataFrame schema, and returns a map from column name to database type (case insensitive unless caseSensitive).

nodes.name: getCustomSchema
nodes.summary: Applies the customSchema option: parses it as a schema, checks name duplication, and replaces the data type of every table column whose name matches (using the given resolver); returns the table schema unchanged when the option is null or empty.

nodes.name: saveTable
nodes.summary: Saves a DataFrame to a JDBC table: builds the insert statement, validates and applies the numPartitions option by coalescing, then runs savePartition on each partition with foreachPartition.

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: Creates a table with the given schema through the dialect, using schemaString for the columns and applying the query timeout; then tries to set the table comment and only logs a warning if that fails.

nodes.name: alterTable
nodes.summary: Applies TableChange changes to a table via the dialect. A single change runs as one statement; several changes run in one transaction (commit, rollback on error) and fail with a multi-action error if the database has no transaction support.

nodes.name: createSchema
nodes.summary: Creates a database schema by calling the dialect's createSchema on a new statement with the query timeout set.

nodes.name: executeStatement
nodes.summary: Private helper that runs one update SQL string on a new statement with the query timeout and always closes the statement. Used by dropTable, renameTable, alterTable, schema comment, dropSchema, createIndex and dropIndex.

nodes.name: checkIfIndexExists
nodes.summary: Runs the given SQL and returns whether it yields a row, meaning the index exists; any exception is logged as a warning and treated as false.

nodes.name: processIndexProperties
nodes.summary: Splits index properties into an index type clause (USING <type>, checked against the dialect's supported list, otherwise an unsupported operation error) and a list of remaining key = value properties.

nodes.name: containsIndexTypeIgnoreCase
nodes.summary: Returns whether a value matches one of the supported index types ignoring case; throws an unsupported operation error if the list is empty.

nodes.name: getSupportedIndexTypeList
nodes.summary: Returns the supported index types for a dialect name: BTREE and HASH for mysql, BTREE, HASH and BRIN for postgresql, and none for other names.

nodes.name: executeQuery
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL query on a new statement with the query timeout, passes the ResultSet to the caller's function and closes both the ResultSet and the statement afterwards.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Runs a block and rethrows SparkThrowable errors unchanged, while converting any other Throwable through the dialect's classifyException using the given condition, parameters and description.

nodes.name: withConnection
nodes.summary: Opens a connection through the dialect's connection factory (wrapping failures as FAILED_JDBC.CONNECTION with the redacted URL), runs the given function with it and always closes the connection.

nodes.name: H2Dialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines H2Dialect, the JDBC dialect used for URLs starting with jdbc:h2. It adds H2-specific type mapping, index SQL, error classification, function push-down support and an H2 SQL builder that rewrites a few expressions.
nodes.languageNotes: Case class mixing in the NoLegacyJDBCError trait; contains a nested builder class that overrides SQL generation methods.

nodes.name: H2Dialect
nodes.summary: Private case class that extends JdbcDialect with NoLegacyJDBCError. canHandle accepts URLs beginning with "jdbc:h2". It maps NUMERIC columns with precision above 38 to a shrunken DecimalType, maps timestamp and time with time zone to TimestampType, supplies CLOB/BOOLEAN/SMALLINT/NUMERIC write types, builds and checks and lists indexes through INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries, translates H2 error codes (42101, 42102, 90079, 42111, 42112) into table, namespace and index exceptions, whitelists the aggregate and scalar functions that may be pushed down, and holds a test-only registry of user-defined functions. Limit, offset and join push-down are enabled.

nodes.name: H2SQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner SQL builder for H2 that extends JDBCSQLBuilder. It rejects DISTINCT on aggregate functions H2 cannot handle, renames EXTRACT fields DAY_OF_WEEK, WEEK and YEAR_OF_WEEK to their ISO variants, and rewrites MD5, SHA1 and SHA2 into RAWTOHEX(HASH(...)) calls. Created by H2Dialect.compileExpression.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Returns true when the lower-cased JDBC URL starts with jdbc:h2.

nodes.name: isSupportedFunction
nodes.summary: Checks whether a function name is in the dialect set of supported aggregate and scalar functions that can be pushed down to H2.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Treats H2 error codes 42102, 42103, 42104 and 90079 as object-not-found errors.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Best-effort syntax error check: true when the SQLState starts with "42".

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps H2 JDBC types to Spark types: NUMERIC wider than 38 is shrunk to precision 38 while keeping the scale-to-size ratio, and timestamp or time with time zone becomes TimestampType; otherwise returns None for default handling.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Spark types to H2 column types for writes (CLOB, BOOLEAN, SMALLINT, NUMERIC(p,s)), falling back to JdbcUtils.getCommonJDBCType.

nodes.name: registerFunction
nodes.summary: Test-only helper that puts a user-defined function into the dialect function map.

nodes.name: functions
nodes.summary: Returns the registered user-defined functions as a sequence of name and UnboundFunction pairs.

nodes.name: clearFunctions
nodes.summary: Test-only helper that empties the dialect function map.

nodes.name: createIndex
nodes.summary: Builds the H2 CREATE INDEX statement from the index name, table identifier and columns, using the index type from JdbcUtils.processIndexProperties.

nodes.name: dropIndex
nodes.summary: Builds the H2 DROP INDEX statement with a schema-qualified index name.

nodes.name: indexExists
nodes.summary: Queries INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INDEXES for a matching schema, table and index name and delegates the check to JdbcUtils.checkIfIndexExists.

nodes.name: listIndexes
nodes.summary: Joins INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INDEXES and INDEX_COLUMNS, runs the query through JdbcUtils.executeQuery and folds rows into one TableIndex per index with all its columns and an optional COMMENT property; logs a warning and returns what it has on failure.

nodes.name: tableNameWithSchema
nodes.summary: Quotes the namespace parts and table name and joins them with dots.

nodes.name: indexNameWithSchema
nodes.summary: Quotes the namespace parts and index name and joins them with dots.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Translates H2 SQLException error codes into specific Spark exceptions (TableAlreadyExistsException, NoSuchTableException, NoSuchNamespaceException, IndexAlreadyExistsException, NoSuchIndexException) and otherwise defers to the parent classifyException.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression into H2 SQL using H2SQLBuilder; any non-fatal failure is logged and yields None so push-down is abandoned.

nodes.name: supportsLimit
nodes.summary: Declares that LIMIT can be pushed down to H2.

nodes.name: supportsOffset
nodes.summary: Declares that OFFSET can be pushed down to H2.

nodes.name: supportsJoin
nodes.summary: Declares that JOIN can be pushed down to H2.

nodes.name: visitAggregateFunction
nodes.summary: Throws a SparkUnsupportedOperationException when DISTINCT is requested for an aggregate in the unsupported-distinct set (for example CORR, MODE, PERCENTILE_CONT); otherwise calls the parent implementation.

nodes.name: visitExtract
nodes.summary: Builds EXTRACT(field FROM source), renaming DAY_OF_WEEK, WEEK and YEAR_OF_WEEK to ISO_DAY_OF_WEEK, ISO_WEEK and ISO_WEEK_YEAR.

nodes.name: visitSQLFunction
nodes.summary: Rewrites MD5, SHA1 and SHA2 into RAWTOHEX(HASH(...)) expressions and delegates every other function to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: JdbcDialects.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the JDBC dialect extension point: the JdbcType case class, the abstract JdbcDialect base class (type mapping, SQL text generation for DDL, indexes, truncate, limit and offset, expression compilation, exception classification), the NoLegacyJDBCError trait, the JdbcDialects registry object and the NoopDialect default.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with many overridable methods that have default bodies; dialect registry uses a mutable list and ServiceLoader.

nodes.name: JdbcType
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi case class pairing a database type definition string with the java.sql.Types code used to send null values for that type. Returned by JdbcDialect.getJDBCType.

nodes.name: NoLegacyJDBCError
nodes.summary: Private[sql] trait that extends JdbcDialect and overrides classifyException so the original failure is wrapped with the given error condition and message parameters: a SparkRuntimeException when isRuntime is true, otherwise an AnalysisException. Mixed into dialects such as H2Dialect.

nodes.name: JdbcDialects
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi registry object of dialects. registerDialect puts a dialect at the front of the list, unregisterDialect removes it, and the initializer loads dialects through ServiceLoader. get(url) returns NoopDialect when none matches, the single match when one matches, and an AggregatedDialect when several match.

nodes.name: NoopDialect
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object extending JdbcDialect whose canHandle always returns true; used as the neutral dialect when no registered dialect matches a URL.

nodes.name: registerDialect
nodes.summary: Adds a dialect to the front of the registered list (moving it to the front if already present).

nodes.name: unregisterDialect
nodes.summary: Removes a dialect from the registered list; does nothing if it is absent.

nodes.name: registerDialects
nodes.summary: Loads every JdbcDialect found by ServiceLoader on the context or Spark class loader and registers it; invoked once when the object is initialized.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Selects the dialect for a URL: filters registered dialects by canHandle, then returns NoopDialect, the single match, or a new AggregatedDialect over all matches.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Wraps the original exception: SparkRuntimeException with the given condition when isRuntime is true, otherwise AnalysisException with the condition and message parameters.

nodes.name: JdbcDialect
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi abstract base class (Serializable with Logging) that holds the quirks of one database or JDBC driver. Required method: canHandle(url). Type mapping: getCatalystType (read path) and getJDBCType (write path), plus timestamp and interval conversions. SQL text defaults: quoteIdentifier, createTable, insertIntoTable, getTableExistsQuery, getSchemaQuery, getTruncateQuery, renameTable, alterTable with column query builders, schema and table comment queries, dropSchema, dropTable. Other groups: createConnectionFactory, beforeFetch and getFetchSize, escapeSql and compileValue, expression push-down through compileExpression and the nested JDBCSQLBuilder, function support via isSupportedFunction, schema listing, index methods (createIndex, indexExists, dropIndex, listIndexes) that throw by default, exception classification (isObjectNotFoundException, isSyntaxErrorBestEffort, classifyException), LIMIT/OFFSET/TABLESAMPLE/hint/join capability flags, and updateExtraColumnMeta. Dialects subclass it and override only what differs.

nodes.name: JDBCSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Private[jdbc] inner class extending V2ExpressionSQLBuilder that renders connector V2 expressions as dialect SQL. It prints AlwaysTrue and AlwaysFalse as (1 = 1) and (1 = 0), quotes column names with the dialect quoteIdentifier, compiles literal values with compileValue, builds CAST with the dialect JDBC type, and throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException for SQL functions, aggregates, inverse distribution functions, OVERLAY and TRIM that isSupportedFunction rejects. It also offers helpers for dialects without boolean types. Created by compileExpression.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Abstract method: returns true if the dialect can be applied to the given JDBC URL. Used by JdbcDialects.get to pick dialects.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps JDBC metadata (SQL type, type name, size, metadata builder) to a Spark DataType when reading a table; default returns None so standard handling applies.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps a Spark DataType to a JdbcType when writing a table; default returns None.

nodes.name: getYearMonthIntervalAsMonths
nodes.summary: Parses a year-month interval string and returns the total number of months.

nodes.name: getDayTimeIntervalAsMicros
nodes.summary: Parses a day-time interval string and returns the duration in microseconds.

nodes.name: convertJavaTimestampToTimestampNTZ
nodes.summary: Converts a java.sql.Timestamp to a LocalDateTime with the same wall-clock time using DateTimeUtils; dialects may override it.

nodes.name: convertTimestampNTZToJavaTimestamp
nodes.summary: Converts a LocalDateTime to microseconds and then to a java.sql.Timestamp without calendar rebase.

nodes.name: createConnectionFactory
nodes.summary: Returns a function from partition id to Connection: it registers and fetches the driver through DriverRegistry, opens a connection with ConnectionProvider.create and requires that the connection is not null.

nodes.name: quoteIdentifier
nodes.summary: Wraps an identifier in double quotes, escaping embedded quotes by doubling them (ANSI style).

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: Executes CREATE TABLE with the given name, schema string and the create table options from JdbcOptionsInWrite.

nodes.name: insertIntoTable
nodes.summary: Builds an INSERT INTO statement template with quoted column names and ? placeholders for the given fields.

nodes.name: getTableExistsQuery
nodes.summary: Returns SELECT 1 FROM table WHERE 1=0, the default query used to test whether a table exists.

nodes.name: getSchemaQuery
nodes.summary: Returns SELECT * FROM table WHERE 1=0, the default query used to discover a table schema.

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Returns TRUNCATE TABLE for a table with an optional cascade flag; the one-argument overload (lines 321-323) passes isCascadingTruncateTable().

nodes.name: getFetchSize
nodes.summary: Returns the effective fetch size, by default the fetchSize in JDBCOptions; dialects can supply a default when the user sets none.

nodes.name: beforeFetch
nodes.summary: Hook run before a select; the JDBCOptions overload delegates to the deprecated overload (lines 356-357) that takes a properties map and does nothing by default.

nodes.name: escapeSql
nodes.summary: Escapes single quotes in a SQL string literal by doubling them; null stays null.

nodes.name: compileValue
nodes.summary: Converts a value to SQL literal text: quotes strings, formats timestamps, local date-times, instants and dates, joins arrays, and renders byte arrays as X hex literals.

nodes.name: isSupportedFunction
nodes.summary: Returns whether the database supports a function by upper-cased name; default is false.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression to SQL via JDBCSQLBuilder; failures are logged and produce None, which makes the framework skip push-down. The deprecated compileAggregate calls it.

nodes.name: createSchema
nodes.summary: Creates a schema and, when a non-empty comment is given, builds the comment query first and runs it after CREATE SCHEMA.

nodes.name: schemasExists
nodes.summary: Uses connection metadata getSchemas to check whether a schema with the given name exists.

nodes.name: listSchemas
nodes.summary: Lists schema names from connection metadata as an array of single-element arrays.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Best-effort test for whether a SQLException is a syntax error; default is false.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO using the fully qualified quoted names of two identifiers; a deprecated string-based overload exists at lines 633-636.

nodes.name: alterTable
nodes.summary: Turns TableChange objects (AddColumn, RenameColumn, DeleteColumn, UpdateColumnType, UpdateColumnNullability) on single-level columns into ALTER TABLE statements via the getXxxQuery methods, and raises an error for unsupported changes.

nodes.name: getAddColumnQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN with the quoted column name and type.

nodes.name: getRenameColumnQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN old TO new with quoted names.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET NULL or SET NOT NULL.

nodes.name: dropSchema
nodes.summary: Builds DROP SCHEMA, adding CASCADE when requested.

nodes.name: dropTable
nodes.summary: Builds DROP TABLE for the given table name.

nodes.name: createIndex
nodes.summary: Builds a CREATE INDEX statement; the default throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException, so dialects override it.

nodes.name: indexExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether an index exists on a table; the default throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: dropIndex
nodes.summary: Builds a DROP INDEX statement; the default throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: listIndexes
nodes.summary: Lists the indexes of a table; the default throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Treats a SQLException whose SQLState starts with "42" as an object-not-found error.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Classifies a dialect exception given an error condition, message parameters, description and runtime flag; the default calls the deprecated overload (lines 835-843) that wraps the cause in an AnalysisException with class FAILED_JDBC.UNCLASSIFIED.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns LIMIT n when n is greater than zero, otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: getOffsetClause
nodes.summary: Returns OFFSET n when n is greater than zero, otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: getJdbcSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates the JdbcSQLQueryBuilder used to assemble SELECT statements for this dialect and the given options.

nodes.name: compileTableSample
nodes.summary: Compiles a TableSampleInfo into a TABLESAMPLE clause: when supportsTableSample is true and the sample is Bernoulli without replacement it uses getTableSample, otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: getFullyQualifiedQuotedTableName
nodes.summary: Quotes each namespace part and the table name of an Identifier and joins them with dots.

nodes.name: getTimestampType
nodes.summary: Protected final helper that picks TimestampType or TimestampNTZType from the isTimestampNTZ metadata flag using JdbcUtils.getTimestampType.

nodes.name: updateExtraColumnMeta
nodes.summary: Hook that lets a dialect add extra column metadata while the schema is read; the default does nothing.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Renders AlwaysTrue as (1 = 1) and AlwaysFalse as (1 = 0) so the result is valid inside larger expressions; all other expressions go to the parent builder.

nodes.name: inputToSQLNoBool
nodes.summary: Protected helper for dialects without a boolean type: renders always-true and always-false predicates as 1 and 0 and other predicates as a CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.

nodes.name: predicateToIntSQL
nodes.summary: Wraps a predicate string in CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.

nodes.name: visitLiteral
nodes.summary: Converts a non-null literal to a Scala value and renders it with the dialect compileValue; null falls back to the parent.

nodes.name: visitNamedReference
nodes.summary: Quotes a single-part column reference with quoteIdentifier and raises an error for nested columns.

nodes.name: visitCast
nodes.summary: Builds CAST(expr AS type) using the dialect JDBC type definition when one exists, else the Spark type name.

nodes.name: visitSQLFunction
nodes.summary: For expression inputs: delegates to the parent when the dialect supports the function, otherwise throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException; the string-input overload (lines 460-462) formats dialectFunctionName(args).

nodes.name: visitAggregateFunction
nodes.summary: For expression inputs: delegates to the parent with the dialect function name when supported, otherwise throws; the string-input overload (lines 477-480) just applies dialectFunctionName.

nodes.name: visitInverseDistributionFunction
nodes.summary: Delegates to the parent builder for supported inverse distribution functions (using the dialect name) and throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException otherwise.

nodes.name: dialectFunctionName
nodes.summary: Protected hook returning the dialect specific spelling of a function name; the default returns it unchanged.

nodes.name: visitOverlay
nodes.summary: Delegates OVERLAY to the parent builder if the dialect supports it, otherwise throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: visitTrim
nodes.summary: Delegates TRIM to the parent builder if the dialect supports it, otherwise throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: JDBCRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RDD that reads one table or query from a database over JDBC, plus the JDBCPartition type that carries a per-partition WHERE clause. The JDBCRDD companion object resolves a table schema through a connection and builds a JDBCRDD for a scan.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a case class, a companion object with overloaded resolveTable and getQueryOutputSchema, and a class extending RDD[InternalRow].

nodes.name: JDBCPartition
nodes.summary: Case class (whereClause, idx) extending Partition. It holds the WHERE clause for one slice of a JDBC scan and reports idx as its partition index. Used as the partition type of JDBCRDD.

nodes.name: JDBCRDD
nodes.summary: Companion object plus class for JDBC reads. The object offers resolveTable and getQueryOutputSchema (get a Catalyst schema by preparing the schema query of the dialect), a private pruneSchema, and scanTable (build a JDBCRDD with pushed down columns, predicates, group by, sample, limit, offset and sort orders). The class JDBCRDD extends RDD[InternalRow] with DataSourceMetricsMixin and ExternalEngineDatasourceRDD; its compute opens a connection per partition, runs the optional session init statement, executes the generated query and returns an interruptible, auto-closing iterator of InternalRow, and it exposes two timing metrics.

nodes.name: resolveTable
nodes.summary: Returns the Catalyst StructType of a table or query from the JDBCOptions and an open connection. It builds the dialect schema query (prepareQuery plus getSchemaQuery) and calls getQueryOutputSchema. A missing table (when an Identifier is given) becomes a no-such-table compilation error, and a syntax error becomes a JDBC_EXTERNAL_ENGINE_SYNTAX_ERROR SparkException. A second overload at lines 93-97 takes only the options and opens its own connection through JdbcUtils.withConnection.

nodes.name: getQueryOutputSchema
nodes.summary: Prepares the given query on the connection, applies the query timeout, executes it and derives a StructType from the ResultSet metadata through JdbcUtils.getSchema (all columns nullable, timestamp NTZ preference from the options). An overload at lines 111-116 takes no connection and uses JdbcUtils.withConnection.

nodes.name: pruneSchema
nodes.summary: Private helper that keeps only the requested column names, in the requested order, from a StructType.

nodes.name: scanTable
nodes.summary: Builds a JDBCRDD[InternalRow] for a scan. It quotes the required columns with the dialect (unless group by columns were pushed down, which are already quoted), creates a connection factory from the dialect, and passes the pushed down predicates, partitions, group by, sample clause, limit, offset, sort orders and extra metrics to the JDBCRDD constructor.

nodes.name: generateJdbcQuery
nodes.summary: Builds the SELECT text for a partition (or for no partition) by chaining the dialect query builder with predicates, columns, sort orders, limit and offset, then optional group by columns and table sample clause, and calling build.

nodes.name: getExternalEngineQuery
nodes.summary: Returns the JDBC query text for the whole scan by calling generateJdbcQuery with no partition.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Runs the query for one partition. It gets a connection for the partition index, lets the dialect run beforeFetch, runs the sessionInitStatement if set, prepares a forward-only read-only statement with fetch size and timeout, registers task completion and task interrupt listeners that close the resources, executes the query under the timing metric (syntax errors become a SparkException), and converts the ResultSet to InternalRows with JdbcUtils.resultSetToSparkInternalRows wrapped in a CompletionIterator and InterruptibleIterator.

nodes.name: getMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the metrics of this RDD: fetchAndTransformToInternalRowsNs, queryExecutionTime, followed by the additional metrics passed in.

nodes.name: JDBCOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCOptions, the parsed and validated option set of the JDBC data source (url, dbtable or query, driver, partitioning, fetch and batch sizes, truncate, isolation level, pushdown flags, Kerberos keytab and principal, hint and more), the write variant JdbcOptionsInWrite, and a companion object that holds the option name constants and URL redaction.
nodes.languageNotes: Constructor body of JDBCOptions is a long sequence of vals computed from a case-insensitive map; the companion object registers every option name through newOption.

nodes.name: JDBCOptions
nodes.summary: Class plus companion object for the options of the JDBC source. The class (Serializable, Logging) wraps a CaseInsensitiveMap[String], requires url, resolves tableOrQuery (dbtable or a wrapped query subquery, but not both), registers an optional driver class with DriverRegistry, reads read-only options (partitionColumn, lowerBound, upperBound, numPartitions, fetchsize, queryTimeout), write options (truncate, cascadeTruncate, createTableOptions, batchsize, isolationLevel) and pushdown flags (pushDownPredicate, pushDownAggregate, pushDownLimit, pushDownOffset, pushDownTableSample, pushDownJoin), keytab and principal, prepareQuery, preferTimestampNTZ and hint, and validates them with require. It exposes asProperties and asConnectionProperties (without Spark-internal option names), equals and hashCode on the parameters, and getRedactUrl. The companion object declares the option name constants such as JDBC_URL = "url" and JDBC_TABLE_NAME = "dbtable" via newOption, and redactUrl.

nodes.name: JdbcOptionsInWrite
nodes.summary: Subclass of JDBCOptions used for writes. It additionally requires the dbtable option (the query option is not applicable when writing) and exposes it as table.

nodes.name: getRedactUrl
nodes.summary: Returns the JDBC URL of these options redacted by redactUrl with the string redaction pattern of SQLConf.

nodes.name: newOption
nodes.summary: Private helper that records the lower-cased option name in the set of known JDBC option names (used to filter connection properties) and returns the name unchanged.

nodes.name: redactUrl
nodes.summary: Redacts a JDBC URL for logs and error messages. It keeps only the "jdbc:<subprotocol>:" prefix and replaces everything after it with the redaction text (a malformed URL is replaced entirely), then applies the optional configured regex on top.

nodes.name: AggregatedDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private AggregatedDialect, a virtual JdbcDialect that combines a non-empty list of dialects: type mapping tries each dialect in order and takes the first answer, while query-building hooks delegate to the first dialect.

nodes.name: AggregatedDialect
nodes.summary: Private class extending JdbcDialect with NoLegacyJDBCError, built from a List[JdbcDialect]. canHandle requires all dialects to handle the URL; getCatalystType and getJDBCType return the first defined result; isCascadingTruncateTable merges the answers (true if any says true, unknown if any is unknown, else false); quoteIdentifier, getTableExistsQuery, getSchemaQuery, isSyntaxErrorBestEffort, getTruncateQuery, getFetchSize and beforeFetch delegate to the head dialect.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Returns true only when every wrapped dialect can handle the URL.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps a JDBC type to a Catalyst type by asking each dialect in order and returning the first defined answer.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps a Catalyst type to a JDBC type by asking each dialect in order and returning the first defined answer.

nodes.name: isCascadingTruncateTable
nodes.summary: Combines the dialect answers: Some(true) if any dialect cascades, None if any dialect is unknown, otherwise Some(false).

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Delegates the truncate statement text to the first dialect, passing the cascade option (default isCascadingTruncateTable()).

nodes.name: beforeFetch
nodes.summary: Delegates the pre-fetch hook on the connection to the first dialect.

nodes.name: DB2Dialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private DB2Dialect, the JdbcDialect for "jdbc:db2" URLs. It maps DB2 and Catalyst types, restricts pushdown to a set of aggregate functions, compiles V2 expressions with a DB2 specific SQL builder, writes DB2 DDL (rename table, alter column, drop schema, truncate) and builds queries with FETCH FIRST and OFFSET clauses.

nodes.name: DB2Dialect
nodes.summary: Private case class extending JdbcDialect with SQLConfHelper and NoLegacyJDBCError. Handles URLs starting with jdbc:db2; supports MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, STDDEV_SAMP, COVAR_POP, COVAR_SAMP, REGR_INTERCEPT, REGR_R2, REGR_SLOPE and REGR_SXY for pushdown; recognizes error code -204 as object not found and SQLState prefix 42 as a syntax error; maps SMALLINT, REAL, DECFLOAT, XML and TIMESTAMP types (legacy conf flags for SMALLINT and BOOLEAN); writes TRUNCATE TABLE ... IMMEDIATE, RENAME TABLE, ALTER COLUMN type and nullability, COMMENT ON SCHEMA reset and DROP SCHEMA CASCADE or RESTRICT; classifies SQLState 42893 and 42710 into Spark errors; and supports limit and offset.

nodes.name: DB2SQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner class extending JDBCSQLBuilder that compiles V2 expressions for DB2: it rejects DISTINCT on COVAR_POP, COVAR_SAMP, REGR_INTERCEPT, REGR_R2, REGR_SLOPE and REGR_SXY, and renames VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, COVAR_POP, COVAR_SAMP to the DB2 function names.

nodes.name: DB2SQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner class extending JdbcSQLQueryBuilder whose build puts the OFFSET clause before the FETCH FIRST (limit) clause, after the where, group by and order by clauses, using the prepareQuery and tableOrQuery of the options.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: True when the URL, lower-cased, starts with jdbc:db2.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Treats DB2 error code -204 as an object (table) not found.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression with a new DB2SQLBuilder; on a non-fatal error it logs a warning and returns None so the expression is not pushed down.

nodes.name: compileValue
nodes.summary: Compiles a literal; a byte array becomes a BLOB(X'..') hex literal, everything else is delegated to the parent.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps DB2 JDBC types to Catalyst: SMALLINT to ShortType (unless the legacy numeric mapping conf is on), REAL to FloatType, DECFLOAT to DecimalType(38, 18), XML to StringType, TIMESTAMP* to TimestampType.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst types to DB2 column types: StringType to CLOB, BooleanType to BOOLEAN (CHAR(1) under the legacy flag), ShortType and ByteType to SMALLINT.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Best-effort syntax error test: SQLState starts with 42.

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Returns TRUNCATE TABLE <table> IMMEDIATE; the cascade option is ignored.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Builds RENAME TABLE <old> TO <new> using fully qualified quoted names of the two identifiers.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnTypeQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE <type>.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL or SET NOT NULL.

nodes.name: removeSchemaCommentQuery
nodes.summary: Builds COMMENT ON SCHEMA <schema> IS '' to clear a schema comment.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Maps SQLState 42893 to NonEmptyNamespaceException and SQLState 42710 during FAILED_JDBC.RENAME_TABLE to a table-already-exists compilation error; other cases go to the parent classifyException.

nodes.name: dropSchema
nodes.summary: Builds DROP SCHEMA <schema> CASCADE or RESTRICT depending on the cascade flag.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns FETCH FIRST <n> ROWS ONLY for a positive limit, otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: getOffsetClause
nodes.summary: Returns OFFSET <n> ROWS for a positive offset, otherwise an empty string.

nodes.name: getJdbcSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a new DB2SQLQueryBuilder for this dialect and the given options.

nodes.name: visitAggregateFunction
nodes.summary: Throws an unsupported-operation error when DISTINCT is used with a function in the distinct-unsupported set; otherwise delegates to the parent.

nodes.name: dialectFunctionName
nodes.summary: Translates Spark function names to DB2 names (VAR_POP to VARIANCE, VAR_SAMP to VARIANCE_SAMP, STDDEV_POP to STDDEV, COVAR_POP to COVARIANCE, COVAR_SAMP to COVARIANCE_SAMP) and defers others to the parent.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the SELECT text: prepareQuery, SELECT columns FROM tableOrQuery, then where, group by, order by, offset and limit clauses.

nodes.name: DatabricksDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private DatabricksDialect, the JdbcDialect for URLs starting with "jdbc:databricks". It maps a few types, quotes identifiers with backticks, supports limit, offset and hints, compiles TABLESAMPLE, and lists schemas with SHOW SCHEMAS.

nodes.name: DatabricksDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class extending JdbcDialect with NoLegacyJDBCError. Handles jdbc:databricks URLs; treats SQLState 42P01 and 42704 as object not found and SQLState prefix 42 as a syntax error; maps TINYINT, SMALLINT and REAL to Catalyst and Boolean, Double, String and Binary to JDBC types; quotes identifiers with backticks (doubling embedded backticks); enables limit, offset and hint support; compiles TABLESAMPLE for non-system, no-replacement samples; and implements schemasExists and listSchemas through a SHOW SCHEMAS statement.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: True when the URL starts with jdbc:databricks.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Object not found when the SQLState is 42P01 or 42704.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps TINYINT to ByteType, SMALLINT to ShortType and REAL to FloatType; other types return None.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps BooleanType, DoubleType, StringType and BinaryType to BOOLEAN, DOUBLE, STRING and BINARY column types.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Best-effort syntax error test: SQLState starts with 42.

nodes.name: quoteIdentifier
nodes.summary: Wraps a column name in backticks after doubling any embedded backtick.

nodes.name: compileTableSample
nodes.summary: Returns None for sampling with replacement or the System method; otherwise builds TABLESAMPLE <METHOD> (<percent>) REPEATABLE (<seed>).

nodes.name: schemasExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a schema exists by running SHOW SCHEMAS as a prepared statement and scanning the first column, instead of using driver metadata.

nodes.name: listSchemas
nodes.summary: Lists schemas by running SHOW SCHEMAS as a prepared statement and collecting the first column of each row.

nodes.name: JdbcConnectionProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract JdbcConnectionProvider, a DeveloperApi and Unstable extension point (since 3.1.0) for opening JDBC connections to a particular database, including any authentication setup.

nodes.name: JdbcConnectionProvider
nodes.summary: Abstract class with a unique name, canHandle(driver, options) to say whether the provider fits a driver, getConnection(driver, options) to open the connection, and modifiesSecurityContext(driver, options) to say whether global JVM security configuration is changed (such calls are made synchronized by SecurityConfigurationLock). Exactly one provider must handle a given driver, and providers should not keep unsynchronized state.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns true if this provider can handle a connection started by the given driver with the given options.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Abstract: opens a Connection with the given driver and options.

nodes.name: modifiesSecurityContext
nodes.summary: Abstract: tells whether opening this connection needs to modify global security configuration and so must be synchronized.

nodes.name: JdbcSQLQueryBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the builder that assembles a single SELECT statement for a JDBC scan from pushed-down pieces (columns, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET, table sample, join) using the dialect's SQL syntax, plus a generator for unique join subquery aliases.

nodes.name: JdbcSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder (since 3.5.0) for one SELECT query, created with a JdbcDialect and JDBCOptions. The withXXX methods each set one clause: withColumns, withAliasedColumns (AS aliases), withPredicates (compiled predicates AND-ed with the partition WHERE clause), withGroupByColumns, withSortOrders, withLimit, withOffset, withTableSample (deprecated) and withTableSampleClause, and withJoin (wraps two builders as an aliased join subquery). build() joins the options' prepareQuery, hint, column list, table or join query, sample, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY and the dialect's limit and offset clauses. A non-empty hint is rejected unless the dialect supports hints.

nodes.name: JoinPushdownAliasGenerator
nodes.summary: Object holding an atomic counter; getSubqueryQualifier returns a fresh alias 'join_subquery_<n>' used by JdbcSQLQueryBuilder.withJoin for pushed-down join subqueries.

nodes.name: withPredicates
nodes.summary: Compiles each V2 predicate with the dialect, wraps them in parentheses joined by AND, and combines the result with the partition's WHERE clause into the final WHERE clause (either, both or neither).

nodes.name: withJoin
nodes.summary: Sets the column list and builds a parenthesized 'SELECT columns FROM (left) lq JOIN (right) rq ON condition' subquery from two other builders, aliased with a generated qualifier; it replaces options.tableOrQuery when building.

nodes.name: withAliasedColumns
nodes.summary: Sets the column list from columns and optional aliases, emitting 'column AS alias' where an alias exists; asserts both arrays have equal length.

nodes.name: withTableSample
nodes.summary: Deprecated (4.2.0) setter that asks the dialect to render a TableSampleInfo into a table sample clause; replaced by withTableSampleClause.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Produces the final SQL text: prepareQuery, then SELECT with hint and column list FROM the table or join query with sample clause, followed by WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, and the dialect-specific LIMIT and OFFSET clauses.

nodes.name: getSubqueryQualifier
nodes.summary: Returns 'join_subquery_' followed by the next value of a shared atomic counter, giving each pushed-down join subquery a unique alias.

nodes.name: DriverWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Holds DriverWrapper, a java.sql.Driver that delegates to a wrapped driver so that drivers loaded by the Spark class loader can be registered with java.sql.DriverManager (workaround for SPARK-6913).

nodes.name: DriverWrapper
nodes.summary: Implements java.sql.Driver by forwarding acceptsURL, jdbcCompliant, getPropertyInfo, getMinorVersion, getMajorVersion and connect to the wrapped driver. getParentLogger throws an error from QueryExecutionErrors instead of delegating. It exists because java.sql.DriverManager cannot access drivers loaded by the Spark class loader.

nodes.name: getParentLogger
nodes.summary: Throws the getParentLoggerNotImplementedError from QueryExecutionErrors, naming the wrapper class, rather than delegating to the wrapped driver.

nodes.name: JDBCDatabaseMetadata.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCDatabaseMetadata, a small record of the external database and JDBC driver major and minor versions, with a companion factory that reads them from a connection while tolerating failures per field.

nodes.name: JDBCDatabaseMetadata
nodes.summary: Covers the case class (lines 33-38) with four optional version fields (database major/minor, driver major/minor) and its companion object (lines 44-102). The object's fromJDBCConnectionFactory opens a connection with getConnection(-1), reads each version through the private safeGet (which logs a warning and returns None on failure), returns all-None metadata if the metadata call itself fails, and always closes the connection. The doc comment says the metadata is stored in JDBCRDD.

nodes.name: fromJDBCConnectionFactory
nodes.summary: Builds a JDBCDatabaseMetadata from a connection factory: opens a connection, reads the four version values with per-field error handling, returns empty metadata if reading fails, and closes the connection in a finally block.

nodes.name: safeGet
nodes.summary: Private helper evaluating a by-name integer expression and returning Some(value), or None after logging a warning when a non-fatal exception occurs.

nodes.name: DerbyDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Dialect for Derby databases (URLs starting with jdbc:derby): maps Spark and JDBC types, reports supported aggregate functions, recognizes Derby SQL states for missing objects and syntax errors, and builds Derby-specific rename table, nullability and limit SQL.

nodes.name: DerbyDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class extending JdbcDialect (with NoLegacyJDBCError) for Derby. It handles URLs beginning 'jdbc:derby' and supports the aggregate functions MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP and STDDEV_SAMP. It maps JDBC REAL to FloatType, and StringType to CLOB, Byte/Short to SMALLINT, Boolean to BOOLEAN and Decimal to DECIMAL capped at precision 31. It treats SQL states 42Y07, 42X05 and X0X05 as object-not-found, any state starting with 42 as a syntax error, says truncate does not cascade, rejects renames across schemas, throws for table comments, uses 'ALTER COLUMN ... NULL / NOT NULL' for nullability and returns an empty LIMIT clause. Trivial one-line overrides (canHandle, isSupportedFunction, isCascadingTruncateTable) have no function nodes.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Returns true when the SQLException state is 42Y07, 42X05 or X0X05 (case-insensitive), the Derby codes for an object that does not exist.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps the JDBC REAL type to Spark FloatType and leaves all other types to the default mapping.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Spark types to Derby column types: String to CLOB, Byte and Short to SMALLINT, Boolean to BOOLEAN, and Decimal to DECIMAL with precision capped at 31 (scale reduced by the excess); other types return None.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Best-effort syntax error check: true when the exception has a SQL state starting with '42'.

nodes.name: renameTable
