nodes.summary: Builds 'RENAME TABLE <old quoted name> TO <new name>'; throws cannotRenameTableAcrossSchemaError when the namespaces differ, since Derby cannot rename across schemas.

nodes.name: getTableCommentQuery
nodes.summary: Always throws commentOnTableUnsupportedError because Derby does not support table comments.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Builds 'ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN <quoted col> NULL | NOT NULL', using Derby's second nullability syntax form.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns an empty string, so no LIMIT clause is generated for Derby queries.

nodes.name: AddPartitionExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AddPartitionExec, the physical command that adds one or more partitions to a table that supports partition management. Used when the planner executes an add-partition command against a v2 table.

nodes.name: AddPartitionExec
nodes.summary: Case class command node (a LeafV2CommandExec) holding the table, the resolved partition specs, an ignoreIfExists flag and a refreshCache callback. Its run method splits the specs into existing and missing ones, fails if some exist and ignoreIfExists is false, then creates one partition (createPartition) or, for several, uses createPartitions on a table that supports atomic partition management, otherwise raises an error. It refreshes the cache when the table changed and returns no rows.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns an empty attribute list because the command produces no result columns.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Checks which partitions already exist, throws PartitionsAlreadyExistException unless ignoreIfExists is set, creates the missing partitions (atomically when several and supported), calls refreshCache if anything changed, and returns an empty row list.

nodes.name: AlterNamespaceSetPropertiesExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AlterNamespaceSetPropertiesExec, the physical command that sets properties on a namespace of a catalog. Used when a set-namespace-properties DDL statement runs on a v2 catalog.

nodes.name: AlterNamespaceSetPropertiesExec
nodes.summary: Case class command node (a LeafV2CommandExec) holding a SupportsNamespaces catalog, the namespace name parts and a property map. Its run method turns each entry into NamespaceChange.setProperty and calls catalog.alterNamespace, returning no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds a NamespaceChange.setProperty for every property and applies them with catalog.alterNamespace on the namespace, then returns an empty row list.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns an empty attribute list because the command produces no result columns.

nodes.name: BinaryFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the binaryFile data source, which reads each file as a single row holding path, modificationTime, length and content. Used when a user loads files with format("binaryFile"); writing is not supported.

nodes.name: BinaryFileFormat
nodes.summary: Case class FileFormat (also DataSourceRegister and SessionStateHelper) for the binary file source; its companion object (lines 140-199) holds the fixed schema (path, modificationTime, length, content) and the createFilterFunction helper. inferSchema always returns that schema, prepareWrite throws an unsupported-write error, isSplitable is false, shortName is binaryFile, and buildReader returns a per-file function that builds one UnsafeRowWriter row, enforcing the SOURCES_BINARY_FILE_MAX_LENGTH limit for content.
nodes.languageNotes: Case class with a companion object that holds the schema and string constants; shares one class id.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the fixed binary file schema, ignoring the options and file list.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Always throws the writeUnsupportedForBinaryFileDataSourceError because this source cannot write.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Returns false so each file is read whole as a single row.

nodes.name: shortName
nodes.summary: Returns the short name binaryFile used to look up the source.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns the display name BINARYFILE.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Checks the data schema equals the binary schema, broadcasts the Hadoop conf, turns pushed-down filters into predicates on FileStatus, and returns a function that, for each PartitionedFile passing the predicates, writes path, length, modification time and content (throwing if the length exceeds the configured maximum) into an UnsafeRowWriter row.

nodes.name: createFilterFunction
nodes.summary: Recursively converts a source Filter (And, Or, Not and comparisons on length or modificationTime) into an optional predicate over FileStatus; unsupported filters yield None, and Or/Not with an unsupported side yield an always-true predicate.

nodes.name: CSVDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CSV reading strategies: the abstract CSVDataSource with its factory object, the line-based TextInputCSVDataSource and the whole-file MultiLineCSVDataSource. Used by CSVFileFormat to read CSV files and to infer their schema.

nodes.name: CSVDataSource
nodes.summary: Abstract serializable base (lines 51-86) declaring isSplitable, readFile and the protected infer, with a final inferSchema that returns a single variant column when singleVariantColumn is set, otherwise calls infer if there are input paths. Its companion object (lines 88-121) picks MultiLineCSVDataSource or TextInputCSVDataSource from the multiLine option (apply) and provides setHeaderForSingleVariantColumn.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract class plus companion object sharing one class id.

nodes.name: TextInputCSVDataSource
nodes.summary: Object for line-based CSV input: splittable, reads lines with HadoopFileLinesReader and parses them with UnivocityParser. Schema inference builds a base Dataset[String] from the text file source (re-decoding when the charset is not UTF-8), takes the first non-comment line as header, samples and tokenizes lines and runs CSVInferSchema.

nodes.name: MultiLineCSVDataSource
nodes.summary: Object for CSV with records spanning lines: not splittable, parses a whole file stream with UnivocityParser.parseStream. Schema inference reads each file as a PortableDataStream through BinaryFileRDD, tokenizes with CsvParser (tolerating missing or corrupt files per ignoreMissingFiles and ignoreCorruptFiles), builds the header from the first row and runs CSVInferSchema.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Abstract flag telling whether the CSV files can be split across tasks.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Abstract method that parses one PartitionedFile into InternalRow instances using a parser, header checker and required schema.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Final method: with singleVariantColumn set it returns a one-field variant schema, else it calls the protected infer when input paths are non-empty and returns None for no files.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Protected abstract method implemented by each subclass to infer the StructType from the input file statuses.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that returns MultiLineCSVDataSource when options.multiLine is true, otherwise TextInputCSVDataSource.

nodes.name: setHeaderForSingleVariantColumn
nodes.summary: Returns, when singleVariantColumn needs a header, a callback that fills parser.headerColumnNames from the checker output or by reading the first header line with CSVUtils.readHeaderLine; returns None otherwise.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Reads the file lines through HadoopFileLinesReader (closed on task completion), decodes them with the configured charset, sets the single-variant header callback and parses with UnivocityParser.parseIterator.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Builds the base Dataset of lines, finds the first non-comment non-empty line and delegates to inferFromDataset.

nodes.name: inferFromDataset
nodes.summary: Parses the first line into a safe header, samples the lines, drops comment, empty and header lines per partition, tokenizes them and runs CSVInferSchema under withSQLConfPropagated; returns an empty schema if no first line exists.

nodes.name: createBaseDataset
nodes.summary: Creates a Dataset[String] of text lines by resolving a DataSource with TextFileFormat (glob paths disabled), and re-decodes the bytes when the charset is not UTF-8.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Sets the single-variant header callback and parses the whole file input stream (opened with CodecStreams) via UnivocityParser.parseStream.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Tokenizes the first row of each file stream (skipping missing or corrupt files when configured), builds the header, tokenizes and samples all files and runs CSVInferSchema; returns an empty schema when no row is found.

nodes.name: createBaseRdd
nodes.summary: Builds a BinaryFileRDD of PortableDataStream over the input paths, named CSVFile, and returns only its values.

nodes.name: CSVFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CSVFileFormat, the file format behind the csv data source. It wires option parsing, schema inference, reading and writing of CSV files to CSVDataSource and CsvOutputWriter.

nodes.name: CSVFileFormat
nodes.summary: Case class TextBasedFileFormat and DataSourceRegister named csv. It parses CSVOptions from the session conf (getCsvOptions), decides splitability via CSVDataSource, delegates inferSchema and per-file reading to the chosen CSVDataSource, and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates CsvOutputWriter instances. Variant is readable but not writable, and geometry and geography types are rejected (supportDataType and supportReadDataType).

nodes.name: shortName
nodes.summary: Returns the short name csv.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A file is splittable when the chosen CSVDataSource is splittable and the base text format allows it.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Parses the options and delegates schema inference to CSVDataSource(parsedOptions).inferSchema.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Rejects schemas with unsupported types, applies the compression codec to the job conf, and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates a CsvOutputWriter and whose file extension combines the option extension with the codec extension.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Broadcasts the Hadoop conf, validates the corrupt-record column, drops pushed-down filters that reference it, and returns a function that builds a UnivocityParser and CSVHeaderChecker per file and calls CSVDataSource.readFile, using column pruning only when enabled.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns the display name CSV.

nodes.name: supportDataType
nodes.summary: Private overload with an allowVariant flag: variant follows the flag, geometry and geography are false, atomic types are true, user-defined types check their sqlType, everything else is false. The public one-argument override (lines 149-150) calls it with allowVariant = false.

nodes.name: supportReadDataType
nodes.summary: Same type check as writing but allows variant columns for reading.

nodes.name: allowDuplicatedColumnNames
nodes.summary: Returns true, allowing duplicated column names in CSV data.

nodes.name: getCsvOptions
nodes.summary: Builds CSVOptions from the user options plus the session conf values csvColumnPruning, sessionLocalTimeZone and columnNameOfCorruptRecord.

nodes.name: CSVUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Provides CSV helper functions: filtering comment and empty lines, dropping the header line, making a safe header, sampling for inference, and reading the first header line of a file. Used by the CSV data sources during schema inference.

nodes.name: CSVUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with filterCommentAndEmpty (Dataset and Iterator versions), filterHeaderLine, makeSafeHeader (null and duplicate safe, falls back to _c<index> names), sample (Dataset and RDD versions driven by samplingRatio) and readHeaderLine (opens the file with CodecStreams and returns the first non-comment, non-empty line).

nodes.name: filterCommentAndEmpty
nodes.summary: Dataset version: keeps lines whose trimmed length is above zero and, when a comment character is set, drops lines starting with it. An Iterator overload (lines 138-139) delegates to CSVExprUtils.filterCommentAndEmpty.

nodes.name: filterHeaderLine
nodes.summary: When the header option is on, removes lines equal to the given first line from the iterator; otherwise returns it unchanged.

nodes.name: makeSafeHeader
nodes.summary: Turns the first row into column names: null, empty or nullValue entries become _c<index>, duplicates (case-insensitive when not case sensitive) get the index appended, and without the header option all names are _c<index>.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Dataset version: requires samplingRatio above zero and samples without replacement unless the ratio is above 0.99. An RDD overload (lines 128-136) applies the same rule to RDD[Array[String]].

nodes.name: readHeaderLine
nodes.summary: Opens the file with CodecStreams, wraps a LineReader (custom separator if given) in an anonymous line iterator, filters comments and empty lines and returns the first remaining line, closing the stream afterwards.

nodes.name: CsvOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CsvOutputWriter, the OutputWriter that writes rows as CSV text. Created by CSVFileFormat.prepareWrite for each output file.

nodes.name: CsvOutputWriter
nodes.summary: Class that opens an output stream writer (CodecStreams.createOutputStreamWriter) with the configured charset, creates a UnivocityGenerator, writes the header when the header option is set, then forwards write(row) and close() to the generator.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one InternalRow through the UnivocityGenerator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying generator and its writer.

nodes.name: JsonDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JSON reading strategies: the abstract JsonDataSource with its factory object, the line-based TextInputJsonDataSource and the whole-file MultiLineJsonDataSource. Used by the JSON file format to read files and infer their schema.

nodes.name: JsonDataSource
nodes.summary: Abstract serializable base (lines 47-78) declaring isSplitable, readFile and the protected infer, with a final inferSchema that returns a single variant column when singleVariantColumn is set, otherwise calls infer if there are input paths. Its companion object (lines 80-88) selects MultiLineJsonDataSource or TextInputJsonDataSource via apply from the multiLine option.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract class plus companion object sharing one class id.

nodes.name: TextInputJsonDataSource
nodes.summary: Object for line-delimited JSON: splittable, reads Text lines with HadoopFileLinesReader and parses each with JacksonParser inside a FailureSafeParser. Schema inference builds a Dataset[String] from the text source, samples it with JsonUtils.sample and runs JsonInferSchema.

nodes.name: MultiLineJsonDataSource
nodes.summary: Object for JSON documents spanning lines: not splittable. It creates a BinaryFileRDD of PortableDataStream for inference, samples with JsonUtils, builds Jackson parsers from input streams and runs JsonInferSchema; readFile parses the whole file stream through a FailureSafeParser, using the full file content as the corrupt record text.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Abstract flag telling whether the JSON files can be split across tasks.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Abstract method that parses one PartitionedFile into zero or more InternalRow instances using a JacksonParser and schema.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Final method: with singleVariantColumn it returns a one-field variant schema, else it calls the protected infer when input paths are non-empty and returns None for no files.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Protected abstract method implemented by each subclass to infer the StructType from the input file statuses.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that returns MultiLineJsonDataSource when options.multiLine is true, otherwise TextInputJsonDataSource.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Builds the base Dataset of lines and delegates to inferFromDataset.

nodes.name: inferFromDataset
nodes.summary: Samples the line Dataset with JsonUtils.sample, takes its internal-row RDD, picks a CreateJacksonParser.internalRow parser (with encoding if set) and runs JsonInferSchema.infer under withSQLConfPropagated.

nodes.name: createBaseDataset
nodes.summary: Creates a Dataset[String] of lines by resolving a DataSource with TextFileFormat (glob paths disabled) and selecting the value column.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Reads lines via HadoopFileLinesReader (closed on task completion), builds a Text parser, wraps JacksonParser.parse in a FailureSafeParser using the parse mode and corrupt-record column, and flat-maps the lines through it.

nodes.name: textToUTF8String
nodes.summary: Converts a Hadoop Text value to a UTF8String; used as the corrupt record text.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Creates the PortableDataStream RDD, samples it with JsonUtils.sample, picks a createParser (with encoding if set) and runs JsonInferSchema.infer with isReadFile = true.

nodes.name: createBaseRdd
nodes.summary: Builds a BinaryFileRDD of PortableDataStream over the input paths, named JsonFile, and returns only its values.

nodes.name: dataToInputStream
nodes.summary: Opens a PortableDataStream's path as an input stream through CodecStreams.

nodes.name: createParser
nodes.summary: Creates a Jackson JsonParser from a stream with a given encoding. An overload without encoding (lines 204-206) does the same with the default.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Parses the whole file stream through a FailureSafeParser with JacksonParser.parse; the corrupt-record text is the full file content read by the local partitionedFileString function.

nodes.name: JsonFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the 'json' file format used by the SQL file data source layer: it plugs JSON line files into the read path (schema inference, record parsing) and the write path (output writer factory). It delegates reading and schema inference to JsonDataSource and writing to JsonOutputWriter.

nodes.name: JsonFileFormat
nodes.summary: Case class that extends TextBasedFileFormat and DataSourceRegister and registers the short name 'json'. It builds JSONOptions from the session conf (JSONOptionsInRead when reading), decides splittability through JsonDataSource, infers the schema, prepares writes with a compression codec and an OutputWriterFactory producing JsonOutputWriter (file extension '.json' plus the codec suffix), builds a per-file reader that uses JacksonParser, and checks which Spark data types are supported (variant, atomic, struct, array, map, user defined and null types; geometry and geography are rejected). Used when a query reads or writes with format json.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Returns true only when the JsonDataSource chosen for the parsed options is splittable and the base text file format also allows splitting the file.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the JSON options and delegates schema inference over the given files to JsonDataSource.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Sets the output compression codec on the Hadoop job configuration (when configured) and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates a JsonOutputWriter and whose file extension is '.json' plus the codec extension.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the per-file reader function: broadcasts the Hadoop conf, drops the corrupt record column from the schema, validates the corrupt record column name on the driver, rejects queries that select only that column, and for each PartitionedFile creates a JacksonParser and calls JsonDataSource.readFile.

nodes.name: supportDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively decides whether a data type can be stored in JSON: variant, atomic and null types are accepted, struct, array, map and user defined types are checked through their children, geometry and geography are rejected.

nodes.name: getJsonOptions
nodes.summary: Creates a JSONOptionsInRead (for reads) or a JSONOptions (for writes) from the option map, the session local time zone and the corrupt record column name from the SQL conf.

nodes.name: JsonOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Holds JsonOutputWriter, the OutputWriter that writes rows of a partition as JSON lines to a file through a Jackson-based generator.

nodes.name: JsonOutputWriter
nodes.summary: OutputWriter created by the JSON file format for each output file. It picks the charset from the options (UTF-8 by default), logs a warning when the chosen encoding is in the JSONOptionsInRead deny list (the file can then only be read back with multiLine), opens a compressed output stream writer with CodecStreams, and uses a JacksonGenerator: write() emits one row followed by a line ending, close() closes the generator and the stream.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one InternalRow as a JSON record with the generator and then writes the line ending.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the JacksonGenerator and then the underlying stream writer.

nodes.name: NoopDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the 'noop' data source: a table and write path (batch and streaming) that consumes all input rows and does nothing with them, useful for benchmarking or for forcing a computation without any write overhead.

nodes.name: NoopDataSource
nodes.summary: Entry class of the noop data source. It extends SimpleTableProvider and DataSourceRegister, registers the short name 'noop' and its getTable returns the NoopTable object. The class comment says it does nothing besides consuming its input, which is useful for benchmarking or to cache data without additional overhead.

nodes.name: NoopTable
nodes.summary: Private singleton Table with SupportsWrite named 'noop-table' with an empty schema. newWriteBuilder returns NoopWriteBuilder, and capabilities advertise BATCH_WRITE, STREAMING_WRITE, TRUNCATE and ACCEPT_ANY_SCHEMA.

nodes.name: NoopWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Private singleton WriteBuilder that also supports truncate and streaming update as append; truncate returns itself and build returns NoopWrite.

nodes.name: NoopWrite
nodes.summary: Private singleton Write whose toBatch returns NoopBatchWrite and whose toStreaming returns NoopStreamingWrite.

nodes.name: NoopBatchWrite
nodes.summary: Private singleton BatchWrite that hands out NoopWriterFactory, does not use the commit coordinator, and treats commit and abort as no-ops.

nodes.name: NoopWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Private singleton DataWriterFactory whose createWriter always returns NoopWriter.

nodes.name: NoopWriter
nodes.summary: Private singleton DataWriter of InternalRow where write, commit (returns null), abort and close do nothing, so every record is discarded.

nodes.name: NoopStreamingWrite
nodes.summary: Private singleton StreamingWrite that returns NoopStreamingDataWriterFactory, does not use the commit coordinator and ignores commit and abort for every epoch.

nodes.name: NoopStreamingDataWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Private singleton StreamingDataWriterFactory whose createWriter for a partition, task and epoch returns NoopWriter.

nodes.name: TextFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the 'text' file format: reads each line (or each whole file) as a single string column named 'value' and writes a single string column as lines of text.

nodes.name: TextFileFormat
nodes.summary: Case class extending TextBasedFileFormat with DataSourceRegister, short name 'text', for UTF-8 text files. The schema is always one string column 'value' (inferSchema), writes require exactly one column and reads at most one, splittable unless the wholeText option is set, and only StringType is supported. It builds the reader that turns each line (HadoopFileLinesReader) or each whole file (HadoopFileWholeTextReader) into an UnsafeRow, and the writer factory that creates TextOutputWriter with extension '.txt' plus the codec suffix.

nodes.name: verifySchema
nodes.summary: Throws a compilation error when the schema to write does not have exactly one column.

nodes.name: verifyReadSchema
nodes.summary: Throws a compilation error when the requested read schema has more than one column.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Allows splitting a file only when the base format allows it and the wholeText option is not set.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Always returns a schema with a single string column named 'value'.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Verifies the single column schema, applies the compression codec to the job configuration and returns an OutputWriterFactory creating TextOutputWriter with the configured line separator and the '.txt' extension.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Verifies the read schema, builds TextOptions, broadcasts the Hadoop configuration and returns the reader function from readToUnsafeMem.

nodes.name: readToUnsafeMem
nodes.summary: Returns a function that opens a lines reader or a whole text reader for a PartitionedFile (closed on task completion) and maps each record to an UnsafeRow, using an empty row when no column is required and an UnsafeRowWriter otherwise.

nodes.name: supportDataType
nodes.summary: Returns true only for StringType.

nodes.name: TextOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Holds TextOutputWriter, which writes the single string column of each row as a line of bytes to a text output file.

nodes.name: TextOutputWriter
nodes.summary: OutputWriter used by the text file format. It opens a (possibly compressed) output stream for the path with CodecStreams; write() writes the UTF8 string of column 0 when it is not null and then always writes the line separator bytes; close() closes the stream.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the UTF8 string of column 0 to the stream if the value is not null, then writes the line separator, so null values become empty lines.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the output stream.

nodes.name: XmlDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Contains the XmlDataSource strategies used by the XML file format: a line oriented TextInputXmlDataSource (splittable) and a MultiLineXmlDataSource (whole file per record stream), each providing record parsing and schema inference.

nodes.name: XmlDataSource
nodes.summary: Abstract serializable base class (lines 50-84) with isSplitable, readFile (parse a PartitionedFile into InternalRows with a StaxXmlParser), a final inferSchema (returns a single variant column when singleVariantColumn is set, none for empty input, otherwise calls the protected infer) and the abstract infer. Its companion object (lines 86-94) has apply(options), which returns MultiLineXmlDataSource when multiLine is set and TextInputXmlDataSource otherwise.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Final method that infers the XML schema: a one-column variant schema when singleVariantColumn is configured, None when there are no input files, otherwise the result of the subclass infer.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion object factory that selects MultiLineXmlDataSource when the options enable multiLine and TextInputXmlDataSource otherwise.

nodes.name: TextInputXmlDataSource
nodes.summary: XmlDataSource for the default (not multiLine) mode; it is splittable. It reads lines with HadoopFileLinesReader, decodes them with the configured charset and parses them through a FailureSafeParser. Schema inference loads the files as a string Dataset through the text data source (re-decoding when the charset is not UTF-8) and runs XmlInferSchema over its RDD.

nodes.name: MultiLineXmlDataSource
nodes.summary: XmlDataSource for multiLine mode; it is not splittable. It parses each file as a stream (parseStream for the legacy parser, parseStreamOptimized otherwise). Schema inference reads files as PortableDataStream through a BinaryFileRDD and runs XmlInferSchema, either on tokenized strings (legacy parser, skipping missing or corrupt files when the ignore options allow it) or on StaxXMLRecordReader objects (optimized path).

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Reads the file line by line (closing the reader on task completion), decodes each line using the options charset and flat-maps them through a FailureSafeParser built from the parser options (parse mode, corrupt record column).

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Creates a base string Dataset from the input files and infers the schema from it with inferFromDataset.

nodes.name: inferFromDataset
nodes.summary: Runs XmlInferSchema over the RDD of a string Dataset inside SQLExecution.withSQLConfPropagated, honoring case sensitivity of the analyzer.

nodes.name: createBaseDataset
nodes.summary: Loads the input paths with the text file format (glob expansion disabled) into a Dataset[String]; when the charset is not UTF-8 it rebuilds the strings from the raw bytes using the configured charset.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Parses a whole file as a stream with the legacy parseStream or with parseStreamOptimized depending on useLegacyXMLParser.

nodes.name: infer
nodes.summary: Infers the schema for multiLine XML: uses inferOptimized unless the legacy parser is enabled; the legacy path tokenizes each file stream into strings, skips missing files or the rest of corrupt files when the ignore options allow it (rethrowing access and block errors), and applies XmlInferSchema.

nodes.name: inferOptimized
nodes.summary: Optimized schema inference: converts each PortableDataStream into StaxXMLRecordReader objects and infers the schema with XmlInferSchema.inferFromReaders.

nodes.name: createBaseRdd
nodes.summary: Builds a BinaryFileRDD of PortableDataStream (named 'XMLFile: <paths>') over the input paths with StreamInputFormat and the default minimum partitions, returning only the streams.

nodes.name: XmlFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the 'xml' file format that exposes XML files to SQL: option handling, schema inference, reading (via StaxXmlParser) and writing (via XmlOutputWriter).

nodes.name: XmlFileFormat
nodes.summary: Case class extending TextBasedFileFormat with DataSourceRegister, short name 'xml'. It builds XmlOptions from the session conf, uses XmlDataSource(options) to decide splittability and infer the schema, prepares writes (compression codec plus a factory creating XmlOutputWriter, extension '.xml' plus codec suffix), builds a per-file reader with StaxXmlParser (validating the corrupt record column and dropping it from the pushed schema) and reports supported data types (same rules as the JSON format).

nodes.name: getXmlOptions
nodes.summary: Creates XmlOptions from the parameter map, the session local time zone and the corrupt record column name.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Splittable only when the XmlDataSource for the options is splittable and the base format allows it.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Delegates schema inference over the files to XmlDataSource(options).inferSchema.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Sets the compression codec when present and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates XmlOutputWriter instances with extension '.xml' plus the codec extension.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the per-file read function: broadcasts the Hadoop conf, verifies the corrupt record column name on the driver, removes that column from the pushed schema, rejects queries selecting only that column, and for each file builds a StaxXmlParser and calls XmlDataSource(options).readFile.

nodes.name: supportDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively checks whether a data type is supported for XML (variant, atomic and null accepted; struct, array, map and user defined types checked through their children; geometry and geography rejected).

nodes.name: XmlOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Holds XmlOutputWriter, the OutputWriter that writes rows of a partition as XML elements through a StaxXmlGenerator.

nodes.name: XmlOutputWriter
nodes.summary: OutputWriter used by the XML file format. It opens an output stream writer using the charset from the options and a StaxXmlGenerator; on the first row it writes the XML declaration, then each row is written by the generator, and close() closes the generator.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the XML declaration before the first row only, then writes the row with the generator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the StaxXmlGenerator.

nodes.name: XmlUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Small helpers for XML reading: sampling a string Dataset or an RDD of PortableDataStream by samplingRatio, and validating that a schema is allowed for XML.

nodes.name: XmlUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with sample (overloaded for Dataset[String] at lines 34-42 and for RDD[PortableDataStream] at lines 47-55; it requires samplingRatio > 0, returns the input unchanged above 0.99, otherwise samples without replacement with seed 1) and checkXmlSchema (uses ExprUtils.checkXmlSchema and throws an invalid XML schema error for invalid map key types).

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Samples a Dataset[String] of XML records using options.samplingRatio. An overload at lines 47-55 does the same for an RDD[PortableDataStream]. The ratio must be positive and a ratio above 0.99 returns the input unsampled.

nodes.name: checkXmlSchema
nodes.summary: Checks a schema with ExprUtils.checkXmlSchema: throws invalidXmlSchema for an invalid XML map key type, passes on success, and raises an internal error for any other result.

nodes.name: JsonUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Small helpers for JSON reading: sampling a string Dataset or an RDD of PortableDataStream by samplingRatio, and validating that a schema is allowed for JSON.

nodes.name: JsonUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with sample (overloaded for classic Dataset[String] at lines 34-42 and for RDD[PortableDataStream] at lines 47-55; it requires samplingRatio > 0, returns the input unchanged above 0.99, otherwise samples without replacement with seed 1) and checkJsonSchema (uses ExprUtils.checkJsonSchema and throws an invalid JSON schema error for invalid map key types).

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Samples a Dataset[String] of JSON records using options.samplingRatio. An overload at lines 47-55 does the same for an RDD[PortableDataStream]. The ratio must be positive and a ratio above 0.99 returns the input unsampled.

nodes.name: checkJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Checks a schema with ExprUtils.checkJsonSchema: throws invalidJsonSchema for an invalid JSON map key type, passes on success, and raises an internal error for any other result.

nodes.name: MsSqlServerDialect.scala
nodes.summary: JDBC dialect for Microsoft SQL Server URLs: type mappings in both directions, SQL pushdown rules (boolean handling, TOP limit, sort order emulation, function renames), DDL statements and error classification.

nodes.name: MsSqlServerDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class JdbcDialect (with NoLegacyJDBCError) that handles URLs starting with 'jdbc:sqlserver'. It compiles booleans to 1 or 0 and byte arrays to hex literals, supports a limited set of pushdown functions (MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, STDDEV_SAMP, RPAD, LPAD), maps datetimeoffset, tinyint, smallint, real and geometry/geography types to Catalyst types, maps Catalyst types to SQL Server column types, builds ALTER TABLE and sp_rename statements, uses TOP for limits, and classifies SQL exceptions by error code. Its companion object (lines 293-298) defines the special JDBC type codes GEOMETRY (-157) and GEOGRAPHY (-158).

nodes.name: MsSqlServerSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner expression-to-SQL builder extending JDBCSQLBuilder. It turns predicates into IIF(..., 1, 0) integers, emulates NULLS FIRST/LAST ordering with CASE WHEN, renames variance and standard deviation functions (VARP, VAR, STDEVP, STDEV), rewrites RPAD and LPAD with REPLICATE/CONCAT, and avoids boolean values in comparisons and CASE WHEN by converting them to 1 or 0.

nodes.name: MsSqlServerSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner query builder extending JdbcSQLQueryBuilder. Its build() assembles the prepare query, SELECT with the TOP clause placed before the column list, the table or query, and the where, group by and order by clauses.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Returns true when the JDBC URL (lower cased) starts with 'jdbc:sqlserver'.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Treats SQL error code 208 as an object-not-found error.

nodes.name: compileValue
nodes.summary: Compiles boolean literals to 1 or 0 and byte arrays to 0x-prefixed upper case hex strings; other values use the default compilation.

nodes.name: isSupportedFunction
nodes.summary: Checks whether a function name is in the set of supported aggregate and string functions.

nodes.name: visitSortOrder
nodes.summary: Emits ORDER BY keys; for the two combinations not natively supported (ascending NULLS LAST, descending NULLS FIRST) it adds a CASE WHEN key IS NULL sort term.

nodes.name: dialectFunctionName
nodes.summary: Maps VAR_POP to VARP, VAR_SAMP to VAR, STDDEV_POP to STDEVP and STDDEV_SAMP to STDEV; other names go to the parent.

nodes.name: visitSQLFunction
nodes.summary: Rewrites RPAD as LEFT(CONCAT(str, REPLICATE(pad, len)), len) and LPAD as RIGHT(CONCAT(REPLICATE(pad, len), str), len); other functions use the parent.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds SQL for a V2 expression, avoiding boolean operands: comparison operators use inputToSQLNoBool, and CASE_WHEN is rewritten so boolean results become CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END and the whole expression is compared with 1.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression with MsSqlServerSQLBuilder; on a non-fatal error it logs a warning and returns None so the expression is not pushed down.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps JDBC columns to Catalyst types: datetimeoffset to timestamp (or string with the legacy conf), smallint and tinyint to ShortType, real to FloatType (unless the legacy numeric mapping is on), geometry and geography to BinaryType.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst types to SQL Server column definitions such as DATETIME, NVARCHAR(MAX), BIT, VARBINARY(MAX) and SMALLINT.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Generates an EXEC sp_rename statement from the old and new quoted table names.

nodes.name: getAddColumnQuery
nodes.summary: Generates ALTER TABLE ... ADD <quoted column> <type>.

nodes.name: getRenameColumnQuery
nodes.summary: Generates EXEC sp_rename for a column with the 'COLUMN' object type.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Always throws an unsupported-operation error because changing nullability needs the column data type, which is not available here.

nodes.name: getTableCommentQuery
nodes.summary: Always throws an error: table comments are not supported by this dialect.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns 'TOP (limit)' for positive limits and an empty string otherwise.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Translates SQL Server error 3729 into NonEmptyNamespaceException and error 15335 (for a table rename) into a table-already-exists error; everything else goes to the parent.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds 'SELECT TOP (n) columns FROM table where group-by order-by' prefixed by the prepare query.

nodes.name: getJdbcSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a new MsSqlServerSQLQueryBuilder for the given JDBC options.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Detects syntax errors by checking whether the lower cased exception message contains 'incorrect syntax' or 'syntax error', since there is no consistent error code.

nodes.name: MySQLDialect.scala
nodes.summary: JDBC dialect for MySQL URLs: type mappings, SQL pushdown rules (extract fields, date functions, sort order, LIKE escaping), DDL and index statements, schema listing, LIMIT/OFFSET query building and error classification.

nodes.name: MySQLDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class JdbcDialect (with SQLConfHelper and NoLegacyJDBCError) that handles URLs starting with 'jdbc:mysql'. It pushes down MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, STDDEV_SAMP, DATE_ADD and DATE_DIFF, maps bit, json, tinyint, smallint, mediumint unsigned, real/float and datetime types using the legacy confs, quotes identifiers with backticks, lists schemas and indexes with SHOW statements, builds CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX, ALTER TABLE and DROP SCHEMA statements, and classifies MySQL error codes 1050, 1061 and 1091. It supports limit, offset, hint and join pushdown.

nodes.name: MySQLSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner expression-to-SQL builder extending JDBCSQLBuilder. It maps extract fields to MySQL functions (DAYOFYEAR, WEEKOFYEAR, WEEKDAY + 1) and refuses YEAR_OF_WEEK and SECOND, rewrites DATE_ADD and DATE_DIFF, emulates NULLS ordering with CASE WHEN, doubles backslashes in LIKE patterns, and rejects DISTINCT on variance and standard deviation aggregates.

nodes.name: MySQLSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner query builder extending JdbcSQLQueryBuilder. Its build() produces 'LIMIT offset, limit' when both are set, the dialect limit clause for limit only, and 'LIMIT offset, 18446744073709551615' for offset without limit, after the hint, column list, table, sample, where, group by and order by parts.

nodes.name: visitExtract
nodes.summary: Translates EXTRACT fields: DAY_OF_YEAR to DAYOFYEAR, WEEK to WEEKOFYEAR, DAY_OF_WEEK to (WEEKDAY + 1), unsupported YEAR_OF_WEEK and SECOND are rejected, others use the default.

nodes.name: visitSQLFunction
nodes.summary: Rewrites DATE_ADD as DATE_ADD(x, INTERVAL n DAY) and DATE_DIFF as DATEDIFF(a, b).

nodes.name: visitSortOrder
nodes.summary: Emits ORDER BY keys, adding a CASE WHEN key IS NULL sort term for ascending NULLS LAST and descending NULLS FIRST.

nodes.name: escapeStringLiteralForLikePattern
nodes.summary: Doubles every backslash so LIKE patterns survive MySQL string literal parsing.

nodes.name: visitAggregateFunction
nodes.summary: Throws an unsupported-operation error for DISTINCT on VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP and STDDEV_SAMP; otherwise defers to the parent.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression with MySQLSQLBuilder; a non-fatal error logs a warning and returns None so it is not pushed down.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps MySQL JDBC columns to Catalyst types: bit arrays to binary or long (legacy conf), TINYTEXT and JSON to string, signed and unsigned TINYINT/SMALLINT to wider types, MEDIUMINT UNSIGNED to int, REAL/FLOAT by sign, DATETIME to timestamp without time zone, and TIMESTAMP depending on the legacy NTZ conf.

nodes.name: quoteIdentifier
nodes.summary: Quotes an identifier with backticks, doubling any backtick inside the name.

nodes.name: listSchemas
nodes.summary: Runs SHOW SCHEMAS and collects the 'Database' column; on failure it logs a warning and returns what was collected. schemasExists (lines 201-203) uses it.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnTypeQuery
nodes.summary: Generates ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <quoted column> <type>.

nodes.name: getRenameColumnQuery
nodes.summary: Generates ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN ... TO ... for MySQL 8 and later, and throws an error for older major versions.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Always throws an unsupported-operation error because changing nullability needs the column data type.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst types to MySQL column types: FloatType to FLOAT, StringType to LONGTEXT, ByteType to TINYINT, ShortType to SMALLINT, TimestampNTZType to DATETIME (unless legacy), others via JdbcUtils.getCommonJDBCType.

nodes.name: createIndex
nodes.summary: Builds CREATE INDEX with the quoted column list, the index type and properties parsed by JdbcUtils.processIndexProperties; column properties are ignored.

nodes.name: indexExists
nodes.summary: Checks index existence with SHOW INDEXES ... WHERE key_name = ... through JdbcUtils.checkIfIndexExists.

nodes.name: dropIndex
nodes.summary: Generates DROP INDEX <index> ON <table>.

nodes.name: listIndexes
nodes.summary: Runs SHOW INDEXES for a table and groups the rows by key name into TableIndex objects with their columns, type and COMMENT property; failures are logged.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Maps MySQL error codes to Spark errors: 1050 on table rename to table-already-exists, 1061 on create index to IndexAlreadyExistsException, 1091 on drop index to NoSuchIndexException; UnsupportedOperationException is rethrown.

nodes.name: dropSchema
nodes.summary: Generates DROP SCHEMA and throws an unsupported error when cascade is requested.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the SELECT statement and picks the LIMIT/OFFSET form: 'LIMIT offset, limit', plain limit clause, or 'LIMIT offset, 18446744073709551615' when only an offset is given.

nodes.name: OracleDialect.scala
nodes.summary: JDBC dialect for Oracle URLs: type mappings (NUMBER, timestamps with time zone, intervals, binary float and double), SQL pushdown rules (extract, TRUNC format mapping, BLOB comparison), ROWNUM based limit and offset queries, DDL statements and error classification.

nodes.name: OracleDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class JdbcDialect (with SQLConfHelper and NoLegacyJDBCError) that handles URLs starting with 'jdbc:oracle'. It pushes down MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, STDDEV_SAMP, COVAR_POP, COVAR_SAMP, CORR, REGR_* and TRUNC, maps NUMERIC, timestamp with (local) time zone, BINARY_FLOAT, BINARY_DOUBLE and interval types, maps Catalyst types to NUMBER and VARCHAR2 column types, compiles string, timestamp, date and binary literals, builds TRUNCATE, ADD and MODIFY column statements, emulates LIMIT and OFFSET with ROWNUM, and classifies error 955 on table rename. Its companion object (lines 332-350) defines JDBC type codes BINARY_FLOAT (100), BINARY_DOUBLE (101), TIMESTAMP_TZ (-101), TIMESTAMP_LTZ (-102), INTERVAL_YM (-103) and INTERVAL_DS (-104).

nodes.name: OracleSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner expression-to-SQL builder extending JDBCSQLBuilder. It pushes down EXTRACT only for YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR and MINUTE, maps TRUNC format strings to Oracle formats (WEEK to IW, MONTH to MM, QUARTER to Q, YEAR to YYYY), rejects DISTINCT on variance, deviation, covariance, correlation and regression aggregates, and compares binary literals with DBMS_LOB.COMPARE.

nodes.name: OracleSQLQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner query builder extending JdbcSQLQueryBuilder. Its build() wraps the SELECT in subqueries using ROWNUM aliased as rn to apply limit and offset correctly, using the dialect limit or offset clause when only one is set.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Treats messages containing ORA-00942 or ORA-39165 as object-not-found errors.

nodes.name: visitExtract
nodes.summary: Pushes down EXTRACT only for YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR and MINUTE; any other field is reported as an unexpected expression.

nodes.name: visitSQLFunction
nodes.summary: Rewrites TRUNC(date, format) mapping WEEK to 'IW', MONTH/MM/MON to 'MM', QUARTER to 'Q' and YEAR/YYYY/YY to 'YYYY'; an unmapped format throws so the expression is not pushed down.

nodes.name: visitAggregateFunction
nodes.summary: Throws an unsupported-operation error for DISTINCT on the aggregates in distinctUnsupportedAggregateFunctions; otherwise defers to the parent.

nodes.name: visitBinaryComparison
nodes.summary: Uses compareBlob when either side is a binary literal and the default comparison otherwise.

nodes.name: compareBlob
nodes.summary: Builds a DBMS_LOB.COMPARE based comparison for BLOB values, including a null-safe form for the <=> operator.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression with OracleSQLBuilder; a non-fatal error logs a warning and returns None so it is not pushed down.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps Oracle JDBC columns to Catalyst types: NUMBER without precision or FLOAT-like columns (scale -127) to a wide decimal, timestamps with (local) time zone to TimestampType, BINARY_FLOAT to FloatType, BINARY_DOUBLE to DoubleType, interval types to year-month and day-time intervals.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst types to Oracle column types such as NUMBER(1), NUMBER(10), NUMBER(19), VARCHAR2(255), VARCHAR2(n) and TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE (unless the legacy mapping is on).

nodes.name: compileValue
nodes.summary: Compiles literals: strings are quoted and escaped, timestamps become {ts '...'}, dates {d '...'}, arrays are joined element-wise and byte arrays become HEXTORAW('...').

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Generates TRUNCATE TABLE with an optional CASCADE.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnTypeQuery
nodes.summary: Generates ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY <quoted column> <type>.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Generates ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY <quoted column> NULL or NOT NULL.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns 'WHERE rownum <= n' for a positive limit, since Oracle has no LIMIT clause.

nodes.name: getOffsetClause
nodes.summary: Returns 'WHERE rn > n' for a positive offset, where rn is the alias of rownum.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the SELECT with hint, column list, table, sample, where, group by and order by, and wraps it in ROWNUM subqueries for limit, offset or both before prepending the prepare query.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Maps Oracle error code 955 during a table rename to a table-already-exists error; everything else goes to the parent.

nodes.name: PostgresDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PostgreSQL JDBC dialect: URL detection, type mapping in both directions, SQL generation for truncate, index, rename and alter-column statements, expression and table-sample pushdown, error classification and infinity timestamp handling. Used by the JDBC data source when the URL starts with jdbc:postgresql.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala private case class that mixes in SQLConfHelper and NoLegacyJDBCError; uses pattern matching on java.sql.Types and on SQLState codes.

nodes.name: PostgresDialect
nodes.summary: JdbcDialect for PostgreSQL. canHandle matches urls starting with jdbc:postgresql; getCatalystType and toCatalystType map Postgres column types (including arrays, money, bit, timestamptz, timetz, bpchar) to Spark types; getJDBCType maps Spark types back to Postgres type names; getTruncateQuery emits TRUNCATE TABLE ONLY, optionally with CASCADE; getFetchSize defaults to 1000 and beforeFetch turns autocommit off so the driver can fetch in batches; getUpdateColumnTypeQuery and getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery build ALTER TABLE statements; createIndex, indexExists and dropIndex build index SQL; classifyException turns SQLState values into Spark exceptions; compileExpression, compileValue, compileTableSample and the supportsLimit, supportsOffset, supportsJoin flags control pushdown; renameTable rejects renames across schemas; convertJavaTimestampToTimestamp and convertJavaDateToDate clamp the Postgres infinity constants; updateExtraColumnMeta reads array dimensions from pg_attribute. Also holds the nested PostgresSQLBuilder class.

nodes.name: PostgresSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Inner SQL builder used when compiling V2 expressions for Postgres. visitExtract renames the fields DAY_OF_WEEK to ISODOW, DAY_OF_YEAR to DOY and YEAR_OF_WEEK to ISOYEAR before delegating to the parent; visitBinaryArithmetic replaces the ^ operator with # in the operator name.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Returns true when the SQLState is 42P01, 3F000 or 42704, which this dialect treats as 'object not found'.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: Maps a JDBC column (java.sql.Types code, type name, size) to a Spark DataType: REAL to float, SMALLINT to short, money to string, timestamptz and timetz to timestamp, void to null, other types to string; for arrays it resolves the element type with toCatalystType and wraps it in as many ArrayType levels as the arrayDimension metadata says.

nodes.name: toCatalystType
nodes.summary: Private helper that converts a Postgres type name (bool, int2, int4, int8, float4, float8, varchar, char, text-like types, bytea, timestamp, date, numeric) to a Spark DataType; used for array element types. Unknown names fall back to string and money returns None.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps a Spark DataType to a Postgres JdbcType (TEXT, BYTEA, BOOLEAN, FLOAT4, FLOAT8, SMALLINT, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, NUMERIC(p,s)); for arrays it builds the element type name followed by [] using this method and JdbcUtils.getCommonJDBCType.

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Builds the truncate statement as TRUNCATE TABLE ONLY <table>, adding CASCADE when cascade is Some(true), so descendant (inheritance) tables are not truncated.

nodes.name: getFetchSize
nodes.summary: Returns the user-set fetch size option, or 1000 (POSTGRES_DEFAULT_FETCH_SIZE) with an info log when none is set, to avoid loading all rows into executor memory.

nodes.name: beforeFetch
nodes.summary: Calls the parent beforeFetch and then sets autocommit to false when the fetch size is greater than zero, which the source comment says the driver needs for a non-zero fetch size.

nodes.name: getUpdateColumnNullabilityQuery
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL or SET NOT NULL.

nodes.name: createIndex
nodes.summary: Builds a CREATE INDEX statement with index type and a WITH (...) property list, using JdbcUtils.processIndexProperties for the 'postgresql' dialect.

nodes.name: indexExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether an index exists by querying pg_indexes through JdbcUtils.checkIfIndexExists.

nodes.name: classifyException
nodes.summary: Maps SQLException SQLState values to Spark exceptions: 42P07 to index-already-exists or table-already-exists (also parsing the message with a regex), 42704 on DROP INDEX to NoSuchIndexException, 2BP01 to NonEmptyNamespaceException; everything else goes to the parent classifyException.

nodes.name: compileExpression
nodes.summary: Compiles a V2 expression to Postgres SQL with a new PostgresSQLBuilder; returns None and logs a warning on non-fatal errors.

nodes.name: compileValue
nodes.summary: Renders byte arrays as a hex literal cast to bytea; other values go to the parent compileValue.

nodes.name: compileTableSample
nodes.summary: Builds a TABLESAMPLE clause with the sample method, percentage and REPEATABLE seed; returns None for sampling with replacement.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Builds ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO; throws an error when the old and new tables are in different namespaces.

nodes.name: convertJavaTimestampToTimestamp
nodes.summary: Clamps the Postgres infinity timestamp millisecond constants to 9999-12-31 and 0001-01-01 so they do not overflow Spark microsecond timestamps; other values are returned unchanged.

nodes.name: convertJavaDateToDate
nodes.summary: Same infinity clamping as the timestamp version, applied to java.sql.Date values.

nodes.name: updateExtraColumnMeta
nodes.summary: For ARRAY columns, queries pg_attribute for attndims and stores it in the column metadata as arrayDimension (at least 1); logs a warning if the query fails.

nodes.name: visitExtract
nodes.summary: Renames extract fields that differ for Postgres (DAY_OF_WEEK to ISODOW, DAY_OF_YEAR to DOY, YEAR_OF_WEEK to ISOYEAR) and calls the parent visitExtract.

nodes.name: SnowflakeDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Snowflake JDBC dialect: URL detection for jdbc:snowflake, BOOLEAN type mapping, and SQLState checks for missing objects and syntax errors.

nodes.name: SnowflakeDialect
nodes.summary: JdbcDialect for URLs starting with jdbc:snowflake. getJDBCType maps BooleanType to BOOLEAN (instead of the default BIT(1)) and delegates other types to JdbcUtils.getCommonJDBCType; isObjectNotFoundException checks SQLState 002003; isSyntaxErrorBestEffort checks SQLState 42000.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps BooleanType to the BOOLEAN JdbcType; all other types go to JdbcUtils.getCommonJDBCType.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: Treats SQLState 42000 as a syntax error (best effort, per the comment in the source).

nodes.name: HadoopLineRecordReader.java
nodes.summary: Java record reader inlined from Hadoop's LineRecordReader, adding the compression option and extra codec support (ZSTD) via HadoopCodecStreams. It reads text lines of a file split, with the byte offset as key and the line as value.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class extending Hadoop's RecordReader; the source names Scala's HadoopCodecStreams (getDecompressionCodec, createZstdInputStream), but no cross-language edge is emitted.

nodes.name: HadoopLineRecordReader
nodes.summary: RecordReader<LongWritable, Text> that treats keys as file offsets and values as lines. initialize opens the split, picks a codec through HadoopCodecStreams.getDecompressionCodec (falling back to HadoopCodecStreams.createZstdInputStream when codec setup fails) and skips the first partial line for non-first splits; nextKeyValue reads lines, strips a UTF-8 BOM at position 0 and skips lines longer than the maximum; getProgress reports split progress; close returns the decompressor to the pool. Two constructors exist: a no-arg one and one taking a custom record delimiter.

nodes.name: HadoopLineRecordReader
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores a custom record delimiter (the no-arg constructor at lines 83-84 is empty).

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Opens the file split, creates the line reader (compressed splittable, compressed non-splittable, ZSTD fallback, or uncompressed), and discards the first line when the split does not start at offset 0.

nodes.name: maxBytesToConsume
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum bytes a single readLine may consume: unlimited for compressed input, otherwise bounded by the split end and the maximum line length.

nodes.name: getFilePosition
nodes.summary: Returns the position from the compressed stream when the input is compressed, otherwise the tracked pos.

nodes.name: skipUtfByteOrderMark
nodes.summary: Reads the first line and strips a UTF-8 byte order mark (0xEF,0xBB,0xBF) from it if present, logging when found.

nodes.name: nextKeyValue
nodes.summary: Advances to the next line: sets the key to the current offset, reads a line (using skipUtfByteOrderMark at offset 0), skips lines that are too long, and returns false at end of data.

nodes.name: getCurrentKey
nodes.summary: Returns the current line offset key.

nodes.name: getCurrentValue
nodes.summary: Returns the current line text value.

nodes.name: getProgress
nodes.summary: Returns the fraction of the split already read, between 0 and 1.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the line reader and returns the decompressor to CodecPool.

nodes.name: SchemaColumnConvertNotSupportedException.java
nodes.summary: Java exception class thrown when a Parquet reader finds a mismatch between a column's physical type in a file and the logical type in the schema.

nodes.name: SchemaColumnConvertNotSupportedException
nodes.summary: RuntimeException (annotated Unstable) that records the column name, the physical type in the actual file and the logical type of the schema used to read all files. Getters getColumn, getPhysicalType and getLogicalType expose them; the constructor builds the message from the three values.

nodes.name: TextOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the options of the text data source (compression, wholetext, encoding, lineSep) parsed from a case-insensitive map, with the option name constants in the companion object.

nodes.name: TextOptions
nodes.summary: Parses text data source options. Fields: compressionCodec (from 'compression'), wholeText (from 'wholetext', default false), encoding, lineSeparator (from 'lineSep', must be non-null and non-empty), lineSeparatorInRead (bytes in the given encoding) and lineSeparatorInWrite (defaults to newline). An auxiliary constructor accepts a plain Map. The companion object defines the option names COMPRESSION, WHOLETEXT, ENCODING and LINE_SEP with newOption.

nodes.name: XSDToSchema.scala
nodes.summary: Builds a Spark StructType from an XSD schema (from a path or a string) by walking the XML schema model; unsupported XSD constructs raise IllegalArgumentException.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object using pattern matching over the XmlSchema model classes.

nodes.name: XSDToSchema
nodes.summary: Utility object that converts an XSD into a Spark schema. read parses an XSD from a Path (via ValidatorUtil.openSchemaFile) or from a String; getStructType creates one field per top-level element; getStructField maps simple types (boolean, decimal, integer types, double, float, byte, short, int, long, date, dateTime, else string) and complex types (simple content, complex content extension, plain content with attributes prefixed by an underscore); getStructFieldsFromParticle handles xs:all, xs:choice and xs:sequence (including element refs and wildcards, which use XmlOptions.DEFAULT_WILDCARD_COL_NAME).

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads an XSD from a Hadoop Path (opening it with ValidatorUtil.openSchemaFile and setting the base URI) and returns the Spark StructType. An overload at lines 64-67 reads from an XSD string.

nodes.name: getStructType
nodes.summary: Creates a StructType with one field per top-level schema element; a field is nullable when minOccurs is 0.

nodes.name: getStructField
nodes.summary: Converts an XSD simple or complex type into a StructField, mapping XSD built-in types to Spark types and handling simpleContent, complexContent extension and attributes; throws for unsupported content.

nodes.name: getStructFieldsFromParticle
nodes.summary: Turns an XSD particle (xs:all, xs:choice, xs:sequence) into a list of StructFields, wrapping elements with maxOccurs above 1 in ArrayType and mapping xs:any to a wildcard column.

nodes.name: XmlInputFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines XmlInputFormat and XmlRecordReader, a Hadoop input format that returns the text between a configured start tag and end tag as one record. Used to split XML files into record strings, with support for compressed and split input.

nodes.name: XmlInputFormat
nodes.summary: Class extending TextInputFormat whose createRecordReader returns a new XmlRecordReader. Its companion object (lines 44-51) defines the configuration keys xmlinput.start (START_TAG_KEY), xmlinput.end (END_TAG_KEY) and xmlinput.encoding (ENCODING_KEY).
nodes.languageNotes: Class plus companion object sharing one class id.

nodes.name: XmlRecordReader
nodes.summary: Package-private RecordReader[LongWritable, Text] that reads an XML document and emits each block from a start tag to its matching end tag as one record. initialize opens the split (handling splittable and non-splittable compression codecs, or a bounded input stream for uncompressed data); next scans for the start tag, then reads until the end tag while tracking nested tags, attributes and self-closing tags. File position is derived from the codec stream or from counted bytes minus the reader's buffered bytes. Loosely based on Hadoop's LineRecordReader.

nodes.name: createRecordReader
nodes.summary: Returns a new XmlRecordReader for the split.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Reads the start tag, end tag and encoding from the configuration, opens the file and seeks to the split start, creates a decompressor-backed stream for compressed files (throwing if a non-splittable codec starts mid-file) or a counting bounded stream otherwise, and for uncompressed input reflects into the reader to learn its buffered byte state.

nodes.name: getFilePosition
nodes.summary: Returns the current byte position: the codec stream position for compressed input, otherwise split start plus bytes counted minus those buffered but unprocessed in the reader.

nodes.name: nextKeyValue
nodes.summary: Creates fresh key and value objects and fills them through next.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Finds the next start tag, appends it to the buffer, reads up to the end tag, sets the key to the file position and the value to the buffered text, and resets the buffer; returns false when no start tag is found.

nodes.name: readUntilStartElement
nodes.summary: Reads characters matching the start tag; returns false at end of file or when past the split end, and also accepts a start tag followed by whitespace (attributes), remembering the tag text to write.

nodes.name: readUntilEndElement
nodes.summary: Appends characters to the buffer while matching start and end tags with a nesting depth counter, handling self-closing tags and start tags with attributes; returns true on the matching end tag and false at end of file.

nodes.name: getProgress
nodes.summary: Reports progress as the fraction of the split consumed, 0 when the split is empty.

nodes.name: getCurrentKey
nodes.summary: Returns the current key (file position).

nodes.name: getCurrentValue
nodes.summary: Returns the current value (the XML block text).

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the reader and returns the decompressor to the CodecPool.

nodes.name: TeradataDialect.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TeradataDialect, the JDBC dialect for URLs starting with jdbc:teradata. It adapts type mapping, truncation, renaming, limits and error detection to Teradata behaviour.

nodes.name: TeradataDialect
nodes.summary: Private case class JdbcDialect (with NoLegacyJDBCError) handling jdbc:teradata URLs. It supports only aggregate functions MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, STDDEV_SAMP, COVAR_POP, COVAR_SAMP and CORR; treats error code 3807 as object-not-found and SQLState starting with 42 as a syntax error; maps String to VARCHAR(255), Boolean to CHAR(1) and Byte to BYTEINT; truncates with DELETE FROM <table> ALL; renames with RENAME TABLE; emits no LIMIT clause; and maps NUMERIC columns of size 40 to a system-default decimal.

nodes.name: canHandle
nodes.summary: Returns true when the lower-cased URL starts with jdbc:teradata.

nodes.name: isSupportedFunction
nodes.summary: True when the function name is in the supported set of aggregate functions.

nodes.name: isObjectNotFoundException
nodes.summary: True when the SQLException error code is 3807.

nodes.name: getJDBCType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst StringType, BooleanType and ByteType to VARCHAR(255), CHAR(1) and BYTEINT JdbcTypes; other types return None.

nodes.name: isCascadingTruncateTable
nodes.summary: Returns Some(false) because Teradata does not support cascading a truncation.

nodes.name: isSyntaxErrorBestEffort
nodes.summary: True when the SQLState of the exception starts with 42.

nodes.name: getTruncateQuery
nodes.summary: Returns DELETE FROM <table> ALL, since Teradata lacks the TRUNCATE syntax and cascade.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Builds RENAME TABLE old TO new using fully qualified quoted table names.

nodes.name: getLimitClause
nodes.summary: Returns an empty string, so no LIMIT clause is added.

nodes.name: getCatalystType
nodes.summary: For JDBC NUMERIC columns, maps unspecified precision (size 40) to the system default decimal or DecimalType(MAX_PRECISION, scale), otherwise DecimalType(size, scale); other types return None.

nodes.name: AlterTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines two physical plan nodes for table changes against a v2 TableCatalog: AlterTableExec applies a list of TableChange objects, and AddCheckConstraintExec validates existing rows against a check condition before adding the constraint.

nodes.name: AlterTableExec
nodes.summary: Physical command node for ALTER TABLE on a v2 catalog. It calls catalog.alterTable with the given TableChange list, converts an IllegalArgumentException that is not a SparkThrowable into an unsupported-table-change error, then runs the refreshCache callback and returns no rows.

nodes.name: AddCheckConstraintExec
nodes.summary: Physical unary node that adds a check constraint. Its run first executes the child plan with executeTake(1) and throws a check-violation error if any row is returned (rows that violate the condition), and only then calls catalog.alterTable with the constraint change. withNewChildInternal copies the node with a new child.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs catalog.alterTable(ident, changes), maps illegal-argument failures to an unsupported-table-change error, invokes refreshCache and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Fails with a check-violation error when the child query yields at least one row, otherwise applies the constraint change through catalog.alterTable and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: AlterV2ViewExec.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the physical plan nodes for ALTER VIEW commands on a v2 ViewCatalog: ALTER VIEW AS, SET and UNSET TBLPROPERTIES, WITH SCHEMA BINDING and RENAME TO. Each node builds a replacement view definition from the analysis-time view and hands it to the catalog, after uncaching the view.

nodes.name: V2AlterViewPreparation
nodes.summary: Private trait shared by the ALTER VIEW ... AS exec. It extends V2ViewPreparation and preserves the existing view's comment, collation, owner, user properties and schema binding mode (read from existingView), and supplies an empty user column list, so a replacement View can be built without reloading the view at run time.

nodes.name: AlterV2ViewExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for ALTER VIEW ... AS. Its run builds the new view info with buildViewInfo, uncaches the old view and calls ViewCatalog.replaceView.

nodes.name: AlterV2ViewSetPropertiesExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for ALTER VIEW ... SET TBLPROPERTIES. It merges the new properties over the existing view properties, rebuilds the view info, uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: AlterV2ViewUnsetPropertiesExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for ALTER VIEW ... UNSET TBLPROPERTIES. It removes the listed keys from the existing view properties (missing keys are ignored), rebuilds the view info, uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: AlterV2ViewSchemaBindingExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for ALTER VIEW ... WITH SCHEMA BINDING. It sets the new schema mode on the view info builder, clears the query column names when the mode is SchemaEvolution, uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: RenameV2ViewExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for ALTER VIEW ... RENAME TO. It resolves a name-only new identifier in the old namespace, records the storage level of any cached copy of the view, uncaches and invalidates the old view, calls renameView, then re-caches the view under the new name with the saved storage level.

nodes.name: viewSchemaMode
nodes.summary: Override that decodes the existing view's schemaMode string through CatalogTable.viewSchemaModeFromProperties so the replacement view keeps its schema binding mode.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the replacement view info, uncaches the existing view and replaces it atomically through catalog.replaceView.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Merges the supplied properties into the existing view properties, builds the new view info, uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops the listed property keys from the existing view properties, builds the new view info, uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Applies the new schema mode to the view info builder (clearing query column names for SchemaEvolution), uncaches the view and calls replaceView.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Qualifies the new identifier, looks up the cached data of the old view to remember its storage level, uncaches and invalidates the old view, renames it in the catalog and re-caches it under the new name.

nodes.name: CacheTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan nodes for CACHE TABLE, CACHE TABLE ... AS SELECT and UNCACHE TABLE, sharing a base trait that parses the storagelevel option, caches the plan through the session's CacheManager and optionally materializes it eagerly.

nodes.name: BaseCacheTableExec
nodes.summary: Trait for cache commands. Its run reads the case-insensitive storagelevel option (default from conf.defaultCacheStorageLevel), logs a warning for any other options, builds a Dataset from planToCache and calls CacheManager.cacheQuery, then for non-lazy caches runs count() to materialize it and uncaches the plan if that fails.

nodes.name: CacheTableExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CACHE TABLE on a resolved relation. It uses the quoted multipart identifier as the cache name and the relation itself as the plan to cache.

nodes.name: CacheTableAsSelectExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CACHE TABLE ... AS SELECT. It first creates a local temporary view for the query with CreateViewCommand, then caches the view via the base run, and drops the temporary view again if caching fails.

nodes.name: UncacheTableExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for UNCACHE TABLE. It delegates to CommandUtils.uncacheTableOrView with the relation and the cascade flag and returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Resolves the storage level from options, builds the Dataset to cache, registers it with CacheManager.cacheQuery and, unless lazy, forces evaluation with count(), removing the cache entry and rethrowing if the evaluation fails.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the temporary view for the query, calls the inherited run to cache it, and on a non-fatal error drops the temporary view before rethrowing.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls CommandUtils.uncacheTableOrView for the relation and cascade flag.

nodes.name: CreateIndexExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateIndexExec, the physical command node that creates an index on a table that supports indexes.

nodes.name: CreateIndexExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CREATE INDEX on a SupportsIndex table. It adds the index type to the properties when non-empty, converts the column properties to Java maps and calls table.createIndex; an IndexAlreadyExistsException is logged and ignored when ignoreIfExists is set.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the index properties and per-column property map, calls createIndex on the table, and downgrades an already-exists error to a warning if ignoreIfExists is true.

nodes.name: CreateNamespaceExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateNamespaceExec, the physical command node that creates a namespace in a catalog that supports namespaces.

nodes.name: CreateNamespaceExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CREATE NAMESPACE. It adds the current user as owner to the properties and calls catalog.createNamespace; under IF NOT EXISTS it ignores a concurrent-creation error and also swallows other errors when the namespace is found to exist.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the namespace with owner property; with ifNotExists it ignores NamespaceAlreadyExistsException and, for other non-fatal errors, rechecks namespaceExists and either logs and ignores the error or rethrows it.

nodes.name: CreateTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateTableExec, the physical command node that creates a table through a v2 TableCatalog.

nodes.name: CreateTableExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CREATE TABLE on a v2 catalog. It converts the table spec to properties, and in run builds a TableInfo with columns, partitioning, properties and constraints and calls catalog.createTable if the table does not exist; an existing table raises an error unless ignoreIfExists is set.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Checks tableExists, builds the TableInfo and creates the table, ignoring a concurrent TableAlreadyExistsException when ignoreIfExists is true, and throws a table-already-exists error when the table exists and ignoreIfExists is false.

nodes.name: CreateTableLikeExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateTableLikeExec, the physical command node for CREATE TABLE ... LIKE on a v2 catalog, which delegates the copy to TableCatalog.createTableLike.

nodes.name: CreateTableLikeExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CREATE TABLE ... LIKE. It builds a TableInfo from the source table's columns (without field ids), partitioning and constraints, plus explicit properties, location, provider, serde info and the default owner, and calls targetCatalog.createTableLike; source table properties are intentionally not copied.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates the target table through createTableLike when it does not exist, ignores a concurrent already-exists error under ifNotExists, and throws a table-already-exists error otherwise.

nodes.name: targetColumns
nodes.summary: Derives the new table's columns from the source table: for a V1Table it restores raw CHAR/VARCHAR types via CharVarcharUtils and converts the schema without ids, otherwise it clears the ids of the source columns.

nodes.name: targetProperties
nodes.summary: Combines user properties, serde-derived properties, provider and location, then applies default ownership; source table properties are excluded.

nodes.name: CreateV2MetricViewExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CreateV2MetricViewExec, the physical node for CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS on a v2 ViewCatalog; it reuses the shared create-view logic and only supplies the metric view specific settings.

nodes.name: CreateV2MetricViewExec
nodes.summary: Physical node for CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS. It extends V2CreateViewPreparation, which supplies run, and overrides collation (None), owner (current user), viewSchemaMode (SchemaUnsupported), viewDependencies (the given deps), tableType (METRIC_VIEW_TABLE_TYPE) and retainColumnMetadata (true). DataSourceV2Strategy routes the CreateMetricView plan here for non-session v2 catalogs.

nodes.name: DistributionAndOrderingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Provides DistributionAndOrderingUtils.prepareQuery, which rewrites the query of a write so it satisfies the distribution and ordering the data source requires, by adding repartition or rebalance nodes and a local sort, and then applying type coercion and time zone rules.

nodes.name: DistributionAndOrderingUtils
nodes.summary: Object holding prepareQuery and its helpers. It converts the connector's required distribution and ordering into Catalyst expressions and wraps the query in RepartitionByExpression or RebalancePartitions plus a non-global Sort.

nodes.name: TypeCoercionExecutor
nodes.summary: Private RuleExecutor with two single-iteration batches: type coercion rules (ANSI or legacy depending on conf) and ResolveTimeZone, applied to the rewritten query.

nodes.name: prepareQuery
nodes.summary: For a Write that RequiresDistributionAndOrdering, converts the ordered or clustered distribution to expressions, rejects conflicting partition number and size settings, adds RepartitionByExpression (strict) or RebalancePartitions, adds a local Sort for the required ordering, then runs the type coercion executor; other writes return the query unchanged.

nodes.name: resolveTransformExpression
nodes.summary: Transforms TransformExpression nodes wrapping a ScalarFunction into resolved scalar function calls, prepending the bucket count literal when numBuckets is defined.

nodes.name: typeCoercionRules
nodes.summary: Returns AnsiTypeCoercion rules when ANSI mode is enabled in the conf, and TypeCoercion rules otherwise.

nodes.name: CreateV2ViewExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node for CREATE VIEW on a v2 ViewCatalog, plus two private traits that hold the shared view validation, View construction and create-side run logic. The traits are also referenced by other v2 view execs in the same package.

nodes.name: V2ViewPreparation
nodes.summary: Private trait shared by v2 CREATE VIEW and ALTER VIEW execs.
