Declares the abstract view fields (catalog, identifier, userSpecifiedColumns, comment, collation, owner, userProperties, originalText, query, viewSchemaMode) and provides buildViewInfo, which validates the user column list against the query output, re-aliases the plan, checks for duplicate column names and assembles a View through View.Builder with SQL configs, current catalog and namespace, schema mode and query column names. It also has viewAlreadyExists (builds the already-exists error) and hooks viewDependencies, tableType and retainColumnMetadata that subclasses can override; output is empty.

nodes.name: buildViewInfo
nodes.summary: Builds the View object for a v2 view command. Throws errors when the user column list is longer or shorter than the query output, rejects a user column list combined with EVOLUTION schema mode, checks indeterminate collation and duplicate column names, aliases the query via aliasPlan, then fills a View.Builder (schema, properties, query text, current catalog and namespace, SQL configs, schema mode, query column names, and optional owner, comment, collation, dependencies and table type).

nodes.name: V2CreateViewPreparation
nodes.summary: Private trait that adds the shared CREATE-side run() for v2 view-create execs. It returns early for IF NOT EXISTS when the view exists, calls createOrReplaceView (after uncaching) for OR REPLACE or createView otherwise, and turns a ViewAlreadyExistsException into either a no-op, a cross-type collision error (a table sits at the identifier) or the view-already-exists error. Concrete execs only supply allowExisting, replace and the view fields.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes CREATE VIEW: short-circuits when allowExisting is set and the view exists, builds the View via buildViewInfo, then creates or replaces it in the ViewCatalog and handles ViewAlreadyExistsException by checking whether a table occupies the identifier. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: CreateV2ViewExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for CREATE VIEW on a v2 ViewCatalog. It carries the catalog, identifier, user column list, comment, collation, properties, original SQL text, query plan, allowExisting, replace and view schema mode, inherits the run logic from V2CreateViewPreparation, and sets the owner to the current user (CurrentUserContext.getCurrentUser).

nodes.name: DeleteFromTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node that runs a DELETE FROM on a v2 table supporting delete with predicates.

nodes.name: DeleteFromTableExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for DELETE FROM on a SupportsDeleteV2 table. It calls table.deleteWhere with the predicate array, reports the table's driver metrics in a finally block, commits the optional transaction, runs the refreshCache callback and returns no rows. It exposes custom metrics from the table's supportedCustomMetrics and returns a copy with a new transaction from withTransaction.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs deleteWhere on the table, always posts the driver metrics reported by the table, commits the transaction if one is present and refreshes the cache. Returns an empty row set.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node behind DESCRIBE of a single column on a v2 table.

nodes.name: DescribeColumnExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for DESCRIBE on one column of a v2 Table. run emits rows for col_name, data_type (raw char/varchar type when present) and comment. When isExtended is set and the table is a SupportsRead whose scan reports statistics, it also emits min, max, num_nulls, distinct_count, avg_col_len and max_col_len, printing NULL for values that are absent.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the DESCRIBE COLUMN result rows: name, type and comment, plus optional column statistics read from the scan's estimateStatistics when the extended form is requested.

nodes.name: DescribeNamespaceExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node behind DESCRIBE NAMESPACE on a v2 catalog.

nodes.name: DescribeNamespaceExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for describing a namespace of a SupportsNamespaces catalog. run loads the namespace metadata and emits rows for Catalog Name, Namespace Name and each reserved namespace property that is present; when isExtended is set it adds a Properties row with the remaining properties, redacted through the conf and sorted by key.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Loads namespace metadata from the catalog and returns the describe rows (catalog name, namespace name, reserved properties, and extended properties text).

nodes.name: DescribeTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DESCRIBE TABLE for v2 tables as the DescribeTableExec physical plan node, together with two private row-formatting traits (identifier rows and schema/partitioning/clustering rows). The doc comments say the identifier trait is shared with DescribeV2ViewExec and the base-rows trait with DescribeTablePartitionExec.

nodes.name: DescribeIdentifierRows
nodes.summary: Private trait that formats the Catalog, Namespace, Database and entity-label rows shared by the table and view describe paths. addIdentifierRows writes the catalog name, the quoted namespace, the last namespace segment as Database (for v1 compatibility) and the identifier name under the given label ('Table' or 'View').

nodes.name: addIdentifierRows
nodes.summary: Appends the four identifier rows (Catalog, Namespace, Database, and the entity label row) to the output buffer.

nodes.name: DescribeTableBaseRows
nodes.summary: Private trait with the schema, partitioning and clustering row formatting shared by DescribeTableExec and DescribeTablePartitionExec. addBaseDescription writes one row per column, then a '# Partition Information' section for identity-transform partitioning (or a '# Partitioning' list of transforms for other transforms), then a '# Clustering Information' section. It also defines the emptyRow separator helper.

nodes.name: addBaseDescription
nodes.summary: Entry point of the shared formatting: writes schema rows, then partitioning rows, then clustering rows.

nodes.name: addSchema
nodes.summary: Writes one row per table column with its name, simple type string and comment.

nodes.name: addClusteringToRows
nodes.summary: Writes the '# Clustering Information' header and one row per clustering column, resolving each column in the table schema and asserting that it exists.

nodes.name: addClustering
nodes.summary: Extracts the ClusterBySpec from the table partitioning and, if present, writes the clustering rows.

nodes.name: addPartitioning
nodes.summary: Writes partitioning rows for non-clustering transforms: a '# Partition Information' section with column name, type and comment when all transforms are identity transforms (raising an error if a column is missing from the schema), otherwise a '# Partitioning' list with one 'Part N' row per transform description.

nodes.name: DescribeTableExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for DESCRIBE TABLE [EXTENDED] on a v2 Table. run writes the base schema, partitioning and clustering rows and, for the extended form, also metadata columns, a '# Detailed Table Information' block (identifier rows, Type, reserved properties, redacted Table Properties, default-value metadata), statistics (size in bytes and row count from the scan) and constraints.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the describe result: base description always, and metadata columns, table details, stats and constraints when isExtended is set.

nodes.name: addTableDetails
nodes.summary: Adds the '# Detailed Table Information' block: identifier rows, EXTERNAL or MANAGED type, reserved table properties, the redacted and sorted Table Properties string, and column default-value metadata.

nodes.name: addTableConstraints
nodes.summary: Adds a '# Constraints' section with one row per table constraint (name and description) when the table has constraints.

nodes.name: addMetadataColumns
nodes.summary: Adds a '# Metadata Columns' section with name, type and comment when the table is a SupportsMetadataColumns with metadata columns.

nodes.name: addTableStats
nodes.summary: Reads statistics from the scan of a SupportsRead table that reports statistics and adds a 'Statistics' row with size in bytes and row count when available.

nodes.name: DescribeTablePartitionExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node behind DESCRIBE TABLE with a PARTITION clause on a v2 table that manages partitions.

nodes.name: DescribeTablePartitionExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for DESCRIBE TABLE ... PARTITION on a SupportsPartitionManagement table. run first checks that the partition exists (raising a not-exist error otherwise), writes the shared schema, partitioning and clustering rows from DescribeTableBaseRows, and for the extended form adds a '# Detailed Partition Information' block with the pretty-printed partition values and the sorted partition metadata.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Validates the partition, writes the base description rows and, for the extended form, the partition details.

nodes.name: validateAndGetPartition
nodes.summary: Lists partition identifiers matching the resolved partition spec, raises notExistPartitionError when none match, asserts there is exactly one and returns its row.

nodes.name: addPartitionDetails
nodes.summary: Adds the '# Detailed Partition Information' block: renders each partition value with ToPrettyString and escapePathName as 'name=value', adds a 'Partition Values' row and then the partition metadata entries sorted by key. The source comment says the rendering is consistent with ShowTablePartitionExec.

nodes.name: DropIndexExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node that drops an index from a v2 table that supports indexes.

nodes.name: DropIndexExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical plan node for DROP INDEX on a SupportsIndex table. run calls table.dropIndex(indexName); if the index does not exist and ignoreIfNotExists is set it only logs a warning. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops the named index and swallows NoSuchIndexException with a logged warning when ignoreIfNotExists is true.

nodes.name: CSVDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Registers the CSV file source for the v2 file data source API, with short name 'csv' and a fallback to the v1 CSVFileFormat.

nodes.name: CSVDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: File data source for CSV under the v2 API. fallbackFileFormat returns the v1 CSVFileFormat class, shortName returns 'csv', and the two getTable methods (with and without a user-supplied schema) resolve the paths, table name and options without paths and build a CSVTable. Overloads of getTable share one function node.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds a CSVTable for the given options and an explicit schema (the other overload, lines 32-37, does the same with no schema).

nodes.name: CSVScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CSV file scan for the v2 file data source, which decides splitability, creates the partition reader factory and reports pushed filters.

nodes.name: CSVScan
nodes.summary: Case class scan for CSV files on the v2 API, extending TextBasedFileScan. It builds CSVOptions from the scan options, decides splitability (not splittable in multiLine mode), creates a CSVPartitionReaderFactory with a broadcast Hadoop configuration, and reports PushedFilters in its metadata. It verifies the corrupt-record column on the driver and does not push filters that refer to that column.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A file is splittable only if the CSV data source for the parsed options is splittable and the parent scan agrees.

nodes.name: getFileUnSplittableReason
nodes.summary: Returns the parent's reason when the parent considers the path unsplittable, otherwise the text 'the csv datasource is set multiLine mode'.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Validates the corrupt-record column name, rejects queries that read only that column, drops pushed filters that reference it, broadcasts the Hadoop configuration built from the options and returns a CSVPartitionReaderFactory.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two CSVScans are equal when the parent equality holds and the data schema, options and pushed filters (compared with equivalentFilters) are equal.

nodes.name: getMetaData
nodes.summary: Adds a PushedFilters entry to the metadata map of the parent scan.

nodes.name: CSVScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CSVScanBuilder, the file scan builder for the CSV data source on the v2 read path. It builds a CSVScan and decides which data filters are pushed down to the CSV parser.

nodes.name: CSVScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileScanBuilder for CSV files. build() creates a CSVScan from the file index, the data schema, the pruned read data schema, the read partition schema, the options, and the pushed data, partition and data filters. pushDataFilters() returns the filters accepted by StructFilters.pushedFilters when the csvFilterPushDown SQL setting is on, and an empty array otherwise.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates a CSVScan from the builder state, passing the read data schema, read partition schema, options and the three filter groups (pushed data, partition and data filters).

nodes.name: pushDataFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the data filters that can be pushed into the CSV parser through StructFilters.pushedFilters when SQL conf csvFilterPushDown is enabled; returns an empty array when it is disabled.

nodes.name: CSVTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CSVTable, the v2 file table for CSV. It supplies the scan builder, schema inference and write builder, and states which data types the CSV source supports.

nodes.name: CSVTable
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileTable that represents a CSV table in the v2 file source API. It creates a CSVScanBuilder for reads, infers the schema through CSVDataSource with CSVOptions, returns a WriteBuilder (an anonymous class) that builds a CSVWrite, and its supportsDataType accepts atomic types and user defined types whose sqlType is supported while rejecting geometry, geography and other types. formatName is the string CSV.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a CSVScanBuilder built from the session, file index, schema, data schema and the merged options.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Builds CSVOptions from the table options (column pruning and session time zone from SQL conf) and asks CSVDataSource to infer the schema from the given files.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder whose build() creates a CSVWrite with the table paths, format name, data type check and merged write info.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Pattern matches the data type: geometry and geography are not supported, atomic types are supported, user defined types are checked through their sqlType, and everything else is not supported.

nodes.name: CSVWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CSVWrite, the v2 file write for CSV. Its prepareWrite configures compression and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates CsvOutputWriter instances.

nodes.name: CSVWrite
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileWrite that carries the output paths, the format name, the data type check and the LogicalWriteInfo. It allows duplicated column names. prepareWrite builds CSVOptions from the write options and SQL conf, sets the compression codec on the Hadoop job configuration when one is configured, and returns an anonymous OutputWriterFactory that creates CsvOutputWriter objects and derives the file extension from the CSV extension plus the compression extension.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Creates CSVOptions, applies the compression codec to the job configuration through CompressionCodecs, and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates a CsvOutputWriter and whose getFileExtension returns the CSV extension followed by the compression extension.

nodes.name: DropNamespaceExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DropNamespaceExec, the physical plan node that drops a namespace in a v2 catalog.

nodes.name: DropNamespaceExec
nodes.summary: Leaf command node for dropping a namespace. run() checks that the namespace exists in the namespace catalog, then calls dropNamespace with the cascade flag and converts NonEmptyNamespaceException into a cannotDropNonemptyNamespaceError; when the namespace does not exist and IF EXISTS was not given it raises noSuchNamespaceError. It returns no rows and has an empty output.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops the namespace when it exists (mapping the non-empty case to a compilation error), raises a no-such-namespace error if it is missing and ifExists is false, and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: DropPartitionExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DropPartitionExec, the physical plan node that drops partitions of a v2 partition-managed table.

nodes.name: DropPartitionExec
nodes.summary: Leaf command node holding a SupportsPartitionManagement table, the resolved partition specs, ignoreIfNotExists, purge and a refreshCache callback. run() splits the identifiers into existing and missing ones, raises NoSuchPartitionsException for missing ones unless ignored, then drops or purges a single partition, drops several at once only when the table is a SupportsAtomicPartitionManagement, or raises an error for several partitions on a non-atomic table. It calls refreshCache when the table was altered.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Partitions the identifiers by partitionExists, fails on missing ones unless ignoreIfNotExists, drops or purges one partition or many (many requires atomic partition management), and refreshes the cache if anything changed.

nodes.name: DropTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DropTableExec, the physical plan node for DROP TABLE on a v2 table catalog, including the check that distinguishes a missing table from a view.

nodes.name: DropTableExec
nodes.summary: Leaf command node for dropping a table. run() probes tableExists first, so IF EXISTS on a missing table is a no-op; when the table exists it invalidates the cache and calls purgeTable or dropTable. When the table is absent and the catalog is also a ViewCatalog that has a view at the identifier, it raises wrongCommandForObjectTypeError telling the user to use DROP VIEW; otherwise it raises noSuchTableError unless ifExists is set.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops or purges the table if it exists after invalidating the cache; if absent, reports a wrong-command error when a view of that name exists, a no-such-table error when ifExists is false, and is a no-op otherwise.

nodes.name: DropViewExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DropViewExec, the physical plan node for DROP VIEW on a v2 view catalog, including the check that distinguishes a missing view from a table.

nodes.name: DropViewExec
nodes.summary: Leaf command node for dropping a view. run() calls dropView on the ViewCatalog and invalidates the cache when it returns true. When it returns false and the catalog is also a TableCatalog with a table at the identifier, it raises wrongCommandForObjectTypeError telling the user to use DROP TABLE; otherwise it throws NoSuchViewException unless ifExists is set.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls dropView, invalidates the cache on success, and on failure reports a wrong-command error if a table exists, a NoSuchViewException when ifExists is false, or does nothing.

nodes.name: EmptyPartitionReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines EmptyPartitionReader, a PartitionReader that yields no records.

nodes.name: EmptyPartitionReader
nodes.summary: Generic PartitionReader whose next() always returns false, whose get() throws noRecordsFromEmptyDataReaderError, and whose close() does nothing. It stands in for a reader when a partition has no data to read.

nodes.name: ExplainOnlySparkPlan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExplainOnlySparkPlan, a leaf physical plan that wraps a logical plan only so it can be shown by EXPLAIN.

nodes.name: ExplainOnlySparkPlan
nodes.summary: Case class extending SparkPlan with LeafLike. It has an empty output, its simpleString delegates to the wrapped logical plan, and doExecute throws UnsupportedOperationException, so it can be displayed but never run.

nodes.name: FileBatchWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileBatchWrite, the BatchWrite used by v2 file sources to commit or abort a file write job through a FileCommitProtocol.

nodes.name: FileBatchWrite
nodes.summary: BatchWrite implementation for file-based writes, built from a Hadoop Job, a WriteJobDescription and a FileCommitProtocol. commit() casts the messages to WriteTaskResult, commits the job through the committer while timing it, then calls FileFormatWriter.processStats with the stats trackers; abort() calls abortJob; useCommitCoordinator returns false; createBatchWriterFactory returns a FileWriterFactory.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Collects WriteTaskResult messages, commits the job with the commit messages while measuring elapsed time, logs progress, and processes the per-task stats with the job's stats trackers.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts the write job by calling abortJob on the commit protocol.

nodes.name: createBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Returns a FileWriterFactory built from the job description and the committer.

nodes.name: FilePartitionReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FilePartitionReader, a PartitionReader that reads a sequence of files one after another, with handling for missing and corrupt files.

nodes.name: FilePartitionReader
nodes.summary: Generic PartitionReader built from an iterator of PartitionedFile, a function that builds a PartitionReader per file, and FileSourceOptions. next() opens the next file when no reader is active (setting InputFileBlockHolder), skips missing files when ignoreMissingFiles is set, skips corrupt files when ignoreCorruptFiles is set and DataSourceUtils says the exception is ignorable, attaches the file path to other errors through FileDataSourceV2.attachFilePath, and moves on to the next file when the current reader is exhausted. get() reads from the current reader and close() closes it and unsets InputFileBlockHolder.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances the current file reader, opening the next file lazily, applying the ignoreMissingFiles and ignoreCorruptFiles rules, wrapping failures with the file path, and recursing to the next file when one is finished.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the current reader if any and clears the InputFileBlockHolder.

nodes.name: CSVPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CSVPartitionReaderFactory, the factory that creates PartitionReaders for CSV files in the v2 batch scan.

nodes.name: CSVPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class extending FilePartitionReaderFactory. Its buildReader removes the corrupt-record column from the data and read schemas, creates a UnivocityParser with the pushed filters, picks the pruned or full schema for a CSVHeaderChecker (checking the header only at the start of the file), reads the file through CSVDataSource.readFile, and wraps the resulting iterator in a PartitionReaderFromIterator inside a PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues that appends the partition values.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the PartitionReader for one PartitionedFile: prepares schemas without the corrupt record column, a UnivocityParser, a header checker, reads rows with CSVDataSource, and adds the partition values to each row.

nodes.name: GroupPartitionsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines GroupPartitionsExec, a physical operator that coalesces the input partitions of a child with KeyedPartitioning so that partitions sharing a partition key end up in one output partition, plus the helper classes GroupedPartitionCoalescer and LazyCodeGenOrdering that it uses when building the coalesced RDD.

nodes.name: GroupPartitionsExec
nodes.summary: Unary physical plan node that groups the partitions of its child (which must report a KeyedPartitioning) by partition key. Optional joinKeyPositions projects the key, reducers reduce it, expectedPartitionKeys aligns the groups to a given key list (distributePartitions chooses between spreading splits and replicating them), and enableSortedMerge switches doExecute to a SortedMergeCoalescedRDD k-way merge that keeps the child's ordering. The private lazy val groupedPartitionsTuple (lines 135-161) computes the groups; other lazy vals are groupedPartitions, isGrouped, hasCoalescing, childIsSafeForKWayMerge (true only when every node of the child is a SafeForKWayMerge) and canUseSortedMerge (needs the SQLConf flag v2BucketingPreserveOrderingOnCoalesceEnabled and a non-empty child ordering). Trivial members: output, supportsColumnar, withNewChildInternal, simpleString and stringArgs (both built on planSummaryParts). Used in storage-partitioned joins to align the partitions of the two join sides.

nodes.name: GroupedPartitionCoalescer
nodes.summary: Serializable PartitionCoalescer that builds one PartitionGroup per entry of a pre-computed list of input partition index sequences. For each group it collects the parent partitions and picks the most common preferred location of the parent partitions as the group's preferred location. Passed to CoalescedRDD or SortedMergeCoalescedRDD by GroupPartitionsExec.

nodes.name: LazyCodeGenOrdering
nodes.summary: Private serializable Ordering[InternalRow] that holds the SortOrder expressions and the output schema, and builds the compiled comparator through GenerateOrdering.generate on first use (a transient lazy val). Used by GroupPartitionsExec as the row ordering for the sorted k-way merge so that only the expressions are serialized with the RDD.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Returns the child's output partitioning with every KeyedPartitioning replaced by a new one built from the (optionally projected) key expressions and the grouped partition keys, after asserting that all KeyedPartitioning nodes share identical partition keys. Non-expression partitionings are returned unchanged.

nodes.name: alignToExpectedKeys
nodes.summary: Builds the partition groups from the expectedPartitionKeys list: for each key and split count it either distributes the key's input partitions over numSplits groups (padding with empty ones) or replicates all of them into each group, and reports whether the result is still grouped (no key split into more than one).

nodes.name: groupAndSortByKeys
nodes.summary: Sorts the map from partition key to input partition indices in ascending order of the key row, using a natural ascending RowOrdering built from the key data types.

nodes.name: groupedPartitionsTuple
nodes.summary: Lazy val that computes the grouping: takes the first KeyedPartitioning of the child (failing with a SparkException if there is none), projects the keys by joinKeyPositions, reduces them with the reducers, groups the input partition indices by key, and then either aligns to expectedPartitionKeys or sorts by key. Returns the groups and the isGrouped flag.

nodes.name: tryEnableSortedMerge
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of this node with enableSortedMerge set (and tags copied) when the node coalesces partitions and the config, ordering and SafeForKWayMerge conditions hold; otherwise None.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the child and coalesces its RDD along the groups: an empty RDD when there are no groups, a SortedMergeCoalescedRDD with a LazyCodeGenOrdering when sorted merge is enabled and possible, and otherwise a plain CoalescedRDD with a GroupedPartitionCoalescer.

nodes.name: doExecuteColumnar
nodes.summary: Columnar execution path: coalesces the child's columnar RDD with a CoalescedRDD and GroupedPartitionCoalescer (no sorted merge), or returns an empty RDD when there are no groups.

nodes.name: outputOrdering
nodes.summary: Computes the output ordering: the child's ordering is kept when nothing is coalesced or when sorted merge is used; when partitions are concatenated, only the sort orders on partition key expressions are kept (if there are no reducers and the config v2BucketingPreserveKeyOrderingOnCoalesce is enabled), otherwise the default is used.

nodes.name: planSummaryParts
nodes.summary: Builds the plan description strings JoinKeyPositions, ExpectedPartitionKeys (count), Reducers (display names or identity) and DistributePartitions, used by simpleString and stringArgs.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Implements PartitionCoalescer.coalesce: for each index group collects the parent partitions and their preferred locations, selects the most frequent location, and returns the resulting PartitionGroup array.

nodes.name: JDBCScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JDBCScan case class, the DataSource V2 scan for a JDBC table, which carries the relation plus everything that was pushed down (pruned schema, predicates, aggregates, group-by, table sample, limit, sort orders, offset) and hands them to a V1 relation for execution.

nodes.name: JDBCScan
nodes.summary: Case class implementing V1Scan for JDBC sources. It stores the JDBCRelation, prunedSchema, pushedPredicates, pushedAggregateColumn, groupByColumns, tableSampleClause, pushedLimit, sortOrders and pushedOffset; readSchema returns the pruned schema, toV1TableScan builds a JDBCV1RelationFromV2Scan from all of these fields, and description appends the pruned schema, pushed predicates, pushed aggregates and pushed group-by to the base description for explain output. Created by JDBCScanBuilder.build.

nodes.name: toV1TableScan
nodes.summary: Creates a JDBCV1RelationFromV2Scan from the SQLContext and all the pushed-down parts of this scan and casts it to the requested relation type.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Builds the scan description by splitting the pushed aggregate columns into group-by columns and aggregate expressions (using the length of groupByColumns) and appending the pruned schema, pushed predicates, aggregates and group-by to the base description.

nodes.name: JDBCScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCScanBuilder, the DataSource V2 ScanBuilder for JDBC tables. It accepts pushdown of predicates, aggregates, limit, offset, top-N, table sample, required columns and joins, and builds a JDBCScan that carries the pushed parts.

nodes.name: JDBCScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class (session, schema, jdbcOptions, additionalMetrics) that implements ScanBuilder and the SupportsPushDown interfaces for V2 filters, required columns, aggregates, limit, offset, table sample, top-N and join, and mixes in Logging. It keeps the pushed state in private vars (pushedPredicate, finalSchema, tableSampleClause, pushedLimit, pushedOffset, sortOrders, pushedAggregateList, pushedGroupBys) and uses the JdbcDialect looked up from the URL to compile expressions. Main methods: pushPredicates, pushAggregation (checks the compiled query schema), pushDownJoin (builds a join query and replaces the query option), pushTableSample, pushLimit, pushOffset, pushTopN, pruneColumns, and build, which returns a JDBCScan. isPartiallyPushed (one line) is true when numPartitions is above 1. Each push method is gated by the matching JDBCOptions flag and by dialect support.

nodes.name: pushPredicates
nodes.summary: Splits the given predicates into those the dialect can compile and the rest; stores the compilable ones as pushedPredicate and returns the unsupported ones (all of them when predicate pushdown is disabled).

nodes.name: supportCompletePushDown
nodes.summary: Decides whether an aggregation can be pushed down completely: true when numPartitions is unset or 1, or when there is a single group-by column equal (ignoring case) to the partition column.

nodes.name: pushAggregation
nodes.summary: Compiles the aggregate and group-by expressions with the dialect (returning false if any cannot be compiled), builds a SELECT ... WHERE 1=0 query to resolve the output schema through JDBCRDD.getQueryOutputSchema, and on success stores finalSchema, the select list and the group-by columns; failures are logged and return false.

nodes.name: isOtherSideCompatibleForJoin
nodes.summary: Returns true only if join pushdown is enabled, the dialect supports joins, the other builder is a JDBCScanBuilder, and both builders have equal JDBC options after removing the table name and query options.

nodes.name: calculateJoinOutputSchema
nodes.summary: Private helper that builds the StructType for one join side from its ColumnWithAlias array: a column with an alias is added under the alias name with the original type, nullability and metadata, otherwise the original field is kept.

nodes.name: pushDownJoin
nodes.summary: Pushes a join to the remote database: maps INNER, LEFT OUTER and RIGHT OUTER join types to SQL, compiles the condition, computes the merged output schema, builds both sides' query builders, assembles the join query with JdbcSQLQueryBuilder.withJoin, replaces the table option by the query option in a new JDBCOptions, updates finalSchema, and resets pushedPredicate and tableSampleClause since they are already part of the query. Returns false and logs on unsupported join type or condition.

nodes.name: getJoinPushdownJdbcSQLBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates a JdbcSQLQueryBuilder for one side of a join: quotes the column names and aliases, then applies the pushed predicates and the aliased columns.

nodes.name: pushTableSample
nodes.summary: If table sample pushdown is enabled, builds a TableSampleInfo from the bounds, replacement flag, seed and converted sample method and asks the dialect to compile it; returns whether a sample clause was produced.

nodes.name: pushLimit
nodes.summary: Records the limit as pushedLimit when limit pushdown is enabled and the dialect supports LIMIT; returns whether it was accepted.

nodes.name: pushOffset
nodes.summary: Records the offset when offset pushdown is enabled, the scan is not partially pushed and the dialect supports OFFSET, and reduces an already pushed limit by the offset to match SQL semantics.

nodes.name: pushTopN
nodes.summary: Pushes an ORDER BY with LIMIT: compiles all sort orders with the dialect (failing if any cannot be compiled) and stores them with the limit.

nodes.name: pruneColumns
nodes.summary: Sets finalSchema to the fields of the table schema whose (case-handled) names are in the required schema; nested column pruning is not supported.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Computes the JDBC partitions with JDBCRelation.columnPartition and returns a JDBCScan wrapping a new JDBCRelation together with the final schema and all pushed-down predicates, aggregates, group-bys, table sample, limit, sort orders and offset.

nodes.name: JDBCTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCTable, the DataSource V2 table for one table of a JDBC database. It supports batch read, V1 batch write and truncate, creates scan and write builders, and manages indexes through JdbcUtils.

nodes.name: JDBCTable
nodes.summary: Case class (ident, schema, jdbcOptions, additionalMetrics) implementing Table, SupportsRead, SupportsWrite and SupportsIndex (and DataTypeErrorsBase). Its capabilities are BATCH_READ, V1_BATCH_WRITE and TRUNCATE. newScanBuilder merges the options and returns a JDBCScanBuilder, newWriteBuilder returns a JDBCWriteBuilder over JdbcOptionsInWrite, and createIndex, indexExists, dropIndex and listIndexes open a connection and delegate to JdbcUtils (createIndex and dropIndex classify failures as FAILED_JDBC.CREATE_INDEX and FAILED_JDBC.DROP_INDEX). equals and hashCode use ident, schema and jdbcOptions; name returns ident.toString. Returned by JDBCTableCatalog.loadTable and createTable.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two JDBCTable instances are equal when their ident, schema and jdbcOptions are equal.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Merges the table's JDBC options with the per-scan options and returns a JDBCScanBuilder for the active session with the table schema and metrics.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Merges the table's JDBC options with the write options into JdbcOptionsInWrite and returns a JDBCWriteBuilder.

nodes.name: createIndex
nodes.summary: Creates an index through JdbcUtils.createIndex inside a connection, wrapping failures with JdbcUtils.classifyException under the FAILED_JDBC.CREATE_INDEX condition.

nodes.name: indexExists
nodes.summary: Checks via JdbcUtils.indexExists on a managed connection whether the named index exists on the table.

nodes.name: dropIndex
nodes.summary: Drops an index through JdbcUtils.dropIndex inside a connection, classifying failures under FAILED_JDBC.DROP_INDEX.

nodes.name: listIndexes
nodes.summary: Returns the table's indexes by calling JdbcUtils.listIndexes on a managed connection.

nodes.name: JDBCTableCatalog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCTableCatalog, a V2 catalog that exposes the tables, schemas (as single-level namespaces) and dialect functions of a remote JDBC database. Each catalog operation opens a connection and delegates to JdbcUtils, wrapping failures with classified FAILED_JDBC.* error conditions.

nodes.name: JDBCTableCatalog
nodes.summary: Class implementing TableCatalog, SupportsNamespaces and FunctionCatalog (plus DataTypeErrorsBase and Logging) for JDBC sources. initialize stores the catalog name, builds JDBCOptions with a placeholder table name, and looks up the JdbcDialect and its function map. Table operations: listTables, listTableSummaries (all marked as foreign tables), tableExists, dropTable (returns false only when the object is not found), renameTable, loadTable (resolves the remote schema with JDBCRDD.resolveTable and records a schema-fetch metric, returning a JDBCTable), createTable (rejects partitions, provider and location; maps comment and other properties into JDBC options) and alterTable. Namespace operations map a namespace to a database schema: namespaceExists, listNamespaces, loadNamespaceMetadata, createNamespace, alterNamespace (only the comment property is supported) and dropNamespace. listFunctions and loadFunction serve the dialect's functions. Private helpers: checkNamespace (nested namespaces are rejected), getTableName (quoted identifiers) and toSQLId.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Returns the catalog name, requiring that initialize was called first.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Stores the catalog name (asserting it is only initialized once), creates JDBCOptions from the catalog options with a fake table option so the option check passes, and loads the JdbcDialect and its function map from the URL.

nodes.name: listTables
nodes.summary: Lists the tables of a namespace (zero or one schema name) through JDBC metadata getTables on a managed connection, wrapped in classifyException for FAILED_JDBC.GET_TABLES, and returns them as Identifiers.

nodes.name: listTableSummaries
nodes.summary: Lists the tables and reports each as a TableSummary of foreign table type.

nodes.name: tableExists
nodes.summary: Private overload (the public tableExists(ident) at lines 94-96 opens a connection and calls it) that checks the namespace, builds JdbcOptionsInWrite with the quoted table name, and calls JdbcUtils.tableExists under the FAILED_JDBC.TABLE_EXISTS condition.

nodes.name: dropTable
nodes.summary: Drops the table with JdbcUtils.dropTable and returns true; an SQLException the dialect recognises as object-not-found yields false, while other errors are classified as FAILED_JDBC.DROP_TABLE.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Renames a table through JdbcUtils.renameTable, classifying failures as FAILED_JDBC.RENAME_TABLE.

nodes.name: loadTable
nodes.summary: Loads a table: adds the quoted table name to the options, resolves the remote schema with JDBCRDD.resolveTable under a timing metric, and returns a JDBCTable carrying the schema-fetch metric; failures are classified as FAILED_JDBC.LOAD_TABLE.

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: Creates a remote table: rejects non-empty partitions, the provider and the location properties, turns the comment into the table comment option and other properties into the create-table options string, converts the columns to a StructType and calls JdbcUtils.createTable (FAILED_JDBC.CREATE_TABLE); returns a JDBCTable.

nodes.name: alterTable
nodes.summary: Applies TableChange changes with JdbcUtils.alterTable under FAILED_JDBC.ALTER_TABLE and then reloads and returns the table.

nodes.name: namespaceExists
nodes.summary: For a single-part namespace checks whether the schema exists through JdbcUtils (FAILED_JDBC.NAMESPACE_EXISTS); any other namespace shape returns false.

nodes.name: listNamespaces
nodes.summary: The no-argument overload lists all schemas via JdbcUtils.listSchemas under FAILED_JDBC.LIST_NAMESPACES; the overload that takes a namespace (lines 283-292) delegates to it for the empty namespace, returns an empty array for an existing single-part one and raises a no-such-namespace error otherwise.

nodes.name: loadNamespaceMetadata
nodes.summary: Returns empty metadata for an existing single-part namespace and raises a no-such-namespace error otherwise.

nodes.name: createNamespace
nodes.summary: Creates a schema for a new single-part namespace: only the comment property is honoured, owner is ignored, location and other properties raise errors, then JdbcUtils.createSchema runs under FAILED_JDBC.CREATE_NAMESPACE; an existing namespace or an invalid name raises an error.

nodes.name: alterNamespace
nodes.summary: Handles SetProperty and RemoveProperty changes on a single-part namespace by setting or removing the schema comment through JdbcUtils (FAILED_JDBC.CREATE_NAMESPACE_COMMENT, FAILED_JDBC.REMOVE_NAMESPACE_COMMENT); other properties and change types raise errors.

nodes.name: dropNamespace
nodes.summary: Drops the schema of an existing single-part namespace with JdbcUtils.dropSchema (with the cascade flag) under FAILED_JDBC.DROP_NAMESPACE; otherwise raises a no-such-namespace error.

nodes.name: checkNamespace
nodes.summary: Private check that rejects namespaces with more than one part, since JDBC has no nested schemas.

nodes.name: getTableName
nodes.summary: Private helper that joins the namespace and name of an Identifier as dialect-quoted identifiers separated by dots.

nodes.name: listFunctions
nodes.summary: Lists the dialect's functions as Identifiers when the namespace is empty and returns an empty array otherwise.

nodes.name: loadFunction
nodes.summary: Returns the dialect function with the given name, throwing NoSuchFunctionException for a non-empty namespace or an unknown name.

nodes.name: JDBCV1RelationFromV2Scan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCV1RelationFromV2Scan, a V1 BaseRelation with TableScan that wraps a JDBCRelation so a v2 JDBC scan can be executed through the V1 buildScan path while still passing all v2 pushdowns (predicates, aggregate columns, group by, table sample, limit, sort orders, offset).

nodes.name: JDBCV1RelationFromV2Scan
nodes.summary: Case class relation compatible with the V1 TableScan interface. It holds the pruned schema, the underlying JDBCRelation and the pushed down predicates, aggregate columns, group by columns, table sample clause, limit, sort orders and offset. Its buildScan picks the column list (all pruned schema columns, or the pushed aggregate columns when group by columns are present) and delegates to JDBCRelation.buildScan with all pushdowns. The other members are one-line overrides (sqlContext, schema, needConversion taken from the wrapped relation, and a toString returning 'JDBC v1 Relation from v2 scan').

nodes.name: buildScan
nodes.summary: Chooses the column list, either the names of the pruned schema or the pushed aggregate columns when group by columns are defined, and calls JDBCRelation.buildScan with the pushed predicates, group by columns, table sample, limit, sort orders and offset to produce the RDD of rows.

nodes.name: JDBCWriteBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JDBCWriteBuilder, the v2 WriteBuilder for JDBC tables that supports truncate and builds a V1Write whose insertable relation truncates (optionally) and then saves the data through JdbcUtils.

nodes.name: JDBCWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class WriteBuilder for JDBC output, created from a schema and JdbcOptionsInWrite, and mixing in SupportsTruncate. truncate() sets an internal flag; build() returns a V1Write whose InsertableRelation, when invoked, truncates the target table first if the flag is set (a TODO notes truncate and append are not atomic, SPARK-32595) and then calls JdbcUtils.saveTable with the data, the schema and the case sensitivity setting.

nodes.name: truncate
nodes.summary: Marks the builder to truncate the target table before writing and returns the builder itself.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Returns a V1Write whose toInsertableRelation, when executed, looks up the JDBC dialect from the URL, truncates the table through a new connection if truncate was requested, and then saves the DataFrame with JdbcUtils.saveTable.

nodes.name: JsonScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonScan, the v2 file scan for JSON sources. It decides whether files can be split, builds the JSON partition reader factory and exposes pushed filters in its metadata.

nodes.name: JsonScan
nodes.summary: Case class scan for the JSON file source, extending TextBasedFileScan. It parses the read options into JSONOptionsInRead. isSplitable depends on the JSON data source (multiLine mode makes files unsplittable) and getFileUnSplittableReason reports it. createReaderFactory checks the corrupt record column on the driver, rejects queries on raw files that select only the corrupt record column, broadcasts the Hadoop configuration and returns a JsonPartitionReaderFactory. equals compares the data schema, options and pushed filters, and getMetaData adds PushedFilters.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A JSON file is splittable only when the JSON data source for the parsed options is splittable (not multiLine) and the base scan agrees.

nodes.name: getFileUnSplittableReason
nodes.summary: Returns the reason a file cannot be split: the base reason when the base scan says unsplittable, otherwise a message that the json datasource is set to multiLine mode.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Verifies the corrupt record column name against the data schema, throws a compilation error when only the corrupt record column is read from raw files, broadcasts a Hadoop configuration built from the options and returns a JsonPartitionReaderFactory with the data, read data and partition schemas, parsed options and pushed filters.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two JsonScan objects are equal when the base scan, data schema, options and equivalent pushed filters match. hashCode (line 94) delegates to the base class.

nodes.name: getMetaData
nodes.summary: Adds the PushedFilters entry to the metadata of the base scan.

nodes.name: JsonScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonScanBuilder, the FileScanBuilder for JSON that creates a JsonScan and pushes data filters down only when the JSON filter pushdown setting is on.

nodes.name: JsonScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class scan builder for JSON files extending FileScanBuilder. build() creates a JsonScan from the pruned read data and partition schemas, the pushed data filters, the partition filters and the data filters. pushDataFilters returns the filters accepted by StructFilters.pushedFilters when the jsonFilterPushDown setting is enabled, otherwise an empty array.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates the JsonScan with the session, file index, data schema, pruned read schemas, options and the pushed, partition and data filters.

nodes.name: pushDataFilters
nodes.summary: When jsonFilterPushDown is enabled in the session conf, asks StructFilters which of the data filters can be pushed for the data schema; otherwise pushes nothing.

nodes.name: JsonTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonTable, the v2 FileTable for JSON that wires the scan builder, schema inference, write builder and supported data types of the JSON source.

nodes.name: JsonTable
nodes.summary: Case class FileTable for JSON. newScanBuilder returns a JsonScanBuilder, inferSchema uses JsonDataSource with parsed JSON read options, newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that builds a JsonWrite, supportsDataType accepts atomic, null, struct, array, map and user defined types (rejecting geometry and geography types), and formatName is 'JSON'.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates a JsonScanBuilder using the table file index, schema, data schema and the table options merged with the given scan options.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the JSON schema of the given files with JsonDataSource, using JSONOptionsInRead built from the table options, the session time zone and the corrupt record column name.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a WriteBuilder whose build creates a JsonWrite from the paths, format name, data type check and merged write info.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively checks whether a data type can be stored as JSON: false for geometry and geography, true for atomic and null types, and recursive checks over struct fields, array elements, map keys and values and the SQL type of user defined types.

nodes.name: JsonWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonWrite, the v2 FileWrite for JSON that prepares the compression codec and returns an OutputWriterFactory creating JsonOutputWriter instances.

nodes.name: JsonWrite
nodes.summary: Case class FileWrite for JSON output, created with the output paths, format name, data type support check and LogicalWriteInfo. Its prepareWrite parses the options into JSONOptions, sets the compression codec in the job configuration when one is given, and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates a JsonOutputWriter and whose file extension is '.json' plus the compression extension.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Builds JSONOptions from the options, applies the compression codec to the Hadoop job configuration, and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates JsonOutputWriter objects and names files with the '.json' extension plus the codec extension.

nodes.name: OrcScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcScan, the v2 file scan for ORC. It supports aggregate pushdown (no file splitting, pruned read schema), builds the ORC partition reader factory and reports pushed filters, aggregation and group by in its metadata.

nodes.name: OrcScan
nodes.summary: Case class scan for ORC files extending FileScan. When an aggregate is pushed down, files are not split (only the footer is read) and readSchema returns the already pruned read data schema. createReaderFactory broadcasts the Hadoop configuration, chooses off-heap or on-heap column vectors from the configuration and returns an OrcPartitionReaderFactory. equals also compares pushed aggregates with AggregatePushDownUtils, and getMetaData adds PushedFilters, PushedAggregation and PushedGroupBy.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A file is splittable only when no aggregate has been pushed down, because a pushed aggregate reads the file footer once.

nodes.name: readSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the read data schema directly when an aggregate is pushed down (it was already pruned in OrcScanBuilder), otherwise the base scan read schema.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Broadcasts the Hadoop configuration, picks MemoryMode.OFF_HEAP or ON_HEAP from offHeapColumnVectorEnabled, and creates an OrcPartitionReaderFactory with the schemas, pushed filters, pushed aggregate and OrcOptions.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares two OrcScan objects by base scan, data schema, options, equivalent pushed filters and equivalent pushed aggregates. hashCode (line 93) uses the class hash code.

nodes.name: getMetaData
nodes.summary: Adds PushedFilters, PushedAggregation and PushedGroupBy strings to the base scan metadata; the aggregation strings are computed in a lazy private pair at lines 95-100.

nodes.name: OrcScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcScanBuilder, the FileScanBuilder for ORC with nested schema pruning, ORC filter pushdown and aggregate pushdown, producing an OrcScan.

nodes.name: OrcScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class scan builder for ORC files extending FileScanBuilder and SupportsPushDownAggregates, with nested schema pruning enabled. build() uses the schema pruned by pushAggregation when an aggregate was pushed, otherwise the regular pruned read data schema, and creates an OrcScan. pushDataFilters keeps the filters ORC can convert when orcFilterPushDown is on. pushAggregation, when orcAggregatePushDown is on, asks AggregatePushDownUtils for the schema of the pushed aggregation and records it.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Sets the final schema from the regular column pruning when no aggregate is pushed (the two are mutually exclusive) and creates an OrcScan with the schemas, options, pushed aggregate and filters.

nodes.name: pushDataFilters
nodes.summary: When orcFilterPushDown is enabled, builds a searchable type map from the read data schema and returns the filters OrcFilters.convertibleFilters accepts; otherwise returns no filters.

nodes.name: pushAggregation
nodes.summary: Returns false when orcAggregatePushDown is off; otherwise asks AggregatePushDownUtils.getSchemaForPushedAggregation for the pruned schema, and when one is found stores it as the final schema, remembers the aggregation and returns true.

nodes.name: OrcTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcTable, the v2 FileTable for ORC that wires the scan builder, schema inference through OrcUtils, write builder and supported data types.

nodes.name: OrcTable
nodes.summary: Case class FileTable for ORC. newScanBuilder returns an OrcScanBuilder, inferSchema delegates to OrcUtils.inferSchema, newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that builds an OrcWrite, supportsDataType accepts atomic, struct, array, map and user defined types (rejecting geometry and geography), and formatName is 'ORC'.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates an OrcScanBuilder with the file index, schema, data schema and the table options merged with the given scan options.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the ORC schema of the given files by calling OrcUtils.inferSchema with the table options.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a WriteBuilder whose build creates an OrcWrite from the paths, format name, data type check and merged write info.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively checks whether a data type can be written as ORC: false for geometry and geography, true for atomic types, and recursive checks over struct fields, array elements, map keys and values and the SQL type of user defined types; any other type is rejected.

nodes.name: OrcWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcWrite, the v2 FileWrite for ORC that configures the ORC output schema, compression and output format and returns an OutputWriterFactory creating OrcOutputWriter instances.

nodes.name: OrcWrite
nodes.summary: Case class FileWrite for ORC output. Its prepareWrite parses OrcOptions, sets the ORC output schema string and the compression codec in the job configuration, sets the OrcOutputFormat on the JobConf, reads the vectorized writer batch size from the SQL conf and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates OrcOutputWriter objects and derives the file extension from the compression codec plus '.orc'.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Configures the Hadoop job for ORC (output schema, compression codec, OrcOutputFormat) and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates an OrcOutputWriter with the vectorized batch size and whose getFileExtension is the codec extension followed by '.orc'.

nodes.name: ParquetScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetScan, the v2 file scan for Parquet. It supports aggregate pushdown and variant extraction pushdown (rewriting the read schema), sets the Parquet read support configuration and builds the Parquet partition reader factory.

nodes.name: ParquetScan
nodes.summary: Case class scan for Parquet files extending FileScan. With a pushed aggregate, files are not split and the read schema is the already pruned one. With pushed VariantExtraction entries, the read schema is rewritten so each variant column becomes a struct of ordinal-named fields carrying VariantMetadata (with a placeholder boolean field when only the variant itself would be requested). createReaderFactory writes the requested schema JSON, session time zone, case sensitivity, nested schema pruning and several Parquet conversion flags into the Hadoop configuration, broadcasts it and returns a ParquetPartitionReaderFactory. equals also compares pushed aggregates and variant extractions, and getMetaData adds PushedFilters, PushedAggregation, PushedGroupBy and PushedVariantExtractions.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A file is splittable only when no aggregate has been pushed down, because a pushed aggregate reads the file footer once.

nodes.name: effectiveReadDataSchema
nodes.summary: Private helper returning the read data schema, rewritten for variant pushdown when variant extractions have been pushed.

nodes.name: rewriteVariantPushdownSchema
nodes.summary: Groups the pushed variant extractions by column name, builds for each column a struct whose fields are named by ordinal and carry the extraction metadata and expected type, substitutes a placeholder boolean field when the struct would only hold the variant type, then rewrites the given schema with these structs.

nodes.name: rewriteType
nodes.summary: Recursively walks struct types (skipping structs that are already variant structs) and replaces the data type of any field whose path matches an extracted variant schema.

nodes.name: readSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the effective read data schema when an aggregate is pushed; otherwise takes the base scan schema (data plus partition schema) and applies the variant rewrite when variant extractions exist.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Sets the Parquet read support class, requested row schema, session time zone, nested schema pruning, case sensitivity and the Parquet schema conversion flags in the Hadoop configuration, broadcasts it and creates a ParquetPartitionReaderFactory with the data, effective read and partition schemas, pushed filters, pushed aggregate and ParquetOptions.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Compares two ParquetScan objects by base scan, data schema, options, equivalent pushed filters, equivalent pushed aggregates and pushed variant extractions. hashCode (line 197) uses the class hash code.

nodes.name: getMetaData
nodes.summary: Adds PushedFilters, PushedAggregation, PushedGroupBy and PushedVariantExtractions (formatted as column:metadata:expected type) to the base scan metadata.

nodes.name: ParquetScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetScanBuilder, the FileScanBuilder for Parquet with nested schema pruning, Parquet filter pushdown, aggregate pushdown and variant extraction pushdown, producing a ParquetScan.

nodes.name: ParquetScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class scan builder for Parquet files extending FileScanBuilder with SupportsPushDownAggregates and SupportsPushDownVariantExtractions, with nested schema pruning enabled. pushDataFilters converts the read schema to a Parquet schema and returns the filters ParquetFilters accepts, honoring the date, timestamp, decimal, string predicate and IN threshold settings, when parquetFilterPushDown is on. pushAggregation uses AggregatePushDownUtils when parquetAggregatePushDown is on. pushVariantExtractions accepts all extractions. build() creates the ParquetScan.

nodes.name: pushDataFilters
nodes.summary: When parquetFilterPushDown is on, converts the read data schema to a Parquet schema, creates ParquetFilters with the pushdown settings for date, timestamp, decimal, string predicates and the IN threshold, and returns the convertible filters; otherwise returns none.

nodes.name: pushAggregation
nodes.summary: Returns false when parquetAggregatePushDown is off; otherwise asks AggregatePushDownUtils.getSchemaForPushedAggregation for the pruned schema, and when found stores it, remembers the aggregation and returns true.

nodes.name: pushVariantExtractions
nodes.summary: Stores the given variant extractions and returns an array of true values, since Parquet accepts all of them.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Uses the regular pruned read data schema as the final schema when no aggregate is pushed, then creates a ParquetScan with the schemas, pushed, partition and data filters, options, pushed aggregate and variant extractions.

nodes.name: FilePartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract FilePartitionReaderFactory, which turns a FilePartition into a row or columnar FilePartitionReader using per-file reader builders, and the private PartitionedFileReader pairing a file with its reader.

nodes.name: FilePartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Abstract PartitionReaderFactory for file sources. createReader and createColumnarReader assert the input is a FilePartition and wrap an iterator of its files in a FilePartitionReader that calls buildReader or buildColumnarReader for each file. Subclasses implement buildReader (row reader for one PartitionedFile); buildColumnarReader throws cannotCreateColumnarReaderError by default. The file options come from the protected options member.

nodes.name: PartitionedFileReader
nodes.summary: Package-private case class that pairs a PartitionedFile with its PartitionReader. It forwards next, get and close to the reader and its toString is the file's toString.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Asserts the partition is a FilePartition and returns a FilePartitionReader over its files that builds a row reader for each file with buildReader.

nodes.name: createColumnarReader
nodes.summary: Asserts the partition is a FilePartition and returns a FilePartitionReader over its files that builds a columnar batch reader for each file with buildColumnarReader.

nodes.name: buildColumnarReader
nodes.summary: Default columnar reader builder that throws cannotCreateColumnarReaderError; file formats with columnar support override it.

nodes.name: FileScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract FileScanBuilder, the base of file source scan builders: it handles column pruning, splitting filters into partition and data filters, translating data filters to V1 sources.Filter and calling the format specific pushDataFilters hook.

nodes.name: FileScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Abstract ScanBuilder for file sources with SupportsPushDownRequiredColumns and SupportsPushDownCatalystFilters. It keeps the required schema, partition filters, data filters and pushed data filters. pruneColumns stores the required schema; readDataSchema and readPartitionSchema compute the data and partition columns to read (honoring nested schema pruning and case sensitivity); pushFilters splits deterministic filters into partition and data filters (dropping partition filters with subqueries or Python UDFs), translates data filters and calls pushDataFilters (empty by default, overridden by formats) and returns the filters Spark must still evaluate. partitionNameSet holds the partition column names.

nodes.name: pruneColumns
nodes.summary: Stores the required schema chosen by the optimizer (possibly with pruned nested columns); formats without nested pruning use it only as a reference for top-level columns.

nodes.name: readDataSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the data schema fields to read: from the required schema when nested schema pruning is supported, otherwise from the full data schema, keeping only required names that are not partition columns.

nodes.name: readPartitionSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the partition schema fields whose names are in the required column name set.

nodes.name: pushFilters
nodes.summary: Splits the filters into deterministic and non-deterministic, separates partition filters from data filters, drops partition filters containing subqueries or Python UDFs, translates the data filters to sources.Filter, calls pushDataFilters, and returns the data filters plus the non-deterministic filters as the ones still to be evaluated.

nodes.name: pushDataFilters
nodes.summary: Hook that file formats override to push data filters into the reader; by default nothing is pushed and an empty array is returned.

nodes.name: createRequiredNameSet
nodes.summary: Builds the set of required column names from the required schema, normalized for case sensitivity.

nodes.name: FileWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FileWrite trait, the base of v2 file source writes: it validates inputs, sets up the Hadoop job and commit protocol, builds the WriteJobDescription and returns a FileBatchWrite.

nodes.name: FileWrite
nodes.summary: Trait extending Write for file sources. Implementations provide paths, formatName, supportsDataType, the LogicalWriteInfo and prepareWrite (which returns an OutputWriterFactory). toBatch validates inputs, creates a Hadoop Job, instantiates the configured FileCommitProtocol, sets up the job and returns a FileBatchWrite. validateInputs requires a schema, a query id and exactly one path, checks duplicated column names unless allowed, validates the schema for the format and rejects unsupported data types. createWriteJobDescription calls prepareWrite and fills a WriteJobDescription (no partition columns or bucket spec yet, maxRecordsPerFile and time zone from options or session conf, a BasicWriteJobStatsTracker).

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Validates the inputs, builds the Hadoop Job for the single output path, instantiates the FileCommitProtocol class from the session conf, lazily creates the WriteJobDescription, calls committer.setupJob and returns a FileBatchWrite.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Abstract hook (documented as client side job preparation, such as configuring a custom output committer) that formats implement to configure the job and return an OutputWriterFactory.

nodes.name: validateInputs
nodes.summary: Asserts the schema and query id exist, requires exactly one path, checks column name duplication unless allowDuplicatedColumnNames is true, calls DataSource.validateSchema for the format and throws an error for any column whose type is unsupported by the format.

nodes.name: getJobInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a Hadoop Job from the configuration with Void keys, InternalRow values and the output path set.

nodes.name: createWriteJobDescription
nodes.summary: Calls prepareWrite to get the OutputWriterFactory, converts the schema to attributes, creates the basic write stats tracker and returns a WriteJobDescription with all columns as data columns, no partition columns, maxRecordsPerFile and time zone taken from options or the session conf.

nodes.name: FileWriterFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileWriterFactory, the DataWriterFactory for file sources that creates a single directory or dynamic partition writer per task with a Hadoop task attempt context.

nodes.name: FileWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable DataWriterFactory built from a WriteJobDescription and a FileCommitProtocol. It keeps a serializable job tracker id and recreates the Hadoop job id lazily on each executor (SPARK-42478). createWriter builds a task attempt context, calls committer.setupTask and returns a SingleDirectoryDataWriter when there are no partition columns, otherwise a DynamicPartitionDataSingleWriter.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the task attempt context for the partition and task id, runs committer.setupTask and returns a SingleDirectoryDataWriter if the description has no partition columns, otherwise a DynamicPartitionDataSingleWriter.

nodes.name: createTaskAttemptContext
nodes.summary: Builds TaskID and TaskAttemptID objects for a map task, sets the mapreduce job, task, attempt, ismap and partition keys in the Hadoop configuration and returns a TaskAttemptContextImpl.

nodes.name: GroupBasedRowLevelOperationScanPlanning.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the GroupBasedRowLevelOperationScanPlanning optimizer rule, which builds and pushes filters into the scan for group-based row-level operations (such as replacing data groups in files) and simplifies MERGE join conditions.

nodes.name: GroupBasedRowLevelOperationScanPlanning
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] with PredicateHelper that must run before V2ScanRelationPushDown. For each GroupBasedRowLevelOperation with a ReplaceData plan over a DataSourceV2Relation it creates the scan builder of the row-level operation table, pushes the command condition (not the negated rewrite filter) with PushDownUtils, prunes columns, logs the pushed, evaluated and post-scan filters, and replaces the relation with a DataSourceV2ScanRelation. For MERGE it removes already evaluated filters from the join condition. Helpers split the condition into subquery and non-subquery table filters.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan top down: for each group-based ReplaceData operation, builds the scan builder from the row-level operation table, pushes the operation condition, prunes columns, logs the pushdown result, simplifies MERGE join conditions with the evaluated filters and swaps the matching DataSourceV2Relation for a DataSourceV2ScanRelation.

nodes.name: pushFilters
nodes.summary: Finds the table filters of the condition, pushes those without subqueries through PushDownUtils.pushFilters, and returns the pushed filters, the filters fully evaluated by the data source and the post-scan filters (including subquery filters) that Spark must still evaluate.

nodes.name: findTableFilters
nodes.summary: Splits the condition into conjunctive predicates that only reference the table attributes, normalizes them and partitions them into filters with and without subqueries.

nodes.name: optimizeMergeJoinCondition
nodes.summary: Removes predicates already evaluated by the data source from the MERGE join condition and combines the rest with And, or returns TrueLiteral when none remain.

nodes.name: MergeRowsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan node MergeRowsExec that runs the row-level part of a MERGE statement, together with its helper types for instructions, cardinality validation and the per-partition iterator. It is used when a rewritten MERGE plan, which has joined target and source rows, is executed either through whole-stage code generation or through the interpreted RDD path.

nodes.name: MergeRowsExec
nodes.summary: Case class and unary physical operator that takes joined target and source rows and applies the MERGE instructions (Keep, Discard, Split) for matched, not matched and not matched by source rows. It extends UnaryExecNode with CodegenSupport: doConsume and the generate* helpers emit Java code that routes each row to the right instruction list and updates metrics, while doExecute maps each partition through processPartition and a MergeRowIterator. It declares eight SQL metrics (numTargetRowsCopied, numTargetRowsInserted, numTargetRowsDeleted, numTargetRowsUpdated and the matched or not-matched-by-source update and delete counters), computes producedAttributes and references (adding the row ID attribute when checkCardinality is set), and reports needCopyResult when any instruction is a Split. Trivial overrides (simpleString, withNewChildInternal, doExecute, inputRDDs, supportCodegen, doProduce, createProjection, createPredicate) have no function nodes.

nodes.name: needCopyResult
nodes.summary: Returns true when any matched, not matched or not matched by source instruction is a Split, or when the child code-generating operator needs copied results, because only Split instructions emit two output rows per input row.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Code generation entry point for each input row: wraps the instruction logic in a freshly named private method (so return statements leave only that method) and returns the call to it. Builds the parameter list with constructConsumeParameters and the body with generateInstructionExecutionCode.

nodes.name: generateCardinalityValidationCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that keeps a Roaring64Bitmap of already matched row IDs in a mutable state field and throws the merge cardinality violation error when the same row ID is seen twice.

nodes.name: generateInstructionExecutionCode
nodes.summary: Generates the main routing code: evaluates the source-row-present and target-row-present predicates, then branches to the matched instructions (after optional cardinality validation), the not matched instructions, or the not matched by source instructions. Rows where both sides are absent are dropped.

nodes.name: generateInstructionsCode
nodes.summary: Generates code for a sequence of instructions by concatenating the code of each one, followed by a return so that a row matching no instruction is discarded; returns an empty string for an empty list.

nodes.name: generateSingleInstructionCode
nodes.summary: Generates code for one Keep, Discard or Split instruction: evaluates its condition predicate, updates the matching metrics, projects output rows and passes them to consume, then returns. Throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException for any other instruction type.

nodes.name: generateMetricUpdateCode
nodes.summary: Chooses the metric update code for a Keep instruction from its context (Copy, Insert, Update or Delete); Update and Delete delegate to the update and delete metric generators and any other context throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: generateUpdateMetricUpdateCode
nodes.summary: Generates code that adds one to numTargetRowsUpdated and to either numTargetRowsMatchedUpdated or numTargetRowsNotMatchedBySourceUpdated depending on whether a source row is present.

nodes.name: generateDeleteMetricUpdateCode
nodes.summary: Generates code that adds one to numTargetRowsDeleted and to either numTargetRowsMatchedDeleted or numTargetRowsNotMatchedBySourceDeleted depending on whether a source row is present.

nodes.name: withCodegenContext
nodes.summary: Helper that saves the CodegenContext currentVars and INPUT_ROW, sets currentVars to the input variables from doConsume while a block runs, and restores both afterwards, because expression code generation modifies the context.

nodes.name: generatePredicateCode
nodes.summary: Binds a predicate to the input attributes, generates its Java code inside withCodegenContext and declares a boolean variable that is true only when the result is non-null and true.

nodes.name: generateProjectionCode
nodes.summary: Binds the output expressions to the child output and generates their ExprCode inside withCodegenContext, producing the projected row values for a Keep or Split instruction.

nodes.name: processPartition
nodes.summary: Interpreted (non-codegen) execution of one partition: builds predicates for source and target presence, plans the three instruction lists, picks a BitmapCardinalityValidator (when checkCardinality is set) or the no-op validator, wraps the rows in a MergeRowIterator and filters out the null rows that mean discard.

nodes.name: planInstructions
nodes.summary: Turns each Keep, Discard or Split instruction into its executable counterpart (KeepExec, DiscardExec, SplitExec) with compiled predicates and unsafe projections; any other instruction raises an AnalysisException.

nodes.name: InstructionExec
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the executable form of a MERGE instruction; it only exposes the BasePredicate condition that decides whether the instruction applies to a row.

nodes.name: KeepExec
nodes.summary: Case class for an executable Keep instruction holding its Context (Copy, Insert, Update or Delete), a condition predicate and a projection; apply projects the input row into the output row.

nodes.name: DiscardExec
nodes.summary: Case class for an executable Discard instruction; holds only the condition predicate, and a matching row is dropped (counted as a delete).

nodes.name: SplitExec
nodes.summary: Case class for an executable Split instruction, which turns one input row into two output rows: it holds a condition and two projections, with projectRow giving the first row and projectExtraRow giving the second.

nodes.name: CardinalityValidator
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with a single validate(row) method used to check the MERGE cardinality rule while rows are processed in interpreted mode.

nodes.name: NoopCardinalityValidator
nodes.summary: Object implementing CardinalityValidator with an empty validate; used when checkCardinality is false.

nodes.name: BitmapCardinalityValidator
nodes.summary: Case class that remembers the row IDs it has seen (generated by MonotonicallyIncreasingID) in a Roaring64Bitmap and throws the merge cardinality violation error when the same ID appears again. It assumes the target table is never broadcast or replicated, so all matches for one target row are in one partition.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Reads the row ID at rowIdOrdinal, throws QueryExecutionErrors.mergeCardinalityViolationError if the bitmap already contains it, otherwise adds it.

nodes.name: MergeRowIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over joined target and source rows that applies the planned MERGE instructions and returns a computed row, or null for a row to discard. It lazily resolves the eight metrics once per partition, caches the second row of a Split in cachedExtraRow, and updates the copy, insert, update and delete metrics (split by matched and not matched by source) while it works.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the cached extra row from a Split if there is one, otherwise reads the next row, evaluates source and target presence, validates cardinality for matched rows and applies the matched, not matched or not matched by source instructions (null when neither side is present).

nodes.name: applyInstructions
nodes.summary: Walks the instruction list and executes the first one whose condition is true: Keep updates the metric for its context and returns the projected row, Discard counts a delete and returns null, Split counts an update, caches the extra row and returns the first row. Returns null if nothing matches.

nodes.name: incrementDeleteMetric
nodes.summary: Adds one to numTargetRowsDeleted and to the matched or not-matched-by-source delete metric depending on sourcePresent.

nodes.name: incrementUpdateMetric
nodes.summary: Adds one to numTargetRowsUpdated and to the matched or not-matched-by-source update metric depending on sourcePresent.

nodes.name: OptimizeMetadataOnlyDeleteFromTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the optimizer rule OptimizeMetadataOnlyDeleteFromTable, which replaces a rewritten row-level DELETE plan with a delete using filters when the table can drop the matching data without running the row-level plan. It is used after expression optimization and before scan planning.

nodes.name: OptimizeMetadataOnlyDeleteFromTable
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] (with PredicateHelper) that transforms a ReplaceData or WriteDelta plan for a DELETE on a DataSourceV2Relation. If the table is SupportsDeleteV2 and the condition has no subquery, it splits the condition into conjuncts, normalizes them and tries to translate them to V2 predicates; when table.canDeleteWhere accepts them it produces DeleteFromTableWithFilters, otherwise it tries partition predicates, and finally keeps the original row-level plan. A TruncatableTable with a TrueLiteral condition becomes a plain DeleteFromTable. The doc comment says it must run after expression optimization but before scan planning.

nodes.name: apply
