nodes.summary: Rule entry point: transforms each rewritten row-level DELETE command into DeleteFromTableWithFilters, DeleteFromTable or the unchanged row-level plan depending on what the V2 table supports.

nodes.name: tryDeleteWithPartitionPredicates
nodes.summary: Tries to convert partition-column filters into PartitionPredicate objects through PushDownUtils, combines them with the V2 translation of the remaining data filters and returns a DeleteFromTableWithFilters plan only if the table accepts the combined predicates (Some or None).

nodes.name: tryTranslateToV2
nodes.summary: Translates every expression to a V2 filter with DataSourceV2Strategy.translateFilterV2 and returns the array only if all of them translated, otherwise None; logs the ones that fail at debug level.

nodes.name: RewrittenRowLevelCommand
nodes.summary: Private extractor object whose unapply matches a ReplaceData or WriteDelta plan and returns the plan, its row-level command, the condition and the original table relation.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Pattern-matches ReplaceData and WriteDelta and returns Some of (write plan, operation command, condition, original table), or None for other plans.

nodes.name: JsonDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonDataSourceV2, the file data source entry point registered under the short name json for the v2 read and write path. It is used to build a JsonTable and names JsonFileFormat as the fallback file format.

nodes.name: JsonDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Class extending FileDataSourceV2 for JSON. It sets fallbackFileFormat to JsonFileFormat and shortName to json, and its two getTable overloads compute paths, table name and options without paths, then create a JsonTable (with no schema, or with the user-supplied schema).

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds a JsonTable from the options by reading the paths, deriving the table name and removing the path options; the overload at lines 39-44 does the same but passes Some(schema) instead of None.

nodes.name: JsonPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JsonPartitionReaderFactory, which builds partition readers for JSON files in the v2 file source. It is used on executors to read one PartitionedFile at a time with the schemas, options and pushed filters of the scan.

nodes.name: JsonPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class extending FilePartitionReaderFactory with SQL conf, a broadcast Hadoop configuration, data, read and partition schemas, JSONOptionsInRead and pushed filters. Its buildReader creates a JacksonParser over the read schema without the corrupt record column, reads the file through JsonDataSource, wraps the iterator in a PartitionReaderFromIterator and adds partition values with PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Creates the PartitionReader[InternalRow] for one JSON file: removes the corrupt record column from the schema, builds a JacksonParser with the pushed filters, reads the file with JsonDataSource(options).readFile and appends the partition values.

nodes.name: OrcDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcDataSourceV2, the file data source entry point registered under the short name orc for the v2 path. It is used to build an OrcTable and names OrcFileFormat as the fallback file format.

nodes.name: OrcDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Class extending FileDataSourceV2 for ORC. It sets fallbackFileFormat to OrcFileFormat and shortName to orc, and its two getTable overloads compute paths, table name and options without paths, then create an OrcTable (with no schema, or with the supplied schema).

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds an OrcTable from the options by reading the paths, deriving the table name and removing the path options; the overload at lines 39-44 does the same with Some(schema).

nodes.name: OrcPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines OrcPartitionReaderFactory, which builds row-based and columnar partition readers for ORC files in the v2 file source. It is used on executors for each PartitionedFile and also supports reading pushed-down aggregates from the file footer.

nodes.name: OrcPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class extending FilePartitionReaderFactory with the SQL conf, broadcast Hadoop configuration, data, read and partition schemas, pushed filters, optional Aggregation, OrcOptions and a MemoryMode. supportColumnarReads checks the vectorized reader flags, whole-stage codegen and column types; buildReader reads rows through OrcInputFormat and OrcDeserializer; buildColumnarReader uses OrcColumnarBatchReader and returns a PartitionRecordReader; when an aggregation is pushed down, the two WithAggregates builders produce a single row or batch from the file footer instead. createORCReader opens the file and pushes filters as a search argument.

nodes.name: supportColumnarReads
nodes.summary: Returns true when the ORC vectorized reader is enabled, whole-stage codegen is on, the result schema does not have too many fields and every column type supports columnar reads.

nodes.name: pushDownPredicates
nodes.summary: When ORC filter pushdown is on and filters exist, converts the ORC schema to a Catalyst schema, builds an ORC filter with OrcFilters.createFilter and sets it on the Hadoop configuration as a search argument.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the row-based reader for one file: delegates to buildReaderWithAggregates if an aggregation is pushed down; otherwise reads the ORC schema, computes requested column ids, returns an EmptyPartitionReader when none are needed, or creates an OrcInputFormat record reader with an OrcDeserializer and wraps it with partition values.

nodes.name: buildColumnarReader
nodes.summary: Builds the vectorized reader for one file: delegates to buildColumnarReaderWithAggregates if an aggregation is pushed down; otherwise computes requested column ids (partition columns get -1), initializes an OrcColumnarBatchReader with the result schema and partition values, and returns it wrapped in a PartitionRecordReader.

nodes.name: createORCReader
nodes.summary: Opens an ORC Reader for the file path with case-sensitivity set for schema evolution, pushes filters through pushDownPredicates, and closes the reader if that fails; returns the reader together with its ReaderOptions.

nodes.name: buildReaderWithAggregates
nodes.summary: Returns a PartitionReader that yields exactly one row, computed lazily from the ORC footer by OrcUtils.createAggInternalRowFromFooter for the pushed-down aggregation.

nodes.name: buildColumnarReaderWithAggregates
nodes.summary: Returns a PartitionReader[ColumnarBatch] that yields one batch, built by converting the footer-based aggregate row with AggregatePushDownUtils.convertAggregatesRowToBatch (on-heap).

nodes.name: ParquetDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetDataSourceV2, the file data source entry point registered under the short name parquet for the v2 path. It is used to build a ParquetTable and names ParquetFileFormat as the fallback file format.

nodes.name: ParquetDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: Class extending FileDataSourceV2 for Parquet. It sets fallbackFileFormat to ParquetFileFormat and shortName to parquet, and its two getTable overloads compute paths, table name and options without paths, then create a ParquetTable (with no schema, or with the supplied schema).

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds a ParquetTable with Some(schema) from the options by reading the paths, deriving the table name and removing the path options; the overload at lines 32-37 does the same with None.

nodes.name: ParquetPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetPartitionReaderFactory, which builds row-based and vectorized partition readers for Parquet files in the v2 file source, plus the small ParquetReaderCallback that closes readers at task end. It is used on executors for each PartitionedFile, including the case where an aggregation is answered from the file footer.

nodes.name: ParquetPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class extending FilePartitionReaderFactory with Logging. It reads many Parquet settings from SQLConf (vectorized reader, record filter, INT96 conversion, batch size, filter pushdown flags) and the rebase modes from ParquetOptions. buildReader and buildColumnarReader return either a normal reader or, when an aggregation is pushed down, a reader that gets one row or batch from the footer statistics. buildReaderBase opens the file and footer, builds pushed-down FilterPredicates with ParquetFilters, decides INT96 timezone conversion (skipped for files created by parquet-mr), and initializes either a VectorizedParquetRecordReader or the row-based reader. supportColumnarReads simply returns the precomputed supportsColumnar flag, and createRowBaseReader just calls buildReaderBase with createRowBaseParquetReader; neither has a function node.

nodes.name: openFileAndReadFooter
nodes.summary: Opens the Parquet file and reads its footer. With an aggregation it reads the footer from a HadoopInputFile using ParquetFooterReader.readFooter and no input stream; otherwise it calls ParquetFooterReader.openFileAndReadFooter, which can hand the open stream to the vectorized reader to avoid opening the file and reading the footer twice. Returns an OpenedParquetFooter.

nodes.name: getDatetimeRebaseSpec
nodes.summary: Computes the datetime RebaseSpec for a file from the footer key-value metadata and the configured datetimeRebaseModeInRead via DataSourceUtils.datetimeRebaseSpec.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the row-based PartitionReader. Without an aggregation it uses a vectorized or parquet-mr row reader (createVectorizedReader or createRowBaseReader); with an aggregation it lazily builds one row from the footer with ParquetUtils.createAggInternalRowFromFooter (null if the footer has no blocks). The result is wrapped in PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues.

nodes.name: buildColumnarReader
nodes.summary: Builds the columnar PartitionReader[ColumnarBatch]. Without an aggregation it creates a vectorized reader that returns batches; with an aggregation it builds one batch from the footer row and AggregatePushDownUtils.convertAggregatesRowToBatch, off-heap when enabled and a TaskContext exists.

nodes.name: buildReaderBase
nodes.summary: Shared reader construction: opens the footer, translates the pushed filters to a Parquet FilterPredicate (combined with and) using ParquetFilters, decides the time zone conversion for INT96 timestamps based on the writer, sets the row-group filter on the Hadoop configuration, computes the rebase specs, calls the supplied buildReaderFunc and initializes the reader. It closes the input stream itself unless ownership moved to the vectorized reader.

nodes.name: createRowBaseParquetReader
nodes.summary: Creates the parquet-mr based ParquetRecordReader with a ParquetReadSupport (vectorization off), applies the record-level filter when pushed filters exist and enableRecordFilter is set, adds row index support if needed, and registers the reader iterator with the ParquetReaderCallback so it is closed at task completion.

nodes.name: createVectorizedReader
nodes.summary: Creates the VectorizedParquetRecordReader for a file through buildReaderBase and createParquetVectorizedReader, then initializes its batch with the partition schema and partition values.

nodes.name: createParquetVectorizedReader
nodes.summary: Constructs a VectorizedParquetRecordReader with the time zone, datetime and INT96 rebase modes and zones, the off-heap flag (only when a TaskContext exists) and the batch capacity, and registers it with the ParquetReaderCallback.

nodes.name: ParquetReaderCallback
nodes.summary: Private serializable class that closes the Parquet reader of the current file when a task finishes. It registers one task completion listener per instance (initIfNotAlready), swaps the tracked RecordReaderIterator when a new file starts (advanceFile, which closes the previous one) and closes the current iterator in closeCurrent.

nodes.name: initIfNotAlready
nodes.summary: Adds a task completion listener that calls closeCurrent, only the first time it is called.

nodes.name: advanceFile
nodes.summary: Closes the currently tracked reader iterator and stores the new RecordReaderIterator for the next file.

nodes.name: closeCurrent
nodes.summary: Closes the tracked RecordReaderIterator if there is one.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderFromIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a small PartitionReader implementation that exposes a plain Scala Iterator as a DSv2 partition reader, so any iterator of rows can be returned where a PartitionReader is required.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderFromIterator
nodes.summary: Generic adapter class that implements PartitionReader on top of an Iterator. next() advances the iterator and stores the current element when one exists, get() returns that stored element, and close() does nothing. Used when a reader already holds all its rows as an iterator.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances the wrapped iterator: if hasNext is true it stores the next value as the current value and returns true, otherwise returns false.

nodes.name: PythonCustomMetric.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the custom metric classes used to report Python data source statistics through the DSv2 metric interfaces, and a companion object holding placeholder SQLMetric instances built from the Python metric descriptions.

nodes.name: PythonCustomMetric
nodes.summary: Driver-side CustomMetric with a name and description; a no-argument constructor exists so the metric can be instantiated for aggregation (the source references SQLAppStatusListener.aggregateMetrics). aggregateTaskMetrics formats the task values with a 'size' metric type. The companion object (lines 41-54) holds pythonMetrics, a map of dummy SQLMetric instances keyed by the names in PythonSQLMetrics.pythonSizeMetricsDesc ('size'), pythonTimingMetricsDesc ('timing') and pythonOtherMetricsDesc ('sum'), only so that the existing Python runner can be reused; real values are reported through CustomTaskMetric.

nodes.name: PythonCustomTaskMetric
nodes.summary: Task-side CustomTaskMetric holding a metric name and a Long value. Instances are created from the per-task Python metric values when a Python data source reader or writer reports its current metrics.

nodes.name: aggregateTaskMetrics
nodes.summary: Aggregates the per-task metric values into a display string by calling MetricUtils.stringValue with the 'size' metric type.

nodes.name: PythonMicroBatchStream.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the structured streaming micro-batch read side of a Python data source: offset and read-limit wrappers, a base MicroBatchStream that delegates to a streaming source runner, and variants with admission control and Trigger.AvailableNow support.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSourceOffset
nodes.summary: Case class Offset holding the offset as a JSON string produced by the Python data source.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSourceReadLimit
nodes.summary: Case class ReadLimit holding the read limit as a JSON string produced by the Python data source.

nodes.name: PythonMicroBatchStreamBase
nodes.summary: Abstract MicroBatchStream shared by all Python streaming sources. It gets the initial and latest offsets, plans input partitions, commits offsets and stops by calling a PythonStreamingSourceRunner. When the runner returns prefetched rows (a simple stream reader without partitioning) it stores them as a block in the block manager under a PythonStreamBlockId and caches the single partition for the last offset range. It creates a PythonStreamingPartitionReaderFactory for reading.

nodes.name: PythonMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: Concrete micro-batch stream for Python sources without admission control; it also implements AcceptsLatestSeenOffset, and setLatestSeenOffset calls the runner's partitions method with an empty range to initialize the start offset for prefetching. The companion object (lines 165-189) provides nextStreamId, a synchronized counter, and createPythonStreamingSourceRunner, which builds a PythonStreamingSourceRunner from the data source.

nodes.name: PythonMicroBatchStreamWithAdmissionControl
nodes.summary: Micro-batch stream variant that supports admission control. latestOffset(startOffset, limit) asks the runner for the latest offset under a read limit, getDefaultReadLimit and reportLatestOffset forward to the runner, and the no-argument latestOffset throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: PythonMicroBatchStreamWithTriggerAvailableNow
nodes.summary: Admission-control stream variant that also supports Trigger.AvailableNow; prepareForTriggerAvailableNow forwards to the runner.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Plans input partitions for an offset range. It returns the cached partition if the same start and end offset JSON were planned before; otherwise it calls the runner's partitions. If the runner returned prefetched rows, it stores them in the block manager, replaces the cached partition (dropping the previous cache) and returns one partition with a block id; otherwise it returns one PythonStreamingInputPartition per pickled partition.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Creates a PythonStreamingPartitionReaderFactory using the data source, the read function from the lazily created read info, and the output schema.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits an end offset by passing its JSON to the Python streaming source runner.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Drops the cached input partition's block and stops the Python streaming source runner.

nodes.name: setLatestSeenOffset
nodes.summary: Calls the runner's partitions method with an empty range (the given offset as both start and end) to initialize the start offset for prefetching of a simple reader.

nodes.name: nextStreamId
nodes.summary: Synchronized counter that returns the next stream id, used to build PythonStreamBlockId values for prefetched blocks.

nodes.name: createPythonStreamingSourceRunner
nodes.summary: Builds a PythonStreamingSourceRunner by creating the Python data source function from the data source (getOrCreateDataSourceInPython with the output schema) and passing it with the output schema.

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Overloaded: the no-argument version throws IllegalStateException, and latestOffset(startOffset, limit) wraps the runner's latest offset (computed with the read limit) in a PythonStreamingSourceOffset. This node is the one with the widest range.

nodes.name: getDefaultReadLimit
nodes.summary: Gets the default read limit JSON from the runner and wraps it in a PythonStreamingSourceReadLimit.

nodes.name: reportLatestOffset
nodes.summary: Reports the latest offset from the runner, returning null when the runner returns null and a PythonStreamingSourceOffset otherwise.

nodes.name: prepareForTriggerAvailableNow
nodes.summary: Forwards the Trigger.AvailableNow preparation to the Python streaming source runner.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the input partition and partition reader factory used to read one micro-batch of a Python streaming data source, either from a prefetched cached block or by evaluating the Python read function.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingInputPartition
nodes.summary: InputPartition case class carrying the partition index, the pickled partition bytes and an optional PythonStreamBlockId of prefetched data. dropCache removes that block from the block manager master.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionReaderFactory for Python streaming sources. createReader returns a reader that reads the prefetched block if present (logging a warning when the block is missing), and otherwise runs the 'read_from_data_source' Python function through a map-in-batch evaluator factory created by the data source. The reader reports Python metrics through currentMetricsValues.

nodes.name: dropCache
nodes.summary: Removes the prefetched block, if any, from the block manager master.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Builds an anonymous PartitionReader for the partition. The output iterator comes from the cached block when it exists; otherwise a MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory (created by source.createMapInBatchEvaluatorFactory with the read-input schema, output schema, the shared Python metrics and the job artifact and session UUIDs) evaluates the pickled partition. next and get read from that iterator, and metrics come from source.createPythonTaskMetrics.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSinkCommitRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the runner that starts a Python worker to commit or abort a streaming micro-batch write on the Python data source stream writer.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSinkCommitRunner
nodes.summary: PythonPlannerRunner[Unit] that acts as a proxy to invoke commit or abort on a Python DataSourceStreamWriter (class comment). It uses worker module pyspark.sql.worker.python_streaming_sink_runner. It sends the data source function, schema JSON, overwrite flag, the pickled commit messages (null for failed tasks), the batch id and the abort flag, and throws a runtime error if the Python side reports an exception.

nodes.name: runnerConf
nodes.summary: Adds the Python data source profiler setting from SQLConf, if set, to the runner configuration.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Writes to the Python process: the Python function, the schema JSON, the overwrite flag, the number of commit messages and each pickled PythonWriterCommitMessage (or a NULL marker), the batch id and the abort flag.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads an int code; if it equals PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN it reads the message and throws QueryExecutionErrors.pythonStreamingDataSourceRuntimeError with the action 'abort' or 'commit'.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the streaming write path of a Python data source: a StreamingWrite that creates the writer factory and commits or aborts a micro-batch, and the writer factory that adapts the batch writer factory to the streaming interface.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingWrite
nodes.summary: StreamingWrite for Python data source writing. It stores the pickled data source writer, captures the job artifact UUID and (when Python worker logging is enabled) the session UUID, creates a PythonStreamingWriterFactory after asking the data source for write info with isStreaming = true, and commits or aborts a micro-batch by running a PythonStreamingSinkCommitRunner.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Writer factory that extends PythonBatchWriterFactory and implements StreamingDataWriterFactory; createWriter(partitionId, taskId, epochId) ignores the epoch id and delegates to the batch createWriter.

nodes.name: createStreamingWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Calls the data source's createWriteInfoInPython (streaming) to get the pickled write function and the writer instance, stores the writer bytes, and returns a PythonStreamingWriterFactory.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits a micro-batch by running a PythonStreamingSinkCommitRunner with abort = false, the epoch id as batch id and the truncate flag as overwrite.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts a micro-batch by running a PythonStreamingSinkCommitRunner with abort = true.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Streaming createWriter that delegates to the batch createWriter(partitionId, taskId).

nodes.name: PythonWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Write entry point of a Python data source and its batch write implementation, which creates the batch writer factory and commits or aborts through the Python data source.

nodes.name: PythonWrite
nodes.summary: Write implementation for a Python data source. toBatch returns a PythonBatchWrite, toStreaming returns a PythonStreamingWrite, description is '(Python)', and supportedCustomMetrics returns the metrics created by the data source.

nodes.name: PythonBatchWrite
nodes.summary: BatchWrite for Python data source writing. It stores the pickled writer instance, captures the job artifact UUID and the session UUID (when Python worker logging is enabled), creates a PythonBatchWriterFactory from the write info of the data source, and commits or aborts by calling commitWriteInPython on the data source.

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Returns a new PythonBatchWrite for the same data source, short name, write info and truncate flag.

nodes.name: toStreaming
nodes.summary: Returns a new PythonStreamingWrite for the same data source, short name, write info and truncate flag.

nodes.name: supportedCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the custom metrics created by ds.source.createPythonMetrics().

nodes.name: createBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Calls createWriteInfoInPython (isStreaming = false), keeps the returned writer bytes and returns a PythonBatchWriterFactory built from the write function, schema and UUIDs.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits the write by calling commitWriteInPython with the stored writer and the commit messages.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Aborts the write by calling commitWriteInPython with abort = true.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Core bridge between the JVM and Python for user-defined Python data sources: the UserDefinedPythonDataSource case class with its companion object, result case classes, and six private runners that each start a Python worker module to look up, create, push filters to, plan reads of, write to, and commit or abort a data source. The six runners' runnerConf overrides (which add the Python data source profiler setting) are not given separate nodes.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSource
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping the Python data source class function; it defines the interaction between the JVM and Python for a data source. Driver-side methods run Python workers to create the data source, push down filters, plan a read, create write info and commit or abort a write; executor-side methods create the map-in-batch evaluator factory that runs the pickled read or write function, plus helpers for Python custom metrics and for rebuilding a PythonFunction from pickled bytes. The companion object (lines 201-219) defines the readInputSchema ('partition' binary) and writeOutputSchema ('message' binary) schemas and lookupAllDataSourcesInPython, which finds all Python data sources.

nodes.name: PythonLookupAllDataSourcesResult
nodes.summary: Result case class of the lookup runner: an array of short names and an array of pickled data source bytes.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceLookupRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner that uses worker module pyspark.sql.worker.lookup_data_sources to look up the Python data sources available on the Python path. It sends nothing, then reads the number of sources and, for each, a short name and pickled data source; a Python exception becomes a pythonDataSourceError with action 'lookup'.

nodes.name: PythonDataSourceCreationResult
nodes.summary: Result case class of creating a Python data source: the pickled data source instance bytes and its StructType schema.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner (worker module pyspark.sql.worker.create_data_source) that creates a Python data source in a Python process. It sends the data source function, provider name, optional user-specified schema JSON and the options, then receives the pickled instance and a schema (parsed as DDL or JSON; it must be a StructType, otherwise schemaIsNotStructTypeError is thrown).

nodes.name: PythonFilterPushdownResult
nodes.summary: Result case class of filter pushdown: the new PythonDataSourceReadInfo and a sequence of booleans telling whether each filter was pushed.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceFilterPushdownRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner (worker module pyspark.sql.worker.data_source_pushdown_filters) that pushes filters to a Python data source. It converts supported filters (EqualTo, EqualNullSafe, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual, In, IsNull, IsNotNull, StringStartsWith, StringEndsWith, StringContains, each optionally wrapped in Not) to SerializedFilter values with variant values, serializes them as JSON with Jackson, and sends them with the schema and configs. And/Or and collation-aware filters are not supported. The reply carries the read info and the indices of the pushed filters. isAnyFilterSupported tells whether any filter could be serialized.

nodes.name: SerializedFilter
nodes.summary: Private case class describing one filter for JSON serialization: name, column path, optional VariantVal value, negation flag and the filter index (excluded from JSON).

nodes.name: PythonDataSourceReadInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding the pickled Python read function and the pickled partitions of a planned read. The companion object's receive method reads these from the Python worker stream and turns reported exceptions into pythonDataSourceError.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceReadRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner (worker module pyspark.sql.worker.plan_data_source_read) that sends the data source function, input and output schema JSON and configs (arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch, pythonFilterPushDown, isStreaming, pysparkBinaryAsBytes) and receives a PythonDataSourceReadInfo.

nodes.name: PythonDataSourceWriteInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding the pickled write function and the pickled data source writer instance returned by the write runner.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceWriteRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner (worker module pyspark.sql.worker.write_into_data_source) that creates a Python data source writer and gets the Python function used to write data. It sends the data source function, provider, input schema, the write output schema, options, the overwrite and streaming flags and pysparkBinaryAsBytes, and receives the pickled write function and writer.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonDataSourceCommitRunner
nodes.summary: Private PythonPlannerRunner (worker module pyspark.sql.worker.commit_data_source_write) that sends the pickled writer and the commit messages (null for failed tasks) plus an abort flag, so that Python invokes commit or abort. Python exceptions become pythonDataSourceError with action 'commit or abort'; any non-zero code otherwise fails an assertion.

nodes.name: createDataSourceInPython
nodes.summary: Driver-side: runs UserDefinedPythonDataSourceRunner with the data source function, short name, optional schema and case-insensitive options, returning a PythonDataSourceCreationResult.

nodes.name: pushdownFiltersInPython
nodes.summary: Driver-side: builds a filter pushdown runner for the created data source and runs it only if at least one filter is supported; returns None otherwise.

nodes.name: createReadInfoInPython
nodes.summary: Driver-side: runs UserDefinedPythonDataSourceReadRunner to get the partition read function and the partition information.

nodes.name: createWriteInfoInPython
nodes.summary: Driver-side: runs UserDefinedPythonDataSourceWriteRunner to get the pickled write function and writer.

nodes.name: commitWriteInPython
nodes.summary: Driver-side: runs UserDefinedPythonDataSourceCommitRunner to commit or abort a write operation (abort defaults to false).

nodes.name: createMapInBatchEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Executor-side: wraps the pickled function in a non-deterministic PythonUDF with eval type SQL_MAP_ARROW_ITER_UDF and returns a MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory configured from SQLConf (arrow batch size, time zone, large var types, runner conf map), the metrics and the UUIDs.

nodes.name: createPythonMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates one PythonCustomMetric per entry of PythonSQLMetrics.pythonSizeMetricsDesc; other metrics such as row counts are not added since DSv2 already covers them.

nodes.name: createPythonTaskMetrics
nodes.summary: Converts a map of task metric values into an array of PythonCustomTaskMetric.

nodes.name: createPythonFunction
nodes.summary: Builds a SimplePythonFunction from pickled bytes, reusing the env vars, includes, executable, version, broadcast vars and accumulator of the data source class.

nodes.name: lookupAllDataSourcesInPython
nodes.summary: Companion object method: runs the lookup runner with an empty Python function to find all Python data sources.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Companion object method: reads the pickled read function (or an exception) and the pickled partitions from the stream, with errors reported through pythonDataSourceError for 'initialize reader' and 'generate read partitions'.

nodes.name: getField
nodes.summary: Parses an attribute name as a multipart identifier and finds the nested field in the schema; if not found it throws pythonDataSourceError with action 'plan'.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends nothing to Python (no input needed).

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads the number of sources or an exception marker, then each short name and pickled data source, and returns a PythonLookupAllDataSourcesResult.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends the Python data source function, provider name, a flag and JSON of the optional user-specified schema, and the options as key-value strings.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads the pickled data source instance and the schema (DDL string or JSON), throws if it is not a StructType, and returns a PythonDataSourceCreationResult.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends the data source function, the schema JSON, the serialized filters as a JSON string, arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch and pysparkBinaryAsBytes.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads the read info and the list of pushed filter indices and maps them back to the original filter positions, returning a PythonFilterPushdownResult.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends the data source function, input schema JSON, output schema JSON, arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch, pythonFilterPushDown, the streaming flag and pysparkBinaryAsBytes.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Delegates to PythonDataSourceReadInfo.receive.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends the data source function, provider, input schema JSON, write output schema JSON, options, the overwrite flag, the streaming flag and pysparkBinaryAsBytes.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads the pickled write function (or exception) and the pickled writer, returning a PythonDataSourceWriteInfo.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Sends the pickled writer, the commit messages (a NULL marker for null messages) and the abort flag.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads a status code, throws pythonDataSourceError on a Python exception, and asserts the code is 0.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues, a PartitionReader wrapper that appends partition values to every InternalRow produced by an inner file reader. Used by the v2 file data source readers so that file rows and partition columns come out as one unsafe row.

nodes.name: PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues
nodes.summary: Wraps a PartitionReader[InternalRow] (fileReader) and joins each row with the constant partitionValues row using a JoinedRow, then converts the result with a generated unsafe projection over readDataSchema plus partitionSchema. When partitionSchema is empty it still applies the projection, because the projection also converts safe rows into UnsafeRow. next() and close() delegate to the inner reader, get() returns the converted row.

nodes.name: PartitionRecordReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PartitionRecordReader, a thin adapter exposing a Hadoop RecordReader as a v2 PartitionReader. Used when a record-based reader needs to be consumed through the DataSource V2 read API.

nodes.name: PartitionRecordReader
nodes.summary: Generic PartitionReader[T] that delegates to a Hadoop RecordReader: next() calls nextKeyValue(), get() returns getCurrentValue, and close() closes the underlying reader.

nodes.name: PushedDownOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PushedDownOperators case class, a record of the operators that were pushed down into a v2 scan. Used by v2 scan nodes to describe what the data source evaluates itself.

nodes.name: PushedDownOperators
nodes.summary: Case class holding the optional pushed aggregation, table sample (TableSampleInfo), limit and offset, the pushed sort values and predicates, the pushed-down operators of joined relations, and a relationName for leaf relations (empty for joins). Its body asserts that sort values may only be present together with a limit.

nodes.name: RealTimeStreamScanExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical scan node for Real-time Mode streaming reads plus the helpers it needs: a replaceable clock (LowLatencyClock), a reader wrapper that stops at a deadline (LowLatencyReaderWrap) and its factory wrapper (LowLatencyReaderFactoryWrap). Used when a micro-batch stream that supports real-time mode is read with a fixed batch duration.

nodes.name: LowLatencyClock
nodes.summary: Singleton object that wraps a Clock (a SystemClock by default) and exposes getClock, getTimeMillis, waitTillTime and setClock; the comment says it controls time in testing.

nodes.name: LowLatencyReaderWrap
nodes.summary: Case class that adapts a SupportsRealTimeRead reader to a normal PartitionReader. next() reads with a timeout until lowLatencyEndTime is reached; when no record is returned it adds the partition id and the reader offset to the endOffsets accumulator as a PartitionOffsetWithIndex. get() and close() delegate to the reader.

nodes.name: LowLatencyReaderFactoryWrap
nodes.summary: Case class PartitionReaderFactory that wraps another factory. createReader asserts the created reader is a SupportsRealTimeRead, logs the stop time and returns a LowLatencyReaderWrap with the end time and the endOffsets accumulator.

nodes.name: RealTimeStreamScanExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node (DataSourceV2ScanExecBase) for scanning a data source in Real-time Mode. It asserts the MicroBatchStream is a SupportsRealTimeMode, plans input partitions from the start offset, and builds a DataSourceRDD whose reader factory is a LowLatencyReaderFactoryWrap that ends at now plus batchDurationMs. It owns a collection accumulator for end offsets, has no key-grouped partitioning or ordering, and compares by stream and batchDurationMs.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns whether a record is available: if the current time is past lowLatencyEndTime it reports no record, otherwise it calls reader.nextWithTimeout with the remaining time. When no record is returned it records the end offset for the current task partition id.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Creates the inner reader from the wrapped factory, asserts it supports real-time reads, logs the stop time and wraps it in a LowLatencyReaderWrap.

nodes.name: inputPartitions
nodes.summary: Lazily asks the SupportsRealTimeMode stream to plan input partitions from the start offset and converts the array to an immutable Seq.

nodes.name: inputRDD
nodes.summary: Lazily builds the DataSourceRDD over the scan partitions with a LowLatencyReaderFactoryWrap whose end time is LowLatencyClock time plus batchDurationMs, then posts the scan's driver metrics.

nodes.name: RefreshTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RefreshTableExec, the physical command node that refreshes a v2 table. Used for REFRESH TABLE on tables resolved through a TableCatalog.

nodes.name: RefreshTableExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command that calls catalog.invalidateTable(ident) and then runs the refreshCache callback so that all caches referencing the table are refreshed. Returns no rows and has an empty output.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Invalidates the table in the TableCatalog, calls refreshCache() and returns an empty result.

nodes.name: RenamePartitionExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RenamePartitionExec, the physical command node for renaming a table partition. Used for ALTER TABLE ... RENAME PARTITION on v2 tables that support partition management.

nodes.name: RenamePartitionExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command that calls table.renamePartition(from.ident, to.ident) on a SupportsPartitionManagement table and runs the refreshCache callback only when the rename returned true. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Renames the partition from the old to the new identifier and refreshes caches if the rename succeeded.

nodes.name: RenameTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RenameTableExec, the physical command node that renames a v2 table while preserving its cache state. Used for ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO on tables resolved through a TableCatalog.

nodes.name: RenameTableExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command that renames a table. It first invalidates the cache entry and remembers its storage level, invalidates the old table in the catalog, qualifies the new identifier with the old namespace when it has none (matching the v1 behavior), calls catalog.renameTable, and if the table had been cached it loads the renamed table, builds a DataSourceV2Relation and re-caches it with the old storage level through the cacheTable callback.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Invalidates the cached data, renames the table in the TableCatalog, and re-caches the renamed table with the previous storage level if it was cached.

nodes.name: ReplaceTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the two physical command nodes for REPLACE TABLE and CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE on v2 catalogs: ReplaceTableExec (drop then create) and AtomicReplaceTableExec (staged replace with commit or abort).

nodes.name: ReplaceTableExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command for non-atomic table replacement. If the table exists it invalidates the cache and drops it; if it is missing and orCreate is false it throws cannotReplaceMissingTableError. It then builds a TableInfo from the columns, partitioning, converted table properties and constraints and calls catalog.createTable.

nodes.name: AtomicReplaceTableExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command for replacing a table through a StagingTableCatalog. It invalidates the cache if the table exists, stages either createOrReplace (when orCreate) or replace (translating NoSuchTableException into cannotReplaceMissingTableError), then commits the staged changes or aborts them on failure. It exposes commit metrics from DataSourceV2Utils.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Drops the existing table (or fails when it is missing and orCreate is false) and creates the new table with a TableInfo built from the command's columns, partitions, properties and constraints.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Stages a create-or-replace or replace on the StagingTableCatalog, maps a missing table to a compilation error, and commits or aborts the staged table.

nodes.name: commitOrAbortStagedChanges
nodes.summary: Commits the staged table via DataSourceV2Utils.commitStagedChanges inside Utils.tryWithSafeFinallyAndFailureCallbacks and calls abortStagedChanges in the failure callback.

nodes.name: SetCatalogAndNamespaceExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SetCatalogAndNamespaceExec, the physical command node that changes the current catalog and/or namespace. Used for commands that switch the current catalog or namespace.

nodes.name: SetCatalogAndNamespaceExec
nodes.summary: Leaf v2 command that, given an optional catalog name and optional namespace, first sets the current catalog on the CatalogManager (which resets the current namespace) and then sets the current namespace. Returns no rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Applies setCurrentCatalog first and setCurrentNamespace second, because setting the catalog resets the namespace.

nodes.name: ShowColumnsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowColumnsExec, the physical command node for SHOW COLUMNS on a resolved v2 table.

nodes.name: ShowColumnsExec
nodes.summary: V2 command and leaf exec node that returns one row per column name of resolvedTable.table.columns(), converted with toCatalystRow.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowCreateTableExec, the physical command node that builds the CREATE TABLE statement text for a resolved v2 table. Used for SHOW CREATE TABLE on v2 catalogs.

nodes.name: ShowCreateTableExec
nodes.summary: V2 command and leaf exec node that returns a single row containing the generated DDL. It writes the table name, the column list with constraints (using raw char/varchar types and explicit UTF8_BINARY collations), USING, OPTIONS, PARTITIONED BY or v1-compatible CLUSTERED BY / SORTED BY / INTO BUCKETS, COMMENT, DEFAULT COLLATION, LOCATION (skipped for managed locations) and TBLPROPERTIES (skipping reserved properties and redacting values).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates a StringBuilder, calls showCreateTable and returns the DDL as a single UTF8String row.

nodes.name: showCreateTable
nodes.summary: Assembles the full CREATE TABLE text: name, data columns, USING, options extracted from properties with the option prefix, partitioning, comment, collation, location and remaining properties.

nodes.name: showTableDataColumns
nodes.summary: Writes the column definitions (as DDL, with raw char/varchar types and explicit collations) followed by table constraints, one per line.

nodes.name: showTableOptions
nodes.summary: Writes an OPTIONS clause with redacted, sorted, quoted key-value pairs when any table options exist.

nodes.name: showTablePartitioning
nodes.summary: Writes PARTITIONED BY for ordinary transforms; for a V1Table it turns a BucketTransform into a BucketSpec and writes CLUSTERED BY, SORTED BY and INTO n BUCKETS for v1 compatibility.

nodes.name: showTableLocation
nodes.summary: Writes a LOCATION clause from the location property unless the table has a managed location.

nodes.name: showTableProperties
nodes.summary: Writes a TBLPROPERTIES clause with the sorted, redacted properties that are not reserved, not options and not already shown as options.

nodes.name: ShowFunctionsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowFunctionsExec, the physical command node for SHOW FUNCTIONS on a v2 FunctionCatalog.

nodes.name: ShowFunctionsExec
nodes.summary: V2 command and leaf exec node that lists function names. With systemScope it lists built-in functions from FunctionRegistry and TableFunctionRegistry plus built-in operators; with userScope it lists temporary functions of the session catalog and the functions of the given namespace in the FunctionCatalog, quoted with catalog and namespace. Names are filtered by the optional pattern, de-duplicated, sorted and returned as rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Collects system and user function names according to the scope flags, applies the pattern, then returns the distinct sorted names as rows.

nodes.name: ShowPartitionsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShowPartitionsExec, the physical command node for SHOW PARTITIONS on a v2 table that supports partition management.

nodes.name: ShowPartitionsExec
nodes.summary: V2 command and leaf exec node that lists partitions. It calls table.listPartitionIdentifiers with the optional partition spec (all partitions when none is given), casts each partition value to a string with the session time zone ('null' for nulls), escapes names and values, joins them as col=value/col=value, sorts the strings and returns them as rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Lists the partition identifiers, formats each as an escaped col=value path string using Cast and Literal, sorts them and returns UTF8String rows.

nodes.name: ParquetTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetTable, the v2 FileTable for the Parquet format. Used by the Parquet v2 data source to create scan builders, infer schemas, build writes and decide which data types it supports.

nodes.name: ParquetTable
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileTable for Parquet. newScanBuilder returns a ParquetScanBuilder, inferSchema delegates to ParquetUtils.inferSchema, newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that builds a ParquetWrite, formatName is "Parquet", and supportsDataType accepts atomic types, geometry and geography types with supported SRIDs, and arrays, maps, structs and UDTs whose parts are supported.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder whose build() creates a ParquetWrite from the paths, format name, supportsDataType and the merged write info.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively decides whether Parquet can store a data type: geospatial types only with supported SRIDs, atomic types, structs, arrays, maps and user-defined types by their parts, and nothing else.

nodes.name: ParquetWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ParquetWrite, the v2 file write for the Parquet format. Created by ParquetTable.newWriteBuilder to prepare the Parquet output writer factory.

nodes.name: ParquetWrite
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileWrite (with Logging) that holds paths, format name, a supportsDataType predicate and the LogicalWriteInfo. prepareWrite builds ParquetOptions from the options and SQLConf and returns the OutputWriterFactory from ParquetUtils.prepareWrite.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Creates ParquetOptions and delegates to ParquetUtils.prepareWrite to configure the job and return the OutputWriterFactory.

nodes.name: PythonDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonDataSourceV2, the TableProvider that wraps a Python data source. It lazily creates the Python-side data source and read info and hands out a PythonTable.

nodes.name: PythonDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: TableProvider for a Python data source identified by a short name set once through setShortName. It looks up the UserDefinedPythonDataSource in the session's dataSourceManager, caches the creation result (getOrCreateDataSourceInPython) and the read info (getOrCreateReadInfo, also settable with setReadInfo), infers the schema from the creation result, returns a PythonTable from getTable and reports supportsExternalMetadata as true.

nodes.name: setShortName
nodes.summary: Sets the data source short name once; asserts it was not set before.

nodes.name: getOrCreateDataSourceInPython
nodes.summary: Creates the Python data source once via source.createDataSourceInPython and caches the PythonDataSourceCreationResult.

nodes.name: getOrCreateReadInfo
nodes.summary: Creates the Python read info once, using the cached data source creation result, the output schema and the streaming flag, and caches it.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Returns a new PythonTable built from this provider, the short name and the given schema.

nodes.name: PythonScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonScan and PythonBatch, the v2 Scan and Batch for reading from a Python data source. PythonScan chooses between batch reading and the micro-batch stream variants.

nodes.name: PythonScan
nodes.summary: Scan with SupportsMetadata for a Python data source. toBatch returns a PythonBatch. toMicroBatchStream creates a streaming source runner, calls init and checkSupportedFeatures, and returns a PythonMicroBatchStreamWithTriggerAvailableNow, a PythonMicroBatchStreamWithAdmissionControl or a plain PythonMicroBatchStream depending on the supported features. It reports the output schema, the custom metrics from the data source, no columnar support, and PushedFilters and ReadSchema as metadata.

nodes.name: PythonBatch
nodes.summary: Batch for a Python data source. It reads the current job artifact UUID and, when Python worker logging is enabled, the session UUID. It lazily gets the Python read info (non-streaming), turns its partitions into PythonInputPartition objects, and creates a PythonPartitionReaderFactory with the read function.

nodes.name: toMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: Creates and initializes the Python streaming source runner, queries its supported features and returns the micro-batch stream variant for trigger-available-now, admission control, or the default.

nodes.name: getMetaData
nodes.summary: Returns a map with PushedFilters (the supported filters) and ReadSchema (the output schema's simple string).

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Maps each partition from the Python read info to a PythonInputPartition with its index.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Creates a PythonPartitionReaderFactory from the data source, the Python read function, the output schema and the job artifact and session UUIDs.

nodes.name: PythonScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonScanBuilder, the ScanBuilder for a Python data source with optional filter push-down. Used by the v2 planner to build a PythonScan.

nodes.name: PythonScanBuilder
nodes.summary: ScanBuilder with SupportsPushDownFilters. pushFilters returns all filters unchanged when SQLConf pythonFilterPushDown is off; otherwise it asks the Python data source which filters it can push, stores the read info it returns, remembers the supported filters and returns the unsupported ones. build() creates a PythonScan with the supported filters, and pushedFilters returns them.

nodes.name: pushFilters
nodes.summary: Calls pushdownFiltersInPython on the data source when pythonFilterPushDown is enabled, stores the returned read info, splits the filters into supported and unsupported using isFilterPushed and returns the unsupported ones.

nodes.name: PythonBatchWriterFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the commit message and the per-task writer factory used when a Python data source writes in batch mode. The factory builds a DataWriter that runs the pickled write function in a Python worker and keeps the single binary commit message it returns.

nodes.name: PythonWriterCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Case class that carries the pickled commit message (Array[Byte]) produced by the Python writer for one write task. It extends WriterCommitMessage so it can be sent back to the driver when the task commits.

nodes.name: PythonBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Case class implementing DataWriterFactory for Python data source writes. Its createWriter returns an anonymous DataWriter whose writeAll builds a map-in-batch evaluator for the "write_to_data_source" Python function through UserDefinedPythonDataSource and expects exactly one output row holding the commit message (it raises an error for zero or more than one). The same anonymous writer's write method raises an internal error, commit returns the stored message, abort and close do nothing, and currentMetricsValues reports Python task metrics.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the DataWriter for one partition and task. The returned anonymous writer does all of its work in writeAll, which runs the pickled write function on the whole record iterator in Python and stores the single PythonWriterCommitMessage it yields.

nodes.name: PythonPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the input partition type and the reader factory used when a Python data source is read in batch mode. The factory builds a PartitionReader that runs the pickled read function in a Python worker for one partition and iterates over the rows it returns.

nodes.name: PythonInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class holding a partition index and the pickled partition value (Array[Byte]) produced on the Python side. It implements InputPartition and is cast back from InputPartition by the reader factory.

nodes.name: PythonPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionReaderFactory for Python data sources, built from a UserDefinedPythonDataSource, a pickled read function, the output schema and optional job artifact and session UUIDs. Its createReader returns an anonymous PartitionReader that runs the "read_from_data_source" Python function through a map-in-batch evaluator on the single PythonInputPartition row, then serves next and get from the resulting iterator and reports Python task metrics in currentMetricsValues.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Creates the PartitionReader for one InputPartition. The anonymous reader evaluates the pickled read function in Python for that partition when it is constructed and exposes the output rows through next, get and close.

nodes.name: PythonTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DataSource V2 Table exposed for a Python data source. It reports the schema and the supported capabilities and hands out the scan builder and write builder used for reads and writes.

nodes.name: PythonTable
nodes.summary: Table implementation (with SupportsRead and SupportsWrite) created from a PythonDataSourceV2, a short name and an output schema. name returns the short name and schema returns the output schema. capabilities returns BATCH_READ, BATCH_WRITE, MICRO_BATCH_READ, STREAMING_WRITE and TRUNCATE. newScanBuilder returns a PythonScanBuilder and newWriteBuilder returns a PythonWriteBuilder.

nodes.name: PythonWriteBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WriteBuilder for a Python data source table. It remembers whether truncate was requested and builds a PythonWrite from that flag.

nodes.name: PythonWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: WriteBuilder with SupportsTruncate created from a PythonDataSourceV2, a short name and a LogicalWriteInfo. truncate sets an internal flag and returns the builder itself, and build creates a PythonWrite with the data source, short name, write info and the truncate flag.

nodes.name: StatePartitionReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the partition readers behind the State data source: a factory that picks the reader for a state store partition, a shared base reader that opens the state store provider, and three readers (normal state read, read of all column families as raw bytes, and change data feed). Used when a query reads state store contents of a stateful streaming operator as rows.

nodes.name: AllColumnFamiliesReaderInfo
nodes.summary: Case class carrying extra information for the all-column-families reader: the set of StateStoreColFamilySchema for every column family of the operator, the list of TransformWithStateVariableInfo (used to check variable types), the operator name and an optional state format version.

nodes.name: StatePartitionReaderUtils
nodes.summary: Private helper object. It holds v4JoinCFNames (the state store names returned by SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.allStateStoreNamesV4 for the left and right sides) and isMultiValuedCF, which decides whether a column family stores multiple values per key.

nodes.name: StatePartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionReaderFactory for the State data source. createReader casts the partition to StateStoreInputPartition and returns an all-column-families reader when the internalOnlyReadAllColumnFamilies source option is set, a change data reader when readChangeFeed is set, and the normal StatePartitionReader otherwise. It takes the store conf, Hadoop conf, schema, encoder spec and optional variable, column family, schema provider and join column family inputs.

nodes.name: StatePartitionReaderBase
nodes.summary: Abstract PartitionReader[InternalRow] (also Logging) shared by all state readers. It computes the key and value schema, resolves start and end store checkpoint ids, lazily creates and initializes a StateStoreProvider (registering the column family when column families are used), and implements next, get and close over an abstract iter iterator.

nodes.name: StatePartitionReader
nodes.summary: Reader for the normal mode of the State data source: it reads the state at one batch id. Its lazy store is a read store from the provider, or a read store replayed from a snapshot when fromSnapshotOptions is set. iter yields rows for state variables, multi-valued join column families or ordinary column families; close releases the store and then closes the provider.

nodes.name: StatePartitionAllColumnFamiliesReader
nodes.summary: Reader that returns the raw key and value bytes of every column family of an operator, together with the column family name and partition key, because each column family can have a different schema. It builds a partition key extractor per column family, checks that all column families found in the store are declared in the schema, registers them in one store, and concatenates their iterators; default column family of transformWithState operators is skipped.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangeDataPartitionReader
nodes.summary: Reader for the readChangeFeed mode of the State data source: it reads state changes across a range of batches for one partition. It requires a provider that supports fine-grained replay, obtains a change data reader for the configured start and end batch ids, and turns each change record into a 5-column row (6 columns for map state, which splits the key into grouping key and user key).

nodes.name: isMultiValuedCF
nodes.summary: Returns true when the state variable is a ListState or when the column family name is one of the v4 join column family names, meaning the column family stores several values per key.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Builds the reader for an input partition: all-column-families reader when internalOnlyReadAllColumnFamilies is true (requires allColumnFamiliesReaderInfo), change data reader when readChangeFeed is true, otherwise the normal StatePartitionReader.

nodes.name: getStoreUniqueId
nodes.summary: Resolves the optional state store checkpoint id for this partition by calling SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.getStateStoreCheckpointId with the store name, partition id and the given operator state unique ids. The helpers getStartStoreUniqueId and getEndStoreUniqueId pass the start or end ids from the source options.

nodes.name: provider
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that creates the StateStoreProvider: it builds the StateStoreId and provider id, decides whether column families and multiple values per key are needed, and calls StateStoreProvider.createAndInit. When column families are used it gets a store at batchId + 1, creates the requested column family if absent (marked internal for registered timers or testing internal families) and aborts that store.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances the abstract iterator: stores the next row as the current row and returns true, or clears the current row and returns false when the iterator is exhausted.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Clears the current row and closes the state store provider.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that opens the ReadStateStore. Without snapshot options it asserts start and end store ids are equal and calls provider.getReadStore at batchId + 1; with snapshot options it requires SupportsFineGrainedReplay (otherwise throws StateStoreErrors.stateStoreProviderDoesNotSupportFineGrainedReplay) and calls replayReadStateFromSnapshot.

nodes.name: iter
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that builds the row iterator. It picks the column family name, then uses SchemaUtil.processStateEntries for state variables, iteratorWithMultiValues for v4 join column families, or the plain iterator, converting key and value pairs with SchemaUtil.unifyStateRowPair.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Releases the read store and then calls the base close to close the provider.

nodes.name: cfPartitionKeyExtractors
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that maps each column family name to a StatePartitionKeyExtractor created by StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory.create, using that family's key schema and the matching TransformWithStateVariableInfo. The default column family of transformWithState operators is filtered out.

nodes.name: isMultiValuedCF
nodes.summary: Private method that checks whether one column family stores multiple values per key by delegating to StatePartitionReaderUtils.isMultiValuedCF with the matching state variable info.

nodes.name: provider
nodes.summary: Overrides the base provider with a lazy val that creates and initializes a StateStoreProvider using the all-column-families settings (useMultipleValuesPerKey is false at provider level).

nodes.name: checkAllColFamiliesExist
nodes.summary: Validates that every column family present in the state store (ignoring the default one) is declared in the schema, using require; schema families with no data yet are accepted.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that gets one writable store at batchId + 1, checks the declared column families and registers each non-default one with createColFamilyIfAbsent. A single store is used for registration and iteration because abort would invalidate the loaded version.

nodes.name: iter
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that iterates every non-skipped column family and concatenates the rows, converting each key and value pair with SchemaUtil.unifyStateRowPairAsRawBytes and the column family's partition key extractor; multi-valued families use iteratorWithMultiValues.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Aborts the store and then closes the base reader.

nodes.name: changeDataReader
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that returns a NextIterator of (record type, key row, value row, batch id). It requires a SupportsFineGrainedReplay provider, derives the optional column family name from the state variable or join column family, and calls getStateStoreChangeDataReader for changeStartBatchId + 1 to changeEndBatchId + 1.

nodes.name: iter
nodes.summary: Lazy val (not a def) that maps change records to rows: map state records are flattened into grouping key and user key rows via createFlattenedRowForMapState, other records via unifyStateChangeDataRow.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the change data reader if needed and then closes the base reader.

nodes.name: unifyStateChangeDataRow
nodes.summary: Builds a 5-field GenericInternalRow from a change record: batch id, record type as string, key, value and partition id.

nodes.name: createFlattenedRowForMapState
nodes.summary: Builds a 6-field GenericInternalRow for map state changes: batch id, record type string, grouping key, user key, user value and partition id.

nodes.name: StreamStreamJoinStateHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Helper for reading the state schema of stream-stream join operators from a checkpoint, across join state format versions 1 to 4. Used to find the key and value schemas of one join side and to detect whether a checkpoint uses virtual column families.

nodes.name: StreamStreamJoinStateHelper
nodes.summary: Object with three public methods. readSchema returns a struct with key and value fields for one join side; usesVirtualColumnFamilies returns true when no schema file exists for the left keyToNumValues store (state format version 3 or higher); readKeyValueSchema reads the key and value schemas per format version and, when excludeAuxColumns is true, drops the trailing boolean 'matched' column from the value schema.

nodes.name: readSchema
nodes.summary: Calls readKeyValueSchema and wraps the result as a StructType with a 'key' field and a 'value' field.

nodes.name: usesVirtualColumnFamilies
nodes.summary: Checks whether the checkpoint uses virtual column families: builds the StateStoreId of the left side's first store name, locates its schema file and returns true when that file does not exist.

nodes.name: readKeyValueSchema
nodes.summary: Reads the key and value schemas for one join side with a StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker. Versions 1 and 2 (or no version) read the keyToNumValues store for the key and keyWithIndexToValue store for the value; version 3 reads one default store and finds the two column families by name; version 4 takes both schemas from the primary column family; other versions throw IllegalArgumentException. Then it optionally removes the trailing 'matched' BooleanType column.

nodes.name: ShowTablePropertiesExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for SHOW TBLPROPERTIES on a DSv2 table. Used to return the non-reserved properties of a table, or a single property value.

nodes.name: ShowTablePropertiesExec
nodes.summary: Leaf command exec holding the output attributes, the catalog Table, the table name and an optional property key. Its run method redacts the table properties through conf.redactOptions, removes the reserved properties (CatalogV2Util.TABLE_RESERVED_PROPERTIES, which are shown by DESCRIBE), then returns the requested key (a message 'Table <name> does not have property: <key>' if missing, as one or two columns depending on the output length) or all properties sorted by key.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the result rows: filters out reserved properties after redaction, then returns either the single requested property (value only, or key and value) or every remaining property sorted by key.

nodes.name: ShowTablesExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for SHOW TABLES on a DSv2 catalog. For catalogs that also expose views it includes views in the listing.

nodes.name: ShowTablesExec
nodes.summary: Command exec with output attributes, a TableCatalog, a namespace and an optional name pattern. run lists identifiers with RelationCatalog.listRelationSummaries when the catalog is a RelationCatalog (so views appear as in v1 SHOW TABLES) and with TableCatalog.listTables otherwise, filters names with StringUtils.filterPattern, and emits rows of quoted namespace, table name and an isTemporary flag (true only for temp views when the catalog is the session catalog).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Collects identifiers from the catalog (relation summaries or tables), applies the optional pattern filter and returns one row per match with namespace, name and the temp view flag.

nodes.name: isTempView
nodes.summary: Private helper: when the catalog is the session catalog it asks the session catalog whether the identifier is a temp view, otherwise returns false.

nodes.name: ShowTablesExtendedExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical plan nodes for SHOW TABLE EXTENDED on a DSv2 catalog: one for tables matching a pattern (plus temp views) and one for a single partition of a table. Each builds a text description of the table or partition as a result row.

nodes.name: ShowTablesExtendedExec
nodes.summary: Command exec for showing table information without a partition. run lists tables from the catalog (listTables, matched with a pattern), loads each table and emits a row with namespace, name, isTemporary=false and a detail string; it then adds matching global and local temp views with isTemporary=true and the view's simpleString. getTableDetails builds the detail text.

nodes.name: ShowTablePartitionExec
nodes.summary: Command exec for showing the information of one partition. run builds one row (namespace, table name, isTemporary=false, details) from getTablePartitionDetails, which lists the partition identifiers for the resolved partition spec, throws notExistPartitionError when none match, formats the partition values and adds the partition metadata as 'Partition Parameters'.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Collects rows for tables whose names match the pattern (loading each table and attaching its detail text) and for temp views from the session catalog's listTempViews, scoped to the namespace's single database when one is given.

nodes.name: getTableDetails
nodes.summary: Builds the multi-line detail string in an ordered map: Catalog, Namespace, Table, Type (EXTERNAL or MANAGED), reserved properties other than external, redacted Table Properties, Partition Provider and Partition Columns when the table supports partitions, and the Schema tree string.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Produces a single row holding the namespace, table name, a false temp flag and the partition detail text.

nodes.name: getTablePartitionDetails
nodes.summary: Builds the detail text for one partition: it looks up the partition identifier, raises an error if the partition does not exist, formats each partition value (via ToPrettyString and escapePathName) into 'Partition Values', and appends 'Partition Parameters' from loadPartitionMetadata when present.

nodes.name: ShowViewsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for SHOW VIEWS on a DSv2 ViewCatalog. Lists the views of a namespace, optionally filtered by a name pattern.

nodes.name: ShowViewsExec
nodes.summary: Command exec with output attributes, a ViewCatalog, a namespace and an optional pattern. run enumerates view identifiers with ViewCatalog.listViews, keeps names that match the pattern (StringUtils.filterPattern) and emits rows of quoted namespace, view name and isTemporary=false, because v2 catalogs have no temp views.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Iterates the identifiers returned by listViews, applies the optional name pattern and returns one row per matching view.

nodes.name: SupportsCustomDriverMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a mixin trait for Spark plan nodes that show driver-side custom metrics reported by a connector in the SQL UI.

nodes.name: SupportsCustomDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Trait with a SparkPlan self-type. Implementations declare connector metrics through the abstract customMetrics map and optional Spark-owned sparkMetrics (default empty; these names win on collision). The metrics lazy val is customMetrics ++ sparkMetrics. createCustomMetrics turns an array of CustomMetric into SQLMetrics, and postDriverMetrics applies the CustomTaskMetric values and posts the updates for the current SQL execution id.

nodes.name: createCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Converts an array of connector CustomMetric into a name-to-SQLMetric map using SQLMetrics.createV2CustomMetric.

nodes.name: postDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Sets reported task metric values on the declared metrics (ignoring undeclared names and names that collide with sparkMetrics) and posts them with SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricUpdates under the execution id from the SparkContext local properties.

nodes.name: TableCapabilityCheck.scala
nodes.summary: Analysis check that validates the capabilities of Data Source V2 tables in a logical plan and fails problematic batch or streaming reads and writes early.

nodes.name: TableCapabilityCheck
nodes.summary: Object that is a LogicalPlan => Unit function. apply walks the plan and throws QueryCompilationErrors when a DataSourceV2Relation lacks BATCH_READ, a StreamingRelationV2 lacks MICRO_BATCH_READ and CONTINUOUS_READ, AppendData or InsertOnlyMerge targets a table without BATCH_WRITE or V1_BATCH_WRITE, OverwritePartitionsDynamic needs OVERWRITE_DYNAMIC, or OverwriteByExpression needs TRUNCATE or OVERWRITE_BY_FILTER. It also requires that all streaming sources in one query share micro-batch or continuous execution.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Checks every plan node with the capability rules above, then collects StreamingRelationV2 tables and v1 StreamingRelation nodes; when more than one streaming source exists and they do not all support micro-batch or all support continuous (v1 sources only support micro-batch), it throws streamingSourcesDoNotSupportCommonExecutionModeError.

nodes.name: TableSampleInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a small case class that describes a table sample request (bounds, replacement flag, seed and method).

nodes.name: TableSampleInfo
nodes.summary: Case class with lowerBound, upperBound, withReplacement, seed and sampleMethod (default SampleMethod.Bernoulli). It only carries the parameters of a sample over a table; it has no methods.

nodes.name: TextBasedFileScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract TextBasedFileScan base class for DSv2 file scans over text-based formats. It decides whether a file can be split by checking the compression codec of the path.

nodes.name: TextBasedFileScan
nodes.summary: Abstract class that extends FileScan for text-based file formats. It holds a transient lazy CompressionCodecFactory built from the session's Hadoop configuration plus the scan options. isSplitable asks Utils.isFileSplittable whether the path can be split given its codec, and getFileUnSplittableReason returns a fixed message saying the file is compressed by an unsplittable compression codec. Used as the parent of concrete text file scans.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: Overrides FileScan.isSplitable by delegating to Utils.isFileSplittable with the path and the lazily created compression codec factory.

nodes.name: getFileUnSplittableReason
nodes.summary: Asserts that the path is not splittable and returns the message 'the file is compressed by unsplittable compression codec'.

nodes.name: TruncatePartitionExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TruncatePartitionExec physical plan node that truncates one or more partitions of a partition-managed DSv2 table.

nodes.name: TruncatePartitionExec
nodes.summary: Case class leaf command node for partition truncation, built from a SupportsPartitionManagement table, a ResolvedPartitionSpec and a refreshCache callback. When the spec names fewer columns than the table's partition schema, the table must be a SupportsAtomicPartitionManagement: it lists the matching partition identifiers and truncates them together, otherwise QueryExecutionErrors.truncateMultiPartitionUnsupportedError is thrown. When all partition columns are given it truncates a single partition. If the table was altered, refreshCache is called. It returns no rows and has an empty output.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns an empty attribute list because the command produces no output columns.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Truncates the requested partition(s). Chooses between truncatePartition for a fully specified partition and listPartitionIdentifiers plus truncatePartitions for a partial spec on an atomic table, throws a QueryExecutionErrors error for a partial spec on a non-atomic table, calls refreshCache when the table changed, and returns an empty row sequence.

nodes.name: TruncateTableExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TruncateTableExec physical plan node that truncates a whole DSv2 table and reports connector driver metrics.

nodes.name: TruncateTableExec
nodes.summary: Case class leaf command node for TRUNCATE TABLE on a TruncatableTable, with a refreshCache callback. It mixes in SupportsCustomDriverMetrics: the lazy customMetrics value is created from table.supportedCustomMetrics(). run calls table.truncateTable() and refreshes the cache if it returned true, and in a finally block posts the driver metrics the table reports. It returns no rows and has an empty output.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns an empty attribute list because the command produces no output columns.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Calls table.truncateTable(), calls refreshCache when it returns true, returns an empty row sequence, and always posts table.reportDriverMetrics() through postDriverMetrics in a finally block.

nodes.name: V1FallbackWriters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines physical plan nodes for appending to or overwriting a DSv2 table through the V1 write interface (InsertableRelation), together with the sealed V1FallbackWriters trait and the SupportsV1Write helper trait that performs the insert.

nodes.name: AppendDataExecV1
nodes.summary: Case class physical node for appending to a v2 table with the V1 write interfaces. It takes a SupportsWrite table, a logical plan, a refreshCache callback and a V1Write, and is a V1FallbackWriters.

nodes.name: OverwriteByExpressionExecV1
nodes.summary: Case class physical node for overwriting a v2 table by filters through the V1 write interfaces. Per its comment, atomicity depends only on the target data source, and it implements SaveMode.Overwrite by deleting all rows (filter AlwaysTrue) and then appending the output data set. Same constructor shape as AppendDataExecV1.

nodes.name: V1FallbackWriters
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that is a LeafV2CommandExec with SupportsV1Write and SupportsCustomDriverMetrics.
