It has an empty output, builds customMetrics from write.supportedCustomMetrics(), and its run method calls writeWithV1 with write.toInsertableRelation, refreshes the cache, and in a finally block posts the driver metrics reported by the write. Subtypes supply table, refreshCache and write.

nodes.name: SupportsV1Write
nodes.summary: Trait extending SparkPlan for plan nodes whose table uses V1 writer interfaces to append data. It declares the logical plan and provides writeWithV1, which builds a DataFrame from the plan and calls relation.insert with overwrite = false.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns Nil because the write command produces no output columns.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Writes through the V1 interface: calls writeWithV1(write.toInsertableRelation), then refreshCache(), returns Nil, and in a finally block posts write.reportDriverMetrics().

nodes.name: writeWithV1
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrame from the plan with Dataset.ofRows and inserts it into the given InsertableRelation with overwrite = false.

nodes.name: V2ColumnUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the small V2ColumnUtils helper object that extracts a single top-level column name from a connector expression.

nodes.name: V2ColumnUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with one method, extractV2Column. It is used where a connector expression must be reduced to a plain column name.

nodes.name: extractV2Column
nodes.summary: Pattern matches the connector Expression: a NamedReference with exactly one field name yields Some(that name), anything else (nested references or other expressions) yields None.

nodes.name: V2ScanPartitioningAndOrdering.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the V2ScanPartitioningAndOrdering optimizer rule that copies partitioning and ordering reported by DSv2 scans onto the scan relation as Catalyst objects.

nodes.name: V2ScanPartitioningAndOrdering
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] with Logging. Per its comment it extracts DataSourceV2ScanRelation nodes (through ExtractV2ScanInfo), converts any V2 partitioning and ordering reported by data sources to their Catalyst counterparts, and annotates the plan with the result. The partitioning step handles scans that implement SupportsReportPartitioning: a KeyGroupedPartitioning is converted with V2ExpressionUtils.toCatalystOpt and kept only if all references are in the relation output, UnknownPartitioning gives None, and any other partitioning is ignored with a warning that suggests KeyGroupedPartitioning. The ordering step handles SupportsReportOrdering scans and stores V2ExpressionUtils.toCatalystOrdering of outputOrdering().

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Runs the two scan rules (partitioning, then ordering) in sequence over the plan using foldLeft and returns the final plan.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan top-down; for scans that report partitioning and have no key-grouped partitioning yet, converts the reported partitioning to Catalyst expressions (only valid KeyGroupedPartitioning whose references lie within the output set), logs a warning for unsupported partitioning types, and copies the result into keyGroupedPartitioning.

nodes.name: ordering
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan top-down; for scans that report ordering, converts outputOrdering() to Catalyst sort orders with V2ExpressionUtils.toCatalystOrdering and stores them in the relation's ordering field.

nodes.name: V2TableRefreshUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the V2TableRefreshUtil helper object that reloads the table metadata of DSv2 relations in a logical plan and validates that table identity, column IDs, data columns and metadata columns did not change.

nodes.name: V2TableRefreshUtil
nodes.summary: Package-private object (SQLConfHelper with Logging) with an overloaded refresh method. refresh walks the plan including subqueries, and for each DataSourceV2Relation matched by ExtractV2CatalogAndIdentifier (versioned or all, and without a time travel spec) it loads the current table, either from the session's shared relation cache or from the catalog, memoized per (catalog, identifier). It then validates table identity, data columns and metadata columns against the relation and returns the relation with the refreshed table. Plans containing a Command use SchemaValidationMode.PROHIBIT_CHANGES, other plans use ALLOW_NEW_FIELDS.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Reloads table metadata for all matching DSv2 relations in the plan and validates identity, data columns and metadata columns before replacing the table. The widest overload takes spark, plan, versionedOnly and an explicit schemaValidationMode. A shorter overload (lines 54-58, versionedOnly defaults to false) derives the mode with determineSchemaValidationMode and forwards.

nodes.name: lookupCachedRelation
nodes.summary: Looks up a cached DataSourceV2Relation for the catalog, identifier and table in the session's shared relation cache by delegating to CatalogV2Util.lookupCachedRelation.

nodes.name: determineSchemaValidationMode
nodes.summary: Returns PROHIBIT_CHANGES if the plan contains a Command (for example CTAS, RTAS or MERGE, per the comment) and ALLOW_NEW_FIELDS otherwise.

nodes.name: containsCommand
nodes.summary: Returns true if any node of the plan is an instance of Command.

nodes.name: validateTableIdentity
nodes.summary: Checks that the table ID captured in the relation still matches the current table by calling V2TableUtil.validateTableId.

nodes.name: validateDataColumns
nodes.summary: Calls V2TableUtil.validateCapturedColumns (with checkIds = true) and throws QueryCompilationErrors.columnsChangedAfterAnalysis if there are errors.

nodes.name: validateMetadataColumns
nodes.summary: Calls V2TableUtil.validateCapturedMetadataColumns (with checkIds = true) and throws QueryCompilationErrors.metadataColumnsChangedAfterAnalysis if there are errors.

nodes.name: V2SessionCatalog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines V2SessionCatalog, the built-in DSv2 session catalog that implements TableCatalog, FunctionCatalog and SupportsNamespaces by translating calls to the v1 SessionCatalog, plus its companion object with namespace conversion helpers.

nodes.name: V2SessionCatalog
nodes.summary: TableCatalog, FunctionCatalog, SupportsNamespaces and SQLConfHelper over a v1 SessionCatalog; the companion object (lines 484-514) holds toCatalogDatabase and the CatalogDatabaseHelper implicit class. loadTable reads the catalog table and, unless a custom session catalog implementation is configured (SQLConf.V2_SESSION_CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION other than 'builtin'), tries to resolve a v2 TableProvider for the table provider and builds a v2 table, otherwise returns V1Table; time travel overloads of loadTable always fail. createTable0 builds a CatalogTable (managed or external), checks the provider's schema and partitioning against supportsExternalMetadata, and calls SessionCatalog.createTable. alterTable applies TableChange properties, schema and cluster-by changes, and drop/rename/list/namespace methods map to the matching SessionCatalog calls. Function methods list or load persistent USER functions. Trivial one-line methods are not given their own nodes: name (returns CatalogManager.SESSION_CATALOG_NAME), initialize (no-op), capabilities (SUPPORT_COLUMN_DEFAULT_VALUE), hasCustomSessionCatalog, tableExists, invalidateTable, purgeTable, dropTable, isTempView, loadFunction, functionExists and toString. Overloads: loadTable (three overloads, id shared), createTable (two overloads), listNamespaces (two overloads).

nodes.name: CatalogDatabaseHelper
nodes.summary: Private implicit class in the companion object that adds toMetadata to a CatalogDatabase.

nodes.name: listTables
nodes.summary: Lists tables of a single-part namespace by calling SessionCatalog.listTables and mapping each result to an Identifier; any other namespace shape raises noSuchNamespaceError.

nodes.name: getDataSourceOptions
nodes.summary: Builds a CaseInsensitiveStringMap from the table properties plus a 'path' entry taken from the storage location URI when present.

nodes.name: loadTable
nodes.summary: Loads a table: gets the v1 metadata, and if the table has a provider and no custom session catalog is configured, returns V1Table when the table is in the v1 table cache, otherwise resolves a v2 TableProvider via DataSourceV2Utils.getTableProvider and calls getTable (using stored schema and partitioning when supportsExternalMetadata, else inferred ones) and falls back to V1Table when there is no v2 provider. NoSuchNamespaceException becomes noSuchTableError. The overloads taking a timestamp (lines 133-135) or a version string (lines 137-139) call failTimeTravel.

nodes.name: failTimeTravel
nodes.summary: Computes the table name parts (from the V1Table or from the identifier) and throws QueryCompilationErrors.timeTravelUnsupportedError.

nodes.name: getV2Partitioning
nodes.summary: Combines partition column transforms, a bucket spec transform and a cluster-by spec transform of a CatalogTable into one array of v2 Transforms.

nodes.name: createTable0
nodes.summary: Shared implementation of createTable. Derives provider, storage format and table type (EXTERNAL if the external property is set or a non-managed location is given), decides schema and partitions depending on whether the provider supports external metadata (inferring them when schema is empty, checking that a given schema matches the created table), builds the CatalogTable with properties, cluster-by property, comment and collation, calls SessionCatalog.createTable, maps TableAlreadyExistsException to tableAlreadyExistsError, and returns null to save a loadTable call.

nodes.name: createTable
nodes.summary: StructType-based createTable overload: throws createTableDeprecatedError when Utils.isTesting is true, otherwise calls createTable0. The overload taking Array[Column] (lines 270-276) converts the columns with CatalogV2Util.v2ColumnsToStructType and calls createTable0.

nodes.name: toOptions
nodes.summary: Keeps the properties whose key starts with TableCatalog.OPTION_PREFIX and strips that prefix from the keys.

nodes.name: alterTable
nodes.summary: Applies TableChange values to the stored table: gets the v1 metadata, applies property, schema and cluster-by changes with CatalogV2Util, updates comment, collation, owner and location, then calls SessionCatalog.alterTable for non-column changes and alterTableSchema when column changes exist. Maps NoSuchTableException to noSuchTableError and returns null.

nodes.name: dropTableInternal
nodes.summary: Shared drop and purge logic: loads the table; throws wrongCommandForObjectTypeError for views unless DROP_TABLE_VIEW_ENABLED, returns false when the table is null, otherwise invalidates the cached table and calls SessionCatalog.dropTable with ignoreIfNotExists = true. NoSuchTableException gives false. purgeTable and dropTable call it.

nodes.name: renameTable
nodes.summary: Throws tableAlreadyExistsError if the new identifier exists, then calls SessionCatalog.renameTable.

nodes.name: namespaceExists
nodes.summary: Returns true for a single-part namespace that is an existing database and false for any other shape.

nodes.name: listNamespaces
nodes.summary: Lists namespaces below a given namespace: all databases for an empty namespace, an empty array for an existing database, and an error otherwise. The no-argument overload (lines 379-381) lists all databases.

nodes.name: loadNamespaceMetadata
nodes.summary: Returns the database metadata of a single-part namespace as a map via toMetadata, mapping NoSuchNamespaceException and other namespace shapes to noSuchNamespaceError.

nodes.name: createNamespace
nodes.summary: Creates a database for a single-part namespace from the given metadata, using the default database path as default location; other shapes throw invalidNamespaceNameError.

nodes.name: alterNamespace
nodes.summary: Applies NamespaceChange values to a database: rejects removal of reserved namespace properties, reads current metadata, applies the changes with CatalogV2Util.applyNamespaceChanges and calls SessionCatalog.alterDatabase.

nodes.name: dropNamespace
nodes.summary: Drops an existing single-part database (with the cascade flag) and returns true, returns false when it does not exist, and throws for other namespace shapes.

nodes.name: listFunctions
nodes.summary: Lists persistent USER functions of a database as Identifiers, skipping temporary functions that have no database; other namespace shapes raise noSuchNamespaceError.

nodes.name: toCatalogDatabase
nodes.summary: Companion helper that builds a CatalogDatabase from a namespace name and metadata map: description from the comment property, location from the location property or the default location (else missingDatabaseLocationError), and remaining properties.

nodes.name: toMetadata
nodes.summary: Converts a CatalogDatabase into a Java map holding its properties plus location and comment entries.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceErrors.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the error factory object StateDataSourceErrors, the abstract StateDataSourceException base class and thirteen concrete exception classes, each with a STDS_ error class, used by the State Data Source for streaming state.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceErrors
nodes.summary: Object that groups factory methods for (most) exceptions thrown from the State Data Source; per its comment the State Metadata Data Source may reuse it and the error classes carry the prefix STDS_. Each method returns a StateDataSourceException by constructing the matching exception class: internalError, invalidOptionValue, invalidOptionValueIsNegative, invalidOptionValueIsEmpty, requiredOptionUnspecified, offsetLogUnavailable, offsetMetadataLogUnavailable, failedToReadStateSchema, failedToReadOperatorMetadata, conflictOptions, committedBatchUnavailable, noPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore and mixedCheckpointFormatVersionsNotSupported.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceException
nodes.summary: Abstract base exception for the State Data Source errors; extends SparkRuntimeException and passes through an error class, message parameters and a cause.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceInternalError
nodes.summary: Error for internal failures; constructed with a message (and an optional cause defaulting to null) and carries the parameter 'message'. Error class: STDS_INTERNAL_ERROR. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.internalError.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValue
nodes.summary: Error for an invalid option value with a custom message; parameters are optionName and message. Error class: STDS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE.WITH_MESSAGE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.invalidOptionValue.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValueIsNegative
nodes.summary: Error for an option whose value must not be negative; parameter optionName. Error class: STDS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE.IS_NEGATIVE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.invalidOptionValueIsNegative.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValueIsEmpty
nodes.summary: Error for an option whose value must not be empty; parameter optionName. Error class: STDS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE.IS_EMPTY. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.invalidOptionValueIsEmpty.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceUnspecifiedRequiredOption
nodes.summary: Error for a missing required option; parameter optionName is the missing option name. Error class: STDS_REQUIRED_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.requiredOptionUnspecified.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceOffsetLogUnavailable
nodes.summary: Error raised when the offset log of a batch is unavailable; parameters batchId and checkpointLocation. Error class: STDS_OFFSET_LOG_UNAVAILABLE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.offsetLogUnavailable.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceOffsetMetadataLogUnavailable
nodes.summary: Error raised when the offset metadata log of a batch is unavailable; parameters batchId and checkpointLocation. Error class: STDS_OFFSET_METADATA_LOG_UNAVAILABLE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.offsetMetadataLogUnavailable.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceReadStateSchemaFailure
nodes.summary: Error raised when the state schema cannot be read; takes StateSourceOptions and a cause, parameter sourceOptions is its string form. Error class: STDS_FAILED_TO_READ_STATE_SCHEMA. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.failedToReadStateSchema.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceConflictOptions
nodes.summary: Error for options that conflict with each other; parameter options is the quoted option list in brackets. Error class: STDS_CONFLICT_OPTIONS. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.conflictOptions.

nodes.name: StataDataSourceCommittedBatchUnavailable
nodes.summary: Error raised when no committed batch is available at the checkpoint location (the class name is spelled 'Stata...' in the source); parameter checkpointLocation. Error class: STDS_COMMITTED_BATCH_UNAVAILABLE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.committedBatchUnavailable.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceNoPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore
nodes.summary: Error raised when no partition is found in the state store; takes StateSourceOptions, parameter sourceOptions is its string form. Error class: STDS_NO_PARTITION_DISCOVERED_IN_STATE_STORE. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.noPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceReadOperatorMetadataFailure
nodes.summary: Error raised when operator metadata cannot be read; parameters checkpointLocation and batchId. Error class: STDS_FAILED_TO_READ_OPERATOR_METADATA. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.failedToReadOperatorMetadata.

nodes.name: StateDataSourceMixedCheckpointFormatVersionsNotSupported
nodes.summary: Error raised when the batch range mixes different checkpoint format versions; parameters startBatchId, endBatchId, startFormatVersion and endFormatVersion. Error class: STDS_MIXED_CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSIONS_NOT_SUPPORTED. Created by StateDataSourceErrors.mixedCheckpointFormatVersionsNotSupported.

nodes.name: internalError
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceInternalError as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: invalidOptionValue
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValue as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: invalidOptionValueIsNegative
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValueIsNegative as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: invalidOptionValueIsEmpty
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceInvalidOptionValueIsEmpty as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: requiredOptionUnspecified
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceUnspecifiedRequiredOption as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: offsetLogUnavailable
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceOffsetLogUnavailable as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: offsetMetadataLogUnavailable
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceOffsetMetadataLogUnavailable as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: failedToReadStateSchema
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceReadStateSchemaFailure as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: conflictOptions
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceConflictOptions as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: committedBatchUnavailable
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StataDataSourceCommittedBatchUnavailable as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: noPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceNoPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: failedToReadOperatorMetadata
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceReadOperatorMetadataFailure as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: mixedCheckpointFormatVersionsNotSupported
nodes.summary: Factory method that returns a new StateDataSourceMixedCheckpointFormatVersionsNotSupported as a StateDataSourceException.

nodes.name: StateTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StateTable, the DSv2 Table (with SupportsRead and SupportsMetadataColumns) that exposes streaming state store data, and its companion object holding the table capability.

nodes.name: StateTable
nodes.summary: DSv2 Table implementation for the State Store data source. The constructor takes the session, the schema, StateSourceOptions, StateStoreConf, the batch partition count, the key encoder spec, and optional state variable info, column family schema, state schema provider (used to read state written with older schema versions), join column family, all-column-families reader info and join state format version. It first validates the schema with SchemaUtil.isValidSchema and throws StateDataSourceErrors.internalError if invalid. The name describes checkpoint location, batch id, operator id, store name and optional join side, snapshot and change feed options. It advertises only TableCapability.BATCH_READ (companion object, lines 105-107), creates a StateScanBuilder in newScanBuilder, and has empty properties and no metadata columns.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Builds a descriptive table name string from the state checkpoint location, batch id, operator id and store name, appending join side, snapshot start batch and partition, and change feed start and end batch ids when those options are set.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Returns the CAPABILITY set from the companion object, which contains only TableCapability.BATCH_READ.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Creates a StateScanBuilder, forwarding the session, schema, source options, state conf, partition count, encoder spec and the optional state variable, column family, schema provider, join and reader info values.

nodes.name: properties
nodes.summary: Returns an empty Java map of table properties.

nodes.name: metadataColumns
nodes.summary: Returns an empty array because this table has no metadata columns.

nodes.name: StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the partition reader factory and partition reader that read the state of a stream-stream join (one join side) for the State Data Source, turning join state manager entries into rows of key, value and partition.

nodes.name: StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionReaderFactory for stream-stream join state. It is built with the state store conf, the serializable Hadoop configuration, the user-facing schema, the state schema and an optional join state format version, and createReader casts the partition to StateStoreInputPartition and returns a StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReader.

nodes.name: StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReader
nodes.summary: PartitionReader[InternalRow] with Logging that reads one partition of one join side. At construction it derives key and value schemas, the join side (left or right; JoinSideValues.none is an internal error), whether virtual column families are used (StreamStreamJoinStateHelper.usesVirtualColumnFamilies), the start and end state store checkpoint IDs per side (SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.getStateStoreCheckpointIds), and the input attributes plus state format version: an explicit joinStateFormatVersion (2 or higher drops the trailing matched column, 1 keeps all) or a heuristic that detects a Boolean 'matched' last column (version 3 with virtual column families, else 2). It asserts that the exposed fields equal the user-facing value schema. A lazy iterator creates a SymmetricHashJoinStateManager (with SnapshotOptions when reading from a snapshot and a JoinStateManagerStoreGenerator) and maps its entries to rows; for format version 2 or higher the matched flag is written back into the value row. next/get/close drive the iterator, and close aborts the state manager if needed.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Creates a StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReader for the given InputPartition (cast to StateStoreInputPartition), passing the store conf, Hadoop conf, schemas and join state format version.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances the lazily created row iterator: stores the next row as current and returns true, or sets current to null and returns false when exhausted.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the current InternalRow.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Clears the current row and, if a join state manager was created, calls abortIfNeeded on it.

nodes.name: unifyStateRowPair
nodes.summary: Private helper that builds a three-field GenericInternalRow from a (key, value) pair of UnsafeRows plus the partition id.

nodes.name: SchemaUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SchemaUtil object that decides the output schema of the State Data Source for each kind of state (plain key/value, change feed, raw bytes for all column families, and each transformWithState variable type), validates schemas, and converts state store rows into output rows.

nodes.name: SchemaUtil
nodes.summary: Utility object for the State Data Source. Schema side: getSourceSchema picks the output StructType (partition_key/key_bytes/value_bytes/column_family_name when reading all column families, the per-variable schema for transformWithState state, batch_id/change_type/key/value/partition_id for change feed, otherwise key/value/partition_id), isValidSchema checks field names and types against the expected ones for each state variable type (ValueState, ListState, MapState, TimerState, with change feed and flattened collection options), and getCompositeKeySchema derives the (key, userKey) schema for map state. Row side: unifyStateRowPair, unifyStateRowPairAsRawBytes, unifyStateRowPairWithMultipleValues, unifyMapStateRowPair (groups consecutive rows by grouping key into a map, or flattens them) and unifyTimerRow build output rows, and processStateEntries dispatches on the state variable type to iterate a ReadStateStore. getSchemaAsDataType looks up a field type or throws an AnalysisException.

nodes.name: getSchemaAsDataType
nodes.summary: Returns the data type of the named field of a StructType, or throws an AnalysisException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3074) with the field name and schema if the field is missing.

nodes.name: getSourceSchema
nodes.summary: Chooses the output schema of the state source: raw bytes schema with partition_key, key_bytes, value_bytes and column_family_name (partition key schema comes from StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory) when reading all column families; generateSchemaForStateVar for transformWithState variables; the change feed layout when readChangeFeed is set; otherwise key, value and partition_id.

nodes.name: unifyStateRowPair
nodes.summary: Builds a three-field GenericInternalRow from a (key, value) UnsafeRow pair and the partition id.

nodes.name: unifyStateRowPairAsRawBytes
nodes.summary: Builds a four-field row holding the partition key extracted by a StatePartitionKeyExtractor, the key bytes, the value bytes and the column family name.

nodes.name: unifyStateRowPairWithMultipleValues
nodes.summary: Builds a three-field row from a key row, an array of values and the partition id (used for list state).

nodes.name: unifyMapStateRowPair
nodes.summary: Converts the rows of map state (stored with a composite key of grouping key and user key) into output rows. With flattenCollectionTypes each state row becomes a row of grouping key, user key, value and partition id. Otherwise it returns an iterator that relies on rows with the same grouping key being consecutive and emits one row per grouping key containing a map of user key to value; it throws NoSuchElementException when read past the end.

nodes.name: isValidSchema
nodes.summary: Returns whether the given schema has exactly the expected field names, in order, and field types assignable to the expected classes. The expected names depend on internalOnlyReadAllColumnFamilies, the transformWithState variable type (value, list, map, timer) and the readChangeFeed and flattenCollectionTypes options; unsupported variable types raise an internal error.

nodes.name: generateSchemaForStateVar
nodes.summary: Private method that builds the output StructType for a transformWithState variable: for each of ValueState, ListState, MapState and TimerState it chooses the fields (batch_id and change_type for change feed, list_element or list_value, user_map_key/user_map_value or map_value, expiration_timestamp_ms) from the column family schema and the change feed and flatten options.

nodes.name: checkVariableType
nodes.summary: Returns true if the optional state variable info is defined and its type equals the given StateVariableType.

nodes.name: getCompositeKeySchema
nodes.summary: Derives the composite key schema (grouping 'key' plus 'userKey') of map state from a generated schema, reading user_map_key when flattening or the key type of map_value otherwise; a lookup failure becomes an internal error.

nodes.name: processStateEntries
nodes.summary: Iterates a ReadStateStore for a state variable and returns output rows depending on the type: one row per entry for value state, flattened or array-valued rows for list state (using valuesIterator), grouped or flattened map rows via unifyMapStateRowPair for map state, and timer rows for timer state; anything else throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: unifyTimerRow
nodes.summary: Private helper that builds a three-field row from the grouping key, the expiration timestamp (a long at index 1 of the timer key row) and the partition id.

nodes.name: StateDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the "statestore" data source that lets a user read streaming state store contents as a table, together with its option parsing. It holds StateDataSource (the TableProvider that builds the table and infers the schema), StateSourceOptions with its validated reader options, the small option holders FromSnapshotOptions and ReadChangeFeedOptions, and StateStoreReaderInfo, the bundle of metadata handed to the StateTable.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file where the case class StateSourceOptions and its companion object, and the class StateDataSource and its companion object, share the same class ids.

nodes.name: StateDataSource
nodes.summary: TableProvider and DataSourceRegister for the state store data source, registered under the short name "statestore". getTable parses and checks the options, rebuilds the SQL conf of the chosen batch from the offset log, rejects the internal read-all-column-families mode unless the provider is the RocksDB one, collects store metadata and builds a StateTable. inferSchema derives the key and value schema (from the join side or from the column family schema) and turns it into the user-facing schema. Private helpers validate state variable and timer options for transformWithState, read the state format version of stream-stream joins and pick the key state encoder spec. The companion object (lines 831-851) lists the state metadata entries of one operator and store and returns their old schema file paths.

nodes.name: FromSnapshotOptions
nodes.summary: Case class holding the snapshotStartBatchId and snapshotPartitionId options used when state is read from a snapshot of one partition. Both values must be given together.

nodes.name: ReadChangeFeedOptions
nodes.summary: Case class holding changeStartBatchId and changeEndBatchId, the batch range used when the state source reads a change feed instead of a single batch.

nodes.name: StateSourceOptions
nodes.summary: Case class (lines 484-516) and companion object (lines 518-816) describing the validated options of the state data source: checkpoint location, batch id, operator id, store name, join side, change feed and snapshot options, state variable name, registered timers flag, collection flattening flag, the internal read-all-column-families flag and the operator state unique ids of the start and end batch. The companion extends DataSourceOptions, declares the option names ("path", "batchId", "operatorId", "storeName", "joinSide", "snapshotStartBatchId", "snapshotPartitionId", "readChangeFeed", "changeStartBatchId", "changeEndBatchId", "stateVarName", "readRegisteredTimers", "flattenCollectionTypes", "_readAllColumnFamilies") and its apply method reads them, checks conflicts and ranges, resolves default batch ids from the commit log and raises StateDataSourceErrors for bad input. modifySourceOptions rewrites the options for stream-stream joins that use virtual column families. The case class also provides stateCheckpointLocation and a toString. The apply overload that takes a java Map just wraps it in a CaseInsensitiveStringMap.

nodes.name: JoinSideValues
nodes.summary: Enumeration nested in StateSourceOptions with the values left, right and none. It selects which side of a stream-stream join to read, none meaning a non-join read.

nodes.name: StateStoreReaderInfo
nodes.summary: Case class that bundles what the data source learned from the checkpoint metadata: the optional key state encoder spec, column family schema, transformWithState variable info, state schema provider, join column family name, all-column-families reader info and join state format version. getStoreMetadataAndRunChecks returns it and getTable passes its fields to StateTable.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds the StateTable for a read: parses and adjusts StateSourceOptions, builds the SQL conf of the requested batch, checks that the internal read-all mode only runs with the RocksDB state store provider, loads the store reader info and picks the key state encoder spec (falling back to a no-prefix spec built from the key schema when none exists).

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the table schema from the state checkpoint. It reads the key and value schema from the left or right join side helper, or from the column family schema when no join side is given, then calls SchemaUtil.getSourceSchema; any non-fatal failure is rethrown as failedToReadStateSchema.

nodes.name: getStateFormatVersion
nodes.summary: Returns the join state format version read from the offset log metadata of the batch when the first store entry belongs to a symmetric hash join operator, otherwise None.

nodes.name: isReadAllColFamiliesOnJoinWithVCF
nodes.summary: Tells whether the request reads all column families of a stream-stream join that uses virtual column families (state format version 3 or newer).

nodes.name: buildSqlConfForBatch
nodes.summary: Clones the session SQL conf and overlays the conf stored in the offset log metadata of the given batch; throws offsetLogUnavailable or offsetMetadataLogUnavailable when that log entry or its metadata is missing.

nodes.name: runStateVarChecks
nodes.summary: Validates the stateVarName, storeName and readRegisteredTimers options against the operator found in the metadata. Join operators must use an allowed store name, transformWithState operators must name a defined state variable (checked by the nested runTWSChecks, which also rejects registered timers when TimeMode is None) and other operators may not receive these options.

nodes.name: getStoreMetadataAndRunChecks
nodes.summary: Core metadata loader: reads the store metadata for the operator, runs the state variable checks, locates the schema file paths (from the operator properties for transformWithState or the older location), reads the column family schemas through StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker, derives the key state encoder spec and assembles a StateStoreReaderInfo, including the all-column-families info when the internal read-all option is set.

nodes.name: getKeyStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Chooses the key state encoder spec for a column family. Without metadata it logs a warning and uses a no-prefix spec; with metadata version 1 it uses numColsPrefixKey to pick a no-prefix or prefix-scan spec, with version 2 it takes the spec recorded in the schema file, and otherwise raises an internal error.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Main option parser of the companion object (the overload at lines 539-544 only wraps a java Map). It reads each option, applies defaults, enforces the conflict and range rules for change feed, snapshot, join side, state variable and internal read-all options, resolves the batch id from the commit log, loads the operator state unique ids of the start and end batch and rejects mixed checkpoint format versions.

nodes.name: getLastCommittedBatch
nodes.summary: Returns the latest batch id in the commit log of the checkpoint, or raises committedBatchUnavailable when the log is empty.

nodes.name: getOperatorStateUniqueIds
nodes.summary: Reads the commit log entry of a batch and returns the state unique ids recorded for the given operator, if any; raises committedBatchUnavailable when the entry is missing.

nodes.name: modifySourceOptions
nodes.summary: Rewrites the options when a non-default store name is given for a stream-stream join that uses virtual column families: the store name becomes the state variable name and the store name is reset to the default.

nodes.name: getStateStoreMetadata
nodes.summary: Companion object method that reads all state metadata entries for the checkpoint through StateMetadataPartitionReader and keeps those whose operator id and store name match the options.

nodes.name: getOldSchemaFilePaths
nodes.summary: Returns the state schema file paths recorded in the first matching metadata entry as Hadoop Paths, or an empty list when no metadata exists.

nodes.name: StateScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the read-side scan classes of the state store data source: StateScanBuilder, which builds a StateScan, StateStoreInputPartition, which carries one partition number, and StateScan, which lists the state partition directories of an operator and creates the matching partition reader factory.

nodes.name: StateScanBuilder
nodes.summary: ScanBuilder for the state store data source. It keeps the session, schema, source options, state store conf and the encoder and schema information, and its build method returns a StateScan with the same arguments.

nodes.name: StateStoreInputPartition
nodes.summary: InputPartition that records the partition number, a dummy query id and the StateSourceOptions for one state store partition to read.

nodes.name: StateScan
nodes.summary: Scan and Batch for the state store data source. It broadcasts the Hadoop conf, lists the numeric partition directories under the operator's state checkpoint folder (only those below the batch's partition count, which must be continuous from 0) and makes one StateStoreInputPartition per directory, or just the requested one when reading from a snapshot. createReaderFactory returns a StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReaderFactory for a left or right join side and a StatePartitionReaderFactory otherwise. description builds a text summary of the checkpoint location, batch, operator, store name, join side, snapshot and change feed settings.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates the StateScan from the builder's stored arguments.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Lists the partition directories of the operator's state checkpoint, keeps numeric names below batchNumPartitions, asserts they start at 0 and are continuous, and returns one StateStoreInputPartition each, or only the snapshot partition when fromSnapshotOptions is set (throwing stateStoreSnapshotPartitionNotFound if it is absent). Throws noPartitionDiscoveredInStateStore when none are found.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Selects the PartitionReaderFactory by join side: for left or right it reads the join state schema and builds a StreamStreamJoinStatePartitionReaderFactory, for none it builds a StatePartitionReaderFactory with the encoder spec, variable info, column family schema, schema provider and all-column-families info.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Returns a one-line text description of the scan listing the checkpoint location, batch id, operator id, store name and, when present, the join side, snapshot options and change feed range.

nodes.name: StateMetadataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the "state-metadata" data source, a read-only table listing the operators and state stores found in a streaming checkpoint. It defines the table entry row type with its fixed schema, the provider, table, scan, input partition and reader factory, and StateMetadataPartitionReader, which walks the checkpoint's state and commits folders and converts operator state metadata (versions 1 and 2) into entries. The state data source also uses the reader to find store metadata.

nodes.name: StateMetadataTableEntry
nodes.summary: Case class (lines 44-66) for one operator and state store: operator id and name, store name, partition count, min and max batch id, metadata version, operator properties JSON, numColsPrefixKey and state schema file paths. toRow converts it to an InternalRow. The companion object (lines 68-79) holds the static output schema (operatorId, operatorName, stateStoreName, numPartitions, minBatchId, maxBatchId, operatorProperties).

nodes.name: StateMetadataSource
nodes.summary: TableProvider and DataSourceRegister registered as "state-metadata". getTable returns a StateMetadataTable and inferSchema returns the static schema of StateMetadataTableEntry.

nodes.name: StateMetadataTable
nodes.summary: Table with SupportsRead and SupportsMetadataColumns named "state-metadata-table" that supports BATCH_READ. Its newScanBuilder requires the "path" option, takes the optional "batchId" option or the last committed batch (or 0) and returns a StateMetadataScan. It exposes one metadata column, _numColsPrefixKey.

nodes.name: NumColsPrefixKeyColumn
nodes.summary: Private nested object implementing MetadataColumn for the integer column "_numColsPrefixKey", described as the number of columns in the prefix key of the state store instance.

nodes.name: StateMetadataInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition that carries the checkpoint location string for the single partition of the metadata scan.

nodes.name: StateMetadataScan
nodes.summary: Scan for the metadata table. Its toBatch returns a Batch with exactly one StateMetadataInputPartition and a reader factory built from the active session's Hadoop conf (not broadcast since there is one partition).

nodes.name: StateMetadataPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class PartitionReaderFactory whose createReader returns a StateMetadataPartitionReader for the checkpoint location in the given StateMetadataInputPartition.

nodes.name: StateMetadataPartitionReader
nodes.summary: PartitionReader that produces one InternalRow per state store entry. It lists the batch ids in the "commits" folder, reads the operator ids under the "state" folder, picks the V2 or V1 operator state metadata reader per operator and converts V1 and V2 metadata into StateMetadataTableEntry values (V1 has null operator properties and no schema paths, V2 has numColsPrefixKey -1). A missing metadata folder is logged as a warning and yields no entries. It is also used directly by StateDataSource.

nodes.name: toRow
nodes.summary: Builds a GenericInternalRow from the entry's operator id, name, store name, partition count, min and max batch id, operator properties JSON and numColsPrefixKey, converting strings to UTF8String.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder (a lambda) that checks the "path" option, resolves the batch id from the "batchId" option or the last committed batch in the checkpoint (default 0) and builds a StateMetadataScan.

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous Batch with one StateMetadataInputPartition and a StateMetadataPartitionReaderFactory created from the active session's Hadoop conf and the batch id.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Casts the partition to StateMetadataInputPartition and returns a StateMetadataPartitionReader for its checkpoint location.

nodes.name: batchIds
nodes.summary: Lists the numeric file names in the checkpoint's "commits" folder, sorted, or an empty array when that folder does not exist.

nodes.name: allOperatorStateMetadata
nodes.summary: Lists the operator id folders under the checkpoint's "state" folder and reads each operator's OperatorStateMetadata, using the V2 reader when a V2 metadata directory exists and V1 otherwise; throws failedToReadOperatorMetadata if nothing is read and returns an empty array when files are not found. Visible to the sql package so planning can use it.

nodes.name: stateMetadata
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator of StateMetadataTableEntry values built from allOperatorStateMetadata. For each V1 or V2 operator metadata it emits one entry per state store, filling the min and max batch id from the commit log batch ids (or -1).

nodes.name: TextDataSourceV2.scala
nodes.summary: Registers the V2 text file data source under the short name "text". It extends FileDataSourceV2, falls back to the V1 TextFileFormat and builds TextTable instances with or without a user supplied schema.

nodes.name: TextDataSourceV2
nodes.summary: FileDataSourceV2 for text files. It names the fallback file format TextFileFormat, reports the short name "text" and has two getTable overloads, one without and one with an explicit schema, that resolve the paths, the table name and the options without paths and return a TextTable.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Builds a TextTable from the options with no user schema. A second overload (lines 39-44) takes a StructType and passes it as the user specified schema.

nodes.name: TextPartitionReaderFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TextPartitionReaderFactory, the reader factory of the V2 text source. For each file it opens a line reader or a whole-text reader and turns every record into a single-column UnsafeRow, then adds the partition values.

nodes.name: TextPartitionReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Case class FilePartitionReaderFactory for text files, holding the SQL conf, the broadcast Hadoop conf, the read data schema, the partition schema and the TextOptions. Its buildReader creates a HadoopFileLinesReader (using the line separator option) or a HadoopFileWholeTextReader when wholeText is set, registers closing of the reader at task completion, and maps each line into a one-field UnsafeRow written with UnsafeRowWriter (or a shared empty row when no column is needed). The result is wrapped with the partition values of the file.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Builds the PartitionReader for one PartitionedFile: opens the line or whole-text reader inside a resource creation helper, adds a task completion listener to close it, converts the records to UnsafeRow (empty rows when the read schema is empty) and wraps the iterator with PartitionReaderFromIterator and PartitionReaderWithPartitionValues.

nodes.name: TextScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TextScan, the file scan of the V2 text source. It checks that at most one column is read, decides whether a text file can be split and creates the TextPartitionReaderFactory.

nodes.name: TextScan
nodes.summary: Case class extending TextBasedFileScan for text files. It builds TextOptions from the scan options, refuses a read schema with more than one column, treats files as not splittable in wholetext mode (with the reason "the text datasource is set wholetext mode"), creates a TextPartitionReaderFactory with a broadcast Hadoop conf that includes the case sensitive options, and defines equals (parent equality plus options) and hashCode.

nodes.name: verifyReadSchema
nodes.summary: Throws textDataSourceWithMultiColumnsError when the read schema has more than one column.

nodes.name: isSplitable
nodes.summary: A text file is splittable when the parent scan says so and the wholetext option is off.

nodes.name: getFileUnSplittableReason
nodes.summary: Returns the parent's reason when the file is unsplittable for the parent's reasons, otherwise the text "the text datasource is set wholetext mode".

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Verifies the read schema, builds a Hadoop conf from the case sensitive options, broadcasts it with SerializableConfiguration.broadcast and returns a TextPartitionReaderFactory with the read data schema, partition schema and TextOptions.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two TextScan objects are equal when the parent equality holds and their options are equal.

nodes.name: TextScanBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TextScanBuilder, which builds a TextScan from the file index, schemas, options and the filters collected by the file scan builder.

nodes.name: TextScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileScanBuilder for text files. Its build method returns a TextScan using dataSchema, readDataSchema(), readPartitionSchema(), the options and the partition and data filters kept by the parent.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates a TextScan from the builder's session, file index, data schema, pruned read schemas, options and filters.

nodes.name: TextTable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TextTable, the V2 file table for text files. It supplies the scan builder, the fixed one-column string schema, the write builder and the supported data type.

nodes.name: TextTable
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileTable for text files. Its inferred schema is a single string column named "value", newScanBuilder returns a TextScanBuilder, newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that builds a TextWrite, only StringType is supported and the format name is "Text".

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a TextScanBuilder built from the session, file index, schema, data schema and the merged options.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Always returns Some of a StructType with one StringType field named "value", regardless of the files.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder whose build creates a TextWrite with the table paths, format name, supportsDataType and the merged write info.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Returns true only for StringType.

nodes.name: formatName
nodes.summary: Returns the format name "Text".

nodes.name: TextWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TextWrite, the V2 file write for text files. It checks that exactly one column is written, configures the compression codec and returns an OutputWriterFactory that creates TextOutputWriter instances and names files with a .txt extension.

nodes.name: TextWrite
nodes.summary: Case class extending FileWrite for text files. prepareWrite validates that the schema has exactly one column, builds TextOptions, sets the compression codec in the job configuration and returns an OutputWriterFactory whose newInstance creates a TextOutputWriter with the line separator for writing and whose getFileExtension returns ".txt" plus the compression extension.

nodes.name: verifySchema
nodes.summary: Throws textDataSourceWithMultiColumnsError unless the schema has exactly one column.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Verifies the schema, reads TextOptions, applies the compression codec to the job conf and returns an anonymous OutputWriterFactory that creates TextOutputWriter instances and gives files the extension ".txt" plus the compression extension.

nodes.name: AQEPropagateEmptyRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AQEPropagateEmptyRelation rule, used in the adaptive optimizer to remove joins and other operators whose inputs are known to be empty from the runtime statistics of materialized query stages, including single column null-aware anti joins over a broadcast relation with all null keys.

nodes.name: AQEPropagateEmptyRelation
nodes.summary: Object extending PropagateEmptyRelationBase that is run by the AQE optimizer. It treats a plan as empty when the runtime row count of a materialized query stage is 0 (except a root repartition), as non-empty when the estimated row count is positive, and replaces such plans with EmptyRelation. It also eliminates a single column null-aware anti join to an empty relation when the broadcast build side is HashedRelationWithAllNullKeys, and refuses to drop user-specified repartitions or broadcast stages that cannot run without their join.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Overrides the empty check so a plan is also empty when its estimated runtime row count is exactly 0 and it is not a root repartition.

nodes.name: nonEmpty
nodes.summary: Overrides the non-empty check so a plan is also non-empty when its estimated runtime row count is positive.

nodes.name: isRootRepartition
nodes.summary: Returns true for a LogicalQueryStage that carries the ROOT_REPARTITION tag, so that such a repartition is not treated as empty.

nodes.name: getEstimatedRowCount
nodes.summary: Returns the runtime row count of a plan if it can be known: from a materialized query stage, from the child stage of an aggregate with grouping expressions, or 0 for an EmptyRelation; otherwise None. The comment states 0 means no rows, a positive value may be an over-estimate and None means not materialized or not estimable.

nodes.name: isRelationWithAllNullKeys
nodes.summary: Checks whether a materialized broadcast query stage holds the HashedRelationWithAllNullKeys relation by reading the broadcast relation future.

nodes.name: eliminateSingleColumnNullAwareAntiJoin
nodes.summary: Partial function that replaces a single column null-aware anti join with an empty relation when its right side is a broadcast relation with all null keys.

nodes.name: userSpecifiedRepartition
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook so that a query stage over a shuffle with origin REPARTITION_BY_COL or REPARTITION_BY_NUM counts as a user-specified repartition.

nodes.name: canExecuteWithoutJoin
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook to return false for a LogicalQueryStage over a BroadcastQueryStageExec, because a broadcast stage cannot be executed without its join operator (a TODO notes the pre-broadcast plan could be returned).

nodes.name: applyInternal
nodes.summary: Entry point of the rule: transforms the plan bottom-up with pruning on the LOGICAL_QUERY_STAGE, LOCAL_RELATION and TRUE_OR_FALSE_LITERAL patterns, trying the null-aware anti join elimination first and then the common apply function of the base class.

nodes.name: AQEShuffleReadRule.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AQEShuffleReadRule trait, the common base for physical rules that wrap shuffle query stages in AQEShuffleReadExec and may change the output partitioning.

nodes.name: AQEShuffleReadRule
nodes.summary: Trait extending Rule[SparkPlan] for rules that may create AQEShuffleReadExec on top of ShuffleQueryStageExec. Implementations declare the ShuffleOrigins they support through supportedShuffleOrigins, and isSupported checks a shuffle against that list. The AQE framework skips the rule if applying it introduces extra shuffles.

nodes.name: isSupported
nodes.summary: Returns true when the shuffle origin of the given ShuffleExchangeLike is in supportedShuffleOrigins; subclasses override it to add conditions.

nodes.name: AQEUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the AQEUtils helper object, which computes the data distribution that a plan must keep in order to preserve a user-specified repartition during AQE re-optimization.

nodes.name: AQEUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object with one method, getRequiredDistribution, which walks down a physical plan through Filter, local Sort, CollectMetrics, DeserializeToObject and Project nodes to find a user-specified hash repartition and turns it into a ClusteredDistribution requirement.

nodes.name: getRequiredDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns the Distribution a plan must satisfy to keep a user-specified repartition (by column or by number) that is the root or sits under Project, Filter, local Sort or CollectMetrics. For a ShuffleExchangeExec with HashPartitioning it returns a ClusteredDistribution (with a required partition count for REPARTITION_BY_NUM); under a Project it gives up (None) if the clustering expressions are not kept; any other node yields UnspecifiedDistribution.

nodes.name: AdaptiveRulesHolder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AdaptiveRulesHolder, a simple holder of the SQL extension rules that can be injected into adaptive query execution.

nodes.name: AdaptiveRulesHolder
nodes.summary: Class with four rule sequences: queryStagePrepRules (applied before query stages are created), runtimeOptimizerRules (tune the logical plan from runtime statistics of query stages), queryStageOptimizerRules (applied to a new query stage before execution, after child stages are materialized) and queryPostPlannerStrategyRules (applied between plannerStrategy and queryStagePrepRules to see the whole plan before exchanges are injected).

nodes.name: AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Provides the AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper trait (and a private[sql] object of the same name) with tree traversal helpers that, unlike the TreeNode ones, also descend into AdaptiveSparkPlanExec and QueryStageExec leaves.

nodes.name: AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper
nodes.summary: Trait (with a companion object at line 157 that simply extends it) that offers find, foreach, foreachUp, mapPlans, flatMap, collect, collectLeaves, exists, existsWithSubqueries, collectFirst, collectWithSubqueries, subqueriesAll and stripAQEPlan over a SparkPlan. Traversal goes through allChildren, which looks inside AdaptiveSparkPlanExec (executedPlan) and QueryStageExec (plan).

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Finds the first plan node, in pre-order, that satisfies a predicate, descending through adaptive plans and query stages.

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Applies a function to a node and then recursively to all its children, including those behind adaptive plans and query stages.

nodes.name: foreachUp
nodes.summary: Applies a function recursively to the children first and then to the node itself (post-order).

nodes.name: mapPlans
nodes.summary: Returns a Seq with the result of a function applied to every node in pre-order.

nodes.name: flatMap
nodes.summary: Returns a Seq built by applying a function to every node and concatenating the resulting collections.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Returns the results of a partial function applied to every node on which it is defined.

nodes.name: collectLeaves
nodes.summary: Returns the leaf nodes of the tree, where a leaf is a node with no allChildren.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Returns true if any node in the tree satisfies a predicate.

nodes.name: existsWithSubqueries
nodes.summary: Like exists, but also tests the plans inside subqueries.

nodes.name: collectFirst
nodes.summary: Finds the first node in pre-order where a partial function is defined and applies it.

nodes.name: collectWithSubqueries
nodes.summary: Collects partial function results over the plan and all plans in its nested subqueries.

nodes.name: subqueriesAll
nodes.summary: Returns all subquery plans of the tree, including nested subqueries of the children, by flat-mapping the subqueries of each node and recursing.

nodes.name: allChildren
nodes.summary: Protected method defining the traversal edges: the executedPlan of an AdaptiveSparkPlanExec, the plan of a QueryStageExec, or the normal children of any other node.

nodes.name: stripAQEPlan
nodes.summary: Removes the top AdaptiveSparkPlanExec and ResultQueryStageExec wrappers from a plan and returns the plan inside.

nodes.name: AdjustShuffleExchangePosition.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AdjustShuffleExchangePosition rule, which moves a shuffle exchange from above a DeserializeToObjectExec to below it, because that operator must stay at the root of the plan.

nodes.name: AdjustShuffleExchangePosition
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] used to adjust a shuffle exchange sitting on top of a special operator that does not allow a shuffle above it. Today the only such operator is DeserializeToObjectExec, which produces safe rows and must be the root; since AQE may add a shuffle back to keep a user-specified repartition, the rule swaps their positions.

nodes.name: shouldAdjust
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given plan is a DeserializeToObjectExec, the case that needs the shuffle moved below it.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: For a ShuffleExchangeLike whose child should be adjusted, rebuilds the plan with the child on top and the shuffle placed over the child's children; any other plan is returned unchanged.

nodes.name: DynamicJoinSelection.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DynamicJoinSelection logical rule that uses shuffle map output statistics of materialized query stages to add join strategy hints such as NO_BROADCAST_HASH, PREFER_SHUFFLE_HASH and SHUFFLE_HASH.

nodes.name: DynamicJoinSelection
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] with JoinSelectionHelper that runs on logical plans containing materialized shuffle query stages. It adds a NO_BROADCAST_HASH hint to a side with many empty partitions (shuffle join is faster then), a PREFER_SHUFFLE_HASH hint to a side whose partitions all fit under the local map threshold, and SHUFFLE_HASH when both apply. Existing user strategy hints are left alone.

nodes.name: hasManyEmptyPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns true when the share of non-empty shuffle partitions in the map output statistics is below conf.nonEmptyPartitionRatioForBroadcastJoin.

nodes.name: preferShuffledHashJoin
nodes.summary: Returns true when the advisory partition size and every shuffle partition are not larger than the ADAPTIVE_MAX_SHUFFLE_HASH_JOIN_LOCAL_MAP_THRESHOLD setting, so a shuffled hash join is preferred.

nodes.name: selectJoinStrategy
nodes.summary: For one side of a join backed by a materialized ShuffleQueryStageExec with map statistics, decides whether to demote broadcast hash join (many empty partitions, depending on join type and which side can be built) and whether to prefer shuffle hash join, and returns SHUFFLE_HASH, NO_BROADCAST_HASH, PREFER_SHUFFLE_HASH or None.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms the logical plan top-down; for each equi-join without an existing strategy hint on a side, calls selectJoinStrategy and copies the join with the updated left and right hints.

nodes.name: InvalidAQEPlanException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines InvalidAQEPlanException, thrown when AQE replanning produces an invalid plan so that AQE keeps using the latest valid plan.

nodes.name: InvalidAQEPlanException
nodes.summary: Case class extending Exception with a message and the offending plan (a type parameter bounded by QueryPlan). When it is thrown during AQE replanning, AQE stops the current replanning and keeps using the latest valid plan.

nodes.name: LogicalQueryStage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the adaptive LogicalQueryStage, a logical plan leaf that wraps a QueryStageExec (or a physical snippet containing one) so that re-optimization can see runtime statistics.

nodes.name: LogicalQueryStage
nodes.summary: Case class extending the catalyst LogicalQueryStage. It links a logical plan to the physical plan being executed or already completed, where the physical plan is a QueryStageExec or a snippet whose ancestors of the stage belong to the same logical node (for example FinalAgg over a shuffle stage for a logical Aggregate). It reports the output of the logical plan and the ordering of the physical plan, tags repartition operations with the REPARTITION_OPERATION pattern, and takes statistics from the stage when available.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Computes statistics from the first QueryStageExec found in the physical plan, using the stage statistics (a global aggregate with row count 0 is changed to 1); falls back to the statistics of the logical plan when no physical statistics exist. A TODO notes it is not accurate with other physical nodes above the stage.

nodes.name: isMaterialized
nodes.summary: True when any QueryStageExec inside the physical plan is materialized.

nodes.name: isDirectStage
nodes.summary: True when the physical plan is itself a QueryStageExec.

nodes.name: generateTreeString
nodes.summary: Prints the node with the parent implementation and then prints the wrapped logical plan as an extra last child in the tree string.

nodes.name: LogicalQueryStageStrategy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LogicalQueryStageStrategy, the planner strategy that turns LogicalQueryStage nodes into their physical plans and keeps already broadcast stages as the build side of broadcast joins.

nodes.name: LogicalQueryStageStrategy
nodes.summary: Strategy object (the Strategy type of the classic package, an alias of SparkStrategy) that handles plans containing LogicalQueryStage. It plans a join with a broadcast query stage as BroadcastHashJoinExec (also the null-aware anti join case) or BroadcastNestedLoopJoinExec, so a broadcast stage is not reversed into a shuffle if the larger side finishes first, and otherwise maps a LogicalQueryStage to its physical plan. It must run before the regular join strategies.

nodes.name: isBroadcastStageWithHashedBroadcastMode
nodes.summary: Checks whether a plan is a LogicalQueryStage over a BroadcastQueryStageExec whose broadcast uses HashedRelationBroadcastMode with the same null-aware flag as requested.

nodes.name: isBroadcastStageWithIdentityBroadcastMode
nodes.summary: Checks whether a plan is a LogicalQueryStage over a BroadcastQueryStageExec whose broadcast uses IdentityBroadcastMode.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Strategy entry point. Matches equi-joins with a hashed broadcast stage on either side to BroadcastHashJoinExec, single column null-aware anti joins with a broadcast right side to a null-aware BroadcastHashJoinExec with LeftAnti, other joins with an identity broadcast stage to BroadcastNestedLoopJoinExec, a bare LogicalQueryStage to its physicalPlan, and anything else to Nil.

nodes.name: OptimizeShuffleWithLocalRead.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the OptimizeShuffleWithLocalRead rule, which replaces a shuffle read with a local read (reading map output without moving it) when no additional shuffle would be introduced.

nodes.name: OptimizeShuffleWithLocalRead
nodes.summary: AQEShuffleReadRule that supports shuffles with origin ENSURE_REQUIREMENTS or REBALANCE_PARTITIONS_BY_NONE (not single-partition output). If the plan itself is a supported shuffle stage it adds a local read directly; otherwise it adds local reads on the probe side of broadcast hash joins and the doc says it then runs EnsureRequirements to check for extra shuffles and reverts all local reads if any appear. It is controlled by SQLConf.LOCAL_SHUFFLE_READER_ENABLED.

nodes.name: BroadcastJoinWithShuffleLeft
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply matches a BroadcastHashJoinExec whose left child can use a local shuffle read and returns that child with the join build side.

nodes.name: BroadcastJoinWithShuffleRight
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply matches a BroadcastHashJoinExec whose right child can use a local shuffle read and returns that child with the join build side.

nodes.name: isSupported
nodes.summary: Overrides the base check to also require that the shuffle output partitioning is not SinglePartition.

nodes.name: createProbeSideLocalRead
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan top-down and, for a broadcast hash join whose probe side (the side opposite the build side) is a shuffle stage that can use local read, replaces that child with a local read. The build side is skipped since the broadcast stage is already optimized.

nodes.name: createLocalRead
nodes.summary: Wraps a ShuffleQueryStageExec (or an existing AQEShuffleReadExec over one) in a new AQEShuffleReadExec whose partition specs come from getPartitionSpecs.

nodes.name: getPartitionSpecs
nodes.summary: Builds the partition specs for a local read: when the expected parallelism is at least the number of mappers it splits each mapper output into PartialMapperPartitionSpec ranges, otherwise it groups mappers into CoalescedMapperPartitionSpec ranges. A TODO notes it assumes all shuffle blocks have the same size.

nodes.name: equallyDivide
nodes.summary: Divides n elements into m buckets as evenly as possible (the first n%m buckets get one extra) and returns the start index of each bucket.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: returns the plan unchanged if the local shuffle reader is disabled; otherwise creates a local read when the plan itself can use one, or adds probe side local reads.

nodes.name: canUseLocalShuffleRead
nodes.summary: Returns true for a ShuffleQueryStageExec with map statistics and a supported shuffle, or for an AQEShuffleReadExec over such a stage whose shuffle origin is ENSURE_REQUIREMENTS.

nodes.name: OptimizeSkewInRebalancePartitions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the OptimizeSkewInRebalancePartitions rule, which splits skewed shuffle partitions of rebalance shuffles using map output statistics and the advisory partition size.

nodes.name: OptimizeSkewInRebalancePartitions
nodes.summary: AQEShuffleReadRule that supports shuffles with origin REBALANCE_PARTITIONS_BY_NONE or REBALANCE_PARTITIONS_BY_COL. When some partition exceeds the advisory size it asks ShufflePartitionsUtil.optimizeSkewedPartitions for new partition specs, splitting a skewed reducer partition into pieces per mapper, and wraps the stage in AQEShuffleReadExec. It is enabled by ADAPTIVE_OPTIMIZE_SKEWS_IN_REBALANCE_PARTITIONS_ENABLED.

nodes.name: tryOptimizeSkewedPartitions
nodes.summary: For one shuffle stage, uses its own advisory partition size or the default ADVISORY_PARTITION_SIZE_IN_BYTES, returns the stage unchanged if there are no statistics or no partition exceeds the size, and otherwise computes new partition specs (with ADAPTIVE_REBALANCE_PARTITIONS_SMALL_PARTITION_FACTOR) and returns an AQEShuffleReadExec if the number of partitions changed.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged if the rule is disabled; otherwise transforms bottom-up every supported ShuffleQueryStageExec with tryOptimizeSkewedPartitions.

nodes.name: PlanAdaptiveDynamicPruningFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PlanAdaptiveDynamicPruningFilters rule, which plans dynamic pruning expressions in adaptive plans so that they reuse an existing broadcast exchange where possible.

nodes.name: PlanAdaptiveDynamicPruningFilters
nodes.summary: Case class taking the root AdaptiveSparkPlanExec; it is a Rule[SparkPlan] that also mixes in AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper and reads its conf from the session of the root plan. It rewrites DynamicPruningExpression over InSubqueryExec with a SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec: reuse the broadcast exchange if the same exchange is already a build side of a BroadcastHashJoinExec in the root plan, or use TrueLiteral when the pruning is only useful with broadcast reuse, or plan an aggregate over the build plan as a separate subquery.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged when dynamic partition pruning is disabled; otherwise transforms the expressions that contain a dynamic pruning expression with an in-subquery. It builds a HashedRelationBroadcastMode broadcast exchange over the adaptive build plan, reuses it as SubqueryBroadcastExec when an equal exchange is found in the root plan (and exchange reuse is enabled), falls back to a literal true when onlyInBroadcast is set, and otherwise plans an Aggregate over the build keys through QueryExecution.prepareExecutedPlan as a SubqueryExec.

nodes.name: PlanAdaptiveSubqueries.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PlanAdaptiveSubqueries rule, which replaces logical subquery expressions in an adaptive physical plan with executable subquery expressions built from a precomputed map of subquery plans.

nodes.name: PlanAdaptiveSubqueries
nodes.summary: Case class taking a map from subquery expression id to its SparkPlan; a Rule[SparkPlan] that rewrites scalar subqueries, IN subqueries and dynamic pruning subqueries found in the plan expressions into their physical forms.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Transforms all expressions with scalar subquery, IN subquery or dynamic pruning subquery patterns: a ScalarSubquery becomes an execution ScalarSubquery over a SubqueryExec; an InSubquery becomes an InSubqueryExec (multiple values are packed with CreateNamedStruct, columns named col_N); a DynamicPruningSubquery becomes a DynamicPruningExpression over InSubqueryExec with a SubqueryAdaptiveBroadcastExec. Plans are looked up in subqueryMap by expression id.

nodes.name: ReuseAdaptiveSubquery.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ReuseAdaptiveSubquery rule, which replaces equal subqueries in an adaptive plan with ReusedSubqueryExec using a shared reuse map keyed by canonicalized plan.

nodes.name: ReuseAdaptiveSubquery
nodes.summary: Case class holding a concurrent TrieMap from SparkPlan to BaseSubqueryExec; a Rule[SparkPlan] that deduplicates subqueries when subquery reuse is enabled.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: If subquery reuse is enabled, visits each ExecSubqueryExpression, looks up (or inserts) its canonicalized plan in the reuse map, and when an earlier plan exists swaps in a ReusedSubqueryExec pointing at it.

nodes.name: ValidateSparkPlan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ValidateSparkPlan rule, which checks that AQE replanning did not produce a plan with a broadcast query stage in an invalid position and throws InvalidAQEPlanException if it did.

nodes.name: ValidateSparkPlan
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan] that is meant to run after EnsureRequirements. It returns the plan unchanged but throws if a BroadcastQueryStageExec appears anywhere other than as the immediate build side child of a BroadcastHashJoinExec or BroadcastNestedLoopJoinExec.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Runs validate on the plan and returns the same plan.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Recursively walks the plan; for broadcast hash joins and broadcast nested loop joins it skips validation of a build child that is a BroadcastQueryStageExec and validates the probe side; any other BroadcastQueryStageExec triggers an error, and other nodes validate their children.

nodes.name: errorOnInvalidBroadcastQueryStage
nodes.summary: Throws InvalidAQEPlanException with the message "Invalid broadcast query stage" for the given plan.

nodes.name: simpleCosting.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SimpleCost and SimpleCostEvaluator, the default implementation of the AQE plan cost interfaces, based on counting shuffle exchanges and skew joins.

nodes.name: SimpleCost
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping a Long cost value that implements Cost; it compares only with another SimpleCost and otherwise throws QueryExecutionErrors.cannotCompareCostWithTargetCostError.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares the Long values of two SimpleCosts returning -1, 1 or 0, and throws an error for a Cost of another type.

nodes.name: SimpleCostEvaluator
nodes.summary: Skew join aware CostEvaluator that counts ShuffleExchangeLike nodes in a plan. When forceOptimizeSkewedJoin is true it also counts skew joins (ShuffledJoin or BroadcastHashJoinExec with isSkewJoin) and packs the negated skew join count into the upper 32 bits so that more skew joins mean lower cost.

nodes.name: evaluateCost
nodes.summary: Counts shuffle exchanges in the plan and, if forceOptimizeSkewedJoin is set, skew joins, returning a SimpleCost where fewer shuffles and more skew joins give a lower value.

nodes.name: HashMapGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract HashMapGenerator, a helper that generates Java source for an append-only row-based hash map used as a fast cache for keyed aggregation in generated HashAggregate code.

nodes.name: HashMapGenerator
nodes.summary: Abstract class taking a CodegenContext, the aggregate expressions, the generated class name and the key and buffer schemas. generate() assembles a class from initializeAggregateHashMap, generateFindOrInsert, generateEquals, generateHashFunction, generateRowIterator and generateClose; subclasses supply the abstract pieces. The doc says the generated map does not support nullable keys, which fall back to BytesToBytesMap. It also builds initial buffer variables from the DeclarativeAggregate initial values.

nodes.name: Buffer
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a Spark DataType with the generated variable name; used for the grouping keys and the aggregation buffer values.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Returns the Java source of the whole generated hash map class by concatenating the pieces from initializeAggregateHashMap, generateFindOrInsert, generateEquals, generateHashFunction, generateRowIterator and generateClose.

nodes.name: generateHashFunction
nodes.summary: Generates the Java hash method over all grouping keys, combining per-key hashes from genComputeHash with the 0x9e3779b9 mixing step.

nodes.name: generateClose
nodes.summary: Generates a close method that closes the batch backing the map.

nodes.name: genComputeHash
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that hashes one key variable by data type: integral and date types as int, long, timestamp and time types as long, float and double via bits, decimals by unscaled long or bytes, strings by bytes or by collation hash function, and calendar intervals by hashCode.

nodes.name: MergingSessionsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MergingSessionsExec, a physical aggregate node that merges session windows and aggregates them in one pass over input sorted by group keys plus session start time.

nodes.name: MergingSessionsExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical node (a BaseAggregateExec) that is a variant of SortAggregateExec for session windows. The child must supply rows sorted by the grouping keys without the session expression, then the session expression. doExecute maps each partition through a MergingSessionsIterator, which merges session windows and applies the aggregations on the merged window, so inputs need not be buffered or copied. requiredChildDistributionExpressions and numShufflePartitions are supplied by the caller, so sessions can be merged within a local partition before a shuffle; with both set to None no shuffle is triggered but the sort still happens per partition. Defines a numOutputRows metric, and output and outputOrdering come from the child. For an empty partition it returns an empty iterator when there are grouping expressions, or a single row from outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput when there are none.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child output to be sorted ascending by the grouping expressions without the session expression, followed by the session expression.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs the child and wraps each partition in a MergingSessionsIterator built from the grouping, session, aggregate and result expressions. It handles the empty-input cases (empty iterator for grouped aggregates, one default row for global aggregates) and counts output rows with the numOutputRows metric.

nodes.name: MergingSessionsIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MergingSessionsIterator, the iterator behind MergingSessionsExec that walks rows sorted by group key and session start, merges overlapping session windows and emits one aggregated row per merged session.

nodes.name: MergingSessionsIterator
nodes.summary: AggregationIterator subclass, a variant of SortAggregateIterator for session windows. Input must be sorted by the group keys plus the start time of the session window. For each row it compares the grouping key and the session struct (start at field 0, end at field 1) with the current session: the same key with a start inside the current session extends the session end and updates the shared aggregation buffer; a later start or a different key begins the next group. Input that is not sorted or a null session struct raises an internal error and marks the iterator as corrupted. next() processes one merged session, builds the output grouping key from the grouping key and the merged session struct, generates the output row and resets the buffer, and counts rows in numOutputRows. outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput builds the single output row used when there is no input and no grouping.
