nodes.name: newBuffer
nodes.summary: Creates and initializes an aggregation buffer for all aggregate functions, using an UnsafeProjection-backed row when every buffer field type is mutable in UnsafeRow and a GenericInternalRow otherwise.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Reads the first input row (if any) to set the next grouping key, next session and first row of the next group, and throws an internal error when the session struct is null. It is invoked once from the class body.

nodes.name: processCurrentSortedGroup
nodes.summary: Consumes input rows for the current key and session: expands the session end for rows that start inside the current session, and stops at the first row of a different key or a later session, which it saves via startNewSession. Throws an internal error if the input is not sorted by session start.

nodes.name: startNewSession
nodes.summary: Copies the given row, grouping key and session struct into the next-group state so the following call starts from them.

nodes.name: expandEndOfCurrentSession
nodes.summary: Extends the end timestamp of the current session when the new row ends later. The helpers getSessionStart and getSessionEnd read the start and end longs of a session struct.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Reports whether another sorted group remains; throws an internal error if the iterator was already corrupted by bad input.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Processes the next merged session, generates the output row from the grouping key and aggregation buffer, resets the buffer and increments numOutputRows; throws NoSuchElementException when exhausted.

nodes.name: generateGroupingKey
nodes.summary: Joins the key without session and the current session struct and projects them into the full grouping key row.

nodes.name: outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput
nodes.summary: Initializes the buffer and generates the single output row used for an aggregate with no grouping expressions and no input rows.

nodes.name: ObjectAggregationIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ObjectAggregationIterator, the iterator used by ObjectHashAggregateExec that aggregates in an in-memory hash map and falls back to sort-based aggregation past a size threshold, and SortBasedAggregator, which merges sorted spills with sorted inputs.

nodes.name: ObjectAggregationIterator
nodes.summary: AggregationIterator (with Logging) that aggregates all input in its constructor through processInputs. It first uses hash-based aggregation with an ObjectAggregationMap of grouping key to aggregation buffer. When the map size reaches fallbackCountThreshold and input remains, it logs a message naming the SQLConf OBJECT_AGG_SORT_BASED_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD key, sets sortBased, and increments the numTasksFallBacked metric. It then dumps the map into an external sorter and feeds the remaining rows into a SortBasedAggregator. The mergeAggregationBuffers function is built by rewriting Partial aggregate expressions to PartialMerge and Complete ones to Final and calling initializeAggregateFunctions and generateProcessRow. A task completion listener records spill size into the spillSize metric. hasNext and next iterate the final buffer iterator and produce output rows with generateOutput.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregator
nodes.summary: Helper used together with ObjectHashAggregateExec for the sort-based fallback. addInput inserts (grouping key, input row) pairs into an UnsafeKVExternalSorter. destructiveIterator performs a two-way merge between the sorted initial aggregation buffers and the sorted inputs, picking the smaller grouping key each step (findGroupingKey), first applying processRow for input rows with that key and then mergeAggregationBuffers for existing buffers of that key (findNextSortedGroup), and returns AggregationBufferEntry values. No method may be called after destructiveIterator. The sorter is created from SparkEnv with spill thresholds taken from config.SHUFFLE_SPILL_NUM_ELEMENTS_FORCE_SPILL_THRESHOLD and SHUFFLE_SPILL_MAX_SIZE_FORCE_SPILL_THRESHOLD. A TODO in the source says to eliminate it by reusing the SortAggregateExec code paths.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Takes the next AggregationBufferEntry, generates the output row from its grouping key and buffer, and increments numOutputRows. hasNext (lines 94-96) delegates to the buffer iterator.

nodes.name: outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput
nodes.summary: Generates the single output row from a fresh default aggregation buffer when there are no grouping expressions; throws an internal error if grouping expressions exist.

nodes.name: createNewAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Allocates a SpecificInternalRow sized from the aggregate functions buffer attributes and initializes it; used for new groups and for the sort-based fallback buffer.

nodes.name: initAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Initializes declarative aggregate buffer values with the initial projection and calls initialize on every imperative aggregate.

nodes.name: getAggregationBufferByKey
nodes.summary: Looks up the aggregation buffer for a grouping key in the hash map, creating and storing a new buffer (with a copy of the key) if absent.

nodes.name: processInputs
nodes.summary: Reads all input rows. Without grouping expressions it reuses one buffer; otherwise it aggregates into the hash map until the size threshold triggers fallback, then builds a SortBasedAggregator from the sorted map dump, routes remaining rows to it, and sets aggBufferIterator to either the sort-based or the hash-map destructive iterator.

nodes.name: addInput
nodes.summary: Inserts a grouping key and input row pair into the external sorter for later merging.

nodes.name: destructiveIterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator of AggregationBufferEntry by two-way merging the sorted initial aggregation buffers and the sorted input rows by grouping key; input rows are processed before existing buffers are merged. Contains the inner helpers findNextSortedGroup and findGroupingKey.

nodes.name: createExternalSorterForInput
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeKVExternalSorter keyed by the grouping schema over the input schema, using the block manager, serializer manager, task page size and shuffle spill thresholds.

nodes.name: RowBasedHashMapGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RowBasedHashMapGenerator, a code generator that emits the Java source of an append-only row-based hash map used as a fast first-level cache in generated hash aggregation code.

nodes.name: RowBasedHashMapGenerator
nodes.summary: Subclass of HashMapGenerator that generates a Java class holding an append-only row-based hash map (backed by RowBasedKeyValueBatch, load factor 0.5, a bucket int array and a small maxSteps probe limit) for very fast key-value lookups during aggregation, with fallback to the BytesToBytesMap when a key is not found. It is the row-based counterpart of VectorizedHashMapGenerator; one of the two is chosen as the first-level map. It currently does not support nullable keys, which fall back to BytesToBytesMap. The generated pieces are the constructor and fields, the equals method for group-by keys, findOrInsert (hash, linear probing, append of a new key row with the empty value buffer, return null when full) and rowIterator.

nodes.name: initializeAggregateHashMap
nodes.summary: Returns the Java source for the fields and constructor of the generated hash map: it allocates the RowBasedKeyValueBatch from the key and value schemas, copies the empty aggregation buffer bytes, creates an UnsafeRowWriter sized for variable-length keys, and fills the bucket array with -1.

nodes.name: generateEquals
nodes.summary: Returns the Java source of an equals(idx, keys...) method that compares the stored key row at a bucket with the given group-by key values using ctx.genEqual.

nodes.name: generateFindOrInsert
nodes.summary: Returns the Java source of findOrInsert: it hashes the keys, probes up to maxSteps buckets, writes a new key row with UnsafeRowWriter and appends it to the batch when an empty slot is found, returns the existing value row when the key matches, and returns null when there is no room. Throws IllegalArgumentException for key types other than primitives, strings, calendar intervals and decimals.

nodes.name: generateRowIterator
nodes.summary: Returns the Java source of rowIterator, which returns the batch row iterator as a KVIterator of UnsafeRow pairs.

nodes.name: TypedAggregateExpression.scala
nodes.summary: Hooks a typed Aggregator into the aggregation system: a factory object, a common trait, and two AggregateFunction implementations (declarative for simple buffers, imperative for complex ones).

nodes.name: TypedAggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Companion object plus trait for typed aggregates (the object spans lines 32-82 and the trait lines 87-110). The object apply(aggregator) builds the buffer and output encoders and checks whether the buffer serializer is an Alias of a BoundReference not serialized as struct; if so it returns SimpleTypedAggregateExpression (supports whole stage codegen), otherwise ComplexTypedAggregateExpression. The trait, a helper that hooks an Aggregator into the aggregation system and extends AggregateFunction, declares aggregator, inputDeserializer, inputClass, inputSchema and withInputInfo, and defines toString (nodeName plus the input type) and nodeName from the aggregator class simple name.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that chooses between SimpleTypedAggregateExpression and ComplexTypedAggregateExpression for an Aggregator based on whether its buffer object needs serialization; wires in buffer serializer and deserializer and output encoder parts.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Prints the node name with the input deserializer data type, or unknown when no input is set.

nodes.name: SimpleTypedAggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Case class DeclarativeAggregate (also TypedAggregateExpression and NonSQLExpression) used when the buffer is simple. It expresses the aggregator as catalyst expressions: initialValues from aggregator.zero, updateExpressions by invoking reduce, mergeExpressions by invoking merge on left and right buffer references, and evaluateExpression by invoking finish and serializing the result (producing a null struct when the object is null for struct output). It is resolved once inputDeserializer is defined, and withInputInfo copies in the input deserializer, class and schema.

nodes.name: serializeToBuffer
nodes.summary: Replaces BoundReference nodes in the buffer serializer with a given expression, to write an object value into the buffer columns.

nodes.name: initialValues
nodes.summary: Initial buffer values: the aggregator zero value serialized into the buffer attributes.

nodes.name: updateExpressions
nodes.summary: Update expressions that invoke the aggregator reduce method on the deserialized buffer and the input, then serialize the result.

nodes.name: mergeExpressions
nodes.summary: Merge expressions that invoke the aggregator merge method on the left and right deserialized buffers and serialize the result.

nodes.name: evaluateExpression
nodes.summary: Final expression that invokes the aggregator finish method and serializes the result with the output serializer, wrapping struct output so a null object gives a null struct.

nodes.name: ComplexTypedAggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Case class TypedImperativeAggregate (also TypedAggregateExpression and NonSQLExpression) used when the buffer object needs serialization. It keeps the buffer as an object: createAggregationBuffer returns aggregator.zero, update and merge call aggregator reduce and merge (skipping null input objects), eval calls finish and converts the result with an UnsafeProjection, and serialize and deserialize convert the buffer object to and from UnsafeRow bytes with generated projections. It also has mutableAggBufferOffset and inputAggBufferOffset with copy-based setters.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Converts the input row to an object with a safe projection and calls aggregator.reduce on the buffer, returning the buffer unchanged for null input objects.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges two buffer objects with aggregator.merge.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Calls aggregator.finish on the buffer and converts the result object to its internal value, returning null for a null result.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes the buffer object to bytes through the buffer serializer projection.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Restores the buffer object from bytes by pointing an UnsafeRow at them and applying the buffer deserializer.

nodes.name: UpdatingSessionsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UpdatingSessionsExec, a physical node that rewrites the session window of every input row from neighbor rows, keeping the row count unchanged, for cases where session assignment and aggregation cannot be done together.

nodes.name: UpdatingSessionsExec
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryExecNode that updates the session window spec of each input row by analyzing neighbor rows and deciding which belong to the same session; the number of rows stays the same. The source says it has much more overhead than MergingSessionsExec, which should be used whenever possible, and this node only when session determination and aggregation cannot be done together. doExecute reads the in-memory, spill and spill-size thresholds for the session window buffer from conf (sessionWindowBufferInMemoryThreshold, sessionWindowBufferSpillThreshold, sessionWindowBufferSpillSizeThreshold) and maps each partition through UpdatingSessionsIterator. Output and output partitioning come from the child. Distribution: AllTuples when there are no grouping keys besides the session; for streaming, StatefulOperatorPartitioning.getCompatibleDistribution using numShufflePartitions (internal error if unset); otherwise ClusteredDistribution. Ordering: ascending by grouping keys without session, then the session expression.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Reads the session window buffer thresholds from the SQL conf and runs the child with each partition wrapped in an UpdatingSessionsIterator.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Chooses the required distribution: AllTuples when only the session expression groups, a streaming-compatible stateful operator distribution when streaming (needs numShufflePartitions), or ClusteredDistribution on the grouping keys without the session otherwise.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child sorted ascending by the grouping attributes without the session followed by the session attribute.

nodes.name: udaf.scala
nodes.summary: Adapts user-defined aggregates to the internal aggregation code path. It holds ScalaUDAF (wraps a UserDefinedAggregateFunction as an ImperativeAggregate), ScalaAggregator (wraps a typed Aggregator as a TypedImperativeAggregate, with a companion factory taking a UserDefinedAggregator), the row views over aggregation buffers, and the ResolveEncodersInScalaAgg rule that resolves and binds the encoders of a ScalaAggregator.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a sealed helper trait that builds per-type getter and setter closures, and expressions that use lazy vals and @transient fields.

nodes.name: BufferSetterGetterUtils
nodes.summary: Sealed helper trait that builds specialized getter and setter closures, one per field of a buffer schema, through createGetters and createSetters. Each closure reads or writes a single typed value of an InternalRow by ordinal, mapping each Spark data type (boolean, numeric, decimal, date, timestamp, interval and others) to the matching primitive accessor. Mixed into the aggregation buffer row classes of this file; the comment says it targets the buffer types supported by UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap.

nodes.name: createGetters
nodes.summary: Builds an array of getter functions, one per schema field, each taking an InternalRow and an ordinal and returning the value as a boxed object or null. The getter is chosen by a match on the field data type (NullType, BooleanType, ByteType, ShortType, IntegerType, LongType, FloatType, DoubleType, DecimalType, DateType, timestamp and time types, year-month and day-time intervals, any other type through row.get).

nodes.name: createSetters
nodes.summary: Builds an array of setter functions, one per schema field, each writing a value into an InternalRow at an ordinal and calling setNullAt for null values. Decimal fields call setDecimal with the precision instead of setNullAt, because of the way UnsafeRow handles decimals, as stated in the code comment; unknown types fall back to row.update.

nodes.name: MutableAggregationBufferImpl
nodes.summary: Private mutable Row view over a slice of an InternalRow aggregation buffer, starting at bufferOffset. It implements MutableAggregationBuffer so a user-defined aggregate can read and update buffer values: get converts the stored value to a Scala value and update converts a Scala value to its Catalyst form before writing. Both check the index range and isNullAt is forwarded to the underlying buffer. ScalaUDAF swaps the underlyingBuffer field before every call.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the i-th buffer value after bounds checking, by reading it with the typed getter from the underlying InternalRow and converting it to a Scala value; throws IllegalArgumentException when the index is out of range.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Writes the i-th buffer value after bounds checking, converting the Scala value to its Catalyst form and storing it with the typed setter into the underlying InternalRow.

nodes.name: InputAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Private read-only Row view over a slice of an InternalRow buffer, starting at bufferOffset. It is used as the immutable input buffer passed to the merge and evaluate steps of a user-defined aggregate; get reads through the typed getters and converts to Scala values. It has a getBufferOffset accessor, a copy method and an isNullAt that is forwarded to the underlying input buffer.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the i-th buffer value after bounds checking, using the typed getter on the underlying input InternalRow and a conversion to a Scala value; throws IllegalArgumentException for an invalid index.

nodes.name: ScalaUDAF
nodes.summary: Case class expression that wraps a UserDefinedAggregateFunction so it can run in the internal aggregation code path as an ImperativeAggregate. It derives input types, buffer schema and buffer attributes from the udaf, and lazily creates converters, an input projection and three buffer views (input, mutable and evaluate). initialize, update, merge and eval point those buffers at the Catalyst buffer rows and delegate to the corresponding udaf methods. Its name defaults to the simple class name of the udaf unless udafName is given.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Points the mutable aggregation buffer at the given buffer row and calls udaf.initialize on it.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Points the mutable buffer at the given row, projects the input row through the input projection, converts it to a Scala Row and calls udaf.update.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Points the mutable buffer at the first buffer row and the input buffer at the second, then calls udaf.merge to combine them.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Points the evaluate buffer at the given row, calls udaf.evaluate and converts the result to the Catalyst representation.

nodes.name: ScalaAggregator
nodes.summary: Case class expression that wraps a typed Aggregator[IN, BUF, OUT] as a TypedImperativeAggregate, using ExpressionEncoders for the input, the buffer and the output. createAggregationBuffer returns agg.zero, update calls agg.reduce on a deserialized input, merge calls agg.merge, eval calls agg.finish and serializes the output, and serialize and deserialize turn the buffer into bytes through an UnsafeRow. The companion object (lines 557-570) has an apply(uda: UserDefinedAggregator, children) factory that builds the instance and takes the encoders from the UserDefinedAggregator.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Folds one input row into the buffer: projects the row, deserializes it with the input encoder and returns agg.reduce(buffer, input).

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Calls agg.finish on the buffer and serializes the result with the output encoder; returns the whole row when the output is serialized as a struct at top level, otherwise the first field.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes a buffer object to a byte array through the buffer encoder serializer and UnsafeRow.getBytes.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a buffer object from bytes by pointing a reusable UnsafeRow at the array and applying the buffer encoder deserializer.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a ScalaAggregator from a UserDefinedAggregator and child expressions, taking the aggregator, nullability, determinism and given name from the UserDefinedAggregator and encoders via encoderFor.

nodes.name: ResolveEncodersInScalaAgg
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] used as an extension rule. For every resolved operator it transforms the expressions bottom-up and, for each ScalaAggregator, replaces the input and buffer encoders with resolveAndBind() versions; unresolved plans are returned unchanged.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Walks the plan with resolveOperatorsUp, skipping unresolved nodes, and rewrites each ScalaAggregator expression so that its input and buffer encoders are resolved and bound.

nodes.name: costing.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable cost abstraction of adaptive query execution: the Cost trait (an Ordered[Cost]), the CostEvaluator trait that computes the cost of a physical plan, and the CostEvaluator companion object that instantiates an evaluator from a configured class name.
nodes.languageNotes: Both traits are marked @Unstable and the comments say they may change or move.

nodes.name: Cost
nodes.summary: Marker trait, annotated Unstable, that represents the cost of a plan and extends Ordered[Cost] so costs can be compared.

nodes.name: CostEvaluator
nodes.summary: Unstable trait with a single method evaluateCost(plan: SparkPlan): Cost that evaluates the cost of a physical plan, plus a companion object (lines 45-58, with Logging) whose instantiate(className, conf) loads the evaluator class through Utils.loadExtensions. The error message of instantiate names the config SQLConf.ADAPTIVE_CUSTOM_COST_EVALUATOR_CLASS.

nodes.name: instantiate
nodes.summary: Loads the CostEvaluator class given by className with Utils.loadExtensions and returns the first instance; requires at least one result and otherwise fails with a message that names the config key from SQLConf.ADAPTIVE_CUSTOM_COST_EVALUATOR_CLASS.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionsUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Holds ShufflePartitionsUtil, the helper adaptive query execution uses to coalesce small shuffle partitions up to a target size (with or without skew-join partition specs) and to split skewed reducer partitions by map output size into partial reducer specs.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionsUtil
nodes.summary: Object (with Logging) with two constants, SMALL_PARTITION_FACTOR = 0.2 and MERGED_PARTITION_FACTOR = 1.2. coalescePartitions picks a target size from the advisory size, the minimum number of partitions and the minimum partition size, then packs consecutive shuffle partitions of all shuffles into CoalescedPartitionSpecs, keeping skew sections intact when skew specs are present. createSkewPartitionSpecs and optimizeSkewedPartitions split a partition bigger than a skew threshold by map output sizes into PartialReducerPartitionSpecs, using splitSizeListByTargetSize and the sizes read from the MapOutputTrackerMaster.

nodes.name: coalescePartitions
nodes.summary: Entry point for coalescing: validates that statistics and input specs have equal length, computes the target size as the advisory size capped by total size divided by minNumPartitions and floored at minPartitionSize, logs the sizes, and dispatches to the no-skew or skew variant depending on whether any input partition specs are present. Returns the new specs for each shuffle, or an empty result if no coalescing applies.

nodes.name: coalescePartitionsWithoutSkew
nodes.summary: Coalesces all shuffles when no skew specs exist. It makes an empty partition per shuffle if all inputs have zero partitions, refuses (with a warning) when the shuffles have different partition counts, and otherwise computes coalesced specs over the full range and attaches data sizes, returning nothing if the partition count did not shrink.

nodes.name: coalescePartitionsWithSkew
nodes.summary: Coalesces shuffles whose partitions already carry skew-join specs. It derives a start index for each spec, checks they match across shuffles, finds sections where an index repeats (skewed partitions) and copies those specs unchanged, and coalesces only the partitions before, between and after the skew sections. Returns a result only if the number of partitions decreased.

nodes.name: coalescePartitionsAndGetSpecs
nodes.summary: Packs the partitions in [start, end) of several shuffles into CoalescedPartitionSpecs: it sums the size of each index across shuffles and starts a new coalesced partition when adding the next one would exceed the target size. Partitions below minPartitionSize are merged into the smaller neighbor, and an empty result is avoided unless allowReturnEmpty is set. The doc comment gives a worked example with two shuffles and a 128 MiB target.

nodes.name: attachDataSize
nodes.summary: For each shuffle, copies the coalesced specs with a dataSize equal to the sum of its partition bytes in the range of each spec, or zero when the shuffle has no map statistics.

nodes.name: splitSizeListByTargetSize
nodes.summary: Takes an array of sizes and returns the start indices that split it into groups whose sums are close to the target size. A nested tryMergePartitions merges a group into the previous one when the two together stay below target size times MERGED_PARTITION_FACTOR, or when either is smaller than target size times the small-partition factor. Private[sql] and marked visible for testing.

nodes.name: getMapSizesForReduceId
nodes.summary: Reads from the MapOutputTrackerMaster the size of the block for a reducer id from every map output of a shuffle; the size is -1 for a missing map output (for example after executor loss).

nodes.name: createSkewPartitionSpecs
nodes.summary: Splits one skewed reducer partition by map output sizes into PartialReducerPartitionSpecs of about the target size, each with start map index, end map index and data size. Returns None when some map output is missing or when the split yields only one part.

nodes.name: optimizeSkewedPartitions
nodes.summary: Goes through the bytes of every reduce partition: partitions above skewThreshold are split with createSkewPartitionSpecs (falling back to a single CoalescedPartitionSpec if no split is possible), the others become single-partition CoalescedPartitionSpecs.

nodes.name: V2ViewInspectionExecs.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan nodes for the read-side commands on v2 views: SHOW CREATE TABLE, SHOW TBLPROPERTIES, SHOW COLUMNS, DESCRIBE TABLE and DESCRIBE TABLE ... COLUMN. Each exec receives the resolved View object and formats output rows from it; the file comment says only non-session v2 views reach these execs, since session catalog views are rewritten to v1 commands earlier.

nodes.name: ShowCreateV2ViewExec
nodes.summary: Case class exec for SHOW CREATE TABLE on a v2 view. run builds a single CREATE VIEW statement from the View: the column list with comments from the schema, a COMMENT clause, a DEFAULT COLLATION clause, the user TBLPROPERTIES (sorted, with the reserved keys from CatalogV2Util.TABLE_RESERVED_PROPERTIES removed), WITH SCHEMA when schema binding is enabled, and AS followed by the query text. Returns one output row.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Assembles the CREATE VIEW text piece by piece (name, columns, comment, collation, properties, optional schema mode, query text) and returns it as one Catalyst row.

nodes.name: showViewDataColumns
nodes.summary: Appends the parenthesized column list to the builder, quoting names when needed and adding each field comment.

nodes.name: showViewProperties
nodes.summary: Appends a sorted TBLPROPERTIES clause with the view properties that are not in the reserved set, escaping quotes in keys and values.

nodes.name: ShowV2ViewPropertiesExec
nodes.summary: Case class exec for SHOW TBLPROPERTIES on a v2 view. It redacts the properties through conf.redactOptions; with a requested key it returns that value (even for a reserved key) or a message that the view lacks the property, and without a key it returns all non-reserved properties sorted by key.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Redacts the view properties, then returns either one value row (or a key and value row, depending on the output width) for a requested key or all non-reserved properties as sorted key and value rows.

nodes.name: ShowV2ViewColumnsExec
nodes.summary: Case class exec for SHOW COLUMNS on a v2 view; its run method returns one row with the name of each top-level field of the view schema.

nodes.name: DescribeV2ViewExec
nodes.summary: Case class exec for DESCRIBE TABLE on a v2 view. It first outputs a row (name, data type, comment) for each schema column. With EXTENDED it adds the section '# Detailed View Information': identifier rows from addIdentifierRows, Type, Owner, Comment, Collation, View Text, View Current Catalog, View Current Namespace, View Schema Mode, View Query Output Columns and a redacted Properties row. It ends with default-column metadata rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds the DESCRIBE output: schema rows, then for EXTENDED the detailed view information rows (identifier, type, owner, comment, collation, text, current catalog and namespace, schema mode, query columns, redacted properties), then the default value metadata of the schema.

nodes.name: DescribeV2ViewColumnExec
nodes.summary: Case class exec for DESCRIBE TABLE ... COLUMN on a v2 view. It rejects nested column names, finds the field by the session resolver, and returns rows for col_name, data_type and comment; with EXTENDED it adds NULL rows for the statistics names (min, max, num_nulls, distinct_count, avg_col_len, max_col_len, histogram) and a default row if the column has a default value in its metadata.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Resolves the single column name against the view schema (throwing a nested-column or column-not-found error), then returns the column description rows and, for EXTENDED, the NULL statistics rows and an optional default row.

nodes.name: AQETestHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Testing-only helper object for adaptive query execution that can force a running query to cancel and replan once, triggered when chosen SQL metrics become non-zero.

nodes.name: AQETestHelper
nodes.summary: Object with a volatile set of trigger metric ids and a set of plan ids already cancelled. withForcedCancellation(triggerMetrics)(thunk) sets the metric ids for the duration of the thunk and clears the state afterwards. isForcedCancellationEnabled, shouldForceCancellation and markForcedCancellationTriggeredForPlan let the execution check, per plan, whether a one-time forced cancellation should happen (only when Utils.isTesting is true and a trigger metric is non-zero).

nodes.name: withForcedCancellation
nodes.summary: Stores the ids of the trigger metrics, runs the given block and in a finally clause resets the metric ids and the set of already-triggered plans; returns the block result.

nodes.name: isForcedCancellationEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns true when running in testing mode and at least one trigger metric id is registered.

nodes.name: markForcedCancellationTriggeredForPlan
nodes.summary: Records the plan id as cancelled, asserting that the same plan is not forced to cancel a second time.

nodes.name: shouldForceCancellation
nodes.summary: Decides whether to force a cancellation for the plan: in testing mode, not yet triggered for this plan, and at least one trigger metric accumulator (looked up through AccumulatorContext) is non-zero.

nodes.name: ObjectAggregationMap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ObjectAggregationMap, a hash map from grouping keys to safe aggregation buffers that can hold arbitrary Java objects as aggregate state, together with the AggregationBufferEntry key and buffer holder. Used with ObjectHashAggregateExec, and it can spill its content to an external sorter.

nodes.name: ObjectAggregationMap
nodes.summary: Wraps a LinkedHashMap from UnsafeRow grouping key to InternalRow buffer, with getAggregationBuffer, putAggregationBuffer, size and clear. destructiveIterator hands out AggregationBufferEntry items while removing them, and dumpToExternalSorter moves all entries into a new UnsafeKVExternalSorter (serializing buffers of TypedImperativeAggregate functions in place) and clears the map. Per its comment, it is only used together with ObjectHashAggregateExec.

nodes.name: AggregationBufferEntry
nodes.summary: Simple holder class with two mutable fields, groupingKey (UnsafeRow) and aggregationBuffer (InternalRow), returned by the destructive iterator of ObjectAggregationMap.

nodes.name: destructiveIterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over AggregationBufferEntry values that removes each entry from the map as it is returned; the comment says no method may be called after this one.

nodes.name: dumpToExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeKVExternalSorter from the grouping and buffer attributes with spill thresholds taken from SparkEnv config, drains the map through destructiveIterator, serializes TypedImperativeAggregate buffers in place, inserts each key and projected buffer into the sorter, clears the map and returns the sorter.

nodes.name: UpdatingSessionsIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UpdatingSessionsIterator, an iterator over rows sorted by grouping keys and session start time that rewrites each row so it carries the merged session window of its session. A later aggregation can then group the rows of one session together.

nodes.name: UpdatingSessionsIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator[InternalRow] that tracks the current grouping keys and current session, copies each incoming row, buffers rows of the same session in an ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray, widens the session end when later rows overlap it, and on session or key change replays the buffered rows with the final session value restored in the session column. It requires input sorted by group keys plus session start and throws an internal error otherwise. The doc comment says the copying and buffering make it costlier than MergingSessionsIterator, which should be used whenever possible.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class extending Iterator; public methods hasNext and next, with private helpers for session bookkeeping. The accessor-like helpers getSessionStart, getSessionEnd and updateSessionEnd have no nodes.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Checks the iterator is not corrupted, returns true while previously prepared return rows remain, then clears the finished return buffer and falls back to whether the input iterator has more rows.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next row of a closed session. When none are ready it consumes input rows, copying each one, comparing its grouping keys and session start with the current session, expanding or closing the current session, and raises an error if the sort precondition is broken. At end of input it closes the last session.

nodes.name: startNewSession
nodes.summary: Begins a new current session: fails if the grouping key was already processed (sort violation), stores copies of the key and session struct, and allocates a new ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray holding the first row.

nodes.name: expandEndOfCurrentSession
nodes.summary: Raises the end of the current session to the given value when it is later than the stored end.

nodes.name: handleBrokenPreconditionForSort
nodes.summary: Marks the iterator as corrupted and throws an internal SparkException saying the iterator must be sorted by key and session start.

nodes.name: generateGroupingKey
nodes.summary: Builds the full grouping key by joining the current grouping-without-session keys with a one-column row holding the current session struct.

nodes.name: closeCurrentSession
nodes.summary: Finishes the current session: hands its buffered rows over for return, projects each row's values and restores the full input schema with the final session value, appends the result to any unconsumed return iterator, records the key as processed when the key changed, and resets the current key and session.

nodes.name: assertIteratorNotCorrupted
nodes.summary: Throws an internal SparkException if an earlier error already marked the iterator as corrupted.

nodes.name: VectorizedHashMapGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines VectorizedHashMapGenerator, a code generator that emits Java source for an append-only vectorized hash map used as a fast cache for key-value lookups while evaluating hash aggregates. The generated map falls back to BytesToBytesMap for keys it cannot hold.

nodes.name: VectorizedHashMapGenerator
nodes.summary: Subclass of HashMapGenerator that produces the text of a generated class backed by a power-of-2 index array with linear probing (maxSteps of 2, load factor 0.5) and a columnar batch of OnHeapColumnVector columns that stores keys and aggregate buffers. It generates the constructor and fields, an equals method, a findOrInsert method returning a MutableColumnarRow (or null when the key is missing or the map is full), and a rowIterator method. The doc comment notes it does not support nullable keys.
nodes.languageNotes: The methods build Java source strings with Scala string interpolation and stripMargin; the generated code is shown in the scaladoc examples.

nodes.name: initializeAggregateHashMap
nodes.summary: Generates the fields (vectors, batch, aggBufferRow, buckets, capacity from bitMaxCapacity, loadFactor, numBuckets, maxSteps, numRows) and the constructor that allocates the column vectors, builds the ColumnarBatch, makes a projection over the aggregate buffer columns only, and fills the buckets with -1.

nodes.name: generateEquals
nodes.summary: Generates a private equals(idx, keys...) method that compares the group-by keys stored in the column vectors at buckets[idx] with the given key arguments.

nodes.name: generateFindOrInsert
nodes.summary: Generates the public findOrInsert method: hashes the keys, probes up to maxSteps buckets, returns the existing row if the key matches, otherwise writes the keys and initial aggregate buffer values at numRows and returns the MutableColumnarRow, or null when out of space or after too many probes.

nodes.name: generateRowIterator
nodes.summary: Generates a rowIterator method that sets the batch row count to numRows and returns the batch row iterator.

nodes.name: ValidateRequirements.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ValidateRequirements object, which checks that a physical plan satisfies each operator's required child distribution and ordering, and that multi-child operators with clustered distributions have compatible (co-partitioned) children.

nodes.name: ValidateRequirements
nodes.summary: Scala object (extends Logging) that offers two validate overloads and a private validateInternal. validate(plan) recursively checks all children and then the node itself; validate(plan, requiredDistribution) also requires the plan's outputPartitioning to satisfy the given distribution. Failures are logged at debug level and reported as false.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Two overloads share this node. validate(plan) returns true when every child validates recursively and validateInternal holds for the plan (lines 37-39, the range used here); validate(plan, requiredDistribution) additionally requires plan.outputPartitioning to satisfy the distribution (lines 33-35).

nodes.name: validateInternal
nodes.summary: Checks one operator: each child's outputPartitioning must satisfy its requiredChildDistribution and its outputOrdering must satisfy the required ordering. When there are several children and all required distributions are ClusteredDistribution, it also builds a shuffle spec per child and requires every spec to be compatible with the first.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SortMergeJoinEvaluatorFactory, a PartitionEvaluatorFactory that builds the per-partition evaluator running a sort-merge join over two sorted input iterators for inner, left outer, right outer, full outer, left semi, left anti and existence joins.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow] constructed with the join keys, join type, optional condition, left and right plans, output attributes, spill thresholds (in-memory, spill and size-in-bytes), the numOutputRows and spillSize metrics and the onlyBufferFirstMatchedRow flag. createEvaluator returns a new private SortMergeJoinEvaluator.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private nested PartitionEvaluator whose eval method receives the left and right row iterators of a partition and returns the join result iterator, choosing the iteration strategy from the join type. It wraps SortMergeJoinScanner and reuses LeftOuterIterator, RightOuterIterator and FullOuterIterator for the outer joins.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Returns a new SortMergeJoinEvaluator for a partition.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Asserts two input iterators, binds the optional join condition to the combined output, builds the key ordering and result projection, and then matches on the join type: inner joins use an anonymous RowIterator over SortMergeJoinScanner.findNextInnerJoinRows; LeftOuter, RightOuter and FullOuter use the dedicated iterators; LeftSemi, LeftAnti and ExistenceJoin use anonymous RowIterators over the scanner's inner or outer match search; any other join type raises IllegalArgumentException. Each emitted row increments numOutputRows.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Calls cleanupResources on the left and right child plans; it is passed to the scanners as the cleanup callback.

nodes.name: createLeftKeyGenerator
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeProjection that extracts the left join keys from rows of the left child output.

nodes.name: createRightKeyGenerator
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeProjection that extracts the right join keys from rows of the right child output.

nodes.name: SegmentTreeWindowFunctionFrame.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SegmentTreeWindowFunctionFrame, a moving-frame window function frame that answers each frame's aggregate from a WindowSegmentTree, with a fallback to SlidingWindowFunctionFrame for small partitions.

nodes.name: SegmentTreeWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Private[window] final WindowFunctionFrame (also AutoCloseable) for RowFrame or single-column RangeFrame moving frames whose aggregates are all DeclarativeAggregate without FILTER or DISTINCT. In prepare it either delegates to a lazily created SlidingWindowFunctionFrame (when the partition has fewer rows than spark.sql.window.segmentTree.minPartitionRows) or builds a WindowSegmentTree over the partition rows and keeps monotone lowerBound and upperBound cursors; write then queries the tree for the current frame. A task-completion listener registered in the class body closes it. currentLowerBound and currentUpperBound delegate to the fallback when it is in use. Documented as not thread-safe.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with many private[this] vars and an initializer block that registers a TaskContext completion listener.

nodes.name: newFallback
nodes.summary: Allocates a fresh SlidingWindowFunctionFrame for the small-partition path; called lazily from prepare and factored out so tests can inject a failing fallback.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Called once per partition and frame with the buffered rows. Small partitions prepare the fallback sliding frame and reset segment tree state; larger ones drop the fallback, build a WindowSegmentTree with the configured fanout, block size and cache limit over the rows, bump the segment tree frame metric, and set up row cursors (a single bound iterator for RowFrame, lower and upper iterators plus pre-fetched head rows for RangeFrame).

nodes.name: resetSegtreeState
nodes.summary: Closes and clears the current tree, drops row iterators and cursor rows, and resets lowerBound and upperBound to 0.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the aggregate result for the row at the given index: delegates to the fallback frame when it is in use, otherwise dispatches to writeRow for RowFrame or writeRange for RangeFrame.

nodes.name: writeRow
nodes.summary: RowFrame path: an admit loop extends upperBound (advancing lowerBound in step when a row is already below the lower bound), a drop loop advances lowerBound to the frame's left edge, and when either bound changed it calls the tree's queryInto to compute the frame aggregate into the target row.

nodes.name: writeRange
nodes.summary: RangeFrame path: an admit loop advances upperBound using the upper cursor, a drop loop advances lowerBound using the lower cursor (guarded by lowerBound < upperBound), and when bounds changed it calls queryInto, which also handles an empty frame.

nodes.name: closeIters
nodes.summary: Drops references to the open row-array iterators (bound, lower and upper); idempotent. The comment explains the iterator's close method is protected and the backing sorter is released by the enclosing window operator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the segment tree if present and drops iterator references; also registered as the task completion callback.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WindowGroupLimitExec physical operator and its helper iterators. The operator filters out rows that cannot satisfy a rank-based limit (row number, rank or dense rank) before the window operator, working per partition group.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitMode
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the two modes of WindowGroupLimitExec.

nodes.name: Partial
nodes.summary: Case object WindowGroupLimitMode meaning the limit operator runs before the shuffle (no extra distribution required).

nodes.name: Final
nodes.summary: Case object WindowGroupLimitMode meaning the limit operator runs after the shuffle; it requires AllTuples when there is no partition spec, otherwise a ClusteredDistribution on the partition spec.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitExec
nodes.summary: Unary physical operator (case class with partitionSpec, orderSpec, rankLikeFunction, limit, mode, child) that keeps only rows whose rank within a partition is below the limit, for top-k queries. It declares the child distribution per mode, requires the child ordered by partition spec ascending then order spec, passes through the child's output, ordering and partitioning, exposes a numOutputRows metric, and executes through WindowGroupLimitEvaluatorFactory.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: In Partial mode returns the default distribution; in Final mode returns AllTuples when partitionSpec is empty and otherwise ClusteredDistribution(partitionSpec).

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child to be sorted ascending by the partition spec followed by the order spec.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Creates a WindowGroupLimitEvaluatorFactory and runs it over the child's RDD, using mapPartitionsWithEvaluator when conf.usePartitionEvaluator is set and otherwise mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal with a created evaluator per partition.

nodes.name: BaseLimitIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract Iterator[InternalRow] that stops when the rank reaches the limit. Subclasses define increaseRank and reset; next reads the next UnsafeRow from the input, updates the rank, and increments numOutputRows.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Throws NoSuchElementException when exhausted, otherwise takes the next input row as an UnsafeRow, calls increaseRank, bumps the output row metric and returns the row. (hasNext is a one-line check of rank < limit and input.hasNext.)

nodes.name: SimpleLimitIterator
nodes.summary: BaseLimitIterator that increments the rank by one for every row, which implements row-number style limits; reset sets rank to 0.

nodes.name: OrderSpecProvider
nodes.summary: Trait giving iterators a generated ordering over the order spec and the output attributes, plus a currentRankRow variable used to detect ties.

nodes.name: RankLimitIterator
nodes.summary: BaseLimitIterator with OrderSpecProvider for rank: counts rows and, when the current row's order key differs from the previous rank row, sets rank to the row count (so ties share a rank and gaps follow them).

nodes.name: increaseRank
nodes.summary: Copies the first row as the current rank row; for later rows compares the order key with it and, on a difference, sets rank to the running count and replaces the rank row; then increments count.

nodes.name: DenseRankLimitIterator
nodes.summary: BaseLimitIterator with OrderSpecProvider for dense rank: increments the rank by one each time the order key changes from the previous row.

nodes.name: increaseRank
nodes.summary: Sets the current rank row from the first row; afterwards increments rank by one whenever the order key differs from the current rank row and replaces that row.

nodes.name: GroupedLimitIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over rows sorted by partition spec that applies a per-group limit iterator (created by createLimitIterator) to each group, skipping the rest of a group once its limit is reached and resetting the limit iterator for the next group. It uses an UnsafeProjection of the partition spec to detect group boundaries.

nodes.name: fetchNextRow
nodes.summary: Reads the next input row as an UnsafeRow and computes its group key, or marks that no more rows are available.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: True while rows remain and the limit iterator has more; when the limit iterator is exhausted it skips the remaining rows of the current group and resets the limit iterator for the next group.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Throws NoSuchElementException when hasNext is false, otherwise returns the next row from the limit iterator.

nodes.name: GroupIterator
nodes.summary: Inner iterator exposing the rows of the current group: hasNext is true while the next row's group equals the current group, next returns a copy of the row and fetches the next input row, and skipRemainingRows consumes the rest of the group and switches to the next group.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Throws NoSuchElementException when the group is exhausted; otherwise copies the current row, calls fetchNextRow of the outer iterator and returns the copy.

nodes.name: skipRemainingRows
nodes.summary: Fetches rows until the current group ends, then, if more input exists, copies the next group key as the current group.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WindowGroupLimitEvaluatorFactory, a PartitionEvaluatorFactory that builds the per-partition evaluator used by the window group limit operator. It picks the limiting iterator that matches the rank-like function (row number, rank or dense rank) and optionally wraps it per partition key.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Factory constructed with the partition spec, order spec, rank-like function, limit, child output and a numOutputRows metric. Its createEvaluator method maps RowNumber to SimpleLimitIterator, Rank to RankLimitIterator and DenseRank to DenseRankLimitIterator, and when a partition spec is present wraps the choice in a GroupedLimitIterator so the limit applies per group.

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimitPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Inner PartitionEvaluator that holds a function from an input row iterator to an output row iterator. Its eval method applies that function to the first input iterator of the partition.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Selects the limiting iterator function by matching the rank-like function against RowNumber, Rank and DenseRank. Returns a WindowGroupLimitPartitionEvaluator over that function directly when there is no partition spec, or over a GroupedLimitIterator built from the child output and partition spec otherwise.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Runs the stored iterator transformation on the first input iterator of the partition and returns the limited rows.

nodes.name: WindowSegmentTree.scala
nodes.summary: Implements WindowSegmentTree, a block-chunked segment tree that answers range aggregate queries over a window partition for moving frames in O(log W), together with a companion object holding the allowlist of aggregate classes that may use it. Cached internal tree levels are kept in an LRU and charged to the task memory manager through a private memory consumer that can evict them on spill requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object. The header comment documents memory invariants I1 to I8 (spill never acquires memory, self-trigger returns 0, LRU auto-eviction disabled, acquire/release pairing, conservative per-block bytes, no eviction once the row array spilled).

nodes.name: WindowSegmentTree
nodes.summary: Block-chunked segment tree over an ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray for window aggregates. Rows are split into blocks of blockSize; each block has a small tree with the given fanout, block root aggregates stay resident and internal levels are built on demand and cached in a LRU keyed by block index. It is built with build, queried with query or queryInto, and released with close; it is not thread-safe and requires a non-null TaskMemoryManager. The companion object (lines 569-614) defines DefaultFanout (16), DefaultBlockSize (65536), the EligibleAggregates allowlist (Min, Max, Sum, Count, Average, StddevPop, StddevSamp, VariancePop, VarianceSamp) and the isEligible check. Test hooks include peekBlockCount, testOnlySpiller, peekBlockBytes, peekLevelSize and peekLevelCount.

nodes.name: SegTreeSpiller
nodes.summary: Private final MemoryConsumer that accounts for cached block levels on heap. Its spill method returns 0 when triggered by itself or when the row array has already spilled, and otherwise evicts least recently used cached blocks until the requested size is freed. It never acquires memory itself.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Spill callback: returns 0 for a self-triggered request or when rowArray.spillSize is positive, otherwise calls evictUntil with the requested size and returns the freed bytes.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the tree against a caller-owned row array: computes per-block root aggregates, commits the row array, row and block counts, and then releases all cached block levels. State is left untouched if aggregation throws.

nodes.name: queryInto
nodes.summary: Queries the half-open range [lo, hi) into an internal buffer and then asks the given AggregateProcessor to evaluate that buffer into the target row.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Validates the range [lo, hi), resets the output buffer to the initial aggregate values and merges into it the partial left block, all full blocks in between (using resident block aggregates) and the partial right block, or a single block range when both ends share a block.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Idempotent terminal call: releases all cached block accounting, drops the row array reference, clears block aggregates and counters, and marks the tree closed.

nodes.name: computeBlockAggregates
nodes.summary: Scans the row array once and, for every block, initializes a buffer and updates it with each row to produce the per-block root aggregates. Throws an internal error if the row iterator ends early.

nodes.name: mergeBlockRange
nodes.summary: Merges the leaf range [lo, hi) of one block into the output buffer by fetching the block levels and descending the block tree.

nodes.name: queryDescend
nodes.summary: Recursively descends the per-block tree, merging any node fully inside the query range into the output and recursing into child nodes for partial overlaps.

nodes.name: ensureBlockLevels
nodes.summary: Returns the cached levels of a block or builds them: enforces the LRU capacity by evicting, acquires block memory (with one evict-and-retry, else raising a cannot-acquire-memory error), builds the levels, releasing the memory if building throws, and caches the result.

nodes.name: buildBlockLevels
nodes.summary: Builds all tree levels for a block: level 0 holds one aggregate per row read from the row array starting at the block start, and each higher level merges up to fanout children until a single root remains.

nodes.name: acquireBlockMemory
nodes.summary: Tries to acquire blockBytes from the spiller consumer; on a partial grant it frees what was granted and returns false.

nodes.name: evictUntil
nodes.summary: Evicts least recently used cached blocks until at least the target number of bytes is freed or the cache is empty, and returns the freed bytes. Called from the spiller.

nodes.name: evictEldestReturnBytes
nodes.summary: Removes the eldest entry of the LRU cache, releases the accounting for one block and returns the block byte size (0 if the cache is empty).

nodes.name: releaseAllCachedBlocks
nodes.summary: Clears the block level cache and frees the accounted memory for all cached blocks at once.

nodes.name: isEligible
nodes.summary: Companion object helper that returns true only when the expression is a DeclarativeAggregate whose class is in the EligibleAggregates allowlist.

nodes.name: ColumnVectorUtils.java
nodes.summary: Static helpers for filling and converting column vectors: populating a ConstantColumnVector from one field of an InternalRow, converting ColumnarArray and ColumnarMap values to Java collections, and turning an iterator of external Rows into a single ColumnarBatch. The header marks them as intended for debugging and other non-performance-critical paths.

nodes.name: ColumnVectorUtils
nodes.summary: Utility class with static methods: populate (two overloads, with and without a MemoryMode) writes the value of row[fieldIdx] into a ConstantColumnVector, toJavaIntArray and toJavaIntMap convert columnar array and map data to Java types, appendValue (two overloads) appends one external value or Row field to a WritableColumnVector, and toBatch builds a ColumnarBatch from a schema, memory mode and Row iterator.

nodes.name: populate
nodes.summary: Sets a ConstantColumnVector to the value of row[fieldIdx]: null, each primitive and string type, decimals by precision (int, long or unscaled bytes), calendar interval, variant, struct (recursing into the child constant vectors) and array or map (built in a one-row on-heap or off-heap WritableColumnVector through RowToColumnConverter and attached with setArrayWithBacking or setMapWithBacking). Throws for unsupported types. The three-argument overload at lines 59-61 delegates here with MemoryMode.ON_HEAP.

nodes.name: toJavaIntArray
nodes.summary: Returns the elements of a ColumnarArray as an int[] and throws if any element is null.

nodes.name: toJavaIntMap
nodes.summary: Converts a ColumnarMap with integer keys and values into a Java HashMap by reading its key and value arrays.

nodes.name: appendValue
nodes.summary: Appends a single external Java value of the given DataType to a WritableColumnVector, handling null, primitive, string, binary, decimal, calendar interval, variant, date, timestamp and timestamp without time zone values, and throwing for other types. A second overload at lines 235-259 takes a Row and field index and handles arrays and structs recursively before delegating here.

nodes.name: toBatch
nodes.summary: Allocates on-heap or off-heap column vectors for the schema with a capacity of 4096, appends every field of every Row from the iterator, and wraps the vectors in a ColumnarBatch with the row count set.

nodes.name: ConstantColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines ConstantColumnVector, a ColumnVector that stores a single value and returns it for every row id. It offers set methods for all supported types, including decimals, arrays, maps, structs, calendar intervals and variants.

nodes.name: ConstantColumnVector
nodes.summary: ColumnVector subclass that keeps one copy of the data (null flag, byte, short, int, long, float, double, UTF8String, byte array, child vectors, ColumnarArray or ColumnarMap) and returns it from every getter regardless of rowId. Setters (setNull, setBoolean, setInt, setDecimal, setUtf8String, setBinary, setCalendarInterval, setVariant and others) apply a value to all rows. For array and map values, setArrayWithBacking and setMapWithBacking take ownership of a backing WritableColumnVector that close releases. The constructor pre-allocates child constant vectors for struct, calendar interval and variant types.

nodes.name: ConstantColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor taking the number of rows and a DataType. Pre-allocates child ConstantColumnVectors for struct fields, for calendar intervals (int, int, long) and for variants (two binary children), and leaves children null for other types.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Clears the string and byte array data, closes and nulls all child vectors, drops the array and map references, and closes the owned backing vector if any.

nodes.name: setArrayWithBacking
nodes.summary: Sets the constant array value and takes ownership of the given backing WritableColumnVector so it is closed with this vector.

nodes.name: setMapWithBacking
nodes.summary: Sets the constant map value and takes ownership of the given backing WritableColumnVector so it is closed with this vector.

nodes.name: replaceOwnedBacking
nodes.summary: Closes the previously owned backing vector when it differs from the new one and stores the new backing vector.

nodes.name: getDecimal
nodes.summary: Builds a Decimal from the stored int, long or big-endian byte array value depending on whether the precision fits an int, a long or neither.

nodes.name: setDecimal
nodes.summary: Stores a Decimal as an int, a long or an unscaled big integer byte array depending on the precision.

nodes.name: setChild
nodes.summary: Replaces the child vector at an ordinal, closing the previous child first when it is a different object to avoid leaking its storage.

nodes.name: setCalendarInterval
nodes.summary: Writes the months, days and microseconds of a CalendarInterval into the three child constant vectors.

nodes.name: setVariant
nodes.summary: Writes the value and metadata byte arrays of a VariantVal into the two binary child constant vectors.

nodes.name: OffHeapColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines OffHeapColumnVector, the WritableColumnVector implementation backed by off heap (native) memory, with a static allocateColumns factory, typed put/get methods, dictionary decoding and capacity growth.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class with a platform endianness flag (bigEndianPlatform) selecting between bulk memory copies and per-value byte reversal.

nodes.name: OffHeapColumnVector
nodes.summary: Final WritableColumnVector subclass that stores column values in off heap (native) memory: native memory addresses (long fields nulls, data, lengthData and offsetData) accessed through Platform. It implements the put/get API for null flags, booleans, bytes, shorts, ints, longs, floats, doubles, array offsets and lengths and byte arrays, decodes through a dictionary when one is set, handles little-endian bulk loads with big endian fallbacks, and grows storage through reserveInternal. Used when a columnar batch must be backed by native memory that external components can read directly.

nodes.name: allocateColumns
nodes.summary: Static factory with two overloads (one takes a StructType, one takes StructField[]; this node covers the StructField[] overload) that creates one OffHeapColumnVector per schema field with the given initial capacity.

nodes.name: OffHeapColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor: passes capacity and type to the WritableColumnVector super constructor, then calls reserveInternal(capacity) to allocate storage and reset() to clear state.

nodes.name: releaseMemory
nodes.summary: Frees the nulls, data, lengthData and offsetData native allocations through Platform.freeMemory and resets the addresses to 0.

nodes.name: putNulls
nodes.summary: Marks count consecutive rows as null starting at rowId (writing 1 into the null flag per row) and adds count to numNulls; returns early for an all-null vector.

nodes.name: putBooleans
nodes.summary: Widest of the putBoolean/putBooleans overloads (the others write one value or fill count slots with one value); this one expands one packed byte into 8 boolean slots with expandBoolByteToLong, byte-swapping on big endian platforms, and writes them as one long after asserting 8 slots are available.

nodes.name: putBytes
nodes.summary: Widest of the putBytes overloads (the others fill a value or copy from a byte[]); copies count bytes from a ByteBuffer into the column, handling heap-array, direct and other buffers separately.

nodes.name: getByte
nodes.summary: Returns the byte at rowId, reading directly from storage when there is no dictionary and otherwise decoding the dictionary id via dictionary.decodeToInt.

nodes.name: getBytes
nodes.summary: Returns count bytes starting at rowId as a new byte[], bulk-copying when no dictionary is set and decoding each non-null id through the dictionary otherwise.

nodes.name: putShortsFromIntsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Reads count little-endian 4-byte ints from a byte[] and stores each as a short in the column, reversing bytes first on big endian platforms.

nodes.name: putIntsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian ints from a byte[] into the column: a plain memory copy on little endian platforms and a per-value byte reversal on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getInts
nodes.summary: Returns count ints from rowId as a new int[], copying in bulk when no dictionary is set and decoding non-null dictionary ids through decodeToInt otherwise.

nodes.name: getDictId
nodes.summary: Returns the dictionary id stored at rowId when this vector itself holds dictionary ids; asserts that the vector has no dictionary of its own (the source comment ties this separate method to SPARK-16928).

nodes.name: putLongsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian longs from a byte[] into the column: a plain memory copy on little endian platforms and a per-value byte reversal on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getLongs
nodes.summary: Returns count longs from rowId as a new long[], copying in bulk without a dictionary and decoding non-null ids with decodeToLong otherwise.

nodes.name: putFloatsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian floats from a byte[]: delegates to putFloats on little endian platforms and reads each value through a little-endian ByteBuffer on big endian ones.

nodes.name: putDoublesLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian doubles from a byte[]: delegates to putDoubles on little endian platforms and reads each value through a little-endian ByteBuffer on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getDoubles
nodes.summary: Returns count doubles from rowId as a new double[], copying in bulk without a dictionary and decoding non-null ids with decodeToDouble otherwise.

nodes.name: putArray
nodes.summary: Records the (offset, length) of the array or map element at rowId in the lengths and offsets storage; first asserts the range fits in the first child column.

nodes.name: putByteArray
nodes.summary: Appends the byte range to the child array data via arrayData().appendBytes and records the resulting offset and length for rowId; returns the offset.

nodes.name: reserveInternal
nodes.summary: Slow path that grows or allocates storage to newCapacity: picks the buffer by Spark data type (array/map lengths and offsets, boolean/byte, short, int-like, long-like, float, double), copies old contents, resizes the null flags and sets capacity; throws RuntimeException for an unhandled type and does nothing for an all-null vector.

nodes.name: reserveNewColumn
nodes.summary: Creates a new OffHeapColumnVector of the given capacity and type; used to build child columns of the same kind.

nodes.name: OnHeapColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines OnHeapColumnVector, the WritableColumnVector implementation backed by the JVM heap, with a static allocateColumns factory, typed put/get methods, dictionary decoding and capacity growth.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class with a platform endianness flag (bigEndianPlatform) selecting between bulk memory copies and per-value byte reversal.

nodes.name: OnHeapColumnVector
nodes.summary: Final WritableColumnVector subclass that stores column values in the JVM heap: JVM arrays (a byte[] for nulls, one typed array per primitive type, and int[] arrayLengths and arrayOffsets for array and map types). It implements the put/get API for null flags, booleans, bytes, shorts, ints, longs, floats, doubles, array offsets and lengths and byte arrays, decodes through a dictionary when one is set, handles little-endian bulk loads with big endian fallbacks, and grows storage through reserveInternal. Used when a columnar batch must be kept as ordinary JVM arrays.

nodes.name: allocateColumns
nodes.summary: Static factory with two overloads (one takes a StructType, one takes StructField[]; this node covers the StructField[] overload) that creates one OnHeapColumnVector per schema field with the given initial capacity.

nodes.name: OnHeapColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor: passes capacity and type to the WritableColumnVector super constructor, then calls reserveInternal(capacity) to allocate storage and reset() to clear state.

nodes.name: releaseMemory
nodes.summary: Drops the references to the nulls array, all typed data arrays and the array length and offset arrays so the JVM can collect them.

nodes.name: putNulls
nodes.summary: Marks count consecutive rows as null starting at rowId (writing 1 into the null flag per row) and adds count to numNulls; returns early for an all-null vector.

nodes.name: putBooleans
nodes.summary: Widest of the putBoolean/putBooleans overloads (the others write one value or fill count slots with one value); this one expands one packed byte into 8 boolean slots with expandBoolByteToLong, byte-swapping on big endian platforms, and writes them as one long after asserting 8 slots are available.

nodes.name: putBytes
nodes.summary: Widest of the putBytes overloads (fill a value, System.arraycopy from a byte[] at lines 200-203, and an absolute bulk get from a ByteBuffer at lines 205-209); this node covers the fill variant that writes value into count slots starting at rowId.

nodes.name: getByte
nodes.summary: Returns the byte at rowId, reading directly from storage when there is no dictionary and otherwise decoding the dictionary id via dictionary.decodeToInt.

nodes.name: getBytes
nodes.summary: Returns count bytes starting at rowId as a new byte[], bulk-copying when no dictionary is set and decoding each non-null id through the dictionary otherwise.

nodes.name: putShortsFromIntsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Reads count little-endian 4-byte ints from a byte[] and stores each as a short in the column, reversing bytes first on big endian platforms.

nodes.name: putIntsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian ints from a byte[] into the column: a plain memory copy on little endian platforms and a per-value byte reversal on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getInts
nodes.summary: Returns count ints from rowId as a new int[], copying in bulk when no dictionary is set and decoding non-null dictionary ids through decodeToInt otherwise.

nodes.name: getDictId
nodes.summary: Returns the dictionary id stored at rowId when this vector itself holds dictionary ids; asserts that the vector has no dictionary of its own (the source comment ties this separate method to SPARK-16928).

nodes.name: putLongsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian longs from a byte[] into the column: a plain memory copy on little endian platforms and a per-value byte reversal on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getLongs
nodes.summary: Returns count longs from rowId as a new long[], copying in bulk without a dictionary and decoding non-null ids with decodeToLong otherwise.

nodes.name: putFloatsLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian floats from a byte[]: delegates to putFloats on little endian platforms and reads each value through a little-endian ByteBuffer on big endian ones.

nodes.name: putDoublesLittleEndian
nodes.summary: Writes count little-endian doubles from a byte[]: delegates to putDoubles on little endian platforms and reads each value through a little-endian ByteBuffer on big endian ones.

nodes.name: getDoubles
nodes.summary: Returns count doubles from rowId as a new double[], copying in bulk without a dictionary and decoding non-null ids with decodeToDouble otherwise.

nodes.name: putArray
nodes.summary: Records the (offset, length) of the array or map element at rowId in the arrayOffsets and arrayLengths arrays.

nodes.name: putByteArray
nodes.summary: Appends the byte range to the child array data via arrayData().appendBytes and records the resulting offset and length for rowId; returns the offset.

nodes.name: reserveInternal
nodes.summary: Slow path that grows or allocates storage to newCapacity: picks the buffer by Spark data type (array/map lengths and offsets, boolean/byte, short, int-like, long-like, float, double), copies old contents, resizes the null flags and sets capacity; throws RuntimeException for an unhandled type and does nothing for an all-null vector.

nodes.name: reserveNewColumn
nodes.summary: Creates a new OnHeapColumnVector of the given capacity and type; used to build child columns of the same kind.

nodes.name: ColumnDictionary.java
nodes.summary: Defines ColumnDictionary, a final Dictionary implementation that holds decoded values in one of four primitive arrays (int, long, float, double).

nodes.name: ColumnDictionary
nodes.summary: Final class implementing Dictionary. Each of its four constructors takes one primitive array (int[], long[], float[] or double[]) and stores it in the matching field; decodeToInt, decodeToLong, decodeToFloat and decodeToDouble return the array entry at the given id, and decodeToBinary throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException with the error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3191. Used to decode dictionary encoded column values.

nodes.name: ColumnDictionary
nodes.summary: Constructor taking an int[] dictionary (three more overloads take long[], float[] and double[] at lines 33-43, each storing its array in the matching field; this node covers the first).

nodes.name: decodeToInt
nodes.summary: Returns intDictionary[id].

nodes.name: decodeToLong
nodes.summary: Returns longDictionary[id].

nodes.name: decodeToFloat
nodes.summary: Returns floatDictionary[id].

nodes.name: decodeToDouble
nodes.summary: Returns doubleDictionary[id].

nodes.name: decodeToBinary
nodes.summary: Not supported: throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException with error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3191.

nodes.name: Dictionary.java
nodes.summary: Defines the Dictionary interface used by a ColumnVector to decode dictionary encoded values into int, long, float, double or binary values.

nodes.name: Dictionary
nodes.summary: Public interface with five decode methods (decodeToInt, decodeToLong, decodeToFloat, decodeToDouble, decodeToBinary), each taking a dictionary id. A ColumnVector uses it to decode dictionary encoded values.

nodes.name: decodeToInt
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to an int value.

nodes.name: decodeToLong
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to a long value.

nodes.name: decodeToFloat
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to a float value.

nodes.name: decodeToDouble
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to a double value.

nodes.name: decodeToBinary
nodes.summary: Decodes a dictionary id to a byte[] value.

nodes.name: AggregateHashMap.java
nodes.summary: Defines AggregateHashMap, an illustrative append-only hash map from one long key to one long value, stored in a columnar batch and used as a fast cache for aggregates.

nodes.name: AggregateHashMap
nodes.summary: Illustrative append-only single-key/single-value aggregate hash map. It keeps a power-of-2-sized int[] of buckets (linear probing, at most maxSteps tries, default load factor 0.25, default capacity 65536) pointing into OnHeapColumnVector columns, and hands out a MutableColumnarRow positioned on the matching row. The class comment says it can act as a cache with fallback to BytesToBytesMap when a key is not found and could be codegened in HashAggregate. Constructors assert a schema of exactly two long fields.

nodes.name: AggregateHashMap
nodes.summary: Constructor (schema, capacity, loadFactor, maxSteps), widest of two overloads; asserts a two-long-field schema and a power-of-2 capacity, sizes the bucket array as capacity / loadFactor, allocates OnHeapColumnVector columns, creates the MutableColumnarRow and fills buckets with -1. The one-argument overload at lines 71-73 uses the default capacity, load factor and max steps.

nodes.name: findOrInsert
nodes.summary: Finds the bucket for a long key via find; if it is an empty slot, appends the key with value 0 into the columns and records the row index. Returns the shared MutableColumnarRow with rowId set to that entry.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Probes up to maxSteps buckets starting at hash(key) masked by numBuckets-1 with linear probing; returns the index of an empty slot or of the slot holding the key, or -1 if none was found.

nodes.name: hash
nodes.summary: Cheap hash function that returns the key itself.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Returns whether the key stored for the row in bucket idx equals key1.

nodes.name: MutableColumnarRow.java
nodes.summary: Defines MutableColumnarRow, a mutable InternalRow view over WritableColumnVector columns at a settable rowId, used to avoid object creation in the vectorized hash map and columnar batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally duplicates code from ColumnarRow (per its class comment) to keep both classes final and avoid polymorphism overhead.

nodes.name: MutableColumnarRow
nodes.summary: Final InternalRow subclass wrapping a WritableColumnVector[] with a public mutable rowId. Getters (getBoolean, getInt, getLong, getUTF8String, getStruct, getArray, getMap and others) read from the column at rowId; setters (setNullAt, setBoolean, setInt, setLong, setDecimal, setInterval and others) mark the value not null then put it; copy() builds a GenericInternalRow, get(ordinal, dataType) dispatches by type, update(ordinal, value) writes by column type, and anyNull throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException. The class comment says it is used in the vectorized hash map for hash aggregate and in ColumnarBatch.
nodes.languageNotes: The class comment states the duplication with ColumnarRow is intentional.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Copies the current row into a new GenericInternalRow, branching on each column's data type (primitives, string, binary, geography/geometry, decimal, date, timestamps, struct, array, map, variant) and copying variable-length values; throws RuntimeException for an unhandled type.

nodes.name: get
