nodes.summary: Returns the value at an ordinal as an Object by dispatching on the given DataType to the typed getter; throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3192) for an unsupported type.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Sets a column value from an Object: null calls setNullAt, otherwise it dispatches on the column's data type to the typed setter (boolean, int, short, long, float, double, decimal, calendar interval) and throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException for other types.

nodes.name: ArrowCompressionUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the helper that builds the write-side Arrow compression codec from the codec name and zstd level taken from the Arrow compression settings. Used when serializing Arrow record batches.

nodes.name: ArrowCompressionUtils
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with one method, createCompressionCodec, that maps the names "none", "zstd" and "lz4" to an Arrow CompressionCodec and raises an internal error for any other name. The codec is built directly so that the configured zstd level is not lost.

nodes.name: createCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Returns NoCompressionCodec for "none", a ZstdCompressionCodec built with the given level for "zstd", a Lz4CompressionCodec for "lz4", and throws SparkException.internalError for other names. The comment explains the codec is built directly because the factory overload by codec type ignores the compression level; the level only matters when writing.

nodes.name: ArrowConverters.scala
nodes.summary: Converts between Spark InternalRow iterators and serialized Arrow record batches and IPC streams, and builds DataFrames from Arrow batches. Contains the batch-writing and batch-reading iterators, the stream writer and helpers to read Arrow messages from a file or channel.

nodes.name: ArrowBatchStreamWriter
nodes.summary: Writes serialized Arrow record batches to an OutputStream in the Arrow stream format. The constructor writes the Arrow schema first; writeBatches writes each batch from an iterator of byte arrays; end writes the end-of-stream marker without closing the output stream.

nodes.name: ArrowConverters
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object that groups the Arrow conversion logic: toBatchIterator and toBatchWithSchemaIterator turn rows into serialized batches; fromBatchIterator, fromBatchWithSchemaIterator and fromIPCStream turn serialized batches back into rows; toDataFrame builds a DataFrame from batches; readArrowStreamFromFile and getBatchesFromStream read batches from an Arrow stream; loadBatch and serializeBatch convert a single batch.

nodes.name: ArrowBatchIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator[Array[Byte]] that consumes an InternalRow iterator and produces one serialized Arrow record batch per next() call, taking up to maxRecordsPerBatch rows (all rows when it is not positive). It writes rows with ArrowWriter, applies the compression codec chosen by the SQLConf Arrow compression settings, and closes its root and allocator when rows run out or the task completes.

nodes.name: ArrowBatchWithSchemaIterator
nodes.summary: Subclass of ArrowBatchIterator whose every output batch is a full IPC stream: schema message, record batch and end-of-stream marker. It stops a batch when either the record limit or the estimated byte size limit (maxEstimatedBatchSize) is reached, always writes at least one row, and tracks rowCountInLastBatch.

nodes.name: InternalRowIteratorFromIPCStream
nodes.summary: CloseableIterator[InternalRow] over one or more byte arrays that each hold a valid Arrow IPC stream (schema followed by record batches). It reads them through a ConcatenatingArrowStreamReader, exposes the schema lazily, counts batchesLoaded and totalRowsProcessed, reports allocator memory, and closes resources on completion or task end.

nodes.name: InternalRowIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract Iterator[InternalRow] over serialized Arrow batches. It owns an allocator and a list of resources closed in reverse order, loads the first batch in the constructor, checks that all later batches have the same schema, and leaves nextBatch to subclasses.

nodes.name: InternalRowIteratorWithoutSchema
nodes.summary: InternalRowIterator for batches that carry no schema: the Spark schema is passed in the constructor, converted to an Arrow schema, and each byte array is loaded into a VectorSchemaRoot with VectorLoader.

nodes.name: InternalRowIteratorWithSchema
nodes.summary: InternalRowIterator for batches that each start with a schema: nextBatch opens an ArrowStreamReader on the bytes, loads the first batch and derives the Spark schema from the root, returning an empty iterator when no batch exists.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Reads rows into the Arrow writer until maxRecordsPerBatch is reached or the rows end, finishes the writer, takes a record batch from the unloader, serializes it with serializeBatch and always resets the writer.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Builds a self-contained IPC stream per call: writes the schema, then writes rows while neither the estimated size limit nor the record limit is exceeded (row size is getSizeInBytes for UnsafeRow, else numFields * 16), then writes the record batch and the end-of-stream marker, and returns the bytes.

nodes.name: toBatchIterator
nodes.summary: Creates an ArrowBatchIterator for the given rows, schema, maximum records per batch, time zone, duplicate-field-name flag, large var type flag and task context.

nodes.name: toBatchWithSchemaIterator
nodes.summary: Creates an ArrowBatchWithSchemaIterator, so each output batch begins with the schema, using TaskContext.get() as the context.

nodes.name: createEmptyArrowBatch
nodes.summary: Produces one serialized batch with schema and no rows by subclassing ArrowBatchWithSchemaIterator over an empty iterator with hasNext forced true; closes the iterator itself when no TaskContext exists, to avoid a memory leak.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Loops until the current row iterator has a row, loading the next batch from the reader and counting it; closes and returns false when no batch is left.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns true while the current batch has rows; otherwise loads the next batch, throws IllegalArgumentException if its schema differs from the first, and closes all resources when the input is exhausted.

nodes.name: nextBatch
nodes.summary: Creates a VectorSchemaRoot from the supplied schema, loads the next byte array with loadBatch and a VectorLoader, and returns the rows of the root with the schema.

nodes.name: nextBatch
nodes.summary: Opens an ArrowStreamReader on the next byte array, loads the first batch and returns its rows with the schema read from the stream, or an empty iterator and null schema when the stream holds no batch.

nodes.name: fromBatchIterator
nodes.summary: Maps an iterator of serialized Arrow batches without schema to an iterator of InternalRow through InternalRowIteratorWithoutSchema.

nodes.name: fromBatchWithSchemaIterator
nodes.summary: Maps an iterator of batches that each start with a schema to a pair of the row iterator and the schema, using InternalRowIteratorWithSchema.

nodes.name: fromIPCStream
nodes.summary: Creates an InternalRowIteratorFromIPCStream over an iterator of IPC stream byte arrays and returns it with its schema. A second overload (lines 475-478) wraps a single byte array in Iterator.single and calls this one.

nodes.name: fromIPCStreamWithIterator
nodes.summary: Test-oriented variant of fromIPCStream that takes a TaskContext and returns the concrete iterator so its metrics can be read.

nodes.name: vectorSchemaRootToIter
nodes.summary: Wraps each field vector of a VectorSchemaRoot in an ArrowColumnVector, builds a ColumnarBatch with the root row count and returns its row iterator.

nodes.name: loadBatch
nodes.summary: Deserializes a byte array into an ArrowRecordBatch with MessageSerializer.deserializeRecordBatch.

nodes.name: serializeBatch
nodes.summary: Serializes an ArrowRecordBatch to a byte array with MessageSerializer.

nodes.name: toDataFrame
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrame from serialized Arrow batches. If the total batch size exceeds arrowLocalRelationThreshold it parallelizes the batches into an RDD and decodes them per partition; otherwise it decodes them on the driver and builds a LocalRelation from copied unsafe rows. The public overload (lines 527-538) takes a JSON schema string and session settings and calls this one.

nodes.name: readArrowStreamFromFile
nodes.summary: Reads an Arrow stream file fully into an array of serialized record batches and closes the file.

nodes.name: getBatchesFromStream
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over serialized record batches read from a ReadableByteChannel. Its readNextBatch reads message metadata, skips non-RecordBatch messages, and for a RecordBatch copies the metadata and body into one ByteBuffer-backed array.

nodes.name: closeAll
nodes.summary: Closes every non-null AutoCloseable passed in.

nodes.name: ArrowFileReadWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Saves a DataFrame to a local Arrow file and loads one back, through SparkArrowFileWriter, SparkArrowFileReader and the ArrowFileReadWrite object. Batches are moved as serialized byte arrays via ArrowConverters.

nodes.name: SparkArrowFileWriter
nodes.summary: AutoCloseable that writes an iterator of serialized Arrow record batches to a file at the given Path with ArrowFileWriter. It creates a child allocator and a VectorSchemaRoot for the schema, and write() starts the file, loads each batch with ArrowConverters.loadBatch and closes the file at the end.

nodes.name: SparkArrowFileReader
nodes.summary: AutoCloseable that opens an Arrow file with ArrowFileReader, exposes its schema, and read() returns an iterator of serialized record batches (one byte array per record block, produced with ArrowConverters.serializeBatch).

nodes.name: ArrowFileReadWrite
nodes.summary: Private[spark] object with save(df, path), which writes a DataFrame to an Arrow file, and load(spark, path), which reads an Arrow file into a DataFrame. Both use UTC as the time zone.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Starts the file writer, then for each serialized batch loads it into the root and writes it, closes the batch, and finally closes the file writer.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Maps each record block of the Arrow file to a serialized batch by loading the block, unloading the root and serializing it.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Converts the DataFrame to an Arrow batch RDD using arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch, builds the Arrow schema, and writes the local iterator of batches with SparkArrowFileWriter.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads the file with SparkArrowFileReader, converts the Arrow schema to a Spark schema and creates a DataFrame with ArrowConverters.toDataFrame.

nodes.name: ColumnType.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ColumnType hierarchy used by the in-memory columnar cache: each ColumnType knows how to append a value from an InternalRow to a ByteBuffer and extract it back, with one object or class per supported data type (INT, LONG, STRING, DECIMAL, STRUCT, ARRAY, MAP, VARIANT and others), plus ColumnType.apply that picks the type for a Catalyst DataType.

nodes.name: ByteBufferHelper
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] object with fast native-order helpers: getShort, getInt, getLong, getFloat, getDouble, putShort, putInt, putLong and copyMemory. They read or write the backing array of a ByteBuffer with Platform and advance the buffer position by hand. The comment warns that this only works with HeapByteBuffer.

nodes.name: copyMemory
nodes.summary: Advances the positions of the source and destination buffers by len and copies len bytes between their backing arrays with Platform.copyMemory.

nodes.name: ColumnType
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract base class (generic in the JVM type) describing one column type. It declares dataType, defaultSize, extract, append, actualSize, getField, setField, copyField and clone, with generic boxed versions that subclasses override. A companion object (lines 863-888) provides apply(dataType), which maps a Catalyst DataType to the matching ColumnType.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Abstract extract(buffer) reads one value at the buffer position; the overload extract(buffer, row, ordinal) by default stores the extracted value into row(ordinal) through setField. Subclasses override the overload to avoid boxing.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Abstract append(v, buffer) writes one value into the buffer; the overload append(row, ordinal, buffer) by default reads row(ordinal) with getField and appends it. Subclasses override the overload to avoid boxing.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive factory in the ColumnType companion object. It maps NullType, BooleanType, ByteType, ShortType, integer-like types (Integer, Date, year-month interval) to INT, long-like types (Long, Timestamp, TimestampNTZ, day-time interval, Time) to LONG, Float, Double, String, Binary and CalendarInterval, Decimal to COMPACT_DECIMAL or LARGE_DECIMAL by precision, Array, Map and Struct, a UserDefinedType through its sqlType, and throws unsupportedDataTypeError otherwise.

nodes.name: NULL
nodes.summary: ColumnType object for PhysicalNullType with default size 0: append writes nothing, extract returns null, getField returns null and setField sets the row field to null.

nodes.name: NativeColumnType
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] abstract class that fixes the physical data type and default size of a native column type (constructor parameters dataType and defaultSize); it extends ColumnType. Used as the base of INT, LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, BYTE, SHORT, STRING, COMPACT_DECIMAL and the interval types, and referenced by the compression schemes.

nodes.name: INT
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalIntegerType with a default size of 4 bytes. append and extract use putInt and ByteBufferHelper.getInt; the row accessors use getInt and setInt.

nodes.name: LONG
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalLongType with a default size of 8 bytes. append and extract use putLong and ByteBufferHelper.getLong; the row accessors use getLong and setLong.

nodes.name: YEAR_MONTH_INTERVAL
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalIntegerType with a default size of 4 bytes. Same int-based encoding as INT, kept as a separate object for year-month interval values.

nodes.name: DAY_TIME_INTERVAL
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalLongType with a default size of 8 bytes. Same long-based encoding as LONG, kept as a separate object for day-time interval values.

nodes.name: FLOAT
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalFloatType with a default size of 4 bytes. append and extract use putFloat and ByteBufferHelper.getFloat.

nodes.name: DOUBLE
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalDoubleType with a default size of 8 bytes. append and extract use putDouble and ByteBufferHelper.getDouble.

nodes.name: BOOLEAN
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalBooleanType with a default size of 1 bytes. A boolean is stored as one byte, 1 for true and 0 for false.

nodes.name: BYTE
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalByteType with a default size of 1 bytes. append and extract use buffer.put and buffer.get.

nodes.name: SHORT
nodes.summary: Native column type for PhysicalShortType with a default size of 2 bytes. append and extract use putShort and getShort.

nodes.name: DirectCopyColumnType
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait that adds a fast path for variable-length types. extract copies bytes from the ByteBuffer straight into a MutableUnsafeRow writer, and append writes an UnsafeRow field straight into the buffer with writeFieldTo; other row kinds fall back to the generic code.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: For a MutableUnsafeRow, reads the length prefix, advances the buffer and writes the bytes directly with the row writer; for any other row it calls setField with the extracted value.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: For an UnsafeRow, calls writeFieldTo to copy the field bytes into the buffer; otherwise falls back to the inherited append.

nodes.name: STRING
nodes.summary: Case class (collationId) column type for strings, a NativeColumnType over PhysicalStringType with DirectCopyColumnType. A value is stored as an int length followed by the UTF-8 bytes. A companion object (lines 535-539) has apply(StringType) that uses the collation id.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads an int length, advances the buffer and builds a UTF8String from the backing array.

nodes.name: setField
nodes.summary: Writes the string through the writer of a MutableUnsafeRow, or stores a clone of the value into other rows.

nodes.name: COMPACT_DECIMAL
nodes.summary: Case class (precision, scale) column type for decimals that fit in a long, a NativeColumnType over PhysicalDecimalType with default size 8. It stores the unscaled long value. A companion object (lines 584-588) has apply(DecimalType).

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Builds a Decimal from the stored long, precision and scale; for a MutableUnsafeRow it copies the long straight into the row.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Writes the unscaled long of a Decimal; for an UnsafeRow it copies the long field directly.

nodes.name: ByteArrayColumnType
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] sealed abstract class for types stored as a length-prefixed byte array. Subclasses supply serialize and deserialize; append writes the length and bytes, extract reads them back. It mixes in DirectCopyColumnType.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Serializes the value and writes an int length followed by the bytes.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads an int length, reads that many bytes and deserializes them.

nodes.name: BINARY
nodes.summary: ColumnType object for PhysicalBinaryType with default size 16; the byte array is its own serialized form and the actual size is the array length plus 4.

nodes.name: LARGE_DECIMAL
nodes.summary: Case class (precision, scale) column type for decimals too large for a long, stored as a length-prefixed byte array of the unscaled BigInteger. A companion object (lines 656-660) has apply(DecimalType).

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a Decimal from the bytes by creating a BigInteger, applying the scale and wrapping it with the precision and scale.

nodes.name: STRUCT
nodes.summary: Case class column type for struct values held as UnsafeRow, with default size 20. A value is stored as an int size followed by the row bytes; extract points a new UnsafeRow at the buffer array without copying.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads the size, advances the buffer and returns an UnsafeRow pointed at the buffer array at that offset.

nodes.name: ARRAY
nodes.summary: Case class column type for array values held as UnsafeArrayData, with default size 28. A value is stored as an int size followed by the array bytes.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads the size, advances the buffer and returns an UnsafeArrayData pointed at the buffer array at that offset.

nodes.name: MAP
nodes.summary: Case class column type for map values held as UnsafeMapData, with default size 68. A value is stored as an int size followed by the map bytes.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads the size, advances the buffer and returns an UnsafeMapData pointed at the buffer array at that offset.

nodes.name: CALENDAR_INTERVAL
nodes.summary: ColumnType object for CalendarInterval with default size 16. A value is stored as int months, int days and long microseconds; extract can also copy the 16 bytes straight into a MutableUnsafeRow.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads months, days and microseconds into a CalendarInterval. A second overload (lines 799-809) copies the 16 bytes directly into a MutableUnsafeRow, otherwise calls setField.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Writes months, days and microseconds with ByteBufferHelper.putInt and putLong.

nodes.name: VARIANT
nodes.summary: ColumnType object for VariantVal with default size 2048 (chosen to match VariantType). A value is encoded as value size, metadata size, value bytes, metadata bytes, and is decoded only in extract.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Writes the value length and metadata length, then copies the value bytes and metadata bytes into the buffer with ByteBufferHelper.copyMemory.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Reads both sizes, copies the value and metadata bytes into new buffers and returns a VariantVal built from the two arrays.

nodes.name: GenerateColumnAccessor.scala
nodes.summary: Generates and compiles a Java iterator that walks the rows of a DefaultCachedBatch for the columnar cache. It holds ColumnarIterator, the MutableUnsafeRow helper that column accessors write into, and the GenerateColumnAccessor code generator that picks a column accessor class for each data type.

nodes.name: ColumnarIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract Iterator[InternalRow] that adds initialize(input, columnTypes, columnIndexes), which receives the iterator of DefaultCachedBatch, the column data types and the indexes of the columns to read. The generated class SpecificColumnarIterator extends it.

nodes.name: MutableUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Helper row, used by the column accessors, that forwards setNullAt and the primitive setters (setBoolean, setByte, setShort, setInt, setLong, setFloat, setDouble) to an UnsafeRowWriter. Setters must be called in increasing ordinal order. setDecimal, setInterval, update, genericGet and numFields throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException because the writer is used directly.

nodes.name: GenerateColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Object extending CodeGenerator[Seq[DataType], ColumnarIterator] with Logging. Its create method builds the source of a SpecificColumnarIterator class for the given column types, compiles it and returns an instance. canonicalize and bind return their input unchanged.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: For each column type picks a column accessor class (for example IntColumnAccessor, StringColumnAccessor, StructColumnAccessor) and emits code to construct it over a byte buffer and to call extractTo into a MutableUnsafeRow. When there are more than 200 statements (numberOfStatementsThreshold) it splits them into helper methods to keep the bytecode small. It then writes the iterator class source, whose hasNext loads the next DefaultCachedBatch and whose next fills an UnsafeRowWriter, formats and compiles it with CodeGenerator.compile and returns the instance.

nodes.name: CompressionScheme.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the contracts for column compression in the columnar cache: Encoder and Decoder traits, the CompressionScheme trait, the WithCompressionSchemes and AllCompressionSchemes mixins, and the CompressionScheme object that lists all schemes and looks one up by type id.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait for a column encoder. It has gatherCompressibilityStats (default no-op), compressedSize, uncompressedSize, compressionRatio (compressedSize divided by uncompressedSize, or 1.0 if nothing is stored) and compress(from, to), which writes the compressed bytes into the target buffer.

nodes.name: compressionRatio
nodes.summary: Returns compressedSize.toDouble / uncompressedSize when uncompressedSize is positive, otherwise 1.0.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait for a column decoder. It has next(row, ordinal), which writes the next value into a row, hasNext, and decompress(columnVector, capacity), which decodes into a WritableColumnVector.

nodes.name: CompressionScheme
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait for one compression scheme with typeId, supports(columnType), encoder(columnType) and decoder(buffer, columnType). A companion object (lines 70-87) holds the list of all schemes (PassThrough, RunLengthEncoding, DictionaryEncoding, BooleanBitSet, IntDelta, LongDelta), apply(typeId) to look one up, and columnHeaderSize(columnBuffer).

nodes.name: WithCompressionSchemes
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait that requires a schemes member, a Seq of CompressionScheme.

nodes.name: AllCompressionSchemes
nodes.summary: Private[columnar] trait that fills schemes with CompressionScheme.all, so a mixing class uses every scheme.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Looks up a scheme by type id in a map built from all and throws unrecognizedCompressionSchemaTypeIDError if the id is unknown.

nodes.name: columnHeaderSize
nodes.summary: Reads the null count from a duplicate of the column buffer in native order and returns 4 + 4 * nullCount, the size of the null count plus null positions.

nodes.name: WritableColumnVector.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract WritableColumnVector class, which adds put and append write APIs to the read-only ColumnVector for every supported type, plus capacity management, dictionary support and nested child columns. Concrete subclasses supply the actual storage and are used by the vectorized readers and in-memory caching code to fill column batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Java abstract class with mostly abstract put* methods and final append* helpers that reserve space, call the matching put* method, then advance the write cursor.

nodes.name: WritableColumnVector
nodes.summary: Abstract writable column vector extending ColumnVector. Lines 74-264 and 273-447 declare the abstract put* APIs (putNull, putBoolean, putInt, putLongs, putDoubles, putArray, putByteArray and their batched and little-endian variants) that do not check capacity, so callers must call reserve() first. Lines 555-783 hold the final append* APIs (appendNull, appendInt, appendInts, appendBytes, appendByteArray, appendArray, appendStruct) that reserve space and advance elementsAppended, and appendObjects appends a Java object by its runtime type. It also holds the capacity logic (reserve, reset with huge vector threshold shrinking, close), dictionary state (dictionary, dictionaryIds, reserveDictionaryIds), the getters for decimal, string, binary, array and map values, flags for constant and missing columns, and the constructor, which creates child columns for array, binary, string, struct, map, calendar interval and variant types. Subclasses implement releaseMemory, reserveInternal, reserveNewColumn and the storage-specific put and get methods. It is not valid to mix put and append, and not valid to put after reads until reset().

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets the column for writing so stored values are no longer accessible. It returns early for constant or all-null columns, recursively resets child columns, zeroes elementsAppended, restores not-null flags when numNulls is positive, and, when capacity exceeds hugeVectorThreshold, releases memory and reallocates at defaultCapacity.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes and clears all child columns and the dictionaryIds column, drops the dictionary reference, and calls the abstract releaseMemory. Used when the vector is no longer needed.

nodes.name: reserveAdditional
nodes.summary: Reserves room for additionalCapacity more elements beyond elementsAppended by delegating to reserve.

nodes.name: reserve
nodes.summary: Ensures capacity for requiredCapacity elements. It grows to twice the request (or by hugeVectorReserveRatio above hugeVectorThreshold), capped at MAX_CAPACITY, calls reserveInternal, and converts overflow or OutOfMemoryError into a descriptive exception via throwUnsupportedException.

nodes.name: throwUnsupportedException
nodes.summary: Builds and throws a RuntimeException explaining that contiguous bytes could not be reserved in the vectorized reader. The message suggests reducing the batch size, disabling the vectorized reader or bucketing, and names the Parquet and ORC batch size and enabled settings taken from SQLConf.

nodes.name: reserveDictionaryIds
nodes.summary: Returns an integer column for dictionary ids. It creates one with reserveNewColumn on first use, otherwise resets and reserves the existing dictionaryIds column.

nodes.name: putBooleans
nodes.summary: Overload that writes count booleans from one bit-packed source byte starting at bit srcIndex. It expands the 8 bits into the byte8 scratch array and calls putBytes. Two abstract overloads (lines 247 and 273) write a repeated value and a bit-packed byte of 8 booleans.

nodes.name: putByteArray
nodes.summary: Overload that appends length bytes from a ByteBuffer to the child array data column and records offset and length for rowId with putArray. Other overloads: an abstract one taking a byte array range (line 440) and a final one storing a whole byte array (lines 441-443).

nodes.name: appendBytes
nodes.summary: Overload that appends length bytes from a byte array at offset, reserving space and advancing elementsAppended, and returns the first row id. Other overloads append a repeated byte (lines 618-624) and bytes from a ByteBuffer (package-private, lines 456-462).

nodes.name: getDecimal
nodes.summary: Reads a Decimal at rowId, or null when the row is null. It uses getInt or getLong for precisions that fit, and otherwise reads the bytes as a BigInteger with the given scale.

nodes.name: putDecimal
nodes.summary: Stores a Decimal at rowId as an int, a long, or a big-integer byte array, chosen by the precision.

nodes.name: putInterval
nodes.summary: Stores a CalendarInterval by writing months, days and microseconds into child columns 0, 1 and 2.

nodes.name: getUTF8String
nodes.summary: Returns the UTF8String at rowId, or null. Without a dictionary it reads from the child array data column; with a dictionary it decodes the dictionary id to bytes.

nodes.name: getBinary
nodes.summary: Returns the byte array at rowId, or null. It reads from the child array data column, or decodes through the dictionary when one is set.

nodes.name: getBinaryView
nodes.summary: Returns a BinaryView for the bytes at rowId, or null. It reads a view from the child array data column or builds one from dictionary-decoded bytes.

nodes.name: appendNull
nodes.summary: Appends a null at the write cursor and returns its row id. It asserts that the type is not a struct (appendStruct must be used for structs).

nodes.name: appendNulls
nodes.summary: Appends count nulls after reserving space, asserting that the type is not a struct, and returns the first row id.

nodes.name: appendBooleans
nodes.summary: Overload that appends count bits from a bit-packed byte starting at offset. Another overload (lines 592-598) appends a repeated boolean value.

nodes.name: appendByteArray
nodes.summary: Appends a byte array range as one variable-length value: the bytes are appended to the child array data column and the offset and length are stored at the next row with putArray.

nodes.name: appendArray
nodes.summary: Appends one array entry of the given length: it reserves space for a row and, in each child column, for length elements, then records the child offset and length with putArray.

nodes.name: appendStruct
nodes.summary: Appends a struct row. For a null struct it appends a null here and recursively appends nulls to every child column (using appendStruct for struct and variant children); otherwise it appends a not-null entry.

nodes.name: appendObjects
nodes.summary: Appends length copies of a Java object by testing its runtime class: Boolean, Byte, Decimal, Double, Float, Integer, Long, Short, UTF8String, GenericArrayData, GenericInternalRow and ArrayBasedMapData. It dispatches to the matching append method (recursing into child columns for arrays, rows and maps) and returns Optional.empty() for unsupported values.

nodes.name: getArray
nodes.summary: Returns a ColumnarArray view over the child array data column for the offset and length at rowId, or null for a null row.

nodes.name: getMap
nodes.summary: Returns a ColumnarMap built from child columns 0 (keys) and 1 (values) with the offset and length at rowId, or null for a null row.

nodes.name: setIsConstant
nodes.summary: Marks this column and, recursively, its child columns as constant, so values never change across resets.

nodes.name: isAllNull
nodes.summary: Returns true when the column is missing or its type is NullType, meaning it holds only nulls.

nodes.name: isArray
nodes.summary: Returns true when values are stored as offset and length into a child data column: array, binary, string, geometry and geography types and byte-array decimals.

nodes.name: expandBoolByteToLong
nodes.summary: Looks up BOOL_BYTE_TO_LONG_TABLE to expand each bit of a bit-packed boolean byte into its own byte within a long, in little-endian layout.

nodes.name: WritableColumnVector
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores capacity, reads the huge vector threshold and reserve ratio from SQLConf, and allocates child columns with reserveNewColumn: one for array-like types (byte children for binary and string), one per field for structs, key and value for maps, three for calendar intervals (int, int, long) and two binary columns for variants.

nodes.name: ColumnAccessor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ColumnAccessor trait that reads values one at a time from a columnar byte buffer into an InternalRow, a BasicColumnAccessor base class, one accessor class per data type, and the ColumnAccessor companion object that picks the accessor for a DataType and decompresses a buffer into a WritableColumnVector. Used when reading cached columnar data.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with private[columnar] traits and classes that stack NullableColumnAccessor and CompressibleColumnAccessor as mixins on a basic accessor.

nodes.name: ColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Trait (lines 39-49) for an Iterator-like reader over a columnar byte buffer: hasNext says whether more values remain and extractTo(row, ordinal) writes the next value into a field of an InternalRow using primitive setters to avoid boxing. initialize() is called at construction and underlyingBuffer exposes the buffer. The companion object (lines 139-184, same node id) has apply, which creates the accessor for a DataType (setting the buffer to native byte order and unwrapping user-defined types), and two decompress methods that fill a WritableColumnVector from a NativeColumnAccessor or from a byte array, and throw for non-primitive accessors.

nodes.name: BasicColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Abstract base accessor holding a ByteBuffer and a ColumnType. hasNext is buffer.hasRemaining, extractTo calls extractSingle, and extractSingle asks the column type to extract the next value from the buffer into the row at the given ordinal.

nodes.name: NullColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for the null type; uses the NULL column type and the NullableColumnAccessor mixin.

nodes.name: NativeColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Abstract accessor for primitive-like types, built on BasicColumnAccessor with the NullableColumnAccessor and CompressibleColumnAccessor mixins, so it handles nulls and compressed data. Its decompress method (from the mixin) is what ColumnAccessor.decompress calls.

nodes.name: BooleanColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the BOOLEAN column type.

nodes.name: ByteColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the BYTE column type.

nodes.name: ShortColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the SHORT column type.

nodes.name: IntColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the INT column type; chosen for integer, date and year-month interval types.

nodes.name: LongColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the LONG column type; chosen for long, timestamp, timestamp without time zone, day-time interval and time types.

nodes.name: FloatColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the FLOAT column type.

nodes.name: DoubleColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor using the DOUBLE column type.

nodes.name: StringColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor for strings, built with the STRING column type for the given StringType.

nodes.name: BinaryColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for byte arrays using the BINARY column type and the NullableColumnAccessor mixin (no compression).

nodes.name: IntervalColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for CalendarInterval values using the CALENDAR_INTERVAL column type and the NullableColumnAccessor mixin.

nodes.name: VariantColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for VariantVal values using the VARIANT column type and the NullableColumnAccessor mixin.

nodes.name: CompactDecimalColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Native accessor for decimals whose precision fits in a long, using the COMPACT_DECIMAL column type.

nodes.name: DecimalColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for large decimals, using the LARGE_DECIMAL column type and the NullableColumnAccessor mixin.

nodes.name: StructColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for struct values read as UnsafeRow, using the STRUCT column type over a PhysicalStructType built from the struct fields.

nodes.name: ArrayColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for array values read as UnsafeArrayData, using the ARRAY column type over a PhysicalArrayType with the element type and containsNull flag.

nodes.name: MapColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Accessor for map values read as UnsafeMapData, using the MAP column type over a PhysicalMapType with key type, value type and valueContainsNull flag.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory (tail-recursive) that sets the buffer to native byte order and returns the accessor matching a DataType: null, boolean, byte, short, int (also date and year-month interval), long (also timestamp types, day-time interval, time), float, double, string, binary, compact or large decimal by precision, struct, array and map. A user-defined type recurses on its sqlType; any other type raises QueryExecutionErrors.notSupportTypeError.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Overload that decompresses a NativeColumnAccessor into a WritableColumnVector for numRows rows, throwing notSupportNonPrimitiveTypeError for any other accessor. Another overload (lines 177-183) takes a byte array and a DataType, wraps the array in a ByteBuffer, builds the accessor with apply and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: ColumnBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ColumnBuilder trait and its builder classes that turn rows of one column into a single byte buffer for the in-memory columnar cache, with one builder per data type family. The companion object creates the right builder for a Spark SQL data type.
nodes.languageNotes: Builders are assembled by stacking traits (NullableColumnBuilder, AllCompressionSchemes, CompressibleColumnBuilder) on top of BasicColumnBuilder.

nodes.name: ColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Trait for building a column byte buffer: initialize with an expected size, appendFrom a row ordinal, expose columnStats, and build() the final ByteBuffer. Its companion object (lines 157-211) holds DEFAULT_INITIAL_BUFFER_SIZE (128 KB), MAX_BATCH_SIZE_IN_BYTE (4 MB), ensureFreeSpace (grows a buffer) and apply(dataType, ...) which picks the concrete builder for a DataType, unwraps user defined types to their sqlType and throws for unsupported types.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: maps a DataType to a concrete builder (for example IntegerType, DateType and year-month intervals to IntColumnBuilder; LongType, timestamps, day-time intervals and TimeType to LongColumnBuilder; small decimals to CompactDecimalColumnBuilder), recurses on a user defined type's sqlType, throws via QueryExecutionErrors for other types, then calls initialize on the builder.

nodes.name: ensureFreeSpace
nodes.summary: Returns the given ByteBuffer if it has enough remaining bytes; otherwise allocates a larger native-order buffer (capacity plus the larger of the request or the capacity) and copies the written bytes into it.

nodes.name: BasicColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Base builder that holds a ColumnStats and a ColumnType and writes each non-null value into a growing native-order ByteBuffer. initialize allocates the buffer, appendFrom grows it with ensureFreeSpace and appends via the column type, and build trims the buffer when it is more than 10 percent over-allocated and flips it for reading.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Allocates a native-order ByteBuffer of initialSize times the column type's default size (using DEFAULT_INITIAL_BUFFER_SIZE when the size is 0) and stores the column name.

nodes.name: appendFrom
nodes.summary: Ensures the buffer has room for the actual size of row(ordinal), then appends the value with the column type.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Trims the buffer to its written length when the capacity exceeds the position by more than 10 percent, then flips it and returns it.

nodes.name: NullColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for NullType columns: a BasicColumnBuilder with ObjectColumnStats(NullType) and the NULL column type, mixed with NullableColumnBuilder.

nodes.name: ComplexColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Abstract builder for non-native types that stacks NullableColumnBuilder on BasicColumnBuilder and does not use compression. It is the base of the binary, interval, variant, large decimal, struct, array and map builders.

nodes.name: NativeColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Abstract builder for native fixed-width and string types. Extends BasicColumnBuilder and stacks NullableColumnBuilder, AllCompressionSchemes and CompressibleColumnBuilder so these columns can be compressed.

nodes.name: BooleanColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Boolean column buffer using BooleanColumnStats and the BOOLEAN column type. Supports compression.

nodes.name: ByteColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Byte column buffer using ByteColumnStats and the BYTE column type. Supports compression.

nodes.name: ShortColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Short column buffer using ShortColumnStats and the SHORT column type. Supports compression.

nodes.name: IntColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds an Int column buffer using IntColumnStats and the INT column type. ColumnBuilder.apply also uses it for dates and year-month intervals. Supports compression.

nodes.name: LongColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Long column buffer using LongColumnStats and the LONG column type. ColumnBuilder.apply also uses it for timestamps, day-time intervals and TimeType. Supports compression.

nodes.name: FloatColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Float column buffer using FloatColumnStats and the FLOAT column type. Supports compression.

nodes.name: DoubleColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a Double column buffer using DoubleColumnStats and the DOUBLE column type. Supports compression.

nodes.name: StringColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a string column buffer for a given StringType, using StringColumnStats and STRING(dataType) so collation is respected. Supports compression.

nodes.name: BinaryColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a binary column buffer using BinaryColumnStats and the BINARY column type, without compression.

nodes.name: IntervalColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a CalendarInterval column buffer using IntervalColumnStats and the CALENDAR_INTERVAL column type, without compression.

nodes.name: VariantColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a variant column buffer using VariantColumnStats and the VARIANT column type, without compression.

nodes.name: CompactDecimalColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a column buffer for decimals whose precision fits in a long (precision <= Decimal.MAX_LONG_DIGITS), using DecimalColumnStats and COMPACT_DECIMAL(dataType). Supports compression.

nodes.name: DecimalColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a column buffer for decimals with larger precision, using DecimalColumnStats and LARGE_DECIMAL(dataType), without compression.

nodes.name: StructColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a struct column buffer using ObjectColumnStats and STRUCT(PhysicalStructType(fields)), without compression.

nodes.name: ArrayColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds an array column buffer using ObjectColumnStats and ARRAY(PhysicalArrayType(elementType, containsNull)), without compression.

nodes.name: MapColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds a map column buffer using ObjectColumnStats and MAP(PhysicalMapType(keyType, valueType, valueContainsNull)), without compression.

nodes.name: NullableColumnBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the stackable NullableColumnBuilder trait, which records the positions of null values separately and writes only non-null values into the column buffer. The final buffer is the null count, the null positions, then the non-null elements.

nodes.name: NullableColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Stackable trait over ColumnBuilder for columns that may contain nulls. It keeps a null-position buffer and a null count, gathers column statistics on every append, forwards only non-null values to the underlying builder, and in build() prepends the 4-byte null count and the 4 x N null positions to the non-null data. buildNonNulls() lets compression-aware builders get the non-null part alone.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Allocates a 1024-byte native-order null-position buffer, resets the position and null count, then calls the underlying initialize.

nodes.name: appendFrom
nodes.summary: Gathers statistics for row(ordinal); for a null value records the current position in the null buffer and increments the null count, otherwise delegates to the underlying appendFrom. Always advances the row position.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the non-null data from the underlying builder and returns a new buffer laid out as null count, null positions, then non-null elements.

nodes.name: buildNonNulls
nodes.summary: Rewinds the null buffer and returns the underlying builder's non-null buffer without the null header, for use by the compressible builder.

nodes.name: NullableColumnAccessor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the stackable NullableColumnAccessor trait, the reading counterpart of NullableColumnBuilder, which skips the null header and sets nulls on the output row at the recorded positions.

nodes.name: NullableColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Stackable trait over ColumnAccessor that reads the null count and null positions at the start of the buffer, advances the buffer past them, and on each extractTo writes a null into the row when the current position is a null position, otherwise delegates to the underlying extractTo. hasNext stays true while nulls remain to be returned.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Duplicates the buffer to read the null count and first null index, moves the underlying buffer position past the 4 + 4 x nullCount header bytes, then calls the underlying initialize.

nodes.name: extractTo
nodes.summary: Sets row(ordinal) to null when the current position equals the next null index (and reads the following null index), otherwise delegates to the underlying extractTo; then advances the position.

nodes.name: CompressibleColumnAccessor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CompressibleColumnAccessor trait that reads a compressed column buffer by picking the compression scheme from the stored scheme id and delegating value reads and bulk decompression to its decoder.

nodes.name: CompressibleColumnAccessor
nodes.summary: Trait mixed into a NativeColumnAccessor. On initialize it reads the 4-byte compression scheme id and creates the matching Decoder; extractSingle decodes one value into a row; decompress fills a WritableColumnVector in bulk; hasNext also consults the decoder.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Calls the underlying initialize, then reads the scheme id from the buffer and creates the decoder with CompressionScheme(id).decoder.

nodes.name: extractSingle
nodes.summary: Decodes the next value from the decoder into row(ordinal).

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Passes a WritableColumnVector and a capacity to the decoder so that the whole column is decompressed into the vector.

nodes.name: CompressibleColumnBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CompressibleColumnBuilder trait that picks the best compression encoder for a native column while values are appended and writes the final buffer with a compression scheme id. The companion object records whether the platform allows unaligned access.

nodes.name: CompressibleColumnBuilder
nodes.summary: Stackable trait for native column builders. When compression is enabled it creates an encoder for each scheme that supports the column type, otherwise only PassThrough; each non-null append feeds compressibility statistics to every encoder, and build() picks the encoder with the lowest compressionRatio (used only if below 0.8 and the platform is unaligned-capable) and writes null count, null positions, scheme id and the compressed body. Its companion object (lines 112-114) holds the val unaligned = Platform.unaligned().

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Builds the list of compression encoders (all supporting schemes if useCompression is true, otherwise only PassThrough) then calls the underlying initialize.

nodes.name: isWorthCompressing
nodes.summary: Returns true when the platform supports unaligned access and the encoder's compressionRatio is below 0.8.

nodes.name: gatherCompressibilityStats
nodes.summary: Feeds row(ordinal) to every candidate encoder so it can estimate its compressed size.

nodes.name: appendFrom
nodes.summary: Delegates to the underlying appendFrom and, for non-null values, gathers compressibility statistics.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Gets the non-null buffer, selects the encoder with the smallest compression ratio (or PassThrough if not worth compressing), writes null count and null positions as the header, reserves 4 bytes for the scheme id, and lets the encoder compress the data into the final buffer.

nodes.name: ColumnStats.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the per-column statistics collectors used while building in-memory columnar batches: the schema of the stored stats, and a ColumnStats implementation per data type that tracks lower bound, upper bound, null count, row count and size in bytes.
nodes.languageNotes: ColumnStats avoids Ordering[T] on purpose for performance, so each typed class compares values directly.

nodes.name: ColumnStatisticsSchema
nodes.summary: Serializable helper that builds, for one table attribute a, the five attribute references used to store its batch statistics: lowerBound, upperBound, nullCount, count and sizeInBytes (named a.name + suffix). The schema field lists them in that order.

nodes.name: PartitionStatistics
nodes.summary: Serializable holder that maps each table attribute to its ColumnStatisticsSchema (forAttribute, an AttributeMap) and exposes the flattened list of all statistics attributes as schema. Used to describe the stats row stored per cached batch.

nodes.name: ColumnStats
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for statistics gathered while a column is built. It keeps count, nullCount and sizeInBytes, requires gatherStats(row, ordinal) and collectedStatistics (an array of lower bound, upper bound, null count, count and size), and provides gatherNullStats, which adds 4 bytes for the null position.

nodes.name: gatherNullStats
nodes.summary: Records a null value: increments nullCount and count and adds 4 bytes (the null position) to sizeInBytes.

nodes.name: NoopColumnStats
nodes.summary: ColumnStats that only counts rows and nulls and reports null bounds and size 0. Documented as used for testing purposes only.

nodes.name: BooleanColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Boolean values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the BOOLEAN column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: ByteColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Byte values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the BYTE column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: ShortColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Short values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the SHORT column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: IntColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Int values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the INT column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: LongColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Long values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the LONG column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: FloatColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Float values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the FLOAT column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: DoubleColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Double values (lower and upper bound) of a column via gatherStats and gatherValueStats, adding the DOUBLE column type's default size to sizeInBytes for each value; nulls go through gatherNullStats.

nodes.name: StringColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max UTF8String values using semanticCompare with the collation id (given directly or taken from a StringType through the auxiliary constructor), cloning the bound values, and adds the STRING column type's actual size to sizeInBytes.

nodes.name: gatherValueStats
nodes.summary: Updates upper and lower bound with semanticCompare under the collation id (cloning the string), adds the size, and increments count.

nodes.name: BinaryColumnStats
nodes.summary: Counts rows, nulls and bytes (BINARY actual size) for a binary column; reports null bounds because no min or max is kept.

nodes.name: VariantColumnStats
nodes.summary: Counts rows, nulls and bytes (VARIANT actual size) for a variant column; reports null bounds because no min or max is kept.

nodes.name: IntervalColumnStats
nodes.summary: Counts rows, nulls and bytes (CALENDAR_INTERVAL actual size) for an interval column; reports null bounds because no min or max is kept.

nodes.name: DecimalColumnStats
nodes.summary: Tracks min and max Decimal values (read with the given precision and scale, also constructible from a DecimalType) using compareTo, and adds a fixed 8 bytes per value to sizeInBytes. A TODO in the source notes this is not right for precision above 18.

nodes.name: ObjectColumnStats
nodes.summary: Statistics for complex or object columns (null, struct, array, map): counts rows and nulls and sums the actual size from the ColumnType built for the data type; no bounds are kept.

nodes.name: compressionSchemes.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the six column compression schemes used by the in-memory columnar cache: PassThrough (id 0), RunLengthEncoding (1), DictionaryEncoding (2), BooleanBitSet (3), IntDelta (4) and LongDelta (5). Each scheme is a case object with an Encoder that estimates sizes and compresses a buffer, and a Decoder that reads values one at a time or decompresses a whole column into a WritableColumnVector.
nodes.languageNotes: Each scheme is a case object with nested Encoder and Decoder classes that extend the traits in CompressionScheme.scala (referred to as compression.Encoder and compression.Decoder).

nodes.name: PassThrough
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 0 that supports every column type and stores the data uncompressed: its Encoder writes the scheme id and copies the raw bytes. Its Decoder reads values with the column type and can bulk-copy boolean, byte, short, int, long, float and double data into a WritableColumnVector while handling null positions.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for PassThrough: uncompressedSize and compressedSize are both 0, and compress writes the PassThrough type id followed by the raw contents of the source buffer.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Writes the PassThrough type id into the target buffer, appends the source buffer contents, rewinds and returns the target.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for PassThrough: next extracts one value with the column type, hasNext checks the buffer, and decompress copies data into a WritableColumnVector using type specific helpers (putBooleans, putBytes, putShorts, putInts, putLongs, putFloats, putDoubles) through decompress0.

nodes.name: decompress0
nodes.summary: Generic bulk decompression loop: reads the null count and null positions from a duplicate of the buffer, copies runs of non-null values with the given put function (unit size per element), and puts nulls at the null positions.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the physical data type (boolean, byte, short, integer, long, float, double) and calls decompress0 with the matching unit size and put function.

nodes.name: RunLengthEncoding
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 1 that supports INT, LONG, SHORT, BYTE, STRING and BOOLEAN columns. Consecutive equal values are stored as a (value, run length) pair; the Encoder estimates the compressed size by counting runs and the Decoder expands runs on read or on bulk decompression.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for RunLengthEncoding. While gathering stats it tracks the last value and counts each new run as actual size plus 4 bytes; compress writes the type id and then each run as the value followed by an int run length.

nodes.name: gatherCompressibilityStats
nodes.summary: Adds the value's actual size to the uncompressed size and, when the value differs from the previous one (or is the first), adds actual size + 4 bytes to the compressed size and starts a new run.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Writes the type id and walks the source buffer, emitting a value and an int run length whenever the value changes, plus the final run.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for RunLengthEncoding: next reads a new value and run length when the current run is exhausted and sets the field on the row; decompress and decompress0 fill a WritableColumnVector for boolean, byte, short, integer and long columns, with null handling, and throw an internal error for other types.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: If the current run is used up, reads the next value and its run length; otherwise advances inside the run; then sets the current value on the row.

nodes.name: decompress0
nodes.summary: Bulk decoding loop that reads null positions from a duplicate of the buffer, reads value and run length pairs through the get function, and writes each position with the put function or marks it null.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the physical type (boolean, byte, short, integer, long) to call decompress0 with the matching get and put helpers; any other type raises SparkException.internalError.

nodes.name: DictionaryEncoding
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 2 that supports INT, LONG and STRING columns. Distinct values are written once as a dictionary (at most MAX_DICT_SIZE = Short.MaxValue entries) and each element is stored as a 2-byte index. If the dictionary overflows the Encoder reports Int.MaxValue as its compressed size so the scheme is not chosen.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for DictionaryEncoding. While gathering stats it builds a value-to-short dictionary and the reverse value list, setting an overflow flag when the dictionary is full; compress writes the type id, the dictionary size, the dictionary values and then a short code per element. compressedSize is dictionarySize + count * 2, or Int.MaxValue on overflow.

nodes.name: gatherCompressibilityStats
nodes.summary: For each new distinct value adds a cloned entry to the dictionary and values list (growing the dictionary size by the value's actual size); once the dictionary reaches MAX_DICT_SIZE it sets overflow and clears the structures.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Throws QueryExecutionErrors.useDictionaryEncodingWhenDictionaryOverflowError if the dictionary overflowed; otherwise writes the type id, the dictionary size, every dictionary value, and one short code per value of the source buffer.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for DictionaryEncoding: the constructor reads the dictionary (into generic and, for int or long columns, primitive arrays), next looks up the short code on each read, and decompress sets a ColumnDictionary on the WritableColumnVector and writes dictionary ids per position, putting nulls at null positions.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Reserves dictionary ids on the vector and sets a ColumnDictionary over the int or long dictionary, then stores each element's 2-byte index as a dictionary id and puts nulls at null positions; other types throw an internal error.

nodes.name: BooleanBitSet
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 3 that supports only the BOOLEAN column type. Boolean values are packed 64 per long word (BITS_PER_LONG = 64) after a 4-byte element count.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for BooleanBitSet: counts the uncompressed size as one byte per value; compress writes the type id, the element count and the values as packed long words; compressedSize is the number of long words times 8 plus 4.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Writes the type id and element count, then packs each group of 64 booleans (and a final partial group) into one long word bit by bit.

nodes.name: compressedSize
nodes.summary: Computes the size of the packed words, rounding up to a whole long, plus 4 bytes for the count.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for BooleanBitSet: reads the element count, fetches a new long word every 64 values and extracts one bit per value; decompress does the same into a WritableColumnVector while skipping null positions.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Loads a new long word when the bit index wraps to 0 and sets the row's boolean from the current bit.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Walks capacity positions, putting nulls at null positions and otherwise reading the next bit of the current word into the vector with putBoolean.

nodes.name: IntDelta
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 4 that supports only the INT column type. Each value after the first is stored as a 1-byte delta from the previous one; when the delta does not fit, the marker Byte.MinValue is written followed by the full 4-byte int.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for IntDelta: gathers an estimated size (1 byte per value plus 4 bytes for the first value or for out-of-range deltas) and compress writes the type id, then either deltas or full ints behind the Byte.MinValue marker.

nodes.name: gatherCompressibilityStats
nodes.summary: Computes the delta to the previous int and adds 1 byte to the compressed size, plus 4 bytes if this is the first value or the delta is outside the byte range.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Writes the type id, then the first int behind the Byte.MinValue marker, then for each following int writes a 1-byte delta or the marker with the full int.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for IntDelta: reads a byte, adds it to the previous value or, when it is Byte.MinValue, reads a full int; decompress applies the same decoding into a WritableColumnVector with null handling.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Reads one delta byte and updates the running int (previous + delta, or a full int after the marker), then sets it on the row.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Decodes all deltas into the vector with putInt, putting nulls at the recorded null positions.

nodes.name: LongDelta
nodes.summary: Compression scheme with typeId 5 that supports only the LONG column type. Same layout as IntDelta but for longs: a 1-byte delta, or Byte.MinValue followed by the full 8-byte long.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for LongDelta: estimates size with 1 byte per value plus 8 bytes for the first value or out-of-range deltas, and compress writes the type id followed by deltas or full longs behind the Byte.MinValue marker.

nodes.name: gatherCompressibilityStats
nodes.summary: Computes the delta to the previous long and adds 1 byte to the compressed size, plus 8 bytes if this is the first value or the delta is outside the byte range.

nodes.name: compress
nodes.summary: Writes the type id, then the first long behind the Byte.MinValue marker, then for each following long writes a 1-byte delta or the marker with the full long.

nodes.name: Decoder
nodes.summary: Decoder for LongDelta: reads a byte, adds it to the previous value or reads a full long after the Byte.MinValue marker; decompress applies the same decoding into a WritableColumnVector with null handling.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Reads one delta byte and updates the running long (previous + delta, or a full long after the marker), then sets it on the row.

nodes.name: decompress
nodes.summary: Decodes all deltas into the vector with putLong, putting nulls at the recorded null positions.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowAggregatePythonExec, the physical node that evaluates grouped-aggregate Python UDFs (Arrow and Pandas eval types, with or without the iterator API) by sending grouped, projected input as Arrow record batches to a Python worker. Used when a plan contains aggregation with vectorized Python UDAFs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec
nodes.summary: Physical UnaryExecNode for aggregation with grouped-aggregate vectorized Python UDFs (SQL_GROUPED_AGG_ARROW_UDF, SQL_GROUPED_AGG_ARROW_ITER_UDF, SQL_GROUPED_AGG_PANDAS_UDF, SQL_GROUPED_AGG_PANDAS_ITER_UDF). doExecute groups the child rows (wrapping them in UpdatingSessionsIterator when a session window is present), projects only the deduplicated UDF inputs, buffers grouping keys in a HybridRowQueue, runs an ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner with GroupedPythonArrowInput, then joins each Python result row with its key and applies the post-aggregation result expressions. Requires ClusteredDistribution (or AllTuples when there is no grouping) and ascending ordering by the grouping keys. The companion object apply checks that all aggregate functions share one eval type.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires AllTuples when there are no grouping expressions, otherwise ClusteredDistribution on the grouping expressions.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child to be sorted ascending by the grouping expressions; with a session window the session expression is appended after the other grouping expressions.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.collectFunctions
nodes.summary: Recursively unwraps nested PythonFuncExpression children into a ChainedPythonFunctions plus the result id and the innermost input expressions that can be evaluated directly.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds the argument metadata and input schema from the UDAFs, then per non-empty partition groups the rows, queues keys in a HybridRowQueue, streams the grouped projected rows to the Python runner and joins each aggregate output with its queued key before applying resultExpressions.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.mayAppendUpdatingSessionIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps the row iterator in an UpdatingSessionsIterator (using the window exec buffer thresholds from conf) when a session window expression is present; otherwise returns the iterator unchanged.

nodes.name: ArrowAggregatePythonExec.apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that reads the eval type from the PythonUDAF aggregate functions, asserts that all share the same eval type, and builds the exec node.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonUDTFExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowEvalPythonUDTFExec, the physical node that evaluates a Python UDTF using Arrow. Used for Python table functions whose results are exchanged as Arrow record batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonUDTFExec
nodes.summary: EvalPythonUDTFExec subclass that runs a PythonUDTF through ArrowPythonUDTFRunner. It reads arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch, the session time zone, arrowUseLargeVarTypes and the Python worker logging setting from conf; evaluate batches the input with BatchIterator, flattens the single struct column in each returned ColumnarBatch into the result attributes, and fails with arrowDataTypeMismatchError if the actual types differ from the expected ones. withNewChildInternal copies the node.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonUDTFExec.evaluate
nodes.summary: Splits the input iterator into batches (or one iterator when the batch size is not positive), runs ArrowPythonUDTFRunner, unpacks the struct column of each ColumnarBatch into the result vectors, validates the column data types against resultAttrs (UDT replaced by its sqlType) and yields an iterator of rows per batch.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory and its nested partition evaluator, which compute window bounds per frame and feed data plus bound indices to a Python worker for window-aggregate UDFs. Used by ArrowWindowPythonExec.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory and WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase for Python window UDFs. Its helpers collectFunctions (unwrap chained PythonFuncExpression) and computeWindowBoundHelpers (decide per frame whether the window is bounded or unbounded and assign lower and upper bound column indices) feed the nested WindowInPandasPartitionEvaluator returned by createEvaluator. It carries the "window_bound_types" runner conf key, and private WindowBoundType values "unbounded" and "bounded".

nodes.name: WindowBoundType
nodes.summary: Private sealed case class holding the string value of a window bound type; used only inside the factory to tag frames and to build the "window_bound_types" conf string.

nodes.name: UnboundedWindow
nodes.summary: Private object extending WindowBoundType with the value "unbounded", used for frames that need no bound indices (unbounded window function frames).

nodes.name: BoundedWindow
nodes.summary: Private object extending WindowBoundType with the value "bounded", used for sliding and half-unbounded frames that need lower and upper bound indices.

nodes.name: WindowInPandasPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluator that does the per-partition work. Its constructor body derives frame/expression indices, window bound types, the Python runner conf (with "window_bound_types"), deduplicated data inputs, window-bound BoundReference inputs and the argument offsets of each UDF (shifted past the bound columns). eval builds a HybridRowQueue of input rows, an anonymous iterator that groups rows by partitionSpec, buffers each group in an ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray, prepares the frames and writes window bounds into an index row for every row, runs an ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner with GroupedPythonArrowInput, and joins each Python result with the queued input row.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory.collectFunctions
nodes.summary: Recursively unwraps nested PythonFuncExpression children into a ChainedPythonFunctions plus the result id and the innermost input expressions; same logic as the aggregate exec.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory.computeWindowBoundHelpers
nodes.summary: Instantiates the frame factories with an empty row, tags each frame as bounded or unbounded, assigns two bound columns (lower, upper) to bounded frames and sentinel -1 to unbounded ones, and returns the total bound count, lower/upper index functions and the bound types.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory.createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Returns a new WindowInPandasPartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: WindowInPandasPartitionEvaluator.eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates one partition: queues each input row, iterates window partitions (grouped by partitionSpec) with frame bounds written into an index row, sends projected python input to the Python runner and joins each output row with the queued input row via the result projection. Spill size of the buffer is added to the spillSize metric when input is exhausted.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowWindowPythonExec, the physical node for windowed aggregates computed by vectorized Python UDFs. It prepares window bounds and delegates the per-partition work to ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonExec
nodes.summary: WindowExecBase node supporting SQL_WINDOW_AGG_ARROW_UDF and SQL_WINDOW_AGG_PANDAS_UDF. As its class doc explains, it does not compute window aggregates itself: it computes lower and upper bound per window, groups window expressions that share a frame so they share bounds, prepends the bounds to the data sent to the Python worker, and evaluates bounded windows once per row and unbounded windows once per partition. Metrics are the Python metrics plus a "spillSize" size metric. The companion apply extracts the eval type from the PythonUDAF window expressions and asserts they are all the same.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Creates an ArrowWindowPythonEvaluatorFactory and runs it with mapPartitionsWithEvaluator when conf.usePartitionEvaluator is set, or otherwise creates an evaluator inside mapPartitionsWithIndex.

nodes.name: ArrowWindowPythonExec.apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that derives the eval type from the window expressions via WindowFunctionType.pythonEvalType, asserts a single eval type, and builds the exec node.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.scala
nodes.summary: Defines QueueMode, the Queue trait and the generic HybridQueue base class, a memory consumer whose queue storage can be memory pages or disk and which can spill in-memory queues to disk. Used as the base of HybridRowQueue.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: QueueMode
nodes.summary: Enumeration object with the values IN_MEMORY and DISK, returned by HybridQueue.add to say where an element was stored.

nodes.name: Queue
nodes.summary: Generic trait with add (returns false when full), remove (returns null when empty) and close.

nodes.name: HybridQueue
nodes.summary: Abstract MemoryConsumer holding a linked list of sub-queues that are either in-memory (backed by an allocated page) or on disk. add writes into the current queue and, when it is full, creates a new queue: in memory if allocatePage succeeds, else on disk (SparkOutOfMemoryError is caught). remove reads from the oldest queue and closes it when drained. spill converts in-memory queues (except the last one) into disk queues in the same order, and returns 0 when it is triggered by itself. It tracks numElementsQueued and numElementsQueuedOnDisk. Subclasses supply createDiskQueue, createInMemoryQueue, getRequiredSize, getPageSize and isInMemoryQueue.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.spill
nodes.summary: Spill callback: returns 0 when the trigger is this queue itself; otherwise drains every in-memory queue except the last into a new disk queue (keeping order), closes the old queue and returns the released page bytes.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.createNewQueue
nodes.summary: Tries to allocate a page of the required size and creates an in-memory queue from it, falling back to a disk queue when allocation raises SparkOutOfMemoryError; registers the queue in the list.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.add
nodes.summary: Adds an item to the current writing queue, creating a new queue if it is absent or full; throws failedToPushRowIntoRowQueueError if even a fresh queue rejects it. Returns QueueMode.IN_MEMORY or QueueMode.DISK.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.remove
nodes.summary: Reads the next item from the current reading queue; when it is drained, closes it and takes the next queue from the list. Updates the element counters.

nodes.name: HybridQueue.close
nodes.summary: Closes the reading queue and every remaining queue in the list.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogsExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonWorkerLogsExec, a leaf physical node that reads stored Python worker log lines of the current session as a single JSON-string column.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogsExec
nodes.summary: LeafExecNode with one output attribute (jsonAttr) and a "numOutputRows" metric. doExecute looks up block ids of PythonWorkerLogBlockId for the session UUID, builds a BlockRDD of PythonWorkerLogLine and converts the message of each line into an InternalRow with a String encoder serializer.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogsExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Collects the matching block ids, creates a BlockRDD over them and maps each PythonWorkerLogLine to a copied row built from its message, counting numOutputRows.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogsExec.getBlockIds
nodes.summary: Asks the block manager master (including storage endpoints) for block ids that are PythonWorkerLogBlockId with the given session id and returns the distinct list.

nodes.name: RowQueue.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the UnsafeRow queue types used by Python UDF execution: RowQueue, a page-based InMemoryRowQueue, a file-backed DiskRowQueue and HybridRowQueue, which combines them under a TaskMemoryManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: RowQueue
nodes.summary: Trait specializing Queue for UnsafeRow. Per its doc, it is designed only for Python UDFs: one writer and one reader, with the reader always running behind the writer.

nodes.name: InMemoryRowQueue
nodes.summary: Abstract RowQueue over a MemoryBlock page. Rows are stored as a 4-byte length followed by the row bytes, and -1 marks the end of the page. add returns false when the row does not fit, remove returns null at the end, and both are synchronized so a reader can follow the writer.

nodes.name: DiskRowQueue
nodes.summary: RowQueue backed by a file. It writes length-prefixed rows through a serializer-manager wrapped stream, stops accepting rows once reading has begun (the output is closed on the first remove) and deletes the file on close.

nodes.name: HybridRowQueue
nodes.summary: HybridQueue[UnsafeRow, RowQueue] that creates DiskRowQueue files in a temp dir and InMemoryRowQueue instances over allocated pages (freed with freePage on close). It sizes requests as 4 plus the row size. The companion object apply overloads default the serializer manager to SparkEnv.get.serializerManager and the temp dir to Utils.getLocalDir(conf). It is used by the Python exec nodes to buffer input rows or keys until the Python results come back.

nodes.name: InMemoryRowQueue.add
nodes.summary: Appends a row if it fits in the page (writing length then bytes); otherwise writes the end-of-page marker -1 when 4 bytes remain and returns false.

nodes.name: InMemoryRowQueue.remove
nodes.summary: Returns the next row by pointing a reusable UnsafeRow at the page, or null at the end-of-page marker; asserts that the reader does not pass the writer.

nodes.name: DiskRowQueue.add
nodes.summary: Writes the row length and bytes to the file output stream; returns false if the output has already been closed because reading started.

nodes.name: DiskRowQueue.remove
nodes.summary: On first call closes the output and opens an input stream; then reads the next length-prefixed row into a reusable UnsafeRow, or returns null when no bytes are unread.

nodes.name: DiskRowQueue.close
nodes.summary: Closes input and output streams and deletes the backing file if it exists.

nodes.name: HybridRowQueue.createDiskQueue
nodes.summary: Creates a DiskRowQueue on a new temp file in tempDir with the configured number of fields.

nodes.name: HybridRowQueue.createInMemoryQueue
nodes.summary: Creates an InMemoryRowQueue over the given page whose close frees the page.

nodes.name: HybridRowQueue.apply
