nodes.summary: Companion factory overload (taskMemoryMgr, file, fields) that supplies the serializer manager from SparkEnv; another overload (taskMemoryMgr, fields) at lines 189-191 uses a directory from Utils.getLocalDir.

nodes.name: AttachDistributedSequenceExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AttachDistributedSequenceExec physical operator, which prepends a long index column that increases by one per row to the child's output. The scaladoc says it backs the 'distributed-sequence' default index of the pandas API on Spark and 'DataFrame.zipWithIndex'; it can cache the child RDD according to a session configuration value.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class extending UnaryExecNode. The cache setting is read as a string conf and the surrounding double quotes are stripped because the value is JSON encoded by its writer.

nodes.name: AttachDistributedSequenceExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator (sequenceAttr, child, cache) that outputs the sequence attribute followed by the child's output and keeps the child's partitioning. doExecute runs the child, optionally caches its RDD via cacheRDD, calls zipWithIndex, and in each partition writes the index into an UnsafeRowWriter row that is joined to the input row and projected. cacheRDD reads the conf pandas_on_Spark.compute.default_index_cache (default MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER) and returns the RDD unchanged for one partition or NONE, uses localCheckpoint for LOCAL_CHECKPOINT, and otherwise persists with StorageLevel.fromString. cleanupResources unpersists the cached RDD without blocking. simpleString prints the output and an Index entry.

nodes.name: cacheRDD
nodes.summary: Private helper that optionally caches the child RDD. It reads pandas_on_Spark.compute.default_index_cache from SQLConf (default MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER, surrounding quotes stripped) and returns the RDD as is when it has at most one partition or the value is NONE. For LOCAL_CHECKPOINT it copies rows, calls localCheckpoint and names the RDD; otherwise it copies rows, persists with StorageLevel.fromString, stores the result in the transient field cached and names it.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the child plan, applies cacheRDD when cache is true, then uses zipWithIndex and mapPartitions to build each output row: the index is written with an UnsafeRowWriter, joined to the input row with a JoinedRow and converted with an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Releases resources of the operator. If a cached RDD exists and still has a storage level, it logs a warning with the RDD id and plan id and unpersists it without blocking; super.cleanupResources always runs in a finally block.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Builds the one-line plan description from the node name, the truncated output attributes and an 'Index: <sequenceAttr>' suffix.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonUDTFExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BatchEvalPythonUDTFExec, the physical operator that evaluates a Python user-defined table function over batches of pickled rows, and PythonUDTFRunner (with its companion object), the runner that sends the UDTF definition and arguments to the Python worker.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a case class, a runner class and a companion object that holds the shared wire-format writer writeUDTF.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonUDTFExec
nodes.summary: Case class (udtf, requiredChildOutput, resultAttrs, child) that extends EvalPythonUDTFExec with PythonSQLMetrics. It captures the job artifact UUID and, when Python worker logging is enabled in the session conf, the session UUID. Its evaluate method registers the Row picklers, builds the input iterator with BatchEvalPythonExec.getInputIterator using a fixed batch size of 100, runs a PythonUDTFRunner, unpickles each result batch and converts every result with EvaluatePython.makeFromJava into an iterator of InternalRow per input row. The scaladoc says it is similar to BatchEvalPythonExec.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluates the Python UDTF for one partition. It registers the Row picklers, builds the pickled input iterator with batch size 100 (no separate config exists for UDTFs), computes results through a PythonUDTFRunner, unpickles each batch into an ArrayList, counts rows into the pythonNumRowsReceived metric and converts each result array to an iterator of InternalRow using the converter made from the UDTF's return type.

nodes.name: PythonUDTFRunner
nodes.summary: Runner class (with companion object) for Python UDTFs that extends BasePythonUDFRunner using a single chained function and the SQL_TABLE_UDF eval type. It overrides bufferSize to read BUFFER_SIZE from the SparkEnv conf instead of the UDF setting and overrides writeUDF to delegate to the companion's writeUDTF. The companion object's writeUDTF writes the wire format of a UDTF call to the worker (see its function node).

nodes.name: writeUDF
nodes.summary: Override that writes the UDTF definition to the worker by calling PythonUDTFRunner.writeUDTF with the UDTF and its argument metadata.

nodes.name: writeUDTF
nodes.summary: Companion-object method that writes a UDTF call to the worker's output stream: the argument count and, for each argument, its offset and optional name; the PARTITION BY child indexes (or 0); a flag and the pickled AnalyzeResult bytes if any; the Python function; the result schema as JSON; and the UDTF name.

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the partition evaluator factory for Arrow-based Python UDFs that works on ColumnarBatch input and output, plus a small PeekableIterator helper. It picks one of three execution paths (Arrow columnar, non-Arrow columnar, row fallback) depending on the UDF inputs and the vector types of the first batch.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala: a private[python] factory with a private nested evaluator class; multi-line scaladoc explains the three paths and a TODO about a ProjectExec rule.

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Private[python] factory (childOutput, udfs, output, outputSchema, batchSize, evalType, session time zone, large var types, runner conf, metrics, job artifact and session UUIDs) that extends PartitionEvaluatorFactory[ColumnarBatch, ColumnarBatch]. The scaladoc describes three paths: (1) Arrow columnar, when UDF inputs are plain column references and the columns are ArrowColumnVector, so Arrow FieldVectors are serialized directly and pass-through columns are kept by reference; (2) non-Arrow columnar, where columns are plain references but not Arrow vectors, using HybridRowQueue for pass-through rows; (3) row fallback for complex input expressions, using a MutableProjection and BasicPythonArrowInput. createEvaluator returns the nested evaluator.

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowEvalPythonPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private nested evaluator (extends PartitionEvaluator[ColumnarBatch, ColumnarBatch]) holding the logic of the three paths. eval flattens UDF arguments into a de-duplicated input list with ArgumentMetadata, builds the UDF input schema and output types, peeks at the first batch to see whether it is Arrow-backed, then calls evalArrowColumnar or evalWithRowQueue. Helpers collectFunctions, resolveColumnIndices, validateOutputTypes and rowsToColumnarBatches support them.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Creates a new ColumnarArrowEvalPythonPartitionEvaluator for a partition.

nodes.name: collectFunctions
nodes.summary: Recursively unwraps nested PythonUDF calls into a chain: returns the ChainedPythonFunctions with the result id of the outermost UDF and the innermost children. It asserts the innermost children contain no PythonUDF.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Entry point for a partition. It collects UDF functions and inputs, de-duplicates arguments by semantic equality into ArgumentMetadata (handling NamedArgumentExpression), builds the UDF input schema with fields _0, _1, ..., replaces user-defined types in the output types by their sqlType, resolves plain column indices, peeks at the first batch and chooses evalArrowColumnar (inputs are plain columns and first column is an ArrowColumnVector) or evalWithRowQueue.

nodes.name: resolveColumnIndices
nodes.summary: Maps each UDF input to its position in childOutput by exprId when every input is an AttributeReference; returns None as soon as any input is a complex expression or is not found.

nodes.name: evalArrowColumnar
nodes.summary: Path 1. Queues the pass-through columns and row count of each input batch, runs a ColumnarArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner on the selected column indices, validates each result batch's types, checks that the pass-through row count equals the result row count, and returns a ColumnarBatch of pass-through columns followed by result columns.

nodes.name: evalWithRowQueue
nodes.summary: Paths 2 and 3. Creates a HybridRowQueue in the local dir (closed on task completion) for pass-through rows. With plain column inputs it copies rows into the queue and uses the columnar runner; otherwise it evaluates a MutableProjection per row and uses an ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner with BasicPythonArrowInput. Result rows are joined with queued rows, projected, and converted back to ColumnarBatch by rowsToColumnarBatches.

nodes.name: validateOutputTypes
nodes.summary: Compares the data types of the result batch columns with the expected output types, ignoring compatible collation, and throws QueryExecutionErrors.arrowDataTypeMismatchError for 'pandas_udf()' on mismatch.

nodes.name: rowsToColumnarBatches
nodes.summary: Wraps an iterator of rows into an iterator of ColumnarBatch that reuses one set of OnHeapColumnVector columns (closed on task completion); each next call resets the vectors and converts up to batchSize rows with RowToColumnConverter.

nodes.name: PeekableIterator
nodes.summary: Private[python] iterator wrapper over an underlying iterator that adds peek(), which reads and remembers the first element so the evaluator can inspect the first batch without losing it; hasNext and next return the peeked element first.

nodes.name: peek
nodes.summary: Returns the first element as an Option, pulling it from the underlying iterator once and caching it (None if the iterator is empty).

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowPythonInput.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ColumnarArrowPythonInput trait, mixed into a BasePythonRunner to send ColumnarBatch input to Python over Arrow IPC. Arrow-backed columns are serialized directly, other columns are written row by row through ArrowWriter.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala private[python] trait with a self-type on BasePythonRunner[ColumnarBatch, _].

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowPythonInput
nodes.summary: Trait extending PythonArrowInput[ColumnarBatch] with a self-type of BasePythonRunner. Implementers supply inputColumnIndices (columns of each batch used as UDF input). writeNextBatchToArrowStream takes the next batch, writes it with writeArrowDirect if all selected columns are ArrowColumnVector or writeRowByRow otherwise, adds the bytes written to the pythonDataSent metric, and closes the PythonArrowInput state when the iterator is exhausted. The Arrow-direct path wraps the FieldVectors in a VectorSchemaRoot and serializes them with VectorUnloader and MessageSerializer without copying; the fallback uses a lazy ArrowWriter on the pre-allocated root.

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Writes the next ColumnarBatch to the data stream, choosing the Arrow-direct or row-by-row path, and records the number of bytes sent in the pythonDataSent metric. Returns true if a batch was written, or false after closing the input state when no batches remain.

nodes.name: isArrowBacked
nodes.summary: Returns true when every selected input column of the batch is an ArrowColumnVector.

nodes.name: writeArrowDirect
nodes.summary: Extracts the FieldVectors of the selected ArrowColumnVector columns, wraps them in a VectorSchemaRoot with the batch row count, unloads a record batch and serializes it to the output channel with MessageSerializer. The vectors are not closed because the upstream batch owns them.

nodes.name: writeRowByRow
nodes.summary: Fallback for non-Arrow batches: selects the UDF columns, writes each row with the ArrowWriter, finishes it, serializes the record batch from the unloader of the pre-allocated root, then resets the writer.

nodes.name: selectColumns
nodes.summary: Builds a new ColumnarBatch holding only the columns at inputColumnIndices, with the original row count.

nodes.name: EvalPythonUDTFExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EvalPythonUDTFExec trait, the common base for physical operators that evaluate a Python UDTF one partition at a time and join the UDTF's output rows back to the buffered input rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with one abstract method (evaluate) that concrete operators implement.

nodes.name: EvalPythonUDTFExec
nodes.summary: Trait extending UnaryExecNode whose output is requiredChildOutput followed by resultAttrs. Concrete operators implement evaluate(argMetas, iter, schema, context). doExecute copies the child rows, then per partition buffers input rows in a HybridRowQueue (closed on task completion), de-duplicates the UDTF arguments by semantic equality into ArgumentMetadata (supporting NamedArgumentExpression and table arguments), projects them with a MutableProjection, and calls evaluate. Each group of UDTF output rows is joined with the next queued input row (pruned to requiredChildOutput); rows produced after the input is exhausted (from terminate()) keep the last left row, and a null result is joined with a null row. The scaladoc says it is similar to EvalPythonExec.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs the child, and for each partition buffers input rows in a HybridRowQueue, builds argument metadata and an argument projection, invokes the abstract evaluate, then flat-maps each UDTF output group by joining it with the next queued input row (or the last left row once the input is exhausted) and projecting to the node's output.

nodes.name: EvaluatePython.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EvaluatePython object: conversions between Catalyst values and Java objects suited for pickling, and the custom picklers for StructType, Row and byte arrays. It is used by the Python UDF and UDTF operators in this package.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object with private nested pickler classes registered once under a synchronized flag; the pickled payloads reference names in the module 'pyspark.sql.types'.

nodes.name: EvaluatePython
nodes.summary: Singleton object for Python evaluation support. needConversionInPython tells whether a data type needs conversion (date, timestamp, variant, day-time interval, time, geometry, geography, struct, user-defined types, and arrays or maps of those). toJava converts Catalyst values to Java values (rows to GenericRowWithSchema, arrays to ArrayList, maps to HashMap, decimals to BigDecimal, strings to String, geometry and geography via STUtils, binary optionally wrapped in BytesWrapper). makeFromJava returns a converter from Java values back to Catalyst values by data type, giving null when the Java type is unexpected. registerPicklers installs the StructType, Row and BytesWrapper picklers once, and javaToPython pickles an RDD with AutoBatchedPickler.

nodes.name: BytesWrapper
nodes.summary: Private[python] marker class wrapping a byte array so the pickler writes it as a Python bytes object instead of a bytearray.

nodes.name: StructTypePickler
nodes.summary: Private pickler (IObjectPickler) for StructType. register adds it as a custom pickler; pickle writes a GLOBAL reference to _parse_datatype_json_string in module pyspark.sql.types followed by the schema JSON string and TUPLE1 and REDUCE opcodes.

nodes.name: BytesWrapperPickler
nodes.summary: Private pickler for BytesWrapper. It writes a GLOBAL reference to builtins.bytes, pickles the wrapped byte array with the default pickler, then TUPLE1 and REDUCE so that bytes(bytearray) is called on load.

nodes.name: RowPickler
nodes.summary: Private pickler for GenericRowWithSchema. When asked to pickle itself it writes a GLOBAL reference to _create_row_inbound_converter in pyspark.sql.types; for a row it saves the pickler, the row's schema (the same object for memoization) with TUPLE1 and REDUCE, then marks and saves every value, closing with TUPLE and REDUCE.

nodes.name: needConversionInPython
nodes.summary: Public entry that asks TypeApiOps whether the data type needs Python conversion and falls back to needConversionInPythonDefault.

nodes.name: needConversionInPythonDefault
nodes.summary: Default rule: true for date, timestamp, timestamp without time zone, variant, day-time interval, time, geometry, geography, struct and user-defined types; arrays and maps recurse into their element, key or value types; false otherwise.

nodes.name: toJava
nodes.summary: Converts a Catalyst value to a Java object suitable for pickling according to its data type: null stays null, InternalRow becomes GenericRowWithSchema, ArrayData an ArrayList, MapData a HashMap, user-defined types use their sqlType, Decimal becomes BigDecimal, UTF8String a String, geometry and geography values are deserialized with STUtils, and byte arrays are wrapped in BytesWrapper when binaryAsBytes is set.

nodes.name: makeFromJava
nodes.summary: Returns the Java-to-Catalyst converter for a data type, preferring the one from TypeApiOps and otherwise makeFromJavaDefault.

nodes.name: makeFromJavaDefault
nodes.summary: Builds the default converter function for each data type. Numeric types accept narrower or compatible numbers, decimals accept java.math.BigDecimal, strings call toString, binary accepts a String or byte array, arrays and maps and structs recurse (a struct needs an array of matching length or it throws STRUCT_ARRAY_LENGTH_MISMATCH), variant, geography and geometry accept a HashMap, and any unexpected input becomes null through nullSafeConvert.

nodes.name: nullSafeConvert
nodes.summary: Returns null for null input and otherwise applies a partial function, returning null if the function does not match.

nodes.name: pickle
nodes.summary: Writes the opcodes that make the unpickler call pyspark.sql.types._parse_datatype_json_string with the schema JSON.

nodes.name: pickle
nodes.summary: Writes the opcodes for builtins.bytes applied to the pickled bytearray of the wrapped data.

nodes.name: pickle
nodes.summary: Pickles a row: for the pickler itself emits the reference to _create_row_inbound_converter, otherwise saves that reference, the row schema and the row values with the opcodes needed to rebuild the row on the Python side.

nodes.name: registerPicklers
nodes.summary: Synchronized, idempotent registration: calls SerDeUtil.initialize and registers StructTypePickler, RowPickler and BytesWrapperPickler. The scaladoc says it must be called before serializing these classes and must be placed in the closure in cluster mode.

nodes.name: javaToPython
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD of Java objects to an RDD of pickled byte arrays by calling registerPicklers in each partition and wrapping the iterator in SerDeUtil.AutoBatchedPickler.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInArrowExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapCoGroupsInArrowExec physical node, the concrete cogrouped-map operator whose user function works on Arrow tables. It only fixes the Python eval type; the execution logic lives in FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInArrowExec
nodes.summary: Case class (leftGroup, rightGroup, func, output, left, right) that extends FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec and sets pythonEvalType to PythonEvalType.SQL_COGROUPED_MAP_ARROW_UDF. The scaladoc says it is the physical node for the FlatMapCoGroupsInArrow logical plan: both inputs are cogrouped, each side is sent to the Python worker as its own Arrow stream, the worker turns the batches into pyarrow.Table objects, calls the user function and returns a pyarrow.Table as Arrow record batches that become InternalRows. The scaladoc warns that both the worker and the executor need memory for the largest cogroup. withNewChildrenInternal copies the node with new children.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec trait, the shared base of the Python cogrouped-map operators (Arrow and pandas variants). It declares the required distribution and ordering of both children and executes the cogroup through CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec
nodes.summary: Trait that extends SparkPlan with BinaryExecNode with PythonSQLMetrics. Subclasses supply leftGroup, rightGroup, func (a PythonUDF), output, the two children and the Python eval type. It reads the session time zone, the large-var-types flag and the runner conf map from ArrowPythonRunner.getPythonRunnerConfMap, and wraps the UDF's function in a ChainedPythonFunctions. requiredChildDistribution is AllTuples when a group list is empty, otherwise ClusteredDistribution of the group attributes; requiredChildOrdering sorts each side ascending by its grouping attributes; outputPartitioning is the left child's. doExecute zips the partitions of the two children, groups and projects each side, pairs the groups with CoGroupedIterator and runs a CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner through PandasGroupUtils.executePython, skipping partitions where both sides are empty.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns the required distribution of the two children: AllTuples for a side with no grouping attributes, otherwise ClusteredDistribution of that side's grouping attributes.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Returns the required ordering of the two children: ascending SortOrder on the left and right grouping attributes respectively.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Resolves argument offsets for both sides, reads the job artifact and optional session UUID, then zipPartitions of the left and right child RDDs. For non-empty partitions it groups and projects both sides, builds a CoGroupedIterator of (left group, right group) pairs and a CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner with the function chain, eval type, combined offsets, both dedup schemas, time zone, conf and metrics, and returns the output of executePython.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInPandasExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapCoGroupsInPandasExec physical node, the concrete cogrouped-map operator whose user function works on pandas DataFrames. It only fixes the Python eval type; execution is inherited from FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInPandasExec
nodes.summary: Case class (leftGroup, rightGroup, func, output, left, right) extending FlatMapCoGroupsInBatchExec with pythonEvalType set to PythonEvalType.SQL_COGROUPED_MAP_PANDAS_UDF. The scaladoc says it is the physical node for the FlatMapCoGroupsInPandas logical plan: each side of the cogroup goes to the Python worker as its own Arrow stream, the worker builds pandas.DataFrame objects, calls the user function and returns a pandas.DataFrame as Arrow record batches that are turned into InternalRows. It also notes both sides need memory for the largest cogroup.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInArrowExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapGroupsInArrowExec physical node, the grouped-map operator whose user function works on Arrow data. It wraps each row in an extra struct row so that the Python side sees one DataFrame-like struct column.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInArrowExec
nodes.summary: Case class (groupingAttributes, func, output, child) extending FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec. pythonEvalType is taken from the PythonUDF's evalType. It overrides groupedData to wrap every row of each group in another InternalRow, and groupedSchema to return a schema with one field named struct holding the original schema, so Python sees a struct column. The scaladoc says rows of each group go to the worker as an iterator of Arrow record batches that arrive either as a materialized pyarrow.Table or as an iterator of pyarrow.RecordBatch depending on the UDF's eval type, and that the Table API materializes the whole group in worker memory.

nodes.name: groupedData
nodes.summary: Calls the base groupedData and maps every row of each group into InternalRow(row), wrapping it in another row so the Python side reads it as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: groupedSchema
nodes.summary: Wraps the base grouped schema in a StructType with a single field named struct.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec trait, the shared base of the Python grouped-map operators (Arrow and pandas variants). It declares the clustered distribution and ordering on the grouping attributes and runs each partition's groups through ArrowPythonRunner with GroupedPythonArrowInput.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec
nodes.summary: Trait that extends SparkPlan with UnaryExecNode with PythonSQLMetrics. Subclasses supply groupingAttributes, func (a PythonUDF), output, child and the Python eval type. It reads the time zone, the large-var-types flag and the runner conf map, wraps the UDF function in a ChainedPythonFunctions, and captures the job artifact UUID and the optional session UUID. requiredChildDistribution is AllTuples without grouping attributes, otherwise ClusteredDistribution; requiredChildOrdering is ascending on the grouping attributes; groupedData and groupedSchema are protected hooks that subclasses can override. doExecute resolves argument offsets and, for each non-empty partition, builds an ArrowPythonRunner mixed with GroupedPythonArrowInput and runs it with executePython.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns AllTuples when there are no grouping attributes, otherwise a ClusteredDistribution on them.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Returns an ascending SortOrder for each grouping attribute.

nodes.name: groupedData
nodes.summary: Protected hook that groups the partition's rows by the grouping attributes and projects them to the given attributes, returning an iterator of per-group row iterators.

nodes.name: groupedSchema
nodes.summary: Protected hook that returns the StructType built from the given attributes with DataTypeUtils.fromAttributes.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the child, resolves the de-duplicated attributes and argument offsets for the grouping columns, then maps each non-empty partition: it groups the data, creates an ArrowPythonRunner with GroupedPythonArrowInput (function chain, eval type, offsets, schema, time zone, conf, metrics, artifact and session UUIDs) and returns executePython of the data and output.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FlatMapGroupsInPandasExec physical node, the grouped-map operator whose user function works on pandas DataFrames. It only fixes the Python eval type; execution is inherited from FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasExec
nodes.summary: Case class (groupingAttributes, func, output, child) extending FlatMapGroupsInBatchExec, with pythonEvalType taken from the PythonUDF's evalType. The scaladoc says rows of each group go to the Python worker as an Arrow record batch, the worker turns it into a pandas.DataFrame, calls the user function and returns a pandas.DataFrame as Arrow record batches that become InternalRows, and that both sides need memory for the largest group.

nodes.name: MapInArrowExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MapInArrowExec physical node for map-in-batch operations on Arrow record batches. It only fixes the Python eval type; execution is inherited from MapInBatchExec.

nodes.name: MapInArrowExec
nodes.summary: Case class (func, output, child, isBarrier, profile) extending MapInBatchExec with pythonEvalType set to PythonEvalType.SQL_MAP_ARROW_ITER_UDF. The scaladoc describes it as a relation produced by a function that takes an iterator of PyArrow record batches and returns an iterator of PyArrow record batches.

nodes.name: MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory, the partition evaluator factory for map-in-batch Python operators. Its evaluator sends the rows of a partition to Python through ArrowPythonRunner and turns the returned struct column batches back into rows.

nodes.name: MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Public class (output, chained function, input schema, output data type, batch size, eval type, session time zone, large var types, runner conf, pythonMetrics, job artifact and session UUIDs) that extends PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow]. createEvaluator returns the private nested MapInBatchEvaluator. It is created by MapInBatchExec.doExecute.

nodes.name: MapInBatchEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private nested evaluator (extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow]) whose eval wraps each input row in another row so Python sees a struct DataFrame, runs an ArrowPythonRunner with BatchedPythonArrowInput, optionally validates the returned schema against the expected output type, and flattens the struct column of each returned batch into rows projected with an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Creates a new MapInBatchEvaluator for the partition.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Takes the single input iterator, wraps each row with InternalRow(row), builds an ArrowPythonRunner (input schema wrapped in a struct field named struct, with BatchedPythonArrowInput) and computes the columnar batches. When SQLConf pysparkArrowValidateSchema is set, it checks that the first column's type equals the output type ignoring compatible nullability and otherwise throws QueryExecutionErrors.arrowDataTypeMismatchError. It then takes the children of the struct ArrowColumnVector as the output columns of a new ColumnarBatch and iterates its rows through an UnsafeProjection.

nodes.name: MapInBatchExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MapInBatchExec trait, the shared base of map-in-batch Python operators (Arrow and pandas variants). Its doExecute builds a MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory and runs it over the child RDD, optionally as a barrier stage and with a resource profile.

nodes.name: MapInBatchExec
nodes.summary: Trait extending UnaryExecNode with PythonSQLMetrics for relations produced by applying a function over an iterator of batches (pandas DataFrames or PyArrow record batches) that returns an iterator of batches. Subclasses supply func, pythonEvalType, isBarrier and profile. The scaladoc calls it similar to FlatMapGroupsInPandasExec. It captures the job artifact UUID and the optional session UUID (when Python worker logging is enabled) and its outputPartitioning is the child's.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds the runner conf map and the chained function from the PythonUDF, creates a MapInBatchEvaluatorFactory with the output, child schema, UDF data type, arrow max records per batch, eval type, time zone, large var types, metrics and UUIDs, then applies it with mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or mapPartitionsWithIndex (the Internal variant for non-barrier) depending on conf.usePartitionEvaluator. For a barrier operator the child RDD is made a barrier RDD first, and a resource profile, if present, is applied with withResources.

nodes.name: ArrowPythonUDTFRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowPythonUDTFRunner, the Python runner that sends batches of rows to a Python UDTF over Arrow and reads Arrow batches back. It is the Arrow counterpart of the UDTF runner and is parameterized by a PythonUDTF and its argument metadata.

nodes.name: ArrowPythonUDTFRunner
nodes.summary: Runner for Python user-defined table functions that exchanges data with the Python worker in Arrow format. It extends BasePythonRunner with BatchedPythonArrowInput (rows are written as sized Arrow batches) and BasicPythonArrowOutput (results are read back as ColumnarBatch). At construction it rejects duplicated field names in the input schema (ArrowUtils.failDuplicatedFieldNames) and requires the pandas buffer size to be at least 4 bytes. It copies the environment variables of the first Python function, adds PYSPARK_SPARK_SESSION_UUID when a session id is given, picks the Python executable (the configured worker executable or the function's own), and reads the fault handler, idle timeout, kill-on-idle, traceback dump interval, flush-failure and traceback visibility settings from SQLConf. writeUDF delegates to PythonUDTFRunner.writeUDTF. Used when a Python UDTF is evaluated with Arrow input.

nodes.name: evalConf
nodes.summary: Builds the eval configuration sent to the Python worker. For SQL_ARROW_TABLE_UDF it adds the key input_type holding the schema JSON; otherwise it adds table_arg_offsets, the comma separated offsets of the arguments marked as table arguments in the argument metadata.

nodes.name: CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner, which streams two groups of rows (left and right) as separate Arrow streams to a Python worker for cogrouped UDFs and reads back ColumnarBatch results.

nodes.name: CoGroupedArrowPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Python UDF runner for cogrouped UDFs. Input elements are pairs of row iterators (left group, right group); each pair is written to the worker as two Arrow streams, one per DataFrame side, and the output is read back as ColumnarBatch through BasicPythonArrowOutput. The constructor fails on duplicated field names in either schema. It sets environment variables (including PYSPARK_SPARK_SESSION_UUID), the Python executable and the worker fault handler, idle timeout and traceback settings from SQLConf, and reads the Arrow max records per batch, max bytes per batch and compression codec settings. createUnloader builds a VectorUnloader with compression; newWriter creates the Writer that writes UDFs and the Arrow batches. Used when a cogrouped Python UDF is executed.

nodes.name: createUnloader
nodes.summary: Private helper that creates a VectorUnloader for a VectorSchemaRoot using the compression codec from ArrowCompressionUtils.createCompressionCodec (codec name and zstd level taken from SQLConf).

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the Writer for the runner as an anonymous subclass. The writer's writeCommand sends the UDFs with PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs and its writeNextInputToStream (see that function) writes the cogroup data. It keeps the next left and right iterators and one ArrowWriterWrapper per side.

nodes.name: writeNextInputToStream
nodes.summary: Method of the anonymous Writer created in newWriter. For each cogroup it first writes the number 2 (two DataFrames), then streams the left group and then the right group as sized Arrow batches (limited by max records and max bytes per batch) via BatchedPythonArrowInput.writeSizedBatch, closing each Arrow writer when its iterator is exhausted. When the input is finished it writes 0 and returns false. It adds the bytes written to the pythonDataSent metric.

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowPythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ColumnarArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner, an Arrow Python runner whose input is a ColumnarBatch instead of rows, so Arrow-backed columns can be serialized directly without row conversion.

nodes.name: ColumnarArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner
nodes.summary: Package private runner that extends BaseArrowPythonRunner[ColumnarBatch, ColumnarBatch] and mixes in ColumnarArrowPythonInput and BasicPythonArrowOutput. When the batch columns are Arrow-backed, the Arrow FieldVectors are extracted and written as Arrow IPC without row conversion (per its doc comment). It is the columnar counterpart of ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner. It takes argument metadata with names, the schema, timezone, input column indices and the runner conf; writeUDF writes the schema JSON when the eval type is SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF and then the UDFs with named arguments.

nodes.name: writeUDF
nodes.summary: Writes the UDF payload to the worker: the schema JSON (via PythonWorkerUtils.writeUTF) only when evalType is SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF, followed by PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs with the argument metadata.

nodes.name: MapInPandasExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MapInPandasExec physical operator, a small case class built on MapInBatchExec.

nodes.name: MapInPandasExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator for a relation produced by applying a function that takes an iterator of pandas DataFrames and outputs an iterator of pandas DataFrames. It is a case class with the function expression, output attributes, child plan, isBarrier flag and optional ResourceProfile. It extends MapInBatchExec, sets pythonEvalType to PythonEvalType.SQL_MAP_PANDAS_ITER_UDF, and withNewChildInternal copies the node with a new child. All execution logic lives in MapInBatchExec.

nodes.name: PandasGroupUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the private[python] PandasGroupUtils object with shared helpers for plans that run grouped Python UDFs: running the Python runner and flattening its output, grouping and projecting input rows, and computing deduplicated attributes with argument offsets.

nodes.name: PandasGroupUtils
nodes.summary: Object holding base functionality for plans that execute grouped Python UDFs. executePython passes data to a BasePythonRunner and turns the returned ColumnarBatch into UnsafeRow-projected internal rows; groupAndProject groups an iterator by grouping attributes and projects to the deduplicated schema; resolveArgOffsets computes the deduplicated attributes and the argOffsets array that separates grouping attributes from data attributes.

nodes.name: executePython
nodes.summary: Runs the given BasePythonRunner on the input iterator for the current partition (runner.compute with TaskContext), then for each returned ColumnarBatch takes the struct column at index 0, selects its children as the output vectors, builds a flattened ColumnarBatch and iterates its rows, applying an UnsafeProjection to produce InternalRows.

nodes.name: groupAndProject
nodes.summary: Groups the input rows by the grouping attributes using GroupedIterator and returns, for each key, an iterator of the group's rows projected into the deduplicated schema.

nodes.name: resolveArgOffsets
nodes.summary: Returns the deduplicated attributes and the argOffsets array. Grouping attributes that also appear in the data attributes (compared with semanticEquals) are not repeated. argOffsets starts with the total length, then the number of grouping attributes, then the offsets of the grouping attributes, then the offsets of the data attributes.

nodes.name: PythonPlannerRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract PythonPlannerRunner, a helper that runs a Python function in the Spark driver by starting or reusing a Python worker, sending one request and reading one result, together with its private non-blocking WorkerInputStream.

nodes.name: PythonPlannerRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract helper class (extends Logging) to run Python functions in the Spark driver. Subclasses supply workerModule, optionally runnerConf, writeToPython (write the request with a Pickler) and receiveFromPython (read the result of type T). runInPython does the actual work: it builds the worker environment variables from Spark and SQL configuration, creates the worker, writes the payload into a buffer, reads the response, merges accumulator updates, and releases or destroys the worker. The nested private WorkerInputStream performs the non-blocking socket IO.

nodes.name: runInPython
nodes.summary: Runs the Python function once. It reads buffer size, auth socket timeout, worker reuse and local dirs from the Spark conf, and fault handler, idle timeout, kill-on-idle, traceback and planner memory settings from SQLConf; fills the worker environment (SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS, SPARK_REUSE_WORKER, SPARK_HIDE_TRACEBACK, PYSPARK_PLANNER_MEMORY_MB, SPARK_JOB_ARTIFACT_UUID, SPARK_PYTHON_RUNTIME and others); registers picklers; creates the worker with SparkEnv.createPythonWorker; writes version, files, broadcasts, conf and the subclass payload followed by END_OF_STREAM; reads the result through WorkerInputStream and receiveFromPython; merges accumulator updates; then releases the worker if the stream ended cleanly and reuse is on, otherwise destroys it. IOExceptions become SparkException with a crash message, optionally including the fault handler log.

nodes.name: WorkerInputStream
nodes.summary: Private InputStream wrapper over the non-blocking worker channel. A port and simplification of the reader input stream of the Python runner: it writes the whole request buffer and then reads the response. It tracks the idle timeout and can terminate the worker process when kill-on-idle is enabled.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Overload read(b, off, len) loops on the worker selector with the idle timeout; it logs a warning and, if configured, destroys the worker process on timeout, reads from the channel when readable, writes the pending buffer when writable and switches interest to read once the buffer is empty. If the stream ends after a kill it throws PythonWorkerException with the fault handler log. The single byte read() overload (lines 200-208) delegates to it.

nodes.name: PythonSQLMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PythonSQLMetrics trait and its companion object, which declare the standard SQL metrics (sizes, timings, row count) reported by physical operators that run Python workers.

nodes.name: PythonSQLMetrics
nodes.summary: Trait with self-type SparkPlan that creates pythonMetrics, a Map of SQLMetric built from the companion object's descriptions: size metrics pythonDataSent ('data sent to Python workers') and pythonDataReceived ('data returned from Python workers'); timing metrics pythonBootTime, pythonInitTime, pythonTotalTime and pythonProcessingTime; and the plain metric pythonNumRowsReceived ('number of output rows'). It overrides the lazy val metrics to return them. The companion object holds the three description maps (pythonSizeMetricsDesc, pythonTimingMetricsDesc, pythonOtherMetricsDesc). Mixed into Python-evaluating physical plans.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithStatePythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ApplyInPandasWithStatePythonRunner and its companion object, the runner used for the applyInPandasWithState streaming operation where state information travels with the data in both directions over Arrow.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithStatePythonRunner
nodes.summary: Variant of ArrowPythonRunner for applyInPandasWithState. Unlike the normal runner, input and output carry side data (group state) along with rows, so it uses its own Arrow record batch layout: the input schema is extended with a __state column of STATE_METADATA_SCHEMA, input is (UnsafeRow key, GroupStateImpl, rows) and output is a pair of state iterator and row iterator. It extends BasePythonRunner with PythonArrowInput and PythonArrowOutput, reads the worker and traceback settings and buffer size from SQLConf (forcing a minimum of 4 with a warning), and sends the Arrow max records and bytes settings to the worker in runnerConf. evalConf adds state_value_schema. writeNextBatchToArrowStream uses ApplyInPandasWithStateWriter and deserializeColumnarBatch converts the worker's reply. The companion object defines the type aliases InType, OutTypeForState and OutType and the schemas STATE_METADATA_SCHEMA_FROM_PYTHON_WORKER (properties, keyRowAsUnsafe, object, oldTimeoutTimestamp) and COUNT_COLUMN_SCHEMA_FROM_PYTHON_WORKER (dataCount, stateCount).

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Reads the next (key, group state, data iterator) from the input, lazily creating an ApplyInPandasWithStateWriter, and writes the group with startNewGroup, writeRow for each data row and finalizeGroup, adding the bytes written to the pythonDataSent metric. When the input is exhausted it calls finalizeData, closes the PythonArrowInput part and returns false.

nodes.name: deserializeColumnarBatch
nodes.summary: Converts a ColumnarBatch from the Python worker into an OutType. It reads the data and state row counts from the first (count) struct column, builds an iterator of data rows from the second column using the output schema, and builds an iterator of state tuples from the third column: it parses the JSON properties, rebuilds the key UnsafeRow, unpickles the optional state object with PythonSQLUtils.toJVMRow, creates a GroupStateImpl with GroupStateImpl.fromJson and reads the old timeout timestamp. Schema equality is asserted with DataTypeUtils.sameType.

nodes.name: SQLMetricInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLMetricInfo, a small developer-API class that records the name, accumulator id and metric type of one SQL metric.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: SQLMetricInfo
nodes.summary: Plain holder class (annotated DeveloperApi) with three vals: name, accumulatorId and metricType. It stores information about a single SQL metric and has no methods of its own.

nodes.name: SQLHistoryServerPlugin.scala
nodes.summary: History server plugin that wires the SQL status listener and the SQL tab into a replayed application UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: SQLHistoryServerPlugin
nodes.summary: Implementation of AppHistoryServerPlugin for SQL. createListeners returns a SQLAppStatusListener created with live = false, and setupUI creates a SQLTab only when the SQLAppStatusStore holds at least one execution. displayOrder is 0.

nodes.name: SQLHistoryServerPlugin.createListeners
nodes.summary: Returns a single SQLAppStatusListener built with the given conf and store and with live set to false, so the history server can rebuild SQL status data.

nodes.name: SQLHistoryServerPlugin.setupUI
nodes.summary: Wraps the UI store in a SQLAppStatusStore and attaches a SQLTab to the SparkUI only if executionsCount() is greater than zero.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryHistoryServerPlugin.scala
nodes.summary: History server plugin that registers the streaming query status listener and the streaming query tab for replayed applications.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryHistoryServerPlugin
nodes.summary: Implementation of AppHistoryServerPlugin for streaming queries. createListeners builds a StreamingQueryListenerBus with a StreamingQueryStatusListener attached, and setupUI creates a StreamingQueryTab only when the StreamingQueryStatusStore has query data. displayOrder is 2.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryHistoryServerPlugin.createListeners
nodes.summary: Creates a StreamingQueryListenerBus with no Spark listener bus, adds a StreamingQueryStatusListener that writes to the given store, and returns the bus as the only listener.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryHistoryServerPlugin.setupUI
nodes.summary: Builds a StreamingQueryStatusStore over the UI store and attaches a StreamingQueryTab only if allQueryUIData is non-empty.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SQLLastAttemptAccumulator trait and its companion object, which extend last-attempt accumulator tracking so a metric value can be read for the last execution of a Dataset or QueryExecution. A long header comment explains how RDD scopes, AQE plan changes, driver-only updates and cached or checkpointed plans are handled.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator
nodes.summary: Trait (lines 118-289) and companion object (lines 291-435) that share one id. The trait extends LastAttemptAccumulator and is mixed into an AccumulatorV2 subclass; it keeps per-QueryExecution driver-side values, offers lastAttemptValueForQueryExecution and lastAttemptValueForDataset, and declares abstract hooks newDriverQueryExecutionAcc, addToDriverAcc, setDriverAcc and driverAccValue. The object holds extractStageRDDScopes, which walks an executed plan and collects the RDD scope ids of the nodes that submit stages (result stage, broadcast and shuffle exchanges, reused exchanges, subqueries), bailing out on unknown exchange or subquery types.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.initializeLastAttemptAccumulator
nodes.summary: Calls the parent initialization and then creates the empty map of per-QueryExecution driver values; any non-fatal exception is reported through unexpectedLastAttemptMetricOperation and invalidates the accumulator.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.resetLastAttemptAccumulator
nodes.summary: Resets the parent state and replaces the per-QueryExecution driver value map with a new empty one, invalidating the accumulator on a non-fatal exception.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.assertValid
nodes.summary: Runs the parent validity check and asserts that the per-QueryExecution driver value map has been initialized.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.getOrCreateDirectDriverQueryExecutionValue
nodes.summary: Looks up, under a lock, the driver-side accumulator for a QueryExecution id and creates it with newDriverQueryExecutionAcc when it is missing.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.getActiveDatasetQueryExecutionId
nodes.summary: Reads the local property SparkContext.DATASET_QUERY_EXECUTION_ID_KEY from the active SparkContext and returns it as an Option.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.addQueryExecutionValueIfOnDriverSide
nodes.summary: When the accumulator is valid and the update happens on the driver, adds the value to the driver accumulator for the active QueryExecution id. It must be called from add methods after setValueIfOnDriverSide, and failures invalidate the accumulator.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.setQueryExecutionValueIfOnDriverSide
nodes.summary: Same as addQueryExecutionValueIfOnDriverSide but for set operations: it sets the driver accumulator for the active QueryExecution id to the given value.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.logAccumulatorState
nodes.summary: Builds a log entry from the parent state plus the direct driver QueryExecution values, falling back to a placeholder message when an exception occurs.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.lastAttemptValueForQueryExecution
nodes.summary: Returns the last attempt value for a QueryExecution. It first returns a driver-side value recorded for that QueryExecution id; otherwise it extracts the RDD scopes from the executed plan and aggregates the updates from those scopes. Returns None when the value cannot be established, and the result is undefined for cached or checkpointed plans.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.lastAttemptValueForDataset
nodes.summary: Returns the last attempt value for a Dataset by delegating to lastAttemptValueForQueryExecution with the Dataset queryExecution.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.getDirectDriverQueryExecutionValue
nodes.summary: Test-visible accessor that returns the driver-side value stored for a QueryExecution id, if any.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptAccumulator.extractStageRDDScopes
nodes.summary: Walks the executed plan (through AdaptiveSparkPlanHelper) and returns Right(scope ids) from the root, broadcast exchange, shuffle exchange, reused exchange and subquery nodes that submit stages, or Left(reason) when it meets an unsupported BroadcastExchangeLike, ShuffleExchangeLike or BaseSubqueryExec. WholeStageCodegenExec contributes both its own and its child scope id because codegen may fall back.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLMetric, an AccumulatorV2[Long, Long] used as a metric of a SQL query plan, and the SQLMetrics factory object with creators for sum, size, timing, nano timing, average and data source v2 custom metrics plus helpers to post driver-side updates.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: SQLMetric
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2[Long, Long] that carries a metricType string and an initValue (0 or lower). A value equal to initValue counts as zero or invalid: value then reports 0, the first add or merge sets the value to 0 first, and negative additions are ignored. Executor updates reach the SQL UI through toInfo and toInfoUpdate, which tag the AccumulableInfo with the SQL accumulator identifier; driver updates must be posted explicitly through SQLMetrics.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics
nodes.summary: Companion object of SQLMetric. It defines the metric type names ("sum", "size", "timing", "nsTiming", "average"), a name cache, factory methods createMetric, createV2CustomMetric, createSizeMetric, createTimingMetric, createNanoTimingMetric and createAverageMetric, the postDriverMetricUpdates and postDriverMetricsUpdatedByValue helpers that post SparkListenerDriverAccumUpdates on the listener bus, and withTimingNs, which times a block in nanoseconds.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.copy
nodes.summary: Creates a new SQLMetric with the same metricType and initValue and copies the current raw value into it.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.merge
nodes.summary: Merges another SQLMetric by adding its value when it is not zero (resetting this one from initValue to 0 first); any other accumulator type raises cannotMergeClassWithOtherClassError.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.add
nodes.summary: Adds a non-negative long to the metric, first turning the initial value into 0, and ignores negative inputs.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.set
nodes.summary: Overloaded setter (a Double version at lines 84-86 and a Long version at lines 88-90). Both ignore negative values; the Double version delegates to SQLMetrics.setDoubleForAverageMetrics for average metrics, and the Long version stores the value directly.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.toInfo
nodes.summary: Builds an AccumulableInfo using interned update and value options and the SQL accumulator identifier as metadata so the metric can be recognized as a SQLMetric later.

nodes.name: SQLMetric.toInfoUpdate
nodes.summary: Builds an AccumulableInfo that carries the raw value (possibly -1) so that MetricUtils.stringValue can filter out invalid values.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.setDoubleForAverageMetrics
nodes.summary: Asserts that the metric is of the average type and stores a double as a long by multiplying it by the base of 10.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers a plain sum SQLMetric with the given name, without counting failed values.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createV2CustomMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers a SQLMetric for a data source v2 CustomMetric, using CustomMetrics.buildV2CustomMetricTypeName as the type and the custom metric description as the name.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createSizeMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers a size-type SQLMetric (total, min, med, max in the UI, for example data size or spill size) with initial value -1 by default.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createTimingMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers a timing-type SQLMetric (duration total, min, med, max in the UI) with initial value -1 by default.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createNanoTimingMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers a nsTiming-type SQLMetric, like createTimingMetric but normalizing the unit to milliseconds.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.createAverageMetric
nodes.summary: Creates and registers an average-type SQLMetric (min, med, max in the UI), which must be updated with set rather than add.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricsUpdatedByValue
nodes.summary: Posts a SparkListenerDriverAccumUpdates event to the listener bus with the given (accumulator id, value) pairs when the execution id is not null.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.postDriverMetricUpdates
nodes.summary: Posts a SparkListenerDriverAccumUpdates event built from the id and current value of each given metric, skipping the post when the execution id is null.

nodes.name: SQLMetrics.withTimingNs
nodes.summary: Runs a code block, measures its elapsed time in nanoseconds and adds it to the given SQLMetric, then returns the block result.

nodes.name: AllExecutionsPage.scala
nodes.summary: Web UI page for the SQL tab that renders the list of all SQL executions as a placeholder table filled by JavaScript.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: AllExecutionsPage
nodes.summary: Package-private WebUIPage with an empty path, owned by a SQLTab. Its render method reads the UI_SQL_GROUP_SUB_EXECUTION_ENABLED setting into a hidden div, outputs a "sql-executions-table" div holding a loading spinner, and includes the static scripts sql-table-utils.js and allexecutionspage.js under the "SQL / DataFrame" header.

nodes.name: AllExecutionsPage.render
nodes.summary: Builds the page content with the group-sub-execution flag, a spinner placeholder and script tags, then wraps it with UIUtils.headerSparkPage titled "SQL / DataFrame" using DataTables.

nodes.name: SQLTab.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SQLTab Spark UI tab ("SQL / DataFrame") and its companion object holding the static resource directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: SQLTab
nodes.summary: SparkUITab named "SQL / DataFrame" built from a SQLAppStatusStore and a SparkUI. Its constructor attaches an AllExecutionsPage and an ExecutionPage, attaches itself to the SparkUI, and registers the static handler for "org/apache/spark/sql/execution/ui/static" under "/static/sql". It exposes conf from the SparkUI and has displayOrder 0. The companion object (lines 42-44) only holds the STATIC_RESOURCE_DIR constant and shares this id.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusStore.scala
nodes.summary: Read-only view over a KVStore that returns streaming query UI data and progress records for the streaming query UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusStore
nodes.summary: Stateless wrapper over a KVStore (several instances per application are fine). allQueryUIData reads StreamingQueryData ordered by the startTimestamp index and attaches each query recent progress sorted by timestamp; getQueryProgressData (visible for tests) returns the progress wrappers for one run id; makeUIData builds one StreamingQueryUIData.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusStore.allQueryUIData
nodes.summary: Returns a StreamingQueryUIData for every stored StreamingQueryData, read through the "startTimestamp" index in ascending order.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusStore.getQueryProgressData
nodes.summary: Returns the StreamingQueryProgressWrapper records whose "runId" index equals the given run id (visible for tests).

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusStore.makeUIData
nodes.summary: Loads the progress wrappers for the query run id, sorts their progress by timestamp, and combines them with the summary into a StreamingQueryUIData.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical operator for streaming flatMapGroupsWithState with a pandas UDF: it groups input rows, loads and saves per-key state, handles timeouts, and runs the user function through an Arrow-based Python runner.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala source.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryExecNode with FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecBase that executes the logical FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithState. It requires the child distribution to be compatible with the state partitioning and the child ordering to be ascending on the grouping attributes; initial state is not supported (hasInitialState is false). createInputProcessor returns an InputProcessor whose processNewData groups rows by key and loads state, processTimedOutState feeds timed-out keys with null value rows, and process runs ApplyInPandasWithStatePythonRunner and writes the changed state back when the output iterator completes.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires the child distribution to be one that is compatible with the state store partitioning of the grouping attributes, using StatefulOperatorPartitioning.getCompatibleDistribution.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child output to be sorted ascending by the grouping attributes.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.shortName
nodes.summary: Returns StatefulOperatorsUtils.FLAT_MAP_GROUPS_IN_PANDAS_WITH_STATE_EXEC_OP_NAME as the short operator name.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.withNewChildInternal
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the operator with the child plan replaced.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.createInputProcessor
nodes.summary: Creates the anonymous InputProcessor for a StateStore. Its overridden methods processNewData, processNewDataWithInitialState, processTimedOutState, the private process, and callFunctionAndUpdateState are all nested inside this method (lines 132-242) and are described by their own nodes.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.processNewData
nodes.summary: Groups the incoming rows by the grouping attributes, fetches the saved state for each key from the state manager, projects the value rows, and passes them to process with hasTimedOut false. Defined inside the anonymous InputProcessor created by createInputProcessor.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.processNewDataWithInitialState
nodes.summary: Initial state is not supported by this operator, so it throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException. Defined inside the anonymous InputProcessor created by createInputProcessor.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.processTimedOutState
nodes.summary: When timeouts are enabled, picks the threshold from the batch timestamp (processing-time timeout) or the eviction watermark (event-time timeout), finds stored states whose timeout timestamp is below it, builds rows with the real key and all-null values, and runs them through process with hasTimedOut true. Returns an empty iterator when timeouts are off. Defined inside the anonymous InputProcessor.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.process
nodes.summary: Creates an ApplyInPandasWithStatePythonRunner, wraps each group in a GroupStateImpl for streaming, and computes the output rows through the runner. When the output iterator completes it removes states that were removed, or writes states that were updated, removed or had their timeout changed, and updates the numRemovedStateRows, numUpdatedStateRows and numOutputRows metrics. Defined inside the anonymous InputProcessor.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithStateExec.callFunctionAndUpdateState
nodes.summary: Not supported in this operator (the Python runner does the work), so it throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException. Defined inside the anonymous InputProcessor.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithStateWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ApplyInPandasWithStateWriter, which writes grouped input data plus per-group state into Arrow record batches for the applyInPandasWithState operator. It bin-packs several groups into one batch and chunks large groups, recording chunk offsets in a state metadata column.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object holds STATE_METADATA_SCHEMA and EMPTY_STATE_METADATA_ROW.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithStateWriter
nodes.summary: Arrow batch writer that extends BaseStreamingArrowWriter. The caller invokes startNewGroup, writeRow (inherited), finalizeGroup and finalizeData; the class writes data columns and a trailing state column into the same VectorSchemaRoot with two ArrowWriter instances, pads the state side with empty rows so both sides have equal row counts, and writes a batch when the record limit is reached. The companion object defines STATE_METADATA_SCHEMA (properties, keyRowAsUnsafe, object, startOffset, numRows, isLastChunk) and EMPTY_STATE_METADATA_ROW.

nodes.name: startNewGroup
nodes.summary: Records the grouping key row and GroupStateImpl of the group whose rows are about to be written.

nodes.name: finalizeGroup
nodes.summary: Closes the last chunk of the current group and finalizes the Arrow batch if the batch size limit has been reached.

nodes.name: finalizeData
nodes.summary: Flushes the remaining rows as a final Arrow batch once all groups have been processed.

nodes.name: createArrowWriter
nodes.summary: Allocates the given field vectors and builds an ArrowWriter over them, used separately for the data columns and the state column.

nodes.name: buildStateInfoRow
nodes.summary: Builds the nested state metadata row (state JSON, key bytes, state value, start offset, row count, last-chunk flag) for one chunk.

nodes.name: finalizeCurrentChunk
nodes.summary: Writes the state metadata row for the current chunk, bumps the batch state count and resets the chunk offset bookkeeping.

nodes.name: finalizeCurrentArrowBatch
nodes.summary: Pads the state column with empty rows, finishes both writers, writes the batch to the Arrow stream, then resets the writers and counters.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkDeserializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TransformWithStateInPySparkDeserializer, a helper that decodes data arriving on the state socket of transformWithStateInPySpark into Row objects, either from Arrow batches or from length-prefixed byte records.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkDeserializer
nodes.summary: Deserializer constructed with a Row deserializer from an ExpressionEncoder. readArrowBatches reads an Arrow stream into rows, readListElements reads size-prefixed records until a negative size and converts each with PythonSQLUtils.toJVMRow, and close releases the child Arrow allocator. Used by the state server for list state put and append requests.

nodes.name: readArrowBatches
nodes.summary: Reads all Arrow record batches from the stream, wraps each batch in a ColumnarBatch and returns the deserialized rows as a Seq.

nodes.name: readListElements
nodes.summary: Reads length-prefixed byte records from the stream until a negative size is read and converts each into a Row using the schema and deserializer of the given ListStateInfo.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the Arrow child allocator used for reading.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the state server that answers state requests from the Python side of transformWithStateInPySpark over a dedicated socket, plus the ValueStateInfo, ListStateInfo and MapStateInfo holders. Requests are protobuf StateRequest messages covering implicit grouping keys, stateful processor calls (handle state, state variable creation, timers), state variable operations and utils.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer
nodes.summary: Runnable that runs on a separate thread per task. It accepts one connection on a ServerSocketChannel, loops reading version-tagged protobuf StateRequest messages and dispatches them in handleRequest to handlers for implicit grouping keys, stateful processor calls, value, list and map state calls, timers and utils. It keeps maps of initialized state variables and of open iterators keyed by iterator id, disables Nagle's algorithm on TCP sockets, and sets the handle state to CLOSED on EOF, interruption or error. Many constructor parameters ending in ForTest inject test doubles. The nested PythonResponseWriterUtils object builds and writes the protobuf responses.

nodes.name: PythonResponseWriterUtils
nodes.summary: Private helper object inside the state server holding the response writers: sendResponse, sendResponseWithLongVal, sendResponseWithStringVal, sendResponseWithListGet, sendResponseWithMapKeysOrValues, sendResponseWithMapPair and sendResponseWithTimers. Each builds a protobuf response with a status code, optional error message and payload, and writes the length followed by the bytes to the output stream. The iterator-based ones emit at most arrowTransformWithStateInPySparkMaxRecordsPerBatch rows per call and set requireNextFetch.

nodes.name: ValueStateInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding a value state together with its StructType schema and Row deserializer, stored per state name in the state server.

nodes.name: ListStateInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding a list state with its schema, Row deserializer and Row serializer, stored per state name in the state server.

nodes.name: MapStateInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding a map state with key and value schemas and the matching Row deserializers and serializers, stored per state name in the state server.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Thread body: accepts the socket connection, sets TCP no-delay for non-Unix sockets, then loops reading a version int and a protobuf message, handling it and flushing the output until the handle is CLOSED, handling EOF, interrupts and errors.

nodes.name: parseProtoMessage
nodes.summary: Reads a length-prefixed byte array from the input stream and parses it into a StateRequest.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: Dispatches a StateRequest to the handler for implicit grouping key, stateful processor call, state variable, timer or utils requests, and throws on an unknown method.

nodes.name: handleUtilsRequest
nodes.summary: Handles the parse-string-schema utils request by parsing the schema string with CatalystSqlParser and returning its JSON.

nodes.name: handleTimerRequest
nodes.summary: Handles timer value requests (processing time from batchTimestampMs, watermark) and expiry timer requests that pull expired timers from StatefulProcessorHandleImpl through a cached iterator.

nodes.name: handleImplicitGroupingKeyRequest
nodes.summary: Sets or removes the implicit grouping key (decoded from bytes with PythonSQLUtils.toJVMRow) on ImplicitGroupingKeyTracker and resets the list and timer iterators.

nodes.name: handleStatefulProcessorCall
nodes.summary: Handles stateful processor calls: set handle state, get value, list or map state (with optional TTL), register, delete and list timers, and deleteIfExists.

nodes.name: handleStateVariableRequest
nodes.summary: Routes a StateVariableRequest to the value, list or map state handler.

nodes.name: handleValueStateRequest
nodes.summary: Handles value state calls exists, get, update and clear, answering status 1 if the state is not initialized and status 2 when it has no value.

nodes.name: handleListStateRequest
nodes.summary: Handles list state calls exists, put, get (iterator based), appendValue, appendList and clear, reading Arrow batches through a TransformWithStateInPySparkDeserializer when fetchWithArrow is set.

nodes.name: handleMapStateRequest
nodes.summary: Handles map state calls exists, getValue, containsKey, updateValue, iterator, keys, values, removeKey and clear, using cached iterators per iterator id.

nodes.name: initializeStateVariable
nodes.summary: Creates a value, list or map state on the stateful processor handle from a schema string and optional TTL, registers its info in the matching map, and replies with status 1 if the name already exists.

nodes.name: sendResponse
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponse with status code, optional error message (only when status is not 0) and optional ByteString value.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithLongVal
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithLongTypeVal carrying a long value.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithStringVal
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithStringTypeVal carrying a string value.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithListGet
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithListGet holding up to the per-batch record limit of list rows pulled from an iterator, with requireNextFetch set when rows remain.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithMapKeysOrValues
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithMapKeysOrValues holding up to the per-batch limit of map keys or values pulled from an iterator.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithMapPair
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithMapIterator holding up to the per-batch limit of key and value pairs from a map state iterator.

nodes.name: sendResponseWithTimers
nodes.summary: Writes a StateResponseWithTimer with timer infos (optional key bytes and timestamp) produced by applying a mapping function over an iterator, bounded by the per-batch limit.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer.scala
nodes.summary: Benchmark program for the Python state server. It defines an in-memory StatefulProcessorHandleImpl and a main object that starts a standalone TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer on a TCP or Unix domain socket, so state communication cost can be measured without the real state store.

nodes.name: InMemoryStatefulProcessorHandleImpl
nodes.summary: Benchmark-only StatefulProcessorHandleImplBase that keeps value, list and map state and timers in Scala mutable collections keyed by the implicit grouping key. TTL is not supported (asserted to be TTLConfig.NONE), deleteIfExists is a no-op and getQueryInfo returns a QueryInfoImpl with random UUIDs. Contains the nested InMemoryValueState, InMemoryListState, InMemoryMapState and InMemoryTimers classes. Overloads getValueState, getListState and getMapState (encoder and implicit-encoder variants) share one function node each.

nodes.name: InMemoryValueState
nodes.summary: In-memory ValueState keeping one value per implicit grouping key in a mutable Map; implements exists, get, update and clear.

nodes.name: InMemoryListState
nodes.summary: In-memory ListState keeping an ArrayBuffer per implicit grouping key; implements exists, get, put, appendValue, appendList and clear.

nodes.name: InMemoryMapState
nodes.summary: In-memory MapState keeping a HashMap per implicit grouping key; implements exists, getValue, containsKey, updateValue, iterator, keys, values, removeKey and clear.

nodes.name: InMemoryTimers
nodes.summary: In-memory timer store keeping a sorted TreeSet of expiry timestamps per implicit grouping key, with registerTimer, deleteTimer and listTimers.

nodes.name: BenchmarkTransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer
nodes.summary: Runnable App object that builds a SparkSession, reads Arrow related SQLConf settings, opens a ServerSocketChannel (Unix domain socket when PYTHON_UNIX_DOMAIN_SOCKET_ENABLED is set, else a loopback TCP port), creates the in-memory handle and a TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer with a single-field string grouping key schema, prints the port or socket path, and runs the server until it ends. The scaladoc lists how to launch it from a Spark distribution.

nodes.name: getValueState
nodes.summary: Returns a new InMemoryValueState after asserting TTL is NONE. The second overload (lines 231-233) takes an implicit Encoder and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: getListState
nodes.summary: Returns a new InMemoryListState after asserting TTL is NONE. The second overload (lines 243-245) takes an implicit Encoder and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: getMapState
nodes.summary: Returns a new InMemoryMapState after asserting TTL is NONE. The second overload (lines 256-260) takes implicit Encoders and delegates to this one.

nodes.name: appendValue
nodes.summary: Appends one element to the list of the current implicit key, creating the buffer if absent.

nodes.name: appendList
nodes.summary: Appends an array of elements to the list of the current implicit key, creating the buffer if absent.

nodes.name: updateValue
nodes.summary: Puts a key and value in the map of the current implicit key, creating the map if absent.

nodes.name: registerTimer
nodes.summary: Adds an expiry timestamp to the timer set of the current grouping key.

nodes.name: deleteTimer
nodes.summary: Removes an expiry timestamp from the timer set of the current grouping key if present.

nodes.name: listTimers
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the timers of the current grouping key, or an empty iterator.

nodes.name: CustomMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CustomMetrics object with helpers for DataSource V2 custom metrics: encoding and decoding a metric type name and copying task metric values into SQLMetric instances.

nodes.name: CustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Object with constants V2_CUSTOM ("v2Custom"), NUM_ROWS_PER_UPDATE (100) and BUILTIN_OUTPUT_METRICS (bytesWritten, recordsWritten), plus buildV2CustomMetricTypeName, parseV2CustomMetricType and updateMetrics. updateMetrics sets matching SQLMetrics from CustomTaskMetric values and forwards bytesWritten and recordsWritten to the task output metrics.

nodes.name: buildV2CustomMetricTypeName
nodes.summary: Builds the metric type string "v2Custom_<class name>" for a CustomMetric.

nodes.name: parseV2CustomMetricType
nodes.summary: Returns the CustomMetric class name from a "v2Custom_" prefixed metric type, or None if the prefix is missing.

nodes.name: updateMetrics
nodes.summary: Sets each SQLMetric named by a CustomTaskMetric to its value and, for the built-in output metrics, updates bytesWritten or recordsWritten on the current task's output metrics.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptMetric.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLLastAttemptMetric, a SQLMetric variant that reports the value from the last attempt of each task, and the SQLLastAttemptMetrics factory object.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptMetric
nodes.summary: SQLMetric subclass that mixes in SQLLastAttemptAccumulator. add and set also update the driver-side value and query execution value for non-negative values; it implements partial merge, mergeability (same metricType), a driver accumulator backed by a plain SQLMetric, and copy. It is meant for system counters such as rows processed and does not store user data.

nodes.name: SQLLastAttemptMetrics
nodes.summary: Factory object whose createMetric creates and registers a SUM_METRIC based SQLLastAttemptMetric (without counting failed values) and initializes its last-attempt accumulator.

nodes.name: isMergeable
nodes.summary: Allows merging only with another SQLLastAttemptMetric of the same metricType.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Creates a new SQLLastAttemptMetric with the same metric type, initial value and current value.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds to the metric and, for non-negative values, mirrors the new value and the added amount on the driver side.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets the metric and, for non-negative values, mirrors the new value on the driver side.

nodes.name: createMetric
nodes.summary: Creates, registers and initializes a SQLLastAttemptMetric named after the cached metric name.

nodes.name: SQLShuffleMetricsReporter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the shuffle read and write metrics reporters used by SQL exchange operators. Each reporter forwards updates to the underlying task-level reporter and to SQLMetrics, and each companion object holds metric name constants and a factory for the metrics map.

nodes.name: SQLShuffleReadMetricsReporter
nodes.summary: TempShuffleReadMetrics subclass whose inc* methods (for example incRemoteBlocksFetched, incLocalBytesRead, incFetchWaitTime, incRecordsRead and the merged-block variants) add to a SQLMetric looked up by name and then to the wrapped TempShuffleReadMetrics. The companion defines the 17 metric name constants (lines 138-155) and createShuffleReadMetrics.

nodes.name: SQLShuffleWriteMetricsReporter
nodes.summary: ShuffleWriteMetricsReporter that forwards incBytesWritten, incRecordsWritten, incWriteTime and the dec variants to the wrapped reporter and to the SQLMetrics for shuffle bytes, records and write time. The companion defines SHUFFLE_BYTES_WRITTEN, SHUFFLE_RECORDS_WRITTEN, SHUFFLE_WRITE_TIME and createShuffleWriteMetrics.

nodes.name: createShuffleReadMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates the map of all shuffle read SQLMetrics (blocks, bytes, fetch wait time, records, merged block and chunk counters, request durations) keyed by the constant names.

nodes.name: decRecordsWritten
nodes.summary: Decrements the wrapped reporter and lowers the records written SQLMetric by setting it to its value minus v.

nodes.name: decBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Decrements the wrapped reporter and lowers the bytes written SQLMetric by setting it to its value minus v.

nodes.name: createShuffleWriteMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates the map of shuffle write SQLMetrics: shuffle bytes written, records written and write time.

nodes.name: PythonForeachWriter.scala
