nodes.summary: Defines PythonForeachWriter, a ForeachWriter that streams UnsafeRows to a Python worker, with WriterThread feeding the worker and UnsafeRowBuffer decoupling the query thread from that writer thread.

nodes.name: WriterThread
nodes.summary: Thread that consumes the Python runner's output iterator, which as a side effect ships the buffered input to the Python worker. Non-Spark exceptions are wrapped in ForeachUserFuncException and cached in _exception for the parent thread to rethrow.

nodes.name: PythonForeachWriter
nodes.summary: ForeachWriter[UnsafeRow] backed by a PythonRunner. open starts the WriterThread, process adds rows to the UnsafeRowBuffer, and close marks all rows added, joins the thread and rethrows its exception. The lazily built runner takes its Python executable, fault handler, idle timeout, traceback and flush settings from SQLConf. The companion object contains the nested UnsafeRowBuffer.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowBuffer
nodes.summary: Buffer for exactly two threads: the query thread adds UnsafeRows without blocking and the writer thread reads through a blocking iterator. It stores rows in a HybridRowQueue, counts the rows, blocks readers while the count is zero so the reader never gets ahead of the writer, and rethrows errors from the adding side in the reading side. Lock logic follows ArrayBlockingQueue style (ReentrantLock and Condition).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Pulls the first element from the output iterator to drive the writes to the Python worker and caches any exception.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Initializes the Python runner output iterator, starts the writer thread and registers a task completion listener that closes the buffer.

nodes.name: process
nodes.summary: Adds one UnsafeRow to the buffer.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Marks all rows as added, waits for the writer thread and throws its exception if there was one.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds a row to the queue under the lock, increments the count and signals a waiting reader.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Blocks (polling every 100 ms) until a row is available, all rows are added or an error occurred, then removes a row from the queue or returns null.

nodes.name: allRowsAdded
nodes.summary: Marks the end of input and signals a waiting reader.

nodes.name: withLock
nodes.summary: Runs a block under the interruptible lock and records the first exception thrown so the reader side can rethrow it.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSourceRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PythonStreamingSourceRunner, a JVM-side proxy that starts a Python worker for a streaming data source reader and calls its methods (initial offset, latest offset, partitions, commit, feature checks) over a socket, together with the function id constants it uses.

nodes.name: PythonStreamingSourceRunner
nodes.summary: Class plus companion object. The companion holds the function ids sent to the Python process (INITIAL_OFFSET_FUNC_ID 884 through REPORT_LATEST_OFFSET_FUNC_ID 892), the prefetch status codes, READ_ALL_AVAILABLE_JSON and the SupportedFeatures case class. The class init() starts the worker and sends the Python version, files, function, output schema JSON and Arrow batch size; the other methods write a function id, flush and read the result: checkSupportedFeatures, getDefaultReadLimit, reportLatestOffset, prepareForTriggerAvailableNow, latestOffset, initialOffset, partitions, commit and stop. Python exceptions are turned into QueryExecutionErrors. Prefetched Arrow record batches are read in readArrowRecordBatches and the schema is checked against outputSchema.

nodes.name: SupportedFeatures
nodes.summary: Case class with two flags, admissionControl and triggerAvailableNow, reporting which optional features the Python stream reader supports.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Starts the Python worker through a PythonWorkerFactory, sends version, includes, user function, output schema JSON and arrow batch size, and checks the init status.

nodes.name: checkSupportedFeatures
nodes.summary: Asks the Python side which optional features it supports (bit 0 admission control, bit 1 available-now trigger).

nodes.name: getDefaultReadLimit
nodes.summary: Fetches the default read limit of the reader as a JSON string.

nodes.name: reportLatestOffset
nodes.summary: Fetches the latest offset for reporting, returning null when the reply is empty.

nodes.name: prepareForTriggerAvailableNow
nodes.summary: Tells the Python reader to prepare for an available-now trigger.

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Admission-control variant: sends the start offset JSON and the read limit (a constant JSON for ReadAllAvailable, or the PythonStreamingSourceReadLimit JSON) and returns the latest offset. The no-argument overload at lines 205-215 calls the plain latest offset function.

nodes.name: initialOffset
nodes.summary: Invokes the reader's initialOffset and returns it as a string.

nodes.name: partitions
nodes.summary: Sends start and end offsets, reads the pickled partitions and an optional set of prefetched Arrow record batches, returning both.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Calls commit on the Python reader for the given end offset and checks for exceptions.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the Python worker and its factory, logging any exception.

nodes.name: readArrowRecordBatches
nodes.summary: Reads an Arrow stream from the worker, checks the schema equals outputSchema, and copies all rows out of the ColumnarBatches into an iterator.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical operator TransformWithStateInPySparkExec that runs a user supplied Python stateful processor over grouped streaming (or batch) input, plus a companion factory that builds the plan for batch queries. It sets up state stores, driver side schema validation and per partition Python runners.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator for the logical TransformWithStateInPySpark node; it extends TransformWithStateExecBase and executes the Python function on each group of rows with access to a state store. On the driver it runs a pre-init Python runner to collect column family schemas and state variable infos; on executors doExecute builds the state store (from the checkpoint for streaming, a temporary RocksDB store for batch), optionally zips the child with the initial state, and drives the Python runner. Its companion object (lines 412-456) has generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class with a scalastyle argcount exemption; the companion object shares this node id.

nodes.name: shortName
nodes.summary: Returns the operator short name: the transformWithStateInPandas name when the user facing data type is PANDAS, otherwise the PySpark name, to stay compatible with an earlier release.

nodes.name: getColFamilySchemas
nodes.summary: Returns the column family schemas collected by the driver side processor handle, passing the nullability flags so that nullable schemas set by Python users are checked.

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Starts a TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonPreInitRunner on the driver, runs the pre-init UDF so the processor registers its state variables, stops the runner, and then validates and writes the state schema using the state info and schema directory. A crash of the driver worker is rethrown as a SparkException.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Produces the RDD[InternalRow] of the operator. Three paths: streaming without initial state uses mapPartitionsWithStateStore with column families and multiple values per key; batch mode builds a temporary store per partition; with initial state it zips the child and initial state partitions with stateStoreAwareZipPartitions and gets or creates the store per partition.

nodes.name: initNewStateStoreAndProcessData
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary RocksDB state store provider in a new temp directory for one partition (used for batch queries), runs the given function on the store, and closes the provider when the output iterator completes.

nodes.name: processDataWithPartition
nodes.summary: Processes one partition: filters late rows by watermark in event time mode, groups and projects the input, creates a StatefulProcessorHandleImpl, chooses the eval type (pandas or row, with or without initial state), builds a TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonRunner or the initial state runner, and runs it with executePython. On completion it records update time, does TTL cleanup and commits the store (or aborts it for batch), and updates metrics.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Copies the operator with a new child, and a new initial state plan when the operator has initial state.

nodes.name: generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a TransformWithStateInPySparkExec for batch queries: it creates a StatefulOperatorStateInfo with an empty checkpoint location, a random query run id and the configured number of shuffle partitions, and sets isStreaming to false.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the Python runners used by TransformWithStateInPySpark: a base runner, a runner without initial state, a runner with initial state, a driver side pre-init runner, and a trait that opens and closes the local state server socket (TCP loopback or Unix domain). Each runner starts a state server thread so the Python worker can read and write state over a socket.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Python runner for TransformWithStateInPySpark without initial state. Its writeNextBatchToArrowStream writes the rows of each key group into Arrow batches through a BaseStreamingArrowWriter, packing several keys into one batch, and records the bytes sent in the pythonDataSent metric. The companion object (lines 413-418) defines the type aliases InType and GroupedInType.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object shares this node id and only declares two type aliases.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonInitialStateRunner
nodes.summary: Python runner used when the query has initial state. Its schema has two struct columns, inputData and initState; each row is written as (inputRow, null) or (null, initStateRow), and a batch is finalized when the stream switches between input and initial state groups so batches never mix both.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonBaseRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract base runner extending BasePythonRunner with the Arrow input and output traits. It adds the grouping key schema and state server socket address to the eval configuration, sets Arrow batch size limits in the runner configuration, and in compute starts a TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer on a daemon thread, registering a task completion listener that stops it and closes the socket.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonPreInitRunner
nodes.summary: Driver side runner that extends StreamingPythonRunner. It starts a state server on a daemon thread, then sends the socket port or path and the grouping key schema to the Python worker and reads the status code; a non-zero status throws StreamingPythonRunnerInitializationException. Used by the operator to run the pre-init UDF when validating the state schema.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkPythonRunnerUtils
nodes.summary: Trait with the helpers shared by the runners to host the state server socket: initStateServer opens either a Unix domain socket file (when enabled by configuration) or a loopback TCP server socket, and closeServerSocketChannelSilently closes the channel and deletes the socket file.

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Writes the next Arrow batch: lazily creates the BaseStreamingArrowWriter, takes the next key group iterator if none is active, writes rows until the batch is full, and when no input is left finalizes the batch and closes the Arrow input. Adds the bytes written to the pythonDataSent metric and returns whether input was available.

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Same batch writing loop as the no initial state runner, but each element carries an isInitState flag. Rows are wrapped as (null, row) for initial state or (row, null) for data, and the current batch is finalized early when the source switches, so batches do not mix data and initial state.

nodes.name: runnerConf
nodes.summary: Adds the initial runner configuration and the Arrow max records per batch and max bytes per batch settings to the inherited runner configuration.

nodes.name: evalConf
nodes.summary: Adds grouping_key_schema (JSON of the grouping key schema) and state_server_socket_port (the Unix socket path or the TCP port as text) to the inherited eval configuration.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Initializes the state server socket, starts a TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer on a single thread daemon executor, registers a task completion listener that shuts the executor down and closes the socket, and then delegates to the parent compute to run the Python worker.

nodes.name: writeUDF
nodes.summary: Writes the chained Python functions and their argument offsets to the worker by calling PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Calls the parent init to get the data output and input streams, stores them, starts the state server, and returns the streams.

nodes.name: process
nodes.summary: Sends the state server socket port or path (path is preceded by -1) and the grouping key schema JSON to the Python worker, flushes, reads the integer result and throws StreamingPythonRunnerInitializationException with the worker error message when it is not 0.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the underlying streaming runner, closes the state server socket and interrupts the state server daemon thread.

nodes.name: startStateServer
nodes.summary: Initializes the server socket and starts a daemon thread named stateConnectionListenerThread that runs a TransformWithStateInPySparkStateServer for the driver processor handle; a failure in that thread is rethrown as a SparkException.

nodes.name: initStateServer
nodes.summary: Opens the state server socket: a Unix domain server socket bound to a uniquely named .sock file in the configured directory (or java.io.tmpdir) when Unix domain sockets are enabled, otherwise a loopback TCP server socket on an ephemeral port with backlog 1. Closes the socket if opening fails.

nodes.name: closeServerSocketChannelSilently
nodes.summary: Closes the given server socket channel and deletes the Unix socket file if one was created, logging instead of throwing when this fails.

nodes.name: AvroCompressionCodec.java
nodes.summary: Java enum that maps the Avro compression codecs Spark supports (uncompressed, deflate, snappy, bzip2, xz, zstandard) to the Avro codec names, and records which codecs accept a compression level. Provides parsing from a string and a lower case name lookup.

nodes.name: AvroCompressionCodec
nodes.summary: Enum with constants UNCOMPRESSED, DEFLATE, SNAPPY, BZIP2, XZ and ZSTANDARD, each holding the Avro DataFileConstants codec name and a flag for compression level support (true for DEFLATE, XZ and ZSTANDARD). fromString parses a name case-insensitively, lowerCaseName returns the lower case name from a precomputed EnumMap.
nodes.languageNotes: Java enum with a constructor, a static factory and a static EnumMap built with a stream collector. The private constructor (lines 41-46) is not a separate node.

nodes.name: getCodecName
nodes.summary: Returns the Avro codec name stored for this constant.

nodes.name: getSupportCompressionLevel
nodes.summary: Returns whether this codec supports a compression level setting.

nodes.name: fromString
nodes.summary: Static factory that converts a string to the enum constant using valueOf on the upper cased text (Locale.ROOT).

nodes.name: lowerCaseName
nodes.summary: Returns the lower case name of this codec from the static codecNameMap.

nodes.name: SparkAvroKeyOutputFormat.java
nodes.summary: Java file with a variant of the Avro key output format that injects a custom record writer factory, so Spark can set extra Avro file metadata entries when it writes Avro files. Contains the output format, its nested factory and a forked record writer.

nodes.name: SparkAvroKeyOutputFormat
nodes.summary: Package private output format that extends AvroKeyOutputFormat of GenericRecord. Its constructor takes a metadata map and passes a SparkRecordWriterFactory to the parent so written files carry that metadata.

nodes.name: SparkRecordWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Static nested factory that holds the metadata map and overrides create to return a SparkAvroKeyRecordWriter built from the writer schema, data model, codec, output stream and sync interval.

nodes.name: SparkAvroKeyRecordWriter
nodes.summary: Fork of Avro's AvroKeyRecordWriter that implements Syncable. Its constructor creates a DataFileWriter, copies each metadata entry with setMeta, sets the codec and sync interval and opens the file on the output stream; write appends the datum, close closes the writer and sync forwards to the writer sync.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic Java class SparkAvroKeyRecordWriter<T>; the constructor (lines 69-83) is not a separate node.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Overrides the factory method to build a SparkAvroKeyRecordWriter with the stored metadata.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Appends the datum of the given AvroKey record to the Avro data file writer.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the Avro data file writer when the task attempt finishes.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: Forwards to the data file writer sync and returns the resulting position, as required by Syncable.

nodes.name: BaseStreamingArrowWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BaseStreamingArrowWriter, a helper that writes rows of a group into an Arrow stream sent to a Python worker and splits the data into several Arrow batches when the record count or byte size limit is reached.

nodes.name: BaseStreamingArrowWriter
nodes.summary: Class wrapping an ArrowWriter over a VectorSchemaRoot and an ArrowStreamWriter. writeRow adds a row (finalizing the current batch first when a limit is reached), finalizeCurrentArrowBatch writes the batch to the stream and resets the writer, isBatchSizeLimitReached checks the max records and max bytes per batch, and getTotalNumRowsForBatch returns the row count. An optional ArrowWriter can be passed for tests. Used by the TransformWithStateInPySpark Python runners.

nodes.name: writeRow
nodes.summary: Writes one row: if the batch size limit is already reached it finalizes the current chunk and the Arrow batch, then writes the row, increments the chunk and batch counters, and returns whether the batch had been full.

nodes.name: finalizeCurrentArrowBatch
nodes.summary: Finishes the Arrow writer, writes the batch to the Arrow stream writer, resets the Arrow writer and sets the batch row count to 0.

nodes.name: finalizeCurrentChunk
nodes.summary: Resets the row count of the current chunk; a hook that subclasses can extend because not every writer needs this step.

nodes.name: isBatchSizeLimitReached
nodes.summary: Returns true when the row count reaches the max records per batch, or when the max bytes setting is not Int.MaxValue and the Arrow writer size reaches it; the size is only computed when the byte limit is set.

nodes.name: getTotalNumRowsForBatch
nodes.summary: Returns the number of rows written to the current Arrow batch.

nodes.name: EvalSubqueriesForTimeTravel.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EvalSubqueriesForTimeTravel analyzer rule, which turns scalar subqueries inside a time travel timestamp into literal values.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala rule over LogicalPlan using resolveOperatorsWithPruning and a pattern guard on RELATION_TIME_TRAVEL.

nodes.name: EvalSubqueriesForTimeTravel
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that visits RelationTimeTravel nodes whose resolved timestamp expression contains a subquery. Each ScalarSubquery in the timestamp is wrapped in a Project over OneRowRelation, executed through the session state executePlan path, and replaced by a Literal holding the first collected value. The subquery must not be correlated, because RelationTimeTravel is a leaf node and cannot resolve outer references.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Transforms RelationTimeTravel plans with a resolved timestamp that has a subquery, runs each scalar subquery with SparkSession.active, and copies the node with the evaluated timestamp. Asserts the subquery is not correlated.

nodes.name: InvokeProcedures.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the InvokeProcedures analyzer rule, which runs resolved CALL statements by invoking the bound procedure and returning its local result as a command result.

nodes.name: InvokeProcedures
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that executes CALL statements during analysis. For a resolved, bound Call that is marked to execute and has valid argument types, it optimizes the call with the session optimizer, pulls out the BoundProcedure, evaluates the foldable arguments into an InternalRow, calls the procedure, and converts each returned LocalScan into a LocalRelation. The outcome is wrapped in a CommandResult so Spark Connect sees an eagerly executed SQL command. Procedures that return more than one result, or a scan that is not a LocalScan, raise an internal error.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. For each Call that is resolved, bound, executable and has valid argument types, runs the session optimizer on it and hands the resulting ResolvedProcedure to invoke; throws an internal error if the optimized plan has any other shape.

nodes.name: invoke
nodes.summary: Converts the arguments to an InternalRow, calls the procedure, maps each returned Scan to a relation, and builds a CommandResult: empty for no results, backed by LocalTableScanExec for a single LocalRelation, and an internal error for several results.

nodes.name: toRelation
nodes.summary: Turns a procedure output Scan into a LocalRelation by reading the schema and rows of a LocalScan; any other Scan type raises an internal error.

nodes.name: toInternalRow
nodes.summary: Requires every argument to be foldable, evaluates each one, and packs the values into a GenericInternalRow passed to the procedure.

nodes.name: ReplaceCharWithVarchar.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ReplaceCharWithVarchar analyzer rule, which rewrites CHAR column types to VARCHAR in table DDL commands when the char-as-varchar setting is on.

nodes.name: ReplaceCharWithVarchar
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule (a Scala object) that does nothing unless SQLConf.CHAR_AS_VARCHAR is enabled. When enabled, it rewrites column data types through CharVarcharUtils.replaceCharWithVarchar in the v2 commands CreateTable, ReplaceTable, AddColumns, AlterColumns and ReplaceColumns, and in the v1 commands CreateTableCommand, CreateDataSourceTableCommand, AlterTableAddColumnsCommand and AlterTableChangeColumnCommand.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged when CHAR_AS_VARCHAR is off; otherwise matches each v2 and v1 table command and copies it with CHAR types replaced by VARCHAR.

nodes.name: replaceCharWithVarcharInColumn
nodes.summary: Copies a ColumnDefinition with its data type passed through CharVarcharUtils.replaceCharWithVarchar.

nodes.name: replaceCharWithVarcharInTableMeta
nodes.summary: Copies a CatalogTable with its schema rewritten by CharVarcharUtils.replaceCharWithVarchar and cast back to StructType.

nodes.name: ResolveExecuteImmediate.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ResolveExecuteImmediate analyzer rule, which resolves and runs EXECUTE IMMEDIATE statements during analysis and replaces them with the query result.

nodes.name: ResolveExecuteImmediate
nodes.summary: Analysis rule (a case class taking a SparkSession and CatalogManager) that finds UnresolvedExecuteImmediate nodes once the SQL string, arguments and target variables are all resolved. It evaluates the SQL string, runs it with sparkSession.sql (with bound parameters when arguments are given) under an EXECUTE IMMEDIATE Origin and with local SQL scripting variables hidden, and returns the analyzed plan, or the command-executed plan for commands. With an INTO clause it returns a SetVariable over the eagerly executed source and rejects commands. SQL scripts (CompoundBody) are rejected.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Matches UnresolvedExecuteImmediate when everything is resolved: with target variables builds SetVariable over executeImmediateQuery, otherwise returns executeImmediateQuery directly; unresolved nodes are left for the next iteration.

nodes.name: extractTargetVariables
nodes.summary: Maps the INTO targets to VariableReference values with canFold set to false, unwrapping an Alias; any other expression raises unsupportedParameterExpression.

nodes.name: executeImmediateQuery
nodes.summary: Extracts the SQL string, builds an Origin for EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, runs the SQL (with ParameterBindingUtils.buildUnifiedParameters when arguments exist) inside withHiddenLocalVariables, rejects CompoundBody scripts, forces analysis, and rejects commands when INTO is used. Returns commandExecuted for commands and analyzed otherwise.

nodes.name: extractQueryString
nodes.summary: Validates that the query expression is a VariableReference, an Alias of an allowed expression, or a foldable expression, checks that it is string typed, evaluates it, and fails with a null-SQL-string error when the value is null.

nodes.name: extractOriginalText
nodes.summary: Returns the original SQL text of an expression from its origin (sqlText, startIndex, stopIndex), falling back to expression.sql when origin data is missing; used in the null-string error message.

nodes.name: withHiddenLocalVariables
nodes.summary: Runs a block with a SqlScriptingContextManager whose variable manager is None, so local script variables are not visible inside EXECUTE IMMEDIATE while session variables and the rest of the scripting context are kept. The doc comment gives a DECLARE VARIABLE example.

nodes.name: ResolveMetricView.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ResolveMetricView analyzer rule for CREATE and SELECT on metric views, plus the MetricViewReadOperation extractor and the MetricViewColumn types for dimensions and measures.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy scaladoc at the top explains the YAML definition format and both workflows with plan before and after examples.

nodes.name: ResolveMetricView
nodes.summary: Analysis rule (case class over a SparkSession) with two paths driven by MetricViewPlaceholder nodes. CREATE path: for a placeholder with isCreate and a resolved child, builds an Aggregate that groups by all dimensions and selects dimensions and measures so the analyzer can derive the output schema. SELECT path: for an Aggregate matched by MetricViewReadOperation, builds a Project of source columns plus dimension expressions over the placeholder (wrapped as ResolvedMetricView), then replaces each MEASURE() reference in the Aggregate with the measure expression.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the plan unchanged unless it contains the METRIC_VIEW_PLACEHOLDER pattern; otherwise resolves bottom up, handling the CREATE placeholder case and the SELECT case through MetricViewReadOperation.

nodes.name: buildMetricViewOutput
nodes.summary: Splits the pre-parsed InputColumns into dimension and measure Alias expressions that carry the column metadata, used for the CREATE-time Aggregate.

nodes.name: buildMetricViewColumns
nodes.summary: Pairs the metric view output attributes with the InputColumns by position and builds MetricViewDimension and MetricViewMeasure values that keep the exprId and data type.

nodes.name: transformAggregateWithMeasures
nodes.summary: Rewrites aggregate expressions by replacing each AggregateExpression wrapping Measure(AttributeReference) with the matching measure expression looked up by exprId.

nodes.name: MetricViewReadOperation
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply matches a resolved Aggregate containing the METRIC_VIEW_PLACEHOLDER pattern and returns the MetricViewPlaceholder found under Filter, Expand, Project and SubqueryAlias nodes through the tail recursive collectMetricViewNode helper.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches a resolved Aggregate that contains the metric view placeholder pattern and delegates to collectMetricViewNode on its child.

nodes.name: collectMetricViewNode
nodes.summary: Tail recursive walk down through Filter, Expand, Project and SubqueryAlias nodes that returns the MetricViewPlaceholder if one is found, otherwise None.

nodes.name: MetricViewColumn
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for a metric view column with name, expr, exprId and dataType; namedExpr builds an Alias over an UpCast of the expression to the data type, keeping the exprId.

nodes.name: MetricViewDimension
nodes.summary: Case class for a dimension column of a metric view (name, expression, exprId, data type); extends MetricViewColumn.

nodes.name: MetricViewMeasure
nodes.summary: Case class for a measure column of a metric view (name, aggregate expression, exprId, data type); extends MetricViewColumn.

nodes.name: ResolveSessionCatalog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ResolveSessionCatalog analyzer rule, which rewrites resolved v2 commands into v1 commands when the target is the session catalog, together with the extractor objects it uses to recognize v1 tables, views, databases and functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala rule built mostly from one very large pattern match in apply, plus nested extractor objects with unapply methods.

nodes.name: ResolveSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] (also LookupCatalog and AliasHelper) that converts resolved v2 commands into v1 commands when the catalog is the session catalog, using qualified identifiers so that v1 commands need not qualify them again. Its apply method is one large resolveOperatorsUp pattern match with these groups: ALTER TABLE column and property commands (AddColumns, ReplaceColumns, AlterColumns, AlterTableClusterBy, RenameColumn, DropColumns, SetTableProperties, UnsetTableProperties), constraints (AddConstraint, DropConstraint, AddCheckConstraint rejected for v1), views (SetViewProperties, AlterViewAs, AlterViewSchemaBinding, CreateView, CreateMetricView, DropView, ShowViews), namespaces (DescribeNamespace, SetNamespaceProperties, SetNamespaceLocation, CreateNamespace, DropNamespace), tables (CreateTable, CreateTableAsSelect, ReplaceTable, CreateTableLike, DropTable, RenameTable, DescribeRelation, DescribeColumn, RefreshTable, TruncateTable), SHOW commands (ShowTables, ShowTablesExtended, ShowTablePartition, ShowCreateTable, ShowPartitions, ShowColumns, ShowTableProperties), ANALYZE, REPAIR, LOAD DATA, partition commands (AddPartitions, RenamePartitions, DropPartitions, SetTableSerDeProperties, SetTableLocation), and functions (DescribeFunction, ShowFunctions, CreateFunction, CreateUserDefinedFunction, DropFunction, RefreshFunction). Helpers build v1 CreateTable commands, storage formats and CatalogTable, and constant fold column default values. Nested objects extract v1 identifiers from resolved plans.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: a single resolveOperatorsUp pattern match over resolved v2 commands. For ADD COLUMNS and ALTER COLUMN on v1 tables it checks the limits (no qualified column, no NOT NULL, no bulk, no position) and builds metadata including constant folded defaults. It rewrites many commands to their v1 counterparts (tables, views, namespaces, partitions, functions, ANALYZE, SHOW, DESCRIBE), builds v1 CreateTable commands when the provider is not a v2 provider, and throws QueryCompilationErrors for operations v1 does not support (REPLACE COLUMNS, RENAME COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, constraints, REPLACE TABLE). Non-session catalogs pass through or raise missing-ability errors.

nodes.name: constructV1TableCmd
nodes.summary: Builds the v1 CreateTable command for CREATE TABLE and CTAS: creates the CatalogTable with buildCatalogTable and picks SaveMode.Ignore or ErrorIfExists from ignoreIfExists.

nodes.name: buildStorageFormatFromSerdeInfo
nodes.summary: Builds the CatalogStorageFormat for CREATE TABLE LIKE from a location and optional SerdeInfo through HiveSerDe.buildStorageFormat, reporting invalid STORED AS formats.

nodes.name: getStorageFormatAndProvider
nodes.summary: Decides the storage format and provider of a new table. An explicit USING provider is used as is (and conflicts with serde info); STORED AS or ROW FORMAT yields the Hive provider with an inferred storage format; with neither it creates a native data source table, or a Hive serde table when LEGACY_CREATE_HIVE_TABLE_BY_DEFAULT applies (with a warning).

nodes.name: buildCatalogTable
nodes.summary: Creates a CatalogTable with EXTERNAL or MANAGED type (EXTERNAL when external or a location is given), partition columns, bucket spec and cluster-by property taken from the partitioning transforms, plus comment and collation.

nodes.name: isV2Provider
nodes.summary: Returns true when DataSourceV2Utils.getTableProvider finds a v2 table provider for the given provider name.

nodes.name: addDefaultValueMetadata
nodes.summary: Validates and constant folds a column default value, then writes both CURRENT_DEFAULT and EXISTS_DEFAULT entries into the metadata builder (used by ADD COLUMNS on v1 tables).

nodes.name: constantFoldDefaultValue
nodes.summary: Validates a default value expression, wraps it in a Project over OneRowRelation, runs DefaultColumnOptimizer.FinishAnalysis and ConstantFolding, and returns the SQL of the folded constant; throws defaultValueNotConstantError if the result is not foldable.

nodes.name: supportsV1Command
nodes.summary: True for the session catalog when V2_SESSION_CATALOG_IMPLEMENTATION is "builtin" or the catalog is a CatalogExtension; gates the v1 rewrites.

nodes.name: ResolvedViewIdentifier
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches a ResolvedPersistentView in the session catalog or a ResolvedTempView and returns a TableIdentifier; other catalogs fall through to dedicated v2 strategy cases. Used by the view rewrites (view properties, alter, describe, show).

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches a session-catalog persistent view and returns its identifier with the catalog name, or a temp view and returns a TableIdentifier whose database comes from CatalogManager.databaseForSessionQualifiedViewIdentifier.

nodes.name: ResolvedV1TableIdentifier
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches a ResolvedTable holding a V1Table whose catalog supports v1 commands and returns the table identifier from its CatalogTable.

nodes.name: ResolvedV1TableIdentifierInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Like ResolvedV1TableIdentifier, but requires the catalog to be the session catalog itself; used for commands that exist only as v1 (REPAIR TABLE, LOAD DATA, RECOVER PARTITIONS, SET SERDE, partition location).

nodes.name: ResolvedV1TableOrViewIdentifier
nodes.summary: Extractor that returns the identifier of a v1 table (ResolvedV1TableIdentifier) or a session view (ResolvedViewIdentifier).

nodes.name: ResolvedV1Identifier
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches a ResolvedIdentifier whose catalog supports v1 commands and returns a TableIdentifier qualified with the catalog name; used for CREATE TABLE, CTAS, REPLACE TABLE and DROP TABLE.

nodes.name: CreateViewInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Private extractor object (a ResolvedIdentifierInSessionCatalog for CREATE VIEW) used to match CreateView targets in the session catalog.

nodes.name: DropViewInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Private extractor object (a ResolvedIdentifierInSessionCatalog for DROP VIEW) used to match DropView targets in the session catalog.

nodes.name: CreateFunctionInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Private extractor object (a ResolvedIdentifierInSessionCatalog for CREATE FUNCTION) used to match CreateFunction and CreateUserDefinedFunction targets in the session catalog.

nodes.name: ResolvedIdentifierInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Base extractor class (parameterized by statement and object type for error messages) that matches a ResolvedIdentifier in the session catalog and returns a TableIdentifier. It rejects identifiers that do not have a single-part namespace, raising an error for the builtin namespace or a single-part namespace requirement.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: For a session-catalog identifier, throws operationNotAllowedOnBuiltinNamespaceError for the builtin namespace and requiresSinglePartNamespaceError for other multi-part namespaces; otherwise returns TableIdentifier(name, namespace head, catalog name).

nodes.name: ResolvedV1Database
nodes.summary: Private extractor for a ResolvedNamespace whose catalog supports v1 commands; returns the database name, or raises errors when no database is given or the namespace is nested.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Returns None if the catalog does not support v1 commands, throws databaseFromV1SessionCatalogNotSpecifiedError for an empty namespace, returns the single name, and throws nestedDatabaseUnsupportedByV1SessionCatalogError otherwise.

nodes.name: ResolvedDatabaseInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Private extractor for commands without a v2 implementation (SHOW VIEWS, SHOW FUNCTIONS); matches namespaces in the session catalog and returns the database name, with the same error rules for empty and nested namespaces.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Returns None when the catalog is not the session catalog, throws for an empty or nested namespace, and otherwise returns the single database name.

nodes.name: DatabaseNameInSessionCatalog
nodes.summary: Private extractor used by CREATE NAMESPACE; returns the database name when the catalog supports v1 commands and requires a single-part namespace, otherwise raises requiresSinglePartNamespaceError.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Returns None for catalogs without v1 command support, the single database name for a one-part namespace, and throws requiresSinglePartNamespaceError for others.

nodes.name: ResolveSetCatalogCommand.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ResolveSetCatalogCommand analyzer rule, which turns an unresolved catalog name in a SET CATALOG command into a string literal.

nodes.name: ResolveSetCatalogCommand
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule (a Scala object) for SetCatalogCommand. When the catalog name expression is an UnresolvedAttribute (for example SET CATALOG foo), it is replaced by a string Literal with each name part wrapped in backticks through QuotingUtils.quoteNameParts. Other expressions (such as identifier(), CAST or CONCAT) are left as is, to be resolved by earlier rules and evaluated at runtime.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Matches SetCatalogCommand and copies it with catalogNameExpr replaced by the quoted Literal for UnresolvedAttribute, or unchanged for other expressions.

nodes.name: ArtifactManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArtifactManager, which stores and prepares per-session artifacts (jars, class files, Python files, archives, plain files and cached blocks) for a SparkSession, plus the cleanup state and reference-counted cache id helpers. It is used when artifacts are added to a session, when a session is cloned, and when it is closed.

nodes.name: ArtifactManager
nodes.summary: Handles storage of artifacts for one SparkSession and prepares them for use, isolating sessions by sessionUUID. Jars, class files and Python files go under 'jars', 'classes' and 'pyfiles' sub-directories, other artifacts under the session root, and 'cache/' artifacts are saved as blocks. Main methods: addArtifact, addLocalArtifacts, classloader, withResources, clone, close and uploadArtifactToFs. The companion object (lines 528-584) holds forwardToFSPrefix, the artifact root directory, SparkContextResourceType, StateCleanupRunner and the global cleanup routine.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object sharing one node id; uses a shared java.lang.ref.Cleaner to release global resources.

nodes.name: SparkContextResourceType
nodes.summary: Enumeration with the values JAR, FILE and ARCHIVE. It records which SparkContext add method (addJar, addFile or addArchive) an artifact was registered with, so the registration can be replayed when a session is cloned.

nodes.name: StateCleanupRunner
nodes.summary: Private Runnable registered with the shared Cleaner. When run it calls ArtifactManager.cleanUpGlobalResources with the saved ArtifactStateForCleanup, without holding a reference to the manager itself.

nodes.name: ArtifactStateForCleanup
nodes.summary: Private case class holding the session UUID, the SparkContext, the JobArtifactState and the artifact path of a session. It carries what is needed to clean up global resources after the ArtifactManager is gone.

nodes.name: RefCountedCacheId
nodes.summary: Private wrapper around a CacheId with an atomic reference count that starts at 1. acquire increments the count, and release decrements it and removes the block from the BlockManager when it reaches zero. Updating a count that is already zero throws BLOCK_ALREADY_RELEASED. It lets cloned sessions share cached blocks.

nodes.name: withClassLoaderIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Runs a block under the session classloader as the context classloader when alwaysApplyClassLoader is set or any artifact has been added; otherwise runs it as is. Logs the decision at debug level.

nodes.name: withResources
nodes.summary: Runs a block with the session classloader applied if needed and with this session's JobArtifactState active, so jobs launched inside see the session's artifacts.

nodes.name: getAddedJars
nodes.summary: Returns the URLs of all jar artifacts added to this session by resolving each recorded relative path against the session artifact path. Other small accessors in the class are getPythonIncludes and getCachedBlockId.

nodes.name: transferFile
nodes.summary: Moves or copies a staged file to its target path, creating parent directories first. Replaces an existing target only when allowOverwrite is true, and keeps the source when deleteSource is false.

nodes.name: normalizePath
nodes.summary: Rewrites both slash styles in a path to the system separator and normalizes the result. Used before comparing the relative artifact path against prefixes such as 'cache/', 'classes/' and 'jars/'.

nodes.name: addArtifact
nodes.summary: Adds a staged artifact to the session based on its relative path prefix. 'cache/' paths are saved to the BlockManager as a block keyed by CacheId, tracked by RefCountedCacheId; 'classes/' files are moved into the class directory and reset the cached classloader; other paths are moved under the session path, rejecting a different file at an existing path with ARTIFACT_ALREADY_EXISTS. Jars, pyfiles, archives and files are then registered with the SparkContext via addJar, addFile or addArchive and recorded for later cloning.

nodes.name: addLocalArtifacts
nodes.summary: Adds artifacts that live in a permanent location reachable by the driver, either as local files (not deleted afterwards) or as in-memory streams written to a temp file. Calls addArtifact for each, collects ARTIFACT_ALREADY_EXISTS failures and throws them merged at the end.

nodes.name: classloader
nodes.summary: Returns the cached session classloader, building it with buildClassLoader on first use. Synchronized so that concurrent callers share one instance.

nodes.name: buildClassLoader
nodes.summary: Builds the classloader for session jars and the class directory. With stub prefixes configured it chains ChildFirstURLClassLoader and StubClassLoader in an order that depends on the user-classpath-first setting; without them it uses ChildFirstURLClassLoader or a plain URLClassLoader. The shared state's jarClassLoader is the fallback.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Creates an ArtifactManager for a new session by copying the artifact directory, sharing cached blocks through incremented reference counts, re-registering recorded jars, files and archives with the SparkContext under the new session's state, and copying the tracking lists. Throws an internal error if a cached block was already released during the clone.

nodes.name: cleanUpResources
nodes.summary: Releases everything this session owns: runs the Cleaner action once, releases all cached blocks, clears the jar, Python and SparkContext path lists, and closes and drops the cached URLClassLoader, logging a warning if closing fails.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: AutoCloseable close implementation that delegates to cleanUpResources.

nodes.name: cleanUpResourcesForTesting
nodes.summary: Runs cleanUpResources and then registers a fresh Cleaner action, so a test can reuse the same instance after cleanup.

nodes.name: uploadArtifactToFs
nodes.summary: Copies a staged file to a Hadoop file system path derived from a 'forward_to_fs' relative path. When the destination is a LocalFileSystem it is refused with _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3161 unless the allowDestLocal config is enabled, to avoid overwriting arbitrary files on the driver.

nodes.name: cleanUpGlobalResources
nodes.summary: Companion-object routine that removes a session's added files, archives and jars from the SparkContext and file server (posting an environment update) and deletes the session artifact directory, logging a warning on IOException.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Decrements the reference count and removes the block from the BlockManager when the count becomes zero.

nodes.name: updateRc
nodes.summary: Atomically adds a delta to the reference count, throwing SparkRuntimeException BLOCK_ALREADY_RELEASED if the count is already zero.

nodes.name: AvroFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroFileFormat, the file format that reads and writes Avro files, and its companion object that registers a custom decimal logical type. It is registered under the short name 'avro' and is used when Avro data is read or written through the file source API.

nodes.name: AvroFileFormat
nodes.summary: FileFormat with the short name 'avro'. inferSchema and prepareWrite delegate to AvroUtils; buildReader opens each file with an Avro DataFileReader (skipping files without '.avro' unless ignoreExtension is set), syncs to the split start, picks datetime rebase mode and pushed-down filters, and returns an iterator of rows using AvroDeserializer. Splitting is always allowed, and supportFieldName accepts letters, digits and underscores with a non-digit start. The companion object (lines 178-194) holds IgnoreFilesWithoutExtensionProperty and registerCustomAvroTypes.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id; equals is defined so all instances are equal.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the Spark schema of Avro files by delegating to AvroUtils.inferSchema.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Builds the OutputWriterFactory for a write job by calling AvroUtils.prepareWrite with the session SQLConf, the job, the options and the data schema.

nodes.name: buildReader
nodes.summary: Returns a function from PartitionedFile to rows. It broadcasts the Hadoop configuration, parses AvroOptions, opens a DataFileReader (closed by a task completion listener), syncs to the split start, resolves the datetime rebase mode and filters, and yields an iterator that reads with AvroDeserializer until the split end. Files without the '.avro' extension give an empty iterator unless ignoreExtension is set.

nodes.name: supportFieldName
nodes.summary: Accepts a column name only if it is non-empty, starts with a letter or underscore, and contains only letters, digits and underscores.

nodes.name: registerCustomAvroTypes
nodes.summary: Companion-object method that registers the CustomDecimal logical type under CustomDecimal.TYPE_NAME with Avro's LogicalTypes. It is called from the class body and from the object initializer.

nodes.name: AvroOptions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroOptions, the case-insensitive option holder for the Avro reader and writer, and its companion object with the option name constants. It is built from the user-supplied data source options and a Hadoop Configuration whenever Avro data is read or written.

nodes.name: AvroOptions
nodes.summary: Parses and validates Avro data source options stored in a CaseInsensitiveMap. Fields: schema (from avroSchema JSON or avroSchemaUrl), positionalFieldMatching, recordName (default 'topLevelRecord'), recordNamespace, ignoreExtension (deprecated, falls back to the Hadoop setting), compression (falls back to the SQL config), parseMode, datetimeRebaseModeInRead, useStableIdForUnionType, stableIdPrefixForUnionType (default 'member_') and recursiveFieldMaxDepth (default -1, limit 15, else an error). equals and hashCode compare the parameters plus a map copy of the Hadoop conf. The companion object (lines 194-247) declares the option names via newOption and an apply that builds the options from the active session or a new Configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one node id; the class has an auxiliary constructor taking a plain Map.

nodes.name: parseBoolean
nodes.summary: Converts an option value to a Boolean, throwing QueryCompilationErrors.avroOptionsException with a cast message if the value is not a valid boolean.

nodes.name: getBoolean
nodes.summary: Reads a boolean option by name through parseBoolean, returning the by-name default when the option is absent.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Two AvroOptions are equal when both their parameter maps and the map copies of their Hadoop configurations are equal.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Computes a hash from the parameters and the comparable copy of the Hadoop configuration, consistent with equals.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion-object factory that builds AvroOptions from a plain map, using a new Hadoop conf from the active session state if one exists, otherwise a new Configuration.

nodes.name: AvroOutputWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroOutputWriter, the executor-side OutputWriter that serializes Spark rows to Avro records and writes them to one output file. It is created by AvroOutputWriterFactory for each write task.

nodes.name: AvroOutputWriter
nodes.summary: OutputWriter used on the executor side only. It reads the datetime rebase mode for writes, serializes each InternalRow with AvroSerializer, and writes it through a SparkAvroKeyOutputFormat record writer whose work file and output stream are overridden to use the given path. When the rebase mode is LEGACY it adds legacy datetime and timezone entries to the file metadata, along with the Spark version. write unwraps AppendWriteException to its cause; close closes the record writer.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Serializes one row into an Avro GenericRecord, wraps it in an AvroKey and writes it to the record writer, rethrowing the cause of an Avro AppendWriteException.

nodes.name: AvroOutputWriterFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroOutputWriterFactory, which creates AvroOutputWriter instances and decides the output file extension. It is the OutputWriterFactory used for Avro writes.

nodes.name: AvroOutputWriterFactory
nodes.summary: OutputWriterFactory for Avro. getFileExtension returns '.avro', or '.<codec>.avro' when an output codec is set in the job configuration; newInstance creates an AvroOutputWriter with the catalyst schema, the positional-matching flag and the parsed Avro schema.

nodes.name: getFileExtension
nodes.summary: Returns '.avro' when no output codec is configured (or it is 'null'), otherwise '.<codec>.avro' using the AvroJob output codec setting.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a new AvroOutputWriter for the given path and task attempt context.

nodes.name: AvroUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the AvroUtils helper object used by the Avro data source: it parses Avro schemas, infers a Spark SQL schema from Avro files, checks which data types can be stored, and configures the output job (schema, compression codec and level) for writing. It also defines the RowReader trait, the AvroMatchedField pair and the AvroSchemaHelper that matches Avro record fields to Catalyst fields.

nodes.name: AvroUtils
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with the shared Avro data source utilities. parseAvroSchema parses a JSON schema string and turns a NullPointerException into a SchemaParseException. inferSchema builds a StructType either from the user supplied schema option or from the first readable Avro file. supportsDataType says which Spark types are writable (variant, geometry and geography are not). prepareWrite sets the output key schema and the codec settings on the Hadoop job and returns an AvroOutputWriterFactory. It also offers the field printing and union helpers toFieldStr, isNullable and nonNullUnionBranches, and the constants JSON_INLINE_FORMAT and JSON_PRETTY_FORMAT. It extends Logging.

nodes.name: parseAvroSchema
nodes.summary: Parses an Avro schema from a JSON string with default validation turned off. A NullPointerException raised by the parser for unresolved named types is wrapped into a SchemaParseException with the original exception as cause.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the Spark SQL StructType for Avro files. It builds AvroOptions from the Hadoop configuration, warns when the deprecated ignore extension option is used, takes the schema option or reads one from the files via inferAvroSchemaFromFiles, converts it with SchemaConverters.toSqlType and throws a RuntimeException if the result is not a StructType.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively decides whether a Spark data type can be handled by the Avro source. Atomic types, null, arrays, maps, structs and user defined types (through their SQL type) are accepted, while variant, geometry and geography types are rejected.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Prepares an Avro write job. It picks the output Avro schema (the schema option or one derived by SchemaConverters.toAvroType), registers it on the job, sets the compression flag, codec name and level from the compression option and SQLConf (deflate, xz and zstandard levels, zstandard buffer pool), throws CODEC_SHORT_NAME_NOT_FOUND for unknown codecs, and returns an AvroOutputWriterFactory.

nodes.name: inferAvroSchemaFromFiles
nodes.summary: Private helper that opens the first Avro file that can be read (skipping files without the .avro extension unless ignoring extensions, and optionally skipping corrupted files) and returns its schema. Throws FileNotFoundException when no Avro file is found. Schema evolution across files is not supported.

nodes.name: RowReader
nodes.summary: Trait that gives an iterator-like view over an Avro file: subclasses supply the file reader, an AvroDeserializer and a stop position. hasNextRow advances through records (handling empty blocks, stopping past the sync point and closing the reader), deserializing each record because the deserializer may filter rows, and nextRow returns the buffered InternalRow.

nodes.name: hasNextRow
nodes.summary: Reads Avro records until one passes the deserializer filter or the file is exhausted or past the stop position; closes the reader when done and reports whether a row is buffered.

nodes.name: nextRow
nodes.summary: Returns the buffered InternalRow (calling hasNextRow first if needed), clears the buffer and throws NoSuchElementException if no row is available.

nodes.name: AvroMatchedField
nodes.summary: Case class that pairs a Catalyst StructField and its position with the Avro Schema.Field it was matched to. It is produced by AvroSchemaHelper and consumed by the Avro serializer and deserializer.

nodes.name: AvroSchemaHelper
nodes.summary: Helper that matches the fields of an Avro RECORD schema against a Catalyst StructType, by name (case sensitivity follows SQLConf.resolver) or by position. It computes matchedFields, can validate that no Catalyst field or required Avro field is left unmatched (throwing IncompatibleSchemaException), and looks up an Avro field with getAvroField. It throws if the given Avro schema is not a RECORD.

nodes.name: validateNoExtraCatalystFields
nodes.summary: Throws IncompatibleSchemaException for any Catalyst field without a matching Avro field, optionally ignoring nullable Catalyst fields; the message differs for positional matching.

nodes.name: validateNoExtraRequiredAvroFields
nodes.summary: Throws IncompatibleSchemaException for any non-nullable Avro field that has no matching Catalyst field; nullable Avro fields are ignored.

nodes.name: getFieldByName
nodes.summary: Finds the Avro field with a given name, comparing case insensitively first and then with SQLConf.resolver; returns None when absent and throws IncompatibleSchemaException when several fields match.

nodes.name: getAvroField
nodes.summary: Returns the Avro field for a Catalyst field, using the position when positional matching is on and the field name otherwise.

nodes.name: toFieldStr
nodes.summary: Formats a sequence of nested field names as a readable string such as field 'foo.bar', or top-level record when the sequence is empty. Used in error messages.

nodes.name: isNullable
nodes.summary: Returns true when an Avro field is a UNION that contains a NULL branch.

nodes.name: nonNullUnionBranches
nodes.summary: Returns the branches of an Avro union schema other than NULL, in order.

nodes.name: ResolveDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the analyzer rule ResolveDataSource that replaces UnresolvedDataSource nodes created by the DataFrameReader and DataStreamReader APIs with concrete relations. Batch reads become a V2 relation when a V2 provider loads or a V1 LogicalRelation otherwise, and streaming reads become StreamingRelationV2 or a V1 StreamingRelation.

nodes.name: ResolveDataSource
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] built with a SparkSession. Its apply method uses resolveOperatorsUp with three cases: a batch UnresolvedDataSource, a NamedStreamingRelation wrapping a streaming UnresolvedDataSource (which also passes the user provided source name), and a streaming UnresolvedDataSource. It rejects the hive provider, checks that the path option and the paths argument are not both set, and falls back to the V1 path through loadV1BatchSource.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Resolves UnresolvedDataSource nodes. Batch case: tries DataSource.lookupDataSourceV2 plus DataSourceV2Utils.loadV2Source, else loadV1BatchSource. Streaming cases: instantiate the source with DataSource.lookupDataSource, build a V1 DataSource as a shim, and, for a TableProvider that is not a FileDataSourceV2 and whose table supports micro-batch or continuous reads, return a StreamingRelationV2 (merging session options, setting the short name of a PythonDataSourceV2); otherwise return a V1 StreamingRelation.

nodes.name: loadV1BatchSource
nodes.summary: Builds the V1 batch relation: unless the legacy path option behavior is on, a single path is moved into the options, then a LogicalRelation wraps DataSource(...).resolveRelation(readOnly = true).

nodes.name: AvroDeserializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroDeserializer, which converts Avro values (GenericRecord and nested Avro data) into Catalyst values such as InternalRow, ArrayData and MapData, plus the small updater classes it uses to write into rows and arrays. The Avro data source reader uses it per file, and it can skip rows through pushed down filters.

nodes.name: AvroDeserializer
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class built from a root Avro schema, a root Catalyst type, positional field matching, a datetime rebase spec, StructFilters and the union and recursion options (a secondary constructor takes a rebase mode string and no filters). On construction it builds a converter (a record writer for struct types, a single value writer otherwise) and wraps IncompatibleSchemaException with a message naming both types. deserialize(data) applies the converter and returns Option[Any], None when a filter skips the row. Internally newWriter selects a writer per (Avro type, Catalyst type) pair, covering primitives, dates, timestamps with millis or micros logical types, time, decimals, records, arrays, string keyed maps, unions and interval types; getRecordWriter matches record fields; createArrayData allocates array storage.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Public entry point: applies the converter built at construction to one Avro value and returns Some(row or value), or None if the row is filtered out.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a writer function (updater, ordinal, value) => Unit for one Avro type and Catalyst type pair, matching on both. It handles null, boolean, int, long, float, double, string, enum, fixed and bytes, date and timestamp logical types with rebasing, time-micros, decimals (checking for incompatible precision and scale), year-month and day-time intervals, CustomDecimal, records (via getRecordWriter), arrays, string keyed maps and unions (nullable unions, int/long and float/double unions, or complex unions as structs). Any other pair throws IncompatibleSchemaException.

nodes.name: createDecimal
nodes.summary: Builds a Spark Decimal from a java BigDecimal, using an unscaled Long when the precision fits in Decimal.MAX_LONG_DIGITS and the BigDecimal otherwise.

nodes.name: getRecordWriter
nodes.summary: Builds a writer for an Avro record into a struct: uses AvroUtils.AvroSchemaHelper to match fields, validates there are no extra Catalyst fields, creates a field writer for each matched field (writing null for null values) and returns a function that writes all fields and stops early when applyFilters says to skip the row.

nodes.name: createArrayData
nodes.summary: Allocates an ArrayData of a given length: an UnsafeArrayData backed by a primitive array for boolean, byte, short, int, long, float and double elements, otherwise a GenericArrayData.

nodes.name: CatalystDataUpdater
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that abstracts updating a Catalyst container by ordinal. Subclasses implement set, and the typed setters (setNullAt, setBoolean, setByte, setShort, setInt, setLong, setDouble, setFloat, setDecimal) default to calling set.

nodes.name: RowUpdater
nodes.summary: Final class that implements CatalystDataUpdater on an InternalRow, forwarding each typed setter to the matching row method (setDecimal passes the value precision).

nodes.name: ArrayDataUpdater
nodes.summary: Final class that implements CatalystDataUpdater on an ArrayData, forwarding each typed setter to the matching array method (setDecimal uses array.update).

nodes.name: AvroSerializer.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvroSerializer, which converts Catalyst data (InternalRow and values read through SpecializedGetters) into Avro data such as Record, Utf8, EnumSymbol, Fixed, ByteBuffer, lists and maps. The Avro output writer uses it when writing rows, with field matching, nullability handling and datetime rebasing applied while the converters are built.

nodes.name: AvroSerializer
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class (extends Logging) built from the root Catalyst type, the root Avro schema, nullability, positional field matching and a datetime rebase mode (a secondary constructor reads the rebase mode from SQLConf.AVRO_REBASE_MODE_IN_WRITE). At construction it resolves the Avro type and builds a converter (a struct converter for StructType, a single value converter otherwise), wrapping IncompatibleSchemaException with the two types, and adds a null check when nullable. serialize(catalystData) applies that converter. newConverter picks a getter-to-Avro function per (Catalyst type, Avro type) pair, with helpers for structs, complex unions and nullable unions.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Public entry point: applies the converter built at construction to a Catalyst value (an InternalRow for struct types) and returns the Avro value.

nodes.name: newConverter
nodes.summary: Returns a (SpecializedGetters, ordinal) => Any converter for one Catalyst type and Avro type pair. It handles primitives, decimals as FIXED or BYTES with matching logical type, strings to ENUM (checking the symbols) or STRING, binary to FIXED (checking the size) or BYTES, dates, timestamps and timestamp without time zone with millis or micros logical types, time-micros, arrays, structs as RECORD or complex UNION, float/double and int/long unions, string keyed maps and interval types. Other pairs throw IncompatibleSchemaException.

nodes.name: newStructConverter
nodes.summary: Builds an InternalRow => Record converter for a struct: matches fields with AvroUtils.AvroSchemaHelper, validates there are no extra Catalyst fields or extra required Avro fields, creates a converter per field, and throws SparkRuntimeException AVRO_CANNOT_WRITE_NULL_FIELD when a null is written to a non-nullable Avro field.

nodes.name: newComplexUnionConverter
nodes.summary: Builds the converter for a struct that represents a complex Avro union (fields named member0, member1, ...). It checks the field names or count against the non-null union branches, makes one converter per branch and returns the value of the first non-null struct field.

nodes.name: resolveNullableType
nodes.summary: Resolves a possibly nullable Avro type to its non-null branch via resolveAvroType, and logs a warning if the Avro and Catalyst nullability differ.

nodes.name: resolveAvroType
nodes.summary: Returns a pair (isNullable, resolvedType) for an Avro type: for a UNION it removes the NULL branch when exactly one other branch remains, and returns the type unchanged otherwise.

nodes.name: warnNullabilityDifference
nodes.summary: Logs a warning when the Avro schema is nullable but the Catalyst schema is not, or the reverse (in which case a null value will raise a runtime exception).

nodes.name: nonNullUnionTypes
nodes.summary: Returns the set of Avro types of the non-null branches of a union.

nodes.name: CustomDecimal.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CustomDecimal logical type for Avro: a companion object holding the type name custom-decimal and a LogicalType subclass that reads scale, precision and className from a long typed Avro schema. It marks a long column as a Spark Decimal and is used when converting Avro long values to decimals.

nodes.name: CustomDecimal
nodes.summary: Private[spark] class (with a companion object that defines TYPE_NAME = "custom-decimal") that extends Avro's LogicalType. Its constructor reads the required integer properties scale and precision from the schema (throwing IllegalArgumentException when missing or not an int) and the optional className. Its validate method requires an underlying LONG type, a positive precision of at most DecimalType.MAX_PRECISION, and a scale between 0 and the precision.
nodes.languageNotes: The class and its companion object share one node because they share the name CustomDecimal; the object covers lines 24-26 and the class lines 31-78.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Overrides LogicalType.validate: calls super.validate, then checks that the schema type is LONG, that precision is positive and not above DecimalType.MAX_PRECISION, and that scale is not negative and not greater than precision. Throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise.

nodes.name: SchemaConverters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the public SchemaConverters object that converts Avro schemas to Spark SQL types (toSqlType) and Spark SQL types to Avro schemas (toAvroType, toAvroTypeWithDefaults), including logical types, unions, and recursive record limits. It also defines two package private exception classes, IncompatibleSchemaException and UnsupportedAvroTypeException, used across the Avro source.

nodes.name: SchemaConverters
nodes.summary: Object annotated @DeveloperApi (extends Logging) with the conversion between Avro and Spark SQL schemas. toSqlType (several overloads: with union and recursion options, with defaults, and a deprecated one taking an options map) returns a SchemaType via toSqlTypeHelper. toAvroType maps a DataType to an Avro schema (decimals become fixed, intervals and time carry the spark.sql.catalyst.type property), and toAvroTypeWithDefaults builds a schema where fields are nullable unions with null defaults.

nodes.name: SchemaType
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a Spark SQL DataType with a nullable flag; it is the result of toSqlType.

nodes.name: toSqlType
nodes.summary: Converts an Avro schema to a SchemaType (Spark SQL type plus nullability) using toSqlTypeHelper with the options useStableIdForUnionType, stableIdPrefixForUnionType and recursiveFieldMaxDepth (default -1), asserting the top level result is not null. Other overloads at lines 82-84 (defaults) and 87-94 (deprecated, takes an options Map and reads AvroOptions) delegate to it.

nodes.name: toSqlTypeHelper
nodes.summary: Recursive private converter from an Avro schema to a SchemaType. It maps primitives, enum, null, logical dates and timestamps, decimals (including CustomDecimal), time-micros, the spark.sql.catalyst.type property, arrays, maps, records and unions. Records track recursion depth by full name and throw IncompatibleSchemaException (or drop the recursive field when recursiveFieldMaxDepth allows); nullable unions are unwrapped, int/long and float/double unions are widened, and other unions become structs with member0, member1 or stable id field names.

nodes.name: toAvroType
nodes.summary: Converts a Spark SQL DataType into an Avro Schema (recordName defaults to topLevelRecord). Maps primitives, date and timestamp logical types, time-micros, decimal to a named fixed, arrays, string keyed maps, structs to records, and year-month and day-time intervals; wraps the result in a union with null when nullable. Unsupported types throw IncompatibleSchemaException.

nodes.name: toAvroTypeWithDefaults
nodes.summary: Private recursive converter that builds an Avro schema where every field is a union with null and has a null default; nested structs, arrays and maps are also wrapped in a union with null, and decimals become named fixed types. The public overload at lines 399-401 starts it for a StructType with record name topLevelRecord, empty namespace and nesting level 0. Unsupported types throw IncompatibleSchemaException.

nodes.name: IncompatibleSchemaException
nodes.summary: Private[avro] Exception subclass taking a message and an optional cause. It is thrown when a Catalyst and an Avro schema cannot be converted into each other or matched.

nodes.name: UnsupportedAvroTypeException
nodes.summary: Private[avro] Exception subclass carrying only a message, for Avro types the source does not support.

nodes.name: StreamingCheckpointManager.scala
nodes.summary: Classic (SparkSession-based) implementation of the streaming checkpoint manager API. It validates the arguments of an offline state repartition request and hands the work to an OfflineStateRepartitionRunner.

nodes.name: StreamingCheckpointManager
nodes.summary: Private[spark] @Evolving class that extends the streaming API trait of the same name and mixes in Logging. Its repartition method rejects a null or empty checkpoint location and a non-positive partition count with OfflineStateRepartitionErrors, then builds an OfflineStateRepartitionRunner with the session, checkpoint location, partition count and exactly-once-sink flag and calls run(). Used to repartition the state of a streaming checkpoint offline.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Validates checkpointLocation (not null, not empty) and numPartitions (greater than zero), throwing the matching OfflineStateRepartitionErrors error otherwise. Then creates an OfflineStateRepartitionRunner with enforceExactlyOnceSink (default true) and runs it.

nodes.name: StreamingQuery.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the classic StreamingQuery trait, which narrows the session type of the streaming API StreamingQuery to the classic SparkSession.

nodes.name: StreamingQuery
nodes.summary: Trait that extends the streaming API StreamingQuery and only overrides sparkSession so that it returns the classic SparkSession. Used by classic streaming query implementations that need the concrete session type.

nodes.name: MergeIntoWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of the MergeIntoWriter API. It collects matched, not-matched and not-matched-by-source merge actions and turns them into a MergeIntoTable logical plan that is executed as a command.

nodes.name: MergeIntoWriter
nodes.summary: Experimental class (since 4.0.0) created from a target table name, a source Dataset and a merge condition Column; it extends the sql MergeIntoWriter. It keeps three action buffers (matchedActions, notMatchedActions, notMatchedBySourceActions), and insert, insertAll, update, updateAll and delete append InsertAction, InsertStarAction, UpdateAction, UpdateStarAction or DeleteAction to the right buffer. merge() builds the MergeIntoTable plan through mergeCommand() and executes it with the session state, asserting the command ran; it fails with NO_MERGE_ACTION_SPECIFIED when no action was added.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Executes the merge: builds the plan from mergeCommand(), runs it via sessionState.executePlan and asserts that the command was executed.

nodes.name: mergeCommand
nodes.summary: Throws NO_MERGE_ACTION_SPECIFIED when all three action buffers are empty; otherwise builds a MergeIntoTable over an UnresolvedRelation of the target table (requiring write privileges derived from the actions), the source logical plan, the merge condition expression and the three action lists, plus the schema evolution flag.

nodes.name: insertAll
nodes.summary: Appends an InsertStarAction with the optional condition to notMatchedActions and returns this writer.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Appends an InsertAction with the optional condition and assignments built from a column map to notMatchedActions.

nodes.name: updateAll
nodes.summary: Appends an UpdateStarAction with the optional condition via appendUpdateDeleteAction, choosing the buffer by the notMatchedBySource flag.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Appends an UpdateAction with assignments built from a column map via appendUpdateDeleteAction.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Appends a DeleteAction with the optional condition via appendUpdateDeleteAction.

nodes.name: appendUpdateDeleteAction
nodes.summary: Adds an update or delete action to notMatchedBySourceActions when the flag is true, otherwise to matchedActions.

nodes.name: mapToAssignments
nodes.summary: Converts a Map of target column names to Columns into Assignment expressions, parsing each key with expr().

nodes.name: TypedAggUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object for typed aggregations: builds the grouping key column of a typed grouped Dataset and injects input encoders into typed aggregate expressions.

nodes.name: TypedAggUtils
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with two helpers. aggKeyColumn produces the key column for a grouped Dataset: the first grouping attribute (kept as is or aliased to "key", depending on nameNonStructGroupingKeyAsValue) for a non-struct encoder, or a CreateStruct of the grouping attributes aliased "key" for a struct encoder. withInputType rewrites TypedAggregateExpression nodes that have no input deserializer by attaching the input deserializer, class and schema of the given encoder.

nodes.name: aggKeyColumn
nodes.summary: Returns the NamedExpression used as the grouping key: unaliased or aliased "key" first attribute for a non-struct encoder (decided by SQLConf nameNonStructGroupingKeyAsValue), or a struct of all grouping attributes aliased "key".

nodes.name: withInputType
nodes.summary: Transforms an expression so that every TypedAggregateExpression without an input deserializer receives an UnresolvedDeserializer, the encoder runtime class and the encoder schema through withInputInfo. Untyped aggregates are resolved by the analyzer instead.

nodes.name: QueryExecutionListener.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the QueryExecutionListener callback interface, the ExecutionListenerManager that registers listeners on a session, and the ExecutionListenerBus that forwards SQL execution end events to those listeners.

nodes.name: QueryExecutionListener
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi trait for analyzing execution metrics of queries. onSuccess(funcName, qe, durationNs) is called when a query succeeds and onFailure(funcName, qe, exception) when it fails. Implementations must be thread-safe because callbacks may come from several threads.

nodes.name: onSuccess
nodes.summary: Callback invoked when a query executed successfully, with the action name, the QueryExecution and the duration in nanoseconds.

nodes.name: onFailure
nodes.summary: Callback invoked when a query failed, with the action name, the QueryExecution and the exception (an Error is wrapped in an Exception reachable through getCause).

nodes.name: ExecutionListenerManager
nodes.summary: Manager of QueryExecutionListeners for one session (constructed with the session, its SQLConf and a loadExtensions flag). The listener bus is created lazily on the first register call; at construction it can load listeners named by the QUERY_EXECUTION_LISTENERS static conf. Provides register, unregister, clear, listListeners (for tests) and clone (copies the listeners into a manager for another session).

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Creates the ExecutionListenerBus on first use (under a lock) and adds the listener to it.

nodes.name: unregister
nodes.summary: Removes the given listener from the bus if one exists.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes all registered listeners from the bus if one exists.

nodes.name: listListeners
nodes.summary: Returns the registered listeners as an array (empty if no bus); exposed for testing only.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Creates a new ExecutionListenerManager for another session and SQLConf without loading extensions, and registers all current listeners on it.

nodes.name: ExecutionListenerBus
nodes.summary: Private[sql] SparkListener and ListenerBus that receives SparkListenerSQLExecutionEnd events through onOtherEvent and posts them to all registered QueryExecutionListeners. Its auxiliary constructor adds the bus to the shared listener queue of the SparkContext and registers it with the ContextCleaner. Events are reported only when the execution has a name and was launched by the same session (same sessionUUID).

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: Forwards SparkListenerSQLExecutionEnd events to all listeners through postToAll and ignores other events.

nodes.name: doPostEvent
nodes.summary: If shouldReport accepts the event, calls onFailure (wrapping a non-Exception Throwable with failedToExecuteQueryError) when the execution failed, otherwise onSuccess with the event duration.

nodes.name: shouldReport
nodes.summary: Returns true only for SQL executions that have an execution name and whose QueryExecution session UUID equals this bus session UUID.

nodes.name: ResolveTranspose.scala
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that resolves an UnresolvedTranspose plan into a Transpose plan with literal rows. It collects the casted data to the driver and swaps rows and columns around an index column.

nodes.name: ResolveTranspose
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] constructed with a SparkSession. For UnresolvedTranspose nodes whose child and index columns are resolved, it uses the first column as the index when none is given, casts the index to string (only atomic types allowed), casts all other columns to their least common type, filters out null indexes, sorts by the index, limits to dataFrameTransposeMaxValues + 1 rows, executes the plan and collects the rows.
