It then builds a Transpose with a "key" column plus one column per index value; an empty result yields only the key column with the non-index column names. It fails with TRANSPOSE_NO_LEAST_COMMON_TYPE, TRANSPOSE_INVALID_INDEX_COLUMN or TRANSPOSE_EXCEED_ROW_LIMIT.

nodes.name: leastCommonType
nodes.summary: Reduces a list of data types to their tightest common type with AnsiTypeCoercion.findTightestCommonType; returns StringType for an empty list and throws TRANSPOSE_NO_LEAST_COMMON_TYPE when two types have no common type.

nodes.name: transposeMatrix
nodes.summary: Builds a matrix with one row per non-index column: the first element is the column name and the rest are the values of that column taken from each collected row, so that rows and columns are swapped.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule body: pattern-matches resolved UnresolvedTranspose nodes (pruned by the UNRESOLVED_TRANSPOSE tree pattern), builds the cast, filter, sort, project and limit plan, executes it with executeCollect, checks the row limit and returns the resulting Transpose plan.

nodes.name: CommandResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CommandResult leaf logical plan node that holds the already computed rows of an executed command, together with its logical and physical command plans for EXPLAIN.

nodes.name: CommandResult
nodes.summary: Case class LeafNode holding the output attributes, the command logical plan, the command physical plan and the result rows. The plans are only used to display the plan tree for EXPLAIN (exposed through innerChildren), and all three are transient because the rows may not be serializable and should not be sent to executors. computeStats estimates the size as the per-row size of the output times the number of rows.

nodes.name: SQLFunctionNode.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SQLFunctionNode, a unary logical plan node that wraps the body plan of a SQL function together with the function identity.

nodes.name: SQLFunctionNode
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryNode that holds a SQLFunction and its body plan as the child; its output is the child output and its string arguments are the function name and the child. On construction it throws a tableValuedArgumentsNotYetImplementedForSqlFunctions error when the body contains a table argument expression (FUNCTION_TABLE_RELATION_ARGUMENT_EXPRESSION pattern).

nodes.name: UnresolvedDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UnresolvedDataSource, the unresolved leaf plan created when a data source is loaded through the reader APIs.

nodes.name: UnresolvedDataSource
nodes.summary: Case class UnresolvedLeafNode created by the DataFrameReader and DataStreamReader APIs when loading a data source. It carries the format name, an optional user-specified schema, case-insensitive options, an isStreaming flag and the paths. Its toString (also used for simpleString) prints only the format, the streaming flag and the number of paths.

nodes.name: UserDefinedFunctionUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Holds a single helper that turns a user defined function description into an executable ScalaUDF expression. It lives in the classic package and is private to the sql package.

nodes.name: UserDefinedFunctionUtils
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object with one method, toScalaUDF, which builds a ScalaUDF from a SparkUserDefinedFunction and a list of child expressions. The comment says the method should move into ScalaUDF once SparkUserDefinedFunction moves to sql/api.

nodes.name: toScalaUDF
nodes.summary: Creates a ScalaUDF from the function, data type, nullability, determinism and given name of a SparkUserDefinedFunction. Input encoders are converted with encoderFor and entries equal to UnboundRowEncoder are dropped; the output encoder is converted the same way.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the package object for org.apache.spark.sql.classic with two type aliases: DataFrame as Dataset[Row] and Strategy as SparkStrategy.

nodes.name: classic
nodes.summary: Package object of the classic package. It declares the alias DataFrame = Dataset[Row] and the alias Strategy = SparkStrategy, the latter marked DeveloperApi and Unstable and documented as the way to turn a logical plan into zero or more SparkPlans.

nodes.name: DetectAmbiguousSelfJoin.scala
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that detects ambiguous self joins caused by Dataset column references and fails the query instead of returning confusing results. It also strips the Dataset id metadata from attribute references.

nodes.name: DetectAmbiguousSelfJoin
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] used after analysis when the SQLConf setting FAIL_AMBIGUOUS_SELF_JOIN_ENABLED is on. A Dataset column reference is an AttributeReference carrying Dataset id and column position metadata. When the plan has a Join, the rule compares the exprIds of referenced columns with the real output of the matching Dataset plans and throws ambiguousAttributesInSelfJoinError for references regenerated by the self join, except equal-column conditions and direct self joins against a foldable value. In all cases it removes the special metadata at the end.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object extending Rule with pattern-matching extractors and a private case class.

nodes.name: ColumnReference
nodes.summary: Private case class holding the datasetId, column position and exprId read from the metadata of a Dataset column reference; used as the key when collecting ambiguous references.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanWithDatasetId
nodes.summary: Extractor object that matches a LogicalPlan tagged with Dataset.DATASET_ID_TAG and returns the plan with its set of Dataset ids.

nodes.name: AttrWithCast
nodes.summary: Extractor object that matches an AttributeReference, looking through nested Cast expressions.

nodes.name: isColumnReference
nodes.summary: Returns true when an AttributeReference has both the Dataset id key and the column position key in its metadata.

nodes.name: toColumnReference
nodes.summary: Builds a ColumnReference (dataset id, column position, exprId) from the metadata and exprId of an AttributeReference.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Reads the Dataset id tag of a LogicalPlan and returns the plan together with the id set when the tag exists.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive extractor: unwraps Cast nodes to their child and returns the AttributeReference found, else None.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Main rule body. Returns the plan unchanged if the SQLConf flag is off, only strips metadata if there is no Join, otherwise collects Dataset column references, marks those whose attribute exprId differs from the matching Dataset plan output, filters equal-column and direct self join cases at the root Join, throws ambiguousAttributesInSelfJoinError if any remain, and finally strips the metadata.

nodes.name: stripColumnReferenceMetadataInPlan
nodes.summary: Transforms every expression in the plan and removes the Dataset column reference metadata from matching AttributeReferences.

nodes.name: stripColumnReferenceMetadata
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the metadata of an AttributeReference without the Dataset id and column position keys. Private to the sql package.

nodes.name: CoalesceBucketsInJoin.scala
nodes.summary: Physical planning rule that coalesces the buckets of one side of a SortMergeJoin or ShuffledHashJoin when both sides are bucketed tables with divisible bucket counts, plus the extractor that recognises such joins.

nodes.name: CoalesceBucketsInJoin
nodes.summary: Rule[SparkPlan]. Active when conf.coalesceBucketsInJoinEnabled is true and the ratio of the two bucket counts is at most conf.coalesceBucketsInJoinMaxBucketRatio. It uses ExtractJoinWithBuckets to find joins and sets the number of coalesced buckets on the bucketed FileSourceScanExec of the side with more buckets. For ShuffledHashJoin it only coalesces the stream side to avoid OOM on the build side.

nodes.name: ExtractJoinWithBuckets
nodes.summary: Extractor object matching a ShuffledJoin (sort merge or shuffled hash) where both sides consist of only a scan operation over bucketed tables, join keys match the output partitioning, and the bucket numbers differ but are divisible. It returns the join with the left and right bucket counts.

nodes.name: updateNumCoalescedBucketsInScan
nodes.summary: Transforms a plan bottom up and sets optionalNumCoalescedBuckets on every FileSourceScanExec that has a bucket spec.

nodes.name: updateNumCoalescedBuckets
nodes.summary: Applies the coalesced bucket count to the left child if it differs from the left bucket count, otherwise to the right child, and copies the SortMergeJoinExec or ShuffledHashJoinExec with the updated child.

nodes.name: isCoalesceSHJStreamSide
nodes.summary: Checks whether the side to coalesce in a ShuffledHashJoinExec is the stream side (not the build side), based on buildSide.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Returns the plan if coalescing is disabled; otherwise transforms joins matched by ExtractJoinWithBuckets whose bucket ratio is within the configured limit.

nodes.name: hasScanOperation
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive check that a plan is only filters, projects and broadcast joins (following the non-build side) on top of a bucketed FileSourceScanExec.

nodes.name: getBucketSpec
nodes.summary: Finds the first FileSourceScanExec in the plan that has a bucket spec and no coalesced bucket count yet, and returns its BucketSpec.

nodes.name: satisfiesOutputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Checks that the join keys match the expressions of a HashPartitioning (order ignored), recursing into PartitioningCollection.

nodes.name: isApplicable
nodes.summary: True when both join sides have a scan operation and the left and right keys satisfy the output partitioning of their sides.

nodes.name: isDivisible
nodes.summary: True when the two bucket counts differ and the larger is divisible by the smaller, since bucket id is computed by modulo.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Extractor body: for an applicable ShuffledJoin, reads the bucket specs of both sides and returns the join with both bucket counts when they are divisible, otherwise None.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingLocalVariableManager.scala
nodes.summary: Variable manager for local variables declared inside SQL scripts. It stores variables in the scopes of the SqlScriptingExecutionContext and resolves them by name, with an optional label qualifier.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingLocalVariableManager
nodes.summary: Implements VariableManager (and mixes in DataTypeErrorsBase) on top of a SqlScriptingExecutionContext. create puts a variable in the current scope, set and get find the scope through searchAcrossFrames (names are one part or label.name), qualify returns an identifier in a fake local catalog under the scope label, and remove always fails because local variables cannot be dropped.

nodes.name: getVariableNameForError
nodes.summary: Builds the quoted name used in errors from the current scope label and the variable name.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Adds a variable definition to the current scope; throws VARIABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS if the name is already present in that scope.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Replaces the definition of an existing variable in the scope found for the name parts; throws an unresolved variable error when no scope has it.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the variable definition found by looking up the scope of the name parts.

nodes.name: findScopeOfVariable
nodes.summary: Finds the scope holding a variable, matching a single name by contents or label.name by scope label, using the context searchAcrossFrames helper; any other number of name parts is an internal error.

nodes.name: qualify
nodes.summary: Returns a ResolvedIdentifier in FakeLocalCatalog whose namespace is the current scope label.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Always throws an internal error because local variables cannot be dropped.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Clears all frames of the script context.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: True when no scope in any frame of the context holds a variable.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecutionContext.scala
nodes.summary: Execution state for SQL scripting: the context holding active frames, the frame (script or exception handler) that iterates statements and holds scopes, the scope that stores variables, cursors, cursor states and handler lookup, and the frame type enumeration.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecutionContext
nodes.summary: Keeps the list of active SqlScriptingExecutionFrames of a running script and delegates scope enter and exit to the last frame. Provides generic searchAcrossFrames and performInFrameContaining helpers that respect lexical scope visibility between handler frames and the frames that defined them, and uses them for cursor lookup, cursor state read and update, and error handler lookup. Implements SqlScriptingExecutionContextExtension.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingFrameType
nodes.summary: Enumeration of frame kinds: SQL_SCRIPT, EXIT_HANDLER and CONTINUE_HANDLER.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecutionFrame
nodes.summary: An Iterator over the CompoundStatementExec elements of a CompoundBodyExec execution plan, created per script or per exception handler body. It owns the stack of scopes, and offers enterScope, exitScope (cleaning up scopes), cursor lookup, cursor state get and update, and findHandler that searches scopes depending on the frame type and the first handler scope label.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecutionScope
nodes.summary: A labeled scope with maps of variables, cursors and cursor states and the TriggerToExceptionHandlerMap of that scope. cleanup sets every cursor state to closed; findHandler picks the most appropriate handler by condition, then SQLSTATE, then NOT FOUND for SQLSTATE class 02, then SQLEXCEPTION for other classes except XX and 02.

nodes.name: enterScope
nodes.summary: Enters a labeled scope in the last frame; internal error if there are no frames.

nodes.name: exitScope
nodes.summary: Exits the labeled scope in the last frame; internal error if there are no frames.

nodes.name: searchAcrossFrames
nodes.summary: Generic search over frames: current frame first, then older frames newest to oldest, restricted to scopes visible where the handler frame was defined (lexical scoping). Used for variables and cursors.

nodes.name: performInFrameContaining
nodes.summary: Same frame and scope walk as searchAcrossFrames, but runs an action in the frame where the searched object is found and returns whether it was found.

nodes.name: findCursorByName
nodes.summary: Finds a cursor definition by normalized name across frames using searchAcrossFrames; implements the extension API.

nodes.name: findCursorInScope
nodes.summary: Finds a cursor in a specific labeled scope across accessible frames, for label.cursor references.

nodes.name: getCursorState
nodes.summary: Returns the cursor state across frames, optionally in a given scope label. An overload at lines 214-217 takes a CursorReference and forwards its normalizedName and scopeLabel.

nodes.name: updateCursorState
nodes.summary: Finds the frame containing the cursor with performInFrameContaining and updates the cursor state there; internal error if not found or no frames.

nodes.name: findHandler
nodes.summary: Looks for an exception handler for a condition and SQLSTATE: first in the body of the last frame if it is a handler frame, then in the first (script) frame, remembering the handler scope label.

nodes.name: findCursorByName
nodes.summary: Returns the cursor definition from the newest scope that has the normalized name.

nodes.name: findCursorInScope
nodes.summary: Returns the cursor definition with the given name in the scope with the given label.

nodes.name: findScope
nodes.summary: Finds the newest scope with the given label.

nodes.name: getCursorState
nodes.summary: Returns the cursor state from a labeled scope, or from the newest scope that has one when no label is given.

nodes.name: updateCursorState
nodes.summary: Puts a new cursor state into the labeled scope or into the scope where the cursor is defined; internal error if missing.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next statement from the plan tree iterator; internal error if none remain.

nodes.name: enterScope
nodes.summary: Appends a new SqlScriptingExecutionScope with the given label and handler map (labels are already lowercased by the parser).

nodes.name: exitScope
nodes.summary: Removes scopes down to and including the one with the given label, calling cleanup on each removed scope.

nodes.name: findHandler
nodes.summary: Chooses scopes to search (all scopes for handler frames or when no handler is active; otherwise scopes outside the first active handler scope) and returns the first handler found by a scope.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Transitions the state of every cursor of the scope to CursorClosed.

nodes.name: findHandler
nodes.summary: Finds the handler for an exception: named condition (also the error class before a dot), then SQLSTATE, then NOT FOUND handler for SQLSTATE starting with 02, then SQLEXCEPTION handler for other states except XX and 02.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingInterpreter.scala
nodes.summary: Interpreter that turns a parsed SQL script (CompoundBody) into a tree of executable statement nodes (CompoundBodyExec and the other *StatementExec classes).

nodes.name: SqlScriptingInterpreter
nodes.summary: Case class taking a classic SparkSession. buildExecutionPlan converts a CompoundBody, with a map of parameter expressions and the execution context, into a CompoundBodyExec. Handler declarations become ExceptionHandlerExec objects collected into a TriggerToExceptionHandlerMap (duplicate conditions, SQLSTATEs, NOT FOUND or SQLEXCEPTION raise errors), and each logical script statement (if, case, while, repeat, loop, for, leave, iterate, single SQL statement) is mapped to its executable counterpart.

nodes.name: buildExecutionPlan
nodes.summary: Public entry point: transforms the CompoundBody into an executable tree and casts the result to the top level CompoundBodyExec.

nodes.name: transformBodyIntoExec
nodes.summary: Converts a CompoundBody: builds ExceptionHandlerExec objects for its handlers, fills condition, SQLSTATE, NOT FOUND and SQLEXCEPTION maps (throwing on duplicates), transforms child statements (or a NoOpStatementExec when empty) and creates the CompoundBodyExec with the label, scope flag, context and handler map. Recurses for handler bodies.

nodes.name: transformTreeIntoExecutable
nodes.summary: Pattern matches on the parsed statement and creates the matching executable node, wrapping conditions and queries in SingleStatementExec; unsupported statements raise an internal error. Simple case statements get an internal statement that selects the case expression as caseVariable.

nodes.name: MapperRowCounter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapperRowCounter, an accumulator that records, for one partition, a pair of (mapper index, row count).

nodes.name: MapperRowCounter
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2 (since 3.4.0) whose value is a list of (mapper index, row count) pairs. setPartitionId initializes the single entry with the partition id and a zero count, add increments that count by one per value, and merge appends the entries of another MapperRowCounter (any other accumulator type raises an unsupported-operation error). All access is synchronized and the list is created lazily; copy duplicates the entries, copyAndReset returns a new empty counter and reset drops the list.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Lazily creates the internal ArrayList of (mapper index, row count) pairs and returns it.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Creates a new MapperRowCounter that holds a copy of all current entries, under the lock.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Increments the row count of the single entry by one; asserts that the entry was initialized with setPartitionId.

nodes.name: setPartitionId
nodes.summary: Initializes the accumulator by adding the entry (partition id, 0); asserts that the accumulator is still zero.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Appends all entries of another MapperRowCounter; throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3165) when the other accumulator is of a different class.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Executes a parsed SQL script statement by statement, returning result DataFrames one at a time and routing SQL exceptions to condition handlers. A companion object runs a whole script and returns the result of the last result statement.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecution
nodes.summary: Class SqlScriptingExecution (lines 41-283) plus its companion object (lines 285-330, same node). Built from a CompoundBody script, a classic SparkSession and a map of parameter expressions, it creates a SqlScriptingInterpreter, builds the execution plan, and keeps a SqlScriptingExecutionContext whose frame stack starts with the script frame. Callers wrap use in withContextManager, call getNextResult to advance to the next result DataFrame, and must execute that result before asking for the next one. Exceptions that are SparkThrowables are matched to EXIT or CONTINUE handlers, which run in their own frame; unhandled SQLSTATE class 02 conditions are ignored and other errors are rethrown. The object method executeSqlScript runs a script and returns a LocalRelation with the rows of the last result.

nodes.name: withContextManager
nodes.summary: Runs the given block with the scripting context manager handle active; all calls to the execution API must be wrapped with it.

nodes.name: injectLeaveStatement
nodes.summary: Walks down the current statements of a plan to the deepest leaf and replaces it with a LeaveStatementExec for the given label, used to exit a scope after an EXIT handler finishes.

nodes.name: interruptConditionalStatements
nodes.summary: After a CONTINUE handler, finds the deepest current statement and, if it is a conditional statement whose condition evaluation had started (case variable, FOR query or executed condition), marks it interrupted so that the conditional is skipped.

nodes.name: getNextStatement
nodes.summary: Pops finished frames from the context (exiting the top script scope at the end and injecting a leave statement or interrupting conditionals for EXIT and CONTINUE handler frames) and returns the next statement of the last remaining frame, or None.

nodes.name: getNextResultInternal
nodes.summary: Loops over statements, building and running each unexecuted SingleStatementExec inside withErrorHandling, and returns the first DataFrame whose plan is not a CommandResult; returns None at the end of the script.

nodes.name: getNextResult
nodes.summary: Public entry that returns the next result DataFrame; on a SparkThrowable it calls handleException and retries, other Throwables are rethrown. The returned result must be executed before the next call.

nodes.name: handleException
nodes.summary: Looks up a handler for the error condition and SQLSTATE; if found, pushes a CONTINUE or EXIT handler frame and enters its scope. If not found, rethrows the exception unless its SQLSTATE starts with 02 (completion condition), in which case execution continues.

nodes.name: withErrorHandling
nodes.summary: Runs a block and passes any SparkThrowable to handleException; other Throwables are rethrown.

nodes.name: executeSqlScript
nodes.summary: Companion object method: creates a SqlScriptingExecution, iterates over all result DataFrames inside the context manager, collecting each one, and returns a LocalRelation of the last collected result (an empty LocalRelation if there was none).

nodes.name: SqlScriptingExecutionNode.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the executable node tree used by the SQL scripting interpreter: leaf nodes for single statements, and non-leaf nodes for compound bodies, IF, WHILE, REPEAT, LOOP, FOR, simple and searched CASE, LEAVE, ITERATE and exception handlers. Each node exposes a tree iterator that yields one statement at a time, and handles scopes, label matching and CONTINUE/EXIT handler interruption.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait hierarchy where each non-leaf node implements a lazily built Iterator[CompoundStatementExec] as a small state machine (Condition/Body states) using private Enumerations.

nodes.name: CompoundStatementExec
nodes.summary: Sealed root trait of all SQL scripting execution nodes used during the interpretation phase. It mixes in Logging, has an isInternal flag (false by default) telling whether a statement came from the script or was created by the interpreter, and declares reset() to restore a node to its initial execution state.

nodes.name: LeafStatementExec
nodes.summary: Marker trait for leaf nodes of the execution tree, such as SingleStatementExec, NoOpStatementExec, LeaveStatementExec and IterateStatementExec.

nodes.name: NonLeafStatementExec
nodes.summary: Trait for non-leaf nodes of the execution tree, which are iterators over executable child nodes. It keeps a pointer curr to the statement to be iterated next, requires getTreeIterator for an in-order traversal, and offers evaluateBooleanCondition, which runs a condition statement and requires a single row with a single boolean column (NULL counts as false).

nodes.name: ConditionalStatementExec
nodes.summary: Trait for non-leaf nodes that evaluate a condition (IF, CASE, WHILE, REPEAT, FOR). It holds an interrupted flag used by CONTINUE and EXIT handlers to skip further execution, and declares isInCondition so a CONTINUE handler can tell whether an exception happened while evaluating the condition or while running the body.

nodes.name: SingleStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable leaf node for one parsed SQL statement. It keeps the logical plan, its Origin and named-parameter arguments, an isExecuted flag for statements run during interpretation (for example conditions), returns the original SQL text through getText and builds a DataFrame with buildDataFrame (wrapping the plan in NameParameterizedQuery when arguments exist).

nodes.name: NoOpStatementExec
nodes.summary: Leaf node that does nothing when returned from the iterator. It is emitted by empty BEGIN END blocks and used by loops and FOR to give their parents a statement to return when a body or result set is empty.

nodes.name: TriggerToExceptionHandlerMap
nodes.summary: Holds the exception handlers declared in one compound body, indexed by condition name and by sqlState, plus an optional catch-all SQLEXCEPTION handler and an optional NOT FOUND handler, with getters for each. The companion object offers createEmptyMap for bodies that declare no handlers.

nodes.name: createEmptyMap
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a TriggerToExceptionHandlerMap with empty condition and sqlState maps and no catch-all or NOT FOUND handler.

nodes.name: CompoundBodyExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for a compound body (BEGIN END block). It iterates its child statements in order, descends into nested non-leaf nodes, can act as a labeled scope that registers its exception handlers with the execution context on enterScope and unregisters them on exitScope, and stops iteration when a LEAVE or ITERATE statement is encountered.

nodes.name: enterScope
nodes.summary: Idempotently enters the scope of this body when it is a labeled scope: marks the status as inside and calls context.enterScope with the label and the trigger-to-handler map.

nodes.name: exitScope
nodes.summary: Idempotently leaves the scope of this body: if the scope was entered, marks it exited and calls context.exitScope with the label.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy tree iterator of the compound body. next() returns leaf statements directly, delegates to nested non-leaf nodes (entering scope of nested bodies once and exiting it when they are exhausted), and routes LEAVE and ITERATE statements to the matching handlers.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets every child statement, restarts the local iterator and the current pointer, and clears the stop flag and scope status.

nodes.name: handleLeaveStatement
nodes.summary: When an unmatched LEAVE statement arrives, stops this body's iteration, exits its scope and marks the LEAVE as matched if this body's label equals the leave label.

nodes.name: handleIterateStatement
nodes.summary: When an unmatched ITERATE statement arrives, stops this body's iteration and exits its scope (the label is matched by the enclosing loop, not by the body).

nodes.name: IfElseStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for IF, ELSEIF and ELSE. It alternates between a Condition state, evaluating each condition statement in turn, and a Body state, iterating the body of the first condition that is true (or the ELSE body); it supports interruption by exception handlers.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the IF state machine: evaluates the current condition with evaluateBooleanCondition, moves to the next ELSEIF or ELSE clause when false, and in the Body state returns statements of the selected body; returns an injected LEAVE statement as is.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the initial Condition state, the first condition and clause index, clears the interrupted flag and resets all conditions and bodies.

nodes.name: WhileStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for WHILE. It alternates between evaluating the condition and iterating the body, resets the body at each new iteration, handles LEAVE and ITERATE statements matching its label, and returns a NoOpStatementExec when the last body statement was interrupted by a CONTINUE handler.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the WHILE state machine: in the Condition state evaluates the condition and enters the body when true; in the Body state returns body statements, reacts to unmatched LEAVE or ITERATE statements, and goes back to the condition when the body is exhausted.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the Condition state and current pointer, clears the interrupted flag and resets the condition and the body.

nodes.name: handleLeaveStatement
nodes.summary: Marks a LEAVE statement as matched when its label equals the label of this loop, and stops the loop by clearing the current pointer.

nodes.name: SearchedCaseStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for a searched CASE statement (CASE WHEN condition THEN ...). It evaluates the WHEN conditions in order, then iterates the body of the first true condition, or the ELSE body when none match.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the searched CASE state machine: evaluates each WHEN condition with evaluateBooleanCondition, moves on to the next WHEN or the ELSE body, and iterates the selected body.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the Condition state, first condition and clause index, clears the interrupted flag and resets all conditions and bodies.

nodes.name: SimpleCaseStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for a simple CASE statement (CASE variable WHEN value THEN ...). It evaluates the case variable once and caches it as a literal, builds internal condition statements comparing the literal with each WHEN expression (an EqualTo projection), and iterates the body of the first match or the ELSE body.

nodes.name: validateCache
nodes.summary: Lazily evaluates the case variable statement, stores its first value as a Literal and builds the condition/body iterator; sets hasStartedCaseVariableEvaluation around the evaluation so a CONTINUE handler can detect a failure there.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the simple CASE state machine: in the Condition state takes the next (condition, body) pair, evaluates the condition and switches to Body on a match, falling back to the ELSE body; in the Body state returns statements of the chosen body.

nodes.name: createConditionBodyIterator
nodes.summary: Zips WHEN expressions with their bodies and, for each, builds an internal SingleStatementExec whose plan is a Project of an EqualTo between the cached case literal and the expression, with a synthetic Origin text so error messages read like (1 = 5).

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the Condition state, drops the cached case variable and body, clears the interrupted and evaluation flags and resets the case variable statement, bodies and ELSE body.

nodes.name: evaluateBooleanCondition
nodes.summary: Evaluates a condition statement: marks the SingleStatementExec as executed, builds its DataFrame and requires one column of boolean type; returns the single value (NULL gives false) or raises an internal error for more than one row or invalidBooleanStatement for a non-boolean result.

nodes.name: getText
nodes.summary: Returns the SQL text of this statement by slicing the Origin sqlText between startIndex and stopIndex.

nodes.name: buildDataFrame
nodes.summary: Builds a DataFrame from the (parameterized) logical plan of this statement with Dataset.ofRows on the given session.

nodes.name: LeaveStatementExec
nodes.summary: Leaf node for the LEAVE statement. Its label names the compound or loop to leave, and the hasBeenMatched flag is set once a surrounding compound or loop with that label has been found, so the upward propagation can stop.

nodes.name: IterateStatementExec
nodes.summary: Leaf node for the ITERATE statement. Its label names the loop to continue, and the hasBeenMatched flag is set once the surrounding loop with that label has been found.

nodes.name: RepeatStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for REPEAT ... UNTIL. It starts with the body state, then evaluates the condition and repeats the body while the condition is false; it handles LEAVE and ITERATE statements for its label and returns a NoOpStatementExec when the body was interrupted at its last statement.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the REPEAT state machine: in the Condition state evaluates the UNTIL condition (resetting the body when it is false); in the Body state returns body statements, reacts to unmatched LEAVE or ITERATE statements and switches to the condition when the body is exhausted.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the Body state and current pointer, clears the interrupted flag and resets the body and the condition.

nodes.name: handleLeaveStatement
nodes.summary: Marks a LEAVE statement as matched when its label equals the label of this loop, and stops the loop by clearing the current pointer.

nodes.name: LoopStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for the unconditional LOOP statement. It keeps iterating its body, restarting it after each pass or after an ITERATE statement, and stops only when a LEAVE statement is returned by the body.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator for LOOP: resets the body when it is exhausted or was iterated, returns the next body statement, and sets the interrupted or iterated flag (and marks the statement matched) when an unmatched LEAVE or ITERATE with this loop's label is seen.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears the interrupted and iterated flags and resets the body.

nodes.name: ForStatementExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for FOR over a query result. It collects the query result as a local iterator, and for every row builds a labeled scope body that first declares and sets one variable per column (as internal DECLARE and SET statements) and then runs the user statements, followed by a NoOp so variables are dropped only after the last statement; it handles LEAVE, ITERATE and CONTINUE/EXIT handler interruption.

nodes.name: cachedQueryResult
nodes.summary: Runs the FOR query once, caching the local row iterator and a map of column names to data types; sets hasStartedQueryEvaluation around the run so a CONTINUE handler can detect a failure in the query.

nodes.name: treeIterator
nodes.summary: Lazy iterator implementing the FOR state machine: in VariableAssignment takes the next row, builds the declare and set variable statements and a scoped CompoundBodyExec, then in Body returns its statements while handling unmatched LEAVE and ITERATE, exiting the scope when the body ends; returns a NoOp when the result set is empty.

nodes.name: handleLeaveStatement
nodes.summary: Marks a LEAVE statement as matched when its label equals the FOR label, interrupts the loop and exits the scope of the current body.

nodes.name: createExpressionFromValue
nodes.summary: Recursively turns a Scala value from a result row into a Catalyst expression: maps become CreateMap, rows become CreateNamedStruct, sequences become CreateArray, and anything else a Literal.

nodes.name: createDeclareVarExec
nodes.summary: Builds an internal SingleStatementExec containing a CreateVariable (DECLARE with a NULL default of the column's type) for a FOR column.

nodes.name: createSetVarExec
nodes.summary: Builds an internal SingleStatementExec containing a SetVariable that assigns the current row value, through a one-row Project, to the FOR column variable.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Restores the VariableAssignment state, invalidates the cached query result, clears the interrupted flag, current pointer and body, and marks the next row as the first iteration.

nodes.name: ExceptionHandlerExec
nodes.summary: Executable node for a DECLARE HANDLER. It wraps the handler body (a CompoundBodyExec), the handler type (EXIT or CONTINUE) and the label of the scope where it was defined, and delegates its tree iterator and reset to the body.

nodes.name: PartitionKeyedAccumulator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PartitionKeyedAccumulator, an AccumulatorV2 that records one value per partition id with last-write-wins merging, so each partition contributes exactly once even when tasks run more than once (duplicate or speculative computes). Callers read the de-duplicated result through accumulatedNumPartitions and foldValues.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala generic class backed by a Java ConcurrentHashMap instead of explicit locking.

nodes.name: PartitionKeyedAccumulator
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2 keyed by partition id (input (Int, T), output java.util.Map[Int, T]). add puts the value for a partition and merge uses putAll, so a later value replaces an earlier one; copy, copyAndReset, reset and isZero manage the backing ConcurrentHashMap; value returns an unmodifiable view; accumulatedNumPartitions counts recorded partitions and foldValues folds the values, counting each partition once. add is expected once per task, and values from failed tasks are dropped by the accumulator framework.

nodes.name: copy
nodes.summary: Creates a new accumulator and copies all current partition entries into it.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Records the value for a partition id, replacing any earlier value for the same id.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another PartitionKeyedAccumulator by putAll (last-write-wins per partition id), and throws UnsupportedOperationException for any other accumulator type.

nodes.name: foldValues
nodes.summary: Folds all per-partition values with the given operator and zero, so each recorded partition is counted once.

nodes.name: RecordBinaryComparator.java
nodes.summary: Defines RecordBinaryComparator, a RecordComparator that compares two records byte by byte as unsigned bytes, using 8-byte word comparisons when memory alignment allows it.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class using Platform for raw memory reads and Long.reverseBytes on little-endian machines so word comparison matches byte order.

nodes.name: RecordBinaryComparator
nodes.summary: Final RecordComparator that compares record bytes in memory. A shorter record is smaller; for equal lengths it aligns offsets when unaligned access is unsupported, compares 8 bytes at a time (reversing bytes on little-endian), then finishes the remaining bytes one by one.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares two records given as (object, offset, length) triples: length difference first, then aligned prefix bytes, then 8-byte words compared as unsigned values, then the tail bytes; returns 0 when equal.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalRowSorter.java
nodes.summary: Defines UnsafeExternalRowSorter, which sorts UnsafeRows with an UnsafeExternalSorter (spilling to disk when needed), together with its nested PrefixComputer, Prefix and RowComparator helpers. It is used where rows of a given schema must be sorted by an ordering and a sort prefix.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class that returns a Scala Iterator by wrapping an anonymous RowIterator, and rethrows IOException through Platform.throwException.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalRowSorter
nodes.summary: Sorts rows by inserting each UnsafeRow with its computed key prefix into an UnsafeExternalSorter and returning a sorted iterator. It is created by create (with an Ordering) or createWithRecordComparator (with a comparator supplier), reads memory and spill settings from SparkEnv config, exposes peak memory and sort time, forces spills in tests through setTestSpillFrequency, and frees its resources once the sorted iterator is exhausted.

nodes.name: PrefixComputer
nodes.summary: Abstract nested class whose computePrefix(InternalRow) returns a Prefix (a long value and an isNull flag) for the given row; the returned object may be reused across calls.

nodes.name: Prefix
nodes.summary: Mutable holder of a key prefix: a long value, or the null prefix value when isNull is true.

nodes.name: RowComparator
nodes.summary: Private RecordComparator that points two reusable UnsafeRows at the compared records and delegates to a Scala Ordering of InternalRow.

nodes.name: createWithRecordComparator
nodes.summary: Static factory that builds a sorter from a schema, a RecordComparator supplier, a PrefixComparator, a PrefixComputer, a page size and a radix-sort flag.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Static factory that builds a sorter from a schema and an Ordering of InternalRow by wrapping the ordering in a RowComparator supplier.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalRowSorter
nodes.summary: Private constructor: gets SparkEnv and TaskContext and creates the underlying UnsafeExternalSorter using the task memory manager, block manager, serializer manager and shuffle sort and spill threshold configuration values.

nodes.name: setTestSpillFrequency
nodes.summary: Test-only hook (VisibleForTesting) that makes the sorter spill every given number of inserted rows; asserts the frequency is positive.

nodes.name: insertRow
nodes.summary: Computes the prefix of an UnsafeRow, inserts the row bytes and prefix into the underlying sorter, counts the row and spills when the test spill frequency is reached.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Marks the sorter as released and frees the underlying sorter's memory and spill files.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Gets the sorted iterator from the underlying sorter (cleaning up at once when it is empty) and returns it as a Scala Iterator[InternalRow] through an anonymous RowIterator; it copies the last row and cleans up when the iterator ends. An overload sort(Iterator[UnsafeRow]) at lines 227-232 inserts all input rows first and then calls sort().

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Points two reusable UnsafeRows at the two records (length 0 is enough for ordering) and returns the Ordering comparison result.

nodes.name: UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap.java
nodes.summary: Defines UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap, an unsafe hash map used for aggregation when the aggregation buffers are fixed-width: grouping keys and aggregation buffers are stored as UnsafeRows in a BytesToBytesMap. It can fall back to an UnsafeKVExternalSorter when memory runs out.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class that reuses a single UnsafeRow for the aggregation buffer and returns an anonymous KVIterator over the map's destructive iterator.

nodes.name: UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap
nodes.summary: Hash map from grouping key to aggregation buffer, supporting up to 2 billion keys. getAggregationBuffer encodes the key with an UnsafeProjection and returns the (reused) buffer row for that key, inserting a copy of the empty buffer on first sight (null when memory cannot be allocated); iterator gives a destructive key-value iterator; free is idempotent and is registered as a task completion listener; destructAndCreateExternalSorter sorts and spills the map into an UnsafeKVExternalSorter.

nodes.name: supportsAggregationBufferSchema
nodes.summary: Static check telling whether the map can handle aggregation buffers of a given schema, by asking Aggregate.isAggregateBufferMutable.

nodes.name: UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap
nodes.summary: Constructor: builds the grouping key projection, the reusable buffer row and the BytesToBytesMap, serializes the empty aggregation buffer, and registers a task completion listener that frees the map.

nodes.name: getAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Projects a grouping InternalRow to an UnsafeRow key and returns the aggregation buffer for it; the same row object is returned on every call.

nodes.name: getAggregationBufferFromUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Looks up the key in the map (with a given hash); if absent appends the key with a copy of the empty aggregation buffer, returning null when the append fails; then points the shared buffer row at the stored value. An overload at lines 121-123 computes the hash from the key.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns a KVIterator over the keys and values using the destructive iterator of the map (no other method may be called afterwards); the same key and value rows are reused for each call.

nodes.name: free
nodes.summary: Frees the memory of the underlying BytesToBytesMap; idempotent.

nodes.name: destructAndCreateExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsafeKVExternalSorter that takes over the records of this map (sorting them in place and spilling), using the key and buffer schemas and the spill thresholds from SparkEnv config; the map is reset and the returned sorter cannot take new records.

nodes.name: UnsafeKVExternalSorter.java
nodes.summary: Defines UnsafeKVExternalSorter, an external sorter for key-value records where both key and value are UnsafeRows, with nested KVComparator and KVSorterIterator classes. It can also sort the records of a BytesToBytesMap in place, reusing the map's pointer array.
nodes.languageNotes: Java final class; the constructor has two overloads, and the long one switches between creating a fresh UnsafeExternalSorter and wrapping an existing BytesToBytesMap.

nodes.name: UnsafeKVExternalSorter
nodes.summary: External sorter over (key, value) UnsafeRow records ordered by key. insertKV adds a record with its key prefix, merge absorbs another sorter, sortedIterator returns a KVSorterIterator (the caller must clean up), and getSpillSize, getPeakMemoryUsedBytes, closeCurrentPage and cleanupResources expose memory control. With a BytesToBytesMap passed to the constructor it sorts the map's records in place, borrowing the map's pointer array, and then resets the map.

nodes.name: KVComparator
nodes.summary: Private RecordComparator that skips the leading key-length field of two records, points two reusable UnsafeRows at the keys and compares them with a BaseOrdering.

nodes.name: KVSorterIterator
nodes.summary: KVIterator over the sorted records: next() loads the next record, splits it into key and value UnsafeRows using the stored key length, and cleans up resources when the input ends or fails; close() also cleans up.

nodes.name: UnsafeKVExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Main constructor: builds the prefix computer, prefix comparator and key ordering from the key schema, enables radix sort for a single prefix-sortable key, and either creates a new UnsafeExternalSorter (no map) or inserts every map entry into an UnsafeInMemorySorter backed by the map's pointer array and wraps it in a sorter created with createWithExistingInMemorySorter, then resets the map. A 7-argument overload at lines 57-67 passes a null map.

nodes.name: insertKV
nodes.summary: Computes the key prefix and inserts the key and value rows as one record into the underlying sorter, which spills when memory runs out.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another UnsafeKVExternalSorter into this one by merging the underlying sorters; the other one is emptied.

nodes.name: sortedIterator
nodes.summary: Gets the sorted iterator of the underlying sorter, cleaning up at once if it is empty or on IOException, and wraps it in a KVSorterIterator.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Frees the in-memory structures and spill files of the underlying sorter.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares two records by their key rows, offsetting each record by the aligned-offset size that holds the key length.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances to the next sorted record: loads it, reads the key length, and points the key and value rows at their parts; on end of input sets both rows to null and cleans up, and on IOException cleans up and rethrows.

nodes.name: BufferedRowIterator.java
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract BufferedRowIterator, the iterator interface that generated code for multiple operators (whole stage codegen) implements to hand output rows to the caller. It buffers produced rows in a list and leaves init and processNext to the generated subclass.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract Java class whose public append, shouldStop and incPeakExecutionMemory are public so inner classes of generated code can call them (SPARK-23598).

nodes.name: BufferedRowIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract base for generated row iterators. hasNext calls processNext when the buffer is empty, next removes the head row, append adds a row, shouldStop says whether the generated loop should exit (when a row is buffered), durationMs reports the time since creation, incPeakExecutionMemory adds to the task's peak execution memory, and init and processNext are implemented by generated code.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Calls processNext when no row is buffered and returns whether the buffer now holds a row.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the first buffered row.

nodes.name: durationMs
nodes.summary: Returns the milliseconds elapsed since this object was created, a measure of how long the pipeline has run.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Abstract method that initializes the generated iterator from the partition index and an array of input iterators of InternalRow.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Appends an output row to the buffer of current rows.

nodes.name: shouldStop
nodes.summary: Returns true when a row is buffered, telling the generated processNext loop to exit.

nodes.name: incPeakExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Increases the peak execution memory metric of the current task by the given size.

nodes.name: processNext
nodes.summary: Abstract method implemented by generated code: processes input until at least one output row is buffered, or no more rows are left.

nodes.name: CursorState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the lifecycle states of a SQL scripting cursor: CursorDeclared, CursorOpened, CursorFetching and CursorClosed, as a sealed trait with case objects and case classes. The opened and fetching states hold the result iterator created at OPEN time and its output attributes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait ADT; the transitions are documented as Declared -> Opened -> Fetching -> Closed.

nodes.name: CursorState
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the cursor lifecycle: Declared, Opened, Fetching and Closed.

nodes.name: CursorDeclared
nodes.summary: Case object for a cursor that was declared but not yet opened; the query is not parsed or analyzed until OPEN.

nodes.name: CursorOpened
nodes.summary: Case class for an opened cursor: holds the result Iterator[InternalRow] created at OPEN time, so the data snapshot is fixed then, and the output attributes used for type checking in FETCH.

nodes.name: CursorFetching
nodes.summary: Case class for a cursor being fetched from: same fields as CursorOpened (result iterator and output schema), marking that fetching has begun.

nodes.name: CursorClosed
nodes.summary: Case object for a cursor that was closed and has released its resources.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingContextManagerImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SqlScriptingContextManagerImpl, the implementation of SqlScriptingContextManager backed by a SqlScriptingExecutionContext and a SqlScriptingLocalVariableManager.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingContextManagerImpl
nodes.summary: Implements SqlScriptingContextManager for a given SqlScriptingExecutionContext: getContext returns that context and getVariableManager returns a SqlScriptingLocalVariableManager built from it.

nodes.name: DisableUnnecessaryBucketedScan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a physical-plan rule that turns off bucketed scans of file-source tables when the bucketing gives no benefit to the rest of the plan. It is meant to run right after EnsureRequirements, once the shuffles and sorts have been added.

nodes.name: DisableUnnecessaryBucketedScan
nodes.summary: Rule over SparkPlan that, when bucketing and automatic bucketed scan are both enabled in the conf and the plan contains a bucketed FileSourceScanExec, walks the plan and replaces such a scan by a copy with disableBucketedScan = true. A bucketed scan is kept only if an operator that needs a clustered or all-tuples distribution sits above it and no Exchange sits between them with only allowed unary operators (Sort, Project, Filter, partial aggregate) in the path. The doc comment gives join and aggregate examples.

nodes.name: disableBucketWithInterestingPartition
nodes.summary: Pre-order traversal that carries three flags (interesting partition seen, Exchange seen, only allowed nodes seen). It resets the flags at operators with an interesting partition, sets the Exchange flag at an Exchange, and at a bucketed FileSourceScanExec returns a non-bucketed copy (keeping the logical link) when no interesting partition exists or an Exchange and only allowed nodes lie in between.

nodes.name: hasInterestingPartition
nodes.summary: Returns true when any required child distribution of the plan is a ClusteredDistribution or AllTuples.

nodes.name: isAllowedUnaryExecNode
nodes.summary: Tells whether an operator may sit between a bucketed scan and an operator with interesting partition: SortExec, ProjectExec, FilterExec, or an aggregate without required child distribution expressions (a partial aggregate).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: returns the plan unchanged unless bucketing and auto bucketed scan are enabled and a bucketed scan exists, otherwise starts the traversal with flags false, false, true.

nodes.name: PartitionPruning.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical optimizer rule that inserts dynamic partition pruning predicates on one side of a join using the filter found on the other side. The decision uses the join type, a selective filter and a cost estimate.

nodes.name: PartitionPruning
nodes.summary: Rule over LogicalPlan (with PredicateHelper and JoinSelectionHelper) that implements dynamic partition pruning. For each equi-join it looks for a filterable partitioned scan (v1 file relation, Hive table relation or a v2 scan with runtime filtering) on one side, requires a selective, non-streaming filter on the other side, and wraps the pruned side in a Filter holding a DynamicPruningSubquery. The subquery is kept when exchange reuse is enabled or the estimated benefit (from column statistics or the fallback filter ratio config) exceeds the cost of the extra scan. Correlated subqueries and the case where the conf disables the feature are left untouched.

nodes.name: getFilterableTableScan
nodes.summary: Tracks an expression down a plan to its source and returns the relation when it is a HadoopFsRelation whose partition columns cover the expression, a HiveTableRelation partitioned on it, or a v2 scan supporting runtime filtering on that attribute.

nodes.name: insertPredicate
nodes.summary: Wraps the pruning plan in a Filter with a DynamicPruningSubquery over the filtering plan (requires a single broadcast key), flagged reuse-broadcast-only when there is no benefit; returns the plan unchanged if neither exchange reuse nor benefit holds.

nodes.name: pruningHasBenefit
nodes.summary: Estimates whether pruning is worth it: derives a filter ratio from distinct counts of the join attributes (if statistics are enabled and available) or the fallback ratio, and compares the estimated pruned-side size to the overhead of the other plan.

nodes.name: calculatePlanOverhead
nodes.summary: Heuristic overhead of a plan: the summed size in bytes of non-cached leaves plus a weighted size of cached InMemoryRelation leaves depending on their storage level (full size for disk only, 0.2 of it for memory and disk, zero for memory only).

nodes.name: hasSelectivePredicate
nodes.summary: Checks whether any Filter in the plan has a condition that is likely selective.

nodes.name: hasPartitionPruningFilter
nodes.summary: Requires the filtering side to be non-streaming and to contain a selective predicate.

nodes.name: prune
nodes.summary: Transforms the plan bottom-up: for each join with a condition (and no existing DPP filter on either side), splits the conjunctive predicates, finds EqualTo predicates whose operands come from different sides, and inserts the pruning predicate on the left or right side when the scan, join type and filter conditions allow it.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: skips correlated subqueries and returns the plan unchanged when dynamic partition pruning is disabled, otherwise calls prune.

nodes.name: PlanDynamicPruningFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical planning rule that rewrites DynamicPruningSubquery expressions into executable pruning expressions. It reuses broadcast results when the join is a broadcast hash join and falls back to a duplicated subquery otherwise.

nodes.name: PlanDynamicPruningFilters
nodes.summary: Case class rule over SparkPlan, built from a SparkSession, that does nothing when dynamic partition pruning is disabled. Otherwise it replaces each DynamicPruningSubquery by a DynamicPruningExpression: an InSubqueryExec over a SubqueryBroadcastExec on a new BroadcastExchangeExec when the plan holds a BroadcastHashJoinExec whose build side has the same result, a true literal when pruning is only worthwhile in a broadcast, and otherwise an InSubqueryExec over a SubqueryExec of an aggregate on the build plan.

nodes.name: broadcastMode
nodes.summary: Builds the HashedRelationBroadcastMode for the given keys by rewriting them with HashJoin.rewriteKeyExpr and binding them to the output attributes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: transforms every expression containing the DYNAMIC_PRUNING_SUBQUERY pattern, choosing between reusing the broadcast exchange, a literal true, or a separate subquery, as described on the class.

nodes.name: CleanupDynamicPruningFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a logical rule that removes dynamic pruning filters that were not pushed down to a scan, and removes useless ones on scans.

nodes.name: CleanupDynamicPruningFilters
nodes.summary: Rule over LogicalPlan (with PredicateHelper) that is a no-op when dynamic partition pruning is disabled or the tree has no dynamic pruning. For filters directly above a HadoopFsRelation, HiveTableRelation or DataSourceV2ScanRelation it drops DynamicPruningSubquery conditions that have no references or whose key already has an equality condition; for other Filter nodes it replaces any DynamicPruning condition by true.

nodes.name: collectEqualityConditionExpressions
nodes.summary: Collects the non-constant side of EqualTo and EqualNullSafe predicates in a condition when the other side is foldable and the collected side is deterministic.

nodes.name: removeUnnecessaryDynamicPruningSubquery
nodes.summary: Rewrites each Filter in a plan so that DynamicPruningSubquery conditions on keys with no references, or keys already constrained by an equality condition, become a true literal.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: matches deterministic project and filter nodes over file, Hive or v2 scan relations to call removeUnnecessaryDynamicPruningSubquery, and turns DynamicPruning conditions of any other Filter into true.

nodes.name: RowLevelOperationRuntimeGroupFiltering.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a rule that injects a runtime subquery to filter groups in row-level operations such as DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE when the primary scan supports runtime filtering.

nodes.name: RowLevelOperationRuntimeGroupFiltering
nodes.summary: Rule over LogicalPlan (with PredicateHelper) created with an optimizeSubqueries rule. For group-based and delta-based row-level operations whose condition is not true and whose scan supports runtime v2 filtering, it adds a dynamic pruning filter (an InSubquery over an aggregate of the matching rows) on the scan so the data source knows which groups have changes. It is gated by the runtime row-level operation group filter conf.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point: transforms group-based and delta-based row-level operations that qualify and calls injectGroupFilters.

nodes.name: canInjectGroupFilters
nodes.summary: Returns true when the conf is enabled, the condition is not a true literal and the scan has filter attributes.

nodes.name: injectGroupFilters
nodes.summary: Finds the scan relation by reference equality in the write query, builds the matching-rows plan on the original table, resolves build and pruning keys, wraps the scan in a Filter with the dynamic pruning condition, and runs optimizeSubqueries on the new query.

nodes.name: buildMatchingRowsPlan
nodes.summary: Builds the plan that selects rows matching the operation condition: a Filter for DELETE, a Filter with attributes remapped to scan attributes for UPDATE, and a Filter rewritten by RewritePredicateSubquery for MERGE; the relation is then cloned with new expression ids.

nodes.name: buildDynamicPruningCond
nodes.summary: Builds a DynamicPruningExpression holding an InSubquery with the pruning keys over a ListQuery of an Aggregate on the build keys.

nodes.name: buildTableToScanAttrMap
nodes.summary: Maps table attributes to scan attributes by name using the conf resolver and throws an AnalysisException when a table attribute has no match.

nodes.name: ReuseExchangeAndSubquery.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a physical-plan rule that finds duplicated exchanges and subqueries and makes all references share one instance.

nodes.name: ReuseExchangeAndSubquery
nodes.summary: Case object Rule over SparkPlan. When exchange reuse or subquery reuse is enabled in the conf, it rewrites bottom-up in one pass over the plan and its subquery plans, keeping maps from canonicalized plans to the first Exchange or BaseSubqueryExec; later duplicates become ReusedExchangeExec or ReusedSubqueryExec. The doc comment notes the plan is a mutually recursive structure of plans, expressions and subqueries.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point containing the local recursive reuse function: replaces duplicate exchanges by ReusedExchangeExec and duplicate ExecSubqueryExpression plans by ReusedSubqueryExec, looking up canonicalized plans in mutable maps.

nodes.name: StatFunctions.scala
nodes.summary: Holds statistics helpers for DataFrames: approximate quantiles, Pearson correlation, covariance, cross tabulation and summary statistics.

nodes.name: StatFunctions
nodes.summary: Object (with Logging) of statistical computations built on DataFrame operations. It provides multipleApproxQuantiles (a Greenwald-Khanna style error bound, computed with approx_percentile over exploded columns), pearsonCorrelation and calculateCorrImpl, calculateCov and calculateCovImpl, crossTabulate (group by one column and pivot the other), and summary (count, count_distinct, approx_count_distinct, mean, stddev, min, max and percentiles for numeric and string columns).

nodes.name: multipleApproxQuantiles
nodes.summary: Computes approximate quantiles for several numeric columns in one pass by exploding the columns into (index, value) rows, dropping null and NaN, and applying approx_percentile with an accuracy derived from the relative error.

nodes.name: pearsonCorrelation
nodes.summary: Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of two columns as a Double, via calculateCorrImpl.

nodes.name: calculateCorrImpl
nodes.summary: Validates that exactly two numeric columns are given and the method is pearson, then selects the corr aggregate (NaN when null) as a one-column DataFrame named corr.

nodes.name: calculateCov
nodes.summary: Returns the sample covariance of two numeric columns as a Double, via calculateCovImpl.

nodes.name: calculateCovImpl
nodes.summary: Validates two numeric columns and selects covar_samp (0.0 when null) as a one-column DataFrame named cov.

nodes.name: crossTabulate
nodes.summary: Builds a frequency table of two columns by grouping on the first (nulls as "null"), pivoting on the second, counting, and filling nulls with 0.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Builds the summary DataFrame for the selected statistics (default count, mean, stddev, min, 25%, 50%, 75%, max) over numeric and string columns, parsing percentage names, building a map column per field, and exploding it into one row per statistic; unknown names raise an error.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryPlanTraverseHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Utility object with a plan traversal used in several places of streaming query code.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryPlanTraverseHelper
nodes.summary: Object (with Logging) holding collectFromUnfoldedPlan, which walks an executed SparkPlan and collects values using a partial function while looking inside InMemoryTableScanExec (cached plan), AdaptiveSparkPlanExec (its executed plan, with a warning when it is not final) and QueryStageExec nodes.

nodes.name: collectFromUnfoldedPlan
nodes.summary: Recursively flat-maps the executed plan, unfolding cached, adaptive and query-stage nodes to their underlying plans and applying the partial function where it is defined.

nodes.name: FileStreamSink.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the file-based streaming sink and its companion helpers for the metadata directory that records which output files are valid.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object and the class share one class id; the node range covers the object (39-119) and the class (128-193).

nodes.name: FileStreamSink
nodes.summary: Companion pair. The object defines the metadata directory name _spark_metadata and helpers hasMetadata, getMetadataLogPath, checkEscapedMetadataPath and ancestorIsMetadataDirectory. The class (lines 121-193) is a Sink that writes each micro-batch to its own set of files with FileFormatWriter and a commit protocol, records them in a FileStreamSinkLog, skips batches already committed, and requires an absolute path.
nodes.languageNotes: Object (39-119) and class (128-193) share this node.

nodes.name: hasMetadata
nodes.summary: Returns true when the given paths consist of a single directory that has a metadata log; false if the conf ignores sink metadata, on other path shapes, or on non-Spark errors (logged as a warning).

nodes.name: getMetadataLogPath
nodes.summary: Returns the _spark_metadata path under a base path after running the escaped-path check.

nodes.name: checkEscapedMetadataPath
nodes.summary: When the escaped-path check conf is on and the path has special characters, throws an error if a legacy (unescaped) metadata path exists; access errors are logged and ignored.

nodes.name: ancestorIsMetadataDirectory
nodes.summary: Returns true when the qualified path or any of its ancestors is the metadata directory.

nodes.name: basicWriteJobStatsTracker
nodes.summary: Creates a BasicWriteJobStatsTracker from the serializable Hadoop conf.

nodes.name: addBatch
nodes.summary: Writes one batch: skips it if its id is not greater than the latest logged batch; otherwise instantiates the commit protocol, sets up manifest options when it is a ManifestFileCommitProtocol, resolves partition columns by name, and calls FileFormatWriter.write.

nodes.name: ArrowRRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowRRunner, the runner that sends Spark rows to an R worker and reads results back as columnar batches, using Arrow stream format over the worker socket.

nodes.name: ArrowRRunner
nodes.summary: Extends BaseRRunner (input: iterators of InternalRow, output: ColumnarBatch) to run an R function with the 'arrow' serialization on both sides. Its writer thread converts each input row iterator into Arrow record batches with ArrowWriter and an ArrowStreamWriter, buffers the whole Arrow stream in memory and writes it with a length prefix. Its reader iterator reads a length-prefixed Arrow stream from the worker, wraps the vectors in ArrowColumnVector and ColumnarBatch, handles the TIMING_DATA record (logs boot, init, broadcast, input, compute, output times) and ends on a zero length. The comments say it is similar to ArrowPythonRunner and that the whole stream is sent at once because the R side cannot read batch by batch (ARROW-4512).

nodes.name: bufferedWrite
nodes.summary: Runs the given write function against an in-memory ByteArrayOutputStream, then writes the byte count followed by the bytes to the worker's output stream, so the whole Arrow stream is sent in one block.

nodes.name: newWriterThread
nodes.summary: Creates the WriterThread whose writeIteratorToStream builds the Arrow schema from the StructType, allocates a child allocator and VectorSchemaRoot, then for each input row iterator writes rows with ArrowWriter and emits one Arrow batch, finishing with the end marker. The root and allocator are closed in a finally block rather than in a task completion listener. Used by BaseRRunner when it starts the thread feeding the R worker.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Creates the ReaderIterator that reads the R worker's output: it loads Arrow batches into a ColumnarBatch, logs the timing record sent by the worker, reads a new Arrow stream when a positive length arrives, and marks end of stream on a zero length. It registers a task completion listener that closes the reader and allocator, and wraps errors with handleException.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsRWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapPartitionsRWrapper, a serializable function wrapper that applies an R function to one partition of rows through an RRunner.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsRWrapper
nodes.summary: Case class that is an Iterator[Any] => Iterator[Any] function, holding the serialized R function, package names, broadcast variables and input and output StructTypes. Its apply method checks whether the input schema is the serialized R data schema, converts rows to R bytes (rowToRBytes) or passes the raw bytes, picks ROW or BYTE serialization formats for input and output, runs an RRunner in DATAFRAME_DAPPLY mode via compute, and converts result bytes back to Rows (bytesToRow) or wraps raw bytes in a Row. It is used to run an R function over each partition of a Dataset.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds the R runner for the partition, feeds it the (possibly serialized) rows with partition index -1 (the code notes Dataset has no mapPartitionsWithIndex), and maps output bytes back to Rows according to the output schema.

nodes.name: SQLEventFilterBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Event-log filtering for live SQL executions: SQLEventFilterBuilder tracks live executions with their jobs, stages, tasks and RDDs, and SQLLiveEntitiesEventFilter accepts only events that belong to them.

nodes.name: SQLEventFilterBuilder
nodes.summary: SparkListener and EventFilterBuilder that follows SQL execution start and end events, job starts (using the SQL execution id job property), stage submissions and task starts, keeping maps from live execution to jobs, jobs to stages, stages to tasks and stages to RDDs. On execution end it drops the related jobs, stages, tasks and RDDs. createFilter returns an SQLLiveEntitiesEventFilter built from the live sets (helper accessors liveSQLExecutions, liveJobs, liveStages, liveTasks, liveRDDs). It only tracks jobs relevant to SQL executions.

nodes.name: onJobStart
nodes.summary: Reads the SQL execution id from job properties, ignores jobs without one, and records the job under its execution plus the job's stage ids.

nodes.name: onStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: For stages known to belong to SQL jobs, records the stage's RDD ids and prepares an empty task set.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Adds the started task id to the task set of its stage if the stage is tracked.

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: Dispatches SQL execution start and end events to the handlers and ignores other events.

nodes.name: onExecutionStart
nodes.summary: Registers a new live SQL execution with an empty job set.

nodes.name: onExecutionEnd
nodes.summary: Removes the execution and drops its jobs, stages, tasks and RDDs from the tracking maps.

nodes.name: createFilter
nodes.summary: Creates an SQLLiveEntitiesEventFilter from the currently tracked live executions, jobs, stages, tasks and RDDs.

nodes.name: SQLLiveEntitiesEventFilter
nodes.summary: JobEventFilter subclass that accepts SQL execution start, adaptive update, end and driver accumulator update events only for live executions, accepts job-related events that the job filter accepts, and rejects streaming query progress events. For job events the job filter rejects, it deliberately does not match so other filters can decide.

nodes.name: acceptFn
nodes.summary: Returns the partial function that decides whether an event is accepted.

nodes.name: DebugEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DebugEvaluatorFactory, a partition evaluator factory that counts rows and records the runtime class names of values per column while passing rows through unchanged.

nodes.name: DebugEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow] constructed with a LongAccumulator for the tuple count, the number of columns, an array of SetAccumulator[String] (one per column) and the output attributes. createEvaluator returns a DebugEvaluator. The inner DebugEvaluator passes rows through while updating the accumulators.

nodes.name: DebugEvaluator
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluator whose eval wraps the input iterator: for every row it adds 1 to the tuple count accumulator and, for each non-null column value, adds the value's class name to that column's SetAccumulator, then returns the row unchanged.

nodes.name: createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Creates a new DebugEvaluator.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the first input that updates the row count and per-column class-name accumulators as rows are consumed.

nodes.name: ChecksumCheckpointFileManager.scala
nodes.summary: Checkpoint file manager that adds a CRC32C checksum file next to each checkpoint file. It contains the checksum data classes, the manager wrapper, a verifying input stream, a sequential-only checked stream and a checksum-writing output stream.

nodes.name: ChecksumFileCreatorInfo
nodes.summary: Case class with executorId and taskInfo describing who created a checksum file, kept for debugging. The companion object's apply() fills it from SparkEnv (executor id) and TaskContext (partition, attempt, stage ids) when available.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds the creator info from the current SparkEnv and TaskContext, using empty strings when they are absent.

nodes.name: Checksum
nodes.summary: Case class that is the content of a checksum file: algorithm name, checksum value (Int), main file size, timestamp in ms and the creator info. json() serializes it with a Jackson ObjectMapper (lazy mapper in the companion) and fromJson() reads it back with json4s Serialization.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes this checksum to a JSON string.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string into a Checksum.

nodes.name: ChecksumFile
nodes.summary: Case class holding the path of a checksum file; asserts the path ends with the checksum suffix, and derives the main file path (suffix removed) and the base name without extensions.

nodes.name: ChecksumCheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: CheckpointFileManager that wraps another CheckpointFileManager. createAtomic writes the main file and a '.crc' file through ChecksumCancellableFSDataOutputStream, and open returns a ChecksumFSDataInputStream that verifies the checksum on close (or the plain stream if no checksum file exists). Main and checksum file I/O run concurrently on a daemon thread pool of numThreads threads (0 means run synchronously). delete removes the checksum file first, or both concurrently when allowConcurrentDelete is set (which may leave orphan checksum files); checksum files can also be deleted directly. skipCreationIfFileMissingChecksum falls back to the underlying manager for files that exist without a checksum. list, mkdirs, exists, isLocal and createCheckpointDirectory delegate. close shuts the pool down (500 ms wait, then forced). The range includes the private[streaming] companion object with CHECKSUM_FILE_SUFFIX (".crc"), DEFAULT_THREAD_POOL_SIZE (4), awaitResult, getChecksumPath and isChecksumFile.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object shares the class id. Overloaded list(path) and list(path, filter) share one function node; trivial delegating methods (exists, isLocal) have no nodes.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Delegates listing to the underlying file manager; the overload without a filter (lines 183-185) does the same.

nodes.name: mkdirs
nodes.summary: Delegates directory creation to the underlying file manager.

nodes.name: shouldSkipChecksumCreation
nodes.summary: True when the skip option is on and the file exists but has no checksum file.

nodes.name: createAtomic
nodes.summary: Creates an atomic output stream: either from the underlying manager directly (skip case) or with a checksum file.

nodes.name: createWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Creates the main and checksum streams concurrently with the given create function and wraps them in a ChecksumCancellableFSDataOutputStream.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Opens the main file and its checksum file concurrently; returns a ChecksumFSDataInputStream, or just the main stream (with a warning) if no checksum file is found.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a checksum file directly, or deletes the checksum file and main file (concurrently or in order depending on allowConcurrentDelete).

nodes.name: deleteChecksumFile
nodes.summary: Deletes a checksum path through the underlying manager and logs it.

nodes.name: createCheckpointDirectory
nodes.summary: Delegates creation of the checkpoint directory.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Shuts down the thread pool, waiting 500 ms, then forcing shutdown and logging if it does not terminate.

nodes.name: awaitResult
nodes.summary: Waits for a future via ThreadUtils.awaitResult and unwraps the original cause from the wrapping SparkException.

nodes.name: getChecksumPath
nodes.summary: Returns the main file path plus the '.crc' suffix.

nodes.name: isChecksumFile
nodes.summary: True if the path name ends with the checksum suffix.

nodes.name: ChecksumFSDataInputStream
nodes.summary: FSDataInputStream that reads the main file through a CheckedSequentialInputStream (computing CRC32C incrementally) and, on close, reads the rest of the file, loads the expected Checksum from the checksum stream, and throws QueryExecutionErrors.checkpointFileChecksumVerificationFailed if the checksum or file size differs. closeWithoutChecksumVerification skips verification; both close paths close the main and checksum streams concurrently.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Verifies the checksum, then closes both streams.
