nodes.name: closeWithoutChecksumVerification
nodes.summary: Closes without verification (for files opened, read and closed several times).

nodes.name: closeInternal
nodes.summary: Closes the main and checksum streams concurrently on the thread pool.

nodes.name: verifyChecksum
nodes.summary: Reads remaining bytes, parses the expected checksum JSON, compares value and file size with the computed values and throws on mismatch.

nodes.name: CheckedSequentialInputStream
nodes.summary: Private CheckedInputStream with CRC32C that also implements Seekable and PositionedReadable but throws UnsupportedOperationException for seek, getPos, seekToNewSource and positioned reads so the file is read sequentially and the checksum is correct. The seek and positioned-read methods are trivial and have no nodes.

nodes.name: ChecksumCancellableFSDataOutputStream
nodes.summary: CancellableFSDataOutputStream that writes the main file through a CheckedOutputStream (CRC32C). On close it writes the Checksum JSON (algorithm, value, size, timestamp, creator info) to the checksum stream and closes both streams concurrently; cancel cancels both streams synchronously.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Cancels the main stream and then the checksum stream synchronously (in a finally chain).

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Computes the checksum, closes the main file and writes and closes the checksum file concurrently, logging the created checksum.

nodes.name: AsyncOffsetSeqLog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AsyncOffsetSeqLog, an OffsetSeqLog variant that writes offset log entries to durable storage asynchronously on an executor service.

nodes.name: AsyncOffsetSeqLog
nodes.summary: Subclass of OffsetSeqLog used to write entries to the offset log asynchronously. addAsync caches the batch metadata (the metadata cache must be enabled) and, depending on offsetCommitIntervalMs and the last issue time from the Clock, either submits a write to the ThreadPoolExecutor and returns a CompletableFuture marking that it was persisted, or returns a completed future saying it was not persisted. Pending writes are kept in a map keyed by batch id (getAsyncOffsetWrite, removeAsyncOffsetWrite) and written batches are kept in a deque (writtenToDurableStorage). purge delegates to the parent, and pendingAsyncOffsetWrite (used in tests) returns the pending count.

nodes.name: getAsyncOffsetWrite
nodes.summary: Returns the pending async write future for a batch id, if any.

nodes.name: removeAsyncOffsetWrite
nodes.summary: Stops tracking the pending async write for a batch id.

nodes.name: addAsync
nodes.summary: Writes a new batch asynchronously, honoring the offset commit interval, and caches its metadata. Returns a future of (batchId, persisted flag); the inner write future fails via QueryExecutionErrors.concurrentStreamLogUpdate if the underlying write reports the batch was not written.

nodes.name: addNewBatchByStreamAsync
nodes.summary: Submits a runnable that writes the batch file through the serialization function unless the cache or file already has it; completes the future with true or false, or exceptionally on error.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Purges entries up to the threshold batch id by calling the parent implementation.

nodes.name: pendingAsyncOffsetWrite
nodes.summary: Returns the number of pending async offset writes (used in tests).

nodes.name: ContinuousDataSourceRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ContinuousDataSourceRDD and its partition class, the bottom RDD of a continuous processing read task that polls a shared queued reader for rows.

nodes.name: ContinuousDataSourceRDDPartition
nodes.summary: Serializable Partition holding the partition index and the InputPartition. It also has a private[continuous] mutable queueReader (ContinuousQueuedDataReader) which is initialized only on the executors on the first compute call and shared by later compute calls for that partition.

nodes.name: ContinuousDataSourceRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[InternalRow] taking a SparkContext, queue size, epoch poll interval, input partitions, schema, a ContinuousPartitionReaderFactory and custom SQL metrics. compute rejects task retries (attempt number not 0) with ContinuousTaskRetryException, creates the ContinuousQueuedDataReader for the partition on first use, and returns a NextIterator that reads rows from it, updating custom metrics every CustomMetrics.NUM_ROWS_PER_UPDATE rows and finishing when the reader returns null at the end of an epoch. Preferred locations come from the InputPartition.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Creates one ContinuousDataSourceRDDPartition per input partition.

nodes.name: castPartition
nodes.summary: Casts a Partition to ContinuousDataSourceRDDPartition or throws a SparkException flagged as a bug.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Gets or creates the shared queued reader for the partition and returns an iterator over its rows, updating custom metrics periodically and stopping when the epoch ends.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the preferred locations of the partition's InputPartition.

nodes.name: ManifestFileCommitProtocol.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ManifestFileCommitProtocol, the FileCommitProtocol that structured streaming file sinks use to commit a batch by writing a manifest entry instead of moving files.

nodes.name: ManifestFileCommitProtocol
nodes.summary: A FileCommitProtocol used in structured streaming that tracks the list of valid files in a manifest file (a FileStreamSinkLog) rather than renaming staged output. setupManifestOptions must be called first to supply the sink log and batch id. Each task records the files it writes and returns them as SinkFileStatus entries in its TaskCommitMessage. commitJob gathers all task statuses and adds them to the log under the batch id, throwing IllegalStateException when the add reports a race. abortJob and abortTask do best-effort deletion of files already written. Absolute-path temp files are not supported.

nodes.name: setupManifestOptions
nodes.summary: Stores the FileStreamSinkLog and the batch id for this job. It must be called before any other method of the protocol.

nodes.name: setupJob
nodes.summary: Checks that setupManifestOptions was called and creates the empty list of pending committed file paths for the job.

nodes.name: commitJob
nodes.summary: Flattens the SinkFileStatus entries from all task commit messages and adds them to the sink log under the batch id. It clears the pending file list first so a failed add does not cause committed files to be deleted, and throws IllegalStateException (race while writing batch) when the log add returns false.

nodes.name: abortJob
nodes.summary: Best-effort cleanup after a failed job: deletes each path in the pending commit list (existing files only) and logs a warning for any IOException before continuing with the next one.

nodes.name: onTaskCommit
nodes.summary: Called on the driver for each task commit; appends the Hadoop paths of the task's SinkFileStatus entries to the pending commit list so abortJob can delete them.

nodes.name: setupTask
nodes.summary: Creates the per-task buffer that records the files added by the task (used on executors only).

nodes.name: newTaskTempFile
nodes.summary: Builds a new output file path named part-<split>-<uuid><suffix> under the output path (and optional sub directory), remembers it in the task's added-file buffer and returns it. The UUID prevents conflicts between attempts of the same task.

nodes.name: newTaskTempFileAbsPath
nodes.summary: Always throws the addFilesWithAbsolutePathUnsupportedError error because this protocol cannot add files at absolute paths.

nodes.name: commitTask
nodes.summary: Builds a SinkFileStatus for every file the task added (using the file status read from the file system) and returns them wrapped in a TaskCommitMessage; returns an empty message when the task wrote nothing.

nodes.name: abortTask
nodes.summary: Best-effort cleanup of incomplete files: deletes every file the task had added.

nodes.name: StreamingErrors.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the StreamingErrors object, a small group of builders for the exceptions raised by streaming checkpoint and state handling.

nodes.name: StreamingErrors
nodes.summary: Object that groups error-message builders for streaming query exceptions. It builds SparkException values for checkpoint file manager load failures (CANNOT_LOAD_CHECKPOINT_FILE_MANAGER with ERROR_LOADING_CLASS or UNCATEGORIZED subclasses) and SparkRuntimeException values for a stateful operator that is missing its state directory and for a checkpoint with a missing metadata file.

nodes.name: cannotLoadCheckpointFileManagerClass
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkException with error class CANNOT_LOAD_CHECKPOINT_FILE_MANAGER.ERROR_LOADING_CLASS carrying the path, class name and the cause message.

nodes.name: cannotLoadCheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkException with error class CANNOT_LOAD_CHECKPOINT_FILE_MANAGER.UNCATEGORIZED carrying the checkpoint path and the cause.

nodes.name: statefulOperatorMissingStateDirectory
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkRuntimeException (STREAMING_STATEFUL_OPERATOR_MISSING_STATE_DIRECTORY) that lists the operator id and operator name pairs of the current batch.

nodes.name: missingMetadataFile
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkRuntimeException (STREAMING_CHECKPOINT_MISSING_METADATA_FILE) naming the checkpoint location.

nodes.name: AsyncCommitLog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AsyncCommitLog, a CommitLog variant that writes commit entries to durable storage on a thread pool and can also keep entries only in memory.

nodes.name: AsyncCommitLog
nodes.summary: Implementation of CommitLog that performs asynchronous writes to storage. It asserts the metadata cache is enabled because entries may be kept only in memory, and tracks the batches already persisted in a ConcurrentLinkedDeque (writtenToDurableStorage). addAsync submits the write to the supplied ThreadPoolExecutor and returns a CompletableFuture with the batch id, addInMemory only records the entry in the cache, and purge delegates to the parent implementation. Used when the commit log entry is not persisted synchronously for every micro batch.

nodes.name: addAsync
nodes.summary: Writes a new batch to the commit log asynchronously and returns a CompletableFuture that completes with the batch id when the write finishes (or completes exceptionally on a write error). It requires non-null metadata, serializes it through the stream-based async writer, puts the metadata in the batch cache immediately, and fails with the concurrentStreamLogUpdate error when the write reports false.

nodes.name: addInMemory
nodes.summary: Adds a batch to the commit log cache only, without persisting it to durable storage; returns false when the batch id is already cached and true otherwise. Used when not every micro batch entry is persisted.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Purges commit log entries older than thresholdBatchId by calling the parent purge.

nodes.name: addNewBatchByStreamAsync
nodes.summary: Private helper that completes with false if the batch is already cached; otherwise submits a Runnable to the executor service that checks whether the batch file exists, writes it through the supplied serialization function, records the batch in writtenToDurableStorage, and completes the future with true. Any Throwable is logged and completes the future exceptionally.

nodes.name: ContinuousExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ContinuousExecution, the StreamExecution subclass that runs a continuous processing query with epochs coordinated through an epoch coordinator, plus its companion constants.

nodes.name: ContinuousExecution
nodes.summary: StreamExecution implementation for continuous processing (trigger type ContinuousTrigger). It rewrites the analyzed plan so each DataSourceV2 streaming source is read as a ContinuousStream and the sink becomes a WriteToContinuousDataSource node (rejecting sources without CONTINUOUS_READ and sinks with distribution or ordering requirements). runActivatedStream loops runContinuous while the state returns to ACTIVE after a RECONFIGURING interruption. Each run reads the start offsets from the commit and offset logs, creates an IncrementalExecution, registers an epoch coordinator endpoint and starts an epoch update thread. addOffset and commit are called as epochs report and finish, awaitEpoch blocks until an epoch is committed, and stop/stopInNewThread terminate the query. Only one continuous source is supported. The companion object defines the local property keys START_EPOCH_KEY (__continuous_start_epoch) and EPOCH_COORDINATOR_ID_KEY (__epoch_coordinator_id).
nodes.languageNotes: The node range covers the class (lines 49-501) and its companion object (503-506).

nodes.name: logicalPlan
nodes.summary: Builds the WriteToContinuousDataSource plan from the analyzed plan: replaces every StreamingRelationV2 over a SupportsRead table with a StreamingDataSourceV2ScanRelation (error if the table does not support CONTINUOUS_READ), assigns a numbered metadata path under the checkpoint root, applies column pruning when supported, converts the scan to a ContinuousStream, records the sources, creates the write for the sink, and rejects sinks that require distribution or ordering.

nodes.name: hasDistributionRequirements
nodes.summary: Returns true when the write implements RequiresDistributionAndOrdering with a required distribution other than UnspecifiedDistribution (and no required number of partitions).

nodes.name: hasOrderingRequirements
nodes.summary: Returns true when the write implements RequiresDistributionAndOrdering and declares a non-empty required ordering.

nodes.name: runActivatedStream
nodes.summary: Main body of the query thread: repeatedly calls runContinuous while the state, after turning RECONFIGURING back into ACTIVE, is still ACTIVE, then stops the sources.

nodes.name: getStartOffsets
nodes.summary: Computes the start offsets for a run. If the commit log has a latest epoch, it loads that epoch's end offsets from the offset log (failing if missing), sets committedOffsets and sets the next epoch id to latest + 1. Otherwise it starts a new query at epoch 0 with null offsets.

nodes.name: runContinuous
nodes.summary: Performs one continuous run. It sets the latest seen offset on the sources, rewrites the plan with the start offsets, rejects current-time expressions, plans an IncrementalExecution, sets local properties for start epoch and epoch coordinator id, creates the epoch coordinator endpoint and starts a daemon thread that advances epochs on each trigger (or interrupts the query when the stream needs reconfiguration). It then executes the plan under a new SQL execution id, rethrows a recorded failure, swallows interruptions caused by reconfiguration, and finally stops the coordinator, the epoch thread and cancels the job group.

nodes.name: addOffset
nodes.summary: Reports the ending partition offsets of a stream for an epoch: merges them into a global offset, adds it to the offset log (reading the previous epoch's entry), sets noNewData when the offset is unchanged, and signals threads waiting on the progress lock. Only one continuous source is supported.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Marks an epoch as committed after all readers reported end offsets: records trigger offsets, adds a CommitMetadata entry to the commit log, updates committedOffsets, commits the offset to the source, purges old log entries while keeping minLogEntriesToMaintain entries, and signals the progress lock.

nodes.name: awaitEpoch
nodes.summary: Blocks the current thread until the commit log shows a committed epoch at or after the requested one, polling the progress lock condition every 100 ms and rethrowing the stream death cause if the query died.

nodes.name: stopInNewThread
nodes.summary: Starts a daemon thread named stop-continuous-execution that calls stop() so the query terminates outside the calling thread. The public overload stopInNewThread(error) (lines 460-466) first records the error with compareAndSet, logs it, and then calls this method.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Sets the state to TERMINATED and, if the query execution thread is alive, interrupts it and waits for it to terminate; the thread cleans up itself in runContinuous. Logs that the query was stopped.

nodes.name: legacy.scala
nodes.summary: Holds deprecated aliases in the streaming package for HDFSMetadataLog and SerializedOffset, which now live in the checkpointing and runtime sub-packages.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog
nodes.summary: Deprecated class in the streaming package that simply extends the HDFSMetadataLog of the checkpointing package (imported under the name ActualHDFSMetadataLog); the deprecation message points to org.apache.spark.sql.execution.streaming.checkpointing.HDFSMetadataLog.

nodes.name: SerializedOffset
nodes.summary: Deprecated object whose apply(offset: String) builds the SerializedOffset of the runtime package; the deprecation message points to org.apache.spark.sql.execution.streaming.runtime.SerializedOffset.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Creates a runtime SerializedOffset from the given offset string by delegating to the actual SerializedOffset companion.

nodes.name: FileStreamSinkLog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metadata log of the streaming file sink: SinkFileStatus (one logged output file) and FileStreamSinkLog (the compactible log of those entries), with the log version and add action constants.

nodes.name: SinkFileStatus
nodes.summary: Case class describing a file written by the file sink: path (uri-encoded string), size, isDir, modificationTime, blockReplication, blockSize and an action that must be "add" or "delete". A file is visible only if it appears in the sink log and its action is not delete. sparkPath converts the path to a SparkPath and toFileStatus rebuilds a Hadoop FileStatus. The companion apply(FileStatus) creates an entry with the ADD action from a Hadoop FileStatus.
nodes.languageNotes: The node range covers the case class (40-59) and its companion object (61-72).

nodes.name: FileStreamSinkLog
nodes.summary: A special compactible log for the file sink. It writes one log file per batch whose first line is the version and whose following lines are JSON of SinkFileStatus entries. The class doc says it compacts the log files every spark.sql.sink.file.log.compactLen batches into one big file, merging old logs with the new batch and dropping files marked deleted; the compact interval, cleanup delay and deletion flag are read from the SQL configuration and the interval must be positive. An optional retention in milliseconds makes shouldRetain exclude files whose modification time is older than the retention. The companion object defines VERSION = 1 and ADD_ACTION = "add".
nodes.languageNotes: The node range covers the class (86-125) and its companion object (127-130).

nodes.name: toFileStatus
nodes.summary: Converts the entry back to a Hadoop FileStatus using size, isDir, replication, block size, modification time and the path decoded from its URL string.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a SinkFileStatus from a Hadoop FileStatus, url-encoding the path and using the ADD_ACTION constant of FileStreamSinkLog as the action.

nodes.name: shouldRetain
nodes.summary: Returns false (logging a debug message) when retention is set and the entry's modification time is older than the retention at the current time; otherwise returns true.

nodes.name: StreamingUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StreamingUtils object with helpers to resolve a checkpoint location to a qualified path and to compute the metadata path of a streaming source.

nodes.name: StreamingUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object for streaming. resolvedCheckpointLocation qualifies a possibly relative checkpoint path with the file system URI and working directory. getMetadataPath returns the metadata path of a source: named sources (user provided or flow assigned) use a stable name-based path under the checkpoint root sources directory, while unassigned sources take the next sequential id from an AtomicLong.

nodes.name: resolvedCheckpointLocation
nodes.summary: Turns the checkpoint location into a fully qualified path string using the file system URI and working directory from the Hadoop configuration.

nodes.name: getMetadataPath
nodes.summary: Computes the metadata path of a source: uses $resolvedCheckpointRoot/sources/<name> when the identifying name has a name, and otherwise $resolvedCheckpointRoot/sources/<n> with n taken from nextSourceId.getAndIncrement().

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the debug package object with helpers to print or capture the generated whole-stage code of a query plan and to count tuples and column types in a plan (DebugExec).

nodes.name: debug
nodes.summary: Package object that contains methods for debugging query execution. It offers codegenString, writeCodegen and codegenStringSeq to collect the WholeStageCodegen subtrees and their generated code (with bytecode statistics) from a SparkPlan or a StreamingQuery, implicit classes DebugQuery (debug and debugCodegen on a Dataset) and DebugStreamQuery (debugCodegen on a StreamingQuery), the SetAccumulator accumulator and the DebugExec plan node. Debug execution is not supported for streaming queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Usage shown in the doc comment: import org.apache.spark.sql.execution.debug._ then call debug() or debugCodegen() on a DataFrame or streaming query.

nodes.name: debugPrint
nodes.summary: Private helper that prints a message with println inside scalastyle:off/on markers to avoid the println linter.

nodes.name: codegenString
nodes.summary: Returns all WholeStageCodegen subtrees and their generated code as one string. The plan overload (lines 77-81) writes into a StringConcat through writeCodegen; this StreamingQuery overload unwraps the StreamExecution and uses its last execution's executed plan, returning "No physical plan. Waiting for data." when there is none.

nodes.name: writeCodegen
nodes.summary: Appends a report for each WholeStageCodegen subtree to the given append function: a header with the count, then per subtree the max method code size, constant pool size (with percent of the JVM limit) and inner class count, the subtree text and the generated code.

nodes.name: codegenStringSeq
nodes.summary: Finds all WholeStageCodegenExec subtrees of a plan (descending into AdaptiveSparkPlanExec executed plans, QueryStageExec plans and subqueries), sorts them by codegen stage id, generates and compiles each one's code and returns tuples of subtree string, formatted code and ByteCodeStats (UNAVAILABLE when compilation fails). The StreamingQuery overload (lines 160-167) calls it on the last execution's executed plan, or returns an empty Seq.

nodes.name: asStreamExecution
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns the StreamExecution behind a StreamingQuery (unwrapping StreamingQueryWrapper) and throws IllegalArgumentException for any other type.

nodes.name: DebugQuery
nodes.summary: Implicit class that adds debug methods to a Dataset. debug() wraps each distinct node of the executed plan in a DebugExec, runs the plan, prints the number of results and calls dumpStats on each DebugExec; debugCodegen() prints the generated code of the executed plan.

nodes.name: debug
nodes.summary: Transforms the executed plan so that each distinct SparkPlan node (tracked by TreeNodeRef) is wrapped in DebugExec, executes it, prints the result count and then prints the stats of every DebugExec.

nodes.name: debugCodegen
nodes.summary: Prints to stdout all generated code found in the query's executed plan (the output of each WholeStageCodegen subtree).

nodes.name: DebugStreamQuery
nodes.summary: Implicit class that adds debugCodegen() to a StreamingQuery by printing the result of codegenString for it.

nodes.name: debugCodegen
nodes.summary: Prints the generated code of the streaming query's last executed plan using codegenString.

nodes.name: SetAccumulator
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2 that collects distinct values of type T into a synchronized java Set; isZero, copy, reset, add, merge and value are implemented over that set. DebugExec uses it to gather the runtime data types seen in each output column.

nodes.name: DebugExec
nodes.summary: Case class unary physical node that passes its child's rows through unchanged while counting tuples (a LongAccumulator) and recording the set of element types seen per output column (ColumnMetrics holding a SetAccumulator). dumpStats prints the child description, tuple count and per-column types on the driver. doExecute runs the child through a DebugEvaluatorFactory (partition evaluator or mapPartitionsWithIndex); doProduce, doConsume, inputRDDs, doExecuteBroadcast, doExecuteColumnar, outputPartitioning and supportsColumnar delegate to the child, and withNewChildInternal copies with a new child.

nodes.name: ColumnMetrics
nodes.summary: Case class nested in DebugExec holding one SetAccumulator (elementTypes) per output column, registered with the SparkContext when created.

nodes.name: dumpStats
nodes.summary: Prints, on the driver, the child's simple string, the number of tuples output and for each output attribute its name, declared data type and the set of actual data types observed at runtime.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Creates a DebugEvaluatorFactory with the tuple counter, column count, per-column type accumulators and output, and runs the child through it with mapPartitionsWithEvaluator when conf.usePartitionEvaluator is set, otherwise through mapPartitionsWithIndex.

nodes.name: FrequentItems.scala
nodes.summary: Implements frequent item search for DataFrame columns: the FrequentItems entry point and the CollectFrequentItems aggregate expression that keeps approximate counts in a bounded map.

nodes.name: FrequentItems
nodes.summary: Object with singlePassFreqItems, which finds frequent items for the named columns in a single pass, possibly with false positives, using the frequent element count algorithm of Karp, Schenker and Papadimitriou referenced in its doc comment. It requires support between 1e-4 and 1.0, sizes the counting map as 1/support, and selects one CollectFrequentItems aggregate per column aliased <col>_freqItems. For internal use.

nodes.name: singlePassFreqItems
nodes.summary: Validates that support is in [1e-4, 1], computes the map size as (1 / support).toInt, builds a CollectFrequentItems aggregate for each requested column and returns df.select of those columns, giving a local DataFrame with an array of frequent items per column.

nodes.name: CollectFrequentItems
nodes.summary: Case class TypedImperativeAggregate (also UnaryLike) named collect_frequent_items whose buffer is a mutable Map from value to count limited to size entries. update adds one occurrence per input row, merge folds another buffer into this one, and add implements the bounded counting: when the map is full a new key is admitted only if its count is at least the smallest count, after which counts are decremented and entries that reach zero are dropped. eval returns the keys as an array of the child type, never null. serialize and deserialize write and read the key and count pairs as UnsafeRow bytes terminated by -1. The withNew* methods copy the buffer offsets or the child.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Private helper implementing the bounded frequent-count update: increments an existing key; adds a new key when the map has room; otherwise, when the new count minus the minimum count is non-negative it inserts the key, drops entries not above the minimum and subtracts the minimum from the rest, and when it is negative it subtracts the count from all entries.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Evaluates the child expression on the input row and adds one occurrence of the value (a copy for non-null values, null kept as a key) to the buffer.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another buffer into this one by calling add for each key and count pair of the other map.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Serializes the counts map: for each pair builds an InternalRow of key and count, converts it with an UnsafeProjection and writes its size and bytes to a DataOutputStream, ending with -1; streams are closed in a finally block.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Reads the length-prefixed UnsafeRow records until the -1 terminator and rebuilds the map of key and count pairs.

nodes.name: console.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the console sink of structured streaming: ConsoleSinkProvider (data source registered as console), ConsoleRelation and the ConsoleTable that supplies the streaming write.

nodes.name: ConsoleRelation
nodes.summary: Case class BaseRelation returned by the console sink provider; it wraps the DataFrame that was shown and exposes its schema.

nodes.name: ConsoleSinkProvider
nodes.summary: Data source provider with short name "console" for printing streaming output. getTable returns the ConsoleTable, and createRelation (batch path) reads the numRows option (default 20) and the truncate option (default true), calls data.show with them, and returns a ConsoleRelation.

nodes.name: ConsoleTable
nodes.summary: Singleton Table named "console" with no columns and the STREAMING_WRITE capability. newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that supports truncate (a no-op because the console sink only prints records) and streaming update as append, and whose Write produces a ConsoleWrite for the input schema and the write options.

nodes.name: createRelation
nodes.summary: Batch write entry point: reads the numRows (default 20) and truncate (default true) parameters, prints the data with show and returns a ConsoleRelation over it.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder with SupportsTruncate and SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend; its build creates a Write whose toStreaming asserts the input schema is set and returns a ConsoleWrite with the schema and the write options.

nodes.name: Offset.java
nodes.summary: Declares the deprecated internal Offset class of the streaming package as an alias of the data source v2 streaming Offset.

nodes.name: Offset
nodes.summary: Abstract class that only extends org.apache.spark.sql.connector.read.streaming.Offset. Its doc comment says it is an internal and deprecated alias, that new streaming data sources should use the data source v2 API, and that it will be removed in a future release.

nodes.name: MetadataLog.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the MetadataLog trait, the general interface of a per-batch metadata store used by streaming checkpoints.

nodes.name: MetadataLog
nodes.summary: Generic trait for a log that stores one metadata object per batch id. It declares add (store, false if already stored), two get overloads (one batch, or a range of batches by optional start and end id), getLatest (latest batch id and metadata) and purge (idempotent removal of entries earlier than a threshold batch id).

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Stores the metadata for a batch id and returns true on success; returns false if that batch id was already stored.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the metadata of one batch as an Option (overload at line 40), or the (batch id, metadata) pairs between an optional inclusive start id and end id (this range overload at line 46; with no start id it returns all batches up to the end id).

nodes.name: getLatest
nodes.summary: Returns the latest batch id together with its metadata, if any exist.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Removes all log entries earlier than thresholdBatchId (exclusive); the operation should be idempotent.

nodes.name: MetadataVersionUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MetadataVersionUtil, which parses and validates the version header (such as v1) of streaming metadata log files.

nodes.name: MetadataVersionUtil
nodes.summary: Utility object for the version text of metadata log files. validateVersion accepts a version up to a maximum supported version, validateVersionExactMatch requires an exact version, and the private extractVersion parses text of the form v<positive integer>. Malformed text raises malformedLogFile and a too high or mismatching version raises logVersionGreaterThanSupported or logVersionNotMatch.

nodes.name: validateVersion
nodes.summary: Parses the version from the text and throws logVersionGreaterThanSupported when it exceeds maxSupportedVersion; otherwise returns it.

nodes.name: validateVersionExactMatch
nodes.summary: Parses the version from the text and throws logVersionNotMatch when it differs from matchVersion; otherwise returns it.

nodes.name: extractVersion
nodes.summary: Private parser: the text must start with v followed by an integer greater than zero; anything else (empty text, no v prefix, non-numeric part, zero or negative number) raises malformedLogFile.

nodes.name: StateMessage.proto
nodes.summary: Protobuf definitions (package org.apache.spark.sql.execution.streaming.state) of the state messages: the StateRequest wrapper with a oneof of stateful processor, state variable, implicit grouping key, timer and utils calls, the value, list and map state operation messages, timer messages, several StateResponse variants, the HandleState enum and TTLConfig. Defines 47 messages and 1 enum.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol Buffers proto3 file; every definition is top level and many messages use a oneof named method.

nodes.name: StateRequest
nodes.summary: Top-level request message: an int32 version and a oneof method that carries one of StatefulProcessorCall, StateVariableRequest, ImplicitGroupingKeyRequest, TimerRequest or UtilsRequest.

nodes.name: StateResponse
nodes.summary: Basic response message with an int32 statusCode, a string errorMessage and a bytes value.

nodes.name: StateResponseWithLongTypeVal
nodes.summary: Response with statusCode, errorMessage and an int64 value.

nodes.name: StateResponseWithStringTypeVal

nodes.name: ContinuousQueuedDataReader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ContinuousQueuedDataReader, the per-partition wrapper used by continuous processing reads. It starts a background reader thread and a scheduled epoch-marker generator that both fill one bounded queue, and next() drains that queue so that a reader sees a null at each epoch boundary.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested sealed trait ContinuousRecord with a case object and a case class lets the queue hold either data rows or epoch markers.

nodes.name: ContinuousQueuedDataReader
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a ContinuousPartitionReader[InternalRow] that is created once per partition and reused by successive compute() calls of ContinuousDataSourceRDD, so offsets stay continuous across epochs. It captures the starting offset, creates an ArrayBlockingQueue of dataQueueSize, starts a DataReaderThread (daemon) and schedules an EpochMarkerGenerator every epochPollIntervalMs on a daemon scheduled executor, and registers a task completion listener that calls close(). Main methods: next() returns the next row of the current epoch or null at an epoch end; close() interrupts the reader thread and shuts the executor down; getPartitionReader() returns the wrapped reader.

nodes.name: ContinuousRecord
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the two kinds of entries that are put into the read queue: an EpochMarker or a ContinuousRow.

nodes.name: EpochMarker
nodes.summary: Case object extending ContinuousRecord. When next() takes it from the queue, the current epoch ends for this partition: it reports the current offset to the epoch coordinator and returns null.

nodes.name: ContinuousRow
nodes.summary: Case class extending ContinuousRecord that pairs an InternalRow with the PartitionOffset reported by the reader after producing that row.

nodes.name: DataReaderThread
nodes.summary: Thread (with Logging) that is the data component of the queued reader. It loops while the task is not stopped, calls reader.next(), converts each row to an unsafe row and copies it, and puts a ContinuousRow with reader.getOffset on the queue. An interrupt ends it quietly, a non-fatal error is kept in failureReason for the parent thread, and the reader is closed in a finally block.

nodes.name: EpochMarkerGenerator
nodes.summary: Runnable (with Logging) that is the epoch-marker component. On each scheduled run it asks the epoch coordinator for the current epoch with GetCurrentEpoch and puts one EpochMarker on the queue for every epoch it is behind, so a slow RPC causes catch-up markers and possibly empty epochs for this partition. Failures are saved in failureReason and rethrown.

nodes.name: getPartitionReader
nodes.summary: Returns the wrapped PartitionReader[InternalRow].

nodes.name: shouldStop
nodes.summary: Private helper that is true when the TaskContext is interrupted or completed; used by next() and by the data reader thread.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next row of the current epoch, or null when the epoch is finished. It polls the queue with a 1000 ms timeout, treats a stopped task as an EpochMarker, throws a QueryExecutionErrors error when the data reader thread or the marker generator has recorded a failure, and on an EpochMarker sends ReportPartitionOffset(partitionIndex, current epoch, currentOffset) to the epoch coordinator. For a ContinuousRow it remembers the offset and returns the row. Note that the marker-generator error is built with dataReaderThread.failureReason.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Interrupts the data reader thread and shuts down the epoch-marker executor.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Thread body: sets the TaskContext, then repeatedly calls reader.next() and queues a copied unsafe row with its offset. It throws IllegalStateException when the reader reports no element while the task is still running, quietly stops on InterruptedException, stores other failures in failureReason, and always closes the reader.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Asks the epoch coordinator synchronously for the current epoch, queues an EpochMarker for each epoch of difference to catch up, and stores any Throwable in failureReason before rethrowing.

nodes.name: ContinuousTaskRetryException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the exception thrown when a continuous processing task runs with a nonzero attempt id, since continuous execution does not support task retry.

nodes.name: ContinuousTaskRetryException
nodes.summary: SparkException subclass with the fixed message "Continuous execution does not support task retry" and no cause. ContinuousDataSourceRDD throws it from its compute path (line 79 of that file) when a task attempt is not the first.

nodes.name: ContinuousTextSocketSource.scala
nodes.summary: Continuous-processing version of the text socket source, meant only for tutorials and debugging. The driver reads lines from a TCP socket into per-partition buckets and serves them to executors through an RPC endpoint; executor-side readers poll that endpoint for records.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses json4s Serialization to write and read the offsets as a JSON list of ints.

nodes.name: TextSocketContinuousStream
nodes.summary: ContinuousStream (with Logging) that connects a Socket to host:port in initialize() and starts a daemon thread which reads lines, stamps each with the current time, and distributes the rows round-robin over numPartitions buckets (guarded by this). It serves the buckets through a ContinuousRecordEndpoint set up in planInputPartitions. Main methods: mergeOffsets, deserializeOffset, initialOffset, planInputPartitions (builds one TextSocketContinuousInputPartition per partition and rejects a changed partition count), createContinuousReaderFactory, commit (drops committed rows from the buckets), stop (closes the socket and stops the endpoint). It is documented as unsuitable for production because there is no fault recovery; the includeTimestamp option is read from the options map.

nodes.name: TextSocketContinuousInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition holding driverEndpointName, partitionId, startOffset and includeTimestamp, which the executor-side reader factory uses to build a reader.

nodes.name: TextSocketReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Object extending ContinuousPartitionReaderFactory; its createReader casts the partition to TextSocketContinuousInputPartition and returns a TextSocketContinuousPartitionReader.

nodes.name: TextSocketContinuousPartitionReader
nodes.summary: ContinuousPartitionReader[InternalRow] that finds the driver endpoint with RpcUtils.makeDriverRef and asks it for the record at the current offset with GetRecord. next() sleeps 100 ms between polls until a record arrives and returns false when interrupted; rows are projected to the regular schema unless includeTimestamp is set; getOffset reports a ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset.

nodes.name: TextSocketOffset
nodes.summary: Case class Offset wrapping a List[Int] of per-partition offsets; json serializes the list with json4s Serialization.

nodes.name: mergeOffsets
nodes.summary: Asserts the number of partition offsets equals numPartitions, sorts the ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset values by partition id, and returns them as a TextSocketOffset.

nodes.name: deserializeOffset
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON list of ints into a TextSocketOffset.

nodes.name: initialOffset
nodes.summary: Sets startOffset to a TextSocketOffset of zeros, one per partition, and returns it.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Gives the endpoint its start offsets, registers it on the RPC env under a name with a random UUID, checks that the start offset is a TextSocketOffset with numPartitions entries, and returns one TextSocketContinuousInputPartition per partition.

nodes.name: includeTimestamp
nodes.summary: Reads the includeTimestamp boolean option (default false).

nodes.name: createContinuousReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Returns the TextSocketReaderFactory object.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: For a TextSocketOffset, checks each partition offset against start offset plus bucket size, drops the committed rows from that bucket, then stores the end offset as the new start offset and passes it to the endpoint. Other offset types raise IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the socket (the only way to stop the blocking read thread) and stops the RPC endpoint if it was registered.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Opens the Socket to host:port and starts a daemon read thread. For every line the thread increments the offset and appends a (line, timestamp) row, serialized as an unsafe row, to bucket currentOffset % numPartitions; at end of stream it logs a warning and returns.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Returns a description with the host and port.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Builds a TextSocketContinuousPartitionReader from the fields of a TextSocketContinuousInputPartition.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Fetches a record from the driver, sleeping 100 ms between attempts until one exists, then advances the current offset; returns false when the thread is interrupted.

nodes.name: getRecord
nodes.summary: Sends GetRecord for the current partition and offset to the driver endpoint synchronously and, unless includeTimestamp is set, projects the row to the schema without the timestamp.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the current record.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: No-op close.

nodes.name: getOffset
nodes.summary: Returns a ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset for this partition and the current offset.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes the offsets list to JSON text.

nodes.name: ContinuousWriteRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ContinuousWriteRDD, the RDD that writes to a sink in continuous processing. Each task keeps computing its parent RDD, writing one epoch at a time and committing it to the driver, until the query is shut down.

nodes.name: ContinuousWriteRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[Unit] built on a parent RDD[InternalRow], a StreamingDataWriterFactory and a map of custom SQLMetrics. Its compute() loops while the task is neither interrupted nor completed: it calls prev.compute(), creates a DataWriter for the partition, task attempt and current epoch, writes every row, updates custom metrics, commits, sends CommitPartitionEpoch to the epoch coordinator and increments the epoch. On error the writer is aborted, and the writer is always closed. It reuses the partitions and partitioner of the parent and clears the parent reference in clearDependencies.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the partitions of the parent RDD.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Gets the epoch coordinator, initializes the epoch tracker from the start epoch property, then writes epoch after epoch. For each epoch it writes the rows of prev.compute(), refreshes custom metrics every CustomMetrics.NUM_ROWS_PER_UPDATE rows, commits the writer, sends CommitPartitionEpoch and increments the epoch; InterruptedException just ends the task, and any error aborts the writer. Returns an empty iterator.

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Calls the parent implementation and nulls the prev reference.

nodes.name: WriteToContinuousDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical plan node WriteToContinuousDataSource that represents writing the result of a query to a streaming sink in continuous processing.

nodes.name: WriteToContinuousDataSource
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryNode with a StreamingWrite, the query LogicalPlan and a Seq of CustomMetric. Its child is the query, its output is empty (Nil), and withNewChildInternal copies it with a new query. ContinuousExecution builds it for the streaming write.

nodes.name: child
nodes.summary: Returns the query plan as the single child.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns an empty attribute list, since a write produces no output.

nodes.name: withNewChildInternal
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of this node with the query replaced by the new child.

nodes.name: AcceptsLatestSeenOffsetHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AcceptsLatestSeenOffsetHandler helper object that hands the latest seen offset, taken from a stored offset sequence, to every source that implements AcceptsLatestSeenOffset.

nodes.name: AcceptsLatestSeenOffsetHandler
nodes.summary: Object with two methods. setLatestSeenOffsetOnSources first checks that no source is both an AcceptsLatestSeenOffset and a (data source V1) Source, then converts the optional OffsetSeqBase to a stream progress and calls setLatestSeenOffset on each source that accepts it. The private assertion throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException with the error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3169 listing the unsupported sources.

nodes.name: setLatestSeenOffsetOnSources
nodes.summary: Runs the V1 check, then, when offsets are present, converts them with toStreamProgress(sources, sourceIdMap) and calls setLatestSeenOffset(offset) on each source that implements AcceptsLatestSeenOffset; other sources and missing offsets are ignored.

nodes.name: assertNoAcceptsLatestSeenOffsetWithDataSourceV1
nodes.summary: Throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3169) when any source is both an AcceptsLatestSeenOffset and a Source.

nodes.name: AsyncLogPurge.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AsyncLogPurge trait that lets a streaming query purge its logs (and old stateful operator metadata) on a single background thread instead of inline, and keeps at most one purge of each kind running at a time.

nodes.name: AsyncLogPurge
nodes.summary: Trait (with Logging) that owns a daemon single-thread executor named "async-log-purge" and two AtomicBoolean guards. Implementers supply minLogEntriesToMaintain, errorNotifier, sparkSession, purge(threshold) and purgeStatefulMetadata(plan). It exposes useAsyncPurge (from SQLConf.ASYNC_LOG_PURGE), purgeAsync, purgeStatefulMetadataAsync, asyncLogPurgeShutdown and a test-only arePendingAsyncPurge. A purge that is requested while another is running is skipped with a debug message, and a failure is logged and reported to the ErrorNotifier.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Abstract method that implementers use to remove log entries older than the given threshold batch id.

nodes.name: purgeStatefulMetadata
nodes.summary: Abstract method that implementers use to purge the oldest OperatorStateMetadata and StateSchema files written per run, for the given plan.

nodes.name: purgeAsync
nodes.summary: If no purge is running (compareAndSet on purgeRunning), submits purge(batchId - minLogEntriesToMaintain) to the executor; errors are logged and passed to errorNotifier.markError, and the flag is reset in a finally block. Otherwise it logs that the purge was skipped.

nodes.name: purgeStatefulMetadataAsync
nodes.summary: Same pattern as purgeAsync but guarded by statefulMetadataPurgeRunning; it runs purgeStatefulMetadata(plan) on the executor and reports failures to errorNotifier.

nodes.name: asyncLogPurgeShutdown
nodes.summary: Shuts down the purge executor with ThreadUtils.shutdown.

nodes.name: arePendingAsyncPurge
nodes.summary: Test helper: true if a purge is running, queued or active in the executor.

nodes.name: AsyncProgressTrackingMicroBatchExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AsyncProgressTrackingMicroBatchExecution, a MicroBatchExecution variant that writes the offset log and commit log asynchronously on a single ordered thread, and its companion object with the option names. It accepts only processing-time triggers, a short list of sinks and non-stateful queries.
nodes.languageNotes: The class and its companion object share one class node. The offset log write is chained with thenAccept/exceptionally on a future, and the executor uses a custom RejectedExecutionHandler that blocks on the queue instead of rejecting.

nodes.name: AsyncProgressTrackingMicroBatchExecution
nodes.summary: Subclass of MicroBatchExecution used when async progress tracking is on. A single-thread "async-log-write" executor (queue handler blocks the producer when the queue is full) runs offset-log and commit-log writes in order through an AsyncStreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata, whose offsetLog and commitLog are AsyncOffsetSeqLog and AsyncCommitLog. Offsets become ready for source commit only after the offset write reaches durable storage, and sources are committed on the micro-batch thread from a ConcurrentLinkedQueue. The checkpoint interval comes from the option asyncProgressTrackingCheckpointIntervalMs (default "1000"). Companion constants: asyncProgressTrackingEnabled, asyncProgressTrackingCheckpointIntervalMs and the test-only _asyncProgressTrackingOverrideSinkSupportCheck (lines 310-328).

nodes.name: validateOffsetLogAndGetPrevOffset
nodes.summary: Overrides the parent method: finds the previous batch id in storage and returns the offset sequence of that batch (the second latest in the offset log, which may not be contiguous), or None for batch 0 or when there is none; throws IllegalStateException if the metadata is missing.

nodes.name: markMicroBatchExecutionStart
nodes.summary: Overrides the parent method and only checks that the query is not stateful.

nodes.name: cleanUpLastExecutedMicroBatch
nodes.summary: Overrides the parent method as a no-op, because sources are committed only after the offset write is durable.

nodes.name: checkUnfinishedRepartitionBatch
nodes.summary: Overrides the parent method as a no-op, since stateful queries and state repartitioning are not supported.

nodes.name: markMicroBatchStart
nodes.summary: Does not call the parent. It starts an asynchronous write of the end offsets of the batch to the offset log; when the write is persisted, it checks that batch ids increase, reads the previous batch offsets and puts them on sourceCommitQueue, and records the batch id. Failures are logged and sent to errorNotifier. Afterwards it drains sourceCommitQueue and calls commitSources for each ready offset.

nodes.name: markMicroBatchEnd
nodes.summary: Updates the watermark from the executed plan, then, within a "commitOffsets" timing block, writes the commit log asynchronously when an async offset write was issued for this batch or it is the first batch of the run (to fill commit-log gaps on restart); otherwise it adds the entry in memory and throws a concurrent-update error if that fails. It removes the async offset write record and adds the end offsets to committedOffsets.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Overrides purge: trims the writtenToDurableStorage queues of the offset log and commit log to minLogEntriesToMaintain entries and purges each log up to the head of its queue (based on files actually written, not the batch id threshold).

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Calls the parent cleanup, shuts down the async write executor and logs that the pool for the query was shut down.

nodes.name: areWritesPendingOrInProgress
nodes.summary: Test helper: true if the async write executor has queued or active tasks.

nodes.name: getTrigger
nodes.summary: Overrides getTrigger to return validateAndGetTrigger().

nodes.name: validateAndGetTrigger
nodes.summary: Unless the test override option is true, accepts only the sinks named "noop-table", "console", "MemorySink" and "KafkaTable" and throws IllegalArgumentException for others (also when the sink does not implement name()). Then returns a ProcessingTimeExecutor for a ProcessingTimeTrigger and rejects the Once and AvailableNow triggers and unknown trigger types.

nodes.name: checkNotStatefulStreamingQuery
nodes.summary: On the first batch, collects over the executed plan and throws IllegalArgumentException if any node is a StateStoreWriter.

nodes.name: getAsyncProgressTrackingCheckpointingIntervalMs
nodes.summary: Companion object helper that reads asyncProgressTrackingCheckpointIntervalMs from the extra options as a Long, defaulting to "1000".

nodes.name: AvailableNowMicroBatchStreamWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvailableNowMicroBatchStreamWrapper, which wraps a MicroBatchStream so it supports Trigger.AvailableNow; the shared offset handling lives in AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper.

nodes.name: AvailableNowMicroBatchStreamWrapper
nodes.summary: Class extending AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper and implementing MicroBatchStream around a delegate MicroBatchStream. It forwards planInputPartitions and createReaderFactory to the delegate, while latestOffset() with no arguments throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3166).

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3166); the wrapper does not support asking for the latest offset this way.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Delegates to the wrapped stream to plan input partitions between the start and end offsets.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Delegates to the wrapped stream to create the PartitionReaderFactory.

nodes.name: AsyncStreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AsyncStreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata, the checkpoint metadata holder used when async progress tracking is on: it reuses the base checkpoint metadata class but supplies asynchronous offset and commit logs that write through a shared ThreadPoolExecutor.

nodes.name: AsyncStreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata
nodes.summary: Subclass of StreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata for async state checkpointing. It takes the Spark session, the resolved checkpoint root, a ThreadPoolExecutor for async writes, an async progress checkpointing interval in ms and a trigger Clock. It overrides the lazy vals offsetLog (an AsyncOffsetSeqLog on the offsets directory, given the executor, the interval and the clock) and commitLog (an AsyncCommitLog on the commits directory, given the executor), using the directory names from StreamingCheckpointConstants. The overrides are lazy vals, so no function nodes are created.

nodes.name: AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper, a wrapper that lets a SparkDataStream run under Trigger.AvailableNow by fixing the latest offset once at query start and forwarding everything else to the wrapped stream.

nodes.name: AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper
nodes.summary: Wraps a SparkDataStream (the delegate) to support Trigger.AvailableNow when the delegate does not implement it itself. At construction it logs a warning that this wrapper may introduce deduplication, data loss or correctness issues. prepareForTriggerAvailableNow fetches and stores the latest offset of all available data once: via latestOffset(initialOffset, ReadLimit.allAvailable()) for a SupportsAdmissionControl delegate, via getOffset for a Source, or via latestOffset() for a MicroBatchStream. latestOffset then always returns that stored offset, and getDefaultReadLimit always returns ReadLimit.allAvailable (logging a warning if the delegate had another limit). reportLatestOffset asks the delegate for the real latest offset (used for metrics). initialOffset, deserializeOffset, commit and stop are forwarded to the delegate.

nodes.name: initialOffset
nodes.summary: Forwards initialOffset to the delegate stream.

nodes.name: deserializeOffset
nodes.summary: Forwards deserializeOffset(json) to the delegate stream.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Forwards commit(end) to the delegate stream.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Forwards stop() to the delegate stream.

nodes.name: getInitialOffset
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns null when the delegate is a Source and the delegate's initialOffset when it is a MicroBatchStream; used as the start offset when asking an admission-control delegate for its latest offset.

nodes.name: prepareForTriggerAvailableNow
nodes.summary: Fetches and stores, once at the beginning of the query, the latest offset covering all available data. Chooses the call by delegate type (SupportsAdmissionControl with ReadLimit.allAvailable(), Source.getOffset, or MicroBatchStream.latestOffset) and throws IllegalStateException for any other kind of source.

nodes.name: getDefaultReadLimit
nodes.summary: Always returns ReadLimit.allAvailable(); for an admission-control delegate whose own default limit differs, it logs a warning that the limit is ignored because the source does not support Trigger.AvailableNow queries.

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Returns the offset pre-fetched by prepareForTriggerAvailableNow, ignoring the start offset and read limit it is given.

nodes.name: reportLatestOffset
nodes.summary: Returns the delegate's real latest offset (reportLatestOffset for admission-control delegates, getOffset for a Source, latestOffset for a MicroBatchStream); the source comment says it is only used for metrics.

nodes.name: AvailableNowSourceWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AvailableNowSourceWrapper, the Source flavour of the Trigger.AvailableNow wrapper built on AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper.

nodes.name: AvailableNowSourceWrapper
nodes.summary: Wraps a (legacy) Source so it supports Trigger.AvailableNow. It extends AvailableNowDataStreamWrapper (which holds the pre-fetched latest offset logic) and mixes in Source. schema and getBatch are forwarded to the delegate source; getOffset throws a SparkUnsupportedOperationException with the error class _LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3166, since offsets are served through latestOffset instead.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns the delegate source's schema.

nodes.name: getOffset
nodes.summary: Always throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3166); the wrapper is driven through latestOffset rather than getOffset.

nodes.name: getBatch
nodes.summary: Forwards getBatch(start, end) to the delegate source and returns its DataFrame.

nodes.name: ErrorNotifier.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ErrorNotifier, a small holder that records a Throwable raised out of band and lets another thread inspect or rethrow it.

nodes.name: ErrorNotifier
nodes.summary: Class to notify of errors that happened out of band. It keeps the last error in an AtomicReference: markError logs a fatal error and stores the throwable, getError returns it as an Option, and throwErrorIfExists rethrows it if one is present.

nodes.name: markError
nodes.summary: Logs 'A fatal error has occurred.' with the throwable and stores it in the atomic reference.

nodes.name: getError
nodes.summary: Returns the stored error as an Option (None if no error was marked).

nodes.name: throwErrorIfExists
nodes.summary: Throws the stored error if there is one, otherwise does nothing.

nodes.name: CompactibleFileStreamLog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CompactibleFileStreamLog, an abstract HDFSMetadataLog that periodically compacts its per-batch log files into one file, and its companion object with the batch-id arithmetic for compaction.

nodes.name: CompactibleFileStreamLog
nodes.summary: Abstract metadata log (extends HDFSMetadataLog[Array[T]]) that writes one log file per batch: the first line is the version ("v" plus metadataLogVersion) and each following line is a JSON-serialized entry. To avoid many small files it compacts every compactInterval batches (default is supplied by subclasses through defaultCompactInterval) into a '.compact' file that merges the earlier batches with the new one, filtering entries through shouldRetain. compactInterval is a lazy val that stays compatible with existing .compact files (three cases, SPARK-18187). Subclasses must define fileCleanupDelayMs, isDeletingExpiredLog and defaultCompactInterval. add compacts or delegates to the parent and then deletes expired logs; allFiles returns all non-deleted entries and retries when a concurrent compaction removes files; purge always throws. The companion object (lines 335-404) holds COMPACT_FILE_SUFFIX (".compact"), COMPACT_LATENCY_WARN_THRESHOLD_MS (2000) and the helpers getBatchIdFromFileName, isCompactionBatch, getValidBatchesBeforeCompactionBatch, getAllValidBatches, nextCompactionBatchId and deriveCompactInterval.

nodes.summary: Asserts the class list is non-empty and builds a SparkIllegalArgumentException with error class STREAMING_REAL_TIME_MODE.OPERATOR_OR_SINK_NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST, errorType and a message from classNamesString.

nodes.name: checkAllowedSink
nodes.summary: Checks that the sink table class name is in allowedSinks; otherwise throws or logs a warning according to throwException.

nodes.name: collectRealtimeNodes
nodes.summary: Walks a SparkPlan bottom-up with a nested helper and collects every node whose subtree contains a RealTimeStreamScanExec (the scan node itself is not collected).

nodes.name: checkAllowedPhysicalOperator
nodes.summary: Collects the real-time nodes of a plan, finds distinct operator class names not in allowedOperators, and throws or logs a warning for them according to throwException.

nodes.name: EpochCoordinator.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side coordination of epochs in continuous processing. Defines the RPC message hierarchy, EpochCoordinatorRef (creates or looks up the endpoint) and the EpochCoordinator endpoint that counts the driver epoch, collects reader offsets and writer commits per epoch, and commits epochs in order to the StreamingWrite and the ContinuousExecution query.

nodes.name: EpochCoordinatorMessage
nodes.summary: Private sealed trait (Serializable) that is the parent of all messages sent to the EpochCoordinator.

nodes.name: IncrementAndGetEpoch
nodes.summary: Driver epoch trigger message: atomically increments the current driver epoch and returns the new value.

nodes.name: StopContinuousExecutionWrites
nodes.summary: Synchronous message that makes the coordinator stop forwarding writes to ContinuousExecution, avoiding a race where an old coordinator commits epoch n + 1 after a restart at epoch n.

nodes.name: SetReaderPartitions
nodes.summary: Init message that sets the number of reader partitions; tasks may not start until the coordinator acknowledges it.

nodes.name: SetWriterPartitions
nodes.summary: Init message that sets the number of writer partitions; sent for example by WriteToContinuousDataSourceExec.

nodes.name: GetCurrentEpoch
nodes.summary: Partition task message asking the coordinator for the current driver epoch.

nodes.name: CommitPartitionEpoch
nodes.summary: Partition task message carrying partitionId, epoch and the WriterCommitMessage for committing a partition at that epoch.

nodes.name: ReportPartitionOffset
nodes.summary: Partition task message reporting that a partition ends the given epoch at the given PartitionOffset.

nodes.name: EpochCoordinatorRef
nodes.summary: Helper object (with Logging) to reach the coordinator: create builds an EpochCoordinator and registers it as the RPC endpoint named EpochCoordinator-<id>; get returns a driver reference to an existing endpoint by id.

nodes.name: EpochCoordinator
nodes.summary: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint (with Logging) that keeps the driver epoch counter, the per-(epoch, partition) commit and offset maps, and the last committed epoch. When all reader partitions reported an offset it calls query.addOffset; when all writers committed and all readers reported, it commits the epoch to the writer and the query in order, holding later epochs until earlier ones commit. It stops the query if a queue exceeds the continuous streaming epoch backlog size setting.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates an EpochCoordinator with the write support, stream, query, start epoch and session, registers it on the RpcEnv under its endpoint name and returns the RpcEndpointRef.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns a driver RpcEndpointRef for the EpochCoordinator endpoint with the given id, using RpcUtils.makeDriverRef.

nodes.name: resolveCommitsAtEpoch
nodes.summary: If commits from all writer partitions and offsets from all reader partitions exist for an epoch, commits it when the previous epoch is committed (then also commits any waiting later epochs and cleans old state), otherwise records it as waiting.

nodes.name: commitEpoch
nodes.summary: Commits an epoch: first calls writeSupport.commit with the partition messages, then query.commit(epoch), in that order so a restart cannot drop the commit.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: One-way message handler: ignores everything once writes are stopped; stores CommitPartitionEpoch messages; stores ReportPartitionOffset messages and, once all readers reported, calls query.addOffset; both paths call resolveCommitsAtEpoch and checkProcessingQueueBoundaries.

nodes.name: checkProcessingQueueBoundaries
nodes.summary: Stops the query in a new thread with an IllegalStateException when the offset map, commit map or waiting-epoch set grows beyond the configured backlog queue size.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Request-reply handler: answers GetCurrentEpoch with the driver epoch, IncrementAndGetEpoch with the incremented epoch, and acknowledges SetReaderPartitions, SetWriterPartitions and StopContinuousExecutionWrites.

nodes.name: ContinuousRecordEndpoint.scala
nodes.summary: RPC endpoint and message classes that let continuous readers poll the driver for records held in per-partition buckets.

nodes.name: ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset
nodes.summary: Case class PartitionOffset made of a partitionId and an integer offset within that partition's bucket.

nodes.name: GetRecord
nodes.summary: Request message that asks the endpoint for the record at a given ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset.

nodes.name: ContinuousRecordEndpoint
nodes.summary: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint constructed with data buckets (one sequence of UnsafeRow per partition) and a lock object. On GetRecord it replies, under the lock, with Some(row) at the offset minus the partition start offset, or None when the bucket has no such row. setStartOffsets changes the base offsets per partition.

nodes.name: setStartOffsets
nodes.summary: Under the lock, replaces the per-partition base offsets used when answering GetRecord requests.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles GetRecord: under the lock computes the bucket position from the offset and start offset, and replies with an Option of the stored row.

nodes.name: MetricsReporter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MetricsReporter, a metrics source that exposes the latest progress of a streaming query as gauges in a MetricRegistry.

nodes.name: MetricsReporter
nodes.summary: Class extending the metrics Source (with Logging) for one StreamExecution. It registers gauges inputRate-total, processingRate-total, latency, eventTime-watermark, states-rowsTotal and states-usedBytes, each reading the stream's last StreamingQueryProgress and falling back to a default value; the watermark string is parsed from an ISO8601 UTC timestamp into epoch milliseconds.

nodes.name: convertStringDateToMillis
nodes.summary: Parses an ISO8601 UTC timestamp string into epoch milliseconds, returning 0 when the string is null.

nodes.name: registerGauge
nodes.summary: Registers a Gauge in the metric registry (under the object lock) whose value applies a function to the stream's lastProgress, or returns the default when there is none.

nodes.name: ForeachWriterTable.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the streaming foreach sink as a write-only table. A ForeachWriterTable hands every row to a user supplied ForeachWriter, through a Write, a StreamingDataWriterFactory and a per-partition DataWriter, and it has an empty commit message and a wrapper exception for errors thrown by the user function.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object builds the table from a ForeachWriter and an encoder, and switches to a direct UnsafeRow cast converter when the writer is a PythonForeachWriter.

nodes.name: ForeachWriterTable
nodes.summary: Case class that is a Table with SupportsWrite and is the entry point of the foreach sink. Its name() is "ForeachSink", its schema is empty, and its only capability is TableCapability.STREAMING_WRITE. newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder that supports truncate (as a no-op) and streaming update-as-append, and whose build() creates a ForeachWrite. The converter is either an ExpressionEncoder or a plain InternalRow => T function. The companion object (lines 100 to 112) has apply(writer, encoder).

nodes.name: ForeachWrite
nodes.summary: Write implementation created by ForeachWriterTable. Its toStreaming returns an anonymous StreamingWrite whose commit and abort do nothing and whose createStreamingWriterFactory resolves the row converter and returns a ForeachWriterFactory. When the converter is an encoder it is resolved and bound to the input schema with the analyzer of the active SparkSession and a deserializer is created; when it is a function the function is used as is.

nodes.name: ForeachWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Case class implementing StreamingDataWriterFactory. Its createWriter(partitionId, taskId, epochId) returns a new ForeachDataWriter that wraps the user ForeachWriter and the row converter.

nodes.name: ForeachDataWriter
nodes.summary: DataWriter[InternalRow] that runs in one partition of one epoch and writes its rows to a ForeachWriter. It calls writer.open(partitionId, epochId) when it is constructed and skips all rows if open returned false. write() converts the row and calls writer.process; a non-fatal error that is not a SparkThrowable is wrapped in ForeachUserFuncException, other errors are rethrown, and the error is remembered. commit() returns ForeachWriterCommitMessage, abort() records a foreach-writer-aborted error from QueryExecutionErrors if no error is known, and close() calls writer.close with the remembered error (or null).

nodes.name: ForeachWriterCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Case object extending WriterCommitMessage. It is an empty commit message, because ForeachWriter implementations have no global coordination.

nodes.name: ForeachUserFuncException
nodes.summary: Private[sql] case class extending SparkException with error class "FOREACH_USER_FUNCTION_ERROR". It wraps an exception thrown by the user provided function of the foreach sink; the message parameter "reason" is the cause message or an empty string.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder with SupportsTruncate and SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend. truncate() returns the same builder and does nothing, because the sink just forwards records; build() returns a new ForeachWrite.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory taking a ForeachWriter and an ExpressionEncoder. For a PythonForeachWriter it creates a ForeachWriterTable[UnsafeRow] with a converter that casts the InternalRow to UnsafeRow; for any other writer it uses the encoder as converter.

nodes.name: toStreaming
nodes.summary: Builds the StreamingWrite used by the streaming engine. Commit and abort are empty, and createStreamingWriterFactory resolves the converter (encoder bound with toAttributes(inputSchema) and the active session analyzer, or the given function) and returns ForeachWriterFactory(writer, rowConverter).

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a ForeachDataWriter for the given partition and epoch.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Passes one record to writer.process after converting it with rowConverter, doing nothing if open() returned false. A non-fatal exception that is not a SparkThrowable is stored and rethrown as ForeachUserFuncException; any other Throwable is stored and rethrown unchanged.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: If no error has been recorded yet, records the error from QueryExecutionErrors.foreachWriterAbortedDueToTaskFailureError so that close() reports it to the user writer.

nodes.name: TextSocketSourceProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the "socket" streaming source: the TextSocketSourceProvider that is registered under the short name "socket", the TextSocketTable it creates, and the TextSocketReader object with the two output schemas and a timestamp formatter. The table supports micro-batch and continuous reads.

nodes.name: TextSocketSourceProvider
nodes.summary: Class extending SimpleTableProvider with DataSourceRegister and Logging. shortName() returns "socket". getTable validates the options with checkParameters (it logs a warning that the socket source is not for production and does not support recovery, and requires "host" and "port" and a boolean "includeTimestamp") and then returns a TextSocketTable built from host, port, numPartitions (default is the default parallelism of the active session) and includeTimestamp.

nodes.name: TextSocketTable
nodes.summary: Table with SupportsRead for the socket source. name() is "Socket[host:port]", schema() is TextSocketReader.SCHEMA_TIMESTAMP when includeTimestamp is set and SCHEMA_REGULAR otherwise, and capabilities are MICRO_BATCH_READ and CONTINUOUS_READ. newScanBuilder returns a Scan whose toMicroBatchStream creates a TextSocketMicroBatchStream, whose toContinuousStream creates a TextSocketContinuousStream, and whose columnar support mode is UNSUPPORTED.

nodes.name: TextSocketReader
nodes.summary: Object with constants for the socket source: SCHEMA_REGULAR (a single string column "value"), SCHEMA_TIMESTAMP ("value" string plus "timestamp" timestamp column) and DATE_TIME_FORMATTER (pattern "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US, system default zone). TextSocketTable.schema() reads the two schemas.

nodes.name: checkParameters
nodes.summary: Private validation of the source options: logs a production warning, throws QueryCompilationErrors errors when "host" or "port" is missing, and throws the invalid includeTimestamp error when "includeTimestamp" cannot be read as a boolean.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Validates the options and creates the TextSocketTable from host, port (default -1), numPartitions and includeTimestamp.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns the timestamp schema or the regular schema of TextSocketReader depending on includeTimestamp.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder (written as a lambda) that gives an anonymous Scan: readSchema uses the table columns, toMicroBatchStream returns TextSocketMicroBatchStream(host, port, numPartitions), toContinuousStream returns TextSocketContinuousStream(host, port, numPartitions, options), and columnarSupportMode is UNSUPPORTED.

nodes.name: SerializedOffset.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SerializedOffset, a thin Offset that only holds a JSON string read back from external storage. The sources convert it to their own offset type.

nodes.name: SerializedOffset
nodes.summary: Case class extending the streaming Offset with a json string. It is used when a JSON serialized offset is loaded from external storage; it does not convert the JSON to an object, and sources should define a factory method in their offset companion objects that accepts a SerializedOffset.

nodes.name: StreamExecutionContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the execution contexts of streaming queries: the abstract StreamExecutionContext with the offsets, input data and plan of one batch, the ContinuousExecutionContext for epochs, and the MicroBatchExecutionContext for micro-batches, which can be chained to the previous batch. It also has the MicroBatchExecutionResult and MicroBatchExecutionFailed types.

nodes.name: StreamExecutionContext
nodes.summary: Abstract class that extends ProgressContext and holds the mutable state of one batch of a streaming query: offsetSeqMetadata (starts as OffsetSeqMetadata with watermark 0 and timestamp 0), newData (a map from SparkDataStream to LogicalPlan), startOffsets, endOffsets and latestOffsets (StreamProgress values that only the scheduler thread should change), and executionPlan (IncrementalExecution). It also has empty hooks onExecutionComplete and onExecutionFailure.

nodes.name: ContinuousExecutionContext
nodes.summary: Concrete StreamExecutionContext for continuous execution mode. It adds no members and only passes the epoch id as the batch id of the parent class.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecutionContext
nodes.summary: StreamExecutionContext (with Logging) for one micro-batch. It has the flag isCurrentBatchConstructed, the offsetLogFormatVersionOpt and a link to previousContext. On construction it copies from the previous context startOffsets (set to its endOffsets), endOffsets, latestOffsets, metricWarningLogged, currentTriggerStartTimestamp, executionPlan, sinkCommitProgress and offsetSeqMetadata. getNextContext creates the context of batchId + 1 that points back to this one, and the link is cleared on completion or failure to avoid an infinite chain.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecutionResult
nodes.summary: Case class with two booleans, isActive and didExecute, (both values are plain flags, with no other members).

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecutionFailed
nodes.summary: Case class extending RuntimeException with no fields. It has no message and no cause.

nodes.name: getNextContext
nodes.summary: Creates a new MicroBatchExecutionContext for batchId + 1 with the same ids, clock, sources, sink, reporter, session and offset log format version, and with Some(this) as previous context.

nodes.name: startTrigger
nodes.summary: Calls the parent startTrigger and sets isTriggerActive to true in currentStatus.

nodes.name: onExecutionComplete
nodes.summary: Sets previousContext to None to release the reference (so the chain of contexts does not grow without bound) and then calls the parent hook.

nodes.name: onExecutionFailure
nodes.summary: Same cleanup as onExecutionComplete for the failure case: clears previousContext and calls the parent hook.

nodes.name: carryOverExecStatsOnLatestExecutedBatch
nodes.summary: Sets execStatsOnLatestExecutedBatch from the one of the previous context, used so that progress for an idle trigger does not depend on executionPlan.

nodes.name: StreamMetadata.scala
