nodes.summary: Defines StreamMetadata, the small record with the unique query id that is written to the checkpoint location when a query first starts and read back on every restart, plus the reading and writing code based on json4s and CheckpointFileManager.

nodes.name: StreamMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class StreamMetadata(id: String) with a json method, together with its companion object (lines 48 to 100, which extends Logging and defines the implicit json4s format). The companion has read(metadataFile, hadoopConf), which returns Some(metadata) if the file exists and None otherwise, and write(metadata, metadataFile, hadoopConf), which writes atomically without overwriting.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads the metadata from the file if it exists: creates a CheckpointFileManager for the parent directory, opens the file, parses the UTF-8 JSON into a StreamMetadata and returns Some of it; returns None if the file is missing. A non-fatal error is logged and rethrown, and the input is closed quietly.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes the metadata as JSON through createAtomic with overwriteIfPossible = false. If the file already exists the stream is cancelled and QueryExecutionErrors.multiStreamingQueriesUsingPathConcurrentlyError is thrown; any other error cancels the stream, is logged and is rethrown.

nodes.name: StreamingCheckpointConstants.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the names of the sub-directories of a streaming checkpoint location in one object.

nodes.name: StreamingCheckpointConstants
nodes.summary: Object with four string constants for checkpoint directory names: DIR_NAME_COMMITS = "commits", DIR_NAME_OFFSETS = "offsets", DIR_NAME_STATE = "state" and DIR_NAME_METADATA = "metadata".

nodes.name: StreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata, the accessor for the checkpoint data of one streaming query: the offset log, the commit log and the StreamMetadata with the query id, all located under one resolved checkpoint root.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata
nodes.summary: Class taking a SparkSession, the resolved checkpoint root and a readOnly flag. It exposes lazy offsetLog (an OffsetSeqLog under the "offsets" directory, the write-ahead log written before processing a batch), lazy commitLog (a CommitLog under the "commits" directory, which records completed batches and is used on restart to find the next batch) and the final lazy streamMetadata. streamMetadata reads the file in the "metadata" directory, or, if it is missing, first (when SQLConf.STREAMING_CHECKPOINT_VERIFY_METADATA_EXISTS is on) throws StreamingErrors.missingMetadataFile if the offset or commit log already has data, then creates and writes a new StreamMetadata with a random UUID. The protected checkpointFile(name) builds sub-paths of the root.

nodes.name: checkpointFile
nodes.summary: Final protected helper that returns the path string of a file or directory called name inside the resolved checkpoint root.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the micro-batch stream of the rate-per-micro-batch source and its helper types: the offset (a row count and a timestamp), the input partition, the reader factory and the partition reader. Each batch produces a fixed number of rows and moves the timestamp forward by a fixed step.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: MicroBatchStream with SupportsTriggerAvailableNow and Logging, built from rowsPerBatch, numPartitions, startTimestamp, advanceMsPerBatch and the options. initialOffset is RatePerMicroBatchStreamOffset(0, startTimestamp); the default read limit is ReadLimit.maxRows(rowsPerBatch); latestOffset(start, limit) returns start offset + rowsPerBatch with timestamp + advanceMsPerBatch, and under Trigger.AvailableNow it computes this once and keeps it. planInputPartitions validates that start is not past end (throws SparkRuntimeException with MALFORMED_STATE_IN_RATE_PER_MICRO_BATCH_SOURCE.INVALID_OFFSET or .INVALID_TIMESTAMP), returns an empty array if offsets are equal, and otherwise numPartitions RatePerMicroBatchStreamInputPartition values. The no-argument latestOffset() throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException; commit and stop do nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Overloaded latestOffset: the no-argument version (lines 41 to 43) always throws, the version with (startOffset, limit) (lines 64 to 87) is the one that computes offsets.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStreamOffset
nodes.summary: Case class RatePerMicroBatchStreamOffset(offset, timestamp) that extends the connector Offset; json() serializes it with json4s. Its companion object (lines 151 to 156) has the implicit format and apply(json: String), which reads the JSON back.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStreamInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class extending InputPartition that carries partitionId, numPartitions, startOffset, startTimestamp, endOffset and endTimestamp for one partition of a batch.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStreamReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Object extending PartitionReaderFactory. createReader casts the partition to RatePerMicroBatchStreamInputPartition and creates a RatePerMicroBatchStreamPartitionReader.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchStreamPartitionReader
nodes.summary: PartitionReader[InternalRow] for one partition. Row values are startOffset + partitionId + numPartitions * count, so partitions take interleaved values; next() is true while that value is below endOffset, and get() returns a row of (startTimestamp converted from millis to micros, value) and increments the counter. close() does nothing.

nodes.name: extractOffsetAndTimestamp
nodes.summary: Private helper that returns (offset, timestamp) from a RatePerMicroBatchStreamOffset and throws IllegalStateException for any other Offset type.

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Computes the end offset for a batch: start offset + rowsPerBatch (capped at Long.MaxValue) with the timestamp advanced by advanceMsPerBatch. When prepareForTriggerAvailableNow was called, the first result is stored and returned for all later calls. The ReadLimit argument is not used.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Creates the partitions of a batch from the start and end offsets. It throws SparkRuntimeException for a start offset past the end offset or a start timestamp past the end timestamp (the comment explains the restart with a new startingTimestamp case), returns an empty array if the offsets are equal, and otherwise one RatePerMicroBatchStreamInputPartition per partition index.

nodes.name: prepareForTriggerAvailableNow
nodes.summary: Sets the flag so that latestOffset returns one fixed end offset for the whole Trigger.AvailableNow run.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Casts the InputPartition to RatePerMicroBatchStreamInputPartition and returns a new RatePerMicroBatchStreamPartitionReader with its fields.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Computes the current value as startOffset + partitionId + numPartitions * count, advances count and returns InternalRow(timestamp in microseconds, value).

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStoreMap.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the in-memory map used by the HDFS backed state store: the HDFSBackedStateStoreMap trait with its companion factory, a plain implementation without prefix scan, and an implementation that also keeps a prefix-key index for prefixScan. Both are built on ConcurrentHashMap and verify values with an optional integrity verifier on read.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStoreMap
nodes.summary: Trait with size, get, put, putAll, remove, iterator, entryIterator (raw entries that skip the extra checks of iterator) and prefixScan. The companion object (lines 42 to 73) defines MapType (a ConcurrentHashMap from UnsafeRow to UnsafeRowWrapper, chosen because its iterators are weakly consistent and never throw ConcurrentModificationException), create(keySchema, numColsPrefixKey, readVerifier), which returns the prefix-scannable map when numColsPrefixKey > 0 and the plain one otherwise, and getAndVerifyValueRow.

nodes.name: NoPrefixHDFSBackedStateStoreMap
nodes.summary: Implementation backed by one MapType. get verifies the value row with the read verifier, putAll copies a map of the same class directly or entry by entry otherwise, iterator returns UnsafeRowPair values built from verified rows, and prefixScan throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: PrefixScannableHDFSBackedStateStoreMap
nodes.summary: Implementation that keeps the main MapType and a second ConcurrentHashMap from the prefix key (the first numColsPrefixKey columns of the key schema, projected with an UnsafeProjection) to the set of full keys. put and remove update both maps, putAll copies the prefix index sets so that two versions do not share set instances, and prefixScan returns the pairs of all keys for a prefix key with verified value rows.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Factory that returns PrefixScannableHDFSBackedStateStoreMap when numColsPrefixKey is above zero and NoPrefixHDFSBackedStateStoreMap otherwise.

nodes.name: getAndVerifyValueRow
nodes.summary: Returns null for a null wrapper; otherwise runs the optional read verifier on the key and wrapper and returns the unsafe row of the wrapper.

nodes.name: putAll
nodes.summary: Copies another map: with the same class it calls map.putAll on the inner map, otherwise it puts every entry of the other map one by one.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Maps each raw entry to a shared UnsafeRowPair holding the key and the verified value row.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Puts the value in the main map and adds the key to the set of its projected prefix key in the prefix index (creating the set if absent), returning the previous wrapper.

nodes.name: putAll
nodes.summary: For a map of the same class, copies the main map and puts a new copy of each key set into the prefix index; for other maps, puts entry by entry.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes the key from the main map and, if something was removed, removes it from its prefix key set and drops the set when it is empty.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Maps each raw entry to a shared UnsafeRowPair holding the key and the verified value row.

nodes.name: prefixScan
nodes.summary: Looks up the set of keys for the prefix key in the prefix index and returns an iterator of UnsafeRowPair values with verified value rows from the main map.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the test-oriented continuous-mode memory sink: ContinuousMemorySink, its Write, an RPC endpoint on the driver that collects rows as they arrive, and the StreamingWrite that wires the endpoint to executor-side writers.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemorySink
nodes.summary: In-memory sink for continuous (real-time) queries, intended for unit tests and with no durability. It extends MemorySink and mixes in SupportsWrite, advertising only TableCapability.STREAMING_WRITE. newWriteBuilder returns a WriteBuilder (with SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend) whose build() creates a ContinuousMemoryWrite over a shared ArrayBuffer of Rows. allData returns the buffered rows under a lock and clear empties the buffer. The batch-oriented methods inherited from MemorySink (latestBatchData, dataSinceBatch, write) throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException with error class UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION_FOR_CONTINUOUS_MEMORY_SINK, and latestBatchId returns None, because data is made available after each write rather than at commit.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns an anonymous WriteBuilder (also SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend) that remembers the input schema from LogicalWriteInfo and, on build(), returns a ContinuousMemoryWrite sharing this sink's row buffer.

nodes.name: allData
nodes.summary: Returns a snapshot (Seq) of all rows stored in the sink, copied while holding the buffer lock.

nodes.name: latestBatchData
nodes.summary: Overrides MemorySink.latestBatchData to throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException (UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION_FOR_CONTINUOUS_MEMORY_SINK, operation latestBatchData). dataSinceBatch (lines 89-94) and write (lines 100-105) throw the same error with their own operation names.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Synchronized method that empties the buffered rows.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryWrite
nodes.summary: A Write over the shared row buffer and the input schema. Its toStreaming method returns a new ContinuousMemoryStreamingWrite. Created by the write builder of ContinuousMemorySink.

nodes.name: toStreaming
nodes.summary: Returns a ContinuousMemoryStreamingWrite built from the buffer and schema.

nodes.name: MemoryRealTimeRpcEndpoint
nodes.summary: A ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint that runs on the driver. It builds a row deserializer from the schema (ExpressionEncoder resolved and bound) and, in receive, handles an Array[InternalRow] message by deserializing each row and appending it to the shared ArrayBuffer inside a synchronized block. Receives data sent by RealTimeRowWriter instances.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Message handler: for an Array[InternalRow] it appends each row, converted to a Row by the encoder, to the shared buffer in a synchronized block.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStreamingWrite
nodes.summary: StreamingWrite for the continuous memory sink. It creates a MemoryRealTimeRpcEndpoint over the buffer. createStreamingWriterFactory registers that endpoint under a unique MemoryRealTimeRpcEndpoint-<uuid> name on the driver RpcEnv and returns a RealTimeRowWriterFactory pointing at it, so executors send rows straight to the driver. It does not use the commit coordinator, and both commit and abort only stop the registered endpoint reference.

nodes.name: createStreamingWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Registers the MemoryRealTimeRpcEndpoint on the driver RpcEnv under a UUID-based name and returns a RealTimeRowWriterFactory holding that name and the endpoint address.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Stops the registered endpoint (if any); no data is committed because rows were already delivered.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Stops the registered endpoint (if any) on abort.

nodes.name: RealTimeRowWriterFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RealTimeRowWriterFactory and RealTimeRowWriter, which send rows from executor tasks to a driver RPC endpoint as they are written; intended for tests only.

nodes.name: RealTimeRowWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Case class StreamingDataWriterFactory holding the driver endpoint name and RpcAddress. createWriter ignores partition, task and epoch ids and returns a RealTimeRowWriter. The source notes it is unsuitable for production sinks because all rows go to the driver. Used by ContinuousMemoryStreamingWrite.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a RealTimeRowWriter for the given endpoint name and address.

nodes.name: RealTimeRowWriter
nodes.summary: DataWriter[InternalRow] that resolves a driver endpoint reference with RpcUtils.makeDriverRef and, for every write, sends an array holding a copy of the row (Spark reuses the row instance) to that endpoint. commit returns null, and abort and close do nothing.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Copies the (reused) InternalRow and sends it to the driver endpoint as a one-element array.

nodes.name: ConsoleStreamingWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ConsoleWrite, the StreamingWrite used by the console sink: executors pack rows into commit messages and the driver prints them as a table for each epoch.

nodes.name: ConsoleWrite
nodes.summary: Common StreamingWrite for the console sink. It reads the options numRows (default 20) and truncate (default true) from CaseInsensitiveStringMap and requires an active SparkSession. createStreamingWriterFactory returns PackedRowWriterFactory, so tasks only collect rows. commit prints a 'Batch: <epochId>' header via printRows, which gathers the rows from the PackedRowCommitMessages, wraps them in a LocalRelation and calls show(numRows, truncate) on the resulting Dataset. It does not use the commit coordinator and abort does nothing.

nodes.name: createStreamingWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Returns the PackedRowWriterFactory object, so each task buffers its rows into a commit message.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Called once per epoch on the driver; prints the epoch using the label 'Batch: <epochId>' (kept for compatibility with the pre data source V2 behavior) by delegating to printRows.

nodes.name: printRows
nodes.summary: Collects rows from PackedRowCommitMessage instances, prints a banner and the message, then builds a Dataset from a LocalRelation and shows it with the configured row count and truncation.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryListenerBus.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingQueryListenerBus, which posts streaming query events to the Spark listener bus and dispatches them to registered StreamingQueryListeners for the queries of one SparkSession.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryListenerBus
nodes.summary: A SparkListener and ListenerBus[StreamingQueryListener, StreamingQueryListener.Event] tied to one SparkSession and its StreamingQueryManager. When given a LiveListenerBus it registers itself on the queue named by the companion constant STREAM_EVENT_QUERY ("streams"); with None it acts as a replay bus (used when rebuilding the streaming UI from event logs). It tracks the runIds of active queries in a hash set so events for queries from other sessions are ignored. post sends QueryStartedEvent to the Spark bus and to local listeners synchronously and all other events to the Spark bus; postToAll removes a runId only after the QueryTerminatedEvent was delivered; onOtherEvent receives events back from the Spark bus; doPostEvent calls onQueryStarted, onQueryProgress, onQueryIdle or onQueryTerminated on a listener when the event's runId should be reported. The companion object only holds the constant STREAM_EVENT_QUERY (lines 150-152).

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Entry point used by queries: a QueryStartedEvent registers its runId, is posted to the Spark listener bus and is delivered to local listeners at once via postToAll; every other event is only posted to the Spark listener bus.

nodes.name: postToAll
nodes.summary: Calls the parent postToAll, then drops the runId of a QueryTerminatedEvent from the active set so the terminated query is cleared only after all listeners handled it (SPARK-19594).

nodes.name: onOtherEvent
nodes.summary: SparkListener callback for events coming back from the Spark bus. It forwards StreamingQueryListener events to postToAll, skipping QueryStartedEvent when running in the live listener thread (SPARK-18144) because that event was already delivered synchronously; with no live bus (replay) it forwards all.

nodes.name: doPostEvent
nodes.summary: Delivers one event to one StreamingQueryListener by event type (started, progress, idle, terminated), but only if shouldReport finds the runId among active queries or the bus is a replay bus.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the in-memory source for continuous processing tests: ContinuousMemoryStream with its companion factories, input partition, reader factory, partition reader and offset class.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStream
nodes.summary: Test source that keeps a list of UnsafeRow records per partition (numPartitions, default 2). addData spreads new items round-robin over the partitions and returns a ContinuousMemoryStreamOffset of per-partition record counts. It extends MemoryStreamBase and implements ContinuousStream. planInputPartitions registers a ContinuousRecordEndpoint on the driver RpcEnv under a unique name and builds one ContinuousMemoryStreamInputPartition per partition; executor readers poll that endpoint. initialOffset is all zeros; deserializeOffset and the offset class use json4s JSON; mergeOffsets turns ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset values into one offset; stop stops the endpoint. The companion object (lines 115-145) holds an AtomicInteger id counter and apply / singlePartition factories taking a SQLContext or SparkSession, with or without a partition count.

nodes.name: addData
nodes.summary: Synchronized. Copies each item, converted to an UnsafeRow, into the partition list chosen by index modulo numPartitions, then returns a ContinuousMemoryStreamOffset holding the size of every partition list.

nodes.name: deserializeOffset
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON map of partition to count into a ContinuousMemoryStreamOffset using json4s Serialization.

nodes.name: mergeOffsets
nodes.summary: Builds a ContinuousMemoryStreamOffset from an array of PartitionOffset values, each matched as a ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset (partition, count).

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Under the lock, registers the record endpoint on the driver RpcEnv with a name containing a random UUID and the stream id, then returns one ContinuousMemoryStreamInputPartition (endpoint name, partition, start index) per entry of the start offset.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory overloads (lines 119-136) that create a ContinuousMemoryStream with the next id from an AtomicInteger, given an implicit SQLContext or an explicit SparkSession, optionally with a numPartitions argument. This node covers the overload that takes numPartitions and an implicit SQLContext.

nodes.name: singlePartition
nodes.summary: Companion factory overloads (lines 138-144) that create a ContinuousMemoryStream with exactly one partition, from an implicit SQLContext or an explicit SparkSession.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStreamInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition carrying the driver endpoint name, the partition number and the start index to read from. Built by ContinuousMemoryStream.planInputPartitions.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStreamReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Object ContinuousPartitionReaderFactory whose createReader casts the partition to ContinuousMemoryStreamInputPartition and returns a ContinuousMemoryStreamPartitionReader.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Creates the partition reader from the endpoint name, partition and start offset stored in the input partition.

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStreamPartitionReader
nodes.summary: ContinuousPartitionReader[InternalRow] run in executor tasks. It looks up the driver endpoint with RpcUtils.makeDriverRef and fails with IllegalStateException if no TaskContext is set. next asks the endpoint for the record at the current offset (GetRecord message) and sleeps 10 ms between polls until one exists, then advances; getOffset returns a ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset for the current position.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Blocking read: polls getRecord every 10 ms until a record exists at the current offset, then increments the offset and returns true.

nodes.name: getRecord
nodes.summary: Private helper doing a synchronous RPC askSync with GetRecord(ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset(partition, currentOffset)), returning an Option[InternalRow].

nodes.name: ContinuousMemoryStreamOffset
nodes.summary: Case class Offset wrapping a Map from partition number to record count; json() serializes the map with json4s. Used as initial, latest and merged offset of ContinuousMemoryStream.

nodes.name: ForeachBatchSink.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ForeachBatchSink, which hands each micro-batch to a user function, along with the exception wrapper for errors in that function and a trait and helper for calling a Python foreachBatch function.

nodes.name: ForeachBatchSink
nodes.summary: A Sink created from a batch function (Dataset[T], Long) => Unit and an ExpressionEncoder[T]. addBatch turns the batch's queryExecution.toRdd into a non-streaming LogicalRDD (LogicalRDD.fromDataset), builds a typed Dataset from it and calls the user function through callBatchWriter. The code comment (SPARK-47329) leaves persisting the batch to the user when several actions run on it. callBatchWriter wraps any non-fatal exception that is not a SparkThrowable into ForeachBatchUserFuncException.

nodes.name: addBatch
nodes.summary: Converts the batch DataFrame to a non-streaming Dataset[T] backed by its RDD and invokes the user function with the batch id.

nodes.name: callBatchWriter
nodes.summary: Runs the user batch function and rethrows non-fatal, non-SparkThrowable exceptions as ForeachBatchUserFuncException.

nodes.name: ForeachBatchUserFuncException
nodes.summary: Private[sql] case class extending SparkException with error class FOREACH_BATCH_USER_FUNCTION_ERROR; its message parameter 'reason' is the cause's message. Wraps errors thrown by the user function of a foreachBatch sink.

nodes.name: PythonForeachBatchFunction
nodes.summary: Trait with one method, call(batchDF: DataFrame, batchId: Long). Per its doc comment it is meant to be extended by Python classes via Py4J so that the JVM can call back a user-defined Python foreachBatch function while the query is active.

nodes.name: PythonForeachBatchHelper
nodes.summary: Object whose callForeachBatch(dsw, pythonFunc) registers a foreachBatch handler on a DataStreamWriter[Row]; the handler converts the DataFrame with castToImpl and calls PythonForeachBatchFunction.call with the batch and its id.

nodes.name: callForeachBatch
nodes.summary: Calls dsw.foreachBatch with a lambda that casts the DataFrame via castToImpl and delegates to pythonFunc.call(df, id).

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the memory source for real-time (low latency) mode tests: LowLatencyMemoryStream with its companion factories, input partition, reader factory, partition reader, offset class and a driver RPC endpoint that serves (row, timestamp) pairs.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStream
nodes.summary: Memory source for unit tests of real-time mode, similar to ContinuousMemoryStream but implementing SupportsRealTimeMode. It keeps, per partition, a list of (UnsafeRow, arrival timestamp) pairs; the timestamp comes from an injectable Clock (default LowLatencyClock.getClock). addData spreads rows round-robin, an overload targets one partition (checked by require), and both return a LowLatencyMemoryStreamOffset of per-partition sizes. latestOffset returns current sizes. Two planInputPartitions overloads register a LowLatencyMemoryStreamEndpoint on the driver and create input partitions, with end index Int.MaxValue or taken from an end offset. createReaderFactory returns a LowLatencyMemoryStreamReaderFactory, and reset clears all lists after calling the parent. The companion object (lines 191-224) has apply and singlePartition factories.

nodes.name: addData
nodes.summary: Overload taking a partition id (the node covers this one; the no-partition overload is at lines 86-97). Validates the id, then appends each item with the clock timestamp to that partition and returns the offset of per-partition sizes. The no-partition overload distributes rows by numRecords modulo numPartitions.

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Synchronized; returns a LowLatencyMemoryStreamOffset with the current record count of each partition list, ignoring the start offset and read limit.

nodes.name: mergeOffsets
nodes.summary: Builds a LowLatencyMemoryStreamOffset from ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset values.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Overload with start and end offsets (the node covers this one; the single-offset overload is at lines 136-153 and uses Int.MaxValue as end). Registers the record endpoint under a name made from a UUID and the stream id and returns one LowLatencyMemoryStreamInputPartition per partition, with the end index taken from the end offset.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Calls the parent reset and clears every partition list.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory overloads (lines 194-215) creating a LowLatencyMemoryStream with the next id from an AtomicInteger, from an implicit SQLContext or a SparkSession, optionally with numPartitions. This node covers the SQLContext overload with numPartitions.

nodes.name: singlePartition
nodes.summary: Companion factory overloads (lines 217-223) creating a single-partition LowLatencyMemoryStream from an implicit SQLContext or a SparkSession.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStreamInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition with driver endpoint name and address, partition number, start offset and end offset.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStreamReaderFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionReaderFactory taking a Clock; createReader casts the partition to LowLatencyMemoryStreamInputPartition and creates a LowLatencyMemoryStreamPartitionReader with the endpoint info, offsets and clock.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Builds the partition reader from the fields of the input partition plus the clock.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStreamPartitionReader
nodes.summary: SupportsRealTimeRead[InternalRow] reader that polls the driver endpoint for (row, timestamp) pairs. It requires a TaskContext. nextWithTimeout polls every 10 ms until a record arrives or the timeout (measured with the clock from the caller's start time, SPARK-55699) expires, returning a RecordStatus with or without arrival time. next is a single non-blocking attempt. getRecordWithTimestamp returns None once the current offset reaches the end offset, otherwise it asks the endpoint with GetRecord.

nodes.name: nextWithTimeout
nodes.summary: Polls for a record until one is found or the timeout elapses; returns RecordStatus.newStatusWithArrivalTimeMs with the stored timestamp, or a status without arrival time (false) on timeout.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Single attempt to fetch the record at the current offset; advances the offset and returns true if present, otherwise false.

nodes.name: getRecordWithTimestamp
nodes.summary: Private helper: returns None if the current offset is at or beyond the end offset, otherwise a synchronous askSync with GetRecord for the (row, timestamp) option.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStreamOffset
nodes.summary: Case class Offset wrapping a Map from partition number to record count, serialized to JSON with json4s.

nodes.name: LowLatencyMemoryStreamEndpoint
nodes.summary: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint on the driver that answers GetRecord(ContinuousRecordPartitionOffset) requests with an Option of (UnsafeRow, timestamp) for the requested partition and index, or None if not yet available; the lookup runs under a shared lock object.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles GetRecord messages: under the lock it replies with the record at the requested offset in the requested partition list, or None when the list is shorter.

nodes.name: MicroBatchWrite.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MicroBatchWrite and MicroBatchWriterFactory, which present a streaming write to micro-batch plans through the batch write interfaces with a fixed epoch id.

nodes.name: MicroBatchWrite
nodes.summary: BatchWrite adapter used to hook V2 stream writers into a micro-batch plan. It is constructed with an epoch id and a wrapped StreamingWrite (writeSupport) and forwards useCommitCoordinator, commit(messages) and abort(messages) to the streaming write with that epoch id. createBatchWriterFactory wraps the streaming writer factory in a MicroBatchWriterFactory.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Calls writeSupport.commit(epochId, messages).

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Calls writeSupport.abort(epochId, messages).

nodes.name: createBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Returns a MicroBatchWriterFactory built from the epoch id and the factory the streaming write creates.

nodes.name: MicroBatchWriterFactory
nodes.summary: DataWriterFactory that holds an epoch id and a StreamingDataWriterFactory; createWriter(partitionId, taskId) calls the streaming factory with the stored epoch id.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Delegates to streamingWriterFactory.createWriter(partitionId, taskId, epochId).

nodes.name: PackedRowWriterFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a simple writer path that buffers rows in each task and returns them to the driver inside a commit message: PackedRowWriterFactory, PackedRowCommitMessage and PackedRowDataWriter; used for tests and the console sink.

nodes.name: PackedRowWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Case object StreamingDataWriterFactory whose createWriter returns a new PackedRowDataWriter, ignoring partition, task and epoch ids. The source says all rows go to the driver, so it is unsuitable for production sinks and intended for tests. ConsoleWrite uses it.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Returns a new PackedRowDataWriter.

nodes.name: PackedRowCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Case class WriterCommitMessage holding the array of InternalRows written by a PackedRowDataWriter in the most recent interval.

nodes.name: PackedRowDataWriter
nodes.summary: DataWriter[InternalRow] that appends a copy of every row (Spark reuses the row instance) to a buffer; commit returns a PackedRowCommitMessage with the buffered rows, and close clears the buffer. abort does nothing.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Appends a copy of the row to the buffer.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Returns a PackedRowCommitMessage holding the buffered rows as an array.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the 'rate-micro-batch' streaming source: a provider that validates options, a table exposing micro-batch reads, and a companion with the schema and option names. It produces a fixed set of rows per micro-batch regardless of trigger timing.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchProvider
nodes.summary: Registered under the short name "rate-micro-batch" (DataSourceRegister) and built on SimpleTableProvider. getTable reads and validates the options rowsPerBatch (must be positive), numPartitions (default is the active session's default parallelism, must be positive), startTimestamp (must not be negative) and advanceMillisPerBatch (default 1000, must not be negative), throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise, and returns a RatePerMicroBatchTable. Per its doc comment, unlike the 'rate' source it yields the same rows in each micro-batch regardless of trigger or lag (batch 0 gives 0 to 999, batch 1 gives 1000 to 1999) and supports only micro-batch reads. The companion object (lines 121-131) holds SCHEMA (timestamp: TimestampType, value: LongType), VERSION = 1 and the option name constants.

nodes.name: RatePerMicroBatchTable
nodes.summary: Table with SupportsRead whose only capability is MICRO_BATCH_READ and whose schema is RatePerMicroBatchProvider.SCHEMA. newScanBuilder returns a Scan whose toMicroBatchStream creates a RatePerMicroBatchStream with the configured options; toContinuousStream throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (_LEGACY_ERROR_TEMP_3167) and columnar support is UNSUPPORTED.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Validates the four options of the rate-micro-batch source and returns a RatePerMicroBatchTable built from them; an invalid value raises IllegalArgumentException naming the option.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder lambda producing a Scan that creates a RatePerMicroBatchStream for micro-batch mode and rejects continuous mode.

nodes.name: RateStreamMicroBatchStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the micro-batch implementation of the 'rate' source: RateStreamMicroBatchStream plus its input partition, reader factory and partition reader. Rows are generated from time elapsed since a start time stored in the checkpoint.

nodes.name: RateStreamMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: MicroBatchStream for the rate source, built from rowsPerSecond, rampUpTimeSeconds, numPartitions, options and the checkpoint location. It picks a ManualClock when the option useManualClock is true (tests) and a SystemClock otherwise, and rejects a ramp-up time longer than Long.MaxValue / rowsPerSecond. creationTimeMs is read from, or first written to, an HDFSMetadataLog[LongOffset] at batch 0 under the checkpoint location, with a versioned text format. Offsets are LongOffset values counting seconds since creation: latestOffset advances lastTimeMs to the clock and returns the elapsed seconds. planInputPartitions converts the seconds range to a value range with RateStreamProvider.valueAtSecond and creates one RateStreamMicroBatchInputPartition per partition (an empty array if the range is empty).

nodes.name: latestOffset
nodes.summary: Moves lastTimeMs forward to the current clock time if it is behind and returns a LongOffset of the whole seconds elapsed since creationTimeMs.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Asserts start <= end, checks the end offset against the maximum seconds, repairs lastTimeMs after recovery, computes the value range for the two offsets with valueAtSecond and returns one RateStreamMicroBatchInputPartition per partition carrying range bounds, local start time and milliseconds per value.

nodes.name: RateStreamMicroBatchInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition carrying partitionId, numPartitions, the value range (rangeStart, rangeEnd), the local start time in ms and the relative ms per value.

nodes.name: RateStreamMicroBatchReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Object PartitionReaderFactory whose createReader casts the partition to RateStreamMicroBatchInputPartition and returns a RateStreamMicroBatchPartitionReader.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Creates the partition reader from the fields of the input partition.

nodes.name: RateStreamMicroBatchPartitionReader
nodes.summary: PartitionReader[InternalRow] that emits the values rangeStart + partitionId + numPartitions * count while that value is below rangeEnd. Each row is (timestamp in microseconds, value), where the timestamp is the local start time plus the rounded relative offset of the value times relativeMsPerValue.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Computes the current value and its timestamp, increments the counter and returns an InternalRow of (microsecond timestamp, value).

nodes.name: RateStreamProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the 'rate' streaming source provider and table, which support both micro-batch and continuous reads, and the companion helper valueAtSecond that computes how many rows should exist after a given number of seconds.

nodes.name: RateStreamProvider
nodes.summary: Registered under the short name "rate" (DataSourceRegister) via SimpleTableProvider. getTable validates the options rowsPerSecond (default 1, must be positive), rampUpTime (default 0s, parsed with JavaUtils.timeStringAsSec, must not be negative) and numPartitions (default parallelism, must be positive) and returns a RateStreamTable. The companion object (lines 109-142) defines SCHEMA (timestamp, value), VERSION, the option names and valueAtSecond(seconds, rowsPerSecond, rampUpTimeSeconds), which sums a linear speed ramp up to rowsPerSecond and then continues at a constant rate, with an ordering of the arithmetic to avoid overflow.

nodes.name: RateStreamTable
nodes.summary: Table with SupportsRead advertising MICRO_BATCH_READ and CONTINUOUS_READ. newScanBuilder returns a Scan that builds a RateStreamMicroBatchStream for micro-batch mode and a RateStreamContinuousStream for continuous mode; columnar support is UNSUPPORTED.

nodes.name: getTable
nodes.summary: Validates the rate source options and returns a RateStreamTable for them; invalid values raise IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: valueAtSecond
nodes.summary: Returns the end value (row count) emitted by a given second: the sum of a speed that grows by rowsPerSecond / (rampUpTimeSeconds + 1) each second up to the ramp-up time, then rowsPerSecond per second after it; recursive for the post-ramp part.

nodes.name: newScanBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a ScanBuilder lambda whose Scan creates the micro-batch or continuous stream for the rate source.

nodes.name: TextSocketMicroBatchStream.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the micro-batch reader for the text socket source and its input partition; it reads lines from a TCP socket on a background thread and is meant for tutorials and debugging only.

nodes.name: TextSocketMicroBatchStream
nodes.summary: MicroBatchStream (host, port, numPartitions) that, per its doc comment, is only for tutorials and debugging and does not support fault recovery. On first planInputPartitions it opens a Socket and starts a daemon thread that reads lines, stamps each with the current time in microseconds, appends them to an in-memory buffer and increments a LongOffset. planInputPartitions slices the buffer between two offsets (relative to the last committed offset) and spreads the lines round-robin over numPartitions TextSocketInputPartition objects. commit drops committed lines from the buffer and throws IllegalStateException if offsets are committed out of order. stop closes the socket, which is the only way to end the blocked reader thread.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Private, synchronized. Connects the socket and starts a daemon thread named TextSocketSource(host, port) that reads lines until the stream closes (logging a warning) and appends (line, timestamp) pairs to the buffer while advancing the current offset.

nodes.name: planInputPartitions
nodes.summary: Lazily initializes the socket on first use, slices the buffered lines between the start and end offsets and distributes them over numPartitions TextSocketInputPartition objects.

nodes.name: createReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Returns a PartitionReaderFactory (a lambda) whose readers iterate over the slice of one TextSocketInputPartition and return rows of (line, timestamp).

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Synchronized; removes batches up to the committed offset from the buffer and updates lastOffsetCommitted, failing if the new offset is behind the last committed one.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Closes the socket (ignoring IOException) so the reader thread ends, and clears the reference.

nodes.name: TextSocketInputPartition
nodes.summary: Case class InputPartition holding the slice (a ListBuffer of line and timestamp pairs) assigned to one partition.

nodes.name: WriteToMicroBatchDataSource.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WriteToMicroBatchDataSource, the logical plan node for writing a micro-batch stream to a DataSource V2 target.

nodes.name: WriteToMicroBatchDataSource
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryNode and V2StreamingWriteCommand holding the target relation, the query, queryId, writeOptions, outputMode and an optional batchId. It has no physical plan of its own: per its doc comment it is converted to WriteToDataSourceV2 with a MicroBatchWrite before execution. Its output is empty, its table is the relation, withNewTable swaps the relation, withNewBatchId sets the batch id, and withNewChildInternal replaces the query. For transactional catalogs the target is a V2TableReference resolved per batch, otherwise it is a pre-resolved DataSourceV2Relation.

nodes.name: withNewBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the node with batchId set.

nodes.name: WriteToMicroBatchDataSourceV1.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WriteToMicroBatchDataSourceV1, a marker logical node for a DSv1 sink at the top of a streaming query plan.

nodes.name: WriteToMicroBatchDataSourceV1
nodes.summary: Case class UnaryNode holding an optional CatalogTable, the Sink, the query, queryId, writeOptions, outputMode and an optional batchId. Per its doc comment it is a pass-through marker (its output equals the query output) because microbatch execution handles DSv1 sinks separately; it is removed in the streaming-specific optimization phase and has no physical node. withNewBatchId sets the batch id and withNewChildInternal replaces the query.

nodes.name: withNewBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the node with batchId set.

nodes.name: memory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the in-memory streaming sink used in tests and its write path: MemorySink, its Write, StreamingWrite, writer factory, data writer and commit message, plus MemoryPlan for querying the stored data.

nodes.name: MemorySink
nodes.summary: Table with SupportsWrite and STREAMING_WRITE capability that stores each committed batch as an AddedData(batchId, rows) entry in a synchronized buffer; meant for unit tests and without durability. newWriteBuilder returns a builder supporting truncate and SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend whose build() creates a MemoryWrite. Query methods: allData, latestBatchId, latestBatchData, dataSinceBatch and toDebugString. write(batchId, needTruncate, newRows) ignores a batch whose id is not newer than the latest stored one, otherwise appends it (after clearing when truncating). clear empties the buffer.

nodes.name: newWriteBuilder
nodes.summary: Returns a WriteBuilder with SupportsTruncate and SupportsStreamingUpdateAsAppend; truncate() sets a flag and build() creates a MemoryWrite with the sink, input schema and flag.

nodes.name: allData
nodes.summary: Returns all stored rows from all batches in order, under the sink lock.

nodes.name: dataSinceBatch
nodes.summary: Returns rows from batches with an id greater than the given id. Related accessors latestBatchId (81-83) and latestBatchData (85-87) return the newest batch's id and rows.

nodes.name: toDebugString
nodes.summary: Renders each stored batch as 'batchId: rows', guarding against rows that fail to convert to string.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Commits one batch: skips it if its id is not greater than the latest stored id, otherwise appends it, first clearing earlier batches when needTruncate is true.

nodes.name: MemoryWriterCommitMessage
nodes.summary: Case class WriterCommitMessage with a partition number and the Rows that partition wrote.

nodes.name: MemoryWrite
nodes.summary: Write over a MemorySink, a schema and a truncate flag; toStreaming returns a MemoryStreamingWrite.

nodes.name: MemoryStreamingWrite
nodes.summary: StreamingWrite for MemorySink. createStreamingWriterFactory returns a MemoryWriterFactory for the schema; it does not use the commit coordinator. commit flattens the rows of all MemoryWriterCommitMessages and passes them to sink.write(epochId, needTruncate, rows); abort accepts no new input.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Collects the rows from all MemoryWriterCommitMessages and hands them to MemorySink.write for the epoch.

nodes.name: MemoryWriterFactory
nodes.summary: Case class implementing both DataWriterFactory and StreamingDataWriterFactory for a schema; both createWriter overloads return a MemoryDataWriter, the epoch variant simply delegating to the other.

nodes.name: MemoryDataWriter
nodes.summary: DataWriter[InternalRow] that converts each InternalRow to a Row with a deserializer built from the schema and buffers it. commit returns a MemoryWriterCommitMessage with a copy of the buffered rows and clears the buffer; abort and close do nothing.

nodes.name: MemoryPlan
nodes.summary: Case class LeafNode used to query data written to a MemorySink. Its computeStats multiplies the estimated size per output row (EstimationUtils.getSizePerRow) by the current number of stored rows.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Returns Statistics whose size is the per-row size estimate times the number of rows stored in the sink.

nodes.name: AutoSnapshotLoader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AutoSnapshotLoader, an abstract helper that loads a state store snapshot version from the checkpoint directory and can automatically repair corrupt snapshots by falling back to earlier ones, plus SnapshotLoaderHelper for listing eligible snapshot versions.

nodes.name: AutoSnapshotLoader
nodes.summary: Abstract class (autoSnapshotRepairEnabled, numFailuresBeforeActivating, maxChangeFileReplay, loggingId) that subclasses fill in through hooks: beforeLoad, loadSnapshotFromCheckpoint (must throw on a corrupt snapshot and support version 0), onLoadSnapshotFromCheckpointFailure, getEligibleSnapshots and the optional getAdditionalEligibleSnapshots (default empty; V2 can enrich a sparse lineage). loadSnapshot(versionToLoad) sorts eligible (version, uniqueId) pairs newest first, always including version 0, and tries the newest one up to numFailuresBeforeActivating times (once if repair is off, failing at once). If that fails and repair is on, it tries older snapshots no more than maxChangeFileReplay versions below the requested one, logs each failure, and finally throws StateStoreErrors.autoSnapshotRepairFailed. It returns the loaded version and whether auto repair was used.

nodes.name: loadSnapshot
nodes.summary: Main algorithm: loads the latest eligible snapshot (retrying when repair is enabled), then on repeated failure walks older eligible snapshots within the maxChangeFileReplay limit, calling the beforeLoad, loadSnapshotFromCheckpoint and onLoadSnapshotFromCheckpointFailure hooks. Returns (loaded version, autoRepairCompleted) or throws autoSnapshotRepairFailed.

nodes.name: SnapshotLoaderHelper
nodes.summary: Object with getEligibleSnapshotsForVersion(version, fm, dfsPath, pathFilter, fileSuffix), which lists files in the checkpoint directory through a CheckpointFileManager, strips the suffix to get version numbers and keeps those not above the requested version; if the directory does not exist it returns Seq(0).

nodes.name: getEligibleSnapshotsForVersion
nodes.summary: Lists snapshot files under the given path, parses version numbers from the file names and returns those at or below the requested version, or Seq(0) when the path does not exist.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionErrors.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the error types raised by offline state repartitioning: a factory object plus an exception class hierarchy for invalid parameters (illegal argument errors) and invalid checkpoint states (illegal state errors). Each concrete class sets an error class of the form STATE_REPARTITION_INVALID_PARAMETER.<sub> or STATE_REPARTITION_INVALID_CHECKPOINT.<sub> and fills its message parameters.
nodes.languageNotes: The 14 factory methods of OfflineStateRepartitionErrors are one-line wrappers around constructors, so they have no function nodes of their own.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionErrors
nodes.summary: Factory object with one method per repartition failure: parameterIsEmptyError, parameterIsNotGreaterThanZeroError, parameterIsNullError, lastBatchAbandonedRepartitionError, lastBatchFailedError, missingOffsetSeqMetadataError, noBatchFoundError, noCommittedBatchError, offsetSeqNotFoundError, shufflePartitionsAlreadyMatchError, unsupportedOffsetSeqVersionError, unsupportedStateStoreProviderError, unsupportedStatefulOperatorError and unsupportedTransformWithStateVarTypeError. Each returns the matching exception object, typed as the invalid parameter or invalid checkpoint base class; the repartition runner throws these.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionInvalidParameterError
nodes.summary: Abstract base for errors about a bad argument given to the repartition operation. Extends SparkIllegalArgumentException with error class STATE_REPARTITION_INVALID_PARAMETER.<subClass> and always adds a 'parameter' message parameter.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionParameterIsEmptyError
nodes.summary: Exception for an invalid repartition parameter, using sub error class IS_EMPTY.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionParameterIsNotGreaterThanZeroError
nodes.summary: Exception for an invalid repartition parameter, using sub error class IS_NOT_GREATER_THAN_ZERO.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionParameterIsNullError
nodes.summary: Exception for an invalid repartition parameter, using sub error class IS_NULL.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionInvalidCheckpointError
nodes.summary: Abstract base for errors raised when the checkpoint location is in a state that cannot be repartitioned. Extends SparkIllegalStateException with error class STATE_REPARTITION_INVALID_CHECKPOINT.<subClass> and always adds a 'checkpointLocation' message parameter.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionLastBatchAbandonedRepartitionError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class LAST_BATCH_ABANDONED_REPARTITION, raised when the last batch is an unfinished repartition batch that used a different shuffle partition count than requested.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionLastBatchFailedError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class LAST_BATCH_FAILED, raised when the last batch did not commit and skipping it is not allowed.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionMissingOffsetSeqMetadataError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class MISSING_OFFSET_SEQ_METADATA, raised when an offset log entry has no metadata.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionNoBatchFoundError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class NO_BATCH_FOUND, raised when the offset log has no batch.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionNoCommittedBatchError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class NO_COMMITTED_BATCH, raised when the commit log has no committed batch.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionOffsetSeqNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class OFFSET_SEQ_NOT_FOUND, raised when the offset log entry of a batch is missing.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionShufflePartitionsAlreadyMatchError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class SHUFFLE_PARTITIONS_ALREADY_MATCH, raised when the last committed batch already uses the requested partition count.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionUnsupportedOffsetSeqVersionError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class UNSUPPORTED_OFFSET_SEQ_VERSION, raised when the offset log version is not supported.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionUnsupportedProviderError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER, raised when the state store provider class is not supported.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionUnsupportedStatefulOperatorError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class UNSUPPORTED_STATEFUL_OPERATOR, raised when a stateful operator is not supported.

nodes.name: StateRepartitionUnsupportedTransformWithStateVarTypeError
nodes.summary: Invalid checkpoint exception with sub error class UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM_WITH_STATE_VARIABLE_TYPE, raised when a transformWithState variable type (with its ttlEnabled flag and column family name) is not supported.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Holds OfflineStateRepartitionRunner, which repartitions the state stores of a stopped streaming query to a new partition count. It adds a new offset log batch N+1 with an updated shuffle partition setting, rewrites the state of batch N through a StateRewriter, updates operator metadata, and commits the batch.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionRunner
nodes.summary: Class that runs one repartition pass over a checkpoint location, given a SparkSession, the checkpoint path, the new partition count and an enforceExactlyOnceSink flag (default true). The run method returns the id of the new repartition batch; it picks or retries the batch, rewrites state with a repartition on 'partition_key', writes updated operator metadata and appends a commit.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Public entry point. Gets the last committed and last batch ids, creates (or reuses) the repartition batch, runs a StateRewriter that repartitions the state DataFrame by 'partition_key' into numPartitions, updates operator metadata, commits the batch, logs timing and returns the new batch id. Failures are logged and rethrown.

nodes.name: getLastCommittedBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns the latest batch id in the commit log, or throws noCommittedBatchError when none exists.

nodes.name: getLastBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns the latest batch id in the offset log, or throws noBatchFoundError when the offset log is empty.

nodes.name: createNewBatchIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Decides which batch id to use. If the last batch is committed, a new one is created. If the last batch is an uncommitted repartition batch with the same partition count, it is retried; with a different count an error is thrown. For other uncommitted batches it throws when enforceExactlyOnceSink is set, otherwise it skips them and creates a new batch.

nodes.name: skipUncommittedBatches
nodes.summary: Writes an empty CommitMetadata to the commit log for every batch after the last committed one up to the last batch, throwing on concurrent log update, so those batches are treated as skipped.

nodes.name: createNewBatchFromLastCommitted
nodes.summary: Builds the offset log entry for batch lastBatchId+1 by copying the last committed OffsetSeq (v1) or OffsetMap (v2) and setting the SQLConf.SHUFFLE_PARTITIONS key to the new count. Throws if the entry or metadata is missing, if the count already matches, or if the log type is unsupported, and fails on concurrent offset log update.

nodes.name: updateNumPartitionsInOperatorMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads all operator state metadata of the read batch and, for OperatorStateMetadataV2 entries, rewrites it with numPartitions set on each state store info using a writer for the new batch id. Other metadata versions are skipped with a log message.

nodes.name: commitBatch
nodes.summary: Reads the commit entry of the last committed batch, derives a new commit with withStateUniqueIds(opIdToStateStoreCkptInfo), and appends it to the commit log for the new batch id; throws on concurrent update.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Small utility object for offline state repartitioning: detects whether a batch is a repartition batch by comparing shuffle partition settings with the previous batch, and reads the shuffle partition count from offset metadata.

nodes.name: OfflineStateRepartitionUtils
nodes.summary: Object with isRepartitionBatch and getShufflePartitions. Used by the repartition runner and other streaming components; reads the SQLConf.SHUFFLE_PARTITIONS key from OffsetSeqMetadataBase conf and queries an OffsetSeqLog.

nodes.name: isRepartitionBatch
nodes.summary: Returns true when the shuffle partition count in the given batch's offset metadata differs from the previous batch. Batch 0 always returns false; it uses require checks for negative ids and for missing batches or metadata.

nodes.name: getShufflePartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the SQLConf.SHUFFLE_PARTITIONS value from the metadata conf map as an optional Int.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadata.scala
nodes.summary: Defines operator state metadata for streaming state stores: store and operator info types, V1 and V2 metadata case classes, JSON read/write helpers, versioned readers and writers for the _metadata directory, a file manager that purges old V2 metadata files, and a test-oriented join properties case class.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses json4s Serialization with NoTypeHints and per-companion implicit formats and manifests. Several classes share names with companion objects (StateStoreMetadataV2, OperatorStateMetadataV1, OperatorStateMetadataV2), which map to one class node each.

nodes.name: StateStoreMetadata
nodes.summary: Trait describing one state store instance with storeName, numColsPrefixKey and numPartitions.

nodes.name: StateStoreMetadataV1
nodes.summary: Case class implementing StateStoreMetadata with storeName, numColsPrefixKey and numPartitions (version 1 layout).

nodes.name: StateStoreMetadataV2
nodes.summary: Case class implementing StateStoreMetadata (and Serializable) that adds stateSchemaFilePaths. The companion object (lines 61-67) defines private implicit json4s formats and a manifest for serialization.

nodes.name: OperatorInfo
nodes.summary: Trait with operatorId and operatorName of a stateful operator.

nodes.name: OperatorInfoV1
nodes.summary: Case class implementing OperatorInfo with operatorId and operatorName.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadata
nodes.summary: Trait for the persisted metadata of one operator: version, operatorInfo and stateStoresMetadata.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV1
nodes.summary: Version 1 operator metadata case class (operatorInfo plus an array of StateStoreMetadataV1). The companion object (lines 240-243) builds the path <stateCheckpointPath>/_metadata/metadata via metadataFilePath.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV2
nodes.summary: Version 2 operator metadata case class (operatorInfo, an array of StateStoreMetadataV2 and operatorPropertiesJson). The companion object (lines 245-257) provides metadataDirPath (_metadata/v2) and metadataFilePath(batchId) plus implicit json4s formats and manifest.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataUtils
nodes.summary: Object with the shared serialization helpers: readMetadata, writeMetadata, deserialize, serialize (version-dispatched JSON via json4s), plus getLastOffsetBatch and getLastCommittedBatch which open a read-only StreamingQueryCheckpointMetadata. It also declares the sealed reader and writer traits.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataReader
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with version and read() returning Option of OperatorStateMetadata.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataWriter
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with version and write(operatorMetadata).

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataReader
nodes.summary: Object with createReader, a factory that returns a V1 or V2 reader for the given version (and batchId, createMetadataDir) or throws for unknown versions.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataWriter
nodes.summary: Object with createWriter, a factory returning a V1 or V2 writer by version; version 2 requires a currentBatchId.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV1Writer
nodes.summary: Writer for version 1 metadata. Writes atomically to the single metadata file if it does not exist yet, creating the parent directory first.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV1Reader
nodes.summary: Reader for version 1 metadata, opening the single metadata file and reading it with OperatorStateMetadataUtils.readMetadata. Its comment says V2 metadata is read by the OperatorStateMetadataLog.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV2Writer
nodes.summary: Writer for version 2 metadata that targets the per-batch file <_metadata/v2>/<batchId>; skips writing if the file exists, otherwise creates it atomically.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV2Reader
nodes.summary: Reader for version 2 metadata. On construction it checks that the requested batchId is not past the last offset log entry, and may create the metadata directory (createMetadataDir). read() picks the latest metadata file whose batch id is at most the requested batch.

nodes.name: OperatorStateMetadataV2FileManager
nodes.summary: Manager for V2 metadata files of one stateful operator (takes checkpoint path, SparkSession and a StateStoreWriter). purgeMetadataFiles deletes metadata files older than the oldest batch kept in the commit log, always keeping the newest file below the threshold; schema file deletion is currently a no-op per the TODO comments.

nodes.name: StreamingJoinOperatorProperties
nodes.summary: Case class with useVirtualColumnFamilies whose json method renders it as compact JSON; per its comment it is used only by unit tests that check operator properties are non-empty in OperatorStateMetadataV2.

nodes.name: readMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads the version line from the stream (accepting up to version 2), checks it equals the expected version, deserializes the body and closes the stream.

nodes.name: writeMetadata
nodes.summary: Writes a 'v<version>' header line then the serialized metadata and closes the stream; on any failure logs, cancels the stream and rethrows.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Reads OperatorStateMetadataV1 or V2 JSON from a BufferedReader by version; throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Writes the metadata as JSON through json4s Serialization based on its version (1 or 2); throws for unknown versions.

nodes.name: getLastOffsetBatch
nodes.summary: Opens the checkpoint read-only and returns the id of the latest offset log entry, or throws StateDataSourceErrors.offsetLogUnavailable.

nodes.name: getLastCommittedBatch
nodes.summary: Opens the checkpoint read-only and returns the optional id of the latest commit log entry.

nodes.name: createReader
nodes.summary: Returns an OperatorStateMetadataV1Reader or V2Reader depending on version, or throws IllegalArgumentException for other versions.

nodes.name: createWriter
nodes.summary: Returns an OperatorStateMetadataV1Writer or V2Writer depending on version; version 2 needs currentBatchId, else IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Creates the metadata directory and atomically writes the metadata file unless it already exists.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Opens the V1 metadata file and reads it via OperatorStateMetadataUtils.readMetadata.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Creates the parent directory and atomically writes the V2 file for the current batch unless it exists.

nodes.name: listOffsets
nodes.summary: Lists numeric, non-hidden file names in the offsets directory of the checkpoint as a sorted array of batch ids; empty if the directory is missing.

nodes.name: listOperatorMetadataBatches
nodes.summary: Lists numeric file names in the operator metadata directory as sorted batch ids, or empty if the directories do not exist.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Finds the largest metadata batch id not above batchId, throws failedToReadOperatorMetadata if none, and reads that file.

nodes.name: isBatchFile
nodes.summary: True when the path name parses as a Long.

nodes.name: purgeMetadataFiles
nodes.summary: Finds the threshold batch id from the commit log, deletes older metadata files and then calls deleteSchemaFiles (currently a no-op).

nodes.name: findThresholdBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns the oldest batch on disk in the commit log, or 0.

nodes.name: deleteSchemaFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes schema files whose leading batch id (before an underscore) is at or below the threshold; returns early when the threshold is not positive.

nodes.name: deleteMetadataFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes metadata files with batch ids below the newest one at or under the threshold, and returns 0 (or -1 when nothing qualifies).

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Builds a JSON object with useVirtualColumnFamilies and renders it compactly.

nodes.name: RocksDB.scala
nodes.summary: Wraps a native RocksDB instance as a versioned key-value state store for streaming. The RocksDB class supports load(version), put/get/merge/remove/deleteRange, prefix and range scans, commit that snapshots or writes a changelog to DFS, rollback, maintenance and metrics. The file also holds RocksDBConf (the settings read from the store conf), RocksDBMetrics, the local to DFS file mapping and the lineage manager used with checkpoint ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object; the native library is used through Java wrapper objects (ReadOptions, WriteOptions, Options) imported from org.rocksdb.

nodes.name: RocksDBOpType
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class naming the RocksDB operations that can acquire or release the instance lock. Each subtype only carries a name string returned by toString.

nodes.name: LoadStore
nodes.summary: Case object of RocksDBOpType with the name "load_store", marking one kind of operation that takes the RocksDB instance lock.

nodes.name: RollbackStore
nodes.summary: Case object of RocksDBOpType with the name "rollback_store", marking one kind of operation that takes the RocksDB instance lock.

nodes.name: CloseStore
nodes.summary: Case object of RocksDBOpType with the name "close_store", marking one kind of operation that takes the RocksDB instance lock.

nodes.name: ReportStoreMetrics
nodes.summary: Case object of RocksDBOpType with the name "report_store_metrics", marking one kind of operation that takes the RocksDB instance lock.

nodes.name: StoreTaskCompletionListener
nodes.summary: Case object of RocksDBOpType with the name "store_task_completion_listener", marking one kind of operation that takes the RocksDB instance lock.

nodes.name: RocksDB
nodes.summary: Class that holds one native RocksDB instance and checkpoints each committed version to DFS; it is not thread-safe. It opens the DB with options built from RocksDBConf, loads a version (snapshot plus changelog replay, optionally with checkpoint ids and lineage), serves put, get, multiGet, merge, remove, deleteRange, iterator, prefixScan and rangeScan, tracks virtual column families and key counts, and commits, rolls back, runs maintenance, uploads snapshots and reports metrics and memory use. The companion object (lines 2441-2501) has prefixUpperBound, mainMemorySources, the RocksDBSnapshot case class and helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object shares this class id. Anonymous subclasses of AutoSnapshotLoader, NextIterator and the native Logger are created inside methods and have no separate nodes.

nodes.name: createColFamilyIfAbsent
nodes.summary: Creates a virtual column family with the next id if the name is not yet registered, and marks that a snapshot must be forced. Returns the existing id when it already exists. The isInternal flag separates internal families such as secondary indexes from user-facing ones.

nodes.name: removeColFamilyIfExists
nodes.summary: Removes a column family if present: forces a snapshot, deletes every key of that family through its iterator and remove calls, and drops it from the id and name maps. Returns whether the family existed.

nodes.name: getFullLineage
nodes.summary: Builds the lineage (version and checkpoint unique id pairs) from startVersion to endVersion by walking backwards through lineage stored in changelog files. It throws an invalid checkpoint lineage error if progress stops or the result does not start and end at the right versions or is not increasing by one.

nodes.name: loadWithCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Loads a version when state store checkpoint ids are used. It handles the empty-store case, version 0, and the normal path that builds a sparse or changelog-based lineage, loads a snapshot through loadSnapshotWithCheckpointId and replays changelogs up to the target version. It then resets ids, lineage and key counts and creates a changelog writer for the next version when changelog checkpointing is on and the load is not read-only.

nodes.name: loadWithoutCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Loads a version when no checkpoint id is used: it closes the DB, loads the latest snapshot via loadSnapshotWithoutCheckpointId (or an empty store), replays changelog files from the snapshot version to the target and updates key counts and metrics. It also creates a changelog writer for the next version if enabled and not read-only.

nodes.name: loadSnapshotWithoutCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Creates an AutoSnapshotLoader (an anonymous subclass) that loads a snapshot from DFS, opens the local DB, reports the snapshot version to the coordinator, and can fall back to older snapshots when auto repair is allowed. Records whether a repair was performed and returns the loaded snapshot version.

nodes.name: loadSnapshotWithCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Checkpoint-id aware snapshot loading with auto repair. The anonymous AutoSnapshotLoader checks that the working lineage covers the versions to replay, loads the snapshot, and can enrich the lineage with getFullLineage to find older snapshots. Returns the lineage to assign to the current version.

nodes.name: openLocalRocksDB
nodes.summary: Initializes column family info from the checkpoint metadata, opens the native DB and recreates the default column family when column families are in use. It then sets the key counts from metadata, or counts keys when the snapshot lacks them, and discards counting when row tracking is off.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Public entry point that loads a given version (optionally with a checkpoint id, read-only or empty). It picks loadWithCheckpointId or loadWithoutCheckpointId, records the load time in loadMetrics and refreshes memory usage. Returns this instance.

nodes.name: loadFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Loads from a given snapshot version and applies changelog records up to an end version; the instance is meant to be read-only and is used for the State Data Source per the doc comment. Updates load metrics and reports the snapshot version to the coordinator.

nodes.name: replayFromCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Loads the snapshot checkpoint from DFS, rebuilds column family maps, opens the DB, sets key counts and replays changelogs to the end version. When an end checkpoint id is given it uses getFullLineage to find the versions and ids to replay.

nodes.name: replayChangelog
nodes.summary: Reads each changelog file for the given versions and unique ids and applies its records to the local DB: put, delete, merge and delete-range records, with optional checksum verification for each record. Records the replay duration and the number of replayed files in loadMetrics.

nodes.name: verifyChangelogRecord
nodes.summary: Verifies one changelog record with the row checksum verifier without copying bytes; for values it checks the checksum on the value side and for deletes it checks the key only.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the value for a key or null, including uncommitted writes. If row checksums are enabled the value is decoded and verified.

nodes.name: multiGet
nodes.summary: Looks up many keys in one call using the native multiGetAsList. Keys are given the column family prefix when needed, and values are decoded and verified when row checksums are enabled; missing keys give null.

nodes.name: keyExists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a key exists using the native keyExists call, with a column family prefix when needed. The doc says it gives a 100% guarantee of a correct result.

nodes.name: getMergedValues
nodes.summary: Returns the values stored by merge operations for a key as an iterator of index ranges, so each value can be read without copying. Only allowed when row checksum is enabled.

nodes.name: handleMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Updates the count of keys on the writing version (internal or user keys by column family) on a put, merge or remove. It reads the old value first and only changes the count if the key was newly added or really removed; it does nothing when total row tracking is off.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Puts a value for a key into the native DB with the write options (WAL disabled) and records it in the changelog writer. It adds the column family prefix and, when enabled, a row checksum, and updates key-count metrics. Not durable until commit().

nodes.name: getListValuesInArrayByte
nodes.summary: Packs a list of value rows into one byte array separated by the merge delimiter, adding checksums when needed, so more values can be merged later.

nodes.name: putList
nodes.summary: Puts a list of values for one key as a single delimited byte array built by getListValuesInArrayByte, and records it in the changelog.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Appends a value to the current list of values of a key using the native merge operation (read-modify-write), adds prefix and checksum when needed, updates metrics and logs the merge in the changelog.

nodes.name: mergeList
nodes.summary: Like merge but appends several values at once, packing them with getListValuesInArrayByte.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Deletes a key from the native DB, handling column family prefix and checksum-bearing keys from changelog replay, updating key-count metrics and writing a delete record to the changelog (with a key checksum when enabled).

nodes.name: deleteRange
nodes.summary: Deletes all keys in [beginKey, endKey) with the native deleteRange and writes a delete-range record to the changelog. includesPrefix is true during changelog replay to avoid double encoding. A TODO notes that metrics are not updated yet.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns a NextIterator over all committed and uncommitted key-value pairs, reusing one ByteArrayPair, decoding the column family prefix and verifying checksums, and closing the native iterator on task completion. Another overload (lines 1646-1653) takes a column family name and uses prefixScan with an empty prefix.

nodes.name: countKeys
nodes.summary: Scans the whole DB and counts keys, split into user and internal keys when column families are used. Used when a snapshot has no stored key counts.

nodes.name: prefixScan
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over key-value pairs whose key starts with a prefix in a column family, using an upper bound from RocksDB.prefixUpperBound for the native iterator. Closes the iterator and read options on completion or task end.

nodes.name: rangeScan
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over key-value pairs in [startKey, endKey) for a column family, with optional bounds; when no end key is given the upper bound is the end of the column family prefix.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits the writes as a new version: optionally creates a snapshot (when enough deltas passed or a snapshot is forced), writes the changelog and queues or uploads the snapshot, updates checkpoint ids and lineage, sets the max seen version and records metrics. Returns the new version and StateStoreCheckpointInfo; on failure it invalidates the loaded version.

nodes.name: shouldCreateSnapshot
nodes.summary: Tells whether a snapshot is due: with changelog checkpointing it compares the new version with lastSnapshotVersion against minDeltasForSnapshot; without it, always true.

nodes.name: createSnapshot
nodes.summary: Flushes the DB (WAL is off), optionally compacts, creates a native checkpoint in a temp dir, builds the file mapping with RocksDBFileMapping.createSnapshotFileMapping and returns a RocksDBSnapshot with timing metrics for flush, compact and checkpoint.

nodes.name: uploadSnapshot
nodes.summary: Private helper that uploads a snapshot with fileManager.saveCheckpointToDfs, removes it from the pending upload set, truncates the lineage, updates lastUploadedSnapshotVersion and reports the upload to the coordinator; the snapshot is closed afterwards. A package-private overload at lines 2015-2022 passes the instance fields and stores the returned file manager metrics.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: Drops uncommitted changes: restores key counts, invalidates the loaded version and checkpoint ids, clears lineage and aborts and resets the changelog writer.

nodes.name: doMaintenance
nodes.summary: Maintenance step: uploads only the most recent queued snapshot (optionally replacing stale reused files first) when changelog checkpointing is on, then deletes old versions through the file manager with the configured retention settings.

nodes.name: replaceStaleReusedFilesInSnapshot
nodes.summary: Replaces files in a snapshot that were reused from versions old enough to be deleted by another executor maintenance with new DFS files to upload. Refers to SPARK-55892 in the comments.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Releases all resources: closes the DB and the native options, statistics and logger, closes the cache when memory is not bounded, closes queued snapshots, unregisters from RocksDBMemoryManager, deletes the local root dir and closes the file manager.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Builds a RocksDBMetrics object: key counts, memory usage via RocksDBMemoryManager, SST file bytes, native histograms for get, put and compaction, native tickers such as cache hit and miss counts, commit and load latencies, and file manager metrics.

nodes.name: metricsOpt
nodes.summary: Returns the metrics recorded at commit time if available, otherwise None.

nodes.name: getMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Returns the memory used by this instance by summing the RocksDB.mainMemorySources properties (table readers, memtables, block cache). Only safe from the task thread when the DB is open.

nodes.name: updateMemoryUsageIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Reads the memory usage and reports it to RocksDBMemoryManager if memoryUpdateIntervalMs has passed and the DB is open; failures are only logged at debug level.

nodes.name: openDB
