nodes.summary: Opens the native RocksDB in the working directory with the configured options (asserts it is not already open).

nodes.name: closeDB
nodes.summary: Cancels background work and closes the native DB, either swallowing or rethrowing exceptions depending on ignoreException.

nodes.name: reportSnapshotUploadToCoordinator
nodes.summary: Sends a snapshot uploaded event with the version to the event forwarder when snapshot upload lag reporting is enabled.

nodes.name: createLogger
nodes.summary: Creates a native RocksDB Logger that forwards native log lines to the Spark logger, mapping RocksDB levels to Spark levels and setting the native log level from the active log level.

nodes.name: prefixUpperBound
nodes.summary: Computes the exclusive upper bound of a byte prefix by incrementing the last non-0xFF byte; returns None for an empty or all-0xFF prefix. Used by prefix and range scans.

nodes.name: silentDeleteRecursively
nodes.summary: Deletes a file or directory recursively and only logs a warning if that fails.

nodes.name: RocksDBSnapshot
nodes.summary: Case class (inside the RocksDB companion object) describing a local snapshot ready for upload: checkpoint dir, version, key counts, column family mapping, max column family id, DFS file suffix, file mapping and optional unique id. close() deletes the local checkpoint dir.

nodes.name: RocksDBVersionSnapshotInfo
nodes.summary: Case class (version, dfsFilesUUID) that uniquely identifies a snapshot; several snapshots of the same version differ by their dfsFilesUUID. Used in the set of snapshots pending upload.

nodes.name: RocksDBSnapshotFile
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a RocksDBImmutableFile with the version it was reused from, if any. isUploaded is true when the file was already uploaded so it can be skipped during SST upload.

nodes.name: RocksDBFileMapping
nodes.summary: Maps local SST files to the DFS files and versions they were uploaded as, so unchanged files are not uploaded again and local files can be reused on load. It decides whether a mapped DFS file may be used for a load or a save, purges incompatible mappings, tracks snapshots still pending upload and creates the file mapping for a new snapshot. Must be updated only from the task thread.

nodes.name: ByteArrayPair
nodes.summary: Mutable, reusable pair of key and value byte arrays; set() replaces both and returns the pair. The scan iterators of RocksDB return one shared instance to avoid allocations.

nodes.name: RocksDBConf
nodes.summary: Case class of RocksDB settings (retention, snapshot interval, compaction, changelog checkpointing, block size and cache size, memory bounds, compression, checksum options, merge operator version) plus its companion object. The companion defines the key names under "spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.rocksdb" (for example compactOnCommit, changelogCheckpointing.enabled, blockSizeKB, blockCacheSizeMB, lockAcquireTimeoutMs, formatVersion, trackTotalNumberOfRows, writeBufferSizeMB, maxWriteBufferNumber, boundedMemoryUsage, maxMemoryUsageMB, compression, mergeOperatorVersion) with defaults, and apply(StateStoreConf) parses and validates the values.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object shares this class id. Some defaults are noted in comments as duplicated in SQLConf.

nodes.name: ConfEntry
nodes.summary: Private abstract class for a config entry with a name and default; fullName is the lower-cased key.

nodes.name: SQLConfEntry
nodes.summary: Private case class of ConfEntry whose full name is the RocksDB SQL conf prefix plus the entry name, lower-cased; read from the SQL conf map.

nodes.name: ExtraConfEntry
nodes.summary: Private case class of ConfEntry for settings read from the extra options map rather than the SQL conf.

nodes.name: RocksDBMetrics
nodes.summary: Case class holding stats of a commit: committed and uncommitted key counts, internal keys, memory use, SST bytes, native histograms, commit and load latencies, file copy counts, last uploaded snapshot version, auto-repair count and loaded-from-DFS flag. json serializes it; the companion object defines the json format.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object shares this class id.

nodes.name: RocksDBNativeHistogram
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping the native RocksDB histogram (sum, average, stddev, median, p95, p99, count) with a json method; the companion apply converts a native HistogramData.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object shares this class id.

nodes.name: RocksDBLineageManager
nodes.summary: Package-private helper that keeps the lineage (array of LineageItem version and unique id pairs) when checkpoint unique ids are enabled. All operations (append, truncate from a version, reset, get a copy, contains, clear, toString) are synchronized.

nodes.name: getDfsFileForLoad
nodes.summary: Returns the mapped DFS file for a local file when loading a version. A mapping created at the same or a newer version than the one to load is ignored and cleared, so it returns None.

nodes.name: getDfsFileForSave
nodes.summary: Returns the mapped DFS file and its version for a local file being saved, unless the mapping is from the same or a higher version or the sizes differ, in which case it is cleared and None is returned.

nodes.name: getDfsFileWithIncompatibilityCheck
nodes.summary: Shared lookup of a local file in the mapping: applies an isIncompatible predicate and also rejects files from snapshots still pending upload; incompatible mappings are removed.

nodes.name: purgeIncompatibleMappingsForLoad
nodes.summary: Removes all local file mappings whose DFS version is at or above the version being loaded and returns the removed mappings.

nodes.name: syncWithLocalState
nodes.summary: Drops mappings of files that no longer exist among the given local files.

nodes.name: createSnapshotFileMapping
nodes.summary: Lists the immutable files in a checkpoint dir and maps each to a DFS file, reusing the previously uploaded file if it is compatible or generating a new DFS file name, then syncs with local state and registers the snapshot as pending upload. Returns the DFS file suffix and the mapping.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds a RocksDBConf from a StateStoreConf: reads each entry from the SQL conf map with typed, validated getters (boolean, int, long, ratio between 0 and 1, positive numbers, string) and throws IllegalArgumentException on invalid values. An overload at line 2957 uses a default StateStoreConf.

nodes.name: RocksDBFileManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RocksDBFileManager, which syncs RocksDB checkpoint files between a local directory and a DFS root directory, plus the metadata and immutable-file classes it serializes. Each committed version is a [version].zip holding a JSON metadata file and non-immutable files, while SST and archived log files are uploaded separately under SSTs and logs subdirectories and shared between versions.
nodes.languageNotes: The file header comment documents the local and DFS directory layouts. Several classes are JSON-serialized, so their fields must stay backward-compatible.

nodes.name: RocksDBFileManager
nodes.summary: Saves RocksDB checkpoints to DFS and loads them back to a local directory, incrementally: only new SST and archived log files are uploaded, and they are reused across adjacent versions. It also creates changelog writers and readers, finds the latest snapshot or version, and deletes old versions plus orphan files during maintenance. Used by the RocksDB state store for commit, load and cleanup; thread-safe so maintenance can delete files while a task saves.

nodes.name: getChangelogWriterVersion
nodes.summary: Maps the pair (useColumnFamilies, stateStoreCheckpointIdEnabled) to a changelog writer version 1 to 4.

nodes.name: createDfsRootDirIfNotExist
nodes.summary: Creates the DFS root directory once, guarded by the rootDirChecked flag.

nodes.name: getChangeLogWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the StateStoreChangelogWriter for a version, choosing V1 to V4 from the column family and checkpoint id settings; V3 and V4 need the checkpoint id lineage. Rethrows CANNOT_LOAD_STATE_STORE errors and wraps others as a failed-to-get-changelog-writer error.

nodes.name: getChangelogReader
nodes.summary: Builds a StateStoreChangelogReader for a version through StateStoreChangelogReaderFactory and logs its version.

nodes.name: saveCheckpointToDfs
nodes.summary: Saves a local checkpoint directory as a committed version: uploads immutable files, builds and writes the metadata file with key counts and column family maps, then zips the other files plus metadata into the version zip. Records the zip time in the save metrics.

nodes.name: loadCheckpointFromDfs
nodes.summary: Loads the files of a version from DFS into a local directory. Version 0 clears the directory and file mapping; otherwise it deletes local non-immutable files, unzips the version zip, reads the metadata and copies the needed immutable files. Returns the metadata.

nodes.name: getLatestSnapshotVersion
nodes.summary: Returns the latest snapshot zip version less than or equal to the given version, checking for the exact version first to avoid listing. A second no-argument overload (lines 431-445) returns the latest snapshot version in DFS, or 0 if none.

nodes.name: getEligibleSnapshotsForVersion
nodes.summary: Delegates to SnapshotLoaderHelper to list snapshot versions that can be used to load a version.

nodes.name: getSnapshotVersionsAndUniqueIdsFromLineage
nodes.summary: Lists zip files and returns the (version, uniqueId) snapshot pairs whose names match an item of the given lineage, sorted by version descending.

nodes.name: getLatestVersion
nodes.summary: Scans the DFS root for changelog and zip file names and returns the highest version found, or 0 if there is no data.

nodes.name: findOrphanFiles
nodes.summary: Finds SST or log files not tracked by any version zip: files older than the oldest tracked file are treated as orphans, so files of an ongoing version are not deleted.

nodes.name: deleteChangelogFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes the changelog file of each given (version, uniqueId) pair, logging a warning when a delete fails.

nodes.name: setMaxSeenVersion
nodes.summary: Raises maxSeenVersion to the larger of its current value and the given version, used to estimate stale versions for deletion.

nodes.name: shouldSkipDeletion
nodes.summary: Decides whether batch deletion can be skipped because fewer than minVersionsToDelete stale versions exist, based on maxSeenVersion and minSeenVersion.

nodes.name: deleteOldVersions
nodes.summary: Maintenance routine that keeps numVersionsToRetain versions: it lists snapshots and changelogs, picks the versions to delete, resolves which SST and log files were last used in them, deletes those files plus orphan files, then deletes version zips, changelog files and orphan checksum files. Updates minSeenVersion at the end.

nodes.name: saveImmutableFilesToDfs
nodes.summary: Uploads local SST and log files that are not already uploaded (per the file mapping) to DFS, reuses the others, caches the resulting immutable file list per version, and records copy/reuse metrics.

nodes.name: loadImmutableFilesFromDfs
nodes.summary: Makes the local directory match the required immutable files: deletes local files that differ from the DFS mapping, purges incompatible mappings, copies missing files from DFS with a size check, and records load metrics.

nodes.name: unzipBatchZipFileFromDfs
nodes.summary: Unzips a version zip from DFS into a local directory, reading through the checkpoint file manager when a unique id is present and from the file system otherwise.

nodes.name: getImmutableFilesFromVersionZip
nodes.summary: Unzips a version zip into the temp directory and returns the immutable files listed in its metadata.

nodes.name: zipToDfsFile
nodes.summary: Writes the given files into a single zip on DFS through an atomic output stream, optionally rejecting empty non-log files; on error the output is cancelled so no file is written. Records the uncompressed byte count.

nodes.name: logFilesInDir
nodes.summary: Writes a debug log listing every file under a directory with its size.

nodes.name: newDFSFileName
nodes.summary: Builds a DFS file name as baseName-suffix.extension from a local file name.

nodes.name: dfsFileSuffix
nodes.summary: Extracts the suffix between the first dash and the first dot of an immutable file DFS name.

nodes.name: dfsBatchZipFile
nodes.summary: Returns the DFS path of the version zip, named version.zip or version_uniqueId.zip.

nodes.name: dfsChangelogFile
nodes.summary: Returns the DFS path of the changelog file, named version.changelog or version_uniqueId.changelog.

nodes.name: dfsFilePath
nodes.summary: Maps a file name to its DFS location: SST files go under SSTs, log files under logs, anything else directly under the root.

nodes.name: localFilePath
nodes.summary: Maps a file name to its local location, placing log files in the archive subdirectory.

nodes.name: listRocksDBFiles
nodes.summary: Lists local checkpoint files and returns a pair: immutable files (top-level SST files plus archived log files) and the other top-level files.

nodes.name: RocksDBFileManagerMetrics
nodes.summary: Case class holding file-sync metrics (filesCopied, bytesCopied, filesReused, optional zipFileBytesUncompressed and saveZipFilesTimeMs). Its companion object provides EMPTY_METRICS, returned when no operation has run. RocksDBFileManager keeps the latest save and load metrics in this type.

nodes.name: ColumnFamilyInfo
nodes.summary: Case class recording a virtual column family id (cfId) and whether it is internal (isInternal). Saved inside checkpoint metadata maps by RocksDBFileManager.saveCheckpointToDfs.

nodes.name: RocksDBCheckpointMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class describing a checkpoint stored in DFS: sst files, log files, key counts, and optional column family mappings and max column family id. It writes itself to a metadata file as a version line "v1" followed by JSON (json, prettyJson, writeToFile). The companion reads it back (readFromFile, rejecting an unexpected version line), configures the Jackson mapper, and has several apply overloads (the widest, lines 1228-1245, has a function node; the others build from separate sst/log lists or without column family info). Changes must be backward-compatible.

nodes.name: RocksDBImmutableFile
nodes.summary: Sealed trait mapping a local RocksDB file name to the name of its DFS copy, with sizeBytes and an isSameFile check (same name and size). The companion holds the subdirectory names (SSTs, logs, archive), an apply that builds a RocksDBSstFile or RocksDBLogFile by extension (or null), and the helpers isSstFile, isLogFile and isImmutableFile.

nodes.name: RocksDBSstFile
nodes.summary: JSON-serialized case class for a RocksDB SST file (localFileName, dfsSstFileName, sizeBytes). It implements RocksDBImmutableFile and returns dfsSstFileName as dfsFileName.

nodes.name: RocksDBLogFile
nodes.summary: JSON-serialized case class for a RocksDB log file (localFileName, dfsLogFileName, sizeBytes). It implements RocksDBImmutableFile and returns dfsLogFileName as dfsFileName.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes the metadata to JSON with the Jackson mapper, nulling an empty logFiles list so the field is not written.

nodes.name: writeToFile
nodes.summary: Writes the metadata file: a "v1" version line followed by the JSON text.

nodes.name: readFromFile
nodes.summary: Reads a metadata file, checks the first line equals "v1" (otherwise raises a cannot-read-checkpoint error), and parses the rest as JSON.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that partitions immutable files into SST and log files and builds the metadata with column family information. Other overloads (lines 1214-1293) cover variants with separate sst and log lists or no column family data.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory returning a RocksDBSstFile for .sst names, a RocksDBLogFile for .log names, and null otherwise.

nodes.name: package.scala
nodes.summary: Package object for org.apache.spark.sql.execution.streaming.state. It defines an implicit class on RDD that adds mapPartitionsWithStateStore and mapPartitionsWithReadStateStore, which run a function over each partition together with a StateStore or ReadStateStore.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala package object with an implicit class (extension methods on RDD). The wider mapPartitionsWithStateStore overload disables scalastyle because of its parameter count.

nodes.name: state
nodes.summary: Scala package object of the streaming state package. Its only member is the implicit class StateStoreOps.

nodes.name: StateStoreOps
nodes.summary: Implicit class that adds mapPartitionsWithStateStore (two overloads) and the streaming-private mapPartitionsWithReadStateStore to any RDD. Each wraps the user function so the store is aborted (if not committed) or the thread-local store is cleared when the task completes, then builds a StateStoreRDD or ReadStateStoreRDD from the operator state info. The short overload (lines 35-51) takes an SQLContext and forwards to the long one using the session state and the state store coordinator.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithStateStore
nodes.summary: Maps each partition of an RDD together with a StateStore. It cleans the function, registers a task completion listener that aborts the store when it was not committed, and returns a StateStoreRDD built from the checkpoint location, run id, operator id, store version, schema and encoder spec in the StatefulOperatorStateInfo. The overload at lines 35-51 takes an SQLContext and forwards here.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithReadStateStore
nodes.summary: Read-only variant of mapPartitionsWithStateStore: wraps the function with a task completion listener that clears the thread-local store and returns a ReadStateStoreRDD.

nodes.name: RangeScanBoundaryUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RangeScanBoundaryUtils, helpers that build start or end boundary rows for state store range scans. The rows fill non-ordering columns with the byte-wise smallest defaults so that seek does not skip matching entries.

nodes.name: RangeScanBoundaryUtils
nodes.summary: Package-private object that builds fully typed boundary rows for StateStore.rangeScan and rangeScanWithMultiValues. It uses Literal.default for most types, overrides CharType with n zero bytes, recurses through StructType, unwraps UserDefinedType, and rejects schemas containing VariantType through an assertion. Used by callers that scan a range by an ordering column such as a timestamp.

nodes.name: defaultInternalRow
nodes.summary: Builds an InternalRow whose fields are the recursive byte-wise-smallest defaults of the schema, after checking that the schema is supported.

nodes.name: defaultUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Projects the default InternalRow of the schema into a fresh UnsafeRow copy, usable as a scan boundary where only the ordering prefix matters.

nodes.name: recursiveDefaultValue
nodes.summary: Returns the smallest value for a data type: n zero bytes for CharType(n), a nested row for StructType, the underlying sqlType for a user-defined type, and Literal.default otherwise.

nodes.name: assertBoundarySchemaSupported
nodes.summary: Asserts that the schema contains no VariantType (checked recursively); this is a defensive check that is expected never to fire.

nodes.name: RocksDBLoader.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RocksDBLoader, which loads the native RocksDB library once on a dedicated uninterruptible thread because the native code fails when interrupted. It remembers any load failure and rethrows it to later callers.

nodes.name: RocksDBLoader
nodes.summary: Singleton that wraps loading the native RocksDB library. loadLibrary is synchronized, starts the loader thread if it has not started, waits for it with join, and rethrows a stored exception on this and later calls. It guards against a second task thread starting the already-started thread after the first was interrupted (SPARK-39847). Used before creating RocksDB instances.

nodes.name: loadLibrary
nodes.summary: Loads the RocksDB native library under the object lock: starts the UninterruptibleThread if it is new, joins it, logs progress, and throws the recorded exception if loading failed.

nodes.name: RocksDBMemoryManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RocksDBMemoryManager, a singleton that owns the shared cache and write buffer manager used by all RocksDB state store instances on an executor when bounded memory is enabled. It also tracks per-instance memory use and reports it to Spark as an unmanaged memory consumer.

nodes.name: RocksDBMemoryManager
nodes.summary: Singleton that creates and shares one LRU cache and WriteBufferManager when boundedMemoryUsage is on (otherwise returns a new cache per call). It implements UnmanagedMemoryConsumer, registering itself with UnifiedMemoryManager and reporting off-heap memory use: the maximum of the bounded instances (shared pool) plus the sum of the unbounded ones. Instances register their usage through updateMemoryUsage and unregisterInstance; per-instance figures for bounded mode are divided by the number of bounded instances.

nodes.name: InstanceMemoryInfo
nodes.summary: Private case class holding one instance's memoryUsage in bytes and whether it uses bounded memory. Values are stored in instanceMemoryMap by unique id.

nodes.name: unmanagedMemoryConsumerId
nodes.summary: Returns the consumer id ("RocksDB", "RocksDB-Memory-Manager") used when reporting to the memory manager.

nodes.name: memoryMode
nodes.summary: Reports OFF_HEAP as the memory mode, since RocksDB uses native memory.

nodes.name: getMemBytesUsed
nodes.summary: Returns total RocksDB memory: the maximum usage among bounded instances (they share a pool) plus the sum of unbounded instances; 0 when none are registered.

nodes.name: updateMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Registers or updates an instance's memory usage and bounded flag under its unique id.

nodes.name: unregisterInstance
nodes.summary: Removes an instance from the memory map.

nodes.name: getNumRocksDBInstances
nodes.summary: Counts registered instances whose bounded flag equals the given value.

nodes.name: getInstanceMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Returns an instance's share of memory: total divided by the bounded instance count in bounded mode, the full total otherwise.

nodes.name: getInstancePinnedBlocksMemUsage
nodes.summary: Returns an instance's share of pinned block memory, divided by the bounded instance count in bounded mode and the full value otherwise.

nodes.name: getOrCreateRocksDBMemoryManagerAndCache
nodes.summary: Registers with UnifiedMemoryManager when SparkEnv exists, then returns the shared (WriteBufferManager, Cache) pair. In bounded mode it validates that writeBufferCacheRatio plus highPriorityPoolRatio is below 1.0 and totalMemoryUsageMB is positive, then lazily creates a non-strict LRUCache and a WriteBufferManager sized by the ratio; otherwise it returns (null, new LRUCache of blockCacheSizeMB).

nodes.name: resetWriteBufferManagerAndCache
nodes.summary: Test-only reset that clears the shared write buffer manager, cache and instance memory map.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelog.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the on-disk changelog format of state stores: a RecordType enumeration, versioned writers (V1 to V4) that append put, delete, merge and delete-range records to a compressed changelog file, versioned readers (V1 to V4) that iterate those records back, a factory that picks the reader by the version stored in the first line, and a base iterator that walks a range of changelog files. Used when a state store records changes between snapshots and when they are replayed or read as change data.
nodes.languageNotes: Writers and readers form two parallel hierarchies: V3 extends V1 and V4 extends V2, each adding a lineage line after the version line.

nodes.name: RecordType
nodes.summary: Enumeration of changelog record types (eof_record, put_record, delete_record, merge_record, delete_range_record). Provides conversion of a record type to its byte code (0x00, 0x01, 0x10, 0x11, 0x20), to a short string (update, delete, append, delete_range) and back from a byte. Used by the V2 and V4 writers and readers of changelog files.

nodes.name: getRecordTypeAsByte
nodes.summary: Maps a RecordType to the single byte written in front of each V2 changelog record.

nodes.name: getRecordTypeAsString
nodes.summary: Maps a put, delete, merge or delete-range record type to a readable name and throws an unsupported-operation error for any other type.

nodes.name: getRecordTypeFromByte
nodes.summary: Decodes a record type byte read from a changelog file and throws a RuntimeException for an unknown value.

nodes.name: LineageItem
nodes.summary: Case class holding a state store version and its checkpointUniqueId. An array of these is the lineage written as the second line of V3 and V4 changelog files when state store checkpoint ids are enabled.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract base for changelog writers. Creates the file atomically through a CheckpointFileManager, wraps it in a compressed DataOutputStream, can write the version line and the JSON lineage line, and declares put, delete, merge, deleteRange and commit for subclasses. abort cancels the file and closes the stream quietly.

nodes.name: writeLineage
nodes.summary: Serializes the lineage array to JSON and writes it as a UTF string; asserts the writer version is at least 3.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Cancels the backing file stream and closes the compressed stream, logging non-fatal failures and ignoring IOException wrapped in FSError, then nulls both streams.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogWriterV1
nodes.summary: Version 1 writer. Writes put records as key length, key, value length, value; delete records as key length, key and -1; and ends the file with an Int -1. merge and deleteRange throw UnsupportedOperationException. The version number is not written to the file.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Writes a length-prefixed key and value to the compressed stream.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Writes a length-prefixed key followed by -1 as the value length to mark a deletion.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Writes the -1 end-of-file marker and closes the stream; on any failure it aborts, logs and rethrows, and always clears the stream fields.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogWriterV2
nodes.summary: Version 2 writer. Writes the version line first, then records that start with a record type byte (put, merge, delete, delete range) followed by length-prefixed keys and values, and ends with an EOF_RECORD byte on commit.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Writes a DELETE_RECORD type byte, the length-prefixed key and -1 as the value marker.

nodes.name: deleteRange
nodes.summary: Writes a DELETE_RANGE_RECORD type byte followed by the length-prefixed begin key and end key.

nodes.name: writePutOrMergeRecord
nodes.summary: Shared helper behind put and merge: asserts the record type, then writes the type byte and length-prefixed key and value.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Writes the EOF_RECORD byte and closes the stream; on failure it aborts, logs and rethrows, and always clears the stream fields.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogWriterV3
nodes.summary: Version 3 writer: a V1 writer that additionally writes the version line and then the lineage line, used when state store checkpoint ids are enabled.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogWriterV4
nodes.summary: Version 4 writer: a V2 writer that additionally writes the lineage line right after the version line, used when state store checkpoint ids are enabled.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReaderFactory
nodes.summary: Factory that opens a changelog file through a CheckpointFileManager, reads the first line to learn the version (a first line without the "v" prefix, an EOF or a decoding failure means version 1) and constructs the matching StateStoreChangelogReader (V1 to V4). It closes its probing input afterwards, skipping checksum verification for ChecksumFSDataInputStream. Used wherever a changelog has to be replayed.

nodes.name: constructChangelogReader
nodes.summary: Matches the detected changelog version to a V1 to V4 reader, throws invalidChangeLogReaderVersion for other values, and closes the probing input stream in a finally block.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReader
nodes.summary: Abstract iterator over (RecordType, key bytes, value bytes) tuples of one changelog file. Opens and decompresses the file, offers version verification and a lazy lineage read for versions 3 and above, and closes the input on close. Subclasses implement getNext for each format version.

nodes.name: verifyVersion
nodes.summary: Reads the version line and asserts it equals "v" plus the reader version.

nodes.name: readLineage
nodes.summary: Reads the JSON lineage line and deserializes it into an array of LineageItem; asserts version is at least 3.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReaderV1
nodes.summary: Version 1 reader. Returns put tuples as (PUT_RECORD, key, value) and deletes as (DELETE_RECORD, key, null); a key length of -1 ends the file and any other negative size raises an IOException.

nodes.name: getNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next length-prefixed record, marks the iterator finished on the -1 end marker, and returns a put or delete tuple.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReaderV2
nodes.summary: Version 2 reader. Verifies the version line, then decodes each record by its type byte into put, delete, merge or delete-range tuples and stops at EOF_RECORD.

nodes.name: parseBuffer
nodes.summary: Reads an int block size and then that many bytes from the input.

nodes.name: getNext
nodes.summary: Reads a record type byte and returns the tuple for put, delete, merge or delete-range; finishes on EOF_RECORD and throws IOException on an unknown type.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReaderV3
nodes.summary: Version 3 reader: a V1 reader that first verifies the version line and then reads the lineage line to position the stream before records are read.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangelogReaderV4
nodes.summary: Version 4 reader: a V2 reader that additionally reads the lineage line during initialization to move the file position past it.

nodes.name: StateStoreChangeDataReader
nodes.summary: Abstract iterator over a range of changelog files of one state store, from startVersion to endVersion. Yields (record type, UnsafeRow key, UnsafeRow value, batch id) tuples. It builds the changelog path of each version (with an optional checkpoint unique id), obtains a reader through StateStoreChangelogReaderFactory, moves to the next file when one is exhausted, and holds an optional row checksum verifier created from StateStoreConf. Concrete subclasses supply the changelogSuffix and the conversion of raw bytes to rows.

nodes.name: ChangeLogFileIterator
nodes.summary: Private inner iterator that walks the (version, optional unique id) pairs and produces the Path of each changelog file below the state location, remembering the version of the file returned last.

nodes.name: getChangelogPath
nodes.summary: Builds the changelog Path as "<version>.<suffix>" or "<version>_<uniqueId>.<suffix>" under the state location.

nodes.name: currentChangelogReader
nodes.summary: Returns a changelog reader that still has records, closing exhausted readers and opening the next file through the factory; returns null and sets finished when no file remains.

nodes.name: StateRewriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StateRewriter, which reads the state of every operator of a stateful streaming query from a checkpoint at one batch id, optionally transforms each state store DataFrame, and writes the state to a new batch id in the same or another checkpoint location. Also defines StateRewriterErrors and the StateRewriterInvalidCheckpointError exception family raised for unusable checkpoints. The class comment names offline state repartitioning as an example use.

nodes.name: StateRewriter
nodes.summary: Rewrites state stores of a streaming query. run() calls runInternal, which verifies that the commit log version matches the configured checkpoint format version, reads operator metadata, builds the StateStoreConf from the offset log of the write batch, and for each state store of each operator reads the state through the "statestore" data source with all column families, applies the optional transformFunc (the schema must stay equal), and writes each partition with StatePartitionAllColumnFamiliesWriter on the executors. It returns per-operator state store checkpoint ids when checkpoint ids are enabled. TransformWithState operators get state variable info and a schema provider.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Public entry point: logs the start, runs runInternal while timing it, logs the duration and returns the optional map of operator id to checkpoint ids.

nodes.name: extractCheckpointIdsPerPartition
nodes.summary: When state store checkpoint ids are enabled, regroups the per-store checkpoint info into per-operator arrays indexed by partition and store, asserting partition id, batch version (writeBatchId + 1) and an empty base checkpoint id; otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: runInternal
nodes.summary: Main flow: verifies the checkpoint format version, loads all operator state metadata (throws if none), creates confs from the offset log, broadcasts the Hadoop configuration, rewrites every state store of every operator sequentially and extracts the checkpoint ids; logs and rethrows any failure.

nodes.name: rewriteStore
nodes.summary: Reads one state store via the statestore source (all column families), applies the optional transform and checks the schema is unchanged, then writes each partition with StatePartitionAllColumnFamiliesWriter and collects the resulting StateStoreCheckpointInfo array.

nodes.name: createConfsFromOffsetLog
nodes.summary: Loads the offset sequence of the write batch (it must exist and carry metadata), applies its session conf to a cloned SQLConf and returns the StateStoreConf and that SQLConf.

nodes.name: getStoreToSchemaFilesMap
nodes.summary: Maps each store name of an operator to its schema file paths: empty for StateStoreMetadataV1, the listed paths for StateStoreMetadataV2, and an error for other versions.

nodes.name: getWriterColFamilyInfoMap
nodes.summary: Builds StatePartitionWriterColumnFamilyInfo per column family from the latest schemas, marking useMultipleValuesPerKey for TransformWithState list state variables.

nodes.name: getLatestColFamilyToSchemaMap
nodes.summary: Creates a StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker for the store with a placeholder run id, reads the latest schema file and maps column family names to schemas, filling in missing key encoder specs.

nodes.name: createKeyEncoderSpecIfAbsent
nodes.summary: Keeps an existing key encoder spec; for V1 metadata without one it creates PrefixKeyScanStateEncoderSpec when numColsPrefixKey is above 0 or NoPrefixKeyStateEncoderSpec otherwise; for other cases throws missingKeyEncoderSpecError.

nodes.name: getStateVariablesIfTWS
nodes.summary: For TransformWithState operator names, parses the operator properties JSON of OperatorStateMetadataV2 and returns state variables keyed by state name; otherwise returns an empty map.

nodes.name: createStoreSchemaProviderIfTWS
nodes.summary: For TransformWithState operators builds an InMemoryStateSchemaProvider from the schema files (needed for schema evolution); otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: verifyCheckpointFormatVersion
nodes.summary: Compares the version recorded in the read batch commit log entry with the configured default commit log version and throws stateCheckpointFormatVersionMismatchError when they differ.

nodes.name: StateRewriterErrors
nodes.summary: Private[state] object with four factory methods: missingKeyEncoderSpecError, missingOperatorMetadataError, unsupportedStateStoreMetadataVersionError and stateCheckpointFormatVersionMismatchError. Each returns the matching StateRewriterInvalidCheckpointError subclass.

nodes.name: StateRewriterInvalidCheckpointError
nodes.summary: Abstract SparkIllegalStateException base for rewrite failures caused by an invalid checkpoint. Builds the error class "STATE_REWRITER_INVALID_CHECKPOINT.<subClass>" and always adds the checkpointLocation message parameter.

nodes.name: StateRewriterMissingKeyEncoderSpecError
nodes.summary: Error with subclass MISSING_KEY_ENCODER_SPEC, raised when a V2 metadata column family has no key encoder spec; carries the colFamilyName.

nodes.name: StateRewriterMissingOperatorMetadataError
nodes.summary: Error with subclass MISSING_OPERATOR_METADATA, raised when no operator metadata exists for the read batch; carries the batchId.

nodes.name: StateRewriterUnsupportedStoreMetadataVersionError
nodes.summary: Error with subclass UNSUPPORTED_STATE_STORE_METADATA_VERSION, raised for a state store metadata version other than V1 or V2.

nodes.name: StateRewriterStateCheckpointFormatVersionMismatchError
nodes.summary: Error with subclass STATE_CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSION_MISMATCH carrying expectedVersion, actualVersion and the SQLConf key STATE_STORE_CHECKPOINT_FORMAT_VERSION.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateEncoder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines how streaming state store keys and values are turned into bytes for RocksDB. It holds the key and value encoder traits, the data encoders (plain UnsafeRow layout and Avro with schema ids), the key encoders for no prefix, prefix scan, range scan and timestamp keys, the value encoders for single and multiple values per key, the schema metadata classes, and the RocksDBStateEncoder factory.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing sealed traits, case classes, companion objects and abstract classes. Range scan encoding writes a marker byte plus big endian value and flips bits of negative floats and doubles so that byte order matches numeric order.

nodes.name: RocksDBKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for encoders that turn state key rows into bytes and back. It declares supportPrefixKeyScan, supportsDeleteRange, supportsRangeScan, encodePrefixKey, encodeKey and decodeKey. Implemented by the prefix scan, range scan, no prefix and timestamp key encoders.

nodes.name: RocksDBValueStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for encoders that turn state value rows into bytes and back. It declares supportsMultipleValuesPerKey, encodeValue, decodeValue and two decodeValues overloads (one over a byte array and one over an iterator of ArrayIndexRange). Implemented by the multi valued and single value encoders.

nodes.name: StateSchemaProvider
nodes.summary: Serializable trait that gives access to state schema metadata. getSchemaMetadataValue looks up the schema for a StateSchemaMetadataKey and getCurrentStateSchemaId returns the schema id for a column family and key or value side. Used by the Avro state encoder to find the current and the writer schema.

nodes.name: TestStateSchemaProvider
nodes.summary: Test implementation of StateSchemaProvider backed by a mutable map that can be updated at run time. captureSchema stores a key schema entry and a value schema entry (with their Avro schemas from SchemaConverters.toAvroTypeWithDefaults) for a column family, and getCurrentStateSchemaId returns the largest schema id stored.

nodes.name: InMemoryStateSchemaProvider
nodes.summary: StateSchemaProvider that reads from a StateSchemaMetadata held in memory. getSchemaMetadataValue looks up activeSchemas by key and getCurrentStateSchemaId returns the maximum schema id for a column family and key or value side.

nodes.name: StateSchemaBroadcast
nodes.summary: Case class that wraps a Broadcast of StateSchemaMetadata so the schema evolution information of a stateful operator reaches all executors. It implements StateSchemaProvider by reading activeSchemas from the broadcast value for schema lookups and for the current schema id.

nodes.name: StateSchemaMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class holding activeSchemas, a map from StateSchemaMetadataKey to StateSchemaMetadataValue for all schema versions that may still exist in the state store. Its companion object builds it with createStateSchemaMetadata, which reads the given state schema files from the checkpoint location and creates a key entry and a value entry per column family.

nodes.name: StateSchemaMetadataKey
nodes.summary: Case class used as the lookup key for schema metadata. It combines the column family name, the schema id (version) and an isKey flag that tells whether the schema is for keys or for values.

nodes.name: StateSchemaMetadataValue
nodes.summary: Case class that holds both the Spark SQL schema (StructType) and the equivalent Avro schema of one schema version. The Avro schema is used for compatibility checking and for serialization.

nodes.name: StateSchemaInfo
nodes.summary: Case class that carries the key schema id and the value schema id of a state store. It is used to support schema evolution so that state data written under older schemas can still be read.

nodes.name: StateSchemaIdRow
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a schema id with the encoded bytes of a row. It records which schema version encoded the data, so that decoding still works after schemas have evolved. The bytes hold Avro data or UnsafeRow data depending on the encoder.

nodes.name: DataEncoder
nodes.summary: Trait for encoding UnsafeRows into raw bytes either by their direct byte layout or by converting them to Avro first. It declares encodeKey, encodeRemainingKey, encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan, encodeValue, decodeKey, decodeRemainingKey, decodePrefixKeyForRangeScan, decodeValue and supportsSchemaEvolution. The key encoders and value encoders delegate the actual data encoding to it.

nodes.name: RocksDBDataEncoder
nodes.summary: Abstract base class of the data encoders. It keeps reusable key and value rows, the bit masks and the null, negative and positive marker bytes used for range scan ordering, and helper methods: encodeWithStateSchemaId and decodeStateSchemaIdRow (2 byte schema id prefix), encodeUnsafeRow and decodeToUnsafeRow (one version byte prefix), and unsupportedOperationForKeyStateEncoder.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowDataEncoder
nodes.summary: DataEncoder that writes the UnsafeRow byte layout directly, with a version byte in front, and does not support schema evolution. For range scan keys it rewrites each ordering column as a marker byte plus big endian bytes, flipping bits of negative floats and doubles, and decodePrefixKeyForRangeScan reverses that. decodeKey and decodeRemainingKey choose the field count from the KeyStateEncoderSpec.

nodes.name: AvroStateEncoder
nodes.summary: DataEncoder that serializes state rows with Avro and supports schema evolution. It lazily builds Avro types and projections for the key, prefix key, range scan key and remaining key, and uses a StateSchemaProvider to get the current schema ids and the writer schema. Keys and values get a schema id prefix and a version byte, and range scan keys are written as marker and value byte fields of an Avro record.

nodes.name: captureSchema
nodes.summary: Adds a key schema entry and a value schema entry for a column family to the in memory schema map, converting each Spark SQL schema to Avro with SchemaConverters.toAvroTypeWithDefaults. The schema ids default to 0.

nodes.name: getCurrentStateSchemaId
nodes.summary: Returns the highest schema id among the stored entries that match the column family name and the key or value flag.

nodes.name: getCurrentStateSchemaId
nodes.summary: Returns the highest schema id among the activeSchemas entries that match the column family name and the key or value flag.

nodes.name: getCurrentStateSchemaId
nodes.summary: Returns the highest schema id among the broadcast activeSchemas entries that match the column family name and the key or value flag.

nodes.name: createStateSchemaMetadata
nodes.summary: Builds a StateSchemaMetadata from a list of state schema files. It opens each file through CheckpointFileManager, reads the column family schemas with StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker.readSchemaFile, converts each key and value schema to Avro and adds one entry per side to the map of active schemas.

nodes.name: encodeWithStateSchemaId
nodes.summary: Returns a new byte array with the 2 byte schema id written first and the row bytes copied after it.

nodes.name: decodeStateSchemaIdRow
nodes.summary: Reads the 2 byte schema id at the start of the byte array and copies the rest into a new array, returning both as a StateSchemaIdRow.

nodes.name: unsupportedOperationForKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Creates an UnsupportedOperationException whose message names the operation and the class of the key encoder spec. Used when a method is called for an encoder spec that does not support it.

nodes.name: encodeUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Encodes an UnsafeRow of N bytes as an N+1 byte array: the version byte STATE_ENCODING_VERSION followed by a copy of the row bytes.

nodes.name: decodeToUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Points a reusable UnsafeRow at the given bytes after the version byte and returns it, or returns null for null input. An overload at lines 474-481 takes a field count, allocates a new UnsafeRow and calls this one.

nodes.name: encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan
nodes.summary: Encodes the ordering columns of a range scan key into byte arrays that sort correctly in RocksDB. Each value becomes a marker byte (negative, positive or null) plus the big endian value, with all bits of negative float and double values flipped, written into an UnsafeRowWriter and then encoded by encodeUnsafeRow.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Decodes key bytes to an UnsafeRow, choosing the field count from the KeyStateEncoderSpec: reused key row for no prefix keys, the prefix column count for prefix scan, and the key schema length minus one for timestamp keys. Throws for other specs.

nodes.name: decodeRemainingKey
nodes.summary: Decodes the non prefix part of a key for prefix scan and range scan specs, using the key schema length minus the prefix or ordering column count as field count. Throws for other specs.

nodes.name: decodePrefixKeyForRangeScan
nodes.summary: Reverses encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan: reads the marker byte of each ordering column, sets null where the null marker is found, reads the big endian value and flips the bits back for negative floats and doubles.

nodes.name: getAvroSerializer
nodes.summary: Creates an AvroSerializer for a StructType using the Avro type from SchemaConverters.toAvroTypeWithDefaults.

nodes.name: getAvroDeserializer
nodes.summary: Creates an AvroDeserializer for a StructType, taking its rebase, union and recursion settings from default AvroOptions.

nodes.name: createAvroEnc
nodes.summary: Builds the AvroEncoder with the key and value serializers and deserializers. The key schema depends on the KeyStateEncoderSpec (full key, prefix columns, columns not in the ordering, or all but the timestamp column), and prefix scan specs also get serializers for the suffix key.

nodes.name: getStateSchemaProvider
nodes.summary: Returns the optional StateSchemaProvider and asserts that it is defined, since the Avro encoder always needs it.

nodes.name: encodeUnsafeRowToAvro
nodes.summary: Serializes an UnsafeRow with the given AvroSerializer into an Avro record and writes it with a GenericDatumWriter and a direct binary encoder into the reused output stream, returning the bytes.

nodes.name: prependVersionByte
nodes.summary: Returns a new array with the version byte STATE_ENCODING_VERSION placed in front of the given bytes, to keep the state encoding format versioned.

nodes.name: removeVersionByte
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the bytes without the leading version byte, used before decoding state data.

nodes.name: decodeFromAvroToUnsafeRow
nodes.summary: Reads Avro bytes with a GenericDatumReader that uses a writer schema and a reader schema, deserializes the record to an InternalRow and projects it to an UnsafeRow. Returns null for null bytes. An overload at lines 954-973 does the same with a single Avro schema.

nodes.name: encodeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes a key row to Avro according to the key spec: no prefix and timestamp keys get the current key schema id in front, prefix scan keys are encoded as the prefix only. A version byte is prepended to the result.

nodes.name: encodeRemainingKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the non prefix part of a key to Avro using the suffix serializer for prefix scan or the key serializer for range scan, then adds the key schema id and the version byte.

nodes.name: encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan
nodes.summary: Encodes range scan ordering columns into an Avro record where each column has a marker field (null, negative or positive) and a big endian value field. Negative float and double values have their bits flipped to keep order, and unsupported data types throw. The record is written with a binary encoder and a version byte is prepended.

nodes.name: encodeValue
nodes.summary: Encodes a value row to Avro and prepends the current value schema id and then the version byte.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Removes the version byte and decodes key bytes from Avro to an UnsafeRow. No prefix and timestamp keys first drop the schema id, prefix scan keys are decoded with the prefix schema.

nodes.name: decodeRemainingKey
nodes.summary: Removes the version byte and the schema id, then decodes the remaining key part from Avro for prefix scan (suffix deserializer) or range scan (key deserializer) specs.

nodes.name: decodePrefixKeyForRangeScan
nodes.summary: Reverses encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan: reads the Avro record, checks each marker field, writes nulls or the decoded big endian value to an UnsafeRowWriter and restores negative float and double values by flipping the bits back.

nodes.name: decodeValue
nodes.summary: Removes the version byte, reads the schema id, fetches the writer schema from the StateSchemaProvider for that id and decodes the Avro bytes to an UnsafeRow using the current value Avro type as reader schema.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Factory object for the state encoders of the RocksDB state store. getKeyEncoder asks the KeyStateEncoderSpec for a key encoder, and getValueEncoder returns a multi valued or a single value encoder depending on useMultipleValuesPerKey.

nodes.name: PrefixKeyScanStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Key encoder that supports prefix scan. It splits the key row into the first numColsPrefixKey columns and the remaining columns, encodes both with the data encoder and stores them as a 4 byte prefix length, the prefix bytes and the remaining bytes. It reports supportPrefixKeyScan true and no range scan or delete range support.

nodes.name: RangeKeyScanStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Key encoder that supports range scan over fixed size columns. It projects the ordering columns to the front, encodes them so that byte order equals value order (with null support through a marker byte), joins them with the encoded remaining columns and restores the original column order when decoding. It rejects variable size and null type ordering columns at construction with StateStoreErrors.

nodes.name: NoPrefixKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Key encoder without prefix scan support. encodeKey and decodeKey pass straight to the data encoder, the three capability flags are false, and encodePrefixKey throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: TimestampKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Holds the shared logic of the key encoders whose key ends with a timestamp. The companion object adds and removes the internal __event_time column (keySchemaWithTimestamp, attach and detach projections, attachTimestamp, extractTimestamp). The abstract class encodes the timestamp as 8 big endian bytes with the sign bit flipped so that negative timestamps sort correctly, and decodes it back.

nodes.name: TimestampAsPrefixKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Key encoder that puts the 8 byte timestamp in front of the encoded key so entries can be scanned in timestamp order. It does not support prefix scan or delete range, supports range scan, and encodePrefixKey throws because a key without event time is not allowed.

nodes.name: TimestampAsPostfixKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Key encoder that puts the 8 byte timestamp after the encoded key, so a prefix scan returns the entries of one key ordered by timestamp. It supports prefix scan and range scan and not delete range.

nodes.name: MultiValuedStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Value encoder that supports several values per key. Each value is stored as a 4 byte size followed by the encoded row, values are separated by a delimiter of delimiterSize bytes, and decodeValues returns an iterator over a merged byte array or over ArrayIndexRange slices. It is meant for values merged in RocksDB with the StringAppendOperator merge operator.

nodes.name: SingleValueStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Value encoder for one value per key. encodeValue and decodeValue delegate to the data encoder (decodeValue returns null for null bytes), supportsMultipleValuesPerKey is false and both decodeValues methods throw IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: getKeyEncoder
nodes.summary: Creates the RocksDBKeyStateEncoder for a KeyStateEncoderSpec by calling the spec's toEncoder with the data encoder and the useColumnFamilies flag.

nodes.name: getValueEncoder
nodes.summary: Returns a MultiValuedStateEncoder (with delimiterSize) when useMultipleValuesPerKey is true, otherwise a SingleValueStateEncoder.

nodes.name: encodeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the prefix columns and the remaining columns of a key with the data encoder and packs them as a 4 byte prefix length, the prefix bytes and the remaining bytes.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Reads the prefix length, splits the bytes into prefix part and remaining part, decodes both with the data encoder and joins them back into the full key row with a restore projection.

nodes.name: encodePrefixKey
nodes.summary: Encodes only the prefix columns and puts the 4 byte length in front, giving the byte prefix used to scan all keys with that prefix.

nodes.name: encodeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the ordering columns with encodePrefixKeyForRangeScan and the other columns with encodeRemainingKey, then writes a 4 byte length of the range scan part followed by both parts.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Reads the length of the range scan part, decodes it with decodePrefixKeyForRangeScan and, when the key has other columns, decodes those with decodeRemainingKey and rebuilds the original column order with the restore projection.

nodes.name: encodePrefixKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the ordering columns for range scan and prepends their 4 byte length, giving the byte prefix for range scans.

nodes.name: keySchemaWithTimestamp
nodes.summary: Returns the key schema with an extra non nullable long column named __event_time added at the end. Callers of the timestamp key encoders build their key schema with it.

nodes.name: getAttachTimestampProjection
nodes.summary: Builds an UnsafeProjection that copies the key columns and appends a placeholder long literal for the timestamp.

nodes.name: getDetachTimestampProjection
nodes.summary: Builds an UnsafeProjection over all columns of a key with timestamp except the last one, so the timestamp is dropped.

nodes.name: attachTimestamp
nodes.summary: Object helper that appends a timestamp column to a key with the attach projection and sets the last column to the timestamp value. The abstract class has a protected attachTimestamp (lines 1839-1841) that calls it with its own projection and schema.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Protected helper that copies the key bytes starting at startPos, leaving out the last 8 timestamp bytes, and decodes them with the data encoder.

nodes.name: encodeTimestamp
nodes.summary: Flips the sign bit of the timestamp and writes it as 8 big endian bytes into a reused buffer, so byte order matches timestamp order even for negative values. The buffer is reused, so the encoder is not thread safe.

nodes.name: decodeTimestamp
nodes.summary: Reads 8 big endian bytes from a start position and flips the sign bit back to get the original timestamp.

nodes.name: encodeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the key without its timestamp with the data encoder and writes the 8 byte encoded timestamp first and the key bytes after it.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Reads the timestamp from the first 8 bytes, decodes the key from the following bytes and attaches the timestamp back to the row.

nodes.name: encodeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes the key without its timestamp with the data encoder and writes the key bytes first and the 8 byte encoded timestamp after them.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Decodes the key from the leading bytes, reads the timestamp from the last 8 bytes and attaches it back to the row.

nodes.name: encodeValue
nodes.summary: Encodes a value row with the data encoder and prefixes the bytes with their 4 byte length.

nodes.name: decodeValue
nodes.summary: Reads the 4 byte length, copies that many bytes and decodes one value with the data encoder. Returns null for null bytes.

nodes.name: decodeValues
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator that decodes one value per ArrayIndexRange slice of the underlying array (empty for a null iterator). An overload at lines 2001-2029 walks a single merged byte array, reading each length and skipping the delimiter.

nodes.name: decodeValue
nodes.summary: Returns null for null bytes, otherwise decodes the value with the data encoder.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateMachine.scala
nodes.summary: Defines RocksDBStateMachine, a lock and stamp based state machine that guards a RocksDB instance of a state store so only one task uses it at a time, and AcquiredThreadInfo, a case class that describes the thread and task that currently holds it.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateMachine
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle of one RocksDB instance with the states RELEASED, ACQUIRED and CLOSED and the operations load, release, close and maintenance, using a map of allowed transitions. Each acquire issues a new stamp (acquireStamp) that must be presented to verifyStamp and releaseStamp; close and acquire wait up to the configured lock acquire timeout when another thread holds the instance. Takes a StateStoreId and RocksDBConf.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a private sealed trait and case objects for states and operations, and a Map keyed by (state, operation) pairs for legal transitions.

nodes.name: AcquiredThreadInfo
nodes.summary: Case class that records a weak reference to the current thread and the current TaskContext when a RocksDB instance is acquired. Its toString prints the thread id and, when a task exists, the partition, attempt, stage and task attempt ids, for use in lock timeout error messages.

nodes.name: STATE
nodes.summary: Private sealed trait that is the parent of the three machine states RELEASED, ACQUIRED and CLOSED.

nodes.name: RELEASED
nodes.summary: Case object for the state in which no thread is using the RocksDB instance.

nodes.name: ACQUIRED
nodes.summary: Case object for the state in which a thread currently holds the RocksDB instance.

nodes.name: CLOSED
nodes.summary: Case object for the state in which the RocksDB instance has been closed and cannot be used again.

nodes.name: OPERATION
nodes.summary: Private sealed abstract class that names an operation (its toString returns the name). Parent of LOAD, RELEASE, CLOSE and MAINTENANCE.

nodes.name: LOAD
nodes.summary: Case object for the "load" operation, which moves the machine from RELEASED to ACQUIRED.

nodes.name: RELEASE
nodes.summary: Case object for the "release" operation, which moves the machine from ACQUIRED to RELEASED.

nodes.name: CLOSE
nodes.summary: Case object for the "close" operation, which moves the machine from RELEASED to CLOSED (and CLOSED to CLOSED).

nodes.name: MAINTENANCE
nodes.summary: Case object for the "maintenance" operation, allowed in both RELEASED and ACQUIRED states without changing them.

nodes.name: getAcquiredThreadInfo
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the AcquiredThreadInfo of the thread that holds the instance, or None when released. Exposed for tests and read under the state machine lock.

nodes.name: incAndGetStampWithLock
nodes.summary: Increments the last valid stamp, publishes it in currentValidStamp and logs it. Must be called while holding the state machine lock (asserted with Thread.holdsLock).

nodes.name: awaitNotAcquiredWithLock
nodes.summary: Waits on the state machine lock in 10 ms steps while the state is ACQUIRED, up to rocksDBConf.lockAcquireTimeoutMs, logging every 30 seconds. If still ACQUIRED after the timeout it throws QueryExecutionErrors.unreleasedThreadError with the stack trace of the holding thread.

nodes.name: taskID
nodes.summary: Returns the task attempt id of the active TaskContext as a string, or "undefined" when there is no TaskContext. Used for logging.

nodes.name: validateAndTransitionState
nodes.summary: Core of the state machine. Looks up (current state, operation) in allowedStateTransitions, throws StateStoreErrors.invalidStateMachineTransition when no entry exists, otherwise updates the state, records AcquiredThreadInfo when entering ACQUIRED, logs the transition and returns (oldState, newState). Caller must hold the lock.

nodes.name: verifyStamp
nodes.summary: Compares a given stamp with currentValidStamp and throws StateStoreErrors.invalidStamp (after a warning log) if they differ. Ensures only the task that acquired the instance operates on it.

nodes.name: releaseStamp
nodes.summary: Releases the instance: if the stamp matches it resets currentValidStamp with compareAndSet and applies the RELEASE transition, returning true. On a mismatch it throws invalidStamp when throwEx is true, otherwise returns false.

nodes.name: acquireStamp
nodes.summary: Acquires the instance under the lock: waits until no other thread holds it, applies the LOAD transition and returns a new unique stamp.

nodes.name: verifyForMaintenance
nodes.summary: Applies the MAINTENANCE operation, which is legal in RELEASED and ACQUIRED states and fails (invalid transition) in CLOSED.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the instance permanently. Returns false if already CLOSED; otherwise waits for any holder, applies the CLOSE transition and returns true so the caller knows it must close the underlying instance.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Builds the text "[ThreadId: ..., task: partition ... in stage ..., TID ...]" from the weak thread reference and optional TaskContext.

nodes.name: SchemaHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the readers and writers for the on-disk state schema file of a state store, in versions 1, 2 and 3, plus the StateSchemaFormatV3 case class. Readers decode the file into a list of StateStoreColFamilySchema and writers encode it, splitting long JSON into UTF chunks.

nodes.name: StateSchemaFormatV3
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping a list of StateStoreColFamilySchema as the version 3 schema format.

nodes.name: SchemaHelper
nodes.summary: Object that groups the schema reader and writer types: SchemaReader with V1, V2 and V3 readers, and SchemaWriter with V1, V2 and V3 writers. Used to read and write the state schema file of an operator.

nodes.name: SchemaReader
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for reading a schema file version: declares version and read(FSDataInputStream) and has a protected readJsonSchema that joins the chunked UTF strings. Its companion object builds the right reader from a version string via createSchemaReader (versions 1 to 3).
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 54-64 are the companion object SchemaReader, which shares this id.

nodes.name: SchemaV1Reader
nodes.summary: Reads version 1 files: two UTF strings holding the key and value schema, returned as one default column family schema with ids 0.

nodes.name: SchemaV2Reader
nodes.summary: Reads version 2 files: key and value schemas stored as chunked JSON strings, returned as one default column family schema with ids 0.

nodes.name: SchemaV3Reader
nodes.summary: Reads version 3 files: a count of entries, then for each column family the name, key schema id and schema, value schema id and schema, the key encoder spec JSON and an optional user key encoder schema.

nodes.name: SchemaWriter
nodes.summary: Trait for writing a schema file: write emits the version string "v<version>" then calls the abstract writeSchema, and writeJsonSchema splits a JSON string into chunks of at most 65535 characters. Its companion object createSchemaWriter picks the writer by version (1 only when testing, 2, and 3 or 4 use the V3 writer).
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 168-178 are the companion object SchemaWriter, which shares this id.

nodes.name: SchemaV1Writer
nodes.summary: Writes version 1 files: asserts a single column family and writes its key and value schema JSON as two UTF strings.

nodes.name: SchemaV2Writer
nodes.summary: Writes version 2 files: asserts a single column family and writes key and value schema JSON as chunked strings.

nodes.name: SchemaV3Writer
nodes.summary: Writes version 3 files: the number of column families, then per family the name, key schema id and JSON, value schema id and JSON, the key encoder spec JSON, and the user key encoder schema JSON or an empty JSON object when absent.

nodes.name: readJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Reads a chunk count followed by that many UTF strings and concatenates them into one JSON string.

nodes.name: createSchemaReader
nodes.summary: Validates the version string with MetadataVersionUtil.validateVersion (max 3) and returns a new SchemaV1Reader, SchemaV2Reader or SchemaV3Reader.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads two UTF strings as key and value schema and returns a single-element list for the default column family.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads chunked JSON key and value schemas and returns a single-element list for the default column family.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads all column family entries. For each it parses the key encoder spec JSON with json4s and KeyStateEncoderSpec.fromJson using the key schema, and reads the user key encoder schema with Try so a missing one becomes None.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Final method that writes the version string and then delegates to the subclass writeSchema.

nodes.name: writeJsonSchema
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON string as a chunk count followed by UTF chunks of up to 65535 characters, because writeUTF cannot write longer strings in one call.

nodes.name: createSchemaWriter
nodes.summary: Returns the writer for a version number: V1 (only when Utils.isTesting), V2, or V3 for versions 3 and 4; any other version throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: writeSchema
nodes.summary: Asserts exactly one column family and writes its key and value schema JSON strings.

nodes.name: writeSchema
nodes.summary: Asserts exactly one column family and writes its key and value schemas with writeJsonSchema.

nodes.name: writeSchema
nodes.summary: Writes the family count and, for every column family, its name, ids, key and value schemas, key encoder spec and user key encoder schema; asserts keyStateEncoderSpec is defined.

nodes.name: StatePartitionKeyExtractor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StatePartitionKeyExtractor trait, which gets the shuffle partition key out of a state key row for offline state repartitioning, and three implementations: no-op, index based and drop-last-N-fields.

nodes.name: StatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Trait for extracting the partition key (the key used by shuffle) from a state key UnsafeRow. Declares partitionKeySchema and partitionKey(stateKeyRow); returned rows may be reused between calls, so callers that buffer them must copy.

nodes.name: NoopStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Returns the state key row unchanged as the partition key, for operators whose state key is the partition key. The schema is the given stateKeySchema.

nodes.name: IndexBasedStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Takes the struct field at partitionKeyIndex of the state key row as the partition key; the partition key schema is that field data type, cast to StructType, and the row comes from getStruct.

nodes.name: DropLastNFieldsStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Drops the last numLastColsToDrop fields of the state key and uses the remaining fields as the partition key. The schema is built with dropRight (a require checks the key is not left empty) and rows are produced by an UnsafeProjection over BoundReference expressions.

nodes.name: StatePartitionWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines a writer that puts raw key and value bytes of all column families of one state partition into a freshly created state store and commits it as a snapshot, plus the per-column-family info case class. Used when state is rewritten, for example during repartitioning.

nodes.name: StatePartitionWriterColumnFamilyInfo
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a StateStoreColFamilySchema with a useMultipleValuesPerKey flag (true for ListType state variables in TransformWithState).

nodes.name: StatePartitionAllColumnFamiliesWriter
nodes.summary: Writes input rows of (partition_key, key_bytes, value_bytes, column_family_name) into a state store for the target checkpoint location. It lazily creates a provider and an empty store at currentBatchId (loadEmpty = true), creates non-default column families, rebuilds UnsafeRows from the bytes, and uses put, or merge when a multi-value key already exists. write commits and returns the StateStoreCheckpointInfo, aborting if not committed and always closing the provider.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes every input row with writeRow, commits the store and returns getStateStoreCheckpointInfo. In finally it aborts the store if it did not commit and closes the provider.

nodes.name: writeRow
nodes.summary: Asserts the row has 4 fields, rebuilds key and value UnsafeRows from the binary columns with pointTo, then merges when the column family allows multiple values and the key exists, otherwise puts.

nodes.name: StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker.scala
nodes.summary: Checks and evolves the stored schema of a state store: it reads the schema files of an operator, compares the new key and value schemas with the most recent ones, assigns schema ids, and writes a new schema file when something changed. Also defines the value classes StateStoreColFamilySchema, AvroEncoder and StateSchemaValidationResult.

nodes.name: StateSchemaValidationResult
nodes.summary: Case class returned after schema validation, holding whether the schema evolved (evolvedSchema) and the schema file path (schemaPath).

nodes.name: AvroEncoder
nodes.summary: Serializable case class holding Avro serializers and deserializers for keys, values and optional suffix keys, used to convert between UnsafeRow and Avro bytes in RocksDB state stores. Its documentation names RocksDBStateStoreProvider and RocksDBStateEncoder as its main users.

nodes.name: StateStoreColFamilySchema
nodes.summary: Case class describing the schema of one column family: its name, key and value schema ids and StructTypes, the optional KeyStateEncoderSpec and the optional user key encoder schema.

nodes.name: StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker
nodes.summary: Per-operator checker created with a StateStoreProviderId, Hadoop conf and old and new schema file paths. It creates the schema directory, reads the latest or all schema files, checks key schema equality or compatibility and, when value schema evolution is enabled, Avro read compatibility and the evolution and file-count thresholds, and writes a new schema file via a SchemaWriter. The companion object (lines 314-442) has the static entry point used by operators.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 314-442 are the companion object StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker, which shares this id.

nodes.name: readSchemaFile
nodes.summary: Companion method: reads the version string from the stream, builds a SchemaReader with createSchemaReader, reads the column family schemas, logs and rethrows on failure and always closes the stream. The instance method readSchemaFile() at lines 110-113 (same id) opens the latest schema file and calls this one.

nodes.name: readSchemaFiles
nodes.summary: Reads all old schema files plus the latest one (skipping files that do not exist) and groups the column family schemas by column family name. Used for operator state metadata V2 where schema evolution keeps several files.

nodes.name: createSchemaFile
nodes.summary: Writes the schema list to a new file atomically (without overwrite) at newSchemaFilePath, or at the default location, using the given SchemaWriter and cancelling the stream on failure. The private overload at lines 131-141 (same id) first checks that a path exists for version 3+ and creates the writer for the version.

nodes.name: getExistingKeyAndValueSchema
nodes.summary: Returns the schemas in the latest schema file if it exists, otherwise an empty list.

nodes.name: schemasCompatible
nodes.summary: Checks two StructTypes with DataType.equalsIgnoreNameAndCompatibleNullability.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Compares one new column family schema with its old schemas. Equal schemas return unchanged; an incompatible key schema throws stateStoreKeySchemaNotCompatible; with evolution enabled it validates each old value schema against the new Avro schema (SchemaValidatorBuilder canReadStrategy), enforces the value schema evolution threshold and increments the value schema id; otherwise it throws stateStoreValueSchemaNotCompatible or accepts a compatible change. Returns (schema, evolved).

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Companion entry point used by operators. Rejects binary inequality (collation) key columns, builds the StateStoreConf, provider id and checker, runs the instance validation inside Try, rethrows the error when stateSchemaCheckEnabled is set, and returns a StateSchemaValidationResult with the schema file path (new path for version 3+ when evolved, old last path when not, or the static location below version 3). The instance method at lines 261-311 (same id) reads existing schemas, initializes ids to 0 for new families, calls check per family, enforces the schema file threshold and writes a new file for version 3+.

nodes.name: disallowBinaryInequalityColumn
nodes.summary: Throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException (STATE_STORE_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION_BINARY_INEQUALITY) when the schema is not binary stable according to UnsafeRowUtils.isBinaryStable.

nodes.name: schemaFile
nodes.summary: Returns the default schema file path: the _metadata directory under the store checkpoint location, file name "schema".

nodes.name: StateStoreConf.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StateStoreConf, a serializable holder that copies the state store related settings out of a SQLConf (and a few extra options) into plain vals, plus its companion object. Used by state store providers, maintenance tasks, readers, writers and the state rewriter to get consistent configuration on the executors.

nodes.name: StateStoreConf
nodes.summary: Class and companion for state store configuration. Each val is read from SQLConf: maintenance threads and timeouts (numStateStoreMaintenanceThreads, stateStoreMaintenanceShutdownTimeout, stateStoreMaintenanceForceShutdownTimeout, stateStoreMaintenanceProcessingTimeout, maintenanceInterval; lines 33-49, 126-127); retention and snapshots (minDeltasForSnapshot, minVersionsToRetain, minVersionsToDelete, maxVersionsToRetainInMemory, maxVersionsToDeletePerMaintenance; 51-83); auto snapshot repair (autoSnapshotRepairEnabled, autoSnapshotRepairNumFailuresBeforeActivating, autoSnapshotRepairMaxChangeFileReplay; 57-66); provider and validation (providerClass, formatValidationEnabled, commitValidationEnabled, formatValidationCheckValue taken from extraOptions key "formatValidationCheckValue", stateSchemaCheckEnabled, skipNullsForStreamStreamJoins; 85-124); compression and encoding (compressionCodec, stateStoreEncodingFormat; 113-130); file checksums (checkpointFileChecksumEnabled, fileChecksumThreadPoolSize, checkpointFileChecksumSkipCreationIfFileMissingChecksum; 116-150); checkpoint format (enableStateStoreCheckpointIds, stateStoreCheckpointFormatVersion; 132-136, 167-168); coordinator and runtime behavior (reportSnapshotUploadLag, unloadOnCommit; 152-159); row checksums (rowChecksumEnabled, rowChecksumReadVerificationRatio; 161-165); and sqlConfs, the map of all configs starting with "spark.sql.streaming.stateStore." (170-175). A no-argument constructor uses a new SQLConf; the companion has FORMAT_VALIDATION_CHECK_VALUE_CONFIG, an empty instance and apply(conf).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory method that creates a StateStoreConf from a SQLConf with no extra options.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical operator for streaming flatMapGroupsWithState/mapGroupsWithState: the shared trait FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecBase, the concrete FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec case class, its companion with a batch-query planning helper, and the exception that wraps errors thrown by the user function. Used when a streaming query applies a user function with per-key state, optional timeouts and optional initial state.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecBase
nodes.summary: Trait with the shared execution logic for the FlatMapGroupsWithState physical operator; it extends StateStoreWriter and WatermarkSupport. It requires the child data and the optional initial state to be distributed and sorted by the grouping attributes, decides whether another batch is needed for timeouts, produces no output watermark, validates the state schema, and in doExecute runs the user function per partition over a state store (zipping data with initial state when present). The abstract InputProcessor does the per-key work.

nodes.name: InputProcessor
nodes.summary: Abstract inner class of FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecBase created once per partition around a StateStore. processNewData groups input rows by key and calls the user function with the key's state; processNewDataWithInitialState co-groups data with the initial state, writes the initial state first and then calls the function once per key; processTimedOutState finds keys whose timeout timestamp is below the batch time or watermark and calls the function for them. It also holds the numUpdatedStateRows, numOutputRows and numRemovedStateRows metrics. Subclasses implement callFunctionAndUpdateState.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec
nodes.summary: Case class that is the concrete binary physical operator (child data plus initial state) for FlatMapGroupsWithState; it extends FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecBase with BinaryExecNode and ObjectProducerExec. It supplies createInputProcessor, whose callFunctionAndUpdateState converts rows to objects, builds a GroupStateImpl, wraps user exceptions and writes or removes state when the output iterator completes. The companion object (lines 523-594) holds foundDuplicateInitialKeyException and generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries, which plans batch queries as CoGroupExec or MapGroupsExec. The range covers the class and its companion.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateUserFuncException
nodes.summary: Private case class extending SparkException with error class FLATMAPGROUPSWITHSTATE_USER_FUNCTION_ERROR. It wraps a non-Spark exception thrown by the user-provided function so it is reported with the cause message as the reason.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires both children (the data and the initial state) to be distributed by their grouping attributes using StatefulOperatorPartitioning.getCompatibleDistribution, so that rows of the same key are co-located on one task.

nodes.name: shouldRunAnotherBatch
