nodes.summary: Decides whether a batch without new data must still run: always true for ProcessingTimeTimeout, true for EventTimeTimeout only when the new input watermark exceeds the eviction watermark of the executed plan, otherwise false.

nodes.name: processDataWithPartition
nodes.summary: Runs the user function over one partition: optionally drops late rows for event-time timeouts, processes new data (with initial state when present), then lazily appends the timed-out-state iterator so it sees all state updates. When the combined iterator is fully consumed it records update and removal timings, commits the store and sets store and operator metrics.

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the default column family schema from the grouping attributes and the state manager's schema and passes it to StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker.validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema, returning the single validation result.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the operator: forces lazy init of the state manager and metrics on the driver, checks timeout parameters, then either zips child data with the initial state per partition using stateStoreAwareZipPartitions and a StateStore.get call, or uses mapPartitionsWithStateStore; in both cases it creates an InputProcessor and calls processDataWithPartition.

nodes.name: processNewData
nodes.summary: Groups the input rows by the grouping attributes with GroupedIterator and, for each key, fetches the current state from the state manager and calls callFunctionAndUpdateState with hasTimedOut = false.

nodes.name: processNewDataWithInitialState
nodes.summary: Co-groups the child data and the initial state by key with CoGroupedIterator, writes each key's initial state into the state store (failing if a key has more than one initial row), then calls the user function once per key; keys that have only initial state are skipped when skipEmittingInitialStateKeys is set.

nodes.name: processTimedOutState
nodes.summary: When timeouts are enabled, scans all state in the store and selects keys whose timeout timestamp is set and below the threshold (batch timestamp for processing time, eviction watermark for event time), then calls the user function for them with an empty value iterator and hasTimedOut = true.

nodes.name: callFunctionAndUpdateState
nodes.summary: Abstract method that calls the user function on one key's data and updates the state store lazily once the returned iterator is consumed. The concrete implementation is the anonymous InputProcessor created in FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec.createInputProcessor.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Copies the case class with new child plans; the initial state child is replaced only when hasInitialState is true.

nodes.name: createInputProcessor
nodes.summary: Creates the anonymous InputProcessor. Its callFunctionAndUpdateState converts key and value rows to objects, builds a GroupStateImpl via createForStreaming, wraps non-Spark errors from the user function in FlatMapGroupsWithStateUserFuncException, and on completion of the output iterator removes the state, or writes the updated state and timeout timestamp when it changed.

nodes.name: foundDuplicateInitialKeyException
nodes.summary: Companion object method that throws an IllegalArgumentException saying the initial state contained several rows with the same key and must be de-duplicated.

nodes.name: generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries
nodes.summary: Companion object method that plans FlatMapGroupsWithState for batch queries: with initial state it builds a function that enforces one initial row per key, creates a GroupStateImpl and calls the user function, and returns a CoGroupExec; without initial state it returns a MapGroupsExec.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Holds FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecHelper, which defines the StateManager abstraction that stores user-defined group state and an optional timeout timestamp in a state store, with two row layouts (version 1 flat columns, version 2 nested struct), plus the partition key extractor for this operator. Used by FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec to read, write and scan per-key state.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStateExecHelper
nodes.summary: Object that groups the helpers for state handling of FlatMapGroupsWithState: the supported state format versions (1 and 2, legacy version 1), the StateData holder, the sealed StateManager trait, the createStateManager factory and the private StateManager implementations.

nodes.name: StateData
nodes.summary: Case class with mutable fields keyRow, stateRow, stateObj and timeoutTimestamp that captures deserialized state returned by the state manager. It is intended for reuse; the private withNew method refills the fields in place.

nodes.name: StateManager
nodes.summary: Sealed serializable trait for interacting with FlatMapGroupsWithState data in a StateStore: stateSchema, getState, putState, removeState and getAllState.

nodes.name: StateManagerImplBase
nodes.summary: Private abstract base of the StateManager implementations. It reads and writes state rows in the store, converts between state objects and rows through ObjectOperator serializers and deserializers, and reads or sets the timeout timestamp at an ordinal defined by subclasses when timestamps are stored.

nodes.name: StateManagerImplV1
nodes.summary: Private StateManager version 1 that stores the user state as flattened columns followed by a timeout timestamp column. Its limitation, stated in the source, is that the timestamp cannot be set once the user state was removed, since the columns cannot be marked empty together; getStateRow rejects null state.

nodes.name: StateManagerImplV2
nodes.summary: Private StateManager version 2 that stores the user state as one nested struct column plus a timeout timestamp, so the whole state can be null while a timestamp is still set. It builds null-safe serializer and deserializer expressions over the nested struct.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Extends NoopStatePartitionKeyExtractor: for FlatMapGroupsWithStateExec and the Pandas variants (v1 and v2), the state key is the partition key, i.e. the grouping key.

nodes.name: createStateManager
nodes.summary: Factory that returns StateManagerImplV1 for state format version 1, StateManagerImplV2 for version 2, and throws IllegalArgumentException for any other version.

nodes.name: withNew
nodes.summary: Private method that overwrites the key row, state row, state object and timeout in place and returns this, so one StateData instance can be reused.

nodes.name: getState
nodes.summary: Reads the state row for a key from the store and returns the reused StateData filled with the key row, state row, deserialized state object and timeout timestamp.

nodes.name: putState
nodes.summary: Serializes a state object to a row, sets the timeout timestamp in it and puts it into the store under the key.

nodes.name: removeState
nodes.summary: Removes the key from the state store.

nodes.name: getAllState
nodes.summary: Iterates over every key-value pair in the store and maps each to a reused StateData with the deserialized state and timeout timestamp; used for timeout scans.

nodes.name: getStateObject
nodes.summary: Deserializes a state row to an object using the deserializer built from the state schema, or returns null for a null row.

nodes.name: getStateRow
nodes.summary: Serializes a state object to an UnsafeRow with the lazily created state serializer function.

nodes.name: getTimestamp
nodes.summary: Private method returning the timeout timestamp stored at the timeout ordinal of a non-null state row, or NO_TIMESTAMP when timestamps are not stored.

nodes.name: setTimestamp
nodes.summary: Private method writing the timeout timestamp into the state row at the timeout ordinal when timestamps are stored.

nodes.name: getStateRow
nodes.summary: Overrides getStateRow to require a non-null state object (version 1 cannot represent a removed state) and then delegates to the base implementation.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical operator that performs stream-stream joins with a symmetric hash join: each side buffers past input rows as streaming state and joins new input against the other side's buffer, using event-time watermarks to evict state and to emit unmatched rows for outer joins. Used for streaming Inner, LeftOuter, RightOuter, FullOuter and LeftSemi joins; contains the exec case class and its private helper classes for one join side.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec
nodes.summary: Case class for the stream-stream symmetric hash join operator (BinaryExecNode with StateStoreWriter and SchemaValidationUtils). For each input row it computes the join key, appends the row to its own side's state, probes the other side's state, applies the optional condition and emits joined rows. State is evicted using a state key watermark (watermark column in the join keys) or a state value watermark (time range condition in the join condition). Supports state format versions 1 to 4 (versions 3 and above use virtual column families in one store), rejects unsupported join types and Update output mode for outer joins, and an auxiliary constructor builds it from an optional condition with no state info.

nodes.name: throwBadJoinTypeException
nodes.summary: Throws an IllegalArgumentException saying the operator should not take the given join type.

nodes.name: throwBadStateFormatVersionException
nodes.summary: Throws an IllegalStateException for an unexpected state format version.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires each child to be clustered by its join keys (StatefulOpClusteredDistribution) over the number of partitions given in the state info.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes the output attributes by join type: left plus right for inner, nullable right for left outer, nullable left for right outer, all nullable for full outer, left only for left semi.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Computes the output partitioning by join type: a collection of both children's partitioning for inner, the preserved side's partitioning for outer and left semi joins, and unknown partitioning for full outer.

nodes.name: operatorStateMetadata
nodes.summary: Builds operator state metadata: with virtual column families (format 3 and above) it returns OperatorStateMetadataV2 with one StateStoreMetadataV2 per store and StreamingJoinOperatorProperties; otherwise OperatorStateMetadataV1 with the four store names.

nodes.name: getColFamilySchemas
nodes.summary: Returns the column family schemas for the single virtual-column-family store by combining the schemas of the left and right sides from SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.getSchemasForStateStoreWithColFamily.

nodes.name: shouldRunAnotherBatch
nodes.summary: Returns true when state watermark predicates exist on either side and the new input watermark is greater than the eviction watermark of this plan, so a batch without data is run to evict state.

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Validates the state schema. For virtual column families it calls validateAndWriteStateSchema with a hardcoded schema version 3; otherwise it collects key and value schemas of the four stores from both sides and validates each through StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs the join by zipping the left and right child RDDs with stateStoreAwareZipPartitions so that matching partitions share state stores, and processes each partition with processPartitions.

nodes.name: processPartitions
nodes.summary: Core per-partition logic. It creates metrics, a post-join filter and a OneSideHashJoiner per side (wrapped in OneSideHashJoinerManager), joins each side's new rows against the other side's state (right side first for left semi), then adds the outer rows for LeftOuter, RightOuter or FullOuter by lazily evicting aged-out state whose matched flag is not set (state format 1 re-checks the other side's state instead), projects to the output schema and, on completion of the iterator, removes old state, commits the stores and updates metrics.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Copies the case class with new left and right child plans.

nodes.name: customStatefulOperatorMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns a custom sum metric skippedNullValueCount ('number of skipped null values') when skipping nulls for stream-stream joins is enabled in the store configuration, otherwise no custom metrics.

nodes.name: produceOutputWatermark
nodes.summary: Computes the output watermark as the minimum of the left state watermark, the right state watermark and the input watermark, obtained from StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelper.getStateWatermark, so users may rely on both sides' event time columns.

nodes.name: OneSideHashJoiner
nodes.summary: Private helper class for one side of the join. It consumes this side's input rows, drops late rows, applies a pre-join filter, finds matching rows in the other side's SymmetricHashJoinStateManager, generates joined rows, adds processed rows to its own state, and evicts old state by key or value watermark predicates. For state format 4 it computes a timestamp range from the join condition to limit the scan of the other side's state.

nodes.name: AddingProcessedRowToStateCompletionIterator
nodes.summary: Private CompletionIterator over the joined rows of one input row; when it completes, its completion method decides whether the row is appended to the state store with the matched flag (skipped for matched left semi left rows and for right-side rows that will be evicted in this batch and need no unmatched output).

nodes.name: OneSideHashJoinerManager
nodes.summary: Private case class that holds the left and right OneSideHashJoiner and combines their operations: removing old state, collecting removed rows, merging metrics, committing stores (once when virtual column families share one store) and merging checkpoint info.

nodes.name: LazilyInitializingJoinedRowIterator
nodes.summary: Private Iterator[JoinedRow] that builds the underlying iterator from a function only on first use, so the outer-join output is created after the hash join output is exhausted.

nodes.name: computeTimestampRange
nodes.summary: Private method that returns the timestamp range (event time plus lower and upper offset) to scan in the other side's state for a row, or None when no range scan offsets or event time column apply.

nodes.name: storeAndJoinWithOtherSide
nodes.summary: Consumes this side's input: filters late rows by the watermark, builds the output function for the join type and side, and for each row passing the pre-join filter probes the other side's state for matches (removing matched rows for the right side of a left semi join), then wraps the result so that the row is added to this side's state when the output is consumed. Rows failing the pre-join filter yield an immediate null-joined row for outer sides.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the values stored in this joiner's state manager for a key; it must not be interleaved with mutations.

nodes.name: removeOldState
nodes.summary: Evicts old state according to the state key or state value watermark predicate and returns the number of removed rows, using evictByKeyCondition or evictByValueCondition for condition-based managers and evictByTimestamp for timestamp-based managers.

nodes.name: removeAndReturnOldState
nodes.summary: Builds an iterator over old state key-value pairs that removes them lazily as they are produced; it must be fully consumed before other operations on the state manager. Used to avoid two passes when generating outer join rows.

nodes.name: watermarkMsToStateTimestamp
nodes.summary: Private conversion of a watermark in milliseconds to microseconds, the timestamp unit stored in state format 4.

nodes.name: commitState
nodes.summary: Commits changes to this side's buffered state by calling commit on the state manager.

nodes.name: getMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the StateStoreMetrics of this side's state manager.

nodes.name: getLatestCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the latest checkpoint info of this side's state manager as a JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo.

nodes.name: completion
nodes.summary: On completion decides whether to append the input row and key to the state manager: a left semi left row that already matched is skipped, left-side rows are otherwise added, right-side rows are added if not evicted in this batch or if they need to produce an unmatched row for right or full outer joins. The row is stored with matched equal to whether any joined row was produced.

nodes.name: numRemovedFromOtherSideDuringJoin
nodes.summary: Sum of the rows removed from the other side's state during the join phase by both joiners.

nodes.name: removeOldState
nodes.summary: Sum of removeOldState results of the left and right joiners.

nodes.name: removeAndReturnOldState
nodes.summary: Concatenates the lazily evicted old-state iterators of the left and right joiners.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Returns the left joiner's metrics when virtual column families share one store, otherwise combines left and right metrics with StateStoreMetrics.combine.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Commits one shared store through the left joiner when virtual column families are used, otherwise commits the stores of both sides.

nodes.name: getStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Builds StatefulOpStateStoreCheckpointInfo from the left joiner alone with virtual column families, otherwise merges both sides' checkpoint info via SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.mergeStateStoreCheckpointInfo.

nodes.name: totalNumUpdatedStateRows
nodes.summary: Sums the numbers of state rows updated by the left and right joiners, a count maintained outside the state store.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the helper object for the stream-stream symmetric hash join: join side markers, watermark predicate types for join state, a splitter of the join condition into left-only, right-only and both-sides parts, functions that derive the state watermark and the eviction predicates for each side, a zip-partitions RDD that prefers executors already holding the needed state stores, and small case classes that carry checkpoint information for the join state stores.
nodes.languageNotes: One Scala object that nests sealed traits, case objects, case classes, an RDD subclass and an implicit class.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelper
nodes.summary: Helper object for StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec. It groups the join side markers (LeftSide, RightSide), the state watermark predicate types, the join condition splitter, the functions getStateWatermark and getStateWatermarkPredicates, the state-store-aware zip partitions RDD and its implicit helper, and the checkpoint info and checkpoint id case classes for the left and right join state stores.

nodes.name: JoinSide
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that marks which side of the join an item belongs to. Its only implementations are LeftSide and RightSide.

nodes.name: LeftSide
nodes.summary: Case object for the left side of the join; its toString returns "left".

nodes.name: RightSide
nodes.summary: Case object for the right side of the join; its toString returns "right".

nodes.name: JoinStateWatermarkPredicate
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for a watermark predicate on join state. It exposes the predicate expression and a short description, and its toString prints both.

nodes.name: JoinStateKeyWatermarkPredicate
nodes.summary: Case class for a watermark predicate on the state keys. It holds the expression, the current batch eviction watermark (stateWatermark) and an optional previous batch watermark (prevStateWatermark) that gives the lower bound of the range to evict; its description is "key predicate".

nodes.name: JoinStateValueWatermarkPredicate
nodes.summary: Case class for a watermark predicate on the state values, with the same fields and meaning as the key predicate; its description is "value predicate".

nodes.name: JoinStateWatermarkPredicates
nodes.summary: Case class holding the optional watermark predicate for the left and the right join state. Its toString prints a "state cleanup" line for both sides.

nodes.name: JoinConditionSplitPredicates
nodes.summary: Case class that wraps splits of the join condition: leftSideOnly, rightSideOnly, bothSides and the full condition. Its companion object (lines 118-156, extends PredicateHelper) has an apply method that splits the condition into conjuncts, treats nondeterministic conjuncts as needing both sides, and combines each group with And.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion apply: splits an optional join condition into conjuncts, puts deterministic conjuncts that only reference the left (or right) plan output into leftSideOnly (or rightSideOnly), and puts the rest plus all nondeterministic conjuncts into bothSides, then returns a JoinConditionSplitPredicates with the original condition as full.

nodes.name: getStateWatermark
nodes.summary: Computes the state watermark of the left and the right join input. If a watermarked column is part of the join keys, both sides use the eviction watermark; if only an input column has a watermark, it asks StreamingJoinHelper for the state value watermark from the join condition; otherwise it returns None. It first checks that each side has a single event time column.

nodes.name: getStateWatermarkPredicates
nodes.summary: Builds the JoinStateWatermarkPredicates for both join sides. For a watermarked join key it builds a JoinStateKeyWatermarkPredicate on a bound key reference; for a watermarked input column it builds a JoinStateValueWatermarkPredicate from the state value watermark, also computing the previous watermark from the late-events watermark; with no watermark it returns None for that side.

nodes.name: findJoinKeyOrdinalForWatermark
nodes.summary: Returns the index of the first join key that carries event time watermark metadata, looking at the left keys first and then at the right keys. The same ordinal is used on the other side because both key lists have the same field types.

nodes.name: StateStoreAwareZipPartitionsRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that zips the partitions of two parent RDDs and applies a function to the matching partitions. It is a variant of ZippedPartitionsRDD2 that reports as preferred location the executor where the StateStoreProvider of that partition is already loaded, and it fails if the two partitions have different ids. Used by the stream-stream join to run each join task next to its state stores.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: For a partition, builds a StateStoreProviderId for each state store name and asks the store coordinator for the executor location of each, returning the distinct locations.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Computes one partition: takes the two zipped partitions, throws IllegalStateException if their indexes differ, then calls the stored function with the partition id and the iterators of both parent RDDs.

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Clears the parent RDD references and the function after the parent call so they can be released.

nodes.name: StateStoreAwareZipPartitionsHelper
nodes.summary: Implicit class that adds stateStoreAwareZipPartitions to any RDD. The method zips this RDD with a second RDD into a StateStoreAwareZipPartitionsRDD using the operator state info, store names and store coordinator; it is used by StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec.

nodes.name: stateStoreAwareZipPartitions
nodes.summary: Creates a StateStoreAwareZipPartitionsRDD from this RDD and a second RDD, passing the state info, the store names and the coordinator wrapped in Some.

nodes.name: JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo
nodes.summary: Case class that holds the checkpoint info of one side of the join: one for the keyToNumValues store and one for the keyWithIndexToValue store.

nodes.name: JoinStateStoreCkptInfo
nodes.summary: Case class that holds the JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo of the left side and of the right side of the join.

nodes.name: JoinerStateStoreCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Case class that holds the optional checkpoint ids (strings) of the keyToNumValues store and the keyWithIndexToValue store for one side of the join.

nodes.name: JoinStateStoreCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Case class that holds the JoinerStateStoreCheckpointId of the left side and of the right side of the join.

nodes.name: StateStoreRow.scala
nodes.summary: Defines small wrappers around UnsafeRow for the state store: a trait that exposes the wrapped row, the StateStoreRow class that implements it, and ArrayIndexRange, a view over a range of an array that avoids copying.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowWrapper
nodes.summary: Trait for wrapping an immutable UnsafeRow with extra information without copying it; its single method unsafeRow() returns the wrapped row.

nodes.name: StateStoreRow
nodes.summary: Simple wrapper class over a state store UnsafeRow that returns the row from unsafeRow(). Its companion apply builds an instance from a row. StateStoreRowWithChecksum extends it.

nodes.name: ArrayIndexRange
nodes.summary: Case class that represents a range of indices of an array (array, fromIndex, untilIndex exclusive) so a part of the array can be used without copying. It asserts that the range is valid on construction and its length method returns the number of elements. Used for checksum encoding and decoding of key and value bytes.

nodes.name: StateStoreErrors.scala
nodes.summary: Collects the errors raised by the state store and the stateful processor code. It has the StateStoreErrors object of factory methods, a trait for errors that can be converted to a CANNOT_LOAD_STATE_STORE error, and 45 exception classes, each carrying an error class name and message parameters.
nodes.languageNotes: Most exception classes are thin subclasses of SparkRuntimeException, SparkUnsupportedOperationException or SparkException that only pass an errorClass string and a messageParameters map.

nodes.name: StateStoreErrors
nodes.summary: Object that groups factory methods for (most) exceptions thrown from the state store. Almost all methods (lines 43-327) just create one exception class from this file, for example keyRowFormatValidationFailure, invalidStateMachineTransition, rowChecksumVerificationFailed, stateStoreKeySchemaNotCompatible, stateStoreCommitValidationFailed, autoSnapshotRepairFailed and the stream-stream join inconsistent state errors. It also has two require helpers for state values, two internal errors for transform-with-state, and cannotLoadStore.

nodes.name: ConvertableToCannotLoadStoreError
nodes.summary: Trait for an error that can convert itself to a CANNOT_LOAD_STATE_STORE SparkException through convertToCannotLoadStoreError(). The key and value row format validation failures mix it in.

nodes.name: implicitKeyNotFound
nodes.summary: Returns an internal SparkException (category "TWS") saying the implicit key was not found in the state store for the given state name.

nodes.name: missingTimeValues
nodes.summary: Returns an internal SparkException (category "TWS") saying that time values were not found for the given time mode.

nodes.name: requireNonNullStateValue
nodes.summary: Checks that a state value is not null; otherwise raises the ILLEGAL_STATE_STORE_VALUE.NULL_VALUE error with the state name.

nodes.name: requireNonEmptyListStateValue
nodes.summary: Checks that an array state value is not empty; otherwise raises the ILLEGAL_STATE_STORE_VALUE.EMPTY_LIST_VALUE error with the state name.

nodes.name: cannotLoadStore
nodes.summary: Maps a throwable to a CANNOT_LOAD_STATE_STORE error: a SparkException that already has that condition is returned as is, a ConvertableToCannotLoadStoreError is converted, and any other throwable is wrapped with QueryExecutionErrors.cannotLoadStore.

nodes.name: StateStoreRowChecksum.scala
nodes.summary: Implements row checksums for the state store: a row wrapper that carries a checksum, a verifier trait with a sampling checksum verifier, KeyValueChecksum which computes a CRC32C over key and value bytes, and KeyValueChecksumEncoder which writes and reads the checksum in front of key and value row bytes (single value and merged multi-value formats) so corruption can be detected when rows are read.

nodes.name: StateStoreRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: State store row wrapper that extends StateStoreRow and also holds the checksum of the row, returned by checksum. Its companion apply creates it from a row and a checksum. The verifier expects value rows read from the store to be of this type.

nodes.name: KeyValueIntegrityVerifier
nodes.summary: Trait for verifying that a state store key and value pair is not corrupt. It has three verify overloads: for an UnsafeRow key with a value wrapper, for key and optional value byte arrays with an expected checksum, and for key and value ArrayIndexRange with an expected checksum. The companion object (lines 56-68) has create, which returns a KeyValueChecksumVerifier only when row checksums are enabled and the verification ratio is not zero.

nodes.name: KeyValueChecksumVerifier
nodes.summary: Verifier that computes the checksum of the key and value bytes and compares it with the expected checksum, throwing StateStoreErrors.rowChecksumVerificationFailed on mismatch (and logging an error). It only verifies one of every verificationRatio calls to limit cost, counts requests and verifications, mixes in Logging and is not thread safe. The companion apply (lines 176-180) creates it.

nodes.name: KeyValueChecksum
nodes.summary: Object that creates checksum values (Int) from key and value bytes. Overloads accept UnsafeRow key and optional value row, byte arrays, or ArrayIndexRange values; they all end in one CRC32C computation over the key bytes followed by the value bytes.

nodes.name: KeyValueChecksumEncoder
nodes.summary: Object that encodes a checksum together with row bytes and decodes it back. Value rows can be encoded as checksum + length + bytes (so several values can be merged and decoded one by one), or as checksum + bytes for rows that will only ever have a single value; key rows use the single format. Decode methods either copy the bytes or return an ArrayIndexRange to avoid copies, and the decodeAndVerify methods check the checksum with a KeyValueIntegrityVerifier.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Companion factory. Asserts the verification ratio is not negative and returns Some(KeyValueChecksumVerifier) when row checksums are enabled and the ratio is not zero, otherwise None.

nodes.name: shouldVerify
nodes.summary: Increments the request count and returns true (also counting a verification) once for every verificationRatio calls; the verify methods use it to decide whether to check.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Verifies a key row against a value wrapper, which must be a StateStoreRowWithChecksum. If sampling allows, it computes the checksum from the key and value rows and compares it with the checksum stored in the wrapper. Two more overloads (lines 135-143 and 155-163) take byte arrays or ArrayIndexRange values with an expected checksum and do the same.

nodes.name: verifyChecksum
nodes.summary: Compares expected and computed checksums; on mismatch it logs an error with the store id and both checksums and throws StateStoreErrors.rowChecksumVerificationFailed.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a checksum from the key ArrayIndexRange and an optional value ArrayIndexRange using CRC32C and returns it as an Int. Two other overloads (lines 188-190 and 196-200) accept UnsafeRow and byte arrays and convert them into ranges first.

nodes.name: encodeValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Encodes value row bytes as checksum (4 bytes) + row length (4 bytes) + row bytes, a layout that lets more values be merged onto it later.

nodes.name: decodeAndVerifyValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes bytes holding one or more merged encoded values back to the original bytes, copying each value without its checksum and delimiter handling, and verifying each value checksum through the optional verifier. It first measures the total size, then decodes; it is used to support a get for a key with merged values.

nodes.name: decodeAndVerifyMultiValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator of ArrayIndexRange for each original value in possibly merged encoded bytes, verifying each checksum as it goes and skipping the delimiter between values; returns an empty iterator for null bytes. Cheaper than the copying variant.

nodes.name: decodeOneValueRowIndexWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes bytes with exactly one encoded value and returns its ArrayIndexRange and checksum without copying.

nodes.name: getValueRowIndexAndChecksum
nodes.summary: Private helper that reads the checksum and the row size at a start position and returns the ArrayIndexRange of the row bytes together with the checksum.

nodes.name: encodeKeyRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Encodes key row bytes as checksum + row bytes by calling the single value encoder.

nodes.name: decodeKeyRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes an encoded key row and returns the original key bytes and the checksum, using the single value decoder.

nodes.name: decodeAndVerifyKeyRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes an encoded key row and verifies its checksum with the optional verifier (with no value), then returns the original key bytes.

nodes.name: decodeKeyRowIndexWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes an encoded key row and returns an ArrayIndexRange of the key bytes plus the checksum, without copying.

nodes.name: encodeSingleValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Encodes row bytes that will only ever be a single value as checksum (4 bytes) + row bytes, with no length field.

nodes.name: decodeSingleValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes a single value row encoded with checksum in front and returns a copy of the original bytes with the checksum.

nodes.name: decodeAndVerifySingleValueRowWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes a single value row, verifies its checksum against the key bytes with the optional verifier, and returns the original value bytes.

nodes.name: decodeSingleValueRowIndexWithChecksum
nodes.summary: Decodes a single value row and returns an ArrayIndexRange of the value bytes plus the checksum, without copying.

nodes.name: byteOffsetToIndex
nodes.summary: Private helper that converts a byte array address offset to an array index by subtracting the base offset.

nodes.name: byteIndexToOffset
nodes.summary: Private helper that converts an array index to a byte array address offset by adding the base offset.

nodes.name: GroupStateImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Internal implementation of the user-facing group state used by arbitrary stateful operations on grouped streams. It holds the optional state value, tracks updated and removed flags, validates and stores timeout timestamps for processing time and event time timeouts, and can be written to and rebuilt from JSON. The companion object has the creators for streaming and batch use.

nodes.name: GroupStateImpl
nodes.summary: Private[sql] class implementing TestGroupState[S] (not thread-safe). It wraps an optional value with the batch processing time, the event time watermark, the timeout configuration, the hasTimedOut flag and whether a watermark is present. Public methods are exists, get, getOption, update, remove, setTimeoutDuration, setTimeoutTimestamp, getCurrentWatermarkMs and getCurrentProcessingTimeMs; internal ones are isRemoved, isUpdated, getTimeoutTimestampMs and json. The companion object (lines 203-271) defines NO_TIMESTAMP = -1, createForStreaming, createForBatch, groupStateTimeoutFromString and fromJson.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the state value, or throws the stateNotDefinedOrAlreadyRemovedError when no value is defined.

nodes.name: getOption
nodes.summary: Returns the state value as Some, or None when no value is defined.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Sets a new state value. A null value is rejected with IllegalArgumentException; it marks the state as defined and updated and clears the removed flag.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Marks the state as removed: sets defined and updated to false and removed to true.

nodes.name: setTimeoutDuration
nodes.summary: Sets the processing time timeout as batch processing time plus a positive duration in ms; fails if the timeout configuration is not ProcessingTimeTimeout or the duration is not positive. An overload (lines 109-111) takes a duration string and parses it first.

nodes.name: setTimeoutTimestamp
nodes.summary: Sets the event time timeout timestamp in ms after checking event time timeouts are enabled, that the value is positive, and that it is not before the current watermark. Overloads (lines 126-139) accept a timestamp with an additional duration string, a Date, or a Date with an additional duration, and delegate to this one.

nodes.name: getCurrentWatermarkMs
nodes.summary: Returns the event time watermark in ms, or throws cannotGetEventTimeWatermarkError when no watermark is present.

nodes.name: getTimeoutTimestampMs
nodes.summary: Returns the timeout timestamp as an Optional, empty when it equals NO_TIMESTAMP.

nodes.name: parseDuration
nodes.summary: Private helper that parses an interval string, rejects a negative interval with IllegalArgumentException and returns it in milliseconds.

nodes.name: checkTimeoutTimestampAllowed
nodes.summary: Private check that throws cannotSetTimeoutTimestampError unless the timeout configuration is EventTimeTimeout.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes the constructor arguments and the internal flags (defined, updated, removed, timeoutTimestamp) to compact JSON; the value itself is not included and is serialized elsewhere.

nodes.name: createForStreaming
nodes.summary: Companion factory for streaming. Validates that batchProcessingTimeMs and a present eventTimeWatermarkMs are not negative, and that a timed-out state does not use NoTimeout (MISSING_TIMEOUT_CONFIGURATION), then builds the GroupStateImpl.

nodes.name: createForBatch
nodes.summary: Companion factory for batch use: builds a GroupStateImpl[Any] without a value, using the current system time and NO_TIMESTAMP as the watermark.

nodes.name: groupStateTimeoutFromString
nodes.summary: Maps the names "ProcessingTimeTimeout", "EventTimeTimeout" and "NoTimeout" to the GroupStateTimeout constants, otherwise throws IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a GroupStateImpl from a JSON value and an optional state value: reads the constructor fields, rebuilds the object and then restores the defined, updated, removed and timeoutTimestamp fields.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the converter between the value row stored in the join state store and the (actual value, match) pair used by the stream-stream join. It has a trait, a V1 implementation that stores only the value, a V2 implementation that adds a boolean matched field, and a factory chosen by the state format version.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverter
nodes.summary: Trait for converting between the value row kept in the state store and a ValueAndMatchPair. valueAttributes gives the schema of the stored row, convertValue turns a stored row into a pair, and convertToValueRow builds the row to store from a value and its matched flag. The companion object (lines 106-118) has create, which picks the implementation by state format version.

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverterFormatV1
nodes.summary: V1 converter, used only by state format version 1 for backward compatibility. It stores the value row as is and always reports the match status as false, which has a known correctness issue for outer joins (SPARK-26154 in the comment).

nodes.name: StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverterFormatV2
nodes.summary: V2 converter, the default for state format versions 2 and above. It adds a boolean "matched" attribute to the stored row, using unsafe projections to add and strip the field, which fixes the outer join problem of V1.

nodes.name: convertValue
nodes.summary: Wraps a non-null stored row in a ValueAndMatchPair with matched set to false; returns null for a null row.

nodes.name: convertValue
nodes.summary: Strips the matched field from a non-null stored row with a projection (copied) and returns it with the stored matched boolean; returns null for a null row.

nodes.name: convertToValueRow
nodes.summary: Projects the value into a row with the extra matched field and sets that field to the given flag; the returned row can be reused by the projection.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Companion factory: returns the V1 converter for state format version 1, the V2 converter for versions 2, 3 and 4, and throws IllegalArgumentException for other versions.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorPartitioning.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StatefulOperatorPartitioning object, which picks the required child distribution for a stateful streaming operator. It keeps old checkpoints compatible by choosing between a strict stateful distribution and a plain clustered distribution based on a SQL setting.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorPartitioning
nodes.summary: Object that provides the clustered distribution a stateful operator requires from its child, with backward compatibility. It is used by stateful operators that do not already require StatefulOpClusteredDistribution; its doc points to SPARK-38204 and says to read the note on StatefulOpClusteredDistribution before changing it.

nodes.name: getCompatibleDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns StatefulOpClusteredDistribution(expressions, numPartitions) when the STATEFUL_OPERATOR_USE_STRICT_DISTRIBUTION setting is on, otherwise ClusteredDistribution with requiredNumPartitions set to numPartitions. Overloaded: one variant (lines 36-41) takes a StatefulOperatorStateInfo and forwards its numPartitions to this variant (lines 43-52, the node range).

nodes.name: MergingSortWithSessionWindowStateIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines an iterator that merges sorted input rows with the sessions already stored in state for session window aggregation. It avoids a full sort of input plus state by relying on the input being sorted by group keys and session start time.

nodes.name: MergingSortWithSessionWindowStateIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator[InternalRow] that merge-sorts input rows (already sorted by group keys and session start) with existing sessions read from a ReadStateStore through a StreamingSessionWindowStateManager. Only the existing sessions of one group key are materialized and sorted; input rows are never buffered. Output stays sorted by group keys and session start time.

nodes.name: SessionRowInformation
nodes.summary: Private case class (with a companion object, lines 56-66, sharing this id) that wraps a row with its group keys, session start and session end. The companion method of(row) projects the keys and the session struct out of the row.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Builds a SessionRowInformation from a row: copies the grouping keys using keysProjection and reads session start and end from the session struct produced by sessionProjection.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Returns true while a row is buffered from the input or from the state side, the state session iterator has more rows, or the input iterator has more rows.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Returns the next row of the merged output. It fills the current input row and current state row when empty, then emits the state row when its key differs from the input key or its session start is not later, otherwise the input row. Throws IllegalStateException if neither side has a row.

nodes.name: mayFillCurrentRow
nodes.summary: Pulls the next row from the input iterator, if any, and stores it as the current input row wrapped in SessionRowInformation.

nodes.name: mayFillCurrentStateRow
nodes.summary: Advances the state side. When the state session iterator is exhausted and the current input key is new, it loads all sessions for that key via StreamingSessionWindowStateManager.getSessions, copies and sorts them by session start, and sets the first one as the current state row.

nodes.name: StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the factory that maps a stateful operator name to the StatePartitionKeyExtractor used for offline state repartitioning. Operators not registered here are rejected as unsupported.

nodes.name: StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory
nodes.summary: Object that creates state partition key extractors per stateful operator for offline state repartitioning. Its doc says that to support a new operator one must write an extractor and register it here. It covers streaming aggregation, deduplicate, deduplicate within watermark, session window, symmetric hash join, flatMapGroupsWithState and transformWithState operators.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Matches operatorName against the operator name constants of StatefulOperatorsUtils and returns the matching extractor. The join case delegates to SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.createPartitionKeyExtractor (needs stateFormatVersion), the transformWithState case requires stateVariableInfo and delegates to TransformWithStatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory.create, and unknown operators raise OfflineStateRepartitionErrors.unsupportedStatefulOperatorError. Takes optional storeName, colFamilyName, stateFormatVersion and stateVariableInfo.

nodes.name: StreamingSessionWindowStateManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the state manager abstraction for streaming session window aggregation, its only implementation (format version 1), a helper that extracts session start and end from rows, and the partition key extractor for session window state. State rows are keyed by the group key plus the session start time.

nodes.name: StreamingSessionWindowStateManager
nodes.summary: Sealed serializable trait (lines 29-110; its companion object, lines 112-126, shares this id) describing how session window state is stored. Methods: getStateKeySchema, getStateValueSchema, getNumColsForPrefixKey, extractKeyWithoutSession, newOrModified, getSessions, updateSessions, removeByValueCondition, iterator, commit and abortIfNeeded. The companion lists supportedVersions (Seq(1)) and builds a manager by state format version.

nodes.name: createStateManager
nodes.summary: Companion factory: for stateFormatVersion 1 returns a StreamingSessionWindowStateManagerImplV1 built from the key expressions, session expression and input row attributes; any other version throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: newOrModified
nodes.summary: Trait method: true if the session of the given value is not in the store, or the stored value differs from it. Used to control which rows are output in UPDATE mode.

nodes.name: getSessions
nodes.summary: Trait method: returns all stored sessions for a key that has no session part, as obtained from extractKeyWithoutSession.

nodes.name: updateSessions
nodes.summary: Trait method: replaces all sessions for a key with the given ones; existing sessions not in the given list are removed. Returns a tuple (number of added or updated rows, number of deleted rows).

nodes.name: removeByValueCondition
nodes.summary: Trait method: returns an iterator over values matching a predicate; producing an element removes it from the store. The iterator must be fully consumed without other operations on the manager or store in between.

nodes.name: StreamingSessionWindowStateManagerImplV1
nodes.summary: Version 1 implementation of the session window state manager. The state key is the group key plus a non-null sessionStartTime timestamp column, the value is the whole input row, and the prefix key is the group key columns so that all sessions of a group key are found by prefix scan. Used by streaming session window aggregation.

nodes.name: newOrModified
nodes.summary: Looks up the state key (group key plus session start) in the store and returns true when nothing is stored or the stored row differs from the given value.

nodes.name: updateSessions
nodes.summary: Materializes the new sessions and the currently stored sessions of the key (copying rows), then calls putRows to write the new ones and delete the stale ones.

nodes.name: removeByValueCondition
nodes.summary: Returns a NextIterator that scans all state entries, removes from the store each entry whose value satisfies the predicate and returns the removed value, finishing when the scan ends.

nodes.name: getStateKey
nodes.summary: Builds the state key row for a group key by appending the session start time to it and returns a copy.

nodes.name: putRows
nodes.summary: Writes the new session rows under keys built from the group key and each session start, removes old keys that are no longer present, and returns (upserted rows, deleted rows). Equal session starts are overwritten with put instead of remove plus put to avoid needless tombstones.

nodes.name: abortIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Aborts the state store (after logging its id) if it has not been committed yet.

nodes.name: StreamingSessionWindowHelper
nodes.summary: Helper built from the session window expression and the input schema. Its extractTimePair(value) reads the session_window struct of a row and returns (start, end) as longs. Used by the version 1 state manager.

nodes.name: extractTimePair
nodes.summary: Projects the session window column out of a row and returns its start and end times as a (Long, Long) pair.

nodes.name: StreamingSessionWindowStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: State partition key extractor for session window state: the state key is the session key plus sessionStartTime, so it drops the last field (numLastColsToDrop = 1) to get the partition key. Registered for offline state repartitioning in StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the state manager for one side of the stream-stream symmetric hash join: a base trait with append, get, getJoinedRows, eviction and commit APIs, three older implementations (V1 with four state stores, V2 with one store and virtual column families, both on a shared abstract base) and a newer V4 that buckets values by event time and keeps a timestamp-ordered secondary index. Also holds the companion object with the version factory, store naming, schema, checkpoint-id and partition-key-extractor helpers, plus snapshot option case classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a trait hierarchy, mixin traits for eviction strategy, inner classes that wrap state stores and NextIterator subclasses that perform state mutations as a side effect of iteration.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManager
nodes.summary: Base trait of the state manager for a stream-stream symmetric hash join side. It declares append, get, getJoinedRows (with an optional timestampRange hint and a skipUpdatingMatchedFlag switch), getJoinedRowsAndRemoveMatched, iterator, commit, abortIfNeeded, metrics and getLatestCheckpointInfo; eviction methods live in the separate SupportsEvictByCondition and SupportsEvictByTimestamp traits. The companion object (lines 2025-2413) shares this id and holds the apply factory that picks V1, V2 or V4 by state format version, plus store naming and schema helpers.

nodes.name: SupportsIndexedKeys
nodes.summary: Trait for the older (v1 to v3) state manager implementations so existing tests can look up the state store by key with index. It declares getInternalRowOfKeyWithIndex and the test-only updateNumValuesTestOnly.

nodes.name: SupportsEvictByCondition
nodes.summary: Trait for state manager implementations that evict by a full scan using a predicate. It declares evictByKeyCondition, evictAndReturnByKeyCondition, evictByValueCondition and evictAndReturnByValueCondition; the plain variants return the number of evicted values and the AndReturn variants return an iterator of key-value pairs the caller must consume fully. It has a self type of SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.

nodes.name: SupportsEvictByTimestamp
nodes.summary: Trait for state manager implementations that keep state by event time and can scan only keys older than a timestamp. It declares evictByTimestamp and evictAndReturnByTimestamp with an inclusive endTimestamp and an optional exclusive startTimestamp from which the scan resumes. It has a self type of SymmetricHashJoinStateManager.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerV4
nodes.summary: Version 4 state manager that stores (key, timestamp) -> list of (value, matched) in a primary store and a secondary (timestamp, key) index, both as virtual column families in one state store, so watermark eviction scans only keys older than the watermark. It derives the event time from the value row or the join key, falls back to random bucketing when there is no event time, and its source says it requires RocksDBStateStoreProvider. Created by the factory in the companion object when the state format version is 4.

nodes.name: GetValuesResult
nodes.summary: Reusable holder of a timestamp and its Seq of ValueAndMatchPair returned by KeyWithTsToValuesStore. withNew overwrites both fields in place to avoid allocation.

nodes.name: KeyWithTsToValuesStore
nodes.summary: Primary store of version 4: maps [key][event time] to a list of (value, matched) in a virtual column family. It offers append (blind merge), put (rewrite the list), get, remove, getValues, getValuesInRange (range scan when the upper bound is finite, prefix scan otherwise) and iterator, converting rows with StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverter.

nodes.name: TsWithKeyTypeStore
nodes.summary: Secondary index of version 4: maps [timestamp][key] to a list of empty values in an internal column family, ordered by timestamp. add and remove maintain it, and scanEvictedKeys range-scans it to produce (key, timestamp, count) results used by watermark eviction.

nodes.name: EvictedKeysResult
nodes.summary: Case class holding one evictable (key, timestamp) pair and the number of values counted for it in the secondary index.

nodes.name: getStateStore
nodes.summary: Loads the single state store of V4 with virtual column families enabled. With the coordinator it asks JoinStateManagerStoreGenerator; otherwise it creates its own StateStoreProvider and, if snapshot options are set, replays state from a snapshot (requiring SupportsFineGrainedReplay) or gets the store for the current version.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Appends a value for a key by extracting the event time (from the key if a watermark ordinal exists, otherwise from the value), blind-merging into KeyWithTsToValuesStore and, when event time exists, adding to the TsWithKey index.

nodes.name: getJoinedRows
nodes.summary: Returns joined rows for a key, filtered by the predicate. It reads values for one timestamp when the key carries event time, or a range of timestamps otherwise (using timestampRange), and updates matched flags back into the store when the iterator closes unless skipUpdatingMatchedFlag is set.

nodes.name: getJoinedRowsAndRemoveMatched
nodes.summary: Returns joined rows that pass the predicate and removes them from state in one pass. Entries already marked matched are dropped without being returned; when the iterator closes, the remaining values are rewritten or the (key, timestamp) entry is removed from both stores.

nodes.name: evictByTimestamp
nodes.summary: Evicts all (key, timestamp) entries up to endTimestamp (after an optional startTimestamp) by scanning the secondary index and removing each entry from both stores, and returns the number of removed values. Requires event time to exist.

nodes.name: evictAndReturnByTimestamp
nodes.summary: Like evictByTimestamp but lazily returns the evicted key-value pairs through a reused KeyToValuePair, removing entries from both stores as the iterator is consumed.

nodes.name: abortIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Aborts the state store if it has not committed and closes the state store provider when this class created it itself.

nodes.name: getLatestCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Reads the checkpoint information of the single store twice, asserts both are equal and wraps them in a JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo, keeping the same shape as the other versions.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Replaces the whole value list of a (key, timestamp) entry by converting each value with its matched flag (copying the reused projection output) and calling putList on the state store.

nodes.name: getValuesInRange
nodes.summary: Returns entries with minTs <= timestamp <= maxTs for a key, grouped by timestamp, as an iterator of GetValuesResult. It uses rangeScanWithMultiValues when maxTs is below Long.MaxValue and prefixScanWithMultiValues otherwise, filtering out-of-range entries so both paths agree, and raises a StateStoreErrors error if a range scan returns an unexpected timestamp.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Iterates all entries of the primary column family, detaching the timestamp from each key and returning a reused KeyAndTsToValuePair.

nodes.name: scanEvictedKeys
nodes.summary: Range-scans the timestamp-ordered index from startTimestamp + 1 to endTimestamp (inclusive) and groups consecutive records of the same (key, timestamp) into EvictedKeysResult with a count. Returns an empty iterator when startTimestamp is Long.MaxValue and closes the underlying scan iterator on completion.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base of the older (v1 to v3) join state managers. It models a multi-map by keeping two wrapped stores, KeyToNumValuesStore (key -> value count) and KeyWithIndexToValueStore ((key, index) -> value and matched flag), and implements get, append, getJoinedRows, getJoinedRowsAndRemoveMatched, iterator and the evict-by-key and evict-by-value methods using swap-with-last compaction. Subclasses V1 and V2 supply commit, abortIfNeeded, metrics and checkpoint info.

nodes.name: StateStoreHandler
nodes.summary: Helper base class for the two inner store wrappers. It offers commit, abortIfNeeded (also closes a provider it created), metrics, getLatestCheckpointInfo and getStateStore, which either gets a store from JoinStateManagerStoreGenerator or creates its own provider, optionally replaying a snapshot.

nodes.name: KeyAndNumValues
nodes.summary: Reusable holder of a key row and its number of values, returned while iterating KeyToNumValuesStore.

nodes.name: KeyToNumValuesStore
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a state store that maps a join key to the number of values stored for it. It provides get (0 if absent), put (requires a positive count), remove and iterator, and uses a virtual column family when the state format version is 3 or higher.

nodes.name: KeyWithIndexAndValue
nodes.summary: Reusable holder of a key, a value index, a value and its matched flag. It has two withNew overloads, one taking the raw value and flag and one taking a ValueAndMatchPair (null yields a null value and false).

nodes.name: KeyWithIndexToValueStore
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a state store that maps (key, index) to a value and matched flag, converting rows with StreamingSymmetricHashJoinValueRowConverter according to the state format version. It provides get, getAll (skipping or failing on null values via handleNullValuePair), put, remove, removeAllValues and iterator.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerV1
nodes.summary: State manager that uses separate state stores without virtual column families for each join side and store type. It commits and aborts both stores, checks that their checkpoint info agrees on partition, batch version and presence of a checkpoint id, and combines the metrics of both stores with the side name added to custom metric descriptions. Created by the factory for state format versions other than 3 and 4.

nodes.name: SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerV2
nodes.summary: State manager that keeps both inner stores in one state store with virtual column families. Commit, abort and metrics come from the keyToNumValues wrapper only, and the checkpoint info of the two wrappers is asserted equal. Created by the factory when the state format version is 3.

nodes.name: JoinStateManagerStoreGenerator
nodes.summary: Creates the state store for join state managers. With virtual column families it creates the store once through StateStore.get and returns the same instance on later calls; without them it creates a distinct store every time.

nodes.name: StateStoreType
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the kinds of state stores or column families used by the join state managers.

nodes.name: KeyToNumValuesType
nodes.summary: Case object for the key-to-number-of-values store type, with toString "keyToNumValues".

nodes.name: KeyWithIndexToValueType
nodes.summary: Case object for the (key, index)-to-value store type, with toString "keyWithIndexToValue".

nodes.name: KeyWithTsToValuesType
nodes.summary: Case object for the V4 primary store type, with toString "keyWithTsToValues".

nodes.name: TsWithKeyType
nodes.summary: Case object for the V4 secondary index store type, with toString "tsWithKey".

nodes.name: ValueAndMatchPair
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a stored value row with its matched flag.

nodes.name: KeyToValuePair
nodes.summary: Mutable case class for a key, value and matched flag designed for object reuse. Its two withNew overloads reset the fields from raw values or from a ValueAndMatchPair. Used as the element type of iterator and eviction results.

nodes.name: KeyAndTsToValuePair
nodes.summary: Mutable case class for a (key, timestamp) to (value, matched) record designed for object reuse, with two withNew overloads. Used by the V4 primary store iterator.

nodes.name: SnapshotOptions
nodes.summary: Case class of options for snapshot-based state replay, used by the state data source reader: snapshot and end versions plus start and end checkpoint ids for both stores. getKeyToNumValuesHandlerOpts and getKeyWithIndexToValueHandlerOpts turn it into HandlerSnapshotOptions for one store handler.

nodes.name: HandlerSnapshotOptions
nodes.summary: Package-private case class of snapshot replay options (versions and start and end checkpoint ids) for a single state store handler.

nodes.name: getRightMostNonNullIndex
nodes.summary: Finds the highest index not below stopIndex whose stored value is non-null, searching from the end.

nodes.name: removeValueAtIndex
nodes.summary: Removes the value at an index by swap-with-last compaction: it moves the last element into the hole, cleans up trailing nulls (logging a warning for them), removes the last slot and returns the new value count.

nodes.name: getJoinedRowsAndRemoveMatched
nodes.summary: Streaming one-value-at-a-time implementation that returns joined rows passing the predicate and removes them with removeValueAtIndex. Values already marked matched are removed without being returned, null values go through handleNullValuePair, and the value count is updated or removed at the end.

nodes.name: getJoinedRows
nodes.summary: Returns joined rows for a key that pass the predicate, writing matched = true back to state unless skipUpdatingMatchedFlag is set. The timestampRange hint is ignored in this version.

nodes.name: evictByKeyCondition
nodes.summary: Scans all keys in keyToNumValues, removes every value and the count entry of keys that satisfy the predicate, and returns the number of values removed.

nodes.name: evictAndReturnByKeyCondition
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator of key-value-matched records for keys that satisfy the predicate, removing each from state as it is produced. The iterator must be consumed fully with no interleaved operations.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Full scan that walks every key in keyToNumValues and every index below its count, returning (key, value, matched) records through a reused KeyToValuePair.

nodes.name: evictAndReturnByValueCondition
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over values satisfying the predicate and removes each from the state store through removeValueAtIndex, updating the per-key value count when moving to the next key. Null values go through handleNullValuePair. evictByValueCondition counts the results of this method.

nodes.name: handleNullValuePair
nodes.summary: Called when a stored value is null although the count says it exists. It logs a diagnostic warning once per instance and throws a StateStoreErrors error unless skipNullsForStreamStreamJoins is enabled.

nodes.name: getStateStore
nodes.summary: Gets the StateStore for a handler: the default store name with virtual column families or a name from side and store type otherwise, via JoinStateManagerStoreGenerator or a self-managed provider with optional snapshot replay.

nodes.name: abortIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Aborts the store if not committed and closes the self-managed provider, if any.

nodes.name: getAll
nodes.summary: Iterates the values at indices 0 until numValues for a key, reusing one KeyWithIndexAndValue. Null values are passed to handleNullValuePair, counted in skippedNullValueCount and skipped.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Iterates all (key, index, value) entries of the store with a reused KeyWithIndexAndValue.

nodes.name: getLatestCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Collects checkpoint info of both stores, asserts matching partition id, batch version and checkpoint id presence, and returns a JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Combines metrics of the two stores: key count from keyWithIndexToValue, summed memory, custom metrics renamed with the uppercased join side prefix, and instance metrics of both.

nodes.name: getLatestCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Reads checkpoint info of the two wrappers that share one store, asserts they are equal and wraps them in a JoinerStateStoreCkptInfo.

nodes.name: getStore
nodes.summary: Returns the cached store when virtual column families are used (creating it through StateStore.get on first use) or creates a new store otherwise.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that creates SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerV4 for format version 4 (after requiring the STREAMING_JOIN_STATE_FORMAT_V4_ENABLED setting), V2 for version 3 and V1 otherwise.

nodes.name: allStateStoreNames
nodes.summary: Lists store names for the given join sides with the keyToNumValues and keyWithIndexToValue types. allStateStoreNamesV4 (2081-2086) does the same for the V4 types.

nodes.name: getSchemaForStateStores
nodes.summary: Builds a map from store name to (key schema, value schema): two timestamp-keyed schemas for version 4, otherwise the count store and the key-with-index store, where the value schema carries a matched column for versions 2 and 3.

nodes.name: getSchemasForStateStoreWithColFamily
nodes.summary: Wraps getSchemaForStateStores results in StateStoreColFamilySchema objects with the key encoder spec for the version (timestamp postfix or prefix for version 4, no-prefix otherwise).

nodes.name: mergeStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Asserts the two sides agree on partition, batch version and checkpoint id presence, then merges the four checkpoint ids (and base ids) into arrays in a StatefulOpStateStoreCheckpointInfo.

nodes.name: getStateStoreCheckpointIds
nodes.summary: Splits the merged checkpoint id array of a partition back into per-store ids: the first id for every store when column families are used, otherwise four ids in left and right order.

nodes.name: getStateStoreCheckpointId
nodes.summary: Returns the checkpoint id of the store with a given name for a partition, by matching the name to left or right keyToNumValues and keyWithIndexToValue stores, or None.

nodes.name: getStateStoreName
nodes.summary: Builds the store or column family name as joinSide-storeType.

nodes.name: getStoreType
nodes.summary: Maps a store name back to its StateStoreType for either side, and throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown names.

nodes.name: createPartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Returns a StatePartitionKeyExtractor for a join store: a DropLastNFields extractor (dropping the index column) for keyWithIndexToValue stores and a no-op extractor for the other types.

nodes.name: streamingLimits.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the two physical operators that implement limit in streaming queries: StreamingGlobalLimitExec, which keeps a running row count in state to cap total output across batches, and StreamingLocalLimitExec, which limits rows per partition while draining the child.

nodes.name: StreamingGlobalLimitExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator that ensures no more than streamLimit rows are returned in total. It is meant for logical limits over append-like input, such as a limit on any query in append mode or a limit before the aggregation in a complete mode streaming aggregation. It requires AllTuples distribution and stores the cumulative row count in a state store under a single null key; metrics include numOutputRows, numUpdatedStateRows, allUpdatesTimeMs and commitTimeMs. shortName is globalLimit.

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds a single default column family schema (null key, long value) and validates or evolves it through StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker, returning the validation result list.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs the child with mapPartitionsWithStateStore. It reads the count stored before the batch, filters rows while the cumulative count is below streamLimit, and, when the iterator completes, writes the new count to the store, updates the output and state metrics, commits the store and sets store and operator metrics.

nodes.name: StreamingLocalLimitExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical limit operator that applies the limit per partition. Unlike LocalLimitExec it fully consumes the child iterator on close, so stateful operators inside the child commit their state changes. It passes through the child output, outputPartitioning and outputOrdering.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Wraps each child partition iterator in a NextIterator that returns rows until the limit is reached, then marks it finished; on close it drains the remaining child rows.

nodes.name: StateStoreColumnFamilySchemaUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines helpers for the column families that transformWithState keeps in a state store: naming of internal column families ($ttl_, $min_, $count_ and row counter prefixes), schema builders for value, list, map and timer state, and a conversion of fixed-size fields for range scans.

nodes.name: StateStoreColumnFamilySchemaUtils
nodes.summary: Object holding column family naming and schema helpers for transformWithState. Name helpers (lines 66-105): getTtlColFamilyName, isTtlColFamilyName, getStateNameFromTtlColFamily for the "$ttl_" prefix, the same three for "$min_" (getMinExpiryIndexCFName ...) and "$count_" (getCountIndexCFName ...), isInternalColFamily (name starts with "$") and isTestingInternalColFamily. Schema builders: getValueStateSchema, getListStateSchema, getMapStateSchema, getTimerStateSchema, getSecIndexTimerStateSchema, each returning StateStoreColFamilySchema entries with their state encoder specs, plus TTL index, min expiry and count schemas when TTL is on. Also getBaseStateName and convertForRangeScan.

nodes.name: convertForRangeScan
nodes.summary: Rewrites a schema for range scans: each fixed-size field (byte, boolean, short, int, long, float, double) at the chosen ordinals, or all if none are given, becomes a nullable binary "<name>_marker" field plus a binary "<name>_value" field. The goal is big-endian ordering, since Avro uses zig-zag encoding for ints and longs.

nodes.name: getStateNameForInternalCF
nodes.summary: Private helper that maps an internal column family name ($ttl_, $min_, $count_, row counter or timer) back to its state variable name. For timer secondary index column families it returns the primary index name; unknown internal names raise StateStoreErrors.unknownInternalColumnFamily.

nodes.name: getBaseStateName
nodes.summary: Returns the state variable name that a column family belongs to, for looking up its stateVariableInfo: the mapped name for internal ("$") column families, the name itself for user-facing ones.

nodes.name: getValueStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the column family schemas for a value state: the main column family (no-prefix key encoder spec, value schema with optional TTL) and, when hasTtl is true, a TTL index column family with a range-scan key.

nodes.name: getListStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the column family schemas for a list state: main column family, a row counter column family (long "count"), and with TTL also a TTL index, a min expiry index and a count index.

nodes.name: getMapStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the column family schemas for a map state: the main column family uses a composite (grouping key, user key) schema with a prefix-scan encoder spec on the first column, plus a TTL index when hasTtl is true.

nodes.name: getTimerStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the StateStoreColFamilySchema of a timer primary index column family, with a prefix-scan encoder spec on one key column.

nodes.name: getSecIndexTimerStateSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the StateStoreColFamilySchema of a timer secondary index column family, with a range-scan encoder spec on the first key column.

nodes.name: StateTypesEncoderUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the encoders and schema helpers that transformWithState uses to turn grouping keys, user keys, values, TTL entries and timer keys into UnsafeRow, plus the partition key extractors for its column families and the factory that picks one per state variable.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateKeyValueRowSchemaUtils
nodes.summary: Helper object that builds the key and value row schemas used in state schema files and passed into the state key and value encoders: composite key (key plus userKey), TTL index key (expirationMs plus elementKey), expirationMs row and value-with-TTL schemas.

nodes.name: getCompositeKeySchema
nodes.summary: Returns a struct schema with a "key" struct (grouping key schema) and a "userKey" struct (user key schema). MapState uses it as the element key for TTL.

nodes.name: getTTLRowKeySchema
nodes.summary: Returns the schema of keys in the TTL index: a long "expirationMs" followed by the "elementKey" struct. TTL index entries have no value.

nodes.name: getExpirationMsRowSchema
nodes.summary: Returns a one-field schema holding a long "expirationMs", used for entries of the minimum expiry index.

nodes.name: getValueSchemaWithTTL
nodes.summary: Returns the value schema: when hasTTL is true a struct of "value" plus long "ttlExpirationMs", otherwise the schema unchanged.

nodes.name: StateTypesEncoder
nodes.summary: Class (with companion object, lines 169-177, sharing this id and providing apply with hasTtl defaulting to false) that encodes the implicit grouping key and user values to UnsafeRow and decodes them back, optionally with a TTL expiration. It reuses projections and is not thread safe. Main methods: encodeGroupingKey, encodeValue (with and without expirationMs), decodeValue, decodeTtlExpirationMs, isExpired.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a StateTypesEncoder from key encoder, value encoder, state name and hasTtl (default false).

nodes.name: encodeGroupingKey
nodes.summary: Serializes the implicit grouping key from ImplicitGroupingKeyTracker into an UnsafeRow; throws StateStoreErrors.implicitKeyNotFound if no key is set.

nodes.name: encodeValue
nodes.summary: Encodes a value into an UnsafeRow. Overloaded: encodeValue(value) (lines 126-128) has no TTL; encodeValue(value, expirationMs) (lines 134-137, node range) wraps the value row and the expiration time in the value-with-TTL projection.

nodes.name: decodeValue
nodes.summary: Decodes an UnsafeRow to a value object; when TTL is enabled it first extracts the value struct from the row.

nodes.name: decodeTtlExpirationMs
nodes.summary: Reads the TTL expiration from a value row (asserts TTL is enabled); -1 means none was set and yields None.

nodes.name: isExpired
nodes.summary: Returns true if the row has a TTL expiration that StateTTL.isExpired reports as expired for the given batch timestamp.

nodes.name: CompositeKeyStateEncoder
nodes.summary: Subclass of StateTypesEncoder for map state: encodes a composite row of grouping key plus user key. Its doc notes the grouping key is the prefix column handled by the state encoder. Methods: encodeGroupingKey (wraps key in "key" column), encodeUserKey, encodeCompositeKey (two overloads), decodeCompositeKey.

nodes.name: encodeGroupingKey
nodes.summary: Override that serializes the implicit grouping key and wraps it in a row with a single "key" column; throws implicitKeyNotFound if none is set.

nodes.name: encodeUserKey
nodes.summary: Serializes a user key and wraps it in a row with a single "userKey" column.

nodes.name: encodeCompositeKey
nodes.summary: Encodes grouping key and user key into one row of the composite key schema. Overloaded: encodeCompositeKey(userKey) (lines 233-245, node range) takes the implicit grouping key; encodeCompositeKey(groupingKey, userKey) (lines 247-249) takes both as UnsafeRows.

nodes.name: decodeCompositeKey
nodes.summary: Decodes a composite key row and returns only the user key object, ignoring the grouping key.

nodes.name: TTLEncoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for the TTL index with single key serialization. encodeTTLRow(expirationMs, elementKey) builds an (expirationMs, groupingKey) UnsafeRow.

nodes.name: encodeTTLRow
nodes.summary: Turns an element key row and an expiration time into the TTL index key row (expirationMs, elementKey).

nodes.name: TimerKeyEncoder
nodes.summary: Encoder for timer state keys. Exposes keySchemaForSecIndex (expiryTimestampMs, key), schemaForKeyRow (key, expiryTimestampMs) and a dummy value schema, and encodes/decodes: encodedKey, encodeSecIndexKey, encodePrefixKey, decodePrefixKey.

nodes.name: encodedKey
nodes.summary: Builds the primary index key row (key, expiryTimestampMs) for a grouping key and expiry time.

nodes.name: encodeSecIndexKey
nodes.summary: Builds the secondary index key row (expiryTimestampMs, key) used to scan timers in expiry order.

nodes.name: encodePrefixKey
nodes.summary: Builds the prefix key row (key) from a grouping key, used to find all timers for that key.

nodes.name: decodePrefixKey
nodes.summary: Deserializes a prefix key row back to the grouping key object.

nodes.name: MapStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Partition key extractor for the MapState main column family: the state key is the composite (key, userKey) struct and the partition key is its first field, the grouping key (partitionKeyIndex = 0).

nodes.name: TTLStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Partition key extractor for TTL index column families of Value and List state: keys are (expirationMs, elementKey) and the partition key is the elementKey (partitionKeyIndex = 1).

nodes.name: MapTTLStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Partition key extractor for the MapState TTL column family: first extracts the composite key from the (expirationMs, elementKey) TTL key with TTLStatePartitionKeyExtractor, then the grouping key from it with MapStatePartitionKeyExtractor.

nodes.name: partitionKey
nodes.summary: Applies the TTL extractor and then the map extractor to a state key row to return the grouping key.

nodes.name: TimerStatePartitionKeyExtractor
