nodes.summary: Partition key extractor for timer state keys. The primary index has (key, expiryTimestampMs) and the secondary index (expiryTimestampMs, key); the partition key is the key field (index 0, or 1 when isSecondaryIndex is true).

nodes.name: TransformWithStatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory
nodes.summary: Object that chooses the partition key extractor for a transformWithState column family from its StateVariableInfo (TTL setting and state variable type). Used by StatePartitionKeyExtractorFactory for offline state repartitioning; it requires the default store name and a non-default column family.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Entry point: checks the store and column family names, then delegates to createForTTL when the state variable has TTL enabled, otherwise to createForStateVarType.

nodes.name: createForTTL
nodes.summary: Handles TTL-enabled variables: the TTL index column family gets MapTTL (map state) or TTL (list/value state) extractors, the min expiry and count index column families get a no-op extractor, and the main column family goes to createForStateVarType. Unsupported types raise an error from OfflineStateRepartitionErrors.

nodes.name: createForStateVarType
nodes.summary: Chooses by state variable type: no-op extractor for list and value state, MapStatePartitionKeyExtractor for map state, TimerStatePartitionKeyExtractor (secondary index flag from the column family name) for timer state; other types raise an unsupported-type error.

nodes.name: StatefulProcessorHandleImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StatefulProcessorHandle implementations used by the transformWithState operator: the executor side StatefulProcessorHandleImpl that creates real state variables and timers over a StateStore, and DriverStatefulProcessorHandleImpl that only collects column family schemas. Also holds the implicit grouping key holder, a metrics helper, the handle lifecycle enum and placeholder state classes that fail during the init phase.

nodes.name: StatefulProcessorHandleImplBase.scala
nodes.summary: Abstract base class shared by the executor and driver stateful processor handles. Tracks the handle lifecycle state and validates that timer and state variable operations are legal for the current time mode and state.

nodes.name: ImplicitGroupingKeyTracker
nodes.summary: Singleton holder of the implicit grouping key in an InheritableThreadLocal. Offers getImplicitKeyOption, setImplicitKey and removeImplicitKey so state variables can find the current grouping key without it being passed explicitly.

nodes.name: TWSMetricsUtils
nodes.summary: Small utility object with resetMetric and incrementMetric, which look up a named SQLMetric in a metrics map and reset it or add a count to it if it is present. Used by the state variable classes to update metrics.

nodes.name: resetMetric
nodes.summary: Resets the named SQLMetric in the metrics map if it exists.

nodes.name: incrementMetric
nodes.summary: Adds countValue (default 1) to the named SQLMetric in the metrics map if it exists.

nodes.name: StatefulProcessorHandleState
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the valid lifecycle states of a stateful processor handle: CREATED, PRE_INIT, INITIALIZED, DATA_PROCESSED, TIMER_PROCESSED and CLOSED. The handle classes compare their current state against these values before allowing operations.

nodes.name: QueryInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Concrete QueryInfo holding the query id, run id and batch id, with getters and a toString. Created by the handles to expose information about the running query to the user stateful processor.

nodes.name: StatefulProcessorHandleImpl
nodes.summary: Executor side handle used while a transformWithState task runs. It creates ValueState, ListState and MapState variables (with or without TTL) over the StateStore, registers, deletes, lists and scans timers through TimerStateImpl, builds QueryInfo from the task context, deletes state variables and runs TTL cleanup over all registered TTL states. getValueState, getListState and getMapState each have an overload taking explicit Encoders and one using context bounds.

nodes.name: buildQueryInfo
nodes.summary: Private method that builds a QueryInfoImpl. For batch queries it uses a fixed zero query id and batch 0, for streaming it reads the query id and batch id from the task context local properties, and in tests without a task context it uses a random id.

nodes.name: registerTimer
nodes.summary: Verifies timer operations are allowed, registers a timer for the given expiry timestamp in TimerStateImpl and increments the numRegisteredTimers metric.

nodes.name: deleteTimer
nodes.summary: Verifies timer operations are allowed, deletes the timer with the given expiry timestamp from TimerStateImpl and increments the numDeletedTimers metric.

nodes.name: getExpiredTimers
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator of (grouping key, timestamp) pairs for all timers up to the given inclusive expiry threshold across all grouping keys, optionally skipping timers at or below a previous batch threshold. Delegates to TimerStateImpl.getExpiredTimers after verifying the operation.

nodes.name: listTimers
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over all timers registered for the current implicit grouping key, after verifying that timer operations are allowed.

nodes.name: doTtlCleanup
nodes.summary: Walks every registered TTL state and calls clearExpiredStateForAllKeys, adding the number of removed values to the numValuesRemovedDueToTTLExpiry metric.

nodes.name: deleteIfExists
nodes.summary: Deletes and purges a named state variable by removing its column family from the StateStore, incrementing the numDeletedStateVars metric when something was removed. Only allowed in the CREATED handle state.

nodes.name: getValueState
nodes.summary: Creates a value state variable. If a positive TTL duration is configured it validates the TTL config and builds a ValueStateImplWithTTL (tracked in ttlStates), otherwise it builds a plain ValueStateImpl, and increments the matching variable count metric. The overload taking an explicit Encoder (lines 225-230) delegates here.

nodes.name: getListState
nodes.summary: Creates a list state variable. With a positive TTL duration it validates the TTL config and builds a ListStateImplWithTTL (tracked in ttlStates), otherwise a plain ListStateImpl, and increments the matching variable count metric. The overload taking an explicit Encoder (lines 276-281) delegates here.

nodes.name: getMapState
nodes.summary: Creates a map state variable with separate user key and value encoders. With a positive TTL duration it validates the TTL config and builds a MapStateImplWithTTL (tracked in ttlStates), otherwise a plain MapStateImpl, and increments the matching variable count metric. The overload taking explicit Encoders (lines 311-317) delegates here.

nodes.name: validateTTLConfig
nodes.summary: Private check on a TTLConfig: throws a StateStoreErrors error if the time mode is not ProcessingTime, or if the TTL duration is null, negative or zero.

nodes.name: DriverStatefulProcessorHandleImpl
nodes.summary: Driver side handle used by the transformWithState operator to collect column family schemas and state variable infos after the user stateful processor is initialized, before any data is processed. Its getValueState, getListState and getMapState compute the schemas (plus TTL index schemas) and return InvalidHandle placeholder states, and it adds timer column families when the time mode is not None. Timer operations are present only to satisfy the interface and fail in the PRE_INIT phase.

nodes.name: getColumnFamilySchemas
nodes.summary: Returns the collected column family schemas as an immutable map. When shouldCheckNullable is set it throws if any value schema field is non-nullable, and when shouldSetNullable is set it rewrites each value schema to be nullable.

nodes.name: checkIfDuplicateVariableDefined
nodes.summary: Private check that throws a duplicate state variable error if a column family schema with the given name was already collected.

nodes.name: addTimerColFamily
nodes.summary: Private method that adds the primary and secondary timer column family schemas and the timer state variable info, built from TimerKeyEncoder and the timer state variable names, so registered timers can be read later. Called from the class body when the time mode is not None.

nodes.name: getValueState
nodes.summary: Computes and records the column family schema and variable info for a value state (with TTL schemas if enabled), rejects duplicate names, and returns an InvalidHandleValueState placeholder. Requires the PRE_INIT handle state. The overload with an explicit Encoder (lines 447-452) delegates here.

nodes.name: getListState
nodes.summary: Computes and records the column family schema and variable info for a list state (with TTL schemas if enabled), rejects duplicate names, and returns an InvalidHandleListState placeholder. Requires the PRE_INIT handle state. The overload with an explicit Encoder (lines 481-486) delegates here.

nodes.name: getMapState
nodes.summary: Computes and records the column family schema and variable info for a map state, and returns an InvalidHandleMapState placeholder. Requires the PRE_INIT handle state. Unlike the value and list versions, it does not check for duplicate names or call addTTLSchemas in this source. The overload with explicit Encoders (lines 515-521) delegates here.

nodes.name: getTTLIndexSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the schema of the TTL index column family named $ttl_<stateName>, which maps (expirationMs, elementKey) to an empty row and uses a range key scan encoder spec. Shared by one-to-one and one-to-many TTL states.

nodes.name: getMinExpiryIndexSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the schema of the min expiry index column family named $min_<stateName>, mapping an element key to its minimum expiration time. Used by one-to-many TTL states.

nodes.name: getCountIndexSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the schema of the count index column family named $count_<stateName>, mapping an element key to a long count of entries. Used by one-to-many TTL states to track the number of entries.

nodes.name: addValueStateTTLSchemas
nodes.summary: Private method that adds the TTL index column family schema for a state with one-to-one TTL (used for value state and map state by addTTLSchemas).

nodes.name: addListStateTTLSchemas
nodes.summary: Private method that adds the TTL index, min expiry index and count index column family schemas for a list state with TTL.

nodes.name: addTTLSchemas
nodes.summary: When the state variable info has TTL enabled, adds the TTL related column families according to the state variable type (ValueState and MapState use the value state TTL schemas, ListState uses the list state TTL schemas) and throws for unsupported types.

nodes.name: getQueryInfo
nodes.summary: Overrides getQueryInfo for the driver side by returning a QueryInfoImpl with random query and run ids and batch id 0.

nodes.name: InvalidHandleState
nodes.summary: Private[sql] trait mixed into the placeholder state classes. Declares the stateName and provides throwInitPhaseError, which raises a StateStoreErrors error saying the operation is not allowed in the PRE_INIT phase.

nodes.name: throwInitPhaseError
nodes.summary: Protected method returning Nothing that throws cannotPerformOperationWithInvalidHandleState for stateName.operation in the PRE_INIT phase.

nodes.name: InvalidHandleValueState
nodes.summary: Placeholder ValueState returned on the driver side. exists, get, update and clear all call throwInitPhaseError, so using it before the init phase finishes fails.

nodes.name: InvalidHandleListState
nodes.summary: Placeholder ListState returned on the driver side. exists, get, put, appendValue, appendList and clear all call throwInitPhaseError.

nodes.name: InvalidHandleMapState
nodes.summary: Placeholder MapState returned on the driver side. exists, getValue, containsKey, updateValue, iterator, keys, values, removeKey and clear all call throwInitPhaseError.

nodes.name: StatefulProcessorHandleImplBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base class of the stateful processor handles, constructed with a TimeMode and a key ExpressionEncoder. It holds the protected current handle state (starting at PRE_INIT) with a setter and getter, and the checks verifyTimerOperations and verifyStateVarOperations that throw StateStoreErrors when an operation is not valid.

nodes.name: setHandleState
nodes.summary: Sets the current handle lifecycle state.

nodes.name: getHandleState
nodes.summary: Returns the current handle lifecycle state.

nodes.name: verifyTimerOperations
nodes.summary: Throws if the time mode is NoTime, or if the current handle state is before INITIALIZED or at or after TIMER_PROCESSED. Called before every timer operation.

nodes.name: verifyStateVarOperations
nodes.summary: Throws cannotPerformOperationWithInvalidHandleState unless the current handle state equals the required state. Called before creating or deleting state variables.

nodes.name: ListStateImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ListStateImpl, the StateStore backed implementation of the list state variable used by the transformWithState operator.

nodes.name: ListStateMetricsImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ListStateMetricsImpl trait, which keeps a per grouping key entry count for list states in a separate internal column family.

nodes.name: MapStateImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapStateImpl, the StateStore backed implementation of the map state variable used by the transformWithState operator, storing entries under a composite grouping key plus user key.

nodes.name: ValueStateImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ValueStateImpl, the StateStore backed implementation of a single value state variable used by the transformWithState operator.

nodes.name: ListStateImpl
nodes.summary: List state variable stored in the StateStore with multiple values per key. Created in a column family named after the state, and offers exists, get (an iterator that decodes rows lazily), put (replace the whole list), appendValue, appendList and clear. It mixes in ListStateMetricsImpl to keep entry counts and updates the numUpdatedStateRows and numRemovedStateRows metrics.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Returns true if the store holds a value for the current grouping key.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the values of the list for the current grouping key, decoding each stored row on demand. Returns an empty iterator if nothing is stored.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Replaces the whole list for the current grouping key. Validates the new state, resets and increments numUpdatedStateRows per value, writes the values with putList and updates the entry count.

nodes.name: appendValue
nodes.summary: Appends one non-null value to the list with a store merge and increases the stored entry count by one.

nodes.name: appendList
nodes.summary: Appends an array of values to the existing list using mergeList after validating it, counting each value in numUpdatedStateRows and updating the stored entry count.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes the list for the current grouping key from the store, adds the previous entry count to numRemovedStateRows and removes the stored count.

nodes.name: validateNewState
nodes.summary: Private check that the new array is non-null and non-empty and that every element is non-null, using StateStoreErrors.

nodes.name: ListStateMetricsImpl
nodes.summary: Trait that maintains the number of entries of a list state per grouping key in a separate internal column family, so the count is available without scanning the whole list. Implementers supply stateStore, baseStateName and exprEncSchema. Provides getEntryCount, updateEntryCount and removeEntryCount.

nodes.name: getEntryCount
nodes.summary: Reads the stored count row for an encoded key from the counter column family and returns its long value, or 0 if absent.

nodes.name: updateEntryCount
nodes.summary: Writes the given count for an encoded key into the counter column family using an unsafe projection of a one field row.

nodes.name: removeEntryCount
nodes.summary: Removes the count row for an encoded key from the counter column family.

nodes.name: MapStateImpl
nodes.summary: Map state variable stored in the StateStore with a composite key of grouping key plus user key, created with a prefix key scan spec on the grouping key. Offers exists, getValue, containsKey, updateValue, iterator, keys, values, removeKey and clear, and updates the numUpdatedStateRows and numRemovedStateRows metrics.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Prefix scans the store for the current grouping key and returns whether any entry exists, closing the iterator.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Returns the value for a non-null user key by looking up the encoded composite key, or null if absent.

nodes.name: containsKey
nodes.summary: Returns true if getValue for the user key is not null.

nodes.name: updateValue
nodes.summary: Puts the encoded value under the composite key of grouping key and user key and increments numUpdatedStateRows. Both key and value must be non-null.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Prefix scans the store for the current grouping key and returns an iterator of decoded (user key, value) pairs.

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Returns the user keys of the map for the current grouping key, mapped from iterator.

nodes.name: values
nodes.summary: Returns the values of the map for the current grouping key, mapped from iterator.

nodes.name: removeKey
nodes.summary: Removes one user key's row from the store and increments numRemovedStateRows by one (rows are flattened for map state).

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes the whole map for the current grouping key by calling removeKey on every key.

nodes.name: ValueStateImpl
nodes.summary: Value state variable that stores one value per grouping key in a StateStore column family, created in initialize(). Offers exists, get, update and clear and updates the numUpdatedStateRows and numRemovedStateRows metrics.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Private method that creates the column family for the state name with a no-prefix key encoder spec. Called from the class body.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Returns true if get() is not null.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up the row for the current grouping key and returns the decoded value, or null if absent.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Encodes the new value and puts it under the current grouping key, incrementing numUpdatedStateRows.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes the row for the current grouping key and increments numRemovedStateRows.

nodes.name: AliasAwareOutputExpression.scala
nodes.summary: Defines two Catalyst plan traits: AliasAwareOutputExpression builds a map from expressions to the alias attributes in outputExpressions and projects expressions through it, and AliasAwareQueryOutputOrdering uses that to compute a plan node outputOrdering that still holds after aliasing.

nodes.name: AliasAwareOutputExpression
nodes.summary: Trait mixed into plan nodes that have outputExpressions. It lazily builds aliasMap (canonicalized child expression to up to aliasCandidateLimit Attributes, limit read from SQLConf.EXPRESSION_PROJECTION_CANDIDATE_LIMIT), exposes hasAlias, and projectExpression, which rewrites an expression into a LazyList of equivalent expressions over the output attributes (pruning anything that references attributes not in the output). strip is a hook that returns its argument unchanged by default.

nodes.name: AliasAwareQueryOutputOrdering
nodes.summary: Trait for a QueryPlan that extends AliasAwareOutputExpression and defines orderingExpressions. It overrides strip to drop Empty2Null wrappers and implements outputOrdering: with aliases it projects each SortOrder child through projectExpression (keeping up to aliasCandidateLimit equivalent expressions as sameOrderExpressions), without aliases it keeps only children whose references are in the output set; it stops at the first SortOrder that cannot be kept.

nodes.name: aliasMap
nodes.summary: Lazy transient map from canonicalized (stripped) child expression to a buffer of alias Attributes. Aliases are visited in reverse so the last alias keeps precedence, and plain output Attributes already present in the map are added too, each buffer capped at aliasCandidateLimit.

nodes.name: projectExpression
nodes.summary: Rewrites an expression with multiTransformDown: any sub-expression found in aliasMap is replaced by its alias attributes (plus itself if it has children), and an Attribute that is not in the output set yields no candidates, which prunes that branch.

nodes.name: outputOrdering
nodes.summary: Final method computing the plan outputOrdering from orderingExpressions. If hasAlias it projects each SortOrder child through projectExpression and de-duplicates by canonical form; otherwise it filters to children whose references are a subset of the output attributes. takeWhile on defined results keeps only the leading orderings that survive.

nodes.name: DescribeCommandSchema.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the fixed output schemas used by describe commands: a one-column JSON metadata schema, a col_name/data_type/comment schema, and an info_name/info_value schema.

nodes.name: DescribeCommandSchema
nodes.summary: Private[sql] object that builds Seq[AttributeReference] output schemas for describe commands. describeJsonTableAttributes returns the single non-null string column json_metadata; describeTableAttributes returns col_name, data_type (non-null) and comment (nullable); describeColumnAttributes returns info_name and info_value. Every attribute carries a "comment" metadata entry.

nodes.name: describeJsonTableAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns a one-element schema with the non-null string attribute json_metadata, commented as the JSON metadata of the table.

nodes.name: describeTableAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the three-attribute schema col_name, data_type and comment (string typed; comment is nullable) used to describe table columns.

nodes.name: describeColumnAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the two-attribute schema info_name and info_value (both non-null strings) used to describe column information.

nodes.name: joinTypes.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the join type model of Catalyst plans: the sealed JoinType hierarchy (Inner, Cross, LeftOuter, RightOuter, FullOuter, LeftSemi, LeftAnti, LeftSingle, ExistenceJoin, NaturalJoin, UsingJoin) with its string parser, extractors LeftExistence and LeftSemiOrAnti, and the parsers for as-of join direction, lateral join type, nearest-by direction, nearest-by join type and nearest-by mode.

nodes.name: JoinType
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract base class (with sql: String) for all join types, plus its companion object. JoinType.apply parses a user string (lower-cased, underscores removed) into Inner, FullOuter, LeftOuter, RightOuter, LeftSemi, LeftAnti or Cross, and throws AnalysisException UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE listing the names in JoinType.supported otherwise.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a join type name into a JoinType case object; accepted names are listed in JoinType.supported (for example inner, outer, full, fullouter, left, left_semi, semi, anti, cross). Unknown names raise AnalysisException with error class UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE.

nodes.name: InnerLike
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract JoinType for inner-style joins, declaring explicitCartesian. The flag tells whether the join was built with CROSS so that a cartesian product was explicitly requested.

nodes.name: Inner
nodes.summary: Case object for the inner join; explicitCartesian is false and sql is "INNER".

nodes.name: Cross
nodes.summary: Case object for the cross join; explicitCartesian is true and sql is "CROSS".

nodes.name: LeftOuter
nodes.summary: Case object for the left outer join; sql is "LEFT OUTER".

nodes.name: RightOuter
nodes.summary: Case object for the right outer join; sql is "RIGHT OUTER".

nodes.name: FullOuter
nodes.summary: Case object for the full outer join; sql is "FULL OUTER".

nodes.name: LeftSemi
nodes.summary: Case object for the left semi join; sql is "LEFT SEMI".

nodes.name: LeftAnti
nodes.summary: Case object for the left anti join; sql is "LEFT ANTI".

nodes.name: LeftSingle
nodes.summary: Case object for the left single join; sql is "LEFT SINGLE".

nodes.name: ExistenceJoin
nodes.summary: Case class JoinType carrying the boolean exists Attribute. Per the source comment it is used only at the end of the optimizer and in physical plans, and its sql method throws SparkUnsupportedOperationException because no SQL is generated for it.

nodes.name: NaturalJoin
nodes.summary: Case class JoinType wrapping another join type tpe for NATURAL joins. A require check allows only Inner, LeftOuter, RightOuter and FullOuter; sql is "NATURAL " followed by the wrapped type sql.

nodes.name: UsingJoin
nodes.summary: Case class JoinType for USING joins, holding tpe and usingColumns. A require check allows Inner, LeftOuter, LeftSemi, RightOuter, FullOuter, LeftAnti and Cross; sql is "USING " plus the wrapped type, and toString prints the column list in brackets.

nodes.name: LeftExistence
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply matches LeftSemi, LeftAnti or any ExistenceJoin and returns the join type; used in pattern matches.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Returns Some(joinType) for LeftSemi, LeftAnti and ExistenceJoin, None for everything else.

nodes.name: LeftSemiOrAnti
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply matches only LeftSemi or LeftAnti.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Returns Some(joinType) for LeftSemi and LeftAnti, None otherwise.

nodes.name: AsOfJoinDirection
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for as-of join directions with its companion object. AsOfJoinDirection.apply maps "forward", "backward" or "nearest" (case-insensitive) to Forward, Backward or Nearest and otherwise throws AnalysisException AS_OF_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_DIRECTION.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a direction name into Forward, Backward or Nearest; raises AnalysisException AS_OF_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_DIRECTION for other values.

nodes.name: Forward
nodes.summary: Case object for the forward as-of join direction.

nodes.name: Backward
nodes.summary: Case object for the backward as-of join direction.

nodes.name: Nearest
nodes.summary: Case object for the nearest as-of join direction.

nodes.name: LateralJoinType
nodes.summary: Object that parses the join type of a lateral join. apply accepts inner, leftouter/left/left_outer and cross, returning Inner, LeftOuter or Cross, and throws AnalysisException UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE otherwise; supported lists the accepted names.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a lateral join type name into Inner, LeftOuter or Cross, raising AnalysisException UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE for anything else.

nodes.name: NearestByDirection
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class for nearest-by join directions with its companion object. supported reuses NearestByJoinValidation.SupportedDirections; apply maps "distance" to NearestByDistance and "similarity" to NearestBySimilarity, else throws AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_DIRECTION.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses "distance" or "similarity" (case-insensitive) into the matching nearest-by direction; other values raise AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_DIRECTION.

nodes.name: NearestByDistance
nodes.summary: Case object for the distance nearest-by direction.

nodes.name: NearestBySimilarity
nodes.summary: Case object for the similarity nearest-by direction.

nodes.name: NearestByJoinType
nodes.summary: Object that parses the join type of a nearest-by join. It takes supported and supportedDisplay from NearestByJoinValidation; apply returns Inner for inner and LeftOuter for leftouter/left, else throws AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Parses a name into Inner or LeftOuter for nearest-by joins; other names raise AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE.

nodes.name: NearestByJoinMode
nodes.summary: Object that parses the nearest-by join mode. supported comes from NearestByJoinValidation.SupportedModes; apply returns true for "approx" and false for "exact", else throws AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_MODE.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns true for "approx" and false for "exact" (case-insensitive); other values raise AnalysisException NEAREST_BY_JOIN.UNSUPPORTED_MODE.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateExecBase.scala
nodes.summary: Holds TransformWithStateExecBase, the shared abstract physical operator for transformWithState: state store writer behavior, co-location of data and initial state, custom metrics, watermark propagation, metadata validation, time mode and state store provider validation, and error handling around user processor calls.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateExecBase
nodes.summary: Abstract BinaryExecNode (child on the left, initialState on the right) that also mixes in StateStoreWriter, WatermarkSupport and TransformWithStateMetadataUtils. It holds logic common to concrete transformWithState operators such as TransformWithStateExec and the TransformWithStateInPySparkExec named in its comment: required child distribution and ordering on grouping attributes, shouldRunAnotherBatch, output watermark rule, custom TWS metrics, operator state metadata, an iterator wrapper that sets the implicit grouping key, validation helpers and user-function error wrapping. Supports only the RocksDBStateStoreProvider and schema evolution, with operator state metadata version 2.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns two distributions from StatefulOperatorPartitioning.getCompatibleDistribution, one for groupingAttributes and one for initialStateGroupingAttrs, so data and initial state are co-located on the same task.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires both children to be sorted ascending by their grouping attributes so keys of the data and the initial state line up.

nodes.name: shouldRunAnotherBatch
nodes.summary: Decides whether another batch is needed: always true in ProcessingTime; for Append or Update output mode true only when an eviction watermark is defined and the new input watermark exceeds it; false otherwise.

nodes.name: produceOutputWatermark
nodes.summary: Controls watermark propagation: returns None for ProcessingTime because output rows cannot be read in event time, and otherwise returns the input watermark unchanged.

nodes.name: customStatefulOperatorMetrics
nodes.summary: Declares the sum metrics of the operator: initialStateProcessingTimeMs, numValueStateVars, numListStateVars, numMapStateVars, numDeletedStateVars, timerProcessingTimeMs, numRegisteredTimers, numDeletedTimers, numExpiredTimers, numValueStateWithTTLVars, numListStateWithTTLVars, numMapStateWithTTLVars and numValuesRemovedDueToTTLExpiry.

nodes.name: operatorStateMetadata
nodes.summary: Builds the OperatorStateMetadata for this operator by calling getOperatorStateMetadata with the state schema paths, state info, short name, time mode and output mode.

nodes.name: validateNewMetadata
nodes.summary: Delegates to validateNewMetadataForTWS to compare old and new operator state metadata.

nodes.name: iteratorWithImplicitKeySet
nodes.summary: Wraps an output iterator in an anonymous NextIterator that sets the implicit grouping key on the first call and removes it (after running an optional onClose callback) when the iterator closes. Valid because each key is processed fully before the next.

nodes.name: validateTimeMode
nodes.summary: Validates the time mode: for ProcessingTime it passes batchTimestampMs to TransformWithStateVariableUtils.validateTimeMode, for EventTime it passes eventTimeWatermarkForEviction, otherwise does nothing.

nodes.name: validateStateStoreProvider
nodes.summary: Reads the SQLConf.STATE_STORE_PROVIDER_CLASS setting and, for streaming queries, throws StateStoreErrors.storeBackendNotSupportedForTWS when the provider is not in the supported set (only RocksDBStateStoreProvider).

nodes.name: withStatefulProcessorErrorHandling
nodes.summary: Runs a block and rethrows a SparkThrowable that has a condition as is, while wrapping any other Exception in TransformWithStateUserFunctionException tagged with the user function name.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Holds TransformWithStateExec, the concrete physical operator that runs a user StatefulProcessor over grouped rows (optionally with initial state and timers) against a state store, and its companion factory for batch queries.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator (extends TransformWithStateExecBase with ObjectProducerExec) that executes TransformWithState. It deserializes key and values into objects, calls the user StatefulProcessor handleInputRows per key, handles expired timers, optional initial state on batch 0 and TTL cleanup, and commits or aborts the state store (abort in batch mode). It runs in streaming mode with a state store per partition, or in batch mode with a temporary RocksDB-backed store created on the executors. The companion object generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries builds a non-streaming instance with a fresh StatefulOperatorStateInfo.

nodes.name: getDriverProcessorHandle
nodes.summary: Creates a DriverStatefulProcessorHandleImpl in PRE_INIT state, attaches it to the processor, and runs the user init under error handling so the driver can collect state variable schemas.

nodes.name: closeProcessorHandle
nodes.summary: Closes the driver-side stateful processor and clears its handle; that instance is not used again.

nodes.name: getColFamilySchemas
nodes.summary: Returns the column family schemas collected from the driver processor handle after init, plus a default column family entry (DUMMY_VALUE_ROW_SCHEMA with a no-prefix key encoder spec) that the state encoder expects; nullability is relaxed to nullable.

nodes.name: getStateVariableInfos
nodes.summary: Returns the map of TransformWithStateVariableInfo collected from the driver processor handle, then closes that handle.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Copies the operator with a new child, and a new initialState only when hasInitialState is true.

nodes.name: handleInputRows
nodes.summary: Per-key processing: converts the key row and value rows to objects, sets the implicit grouping key, calls statefulProcessor.handleInputRows with TimerValuesImpl under error handling, maps outputs to rows, then returns the iterator wrapped so the key is set while it is consumed.

nodes.name: processInitialStateRows
nodes.summary: Feeds initial-state rows for one key to handleInitialState of a StatefulProcessorWithInitialState, allowing several initial rows per key, with the implicit key set and error handling.

nodes.name: processNewData
nodes.summary: Groups the incoming rows by groupingAttributes with GroupedIterator and flat-maps each group through handleInputRows.

nodes.name: handleTimerRows
nodes.summary: Calls handleExpiredTimer on the processor for one key and expiry time (with TimerValuesImpl and ExpiredTimerInfoImpl), maps the outputs to rows, and deletes the timer when the returned iterator is closed.

nodes.name: processTimers
nodes.summary: Finds expired timers through processorHandle.getExpiredTimers using the batch timestamp (ProcessingTime) or the eviction watermark (EventTime), counts them in numExpiredTimers and handles each; yields nothing for other time modes. Always scans without a lower bound (SPARK-56566 comment).

nodes.name: processDataWithPartition
nodes.summary: Core per-partition pipeline: optionally drops late events by watermark in EventTime mode, processes new data, then lazily processes timers after the input is exhausted, and on completion runs TTL cleanup, commits (streaming) or aborts (batch) the store, sets metrics, closes the processor and marks the handle CLOSED. Records allUpdatesTimeMs, timerProcessingTimeMs, allRemovalsTimeMs and commitTimeMs.

nodes.name: closeStatefulProcessor
nodes.summary: Calls statefulProcessor.close under error handling.

nodes.name: validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema
nodes.summary: Validates and writes the state schema for this operator by calling validateAndWriteStateSchema with the state info, schema directory, operator metadata version and encoding format.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Entry point of execution. Validates time mode and state store provider, then builds the RDD in one of four ways: with initial state (stateStoreAwareZipPartitions, using a StateStore.get store when streaming or a temporary store when batch) or without it (mapPartitionsWithStateStore when streaming, mapPartitionsWithIndex with a temporary store when batch).

nodes.name: initNewStateStoreAndProcessData
nodes.summary: Used for batch mode: creates a temporary directory and StateStoreProviderId, builds a RocksDBStateStoreProvider with multiple values per key and column families, gets a store, runs the supplied function, and closes the provider and the processor when the output iterator completes.

nodes.name: processData
nodes.summary: Creates a StatefulProcessorHandleImpl on the store, attaches it to the processor, runs init, marks the handle INITIALIZED and delegates to processDataWithPartition.

nodes.name: processDataWithInitialState
nodes.summary: Like processData but also processes initial state: only in batch 0 it groups the initial state rows by key and feeds them to processInitialStateRows, timing it in initialStateProcessingTimeMs, then processes the child data.

nodes.name: generateSparkPlanForBatchQueries
nodes.summary: Companion factory for batch queries: builds a StatefulOperatorStateInfo with an empty checkpoint location, a random query run id and numShufflePartitions partitions, and returns a non-streaming TransformWithStateExec using the current time as batch timestamp.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateVariableUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the metadata model for TransformWithState state variables: a variable info record (name, type, TTL flag), an operator properties record (time mode, output mode, variables) with JSON read and write, and a trait that builds and validates the operator state metadata. It is used to store these properties in the operatorProperties field of the operator state metadata and to check them again after a query restart.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes the json4s DSL (the ~ operator with JString and JBool) for writing with JsonMethods.parse(...).extract[Map[String, Any]] for reading.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateVariableUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton with helpers for state variable metadata: factory methods that build a TransformWithStateVariableInfo for value, list, map and timer state (getValueState, getListState, getMapState, getTimerState), validateTimeMode, and naming helpers for the row counter column family (getRowCounterCFName, isRowCounterCFName, getStateNameFromRowCounterCFName) that use the prefix $rowCounter_. Used when state variables are registered and when column family names are mapped back to state names.

nodes.name: StateVariableType
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the kinds of state variable that TransformWithState supports: ValueState, ListState, MapState and TimerState. It is stored in the variable info record so that a type change after restart can be detected.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateVariableInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding the stateName, stateVariableType and ttlEnabled flag of one state variable, with jsonValue and json to serialize it. Its companion object adds fromJson and fromMap to rebuild an instance from stored JSON. Used to record state variables in the operator properties and to compare them after restart.
nodes.languageNotes: The case class and its companion object share this node id; the companion holds fromJson and fromMap.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateOperatorProperties
nodes.summary: Case class with the timeMode and outputMode strings and the list of state variable infos of a TransformWithState operator. json writes it as compact JSON; the companion object reads it back with fromJson and checks compatibility between an old and a new instance with validateOperatorProperties, which rejects a changed timeMode or outputMode and a changed state variable type for the same stateName.
nodes.languageNotes: The case class and its companion object share this node id; the companion also mixes in Logging.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateMetadataUtils
nodes.summary: Trait that builds the OperatorStateMetadataV2 for the operator (getOperatorStateMetadata) and validates new metadata against old metadata (validateNewMetadataForTWS) by comparing the stored operator properties JSON. It enables schema evolution for the operator by overriding schemaEvolutionEnabledForOperator to true, and requires implementers to supply getStateVariableInfos().

nodes.name: getValueState
nodes.summary: Builds a TransformWithStateVariableInfo of type ValueState for the given state name and TTL flag.

nodes.name: getListState
nodes.summary: Builds a TransformWithStateVariableInfo of type ListState for the given state name and TTL flag.

nodes.name: getMapState
nodes.summary: Builds a TransformWithStateVariableInfo of type MapState for the given state name and TTL flag.

nodes.name: getTimerState
nodes.summary: Builds a TransformWithStateVariableInfo of type TimerState for the given state name with TTL disabled.

nodes.name: validateTimeMode
nodes.summary: Throws StateStoreErrors.missingTimeValues when the time mode is not TimeMode.None() but no timestamp was provided.

nodes.name: getRowCounterCFName
nodes.summary: Returns the row counter column family name for a state name by prepending the $rowCounter_ prefix.

nodes.name: isRowCounterCFName
nodes.summary: Returns true when a column family name starts with the $rowCounter_ prefix.

nodes.name: getStateNameFromRowCounterCFName
nodes.summary: Strips the $rowCounter_ prefix from a row counter column family name to get the state name; requires that the name has the prefix.

nodes.name: jsonValue
nodes.summary: Builds the json4s value with the fields stateName, stateVariableType and ttlEnabled.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Renders jsonValue as a compact JSON string.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON string into a map and delegates to fromMap to build a TransformWithStateVariableInfo.

nodes.name: fromMap
nodes.summary: Reads stateName, stateVariableType (via StateVariableType.withName) and ttlEnabled from a parsed map and builds the info record.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes the time mode, output mode and the state variables (via their jsonValue) into one compact JSON string.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Parses stored operator properties JSON and rebuilds the properties, mapping each state variable entry with TransformWithStateVariableInfo.fromMap.

nodes.name: validateOperatorProperties
nodes.summary: Compares old and new operator properties after a restart and throws if timeMode or outputMode changed, or if a state variable present in both has a different stateVariableType.

nodes.name: getOperatorStateMetadata
nodes.summary: Builds an OperatorStateMetadataV2 from the operator info, one StateStoreMetadataV2 entry (default store name, the partition count and the first state schema path list) and the operator properties JSON made from the time mode, output mode and state variable infos.

nodes.name: validateNewMetadataForTWS
nodes.summary: When both old and new metadata are OperatorStateMetadataV2, parses their operator properties JSON and runs validateOperatorProperties; other combinations are accepted.

nodes.name: TimerStateImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Implements timer storage for the transformWithState operator on top of a StateStore. TimerStateUtils holds the column family naming rules for processing time and event time timers, and TimerStateImpl registers, deletes, lists and expires timers using two column families (a primary index keyed by grouping key and expiry, and a secondary index ordered by timestamp).

nodes.name: TimerStateUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton with the constants and naming helpers for timer column families: $procTimers and $eventTimers as base names, _keyToTimestamp and _timestampToKey as suffixes, getTimerStateVarNames(timeMode) for the pair of names, and the checks isTimerCFName, isTimerSecondaryIndexCF and getPrimaryIndexFromSecondaryIndexCF. Used by timer state and by code that must recognize timer column families.

nodes.name: TimerStateImpl
nodes.summary: Stores the timers of a transformWithState operator in a StateStore for a given TimeMode and key encoder. On construction it creates an internal key-to-timestamp column family (prefix scan on the grouping key) and a timestamp-to-key secondary column family (range scan on the timestamp). It offers registerTimer, deleteTimer and listTimers for the current implicit grouping key, and getExpiredTimers, a range scan over all keys that returns timers at or below a threshold and optionally above the previous batch's threshold.
nodes.languageNotes: getExpiredTimers returns an anonymous NextIterator that stops once a timestamp exceeds the limit; timestamps are encoded as ts+1 so boundary keys act as exclusive bounds.

nodes.name: getTimerStateVarNames
nodes.summary: Returns the (primary index, secondary index) column family names for a time mode string, by appending _keyToTimestamp and _timestampToKey to $eventTimers or $procTimers; asserts the mode is event time or processing time.

nodes.name: isTimerCFName
nodes.summary: True when a column family name starts with the processing time or event time timer base name.

nodes.name: isTimerSecondaryIndexCF
nodes.summary: True when a timer column family name ends with _timestampToKey; asserts that the name belongs to a timer.

nodes.name: getPrimaryIndexFromSecondaryIndexCF
nodes.summary: Maps a secondary index column family name to its primary index name by replacing _timestampToKey with _keyToTimestamp.

nodes.name: encodeTimestampAsKey
nodes.summary: Builds a secondary index key row with timestamp+1 and a default grouping key, for use as an exclusive range scan bound; returns None when the timestamp is Long.MaxValue to avoid overflow.

nodes.name: getGroupingKey
nodes.summary: Returns the current implicit grouping key or throws StateStoreErrors.implicitKeyNotFound when none is set.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Checks whether a timer for the grouping key and expiry timestamp is already registered.

nodes.name: getImpl
nodes.summary: Reads the primary index entry for the encoded (grouping key, expiry timestamp) key.

nodes.name: registerTimer
nodes.summary: Registers a timer for the current grouping key and expiry timestamp by writing an empty row to both the primary and the secondary index; logs a warning and skips the write if the timer already exists.

nodes.name: deleteTimer
nodes.summary: Deletes the timer for the current grouping key and expiry timestamp from both indexes; logs a warning if it does not exist.

nodes.name: listTimers
nodes.summary: Returns the expiry timestamps of all timers of the current grouping key by a prefix scan of the primary index.

nodes.name: getTimerRowFromSecIndex
nodes.summary: Decodes a secondary index key row into the grouping key object and the expiry timestamp.

nodes.name: getExpiredTimers
nodes.summary: Range scans the secondary index from an optional exclusive lower bound (previous batch threshold) to the given threshold and returns an iterator of (grouping key, timestamp) for all timers at or below the threshold, across all grouping keys.

nodes.name: ListStateImplWithTTL.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ListStateImplWithTTL, the list state variable of transformWithState with TTL expiration support. It stores multiple values per grouping key in a state store column family, and reuses the one-to-many TTL state base class to expire values and maintain its indexes.

nodes.name: ListStateImplWithTTL
nodes.summary: List state with TTL used inside the transformWithState operator. It extends OneToManyTTLState and implements ListState: get skips expired entries, put overwrites the list, appendValue and appendList add entries, and clear removes all state of the grouping key. clearExpiredValues rewrites the list without expired values and reports the count removed and the new minimum expiration. Package-private helpers (getWithoutEnforcingTTL, getTTLValues, getMinValues, getValueInTTLState) let tests inspect the stored TTL data.
nodes.languageNotes: The column family is created with useMultipleValuesPerKey = true and values carry a TTL expiration column (getValueSchemaWithTTL).

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates the state column family for the state name with the grouping key schema, the value schema with a TTL column, and multiple values per key enabled.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the list values of the current grouping key, skipping expired values at the head and decoding each remaining row; returns an empty iterator if nothing exists.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Replaces the whole list with the given array after validating it; encodes each value with the new expiration and updates the primary and secondary indexes with overwrite enabled.

nodes.name: appendValue
nodes.summary: Appends one value with the new expiration to the list of the current grouping key and updates the indexes without overwriting.

nodes.name: appendList
nodes.summary: Appends an array of values to the existing list; the encoded rows are reused and must only be consumed lazily by the index update.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes all state of the current grouping key by calling clearAllStateForElementKey.

nodes.name: validateNewState
nodes.summary: Checks that the new list and each of its elements are non-null and that the list is non-empty.

nodes.name: clearExpiredValues
nodes.summary: Reads all values of an element key, removes the key, then puts back only non-expired values (first with put, the rest with merge) and tracks the minimum expiration of survivors. Returns a ValueExpirationResult with the number expired and the new minimum expiration.

nodes.name: getWithoutEnforcingTTL
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the list values of the grouping key including expired ones.

nodes.name: getTTLValues
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns each stored value paired with its TTL expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: getMinValues
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the minimum expiration values of the min-expiry index for the current grouping key.

nodes.name: getValueInTTLState
nodes.summary: Test helper that reads the TTL index rows for the current grouping key, asserts there is at most one, and returns its expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: MapStateImplWithTTL.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapStateImplWithTTL, the map state variable of transformWithState with TTL expiration support. Each map entry is stored under a composite key (grouping key plus user key), with the one-to-one TTL state base class maintaining the TTL index.

nodes.name: MapStateImplWithTTL
nodes.summary: Map state with TTL used inside the transformWithState operator. It extends OneToOneTTLState and implements MapState: getValue returns null for missing or expired entries, updateValue writes a value with a new expiration through the base-class index update, iterator prefix-scans all entries of the grouping key and skips expired ones, keys and values project the iterator, removeKey deletes one entry, and clear removes all entries of the grouping key. Package-private helpers expose stored TTL data for tests.
nodes.languageNotes: Rows are flattened per map key, so removal metrics count one row per removed key. The column family uses a prefix scan on the first column of the composite key.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates the column family for the state name with the composite key schema, the value schema with a TTL column and a prefix scan encoder spec on the grouping key.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Returns true when the iterator over the map entries of the grouping key is non-empty.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Looks up the value of a user key; returns null when the key is absent or its row is expired.

nodes.name: containsKey
nodes.summary: Returns true when getValue for the user key is non-null.

nodes.name: updateValue
nodes.summary: Validates the key and value, computes the expiration from the TTL config and batch timestamp, encodes the value, and updates the primary and secondary indexes.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Prefix scans the entries of the current grouping key and returns an iterator of (user key, value) pairs, skipping expired entries.

nodes.name: keys
nodes.summary: Returns the user keys of the current grouping key's map.

nodes.name: values
nodes.summary: Returns the values of the current grouping key's map.

nodes.name: removeKey
nodes.summary: Removes one user key from the map state and increments the numRemovedStateRows metric.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Prefix scans all entries of the grouping key and calls clearAllStateForElementKey for each entry key.

nodes.name: getWithoutEnforcingTTL
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the value of a user key even if it has expired.

nodes.name: getTTLValue
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the stored value and its TTL expiration for a user key.

nodes.name: getKeyValuesInTTLState
nodes.summary: Test helper that filters the TTL index rows to the current grouping key and returns each user key with its expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: TTLState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TTL machinery for transformWithState state variables: the TTLState trait with a TTL index (expirationMs, elementKey) kept in a separate column family, OneToOneTTLState for variables with one value per element key, OneToManyTTLState for list-like variables that keep a min-expiry index and an entry count index per key, and the StateTTL helper object for expiration arithmetic. Value, list and map state with TTL build on these classes to evict expired state.

nodes.name: TTLState
nodes.summary: Base trait that every TTL-aware state variable implements. It holds the shared TTL index, a column family named $ttl_<stateName> with keys (expirationMs, elementKey) and an empty value, created with a range scan encoder so that expired keys can be found efficiently. It provides insertIntoTTLIndex, deleteFromTTLIndex (two overloads), toTTLRow, getTTLRows and ttlEvictionIterator (a bounded range scan from the previous batch timestamp to the current one), and declares the abstract clearExpiredStateForAllKeys and clearAllStateForElementKey.
nodes.languageNotes: Two deleteFromTTLIndex overloads share one function node: one takes (expirationMs, elementKey) and builds the key, the other takes the already encoded ttlKey row (lines 159-161).

nodes.name: TTLRow
nodes.summary: Package-private (private[sql]) case class nested in TTLState that holds a row of the TTL index: the elementKey and its expirationMs. It is exposed for testing and returned by getTTLRows and toTTLRow.

nodes.name: OneToOneTTLState
nodes.summary: Abstract TTL state for variables where each element key maps to exactly one value, with a primary index [elementKey -> (value, expiration)] and the TTL index from TTLState. updatePrimaryAndSecondaryIndices writes a value and moves the TTL index entry only when the expiration changed; clearExpiredStateForAllKeys walks ttlEvictionIterator and removes expired entries from both indexes; clearAllStateForElementKey removes one key. Used by value state and map state with TTL.

nodes.name: OneToManyTTLState
nodes.summary: Abstract TTL state for variables where one key holds several values that each expire at their own time (documented as currently used by list state with TTL). Besides the TTL index it keeps a min-expiry index per element key ($min_<stateName>) and an entry count index ($count_<stateName>), because merged values cannot be deleted one by one. Subclasses implement clearExpiredValues, which returns a ValueExpirationResult, and this class re-registers the new minimum expiration and fixes the count.

nodes.name: ValueExpirationResult
nodes.summary: Case class returned by clearExpiredValues in a one-to-many TTL state: numValuesExpired (for metrics) and newMinExpirationMs, the minimum expiration of the values that remain.

nodes.name: StateTTL
nodes.summary: Helper object for state TTL: calculateExpirationTimeForDuration adds a TTL duration in milliseconds to a batch timestamp, and isExpired returns true when the batch timestamp is at or beyond the expiration time.

nodes.name: insertIntoTTLIndex
nodes.summary: Encodes (expirationMs, elementKey) into a TTL index key and puts it with an empty value row.

nodes.name: deleteFromTTLIndex
nodes.summary: Removes the TTL index entry for the given expiration time and element key by encoding the key first; the overload taking an already encoded ttlKey row just removes it (lines 159-161).

nodes.name: toTTLRow
nodes.summary: Converts a TTL index key row into a TTLRow by reading the expiration from column 0 and the element key struct from column 1.

nodes.name: getTTLRows
nodes.summary: Iterates the whole TTL index and maps each key to a TTLRow; used by tests.

nodes.name: ttlEvictionIterator
nodes.summary: Returns the TTL index keys that have expired, using a bounded range scan from prevBatchTimestampMs+1 to batchTimestampMs+1 and a safety filter with StateTTL.isExpired. It does not delete the keys; callers must.

nodes.name: clearExpiredStateForAllKeys
nodes.summary: Abstract method: evicts the state of this variable that expired due to TTL, for all grouping keys and all indexes, and returns the number of values cleaned up.

nodes.name: clearAllStateForElementKey
nodes.summary: Abstract method: clears all state of one element key from the primary index and any secondary indexes, called when the user clears the variable.

nodes.name: updatePrimaryAndSecondaryIndices
nodes.summary: Writes the element value to the primary index and keeps the TTL index in sync: inserts into both if the key is new, and for an existing key with a different value rewrites it and moves the TTL index entry only if the expiration changed. Increments numUpdatedStateRows.

nodes.name: clearExpiredStateForAllKeys
nodes.summary: Iterates ttlEvictionIterator, deleting each expired key from the TTL index and the primary index, then adds the count to numRemovedStateRows and returns it.

nodes.name: clearAllStateForElementKey
nodes.summary: Removes one element key from the primary index and deletes its TTL index entry, using the stored expiration; increments numRemovedStateRows.

nodes.name: getEntryCount
nodes.summary: Reads the number of list entries of an element key from the count index, or 0 if absent.

nodes.name: updateEntryCount
nodes.summary: Writes the entry count of an element key into the count index using a reused row and projector.

nodes.name: removeEntryCount
nodes.summary: Removes the count index entry of an element key.

nodes.name: writePrimaryIndexEntries
nodes.summary: Writes the values of an element key to the primary index, with put for the first value on overwrite and merge for the rest, counts them, updates numUpdatedStateRows and the count index.

nodes.name: updatePrimaryAndSecondaryIndices
nodes.summary: Writes the values with writePrimaryIndexEntries, then updates the min-expiry index and the TTL index: it inserts new entries if none exist, or replaces them when overwriting or when the new expiration is lower than the stored minimum.

nodes.name: clearExpiredValues
nodes.summary: Abstract protected method: removes the expired values of one element key and returns a ValueExpirationResult.

nodes.name: clearExpiredStateForAllKeys
nodes.summary: For each expired TTL index key, deletes it from the TTL and min-expiry indexes, calls clearExpiredValues, re-inserts the new minimum expiration if any values remain, adjusts or removes the count index, and returns the total number of values expired.

nodes.name: clearAllStateForElementKey
nodes.summary: If the key has a min-expiry entry, removes its values, its count index entry, its min-expiry entry and its TTL index entry, and increments numRemovedStateRows by the entry count.

nodes.name: minIndexIterator
nodes.summary: Test-exposed iterator over the min-expiry index returning (element key row, minimum expiration).

nodes.name: calculateExpirationTimeForDuration
nodes.summary: Returns the batch timestamp plus the TTL duration in milliseconds.

nodes.name: isExpired
nodes.summary: Returns true when the batch timestamp is greater than or equal to the expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: ValueStateImplWithTTL.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ValueStateImplWithTTL, the single-value state variable of transformWithState with TTL expiration support. It stores one value per grouping key and relies on the one-to-one TTL state base class to maintain the TTL index.

nodes.name: ValueStateImplWithTTL
nodes.summary: Value state with TTL used inside the transformWithState operator. It extends OneToOneTTLState and implements ValueState: get decodes the stored row and returns null when it is missing or expired, update writes a value with a new expiration through the base-class index update, exists checks get() != null, and clear removes the state of the grouping key. Package-private helpers (getWithoutEnforcingTTL, getTTLValue, getValueInTTLState) let tests inspect stored TTL data.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Creates the state column family with the grouping key schema, the value schema with a TTL column, and a no-prefix key encoder spec.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Returns true when get() returns a non-null value.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Reads the row for the current grouping key, decodes the value, and returns it unless the row is expired, in which case it returns null (also null if no row exists).

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Computes the expiration from the TTL config and batch timestamp, encodes the value with it, and updates the primary and secondary indexes.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Removes the state of the current grouping key by calling clearAllStateForElementKey.

nodes.name: getWithoutEnforcingTTL
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the stored value of the grouping key even if it has expired.

nodes.name: getTTLValue
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the stored value together with its TTL expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: getValueInTTLState
nodes.summary: Test helper that reads the TTL index rows for the current grouping key, asserts at most one exists, and returns its expiration timestamp.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryPage.scala
nodes.summary: Renders the Structured Streaming tab's main page in the web UI: a collapsible table of active streaming queries and one of completed queries. The file holds the page, a paged table with sortable columns (Name, Status, ID, Run ID, Start Time, Duration, Avg Input /sec, Avg Process /sec, Latest Batch, and Error for completed queries), a row type for sorting, and the data source that sorts and slices rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Scala XML literals to build HTML, with scalastyle checks turned off around the long literals.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryPage
nodes.summary: WebUIPage (empty path) of the streaming query tab. render builds the content and wraps it with the Spark UI header under the title Streaming Query. generateStreamingQueryTable splits the queries from the tab's store into active and inactive ones and adds a collapsible section with a table for each non-empty group; queryTable reads the page number for the table tag and builds a StreamingQueryPagedTable, showing an error alert if rendering fails.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryPagedTable
nodes.summary: PagedTable of StructuredStreamingRow that draws the streaming query list. It reads sort column, order and page size from the request (default sort column Start Time), builds page links and the go-button path, defines the header columns, and renders each row with the query name, status, id, a run id link to the statistics page, start time, duration, average input and processing rates, latest batch id, and an error cell for completed queries.

nodes.name: StructuredStreamingRow
nodes.summary: Package-private case class pairing a StreamingQueryUIData with precomputed duration, avgInput and avgProcess values so the table can sort on them.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryDataSource
nodes.summary: PagedDataSource that turns StreamingQueryUIData into StructuredStreamingRow objects (streamingRow computes duration and the average input and processing rates over recent progress) and sorts them with the ordering for the chosen column, reversed for descending order. dataSize and sliceData return the size and a page slice of the sorted rows.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Builds the page content with generateStreamingQueryTable and returns it wrapped by headerSparkPage with the title Streaming Query.

nodes.name: generateStreamingQueryTable
nodes.summary: Partitions all query UI data into active and inactive queries and builds an Active Streaming Queries section and a Completed Streaming Queries section as collapsible HTML blocks, each only when non-empty.

nodes.name: queryTable
nodes.summary: Creates a StreamingQueryPagedTable for the given data and table tag (reading the tag's page parameter) and renders the requested page; on IllegalArgumentException or IndexOutOfBoundsException it returns an alert with the exception text.

nodes.name: pageLink
nodes.summary: Builds the URL for a page that keeps page number, sort column, sort order and page size, ending with the table tag anchor.

nodes.name: headers
nodes.summary: Defines the sortable header columns (Name through Latest Batch, plus a non-sortable Error column for completed queries), validates the sort column, and builds the header row.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Renders one table row for a StructuredStreamingRow, with a run id link to the query statistics page, formatted start time and duration, rates and batch id formatted with withNoProgress, and an error message cell when the query is not active.

nodes.name: streamingRow
nodes.summary: Builds a StructuredStreamingRow: duration is now minus start for active queries or last progress time minus start for completed ones; avgInput and avgProcess are the mean of inputRowsPerSecond and processedRowsPerSecond over recent progress.

nodes.name: ordering
nodes.summary: Returns the Ordering for a sort column name (Name, Status, ID, Run ID, Start Time, Duration, Avg Input /sec, Avg Process /sec, Latest Batch), reversed when descending, and throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown column.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatisticsPage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingQueryStatisticsPage, the Structured Streaming UI page "statistics" that shows timelines and histograms for one streaming query selected by its run id. It is attached to the Structured Streaming tab and is rendered when a user opens the statistics page of a query.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatisticsPage
nodes.summary: Private[ui] web page class (extends WebUIPage("statistics") with Logging) that renders the statistics view of a single streaming query. On construction it creates a StateStoreProvider from the STATE_STORE_PROVIDER_CLASS setting to learn its supportedCustomMetrics and reads the ENABLED_STREAMING_UI_CUSTOM_METRIC_LIST setting. render() looks up the query by the "id" request parameter (the run id) and builds the load resources, basic info and stat table; helper methods emit the JavaScript maps (timeFormat, timeTipStrings, formattedTimeTipStrings, formattedTimeToValues) and GraphUIData based rows for input rate, process rate, input rows, batch duration, operation duration, global watermark gap, aggregated state operator metrics and enabled custom metrics.

nodes.name: generateLoadResources
nodes.summary: Returns the script and stylesheet tags (d3.min.js, streaming-page.css, streaming-page.js, structured-streaming-page.js) that the statistics page needs, with URLs prefixed by the base URI of the request.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the page: requires a non-empty "id" parameter, finds the matching StreamingQueryUIData by run id in the parent store (throws IllegalArgumentException if missing), and wraps the load resources, basic info and stat table in a Spark page titled "Streaming Query Statistics".

nodes.name: generateTimeMap
nodes.summary: Builds a script block with a JavaScript timeFormat map from batch timestamp to its formatted time string.

nodes.name: generateTimeTipStrings
nodes.summary: Builds a script block with a timeTipStrings map from timestamp to a "batch <id> (<time>)" tooltip string.

nodes.name: generateFormattedTimeTipStrings
nodes.summary: Builds a script block with a formattedTimeTipStrings map keyed by the formatted time string, giving the batch id tooltip text.

nodes.name: generateTimeToValues
nodes.summary: Builds a script block with a formattedTimeToValues map from formatted time to the list of operation duration values, after padding the duration data.

nodes.name: generateBasicInfo
nodes.summary: Produces the header block of the page: how long the query has been running (current time minus start for active queries, last minus first progress timestamp otherwise), the start date, number of completed batches, query name, id and run id.

nodes.name: generateWatermark
nodes.summary: Creates the "Global Watermark Gap" table row (timeline and histogram, in seconds) from the watermark event time of each recent progress; returns an empty sequence when the last progress has no watermark or no positive watermark values exist.

nodes.name: generateAggregatedStateOperators
nodes.summary: Creates table rows for aggregated state operator metrics (total, updated and removed state rows, state memory used in bytes, late rows dropped by watermark), each summed over all state operators per progress; appends the custom metric rows when custom metrics are enabled, and returns an empty NodeBuffer when there are no state operators.

nodes.name: generateAggregatedCustomMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates one table row per enabled state store custom metric found in the first state operator, summing the metric over operators for each recent progress and using the description of the matching supported custom metric as tooltip.

nodes.name: generateStatTable
nodes.summary: Builds the main statistics table with GraphUIData timelines and histograms for input rate, process rate, input rows, batch duration and an area-stack of operation durations (with "triggerExecution" removed), plus the watermark and aggregated state operator rows; shows "No visualization information available." when there is no last progress. Also emits the JavaScript time maps and the JS collected by the JsCollector.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusListener.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the listener and data classes behind the Structured Streaming UI store: StreamingQueryStatusListener records query start, progress and termination events in an ElementTrackingStore, together with the stored records StreamingQueryData, StreamingQueryUIData and StreamingQueryProgressWrapper.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryStatusListener
nodes.summary: A StreamingQueryListener used by the Structured Streaming UI, keeping data for both active and inactive queries. It reads the limits STREAMING_UI_RETAINED_PROGRESS_UPDATES and STREAMING_UI_RETAINED_QUERIES from StaticSQLConf, registers a trigger on StreamingQueryData that deletes the oldest inactive queries, writes a StreamingQueryData on start and on termination, and writes one StreamingQueryProgressWrapper per progress event while keeping at most the retained number per run id.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryData
nodes.summary: Plain stored record of a streaming query run: name, id, run id (indexed), isActive (indexed as "active"), optional exception text, start timestamp (indexed) and optional end timestamp. It is the summary of a query shown in the UI.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryUIData
nodes.summary: Case class combining a StreamingQueryData summary with the array of recent StreamingQueryProgress objects of one query, as used by UI pages. Its lastProgress method returns the last progress or null when there is none.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryProgressWrapper
nodes.summary: Wrapper that stores a StreamingQueryProgress in the KV store with a unique id index (run id, batch id and timestamp) and a "runId" index. Its companion object holds getUniqueId, which joins run id, batch id and timestamp so that empty progress reports with the same batch id stay distinct.

nodes.name: cleanupInactiveQueries
nodes.summary: Private method called by the store trigger: reads inactive queries from the "active" index, and when their number exceeds the retention limit deletes the oldest ones by end timestamp together with all their progress wrappers (removed in one pass by run id).

nodes.name: onQueryStarted
nodes.summary: Handles a query started event by writing a new active StreamingQueryData with the start timestamp parsed from the event.

nodes.name: onQueryProgress
nodes.summary: Handles a progress event: queues a unique progress id per run id, writes a StreamingQueryProgressWrapper, and deletes the oldest wrappers once the queue exceeds the retained progress updates limit.

nodes.name: onQueryIdle
nodes.summary: Handler for the query idle event; it does nothing.

nodes.name: onQueryTerminated
nodes.summary: Handles a query terminated event by reading the stored summary and writing it again as inactive, with the event exception and the current time as end timestamp, then dropping the per-run progress queue.

nodes.name: lastProgress
nodes.summary: Returns the last element of recentProgress, or null when the array is empty.

nodes.name: getUniqueId
nodes.summary: Companion method that builds the string "<runId>_<batchId>_<timestamp>" used as unique id of a stored progress.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryTab.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingQueryTab, the "Structured Streaming" tab of the Spark UI, and its companion object holding the static resource directory. It is created when the SQL UI is set up for streaming queries.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryTab
nodes.summary: Spark UI tab (extends SparkUITab(sparkUI, "StreamingQuery") with Logging) named "Structured Streaming" with display order 2. Its constructor attaches the StreamingQueryPage and StreamingQueryStatisticsPage pages, attaches itself to the SparkUI and registers a static handler for the resource directory "org/apache/spark/sql/execution/ui/static" under "/static/sql". The companion object only holds the private STATIC_RESOURCE_DIR constant.

nodes.name: displayOrder
nodes.summary: Overrides the tab order so that it is shown at position 2.

nodes.name: InMemoryStatefulProcessorHandle.scala
nodes.summary: Test helper that provides in-memory ValueState, ListState, MapState and timers plus InMemoryStatefulProcessorHandle, a StatefulProcessorHandle implementation backed by Scala mutable collections. It is used to run stateful processor logic in tests without a state store, and lets tests peek at and set state directly.

nodes.name: InMemoryValueState
nodes.summary: In-memory ValueState keeping one value per implicit grouping key in a mutable map; exists, get, update and clear all act on the key from ImplicitGroupingKeyTracker. The clock and TTL config are accepted but not used.

nodes.name: InMemoryListState
nodes.summary: In-memory ListState keeping an ArrayBuffer per implicit grouping key; supports exists, get (iterator), put, appendValue, appendList and clear for the current key.

nodes.name: InMemoryMapState
nodes.summary: In-memory MapState keeping a HashMap per implicit grouping key; supports exists, getValue, containsKey, updateValue, iterator, keys, values, removeKey and clear for the current key.

nodes.name: InMemoryTimers
nodes.summary: In-memory timer registry mapping expiry timestamps to sets of grouping keys. It registers, deletes and lists timers of the current grouping key, and lists all expired timers (expiry <= given time) as (timestamp, key) pairs sorted by timestamp.

nodes.name: InMemoryStatefulProcessorHandle
nodes.summary: In-memory StatefulProcessorHandle for tests. It stores state objects by name in a map, hands out in-memory value, list and map states, checks time mode rules for timers (no timers with TimeMode.None; event time timers must be later than the watermark), and exposes peekXxxState, updateXxxState, deleteState and setWatermark so tests can inspect and prepare state directly.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Replaces the list of the current grouping key with the given array.

nodes.name: appendValue
nodes.summary: Appends one element to the list of the current grouping key, creating the list first when absent.

nodes.name: appendList
nodes.summary: Appends all elements of an array to the list of the current grouping key, creating the list first when absent.

nodes.name: updateValue
nodes.summary: Sets one key and value in the map of the current grouping key, creating the map first when absent.

nodes.name: registerTimer
nodes.summary: Adds the current grouping key to the set registered for the given expiry timestamp.

nodes.name: deleteTimer
nodes.summary: Removes the current grouping key from the given expiry timestamp and drops the timestamp entry when its set becomes empty.

nodes.name: listTimers
nodes.summary: Returns the expiry timestamps that have a timer for the current grouping key.

nodes.name: listExpiredTimers
nodes.summary: Returns (expiry timestamp, key) pairs for all timers with expiry less than or equal to the given time, sorted by timestamp.

nodes.name: setWatermark
nodes.summary: Stores the current watermark in milliseconds, used to validate event time timers; the source comment says TwsTester uses it to sync watermark state.

nodes.name: getValueState
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory value state registered under the name, creating it on first use (an overload at lines 228-229 takes an implicit Encoder and delegates here).

nodes.name: getListState
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory list state registered under the name, creating it on first use (an overload at lines 240-241 takes an implicit Encoder and delegates here).

nodes.name: getMapState
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory map state registered under the name, creating it on first use (an overload at lines 253-256 takes implicit Encoders and delegates here).

nodes.name: registerTimer
nodes.summary: Registers a timer; fails when the time mode is None, and for event time requires the expiry to be later than the current watermark.

nodes.name: deleteTimer
nodes.summary: Deletes a timer after requiring that the time mode is not None.

nodes.name: listTimers
nodes.summary: Lists timers of the current grouping key after requiring that the time mode is not None.

nodes.name: updateValueState
nodes.summary: Test helper that sets the value of an initialized value state for the current key.

nodes.name: peekValueState
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the current value of a value state as an Option.

nodes.name: updateListState
nodes.summary: Test helper that replaces the content of an initialized list state with the given list.

nodes.name: peekListState
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the content of a list state as a List.

nodes.name: updateMapState
nodes.summary: Test helper that clears an initialized map state and fills it from the given Map.

nodes.name: peekMapState
nodes.summary: Test helper that returns the content of a map state as an immutable Map.

nodes.name: deleteState
