nodes.summary: Test helper that clears an initialized state (value, list or map) by name; it requires the state to exist.

nodes.name: ExpiredTimerInfoImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExpiredTimerInfoImpl, a concrete ExpiredTimerInfo that gives a stateful processor the expiry time of the timer that fired.

nodes.name: ExpiredTimerInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Implementation of ExpiredTimerInfo built from an optional expiry time in epoch milliseconds (default None). getExpiryTimeInMs returns the value or -1 when it is absent; the value is only meaningful if the ExpiredTimerInfo is valid.

nodes.name: getExpiryTimeInMs
nodes.summary: Returns the expiry time in milliseconds, or -1 when no expiry time is set.

nodes.name: TimerValuesImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TimerValuesImpl, a concrete TimerValues that exposes the current processing time and watermark to a stateful processor.

nodes.name: TimerValuesImpl
nodes.summary: Implementation of TimerValues built from an optional current processing time and an optional current watermark (both in milliseconds). Each getter returns the value or -1 when it is not available.

nodes.name: getCurrentProcessingTimeInMs
nodes.summary: Returns the available processing time in milliseconds, or -1 otherwise.

nodes.name: getCurrentWatermarkInMs
nodes.summary: Returns the available watermark in milliseconds, or -1 otherwise.

nodes.name: TestGroupState.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TestGroupState trait and its companion factory, an extension of GroupState that exposes extra getters (isRemoved, isUpdated, getTimeoutTimestampMs) so state transition functions can be unit tested for both Scala and Java.

nodes.name: TestGroupState
nodes.summary: Evolving trait extending GroupState[S] with isRemoved, isUpdated and getTimeoutTimestampMs (the timeout timestamp, or Optional.empty if not set). Its companion object has create(), which builds an instance with the same behavior as the engine for given configuration. The scaladoc shows how to use it in Scala and Java tests of a state transition function.

nodes.name: isRemoved
nodes.summary: Abstract member telling whether the state has been marked for removal.

nodes.name: isUpdated
nodes.summary: Abstract member telling whether the state has been updated but not removed.

nodes.name: getTimeoutTimestampMs
nodes.summary: Abstract member returning the timeout timestamp when setTimeoutTimestamp() was called, batch time plus duration when setTimeoutDuration() was called, or Optional.empty otherwise.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Factory that creates a TestGroupState from an optional state, timeout configuration, batch processing time, optional event time watermark and a timed-out flag, by delegating to GroupStateImpl.createForStreaming; documented to throw IllegalArgumentException for negative times and UnsupportedOperationException when timed out without a timeout configured.

nodes.name: TwsTester.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TwsTester, a unit-testing utility that simulates transformWithState for a StatefulProcessor without running a streaming query, using an in-memory processor handle and a manual clock.

nodes.name: TwsTester
nodes.summary: Generic class TwsTester[K, I, O] (since 4.2.0) for testing a StatefulProcessor. On construction it requires an eventTimeExtractor in EventTime mode, wires an InMemoryStatefulProcessorHandle with a ManualClock, calls init, and feeds initialState through handleInitialState when the processor supports it (otherwise requires empty initial state). test() runs handleInputRows for one key (dropping late events in EventTime mode); update/peek methods read and write value, list and map state; setProcessingTime and setWatermark advance time and fire expired timers. TTL and automatic watermark propagation are documented as not supported.

nodes.name: handleInitialState
nodes.summary: Casts the processor to StatefulProcessorWithInitialState and calls handleInitialState for each (key, state) pair with the implicit key set.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Processes the input rows of one key: sets the implicit key, filters late events, and returns all outputs of processor.handleInputRows as a List. In EventTime mode the watermark must be set manually with setWatermark.

nodes.name: filterLateEvents
nodes.summary: In EventTime mode keeps only values whose extracted event time is greater than the current watermark; otherwise returns the values unchanged.

nodes.name: updateValueState
nodes.summary: Sets the value state stateName for a key through the in-memory handle.

nodes.name: peekValueState
nodes.summary: Returns the value state stateName for a key as an Option.

nodes.name: updateListState
nodes.summary: Sets the list state stateName for a key (needs an implicit ClassTag).

nodes.name: peekListState
nodes.summary: Returns the list state stateName for a key as a List.

nodes.name: updateMapState
nodes.summary: Sets the map state stateName for a key from a Map.

nodes.name: peekMapState
nodes.summary: Returns the map state stateName for a key as a Map.

nodes.name: deleteState
nodes.summary: Deletes the state stateName for a key through the handle.

nodes.name: handleExpiredTimers
nodes.summary: Returns nothing when TimeMode is None. Otherwise lists timers expired at or below the processing-time clock (ProcessingTime) or the current watermark (EventTime), calls processor.handleExpiredTimer for each with ExpiredTimerInfoImpl, deletes the timer, and returns all outputs.

nodes.name: setProcessingTime
nodes.summary: Moves the simulated processing time forward (requires ProcessingTime mode and a strictly increasing time) and fires expired timers, returning their outputs.

nodes.name: setWatermark
nodes.summary: Sets the watermark manually (requires EventTime mode and a strictly increasing value), passes it to the handle, and fires expired event-time timers, returning their outputs.

nodes.name: getTimerValues
nodes.summary: Builds a TimerValuesImpl with the current processing time (when the time mode is not None) and the watermark (EventTime only).

nodes.name: UIUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object for the structured streaming UI pages: number sanitizing, query name and status labels, and parsing of progress timestamps.

nodes.name: UIUtils
nodes.summary: Private[ui] object with small helpers used when rendering streaming query UI data. It replaces NaN or infinite doubles by 0.0 (withNumberInvalid), runs a body only when a query has a last progress (withNoProgress), derives a display name (getQueryName, "<no name>" when empty) and a status (getQueryStatus: RUNNING, FAILED or FINISHED), and converts an ISO8601 UTC progress timestamp string to epoch milliseconds (parseProgressTimestamp). It is a separate object from the core UIUtils.

nodes.name: withNumberInvalid
nodes.summary: Returns 0.0 when the by-name double is NaN or infinite, otherwise the value.

nodes.name: withNoProgress
nodes.summary: Evaluates the by-name body when the query already has a completed batch (lastProgress is not null), otherwise returns the default value.

nodes.name: getQueryName
nodes.summary: Returns the query summary name, or "<no name>" when it is null or empty.

nodes.name: getQueryStatus
nodes.summary: Returns "RUNNING" for an active query, "FAILED" when the summary has an exception, and "FINISHED" otherwise.

nodes.name: parseProgressTimestamp
nodes.summary: Parses a progress timestamp in the pattern yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z' (UTC zone) and returns the epoch millisecond value.

nodes.name: AnalysisHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AnalysisHelper trait and its companion object. The trait adds an analyzed flag plus the resolveOperators* and resolveExpressions* families of tree rewrites that skip sub-plans already analyzed, and guards the plain transform methods in test mode.

nodes.name: AnalysisHelper
nodes.summary: Trait for LogicalPlan (it extends QueryPlan[LogicalPlan] with a LogicalPlan self type) that holds a private analyzed flag and offers the resolveOperators, resolveOperatorsUp, resolveOperatorsDown and resolveExpressions variants (each with a WithPruning form) used by analyzer rules. These variants do not descend into sub-plans whose analyzed flag is true, and they mark the work with a depth counter. The trait also overrides transformDownWithPruning, transformUpWithPruning and transformAllExpressionsWithPruning to throw (through assertNotAnalysisRule) when used inside the analyzer in test mode, and clone keeps the analyzed flag. The companion object holds two thread-local int counters (resolveOperatorDepth and inAnalyzer) with the helpers allowInvokingTransformsInAnalyzer and markInAnalyzer.

nodes.name: setAnalyzed
nodes.summary: Marks this plan and, recursively, all its children as analyzed by setting the private analyzed flag. The source comment says it should only be called by CheckAnalysis.

nodes.name: resolveOperators
nodes.summary: Applies a partial function to the plan tree (skipping analyzed sub-trees) with no pruning condition and an unknown rule id; no particular traversal order is promised.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsWithPruning
nodes.summary: Pruned form of resolveOperators: takes a tree-pattern condition and a rule id and delegates to resolveOperatorsDownWithPruning.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsUp
nodes.summary: Applies a rule bottom-up (children first, then the node), skipping analyzed sub-trees, with no pruning.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsUpWithPruning
nodes.summary: Bottom-up rewrite that skips analyzed nodes, nodes failing the condition and nodes where the rule id was already marked ineffective. It maps the children first, applies the rule under the node origin, marks the rule ineffective if nothing changed, and copies tags to a changed result.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsUpWithSubqueriesAndPruning
nodes.summary: Like resolveOperatorsUpWithPruning but also applies the rule to the plans inside subquery expressions of every node, by wrapping the rule in a partial function that rewrites SubqueryExpression plans recursively first.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsDown
nodes.summary: Top-down variant of resolveOperatorsUp with no pruning.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsDownWithPruning
nodes.summary: Top-down rewrite that skips analyzed nodes, nodes failing the condition and nodes whose rule id is marked ineffective. It applies the rule to the node first, then to the children, returns the old instance when nothing changed to avoid garbage, and copies tags onto new plans.

nodes.name: resolveOperatorsUpWithNewOutput
nodes.summary: Variant of transformUpWithNewOutput that does nothing when the plan is already analyzed; otherwise it calls transformUpWithNewOutput with skipCond set to analyzed plans and canGetOutput set to resolved plans.

nodes.name: transformUpWithNewOutput
nodes.summary: Override that runs the parent implementation inside allowInvokingTransformsInAnalyzer so that the rewrite is permitted during analysis.

nodes.name: updateOuterReferencesInSubquery
nodes.summary: Override that runs the parent implementation inside allowInvokingTransformsInAnalyzer.

nodes.name: resolveExpressions
nodes.summary: Transforms the expressions of every node in the tree, skipping analyzed nodes, with no pruning.

nodes.name: resolveExpressionsWithPruning
nodes.summary: Pruned form of resolveExpressions that delegates to resolveExpressionsDownWithPruning.

nodes.name: resolveExpressionsDown
nodes.summary: Top-down expression transform that skips analyzed nodes, with no pruning.

nodes.name: resolveExpressionsDownWithPruning
nodes.summary: Top-down expression transform with pruning; implemented with resolveOperatorsWithPruning, applying transformExpressionsWithPruning to each plan node.

nodes.name: resolveExpressionsUp
nodes.summary: Bottom-up expression transform that skips analyzed nodes, with no pruning.

nodes.name: resolveExpressionsUpWithPruning
nodes.summary: Bottom-up expression transform with pruning; implemented with resolveOperatorsUpWithPruning, applying transformExpressionsUpWithPruning to each plan node.

nodes.name: assertNotAnalysisRule
nodes.summary: Throws QueryExecutionErrors.methodCalledInAnalyzerNotAllowedError when running in test mode, inside the analyzer, and outside any resolveOperator call (depth counter equal to zero).

nodes.name: transformDownWithPruning
nodes.summary: Override that first calls assertNotAnalysisRule, then the parent implementation. Per its comment, analyzer code should use resolveOperatorsDown instead.

nodes.name: transformUpWithPruning
nodes.summary: Override that first calls assertNotAnalysisRule, then the parent implementation. Per its comment, analyzer code should use resolveOperators instead.

nodes.name: transformAllExpressionsWithPruning
nodes.summary: Override that first calls assertNotAnalysisRule, then the parent implementation. Per its comment, analyzer code should use resolveExpressions instead.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Clones the plan through the parent implementation and calls setAnalyzed on the copy when this plan is analyzed.

nodes.name: allowInvokingTransformsInAnalyzer
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that increments the thread-local resolveOperatorDepth, runs the given block, and decrements the counter in a finally clause so that transforms are allowed inside it.

nodes.name: markInAnalyzer
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that increments the thread-local inAnalyzer counter around a block and decrements it afterwards; the counter is an int so nested analyzer runs are handled.

nodes.name: ColumnDefinition.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ColumnDefinition (the user-specified column of a CREATE or REPLACE TABLE command, modelled as an expression) with its companion, and DefaultValueExpression (a placeholder expression holding a default value and its original SQL text).

nodes.name: ColumnDefinition
nodes.summary: Case class (plus companion object) for a column given in CREATE or REPLACE TABLE: name, data type, nullability, comment, optional DefaultValueExpression, optional generation expression, optional identity column spec and metadata. It is an Unevaluable Expression so the analyzer can resolve the default value child; it asserts that a generation expression and an identity spec are not both set. Methods toV2Column and toV1Column convert it to a v2 Column or a StructField with metadata, and isDefaultValueTypeCoerced checks the default value type. The companion adds isDefaultValueTypeMatched, fromV1Column, checkColumnDefinitions (called by CheckAnalysis) and checkDefaultColumnConflicts.

nodes.name: DefaultValueExpression
nodes.summary: Case class holding the child expression of a column or variable default value, its originalSQL text and an optional analyzedChild. It is an Unevaluable unary expression and AnalysisAwareExpression, prints as DEFAULT plus the SQL, and offers toV2 and toV2CurrentDefault to build the data source v2 ColumnDefaultValue or DefaultValue; both require a Literal child and otherwise raise defaultValueNotConstantError.

nodes.name: toV2Column
nodes.summary: Builds a v2 ColumnImpl from this definition, converting the default value with toV2 and encoding the metadata as JSON; the column id is left null because connectors assign it.

nodes.name: toV1Column
nodes.summary: Builds a StructField whose metadata carries the comment, the current default and exists default SQL, the generation expression and the identity column info; the exists default uses the literal SQL when the default is a Literal.

nodes.name: encodeIdentityColumnSpec
nodes.summary: Writes the identity column start, step and allow-explicit-insert values into a MetadataBuilder.

nodes.name: isDefaultValueTypeCoerced
nodes.summary: Returns true when the default value (if any) has a type equal to the column type after replacing CHAR and VARCHAR by STRING.

nodes.name: isDefaultValueTypeMatched
nodes.summary: Companion helper comparing a default value type with the target type after CharVarcharUtils.replaceCharVarcharWithString has been applied to the target.

nodes.name: fromV1Column
nodes.summary: Builds a ColumnDefinition from a StructField: strips the comment, field id, default, generation and identity keys from the metadata, parses the current default SQL with the given ParserInterface, and rebuilds the generation expression and identity spec.

nodes.name: checkColumnDefinitions
nodes.summary: Called by CheckAnalysis for DDL plans whose children are resolved: validates default value expressions of CreateTable and ReplaceTable (through V2CreateTablePlan), AddColumns and AlterColumns, and throws an internal error if another command carries a default.

nodes.name: checkDefaultColumnConflicts
nodes.summary: Throws an AnalysisException when a column with a default value also has a generation expression (GENERATED_COLUMN_WITH_DEFAULT_VALUE) or an identity spec (IDENTITY_COLUMN_WITH_DEFAULT_VALUE).

nodes.name: toV2
nodes.summary: Converts a Literal default into a ColumnDefaultValue holding the original SQL, the current default built by V2ExpressionBuilder from the analyzed child, and the literal as exists default; a non-literal default raises defaultValueNotConstantError.

nodes.name: toV2CurrentDefault
nodes.summary: Converts a Literal default into a v2 DefaultValue made of the original SQL and the current default expression; a non-literal default raises defaultValueNotConstantError.

nodes.name: Command.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Command trait for non-query logical nodes that are executed eagerly, its leaf, unary and binary shapes, AnalysisOnlyCommand and SupervisingCommand.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Trait for a logical node that is a non-query command executed eagerly (for example DDL operations produced by parsers). It has an empty output, reports produced attributes as its outputSet, returns Statistics.DUMMY from stats, and carries the COMMAND node pattern.

nodes.name: LeafCommand
nodes.summary: Command with no children (mixes in LeafLike[LogicalPlan]).

nodes.name: UnaryCommand
nodes.summary: Command with one child (mixes in UnaryLike[LogicalPlan]).

nodes.name: BinaryCommand
nodes.summary: Command with two children (mixes in BinaryLike[LogicalPlan]).

nodes.name: AnalysisOnlyCommand
nodes.summary: Trait for a command whose children are only analyzed, not optimized (the comment gives create view as an example). The children method returns Nil once isAnalyzed is true, and innerChildren then exposes childrenToAnalyze; markAsAnalyzed lets the command update its state from the AnalysisContext when analysis finishes.

nodes.name: SupervisingCommand
nodes.summary: Leaf command that does not expose sub-nodes as children but supervises them in its own way; withTransformedSupervisedPlan applies a plan transformer to the supervised plan and returns a copy of the command.

nodes.name: DistinctKeyVisitor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the DistinctKeyVisitor object, a LogicalPlanVisitor that computes, for each logical operator, the sets of expressions known to be distinct (unique) in its output.

nodes.name: DistinctKeyVisitor
nodes.summary: Object extending LogicalPlanVisitor[Set[ExpressionSet]]. For each plan operator it returns the distinct key sets: Aggregate adds its grouping expressions and then projects the keys; Distinct, and non-ALL Except and Intersect, return the whole output; limits and offsets with maxRows of at most 1 make every output attribute a key; Filter, sorts, windows, repartitions and similar operators pass child keys through; Join combines or forwards child keys depending on join type and equi-join keys; Project keeps keys that survive the projection list (renaming aliases); Expand, Generate, Pivot, ScriptTransformation and Union return no keys.

nodes.name: projectDistinctKeys
nodes.summary: Private helper that keeps the distinct key sets that are subsets of the project output. When the project list has deterministic aliases, it also rewrites keys through the alias attributes, so that aliased columns still count as keys.

nodes.name: addDistinctKey
nodes.summary: Private helper that adds an ExpressionSet to the key sets while keeping them minimal: it returns the input if a subset already exists, otherwise it drops supersets of the new set and adds it.

nodes.name: visitAggregate
nodes.summary: Adds the grouping expressions as a distinct key to the child keys and projects them through the aggregate expressions.

nodes.name: visitExcept
nodes.summary: Returns the whole output as one key for a non-ALL Except, otherwise no keys.

nodes.name: visitGlobalLimit
nodes.summary: If maxRows is at most 1, every output attribute is a key; otherwise passes the child keys through.

nodes.name: visitOffset
nodes.summary: If maxRows is at most 1, every output attribute is a key; otherwise passes the child keys through.

nodes.name: visitIntersect
nodes.summary: Returns the whole output as one key for a non-ALL Intersect, otherwise no keys.

nodes.name: visitJoin
nodes.summary: For semi and anti joins returns the left keys. For equi-joins (found with ExtractEquiJoinKeys) it combines the keys of both sides for an inner join whose join keys cover a key on each side, or forwards the left or right keys for inner and outer joins when the other side is unique on its join keys; otherwise no keys.

nodes.name: visitProject
nodes.summary: Projects the child keys through the project list when the child has keys, otherwise returns no keys.

nodes.name: visitSample
nodes.summary: Passes the child keys through when sampling is without replacement, otherwise returns no keys.

nodes.name: EmptyRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EmptyRelation leaf logical node, which stands for a plan known to produce no rows while keeping the output of the plan it replaced.

nodes.name: EmptyRelation
nodes.summary: Case class leaf node wrapping a logical plan. It copies isStreaming, outputOrdering and output from the wrapped plan, reports zero size and a row count of 0 from computeStats, and returns Some(0) for maxRows and maxRowsPerPartition.

nodes.name: EventTimeWatermark.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EventTimeWatermark and UpdateEventTimeWatermarkColumn unary logical nodes and the companion helpers that tag an attribute with the watermark delay in its metadata.

nodes.name: EventTimeWatermark
nodes.summary: Case class unary node (with companion object) that marks a user-specified column as holding the event time of a row. Its output is the child output with the delay (in the metadata key spark.watermarkDelayMs) set on the event time attribute and removed from other attributes. The companion object defines delayKey, getDelayMs and updateEventTimeColumn. The source comment says updating this metadata is not allowed by default and is kept for a compatibility flag.

nodes.name: UpdateEventTimeWatermarkColumn
nodes.summary: Case class unary node that changes the event time column to the given attribute in the child output; any watermark calculation after it uses the new column. When a delay is given its output tags the column with the delay, otherwise it passes the child output unchanged.

nodes.name: getDelayMs
nodes.summary: Converts a CalendarInterval delay to milliseconds with IntervalUtils.getDuration.

nodes.name: updateEventTimeColumn
nodes.summary: Maps the given attributes: the attribute semantically equal to the new event time gets the delay (in milliseconds) put into its metadata, any other attribute carrying the delay key has it removed, and the rest are unchanged.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns the child output with the event time column tagged with the delay when a delay is defined (using getDelayMs and updateEventTimeColumn), otherwise the child output.

nodes.name: ExecutableDuringAnalysis.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutableDuringAnalysis trait for logical nodes that must be executed while the plan is being analyzed.

nodes.name: ExecutableDuringAnalysis
nodes.summary: Trait for a logical plan node that requires execution during analysis; it declares stageForExplain, which returns the logical plan node to use for EXPLAIN.

nodes.name: FunctionBuilderBase.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FunctionBuilderBase (the base trait for function builders), NamedParametersSupport (named-argument validation and rearrangement), and the InputParameter and FunctionSignature case classes.

nodes.name: FunctionBuilderBase
nodes.summary: Base trait for builders that construct an expression or logical plan from a function call. It exposes an optional functionSignature (one signature per builder, required parameters before optional ones), a rearrange method that reorders the provided arguments by position using NamedParametersSupport.defaultRearrange before build is called, an abstract build(funcName, expressions), and a supportsLambda flag.

nodes.name: NamedParametersSupport
nodes.summary: Object with the argument handling for functions and procedures that accept named arguments. It splits named from positional arguments (rejecting positional after named and duplicate names), checks for unknown parameter names, double assignment and wrong argument counts, and rearranges the arguments into the signature order, filling defaults for omitted optional parameters. It has overloads taking a FunctionSignature or a BoundProcedure.

nodes.name: InputParameter
nodes.summary: Case class for one parameter of a function: a name and an optional default Expression; no default means the argument is required.

nodes.name: FunctionSignature
nodes.summary: Case class holding the list of InputParameter values of a function; overloads are not supported, so a function expression has one signature.

nodes.name: rearrange
nodes.summary: Default implementation that reorders provided arguments to positional order for the expected signature by calling NamedParametersSupport.defaultRearrange; it runs before build.

nodes.name: splitAndCheckNamedArguments
nodes.summary: Splits the argument list at the first NamedArgumentExpression into positional and named arguments, and throws if a name repeats (doubleNamedArgumentReference) or a positional argument follows named ones (unexpectedPositionalArgument).

nodes.name: defaultRearrange
nodes.summary: Private core overload (the widest of three defaultRearrange overloads; the other two, at lines 130-136 and 138-147, take a FunctionSignature or a BoundProcedure and delegate here). It validates parameter order and names and the argument count, then returns positional arguments followed by named arguments placed in parameter order with defaults filled in.

nodes.name: toInputParameter
nodes.summary: Private helper turning a ProcedureParameter into an InputParameter, analyzing its default value through ResolveDefaultColumns.analyze for the CALL statement.

nodes.name: LocalRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LocalRelation logical leaf node, a scan over a local in-memory collection of InternalRow values, and its companion factory methods.

nodes.name: LocalRelation
nodes.summary: Case class leaf node holding resolved output attributes and a local Seq[InternalRow] (not shipped to executors), with optional streaming flag and stream source. It requires resolved output, supports newInstance with fresh attribute ids (MultiInstanceRelation), withStream and getStream (StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan), computes statistics from the row size and row count (the row count is hidden in test mode unless a test conf key says otherwise), renders itself with toSQL as a VALUES clause, and reports maxRows equal to the data length. The companion object builds instances from attributes, StructFields or a StructType, and from external Rows or Products with a Catalyst converter.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory building a LocalRelation from a StructType by converting it to attributes with DataTypeUtils.toAttributes. Two other apply overloads (line 32 for attributes, lines 34-36 for StructFields) are folded into this node.

nodes.name: fromExternalRows
nodes.summary: Creates a LocalRelation from Rows by converting each one to an InternalRow with a Catalyst converter built from the schema of the output attributes.

nodes.name: fromProduct
nodes.summary: Creates a LocalRelation from Product values (such as tuples or case classes) by converting each one with a Catalyst converter built from the output attributes.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Returns a copy with new expression ids on every output attribute, needed when the relation appears more than once in a query.

nodes.name: stringArgs
nodes.summary: Provides the arguments shown in the tree string: "<empty>" plus the output when there is no data, otherwise only the output.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Computes statistics as size per row (EstimationUtils.getSizePerRow) times the number of rows; the row count is omitted in test mode unless spark.sql.test.localRelationRowCount is set to true.

nodes.name: toSQL
nodes.summary: Renders the relation as a SQL VALUES clause with one tuple per row, each cell written with Literal.sql, aliased to the given inline table name and the output column names; requires non-empty data.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanDistinctKeys.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LogicalPlanDistinctKeys trait that gives a LogicalPlan a lazily computed distinctKeys set.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanDistinctKeys
nodes.summary: Trait for LogicalPlan that adds distinct attributes: the doc example is a GROUP BY a, b query whose distinct keys are a and b. Its single member is a lazy val distinctKeys.

nodes.name: distinctKeys
nodes.summary: Lazy val returning the set of distinct key ExpressionSets of the plan: it runs DistinctKeyVisitor.visit on the plan when the PROPAGATE_DISTINCT_KEYS_ENABLED configuration is on, and otherwise returns an empty set.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanVisitor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LogicalPlanVisitor[T] trait, a visitor over LogicalPlan operators with one abstract visit method per supported operator.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanVisitor
nodes.summary: Trait for computing a property T over a LogicalPlan tree. Its visit method pattern-matches the plan and dispatches to visitAggregate, visitDistinct, visitExcept, visitExpand, visitFilter, visitGenerate, visitGlobalLimit, visitOffset, visitIntersect, visitJoin, visitLocalLimit, visitPivot, visitProject, visitRepartition, visitRepartitionByExpr, visitRebalancePartitions, visitSample, visitScriptTransform, visitUnion, visitWindow, visitTail, visitSort or visitWithCTE, and falls back to default for any other plan. Implementers define all these abstract methods.

nodes.name: visit
nodes.summary: Matches the plan against 23 operator types (Aggregate through WithCTE) and calls the corresponding visitX method, or default(p) for other plans.

nodes.name: MergeRows.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MergeRows unary logical node used when a MERGE operation is rewritten, and its companion with the Instruction hierarchy (Keep, Discard, Split) and the Context values.

nodes.name: MergeRows
nodes.summary: Case class unary node (with companion object) placed on top of the join of target and source tables in a rewritten MERGE. It takes presence expressions for the source and target rows, three instruction lists (matched, not matched, not matched by source), a checkCardinality flag, the output and the child. It computes producedAttributes as output attributes missing from the input, references (adding the "__row_id" attribute of the child when cardinality is checked), the combined instructions list and the outputs of all instructions. The companion holds ROW_ID and the Instruction, Context, Keep, Discard and Split definitions.

nodes.name: Instruction
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for an expression that derives output rows from a joined row for one MATCHED, NOT MATCHED or NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clause. It is an Unevaluable Expression (so analyzer and optimizer transform it), declares condition and outputs, is non-nullable and reports NullType as its data type because only MergeRows contains it.

nodes.name: Context
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the kind of row operation attached to a Keep instruction.

nodes.name: Copy
nodes.summary: Case object Context value for copying a row.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Case object Context value for deleting a row.

nodes.name: Insert
nodes.summary: Case object Context value for inserting a row.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Case object Context value for updating a row.

nodes.name: Keep
nodes.summary: Case class Instruction that emits one output row (a list of expressions) when its condition holds, tagged with a Context; its children are the condition followed by the output expressions.

nodes.name: Discard
nodes.summary: Case class Instruction (also UnaryLike) that discards the row when its condition holds; it produces no outputs and its single child is the condition.

nodes.name: Split
nodes.summary: Case class Instruction that emits two output rows (output and otherOutput) when its condition holds; its children are the condition followed by both output lists.

nodes.name: producedAttributes
nodes.summary: Lazy val: the output attributes that are not part of the input set.

nodes.name: references
nodes.summary: Transient lazy val: the references of all expressions (plus the child "__row_id" attribute, asserted to exist, when cardinality is checked) minus the produced attributes.

nodes.name: instructions
nodes.summary: Concatenates the matched, not matched and not matched by source instruction lists.

nodes.name: outputs
nodes.summary: Flat-maps the outputs of every instruction into a sequence of output expression lists.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Short display string: "MergeRows" followed by the truncated output list.

nodes.name: MultiResult.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the MultiResult logical node, which holds several plans and exposes the output of the last one.

nodes.name: MultiResult
nodes.summary: Case class logical plan whose children are a sequence of plans; its output is the output of the last child (or empty if there are none), and withNewChildrenInternal copies it with new children.

nodes.name: NearestByJoin.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the NearestByJoin binary logical node for a nearest-by top-K ranking join, and a companion exposing MaxNumResults.

nodes.name: NearestByJoin
nodes.summary: Case class binary node (with companion object) for a nearest-by join: for each left row it returns up to numResults right rows ordered by a rankingExpression, with NearestByDistance taking smallest values first and NearestBySimilarity largest first. It accepts only Inner or LeftOuter join types, keeps the APPROX or EXACT choice in the approx flag (both currently use the same rewrite), allows nondeterministic ranking expressions, and declares all output attributes nullable to match the schema of RewriteNearestByJoin. The companion exposes MaxNumResults from NearestByJoinValidation.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Returns left and right child output attributes, all widened to nullable.

nodes.name: duplicateResolved
nodes.summary: True when the left and right output attribute sets do not intersect.

nodes.name: resolved
nodes.summary: Lazy val that is true when children and all expressions are resolved and there are no duplicate attributes between the sides.

nodes.name: basicLogicalOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the core logical plan operators of Catalyst: projection, filter, generate, set operations (Intersect, Except, Union), joins, sort, range, aggregate, window, expand, pivot and unpivot, limits and offset, subquery alias, sampling, distinct and deduplicate, repartition and rebalance, lateral and as-of joins, and a few marker traits. Most are case classes extending UnaryNode, BinaryNode or LeafNode and implement output, maxRows, constraints, node patterns and withNewChild(ren)Internal; they are used by the analyzer, optimizer and planner.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file where most operators are case classes with companion objects; companion objects hold factories, extractors (unapply) and helpers, and companion and class share one class node id.

nodes.name: ReturnAnswer
nodes.summary: Unary logical node inserted at the top of the plan before the query planner runs for take() or collect(). Rules can pattern-match on it to apply transformations that only take effect at the top of the plan; it passes output and maxRows through from its child.

nodes.name: Subquery
nodes.summary: Unary node placed at the top of a subquery when it is optimized, so that a subquery can be recognized as such by subquery-aware transformations. It carries a correlated flag; the companion object's fromExpression builds one from a SubqueryExpression using its plan and whether it has a correlated subquery.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Logical projection that computes projectList over the child rows; its output is the attributes of the project list and it is only resolved when the list holds no aggregate, generator or window expressions. doCanonicalize strips a Project that only renames. The companion object holds hiddenOutputTag and matchSchema, which wraps a plan in a Project that reorders, casts and null-fills columns to match a target StructType (helpers reconcileColumnType, reorderFields, createNewColumn).

nodes.name: DataFrameDropColumns
nodes.summary: Placeholder unary node for dropping columns by a list of expressions; it reports an empty output and is never resolved (resolved is false), so it must be replaced before the plan is considered resolved. maxRows and maxRowsPerPartition come from the child.

nodes.name: Generate
nodes.summary: Applies a Generator to each input row and combines its output rows with the input, similar to flatMap with the option to join input rows with the generated ones. Supports an outer flag (emit a row even when the generator yields nothing), an optional qualifier and an unrequiredChildIndex list that the optimizer fills to omit unneeded child columns. Output is the required child output plus the qualified, nullability-adjusted generator output.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.summary: Logical filter that keeps rows matching a condition. maxRows is 0 when the condition is the false literal; validConstraints are the child constraints plus the conjunctive predicates of the condition that contain no correlated subquery.

nodes.name: SetOperation
nodes.summary: Abstract base for binary set operators (Intersect and Except). It defines duplicateResolved, the left and right constraint helpers (the right side is rewritten to the left attributes) and resolved, which requires equal column counts with the same types and no duplicate output attributes. The companion object provides an unapply extractor for the two children.

nodes.name: Intersect
nodes.summary: Logical INTERSECT (optionally ALL) of two plans. Output merges child outputs by taking the left attributes with nullability combined using AND (lazily computed when SQLConf.LAZY_SET_OPERATOR_OUTPUT is set); maxRows is the minimum of the children's maxRows. The companion object has mergeChildOutputs.

nodes.name: Except
nodes.summary: Logical EXCEPT (optionally ALL) of two plans. Output and constraints come from the left child only (mergeChildOutputs returns the first child's output), and maxRows is the left maxRows.

nodes.name: UnionBase
nodes.summary: Abstract helper shared by Union and UnionLoop (the doc comment says UnionLoop covers the recursive CTE case). It computes the merged output (lazily when SQLConf.LAZY_SET_OPERATOR_OUTPUT is set) using Union.mergeChildOutputs, merges children constraints (rewriteConstraints, merge) and offers allChildrenCompatible, which checks that all child outputs match the first child with DataType.equalsStructurally.

nodes.name: SequentialOrSimpleUnion
nodes.summary: Extractor and helper object for Union and SequentialStreamingUnion (it does not match other UnionBase subtypes such as UnionLoop). It provides unapply to match either type, isSameType to avoid merging the two kinds when flattening, byName and allowMissingCol accessors, and withNewChildren to rebuild a union of the same concrete type.

nodes.name: Union
nodes.summary: Logical UNION ALL of any number of child plans, with byName and allowMissingCol flags for column-name based resolution. Child order is not significant. maxRows and maxRowsPerPartition sum the children (overflow gives None) and resolved needs more than one compatible child. The companion object (lines 471-490) has apply(left, right) and mergeChildOutputs, which unifies nullability and merges data types across children.

nodes.name: Join
nodes.summary: Logical join of two plans with a JoinType, optional condition and JoinHint. Output depends on the join type via the companion Join.computeOutput (existence joins, semi/anti, outer joins add nullability); maxRows, validConstraints and metadataOutput are computed per join type. A join is resolved only if children and expressions are resolved, no duplicate expression ids exist and the condition is boolean; natural and using joins are never resolved until rewritten. The hint is ignored in canonicalization.

nodes.name: InsertIntoDir
nodes.summary: Unresolved logical node that writes a query result into a directory (local or not), described by a CatalogStorageFormat, an optional provider and an overwrite flag. It reports an empty output, is never resolved and is replaced by concrete implementations during analysis.

nodes.name: View
nodes.summary: Container for a view description (CatalogTable) and whether the view is temporary; its child is the plan parsed from the view text, or an already resolved plan for a temporary view created from a dataframe. The operator is removed at the end of analysis. doCanonicalize drops the extra cast/alias Project added when resolving a SQL view. The companion View.effectiveSQLConf builds the SQLConf to use for the view from stored configs.

nodes.name: WithWindowDefinition
nodes.summary: Unary node that holds named window definitions (a map from name to WindowSpecDefinition) above its child, with a forPipeSQL flag; output is the child's output. Used while the named windows are being resolved.

nodes.name: Sort
nodes.summary: Logical sort by a list of SortOrder, either global over the whole data set or only within each partition, with an optional SortHint. outputOrdering is the order list and maxRowsPerPartition equals maxRows for a global sort.

nodes.name: Range
nodes.summary: Leaf node that produces a table of Long values id from start to end (exclusive) by step, optionally split into numSlices partitions; it backs the SQL range table function (see the ExpressionDescription). Auxiliary constructors accept Expression arguments that are evaluated through Range.toLong/toInt (castAndEval with implicit casts under TypeCoercion or AnsiTypeCoercion). It computes numElements, maxRows, per-partition maxRows, ascending or descending outputOrdering, and statistics with min, max, distinct count and an optional histogram.

nodes.name: Aggregate
nodes.summary: Group-by operator holding grouping expressions, aggregate (project-list) expressions and an optional AggregateHint. It is unresolved if the list contains window expressions; maxRows is 1 when there are no grouping expressions; groupOnly detects aggregates that only group. The companion object has isAggregateBufferMutable, supportsHashAggregate and supportsObjectHashAggregate, which decide hash-based aggregation support from buffer mutability and binary-stable types.

nodes.name: Window
nodes.summary: Logical window operator computing windowExpressions over partitionSpec and orderSpec, with an optional WindowHint. Output is the child output plus the window expression attributes, which are also its produced attributes (windowOutputSet).

nodes.name: WindowGroupLimit
nodes.summary: Unary node that limits rows per window partition using a rank-like function and an integer limit; it asserts a non-empty orderSpec and a positive limit and passes the child output through.

nodes.name: Expand
nodes.summary: Expand applies several projections to every input row, so one input row produces multiple output rows (used for grouping sets and rollup). The companion Expand.apply builds the projections from grouping set attributes, nulls out attributes not in the set, appends a grouping id bitmask (buildBitmask), adds a _gen_grouping_pos column when grouping sets repeat and optionally tags pass-through duplicate attributes (tagPassthroughDuplicates). The case class reports no constraints because attributes may be nulled.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes a Project; if the projection list only renames or re-ids the child's attributes with no semantic change, the Project is removed and the canonicalized child is returned.

nodes.name: matchSchema
nodes.summary: Builds a Project over a resolved plan so its columns follow a target StructType, delegating to reorderFields to reorder, cast and fill missing nullable columns.

nodes.name: reconcileColumnType
nodes.summary: Reconciles one column expression with an expected data type and nullability. It recurses into struct fields, array elements (ArrayTransform) and map keys and values (MapFromArrays), applies an ANSI store-assign cast when allowed, and raises compilation errors on null violations or incompatible types.

nodes.name: reorderFields
nodes.summary: Matches input fields to expected struct fields by name using the resolver, filling missing nullable fields with null and raising errors for missing non-nullable, ambiguous or unresolved fields. Matched columns go through reconcileColumnType and createNewColumn.

nodes.name: createNewColumn
nodes.summary: Wraps an expression as a named column, merging original and new metadata: attributes are renamed with the merged metadata, other expressions get an Alias, with explicit metadata only when it is non-empty.

nodes.name: rightConstraints
nodes.summary: Returns the right child's constraints rewritten to refer to the left child's attributes, requiring both outputs to have the same size.

nodes.name: mergeChildOutputs
nodes.summary: Builds the Intersect output from the left attributes, with nullability set to true only when both sides are nullable (the right side is not used otherwise since its rows are excluded).

nodes.name: mergeChildOutputs
nodes.summary: Merges the output attributes of all union children position by position: nullable if any child is nullable, with the data type unified through StructType.unionLikeMerge, creating a new AttributeReference when the type changes.

nodes.name: rewriteConstraints
nodes.summary: Maps constraints written over one child's attributes onto a reference child's attributes by transforming attribute references.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Combines two constraint sets from union branches: keeps common constraints and loosens single-reference constraints into an Or of Ands on the same attribute ((A1 || A2) && (B1 || B2) style).

nodes.name: allChildrenCompatible
nodes.summary: Checks that all children have the same output length as the first child and structurally equal data types, assuming children are resolved.

nodes.name: computeOutput
nodes.summary: Computes the output attributes of a join for a given join type: existence joins append the exists attribute, semi/anti return the left side, outer joins mark the null-producing side nullable, and other joins concatenate both outputs.

nodes.name: canRemoveProject
nodes.summary: Decides whether a Project added to cast and alias a view's columns does nothing semantic (same length, cast of an attribute with matching type and name) so it can be removed during canonicalization.

nodes.name: effectiveSQLConf
nodes.summary: Builds the SQLConf used to resolve a view: the active conf when current configs are configured for non-temporary views, otherwise a new conf from stored view configs with resolution configs retained from the active conf through Analyzer.retainResolutionConfigsForAnalysis.

nodes.name: castAndEval
nodes.summary: Evaluates a foldable range argument after an implicit cast to the expected type, raising compilation errors for non-foldable arguments or unexpected data types.

nodes.name: toSQL
nodes.summary: Renders the Range as a SELECT id FROM range(...) SQL string, including numSlices when it is defined.

nodes.name: maxRowsPerPartition
nodes.summary: Estimates the maximum rows per partition as numElements divided by numSlices rounded up, falling back to maxRows when slices are unset or the result overflows a Long.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Computes Statistics for the range: zero size when empty, otherwise size, row count and a ColumnStat (min, max, distinct count, lengths, optional histogram) for the id column.

nodes.name: computeHistogramStatistics
nodes.summary: Builds an equal-height histogram of the range values using the configured number of bins, folding over percentile positions to create HistogramBin entries.

nodes.name: getRangeValue
nodes.summary: Returns the range value at a given index, reversing the order when the step is negative.

nodes.name: groupOnly
nodes.summary: True when the aggregate only groups: grouping expressions are non-empty and every aggregate expression is foldable or semantically equal to a grouping expression.

nodes.name: supportsHashAggregate
nodes.summary: Checks whether hash aggregation is possible: the aggregation buffer schema is mutable and all grouping expressions have binary-stable types.

nodes.name: supportsObjectHashAggregate
nodes.summary: Checks whether object hash aggregation applies: no grouping expression has a binary-unstable type and at least one aggregate function is a TypedImperativeAggregate.

nodes.name: buildBitmask
nodes.summary: Builds the grouping id bitmask for one grouping set: a bit is 0 for each selected grouping attribute and 1 otherwise, computed by reducing masks with AND, with the example in the doc of (a, c) in (a, b, c, d) giving 5.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that builds an Expand from grouping sets: one projection per grouping set with unselected group-by attributes set to null, a grouping id literal from the bitmask, an extra _gen_grouping_pos column when grouping sets repeat, nullability fixes, optional duplicate tagging, and a Project of child output plus group-by aliases as the child.

nodes.name: tagPassthroughDuplicates
nodes.summary: Adds __is_duplicate metadata to child output attributes that are also wrapped by a simple-attribute group-by alias, so name-based resolution can pick the produced grouping attribute instead of reporting ambiguity.

nodes.name: Offset
nodes.summary: Logical OFFSET that skips a number of rows from the start of the child's output. maxRows subtracts an integer-literal offset from the child's maxRows.

nodes.name: Pivot
nodes.summary: Placeholder for a pivot operation (group-by expressions, pivot column, pivot values, aggregates) that is never resolved and is replaced by a Project or Aggregate during analysis. Its output lists the group-by attributes followed by one attribute per pivot value (and per aggregate when several).

nodes.name: Transpose
nodes.summary: Leaf node for a transpose whose result is already collected: output holds the schema and data holds the transposed InternalRow values. The doc says it is later converted to a LocalRelation at ReplaceTranspose during optimization.

nodes.name: Unpivot
nodes.summary: Placeholder for an unpivot (melt): id columns, one or more groups of value columns, optional aliases, a variable column name and value column names. It is converted to an Expand during analysis; the doc explains that ids or values may be None and are filled in later. canBeCoercioned and valuesTypeCoercioned check whether value columns are resolved and share data types.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.summary: Factory and extractor object for a logical limit, which is split into a GlobalLimit over a LocalLimit so limits can be pushed down separately. apply builds GlobalLimit(limitExpr, LocalLimit(limitExpr, child)); unapply matches that pair when both limit expressions are equal. The doc comment explains why a partition-local limit is pushed below a union.

nodes.name: GlobalLimit
nodes.summary: Global (coordinated) limit that emits at most limitExpr rows in total; maxRows is set when the expression is an integer literal. It deliberately does not extend OrderPreservingUnaryNode, because a shuffle between the child and the limit can break ordering.

nodes.name: LocalLimit
nodes.summary: Partition-local (non-coordinated) limit that emits at most limitExpr rows on each physical partition; maxRowsPerPartition is set for an integer-literal limit.

nodes.name: LimitAll
nodes.summary: Logical LIMIT ALL node. It is usually a no-op for compatibility, but for recursive CTEs it overrides the default row limit determined by a flag and negates the row limit; output is the child's output.

nodes.name: OffsetAndLimit
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches a GlobalLimit over an Offset over a LocalLimit when globalLimit + offset equals localLimit (the shape left after the optimizer pushes the local limit through the offset) and returns offset, limit and child.

nodes.name: LimitAndOffset
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches an Offset directly over a Limit with integer literals and returns the limit, the offset and the child plan.

nodes.name: Tail
nodes.summary: Logical tail operator that returns the last limitExpr rows. Unlike Limit it has no separate global and local plans (the doc points to CollectTailExec and CollectLimitExec) and can only be a root node.

nodes.name: SubqueryAlias
nodes.summary: Aliased subquery: renames the child plan with an AliasIdentifier so its output attributes carry the alias as qualifier. metadataOutput propagates the child's metadata columns (with the new qualifier) depending on SQLConf.SUBQUERY_ALIAS_ALWAYS_PROPAGATE_METADATA_COLUMNS or the child type; canonicalization drops the alias. The companion object has apply overloads taking a String, a database or a multipart identifier, and generateSubqueryName.

nodes.name: SampleMethod
nodes.summary: Sealed trait describing how a Sample is drawn, with two case objects in its companion: Bernoulli (row-level sampling, no I/O savings) and System (whole partitions or splits included or skipped).

nodes.name: Bernoulli
nodes.summary: Case object for row-level sampling (BERNOULLI), where each row is independently selected and there are no I/O savings.

nodes.name: System
nodes.summary: Case object for system-level sampling (SYSTEM), where entire partitions or splits are included or skipped.

nodes.name: Sample
nodes.summary: Logical sampling of a dataset between a lower and upper probability bound, with or without replacement, an optional seed (None means a random seed is generated at execution time) and a SampleMethod (default Bernoulli). It requires a valid fraction on construction, and maxRows is unknown when sampling with replacement. The companion object offers apply overloads that wrap a concrete seed in Some.

nodes.name: Distinct
nodes.summary: Logical node that removes duplicate input rows; output and maxRows come from the child and it carries the DISTINCT_LIKE tree pattern.

nodes.name: RepartitionOperation
nodes.summary: Abstract base for Repartition and RepartitionByExpression. It declares shuffle, numPartitions and partitioning, and fixes maxRows and output to the child's values.

nodes.name: Repartition
nodes.summary: Logical node that gives exactly numPartitions partitions, created directly by coalesce or repartition calls. When shuffle is true its partitioning is SinglePartition for one partition or RoundRobinPartitioning otherwise; numPartitions must be positive.

nodes.name: HasPartitionExpressions
nodes.summary: Trait shared by RepartitionByExpression and RebalancePartitions that holds partitionExpressions, optNumPartitions and optAdvisoryPartitionSize. numPartitions defaults to the configured number of shuffle partitions, and partitioning is chosen as round robin (no expressions), ShufflePartitionIdPassThrough (a single DirectShufflePartitionID), RangePartitioning (all SortOrder) or HashPartitioning.

nodes.name: RepartitionByExpression
nodes.summary: Repartitions data by expressions into an optional number of partitions (defaulting to the configured shuffle partition count, which can be coalesced by AQE), used when the consumer needs a specific ordering or distribution. It always shuffles and uses SinglePartition when numPartitions is 1; the companion apply takes a plain Int partition count.

nodes.name: RebalancePartitions
nodes.summary: Operator that rebalances the child's output partitions so each is of reasonable size and tries to partition by the given expressions, splitting skewed partitions; useful before writing to a table to avoid too small or too big files. The doc says it only makes sense when AQE is enabled.

nodes.name: OneRowRelation
nodes.summary: Leaf relation with exactly one row and no columns, used for SELECT statements without a FROM clause. It overrides makeCopy because TreeNode.makeCopy does not support a zero-argument constructor.

nodes.name: Deduplicate
nodes.summary: Logical plan for dropDuplicates on a set of key attributes; output and maxRows come from the child and it carries the DISTINCT_LIKE tree pattern.

nodes.name: DeduplicateWithinWatermark
nodes.summary: Deduplication on key attributes inside an event-time watermark window. Its references include the key attributes plus child output columns carrying EventTimeWatermark.delayKey metadata so event time columns are not pruned.

nodes.name: SupportsSubquery
nodes.summary: Marker trait for commands that support subqueries, so such commands are allowed in the subquery-related checks.

nodes.name: SupportsNonDeterministicExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for logical plans that can declare through allowNonDeterministicExpression whether non-deterministic expressions are allowed, so they can pass the CheckAnalysis rule.

nodes.name: CollectMetrics
nodes.summary: Collects named metrics (aggregate functions or literals) from a dataset, behaving like a global aggregate; when a batch or a streaming epoch completes, an event is emitted on the driver that a listener can observe. It is resolved when the name and metrics are non-empty and resolved, and canonicalization resets dataframeId to 0.

nodes.name: DomainJoin
nodes.summary: Placeholder join of domain attributes with the child, added when decorrelating subqueries and rewritten during optimization; only Inner and LeftOuter join types are allowed. Output is the domain attributes followed by the child output (made nullable for left outer).

nodes.name: LateralJoin
nodes.summary: Logical lateral join between a left plan and a LateralSubquery, allowing Inner, LeftOuter and Cross types. Children are resolved against both sides via resolveChildren, output concatenates left and right outputs (right nullable for left outer), and resolution requires no duplicate attributes and a boolean condition. The companion holds the BY_TABLE_ARGUMENT tag, which marks lateral joins added by resolving a table argument.

nodes.name: AsOfJoin
nodes.summary: Logical as-of join of two plans with an as-of condition, an optional extra condition, an Inner or LeftOuter join type, an ordering expression and an optional tolerance assertion. The companion apply builds the condition (makeAsOfCond) and ordering expression (makeOrderingExpr) from the two as-of columns, a tolerance, allowExactMatches and the direction (Backward, Forward or Nearest).

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes the Pivot output: group-by attributes followed by one attribute per pivot value, or per value and aggregate (named value_aggSql) when there are several aggregates.

nodes.name: canBeCoercioned
nodes.summary: True when value columns are defined, non-empty and resolved and the id columns (if given) are resolved, so type coercion of values can run after id detection.

nodes.name: valuesTypeCoercioned
nodes.summary: True when coercion is possible and the inner values at each position share the same data type across all value groups.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds the two-level limit GlobalLimit(limitExpr, LocalLimit(limitExpr, child)).

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches a GlobalLimit directly over a LocalLimit with equal limit expressions and returns the expression and the child.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches GlobalLimit over Offset over LocalLimit with integer literals where globalLimit plus offset equals localLimit, returning offset, global limit and child.

nodes.name: unapply
nodes.summary: Matches an Offset over a Limit with integer literals and returns limit, offset and child.

nodes.name: metadataOutput
nodes.summary: Returns the child's metadata columns re-qualified with the alias when propagation is allowed (config SUBQUERY_ALIAS_ALWAYS_PROPAGATE_METADATA_COLUMNS, or the legacy rule that the child is a LeafNode or SubqueryAlias), skipping qualified-access-only columns, else Nil.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that creates a SubqueryAlias from a name plus database (here with a database part); other overloads accept a plain name (lines 1891-1895) or a multipart identifier (lines 1904-1908).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that wraps a Long seed in Some and takes an explicit SampleMethod; an overload at lines 1929-1936 does the same without a SampleMethod.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Returns SinglePartition for one partition or RoundRobinPartitioning otherwise; requires shuffle to be true.

nodes.name: partitioning
nodes.summary: Chooses a Partitioning from partitionExpressions: round robin if empty, ShufflePartitionIdPassThrough for a single DirectShufflePartitionID, RangePartitioning when all expressions are SortOrder, else HashPartitioning; mixed SortOrder and non-SortOrder input is rejected.

nodes.name: resolveChildren
nodes.summary: Resolves name parts against the attributes of both the left plan and the lateral subquery plan, falling back to metadata attributes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds an AsOfJoin from the left and right as-of columns, tolerance, allowExactMatches and direction by creating the as-of condition and ordering expression, and a tolerance assertion (tolerance >= default value).

nodes.name: makeAsOfCond
nodes.summary: Builds the as-of join condition for each (allowExactMatches, direction) pair using comparison operators, and adds range limits using the tolerance when given.

nodes.name: makeOrderingExpr
nodes.summary: Builds the ordering expression for choosing the closest match: left minus right for Backward, right minus left for Forward, and the absolute difference through an If for Nearest.

nodes.name: cteOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical plan nodes that represent common table expressions (CTEs) and recursive CTEs: UnionLoop, UnionLoopRef, CTERelationDef, CTERelationRef, WithCTE, CTEInChildren and UnresolvedWith. UnresolvedWith is the container produced for a WITH clause; analysis turns it into WithCTE with CTERelationDef definitions and CTERelationRef references, and a recursive CTE uses UnionLoop with UnionLoopRef.

nodes.name: UnionLoop
nodes.summary: Case class logical node for CTE recursion. It holds an anchor plan (initial element) and a recursion plan that contains an UnionLoopRef, and behaves like a Union of the two children that loops until the last generated child is empty. Output attributes get the ids in outputAttrIds, optional limit and maxDepth bound the loop, and a Union inside a recursive CTE is resolved into this node.

nodes.name: computeOutput
nodes.summary: Computes the node output by merging the children outputs with Union.mergeChildOutputs and then re-tagging each attribute with the matching id from outputAttrIds.

nodes.name: argString
nodes.summary: Builds the argument string of the node: the loop id followed by the optional limit and maxDepth values.

nodes.name: UnionLoopRef
nodes.summary: Case class leaf node that is the recursive reference inside the recursive child of an UnionLoop. A CTERelationRef in a recursive CTE is resolved into it. The accumulated flag says whether it stands for the previous iteration result (false) or the union of all previous iteration results (true). It creates new instances with fresh attributes, reports the default size in bytes as statistics, and prints the loop id, output and accumulated flag in verbose explain output.

nodes.name: verboseStringWithOperatorId
nodes.summary: Renders the verbose explain text of the node with its formatted name, loop id, output attributes and accumulated flag.

nodes.name: CTERelationDef
nodes.summary: Case class unary node (with companion object) that wraps a CTE definition plan together with a unique id taken from CTERelationDef.newId. It also carries originalPlanWithPredicates (used by CTE predicate pushdown rules), underSubquery, and maxDepth for recursion. maxRows depends on the CTE_RELATION_DEF_MAX_ROWS config. Lazy vals hasSelfReferenceAsCTERef, hasSelfReferenceInAnchor, hasSelfReferenceInSubCTE and hasSelfReferenceAsUnionLoopRef detect recursive self references in the child plan. The companion object keeps a static atomic counter and the newId method.

nodes.name: maxRows
nodes.summary: Returns the child maxRows when the CTE_RELATION_DEF_MAX_ROWS config is enabled, otherwise None.

nodes.name: hasSelfReferenceInAnchor
nodes.summary: Lazy val that matches the child against SubqueryAlias (optionally under UnresolvedSubqueryColumnAliases and WithCTE) around a Union and checks whether the first union child, the anchor, contains a recursive CTERelationRef to this CTE id.

nodes.name: hasSelfReferenceInSubCTE
nodes.summary: Lazy val that matches the child against a WithCTE under SubqueryAlias and checks whether any nested CTE definition contains a recursive CTERelationRef to this CTE id.

nodes.name: newId
nodes.summary: Companion object method that returns the next unique CTE definition id from a shared AtomicLong counter.

nodes.name: CTERelationRef
nodes.summary: Case class leaf node that stands for a reference to a CTE. It stores the id of the CTE definition (cteId), a resolved flag, its own output attributes (which may differ from the definition after de-duplication), optional statistics, a recursive flag and isUnlimitedRecursion for non-recursive references to a recursive CTE. newInstance regenerates attribute ids while keeping duplicated attributes on the same id, and computeStats uses statsOpt or the default size in bytes.

nodes.name: stringArgs
nodes.summary: Returns the string arguments for explain, dropping the last isUnlimitedRecursion value when it is false so golden files stay unchanged.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a new instance with new attribute ids but keeps duplicated attributes on the same id so column resolution still works; with the LEGACY_CTE_DUPLICATE_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES config it assigns fully new attributes instead.

nodes.name: WithCTE
nodes.summary: Case class logical node that is the resolved version of UnresolvedWith. It holds the main plan and the CTERelationDef definitions, and references are linked to definitions by unique ids instead of aliases. Its children are the cteDefs followed by the plan, its output, maxRows and maxRowsPerPartition come from the plan, and withNewPlan replaces only the main plan.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the node from new children, treating the last child as the plan and the earlier ones as CTE definitions.

nodes.name: withNewPlan
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the node whose main plan is replaced by the given plan while the CTE definitions are kept.

nodes.name: CTEInChildren
nodes.summary: Trait for logical nodes that place the WithCTE node on each of their children. Its withCTEDefs method wraps every child in a WithCTE with the given definitions.

nodes.name: withCTEDefs
nodes.summary: Wraps every child of the node in a WithCTE carrying the given CTE definitions and returns the node with the new children.

nodes.name: UnresolvedWith
nodes.summary: Case class unary node produced for a WITH clause. It holds the final query as child, a sequence of (alias, SubqueryAlias, optional int) CTE relations and an allowRecursion flag. It is removed during analysis and the relations are substituted into the child. It prints a short 'CTE [aliases]' line and exposes the CTE subquery aliases as inner children.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Builds the short plan description 'CTE [alias1, alias2]' with the aliases truncated to maxFields.

nodes.name: hints.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the hint model of the logical plan layer: UnresolvedHint and ResolvedHint plan nodes, JoinHint and HintInfo to carry hints on a join, the JoinStrategyHint hierarchy (BROADCAST, SHUFFLE_MERGE, SHUFFLE_HASH, SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL plus internal NO_BROADCAST_HASH, PREFER_SHUFFLE_HASH, NO_BROADCAST_AND_REPLICATION), empty AggregateHint, WindowHint and SortHint marker classes, and the HintErrorHandler callback trait.

nodes.name: UnresolvedHint
nodes.summary: Case class unary node generated by the parser for a general hint (name and parameter expressions) on a child plan that is not yet resolved. It reports itself as resolved when its child is, so analysis can continue, and it is eliminated after analysis once the analyzer has converted it into a ResolvedHint.

nodes.name: ResolvedHint
nodes.summary: Case class unary node that holds a HintInfo for its child. The analyzer converts every UnresolvedHint into it, and it is eliminated before optimization starts. Its output equals the child output and its canonical form is the canonicalized child.

nodes.name: JoinHint
nodes.summary: Case class (with companion object holding the NONE constant) that carries the optional HintInfo for the left child and for the right child of a Join. isEmpty is true when neither side has a hint and toString prints the present sides as leftHint=... and rightHint=....

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Prints the left and right hints that are defined as 'leftHint=...' and 'rightHint=...' joined by a comma.

nodes.name: HintInfo
nodes.summary: Case class holding the hint attributes applied on a specific node, currently the preferred join strategy as an optional JoinStrategyHint. merge combines it with another HintInfo, keeping its own strategy if defined and otherwise the other one, and calls hintOverridden on the HintErrorHandler when both define different strategies.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges this HintInfo with another one: this strategy wins when defined, otherwise the other strategy is used, and the error handler is notified through hintOverridden when both strategies are set and differ.

nodes.name: JoinStrategyHint
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class (with companion object) for join strategy hints. Each hint gives a displayName and a set of hintAliases, and toString returns the display name. The object lists the user-facing strategies BROADCAST, SHUFFLE_MERGE, SHUFFLE_HASH and SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL in a set called strategies. When hints on both sides of a join contradict each other, the priority is BROADCAST over SHUFFLE_MERGE over SHUFFLE_HASH over SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL.

nodes.name: BROADCAST
nodes.summary: Case object for the hint requesting a broadcast hash join or broadcast nested loop join, depending on whether equi-join keys exist. Display name is broadcast; aliases are BROADCAST, BROADCASTJOIN and MAPJOIN.

nodes.name: SHUFFLE_MERGE
nodes.summary: Case object for the hint requesting a shuffle sort merge join. Display name is merge; aliases are SHUFFLE_MERGE, MERGE and MERGEJOIN.

nodes.name: SHUFFLE_HASH
nodes.summary: Case object for the hint requesting a shuffle hash join. Display name is shuffle_hash; the only alias is SHUFFLE_HASH.

nodes.name: SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL
nodes.summary: Case object for the hint requesting a shuffle-and-replicate nested loop join (cartesian product join). Display name is shuffle_replicate_nl; the only alias is SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL.

nodes.name: NO_BROADCAST_HASH
nodes.summary: Case object for an internal hint, used by adaptive query execution, to discourage broadcast hash join. Display name is no_broadcast_hash and it has no user aliases.

nodes.name: PREFER_SHUFFLE_HASH
nodes.summary: Case object for an internal hint, used by adaptive query execution, to encourage shuffle hash join. Display name is prefer_shuffle_hash and it has no user aliases.

nodes.name: NO_BROADCAST_AND_REPLICATION
nodes.summary: Case object for an internal hint that prohibits broadcasting and replicating one side of a join, used by rules where that is not permitted, such as the cardinality check in MERGE operations. Display name is no_broadcast_and_replication and it has no user aliases.

nodes.name: AggregateHint
nodes.summary: Empty abstract marker class for hints that apply to aggregates. It declares no members in this file.

nodes.name: WindowHint
nodes.summary: Empty abstract marker class for hints that apply to window operations. It declares no members in this file.

nodes.name: SortHint
nodes.summary: Empty abstract marker class for hints that apply to sorts. It declares no members in this file.

nodes.name: HintErrorHandler
nodes.summary: Trait of callbacks for customized handling of hint problems. It has methods for an unrecognized hint (hintNotRecognized), relation names in a hint that match no relation in scope (hintRelationsNotFound), a join hint on a relation that is not part of a join (joinNotFoundForJoinHint), a join hint on a join that does not support the build side or lacks equi-join keys (joinHintNotSupported), and a hint overridden by a conflicting one (hintOverridden).

nodes.name: PlanHelper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the PlanHelper object, a small shared utility for the Analyzer and Optimizer that finds expressions hosted by the wrong kind of logical operator (for example an aggregate function in a Filter).

nodes.name: PlanHelper
nodes.summary: Utility object with specialExpressionsInUnsupportedOperator, which returns the window expressions, aggregate expressions and generators that an operator hosts although it is not a Window, Aggregate/Window/CollectMetrics/LateralJoin, or Generate/BaseEvalPythonUDTF. It is used when user input contains such expressions (the doc gives a WHERE max(c1) > 0 example) or when a rewrite produces an invalid plan.

nodes.name: specialExpressionsInUnsupportedOperator
nodes.summary: Collects, over every expression tree of the plan, WindowExpression nodes when the plan is not a Window, AggregateExpression nodes when the plan is not an Aggregate, Window, CollectMetrics or an aggregate-free LateralJoin, and Generator nodes when the plan is neither Generate nor BaseEvalPythonUDTF. Returns the offending expressions.

nodes.name: onlyInLateralSubquery
nodes.summary: Private check that is true when the plan is a LateralJoin and neither its join condition nor the right side's join condition contains an aggregate expression.

nodes.name: QueryPlanConstraints.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the QueryPlanConstraints trait that gives logical operators a lazily computed `constraints` set, and the ConstraintHelper trait with the logic that infers extra equality constraints and IsNotNull constraints from an existing constraint set.

nodes.name: QueryPlanConstraints
nodes.summary: Trait mixed into LogicalPlan (self type LogicalPlan, extends ConstraintHelper). Its lazy val constraints returns an ExpressionSet of invariants about the rows an operator outputs: validConstraints (overridable by operators, empty by default) united with inferAdditionalConstraints and constructIsNotNullConstraints, filtered to deterministic constraints whose references are non-empty and a subset of the output. It returns an empty set when conf.constraintPropagationEnabled is false.

nodes.name: ConstraintHelper
nodes.summary: Trait holding the constraint inference rules. inferAdditionalConstraints derives new equalities from equality constraints (a = 5 and a = b give b = 5, also through a Cast of an attribute), constructIsNotNullConstraints derives isNotNull constraints from null-intolerant expressions and from non-nullable output attributes, and private helpers walk the expression trees (including struct and array-struct field extraction).

nodes.name: inferAdditionalConstraints
nodes.summary: Takes the non-IsNotNull equality predicates and, for each EqualTo between two attributes (or an attribute and a Cast of an attribute), substitutes one side for the other in the remaining constraints. Returns only the newly inferred constraints, not those already present.

nodes.name: replaceConstraints
nodes.summary: Private helper that rewrites every constraint by replacing sub-expressions semantically equal to `source` with `destination`.

nodes.name: constructIsNotNullConstraints
nodes.summary: Builds IsNotNull constraints: first from the null-intolerant attributes found in the given constraints, then for every non-nullable attribute of the operator output. Returns only those not already in the input set.

nodes.name: inferIsNotNullConstraints
nodes.summary: Private helper that maps a constraint to IsNotNull constraints on the attributes reachable through null-intolerant expressions, treating a root IsNotNull specially by looking only at its child.

nodes.name: isExtractOnly
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive private predicate that is true when an expression is an Attribute reached only through GetStructField or GetArrayStructFields nodes.

nodes.name: scanNullIntolerantAttribute
nodes.summary: Recursively walks null-intolerant expressions and returns the attributes, and the extract-only ExtractValue expressions for nested types, that they contain.

nodes.name: ScriptTransformation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ScriptTransformation logical operator, which pipes its child's rows through an external script, and the ScriptInputOutputSchema case class describing how rows are formatted when sent to and read from the script.

nodes.name: ScriptTransformation
nodes.summary: Unary logical operator holding the script command string, the output attributes produced by the script, the child plan and a ScriptInputOutputSchema. It extends UnaryNode with ReferenceAllColumns (so it needs all child columns) and implements withNewChildInternal via copy. BasicStatsPlanVisitor.visitScriptTransform uses the default estimate for it.

nodes.name: ScriptInputOutputSchema
nodes.summary: Case class with the input and output properties used when passing data to a script: input and output row formats, input and output SerDe classes and properties, record reader and writer classes, and a schemaLess flag. The doc comment says that in Hive this would specify which SerDes to use.

nodes.name: SequentialStreamingUnion.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SequentialStreamingUnion logical node, a marker that unions streaming children one after another (backfill then live) instead of concurrently, together with its companion helpers.

nodes.name: SequentialStreamingUnion
nodes.summary: Case class (children, byName, allowMissingCol) extending UnionBase that processes each streaming child to completion before the next, so child order is significant. It is only a logical placeholder: the streaming execution engine matches it during physical planning and creates sequential steps instead of a physical operator. It requires at least 2 children, is resolved only when column resolution is by position, and asserts allowMissingCol implies byName. Its tree pattern is SEQUENTIAL_STREAMING_UNION. The companion adds apply(left, right) and flatten.

nodes.name: flatten
nodes.summary: Companion helper that recursively replaces direct SequentialStreamingUnion children by their own children, so chained followedBy calls collapse into one node.
