Unions nested under other operators are not flattened. The companion's two-plan apply (lines 109 to 111) builds a union by position with byName and allowMissingCol false.

nodes.name: StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan mixin trait for source logical nodes that need to carry the stream they read from.

nodes.name: StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan
nodes.summary: Trait extending LogicalPlan for logical nodes that can be leaf nodes of Source.getBatch(). withStream(stream) is called by Spark to set the stream and should return a copy of the node with it set; getStream returns the associated stream as an Option. The stream type is SparkDataStream.

nodes.name: Statistics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the statistics model of logical plans: Statistics (size, row count, per-column stats), ColumnStat, the equi-height Histogram with its bins, and HistogramSerializer for turning a histogram into a compact string.

nodes.name: Statistics
nodes.summary: Case class with sizeInBytes (BigInt), optional rowCount, attributeStats (an AttributeMap of ColumnStat) and an isRuntime flag set when the numbers come from adaptive query execution stage statistics. BigInt is used because cardinality estimates such as cartesian joins can overflow 64 bits. simpleString prints size and the row count in scientific notation. The companion object defines DUMMY with Long.MaxValue size.

nodes.name: ColumnStat
nodes.summary: Case class of statistics for one column: distinctCount, min, max, nullCount, avgLen, maxLen, an optional Histogram and a version defaulting to CatalogColumnStat.VERSION. min and max hold the internal Catalyst representation. It exposes hasCountStats, hasMinMaxStats and hasLenStats, converts to a CatalogColumnStat with toCatalogColumnStat, and rescales counts with updateCountStats.

nodes.name: Histogram
nodes.summary: Case class implementing an equi-height histogram: a height (rows per bin) and an array of HistogramBin. It overrides equals and hashCode so arrays of bins compare by content.

nodes.name: HistogramBin
nodes.summary: Case class for one histogram bin: lower bound lo, upper bound hi (both Double) and an approximate distinct value count ndv.

nodes.name: HistogramSerializer
nodes.summary: Object with serialize and deserialize that convert a Histogram to and from a Base64 string. The binary form is written through an LZ4 block stream, with all lo values, then all hi values, then all ndv values grouped together for better compression. The doc says such advanced statistics are not made human readable in the metastore's string properties.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Builds the readable text used by toString: the size in bytes formatted with Utils.bytesToString, followed by the row count in 3-digit scientific notation when it is defined.

nodes.name: toCatalogColumnStat
nodes.summary: Converts this ColumnStat to a CatalogColumnStat for storage in the catalog, turning min and max into external strings with CatalogColumnStat.toExternalString using the column name and data type.

nodes.name: updateCountStats
nodes.summary: Returns a ColumnStat (this one or a supplied updated one) whose distinctCount and nullCount are rescaled from the old row count to the new row count through EstimationUtils.updateStat.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Writes the histogram height, bin count and the lo, hi and ndv columns to an LZ4-compressed data stream, terminates with -1, and returns the bytes as a Base64 string.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Decodes a Base64 string through an LZ4 block input stream, reads height, bin count and the lo, hi and ndv arrays, and rebuilds a Histogram of HistogramBin objects.

nodes.name: SqlScriptingLogicalPlans.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical operators produced when parsing a SQL script: statements, compound bodies (BEGIN END blocks), IF, CASE, WHILE, REPEAT, LOOP, FOR, LEAVE and ITERATE control flow, error conditions and exception handlers. They are consumed by the SQL Scripting interpreter to generate execution nodes.

nodes.name: CompoundPlanStatement
nodes.summary: Sealed trait extending LogicalPlan that is the common parent of all SQL Scripting logical operators created by the parsing phase.

nodes.name: SingleStatement
nodes.summary: Wraps the parsed logical plan of one SQL statement to be executed against Spark. It takes its origin from CurrentOrigin, reports the output and children of the parsed plan, and getText returns the original SQL text slice between the origin's start and stop index.

nodes.name: CompoundBody
nodes.summary: Logical operator (a Command and a CompoundPlanStatement) for a compound body holding its statements, an optional label (a UUID when set by the system), an isScope flag for labeled scopes that group local variables and handlers, the ExceptionHandler list and a map of declared error conditions. Its children are the contained statements.

nodes.name: IfElseStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for IF / ELSEIF / ELSE: parallel lists of condition SingleStatements and CompoundBody branches plus an optional else body. Children are conditions, bodies and the else body, and withNewChildrenInternal rebuilds the else body from a trailing extra body.

nodes.name: WhileStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for WHILE with a condition SingleStatement, a CompoundBody and an optional label that LEAVE or ITERATE can target. The body runs as long as the condition is true.

nodes.name: RepeatStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for REPEAT with a condition SingleStatement, a CompoundBody and an optional label. The body runs once and then repeats while the condition is false.

nodes.name: LeaveStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for LEAVE with the label of the compound or loop to leave; execution continues after that body or loop.

nodes.name: IterateStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for ITERATE with the label of a loop; the rest of the loop body is skipped and the next iteration starts. It is only valid for loops.

nodes.name: SearchedCaseStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for the searched CASE statement (CASE WHEN condition THEN ...): condition SingleStatements, their CompoundBody branches and an optional else body. Same children layout as IfElseStatement.

nodes.name: SimpleCaseStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for the simple CASE statement (CASE x WHEN 1 THEN ...): a case variable expression, the WHEN condition expressions, their CompoundBody branches and an optional else body. Only the bodies are children; the expressions are kept as fields.

nodes.name: LoopStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for LOOP with a CompoundBody and an optional label; the body runs until a LEAVE statement ends it.

nodes.name: ForStatement
nodes.summary: Logical operator for FOR: a query SingleStatement run once, an optional variable name that exposes the current row, a CompoundBody run for each result row and an optional label.

nodes.name: ErrorCondition
nodes.summary: Logical operator declaring a named error condition together with its SQLSTATE or error code.

nodes.name: ExceptionHandlerType
nodes.summary: Enumeration of handler kinds, EXIT and CONTINUE, plus the ExceptionHandlerType type alias used by ExceptionHandler.

nodes.name: ExceptionHandlerTriggers
nodes.summary: Mutable class that records what triggers a handler: sets of SQLSTATEs and condition names, and flags for SQLEXCEPTION and NOT FOUND. Its addUnique methods throw a SqlScriptingErrors error when the same trigger is declared twice, and upper-case SQLSTATE and condition names first.

nodes.name: ExceptionHandler
nodes.summary: Logical operator for a handler declaration with its ExceptionHandlerTriggers, a CompoundBody to run and a handler type (CONTINUE or EXIT). Its only child is the body.

nodes.name: getText
nodes.summary: Returns the SQL text of this statement by slicing origin.sqlText from startIndex to stopIndex plus one; it asserts that all three origin values are defined.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the IF/ELSE node from a new children sequence by splitting it into SingleStatement conditions and CompoundBody bodies; when there is one more body than conditions the last body becomes the else body.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the searched CASE node from a new children sequence, using the same split into conditions, bodies and an optional trailing else body as IfElseStatement.

nodes.name: addUniqueSqlException
nodes.summary: Sets the SQLEXCEPTION flag, throwing duplicateConditionInHandlerDeclaration if it was already set.

nodes.name: addUniqueNotFound
nodes.summary: Sets the NOT FOUND flag, throwing duplicateConditionInHandlerDeclaration if it was already set.

nodes.name: addUniqueCondition
nodes.summary: Upper-cases a condition name and adds it to the condition set, throwing duplicateConditionInHandlerDeclaration if it is already present.

nodes.name: addUniqueSqlState
nodes.summary: Upper-cases a SQLSTATE and adds it to the SQLSTATE set, throwing duplicateSqlStateInHandlerDeclaration if it is already present.

nodes.name: object.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical operators and factory objects that support typed Dataset operations on domain objects: serializing and deserializing rows to objects, map-partitions, map-elements, typed filter, appended columns, grouped map, stateful group operators, R function operators, cogroup, and the typed joinWith rewrite.

nodes.name: CatalystSerde
nodes.summary: Object with helpers that wrap a plan in object conversion: deserialize puts a DeserializeToObject over a child using an Encoder's deserializer (as an UnresolvedDeserializer), serialize puts a SerializeFromObject using the encoder's named expressions, and generateObjAttr creates the single `obj` attribute whose type comes from the encoder and which is nullable unless the class is primitive.

nodes.name: ObjectProducer
nodes.summary: Trait for logical operators whose output is one object field. It requires outputObjAttr, makes that the only output attribute and the produced attribute.

nodes.name: ObjectConsumer
nodes.summary: Trait for unary operators that consume a child whose output is a single object column; it asserts the child output length is 1 and exposes inputObjAttr. It also references all child columns.

nodes.name: DeserializeToObject
nodes.summary: Unary operator that turns each input row from the child into an object with a deserializer expression and outputs it in outputObjAttr. Its tree pattern is DESERIALIZE_TO_OBJECT.

nodes.name: SerializeFromObject
nodes.summary: Object consumer that turns the object produced by the child back into rows with serializer named expressions; its output is the serializer attributes. Its tree pattern is SERIALIZE_FROM_OBJECT.

nodes.name: MapPartitions
nodes.summary: Operator (object consumer and producer) that applies a function from Iterator[Any] to Iterator[Any] to each partition of the child. The companion apply wraps the operator between a deserialize and a serialize step using the type's Encoders.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsInR
nodes.summary: Operator that applies a serialized R function (function bytes, package names, broadcast variables, input and output schema) to each partition of the child, as an object consumer and producer. The companion apply picks MapPartitionsInRWithArrow when SQLConf.get.arrowSparkREnabled is true, otherwise it wraps this operator in deserialize and serialize steps.

nodes.name: MapPartitionsInRWithArrow
nodes.summary: Unary operator like MapPartitionsInR that sends input and output in Arrow format. It always references all child columns, produces its own output attributes and compares itself in the doc comment to ArrowEvalPython.

nodes.name: MapElements
nodes.summary: Operator that applies a function to each element of the child, recording the argument class and schema. The companion apply wraps it between deserialize and serialize using the Encoders of T and U.

nodes.name: TypedFilter
nodes.summary: Unary operator that keeps the elements for which a function returns true. It is logically a Filter whose condition decodes the row and calls the function, kept as its own node to make optimizer rules easier. withObjectProducerChild builds that Filter over an object-producing child, and typedCondition builds the Invoke expression (FilterFunction.call or Function1 apply). Its tree pattern is TYPED_FILTER.

nodes.name: FunctionUtils
nodes.summary: Object that chooses the method name to call on a Scala Function1: the specialized apply$mc..$sp method when input and output types are among Int, Long, Float, Double (output also Boolean), otherwise plain apply.

nodes.name: AppendColumns
nodes.summary: Unary operator that applies a function to each element and appends the result columns (serializer) after the child's output. Its factory apply has three overloads (lines 319 to 329 with Encoders, 331 to 342 with input attributes, 344 to 358 private[sql] with ExpressionEncoders); the node id covers them under the widest one. Its tree pattern is APPEND_COLUMNS.

nodes.name: AppendColumnsWithObject
nodes.summary: Optimized form of AppendColumns that runs directly on deserialized objects; it holds the child serializer and the new columns serializer, and its output is their combined attributes.

nodes.name: MapGroups
nodes.summary: Operator that applies a function to each group of the child, giving it the grouping key object and an iterator of the group's rows as objects, optionally sorted by dataOrder. The companion apply builds it with key and value UnresolvedDeserializers and wraps it in serialize; sortOrder turns expressions into SortOrder values (Ascending by default).

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsWithState
nodes.summary: Binary operator (child plus initialState) for stateful per-group processing, with a state encoder, output mode, timeout, a flag for mapGroupsWithState and optional initial state. Two companion apply overloads (lines 453 to 482 without initial state, 484 to 515 with it) build the node with an empty LocalRelation or the given initial state; the node id is described by the widest one. When created for mapGroupsWithState it asserts OutputMode.Update.

nodes.name: TransformWithState
nodes.summary: Binary operator (child plus initialState) that applies a StatefulProcessor per group key with a TimeMode and OutputMode, a key encoder and optional initial state. The companion has two apply overloads (lines 573 to 601 without initial state, 604 to 633 with it); the node id uses the widest one.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInR
nodes.summary: Unary object-producing operator that applies a serialized R function to each group of the child, with key and value deserializers. The companion apply chooses FlatMapGroupsInRWithArrow when SQLConf.get.arrowSparkREnabled is set, otherwise wraps this node in serialize.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInRWithArrow
nodes.summary: Unary operator like FlatMapGroupsInR that exchanges data in Arrow format; it always needs all child columns and produces its own output attributes. The doc comment calls it somewhat similar to FlatMapGroupsInPandas.

nodes.name: CoGroup
nodes.summary: Binary operator that applies a function to each grouping key and the associated values from the left and right children, with per-side group attributes, data attributes and sort orders. The companion apply requires equal group schemas on both sides and resolves the key deserializer from the left group.

nodes.name: JoinWith
nodes.summary: Object holding the typed joinWith logic: resolveSelfJoinCondition and typedJoinWith. A TODO in the source (SPARK-44225) says it should move into the analyzer.

nodes.name: deserialize
nodes.summary: Creates a DeserializeToObject over the child using an UnresolvedDeserializer of the encoder's deserializer and a generated object attribute.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Creates a SerializeFromObject over the child using the encoder's named expressions as serializer.

nodes.name: generateObjAttr
nodes.summary: Builds the AttributeReference named obj whose data type is the encoder deserializer's type, nullable unless the class is a primitive.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Wraps the child in CatalystSerde.deserialize, a MapPartitions node and CatalystSerde.serialize for the given function and Encoders.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that returns MapPartitionsInRWithArrow when arrowSparkREnabled is true, otherwise a MapPartitionsInR wrapped between deserialize and serialize steps with an ExpressionEncoder of the output schema.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Wraps the child in deserialize, a MapElements node (with the argument class and schema from the input Encoder) and serialize.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds a TypedFilter from the function, the input Encoder's class and schema, and an UnresolvedDeserializer of its deserializer.

nodes.name: withObjectProducerChild
nodes.summary: Asserts the given plan has one output column and returns a regular Filter over it whose condition is typedCondition of that column.

nodes.name: typedCondition
nodes.summary: Creates the boolean Invoke expression that calls the filter function on the input: FilterFunction.call for a FilterFunction, otherwise the Function1 method chosen by FunctionUtils.getFunctionOneName.

nodes.name: getMethodType
nodes.summary: Private mapping from Int, Long, Float, Double and (for outputs) Boolean data types to the JVM specialization letters I, J, F, D and Z.

nodes.name: getFunctionOneName
nodes.summary: Returns the Function1 class and the method name, either apply$mc<out><in>$sp when both types have a specialization or apply.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Widest of three factory overloads: builds an AppendColumns from a function, input and output ExpressionEncoders, a child and optional input attributes. The other two overloads take implicit Encoders, one of them with input attributes.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds a MapGroups node with key and value UnresolvedDeserializers and a generated output attribute, then wraps it in CatalystSerde.serialize.

nodes.name: sortOrder
nodes.summary: Maps sort expressions to SortOrder, keeping existing SortOrder values and giving other expressions ascending order.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Widest of two factory overloads: builds FlatMapGroupsWithState with hasInitialState true, given initial state attributes, deserializer and plan, and serializes the result. The other overload (lines 453 to 482) uses an empty LocalRelation as initial state.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Widest of two factory overloads: builds TransformWithState with hasInitialState true and the initial state plan. The other overload (lines 573 to 601) uses an empty LocalRelation initial state.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory that returns FlatMapGroupsInRWithArrow when arrowSparkREnabled is true, otherwise a FlatMapGroupsInR wrapped in serialize with an ExpressionEncoder of the schema.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Requires equal group schemas, builds a CoGroup node with key, left and right UnresolvedDeserializers and a generated output attribute, then wraps it in serialize.

nodes.name: resolveSelfJoinCondition
nodes.summary: Rewrites trivially true EqualTo and EqualNullSafe conditions between the same attribute reference so each side is resolved against the left and right child by name, throwing an unresolved column error if not found.

nodes.name: typedJoinWith
nodes.summary: Builds the plan for joinWith: rejects LeftSemi and LeftAnti, optionally resolves self-join conditions, aliases each side as _1 and _2 (as a struct when the side is flattenable to a row). Inner joins project the two aliases over the join; outer joins project each side first and rewrite the condition to GetStructField accesses.

nodes.name: statements.scala
nodes.summary: Defines base types for logical plans that hold exactly what the SQL parser produced (ParsedStatement and its leaf and unary forms), plus the SerdeInfo and FormatClasses helpers, the QualifiedColType column description, the InsertIntoStatement, and the InsertReplaceCriteria classes.

nodes.name: ParsedStatement
nodes.summary: Abstract logical plan (with CTEInChildren) that keeps what was parsed from SQL so one parsed node can later be converted into several implementations, for example CREATE TABLE for v1 and v2. It redacts Map arguments through conf.redactOptions when printed, has empty output and is never resolved.

nodes.name: LeafParsedStatement
nodes.summary: Trait for parsed statements with no children, combining ParsedStatement with LeafLike.

nodes.name: UnaryParsedStatement
nodes.summary: Trait for parsed statements with one child, combining ParsedStatement with UnaryLike.

nodes.name: SerdeInfo
nodes.summary: Case class for Hive serde information: storedAs, formatClasses, serde and serdeProperties. It asserts that STORED AS and INPUTFORMAT/OUTPUTFORMAT are not both given, describe renders the clauses, and merge combines two infos, failing on conflicting values. The companion object (lines 114 to 124) has the empty instance and checkSerdePropMerging.

nodes.name: FormatClasses
nodes.summary: Case class with input and output format class names; toString prints INPUTFORMAT ... OUTPUTFORMAT ....

nodes.name: QualifiedColType
nodes.summary: Unevaluable expression carrying column data as parsed by ALTER TABLE ADD or REPLACE COLUMNS: optional path, name, type, nullability, comment, position and default value. It is resolved when path, position and default are, gives the full name, can build a v2 default via getV2Default, and reports whether the default value's type was coerced to the column type.

nodes.name: InsertIntoStatement
nodes.summary: Unary parsed statement for INSERT INTO or OVERWRITE with table, partition spec, user-specified columns, query, overwrite, IF NOT EXISTS, byName, an optional InsertReplaceCriteria and a schema-evolution flag. Several require checks reject invalid combinations. It extends TransactionalWrite so QueryExecution can detect a transaction before analysis, and getDefaultTreePatternBits adds the table's pattern bits since the table is not a child.

nodes.name: InsertReplaceCriteria
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract unevaluable expression, non-nullable, whose dataType throws UnresolvedException; parent of the INSERT REPLACE matching criteria.

nodes.name: InsertReplaceUsing
nodes.summary: Replace criteria matching rows by equality on the listed column names, which must exist in both table and query.

nodes.name: InsertReplaceOn
nodes.summary: Replace criteria matching rows by a boolean condition expression, with an optional table alias; the condition is its only child.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Builds the SQL-like description: STORED AS with the format or format classes, followed by ROW FORMAT SERDE or DELIMITED when a serde or serde properties exist.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges two SerdeInfo values field by field; a field set on both sides must be equal or an assertion fails, and serde properties are merged after checking for key conflicts.

nodes.name: checkSerdePropMerging
nodes.summary: Companion method that throws cannotSafelyMergeSerdePropertiesError when two property maps share keys.

nodes.name: getV2Default
nodes.summary: Converts the optional default value to a v2 ColumnDefaultValue using the statement text and column name, or null if there is no default.

nodes.name: isDefaultValueTypeCoerced
nodes.summary: True when there is no default or the default's data type matches the column data type according to ColumnDefinition.isDefaultValueTypeMatched.

nodes.name: getDefaultTreePatternBits
nodes.summary: Extends the default tree-pattern bits with those of `table`, so pattern pruning sees patterns such as PARAMETER or PLAN_WITH_UNRESOLVED_IDENTIFIER that live in the non-child table plan.

nodes.name: AggregateEstimation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines AggregateEstimation, which estimates the output statistics of an Aggregate from the distinct counts of its group-by columns.

nodes.name: AggregateEstimation
nodes.summary: Object used by BasicStatsPlanVisitor.visitAggregate. Its estimate method returns Statistics when the child has a row count and count stats for every group-by column, and None otherwise so the caller can fall back.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Multiplies the distinct counts of the group-by attributes (adding 1 when a column has nulls) as an upper bound, uses 1 row when there are no grouping expressions, otherwise caps by the child's row count. It computes alias stats, the output attribute stats and the output size, and returns Statistics with rowCount.

nodes.name: BasicStatsPlanVisitor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BasicStatsPlanVisitor, the LogicalPlanVisitor that computes Statistics for the cost-based optimizer by delegating to per-operator estimators and falling back to the size-only visitor.

nodes.name: BasicStatsPlanVisitor
nodes.summary: Object implementing LogicalPlanVisitor[Statistics]. It uses AggregateEstimation, FilterEstimation, JoinEstimation, ProjectEstimation and UnionEstimation for those operators, an inline rule for Distinct and Intersect, and the default product-of-children estimate for Generate, Pivot and ScriptTransformation. Except, Expand, limits, Offset, repartition operators, Sample, Window, Sort, Tail and WithCTE fall back to SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor through the private fallback helper.

nodes.name: default
nodes.summary: Leaf nodes use computeStats. For other plans the row count and size are the products of the children's positive values, with row count None when any child lacks one.

nodes.name: visitAggregate
nodes.summary: Uses AggregateEstimation.estimate and falls back to the size-only estimate when it returns None.

nodes.name: visitDistinct
nodes.summary: Estimates Distinct as an Aggregate that groups by and outputs all child output attributes.

nodes.name: visitFilter
nodes.summary: Uses FilterEstimation(p).estimate with a fallback to the size-only estimate.

nodes.name: visitIntersect
nodes.summary: Takes the statistics (size and row count) of the smaller of the two children as the estimate.

nodes.name: visitJoin
nodes.summary: Uses JoinEstimation(p).estimate with a fallback to the size-only estimate.

nodes.name: visitProject
nodes.summary: Uses ProjectEstimation.estimate with a fallback to the size-only estimate.

nodes.name: visitUnion
nodes.summary: Uses UnionEstimation.estimate with a fallback to the size-only estimate.

nodes.name: EstimationUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EstimationUtils object: shared helpers for statistics estimation, covering row count and column stat checks, output size computation, double conversion of min/max values, and equi-height histogram range and overlap calculations. Used by the filter, join, project, union and size-only estimators.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object of pure helper functions plus one nested case class (OverlappedRange).

nodes.name: EstimationUtils
nodes.summary: Utility object that holds the helpers used by the statistics estimators: existence checks for row counts and column stats, null column stats, scaling of stats when rows shrink, per-row and total output size, Double conversion of min/max values, and histogram bin and overlap math. Called by FilterEstimation, JoinEstimation, ProjectEstimation, UnionEstimation, ValueInterval and the size-only visitor.

nodes.name: OverlappedRange
nodes.summary: Case class describing one overlapped range produced when two equi-height histograms are joined: lower and higher bound, the NDV on each side and the number of rows on each side. Returned by getOverlappedRanges and consumed by the histogram-based join estimate.

nodes.name: rowCountsExist
nodes.summary: Returns true when every given logical plan has a rowCount in its statistics.

nodes.name: columnStatsExist
nodes.summary: Returns true when every (Statistics, Attribute) pair has a column stat for that attribute.

nodes.name: columnStatsWithCountsExist
nodes.summary: Returns true when every (Statistics, Attribute) pair has a column stat that contains distinct and null counts (hasCountStats).

nodes.name: nullColumnStat
nodes.summary: Builds the ColumnStat for a column that holds only NULLs: distinct count 0, no min or max, null count equal to the row count, and average and maximum length set from the type's default size.

nodes.name: updateStat
nodes.summary: Scales down a statistic (such as the number of distinct values) in proportion to the drop in row count after an operation such as filter or join; otherwise returns the updated value unchanged. No scaling is done when the statistic is already 1 or lower.

nodes.name: ceil
nodes.summary: Rounds a BigDecimal up to the next BigInt using CEILING rounding.

nodes.name: getOutputMap
nodes.summary: Selects, from an input map of column stats, the entries for the given output attributes.

nodes.name: getAliasStats
nodes.summary: Returns column stats for aliases in a projection: an alias of a known attribute reuses that attribute's stat, and an alias of a foldable deterministic expression gets a stat derived from the evaluated constant (single value, or all nulls when the value is null).

nodes.name: getSizePerRow
nodes.summary: Estimates the size in bytes of one row as a fixed 8 byte overhead plus, per attribute, the average length from the column stat (with extra bytes for strings) or the data type's default size.

nodes.name: getOutputSize
nodes.summary: Computes output size in bytes as row count times size per row, and returns 1 when the row count is not positive so that sizes of binary nodes never become zero.

nodes.name: toDouble
nodes.summary: Converts a numeric, date, timestamp or boolean min/max value to Double so that range logic can use a single number type; boolean maps to 0 or 1.

nodes.name: fromDouble
nodes.summary: Converts a Double back to the value representation of a given data type (boolean, date, timestamp, integral, floating or decimal); inverse of toDouble.

nodes.name: findFirstBinForValue
nodes.summary: Returns the index of the first histogram bin whose upper bound is not below the value, for an equi-height histogram.

nodes.name: findLastBinForValue
nodes.summary: Returns the index of the last histogram bin whose lower bound is not above the value, for an equi-height histogram.

nodes.name: binHoldingRangePossibility
nodes.summary: Returns the fraction of one histogram bin that falls in a [lowerBound, upperBound] range: 1.0 for a single-value bin, 1/NDV for a single-point range, otherwise the prorated share of the bin width.

nodes.name: numBinsHoldingRange
nodes.summary: Returns the (fractional) number of histogram bins holding values within a range, honoring inclusive or exclusive bounds. It sums the partial lower bin, the partial upper bin and the bins between; used by filter selectivity on histograms.

nodes.name: getOverlappedRanges
nodes.summary: Finds the overlapped ranges between the bins of two histograms inside a value range. It trims each pair of bins and, for each of four overlap cases, produces an OverlappedRange with the NDV and rows contributed by each side; used by the histogram-based join estimate.

nodes.name: trimBin
nodes.summary: Trims a histogram bin to a given value range and returns the trimmed bin together with its scaled row count, prorating NDV and height by the remaining width (a single-value result gets NDV 1).

nodes.name: FilterEstimation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FilterEstimation, which estimates statistics (row count, size in bytes and column stats) after a Filter plan node from the selectivity of its condition, and ColumnStatsMap, the helper that tracks column stats updated while the conditions are applied. Used when a Filter node needs estimated statistics.

nodes.name: FilterEstimation
nodes.summary: Case class built from a Filter plan node. Its estimate method computes the filter selectivity of the condition (AND, OR and NOT are decomposed; comparisons of a column against a literal, IN, InSet, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL and column versus column comparisons are evaluated from min, max, NDV, null counts and histograms), then derives the filtered row count, size and updated column stats. Unsupported conditions count as selectivity 1.0.

nodes.name: ColumnStatsMap
nodes.summary: Case class that holds the original column stats of the child plan together with an updatedMap of the latest stats. Stats are updated after each applied predicate (for example c > 40 AND c <= 50 narrows the range step by step), read back through get, apply and the has*Stats checks, and finally scaled by outputColumnStats when the row count drops.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Returns the Statistics of the filtered plan or None when the child has no row count. It gets the selectivity of the condition (default 1.0), computes the filtered row count and updated column stats, and takes the smaller of the size from output attributes and the size scaled from the child.

nodes.name: calculateFilterSelectivity
nodes.summary: Recursively estimates the selectivity of a compound condition: AND multiplies, OR uses p1 + p2 - p1*p2, NOT is pushed down through AND and OR, double NOT is collapsed, and other nodes go to calculateSingleCondition. Stats are updated only along AND branches.

nodes.name: calculateSingleCondition
nodes.summary: Pattern matches a single predicate (literal, equality, <, <=, >, >=, In, InSet, IsNull, IsNotNull, or two-column comparison), normalizes literal-on-the-left forms and dispatches to the matching evaluate method; anything else is logged as unsupported and returns None.

nodes.name: evaluateNullCheck
nodes.summary: Estimates the fraction of rows matching IS NULL or IS NOT NULL from the column's null count and the row count, and optionally updates the column stat (no distinct values for IS NULL, zero nulls for IS NOT NULL).

nodes.name: evaluateBinary
nodes.summary: Estimates a column-versus-literal comparison. Numeric, date, timestamp and boolean columns go to evaluateBinaryForNumeric; string and binary columns are not supported and give None.

nodes.name: evaluateEquality
nodes.summary: Estimates an equality predicate on a column and literal: 0.0 when the literal is outside [min, max], histogram-based when a histogram exists, else 1/NDV; then optionally sets the column stat to a single distinct value with no nulls.

nodes.name: evaluateLiteral
nodes.summary: Returns selectivity for a literal condition: 0.0 for null or false, 1.0 for true, None otherwise.

nodes.name: evaluateInSet
nodes.summary: Estimates an IN or InSet predicate. For numeric-like types it keeps only the set values inside [min, max] and updates min, max and NDV; for string and binary it caps NDV by the set size; the result is new NDV divided by old NDV.

nodes.name: evaluateBinaryForNumeric
nodes.summary: Estimates <, <=, > or >= of a numeric-like column against a literal: no overlap gives 0, complete overlap gives 1, partial overlap prorates the range (uniform assumption) or uses histogram bins, then optionally narrows min, max and NDV in the column stat.

nodes.name: computeEqualityPossibilityByHistogram
nodes.summary: Computes equality selectivity from an equi-height histogram as bins holding the literal divided by bins holding the column's current [min, max] range.

nodes.name: computeComparisonPossibilityByHistogram
nodes.summary: Computes comparison selectivity from an equi-height histogram: the number of bins holding the matching range (lower/upper bound inclusion depends on the operator) divided by the bins holding the column's [min, max] range.

nodes.name: evaluateBinaryForTwoColumns
nodes.summary: Estimates a comparison between two columns of the same plan from their min/max intervals: no overlap gives 0, complete overlap (only if no nulls) gives 1, partial overlap uses 1/3 and optionally narrows min, max and NDV of both columns. String and binary types are not supported.

nodes.name: boundProbability
nodes.summary: Clamps a probability value into the range [0, 1].

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Returns true when the attribute has a column stat in the updated map or the original map.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the column stat of an attribute, preferring the updated map over the original map.

nodes.name: hasCountStats
nodes.summary: Returns true when the attribute's current column stat has distinct and null counts.

nodes.name: hasDistinctCount
nodes.summary: Returns true when the attribute's current column stat has a distinct count.

nodes.name: hasMinMaxStats
nodes.summary: Returns true when the attribute's current column stat has min and max values.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns the current column stat of an attribute (calls get and unwraps it).

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Stores an updated column stat for an attribute in the updated map, keyed by its ExprId.

nodes.name: outputColumnStats
nodes.summary: Builds the output column stat map from the original stats, calling updateCountStats on each with the row counts before and after the filter and the updated stat if any.

nodes.name: SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor, a LogicalPlanVisitor that computes only the size in bytes (and a row count where simple) for each logical operator. It is the visitor used when the cost-based path is off.

nodes.name: SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor
nodes.summary: Object extending LogicalPlanVisitor[Statistics] with one visit method per logical operator. Leaf nodes use computeStats; other nodes default to the product of children sizes; unary operators scale the child size by row size; limits, offset, tail and sample compute row counts; union sums children; join, intersect and except have their own rules. Column stats are generally not propagated.

nodes.name: visitUnaryNode
nodes.summary: Default estimate for unary nodes: assumes the same row count as the child and scales the child size by the ratio of output row size to child row size, never returning 0; rowCount and attributeStats are not propagated.

nodes.name: default
nodes.summary: Fallback estimate: leaf nodes use their own computeStats, other nodes use the product of the children's sizeInBytes (ignoring non-positive sizes).

nodes.name: visitAggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregate without grouping expressions yields one row; otherwise uses the unary node estimate.

nodes.name: visitDistinct
nodes.summary: Distinct uses the unary node estimate.

nodes.name: visitExcept
nodes.summary: Except takes a copy of the left child's stats.

nodes.name: visitExpand
nodes.summary: Expand multiplies the unary node size by the number of projections.

nodes.name: visitFilter
nodes.summary: Filter uses the unary node estimate.

nodes.name: visitGenerate
nodes.summary: Generate uses the default estimate.

nodes.name: visitGlobalLimit
nodes.summary: GlobalLimit sets the row count to the smaller of the limit and the child row count and computes the size from it, without column stats.

nodes.name: visitOffset
nodes.summary: Offset subtracts the offset from the child row count (floor 0) and computes the size from the result.

nodes.name: visitIntersect
nodes.summary: Intersect uses the smaller of the left and right child sizes.

nodes.name: visitJoin
nodes.summary: Join estimate: left semi and left anti use the left child stats; inner and outer joins whose join keys contain a distinct key set on either side use the sum of child sizes (above 1); all other cases use the default product.

nodes.name: visitLocalLimit
nodes.summary: LocalLimit gives size 1 and row count 0 for limit 0; otherwise reuses the child stats without column stats.

nodes.name: visitPivot
nodes.summary: Pivot uses the default estimate.

nodes.name: visitProject
nodes.summary: Project uses the unary node estimate.

nodes.name: visitRepartition
nodes.summary: Repartition returns the child's stats.

nodes.name: visitRepartitionByExpr
nodes.summary: RepartitionByExpression returns the child's stats.

nodes.name: visitRebalancePartitions
nodes.summary: RebalancePartitions returns the child's stats.

nodes.name: visitSample
nodes.summary: Sample scales the child size and row count by the sampling ratio (upperBound - lowerBound), with size at least 1.

nodes.name: visitScriptTransform
nodes.summary: ScriptTransformation uses the default estimate.

nodes.name: visitUnion
nodes.summary: Union sums the sizeInBytes of its children.

nodes.name: visitWindow
nodes.summary: Window uses the unary node estimate.

nodes.name: visitSort
nodes.summary: Sort returns the child's stats.

nodes.name: visitTail
nodes.summary: Tail sets the row count to the smaller of the limit and the child row count and computes the size from it.

nodes.name: visitWithCTE
nodes.summary: WithCTE returns the stats of its main plan.

nodes.name: JoinEstimation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines JoinEstimation, which estimates statistics (output rows, size in bytes and column stats) for a Join plan node using row counts and join key column stats, with a histogram-based path when both keys have histograms. Used when a Join node needs estimated statistics.

nodes.name: JoinEstimation
nodes.summary: Case class built from a Join plan node. estimate dispatches on the join type: inner, cross and the outer joins use estimateInnerOuterJoin (cardinality T(A) * T(B) / max(V(A.k), V(B.k)) using the most selective key, or histogram overlap, with adjustments for outer join types), left semi and left anti propagate left stats, and other join types return None.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Returns estimated Statistics for the join: inner-like and outer join types use estimateInnerOuterJoin, left semi and left anti use estimateLeftSemiAntiJoin, other join types are logged as unsupported and give None.

nodes.name: estimateInnerOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Estimates rows and column stats for inner, cross and outer joins. With equi-join keys it computes cardinality and key stats, bumps the row count for outer join types, then updates or propagates column stats per join type; without equi-join keys it treats the join like a cartesian product. Returns None when row counts are missing.

nodes.name: computeCardinalityAndStats
nodes.summary: Computes the inner join cardinality and the column stats of the join keys. It starts from a bound based on key uniqueness, checks each key pair for disjoint intervals, uses histograms or NDV per pair, and keeps the smallest (most selective) cardinality; disjoint keys give 0.

nodes.name: computeByNdv
nodes.summary: Computes the cardinality of one key pair as rows(A) * rows(B) / max(NDV) and builds the intersected column stat (min NDV, given min/max, zero nulls, min of max lengths, mean of average lengths).

nodes.name: computeByHistogram
nodes.summary: Computes the cardinality of one key pair from two equi-height histograms by summing, over the overlapped ranges, leftRows * rightRows / max(leftNdv, rightNdv), and builds the key column stat with the summed NDV.

nodes.name: updateOutputStats
nodes.summary: Returns column stats for the join output: join key attributes take the stats computed after the join, and other attributes have their count stats scaled to the output row count with updateCountStats.

nodes.name: extractJoinKeysWithColStats
nodes.summary: Pairs left and right join keys and keeps only those that are both AttributeReferences with distinct and null count stats on both sides.

nodes.name: estimateLeftSemiAntiJoin
nodes.summary: Estimates a left semi or left anti join by propagating the left child's row count and column stats (a noted TODO says more accurate estimation is needed); returns None when the left child has no row count.

nodes.name: ProjectEstimation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ProjectEstimation, which estimates statistics for a Project plan node by carrying over the child's row count and column stats for the projected columns and deriving stats for aliases.

nodes.name: ProjectEstimation
nodes.summary: Object with a single estimate method for Project nodes. Used when the child has a row count: it keeps the child stats for the output columns, adds alias stats and recomputes the size in bytes.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Returns Statistics for a Project: when the child has a row count, copies the child's stats with column stats restricted to the project output (including alias stats) and size recomputed from the row count; otherwise None.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanStats.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the LogicalPlanStats trait, which adds a cached stats method and cache invalidation to LogicalPlan. It selects the visitor that computes statistics based on the cboEnabled setting.

nodes.name: LogicalPlanStats
nodes.summary: Trait with a LogicalPlan self-type that provides the stats of a plan node. stats computes the value once and caches it in statsCache, using BasicStatsPlanVisitor when conf.cboEnabled is set and SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor otherwise; invalidateStatsCache clears the cache of the node and its children.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Returns the estimated Statistics for the node, computing and caching it on first use: BasicStatsPlanVisitor when cboEnabled is set, otherwise SizeInBytesOnlyStatsPlanVisitor.

nodes.name: invalidateStatsCache
nodes.summary: Resets statsCache to None for this node and recursively for all children, so stats are recomputed (for example after the configuration changes).

nodes.name: UnionEstimation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UnionEstimation, which estimates statistics for a Union node: summed size and row count, plus per-column min, max, null count and distinct count combined from the children. Used when a Union needs estimated statistics.

nodes.name: UnionEstimation
nodes.summary: Object with an estimate method for Union nodes. Sizes and row counts are summed; for each output column, min and max are the overall min and max over children (supported numeric, date, timestamp and interval types only), nullCount is summed and distinctCount is the maximum over children capped by the total row count.

nodes.name: createStatComparator
nodes.summary: Returns a less-than comparison function for min/max values of a data type, taken from the physical data type ordering.

nodes.name: isTypeSupported
nodes.summary: Returns true for the numeric, decimal, date, timestamp (with and without time zone) and ANSI interval types whose min/max stats can be combined.

nodes.name: estimate
nodes.summary: Returns Statistics for a Union: summed sizeInBytes, summed rowCount when every child has one, and column stats from computeColumnStats.

nodes.name: computeColumnStats
nodes.summary: For each output column, combines the children's column stats: overall min and max (supported types), summed null count, and maximum distinct count capped by the output row count. A column gets a stat only if at least one of these is available.

nodes.name: ValueInterval.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ValueInterval trait and its implementations (numeric, default and null intervals) plus the ValueInterval companion with apply, isIntersected and intersect. Used by filter and join estimation to test whether a literal or another column range lies within a column's min/max range.

nodes.name: ValueInterval
nodes.summary: Trait for the value range of a column with a contains(Literal) method. The ValueInterval companion object (lines 51-96) builds an interval from min, max and data type (apply), tests whether two intervals intersect (isIntersected) and computes the intersected min and max (intersect); the trait itself is lines 26-28.

nodes.name: NumericValueInterval
nodes.summary: Case class holding a numeric [min, max] range as Doubles; contains tests whether a literal, converted to Double, lies inside it.

nodes.name: DefaultValueInterval
nodes.summary: Interval for string and binary types, which have no min/max stats here; contains always returns true.

nodes.name: NullValueInterval
nodes.summary: Interval for columns that contain only nulls; contains always returns false.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Converts the literal to Double with EstimationUtils.toDouble and returns whether it lies between min and max.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Creates a ValueInterval from optional min, max and a data type: DefaultValueInterval for string and binary, NullValueInterval when min or max is missing, otherwise a NumericValueInterval from the converted values.

nodes.name: isIntersected
nodes.summary: Returns whether two intervals intersect: true when either is a default interval (conservative), false when either is a null interval, and a numeric overlap test for two numeric intervals; other pairs raise an error.

nodes.name: intersect
nodes.summary: Returns the intersected (min, max) of two overlapped numeric intervals converted back to the data type; default intervals give (None, None); other pairs raise an error.

nodes.name: v2AlterTableCommands.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical plans for ALTER TABLE style commands on v2 tables. Each command is an AlterTableCommand that turns its fields into a list of TableChange objects through its changes method (comment, location, properties, add, replace, drop, rename and alter columns, cluster by, collation, constraints).

nodes.name: AlterTableCommand
nodes.summary: Base trait for commands that alter a v2 table with TableChanges: declares changes and table, and fixes child to table. It extends UnaryCommand.

nodes.name: CommentOnTable
nodes.summary: Logical plan for COMMENT ON TABLE ... IS ('text' | NULL). changes sets the comment property, or removes it when the comment is null.

nodes.name: SetTableLocation
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... SET LOCATION. changes sets the location property and throws a compilation error when a partition spec is given.

nodes.name: SetTableProperties
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES. changes produces one set-property change per entry.

nodes.name: UnsetTableProperties
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... UNSET TBLPROPERTIES. changes produces one remove-property change per key (a one-line method, so it has no function node).

nodes.name: AddColumns
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS. The constructor rejects interval and unsupported data types; changes turns each QualifiedColType into an add-column change with nullability, comment, position and default value.

nodes.name: ReplaceColumns
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... REPLACE COLUMNS. changes deletes every existing column of the resolved table and then adds the specified columns (no path or position allowed).

nodes.name: DropColumns
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMNS. changes produces a delete-column change per resolved FieldName, honoring ifExists.

nodes.name: RenameColumn
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN. changes produces a rename-column change for the resolved field.

nodes.name: AlterColumnSpec
nodes.summary: Expression (unevaluable) describing one ALTER COLUMN action: column, optional new data type, nullability, comment, position, default expression, and a dropDefault flag. Its children are the column, position and default expression; isDefaultValueTypeCoerced checks the default's type against the new data type.

nodes.name: AlterColumns
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN. changes expands every AlterColumnSpec into type, nullability, comment, position, default value and drop-default changes.

nodes.name: AlterTableClusterBy
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY (col1, ...) and CLUSTER BY NONE; changes produces a cluster-by change with the column names or an empty array.

nodes.name: AlterTableCollation
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... DEFAULT COLLATION; changes sets the collation table property (a short method, so it has no function node).

nodes.name: AddConstraint
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT for primary key, foreign key and unique constraints. changes converts the TableConstraint to a v2 constraint and adds it with a null table version.

nodes.name: AddCheckConstraint
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT of a check constraint. It extends UnaryCommand directly rather than AlterTableCommand because its child is a filtered table scan.

nodes.name: DropConstraint
nodes.summary: Logical plan for ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT with ifExists and cascade flags; changes produces a drop-constraint change (a short method, so it has no function node).

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Returns a remove-comment change when the comment is null, otherwise a set-comment change.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Throws an error if a partition spec is present; otherwise returns a set-location property change.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Maps each property entry to a set-property change.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Requires resolved field names and positions and maps each column to an add-column change (name, type, nullability, comment, position, default value).

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Builds delete-column changes for every existing column and add-column changes for the new columns, concatenated.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Maps each resolved FieldName to a delete-column change with the ifExists flag.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Returns a rename-column change for the resolved field and the new name.

nodes.name: withNewChildrenInternal
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the spec from new children by casting them back to the column, optional position and optional default expression.

nodes.name: isDefaultValueTypeCoerced
nodes.summary: Returns true if the default expression's type matches the new data type (always true when either is absent), using ColumnDefinition.isDefaultValueTypeMatched.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: For each spec, builds optional type, nullability, comment, position and default-value changes plus a drop-default change, and concatenates them.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Returns a cluster-by change with the column names of the spec, or an empty array when there is no spec.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Converts the table constraint to a v2 constraint and returns an add-constraint change with a null table version.

layers.name: Tree and Rule Foundation
layers.description: Generic Catalyst machinery: the TreeNode abstraction and the RuleExecutor that applies rule batches to trees.

layers.name: Logical and Physical Plan Model
layers.description: Shared QueryPlan base, logical operators (LogicalPlan) and physical operators (SparkPlan).

layers.name: Parsing
layers.description: Turning SQL text into an unresolved logical plan: AstBuilder converts the parse tree, and SparkSqlParser extends it for SQL commands.

layers.name: Analysis
layers.description: The Analyzer, which resolves a parsed logical plan before optimization.

layers.name: Optimization and Planning
layers.description: The optimizer that rewrites logical plans, the planner machinery and the strategies that turn them into physical plans.

layers.name: Query Execution Driver
layers.description: QueryExecution, which drives a query through the pipeline stages.

layers.name: Whole-Stage Code Generation
layers.description: The produce/consume code generation protocol and the rule that fuses operators into generated stages.

layers.name: Adaptive Query Execution
layers.description: Runtime re-optimization: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec, the query stages it materializes, the logical re-optimizer and the shuffle-partition rules.

layers.name: Exchange and Joins
layers.description: Physical operators that move data (shuffle and broadcast exchanges, and the EnsureRequirements rule that inserts them) and the physical join operators.

layers.name: Aggregation and Window
layers.description: Physical aggregation operators (hash, object hash, sort), their shared base and code generation support, and the window operator with its frame evaluation.

layers.name: Python UDF Bridge (JVM side)
layers.description: How Python UDFs and pandas UDFs in a query become physical operators and how the JVM exchanges rows with the Python worker process: UDF extraction, the EvalPython operators, the Python runners with Arrow input and output, and the worker factory.

layers.name: Python Worker Side
layers.description: What runs inside the Python worker processes: the daemon that forks workers, the worker main loop that reads the JVM handshake and executes UDFs, the serializers (pickle and Arrow) that frame data on the socket, and the Python UDF API that creates JVM UDF objects.

layers.name: Data Source Read Path
layers.description: How a file-based read such as spark.read.parquet(...).filter(...) becomes a scan: the planning strategies and pruning rule, the file index and relation, the scan operator and RDD that read splits, and the file format with Parquet filter pushdown.

layers.name: Spark Connect Python Client
layers.description: The thin PySpark client of Spark Connect: SparkSession.builder.remote, the lazy DataFrame that only builds protobuf plans, the plan classes, and the gRPC client with reattachable response streams.

layers.name: Spark Connect Server
layers.description: The Spark Connect server inside the Spark driver: the gRPC service and session management, the per-operation holders and execution threads that stream Arrow results back, and the planner that converts protobuf relations, expressions and commands to Catalyst plans.

layers.name: Job and Task Scheduler
layers.description: Spark core job execution: SparkContext as the entry point, RDDs and dependencies, DAGScheduler splitting jobs into stages at shuffle boundaries, TaskSchedulerImpl and TaskSetManager scheduling tasks with locality, pools and speculation, MapOutputTracker, and the scheduler backend sending tasks to executors. Also included: executor health tracking and exclusion (HealthTracker), executor resource accounting, the output commit coordinator, merge status for push based shuffle, cluster messages between driver and executors, and the dynamic allocation ExecutorMonitor. Also covers barrier execution mode (BarrierCoordinator, BarrierTaskContext) and the task end reasons reported to the scheduler.

layers.name: Shuffle and Block Storage
layers.description: The shuffle subsystem: the ShuffleManager and handle abstraction, the three map-side writers (bypass merge sort, unsafe serialized sort, general sort) with their sorters and spill files, the index and data file resolver, the reduce-side reader and block fetch iterator, and the BlockManager that stores and serves blocks. StorageLevel describes how a block is stored and BlockId names every kind of block. Also covers BlockManagerMaster and its endpoint on the driver, the block manager messages, replication policies, decommissioning and the fallback storage. Also covers the pluggable shuffle IO API (ShuffleDataIO, driver and executor components, map output writers) with its local disk implementation, push based fetch helpers, rolling log block writers and storage reporting utilities. Also covers push based shuffle on the map side (ShuffleBlockPusher), checksums, shuffle metrics reporters and the sort data format. Also covers the block transfer service (BlockTransferService and its Netty implementation) used to fetch and push blocks between executors.

layers.name: Structured Streaming
layers.description: How a streaming query runs: the micro-batch execution loop and triggers, incremental planning of each batch, offset and commit logs in the checkpoint, watermarks, stateful operators, and the versioned state store (HDFS-backed and RocksDB).

layers.name: Catalyst Expressions and Codegen
layers.description: The expression system under every plan: the Expression tree, named attributes and literals, predicates, arithmetic and casts with ANSI semantics, type coercion, aggregate and window function interfaces, UDF expressions, and the code generator that compiles expressions to Java.

layers.name: PySpark SQL API
layers.description: The public PySpark DataFrame API: abstract DataFrame, Column, Window, GroupedData, readers and writers, SparkSession and the type system, plus the classic (py4j) implementations that forward every call to the JVM Dataset. The Spark Connect implementations live in their own layer and share these parent classes.

layers.name: Memory Management and Caching
layers.description: How executors share memory and how cached data is held: the unified execution/storage memory manager and pools, per-task Tungsten memory with forced spilling, spillable sorters, the SQL cache (CacheManager, columnar InMemoryRelation and its scan), the sort operator and the reduce-side shuffle row RDD. Also covers the memory package errors (SparkOutOfMemoryError, TooLargePageException) and unmanaged memory consumers. Also covers BytesToBytesMap, the off-heap hash map used by hash aggregation and joins, and its growth strategy.

layers.name: Executor, Environment and Deploy
layers.description: The processes around a job: spark-submit and its argument handling, the standalone Master and Worker, the scheduler backends for local and standalone mode, the executor process (backend, Executor, TaskRunner, task context and metrics), SparkEnv that wires the services, and dynamic allocation. SparkConf holds the spark.* settings. Also covers executor metrics (ExecutorMetrics, the poller and sources), the executor class loader, exit codes and the task level input and output metrics. Also covers heartbeats between executors and the driver, the ContextCleaner for removing unused RDDs, shuffles and broadcasts, executor allocation requests and job artifacts. Also covers the standalone deploy messages and descriptions (DeployMessage, ApplicationDescription, DriverDescription, ExecutorState), the standalone Client, ExternalShuffleService, LocalSparkCluster, SparkHadoopUtil, the Python and R runners used by spark-submit, and the deploy JSON protocol.

layers.name: DataSource V2 and Catalogs
layers.description: The V2 data source and catalog API that table formats and connectors plug into: the Table and catalog interfaces with capabilities, CatalogManager and the session catalog, DataSourceV2Relation, the strategy and optimizer rule that plan scans with pushdown, the scan execution and RDD, the file based V2 sources, and the V2 write path. The public Java interfaces connectors implement are included: TableProvider, the read side (ScanBuilder, Scan, Batch, InputPartition, PartitionReader and the pushdown and reporting mix-ins) and the write side (WriteBuilder, Write, BatchWrite, DataWriter, commit messages, overwrite and truncate modes, row level operations, required distribution and ordering).

layers.name: RDD Library and Shared Variables
layers.description: The RDD API under every DataFrame: the RDD base class and dependencies, partitioners, the key/value operations (PairRDDFunctions, OrderedRDDFunctions), the concrete RDDs for narrow transformations, unions, cogroup, coalesce, zip, Hadoop input and parallelize, checkpointing, and the shared variables: broadcast (TorrentBroadcast and BroadcastManager) and accumulators (AccumulatorV2). Also covers approximate results (PartialResult and the evaluators for count, mean and sum), asynchronous RDD actions, BlockRDD and BinaryFileRDD. Also covers the remaining RDD classes: pipe, sampling, subtract, partition pruning, partitioner aware union, zip with index, checkpoint RDDs, JDBC input, the periodic checkpointer and the RDD operation scope used to label jobs in the UI.

layers.name: Spark UI, Status Store and Metrics
layers.description: How Spark reports on itself: AppStatusListener turns listener bus events into live entities stored in an ElementTrackingStore (a KVStore), AppStatusStore and the REST resources read from it, the Jetty based web UI (SparkUI, tabs and pages for jobs, stages, executors and SQL), the SQL status listener and plan graph, and the MetricsSystem with its sources and sinks. Also covers the concrete metrics sinks (servlet, Prometheus servlet, StatsD, SLF4J) and sources (JVM, JVM CPU, accumulators, static sources). Also covers the console progress bar, thread dump and heap histogram pages, the pool pages, the HTTP security and JWS filters, CspNonce and the flame graph node. Also covers the REST API resources and enums under status/api/v1 (applications, stages, Prometheus), the paged table helper, RDD operation graph, storage page and tab, tool tips, the app status source and the history server plugin hook.

layers.name: Scala DataFrame API and SparkSession
layers.description: The Scala and Java user API: the abstract API classes in sql/api shared by classic Spark and Spark Connect (SparkSession, Dataset, Column, Row, Encoders, readers and writers), and the classic implementations in sql/core: SparkSession with its session and shared state, Dataset as a logical plan plus QueryExecution, grouped datasets, DataFrameReader and Writer, Catalog, RuntimeConfig, UDFRegistration, streaming reader, writer and query manager, and the conversion of the API column tree to Catalyst expressions.

layers.name: Listener Bus and Events
layers.description: How scheduler events are published: SparkListener and its event classes, the LiveListenerBus with its AsyncEventQueues, the event log writer and replay bus, and the job result and waiter types used by the DAGScheduler.

layers.name: Serialization
layers.description: How Spark turns objects into bytes: the Serializer and SerializerInstance abstraction, the Java and Kryo serializers, the SerializerManager that chooses a serializer per block, a serialization debugger for finding the field that cannot be serialized, and the Avro helper.

layers.name: RPC and Security
layers.description: How the driver, executors and masters talk to each other and keep it safe: the RpcEnv and RpcEndpoint abstraction with its Netty implementation (dispatcher, inbox and outbox, message loops, stream manager), timeouts and addresses, plus the security helpers: encryption of IO streams, authentication of local sockets, delegation token providers and group mapping. Also covers SecurityManager (authentication, ACLs and secret handling) and SSLOptions. Also covers HadoopDelegationTokenManager, which obtains and renews Hadoop delegation tokens. Also covers the Hadoop file system and HBase delegation token providers.

layers.name: Hadoop IO and Commit Protocols
layers.description: How Spark reads and writes files through Hadoop APIs: compression codecs and IO stream helpers, input formats and record readers for whole text files, fixed length binary files and portable data streams, and the commit protocols (FileCommitProtocol and its Hadoop implementations, SparkHadoopWriter) that make job output atomic.

layers.name: Java and Python API Bridges
layers.description: The language facing APIs of core: JavaSparkContext, JavaRDD, JavaPairRDD and JavaDoubleRDD wrap the Scala API for Java callers, with Optional, StorageLevels and the Java status tracker, while api/python holds the JVM side of PySpark: the Py4J gateway server, Python partitioner and Hadoop data conversion helpers. Also covers the Python worker utilities (PythonWorkerUtils, SerDeUtil, StreamingPythonRunner, worker log capture) and the R API bridge: RBackend and its handlers, RRunner, RRDD and the R serialization code.

layers.name: Resource Profiles and Scheduling
layers.description: How tasks and executors declare the resources they need: ResourceProfile with ExecutorResourceRequests and TaskResourceRequests, the builder, the ResourceProfileManager that tracks profiles in use, resource discovery (ResourceUtils and the discovery script plugin), ResourceInformation and the ResourceAllocator that hands out resource addresses.

layers.name: Core Configuration Entries
layers.description: Where the spark.* settings of core are defined: the ConfigBuilder based entries with their keys, defaults and documentation in the internal.config package (the main package object and per area files for deploy, history server, Kryo, network, Python, R, status, streaming and tests), plus the provider that reads them from SparkConf.

layers.name: Core Utilities
layers.description: General purpose helpers used all over core: the Utils object (class loading, temp directories, file fetching, host names, size and time parsing, call sites, process execution, resource management helpers), clocks, byte buffer streams, class loaders for user jars, lazy value helpers, bounded priority queues, dependency resolution for jars and files, and small command line helpers. Also covers JsonProtocol (JSON for scheduler events used by the event log), ListenerBus, the shutdown hook manager and signal handling, Hadoop file system listing, serializable wrappers for Hadoop configuration, the last attempt accumulator and small data structures. Also covers SizeEstimator (object size estimation), ThreadUtils and UninterruptibleThread, StatCounter, the uncaught exception handler and exit codes, the stub class loader and task completion listeners. Also covers chunked byte buffers, rolling log appenders and the driver log, random samplers (Bernoulli, Poisson, stratified sampling), the XORShift random generator, SparkPath and the SparkCoreErrors factory.

layers.name: Sorting and Collections
layers.description: Data structures and sorters used for shuffle and aggregation: bit sets, compact buffers, the spillable external append-only map, TimSort, radix sort, prefix comparators and the unsafe sorter spill writer, reader and mergers. Also covers the open hash map and set, size tracking collections used by the shuffle and aggregation buffers, the pair buffer, the primitive vector, the percentile heap, and the Sorter wrapper over TimSort with its SortDataFormat.

layers.name: Standalone Master, Web UI and REST Submission
layers.description: The state kept by the standalone Master (worker, driver and executor descriptions and states), its pluggable recovery persistence engines (file system, RocksDB, ZooKeeper) and leader election, the master web UI pages, and the REST protocol and client/server used to submit applications to the standalone cluster.

layers.name: Standalone Worker and Web UI
layers.description: Support classes for the standalone Worker: launching driver processes (DriverRunner, DriverWrapper), building commands, command line arguments, the worker watcher, metrics source and the worker web UI pages.

layers.name: History Server and Event Logs
layers.description: Reading and writing event log files (single file and rolling), compacting them with event filters, the application cache and the application history provider interface used by the history server. Also covers FsHistoryProvider (scans the log directory and builds application listings), HistoryServer and its pages, HistoryAppStatusStore, the disk and memory managers that limit how many applications are held, and HybridStore.

layers.name: Status Store Protobuf Serializers
layers.description: Serializers that convert status store objects (job, stage, executor and application data, accumulables, executor metrics) to and from protobuf messages so the KVStore can persist them for the history server. Also covers ProtobufSerDe (the serializer trait), KVStoreProtobufSerializer (the KVStore serializer that dispatches by class) and the stage, task, RDD storage, pool, resource profile and process serializers.

layers.name: SQL Configuration and Session State
layers.description: SQLConf and StaticSQLConf (all SQL settings), and the per-session state (SessionState, SharedState) with the builder that creates the analyzer, optimizer, planner and catalog for a session.

layers.name: Spark Connect Protocol and Client
layers.description: Protobuf definitions of the Spark Connect protocol (relations, expressions, commands, types) and the shared client code, including the Scala client and Arrow handling.

layers.name: SQL Commands (DDL and DML)
layers.description: Physical run-style commands: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, SHOW, DESCRIBE, SET, INSERT-style writes and cache commands, including the v2 command variants.

layers.name: Columnar and Vectorized Execution
layers.description: Columnar batches, the in-memory columnar cache format with its compression, vectorized column vectors and readers, and Arrow conversion.

layers.name: SQL Scripting
layers.description: SQL scripting: compound statements, control flow, variables and the script executor.

layers.name: Streaming State Store
layers.description: State store providers, the RocksDB state store, state schema and checkpoint files, and the state data sources used by stateful streaming operators.

layers.name: Streaming Stateful Operators
layers.description: Physical operators for stateful streaming: aggregation, deduplication, joins, flatMapGroupsWithState and transformWithState, with their state managers.

tour.title: The pipeline driver: QueryExecution
tour.description: Start here. QueryExecution exposes each stage of query processing as a member: analyzed, commandExecuted, withCachedData, optimizedPlan, sparkPlan, executedPlan and finally toRdd. It wires together the optimizer, the planner and the physical plan classes covered in the next steps.

tour.title: Everything is a tree: TreeNode and QueryPlan
tour.description: Both logical and physical plans are Catalyst trees. TreeNode provides traversal and transform APIs, which is what lets rules rewrite plans by pattern matching. QueryPlan extends TreeNode and is the base shared by logical and physical plans, adding expression transforms, subquery-aware traversal and canonicalization.

tour.title: Applying rules: RuleExecutor
tour.description: RuleExecutor runs ordered batches of rules over a tree, either once or repeatedly until a fixed point. The optimizer is built on it. Rule is the abstract base of every optimizer, analyzer and planner-preparation rule: it has a name and an apply method that rewrites a plan, and RuleExecutor runs batches of Rule instances.

tour.title: Logical operators: LogicalPlan
tour.description: LogicalPlan is the base of all logical operators, with LeafNode, UnaryNode and BinaryNode shapes. This is the tree that analysis and optimization work on.

tour.title: From SQL text to a plan: SparkSqlParser and AstBuilder
tour.description: AstBuilder walks the parse tree and builds Catalyst logical plans and expressions through its visit methods (the graph shows 34 of the 261 it contains). SparkSqlParser holds SparkSqlAstBuilder, which extends AstBuilder to handle SQL commands. The ANTLR grammar and the generated parser are not part of this graph.

tour.title: Resolving the plan: Analyzer
tour.description: Analyzer extends RuleExecutor and runs batches of resolution rules over the logical plan. The batch order comes from earlyBatches plus the main rule list in batches (Analyzer.scala line 538). The file defines many more rules than the graph shows individually.

tour.title: Rewriting the plan: Optimizer and SparkOptimizer
tour.description: Optimizer extends RuleExecutor, and its batch list is built in defaultBatches (Optimizer.scala line 100). Some well-known rules such as ConstantFolding and ReorderJoin are not defined in this file: they live in optimizer/expressions.scala and optimizer/joins.scala. SparkOptimizer extends Optimizer and adds engine-specific batches through its own defaultBatches. Many of the rules that defaultBatches lists live in other files, for example ConstantFolding in optimizer/expressions.scala and ReorderJoin in optimizer/joins.scala.

tour.title: From logical to physical: QueryPlanner, SparkPlanner and SparkStrategies
tour.description: QueryPlanner applies a list of strategies to a logical plan and expands planLater placeholders. SparkStrategies defines SparkStrategy, PlanLater and the built-in physical planning strategies (limits, joins, aggregation, windows, streaming, Python evals, basic operators). SparkPlanner extends SparkStrategies and supplies the concrete strategy order.

tour.title: Physical operators: SparkPlan
tour.description: SparkPlan is the base of physical operators, with LeafExecNode, UnaryExecNode and BinaryExecNode shapes. Its subclasses execute the query.

tour.title: Moving data: exchanges and EnsureRequirements
tour.description: EnsureRequirements is a physical planning rule that inserts ShuffleExchangeExec, BroadcastExchangeExec and sorts so every operator's required child distribution and ordering are satisfied. ShuffleExchangeExec repartitions rows by a Partitioning through a shuffle dependency. BroadcastExchangeExec collects a child plan on the driver, builds a broadcast relation and distributes it to executors. Exchange is the abstract base of the data-movement operators (shuffle and broadcast), and ReusedExchangeExec is a leaf wrapper that reuses an existing exchange under different output attribute ids.

tour.title: Joins: choosing and executing
tour.description: JoinSelection in SparkStrategies chooses a join, using JoinSelectionHelper (in optimizer/joins.scala) for the shared logic that picks broadcast or shuffled hash join build sides. BroadcastHashJoinExec broadcasts the build side so the streamed side is not shuffled. ShuffledHashJoinExec shuffles both inputs and builds a hash table per partition. SortMergeJoinExec requires both children shuffled and sorted by the join keys and merges them with a streaming scanner. BaseJoinExec describes a join (type, condition, keys) and shares the EXPLAIN output of all join operators. HashJoin is shared by BroadcastHashJoinExec and ShuffledHashJoinExec, and ShuffledJoin by the joins that shuffle both children (sort-merge and shuffled hash). HashedRelation is the build-side data structure of hash joins.

tour.title: Aggregation: AggUtils and the aggregate operators
tour.description: AggUtils turns a logical Aggregate into physical aggregation plans, choosing HashAggregateExec, ObjectHashAggregateExec or SortAggregateExec and building the partial and final stages (also distinct, streaming and session-window variants). HashAggregateExec is the Tungsten hash-based operator with whole-stage codegen that falls back to sort-based aggregation when memory is exceeded. ObjectHashAggregateExec handles TypedImperativeAggregate functions whose buffers hold JVM objects, without codegen. SortAggregateExec needs a child sorted on the grouping expressions and is the general fallback. BaseAggregateExec holds the shared logic and AggregateCodegenSupport the shared codegen. AggregationIterator is the shared base of the per-group iterators (TungstenAggregationIterator, SortBasedAggregationIterator): it builds the update and merge projections for the aggregate functions. SortBasedAggregationIterator walks sorted input and emits one result when the grouping key changes.

tour.title: Window functions: WindowExec and frames
tour.description: WindowExec evaluates window functions over sorted partitions by delegating to a WindowEvaluatorFactory. The frame types are the entire partition, growing, shrinking, moving and offset frames, with row or range boundaries. WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase groups window expressions by frame and creates the matching WindowFunctionFrame factories, and WindowFunctionFrame and its implementations compute the result for each row of a partition. WindowExecBase holds the logic common to window operators. WindowEvaluatorFactory builds the per-partition evaluator that WindowExec runs. AggregateProcessor evaluates aggregate window functions over a frame, and BoundOrdering (row or range) decides which input rows fall inside the frame boundaries.

tour.title: Fusing operators: whole-stage code generation
