tour.description: WholeStageCodegenExec compiles a pipeline of physical operators into one Java class using the CodegenSupport produce/consume protocol. The CollapseCodegenStages rule inserts these stages into a physical plan, with InputAdapter as the leaf where fusion stops.

tour.title: Adapting while running: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec and query stages
tour.description: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec splits the physical plan into query stages (QueryStageExec and its shuffle, broadcast, table cache and result variants), materializes them as their dependencies finish, then re-optimizes the remaining plan using runtime statistics through AQEOptimizer. InsertAdaptiveSparkPlan is the preparation rule that decides whether a plan gets wrapped in AdaptiveSparkPlanExec.

tour.title: Runtime rewrites: coalescing and skew handling
tour.description: CoalesceShufflePartitions merges adjacent small shuffle partitions using map output statistics. OptimizeSkewedJoin splits skewed partitions of joins and replicates the matching side. Both read shuffle data through AQEShuffleReadExec, which reads a shuffle stage according to an explicit list of partition specs.

tour.title: Python UDFs in a query plan
tour.description: ExtractPythonUDFs is an optimizer-stage rule that pulls Python UDF calls out of expressions into separate logical EvalPython operators (batched UDFs, Arrow-based pandas UDFs, UDTFs, and aggregate variants). The planner then maps them to physical operators: EvalPythonExec is the shared base, BatchEvalPythonExec sends pickled rows, ArrowEvalPythonExec sends Arrow batches. Their evaluator factories build the Python runner for each partition and join the UDF results back to the input rows. The logical operators BatchEvalPython and ArrowEvalPython (pythonLogicalOperators.scala) are what ExtractPythonUDFs produces. UserDefinedPythonFunction is the JVM object that the Python udf() call creates, wrapping a SimplePythonFunction (in PythonRDD.scala) that holds the pickled command.

tour.title: Talking to the Python worker
tour.description: BasePythonRunner (core) drives one task's exchange with a Python worker: it obtains a worker from PythonWorkerFactory (a daemon that forks workers, or a directly launched process, with an idle pool), writes a header (eval type, configuration, UDF payload) and the input data from a writer thread, and reads results back with length-prefixed framing. ArrowPythonRunner and PythonUDFRunner specialize it, with PythonArrowInput and PythonArrowOutput providing the Arrow stream writing and reading. PythonUtils holds shared configuration helpers.

tour.title: Inside the Python worker process
tour.description: On the Python side, daemon.py is started by the JVM PythonWorkerFactory and forks one worker per task. Each worker runs worker.main, which reads the handshake the JVM Writer wrote (partition index, Python version, task context, files and broadcasts, eval type, runner and eval configuration, then the serialized UDFs), picks the code path for the eval type in read_udfs or read_udtf, loops over the input stream, and writes results, timing data and an end-of-data marker back. worker_util.py holds shared setup helpers.

tour.title: Serializers and the UDF API
tour.description: serializers.py defines the Serializer family (framed, batched, pickle and cloudpickle serializers) and the length-prefixed framing helpers. sql/pandas/serializers.py builds on Arrow streams for pandas UDFs, grouped map, cogroup, aggregate, UDTF and stateful serializers. sql/udf.py is the user-facing side: udf() and UserDefinedFunction create the JVM UserDefinedPythonFunction wrapping a pickled Python function, and UDFRegistration registers it for SQL.

tour.title: Planning a file scan
tour.description: FileSourceStrategy and DataSourceStrategy are planner strategies (listed in SparkPlanner) that turn a logical relation into a scan operator. FileSourceStrategy splits the filters into partition filters, data filters and post-scan filters, works out the required columns and the bucket set, and creates FileSourceScanExec. DataSourceStrategy handles V1 sources and translates Catalyst filters to source filters. PruneFileSourcePartitions is an early optimizer rule that prunes partitions using the file index. HadoopFsRelation ties a FileIndex, a FileFormat and the schemas together. LogicalRelation wraps a BaseRelation (the V1 data source API in sources/interfaces.scala) as a leaf of the logical plan.

tour.title: Listing, splitting and reading files
tour.description: FileIndex implementations (PartitioningAwareFileIndex, InMemoryFileIndex) list leaf files, discover partition columns and cache the listing. FileSourceScanExec turns the selected partitions into FilePartitions (bin-packed splits up to maxSplitBytes) and a FileScanRDD, which opens each PartitionedFile with the reader function built by FileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues. ParquetFileFormat builds that reader, choosing the vectorized or parquet-mr reader, and ParquetFilters converts Catalyst predicates to Parquet predicates for row group filtering. FileStatusCache caches directory listings and PartitionedFileUtil splits files into PartitionedFile ranges. ParquetReadSupport clips the requested schema for parquet-mr reads, VectorizedParquetRecordReader reads column batches, and ParquetUtils holds shared Parquet schema and footer helpers.

tour.title: Spark Connect: the client builds a plan
tour.description: With Spark Connect, SparkSession.builder.remote(...) creates a client session that holds a SparkConnectClient (a gRPC channel). DataFrame methods do not run anything: each transformation wraps the current plan in a new plan node from plan.py (Project, Filter, Join, Aggregate, ...). Only an action such as collect, show or toPandas converts the plan tree to a protobuf Relation and sends it through the client. Reattachable iterators let a long running operation resume after a network failure.

tour.title: Spark Connect: the server runs the operation
tour.description: SparkConnectService receives ExecutePlan, looks up or creates the session through SparkConnectSessionManager and SessionHolder, and creates an ExecuteHolder for the operation. ExecuteThreadRunner runs it on its own thread; SparkConnectPlanExecution turns the planned Dataset into Arrow batches; ExecuteResponseObserver buffers responses so a client can reattach, and ExecuteGrpcResponseSender streams them back.

tour.title: Spark Connect: from protobuf to a Catalyst plan
tour.description: SparkConnectPlanner transforms the protobuf Relation tree into Catalyst logical plans (transformRelation dispatches on the relation type), protobuf Expressions into Catalyst expressions, and Commands (write, create view, register UDF, streaming) into actions. The resulting LogicalPlan then goes through the normal QueryExecution pipeline described in the earlier tour steps.

tour.title: SparkContext, RDDs and dependencies
tour.description: SparkContext is the entry point of core Spark: when it starts it creates the environment, the DAGScheduler, the TaskScheduler and the scheduler backend chosen from the master URL (createTaskScheduler). Under every DataFrame there are RDDs: an RDD defines partitions, a compute function and dependencies. A narrow dependency keeps a partition within one task chain, a ShuffleDependency marks a stage boundary. Actions such as collect and count on RDDs, SparkPlan.executeTake, ShuffleExchangeExec.submitMapStage and PythonRDD.runJob all end in SparkContext.runJob or submitMapStage, which call the DAGScheduler.

tour.title: From a job to stages and tasks
tour.description: An action submits a job to DAGScheduler through its event loop (JobSubmitted). DAGScheduler builds a ResultStage for the final RDD and walks its shuffle dependencies to create ShuffleMapStages, submits parent stages first (submitStage, getMissingParentStages), and for each stage creates one task per partition: ShuffleMapTask writes shuffle output, ResultTask computes the final partition result. On task completion or failure (CompletionEvent, fetch failures, executor loss) it updates stage state, resubmits stages and finishes the job. MapOutputTracker (on the driver) records where each map task wrote its shuffle output so reduce tasks and stage resubmission can find it, ShuffleWriteProcessor writes the output of a map task, and StageInfo is the summary used by listeners and the UI.

tour.title: Scheduling tasks onto executors
tour.description: DAGScheduler hands each stage's tasks to TaskSchedulerImpl as a TaskSet. TaskSchedulerImpl wraps it in a TaskSetManager and puts it in a scheduling Pool (FIFO or FAIR, built by SchedulableBuilder). When executors offer free resources, resourceOffers asks the pools for tasks in order; TaskSetManager picks tasks by data locality level (process, node, rack, any) with delay scheduling, tracks failures and launches speculative copies of slow tasks.

tour.title: Launching tasks on executors
tour.description: SchedulerBackend is the cluster-manager facing interface. CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend runs a DriverEndpoint RPC endpoint on the driver: executors register with it, it makes resource offers to TaskSchedulerImpl (makeOffers), serializes the chosen tasks and sends LaunchTask messages, and receives status updates that flow back to TaskSchedulerImpl and DAGScheduler.

tour.title: Writing shuffle output on the map side
tour.description: A ShuffleMapTask calls ShuffleWriteProcessor.write, which asks the ShuffleManager (SortShuffleManager) for a ShuffleWriter chosen by the shuffle handle. BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter writes one file per reduce partition and concatenates them (used when there is no map-side combine and few partitions); UnsafeShuffleWriter serializes records into pages, sorts compact pointers (ShuffleExternalSorter, ShuffleInMemorySorter) and merges spill files; SortShuffleWriter uses ExternalSorter with an AppendOnlyMap for aggregation. All of them end with one data file plus an index file per map task, managed by IndexShuffleBlockResolver, and DiskBlockObjectWriter does the buffered file writing.

tour.title: Reading shuffle data on the reduce side
tour.description: BlockStoreShuffleReader asks the MapOutputTracker which executors hold the map outputs for its reduce partitions, then ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator fetches the blocks: local and host-local blocks are read directly, remote blocks are requested over the network within limits (maxBytesInFlight and related settings), with retries and optional corruption checks. Failures surface as FetchFailedException, which the DAGScheduler handles by resubmitting the map stage. Records are then deserialized and, if needed, aggregated or sorted with ExternalSorter.

tour.title: BlockManager: where blocks live
tour.description: BlockManager is the per-executor (and driver) storage service for blocks: cached RDD partitions, broadcast variables, shuffle blocks and task results. It coordinates a memory store and a disk store, reports block status to the driver, serves remote fetch requests, replicates blocks and supports block migration during decommissioning. Shuffle files are served through it and the IndexShuffleBlockResolver.

tour.title: The micro-batch loop
tour.description: A streaming query is a StreamExecution running on its own thread; MicroBatchExecution is the micro-batch implementation. A TriggerExecutor decides when to run a batch. Each batch: ask the sources for the latest offsets, write the planned offsets to the offset log (before processing), build an IncrementalExecution that plans the batch as a normal query over just the new data (the streaming relations are replaced by the sources' batch data), run it into the sink, then write the commit log. ProgressReporter produces the progress metrics seen in query.lastProgress.

tour.title: Checkpoint, offsets and exactly-once recovery
tour.description: The checkpoint directory holds an offset log (what range each batch will process, written first) and a commit log (which batches finished), both HDFSMetadataLog implementations that write atomically through a CheckpointFileManager. On restart the query reads the logs to decide whether to re-run the last planned batch or plan the next one, which with replayable sources and idempotent sinks gives end-to-end exactly-once. Watermarks (WatermarkTracker, WatermarkPropagator, EventTimeWatermarkExec) are tracked in the offset metadata and decide which late data is dropped and which state can be evicted.

tour.title: Stateful operators and the state store
tour.description: Operators such as streaming aggregation, deduplication and stream-stream joins keep state per key in a StateStore, one versioned key-value store per shuffle partition. StateStoreRDD loads version N for the partition, the operator updates it during the batch and commits version N+1 at the end. HDFSBackedStateStoreProvider keeps the map in memory and persists delta and snapshot files in the checkpoint; RocksDBStateStoreProvider keeps state in a local RocksDB instance and uploads its files, which allows state larger than memory. A background maintenance task writes snapshots and cleans up old versions.

tour.title: Expressions: the tree inside every plan
tour.description: Every column, filter condition and function in a query is an Expression tree. Expression defines eval (interpreted), genCode (generated Java), nullability, foldability and determinism; helper traits (UnaryExpression, BinaryExpression, ...) fix the number of children. Attributes and aliases (namedExpressions) name the columns of a plan, Literal holds constants, SortOrder describes ordering, and EquivalentExpressions finds common subexpressions to compute once. The optimizer rules from the earlier steps (ConstantFolding, NullPropagation) work by inspecting these properties.

tour.title: Predicates, arithmetic, casts and type coercion
tour.description: Predicates implement SQL three-valued logic (NULL handling in And, Or, Not, In). Arithmetic and Cast carry an eval mode: in ANSI mode (the default in Spark 4) overflow, invalid casts and divide by zero raise errors, in legacy mode they return NULL or wrap, and try_cast always returns NULL on failure. TypeCoercion and AnsiTypeCoercion are analyzer rules that insert implicit casts so the operands of an expression have compatible types.

tour.title: Aggregate, window and UDF expressions
tour.description: Aggregate functions implement a buffer protocol: DeclarativeAggregate expresses initial values, update, merge and evaluate as expressions (Sum, Count) while ImperativeAggregate and TypedImperativeAggregate do it with code and arbitrary buffers. Window expressions pair a window function with a frame specification. PythonUDF and ScalaUDF are expressions that cannot be evaluated by the engine itself: PythonUDF is extracted into EvalPython operators, ScalaUDF is evaluated on the JVM with converters between Catalyst and Scala types.

tour.title: Code generation for expressions
tour.description: CodeGenerator turns expression trees into Java source using a CodegenContext (mutable state, helper functions, subexpression elimination, method splitting to stay under JVM limits) and compiles it with Janino, caching the compiled class. GenerateUnsafeProjection, GeneratePredicate and GenerateOrdering produce the projections, filters and comparators used by operators, and whole-stage codegen builds on the same context. Expressions that cannot generate code use CodegenFallback, which calls the interpreted eval.

tour.title: The PySpark API: one interface, two backends
tour.description: pyspark.sql.DataFrame, Column, Window and the other public classes are mostly abstract: their methods are stubs decorated with dispatch helpers from utils.py that route each call to the classic implementation (py4j proxy of the JVM Dataset) or the Spark Connect implementation (a plan built on the client) depending on the type of the object. SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate creates either a classic session over a JVM SparkContext or, in remote mode, a Connect session. Transformations such as select, filter and join only build a new DataFrame; actions such as collect, count and show are what start a job.

tour.title: Classic PySpark: a thin wrapper over the JVM
tour.description: In classic mode a DataFrame holds a py4j reference to a JVM Dataset (_jdf); each method converts Python arguments to JVM objects (_jseq, _jcols), calls the Dataset method and wraps the result in a new Python DataFrame. Column wraps a JVM Column (_jc) and builds expressions the same way. No data is processed in Python except in UDFs and when results are collected.

tour.title: Executor memory: one pool, shared by tasks
tour.description: UnifiedMemoryManager splits the usable heap (spark.memory.fraction of heap minus a 300MB reserve) into an execution pool and a storage pool that can borrow from each other: execution may evict cached blocks to grow, storage can only use free execution memory. Within execution memory each running task gets between 1/(2N) and 1/N of the pool. Tasks request memory through TaskMemoryManager, which can force other consumers (sorters, hash maps) to spill, and allocates Tungsten pages addressed by a 64-bit page number plus offset.

tour.title: Where cached and shuffle data are stored
tour.description: BlockManager keeps blocks in a MemoryStore (deserialized objects or serialized bytes, evicting least recently used blocks of other RDDs when space is needed), a DiskStore (files located by DiskBlockManager in hashed sub-directories of the local dirs, which also holds shuffle files) and tracks reader/writer locks per block in BlockInfoManager. MapStatus records where each map task wrote its shuffle output and how large each partition is; ShuffledRDD and ShuffledRowRDD read shuffle data on the reduce side.

tour.title: df.cache() and sorting
tour.description: CacheManager registers a query plan to cache and later rewrites matching plans (by canonicalized form) to read the cache. The data is built lazily on the first action into compressed columnar batches (InMemoryRelation / CachedRDDBuilder) persisted through the RDD storage level, and InMemoryTableScanExec reads them, skipping batches using their statistics. SortExec sorts rows with an external sorter that spills to disk when memory is short.

tour.title: spark-submit and the standalone cluster
tour.description: SparkSubmit parses the arguments (SparkSubmitArguments, merging spark-defaults.conf), works out from --master and --deploy-mode which cluster manager and main class to use, and runs the application's main in the right place (for PySpark through a Python runner). In standalone mode StandaloneSchedulerBackend registers the application with the Master through StandaloneAppClient; the Master decides which Workers start executors (spreading out or packing), and each Worker launches an executor process with ExecutorRunner. Local mode instead runs LocalSchedulerBackend with an executor inside the driver JVM.

tour.title: The executor process and SparkEnv
tour.description: CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend is the main of an executor process: it creates a SparkEnv (serializer, shuffle manager, memory manager, block manager, map output tracker, RPC), registers with the driver and receives LaunchTask messages. Executor runs each task on a pool thread in a TaskRunner: deserialize the task, set up a TaskContextImpl and task memory manager, run it, and send the result back directly or through the block manager when it is large, while heartbeats report metrics. ExecutorAllocationManager on the driver adds or removes executors with dynamic allocation.

tour.title: DataSource V2: tables, catalogs and capabilities
tour.description: In the V2 API a data source is a Table found through a catalog. CatalogManager resolves catalog names (spark_catalog is the session catalog, which can delegate to a user configured implementation; other names come from spark.sql.catalog.<name> and are loaded by Catalogs). A Table declares its schema, partitioning and TableCapability values, and mixes in SupportsRead or SupportsWrite to hand out scan and write builders. DataSourceV2Relation is the logical plan leaf that wraps the table.

tour.title: DataSource V2: scans, pushdown and writes
tour.description: The optimizer rule V2ScanRelationPushDown creates the ScanBuilder and pushes sample, filters, joins, aggregates, variants, limit and offset and column pruning into it (PushDownUtils), leaving in Spark whatever the source cannot handle. DataSourceV2Strategy then plans a BatchScanExec whose partitions are read by DataSourceRDD through a PartitionReaderFactory. Writes go through V2Writes, which builds the Write, and the exec nodes in WriteToDataSourceV2Exec, which run one DataWriter per task and finish with an atomic BatchWrite commit or an abort. The file based sources (FileTable, FileScan) implement the same interfaces.

tour.title: DataSource V2: the interfaces a connector implements
tour.description: A connector is built from small interfaces. TableProvider creates a Table. On the read side the Table returns a ScanBuilder, which can accept pushed down filters, required columns, aggregates, limit and top N through the SupportsPushDown mix-ins, and builds a Scan. The Scan produces a Batch that plans InputPartitions on the driver, and a PartitionReaderFactory that creates a PartitionReader on each executor. On the write side a WriteBuilder (with SupportsOverwrite, SupportsTruncate or SupportsDynamicOverwrite) builds a Write, whose BatchWrite creates a DataWriterFactory. Each task writes with a DataWriter and returns a WriterCommitMessage, and the driver then commits or aborts the whole job.

tour.title: The RDD library: pair operations and concrete RDDs
tour.description: Most RDD methods are thin wrappers that build one of a few RDD classes. map and filter create a MapPartitionsRDD, union a UnionRDD, coalesce a CoalescedRDD, zipPartitions a ZippedPartitionsRDD and cartesian a CartesianRDD. The key/value operations (reduceByKey, groupByKey, join, partitionBy) come from PairRDDFunctions: they end up in combineByKey or in CoGroupedRDD, and a Partitioner decides the shuffle layout. sortByKey in OrderedRDDFunctions uses a RangePartitioner. Input RDDs such as HadoopRDD and NewHadoopRDD read files and ParallelCollectionRDD turns a local collection into partitions.

tour.title: Checkpoints, broadcast variables and accumulators
tour.description: RDD.checkpoint is carried by an RDDCheckpointData object: the reliable variant writes the partitions to a checkpoint directory through ReliableCheckpointRDD and cuts the lineage, the local variant keeps blocks in executor storage. A broadcast variable is created by BroadcastManager; TorrentBroadcast splits the value into blocks that executors fetch and cache through the BlockManager. An AccumulatorV2 is registered on the driver, updated by tasks through add and merged back when a task finishes. SparkConf holds the spark.* settings, and StorageLevel and BlockId describe where cached and shuffle blocks are kept.

tour.title: Where the UI gets its data: listener, store and REST
tour.description: The UI does not read scheduler objects directly. AppStatusListener is a listener on the bus: for every job, stage, task and executor event it updates a Live* entity (LiveEntity) and writes it into the ElementTrackingStore, a KVStore that also triggers cleanup of old jobs, stages and tasks. AppStatusStore wraps the store with query methods, and both the web pages and the REST resources (ApiRootResource, OneApplicationResource, with the data classes in api.scala) read from it. The SQL tab has its own listener, SQLAppStatusListener, which builds execution data and aggregates SQL metric values.

tour.title: The web UI and the metrics system
tour.description: SparkUI extends WebUI and attaches tabs (Jobs, Stages, Executors and the SQL tab) whose pages are served by Jetty handlers created in JettyUtils; UIUtils renders the common page layout and tables. AllJobsPage, JobPage and StagePage show timelines and task tables from the status store, and the SQL ExecutionPage draws the plan graph built by SparkPlanGraph. Separately, MetricsSystem reads its configuration (MetricsConfig), registers Sources and starts Sinks, and ExecutorMetricType defines the executor metrics that are collected.

tour.title: SparkSession and Dataset in Scala
tour.description: SparkSession is the entry point. The API classes in sql/api are abstract so that the same code can run on classic Spark or Spark Connect; the classic SparkSession builds its sessionState and sharedState lazily, and sql() and the readers create Datasets. A classic Dataset is a logical plan plus a QueryExecution: transformations such as select, filter, join and groupBy create a new Dataset around a new LogicalPlan, and actions such as collect and count run the plan through the execution pipeline. Column wraps an expression tree that conversions and columnNodeSupport translate into Catalyst expressions.

tour.title: Reading, writing, catalog and configuration
tour.description: DataFrameReader resolves a data source into a plan when load is called, and DataFrameWriter (and the V2 writer) turn save, saveAsTable and insertInto into commands that are executed. The streaming reader and writer, together with StreamingQueryManager, start and track streaming queries. Catalog exposes databases, tables, functions and caching, RuntimeConfig gives access to SQL settings, and UDFRegistration registers user defined functions by name.

tour.title: Scheduler events: the listener bus
tour.description: Everything the scheduler does is announced as an event. The DAGScheduler and others post SparkListenerEvents to the LiveListenerBus, which queues them in AsyncEventQueues and delivers them on separate threads to listeners: the UI status listener, the event log writer, and others. EventLoggingListener writes the events to a log and ReplayListenerBus replays them later. Executors are tracked in the same way: HealthTracker excludes bad executors, ExecutorMonitor feeds dynamic allocation, and OutputCommitCoordinator decides which task attempt may commit its output.

tour.title: BlockManagerMaster: the driver's view of all blocks
tour.description: Each BlockManager registers with the BlockManagerMaster on the driver (through BlockManagerMasterEndpoint) and reports the blocks it holds, so the driver knows where every block lives. The messages are defined in BlockManagerMessages, the master can ask executors to remove blocks through BlockManagerStorageEndpoint, replication policies choose peers for replicated blocks, and the decommissioner migrates blocks away from an executor that is shutting down.

tour.title: The shuffle IO plugin API
tour.description: Where shuffle data is written can be replaced. ShuffleDataIO gives the driver and executor components; on an executor ShuffleExecutorComponents creates a ShuffleMapOutputWriter per map task, which hands out a ShufflePartitionWriter for each reduce partition and returns a MapOutputCommitMessage when committed. The default local disk implementation (LocalDiskShuffleDataIO and its writers) writes data and index files, and a single spill output can take a shortcut through SingleSpillShuffleMapOutputWriter.

tour.title: Serializers
tour.description: Data crossing a process or disk boundary must be serialized. Serializer creates SerializerInstances; JavaSerializer is the default Java implementation and KryoSerializer is a faster alternative that registers classes. SerializerManager picks the serializer and compression for each block depending on its type and where it is stored, and SerializationDebugger explains which field made a Java serialization fail.

tour.title: Executor metrics
tour.description: Executors report resource usage in two ways. Per task, TaskMetrics holds input, output and shuffle numbers (InputMetrics, OutputMetrics and the shuffle reporters). Per executor, ExecutorMetricsPoller samples JVM and memory metrics and ExecutorMetrics carries them to the driver, while ExecutorSource and ExecutorMetricsSource expose them to the metrics system.

tour.title: RPC: endpoints, the dispatcher and the inbox
tour.description: Spark components talk through an RpcEnv. An RpcEndpoint receives messages and replies through an RpcCallContext; an RpcEndpointRef is the handle used to send or ask. In the Netty implementation NettyRpcEnv registers endpoints in the Dispatcher, which puts each incoming message in the endpoint's Inbox, processed by a MessageLoop on a thread pool; messages to remote endpoints go through an Outbox per address. RpcTimeout wraps the timeouts of asks.

tour.title: Writing files: commit protocols
tour.description: saveAsHadoopFile and the DataFrame file writers do not write to the final directory directly. A FileCommitProtocol creates temporary files for each task attempt, commits a task by moving its files, and commits the job at the end (or aborts it), so output appears atomically. HadoopMapReduceCommitProtocol and HadoopMapRedCommitProtocol implement it on top of the Hadoop output committers, and SparkHadoopWriter runs the write tasks for an RDD and applies the protocol.

tour.title: Moving blocks between executors: the block transfer service
tour.description: When a task needs a block held by another executor, the BlockManager asks a BlockTransferService. The Netty implementation (NettyBlockTransferService) opens a client connection configured by SparkTransportConf, and the serving side NettyBlockRpcServer answers fetch and upload requests by reading from the local BlockDataManager.

tour.title: Heartbeats and cleanup
tour.description: Executors report to the driver on a schedule: Heartbeater sends a heartbeat with task metrics, and the driver side HeartbeatReceiver answers, and marks executors dead when they stay silent. ContextCleaner runs on the driver and removes shuffle files, broadcasts, accumulators and cached RDDs once the objects that referred to them are garbage collected.

tour.title: Barrier execution mode and task end reasons
tour.description: In barrier mode all tasks of a stage start together and can synchronize. BarrierTaskContext gives a task barrier() and allGather(), and BarrierCoordinator on the driver collects the requests. When a task ends, a TaskEndReason (Success, FetchFailed, ExceptionFailure, TaskKilled and others) tells the scheduler what to do next.

tour.title: The Java API and the Py4J gateway
tour.description: JavaSparkContext and the JavaRDD classes are thin wrappers that give Java callers the same operations as the Scala SparkContext and RDD, converting functions and collections. On the Python side, PythonGatewayServer starts a Py4JServer that the PySpark driver connects to, so Python can call JVM objects, and helpers such as PythonPartitioner and PythonHadoopUtil convert partitioners and Hadoop data between the two sides.

tour.title: Resource profiles: what tasks and executors ask for
tour.description: A ResourceProfile describes the executor resources (cores, memory, GPUs and other custom resources) and the task resources a stage needs. It is built with ResourceProfileBuilder from ExecutorResourceRequests and TaskResourceRequests, registered with the ResourceProfileManager, and its resources are discovered on a node by ResourceUtils (optionally through a discovery script) and handed to tasks by ResourceAllocator as ResourceInformation.

tour.title: Where spark.* settings are defined
tour.description: Core settings are not read as bare strings: each one is declared once as a ConfigEntry with ConfigBuilder, giving its key, type, default and documentation. The big package object in internal.config holds most entries, and separate files group the entries for deploy, the history server, Kryo, network, Python, R and the status store. SparkConf reads values through these entries.

tour.title: Utils and small helpers
tour.description: Most of core leans on a few shared helpers. Utils collects hundreds of small functions: loading classes with the right class loader, creating and deleting temp directories, fetching files and archives, resolving host names, parsing sizes and time strings, finding the user call site of an RDD operation and running external commands. Alongside it are Clock implementations for testable time, byte buffer streams, class loaders that let user jars override Spark's, and DependencyUtils which resolves the jars and files given to spark-submit.

tour.title: Events as JSON: JsonProtocol and ListenerBus
tour.description: ListenerBus is the generic base for posting an event to a list of listeners and catching listener failures. For the event log and the history server, JsonProtocol turns each scheduler event into a JSON line and parses it back, including task metrics, accumulables and failure reasons, so that ReplayListenerBus can rebuild the same events later.

tour.title: Spilling sorters: UnsafeExternalSorter and its spill files
tour.description: When records no longer fit in memory, UnsafeExternalSorter hands sorted runs to UnsafeSorterSpillWriter. UnsafeSorterSpillReader reads a run back, and UnsafeSorterSpillMerger with UnsafeSorterBoundedSpillMerger merge the runs through the UnsafeSorterIterator interface. PrefixComparators and RadixSort speed up the in-memory sort.

tour.title: Sampling: RandomSampler and XORShiftRandom
tour.description: RandomSampler is the trait behind sample, with Bernoulli and Poisson samplers that draw from a seeded generator. XORShiftRandom is the fast Random replacement they use, and StratifiedSamplingUtils computes per-key acceptance thresholds for sampleByKey.

tour.title: Standalone deploy messages: DeployMessage and the descriptions
tour.description: DeployMessage holds the case classes that the standalone Master, Worker, driver client and applications exchange over RPC: registration, launching and killing executors and drivers, and state changes. ApplicationDescription, DriverDescription and ExecutorDescription describe what to run, and Client submits and kills drivers on a standalone cluster.

tour.title: Standalone Master recovery: persistence engines and leader election
tour.description: PersistenceEngine stores applications, drivers and workers so a new Master can rebuild its state. FileSystemPersistenceEngine, RocksDBPersistenceEngine and ZooKeeperPersistenceEngine are the implementations, created through RecoveryModeFactory. ZooKeeperLeaderElectionAgent decides which Master is the leader and reports changes through LeaderElectionAgent.

tour.title: Event log files: writers, readers and compaction
tour.description: EventLogFileWriters creates the writer for a single file or a rolling set of files, and EventLogFileReaders opens either form again. EventLogFileCompactor rewrites old rolling files using EventFilter and BasicEventFilterBuilder to drop events that are no longer needed, such as those of finished jobs.

tour.title: History server: from log directory to a rebuilt UI
tour.description: FsHistoryProvider scans the event log directory, replays logs through ReplayListenerBus into a status store, and lists the applications. HistoryServer serves those listings and, through the ApplicationCache, a SparkUI per application. HistoryServerDiskManager and HistoryServerMemoryManager bound the resources, and HybridStore keeps a store in memory while it is written to disk.

tour.title: REST API: from resource class to status store
tour.description: ApiRootResource dispatches to resource classes such as ApplicationListResource and StagesResource. They read data from AppStatusStore, convert it to the api.scala classes, and JacksonMessageWriter writes it as JSON. PrometheusResource exposes executor metrics in the Prometheus text format.

tour.title: BytesToBytesMap: an off-heap hash map
tour.description: BytesToBytesMap stores keys and values as raw bytes in memory pages obtained from TaskMemoryManager, with open addressing over a long array. HashMapGrowthStrategy decides how the array grows, and the map can spill or hand its records to UnsafeExternalSorter when memory runs short.
